name: 1d-cnn-backbone-training

name: 1d-cnn-training-on-metabolomic-signals

name: 1d-convolutional-layer-configuration-for-ms-vectors

description: Use when a preprocessed spatial metabolomics peak intensity matrix (pixels x m/z ions) from MALDI/DESI-MSI is available and you need to flag which ions are adduct forms and quantify the adduct distribution.

name: adduct-ion-species-prediction
description: Use when you have a list of molecular formulae for LC-IM-MS / drift tube IM-MS data and need predicted ion species (primary ion plus adducts, positive or negative mode, multiply charged) to build targeted m/z search traces.

name: adduct-ion-targeted-search-in-rt-window
description: Use when the primary ion of a molecular formula has a confirmed RT window in a profile LC-DTIM-MS mzML file and you need to screen additional adduct ions (positive/negative mode), extract IM peaks, and derive DTCCS(N2) values.

name: adduct-ion-variant-matching
description: Use when validating a molecular network's ability to recover adduct-related spectral pairs — specifically sodiated variants disconnected from protonated precursors under similarity-threshold networking.

name: adduct-ionmode-cross-validation
description: Use when cleaning an MS/MS spectral library where spectra carry adduct, ionmode, precursor m/z and parent mass metadata (e.g. .msp/.MGF GNPS entries) and you must detect inconsistent annotations before matching.

name: adduct-isotope-confidence-rating
description: Use when interpreting mummichog metabolite predictions from an untargeted LC/MS feature table: predicted compounds must be rated by the presence of expected ion forms (M+H[1+], M−H[−], adducts, C13 isotopes) before counting or reporting them.

name: adduct-isotope-derivative-enumeration
description: Use when an untargeted LC/MS feature table (m/z, retention time, p-value) must be mapped to metabolites without MS/MS spectra, by enumerating isotopic and adduct forms (e.g. M+H[1+], M(C13)+H[1+], M+Na[1+], M−H[−]) from neutral compound formulas in a genome-scale metabolic model.

name: adduct-isotope-pattern-annotation
description: Use when a processed peak list (post peak-picking/alignment, e.g. from XCMS or the DIMS SIM-stitch pipeline) needs metabolite annotations where adduct forms and isotopic abundance patterns across co-eluting/co-occurring peaks should be exploited rather than matching single masses alone.

name: adduct-isotope-two-tier-tree-alignment
description: Use when a feature table from LC-MS untargeted metabolomics or isotope tracing must be organized into empirical compounds: pattern-matched feature pairs (e.g. 1.0034 Da 13C/12C, 22.9893 Da Na+) form a mass distance network that needs tree conversion and neutral mass inference.

name: adduct-isotopologue-assignment
description: Use when an Asari-derived feature table must be grouped into empirical compounds (empCpds) prior to MS1 or MS2 annotation, so that isotopologues and adducts of the same metabolite are annotated as one unit.

name: adduct-level-annotation-counting
description: Use when comparing coverage of two or more in-silico lipid fragmentation libraries and you need a per-lipid-class, per-adduct count matrix of library entries and annotated features to flag classes present in only one library.

name: adduct-mass-calculation
description: Use when building an in-house RT/m/z metabolite library from mzML files of authentic standards and you need expected per-adduct m/z values to target EIC extraction before peak finding.

name: adduct-mass-calculation-positive-mode
description: Use when a list of significant ion m/z values (e.g. up/down-regulated ions from an rMSIKeyIon 'ions' output list) must be assigned putative metabolite identities in positive-ion LDI/MSI data.

name: adduct-mass-correction
description: Use when preparing raw tandem MS/MS spectra (from NIST20/23 SDF exports or MassSpecGym TSVs) for ICEBERG/SCARF training or evaluation, where peaks must be expressed as neutral fragment masses.

name: adduct-mass-range-restriction
description: Use when preparing a CCS training set from the McLean Unified CCS Compendium for [M-H]-, [M+H]+ or [M+Na]+ adducts and entries must be restricted to the mass ranges supported by DeepCCS, AllCCS or CCSbase.

name: adduct-mass-shift-calculation
description: Use when a list of unannotated experimental m/z peaks (e.g. 200 peaks of 150-300 Da from an E. coli untargeted metabolomics dataset) must be matched against predicted compounds from a Pickaxe network expansion by enumerating adducted m/z values.

name: adduct-mass-shift-calculation
description: Use when preparing an m/z annotation reference index from SDF-derived compound databases (ChEBI, HMDB, GNPS, LIPIDMAPS) where each neutral mass must be expanded into ion masses for the polarity and adduct set being searched.

name: adduct-mass-subtraction-from-fragment-peaks
description: Use when an MS2 peak list must be annotated with subformulae of a candidate precursor formula to score formula/adduct candidates de novo — e.g. when building inputs for a formula transformer and fragmentation trees are too slow or unnecessary.

name: adduct-mz-rt-conflict-detection
description: Use when finalizing an in-house LC-MS metabolite standard library built with metScribeR and you must flag adduct pairs whose m/z and RT overlap within the LC-MS method's separation ability before CSV export.

name: adduct-mz-variant-prediction
description: Use when a neutral-mass compound database (e.g. HMDB, FooDB) must be converted into an m/z-searchable annotation resource, or when matching observed peak m/z values (with a known ppm error margin) against compounds whose adduct and isotope variants are not yet enumerated.

name: adduct-notation-normalization
description: Use when merging spectral-library or feature-table records whose ion-identity annotations appear in inconsistent spellings (e.g. 'M + H', 'M + H +', '[M + H]+') and you need them aggregated as one ion identity before networking or counting.

name: adduct-precursor-mass-calculation
description: Use when a compound list supplies molecular formulas or SMILES strings (target/suspect entries) and precursor ion masses must be derived under a chosen adduct before peak extraction.

name: adduct-probability-feature-correlation-scoring
description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics dataset carries multiple putative annotations per feature (CMM-generated annotation tables) and annotations must be prioritized for pathway analysis using adduct probability and feature-correlation evidence.

name: adduct-probability-ranking
description: Use when a RowMerger-merged annotation table contains multiple putative annotations per feature and a feature-intensity table is available, and the goal is to prioritize the most probable annotation per feature.

name: adduct-redundancy-accounting
description: Use when counting unique lipid ions, features, or lipid types from annotation workbooks produced by LipidMatch or comparable lipid identification software, where multiple adducts of the same lipid species appear across features.

name: adduct-reference-mass-matching
description: Use when you have a binned mass-difference histogram from MALDI-MSI peak pairs and want to count occurrences of known adducts (Na+, K+, 13C, DHB or CHCA matrix adducts) within instrument mass tolerance.

name: adduct-relationship-inference
description: Use when a processed, annotated LC-MS feature table (tidymass massdataset) contains suspected in-source fragmentation products misannotated as genuine metabolites and no in-pipeline deconvolution exists.

name: adduct-rule-based-ion-annotation
description: Use when you have CAMERA pseudo-spectra from LC/MS data in positive or negative ion mode and need to label peaks as isotope, adduct or fragment species and derive the quasi-molecular ion mass.

name: adduct-rule-table-matching
description: Use when grouping has produced CAMERA compound spectra from LC/MS peak lists (positive and/or negative ESI mode) and you need to assign ion-species annotations and propose accurate compound masses from adduct/isotope rules.

name: adduct-series-mass-difference-validation
description: Use when identify_adducts() output from a direct-injection plasma ionization (DBDI) MS dataset must be checked: candidate features should share a base analyte and differ by exact O-adduct deltas.

name: adduct-species-annotation
description: Use when you have an untargeted LC-MS metabolomics feature table (m/z per sample) plus MS2 spectra in .mgf or .mzML format and need to assign metabolite identities to peaks at MS1 and MS2 levels.
tools: CEU Mass Mediator (via CMMR R package)

name: adduct-species-simulation
description: Use when you need to stress-test an LC-HRMS feature alignment tool (e.g. MetMatch) against a known ground truth by injecting artificial adduct variants and retention-time perturbations into a reference feature list.

name: adduct-specific-ccs-benchmarking
description: Use when you have a dataset of compounds with SMILES, an adduct type from {[M+H]+, [M-H]-, [M+Na]+}, and experimental CCS values, and need to quantitatively compare two or more CCS predictors.

name: adduct-specific-model-comparison
description: Use when you have trained CCSP 2.0 linear SVR models for multiple adduct ion types and need to understand which Mordred descriptor classes and counts each adduct-specific model relies on.

name: adduct-state-matching-for-ccs-comparison
description: Use when experimentally measured CCS values (e.g., TWIMS from Supporting Information Tables S1/S2) must be compared against literature CCS values per metabolite/adduct pair to quantify between-laboratory deviation or justify a ±3% acceptance threshold.

name: adduct-stratified-model-evaluation
description: Use when you need to rank a machine-learning collision cross section predictor (e.g. CCSP 2.0) against alternatives like CCSbase, AllCCS or DeepCCS using held-out test splits drawn from a measured CCS compendium stratified by adduct type.

name: adjacency-index-maximal-clique-deduplication
description: Use when a large tokenised BGC dataset (e.g. antiSMASH-DB domain-tokenised clusters) contains near-duplicate clusters that must be reduced to a non-redundant set before motif/sub-cluster mining.

name: adjacency-matrix-construction
description: Use when building pathway-level adjacency matrices from gene-gene interaction edges for NetGSA, especially when networks are large (>1,000 genes per component) and block-diagonal per-condition structure is needed.

name: adjacency-matrix-prior-design-ablation
description: Use when validating design choices of a discrete graph diffusion model for molecular generation — specifically whether the prior distribution over edge-type categories in the adjacency matrix materially affects top-k accuracy, MCES distance, or Tanimoto similarity.

name: adjacency-matrix-symmetry-validation
description: Use when a metabolite/pathway graph is supplied as an adjacency matrix that must feed into Laplacian construction, since the regularized normalized Laplacian and downstream kernel are only valid for symmetric, undirected graphs.

name: adjacency-matrix-tensor-construction
description: Use when converting rooted molecular fragment graphs (atom/bond-labeled, rooted at a cleaved-bond atom) into fixed-length topological feature vectors for training or applying CFM-ID-style fragmentation transition models.

name: adjusted-rand-index-cluster-comparison
description: Use when spatial transcriptome and MALDI-MSI (or other spatial omics) sections have been aligned by competing methods and cluster labels exist on both sections, and you need label transfer AC/ARI to rank the alignments.

name: adjusted-rsquared-batch-variability-quantification
description: Use when you have a batch-corrected (or raw) metabolomics matrix with a batch-level column and need to measure per-metabolite residual association with batch to select the correction model.

name: adversarial-autoencoder-loss-configuration
description: Use when running or ablating RALPS's composite objective on multi-batch metabolomics intensity tables to test whether the classifier, autoencoder-regularization and variation loss terms each contribute measurably to normalization quality.

name: aems-ejection-time-estimation
description: Use when AEMS .wiff raw data lacks explicit ejection times and each shot must be associated with its detected peak — e.g. evenly spaced acoustic ejections at a ~1000 ms nominal interval from a 384-well plate run.

name: aems-full-scan-peak-detection
description: Use when processing full-scan AEMS plate data (384- or 1536-well) in R where persistent high-intensity baseline signals obscure analyte peaks and shot-to-peak association plus baseline correction and area integration must be automated.

name: aems-full-scan-plate-processing
description: Use when a full 384-well plate of AEMS data in full-scan (PI) mode must be processed end-to-end with rtmsEcho and the elapsed wall-clock time must be verified against the reported <30 s (up to a 60 Da window) benchmark.

name: aems-full-scan-spectrum-reconstruction
description: Use when processing AEMS full-scan acquisitions (PI or NL mode) stored in .wiff/.wiff.scan files and you need a per-ejection spectrum compatible with the rtms R package data structure rather than vendor software output.

name: aems-mrm-plate-processing
description: Use when you must process a 384-well AEMS plate in MRM mode (<5 transitions) with rtmsEcho and check whether the sub-2 s per-plate processing benchmark reported in the paper holds on your run.

name: aems-shot-window-quantification
description: Use when analyzing AEMS MRM raw data (XIC per transition across multiple ejections) where per-well peak areas must be computed by aligning the ejection detection-window table, subtracting the per-transition baseline, and summing baseline-corrected intensities inside each ejection's window.

name: afff-nontargeted-data-processing
description: Use when processing LC-HRMS/MS acquisitions of AFFF or environmental/biological samples for non-targeted PFAS annotation, where raw MS/MS data must be filtered and scored rather than curated manually.

name: affine-transform-application-to-msi-images
description: Use when you have imzML MALDI-MSI data plus an H&E image and an already-computed co-registration matrix (e.g. from MSIght register_he_msi), and need per-peptide or per-protein ion images spatially transformed into histology coordinates for overlay.

name: affine-transformation-estimation
description: Use when two neighboring spatial-omics sections (e.g. h5ad files with obsm['spatial'] coordinates from 10X Visium and MALDI-MSI) share no spots or features and must be registered before spot-to-spot integration.

name: affine-transformation-of-bimodal-images
description: Use when paired IMC and TOF-SIMS images of the same tissue FOV must be spatially aligned before single-cell segmentation or protein-metabolite correlation, and simple rotation-only or random-shift alignment is insufficient.

name: affinity-propagation-gene-cluster-family-clustering
description: Use when benchmarking BGC clustering quality against manually curated MIBiG group labels (e.g., reproducing a V-score baseline), or when non-convex GCF structure is expected and pairwise network-based clustering is affordable for the dataset size.

name: age-group-classification-mouse-brain-metabolomics
description: Use when a labeled LC-MS metabolomics feature table (e.g., the Zenodo-deposited Aging Mouse Brain data) must be turned into a phenotype-prediction classifier distinguishing sample groups such as adolescence vs middle-age.

name: age-stratified-survival-analysis
description: Use when testing whether biomarker–mortality associations hold across age groups, especially where conventional risk factors (e.g., systolic blood pressure, total cholesterol) show opposite associations in the elderly versus middle age.

name: agglomerative-fuzzy-cluster-merging
description: Use when a Fisher's-test pathway enrichment table contains many significantly enriched pathways with substantial content overlap (within or across pathway databases), and a non-redundant grouping of enriched pathways is needed for interpretation.

name: agglomerative-maximum-linkage-clustering
description: Use when raw N-dimensional (m/z, drift time, retention time) mass spectrometry peak lists from multiple samples—e.g. the 152 plasma samples of the SRM 1950 study—must be reduced to one feature per row aligned across samples under tight tolerances.

name: aggregate-detection-rate-calculation
description: Use when you have a set of BioTransformer 3.0-predicted metabolites for a panel of drugs and matched LC-HRMS detections from 24-hour S9 incubation samples, and need an aggregate detected/predicted percentage.

name: aggregate-p-value-combination
description: Use when contributing studies report only aggregate statistics (p-value, fold-change, sample size per compound) and you need a combined meta-analysis estimate per compound without access to individual-level data.

name: aggregate-statistics-meta-analysis
description: Use when input consists of published per-study aggregate statistics (p-value and fold-change) for metabolites across clinical studies, and compounds must be harmonized across synonym identifiers before combining.

name: aggregated-feature-run-detection-in-randomized-sequences
description: Use when auditing a randomized or complete-randomized LC/GC-MS injection sequence for clustered features, e.g. consecutive same-group runs in treatment/gender/age strata.

name: agilent-masshunter-raw-file-handling
description: Reference for examining IM-MS instrument settings and acquisition performance when the input is an Agilent ".d" raw MS-file that must be opened or whose acquisition parameters need to be exported to a text file.

name: aic-based-regression-model-selection
description: Use when a lipidomics abundance table carries attached sample study variables (e.g., body mass index, tissue, condition) and you must identify which lipids exert the highest effect in distinguishing those variables.

name: aicc-model-ranking
description: Use when multiple plausible moiety/deconvolution models exist for MS-measured isotopologue timecourses and you must objectively select the model, e.g. ranking 41 UDP-GlcNAc models fitted with SAGA by AICc.

name: aif-fragment-down-weighting-scoring
description: Use when ranking candidate metabolite annotations for features from all-ion fragmentation (AIF) LC–MS data, where each candidate must be scored by combining m/z error with pseudo-MS/MS fragment matching and AIF-only matches must be penalized.

name: aif-lcms-metabolite-annotation
description: Use when annotating features from centroid-mode LC-MS AIF chromatograms (e.g., xcms/RAMClustR output) against fragment libraries, especially when isotopologues, in-source fragments, and adducts must be labeled and only a statistically significant subset of features needs annotation.

name: aif-parent-fragment-deconvolution
description: Use when processing centroid-mode AIF LC–MS chromatograms whose parent–fragment relationships must be deconvoluted into pseudo-MS/MS spectra for metabolite annotation of isotopologues, adducts, and in-source fragments.

name: aif-pseudo-msms-deconvolution
description: Use when processing centroid-mode AIF LC–MS/MS chromatograms where no targeted MS/MS scans exist, and the goal is to recover parent–fragment relationships and annotate adducts, isotopologues, and in-source fragments.

name: aird-format-ms-data-loading
description: Use when vendor DDA LC-MS files (.wiff, .raw) must be converted to Aird format and imported into MetaPro for multi-batch target search or QC inspection.

name: aird-metadata-schema-handling
description: Use when reading, validating, generating, or comparing the metadata/index side of an Aird file pair (.json index + .aird data), or when deciding between JSON and XML for mass spec metadata storage.

name: aird-vs-mzml-decoding-comparison
description: Use when choosing or validating an MS data storage format for MRM acquisition files, or when replicating decoding-speed benchmarks between Aird and mzML on full-file and random-access reading modes.

name: algorithm-order-invariance-testing
description: Use when aligning two or more independently processed nontargeted LC-MS datasets with Eclipse's MSAligner and you need to verify that the graph-based feature grouping result does not depend on dataset insertion order.

name: algorithm-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when several candidate peak-picking algorithms must be compared for reliability vs. wall-clock runtime on LC-HRMS chromatogram data (mzXML), e.g. to choose a MetMatch peak-picking backend.

name: aligned-feature-table-processing
description: Use when you need to estimate or reproduce the alignment FDR of DeepRTAlign output — e.g. re-deriving information_target.csv filtering from information_all.csv using the decoy/target ratio with the default fdr=0.01 threshold.

name: alignment-accuracy-evaluation-metrics
description: Use when an LC–MS feature alignment output (consensus feature table) must be quantitatively scored against a manually annotated feature dataset, e.g. benchmarking G-Aligner vs OpenMS/MZmine2/XCMS on MTBLS562, QE_HF or TripleTOF_6600.

name: alignment-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantify how many more peptides or MS features a candidate LC-MS retention time alignment workflow aligns versus MBR-based or feature-based baselines, while checking that quantitative accuracy is not compromised.

name: alignment-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when a new or modified LC-HRMS alignment configuration needs quantitative validation against a ground-truth benchmark, e.g. after changing m/z or retention-time tolerance settings or adduct-recombination rules.

name: alignment-benchmark-reanalysis
description: Use when re-evaluating an LC-MS peak-list alignment algorithm against published ground-truth alignments and you need precision/recall recomputed per dataset fraction and per feature count, especially for RANSAC vs Join comparisons on proteomic (P1, P2) and metabolomic (M1, M2) data.

name: alignment-coverage-count-validation-against-reference-table
description: Use when reproducing a multi-dataset LC-MS feature alignment where the number of features found in all datasets and in n≥k datasets must be checked against a published reference table (e.g., Supplementary Table S2 values 976 and 5334).

name: alignment-loss-quantification
description: Use when you have both unaligned and aligned NPP output tables (e.g. XCMS_unaligned_run3.csv and XCMS_aligned_run3.csv) plus a generated benchmark, and you need to quantify peaks lost or misaligned during sample alignment.

name: alignment-order-dependence-assessment
description: Use when combining three or more independently processed LC-MS feature tables with a sequential alignment tool and you must verify that matched annotations are order-invariant and that spurious annotation mismatches are quantified against a reference alignment.

name: alignment-precision-recall-evaluation
description: Use when you must quantitatively compare a peak list alignment method's output rows to known ground-truth correspondences, or reproduce the RANSAC vs Join aligner benchmark on synthetic lipidomic and real Lange et al. datasets.

name: alignment-representative-spectra-export
description: Use when you must reproduce MS-DIAL's aligned LC-MS output (text export and .dcl representative spectra) from source without building a GUI project file or EIC cache, e.g. for large file-count cohorts where the full alignment mode is too memory-heavy.

name: all-ion-fragmentation-controller-configuration
description: Use when simulating DIA-mode LC-MS/MS acquisition over a set of generated or extracted chemicals — e.g. you need fragmentation scans covering an m/z range rather than single-precursor DDA selections.

name: allen-atlas-anatomical-mapping
description: Use when pixel-level clustering of a brain IMS feature matrix (e.g., 14,260 pixels x 3,044 m/z ions) must be validated against a reference anatomy atlas to confirm clusters recover known tissue divisions.

name: ambiguous-identifier-aggregation
description: Use when a metabolomics table has sparse or missing cross-database identifiers (HMDB, ChEBI, KEGG, PubChem, LIPID MAPS) and records of the same metabolite must be linked across databases despite mismatches and missing foreign references.

name: amine-derivatization-site-detection
description: Use when predicting m/z values of amine-derivatized metabolites (e.g. dopamine, GABA, spermidine with AMPP) where reactive sites and the resulting mass shifts must be computed from structural SMILES before annotation.

name: amino-acid-biocrates-p180-kit-analysis
description: Use when raw SRM/MRM files from a Biocrates AbsoluteIDQ p180 plate (e.g., Waters Xevo TQ-S serum runs) must be reanalyzed in Skyline to reproduce or audit vendor-reported amino acid concentrations.

name: amino-acid-composition-analysis
description: Use when you have a FASTA collection of peptide sequences and need the overall residue frequency distribution to determine which amino acids dominate, e.g., characterizing natural peptide hormone composition.

name: amino-acid-derivatization-response-ratio-quantification
description: Use when GC-MS peak-area tables of amino acids paired with stable-isotope-labeled internal standards are available and you need to compare precision (RSD) across derivatization reagents or report one-to-one ISTD-normalized amino-acid quantities.

name: amino-acid-level-mass-matching-evaluation
description: Use when raw per-tool de novo prediction sets (peptide sequence + tool-specific confidence score) must be filtered to a precision-calibrated subset, using a pseudo-ground-truth peptide list from database search at 1% FDR.

name: amino-acid-mass-matching-criterion
description: Use when comparing de novo peptide predictions to reference peptide sequences where exact string equality is too strict, e.g. to classify incorrect predictions into error categories (last-3-AA inversions, 1-AA replacements, >6 wrongly assigned AAs) across tools like Casanovo or PointNovo.

name: amino-acid-matching-metric-computation
description: Use when scoring de novo sequencing predictions (e.g. from Casanovo, PointNovo, DeepNovo, SMSNet, Novor, pNovo 3) against a PSM-derived ground truth to get peptide recall, amino acid recall/precision, or precision-recall AUC across enzymatic digests.

name: amino-acid-metabolomics-meta-analysis-comparison
description: Use when you have a table of per-study effect sizes and standard errors for multiple metabolite/amino acid compounds and need to pool them per compound, test heterogeneity (Cochran's Q, I2), and reproduce or cross-check a published significant compound-level result.

name: amino-acid-precision-metric-computation
description: Use when evaluating de novo peptide sequencing predictions (e.g. from Casanovo) against annotated MGF benchmark spectra and you need peptide-level AP, amino acid-level AP, and precursor mass accuracy to compare against published values.

name: analog-pair-eligibility-filtering
description: Use when building an evaluation benchmark of analog pairs for modification-site localization, or when you need a defensible subset of structurally related compound pairs from GNPS libraries before running ModiFinder, CFM-ID, or random baselines.

name: analogues-test-set-cross-validation-design
description: Use when benchmarking MS2 library-matching or analogue-search methods on an annotated spectral library and you need a leakage-free test set with structure-based (Tanimoto vs recall) evaluation rather than only spectral scores.

name: analytical-variation-assessment-metabolomics
description: Use when you have a post-XCMS RAMClustR clustered metabolomics object and need to demonstrate that spectral aggregation lowers analytical variation (CV) relative to single-feature measurements.

name: anchor-peak-selection-by-spacing-and-noise
description: Use when aligning LC-MS feature tables across many chromatograms where retention-time drift is nonlinear and QC-pool peak metadata (RT, m/z, height, spacing, noise) are available to define anchors.

name: anchor-sample-linear-rt-rescaling
description: Use when LC-MS feature lists from multiple runs exhibit global (monotonic) retention time drift and you need a coarse RT correction before deep-learning-based direct matching in DeepRTAlign.

name: anchor-suspect-pair-spectral-similarity-benchmarking
description: Use when you have anchor–suspect spectral pairs (e.g. from GNPS molecular networking) and need to quantify what fraction of suspect structures can be recovered by applying biotransformation rules and ranking derivatives.

name: angularjs-single-page-app-development
description: Use when migrating static HTML data pages into a dynamic repository: a relational backend (PostgreSQL) and REST-like API (mibig-api) already exist, and users need in-browser filtering, sorting and query building over annotation metadata.

name: ann-fingerprint-prediction
description: Use when an unknown LC-MS/MS analyte spectrum (precursor mass + m/z/intensity peak list) must be annotated by predicting a 528-bit fingerprint and ranking candidate compounds retrieved by precursor m/z or molecular formula.

name: ann-index-benchmarking
description: Use when an open spectral library search is too slow with exact candidate selection and alternative ANN index structures must be compared against the ANN-SoLo random projection tree baseline on large peptide spectral libraries.

name: ann-index-configuration-tuning
description: Use when configuring ANN-SoLo's ANN index (ensemble of random projection trees, nodes inspected per query) for an open modification spectral library search, to trade identification counts toward the full-search baseline against search speed.

name: ann-multilabel-fingerprint-training
description: Use when training a fingerprint predictor from labeled MS/MS spectra (positive mode, collision-cell HCD/QqQ/Q-TOF or IT instruments, 100–1010 Da, H+ or NH4+ adducts) and you need a single network outputting the full fingerprint vector rather than per-digit models.

name: ann-recall-versus-speed-tuning
description: Use when configuring or re-running the ANN candidate-selection stage of an ANN-SoLo open search on large spectral libraries (e.g., MassIVE-KB or NIST human HCD), where you must trade recall of candidate library spectra against query traversal cost.

name: annotated-feature-list-export
description: Use when an aligned peak table (m/z, retention-time pairs) exported from a peak-detection/alignment stage needs formula assignments, isotopic-pattern scores, and MS/MS library identifications.

name: annotated-mgf-spectra-finetuning
description: Use when a pretrained de novo sequencing model shows a systematic bias on a target spectral domain (e.g. reduced precision on non-tryptic peptides) and annotated MGF training/validation/test splits for that domain are available.

name: annotated-mgf-training-data-downsampling
description: Use when comparing two de novo sequencing training sets of different sizes: you need size-matched training data to test whether data quality (e.g., curated MassIVE-KB PSMs) rather than peptide count drives performance.

name: annotathon-contribution-quantification
description: Use when a curated repository article describes multiple human-curation channels and the goal is to tally new entries per channel and attribute specific records (e.g. compounds) to a channel.

name: annotation-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when SIRIUS/ZODIAC result files are available for LC-MS/MS datasets with known ground-truth formulas, and you need to quantify how annotation correctness varies with ZODIAC score thresholds (e.g. 0.7–0.99).

name: annotation-accuracy-computation
description: Use when top-ranked molecular formula annotations (e.g. from SIRIUS or ZODIAC) for untargeted LC-MS/MS compounds must be scored against a manually validated ground truth across datasets.

name: annotation-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when you must judge whether a peak-annotation method (e.g., KGMN network layer vs CAMERA isotope/adduct rules) assigns ion forms correctly, using a manually curated benchmark peak table with known ion forms.

name: annotation-agreement-statistics
description: Use when comparing compound annotations produced by two spectral libraries (e.g. CalicoLipids vs MS-DIAL) over the same feature table and you must reproduce per-library, shared, and concordance counts stratified by instrument or ionization mode.

name: annotation-alignment-separation-from-rs-module
description: Use when QC specimens include external standards acquired in a different biological matrix than the reference standard, and their features must be matched to a separate .msp target library independent of the RS module.

name: annotation-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when you need baseline annotation performance for ISDB-DNP, Sirius, or MS-Finder on a labelled MS/MS spectra set (e.g. 2,107 reference-identified spectra) before evaluating any re-ranking or rescoring method.

name: annotation-candidate-true-positive-classification
description: Use when evaluating whether predicted-vs-measured CCS differences can separate true from false annotation candidates, e.g. sweeping ΔCCS thresholds across 10, 7, 5, 3, 1, or 0 ppm mass windows to compute ROC AUC for CCSP-based filtering.

name: annotation-concordance-benchmarking
description: Use when SpaMTP-produced m/z annotations must be validated against a deposited reference table or an external tool (METASPACE), to estimate annotation concordance on a control dataset.

name: annotation-confidence-assignment
description: Use when a MetDNA3/MrnAnnoAlgo3 result table from recursive network annotation propagation (getMetAnno()) must be turned into a confidence-assigned, redundancy-filtered annotation table before computing coverage or Top 1/3/10 correct rates and Top 3 FDR.

name: annotation-confidence-binning-analysis
description: Use when ranked metabolite annotation candidates exist with per-query cosine scores and correctness labels, and the goal is to quantify how annotation reliability grows with the Δcos gap between top-1 and top-2 candidates.

name: annotation-confidence-level-assignment
description: Use when empCpd JSON from pcpfm has MS2 spectra already mapped to features/empirical compounds and reference .msp spectral libraries are available, and Level 2 identifications are needed.

name: annotation-confidence-level-grading
description: Use when you have a pre-processed untargeted feature table from patRoon or MS-DIAL and need one Schymanski confidence level per annotated feature before statistics or reporting.

name: annotation-confidence-level-mapping
description: Use when curating or transcribing a metabolomics software catalog where LC-MS/GC-MS annotation tools must be tagged with Schymanski confidence levels (Level 4, Level 3, Level 2a) alongside functional category and instrumental data type.

name: annotation-confidence-metadata-handling
description: Use when untargeted metabolomics feature tables produced by patRoon (featureGroups/MFsummary objects) or MS-DIAL (area exports) need to be imported into R with annotation confidence levels assigned before QC filtering and statistics.

name: annotation-consistency-checking
description: Use when a mass spectral library entry carries SMILES/InChI/InChIKey metadata whose mutual agreement must be verified before the spectrum is accepted, e.g. during library cleaning or validation-filter reporting.

name: annotation-consistency-statistics
description: Use when KGMN/MetDNA2-annotated unknown peaks (e.g., from NIST urine pos/neg mode) lack standards and spectral library entries, and you need in silico MS/MS tool agreement statistics to corroborate annotations.

name: annotation-correctness-overlap-analysis
description: Use when two annotation/ prediction methods have been run on the same query spectra and you need to quantify overlap vs. complementarity of their correct-annotation sets (e.g., BAM vs. SIRIUS on 60,368 anchor–suspect pairs).

name: annotation-count-reproducibility-check
description: Use when a khipu run on a reference feature table (e.g. ecoli_pos.tsv from asari v1.9.2) must be verified before the annotations are used downstream, or when confirming a new khipu install/setup behaves identically to the published 548-empirical-compound result.

name: annotation-coverage-quantification
description: Use when you have run ConCISE consensus annotation propagation on GNPS feature-based molecular networking jobs and need to report how many ion features were annotated and how much coverage expanded beyond library matches.

name: annotation-database-versioning
description: Use when building or reproducing a reference annotation database (e.g. from HMDB, MassBank) so that downstream MetaboAnnotation matching runs against a fixed, documented compound and MS2 spectrum version rather than a shifting external resource.

name: annotation-disagreement-statistics
description: Use when a FluoroMatch 2.0 (or Modular) annotation output contains suspect-level B/B− assignments that must be benchmarked against trusted level-A assignments and Find-by-Formula results before reporting.

name: annotation-fdr-computation
description: Use when comparing two metabolite-annotation matching strategies (e.g., longitudinal Jaccard-similarity profiling at 0.5 threshold vs cross-sectional optimal-entropy at 0.75 threshold) and you need per-mode accuracy and FDR numbers to quantify identification gains.

name: annotation-field-consistency-validation
description: Use when cleaning annotated MS/MS library spectra whose SMILES, InChI, and InChIKey metadata fields are mutually inconsistent (e.g. after salt repair or adduct correction) and must be reconciled against the parent mass.

name: annotation-filtering-for-mass-spectrometry-features
description: Use when a MetMiner compound annotation run against the plant-specific PM database returns an annotation table that must be filtered to reliable metabolites before counting, comparing platforms, or downstream statistics.

name: annotation-fraction-benchmarking
description: Use when a pixel-by-m/z feature matrix from an imaging mass spectrometry run needs its isotope and adduct peak fractions quantified, or when reproducing SMAnalyst's reported annotation percentages (5.92% isotopic, 4.19% adduct) on the mouse brain Dataset 1.

name: annotation-hit-filtering-by-isotope-and-ppm-error
description: Use when an m/z database search (e.g. against HMDB via MetaboShiny) returns multiple matched compounds and you need to collapse duplicate hits, filter by isotope/adduct status, and rank remaining candidates by ppm error before annotation export.

name: annotation-match-comparison-analysis
description: Use when two or more nontargeted LC-MS datasets (feature tables with annotations) have been independently processed and you must quantify how many annotated features two aligners recover identically and how many spurious mismatches each introduces.

name: annotation-match-concordance-evaluation
description: Use when two or more independently processed, annotated, same-method LC-MS datasets have been aligned (e.g. with Eclipse) and you must report how accurately overlapping annotated features were matched, including a spurious-mismatch count.

name: annotation-metric-evaluation
description: Use when you have mWISE (or xMSannotator) candidate annotations for LC-MS peaks and a reference annotation table, and you need per-assay sensitivity/specificity/precision/F1 to benchmark a prioritization configuration.

name: annotation-mismatch-categorization
description: Use when comparing HGVSc/HGVSp or coding-impact outputs of ANNOVAR, SnpEff, or VEP against ClinVar two-star variants and you need to break down why each mismatch occurred rather than just count match rates.

name: annotation-overlap-comparison-across-annotation-tools
description: Use when evaluating a new or existing automated annotation workflow for AIF LC–MS data by benchmarking its annotations against a competing tool (e.g. MS-DIAL) and a manually curated expert list, to quantify agreement per dataset.

name: annotation-performance-evaluation
description: Use when an mWISE (or similar LC-MS annotation) pipeline has produced prioritized compound lists for peaks and you need quantitative sensitivity/specificity/F1 against a ground-truth reference compound set.

name: annotation-power-and-tpr-metric-computation
description: Use when comparing metabolite annotations from two annotation methods (e.g., ML vs rule-based) at FDR < 10% against an independent MS/MS-validated LC-MS/MS reference set, to compute MAP and TPR metrics.

name: annotation-precision-recall-f1-evaluation
description: Use when comparing predicted peak-level formula annotations against expert-curated annotations (e.g. NIST20) to score a spectrum-prediction model's annotation quality with recall, precision, and F1.

name: annotation-rate-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to report what proportion of chemical features in an untargeted LC-MS/MS dataset receive structural annotations from spectral library matching versus in silico fingerprint prediction, or to benchmark annotation coverage against the Qemistree food-omics reference rates.

name: annotation-rate-comparison-across-preprocessing-methods
description: Use when you have feature tables produced by multiple LC/MS preprocessing methods or settings and need an objective downstream metric — the fraction of features annotated to known metabolites — to rank their quality (e.g. reproducing Fig. 3b).

name: annotation-rate-quantification
description: Use when CAMERA xsAnnotate objects exist for paired positive- and negative-ion-mode LC/MS runs and you must report annotation counts/rates before vs. after cross-polarity verification.

name: annotation-rate-statistics-computation
description: Use when a GNPS FBMN job's feature counts, ion identity network groups, singleton/edge counts, and library- vs in-silico-annotation rates must be reproduced, cleaned, and written to a summary table for validation.

name: annotation-score-discounting
description: Use when per-feature GNPS/FBMN annotations contain missing or InChI-less matches that would otherwise be dropped, and MS2DECIDE needs complete c_g, t_g,i, t_g,s indicator values per feature.

name: annotation-source-filtering
description: Use when a PUG-View bulk annotation request under a 'heading' path returns more entries than needed and you want to restrict results to one provider (e.g. source=DrugBank) rather than all annotation sources.

name: annotation-statistics-reproduction
description: Use when a task requires exactly reproducing published KGMN annotation counts (seeds, knowns, unknowns) from NIST urine or similar untargeted LC-MS metabolomics data using MetDNA2Vis output folders.

name: annotation-string-canonicalization
description: Use when ion-identity annotation strings from GNPS, MassBank of North America, or IIMN-propagated library entries exist as inconsistent variants (e.g., 'M + H', 'M + H +', '[M + H]+') and must be harmonized before counting or merging identities.

name: annotation-success-rate-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when you have deconvolved MS2 spectra from SWATH-MS untargeted metabolomics data and need to quantify what fraction can be assigned a metabolite/formula annotation by MetDNA or Sirius, compared against a reported ~90% benchmark.

name: annotation-table-csv-processing
description: Use when MZmine/GNPS2 FBMN output (annotated feature tables with row ID, m/z, retention time) needs consolidation into a per-strain .csv summary, especially when KEGG pathway assignments must be attached and compared across strains.

name: annotation-table-format-handling
description: Use when working with an MSHub deconvolution feature/quantification table of GC-MS compounds and you must attach a balance score to each compound row and filter the annotation set at a threshold before downstream use.

name: annotation-table-merging-across-methods
description: Use when two annotation methods (e.g. SMART 2.0 and atomic sort) have been run on the same compounds and you need a side-by-side concordance table with explicit difference notes per mismatched call.

name: annotation-threshold-benchmarking
description: Use when you have experimental MS/MS spectra (e.g. human blood metabolomics MGF files) and need to quantify which reference library annotates the most spectra across a range of similarity cutoffs, to choose a library or benchmark coverage gains.

name: annotation-tool-output-aggregation
description: Use when an FBMN feature table (.csv quantitative export from MZmine >2.53) plus MGF spectra have parallel annotations from GNPS, Sirius 6, and ISDB-LOTUS and you must rank features by knownness/novelty.

name: annotation-tool-transcript-counting
description: Use when comparing variant annotation tools (ANNOVAR, SnpEff, VEP) and you need to measure how many NM/NR or ENST transcripts each tool exposes on RefSeq/Ensembl and how much their transcript-accession sets overlap, to explain downstream annotation discordance.

name: anova-contrast-testing
description: Use when comparing RMSE distributions of multiple imputation methods (e.g. KNN-TN vs KNN-CR vs KNN-EU) across 100 simulated datasets to test whether observed differences are statistically significant.

name: anova-f-score-confounder-analysis
description: Use when a metabolomics dataset has sample metadata (e.g., demographics) and you need to assess which variables drive variation (SOV), or when exploratory PCA/t-SNE views are needed before classification.

name: anova-posthoc-tukey-hsd-analysis
description: Use when a transf_data-normalised targeted or untargeted metabolomics feature table has one or two grouping factors (e.g. study group, time point) and per-feature ANOVA plus post-hoc Tukey HSD pairwise tables are needed.

name: anova-tukey-kramer-posthoc-analysis
description: Use when PCA sample scores derived from a prepared DSO (X data matrix with biological/blank class labels) must be tested for class separation across biological groups, especially when more than two classes require post hoc comparisons.

name: answer-set-programming-inference
description: Use when a pathway must be completed by inference from a knowledge base of atom/bond-encoded molecules and reactions (e.g. .lp files), given a source metabolite, goal molecules, and constraints like m/z filtering or absent molecules.

name: antibacterial-bgc-amr-correlation-analysis
description: Use when the task requires benchmarking newly mined BGCs against known-function clusters in MIBiG 2.0, quantifying the fraction of BGCs lacking MIBiG homology, or correlating antibacterial BGC abundance with AMR gene counts across metagenomic soil samples.

name: antibody-reference-database-construction
description: Use when antibody amino acid sequences must be turned into a protein search database to generate database-search-derived pseudo-ground truth (high-confidence PSMs) against which de novo sequencing tool predictions on antibody MS/MS data are evaluated.

name: antibody-sequence-coverage-accuracy-calculation
description: Use when you have assembled contigs from de novo peptide predictions for monoclonal antibody chains and need to quantify sequence coverage and accuracy against known light/heavy chain references, including CDR regions.

name: antimicrobial-screening-data-integration
description: Use when a MADByTE chemical similarity network from an NMR platform (TOCSY/HSQC spin system features) of a prefractionated extract library must be annotated with antimicrobial screening results to identify which network clusters concentrate activity.

name: antismash-baseline-comparison
description: Use when evaluating a BGC product-class or chemical-activity classifier on MIBiG-labeled Pfam TSV training data and you need the antiSMASH rule-based product-type AUC (0.78) as a comparative baseline in a 5-fold cross-validation table.

name: antismash-module-customisation-for-bgc-page-generation
description: Use when BGC detail pages must be rendered for curated BGC entries (e.g. MIBiG annotations stored as JSON) rather than recomputed from scratch, using antiSMASH 5 sideloading instead of full de novo genome-mining detection.

name: antismash-phmm-model-merging
description: Use when reconstructing BiG-SLiCE feature set 1: a curated biosynthetic pHMM library (full-length biosynthetic-Pfam plus fragmented sub-pfam models) that replaces full Pfam for BGC feature computation.

name: ants-synra-deformable-registration
description: Use when MALDI MSI and IFM images are from consecutive tissue sections and IFM-derived cell masks must be warped into the MSI pixel frame for cell-population-level lipid assignment.

name: api-latency-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify how a TurboPutative-based pipeline's runtime scales with input table size, by submitting compound annotation TSV tables of different row counts to its RESTful API and measuring submission-to-completion times.

name: app-output-validation-against-manual-annotations
description: Use when an automated glycan-identification or peak-assignment tool must be validated before adoption: a manually curated glycan list exists for the same spectrum, and you need to confirm the tool's output reproduces it (all true positives recovered, extra calls explainable).

name: applicability-domain-filtering
description: Use when predicting bitterness (or any property) with a structure-based classifier like BitterPredict whose validity is restricted to a chemical-property envelope, and you must decide which compounds are 'covered' before scoring precision/recall.

name: approach-exclusive-ion-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when comparing two FDR-controlled annotation approaches on imaging MS datasets against an independent LC-MS/MS validation set, and you need TPRs split by ions shared vs exclusively captured by each approach.

name: approximate-nearest-neighbor-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify the accuracy/speed trade-off of an ANN index (e.g., hnswlib HNSW) against exact nearest-neighbor search over a million-scale spectral library.

name: approximate-nearest-neighbor-graph-construction
description: Use when you have a large corpus of spectral embeddings (e.g. 1,024-d DreaMS vectors) and need a scalable similarity graph for annotation propagation or atlas construction.

name: approximate-nearest-neighbor-indexing
description: Use when clustering or comparing millions of MS/MS spectra where exhaustive all-vs-all pairwise comparison is computationally infeasible and a sparse distance matrix to each spectrum's nearest neighbors suffices.

name: approximate-nearest-neighbor-query-retrieval
description: Use when an open modification spectral library search needs to preselect a limited, approximate set of most-similar library spectra per query before accurate spectrum-spectrum match scoring.

name: approximate-string-matching
description: Use when free-text organism fields (vernacular, TCM, misspelled scientific names) in occurrence tables must be mapped to canonical taxa before aggregation or cross-database comparison.

name: arabidopsis-metabolite-accumulation-data-curation
description: Use when building or reproducing a metadata-annotated metabolomics MOG project from Arabidopsis GC-MS metabolite accumulation data and mutation metadata hosted on PMR, e.g. the 656-sample, 50-mutant AT-metab-dataset.

name: arachidonic-acid-pool-attribution
description: Use when targeted lipidomics abundance data across multiple platelet agonist stimulations (0.01/1 U/mL thrombin, 1/5 µg/mL CRP vs unstimulated) must be attributed to a lipid class as the dominant AA reservoir, testing PI depletion against PC/PE stability.

name: archaeplastida-class-coverage-computation
description: Use when you need family-level natural product census numbers — unique NPs, genera, species counts, and chemical-class coverage relative to Archaeplastida — from LOTUS, e.g. to benchmark literature-reported chemical space of a taxon.

name: architecture-depth-comparison-analysis
description: Use when selecting a GNN architecture or network depth for tandem MS/MS spectral prediction, and validation-split performance (median cosine similarity) must drive the choice before final benchmarking.

name: archive-content-enumeration
description: Use when a task requires verifying the exact contents of a deposited data archive — e.g. confirming a stated file total (408 .pdb files: 54 PDB-derived, 354 AlphaFold DB-derived) against the deposit itself.

name: argoum-collider-initial-condition-sampling
description: Use when you have an optimized protonated molecular ion (.xyz) and need collisional starting geometries/velocities for CID-MS/MS in silico spectra via ab initio MD.

name: arrival-time-gaussian-peak-fitting
description: Use when raw TWIM-MS calibration or experimental files (.mzML) must be converted into feature-level arrival times before power-law CCS calibration, e.g. for MOCCal RawDT workflows.

name: arrow-duckdb-zero-copy-querying
description: Use when a Parquet-stored HRMS dataset is too large for RAM and you need filtered aggregates such as an EIC for a specific m/z window (e.g. 216.0016 < mz < 216.2016 around atrazine) or a TIC, computed with SQL-grade speed.

name: arrow-on-disk-parquet-querying
description: Use when an HRMS Parquet file (e.g., arcMS-converted Waters UNIFI data) is too large to load into memory and you need derived quantities like TIC, BPI, EIC or MS spectra.

name: arus-spectrum-annotation
description: Use when you need to annotate previously unidentified recurrent MS/MS spectra (e.g. ARUS plasma/urine spectra) by ranking candidate compounds via in silico predicted fragment spectra.

name: asari-feature-table-metric-verification
description: Use when you need to independently verify or reimplement the snr and cSelectivity values exported with asari feature tables, using parent_masstrack_id links to composite mass track (EIC) intensity vectors and left_base/right_base peak boundaries.

name: asari-xcms-comparative-feature-detection
description: Use when you have centroided mzML files from an LC-MS experiment with a known sample ordering (dilution series, mixing ratios, spike-ins) and need to compare how well two processing tools (asari vs XCMS) detect features and whose peak areas track the expected signal.

name: asics-linear-mixture-fitting
description: Use when you have one or more 1H NMR plasma spectra (chemical shifts plus one intensity column per sample) and need a baseline automated deconvolution into reference metabolite spectra with fitted concentrations, e.g. for RMSE-based reconstruction benchmarking.

name: asp-data-file-reference-diff-validation
description: Use when a Pathmodel/ASP input datafile (e.g. MAA_pwy.lp, sterol_pwy.lp) has been manually encoded or edited and must be verified to ground cleanly and match a reference before running inference.

name: asp-fact-encoding-of-molecular-structures
description: Use when building or extending a PathModel knowledge base (.lp fact file) where each molecule must be represented as numbered atoms and bonds and each reaction as a reactant-product pair, prior to extracting biochemical transformations.

name: asp-knowledge-base-encoding
description: Use when preparing a PathModel input knowledge base: you need to encode molecule structures (atom/bond facts), reactions, source/goal endpoints, and m/z or absent-molecule filters as ASP facts.

name: assignment-graph-construction
description: Use when you have SIRIUS top-50 molecular formula candidate lists for a batch of compounds (e.g. from a dendroides-style LC-MS/MS run) and need to build the weighted candidate/edge graph that ZODIAC's Bayesian Gibbs-sampling model consumes.

name: asymmetric-least-squares-baseline-estimation
description: Use when 1H-NMR spectra (rows = samples, columns = chemical shifts in ppm) still show baseline distortions after phase correction and internal referencing, and a smooth baseline must be fit and subtracted before downstream analysis.

name: asymmetric-least-squares-baseline-estimation
description: Use when a raw GCxGC chromatogram (e.g. a 2D-TIC folded from a NetCDF file within the RGCxGC environment) shows a steady increasing baseline that must be removed before smoothing, peak alignment, or multivariate analysis.

name: asymmetric-similarity-matrix-construction
description: Use when spin system feature tables (from TOCSY+HSQC peak picking) are available for a set of NMR samples and a pairwise sample similarity matrix is needed as input for chemical similarity network generation.

name: asymmetry-factor-evaluation
description: Use when comparing LC-MS mobile phases (e.g. HILIC phases A and B on 20-chemical-standard mixtures) and you need peak shape quality — the averaged asymmetry factor of commonly validated peaks — as part of a peak quality score.

name: asymptotic-consistency-validation
description: Use when implementing or verifying the MaRR procedure's k-hat threshold and mFDR estimation and need to confirm consistency (pi1-hat -> pi1) and correct irreproducible-null distribution assumptions.

name: asynchronous-request-rate-limiting
description: Use when an asynchronous Python client queries a rate-limited web service (e.g. PubChem at ~5 req/s) during batch metadata enrichment and requests must be spaced without serializing the whole pipeline.

name: asynchronous-web-service-querying
description: Use when a .msp mass spectral library has records missing metadata such as SMILES, InChI, InChIKey, IUPAC name, CAS number, or formula, and those fields can be derived from existing fields via external chemical identifier services.

name: atlas-label-based-region-extraction-msi
description: Use when a registered 3D MSI volume (e.g., coronal3D_propagated_decoded.h5) carries pixel-level brain-region labels from an atlas, and per-structure lipid enrichment or differential abundance statistics are needed.

name: atlas-region-label-mapping
description: Use when registered 2D MSI serial sections must be assigned anatomical labels from the Waxholm Space rat brain atlas and per-region Dice-index quality scores or regional chemical profiles are the deliverable.

name: atom-bond-set-difference-computation
description: Use when reactions are encoded as ASP facts (atom/ground predicates with reactant-product links, e.g. sterol_pwy.lp, MAA_pwy.lp) and distinct before/after reaction sites must be abstracted into reusable molecular transformations.

name: atom-nomenclature-consistency-checking
description: Use when converting or curating BMRB NMR-STAR entries (chemical shifts, NOE/dihedral restraints) toward NEF or OneDep submission and residue/atom names must stay consistent across files.

name: atomic-composition-atom-count-filtering
description: Use when expanding a reaction network with Pickaxe/minedatabase and you need to prune generated compounds by per-element atom counts (e.g. carbon count caps for non-cofactors) before further generations.

name: atomic-to-molecular-purity-conversion-verification
description: Use when reconstructing or validating the theoretical correction matrix for LC-MS isotope labeling data — e.g., checking that an (Nt+1)x(Nt+1) matrix correctly converts nutrient atomic purity (Step 3 parameter, e.g., 0.99) into molecular purity for a tracer like U-13C6 glucose.

name: atpase-system-comparative-genomics
description: Use when you have a per-genome KEGG module presence/absence matrix derived from IMG/KEGG modules (M00082, M00083, M00086, M00087, M00088, M00157, M00159) and need to determine which taxa encode F-type vs V/A-type ATPases, or both.

name: attention-weight-inspection-in-lipid-model
description: Use when you have a trained transformer lipid identification model plus preprocessed MS2 spectra and need to verify that the predicted lipid tokens are attributable to specific, known fragment m/z peaks.

name: attribute-importance-quantification
description: Use when you must rank which node attributes of a trained graph neural network (e.g., SigmaCCS atom features in model.h5) drive CCS prediction accuracy, by masking each attribute and measuring the prediction-error increase on a test set.

name: auc-estimation-and-annotation
description: Use when binary classification performance for an omics predictor must be visualized as an ROC curve with an AUC legend entry, especially by users without programming skills.

name: auc-feature-table-extraction-from-qc-runs
description: Use when TARDIS targeted peak integration of raw LC–MS files (e.g. MetaboLights MTBLS8735 or cohort runs) has completed and you need the per-target, per-run AUC data.frame and QC-averaged metric tibble as a processed feature table.

name: auc-model-comparison-analysis
description: Use when several classifiers have been trained on an identical labeled training split and the goal is a fair, ranked comparison of discrimination performance via AUC on a held-out test set.

name: auc-roc-performance-evaluation
description: Use when comparing BGC detectors or any sequence-labeling classifier on held-out data and you need a threshold-independent performance metric (AUC ROC) to quantify detection accuracy, e.g., generalization to unseen classes.

name: auc-tabulation-across-mass-windows
description: Use when you need to test whether a threshold-based candidate filtering metric (e.g., ΔCCS between predicted and measured CCS) remains effective as candidate-list mass tolerance tightens from 10 ppm down to the isobaric 0 ppm case.

name: aucroc-model-benchmarking
description: Use when a SciKitLearn-compatible classifier must be evaluated on pathway-transformed multi-omics scores and compared against the random-forest Single-View benchmark AUROC of 0.95 on COVID-19 data.

name: augmentation-ablation-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantify how much of a diffusion-based molecular generator's accuracy comes from built-in equivariance versus training-time data augmentation, i.e., when ablating an augmentation flag from a config and re-evaluating.

name: augmented-spectral-library-construction
description: Use when unknown EI mass spectra must be identified against a library that lacks the query molecule, and predicted spectra can fill coverage gaps.

name: augmented-training-set-composition-and-comparison
description: Use when training NetAurHPD (or a similar M5-based classifier) on metabolite correlation networks and you must decide how many artificial augmented networks to include in training, or when you need to quantify how augmentation affects AUC stability across repeated cross-validation sessions.

name: auroc-accuracy-classification-evaluation
description: Use when a trained or adapted classifier on SCMS metabolomics feature data must be scored on held-out cells and its AUROC, F-1, and accuracy compared against published baselines or adaptation thresholds.

name: auroc-computation-for-binary-enzyme-classification
description: Use when a molecule dataset carries binary reactant labels per CYP450 enzyme and per-enzyme or averaged AUROC is needed to benchmark a reactant-prediction tool like CypReact, SMARTCyp, or ADMET Predictor.

name: auroc-f1-accuracy-metric-computation
description: Use when meta-evaluating or comparing trained classifiers on held-out SCMS tasks (e.g., 1-, 5-, 10-shot MAML adaptation) and quantitative, threshold-free metrics are needed to select a model or report performance.

name: auroc-retrieval-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether a preprocessing step (centroiding, denoising, ion filtering) helps or hurts spectral-similarity retrieval, by measuring AUROC of cosine scores against a same/different compound label matrix.

name: authentic-vs-spurious-identification-separation
description: Decision support for choosing score cutoffs that distinguish true from false MAVEN2 spectral matches when annotating features against the CalicoLipids or MS-DIAL in-silico lipidomics libraries.

name: auto-scaling-to-unit-variance
description: Use when a normalized metabolomics feature table (e.g. the MetaboReport cancerCell demo dataset) has mass features on incomparable scales and you need per-feature unit-variance scaling before statistical analysis.

name: auto-tracked-ion-detection
description: Use when running omics-agnostic MS quality control on batch MS1 data (mzML or Agilent .d, Thermo .raw, Bruker .d inputs) and no theoretical/reference ion list is available to specify as tracking targets.

name: auto-tracked-ion-metric-tracking
description: Use when precursor-ion peak metrics have been extracted for auto-tracked and user-specified ions and the operator needs packaged CSV reports and JPG/PDF figures to inspect and track ion metrics over a batch of MS runs.

name: autocorrelation-based-psf-block-size-estimation
description: Use when a colocalization significance test requires scrambled randomizations of a two-color image (e.g., CFP/YFP or red/green confocal pairs) and the independent scrambling unit (block size) must match the image texture or PSF rather than individual pixels.

name: autocorrelation-width-block-sizing
description: Use when a two-channel fluorescence image shows correlated pixel intensities from texture or the microscope PSF, so that per-pixel scrambling would produce an unrealistically narrow random-overlap distribution and a significance threshold that falsely flags colocalization.

name: autoencoder-based-batch-normalization-training
description: Use when untargeted GC-MS metabolomics peak tables (e.g. xlsx with batch/sampleType/time/label columns and a No compound index) span long acquisition periods and pooled QC samples should be used to train a data-driven normalization model.

name: autoencoder-training-on-msi-feature-vectors
description: Use when you have a reconstructed, peak-binned and TIC-normalized 3D MSI dataset and need coherent per-section feature images with anatomical contrast to serve as moving images for multimodal MRI-atlas registration.

name: automated-phase-correction
description: Use when a series of 1H-NMR spectra (e.g. metabolite mix replicates or Daphnia extract CryoProbe data) needs phasing without manual per-spectrum adjustment, or when choosing among automatic phasing algorithms by speed or phase consistency.

name: automated-pipeline-qc-gating
description: Use when RAW LC-MS/MS runs must be flagged or gated automatically before database searching based on acquisition-side signals, e.g. an MS2 TIC below a configurable percentage of the MS1 TIC.

name: automated-vs-manual-optimization-agreement-analysis
description: Decision support for targeted LC-MS/MS external-calibration quantification when calibration curves need model/weight/level selection per compound and you must verify that automatic regression optimization matches manual expert optimization.

name: automated-vs-manual-pipeline-comparison
description: Use when you must reproduce or verify an efficiency claim comparing an automated pipeline to a manual workflow, e.g. metScribeR's ~10 s per standard and 26-fold time reduction over 603 IROA standards.

name: automated-vs-manual-processing-time-analysis
description: Use when a study claims an automated data-processing tool accelerates preprocessing of a large dataset and the actual wall-clock times and speedup ratio versus manual expert processing must be measured or reproduced.

name: automated-vs-manual-speedup-comparison
description: Use when you have a runnable automated pipeline for targeted/untargeted metabolomics (e.g. SmartPeak on mzML injections) and need to measure how much faster it processes a sequence than manual analyst-driven processing.

name: autophase-rms-peak-optimization
description: Use when Fourier-transformed NMR spectra (samples × chemical-shift ppm DataFrame) show dispersive/negative peak contributions or unflat baselines, and an automatic zero-/first-order phase correction is needed before referencing or baseline correction.

name: autoq-integration-table-processing
description: Use when you already hold the isoSCAN autoQ integration table from high-resolution GC-CI-MS (GC-(q)TOF or GC-Orbitrap) stable-isotope-labelling runs and need per-metabolite isotopologue summaries or a barplot of a single compound such as Gly across sample groups.

name: autoregressive-smiles-token-modeling
description: Use when the goal is to generate novel metabolite-like SMILES from a corpus of known metabolite structures, or to reproduce/extend DeepMet-style training with PyTorch and Snakemake.

name: autoregressive-token-sequence-decoding
description: Use when reconstructing or extending how a transformer model decodes MS2 spectra into lipid shorthand notation strings (headgroup, fatty-acyl chains, adduct), or when implementing greedy/beam search decoding with per-prediction confidence scores.

name: autotuner-parameter-optimization
description: Use when raw LC-MS-based metabolomics data (e.g., .mzML/.mzXML) must be processed for feature extraction but peak-picking parameters are unknown or default values underperform, and an automated, data-driven parameter measurement is needed.

name: average-distance-evaluation-score-computation
description: Use when you have run ModiFinder's MF-R likelihood computation on a known/unknown analog pair and need a scalar score (e.g. the 0.86→0.93 Kirromycin and 0.56→0.72 Naphthomycin B case studies) to quantify modification-site localization accuracy.

name: average-distance-modification-site-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking atom-level modification site likelihood scores (e.g., MF-R/MF-O outputs, random baselines, CFM-ID analog permutations) on analog pairs and you need a metric that rewards both closeness to the true site and score informativeness.

name: average-precision-comparison-analysis
description: Use when two de novo sequencing models differ in training-set provenance (e.g. curated MassIVE-KB vs custom-labeled data) and you must test whether performance gains stem from data quality rather than peptide-count scale.

name: averagine-isotope-pattern-simulation
description: Use when you need synthetic peptide isotope patterns spanning defined monoisotopic mass and charge-state ranges — e.g., to create labeled signal+noise TIMS windows or to build an LSH reference database of isotope patterns for timsTOF data.

name: avre-benchmark-error-computation
description: Use when a 1H NMR mixture spectrum has a known gravimetric composition and you need to quantify how accurately an optimal-transport quantifier (Magnetstein) recovers relative concentrations, especially for overlapping/shifted peaks, distorted lineshapes, or low-field benchtop data.

name: back-calculated-accuracy-evaluation-of-qc-samples
description: Use when a targeted metabolomics dataset contains calibration points, QC samples, and internal standard intensities and you must verify quantification accuracy (%) by back-calculation from fitted calibration curves.

name: background-enrichment-threshold-configuration
description: Use when re-running DIMPLE preprocessing on maize-root DESI-MSI replicate data and you need to set or sensitivity-test the minimum background-enrichment threshold (default 1.5) or the ppm mass tolerance (default 2.5).

name: background-noise-threshold-estimation
description: Use when a TIC trace from acoustic ejection mass spectrometry (AEMS) data must be split into per-ejection detection windows bounded by a background-noise threshold or smoothed local minima between adjacent ejection times.

name: background-percentile-significance-thresholding
description: Use when you need to decide which metabolites or microbe-metabolite interactions are statistically significant after cross-validated prediction on paired microbiome-metabolome data, rather than picking arbitrary cutoffs.

name: background-spectral-correlation-analysis
description: Use when a spatial metabolomics feature matrix (pixels x m/z ion intensities) must be QC-checked before preprocessing, specifically to verify that background-region spectra are spatially consistent prior to background pixel removal and noise ion filtering.

name: background-suppression-thresholding
description: Use when filtering raw untargeted DESI-MSI pixel-level mass spectra (e.g., maize root imaging workspaces) down to a defensible list of biological m/z signatures before downstream annotation or gradient clustering.

name: bacteria-fungi-spectrum-classification
description: Use when a consensus .mgf of spectra has been batch-searched against microbeMASST and you need to (a) subtract spectra with non-microbial (e.g., human cell line) matches and (b) split the remaining putative microbial spectra by taxonomic origin into bacteria, fungi, or both.

name: bacterial-lipid-class-interpretation
description: Use when an annotated bacterial lipidomics feature table (multiple strains/conditions, replicate structure) needs class-level biological interpretation — e.g. verifying that resistance (Dap2 vs Par MRSA) reproduces reported DGDG/LysylPG/fatty-acid-chain-length shifts.

name: bacterial-producer-strain-annotation
description: Use when screening bacterial culture MS data (e.g. HMP isolates, MSV000084475 and MSV000087889) to determine which genera or strains produced specific amino-acid-conjugated bile acids, requiring joint agreement of m/z, retention time, drift time, and isotope dot-product.

name: bag-of-fragments-spectral-representation
description: Use when raw MS2 peak lists (e.g., GNPS MGF spectra from Orbitrap acquisitions such as the Q-Exactive) must be converted into fragment/neutral-loss count vectors before topic modeling or other unsupervised substructure discovery.

name: bagging-bootstrap-ensemble-correction
description: Use when a .csv metabolomics matrix (experiments in rows, features in columns, batch levels in the first column) shows across-batch signal drift and you want the ber-bagging ensemble correction or to compare it against the ber, parametric-ComBat, and nonparametric-ComBat outputs.

name: bagging-bootstrap-model-aggregation
description: Use when correcting across-batch signal drift in a log2-transformed metabolomics feature table and you want to stabilize the ber (two-stage linear L/S fitting) model via partial bagging with n=150 bootstrap samples, or benchmark bagged ber against ComBat variants.

name: balance-score-threshold-analysis
description: Decision support for choosing spectral-match filter thresholds (cosine similarity and balance score) on MSHub/GNPS GC-MS deconvolution output when the goal is to minimize the FDR of top-match annotations.

name: balanced-accuracy-and-auc-evaluation
description: Use when comparing normalization methods (e.g. none, median, EigenMS, NOMIS, CRMN) on a feature table to decide which produces the downstream classification performance before pipeline adoption.

name: balanced-accuracy-model-evaluation
description: Decision support for choosing among multiple classifier–dataset combinations: assemble binned feature matrices for each spectral dataset, run fivefold CV grid search per pair, and rank by balanced accuracy on held-out test splits.

name: barabasi-albert-network-generation
description: Use when simulating pathway graph structures (e.g., metabolite networks) for kernel machine test power or type I error studies, or when evaluating robustness to incorrect/incomplete pathway edges via controlled edge permutation.

name: barabasi-albert-random-graph-generation
description: Use when simulation studies need synthetic pathway graphs emulating KEGG metabolite network topology — e.g., generating Barabási-Albert graphs of size 15, 30, or 45 nodes to evaluate kernel association tests like PaIRKAT.

name: base-peak-extraction-from-centroided-spectra
description: Use when you hold a Thermo Fisher .raw file, need per-MS1-scan base peak m/z and intensity, and want direct in-R access without ProteoWizard/mzML conversion.

name: base-peak-identification-per-spectrum
description: Use when you have a Thermo .raw file from an Orbitrap instrument and need per-MS1-scan base-peak m/z and intensity values, e.g. to track signal drift or confirm acquisition quality across a run.

name: base-peak-normalization
description: Use when raw MS2 lipid spectra must be put on a common intensity scale before model training or filtering — e.g. to compute a base-peak-normalized median intensity for a noise-score cutoff.

name: base3-histogram-quantization
description: Use when a mass spectrum given as a single-line 'ion:intensity ion:intensity ...' string (e.g. MassBank record PR100026) must be reduced to its 4-digit SPLASH second summary block via 5 Da binning, base-3 digit scaling, and base-36 conversion.

name: base36-block-encoding
description: Use when a single-line 'ion:intensity ion:intensity ...' mass spectrum (e.g. MassBank PR100026 caffeine) must be reduced to its SPLASH second summary block for search-space reduction or identifier validation.

name: baseline-conditional-quantification-of-weak-signals
description: Use when processing full-scan AEMS data (e.g. precursor-ion or neutral-loss scans from 384-/1536-well plates) where a persistent high-intensity baseline signal obscures weak analyte peaks, so that frame boundaries must be derived from clear high-mass reference peaks rather than from the weak.

name: baseline-correction-airpls-chromatograms
description: Use when raw extracted-ion chromatograms of targeted MS metabolites (or their isotopologues) contain drifting baselines that must be removed prior to peak detection and peak-area quantification.

name: baseline-method-comparison-tabulation
description: Use when a new signal-reconstruction or dimensionality-reduction method for mass spectrometry imaging must be benchmarked against standard FT, zero-padded FT, or linear-subspace baselines on data with known ground truth.

name: baseline-method-output-integration-sirius-buddy
description: Use when benchmarking molecular formula prediction on MS/MS spectra against SIRIUS and BUDDY baselines, or when running FIDDLE's integrated variant that consumes baseline candidate outputs on the same spectra.

name: baseline-method-performance-comparison
description: Use when introducing a new spectral library-matching or reconstruction algorithm and you need a defensible performance comparison on the same target spectra (artificial mixtures N925/N987/N988 and plasma N907/N926) against named competing tools.

name: baseline-ml-model-benchmarking
description: Use when a new deep learning model on aligned LC-MS features (or a comparable tabular classification task) must be compared against RF, KNN, SVM, and LR baselines to prove it adds predictive value.

name: baseline-model-benchmarking
description: Use when a new predictive model (e.g., SigmaCCS for CCS prediction) must be validated against a published baseline (e.g., DeepCCS) on the same curated test set to confirm the reported performance gap.

name: baseline-model-benchmarking-trial-efficiency
description: Use when evaluating whether transfer learning from a pre-trained metabolomics VAE (e.g. 2,736-feature mzLearn matrix) improves downstream prediction and Optuna search efficiency versus random initialization or traditional ML.

name: baseline-registration-ablation-analysis
description: Use when a multi-modal imaging pipeline needs quantitative proof that its registration step outperforms simpler baselines — e.g. affinely registered SIMS vs IMC patches evaluated with SSIM/NRMSE across multiple FOVs.
