name: baseline-similarity-metric-comparison
description: Use when evaluating a new or existing MS/MS spectral similarity metric against established baselines (Cosine, Modified Cosine, Spec2Vec, MS2DeepScore) on spectra paired with known structures, to test whether predicted spectral similarity correlates with structural (Tanimoto) similarity.

name: baseline-spectra-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a de novo or library-search structure predictor has been run on MS2/MSn spectra and you need a head-to-head accuracy and statistical-significance comparison against SIRIUS4 and MetFrag baselines.

name: baseline-spectrum-prediction-comparison
description: Use when you must show a spectrum-prediction model significantly outperforms baselines on the same held-out compounds: predictions and baselines run under identical adducts ([M+H]+, [M-H]-) and collision energies, compared by cosine similarity.

name: baseline-tool-sirius-cfmid-run-and-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating a new metabolomics annotation/ranking method against pretrained baselines (SIRIUS, CFM-ID) and you need leakage-controlled test subsets so each baseline is only scored on molecules unseen in its own pre-training.

name: basepeak-isomer-refinement
description: Use when you already have PuInc_seeker output (putative 13C-labeled/unlabeled feature pairs from an XCMSet) and need to locate the base peaks of labeled features — e.g. ppm.s=6.5 mass windows around UL.atomM=12.0 vs L.atomM=13.003355 — before database annotation.

name: basis-function-spectral-agreement-assessment
description: Use when a newly simulated metabolite basis set (e.g. from 1D-projection density-matrix simulation) must be checked against a ground-truth FID-A reference or vendor/measured basis set before accepting it for LCModel-style analysis.

name: batch-aware-run-order-modeling

name: batch-aware-two-pass-normalization

name: batch-aware-two-stage-feature-alignment

name: batch-construction-for-pairwise-learning

name: batch-corrected-metabolomics-interpretation
description: Use when a batch-corrected metabolomics abundance matrix (e.g. hRUV-normalized from >1,000 plasma samples run across multiple batches) is available together with sample-level phenotype annotations, and the goal is to identify metabolites significantly differentially abundant with that phenotype.

name: batch-correction-analysis
description: Use when raw ion concentrations (e.g. ICP-MS ppm values) span multiple measurement batches and you need to remove batch effects prior to standardisation, clustering, or network inference on element profiles.

name: batch-correction-effect-assessment
description: Use when targeted LC-MS peak-area data spanning multiple batches (e.g. dMRM MRM measurements with internal standards) has been batch-corrected and you must demonstrate that SQC samples align across batches and QC RSD drops before trusting downstream statistics.

name: batch-correction-method-benchmarking
description: Use when you have LC-MS or GC-MS metabolomics/proteomics peak tables with pooled QC injections interspersed among study samples (e.g. every 5, 6 or 8 samples) and need to decide which batch-correction algorithm to apply by comparing post-correction RSD distributions.

name: batch-correction-parameter-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when comparing batch-correction configurations (e.g. WaveICA vs ComBat vs none) on a batch-labeled metabolomics feature table, where the outcome metric is the count of two-sample t-test features passing FDR <= 0.2 between biological groups.

name: batch-correction-peak-area-ratio-normalization
description: Use when targeted LC-MS peak-integrated data (e.g. SCIEX OS dMRM exports) show between-batch drift in median ratios across batches and need correction via stable-isotope internal standards before downstream analysis.

name: batch-correction-robustness-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether an adversarial batch-correction method for multi-batch untargeted metabolomics data tolerates randomly distributed missing values, or when comparing several normalization methods on replicate-containing benchmarking data.

name: batch-directory-spectrum-import
description: Use when the starting data are many single-spectrum .CSV files (one spectrum per file) or raw .ascii instrument output, and each spectrum must be converted into a pairwise m/z/intensity data frame — including batch conversion of a whole folder into .rda files.

name: batch-effect-assessment-in-lc-msms-metabolomics
description: Use when LC-MS/MS samples were acquired in multiple batches (e.g. before vs after a ~2017-10-26 instrument date) and you need to test whether a batch split in PCoA is driven by feature-table metrics and whether MS2-fingerprint-based MEMO dissimilarities reduce it.

name: batch-effect-aware-preprocessing

name: batch-effect-correction-benchmarking

name: batch-effect-correction-execution
description: Use when a quantitated MRM abundance table (e.g., MAT-file or xlsx output) contains QC samples such as batch-pooled QCs (BQCs) and abundance trends with injection order must be removed across batches.

name: batch-effect-normalization-eigenms
description: Use when processing a metabolomic or lipidomic feature table through the MultiABLER pipeline and a single normalization approach that corrects for batch effects is needed before downstream differential-expression analysis (e.g. limma) or cross-validated classification.

name: batch-effect-qc-evaluation
description: Use when a study's samples were acquired in multiple batches (a 'Batch' metadata field exists) and PCA or log TIC QAQC plots of the feature table show sub-clustering by batch that must be corrected before downstream statistics.

name: batch-effect-qc-sequence-design
description: Use when block randomization averages out natural numerical characteristics of sample feature distributions (e.g. gender or age-group counts) and you need to quantify the resulting aggregation/clustering behavior in the injection sequence as a baseline comparison.

name: batch-effect-quantification
description: Use when raw NMR biomarker data (e.g. UK Biobank fields #23651-23948) plus sample processing QC flags are available and you need to rank technical covariates by per-biomarker variance explained before deciding on correction steps.

name: batch-effect-quantification-across-layers
description: Use when a trained DenseNet121 (DeepMSProfiler ensemble) is available on raw LC-MS .npy data and you need to measure, layer by layer, whether hidden representations shed batch/hospital variation while retaining disease-class information.

name: batch-effect-removal-evaluation
description: Use when you have metabolomics abundance data from multiple plates/batches over an extended acquisition period and need to compare normalization methods on unwanted-variation removal, replicate variability, and retention of biological signal (e.g. disease-status classification).

name: batch-file-validation-error-aggregation
description: Use when a corpus of mwTab-format files (e.g. all Metabolomics Workbench studies) must be parsed, validated against required MS/NMR schemas, and rolled up into counts of error categories per file.

name: batch-identifier-conversion
description: Use when source metabolomics datasets report metabolites by names or non-systematic identifiers (PubChem, CheBI, HMDB, KEGG, LipidMaps, DrugBank, Bin ID, CAS) and you need a unified InChIKey column before merging studies.

name: batch-integration-of-ms-omics-data
description: Use when raw MS-based metabolomics or proteomics feature intensities from multiple injection batches must be corrected for intra- and inter-batch drift and merged into one table for statistical analysis.

name: batch-level-feature-collapsing

name: batch-metabolomics-data-format-conversion

name: batch-mzml-data-processing

name: batch-normalization-comparison-across-methods

name: batch-reference-curve-fitting

name: batch-replicate-pair-matching
description: Use when you have replicate pairs of identical biological samples run in subsequent batches, log(e)-transformed intensities, and need to rank normalization methods by cross-batch correspondence rather than by QC-sample RSD reduction or differential-abundance counts.

name: batch-rt-correction-with-internal-standards
description: Use when multi-batch DDA LC-MS data (e.g. converted TripleTOF or QE HF vendor files) show retention-time shifts for targeted compounds between batches and quantification peaks must be re-integrated at corrected TargetRT values batch-wide.

name: batch-sample-list-construction-for-alignment

name: batch-spectra-parallel-processing

name: batch-study-accession-processing
description: Use when benchmarking whole-process conversion correctness across a cohort of study accessions (e.g. 41 accepted data sets or 52 repository studies), needing per-study success/failure status plus aggregate correct-output percentages.

name: batch-variable-association-visualization

name: batchwise-metabolomics-normalization

name: bayesian-posterior-probability-annotation

name: bcftools-command-line-processing

description: Use when evaluating a candidate-ranking tool (e.g. JESTR vs SIRIUS/CFM-ID) on tandem mass spectra and you need benchmark subsets from MassSpecGym that exclude molecules a pretrained baseline already saw.

name: benchmark-dataset-retrieval-and-standardization
description: Use when a metabolomic peak table from a benchmark study (MetaboLights MTBLS accession or the NOREVA_exampledata.zip archive) must be obtained and reformatted into NOREVA's unified row-sample/column-metabolite layout before workflow processing.

name: benchmark-delta-reproduction-and-win-rate-analysis
description: Use when you need to independently reproduce a paper's headline benchmark numbers (average deltas and pairwise win rates) by re-running random and tool-based baselines on the identical filtered analog-pair benchmark and comparing aggregated metrics.

name: benchmark-dose-calculation
description: Use when a metabolomics feature table contains samples measured across multiple dose levels of an exposure (e.g. in vitro assays or animal models) and you need fitted dose-response curves and per-feature benchmark dose (BMD) values for risk assessment.

name: benchmark-error-aggregation-across-missingness-levels
description: Use when imputation methods have been benchmarked at several completely-at-random missingness proportions (e.g. 10–30%) on continuous, categorical or mixed-type datasets and you must localize where a method's error reduction is largest and whether it is significant.

name: benchmark-evaluation-on-nplib1
description: Use when validating de novo chemical formula prediction from tandem MS/MS against reported top-1 accuracy on NPLIB1, or when quantifying how peak visibility (Np) affects model accuracy, including the MS1-only equivalence baseline.

name: benchmark-feature-list-evaluation
description: Use when you have feature lists (CSV with m/z, RT, area columns) extracted from LC–MS runs of the MTBLS562, QE_HF or TripleTOF_6600 benchmark datasets and need to score alignment accuracy against manually annotated library analytes.

name: benchmark-identification-rate-comparison
description: Use when reproducing a published metabolite-identification benchmark on CASMI 2016/2022 spectra, or when comparing a spectral-embedding predictor against SIRIUS or another baseline by ranking candidate structures per query spectrum.

name: benchmark-method-comparison-across-simulation-conditions
description: Use when a new pathway-enrichment method must be evaluated against competing topology-based methods, and statistical power needs to be estimated per simulation condition (e.g., by number of dysregulated genes) with standard errors across replicates.

name: benchmark-metric-computation
description: Use when comparing peak-detection or feature-detection performance of LC-MS processing tools against a ground-truth feature list (synthetic mzML with known single/double peaks) or manually labeled extracted-ion chromatograms, and accuracy metrics must be computed per category.

name: benchmark-metric-computation-tanimoto-mces
description: Use when a generative structure-elucidation model (e.g. MS-BART, DiffMS, FRIGID) has produced candidate molecules per spectrum and you must score them on MassSpecGym or NPLIB1 with Top-1/Top-10 InChIKey accuracy, MCES distance, and Tanimoto similarity.

name: benchmark-metric-table-compilation
description: Use when several integration methods (e.g. SpatialMETA, Seurat CCA/RPCA, scVI, scANVI, scPoli, spaVAE, PCA) have been run on the same inputs and their embedding-level scores must be collected into one comparable metric table.

name: benchmark-metrics-table-generation
description: Use when a graph-based alignment method (G-Aligner) has been run alongside a baseline workflow (OpenMS/MZmine2/XCMS) on self-extracted features and you must quantify alignment gains in a reproducible metrics table.

name: benchmark-peak-extraction-quality-filtering
description: Use when a validated benchmark peak set must be derived from chromatographic ROIs of target molecules — i.e., after get_ROIs has produced an ROI data.table and peaks must be extracted, consistency-checked, and filtered before benchmark export.

name: benchmark-peak-matching
description: Use when you have a validated benchmark (e.g. Benchmark.csv from MTBLS267) plus unaligned and aligned NPP output csv files and need to join them to quantify split peaks, missed peaks, degenerated isotopologue ratios, or alignment errors.

name: benchmark-reaction-set-curation
description: Use when validating a reaction-rules prediction engine against a curated set of experimentally characterized biosynthetic reactions, to report coverage proportions and their statistical significance.

name: benchmark-reanalysis-against-reference-method
description: Use when a published tool reports equivalence or ity against a reference method on a fixed benchmark and you need to verify whether that outcome survives systematic variation of an internal configuration choice (fingerprint type, kernel, scoring variant).

name: benchmark-reproduction-against-ground-truth-features
description: Use when a publicly available LC-MS/MS dataset with a published ground-truth feature list (e.g. MetaboLights MTBLS736) must be used to benchmark a feature detection, quantification or marker selection pipeline.

name: benchmark-reproduction-against-published-values
description: Use when a paper reports a concrete quantitative result (peak detection rate, annotation count, threshold behavior) and you must rerun the pipeline with the stated parameters to confirm or compare against those values.

name: benchmark-reproduction-against-reported-metrics
description: Use when an article reports headline accuracy metrics (e.g., AvRE) for a method on named experiments and the deposited spectra/data are available, and the task is to reproduce those numbers and compare against reported baselines.

name: benchmark-result-reproduction
description: Use when a paper or task card reports a concrete quantitative result (feature counts, match rates, tolerance thresholds) that must be re-derived from the deposited datasets and workflow scripts to verify it reproduces.

name: benchmark-result-reproduction
description: Use when reproducing published molecular-formula or structure-identification benchmark results from LC-MS/MS challenge data using SIRIUS 4 with CSI:FingerID and isotope-pattern scoring.

name: benchmark-result-reproduction
description: Use when a published software benchmark reports per-dataset success/failure counts or percentages (e.g., '38/41 correct outputs, 92.7%') and the goal is to verify them by re-executing the pipeline on the same study IDs.

name: benchmark-result-reproduction-from-deposited-predictions
description: Use when a paper's headline accuracy numbers are tied to deposited prediction files (e.g. Zenodo file#5) and you must independently verify the reported metrics rather than retrain the model or re-run inference.

name: benchmark-result-tabulation-csv
description: Use when a study reports surrogate-model performance (ROC AUC, LOBOV validation AUC) and Platt-calibration quality (ECE/MCE/logLoss deltas) that must be reproduced as a structured, machine-readable results table.

name: benchmark-runtime-table-processing
description: Use when a runtime benchmark table containing CPU DP and G.A.M.E. GPU DP running times per dataset exists and per-dataset acceleration factors (CPU time / GPU time) must be computed and validated against the reported 10–1000x range.

name: benchmark-sensitivity-aggregation
description: Use when comparing annotation algorithms across several public LC-MS studies and ionization modes and you need a sensitivity mean (SD) summary table, scored against known compound references.

name: benchmark-size-validation
description: Use when an mzRAPP 'Generate Benchmark' run has just produced a Benchmark.csv and you must confirm it matches the reference benchmark size and passed the isotopologue quality filtering before running NPP reliability assessment.

name: benchmark-spectra-extraction-with-precursor-tolerance
description: Use when preparing reference MS/MS spectra from contest or benchmark datasets (CASMI 2016/2022) where spectra must be located in raw measurements by precursor m/z and retention time before comparing predicted vs. reference spectra.

name: benchmark-table-compilation
description: Use when two or more annotation tools must be evaluated side-by-side on identical benchmark datasets and the results need to be assembled into a per-assay table of metrics (computation time, sensitivity, specificity, F1) for direct comparison.

name: benchmark-table-compilation
description: Use when you must compare a newly trained or pretrained spectrum predictor against reimplemented baselines on the same test split, and want one CSV table with average cosine similarity per model per dataset rather than scattered per-run metrics.

name: benchmark-table-generation
description: Use when a paper reports the same error metric (e.g., averaged relative error, AvRE) for a method and competing baselines across multiple experiments that differ in spectrum difficulty, and a per-experiment gap table sorted by difficulty is needed for benchmark validation.

name: benchmark-timing-table-generation
description: Use when comparing query speed of spectral library search algorithms (e.g., EQ vs flash entropy search) and you need wall-clock timings recorded per (method, library-size) pair into a machine-readable benchmark table.

name: benchmark-train-test-split-construction
description: Use when evaluating a tandem MS annotation/scoring engine against published retrieval statistics and you need a reproducible held-out test split of reference spectra with known chemical structures.

name: benchmark-workflow-ranking-reproduction
description: Use when a task asks to reproduce a published metabolomics workflow-optimization benchmark (e.g., PMID28528106 / MTBLS403) by running NOREVA's full workflow scan and validating the resulting overall ranking of processing workflows.

name: benford-law-conformance-testing-of-lipid-quantity-values
description: Use when a lipidome quantity table (csv/xlsx flat or pivot table, or mzTab-M) is loaded into LipidSpace and you must verify that the distribution of digits in the lipid quantity values follows Benford's law as part of the built-in import quality control workflow.

name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction
description: Use when you have feature-wise p-values from univariate tests (Welch's t-test, Mann-Whitney U, or one-way ANOVA) across a large LC-MS metabolomics feature table and need multiplicity-corrected q-values to select candidate biomarkers.

name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction
description: Use when a table of per-reaction concordance scores (Cohen's kappa, Pearson correlation of RPS vs RAS and RPS vs FFD) needs multiple-comparison correction to decide which reactions are statistically significantly concordant at 5% FDR.

name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction
description: Use when a MOFA factor-interpretation step yields many nominal p-values from Pearson (numeric clinical features) and Wilcoxon (binary clinical features) tests that must be FDR-corrected before ranking discriminant factors.

name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction
description: Use when a spatial metabolomics feature matrix (e.g., 14,260 pixels x 3,044 ion peaks) has been grouped into two regions (e.g., pixel clusters MB vs HIP) and every ion's raw p-value from a univariate test must be multiplicity-corrected before calling differential metabolites.

name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction
description: Use when a feature table from LC/MS preprocessing (apLCMS, XCMS, or two-stage apLCMS, batch-corrected or not) has per-feature t-test p-values between two cell types and you need multiplicity-adjusted significance counts at a lenient FDR cutoff such as 0.2.

name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-edge-significance-testing
description: Use when constructing a multi-omics co-occurrence network from paired feature tables (e.

name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when a differential analysis of grouped NMR peak features produces thousands of per-feature p-values and you need FDR-controlled significance calls comparable across frameworks such as speaq 2.0 and MetaboAnalyst.

name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when many metabolite features (e.g. bile-amidate feature rows in a relative-quantification table) have each been tested with a Wilcoxon rank-sum test, producing a family of raw p-values that must be FDR-adjusted before calling disease associations.

name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when a metabolomics pathway-enrichment step yields one raw p-value per pathway (e.g. from Fisher's Exact Test on 2x2 contingency tables or fgsea MetSEA) and pathways must be ranked by adjusted p-value with a significance cutoff (adjusted p < 0.05).

name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when per-term p-values from S2IsoMEr bootstrapping ORA/MSEA (one-tailed Fisher's exact tests over >=50-1000 bootstrap iterations) must be FDR-controlled before reporting overrepresented HMDB/RAMP-DB or LION terms.

name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when a metabolomics (or other omics) feature table requires a per-feature significance test (e.g. linear regression for diet/group effect) across thousands of features and raw p-values must be adjusted before selecting differential features with cutoffs such as Log2FC > 1.5 and adj-p < 0.05.

name: benjamini-hochberg-pvalue-correction
description: Use when running MetaboDiff diff_test on a metabolite measurement table with two or more groups (e.g. MYC-high vs AKT1-high), where raw Student's t-test or ANOVA p-values must be adjusted for multiple testing across metabolites.

name: benjamini-yekutieli-fdr-correction
description: Use when a large, dependent family of p-values (e.g. hypergeometric tests for gene-pair adjacency or co-localisation in BGCs) must be FDR-corrected before thresholding, as in PRESTO-STAT sub-cluster detection.

name: bertz-relative-prediction-error-analysis
description: Use when fine-tuning a pre-trained DreaMS transformer on MS/MS spectra for molecular-property prediction and you need to benchmark Bertz complexity regression against XGBoost and MS2Prop baselines.

name: best-incorrect-candidate-selection
description: Use when comparing annotation methods that return multiple candidate structures per MS2 spectrum and you need to characterize the quality of their incorrect prediction rather than only top-1 accuracy.

name: beta-diversity-pcoa-ordination
description: Use when QIIME beta diversity distance matrices have been ordinated to principal coordinates (PCoA) and you need interactive 3D exploration of sample clustering colored by metadata, or jackknifed confidence display.

name: between-group-fold-change-analysis
description: Use when a preprocessed LC-MS feature table (features x samples) has labeled biological groups (e.g. 14 lamprey tissues, 94 samples) and you need to rank which features are massively enriched in one group versus the pooled rest, with FDR-controlled significance.

name: between-replicate-dispersion-quantification
description: Use when an LC-MS metabolomics experiment includes replicate runs (or pooled QC replicates) and you need to score how well a normalization method (tGAM, rGAM, rLOESS, QC-RLSC, QC-RSC, SERFF, TIGER) reduced between-replicate technical dispersion.

name: between-treatment-significance-testing
description: Use when a standardized compound-area table from GC-MS peak extraction exists and the goal is to test whether compound composition differs between treatments, e.g. reproducing a published study's NMDS-based significance pattern.

name: betweenness-centrality-computation
description: Use when a metabolomics differential analysis has yielded a significant metabolite list (absolute fold change ≥ 1, adjusted p-value < 0.05) and you need to identify hub metabolites or rank pathways by structural network impact rather than enrichment p-value alone.

name: bfs-neighborhood-collapsing
description: Decision support for building a compact molecular network from dense 3-NN graphs of MS/MS embeddings when highly similar spectra (similarity > 0.9) should be merged into single nodes to reduce redundancy before annotation propagation.

name: bgc-accession-request-submission
description: Use when a task requires submitting or simulating submission of a new biosynthetic gene cluster entry to MIBiG, or structuring BGC metadata into the accession-request → staff-approval → extended-annotation pipeline.

name: bgc-biosynthetic-class-categorisation
description: Use when a BGC metadata table (e.g. the 851 new MIBiG 2.0 entries) must be grouped by structure-based biosynthetic class to quantify composition, dominance of Polyketides/NRPs, or database growth.

name: bgc-chemical-property-gap-quantification
description: Use when auditing annotation completeness of a known-function BGC database — e.g. quantifying how many entries lack a chemical structure or have empty molecular formula/mass/chirality fields before and after a re-curation release.

name: bgc-class-annotation-mapping
description: Use when linking BGCs to MS/MS spectra requires a mapping between genome-side BGC classes and structure-side chemical classes, or when reproducing/ updating NPClassScore scoring tables from MIBiG entries.

name: bgc-compound-crosslink-mapping
description: Use when a curated set of BGC entries with compound name and structure annotations needs to be linked out to chemical databases (Natural Products Atlas, GNPS, PubChem) to build a linkage inventory per accession.

name: bgc-curation-channel-count-extraction
description: Use when an article or report describes multiple curation channels contributing entries to a biosynthetic gene cluster repository (e.g. crowdsourced submissions, Annotathons, classroom curation) with numeric per-channel counts that must be tabulated and validated.

name: bgc-distance-metric-weight-optimization
description: Use when BiG-SCAPE distance weights for JI, AI, and DSS must be calibrated per BGC class against known compound structures (MIBiG) so that BGC similarity networks reflect chemical similarity.

name: bgc-domain-architecture-similarity-comparison
description: Use when input is antiSMASH-processed GenBank files of BGCs and the goal is pairwise domain-architecture distances, a similarity network, or benchmarking clustering quality (NMI/ARI/V-score) against MIBiG curated groups.

name: bgc-euclidean-feature-vectorization
description: Use when BGC datasets are too large for pairwise comparison tools (e.g., hundreds of thousands to millions of BGCs from antiSMASH runs) and GCF clustering must scale near-linearly, or when fragmented BGCs must be mapped onto prebuilt GCF centroid models via query mode.

name: bgc-feature-extraction-from-antismash-output
description: Use when a newly sequenced putative BGC — available as an antiSMASH output folder — must be placed into previously computed BiG-SLiCE gene cluster families (GCFs) to assess its function and/or novelty without rerunning a full clustering analysis.

name: bgc-gcf-clustering-threshold-optimization
description: Use when a BiG-SLiCE run's threshold parameter T must be selected or validated, e.g. when balancing the number of GCF models against fidelity to known MIBiG compound groups.

name: bgc-gcf-label-aggregation
description: Use when paired genome–MS/MS samples need candidate GCF labels per MS/MS spectrum aggregated from kNN neighbor votes, and candidate links must be confidence-filtered against PoDP-validated gene–metabolite links.

name: bgc-gcf-similarity-scoring
description: Use when a new antiSMASH-annotated BGC needs to be assigned to existing GCF models from a prior BiG-SLiCE run (stored as an SQLite3 database), and a full re-clustering of the corpus would be wasteful.

name: bgc-gene-cluster-family-classification
description: Use when you have paired genome-MS/MS samples (e.g. PoDP genomes plus LC-MS/MS spectra), a query MS/MS spectrum (GNPS reference or cryptic), and want to link it to a gene cluster family with precision ~0.929 top-10.

name: bgc-gene-cluster-family-fingerprint-construction
description: Use when paired genome-MS/MS samples have been antiSMASH-annotated and BiG-SCAPE-scored, and you need per-BGC genome-wide similarity vectors plus GCF labels as a KNN training matrix.

name: bgc-homology-search-against-mibig-reference
description: Use when you need to benchmark newly mined BGCs (e.g. from uncultivated soil bacteria or soil metagenomes) against a curated set of experimentally characterized BGCs of known function.

name: bgc-metabolite-link-scoring
description: Use when you have PoDP project metadata (JSON from Zenodo or pairedomicsdata.bioinformatics.nl) with validated BGC–metabolite links and need to compute and rank scores for candidate BGC–metabolite pairs in NPLinker.

name: bgc-metadata-quality-audit
description: Use when auditing a versioned repository of biosynthetic gene cluster annotations — typically MIBiG JSON entries — to quantify missing chemical structures, incomplete property fields, or annotation deltas between releases.

name: bgc-molecule-linkage-analysis
description: Use when identified molecules from GNPS microbial mass spectrometry datasets have paired strain genome data and you need to link molecules to biosynthetic gene clusters via MIBiG/BLAST validation.

name: bgc-msms-candidate-link-scoring
description: Use when you have paired omics data (genome-derived GCFs plus GNPS molecular networking MS/MS spectra) and need to reduce long candidate BGC–spectrum link lists, e.g. via NPLinker with Metcalf scoring followed by NPClassScore class-matching.

name: bgc-msms-link-curation
description: Use when parsing PoDP project JSON documents (Zenodo-archived, ~70 projects) to enumerate or verify BGC–MS/MS links, i.e., records connecting a MIBiG identifier to an MS/MS URL and scan number.

name: bgc-msms-link-filtering-threshold-application
description: Use when a Metcalf-scored list of candidate BGC–MS/MS spectrum links must be reduced and prioritised using genome-based (BiG-SCAPE/antiSMASH) versus structure-based (CANOPUS/MolNetEnhancer) chemical class agreement.

name: bgc-msms-linkage-analysis
description: Use when candidate BGC–metabolite (BGC–MS/MS) links need to be scored and ranked within NPLinker, and validated paired-omics links are available from the PoDP as JSON with MIBiG identifiers and MS/MS URLs with scan numbers.

name: bgc-msms-linking-tool-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing biosynthetic gene cluster-to-mass-spectra linking performance of multiple published tools against a gold-standard set of validated BGC–metabolite pairs from paired omics data.

name: bgc-multi-locus-phylogeny-inference
description: Use when antiSMASH-processed GenBank BGCs plus a chosen query gene are available and network-based GCF clustering (BiG-SCAPE) is suspected to have split or omitted related clusters — e.

name: bgc-product-class-classification
description: Use when you have MIBiG-labeled BGC training sets in Pfam TSV format (e.g. biosynthetic-class with 1355 samples, chem-act with 370 samples) and need to predict product class or chemical activity per BGC via multi-label classification with AUC-ROC evaluation.

name: bgc-query-to-subcluster-motif-matching
description: Use when tokenised (sub)Pfam-domain BGCs must be matched against pre-trained LDA sub-cluster motifs to predict biosynthetic sub-clusters, or to validate predicted sub-clusters against known SubClusterBlast entries.

name: bgc-redundancy-network-filtering
description: Use when a large tokenised BGC set (e.g. antiSMASH output with per-gene (sub)Pfam tokens) must be de-duplicated before motif/sub-cluster mining, and near-identical clusters (Adjacency Index > 0.95 or full containment) should be collapsed.

name: bgc-region-post-processing
description: Use when per-domain BGC detector scores (DeepBGC BiLSTM or ClusterFinder HMM) must be thresholded at a calibrated operating point (10% FPR or 80% TPR) and collapsed into discrete BGC regions for genome-scale precision evaluation.

name: bgc-repository-statistics-extraction
description: Use when you need aggregate counts of curated BGCs — totals, per-class (e.g. Polyketide 825, NRP 627) or per-taxon (e.g. Streptomyces 568) breakdowns — from MIBiG or a similar curated BGC repository.

name: bgc-similarity-fingerprint-construction
description: Use when building the labeled BGC training matrix for NPOmix from antiSMASH .gbk files and BiG-SCAPE pairwise similarity outputs, prior to KNN classification of MS/MS fingerprints.

name: bgc-spectral-candidate-link-counting
description: Use when quantifying how many candidate BGC–MS/MS spectrum links each GCF retains under co-occurrence-only scoring versus chemical-class filtering, e.g. to reproduce or assess manageable candidate-link histograms.

name: bgc-spectrum-link-ranking
description: Use when paired genomic-metabolomic data (AntiSMASH BGCs, GNPS molecular networking spectra, strain mappings) must be linked and candidate links prioritised by rank, e.g. to reproduce Table 3-style top-n performance comparisons.

name: bgc-spectrum-pairing
description: Use when building an evaluation set of known BGC–metabolite–MS2 spectrum links: MIBiG records contain no MS2 data and GNPS spectra lack BGC provenance, so pairing must be done through shared compound structural identifiers.

name: bgc-subcluster-motif-annotation
description: Use when a trained PRESTO-TOP model with latent sub-cluster motifs exists and the goal is to assign substructure-level annotations (e.g. aminoglycoside, moenomycin motifs) by matching motif instances to validated sub-clusters in MIBiG and antiSMASH SubClusterBlast data.

name: bh-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when univariate association tests (e.g. partial Spearman correlations) have been run for every metabolic feature against a clinical phenotype and a multiple-testing-corrected pFDR column is needed before calling associations.

name: bic-lambda-hyperparameter-tuning
description: Use when building GGM partial-correlation metabolite networks with DNEA on two-condition metabolomics data and the lambda penalty for glasso regularization must be set — either via BIC tuning (~500+ samples per group) or via the small-sample approximation.

name: bidirectional-edge-filtering
description: Use when combining pairwise subalignment match tables from two or more independently processed nontargeted LC-MS datasets into a feature graph, and only mutually supported (bidirectional) matches should become edges before clustering into feature groups.

name: bigscape-bgc-similarity-fingerprinting
description: Use when you have antiSMASH .gbk BGCs from paired genome–metabolome samples and need BGC fingerprint rows (with GCF labels) to train the NPOmix KNN classifier or to query against its space.

name: bigscape-network-concatenation
description: Use when a set of antiSMASH GenBank BGCs (training set plus query genomes) must be converted into pairwise similarity scores and GCF assignments feeding an NPOmix BGC fingerprint matrix.

name: bigscape-similarity-output-concatenation
description: Use when you have antiSMASH .gbk BGCs from multiple genomes and need a unified pairwise BGC similarity table per biosynthetic class to build NPOmix training fingerprints.

name: bile-acid-conjugate-annotation
description: Use when a GNPS molecular network contains a library-annotated seed node (e.g. glycocholic acid, m/z 466.316) and structurally related analogs must be discovered by reading edge mass shifts (e.g. +79.993 Da for sulfation) to neighboring unannotated nodes.

name: bile-acid-conjugate-chemistry
description: Use when constructing an in silico structure database of bile acid conjugates from scaffold cores plus amino-acid/acyl building blocks, requiring an exact combinatorial enumeration count (28,630 structures) as validation.

name: bile-acid-msms-spectral-networking
description: Use when analyzing untargeted metabolomics MS/MS spectra of bile acids (or related lipid families) where conventional cosine-threshold molecular networking fragments metabolite families and novel conjugates may be hidden as missed connections.

name: bile-amidate-feature-annotation
description: Use when an untargeted LC–MS/MS feature table from human fecal/stool cohorts contains unannotated features suspected to be bile acid–amino acid conjugates and the goal is to assign bile-amidate identity via repository spectral matching and test IBD/CD association.

name: bile-amidate-spectral-library-matching
description: Use when raw positive-mode LC-MS/MS (e.g., Bruker Q-ToF MSV000084475) or negative-mode LC-IMS-MS (e.g., Agilent 6560 IM-Q-ToF MSV000087889) culture or fecal data must be annotated against synthetic conjugated-bile-acid standard spectra to identify per-strain bile amidate producers.

name: bimodal-tissue-enrichment-classification
description: Use when DIMPLE has produced clustered hyperspectral channel assignments along a linear root developmental gradient (e.g., B73 roots in .cdf/.mat workspace files) and you need to separate bimodal developmental signatures from cell-layer-enriched signatures for annotation and tabulation.

name: bin-weighted-summary-statistics
description: Use when a table of per-peak AutoTuner parameter estimates must be reduced to one dataset-wide eight-parameter set before returning parameters to the user or feeding centWave processing in XCMS/MZmine2.

name: binary-classification-evaluation-measures-calculation
description: Use when comparing multiple binary classifiers trained on the same labeled dataset (e.g. high-quality vs low-quality LC-MS peaks) and you need a rigorous, statistically defensible selection of the model using recall, precision, F-measure and Friedman-Nemenyi ranking.

name: binary-classification-f1-evaluation
description: Use when the goal is to compare classifier variants that predict peak presence/absence per m/z bin from molecular structure (SMILES), and benchmark them with mean F1 on a test split rather than predicting full spectra or peak intensities.

name: binary-classification-metric-computation
description: Use when comparing in silico MS/MS prediction tools (e.g., SingleFrag vs. CFM-ID vs. 3DMolMS) on the same test compounds and you need peak-level classification metrics plus spectral cosine similarity on a common m/z grid.

name: binary-classification-metric-computation
description: Use when a compound-identification run yields binary detection/containment calls per compound (e.g. mcfNMR assignment values vs. a detection threshold) and you need F1, precision and recall against a known mixture composition for benchmarking.

name: binary-classification-metric-computation
description: Use when an automated per-item quality decision (e.g. metScribeR peak filtering on 860 adduct peaks) must be benchmarked against manual binary ground-truth labels with precision/recall/F1.

name: binary-classification-metric-evaluation
description: Use when a CNN or ML model outputs binary class probabilities (e.g. DPPH high vs. low activity) and you need AUC, accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 with confidence from cross-validation.

name: binary-classification-metric-evaluation
description: Use when a binary bitter/nonbitter classifier (e.g. BitterMasS Random Forest on positive-ion-mode EI-MS or ESI-MS/MS spectra) must be scored on held-out or literature-derived test compounds.

name: binary-classification-metric-reporting
description: Use when a binary-classification MB-PLS model (e.g., encoded outcome such as Female=1/Male=0 in alz_metadata.csv) has been fitted to multiassay LC-MS feature blocks and its predictive performance must be quantified on an independent test set or via repeated resampling.

name: binary-classifier-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when a trained binary classifier (e.g. EVA CNN distinguishing good vs poor EIC plots) must be evaluated on a large manually labeled dataset and overall accuracy validated against a published performance claim.

name: binary-classifier-evaluation-metrics
description: Reference for scoring any binary classifier on expert Pass/Fail labels — e.g. MetaClean peak-quality predictions on an independent LC–MS test set such as ST000695.

name: binary-classifier-f-measure-computation
description: Use when evaluating a binary classifier (e.g., peak Pass/Fail quality in untargeted LC–MS metabolomics) where both high- and low-quality classes are important and single accuracy is insufficient.

name: binary-cross-entropy-model-evaluation
description: Use when a trained pSCNN model on NMR spectra of mixtures must be scored, or when benchmarking binary compound-identification performance with ACC/TPR/FPR metrics.

name: binary-fingerprint-output-validation
description: Use when DeepEI (or a similar fingerprint predictor) has converted EI mass spectra into structural fingerprints and you must verify each vector is binary and correctly dimensioned before merging into .msp or saving as .npy.

name: binary-indicator-encoding-of-cluster-assignments
description: Use when M datasets each carry a cluster label vector c_m with K_m clusters and you must summarise these heterogeneous clusterings into one binary matrix (MOC) before integrative consensus clustering such as COCA.

name: binary-metabologenomic-correlation-analysis

name: binary-spectral-data-handling

name: binomial-labelling-model-inference

name: bioactivity-correlation-scoring

name: bioactivity-coverage-tabulation

name: bioactivity-functional-category-mapping

name: bioassay-data-normalization

name: bioassay-guided-fractionation-comparison

name: bioassay-label-normalization-and-binarization

name: bioassay-profile-normalization

description: Use when evaluating whether a learned scoring/filtering model retains the true chemical formula among its top-ranked candidates (e.g., top-256 recovery) and how large enumerated candidate sets are before filtering.

name: candidate-formula-ranking
description: Use when a formula-identification pipeline produces multiple candidate formulas per MS/MS spectrum (e.g. after SENIOR-rule refinement against precursor mass) and you need to order them by predicted correctness using learned MS/MS spectral features.

name: candidate-frequency-ranking-for-denovo-annotation
description: Use when a diffusion-based or other generative structure-prediction model outputs many candidate molecular graphs per mass spectrum and you must distill them into a frequency-ranked top-1/top-10 prediction and score it against known ground-truth molecules.

name: candidate-gene-prioritization
description: Use when a Bayesian direction-of-effect model identifies traits with confident positive enrichments or depletions and you need to name the concrete genes (e.g. Fig. 6 candidates) driving those enrichments across time points and tissues.

name: candidate-gene-prioritization-benchmarking
description: Use when validating a candidate causal gene prioritization tool or component against curated molecular QTL reference assignments, to quantify how many true positive causal genes are recovered and how many false positives are introduced.

name: candidate-gene-prioritization-scoring
description: Use when you have both metPropagate (LPA) propagated scores and Exomiser-Phenotype scores for the same patient's candidate gene list and want a combined ranking that reduces metabolomic false-positive prioritization in suspected IEM patients.

name: candidate-gene-rank-evaluation
description: Use when you have per-patient prioritized candidate gene lists (281-609 genes from Exomiser filtering) plus each patient's previously diagnosed causative gene, and need head-to-head rank comparison of scoring schemes.

name: candidate-gene-rank-percentile-analysis
description: Use when you have per-gene propagated network scores and a WES-derived candidate gene list (e.g., 281-609 Exomiser genes) and need to assess whether causative genes rank in the top 20th percentile.

name: candidate-gene-set-contingency-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking gene-prioritization criteria against a reference set of curated causal genes at QTL loci and you need per-criterion odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals from 2x2 contingency tables.

name: candidate-list-score-normalization
description: Use when you have MetFrag fragment scores for multiple candidate structures (from PubChem/ChemSpider/SDF retrieval) plus auxiliary terms (PubChem/ChemSpider reference counts, log P-based RT predictions, suspect/substructure penalties) that must be placed on a common scale before weighted.

name: candidate-list-stereoisomer-filtering
description: Use when a candidate structure list (from PubChem, ChemSpider, KEGG, or a user SDF) contains stereoisomeric duplicates that would crowd out distinct scaffolds in the ranked MetFrag output.

name: candidate-mass-tolerance-filtering
description: Use when a detected MS1 metabolic feature (precursor m/z) must be matched against a candidate compound database (e.g., CQMD, KEGG, HMDB) before MS/MS-based LFP scoring, and candidates need pruning to a ppm-level mass window prior to similarity ranking.

name: candidate-molecule-fragmentation-scoring
description: Use when you have MS/MS or MSn peak lists (hierarchical m/z:intensity parenthesis format) for an unknown precursor, a set of candidate structures from PubChem/cheminformatics database, and you need to rank candidates by how well the observed fragment peaks are explained by in silico generated.

name: candidate-pool-size-verification
description: Use when reproducing or validating the FMP-10 candidate-pool reduction over HMDB — i.e., before metabolite identification in MALDI-MSI, to confirm the derivatization-filter subset counts (26,202 all vs 4,951 endogenous) against reported values.

name: candidate-rank-optimization
description: Use when ranking candidate structures for an LC-HR-MS/MS unknown where spectral library matches are insufficient and extra evidence (reference/patent counts, RT–log P, CFM-ID predictions) should be fused into the MetFrag score.

name: candidate-rank-re-ranking-evaluation
description: Use when you have ranked candidate structure lists from tools like ISDB-DNP, Sirius or MS-Finder plus organism taxonomy, and want to quantify how taxonomically informed re-ranking changes rank-1 annotation correctness.

name: candidate-ranking-annotation-evaluation
description: Use when an MS/MS analyte (positive or negative mode) has been searched against a compound database by precursor m/z with a ppm tolerance, producing a candidate InChIKey list that must be ranked for annotation.

name: candidate-ranking-evaluation
description: Use when a workflow must prioritize and validate one annotation candidate per MS2 feature — e.g. merging spectral database dereplication (GNPS/HMDB/MassBank) with MetFrag/SIRIUS candidate lists and checking ranks, scores, or coverage percentages.

name: candidate-ranking-evaluation-mass-spectrometry
description: Use when you have spectra paired with candidate molecule sets (e.g. torch_tecand_*.pkl from PubChem) and must quantify annotation performance via average rank and Rank@k metrics.

name: candidate-ranking-gap-stratification
description: Decision support for judging how trustworthy a top-1 metabolite annotation is: after ranking candidate molecules by cosine similarity between predicted and experimental MS/MS spectra, stratify correctness by the Δcos gap to identify confidence cutoffs.

name: candidate-ranking-with-tie-breaking
description: Use when a list of candidate molecules (e.g. retrieved from PubChem within a 10 ppm mass window) must be ranked against an MS/MS peak list without reference spectra, and ties between equally scoring candidates need deterministic resolution.

name: candidate-retrieval-quality-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking an alternative ANN index structure (e.g. HNSW, LSH, product quantization) for candidate selection in open spectral library searching, to quantify candidate-retrieval quality against a baseline.

name: candidate-spectrum-similarity-ranking
description: Use when you have an unidentified experimental MS/MS spectrum (e.g. an ARUS recurrent unidentified spectrum), a candidate molecule list with SMILES and assigned formulas, and need to rank candidates by spectral similarity for annotation.

name: candidate-structure-fragmentation-scoring
description: Use when a KGMN/MetDNA2 annotation run has labeled unknown peaks in untargeted LC-MS/MS data (e.g., NIST urine pos/neg mode) that need reliability corroboration because no spectral-library match or chemical standard exists.

name: candidate-structure-graph-construction-from-identification-candidates
description: Use when a ready-to-identify dataset pairs candidate structures with MS/MS spectral scores and ROASMI retention-order probabilities, and you must rank structures for each peak.

name: candidate-structure-list-generation
description: Use when you have a measured precursor m/z and assigned adduct (e.g. [M+H]+, [M−H]−, [M+Na]+) and need a structured candidate-compound list with exact masses and descriptors as the input table for CCS-based false-positive filtering in metabolomics.

name: candidate-structure-rank-evaluation
description: Use when annotation outputs (ISDB-DNP, Sirius, MS-Finder candidate lists) must be re-ranked using biological-source taxonomy of the producing organism, and rank-1 annotation accuracy on a benchmarking dataset must be quantified.

name: candidate-structure-ranking
description: Use when a predicted Morgan fingerprint bit string from an upstream DeepSAT 1H-13C HSQC prediction must be scored against fingerprints of candidate structures (e.g., from PubChem) to produce a ranked, thresholded annotation list.

name: candidate-structure-re-ranking
description: Use when a spectral-matching tool (ISDB-DNP, MS-Finder, Sirius) returns multiple candidate structures for a feature and the biological source's taxonomy (species, genus, family) is known, so candidates can be re-ranked by taxonomic distance.

name: candidate-structure-retrieval-from-pubchem-chemspider
description: Use when tandem-MS spectra need candidate structures scored by in silico fragmentation and no candidate list exists yet; trigger on a precursor neutral mass or molecular formula plus a chosen compound database (PubChem, ChemSpider).

name: canonical-correlation-analysis-feature-derivation
description: Use when integrating spatial transcriptome (a.h5ad) and MALDI-MSI (b_prime.h5ad) data that share no spots or features, after gross/ICP alignment and anchor spot-pair selection (Simpson diversity < 0.2), to create a CCA-derived variate that improves alignment accuracy.

name: canonical-fragment-feature-encoding
description: Use when a fragment must be converted from a rooted molecular graph (e.g. from RDKit) into a fixed, index-invariant topological feature vector for training or applying CFM-ID 4.0-style fragmentation transition models.

name: canonical-spectrum-string-normalization
description: Use when a mass spectrum needs a database-independent, reproducible identifier (SPLASH) and the input is a peak list such as a MassBank record (e.g. caffeine PR100026) rather than an existing SPLASH string.

name: canopus-benchmark-protocol
description: Use when you must benchmark a fingerprint-prediction model on tandem MS/MS spectra against MIST on the CANOPUS benchmark, or when reproducing DreaMS's fingerprint retrieval and molecular-property prediction results.

name: canopus-chemical-class-prediction
description: Reference for annotating per-feature chemical classes from DDA MS2 spectra after MZmine feature detection, when structural annotation (SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID) and class taxonomy (CANOPUS, NPClassifier) are needed in an RDF workflow.

name: canopus-npclassifier-class-confidence-filtering
description: Use when a canopus_npc_summary table of predicted chemical classes per feature/extract must be reduced to high-confidence, recurring classes prior to novelty scoring (e.g., computing the CC score against LOTUS/NPClassifier reports).

name: carbon-chain-pairwise-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantify how likely two arbitrary carbon chains share no double bond at the same position (mismatch probability) — e.g. to validate that a lipidomics tool's double bond similarity is meaningful rather than trivially satisfied.

name: carbon-number-prediction-modeling
description: Use when IDSL.IPA peaklists contain R13C peak properties and you need to predict carbon counts for elemental composition, or validate that experimental R13C agrees with theoretical isotope ratios from formulas.

name: carbon-shift-ambiguity-scoring
description: Decision support for ranking or weighting compound identifications in INADEQUATE-based NMR metabolomics when a simulated INADEQUATE database derived from BMRB contains metabolites whose carbons have multiple possible chemical shift assignments.

name: carbon-shift-matching-tolerance-configuration
description: Reference for setting match thresholds when scoring filtered peak networks from 13C INADEQUATE spectra against a simulated INADEQUATE database of metabolites.

name: caret-cross-validated-model-tuning
description: Use when building a classification model from metabolomics PDS score features and you need to compare multiple ML algorithms under caret-based hyperparameter tuning with n-fold cross-validation and held-out test metrics.

name: caret-hyperparameter-tuning
description: Use when a labeled set of peak quality scores (qslog.tsv) plus an expert annotation file (manual_peakcheck.xlsx with scores 0/1/2) is available and a peak-reporting classification model must be trained, tuned, and serialized in R.

name: carnitine-subnetwork-annotation
description: Use when hundreds of non-annotated, differentially abundant MS/MS features fall inside a molecular-network subnetwork with known annotated neighbors (e.g. carnitines), and you need putative class-level identities via in-silico tools like SIRIUS.

name: carriage-only-biomarker-candidate-selection
description: Use when metabolite profiles from a chronic carriage study must be compared with those of acute infection to find metabolites elevated in carriage only, e.g. GCxGC-TOFMS data of S. Typhi/S. Paratyphi A carriage vs controls, cross-referenced against acute enteric fever significant metabolite lists.

name: cartographical-snapshot-reproducibility
description: Use when a finalized 'ili molecular map view (spot rendering on an STL 3D model or PNG 2D background) must be saved, shared, or exactly reproduced later, or when validating that a received cartographical_snapshot.json restores the intended view.

name: cartographical-snapshot-sharing
description: Use when a spatial molecular map visualized in 'ili must be shared or re-displayed reproducibly, e.g. after tuning a logarithmic scale or hotspot quantile to reveal faint keypad traces, so the identical view can be restored.

name: cascade-open-modification-spectral-search
description: Use when searching high-resolution query spectra (e.g. iPRG2012 TripleTOF mzML) against a large target-decoy spectral library and you need to confidently identify both unmodified and modified peptides via open modification searching at 1% FDR.

name: cascade-search-configuration
description: Use when performing open modification spectral library searches where unmodified and modified peptides must be identified separately with strict FDR control, e.g. searching query spectra against a large target-decoy spectral library with ANN-SoLo.

name: case-control-pathway-ranking-analysis
description: Use when you have a peak-intensity matrix with case/control experimental groups (e.g. Stage_1/Control, Stage_2/Control comparisons) plus peak-to-compound annotations (KEGG or ChEBI IDs) and need to rank significantly changing metabolite sets.

name: case-control-simulated-metabolomics-dataset-construction
description: Use when a simulation experiment requires multiple chemical datasets (e.g. 'control' vs 'case' samples) derived from one shared base chemical list, with configurable per-chemical dropout rates or cross-sample intensity variation.

name: casmi-2017-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when a de novo structure-prediction model must be benchmarked on CASMI 2017 challenge spectra and compared with SIRIUS4/MetFrag baselines using correct-structure rate and molecular similarity metrics.

name: casmi-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating predicted tandem mass spectra against CASMI 2016/2022 challenge data, or when you need to quantify how peak-annotation coverage bounds cosine similarity of in silico fragmentation predictions.

name: casmi-benchmark-structure-retrieval-evaluation
description: Use when you have CASMI 2016 positive-mode MS2 spectra with reference structure annotations and de novo candidate SMILES from MSNovelist, and need retrieval/top-1 metrics.

name: casmi-challenge-candidate-ranking
description: Use when you have ready-to-identify candidate lists (e.g. SIRIUS or MS-DIAL outputs for CASMI 2022 challenges) and want to check whether retention-order scores improve correct-structure ranking or prune candidates before MS/MS scoring.

name: casmi-contest-score-retrieval-and-harmonization
description: Use when benchmarking an annotation confidence score against published contest scores: you need the CASMI 2016 per-compound hit scores from MetFrag, MAGMa+, CFM-ID, CSI:FingerID and CSI:FingerID IOKR to compute ROC curves, FDR-corrected hit counts, and mean ranks of correct hits.

name: casmi2016-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when a trained MS2-to-structure model needs standardized head-to-head comparison on the CASMI 2016 Challenge set, e.g. to report direct ISMILES accuracy and fingerprint-similarity top-1 ranking accuracy on positive-mode spectra.

name: casmi2016-compound-identification-scoring
description: Use when benchmarking an MS-to-compound (MS2C) identification method on the 208-spectrum CASMI 2016 category 3 Orbitrap dataset, or when a QTOF-trained model needs an instrument-transfer evaluation against the published 147/208 baseline.

name: casmi2022-positive-mode-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating a formula-annotation model on prospective challenge spectra: you have CASMI 2022 mzML files, formula candidates, and need head-to-head accuracy comparison vs SIRIUS without manual curation.

name: casrn-and-canonical-smiles-deduplication
description: Use when fusing multiple chemical source databases or lists into one exposome/inventory table and you must eliminate duplicates and non-applicable chemical classes before downstream prioritization or annotation.

name: catalogue-of-life-taxonomic-resolution-filtering
description: Use when biological-source metadata contains free-text organism names that must be resolved against the Catalogue of Life and filtered to species-level completeness before joining structures to sources.

name: categorate-result-query-construction
description: Use when you have a categorate() result (eight standard tables: reactives, LOTUS, KEGG, FEMA, FDA_SPL, FMCS, FunctionalGroups, ChemMatch) and need to derive a filtered chemical query list by database membership, FMCS properties, or chemical-library group.

name: categorical-annotation-filtering
description: Use when a table carries categorical annotation columns (e.g. GO terms, cellular localization, signaling pathway) and rows must be retained only if their category term matches a searched category, then annotated.

name: categorical-frequency-counting
description: Use when a labeled spreadsheet/CSV has one categorical column (e.g., peptide hormone family annotations) and the goal is a frequency table of all distinct categories plus identification of the most abundant category.

name: categorical-item-factor-extraction
description: Use when a set of categorical behavioral questionnaire items (e.g., ASEBA CBCL item scores) must be reduced to a small number of continuous dimensions whose explained variance can be reported per dimension.

name: category-level-record-classification-verification
description: Use when auditing a curated database deposit (e.g., HORDB's /datasets/ folder) to confirm per-category record counts match the manuscript-reported totals, such as 6024 total entries split into 5729/40/255.

name: cathinone-analog-screening
description: Use when enumerating cathinone-templated derivative libraries and you must prune functional groups whose repeated substitution (n = 2, 3) makes derivatives too hard to synthesize, per ΔSCScore < α^n.

name: causative-gene-rank-comparison
description: Use when patients have both a metPropagate post-propagation score file and a competing prioritization tool's score list (e.g. Exomiser hiPHIVE), plus a known causative gene, and you need a head-to-head ranking comparison.

name: cause-specific-mortality-endpoint-classification
description: Use when a cohort has cause-of-death coded vital status (e.g., cardiovascular, cancer, infection, other) and you must test whether metabolic biomarkers associated with all-cause mortality also associate with specific causes of death.

name: ccs-based-annotation-filtering
description: Use when annotating IM-MS features in untargeted metabolomics and a list of molecular-formula/structure candidates exists for an m/z within ~10 ppm, and an experimental CCS value is available to prune false positives.

name: ccs-based-compound-identification
description: Use when a metabolomics/lipidomics query set has measured precursor m/z (and optionally RT) and you must narrow a large candidate library (e.g. LipidBlast) using CCS from a 3D-conformer GNN before identification.

name: ccs-based-false-positive-filtering
description: Use when a candidate list of molecular structures (e.g. PubChem hits within a 10 ppm mass window of a deprotonated/protonated ion) must be filtered using ion-mobility-derived CCS values.

name: ccs-bias-calculation
description: Use when measured (LC-)IM-MS lipidomics data contain U13C-labeled ('heavy') lipid entries with CCS values and you need to quantify CCSN2 bias against the DTCCSN2 library, per lipid class-adduct combination.

name: ccs-bias-calculation-ion-mobility-lipidomics
description: Use when LC-IM-MS lipidomics samples (e.g., from a Bruker timsTOF Pro TIM-MS or Agilent 6560 DTIM-MS) are spiked with U13C-labeled yeast extract standards and you need to quantify CCSN2 bias per ionization mode against a DT reference library.

name: ccs-calibration-curve-fitting
description: Use when IMS-MS feature tables contain calibrant ions with reference CCS values and you need a fitted calibration function (linear, polynomial, or linearized power) to convert arrival times into CCS for unknown analytes.

name: ccs-compendium-reference-value-handling
description: Use when calibrating traveling-wave ion mobility arrival times or assigning unknown features to biomolecular classes and you need trusted DTCCSN2 reference values for small molecules, lipids, or peptides.

name: ccs-correction-function-regression
description: Use when IM-MS lipidomics data spiked with U13C-labeled yeast internal standards show CCSN2 bias versus the DTCCSN2 library, and lipid class-adduct combinations contain ≥3 U13C-labeled lipids for regression-based correction.

name: ccs-database-joining-by-adduct
description: Use when you have a large table of predicted CCS values plus an independent reference CCS database and need adduct-stratified agreement statistics rather than a single pooled correlation.

name: ccs-database-standardization
description: Use when a raw CCS database download (excel/csv from ccsbase.net or METLIN) must be cleaned into a model-ready table and contains duplicate SMILES-adduct entries with disagreeing CCS values before GNN training.

name: ccs-graph-neural-network-training
description: Use when you need a within-database baseline of GNN-based CCS prediction accuracy: you have SMILES + adduct + CCS values from CCSBase (v1.3) or METLIN-CCS already split 80/20 and want R2/MRE per model.

name: ccs-literature-value-collation
description: Use when benchmarking in-silico CCS predictions or a new instrument's TWIMS/DTIM measurements against literature CCS database values and you need a percent-deviation table keyed by metabolite and adduct state.

name: ccs-percent-error-benchmarking
description: Use when a metabolite has SMILES input plus an experimental/consensus CCS reference and you need per-state computed CCS values and percent errors (e.g., carnosine's five states vs 150.1 Å² [M + H]+).

name: ccs-prediction-accuracy-evaluation
description: Reference for validating that a CCS prediction model (e.g., a newly trained or user-curated SVR model) reaches the accuracy level expected of published ML predictors before using it to filter metabolite annotations.

name: ccs-prediction-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when comparing the prediction accuracy of multiple CCS prediction tools on the same test sets, or when reproducing reported median MRE/RMSE rankings for [M-H]-, [M+H]+, or [M+Na]+ adducts.

name: ccs-prediction-error-labeling
description: Use when you have per-molecule CCS predictions paired with true experimental CCS values (METLIN-CCS, CCSBase) and need binary error labels to train a confidence model or to evaluate filtered vs unfiltered MAE/MRE.

name: ccs-prediction-model-application
description: Use when an IM-MS lipidomics feature has an m/z and measured drift/collision cross section but no experimental CCS entry exists in the reference database, or when building a predicted lipid database covering fatty acyl chains of 10–30 carbons with 0–6 unsaturations.

name: ccs-prediction-model-evaluation
description: Use when you need to quantify how well a CCS prediction model (e.g. SigmaCCS vs CCSbase) performs on an external test set or a specialized dataset such as plant metabolites, using R2, RMSE, and Median RE metrics.

name: ccs-prediction-via-linear-svr
description: Use when candidate structures retrieved for an IM-MS feature (e.g., PubChem hits within a 10 ppm mass window of an [M-H]- or [M+H]+ precursor) must be filtered or ranked by predicted CCS, or when CCS values must be predicted for user-curated training sets of molecules.

name: ccs-reference-library-matching
description: Use when IM-MS lipidomics data spiked with U13C-labeled yeast internal standards needs CCS quality control: measured TIMCCSN2 or DTIMCCSN2 values must be matched to a DTCCSN2 reference library to quantify per-lipid CCS bias by ionization mode.

name: ccs-reference-value-comparison
description: Use when you have AutoCCS-computed CCS values from two or more calibration methods or IMS platforms and authoritative reference CCS values (e.g. DTIMS-derived or vendor-software values) to validate accuracy per analyte.

name: ccs-threshold-roc-curve-computation
description: Use when evaluating annotation-candidate filtering by predicted-vs-measured CCS, especially when testing whether ROC AUC holds across candidate-list mass windows (10, 7, 5, 3, 1, 0 ppm) or across SVR training-set compositions (chemically diverse vs class-matched).

name: ccs-training-data-preparation
description: Use when building or customizing a CCS prediction training set from McLean CCS Compendium-style records (neutral InChI strings, per-adduct CCS values) before fitting linear SVR models.

name: ccs-training-set-curation
description: Use when you need CCS predictions for an adduct or compound class not covered by CCSP 2.0's shipped models (e.g., [2M+H]+, [2M−H]−, [M+K]+ beyond default coverage, or a specific superclass), and you can assemble experimental CCS values into a curated training table to rebuild the SVR model.

name: ccs-value-mean-absolute-deviation-filtering
description: Use when a CCS training table (e.g. CCSBase parquet/CSV with 'ccs', 'smiles', 'adduct' columns) contains multiple experimental records per SMILES-adduct pair and inconsistent replicate values must be removed before model training.

name: ccs-value-regression-prediction
description: Use when a metabolite annotation list (e.g., PubChem candidates within 10 ppm of an exact mass) needs CCS values predicted for [M-H]-, [M+H]+ or [M+Na]+ adducts to enable ΔCCS-threshold filtering.

name: ccsbase-duplicate-smiles-adduct-grouping
description: Use when preparing CCSBase for CCS-prediction model training and the loaded table contains multiple records sharing the same SMILES and adduct, requiring deduplication driven by a deviation-based consistency threshold.

name: cdk-chemical-descriptor-calculation
description: Use when a compound library (SMILES + experimental retention times, e.g. HILIC MoNA or RPLC RIKEN PlaSMA sets) must be converted into a numeric molecular-descriptor feature table for training or applying retention time prediction models.

name: cdk-descriptor-generation
description: Use when you need to convert SMILES structures of metabolomics compound sets into a CDK descriptor matrix — e.g., for Retip retention-time models or PCA chemical-space overlap checks before training/test validation.

name: cdk-fingerprint-bit-occupancy-filtering
description: Use when training or applying FingerScorer-style SVM fingerprint predictors over a 11416-bit CDK fingerprint space, and you must prune to the 2500 occupied bits before per-bit model training or Jaccard ranking.

name: cdk-molecular-descriptor-feature-generation
description: Use when building a bond-of-metabolism (BoM) or site-of-metabolism classifier from annotated SDF compounds (e.g. EBoMD.sdf) and you need per-bond feature vectors for training/evaluation.

name: cdk-substructure-pattern-matching
description: Use when a query molecule's subgraph fingerprint has already narrowed candidates (e.g. via $allBitsSet on PubChem fingerprints stored as BinData in MongoDB) and you must confirm true substructure isomorphism with CDK pattern matching.

name: cdk-xlogp-descriptor-calculation
description: Use when ranking LC-MS/MS candidate structures where reference standards with measured RTs are available on a reverse-phase column and retention-time plausibility should contribute to MetFrag scoring.

name: cdr-region-assembly-validation
description: Use when de novo peptide predictions have been assembled into antibody contigs (e.g. with ALPS) and you must verify that CDR and variable-region sequences were recovered, not just overall chain coverage.

name: cell-image-segmentation-with-cellprofiler
description: Use when running the SpaceM workflow on MALDI-imaging mass spectrometry data from cultured cells and you need per-cell segmentation of the stitched pre-MALDI microscopy tiles to assign metabolite intensities to individual cells.

name: cell-relative-metabolic-model-flux-sampling-context
description: Use when randomSampling CSVs from multiple cell-relative models (MCF102A, SKBR3, MCF7, MDAMB231, MDAMB361) must be embedded (e.g. t-SNE) to test whether combined constraints better separate cell lines than each constraint type alone.

name: cell-transition-metabolite-association
description: Use when you have longitudinal/high-dimensional metabolomics data (e.g., 1H-NMR concentration tables) spanning sequential cell states and need to extract transition-specific metabolite subnetworks rather than global correlations.

name: cell-type-differential-abundance-testing
description: Use when a samples-by-features LC/MS intensity matrix (raw or batch-corrected) has group labels and the goal is to rank or count metabolomic features that differ between groups at a relaxed FDR threshold such as ≤ 0.2.

name: cell-type-flux-differential-testing
description: Use when per-cell metabolic fluxes have been predicted from scRNA-seq (scFEA) and must be compared across reported cell-type labels (e.g. cancer, myeloid, T cells) to test which population has the highest glucose metabolic rate.

name: cellprofiler-cell-segmentation-pipeline-configuration
description: Use when running the SpaceM pipeline on MALDI-imaging data (*.RAW, *.UDP, *.imzML, *.ibd) plus pre/post-MALDI tiled microscopy, and per-cell segmentation via a CellProfiler pipeline must be configured in paths.json.

name: center-of-mass-peak-merging
description: Use when peak-picking a 2D 13C INADEQUATE NMR spectrum in PyINETA where a single intensity threshold cannot separate overlapping cross-peaks, and nearby picked peaks must be merged before network filtering.

name: central-carbon-metabolite-isotopologue-annotation
description: Use when processing GC-CI-MS isotope-labelling data (e.g. U-13C-glucose or U-13C-arginine cell cultures) to quantify isotopologue distributions of glycolytic and TCA cycle metabolites across LRMS and HRMS acquisitions.

name: central-pathway-classification-counting
description: Use when comparing hyperlink prediction models (e.g., NetAurHPD vs CHESHIRE) on metabolic pathway classification and you must report survival-critical central-pathway recovery, not just AUC.

name: central-versus-peripheral-metabolite-classification
description: Use when interpreting ML predictor features for a metabolite and you must determine whether that metabolite is in central vs peripheral metabolism based on topological proximity of predictors to its reactions in Recon3D.

name: centroid-peak-count-filtering
description: Use when building qualified MS/MS test datasets from raw HMDB/GNPS/CASMI spectra and you must enforce element-composition, mass (<1500 Da), precursor-type, and minimum-centroid-peak (>=3) inclusion rules before formula ranking.

name: centroid-peak-merging-mass-accuracy
description: Use when building an isotopic profile database (IPDB) from a molecular formula list so that only centroid-level theoretical peaks are queried against experimental MS1 LC/HRMS peaklists.

name: centroided-ms-data-import
description: Use when centroided LC/MS raw data files (.mzML or .mzXML) from an untargeted HPLC-HRMS/MS experiment must be imported into Metaboseek prior to XCMS feature detection and alignment.

name: centroided-mzml-preprocessing
description: Use when starting from converted centroided mzML files plus experiment metadata (sample names mapped to file paths) and raw LC-MS data must be turned into m/z/RT-annotated feature tables before QC or annotation.

name: centroided-spectrum-format-validation
description: Use when raw instrument-specific mass-spectrometry files (e.g. from Agilent MassHunter, Thermo Xcalibur, AB SCIEX, Bruker, Waters MassLynx, Shimadzu) must be converted to an open format for GNPS molecular networking.

name: centroided-spectrum-preprocessing
description: Use when MS/MS peaks are already centroided and normalized (sum = 1) and a low-entropy, ion-poor spectrum (S < 3) needs intensity re-weighting prior to entropy similarity or library matching.

name: centroided-spectrum-variant-generation
description: Use when you have raw profile-mode MGF spectra from the Spectraverse deposit and need to quantify, via AUROC of cosine similarity, whether centroiding degrades same-vs-different compound discrimination before deciding whether to include a centroiding filter in a preprocessing pipeline.

name: centwave-feature-detection-lcms
description: Use when starting from raw LC–MS files (e.g., mzML) from untargeted metabolomics acquisitions and you need feature detection — peak picking, deisotoping, adduct grouping — to build the extracted data matrix that subsequent curation filters will operate on.

name: centwave-parameter-aggregation
description: Use when AutoTuner peak detection has produced per-peak parameter estimates across raw metabolomics samples (mzML, mzXML, CDF) and they must be reduced to one dataset-wide centWave parameter vector.

name: centwave-parameter-estimation-from-raw-scan-data
description: Use when raw untargeted metabolomics data (mzML, mzXML, or CDF from qTOF, orbitrap, or FT-ICR analyzers) must be processed with XCMS/MZmine2 centWave and dataset-specific peak-picking parameters must be estimated in one pass rather than by iteratively testing parameter combinations.

name: centwave-peak-detection-parameterization
description: Use when starting an untargeted metabolomics workflow from raw MS files and the XCMS/MZmine2 centWave parameters (peakwidth, ppm, snthresh, noise, mzdiff, etc.) have not yet been tuned for this dataset.

name: centwave-peak-picking-parameterization
description: Use when raw LC-HRMS data (mzXML from e.g. Bruker Impact II UHR-QqTOF runs) must be converted into a feature table, and the analysis relies on XCMS 3.11.4+ centWave feature detection feeding downstream rescue or annotation steps.

name: ceramide-nomenclature-mapping
description: Use when lipid molecule name strings (e.g. from Metabolomics Workbench study ST001111 or Skyline exports) need class/chain-length/double-bond annotations, or when full-chemical-name ceramide entries fail name parsing and must be mapped to shorthand notation.

name: cerebellum-tissue-region-classification
description: Use when you have a TIC-normalised, lipid-annotated MSI pixel matrix (e.g. massPix image.norm.csv) and need to segment pixels of high spectral similarity into anatomical tissue regions and extract their average spectra.

name: certified-feature-list-matching
description: Use when benchmarking feature detection of LC-MS processing tools on datasets with known ground truth, e.g. HZV029 (402 Thermo-verified features), Yeast2021 (314 certified features), or E. coli (643 certified features).

name: ceumass-restful-querying
description: Use when a task needs compound records from CMM 3.0 via its RESTful API, or when verifying that newly added taxonomy and ontology metadata fields are present and populated for a set of queried metabolites.

name: cf-ratio-distribution-interpretation
description: Use when diagnosing why FSA rank-1 formula accuracy differs across datasets by comparing spectral-feature distributions (fragment count, peak-distance SD, CF ratio, top-2 score gap) between R1 and R2+ assignments.

name: cfm-id-in-silico-spectrum-prediction
description: Use when benchmarking modification-site-localization on analog pairs: candidate analog structures are available (e.g. via substructure permutation), each has a known formula, and an empirical MS2 spectrum of the unknown compound is available for cosine scoring.

name: cfm-id-spectral-prediction-scoring
