description: Use when ranking candidate compounds for Orbitrap HR-MS/MS spectra by fragmentation-only scoring (no reference or retention terms), particularly when comparing in silico fragmenters or when MetFrag's bond-dissociation scoring alone underperforms.

name: chain-extension-with-ppm-and-rt-tolerances
description: Use when an LC-MS peak table (mz/rt/intensity) must be annotated with homologue series by seeding 2-tuples from root peaks and extending chains under an m/z increment, 5 ppm tolerance, and 1–100 s rt constraints (targeted mz_steps like 44.02628 or untargeted 10–20 Da).

name: chain-length-enrichment-visualization
description: Use when a lipidr differential analysis (e.g. two-group Cancer vs Benign contrast) has been ranked by logFC and you need to render and save enrichment plots for chain-length or class lipid sets.

name: character-trigram-tfidf-vectorization
description: Use when user-submitted freetext sample metadata strings must be mapped onto terms of a constrained, non-overlapping vocabulary (e.g., MeSH, NCBI Taxonomy, Cellosaurus, NCIT, FDA) via character n-gram similarity.

name: characteristic-fragment-determination
description: Use when ranking precursor chemical formula candidates from LC-MS/MS fragment peaks and you need to flag fragments whose mass-difference relationships are unique to each candidate formula set, per the FSA algorithm.

name: charge-neutralization-rule-handling
description: Use when a spectral library (MGF/CSV with a SMILES field) contains charged or zwitterionic molecules that must be neutralized with rule-based RDKit transforms, and net-charge changes require duplicating spectra as charged and uncharged forms.

name: charge-normalized-mass-difference-computation
description: Use when comparing a modified query spectrum to an unmodified library spectrum and the precursor m/z difference must be converted into a neutral mass delta (charge-normalized) to derive candidate modification-induced peak shifts.

name: charge-normalized-precursor-mass-difference-calculation
description: Use when analyzing open-search SSM results where modified peptide matches must be grouped by their precursor mass shift to enable per-group target–decoy FDR estimation, especially when deciding whether each subgroup is large enough (≥20 SSMs) to support separate FDR filtering.

name: charge-state-deduction-from-mz-spacing
description: Use when you need to label which LC/MS peaks in a grouped compound spectrum (pseudospectrum) are isotope peaks and deduce the charge state z from their 1.0033/z spacing, e.g. on an xsAnnotate object before adduct annotation.

name: charge-state-enumeration-peak-matching
description: Use when a monoisotopic theoretical glycan mass must be matched to an observed MS1 peak in an mzXML extract-ion chromatogram across several charge states within a ppm tolerance.

name: charge-state-inference-from-isotope-spacing
description: Use when an LC-MS untargeted metabolomics feature table (m/z, RT, intensities per sample) contains isotope peaks that must be collapsed into isotope fingerprints and charged species inferred before probabilistic annotation.

name: charged-ion-species-annotation
description: Use when expanding a small-molecule annotation database for LC-HRMS adductomics: each drawn structure needs charged monoisotopic masses for detectable ion species and standardized identifiers (SMILES, InChI, InChIKey).

name: checkpoint-based-model-inference
description: Use when a task requires reproducing reported de novo generation metrics (NPLIB1 top-1 accuracy 8.34%, MassSpecGym 2.30%) from pretrained DiffMS weights rather than training from scratch, given processed NPLIB1/MassSpecGym test spectra.

name: chembl-bioactivity-annotation-retrieval
description: Use when confident structural annotations from LC-MS/MS metabolomics (e.g., ISDB/SIRIUS annotations in an RDF knowledge graph) must be connected to reported bioactivities in ChEMBL to rank analogs of known actives.

name: chembl-bioactivity-metadata-linking
description: Use when a bioactive natural extract's annotated features should be prioritized by checking whether known structures in the KG already have reported activity against the screened organism, e.g. anti-T. cruzi quinoline alkaloids in Waltheria indica extracts.

name: chemical-annotation-matrix-construction
description: Use when the goal is a repository-scale, file-level chemical annotation table (e.g., compound presence/absence across thousands of public MS/MS files) built from ReDU/GNPS library search output rather than from raw spectra.

name: chemical-annotation-matrix-pca-analysis
description: Use when you have a file-by-chemical annotation table (GNPS spectral library matches per MassIVE file) and want to reproduce ReDU's repository-scale, unsupervised PCA ordination of public tandem MS files.

name: chemical-annotation-retrieval
description: Use when you need programmatic access to PubChem's chemical annotations or summary information (e.g., LCSS, solubility, experimental properties) for a single record, and PUG-REST is unsuitable for such annotation data.

name: chemical-attribute-retrieval-from-databases
description: Use when a merged metabolite table keyed on InChIKeys lacks attributes such as CID, SMILES, RefMet name, HMDB/KEGG/ChEBI IDs, or chemical ontology and must be enriched before interstudy comparison.

name: chemical-attribute-retrieval-via-rest-api
description: Use when a merged metabolite dataset already carries InChIKeys (output of MMS Step 1) and you need per-metabolite chemical properties and cross-database identifiers to enable interstudy comparability.

name: chemical-attribute-serialisation
description: Use when a ViMMS 2.0 workflow has just sampled a synthetic chemical mixture (e.g. via ChemicalMixtureCreator with HMDB-backed or uniform m/z formula samplers) and the sampled chemical attributes need to be persisted for simulation, replay or ground-truth comparison.

name: chemical-candidate-dereplication-and-platt-reranking
description: Use when you have generated k candidate SMILES from MSNovelist's RNN decoder for a tandem mass spectrum and need to deduplicate, validate, and rank them to pick the top de novo structure.

name: chemical-chemical-interaction-network-construction
description: Use when a set of significant metabolites (e.g. fold change ≥1, adjusted p < 0.05) needs to be interpreted structurally as an interaction network, to identify hub metabolites and compare topology against a published network figure.

name: chemical-chromatogram-perturbation
description: Use when a simulated chemical dataset (pickled Chemical objects from ChemicalMixtureCreator) must be perturbed with reproducible RT offsets, systematic RT drift across successive injections, and random RT/intensity noise prior to fragmentation-strategy simulation.

name: chemical-class-annotation-aggregation
description: Use when you have a final merged MAW candidates table (file_id_mergedResults-with-one-Candidates.csv) with CANOPUS/ClassyFire class assignments per feature and need to summarize which chemical classes and subclasses dominate the annotated features.

name: chemical-class-based-link-filtering
description: Use when a genome–metabolome pairing workflow yields long candidate lists of GCF–spectrum links (e.g. from Metcalf scoring) and class-ontology annotations (CANOPUS/MolNetEnhancer for spectra, MIBiG-derived classes for BGCs) are available to prune unlikely matches.

name: chemical-class-based-metabolite-grouping
description: Use when a metabolomics/lipidomics feature table contains redundant or chemically related features (e.g. correlated isomers, shared chemical class) that should be collapsed into single nodes prior to DNEA network construction.

name: chemical-class-dictionary-term-mapping
description: Use when ClassyFire/ChemOnt category assignments must be translated into another chemical ontology (ChEBI classes, MeSH headings) for cross-database comparison or annotation exchange.

name: chemical-class-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when an IDSL.CSA-aligned compound matrix annotated with InChIKey/SMILES/molecular formula meta-variables must be clustered into chemical families and statistically tested for class-level abundance differences between two sample groups (e.g. Crohn's vs healthy controls).

name: chemical-class-enrichment-statistics
description: Use when a batch of MS/MS spectra (e.g. .mgf exports from HILIC- or CSH-Q Exactive HF runs) has been assigned putative compound names at MSI level 3 and you need chemical-ontology class distributions or enrichment statistics rather than single-compound IDs.

name: chemical-class-fraction-quantification
description: Use when you have a list of metabolites identified by NMR (Chenomx) or similar profiling and need to report the chemical-class composition as fractions/percentages of the total detected metabolome.

name: chemical-class-grouping-analysis
description: Use when an aligned annotated molecular formula table (from IDSL.UFA) contains many related formulas and the goal is to collapse them into homologous formula-class clusters (e.g., perfluorinated, halogenated, or lipid chain families) rather than treating each peak independently.

name: chemical-class-novelty-scoring
description: Decision support for prioritizing natural extracts whose MS/MS-derived chemical taxonomy (CANOPUS/NPC classes) contains classes absent from literature reports for the same species or genus, as one of four components in Inventa's Priority Score ranking.

name: chemical-class-ontology-lookup-scoring
description: Use when NPLinker has produced candidate BGC–MS/MS spectrum links (e.g., via standardised Metcalf scoring) and you need to filter false positives by matching genome-based and structure-based chemical class ontologies.

name: chemical-class-propagation-onto-networks
description: Use when a GNPS molecular network plus an MS2LDA experiment exist and molecular families lack GNPS spectral library matches, so NAP/DEREPLICATOR annotations and ClassyFire classes can be propagated onto nodes/edges to reach MSI annotation level 3.

name: chemical-class-set-comparison-across-taxonomic-levels
description: Use when you have a canopus_npc_summary.tsv from a recomputed SIRIUS project space plus taxon-level reported-class tables and want to flag extracts whose predicted chemical classes are novel to the species or genus.

name: chemical-class-taxonomy-integration
description: Use when a GNPS molecular network (classical or feature-based) needs chemically interpretable node annotation — e.g., nodes colored by CF_subclass in Cytoscape — after spectral library/in silico annotation steps are complete.

name: chemical-class-term-curation
description: Reference for constructing or auditing a chemical classification dictionary — when you must choose preferred labels and synonyms for chemical classes (e.g. resolving 'Imidazolines' vs 'Dihydroimidazoles') rather than classify individual structures.

name: chemical-classification-benchmark-reporting
description: Use when an article reports compound-classification counts per database (e.g. '>60,000,000 molecules in PubChem') and these per-database thresholds must be compiled into a verifiable table or CSV without converting them to exact figures.

name: chemical-compound-metadata-extraction
description: Use when you need to enumerate the compound library of a PeakForest instance (e.g. a MetaboHUB demonstrator) and extract per-compound metadata into a flat table for inventory, curation, or downstream annotation reuse.

name: chemical-compound-record-field-validation
description: Use when batch-importing large compound lists into PeakForest from the compound-import template file (XLSX, Online Resource 2) and each row must be checked for the mandatory common name, InChI and InChIKey fields before creating compound cards.

name: chemical-database-candidate-selection
description: Use when running VInSMoC on run.npanalysis.org and you must pick which chemical database to search against, or associate an uploaded spectrum file with a project so it can serve as input to a database-search task.

name: chemical-database-crosslink-counting
description: Use when a database release claims compound structure coverage (e.g. '1188 structures with SMILES', '1347→1860 BGCs with structure data') and you need to reproduce those counts and per-database cross-link tallies.

name: chemical-database-curation
description: Use when curating or auditing a natural product database where each BGC record has an associated product structure (e.g. MIBiG/PubChem links), and you need to detect entries whose linked SMILES/structure mismatches the biosynthetically predicted product.

name: chemical-database-curation-audit
description: Use when reproducing or verifying aggregate counts of a curated chemical database assembled from multiple public sources, or when reconciling per-source entry totals against published unique-molecule statistics after deduplication.

name: chemical-database-field-completeness-checking
description: Use when a curated chemical/adduct database is distributed as structure files (.mol/.cdxml) plus a spreadsheet, and you must verify identifier columns are populated and reproducible entry-by-entry.

name: chemical-database-search-configuration
description: Use when raw mass spectra (MGF, mzXML, or mzML) must be searched against a candidate chemical database (e.g., NPAtlas, COCONUT, PubChem) and the VInSMoC task parameters need to be set to match the input spectra's ion mode, precursor m/z, and expected adducts.

name: chemical-database-structure-retrieval
description: Use when a predicted Morgan fingerprint bit string from an HSQC spectrum (DeepSAT output) is available and candidates must be retrieved, ranked, and annotated against known-molecule fingerprint databases.

name: chemical-dataset-record-counting
description: Use when a deposited .sdf dataset must be audited to confirm its record counts match published per-category totals, especially when annotations need deduplication or category classification.

name: chemical-decontamination-filtering
description: Use when extracting component areas from a spreadOut()-processed GC-MS hit table and you must purge chemicals that lack strong cross-sample library matches, PubChem records, or canonical SMILES before downstream standardization.

name: chemical-descriptor-importance-extraction
description: Use when a fitted retention time prediction model (e.g. Retip Keras on HILIC or RPLC) needs interpretation: which molecular descriptors most strongly predict RT, with percentage importance weights.

name: chemical-dropout-probability-sampling
description: Use when you need synthetic chemical datasets for multiple samples (e.g. control vs case groups) where each chemical is present in only a subset of samples according to a configurable dropout rate.

name: chemical-element-frequency-filtering
description: Use when curating McLean CCS Compendium training data for [M-H]-, [M+H]+ or [M+Na]+ adducts and entries containing rare chemical elements (fewer than five occurrences in the database) must be excluded before model training.

name: chemical-formula-accuracy-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking formula-prediction methods on CASMI 2016/2017 or EMBL-MCF 2.0 spectra and you need comparable top-1/top-5 accuracy per tool and ion mode after excluding training-set overlaps.

name: chemical-formula-constraint-filtering
description: Use when generating or filtering de novo formula candidates from MS1 precursor masses and you need to know which element-count restrictions are acceptable, or when auditing what fraction of a reference formula set survives candidate-space pruning.

name: chemical-formula-count-parsing
description: Use when featurizing a chemical formula candidate (e.g. a precursor formula from MIST-CF/SIRIUS decomposition) into a fixed-length numerical vector for a neural network, or when reproducing MIST-CF's count-based formula encoder.

name: chemical-formula-prediction-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking a de novo chemical formula predictor on MS/MS spectra (e.g., NPLIB1 test set) and you need reproducible top-1 accuracy values, especially as a function of how many MS2 peaks are visible to the model.

name: chemical-formula-prediction-from-tandem-ms
description: Use when you have MS/MS spectra (MGF with title, precursor_mz, precursor_type, collision_energy) from Q-TOF or Orbitrap instruments and need candidate molecular formulas ranked by confidence.

name: chemical-formula-stoichiometry-parsing
description: Use when the input is a metabolite with a known chemical formula and the goal is a theoretical isotopic envelope (M, M+1, M+2, ...) under natural or SIP-enriched abundances.

name: chemical-graph-parsing-and-featurization
description: Use when a task requires converting molecular structures (SMILES/MolBlock/SDF from spectral libraries like NIST20) into molecular graphs and heavy-atom-only skeletons H(G) as input to bond-breaking fragmentation or GNN featurization.

name: chemical-hierarchy-construction-from-fingerprints
description: Use when you have a feature table plus MS/MS spectra (MGF) from LC-MS/MS feature detection (e.g. MZmine2/GNPS) and want a fingerprint-based chemical tree for UniFrac-type sample comparison or cross-dataset merging without re-alignment.

name: chemical-identifier-conversion-annotation
description: Use when a .msp mass spectral library file contains records with incomplete metadata (e.g. missing SMILES, InChI, or CAS numbers) and known identifiers that can be converted via public chemical web services.

name: chemical-identifier-format-validation
description: Use when a mass spectral library file has been annotated with externally fetched metadata (e.g. via MSMetaEnhancer services CIR, CTS, IDSM, PubChem, BridgeDb) and you must check each InChI, InChIKey, SMILES, or CAS attribute for well-formedness before downstream use.

name: chemical-identifier-reconciliation
description: Use when converting a curated tabular natural-products dataset (structure, organism, reference columns) into Wikidata entries and you must determine which entities already exist before writing.

name: chemical-identifier-standardization-smiles-inchi
description: Use when integrating heterogeneous OMSL entries (.MSP, .MGF, .JSON, .CSV) whose SMILES/InChI/InChIKey fields are inconsistent, missing, or nonstandard and must be normalized with RDKit before annotation workflows.

name: chemical-identity-subsetting
description: Use when you have a categorate() output from uafR and need to reduce a compound list to those matching explicit database, structural, or library-group criteria before downstream GC-MS extraction.

name: chemical-language-model-sampling
description: Use when you have one or more trained RNN/CLM checkpoints and need to generate a ranked database of candidate chemical structures (with calculated mass, formula, and InChIKey) whose sampling frequency can prioritize metabolites for discovery.

name: chemical-library-categorization-flagging
description: Use when you have a list of tentative compound names (or PubChem CIDs) from GC-MS peak picking and need categorical/functional annotation plus structural matches against labeled chemical categories.

name: chemical-list-serialization-pickle
description: Use when a chemical list extracted from an mzML file (e.g. Beer_multibeers_1_T10_POS.mzML) or sampled synthetically must be persisted between ViMMS runs so controllers and the Environment can consume it as an alternative chemical source.

name: chemical-mixture-configuration
description: Use when you need to produce synthetic chemical datasets (m/z, RT, intensity, formula) for ViMMS 2.0 simulations, either sampled from a database like HMDB or over a uniform m/z range.

name: chemical-noise-sampling-from-formula-db
description: Use when benchmarking an MS/MS denoising or spectral-matching algorithm's robustness by deliberately contaminating clean spectra with chemically plausible synthetic noise ions whose intensity can far exceed true fragment ions.

name: chemical-nomenclature-synonym-mapping
description: Reference for constructing a synonym table for a chemical taxonomy, especially when resolving competing class names and cross-ontology mappings (ChEBI, LIPID MAPS, MeSH) for classification text.

name: chemical-object-serialisation
description: Use when a workflow must persist, reload or hand off ViMMS Chemical objects between pipeline stages — e.g. a chemical mixture generated by ChemicalMixtureCreator needs to be saved as a .p/.pkl file, or a saved chemical dataset is the input to noise/RT-drift perturbation modules.

name: chemical-occurrence-record-deduplication
description: Use when a deposited, curated natural-products occurrence table (e.g. LOTUS 3_curated/table.tsv.gz from Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.5607264) must be tallied for unique structure-organism pairs to validate a reported figure such as 750,000+ pairs.

name: chemical-ontology-coverage-quantification
description: Decision support for measuring the fraction of a compound collection (e.g. PubChem's >91 million compounds as of June 2016) classified under a manually maintained chemical ontology such as MeSH, when arguing for automated classification.

name: chemical-prioritization-overlap-analysis
description: Use when two chemical prioritization rankings (e.g., RI vs PrHQ) cover overlapping chemical sets and you need to quantify agreement between their orderings via rank correlation and overlap extraction.

name: chemical-priority-ranking
description: Use when you have human exposure estimates and predicted toxicity (e.g., oral LD50) for a chemical set and need a ranked risk prioritization spanning many orders of magnitude.

name: chemical-record-identifier-mapping
description: Use when a task needs the complete annotation/summary content for one specific PubChem record (e.g. Compound Summary for a CID) via programmatic access, and the record can be named by a single CID, SID, or AID.

name: chemical-safety-qr-linking
description: Use when you need programmatic SVG QR codes linking a compound (CID) to its PubChem safety summary, or to retrieve biologic depiction images and annotation attachments via PUG-View special reports.

name: chemical-shift-axis-partitioning
description: Use when preprocessed, window-selected 1H-NMR spectra (spectra_df) still contain residual peak shifts and must be reduced to a lower-dimensional bucketed feature table before multivariate statistical analysis.

name: chemical-shift-calibration-and-alignment
description: Use when 1D 1H NMR metabolomics spectra show uncontrolled chemical-shift variations between spectra that must be calibrated and realigned before binning or statistical analysis.

name: chemical-shift-deviation-computation
description: Use when you have paired experimental NMR mixture spectra and pure-component reference spectra and need to quantify how far identical peaks shift (ppm) between mixture and reference before applying shift-tolerant identification.

name: chemical-shift-roi-matching
description: Use when user-defined 1H NMR ROIs (e.g., 18 ROIs over 0.5-4.5 ppm) must be screened against a reference metabolite library to list every metabolite with at least one chemical shift peak inside each ROI.

name: chemical-shift-table-extraction
description: Use when a task requires per-atom assigned chemical shifts (residue, atom name, shift value) from a BMRB macromolecule or metabolomics entry, or when building CSV/NEF tables from NMR-STAR files.

name: chemical-shift-variation-simulation
description: Use when you need to verify that a spectral mixture-identification model is robust to chemical shift variation, by generating shifted spectral pairs and mapping the shift interval over which predictions stay above a threshold (here 0.5).

name: chemical-similarity-cutoff-filtering
description: Use when running a Pickaxe/MINE-Database reaction-rule expansion that explodes in compound counts and you want to bias the network toward chemical space near defined target structures via a hard Tanimoto cutoff.

name: chemical-similarity-network-edge-filtering
description: Use when you need to connect metabolites lacking known biochemical intermediates via structural similarity: identifiers (names, KEGG, HMDB, InChIKey) must be converted to PubChem CIDs, fingerprints compared by Tanimoto coefficient, and edges filtered at a specified cutoff.

name: chemical-similarity-network-generation
description: Use when you have TOCSY/HSQC spectra for a sample set (e.g., prefractionated extract library) and need to cluster samples by shared structural features to dereplicate known scaffolds or locate bioactivity hotspots.

name: chemical-similarity-scoring
description: Use when sample-level NMR feature tables (spin systems with 1H/13C shifts) from multiple samples must be compared to build a similarity matrix for network generation or dereplication.

name: chemical-space-boundary-definition
description: Use when you need a database-independent molecular formula candidate space for untargeted LC/HRMS annotation (e.g., exposomics compounds absent from metabolite databases) and must constrain which elemental compositions are enumerated before building a theoretical isotopic profile database (IPDB).

name: chemical-space-coverage-comparison
description: Use when you have multiple MGF-format spectral libraries with SMILES structure annotations and need a visual, structure-based comparison of which library spans more chemical space.

name: chemical-space-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when you need to visually compare the structural diversity or chemical-space coverage of multiple compound libraries (e.g., OMSLs vs. natural-product catalogues) by embedding a fixed molecular fingerprint representation into 2-D with t-SNE.

name: chemical-standardization-inchikey-resolution
description: Use when a user-supplied table of compound names (with aggregate p-value/fold-change statistics) contains naming synonyms or ambiguous identifiers that must be harmonized to a single identifier scheme before meta-analysis.

name: chemical-structural-feature-extraction
description: Use when you have standardized chemical structures (SMILES/Molfile) and need machine-readable structural features — functional groups, ring counts, heteroatom composition, property constraints — to drive rule-based category assignment.

name: chemical-structure-annotation-coverage-analysis
description: Use when auditing a curated BGC or compound database (e.g. MIBiG JSON entries) before/after a re-curation release, to quantify entries lacking product chemical structures and entries with incomplete property annotations.

name: chemical-structure-classification
description: Use when a GNPS molecular network's nodes have structure annotations (GNPS library hits, NAP or DEREPLICATOR outputs with SMILES) and you need per-molecular-family chemical class scores at each ClassyFire ontology level.

name: chemical-structure-correspondence-curation
description: Use when a curated BGC entry carries compound name and chemical structure metadata and you need to inventory which external chemical resources (PubChem, Natural Products Atlas, GNPS) hold a corresponding cross-link for that entry.

name: chemical-structure-curation-flagging
description: Use when a chemical structure dataset (e.g. MIBiG JSON entries with compound SMILES and substrate SMILES fields) needs syntax-level correctness checking before downstream ML training or database release.

name: chemical-structure-format-conversion
description: Use when editable ChemDraw .cdxml structure records (e.g., DNA adducts drawn with unspecified modification positions) must be converted to .mol files and standard identifiers (SMILES, InChI, InChIKey) for a chemical database.

name: chemical-structure-identifier-extraction
description: Use when building or extending a small-molecule/chemical database where each entry needs machine-readable structure identifiers (.mol, .cdxml, SMILES, InChI, InChIKey) before spectral prediction or search.

name: chemical-structure-readability-evaluation
description: Use when a tool renders many predicted biosynthetic cluster diagrams (PKS, NRPS, or hybrid 'spaghetti diagrams') and you must quantify how many are structurally correct and visually legible.

name: chemical-structure-similarity-calculation
description: Use when building a weighted molecular network for annotation propagation and you need edge weights that blend MetFrag candidate scores, spectral cosine similarity and structural similarity of candidate compounds.
tools: GNPS (Global Natural Products Social Molecular Networking)

name: chemical-structure-substructure-descriptor-extraction
description: Use when tentative GC-MS compound names (e.g. from Unknowns Analysis output with a Match.Factor column) need substructure descriptors or Tanimoto structural matching against a user-defined chemical category library.

name: chemical-subformula-enumeration
description: Use when training or scoring RASSP models that need a candidate set of fragment subformulae and atom subsets for a small molecule (≤48 atoms, HCONFSPCl only), or when reproducing the RASSP featurization pipeline that converts molecules into graph, subformula, and spectra tensors.

name: chemical-superclass-annotation
description: Use when you have MS/MS spectra with InChIKey annotations and 2D embeddings (e.g., t-SNE or UMAP of MS2DeepScore vectors) and need to check whether the projection groups spectra by chemical (super)class.

name: chemical-superclass-classification-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating a chemical structure-class classifier (e.g., DeepSAT on HSQC spectra) and you need per-superclass F1-scores to identify the lowest-performing NPClassifier structure classes and their causes.

name: chemical-target-annotation-extraction
description: Use when you need compound-level bioactivity and molecular-target coverage statistics from MIBiG JSON entries, e.g. to reproduce the 1002-compound / 51-bioactivity / 95-target annotation table.

name: chemical-taxonomy-assignment
description: Use when a merged Qemistree feature-data artifact already carries structures (ms2_smiles and/or csi_smiles) and you need ClassyFire chemical ontology labels per molecule to color tree subtrees, check class-level sample patterns, or compute class annotation coverage.

name: chemical-taxonomy-hierarchy-aggregation
description: Use when a structure list (e.g. SMILES tagged by organism origin) must be classified with NPClassifier and summarized into per-pathway or per-superclass counts to compare chemical space across organism groups.

name: chemical-taxonomy-hierarchy-construction
description: Use when building or reconstructing a hierarchical chemical ontology from structural classification rules — e.g. assembling the ChemOnt tree from SMARTS/Markush rules into an OBO file with parent 'is_a' links.

name: chemical-tree-construction
description: Use when untargeted LC-MS/MS features have predicted molecular fingerprints (e.g., from SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID on MZmine2 MGF output) and you need a chemical hierarchy for downstream tree-based analyses like UniFrac or Faith's phylogenetic diversity.

name: cheminformatics-adduct-mass-correction
description: Use when raw MS/MS peak lists contain m/z values of adducted ions (e.g. [M+H]+, [M-H]-) that must be converted to monoisotopic neutral Da before fragment formula matching or precursor mass comparison.

name: cheminformatics-bond-feature-generation
description: Use when building or reproducing a bond-of-metabolism (BoM) or site-of-metabolism predictor that requires numeric features per [compound, bond] instance from SDF/SMILES structures, following the CypBoM/CDK feature scheme.

name: cheminformatics-candidate-ranking
description: Use when an untargeted MS2 feature (mzML) has a shortlist of putative candidates from spectral/compound database dereplication and one final prioritized structure per feature is needed.

name: cheminformatics-candidate-structure-selection
description: Use when a candidate list per LC-MS/MS feature exists from spectral and compound database dereplication and one structure per feature must be prioritized via structural scoring (e.g. Tanimoto similarity on SMILES) in Python.

name: cheminformatics-feature-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when a descriptor/fingerprint feature matrix (e.g., alvaDesc output on SMRT molecules) must be reduced before training RT prediction regressors and pairwise feature correlation may exceed 0.9.

name: cheminformatics-fingerprint-generation
description: Use when a compound database must be featurized into fingerprint vectors for ChemDistiller's FingerScorer SVM — e.g. reproducing the metabolite-likeness classifier or rebuilding/repackaging an HDF5 compound database.

name: cheminformatics-structure-parsing
description: Use when a dataset contains SMILES strings for small molecules or enzyme substrate structures (e.g. JSON curation entries) and you must confirm each string parses as syntactically correct before downstream use or database release.

name: cheminformatics-structure-standardization
description: Use when aggregating small-molecule structures from heterogeneous sources (SDF, SMILES, csv/tsv) and you need consistent curation rules plus deduplication into unique entries keyed on InChI keys.

name: cheminformatics-substructure-editing
description: Use when generating metabolite structures by applying a SMIRKS reaction rule to the substructure of a substrate identified by predicted reactive bond pairs (BoM pairs), then merging the product back onto the parent scaffold.

name: chemistry-dashboard-metadata-joining
description: Use when a compiled chemical list (e.g. CASRN-indexed exposome entries) needs chemical names, synonyms, and structural identifiers such as canonical SMILES and InChIKey attached from the U.S. EPA Chemistry Dashboard.

name: chemodiversity-metric-computation
description: Use when you have a processed FT-ICR MS peak table with assigned molecular formulas and need per-sample diversity metrics (Shannon, Gini-Simpson, Chao1, Rao's Q) grouped by experimental variables.

name: chemont-category-description-generation
description: Use when a taxonomy of chemical classes needs human-readable English descriptions derived from computable structural definitions (SMARTS, Markush, physico-chemical constraints) rather than free-text curation.

name: chemont-hierarchy-consensus-annotation
description: Use when you have GNPS feature-based molecular networking output (Node_info.tsv, spectral library matches) plus CANOPUS in silico class predictions (canopus_summary.tsv) and need to annotate ion features lacking library hits via subnetwork consensus.

name: chemont-hierarchy-mapping
description: Use when top-ranked per-feature annotations (e.g. from MAW's mergedResults-with-one-Candidates.csv) carry CANOPUS/ClassyFire class strings that must be rolled up into ChemOnt superclass/class/subclass proportions.

name: chemont-ontology-level-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether a consensus annotation workflow assigns correct chemical classes at superclass, class, and subclass levels of the ChemOnt ontology, e.g. validating ConCISE output against GNPS-reported identities on MassIVE datasets.

name: chemont-ontology-superclass-summarization
description: Use when a GNPS FBMN task has ConCISE consensus annotations with ChemOnt superclass labels and you need organism- or group-level compositional summaries (e.g., which structural classes dominate which exudates) rather than compound-level IDs.

name: chemont-taxonomy-category-reduction
description: Use when a compound's detected structural features have been mapped to ChemOnt categories and you must prune redundant ancestor categories before picking the direct parent in a ClassyFire-style pipeline.

name: chemotaxonomic-distribution-analysis
description: Use when annotated molecular network nodes (with CF_superclass/class/subclass labels) must be summarized per taxon or clade, e.g. contrasting metabolite classes between plant clades or bacterial groups.

name: chemotion-eln-attachment-storage
description: Use when a host application or pipeline must store processed spectra per the Chemotion ELN contract: one original byte-preserving artifact plus a server-composed edited version and generated png per upload.

name: chemspider-reference-count-retrieval
description: Use when ranking MetFrag2.2 candidate structures needs non-spectral evidence: ChemSpider reference/data-source/patent counts per candidate must be fetched via web services and normalized across the candidate list.

name: chi-square-significance-testing
description: Use when tabulating binary found/missing outcomes (e.g., 134 of 187 experimentally characterized reactions present in RetroRules via MEANtools) and you must test if the presence rate exceeds chance (χ2, DF = 1).

name: chi-square-significance-testing
description: Use when a linear mixed-effects model has been fitted per metabolite (e.g. with fixed effects 'Sex','Age','BMI','Stage','Location','Tissue' and random intercept '(1|Id)') and you need chi-square p-values for fixed-effect terms such as a VAT-vs-SAT tissue effect.

name: chi-square-tail-probability-evaluation
description: Use when a kernel machine score statistic's null distribution is approximated by moment matching and the final deliverable is an upper-tail chi-square p-value per pathway.

name: chimeric-spectrum-cofragmentation-quantification
description: Use when you have a SMITER-simulated mzML with known precursor peptides and overlapping retention times and need to predict how many peptides co-fragment into each MS2 spectrum before running a real MS experiment.

name: chip-chip-data-clustering
description: Use when integrating a discretised ChIP-chip regulator-gene matrix with another omic dataset (e.g. yeast time-course expression) and you need a per-dataset kernel for multiple-kernel integrative clustering with KLIC.

name: chisquare-significance-testing
description: Use when you have a finite set of characterized substrate/product structures and a reference database (e.g., LOTUS), and you must report how many structures are present plus the statistical significance of that overlap.

name: chokepoint-computation-genome-scale-models
description: Use when the goal is to identify potential drug targets in an SBML genome-scale metabolic model by computing chokepoint reactions whose flux bounds and dead-end-metabolite status have been refined via FVA.

name: chokepoint-essential-reaction-intersection-analysis
description: Use when you have an integrated host–pathogen genome-scale metabolic model plus experimental PPI data (e.g. Gordon et al 2020 SARS-CoV-2 PPIs) and need to pinpoint which host metabolic reactions hijacked via PPIs are also network bottlenecks or essential for viral growth.

name: chokepoint-pipeline-model-preprocessing
description: Use when a steady-state SBML metabolic model (e.g. iHsaEC21_SARS-CoV-2, MODEL2007210001) must be refined before chokepoint or bottleneck analysis: flux bounds need updating from FVA, dead-end metabolites must be excluded, or reaction reversibility must be determined from flux ranges.

name: cholesterol-fraction-computation
description: Use when you have a post-QC NMR biomarker table (output of remove_technical_variation()) filtered to the 107 non-derived biomarkers and need to derive the 76 additional ratios of biological significance, including cholesterol fractions.

name: chromatogram-aird-compression
description: Use when a workflow needs to shrink large MRM raw datasets (e.g. PXD009543, PXD031038, Skyline test set) for web-based rendering or storage, or when benchmarking file-format compression ratios.

name: chromatogram-binning-and-noise-level-estimation
description: Use when processing centroided high-resolution LC-MS mzML files where you need to convert sparse MS1 spectra into continuous chromatographic mass tracks and quantify baseline noise to gate smoothing and peak-detection thresholds.

name: chromatogram-cdf-file-import
description: Use when raw GCxGC-MS acquisition data are stored as NetCDF/CDF files (e.g. 08GB.cdf, 09GB.cdf from MetaboLights MTBLS579) and must be converted into RGCxGC 2D-TIC chromatogram objects before preprocessing or multivariate analysis.

name: chromatogram-cosine-similarity-optimization
description: Use when MRM/LC-MS samples show retention time shifts that break peak correspondence across EICs and you need per-sample drift estimates to align peaks or group EICs across runs.

name: chromatogram-cross-correlation-rt-shift-estimation
description: Use when preprocessing a batch of mzML MRM chromatograms (quantifier + qualifier traces) whose peak RTs drift between samples and need alignment before peak integration, e.g. HILIC 1a-style demodata batches in automRm.

name: chromatogram-deconvolution
description: Use when raw LC-HRMS2 chromatograms (converted from Thermo RAW via MSConvert) contain co-eluting or partially resolved peaks that the ADAP chromatogram builder grouped into a single chromatogram, and distinct peak boundaries must be recovered before MS2 export.

name: chromatogram-deconvolution
description: Use when you have MS1-only LC/HRMS data (mzXML, mzML, netCDF) from untargeted metabolomics and need to deconvolve co-eluting MS1 ions into composite spectra without DDA MS2 files.

name: chromatogram-extracted-ion-generation
description: Use when starting from raw mzXML/mzML LC-MS files of chemical standards (e.g., HILIC metabolomics replicates) and per-analyte EICs are needed for peak quality metrics such as MCQ, asymmetry factor, FWHM, or Std/Blk ratio.

name: chromatogram-extraction-from-parquet-ms-data
description: Use when a chromatogram (TIC, BPI, or EIC for a specific m/z window) must be computed from an on-disk Parquet HRMS file too large to load fully into memory (e.g. ~1.9 Gb in-RAM, 200-400 MB Parquet profile data).

name: chromatogram-import-and-processing-in-ms-dial
description: Use when raw centroid-mode LC–MS all-ion-fragmentation chromatograms need feature detection and pseudo-MS/MS deconvolution to produce a comparable annotation baseline (e.g. against MetaboAnnotatoR rank-1 or manual expert lists) on datasets like Lipid+, Lipid−, or HILIC+.

name: chromatogram-netcdf-import
description: Use when the starting point of a GCxGC-MS analysis is a raw instrument chromatogram stored in NetCDF (e.g. a .cdf file) and it must be converted into a folded 2D-TIC object before preprocessing or multivariate analysis.

name: chromatogram-peak-alignment-2dcow
description: Use when a smoothed, baseline-corrected two-dimensional chromatogram (2D-TIC) must be warped pixel-wise onto a reference chromatogram of the same dataset to remove retention-time shifts before multivariate analysis.

name: chromatogram-plotting-from-massql-results
description: Use when MassQL queries have been run over a directory of mzML files (e.g., SST deuterated acylcarnitine standards on a UHPLC-HRMS) and the peak/scan results need to be visualized as EICs, Gaussian fits, and MS2 plots and exported as tables and PDF reports.

name: chromatogram-quality-label-comparison
description: Use when you have a feature table plus .mzXML/.mzML raw files, a CNN model (EVA/pyEVA) producing predicted EIC quality classes, and manually annotated good/poor labels against which classification accuracy must be measured.

name: chromatogram-smoothing-parameter-tuning
description: Use when building an in-house LC-MS RT/m/z library with metScribeR and EIC peaks (from mzML files of authentic standards) show poorly assigned start/end boundaries or noisy baselines, requiring tuning of smoothing and density-filter settings before applying peak-finding thresholds.

name: chromatogram-smoothing-similarity-analysis
description: Use when an LC/MS EIC must be scored for quality via smoothing- and background-similarity measures, or when benchmarking a comparator EIC metric against a proposed alternative (e.g. the global zigzag index).

name: chromatogram-tic-xic-bpc-computation
description: Use when the input is a proprietary Thermo Fisher Scientific .raw file and the analysis goal is TIC/XIC/BPC traces from within R, especially to avoid ProteoWizard/mzML conversion steps.

name: chromatogram-total-ion-current-aggregation
description: Use when you have a columnar Parquet HRMS file with rt, intensity and mslevel columns and need a TIC (intensity summed per retention time for MS1 scans) without loading the whole file into memory.

name: chromatogram-trace-plotting
description: Use when you have retention-time and intensity arrays extracted from an MZA (HDF5-based) file with mzapy (e.g., via get_tic or collect_xic_arrays_by_mz) and need a visual chromatogram saved as an image like PNG.

name: chromatogram-trace-reconstruction
description: Use when you have an mzML file (e.g. a Beer_multibeers_1_T10_POS.mzML-style acquisition) and want to derive the chemical list for a ViMMS simulation from its real peaks rather than sampling synthetic chemicals from HMDB.

name: chromatogram-xic-extraction-from-raw-files
description: Use when the input is a Thermo Fisher Orbitap .raw file (e.g., 20181113_010_autoQC01.raw) and you need chromatographic traces/XICs for target masses in R, e.g., to derive retention times for iRT peptides.

name: chromatographic-anomaly-diagnosis
description: Use when longitudinal LC-MS/MS SST data (e.g., deuterated acylcarnitine standards in mzML) must be screened for retention time drift, column-lot shifts, or wrong chromatographic method use prior to experimental acquisition.

name: chromatographic-auto-correlation-noise-filtering
description: Use when raw LC/MS data in mzML format must be converted into an MS1 ion-feature table without manually tuned detection thresholds, and noise must be separated from true chromatographic peaks in a data-driven, parameter-free way.

name: chromatographic-background-signal-modeling
description: Reference for modeling non-peak background signals (e.g. walls spanning large chromatogram parts) when generating augmented training instances for peak-picking CNN training in LC-HRMS.

name: chromatographic-baseline-correction
description: Use when raw LC-MS EICs contain baseline drift that would distort peak-position detection or peak-area integration of targeted metabolites and their isotopologues, prior to MassSpecWavelet peak picking.

name: chromatographic-baseline-estimation
description: Use when processing acoustic ejection MS MRM data where per-ejection peak areas must be baseline-corrected before quantification, e.g. to compute A(m,k) transition areas from rtmsEcho-extracted XICs.

name: chromatographic-batch-variation-assessment
description: Use when LC-MS/MS samples span two chromatographic batches (a metadata 'batch' column) and you need to test whether chemical-hierarchy-based beta diversity mitigates the batch effect versus an unweighted feature-table distance.

name: chromatographic-calibration-curve-fitting
description: Use when comparing quantification accuracy of two MRM analysis tools (e.g., MRMPro vs. Skyline) on a shared multi-file dataset with defined transitions, where peak areas can be regressed against known concentrations.

name: chromatographic-column-scaling-analysis
description: Use when measured HILIC RTs come from a modified gradient or a shorter column (100/50/30 mm Kinetex HILIC) and must be mapped onto the reference database RT scale before lipid identification by retention time.

name: chromatographic-data-integration-qc
description: Use when you need batch-consistent peak areas/intensities per feature across GC×GC–MS samples (e.g. a serial dilution QC series) and must verify quantitative agreement with gold-standard software like ChromaTOF.

name: chromatographic-data-storage-comparison
description: Use when comparing mass spectrometry data conversion pipelines or storage formats (e.g., Parquet vs mzML/mz5/mzMLb) on conversion time, file size, and data read/query speed for HRMS or IMS-HDMS^E datasets.

name: chromatographic-eic-extraction
description: Use when raw LC–MS mzML files must yield EICs for specific target compounds — e.g., extracting chromatograms for the five system suitability solution standards (leucine enkephaline, lysophosphatidylcholine (0:0/18:0), L-phenylalanyl-L-phenylalanine, L-tryptophan, alogliptin) from QC injections.

name: chromatographic-eic-visualization
description: Use when targeted LC–MS metabolomics/lipidomics data (mzML raw runs) must be sanity-checked before peak integration — e.g., verifying that target peaks are visible within expected m/z and RT windows in QC runs prior to running full TARDIS integration.

name: chromatographic-elution-order-comparison
description: Use when predicted retention times from one chromatographic method (e.g., SMRT reverse-phase) must be made comparable to RTs measured under other experimental methods (e.g., PredRet ECMs), and median absolute projection errors are needed.

name: chromatographic-error-window-coverage-calculation
description: Use when you have trained retention-time prediction models (e.g. Retip's fit.rf, fit.keras, fit.xgboost, fit.lightgbm, fit.brnn) and experimental RT values for test/validation compounds, and need to quantify what fraction of true positives fall within a fixed RT error window.

name: chromatographic-feature-correlation-clustering
description: Use when input is MS1-only mzML/mzXML (or imzML) data lacking tandem spectra and the goal is to assemble in-source fragments correlated with a precursor into pseudo MS/MS spectra for structural annotation.

name: chromatographic-feature-correlation-filtering
description: Use when you have a chromatographic peak table from LC-MS lipidomics (e.g. Compound Discoverer output) with identified lipid features and numerous unidentified features, and you want to filter out co-eluting spurious/redundant features before downstream statistics.

name: chromatographic-feature-matching
description: Use when two peak-detection tools have been run on the same LC-HRMS samples and you must match their detected features, compare peak areas, and quantify correlation (R2) and systematic area-scaling factors.

name: chromatographic-feature-metadata-extraction
description: Reference for extracting per-feature metadata such as peak_area and calibration/IS metavalues from FeatureDB reports in targeted metabolomics workflows before fitting calibration curves or computing quantitation.

name: chromatographic-feature-table-construction
description: Use when starting from raw LC-MS/MS MS1 scans (mzML or Bruker .d) and a feature table with complete signal coverage is needed before adduct grouping, alignment, or annotation.

name: chromatographic-fwhm-overlap-scoring
description: Use when assembling LC-MS mass traces into metabolite isotope features and you must verify that candidate isotope traces co-elute with the monoisotopic trace before accepting a feature hypothesis.

name: chromatographic-gradient-evaluation
description: Use when raw LC-MS (mzML/mzXML) data from a gradient run must be reduced to a single separation-performance number (GSI) to evaluate or optimize a chromatographic gradient.

name: chromatographic-gradient-parameterization
description: Use when you must define the candidate LC-MS gradient space before fitting the GP model: you have gradient-definition parameters (dimensionality, time points, mobile-phase settings) and need the constrained gridX/scaledX candidate set.

name: chromatographic-ion-clusterisation
description: Use when analysing HPTLC coupled with high-resolution mass spectrometry data (e.g. mzXML-derived extracted ion chromatograms) and you need to partition ions of interest from background ions before structure elucidation.

name: chromatographic-local-maxima-detection
description: Use when processing raw profile-mode LC-HRMS chromatograms (mzXML/mzML) and you need to enumerate all candidate peak-apex signals before machine-learning peak/background classification.

name: chromatographic-model-peak-selection
description: Use when SWATH-MS data have multiplexed MS/MS spectra in which fragment ions co-elute and chromatographic peaks are unresolved, and metabolite-specific MS2 spectra must be reconstructed for downstream annotation.

name: chromatographic-modulation-folding
description: Use when raw comprehensive two-dimensional GC–MS data in CDF files must be folded into a 4D tensor (samples, m/z fragments, second-dimension and first-dimension retention time) as the entry point of an untargeted GC×GC–MS workflow.

name: chromatographic-peak-alignment-input-preparation
description: Use when raw LC/HRMS data (mzXML, mzML, netCDF) must be converted into chromatographic m/z-RT peaklists and an aligned peak table before running the CSA, DDA, or DIA deconvolution workflows of IDSL.CSA.

name: chromatographic-peak-alignment-qc
description: Use when GC/MS chromatograms have already been deconvolved with eRah and aligned compound tables contain gaps (compounds found in some samples but not others) that must be filled before quantification.

name: chromatographic-peak-area-integration
description: Use when processing targeted MS data where peak detection has produced EICs (after airPLS baseline correction and MassSpecWavelet peak positioning) and per-sample peak areas must be computed for a chosen isotopologue or metabolite.

name: chromatographic-peak-baseline-reconstruction
description: Use when MRM ion chromatograms contain noisy peaks, unevenly sampled signals, or coeluted isomers where connecting nearby valleys (e.g., TargetLynx) misestimates the baseline; adaptive section-wise background reconstruction is needed before peak integration.

name: chromatographic-peak-boundary-correction
description: Use when refining the start/stop limits of peaks detected in smoothed CE-MS or HILIC-MS ROI chromatograms (intensity-vs-retention-time traces), after CWT/Mexican-hat peak-center detection but before peak integration of RT, area, and height.

name: chromatographic-peak-boundary-detection
description: Use when reconstructing chromatographic peak boundaries from centroided LC-MS data — e.g. when a growing mass trace spans several valleys and must be split so each trace corresponds to one chromatographic peak, or when apex-based boundary definition is needed.

name: chromatographic-peak-detection
description: Use when raw LC-MS targeted metabolomics EICs (e.g. centWave-exported chromatograms such as the MM14 or human blood datasets) need peak positions, bounds and areas quantified per compound, especially when multiple candidate peaks must be resolved to the true M+H/M+Na/M+K isotopologue peak.

name: chromatographic-peak-detection
description: Use when MRM-mode LC-QQQ-MS raw data (mzML) must be preprocessed into peak intensity tables without manual review, e.g. batches from instruments like an Agilent 6495 QQQ-MS needing automatic peak picking and quality control.

name: chromatographic-peak-edge-detection
description: Use when processing raw LC-MS ROI intensity arrays (e.g. mzML or Bruker TDF2 .d via MassCube) and you need to split each mass trace into discrete chromatographic peak segments bounded by start/end edge indices.

name: chromatographic-peak-fwhm-window-grouping
description: Use when an aligned XCMS feature table (m/z, retention time, apex intensity, per-sample intensities) must be partitioned into co-eluting compound spectra as the first CAMERA grouping step before isotope/adduct annotation.

name: chromatographic-peak-integration-rt-area-height
description: Use when untargeted metabolomics ROIs (intensity-vs-retention-time traces from CE-MS or HILIC-MS runs, e.g. .mzML/.mzXML converted profiles) must be converted into a per-peak table of apex RT, area, and height for feature integration.

name: chromatographic-peak-ms2-spectra-extraction
description: Use when you have an xcms result object with centWave-detected chromatographic peaks (e.g. from an mzML LC-MS/MS run like HighIS_Mix07_CE20_POS.mzML) and need the tandem MS2 spectra behind those peaks to compare against a reference library such as an HMDB 5.0 CompDb.

name: chromatographic-peak-picking
description: Use when starting from raw HRMS .mzML files and you need to extract chromatographic features (m/z–RT pairs) for non-targeted analysis, e.g. ENTACT-style mixtures or environmental water samples.

name: chromatographic-peak-picking
description: Use when starting from raw MS data files (e.g. LC-MS runs) and a feature-level peak list is needed as the basis for deisotoping, alignment, and gap filling.

name: chromatographic-peak-picking
description: Use when raw LC-MS mzXML files (any vendor format compatible with MS-Convert) need MS1 peak picking to build a JPA feature table, or as the PP baseline step before MR and targeted feature extraction in metabolomics/exposomics processing.

name: chromatographic-peak-quality-assessment
description: Use when extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) from LC/MS metabolomics profiles have already been peak-detected and individual peaks (or EICs) must be scored, filtered, or classified as good vs. bad before downstream processing.

name: chromatographic-peak-quality-assessment
description: Use when you have targeted/suspect HRMS data (mzML) plus a compound or mass list and need per-peak QC (MS1/MS2 existence, noise, RT shift) before further identification or spectral upload.

name: chromatographic-peak-quality-filtering
description: Use when processing LC-MS mzML files of authentic metabolite standards and you need to find peaks on adduct EICs and remove low-quality detections before assigning retention times and m/z for an in-house reference library.

name: chromatographic-peak-quality-filtering
description: Use when processing MS1-level LC/HRMS peak candidates (e.g. from IDSL.IPA EIC detection) and you need to discard low-quality or redundant isotope peaks using the seven-parameter peak quality filter before building aligned data matrices.

name: chromatographic-peak-quality-filtering
description: Use when raw centroid/profile HRMS scans (.mzML) have been peak-picked and the feature list must be cleaned of low-quality peaks — split peaks, peaks spanning too few scans, and high-baseline-noise features — before annotation or statistical analysis.

name: chromatographic-peak-quality-metric-computation
description: Use when LC/MS chromatographic peaks have been detected on extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) and you need per-peak numeric quality scores to filter 'bad' peaks before downstream metabolomics processing.

name: chromatographic-peak-quality-metric-computation
description: Use when you have an XCMS pre-processed untargeted LC–MS dataset (getEIC + fillPeaks output) and need numeric per-peak quality features to train or apply a Pass/Fail peak-quality classifier.

name: chromatographic-peak-quality-metrics
description: Use when evaluating LC-MS metabolomics peak quality for chemical standards: you have EICs from mzXML/mzML files (with optional replicate and blank runs) and need standardized per-peak quality metrics to validate or rank peaks.

name: chromatographic-peak-quality-score-computation
description: Use when preprocessing LC-QQQ-MS raw data in MRM mode and you need per-candidate peak quality metrics (shape, quantifier/qualifier coelution, RT deviation) before ML-based peak reporting.

name: chromatographic-peak-quality-scoring
description: Use when raw MRM-mode LC-MS data (mzML with quantifier plus qualifier transitions and expected RTs in metabdb.xlsx) must be converted into a trustworthy set of reported peaks, i.e. deciding which of several peak candidates per metabolite/sample is the correct one.

name: chromatographic-peak-r13c-computation
description: Reference for quantifying the 12C/13C isotope-pair intensity ratio of individual chromatographic peaks and correlating it with molecular formulas or predicted carbon number.

name: chromatographic-peak-shape-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when a peak-detection algorithm needs quantitative accuracy assessment against ground-truth manually labeled EIC peak-shape classes (double vs single peak) on experimental LC-MS data.

name: chromatographic-peak-shape-analysis
description: Use when raw CE-MS or LC-MS data (converted to .mzXML/.mzML via msconvert) has been peak-detected with the CWT/ROI search step and noise/false-positive peaks must be culled by shape before feature integration, scaling, and mid-level data fusion.

name: chromatographic-peak-shape-correlation
description: Use when processing untargeted LC-MS raw data (mzML or Bruker .d) where co-eluting ions must be distinguished as genuine metabolites versus in-source fragments or alternative adducts before quantification.

name: chromatographic-peak-shape-correlation-analysis
description: Decision support for splitting CAMERA pseudospectra that the retention-time window alone left ambiguous — i.e. when features co-elute within one FWHM group but their EIC peak shapes (corval, pval thresholds on calcCaS edges) indicate two overlapping analytes.

name: chromatographic-peak-smoothing-and-noise-estimation
description: Use when performing semi-targeted LC-MS peak quantification on converted Aird data (e.g. TripleTOF or QE HF acquisitions) and a smoothing or noise-estimation strategy must be selected among MetaPro's 4 smoothing and 3 noise-estimation options before peak selection and integration.

name: chromatographic-peak-snr-filtering
description: Use when filtering candidate peaks detected from GC×GC–MS 4D intensity arrays (CDF-derived GcDuo objects) by signal-to-noise and peak-shape criteria before deconvolution, to discard false positives such as incomplete or sub-threshold signals.

name: chromatographic-peak-tip-detection
description: Use when processing high-throughput LC-MS/MS MRM ion chromatograms where peaks may be coeluted, noisy, or unevenly sampled and per-transition peak tips, valleys, and coelution flags must be resolved before quantitation.

name: chromatographic-peak-tracking-for-user-defined-compounds
description: Use when you have raw untargeted metabolomics files (mzML/mzXML/mzData) plus a user-defined list of m/z and RT pairs for QC or contaminant compounds, and need to track observed m/z, retention time, intensity, and peak shape over time or batches.

name: chromatographic-peak-validation
description: Use when replicate LC/MS injections of chemical standard mixtures (mzXML/mzML with blank runs) must be filtered into validated peaks to build a retention-time reference library, e.g. the HILIC LC-MS platform's 571-metabolite library.

name: chromatographic-peak-vs-background-classification
description: Use when you have profile-mode LC-HRMS chromatograms and a user-defined reference-feature list (ground truth) and need to distinguish true chromatographic peaks from background/walls with a custom-trained CNN.

name: chromatographic-peak-width-measurement
description: Use when you need to set chromatographic peak-width parameters for an LC-MS feature extraction run (e.g. XCMS CentWave peak width, MS-DIAL tolerances) from raw untargeted metabolomics data.

name: chromatographic-peak-width-tuning
description: Use when configuring eRah deconvolveComp() on GC-EI MS chromatograms (netCDF/mzXML) and you must set min.peak.width, min.peak.height, noise.threshold, or avoid.processing.mz before running CMLC/OSD.

name: chromatographic-quality-metric-calculation
description: Use when targeted LC–MS peak integration (e.g., TARDIS on raw metabolomics/lipidomics runs) has produced per-target peak tables and you need quantitative quality metrics to filter poor-quality peaks or validate QC-run clustering.

name: chromatographic-quality-metric-implementation
description: Use when you must programmatically score the quality of extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) or detected chromatographic peaks in LC/MS metabolomics data — especially EICs with high background signals or containing only a single peak — before downstream peak detection.

name: chromatographic-quantitation-curve-modeling
description: Use when absolute quantitation of targeted compounds from MRM data is needed and calibration standard samples (e.g. 14 standards spanning 0.025–500 mol/mL) are available to build concentration–abundance curves.

name: chromatographic-retention-matching-window-analysis
description: Use when a predicted-versus-true retention time table exists and you need to set an RT matching window (e.g., ±2 SD) for metabolite identification and quantify how many true matches that window would exclude.

name: chromatographic-retention-order-prediction
description: Use when the goal is to predict elution order of metabolites directly from molecular structure (InChI) across LC systems, especially when retention times are not comparable across instruments/configurations.

name: chromatographic-retention-time-error-tracking
description: Use when raw LC-MS or LC-IMS-MS files (Agilent 'd', Thermo '.raw', Bruker 'd', mzML) need per-ion mass, retention-time, and arrival-time error metrics for QC of chromatographic performance.

name: chromatographic-rt-dataset-preparation
description: Use when you need to train or retrain RT-Transformer on a retention time dataset prepared as InChI+RT CSV, or reproduce the SMRT full-data MAE of 33.41 s.

name: chromatographic-rt-prediction-benchmark-analysis
description: Use when comparing retention time prediction models on a benchmark dataset and you need to determine which achieves the lowest mean/median relative error, e.g. GNN-RT (4.9% mean, 3.2% median) vs RF, Bayesian ridge, CNN, DLM.

name: chromatographic-rt-tolerance-configuration
description: Use when constructing metScribeR reference libraries from mzML files of authentic standards and you must choose the m/z and RT tolerances for EIC extraction and adduct distinction.

name: chromatographic-shape-similarity-analysis
description: Use when processing MRM acquisition data where EIC peak features across samples must be grouped by chromatographic shape (e.g., same target peptide transition across samples), and manual inspection needs pre-grouped EICs to keep low-intensity noise features separated from real signal.

name: chromatographic-shift-correction-evaluation
description: Use when aligning feature retention times across many LC-MS chromatograms (e.g., large QC-pooled metabolomics studies) and you need quantifiable residual RT-shift benchmarks after correction.

name: chromatographic-signal-preprocessing
description: Use when raw GCxGC-MS chromatograms (e.g., NetCDF files folded into 2D-TIC matrices) contain a steady increasing baseline, noise, or retention-time shifts that must be removed prior to MPCA or supervised modeling.

name: chromatographic-snr-computation-from-eic-flanks
description: Use when validating asari feature quality without manual inspection: you have full_Feature_table.tsv plus export/cmap.pickle and must recompute snr, cSelectivity, or peakshape to check exported values.

name: chromatographic-space-similarity-quantification
description: Use when you have paired RPLC retention datasets (e.g., RepoRT, PredRet, Metabolome Workbench, MetaboLights sources) sharing compounds across different chromatographic methods and need to measure retention-order replicability or attribute it to specific method differences.

name: chromatographic-system-train-test-splitting
description: Use when evaluating RankSVM or SVR retention order/time prediction across multiple chromatographic systems (e.g. Eawag_XBridgeC18, FEM_long, RIKEN, UFZ_Phenomenex, LIFE_old) and you must decide which systems serve as training vs. target data.

name: chromatographic-trace-extraction
description: Use when you have a profile-mode mzML file from LC-DTIM-MS and a list of molecular formulae (or predicted ion m/z values) and need to locate each monoisotopic primary-ion m/z trace over RT and arrival time, then peak-pick in the RT dimension.

name: chromatographic-transferability-assessment
description: Use when deciding whether fine-tuning a pre-trained ROASMI model with a specific reference dataset will yield substantial rank-score gains on a target prediction set, or when grouping retraining results by ChemSS/ChrSS similarity.

name: chromatography-ms-2d-map-visualization
description: Use when input is a two-dimensional chromatography–MS map (m/z vs retention time) from GC–MS or LC–MS and you need to discriminate analytes and identify/visualize marker features without conventional peak picking.

name: chromatography-ms-map-image-processing
description: Use when raw 2D chromatography–MS maps (m/z vs retention time, GC–MS or LC–MS) need analyte discrimination and marker-feature identification/visualization and conventional peak picking is unreliable or causes false peak detections.

name: chromatography-ms-marker-feature-identification
description: Use when you have raw two-dimensional chromatography–MS maps (GC–MS or LC–MS, e.g. m/z vs retention time) and need untargeted marker feature identification without prior peak picking.

name: ci-vs-ei-fragmentation-comparison
description: Use when choosing a GC-MS ionization method or reagent gas for stable-isotope labeling metabolomics and you need to quantify which technique concentrates the [M+H]+ isotopic envelope with least fragmentation.

name: cid-hcd-fragmentation-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when you have matched sets of CID and HCD tandem MS spectra of the same compounds (e.g., 44 CID + 44 HCD NRP/PK spectra) and need to measure or compare how the fragmentation method changes annotation/dereplication tool accuracy.

name: cid-hcd-fragmentation-mode-comparison
description: Use when LC-MS/MS DDA data were acquired on a system suitability standard under both HCD and CID at stepped normalized collision energies (e.g., NCE 10-60), and the goal is to compare product ion signal between the two fragmentation modes.

name: cid-parameter-sweep-configuration
description: Use when generating a library of in silico CID-MS/MS spectra from optimized protonated molecular ions and need to explore multiple collider velocities, trajectory counts, reaction times, and b cutoffs per protomer rather than committing to a single parameter set.

name: cidmd-collider-trajectory-sampling
description: Use when an optimized protonated molecular ion structure (xyz format) must be converted into a user-defined number of collision input files with varied collisional geometry before running CIDMD trajectories.

name: cidmd-spectrum-aggregation-statistics
description: Use when you have a cohort of predicted (in silico) MS/MS spectra and matched experimental library spectra and need cohort-level accuracy statistics (e.g., mean entropy similarity ± SD) plus per-spectrum score files.

name: circular-phylogeny-visualization
description: Use when you need a publication-quality circular visualization of a taxonomic/phylogenetic tree (e.g., BIOM abundance tables from 16S studies, MetaPhlAn/LEfSe/HUMAnN outputs) annotated with metadata or biomarkers.

name: circular-taxonomic-tree-rendering
description: Use when you need a publication-quality circular cladogram of a microbial taxonomy (e.g., HMP aerobiosis LEfSe biomarkers or saliva BIOM tables), mapping LDA scores to clade sizes and class assignments to shaded backgrounds.

name: cis-eqtl-gene-annotation
description: Use when sentinel and proxy variant lists (rsID + GRCh37 coordinates) at molecular QTLs require cis-eQTL target gene annotation from GTEx v7 across user-specified tissues as part of a bottom-up candidate-gene prioritization.

name: cis-eqtl-target-gene-extraction
description: Use when you have sentinel/proxy variant rsIDs with GRCh37 coordinates and need to flag which local genes are cis-eQTL targets in GTEx tissues, as bottom-up evidence for causal gene prioritization at molecular QTLs.

name: citation-evidence-extraction
description: Use when an article makes comparative claims about MS data formats (mzML, mzMLb, imzML, vendor RAW) and you must extract each claim verbatim, tag it with a trade-off dimension, and attach cited evidence in a structured table.

name: citation-network-construction
description: Use when the goal is to construct a heterogeneous non-biological network (e.g. authors linked to articles linked to journals) via automated two-step linkset extension in Cytoscape.

name: citation-threshold-inclusion-filtering
description: Use when compiling a curated catalogue of metabolomics analysis tools from a broader candidate list and an objective, reproducible popularity criterion is needed to decide which tools qualify as 'most widely used'.

name: clade-level-false-positive-negative-identification
description: Use when two taxonomic profiles (a profiler output and a ground truth) receive similar single-value metric scores but you need to identify which specific taxonomic clades differ between them.

name: clade-size-abundance-scaling
description: Use when converting MetaPhlAn/LEfSe (or HUMAnN) output into GraPhlAn tree and annotation files and you need biomarker clades to be visually emphasized by size rather than a uniform node radius.

name: class-imbalance-upsampling
description: Use when training or evaluating a BGC detector on class-imbalanced Pfam TSV training sets — e.g., scoring a held-out MIBiG class with too few examples for stable AUC estimation, or when ClusterFinder-comparable leave-class-out AUCs are the target metric.

name: class-matched-versus-diverse-model-comparison
description: Use when evaluating whether a custom SVR CCS prediction training set (class-matched vs chemically diverse) sustains filtering power of annotation candidates as the mass-error window narrows from 10 ppm to isobaric 0 ppm.

name: class-share-computation
description: Use when analyzing the composition of MIBiG 2.0's 851 newly added BGCs across the seven structure-based classes, or when quantifying growth of a curated database relative to a prior version.

name: class-specific-ccs-parameter-optimization
description: Use when raw or processed TWIM-MS calibrant data (e.g. Waters Major Mix, Agilent ESI-L Tune Mix) must be converted into class-specific power-law calibration parameter sets for TWCCSN2 calculation.

name: class-specific-internal-standard-normalization
description: Use when quantitative MSI lipid maps in absolute units (pmol/mm2) are needed and class-specific internal standards have been co-sprayed onto the tissue, e.g. centroided .imzML files from timsTOF or other MALDI/DESI platforms.

name: classical-vs-deep-learning-agreement-assessment
description: Use when a deep-learning (NN-predicted) isotopomer distribution must be validated against a classical multiplet-fit distribution for the same metabolite, e.g. lactate from HSQC + GC-MS data, to confirm agreement.

name: classification-ablation-evaluation
description: Use when you need to test whether restricting raw LC-MS input to published lung-cancer serum biomarker m/z signals (3 ppm window, PC>1/3/8 thresholds) degrades classifier accuracy versus the full-data model.

name: classification-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when a CNN-classified set of EIC plots from LC-MS feature tables needs benchmarking against manually annotated good/poor labels, or when verifying that an extended pyEVA deployment maintains reported accuracy.

name: classification-bias-quantification
description: Decision support for whether reported colocalization coefficients overestimate true colocalization when pixel intensities are sums of colocalized and non-colocalized signals.

name: classification-evaluation-measure-computation
description: Reference for quantitatively comparing peak-quality classifiers — or a classifier against RSD < 30% pooled-QC filtering — on labeled Pass/Fail peaks from untargeted LC–MS datasets.

name: classification-metric-aggregation-across-folds
description: Use when a classification pipeline (CNN on molecular fingerprint images, Random Forest, PCA, OPLS-DA) has been trained under StratifiedKFold fivefold cross-validation and per-fold accuracy, recall, precision and F1 must be averaged into one comparable table.

name: classification-metric-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing two peak-classification approaches on identical LC/MS data and needing to quantify whether a low-label active-learning model matches or beats a transfer-learning model trained on more labels.

name: classification-metric-computation
description: Decision support for quantifying whether an integrated multi-assay MB-PLS model outperforms single-block PLS models on a binary classification task (e.g. sex prediction), using per-repeat metrics from Monte Carlo cross-validation.

name: classification-metric-computation-acc-tpr-fpr
description: Use when a binary compound-identification model (e.g., FlavorFormer on 1H NMR spectra) must be evaluated and its variants compared using ACC, TPR, and FPR reported as mean ± std across runs.

name: classification-metric-reporting-accuracy-f1
description: Use when a categorical-labeled dataset (e.g. wine quality ratings) has been split into training and held-out test partitions and you need to quantify prediction quality of a fitted pipeline before saving or reusing it.

name: classification-model-label-permutation-testing
description: Use when a supervised classifier has been trained on labeled data (e.g. 500-peak LC–MS Pass/Fail labels) and you must rule out that reported test-set performance is an artifact of random chance rather than genuine signal in the features.

name: classification-performance-metrics-computation
description: Use when class predictions from a PLS/OPLS-DA-derived classifier on held-out test folds (e.g. malignant vs non-malignant lung GC-TOF MS tissue) must be quantified by accuracy, precision, sensitivity and specificity.

name: classification-performance-metrics-computation
description: Use when labeled 'relevant' (e.g., natural products, prenylated flavonoids) and 'other' (e.g., wheat ear extract) MS/MS reference spectra are available and you must quantify how well custom-trained classifiers discriminate the 'other' class.

name: classification-precision-recall-evaluation
description: Use when two classifiers must be compared on compounds that carry sensory bitter/nonbitter ground-truth labels, and precision, recall, balanced accuracy, and F1 must be tabulated to decide which tool is preferable.

name: classification-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when a trained model (e.g., massNet on MALDI FT-ICR MSI spectra) must be evaluated on an independent test set for accuracy, per-class AUC, and classification speed relative to a baseline method like SVM.

name: classification-uncertainty-mapping
description: Use when you have per-spectrum probabilistic outputs (0–1) from a pixel-based classifier on mass spectrometry imaging data and need to visualize where classification confidence breaks down, e.g. to detect infiltrative tumor margins versus tumor core or normal tissue.

name: classifier-free-guidance-training
description: Use when training a graph-based generative model for de novo molecular structure generation where an MS/MS spectrum must guide generation from a fixed scaffold, and guidance strength at sampling must be tunable without retraining a separate classifier.

name: classifier-independent-cohort-validation
description: Use when a trained classifier must be independently tested on a new cohort — e.g., sPRM/Skyline peak areas for the 15 HCC features in 23 HCC-R2 samples with known early-recurrence labels — to verify generalizability against a reported AUC.

name: classifier-metrics-comparison
