description: Use when a paper discusses multiple community tools/repositories in the context of programmatic sample-level metadata analysis and you must classify each cited design choice as favorable or hindering for that purpose.

name: community-view-dereplication-interpretation
description: Use when an NP Analyst community lacks a single dominant bioactive MS feature but contains multiple high Activity-Score features that co-retain, requiring RT-vs-m/z stripe grouping for dereplication.

name: community-view-metabolite-prioritization
description: Use when a basketed, bioactivity-scored MS feature network (nodes = MS features/samples with activity and cluster scores) needs to be partitioned into communities and priority MS features identified from the network, scatter, and community views.

name: comparative-benchmark-evaluation-against-sirius
description: Use when a new MS/MS molecular structure annotation method needs a fair baseline comparison on identical query spectra, and SIRIUS is an appropriate reference tool with a defined structural database.

name: comparative-claim-verification
description: Decision support for claims like 'ANOVA and PCA are in all three Galaxy metabolomics toolkits' or 'SECIMTools uniquely offers LASSO and Elastic Net' — trigger when a finding asserts presence/absence of a tool across ≥2 named software suites.

name: comparative-metabolomics-feature-filtering
description: Use when an xcms-derived feature table (csv/.mskFT with 'mz' and 'rt' columns and grouped intensity columns) must be reduced to features differentially enriched between sample groups, e.g. mutant vs. WT exo-metabolomes.

name: comparative-metabolomics-groupwise-differential-analysis
description: Use when comparing untargeted LC/MS feature intensities between two sample groups (e.g., hacl-1 mutant vs wild-type) to identify enriched molecular features and collapse them into metabolites.

name: comparative-table-aggregation
description: Use when simulated DDA runs for multiple fragmentation controllers (e.g. Top-N, SmartROI, WeightedDEW) have completed in ViMMS 2.0 over the same chemical set and their evaluation reports must be merged into one comparative benchmark table.

name: comparems2-parameter-estimation
description: Use when you need to choose compareMS2 m/z windows and spectral similarity thresholds for new LC-MS/MS MGF data, or to inspect mass accuracy, charge states and isotope errors before any database search.

name: compartmentalized-community-model-simulation
description: Use when you need to simulate a multi-species metabolic community with member-attributable compartments, predict feasible community compositions or maximum growth rates at a given abundance profile, and enumerate cross-feeding interactions independent of abundance.

name: compartmentalized-model-generation
description: Use when multiple genome-scale SBML member models must be merged into a single reusable community metabolic model with member-of-origin compartmentalization and openCOBRA/COBRApy compliance for growth-rate or abundance-profile simulations.

name: compendium-duplicate-averaging
description: Use when preparing an ion-mobility CCS training set from McLean Unified CCS Compendium adduct sheets where duplicate entries with differing measured CCS values exist and must be collapsed before further scrubbing or model fitting.

name: complementary-method-comparison-visualization
description: Use when two annotation methods have been run over the same query spectra and each query carries a Boolean correctness label per method, and the goal is to quantify and visualize overlap of correct annotations (contingency table / Venn-style breakdown).

name: complete-linkage-agglomerative-clustering
description: Use when you have pairwise similarity indexes (Ssim, Psim, PsimW, Csim) for >2 KEGG organisms and want to test whether hierarchical clustering of the resulting distance matrix recovers known phylogenetic groupings.

name: completely-at-random-missingness-simulation
description: Use when evaluating a missing-value imputation method on complete source data and you need reproducible MCAR-masked test matrices paired with ground truth at fixed missingness fractions.

name: completeness-entropy-metric-computation
description: Use when clustering quality of MS/MS spectra clustering must be quantified as completeness from peptide-spectrum match labels, e.g. comparing DBSCAN vs hierarchical clustering (complete linkage) across hypervector dimensions D = 128 to 8192.

name: completeness-metric-n10-calculation
description: Use when you have post-processed MS/MS clustering output (filename, scan, precursor mass, retention time, cluster index) and need a database-search-free completeness metric for benchmarking tools like Falcon, MaRaCluster, or msCluster.

name: complex-valued-signal-handling
description: Use when the input is an unprocessed 1D time-domain FID of complex points (e.g., 16,384 complex samples) that must be truncated and randomly partitioned into train/validation/test subsets before peak-decomposition fitting, to avoid overfitting and infer a reasonable number of peaks.

name: component-abundance-ranking
description: Use when a non-targeted UPLC-HRMS fingerprint peak list (positive and negative ESI modes) must be tabulated by ionization mode and ranked by extracted peak intensity to nominate the most abundant prototype components, e.g. amygdalin and prunasin in CKXR.

name: component-level-metric-aggregation-across-mixture-complexity-levels
description: Use when benchmarking multi-component identification from 1H NMR spectra and you need mixture-level metrics broken down by component count (2–5 components) rather than a single pooled score.

name: component-relationship-network-construction
description: Use when in vivo metabolite feature lists (m/z, MS1/MS2 mass defects, MS2 fragment spectra) must be linked to in vitro prototype components from a non-targeted identification step to map metabolic transformations.

name: component-stability-assessment
description: Use when you need to choose the decomposition order (number of components) for ICA applied to transcriptomic/cancer omics data, and want the choice justified by across-run stability rather than by variance-explained or visual inspection.

name: composite-masstrack-intensity-vector-extraction
description: Use when a full_Feature_table.tsv feature needs its underlying extracted-ion-chromatogram trace — e.g. to verify peak shape, recompute SNR/cSelectivity, or backtrack a feature to its mass track.

name: composite-masstrack-peak-detection
description: Use when processing multiple centroided LC-MS metabolomics mzML files where features must be detected reproducibly across samples and each feature must be traceable back to its underlying mass track (EIC).

name: composite-spectra-cluster-aggregation
description: Use when you have IDSL.IPA-generated 'peaklists' and 'peak_alignment' outputs from LC/HRMS MS1-only data and need to group co-eluting, correlating ions into CSA clusters for downstream composite spectra library creation and chemical annotation.

name: composite-spectra-clustering-from-ms1-ions
description: Use when you have MS1-only LC/HRMS data (mzXML, mzML, netCDF) already peak-picked with IDSL.IPA and need composite spectra libraries (MSP) for annotating co-eluting ions such as adducts, isotopologues, and in-source fragments.

name: composite-spectra-deconvolution-from-ms1-peaks
description: Use when input is MS1-only LC/HRMS data (mzXML/mzML/netCDF) with IDSL.IPA peaklists and peak_alignment output, and the goal is composite-spectra (.msp) generation or annotation without MS2 fragmentation.

name: composite-spectra-library-matching
description: Use when you have an .msp CSA spectra library (or unique CSA spectra variants) from an MS1-only or DDA/DIA study and want to annotate peaks by spectral similarity searching against an MS/MS library (e.g. NIST 2020) or a CSA library built from a different study.

name: composition-table-generation
description: Use when a metabolite standards library inventory lists metabolites with chemical class and ionisation mode, and you must report mode-level totals and per-class composition percentages.

name: compositional-microbiome-transformation-ra-clr
description: Use when input is a samples-by-features CSV of raw microbial or metabolite counts (e.g., IBD PRISM, cystic fibrosis, soil paired datasets) that must be made compositional prior to MiMeNet training.

name: compound-activity-mapping
description: Use when you have an extract/prefraction library with MS feature data (mzML, MZmine 2 peak lists, or GNPS .graphml networks) and bioassay screening data, and need to identify which MS features or metabolites drive the observed bioactivity.

name: compound-annotation-confidence-estimation
description: Use when formula and compound structure annotation results exist for LC-HRMS features and each annotated feature needs an automatic, reproducible identification confidence level (Schymanski 2014 levels 1–5) assigned from a rules file.

name: compound-annotation-cross-tissue-comparison
description: Use when you have PyINETA-annotated compounds from INADEQUATE-13C-JRES spectra of multiple tissues (e.g., liver, spleen, pancreas, muscle, lung) from labeled-diet mouse studies and need to determine which metabolites are enriched, depleted, or co-enriched per organ.

name: compound-annotation-filtering
description: Use when a feature table with candidate compound annotations from the MetMiner plant-specific MS database needs to be subsetted or labelled by annotation level, or when low-confidence m/z-only matches must be separated from full evidence annotations.

name: compound-annotation-resource-validation
description: Use when constructing or auditing a reference compound/MS2-spectrum database (e.g., HMDB-derived CompDb.Hsapiens.HMDB.5.0.sqlite) where exact annotation counts must be reproducible and predicted spectra excluded.

name: compound-annotation-sensitivity-evaluation
description: Use when you have per-peak top-N compound annotations from an LC-MS annotation pipeline (e.g. mWISE top three candidates) plus a reference set of true compounds per assay, and you need entity-level sensitivity/F1/Tanimoto metrics to compare configurations or algorithms.

name: compound-annotation-table-generation
description: Use when consensus MS2 spectra with reconstructed precursor m/z and retention time are available and named chemical identities are needed for detected MS1 features.

name: compound-class-annotation
description: Use when Denoising Search batch results on plasma MS/MS spectra (Orbitrap Astral vs Exploris 240) need to be aggregated into per-instrument annotation counts and classified by compound class via ClassyFire superclasses.

name: compound-class-assignment-from-molecular-formulas
description: Use when you have a peak table (e.g. Report.csv) from direct-injection FT-ICR MS where molecular formulas are already assigned and you need elemental/biochemical compound-class labels before chemodiversity or Van Krevelen analysis.

name: compound-class-level-querying
description: Use when the goal is broad meta-analysis across many BinBase GC–TOF MS studies where sample or compound metadata should be aggregated by ontology adjacency (OGDA), e.g. asking which metabolites differ between 'digestive tract' vs bacteria or across 'rodents'.

name: compound-class-prediction-canopus
description: Use when MS/MS spectra (e.g. peak lists from a microbeMASST search) lack confident library matches but need putative class-level annotation, and spectra have parent mass < 850 Da.

name: compound-concentration-factor-extraction
description: Use when a minimum cost flow assignment over an HSQC peak network has been solved (e.g. with HiGHS via SciPy) and per-compound concentrations or detection indicators are needed from the resulting flows.

name: compound-coverage-calculation
description: Use when a spectral library release (e.g. the MSnLib Zenodo 11163380 deposit) must be audited for which of its constituent compounds actually have spectra, to reproduce headline coverage/total counts reported in a paper.

name: compound-database-annotation-enrichment
description: Use when you have a list of tentative compound names (or PubChem CIDs) from GC-MS peak annotation and need database-backed categorization, substructure descriptors, and strong/moderate structural matches to a user-defined chemical library.

name: compound-database-ingestion
description: Reference for building a searchable m/z compound database before metabolite annotation in MetaboShiny — needed once per database when the user wants m/z matches across adducts and isotopes.

name: compound-database-mass-matching
description: Use when peak lists (DIMS or LC-MS) already contain accurate m/z values and you must assign putative metabolite identities via empirical formulae, single-peak matches, transformation mapping, or adduct/isotopic peak-pattern evidence.

name: compound-database-mass-search
description: Use when you have background-subtracted UPLC-HRMS peak lists (positive and/or negative ESI modes) of an herbal extract and need to assign putative compound identities from accurate masses before metabolite-bridging analysis.

name: compound-database-mz-window-retrieval
description: Use when a tandem-MS metabolite annotation pipeline needs a candidate compound list per MS1 precursor peak from a pre-built database (e.g. HMDB, ChEBI, MassBank, NIST14 in HDF5), before any MS2 scoring.

name: compound-database-normalisation
description: Use when preparing metabolite reference databases for m/z annotation of MALDI/spatial metabolomics peaks and the raw SDF entries contain inconsistent fields, non-natural-product elements, or absent adduct masses.

name: compound-database-querying
description: Use when chromatographic peaks or features from an xcms-processed mzML dataset must be annotated against a reference compound library, and a CompDb (e.g. HMDB-derived SQLite) is available or must be built.

name: compound-dataset-splitting
description: Use when training per-m/z peak-presence models (ANN, GNN or COM) from merged binarized MS/MS spectra and a compound-level split must be defined before ANNmodel.py / GNNmodel.py / COMmodel.py are invoked.

name: compound-decontamination-filtering
description: Use when processing a GC-MS hit table (columns Component.RT, Component.Area, Base.Peak.MZ, File.Name, Compound.Name, Match.Factor) and you need to drop low-confidence tentative identifications before aggregating component areas across samples.

name: compound-density-histogram-visualization
description: Use when an HRMS feature list (e.g., external_feature_list.xlsx from PFΔScreen FeatureFinding) must be inspected as MD/C vs. m/C density to see whether potential PFAS separate from hydrocarbon matrix components before applying m/C and MD/C cutoffs.

name: compound-dereplication-from-activity-profile
description: Use when a prefractionated extract library has both processed MS feature data (mzML, MZmine 2 peak lists, or GNPS graphML/CSV) and normalized bioassay columns, and the goal is to identify which MS feature explains the community's activity profile and dereplicate the compound behind it.

name: compound-discoverer-peak-extraction
description: Use when starting from Thermo .raw LC-MS lipidomics files and a downstream peak table is needed — specifically when the pipeline requires Compound Discoverer 3.3 .cdResult files as input to LipiDex 2 Peak Finder.

name: compound-filter-table-export
description: Use when a Pickaxe expansion generation has applied a similarity cutoff or similarity sampling filter and you must persist the retained compounds with per-compound maximum-similarity scores and filter settings as a reusable table.

name: compound-fingerprint-generation
description: Use when building an ANN that maps binned MS/MS spectra to compound fingerprints, or when swapping a baseline fingerprint representation (e.g. MACCS/FP3/FP4) for an alternative such as RDKit topological fingerprints.

name: compound-fragmentation-entropy-quality-screening
description: Use when preparing MS/MS spectra (e.g. dilution-series or reference-library .msp files) for denoising or spectral matching, and you must exclude compounds whose spectra lack sufficient genuine fragment ions to support similarity comparisons.

name: compound-growth-measurement-across-expansion-generations
description: Use when planning or characterizing a rule-based network expansion and you need per-generation compound/reaction counts plus runtime measurements to decide how many generations or cutoffs are tractable.

name: compound-identification-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when you must quantify top-hit compound identification accuracy of an in silico MS2C tool on a labeled benchmark (e.g. CASMI 2016 category 3, 208 compounds) and compare it against prior versions or competing tools.

name: compound-identification-recall-metrics
description: Use when evaluating compound identification accuracy of a spectral library search against measured electron ionization mass spectra, especially for molecules beyond a reference library, using recall@k metrics.

name: compound-identification-reliability-scoring
description: Use when you have MS2 peak lists that need vetting before metabolite annotation/identification and you need a per-spectrum reliability verdict plus a numeric quality score.

name: compound-identifier-mapping
description: Use when a user-supplied compound list uses heterogeneous names or synonyms and must be mapped to standardized cross-database identifiers (PubChem CID, InChIKey, KEGG, ChEBI, HMDB, DrugBank) before downstream analysis.

name: compound-identifier-mapping-to-kegg
description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics dataset holds compound names that must be mapped to KEGG compound identifiers before ORA against KEGG release 96 human pathway sets.

name: compound-identity-collision-handling-smiles-vs-formula
description: Use when a metabolite annotation search returns multiple compounds at one m/z — e.g. identically-named or same-formula hits — and you must decide whether rows represent distinct structures or merely the same molecular formula before ranking or exporting annotation tables.

name: compound-identity-decontamination
description: Use when a GC-MS library-hit table contains tentative Compound.Name entries with varying Match.Factor values and you must drop unreliable IDs (no strong cross-sample match, no PubChem record, or no canonical SMILES) before aggregating Component.Area across samples.

name: compound-input-csv-preparation
description: Use when a batch of compounds must be formatted for FIORA spectral prediction (e.g. test compound lists for benchmarking against CFM-ID/ICEBERG, or augmenting spectral libraries) and an fiora-predict-compatible CSV is needed.

name: compound-label-transfer-between-nmr-experiments
description: Use when raw 13C-JRES spectra from 13C-labeled samples must be annotated using compound networks already identified from INADEQUATE spectra in preceding PyINETA steps.

name: compound-level-data-split-stratification
description: Use when a dataset contains multiple spectra (e.g., EI-MS and ESI-MS/MS from MassBank) per compound and a classifier such as Random Forest must be evaluated without compound-level spectral leakage.

name: compound-level-vote-aggregation-across-studies
description: Use when input metabolomics studies report only the compound identifier and a trend label (up-regulated/down-regulated/no trend) rather than p-values, fold-changes, or variance, and a cross-study qualitative meta-analysis per compound is needed.

name: compound-list-metfrag-preparation
description: Use when a validated Shinyscreen compound list (compound list-based screening entries carrying molecular formula and/or SMILES) must be converted into a MetFrag-consumable candidate CSV with precursor ion masses for a chosen adduct.

name: compound-list-precursor-mass-calculation
description: Use when a validated compound list (CSV) plus a high-resolution mzML file must be converted into a set of precursor ion masses for extraction, and no explicit precursor m/z column is supplied.

name: compound-list-structural-field-validation
description: Use when preparing a compound list (CSV) for Shinyscreen screening: target/suspect rows must carry a molecular formula or SMILES, non-target rows must carry a precursor m/z.

name: compound-mass-reference-matching
description: Use when a CAMERA-annotated LC/MS feature list must be compared to a reference compound list (e.g. MM39) to count correctly extracted molecular masses per ion mode.

name: compound-mass-window-filtering
description: Use when retrieving candidate molecules from a large chemical database (e.g. PubChem) by precursor m/z and you need to quantify or exploit how a high-accuracy ppm mass window narrows the candidate list.

name: compound-match-ppm-error-prioritization
description: Use when you have a short list of statistically significant m/z values (e.g. t-test hits at 264, 308, 441, 561 m/z) and must rank candidate compound matches from a built database such as HMDB by isotope/adduct status and ppm error.

name: compound-metadata-template-parsing
description: Use when a batch list of compounds must be imported into a PeakForest database from the supplementary compound-import template (Online Resource 2), where common name, InChI and InChIKey are mandatory per row.

name: compound-molecular-weight-filtering
description: Use when preparing starting-compound sets (e.g. KEGG, EcoCyc, YMDB SMILES/CSV) for a Pickaxe/MINE-Database expansion and you need to constrain network size by compound molecular weight before rule application.

name: compound-name-formula-mass-identifier-linking
description: Use when a mass spectral library (e.g. the GNPS ALL_GNPS.json file, 154,820 spectra) contains spectra lacking InChIKey annotations and you need structural identifiers for downstream structure-based analyses.

name: compound-name-harmonization
description: Use when a metabolomics meta-analysis input table contains mixed identifier types or compound synonyms across contributing studies, causing the same compound to appear as multiple rows with split vote counts.

name: compound-name-mass-synthetic-data-generation
description: Use when benchmarking TurboPutative's end-to-end processing time against input table size, or when synthetic compound-name/mass tables in TurboPutative's input format are needed to probe runtime scaling in the 500–30,000-row range.

name: compound-name-to-smiles-derivation
description: Use when library spectra carry only a compound name (no SMILES/InChI) and machine-readable structures must be recovered, e.g. many GNPS-library annotations are compound names without SMILES.

name: compound-overlap-exclusion-across-spectral-libraries
description: Use when evaluating a spectral-prediction model on an external public library (e.g., MoNA Q-TOF) while the model was trained on licensed libraries (Agilent PCDL/NIST20) and train/test overlap must be eliminated.

name: compound-pathway-size-filtering
description: Use when building ORA inputs for metabolomics: after harmonising metabolite identifiers to KEGG, Reactome (ChEBI), or BioCyc identifiers, before running the right-tailed Fisher's exact test per pathway.

name: compound-peak-tracking
description: Use when you have mzML/mzXML/mzData files from untargeted MS-based metabolomics and a list of m/z and RT pairs (e.g. from a long-term QC pool like MetNexs) and need to track compound peaks across batches to expose RT or intensity drift.

name: compound-record-grouping-by-instrument-class
description: Use when handling multiple ESI-MS2 MassBank records of the same compound measured at different collision energies and you need to partition records into per-compound, per-instrument-class groups before spectrum merging.

name: compound-redundancy-quantification
description: Use when multiple OMSL files (e.g., GNPS .MGF, MoNA .MSP, MassBank, MS-Dial-VS17) have been integrated or are being compared and you need the fraction of compounds covered by more than one library versus single-library exclusives.

name: compound-retrieval-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when comparing C2MS spectrum-prediction models (e.g. FraGNNet-D4, ICEBERG, MassFormer, NEIMS) on a held-out MS/MS test set and you need retrieval-based compound identification accuracy rather than raw prediction error.

name: compound-score-integration
description: Use when a peak (precursor m/z, RT, MS/MS spectrum) must be scored against candidate metabolite annotations, e.g. reproducing reported annotation scores like the sinapate example at m/z 385.1118, RT 1.27 min in negative mode.

name: compound-spectra-data-model-mapping
description: Use when a laboratory needs to ingest LC-MS/MS (or NMR) spectra with their metadata into a local PeakForest database via the prefilled spreadsheet import template, associating each spectrum with a compound and a biological matrix such as human urine.

name: compound-spectra-deisotoping-annotation
description: Use when an XCMS feature table from LC/MS or UPLC/ESI-QTOFMS data must be grouped into compound spectra, deisotoped, and annotated with ion species before downstream screens such as stable-isotope label difference searches.

name: compound-standards-matching-inchikey
description: Use when computing detected vs. correctly annotated compound rates by matching tool-reported identifications against a known standards list via exact InChIKey plus RT (<20 s) and mass (5 ppm) criteria.

name: compound-structure-coverage-tallying
description: Use when you need to measure how many biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) entries carry compound structural data (SMILES) and how these compounds are cross-linked to external structure databases.

name: compound-structure-distance-computation
description: Use when you need a compound-vs-compound structural distance matrix from a reference set (e.g. MIBiG release 1.3) to benchmark or weight-cluster BGC distances such as BiG-SCAPE's Jaccard, Adjacency Index and Domain Sequence Similarity components.

name: compound-structure-standardization
description: Use when a metadata sheet of small-molecule samples needs a shared template structure with same column names, standardized structures, and unique sample ids before spectral-library or acquisition work.

name: compound-superclass-annotation
description: Use when per-compound spectral prediction quality (e.g., spectral_sqrt_cosine from fiora-eval) must be grouped by chemical class, or when graph embeddings must be colored by superclass for UMAP visualization.

name: compound-target-interaction-mapping
description: Use when a protein-protein or gene network in Cytoscape must be enriched with drug/compound-target edges from ChEMBL linksets, e.g. to annotate disease-gene networks with pharmacological interactions.

name: compound-to-taxon-mapping
description: Use when you have GNPS library or experimental MS/MS spectra (as .mgf entries or USIs) of candidate microbial metabolites and need to determine which microbial taxa they associate with, or whether they appear in non-microbial sources like human cell lines.

name: compression-file-size-benchmark-tabulation
description: Decision support for choosing a mass-spectrometry storage format when you need to compare file sizes (and optionally decode cost) of a lossy-precision format like Aird against lossless reference formats (mzML, mgf, mz5) and the original vendor RAW across multiple public datasets.

name: compression-ratio-benchmarking
description: Use when converting vendor MRM chromatograms to a compressed format (e.g., Aird) and you must quantify storage savings versus vendor and mzML files, or when implementing RT delta + FastPFor + ZSTD encoding.

name: compression-ratio-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify whether a specialized compressor (ZDPD/Stack-ZDPD vs Zlib, or Brotli/Snappy/Zstd alternatives) actually beats a general-purpose baseline on your MS data arrays, in bytes and decode speed.

name: computation-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when measuring how PyCoMo community model construction, FBA, and exchange-metabolite/cross-feeding analysis runtimes scale with community size on AGORA SBML models up to 40 members.

name: computation-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing computational cost of an MSI analysis between raw and peak-picked spectra, or when documenting runtime of a Cardinal computation as evidence that pre-processing yields a speedup.

name: computation-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing wall-clock runtimes of alternative NetGSA computational variants (NetGSA.REHE.Cl, NetGSA.REHE, NetGSA.REML.All) on cancer gene expression datasets, or when validating that an overhauled pipeline meets a runtime budget (minutes on a personal computer).

name: computation-time-and-memory-profiling
description: Use when comparing computational efficiency of network-construction tools on feature abundance matrices (e.g., 50–1,000 features) and you need defensible median elapsed-time and memory measurements per package.

name: computation-time-profiling
description: Decision support for selecting an LC-MS annotation algorithm based on computation time: time each annotator on identical filtered peak lists across multiple assays and compare per-dataset runtimes.

name: computational-efficiency-qualitative-ranking
description: Use when a low-resolution MSI composite/cluster image must be resampled to the pixel dimensions of a co-registered H&E image and a defensible choice among interpolation kernels (nearest neighbor, bilinear, bicubic, Lanczos) is needed.

name: computational-performance-validation
description: Use when a paper reports a concrete computational throughput or runtime figure (e.g. 60,000 transition pairs/sec) and you must reproduce or sanity-check that number on available hardware before trusting the tool at scale.

name: computational-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when quantifying the computational-efficiency gain of an updated annotation pipeline over its predecessor, e.g. MetDNA3 vs MetDNA2 runtimes (77 min vs 1082 min per dataset) over the same 12 datasets.

name: computational-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when validating that a sample-vectorization or matrix-building step (e.g., MEMO MS2 fingerprinting of a 1,600+ extract dataset) completes within reported computational-time bounds on commodity hardware.

name: computational-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when re-running a published computational pipeline (e.g. compareMS2 pairwise distance calculations over PXD034932 serum datasets) and you need a measured runtime to compare against the paper's reported wall-clock time on its reference hardware.

name: computational-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing wall-clock runtime of pathway enrichment tools (e.g., EnrichMet vs MetaboAnalystR vs FELLA) on the same metabolite list to quantify computational efficiency claims.

name: computational-runtime-comparison-reporting
description: Use when a paper claims computational feasibility of a pipeline (e.g., 'not prohibitively so') and you need to reproduce or report per-stage runtimes on a defined input, such as one MS/MS sample with 300 Mass2Motifs.

name: computational-runtime-measurement
description: Use when comparing algorithmic efficiency of spectrum clustering tools (e.g. falcon vs msCRUSH vs brute-force pairwise comparison) and you need concrete runtime and per-spectrum comparison counts on a large public MS/MS dataset.

name: computational-runtime-profiling
description: Use when you need to quantify whether an iterative reaction-rule network expansion (e.g., Pickaxe generations) grows exponentially in compounds/reactions and when its runtime or memory cost becomes prohibitive.

name: computational-runtime-scaling-analysis
description: Use when comparing computational cost of normalization methods (rLOESS, rGAM, tGAM, QC-RLSC, QC-RSC) across targeted (53-compound) and untargeted (8913-feature) metabolomics datasets, or when deciding whether parallelization over cores is needed to keep normalization tractable.

name: compute-converter-integration-in-msmetaenhancer
description: Use when annotating .msp mass spectral library records that already carry SMILES (or similar existing metadata) and a derived attribute such as molecular weight should be computed locally instead of querying external services.

name: compute-performance-visualization
description: Use when you must verify a tool's compute scaling: clustering progressively larger MGF subsets and plotting runtime versus number of spectra to check for the near-linear trend.

name: concentration-column-numeric-validation
description: Use when a metabolomics table (.csv or .xlsx) has been uploaded to Viime and designated concentration columns must be checked for non-numeric values before imputation, normalization, or analysis can proceed.

name: concentration-error-metric-computation
description: Use when MCF-based concentration reconstruction (mcfNMR setup A/B/C) has produced predicted concentrations c_k for a mixture of known composition and you must quantify reconstruction accuracy via mean relative error across compounds, sweeping assignment radius r to locate the optimum.

name: concentration-inference-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating how accurate an absolute-concentration inference pipeline is on simulated or real time-course metabolomics data — i.e. when you need per-model accuracy metrics at defined kinetic-knowledge levels rather than just qualitative 'it works' claims.

name: concentration-inference-significance-assessment
description: Use when assessing whether inferred absolute concentrations from relative-abundance time-course GC-MS metabolomics data remain significant under realistic experimental conditions — noise (CoV 5–15%) and sparser timepoint sampling (50→15) — rather than on clean simulated data.

name: concentration-method-comparison-statistics
description: Use when two or more drift-correction or quantification strategies have produced concentration tables for the same targeted LC-MS/MS compounds and you need to measure their agreement (slopes ≈ 1 vs ≠ 1, bias, LoA) or attribute differences to matrix effects.

name: concentration-range-sigma-estimation
description: Use when generating simulated metabolite concentrations from HMDB 5.0 concentration ranges (mean and SD) and a discrete outcome such as case-control status, where each metabolite's range must be converted into a standard deviation before sampling.

name: concordance-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when concordance_scores.csv (Cohen's kappa and Pearson values with p-values and adjusted p-values) is available and reactions must be classified by regulatory class and visualized as RPS-vs-RAS and RPS-vs-FFD heatmaps matching Fig 4.

name: conda-environment-dependency-setup
description: Use when a published tool's README specifies a conda environment with pinned Python version and channel configuration (defaults, bioconda, conda-forge, plus extra channels like etetoolkit) that must be created before running the tool's pipeline.

name: conda-environment-reproducibility
description: Use when reproducing the MetaboliteChat checkpoint evaluation or training pipeline and a Python 3.9+ environment matching the authors' environment.yml must be instantiated before running demo.sh or train.py.

name: condition-grouped-metabolomics-data-handling
description: Use when a metabolite intensity matrix must be organized by condition group and converted into per-condition covariance matrices as the numeric substrate for Jacobian network inference in MInfer.

name: condition-wise-effect-size-comparison
description: Use when a lipid abundance matrix spans multiple stimulation conditions (e.g. 0.01/1 U/mL thrombin, 1/5 µg/mL CRP) plus an unstimulated control, and the goal is to rank which lipid classes respond to stimulation and which stimulus is the stronger regulator.

name: condition-wise-state-proportion-analysis
description: Use when single cells have already been clustered into metabolic states and you need per-condition state fractions to test whether a perturbation (e.g. IL-17A inflammation, TPCA-1 treatment) changes the composition of a cell population.

name: conditional-generation-language-model-training
description: Use when pretraining a sequence-to-sequence generative model on paired structured representations (e.g., 4096-bit Morgan fingerprint tokens and SELFIES strings) to learn cross-modal conditional generation before downstream fine-tuning.

name: conditional-heritability-enrichment-across-tissues
description: Use when a tissue-specific gene-set annotation shows significant LDSC heritability enrichment and you must test whether that signal is independent of overlapping gene sets from other tissues.

name: conditional-vae-latent-embedding-extraction
description: Use when you have aligned, KNN-reassigned joint ST-SM AnnData (batch-biased SVGs/SVMs already removed) and need a single fused embedding that corrects batch effects across samples while fusing transcriptomic and metabolomic modalities.

name: conditional-vae-model-training
description: Use when multiple spatial metabolomics (SM) or paired ST-SM AnnData samples have been QC-filtered and batch-corrected preprocessing is done, and you need cross-sample/cross-modal latent integration embeddings.

name: confidence-interval-estimation-from-resamples
description: Use when a metabolite–phenotype point estimate (e.g. confounder-adjusted Spearman correlation with BMI) from an MWAS model needs uncertainty quantification or validation via subject-level resampling with replacement.

name: confidence-interval-reporting
description: Use when exposure predictions from a statistical model (e.g., SEEM consensus exposure estimates over the HExpMetDB chemical list) must be reported per substance with median values, 95% CI bounds, and coverage fractions rather than point estimates alone.

name: confidence-level-annotation-interpretation
description: Use when interpreting LC-HRMS/MS annotation outputs for PFAS (e.g., AFFF samples) where suspect-level (B/B−) calls must be benchmarked against level-A assignments or against vendor formula confirmation (Agilent MassHunter Find-by-Formula).

name: confidence-model-training
description: Use when GNN-predicted CCS values (e.g. Mol2CCS outputs on METLIN-CCS or CCSBase) must be filtered for reliability, and per-prediction absolute relative error is available on a labeled subset to train a confidence classifier.

name: confidence-score-calibration-binning
description: Use when a frequency- or likelihood-based prioritization score (e.g. DeepMet sampling frequency given an exact mass within ±10 ppm) must be shown to be calibrated before being trusted for metabolite annotation or prospective discovery.

name: confidence-score-fdr-estimation
description: Use when in-silico structure annotations (e.g. CSI:FingerID candidate rankings on LC–MS/MS data) must be ranked by confidence and reported at a controlled false discovery rate, especially for structures absent from spectral libraries.

name: confidence-score-ranking-and-rescoring
description: Use when you have multiple candidate formulas per MS/MS spectrum and need to rank them by a learned confidence score to pick the correct formula, e.g., after FIDDLE prediction plus candidate-formula generation on Q-TOF or Orbitrap spectra.

name: confocal-image-background-correction
description: Use when raw two-color confocal images (e.g., CFP/YFP channels excited at 458/514 nm on a Zeiss LSM 510) must be background-corrected before automatic colocalization thresholding, block-scrambling randomization, or 2D-histogram proportion analysis.

name: confocal-image-colocalization-analysis
description: Use when analyzing two-channel (e.g., CFP/YFP) 3D confocal stacks of cells to decide whether two proteins truly colocalize beyond random overlap and to quantify it objectively without a manually chosen intensity threshold.

name: conformation-generation-and-filtering
description: Use when predicting CCS values from SMILES structures for protonated/deprotonated/neutral molecular states of conformationally flexible metabolites, where a structurally distinct conformer ensemble must be prepared before QM optimization and CCS calculation.

name: conformational-ensemble-interpretation
description: Use when a ccs.txt output from the Snakemake CCS workflow (ensemble or ensemble_fast folder) exists and the goal is to judge whether ensemble averaging outperforms the global-minimum conformer against experimental TWIMS CCS values.

name: conformer-protomer-entry-handling
description: Use when building LC-IM-MS (drift tube) database entries where one molecular formula yields chromatographically separated isomers or multiple IM-separated ion species (protomers/conformers) that must each become its own database entry.

name: confusion-matrix-analysis
description: Use when evaluating classification performance of the DenseNet121 ensemble on raw LC-MS (.npy/.mzML) test samples — especially when comparing full-data vs biomarker-filtered (PC>1/3/8, 3 ppm) models via Fig. 4f-style ablation.

name: confusion-matrix-and-auc-visualization
description: Use when evaluating a trained DeepMSProfiler (DenseNet121 ensemble) classifier on a held-out LC-MS test split and you need ROC/AUC curves and a per-class confusion matrix to confirm accuracy, precision, recall, F1, and AUC.

name: confusion-matrix-auc-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when semi-synthetic multi-omics data contain a known enriched target pathway and you need a quantitative detection benchmark (confusion-matrix AUC) over pathway importance statistics across effect sizes.

name: confusion-matrix-evaluation
description: Use when comparing automated peak-filtering calls to manual peak-quality labels (e.g. Good/Bad Peak clicks) on LC-MS standard library peaks to quantify filtering precision, recall, and F1.

name: confusion-matrix-evaluation-of-diagnostic-accuracy
description: Use when an end-to-end LC-MS metabolomics classifier must be validated on held-out testing samples and its per-class accuracy visualized as a confusion matrix.

name: confusion-matrix-metric-computation
description: Use when a classification model fitted on metabolomics/proteomics feature data needs external validation on held-out test samples, and confusion matrix, accuracy and error rate must be reported without training-set leakage.

name: confusion-matrix-metric-derivation
description: Use when you have a trained multi-class classifier's confusion matrix (e.g., DeepSAT's 59 NPClassifier superclass predictions on 143,467 HSQC spectra) and need per-class precision/recall/F1 to diagnose weak classes.

name: confusion-matrix-metrics-reproduction
description: Use when validating a re-trained DeepMSProfiler model on an independent test split of raw LC-MS data and you need to confirm reported accuracy/precision/recall/F1 and reproduce confusion_matrix.svg.

name: confusion-matrix-performance-analysis
description: Use when a probabilistic pixel-based classifier has been applied to a labeled withheld test set (e.g., 9,798 normal and 2,861 tumor MALDI FT-ICR MSI spectra) and you must quantify accuracy, ROC AUC, and runtime against a benchmark such as SVM.

name: conjugate-base-acid-compound-harmonization
description: Use when a merged metabolite table keyed by full 27-character InChIKeys contains both protonated and deprotonated forms of the same compound (identical first-14-character molecular-skeleton block) and must be deduplicated before attribute retrieval.

name: connected-component-feature-detection
description: Use when a random scattered-sample optical image (flatbed scanner or cell phone camera, samples >300 μm) must be converted into a list of discrete target coordinates with per-region morphological measurements before MALDI-TOF MS geometry generation.

name: connected-component-graph-construction-for-ms-features
description: Use when you have replicate mzML-derived peak lists or CSV feature tables from multiple analytical runs and need to combine signals with consistent m/z and RT values into replicated/basketed features before scoring.

name: connected-component-partitioning
description: Use when a gene-gene edge list yields a 0-1 adjacency matrix too large for weighted adjacency estimation and you need connected-component decomposition plus community detection capped at 1,000 genes per cluster.

name: connected-component-statistics-computation
description: Use when you have built an approximate k-NN molecular network (e.g. the DreaMS Atlas 3-NN graph over ~34M spectra) and need to quantify its connectivity and distance to annotated nodes.

name: connectivity-matrix-topology-feature-engineering
description: Use when retraining or extending a competitive-fragmentation-model predictor on QTOF ESI-MS/MS training sets (e.g. Metlin [M+H]+/[M-H]- at 10/20/40 eV) and you need bond-topology-aware fragment features, or when running component-ablation to quantify topology-feature contribution.

name: consecutive-run-violation-detection
description: Use when an intra-batch randomized injection-order sequence (e.g., treatment vs placebo) has been produced by block randomization with block size 2 and you must verify the no-three-consecutive-same-group guarantee before export.

name: consensus-annotation-aggregation
description: Use when untargeted MS/MS ion features annotated via GNPS feature-based molecular networking plus a CANOPUS summary file must be fused into consensus ClassyFire (or NPClassifier) labels with confidence thresholds, or when consensus chemical-class profiles must be clustered across species/samples.

name: consensus-annotation-propagation
description: Use when a GNPS feature-based molecular networking job has both spectral library matches (DBResult/Node_info) and SIRIUS/CANOPUS canopus_summary.tsv predictions, and you need consensus chemical class annotations for ion features and whole subnetworks.

name: consensus-chemical-classification-aggregation
description: Use when a GNPS FBMN task plus a CANOPUS canopus_summary.tsv must be converted into subnetwork-level consensus superclass/class/subclass annotations (ChemOnt) to compare compositional profiles (e.g., organic acids vs organoheterocycles) across organisms or treatments.

name: consensus-classification-propagation
description: Use when untargeted LC-MS/MS feature-based molecular networking data has both GNPS library matches and SIRIUS/CANOPUS in silico class predictions, and you need consistent class annotations propagated to entire subnetworks.

name: consensus-clustering-kernel-construction
description: Use when integrating multi-omics datasets (e.g. copy number, methylation, mRNA, miRNA, protein layers) for clustering and per-layer similarity kernels are needed as inputs to KLIC or MKL.

name: consensus-clustering-module-detection
description: Use when you have a microbe-by-metabolite interaction/attribution score matrix from MiMeNet and want to group features with shared interaction patterns into modules and build a module-level network.

name: consensus-clustering-of-metabolic-networks
description: Use when a two-condition metabolomics/lipidomics dataset has already been modeled as glasso partial-correlation networks (DNEAobject with estimated networks) and you need to partition the edge-weighted graph into metabolic modules for downstream enrichment testing.

name: consensus-feature-averaging
description: Use when raw centroided mzML-derived peak lists (one CSV per replicate injection) must be reduced to a single basketed feature table of unique MS features before bioactivity integration in NP Analyst.

name: consensus-feature-linking
description: Use when you have RT-aligned, centroided mzML-derived feature maps from multiple LC-MS/MS samples and need a single consensus feature table linking each feature's m/z, RT, adduct and per-sample intensities.

name: consensus-peak-multiple-spectrum-alignment
description: Use when you need consensus/aligned peaks across multiple MS/MS spectra of one molecular network component (e.g., GNPS2 FBMN family) to find shared fragments and m/z-shifted peaks from modifications, beyond pairwise cosine.

name: consensus-peak-picking-with-ppm-tolerance
description: Use when you have pixel-level DESI-MSI data along a tissue axis (e.g. maize root sections) and need a per-sample list of m/z signatures from untargeted spectra.

name: consensus-peak-set-identification
description: Use when a molecular family (e.g. ~80 rhamnolipid or albicidin MS/MS spectra from GNPS2) needs a global peak alignment that explains which consensus peaks cause spectra to cluster, rather than only pairwise cosine scores.

name: consensus-peak-set-identification-across-adduct-spectra
description: Use when several MS/MS spectra of the same metabolite with different adducts or charge carriers (e.g., [M+H]+, [M+Na]+, water-loss in-source fragments) are available from a GNPS2 molecular networking task and you need shared/consensus fragment peaks to argue fragmentation consistency.

name: consensus-reference-averaging
description: Use when a calculated property (e.g. Boltzmann-average CCS from ccs.txt) must be validated against two independent experimental reference sets and a consensus of both, with a percent-error tolerance.

name: consensus-spectra-clustering-cleaning
description: Use when raw LC–MS/MS per-sample MGF files contain redundant, noisy, or duplicate MS2 spectra (e.g., multiple scans of the same precursor, isotopes, or media/blank signals) that must be collapsed into one cleaned consensus spectrum per compound before annotation or BCC ranking.

name: consensus-spectra-library-matching
description: Use when consensus spectra have been obtained from GC × GC–MS deconvolution (e.g. GcDUO Module III DuoResults with $cor_spectra) and each peak feature must be assigned a compound identity against an MSP library.

name: consensus-spectrum-candidate-ranking
description: Use when a molecule has multiple query MS/MS spectra (e.g. three collision-energy levels from MZmine3 feature extraction) and you need a single ranked candidate list rather than per-spectrum rankings.

name: consensus-spectrum-construction
description: Use when a molecule has multiple constituent MS/MS spectra (e.g., several collision energies in MassSpecGym) and you need one aggregate query view for candidate ranking instead of rank-then-aggregate scoring.

name: consensus-spectrum-dereplication
description: Use when clustered MS2 spectra from LC–MS/MS samples must be dereplicated into non-redundant consensus spectra while keeping isomers separated, e.g. NP3 MS Workflow Cleaning steps 3–5 on per-sample MGF input.

name: consensus-spectrum-embedding-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking metabolite annotation models on MassSpecGym and you need to compare aggregate-then-rank (consensus spectrum) versus rank-then-aggregate (individual spectra) candidate retrieval, reporting rank@1 per ranking view and candidate condition.

name: consensus-spectrum-generation
description: Use when raw MS2 peak lists (.mzXML/.mzML) must be deduplicated into consensus spectra before molecular networking or library search, and the Minimum Cluster Size and precursor mass tolerance need to be justified.

name: conservative-fold-change-aggregation
description: Use when a broad ontology-backed comparison (e.g. 'Digestive Tract' vs 'Bacteria') expands into multiple metadata-combination contrasts and each compound needs one aggregated p-value and one fold-change instead of many pairwise results.

name: conservative-pvalue-foldchange-aggregation
description: Decision support for ontologically grouped differential analysis (OGDA) queries in BinDiscover where a broad term (e.g. 'digestive tract') expands to many metadata combinations and each compound yields multiple pairwise Welch t-test results that must be condensed into one conservative call.

name: constant-zero-row-flagging-per-group
description: Use when a lipidomic data matrix (CSV/TXT with lipid names as row index and samples as columns) must be validated before upload to Lipid One 2.0, e.g. to catch duplicated lipid names and all-zero or zero-variance rows within each experimental group before the tool rejects the upload.

name: constraint-based-community-model-evaluation
description: Use when you have gap-filled community member GEMs (e.g., COMMIT-output SBML models) plus a community medium, and need to predict or cross-validate pairwise cross-feeding interactions and community interaction potential.

name: constraint-based-flux-balance-analysis-of-community-models
description: Use when you have gap-filled SBML or Matlab community GEMs and need to identify which extracellular metabolites are exchanged among members and which members depend on which cross-feeding metabolites.

name: constraint-based-flux-perturbation-analysis
description: Use when an integrated host–virus genome-scale metabolic model (SBML) is available and you need to quantify host-optimum vs virus-optimum growth rates, or test whether maximizing viral biomass renders the host cell non-viable.

name: constraint-based-flux-sampling
description: Use when you have cell-relative SBML (or irreversible mat) constraint-based models and need empirical flux distributions to test which reactions differ between samples, rather than relying on a single FBA optimum.

name: constraint-based-flux-sampling-of-cell-relative-models
description: Use when you have cell-relative metabolic models (built from a generic model plus RAS and extracellular-flux constraints) and need per-reaction, pairwise flux-difference classifications to feed FFD-vs-RPS concordance scoring.

name: constraint-based-gap-filling
description: Use when draft genome-scale metabolic reconstructions of a multi-species community fail to produce biomass on a minimal medium and gap filling must respect community composition and metabolite permeability/leakage.

name: constraint-based-metabolic-modeling
description: Use when combining genome-scale member models (SBML) into a community model where flux bounds must vary with member abundance, and the SBML/openCOBRA format requires bounds to be represented implicitly rather than as variable parameters.

name: constraint-based-metabolic-modeling
description: Use when draft genome-scale metabolic reconstructions (SBML) must be made functional on a defined minimal medium via gap filling, then assessed with memote and used for FBA/community interaction analysis.

name: constraint-scenario-comparison-analysis
description: Use when randomSampling CSVs exist for multiple cell-relative models under several constraint configurations and the goal is to test whether combined constraints (medium + YSI + RAS) yield better inter-model separation of sampled feasible flux distributions than single-constraint scenarios.

name: containerized-pipeline-configuration
description: Use when running an LC-HRMS metabolomics pipeline (.mzML/.abf inputs) under Nextflow where MS-DIAL and MS-FLO must execute in containers on a local machine or HPC/Slurm environment, or when diagnosing container profile, resource-limit, or configuration-file setup issues.

name: containerized-pipeline-deployment-with-docker
description: Use when an instrument PC or server must run QC4Metabolomics's continuously running file-ingestion process and Shiny web dashboard, especially when R, Shiny, renv, xcms, ggplot2/plotly, and mariaDB would otherwise need local installation.

name: containerized-pipeline-execution-docker-singularity
description: Use when processing raw LC-HRMS metabolomics files (.mzML or .abf) with MS-DIAL and MS-FLO and you need containerized, reproducible execution locally or on Slurm-based HPC.

name: containerized-pipeline-reproducibility-testing
description: Use when validating that a containerized Nextflow LC-MS metabolomics pipeline (e.g. .mzML inputs through MS-DIAL and MS-FLO) yields identical run-to-run outputs, or when reproducing a paper's cross-platform consistency claim.

name: contaminant-feature-filtering
description: Use when an Asari-derived feature table (TSV) contains features driven by background ions or contaminants and sample metadata distinguishes blank injections (e.g. 'Blank' vs 'Unknown' sample_type) so features can be filtered by sample-vs-blank intensity ratio.

name: contaminant-feature-flagging
description: Use when raw untargeted metabolomics or lipidomics feature-intensity tables contain procedural-blank injections alongside real samples, and features enriched in blanks must be flagged as background contaminants before signal-drift or RSD filtering.

name: contaminant-ion-screening-in-ms-data
description: Use when mzML/mzXML/mzData files from untargeted MS-based metabolomics acquisition must be checked for known background contaminants — e.g. to diagnose carryover, contamination from labware, or user-defined compound exposure.

name: contaminant-peak-detection
description: Use when monitoring background contaminants (e.g. from solvents or sample carryover) across pooled-QC injections in an mzML-based untargeted metabolomics run, where you want time-series, per-sample composition, or heatmap views of contaminant levels.

name: contaminant-source-tracking-prediction
description: Use when HRMS feature data from known contaminant sources (e.g., roadway runoff) mixed at known dilutions is available and the goal is to predict source contribution in unknown mixed environmental samples.

name: contig-to-reference-blast-alignment
description: Use when assembled de novo contigs (e.g. from ALPS over Casanovo predictions) must be scored against a reference antibody sequence to compute per-chain coverage and amino-acid accuracy, including CDR-level evaluation.

name: contingency-table-construction
description: Use when two annotation or prediction methods have been run on the same query spectra set and you need to quantify overlap vs. uniqueness of correct results to support a complementarity claim.

name: contingency-table-construction-from-identification-results
description: Decision support for judging whether DeepMASS identifications can be trusted for an unknown: use when you have identification results (e.g. LOOCV on 662 KEGG compounds or external biomarker tests) and need to tabulate validity against presence of a structure-related metabolite in the database.

name: contingency-table-construction-oncogene-subgroups
description: Use when binary or k-means-segregated oncogene activation subgroups (phosphoAKT1-high/low crossed with MYC-high/low) must be tested for association with ordinal clinical variables such as Gleason grade or pathologic stage.

name: continuous-outcome-metabolomics-prediction
description: Use when predicting a continuous phenotypic outcome (e.g. clinically measured bilirubin in serum) from multi-assay LC-MS metabolomics feature tables and you need cross-assay feature importance and significance calls.

name: continuous-outcome-spectra-group-generation
description: Use when developing or benchmarking a metabolomics algorithm (e.g. PCA, regression) that requires many simulated spectra with a continuous covariate, and no real spectra with known ground-truth concentrations are available.

name: continuous-per-ion-fdr-computation
description: Use when you have METASPACE-ML prediction scores for target ions and sampled decoy ions with associated standard deviations (SD), and need per-ion continuous FDR confidence values rather than a single thresholded FDR cutoff.

name: contrast-level-statistics-integration
description: Use when msFeaST pipeline outputs need to be integrated and serialized into a single .json file for interactive dashboard consumption.

name: contrast-mode-false-positive-negative-highlighting
description: Use when comparing one profiler's taxonomic profile against a known ground truth (e.g., a CAMI marine sample) and you need to see exactly which taxa are false positives/false negatives rather than relying on F1 or L1 scores alone.

name: contrastive-learning-ablation
description: Use when reproducing or adapting the FIDDLE ablation study to measure how spectrum noise augmentation, contrastive loss, and post-processing (candidate generation + rescore ranking) each affect top-1/top-5 formula accuracy, missed-atom distributions, and confidence-score ROC AUC.

name: contrastive-learning-model-training
description: Use when you need annotation-free dense vector representations of ion images from preprocessed MSI pixel-by-ion matrices for downstream colocalized-ion or isotope-ion retrieval tasks.

name: contrastive-pair-loss-model-training
description: Use when reproducing the GLEAMS embedder training procedure: you have MassIVE-KB PSM pairs (grouped per precursor charge state) and need to train a Siamese network with contrastive loss to a 32-dimensional embedding space.

name: contrastive-rank-loss-alignment
description: Use when reducing molecular hallucinations after fingerprint-conditioned generation: candidates are sampled from MS-BART and their probability mass must be shifted toward structures most Tanimoto-similar to the reference.

name: contrastive-scaffold-retrieval-from-mass-spectra
description: Use when an MS/MS spectrum must be assigned a scaffold (not a full structure) from a candidate set — e.g. before scaffold-conditioned de novo generation, or to compute Scaffold Prediction Accuracy (SPA) on NIST23, CANOPUS, or MassSpecGym.

name: contrastive-view-generation
description: Use when implementing self-supervised contrastive learning on mass spectrometry imaging ion images and you need modality-specific augmented positive pairs that respect MSI characteristics (Poisson-distributed ion abundance and missing-value patterns).

name: contribution-heatmap-peak-filtering
description: Use when a trained DeepMSProfiler model has produced ensemble_RISE.npy heatmaps and you must select the disease-contributing m/z peaks for metabolite annotation and metabolite-protein network reconstruction.

name: control-chart-limit-calculation
description: Use when pooled QC samples are injected at regular intervals in a sequence and you need to flag 'out-of-control' observations or signal drifts per chemical descriptor before releasing a metabolomics/lipidomics batch.

name: control-chart-variability-assessment
description: Use when validating automated preprocessing software against a manual analyst by comparing metabolite peak-area variability in repeat pooled QC samples (e.g., 420 QCs in ENANI-2019), before and after QC-based batch correction.

name: control-experiment-cross-condition-feature-tallying
description: Use when random forest regression feature importances have been generated per metabolite per feature set and you must separate robust regulator–metabolite associations from confounders driven by tissue type, culture conditions (suspension/adherent), or sample origin (primary/metastatic).

name: controlled-vocabulary-alias-mapping
description: Use when lipid annotations arrive as heterogeneous shorthand or alias terms (e.g. PC(16:0_18:2), PONPC, HETE) from different databases/programs and must be normalized to canonical, computer-processable identifiers.

name: controlled-vocabulary-catalogue-annotation
description: Use when building or extending a curated tool catalogue that must be classified and searchable via a simple controlled vocabulary, e.g. labelling metabolomics software by instrument data type (LC-MS/GC-MS/NMR) and major functionality.

name: controlled-vocabulary-classification
description: Use when a curated list of metabolomics software tools must be normalized to a controlled vocabulary of functionality category, instrumental data type, software type and MS annotation confidence level.

name: controlled-vocabulary-construction
description: Use when user-submitted freetext sample metadata must be standardized against fixed vocabularies, or when you need to construct non-overlapping term sets per metadata header and train a term-mapping model from source ontology dumps.

name: controlled-vocabulary-metadata-validation
description: Use when preparing or checking a ReDU sample-information table (gnps_metadata.tsv schema: Filename, MassIVE accession, SampleType, ...) before File Selector cohort assembly or contribution to ReDU.

name: controller-environment-orchestration
description: Use when you need to simulate a tandem MS acquisition over a set of chemical objects in ViMMS 2.0 — e.g. after generating chemicals with ChemicalMixtureCreator — and produce scan-level mzML output for a chosen controller.

name: controller-mass-spectrometer-interface-wiring
description: Use when a chemical mixture (e.g. from ChemicalMixtureCreator) and a configured controller (e.g. Top-N DDA) already exist and the goal is to execute the simulated tandem-MS acquisition and produce an mzML scan file.

name: conventional-ann-classification
description: Use when benchmarking a meta-learning or transfer-learning SCMS classifier and you need a conventional deep-learning baseline trained on the same train/validation/test splits of pretreated, peak-aligned single-cell metabolomics data.

name: conventional-risk-factor-score-construction
description: Use when building a conventional-risk-factor comparison score for mortality prediction: Cox regression on sex, BMI, SBP, cholesterol, HDL, triglycerides, creatinine, smoking, alcohol, diabetes with age as time scale.

name: conversion-benchmark-timing-measurement
description: Use when you need to measure and compare how fast different MS data conversion tools (MZA vs mzMLb vs ProteoWizard) convert the same vendor raw files (.d, .raw) to open formats.

name: convex-combination-bound-recalculation
description: Use when a host genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. RECON3D in SBML) must be modified so metabolites produced or consumed by gut microbiota models alter the host exchange-reaction lower bounds, with a tunable weight α ∈ [0,1].

name: convex-quadratic-programming-weight-estimation
description: Use when several N x N consensus/similarity kernel matrices over the same N samples must be combined via per-sample convex weights, and noisy datasets should be down-weighted relative to informative ones.

name: convolution-based-isotopic-distribution-modeling
description: Use when you need theoretical isotopic peak envelopes of a user-defined peptide sequence or chemical formula at arbitrary SIP enrichment levels (partial or full labeling), for plotting, PSM scoring, or validating proteomic SIP database-search outputs.

name: convolutional-autoencoder-training
description: Use when raw LC/MS mzML files and an XCMS-generated peak list (mz, rt columns) must be converted into learned EIC embeddings for peak curation, and no task-specific labeled training set is available for the encoder stage.

name: cooccurrence-metcalf-link-computation
description: Use when you have paired genome (antiSMASH/BiG-SCAPE GCFs) and metabolome (GNPS molecular networking) data and need to rank candidate BGC–MS/MS links per GCF by strain co-occurrence before applying class-based filtering.

name: coordinate-offset-statistics-aggregation
description: Use when you have paired files of intended target coordinates (device geometry output) and measured ablation-mark positions, and need per-mode targeting-accuracy statistics in micrometers.

name: coordinate-recovery-from-distorted-images
description: Use when target coordinates for optically guided MS are extracted from images acquired with flatbed scanners or cell phone cameras that introduce moderate lens distortion or imperfect perspective, and accurate stage coordinates are required before generating device geometry files.

name: copd-metabolomics-stratification-by-gold-stage
description: Use when reproducing or extending the real-data COPDGene metabolomics result comparing DisCo-based vs PrsCo-based effective-number-of-tests adjustment for Welch t-tests within severe COPD (GOLD 3/4) and control (GOLD 0) strata.

name: corason-conserved-core-determination
description: Use when a set of related BGCs (e.g., tauD-expansion clusters) needs a phylogeny-resolved organization beyond BiG-SCAPE GCF clustering, especially when fragmented assemblies or merged adjacent clusters split them into different GCFs.

name: core-data-model-reconstruction
description: Use when you must recover the architecture of a modular data-processing framework from source code — specifically how modules declare parameters, depend only on core types, and sequence tasks.

name: corpus-statistics-reproduction
description: Use when a task asks to reproduce or verify published corpus-level counts for the PoDP Zenodo deposit — e.g. 'how many metagenomes, genomes, and MAGs among the >2,600 genomic sources?' — by recomputing them from the archived JSON project metadata.

name: correlated-feature-pattern-scoring
description: Use when validating matched feature pairs between two untargeted LC-MS metabolomics datasets (reference and target) after matching on RT, m/z, and FI, and you need an orthogonal, annotation-free quality metric computed from each feature's correlated neighbors.

name: correlated-feature-removal-thresholding
description: Use when a continuous molecular descriptor matrix (e.g., alvaDesc descriptors for SMRT molecules) contains highly correlated features that could destabilize downstream regressors, after zero-variance features have already been dropped.

name: correlation-analysis-metabolomics-vs-transcriptomics
