description: Use when the same physical mass spectrum must be reconciled across MassBank, MoNA, GNPS, HMDB, MetaboLights, or mzCloud entries whose accession IDs differ, and a database-independent identifier is needed to confirm they refer to the same spectrum.

name: cross-dataset-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when replicating or validating a published benchmark (e.g., FSA rank#1/top-5 accuracy and runtime) across several MS/MS test datasets against reported numeric results.

name: cross-dataset-algorithm-comparison
description: Use when a new alignment or feature-correspondence method must be validated against established software on ≥2 benchmark datasets with ground-truth manual annotations, and per-dataset accuracy deltas are the target output.

name: cross-dataset-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a spectral/annotation method's accuracy claim must be validated across two or more independent test sets (e.g. NPLIB1 vs MassSpecGym) rather than a single benchmark.

name: cross-dataset-bgc-cross-referencing
description: Use when mass spectrometry identifications from multiple GNPS microbial datasets can be paired with genome mining data from the same strains and you need to validate identifications or discover novel BGC-to-molecule links.

name: cross-dataset-clustering-ordering-comparison
description: Use when you have clustered spectra from ≥2 MS/MS clustering tools on ≥2 metabolomics datasets and need MS-RT purity/N10 scores to test whether tool rankings (e.g. Falcon vs MaRaCluster) transfer across instruments.

name: cross-dataset-feature-match-audit
description: Use when two LC–MS metabolomics feature tables have already been matched (e.g., 4953 unique matches via M2S) and you must verify correctness using the subset of features annotated at MSI confidence level 2.

name: cross-dataset-feature-matching
description: Use when two peak-picked, conventionally aligned untargeted LC-MS feature tables acquired under non-identical conditions (different gradients, instruments, or laboratories) must have their overlapping features identified and concatenated.

name: cross-dataset-feature-matching
description: Use when integrating two untargeted LC-MS metabolomics peak tables (e.g. MESA reference vs Rotterdam target) that share RT, m/z, and FI dimensions but were acquired in separate runs, and you need unique feature correspondence without MS/MS or annotation-level matching.

name: cross-dataset-feature-matching-evaluation
description: Use when you have completed feature matching between two LC-MS metabolomics datasets and need to quantify match correctness — e.g. via annotated feature concordance or a simulated dataset with known embedded correspondences.

name: cross-dataset-generalization-evaluation
description: Use when you need to test whether a CCS prediction model's reported accuracy transfers beyond its training dataset's chemical space, using METLIN-CCS (~27k structures) and CCSBase v1.3 (16,989 values) as train/test pairs.

name: cross-dataset-generalization-metrics-aggregation
description: Use when a trained GNN CCS predictor must be evaluated on a structurally different database than its training set (e.g. CCSBase→METLIN-CCS or METLIN-CCS→CCSBase) and per-model R2/MAE/MRE must be compiled into a cross-database comparison table.

name: cross-dataset-map-aggregation
description: Use when comparing two annotation scoring methods across a corpus of imaging mass spectrometry datasets and you need a single ranking-quality metric (MAP) per method per sample type, plus counts of datasets with statistically significant AP differences.

name: cross-dataset-mass-signature-pooling
description: Use when multiple replicate DESI-MSI datasets of the same tissue type (e.g., root sections) have each been processed along a linear developmental gradient and you need a pooled, de-replicated mass signature list for cross-sample clustering and variety comparison.

name: cross-dataset-masst-search
description: Use when an annotation made in one full-scan dataset (e.g. a pseudo MS/MS spectrum from NIST feces MSV000095787) must be validated or propagated by finding the top cosine match in a pool of pseudo MS/MS spectra from another dataset (e.g. IBD, PR000639).

name: cross-dataset-match-count-reporting
description: Use when an Eclipse MSAligner one-by-all alignment has been run (e.g., a reference dataset like rat plasma DS5 against comparison datasets DS6–DS9) and you must report how many of the reference features matched in all datasets, partially matched, or had no match.

name: cross-dataset-metagene-network-construction
description: Use when two ICA decompositions of different cancer transcriptomic datasets must be compared component-wise to assess reproducibility, and no one-to-one component ordering exists between them.

name: cross-dataset-model-benchmarking
description: Use when you must quantify how much a model component (e.g. predicted fingerprint input) contributes by re-running the identical generation/re-ranking pipeline with that component removed on held-out spectra from multiple reference datasets.

name: cross-dataset-model-transfer-validation
description: Use when ML models trained on one cell-line panel (e.g. CCLE) have produced top features, and you need to confirm those features generalize by measuring their importance in independent datasets such as NCI60 or single-cell data.

name: cross-dataset-molecule-deduplication
description: Use when building a screening library from multiple structure databases (SDF/gzipped SDF) and non-organic, ionic, or duplicate molecules must be removed before spectrum prediction or other downstream chemistry.

name: cross-dataset-molecule-matching
description: Use when predicted RTs from one chromatographic method must be made comparable to RTs measured under independent experimental reverse-phase methods, and per-method projection errors (e.g. median absolute error in seconds) must be quantified.

name: cross-dataset-ms-alignment-benchmarking
description: Use when you must reproduce or extend a head-to-head comparison of LC-MS alignment tools (e.g. metabCombiner vs Eclipse) on multiple same-method datasets and report overlap and spurious-match counts.

name: cross-dataset-overlap-analysis
description: Use when a list of candidate microbial MS/MS spectra (.mgf from MZmine/GNPS networking) must be cross-validated against an independent public dataset with treatment-vs-control metadata to test biological exclusivity.

name: cross-dataset-peak-intensity-correlation
description: Use when reanalyzing publicly deposited MRM mzML raw data to verify that an automatic peak-integration pipeline reproduces previously reported, manually reviewed peak intensities on a per-metabolite basis.

name: cross-dataset-peak-recovery-assessment
description: Use when replicating or validating an MSI peak-identification pipeline against a published peak list (e.g., the 63 peaks of Zhang et al. 2023) using multiple replicate DESI-MSI datasets.

name: cross-dataset-provenance-merging
description: Use when metabolite entries from datasets being merged carry non-systematic identifiers (CAS, HMDB, KEGG, PubChem, ChEBI, LipidMaps, DrugBank, Bin ID) that must be converted to InChIKeys before datasets can be integrated.

name: cross-dataset-retention-order-alignment
description: Use when you have paired RPLC retention datasets (e.

name: cross-dataset-spectral-comparison
description: Use when you hold MGF peak lists (with precursor m/z) from two LC-MS/MS datasets and want to compare spectral similarity versus precursor m/z difference pre-database-search, e.g. human vs. chimpanzee or human vs. E. coli serum.

name: cross-dataset-spectral-match-aggregation
description: Use when you have KGMN-annotated unknown metabolites (e.g., from Demo_MetDNA2_NIST_urine_pos) and need to test whether their MS/MS spectra recur across public GNPS/MassIVE data sets as independent evidence for annotations lacking chemical standards.

name: cross-dataset-training-set-size-analysis
description: Use when you must justify a database's suitability as an ML training resource by comparing its labelled instance count against the training-set sizes of existing predictors in the same domain.

name: cross-decomposition-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you need to assess which matrix factorization method produces the most reproducible metagene signatures from the same omics matrix, e.g. by correlating ICA, PCA, and NMF components against a significance threshold.

name: cross-disease-common-gene-extraction
description: Use when you need to determine whether a defined group of intestine-related diseases (e.g., colon cancer, colorectal cancer, IBD, constipation, diarrhea, ileus) shares common genes, and which genes are flagged as etiologically linked to specific syndromes.

name: cross-disease-metabolite-comparison
description: Use when you have multiple fine-tuned transformer checkpoints trained on NMR metabolomics (e.g., 249 UK Biobank metabolite features per disease) and need to rank metabolite features by attention importance and compare rankings across diseases to find recurring biomarkers.

name: cross-feeding-dependency-verification
description: Use when you have gap-filled genome-scale community models (e.g. Matlab workspaces from COMMIT gap filling) and need to enumerate extracellular exchanges and validate which members depend on which secreted metabolites via uptake-blocking FBA.

name: cross-feeding-exchange-metabolite-enumeration
description: Use when a genome-scale community metabolic model (e.g. AGORA SBML member models) needs systematic enumeration of which metabolites members can exchange and which cross-feeding interactions are feasible, without fixing an abundance profile.

name: cross-feeding-interaction-identification
description: Use when a PyCoMo-generated community metabolic model (SBML) must be queried for which metabolites members can exchange and which member-to-member cross-feeding routes are feasible, independent of a specific abundance profile.

name: cross-feeding-metabolite-overlap-analysis
description: Use when two independent metabolic interaction predictors (e.g. SMETANA and COMMIT) have been run on the same gap-filled community models and you need to quantify their agreement at the level of member pairs and shared exchanged metabolites.

name: cross-feeding-reaction-tracing
description: Use when a community metabolic model (e.g. PyCoMo SBML biogas community model) predicts cross-feeding exchanges — such as spurious D. vulgaris H2 uptake — that were absent from the original member-model analysis, suggesting an internal thermodynamically infeasible cycle.

name: cross-fold-hyperparameter-representation-comparison
description: Use when several molecular featurizations are candidates for a property/retention prediction model and you need a fair, fold-level performance comparison plus an independent-dataset generalizability check before choosing one.

name: cross-fold-sampling-frequency-aggregation
description: Use when multiple cross-validation folds or seed-replicated generative RNN models have each produced per-molecule sampling-frequency tables that must be merged into one averaged frequency table for ranking candidate metabolites.

name: cross-group-feature-matching
description: Use when two or more feature tables from different separation platforms (e.g. HILIC-MS ESI+/ESI- and CE-MS via nanoCEasy) must be fused into one augmented dataset for joint chemometric evaluation.

name: cross-hardware-performance-comparison
description: Use when a published method reports a concrete runtime on named hardware (e.g. compareMS2 2.0's 40 min for 10 pairwise serum dataset comparisons on an Intel Xeon W-2135 at 3.70 GHz) and a re-run's performance must be assessed on possibly different machines.

name: cross-instrument-generalization-evaluation
description: Use when testing whether a formula-prediction model trained on one instrument's MS/MS spectra (e.g. Orbitrap) generalizes to another (e.g. Q-TOF) on identical compound sets.

name: cross-instrument-spectral-matching
description: Use when you need to measure how well MS2 reference spectra acquired on one instrument type identify compounds queried from another (e.g. QS=[QqQ] vs TS=[QqTOF]), and to evaluate whether merged ESI-MS2 target sets improve precision at a fixed similarity-score cutoff.

name: cross-ionization-mode-compound-set-intersection
description: Use when flow injection–Orbitrap MSn data have been acquired in both positive and negative ionization modes, per-mode feature lists (e.g. from mzmine) and cleaned metadata exist, and the goal is to quantify how many unique compounds are detected in positive-only, negative-only, and both modes.

name: cross-ionization-mode-loss-evaluation
description: Use when you need to quantify whether dual-ionization-mode training trades off within-mode prediction accuracy, by benchmarking single-mode ablations on held-out same-mode spectrum pairs per Tanimoto bin.

name: cross-ionization-mode-molecular-networking
description: Use when you have MS/MS spectra acquired in both positive and negative ionization modes (e.g. mgf/msp from LC-MS metabolomics) and want a single molecular network spanning both modes rather than separate per-mode networks.

name: cross-ionization-mode-similarity-prediction
description: Use when positive and negative ionization mode MS/MS spectra of structurally identical or related compounds must be compared, and classical spectrum similarity scores (cosine, modified cosine) miss cross-mode similarity.

name: cross-ionization-mode-spectra-pair-sampling
description: Use when constructing training pairs for a Siamese spectral-similarity model (e.g. MS2DeepScore) from spectra spanning both ionization modes, especially when raw pair enumeration would over-represent high-frequency molecules or easy (very high/very low) Tanimoto bins.

name: cross-ionization-mode-spectral-similarity-modeling
description: Use when positive- and negative-ionization-mode MS/MS spectra must be compared in one unified analysis, or when evaluating whether spectral metadata (precursor m/z, ionmode, adduct, instrument type) improves similarity prediction.

name: cross-ionization-mode-spectral-visualization
description: Use when you have processed MS/MS spectra in both ionization modes and want a unified chemical-space plot (2D UMAP or interactive HTML) that shows cross-mode similarity of the same metabolites.

name: cross-laboratory-rank-comparison
description: Use when two or more replicate experiments (e.g., within-lab biological replicates or between-lab same-platform comparisons of RNA-seq read counts) need reproducibility assessment as gene rank lists with error control at a target FDR.

name: cross-language-spectrum-conversion
description: Use when an R-based Spectra workflow must consume or hand off MS2 peak tables to/from Python matchms or spectrum_utils objects in one session, without duplicating data across languages.

name: cross-layer-edge-counting-and-sign-summary
description: Use when a built multi-omics network (e.g. microbiome x transcriptome, chemicals x genes) must be summarized per layer pair, to test whether exposure classes show distinct correlation-sign patterns and to report node/edge counts per layer pair.

name: cross-library-annotation-comparison
description: Use when you have one aligned MS/MS feature list (e.g., an MS-Dial peak table) and need to quantify how many features each candidate spectral library can annotate, to choose or justify a library.

name: cross-library-compound-overlap-assessment
description: Use when you must decide whether ML models trained on molecular descriptors (e.g., CDK descriptors for retention-time prediction) will generalize to a test or validation library with a different chemical profile.

name: cross-library-compound-overlap-removal
description: Use when compiling a training .msp set (e.g., from MoNA or GNPS) while an independent evaluation set will be annotated via reference libraries such as NIST 20 or in-silico LipidBlast; overlapping compounds must be removed.

name: cross-library-coverage-comparison
description: Use when you have MS/MS search results from the same features against multiple in-silico lipidomics libraries and need to quantify which lipid classes or adducts each library covers, or which classes are unique to a single library.

name: cross-library-lipidomics-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when annotations of the same LC-MS/MS features were produced with two different spectral libraries and you need library-specific hypergeometric score cutoffs to separate authentic from spurious identifications.

name: cross-library-overlap-analysis
description: Reference for aggregating multiple MS/MS spectral libraries (e.g., NIST20, METLIN, GNPS, MSDIAL) into a deduplicated reference set, and for quantifying pairwise or multiway overlap via InChIKey prefix matching before assigning each compound to a single source library.

name: cross-library-performance-comparison
description: Use when choosing a Python library for a fixed spectrum-processing pipeline (m/z trimming, precursor removal, intensity filtering, scaling) and per-spectrum runtime on identical spectra must be measured and compared across libraries.

name: cross-library-pipeline-portability-testing
description: Use when a matchms library-cleaning workflow (fixed filter order + settings captured in YAML) must be validated as a portable configuration on a different public spectral library, e.g., porting the GNPS setup to MassBank or MoNA.

name: cross-matrix-metabolomics-method-transfer
description: Decision support for extending an MTI/internal-standard-calibrated MSI-CE-MS annotation pipeline beyond its validated serum matrix to urine, saliva, stool, or serial-injection isocratic LC-MS data.

name: cross-matrix-workflow-benchmarking
description: Use when an annotation workflow validated on one matrix (e.g. human serum) must be tested on other biological matrices or instrument types, with precision/recall computed against expert manual annotations.

name: cross-method-annotation-agreement-evaluation
description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics dataset has both a computational metabolite prediction (e.g., mummichog on a significant m/z feature list) and an independent targeted annotation, and you need to measure their agreement to validate the prediction approach.

name: cross-method-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when two or more microbiome-metabolome prediction models (e.g., MiMeNet vs. MelonnPan vs. NED) must be compared under an identical cross-validation protocol on paired community profiles.

name: cross-method-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a new method (e.g. NPFimg) claims lower error rates of signal acquisition or marker identification than a baseline (e.g. XCMS) and the same raw chromatography–MS data can be processed by both.

name: cross-method-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when two computational prediction methods must be compared on the same external test data and headline metrics (R2, RMSE, Median RE) are needed to judge which performs better without training-set leakage.

name: cross-method-calibration-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantify how robust a CCS calibration/feature-class-assignment pipeline is to calibration error and whether it outperforms single-trendline or IMSCal baselines.

name: cross-method-dam-overlap-benchmarking
description: Use when one raw feature table has been normalized by ≥2 methods and you must quantify how normalization affects differential abundance results, e.g. reproduce a reported DAM overlap range between robust and QC-RLSC normalization.

name: cross-method-elution-order-mapping
description: Use when you have predicted RTs from one chromatographic context and experimental RTs from a different method (e.g. a PredRet ECM such as FEM_long, LIFE_old, RIKEN, or FEM_orbitrap_plasma) and need to align/project RTs across methods for candidate ranking or filtering.

name: cross-method-formula-assignment-comparison
description: Use when a two-column (m/z, intensity) ultrahigh-resolution FT-ICR or Orbitrap spectrum of an environmental complex mixture (e.

name: cross-method-normalisation-comparison
description: Use when a large-scale metabolomics dataset (e.g. >1,000 plasma samples acquired over 44 days on an Agilent 1260 HPLC/Qtrap5500 platform) has been normalised by two or more competing methods and you need an empirical, replicate-based comparison of which removes unwanted variation while preserving.

name: cross-method-retrieval-performance-comparison
description: Use when a small-molecule NMR structure-search system (e.g. a neural fingerprint predictor) must be benchmarked against spectral-library shift-matching baselines on the same query spectra and ground-truth structures.

name: cross-method-search-result-comparison
description: Use when evaluating or benchmarking tandem MS database search methods: you have query MS/MS spectra, a spectral library, a molecular structure database (DNP or MoNA), and need top-k accuracy comparisons across multiple search tools.

name: cross-method-top5-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify how robust competing molecular-formula identification methods are to increasing spectral noise, on matched MGF test spectra from Q-TOF or Orbitrap instruments.

name: cross-modal-hybrid-denoising-pretraining
description: Use when pretraining a sequence-to-sequence model on a corpus of fingerprint–SELFIES pairs (e.g. 4M PubChem molecules) to teach cross-modal mapping between Morgan fingerprint tokens and molecular structures before finetuning on spectra.

name: cross-modality-image-registration-evaluation
description: Use when paired multi-modal images (e.g., TOF-SIMS metabolite and IMC protein channels) need alignment and you must quantitatively verify that a registration method beats simpler baselines.

name: cross-modality-roi-assignment-handling
description: Use when joint protein-metabolite single-cell analysis in crowded human tissues requires correctly registered IMC and SIMS modalities per imaging region, e.g. before computing neighbor-based metabolite competition ratios or distance-to-vessel maps.

name: cross-mode-annotation-verification
description: Decision support for consolidating LC/MS feature annotations when the same extract was analyzed in both positive and negative ion mode and you need to verify which quasi-molecular ion (e.g. [M+H]+ vs [M-H]−) each grouped compound spectrum really represents.

name: cross-model-inference-speedup-analysis
description: Use when you need to quantify the inference-time advantage of a proposed spectral-to-molecule model over diffusion-based competitors on a shared benchmark (e.g. MassSpecGym test fold).

name: cross-model-llm-output-comparison
description: Use when you have a set of m/z values from metabolomics peaks and need to determine which LLM(s) correctly annotate them, by running the same peak-identification prompt across multiple models and tabulating per-model successes and failures.

name: cross-model-metabolite-comparison
description: Use when metabolomics data exist for two or more systems modeling the same disease driver question — e.

name: cross-ms-level-tic-ratio-analysis
description: Use when Thermo RAW files have been processed with MetaXtract and you must automatically flag acquisitions whose MS2 TIC drops below a set fraction of MS1 TIC, without running identifications.

name: cross-omics-feature-pair-conversion
description: Use when integrating two spatial omics modalities (e.g. 10X Visium spatial transcriptome and MALDI-MSI metabolome) that share no features, and you need a cross-omics correlated feature to guide spot-to-spot alignment.

name: cross-omics-identifier-mapping
description: Use when merging or enriching multi-omics results (e.g. isoforms, miRNAs, proteins, lipids from MOI Salmon/isoformSwitchAnalyzeR outputs) that must be converted to gene-level features before pathway analysis.

name: cross-omics-pearson-spearman-correlation
description: Use when multiple aligned omics feature matrices (e.g. mRNA, miRNA, isoform, proteomics, lipidomics tables) are available after MOI's MCIA integration step and noisy feature-to-feature connections must be filtered out before pathway enrichment analysis.

name: cross-omics-regulator-consistency-check
description: Use when per-metabolite model feature importances are available for multiple omics feature sets and you need to identify globally influential regulators, e.g. confirming YAP1 as a top predictor across 4 omic layers.

name: cross-omsl-comparative-statistics
description: Reference for comparing chemical-class coverage, spectral redundancy (median spectra per compound), and compound counts across multiple open mass spectral libraries before integrating them or choosing which OMSL to use.

name: cross-organism-metabolic-comparison
description: Use when the goal is to compare metabolisms of two or more KEGG organisms via similarity indexes (set/multiset reaction sets) or to check whether index-based groupings reproduce known evolutionary relationships.

name: cross-organism-metabolic-complementation-analysis
description: Use when two KEGG-coded organisms with suspected metabolic interdependence (e.g. host–endosymbiont pairs) need their metabolisms reconstructed from KGML data and compared pathway-by-pathway to reveal complementation.

name: cross-organism-metabolite-protein-interaction-evaluation
description: Use when two organism-specific MPI classifiers must be compared on identical shared metabolite-protein pairs to test whether predictions are consistent across metabolic networks.

name: cross-organism-topology-visual-comparison
description: Use when two (or a set of) KEGG organisms' metabolisms must be compared at the structural/topological level and a qualitative visual judgement of network shape difference (e.g. complex host vs. simple symbiont) is the deliverable.

name: cross-package-capability-matrix-compilation
description: Use when selecting an R package to import/export spectral libraries in NIST msp or MoNA/GNPS dialects, and you need a reproducible support matrix rather than documentation claims.

name: cross-package-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing computational efficiency (elapsed time, memory allocation) of alternative R packages performing the same network-construction task on identically sized, identically seeded inputs, e.g. to substantiate claims like 'up to 100-fold faster'.

name: cross-pipeline-matrix-comparison-idsl-ipa-vs-msdial
description: Use when two peak-intensity/height data matrices were generated from the same raw LC/HRMS study by different pipelines (e.g. IDSL.IPA vs MS-DIAL) and you need a statistically grounded comparison of how many features each detects as associated with a phenotype.

name: cross-platform-annotation-table-compilation
description: Use when an unassigned LC-HRMS signal recurs across two or more instruments/modes and you need to pull its spectral and compound records from a spectral database and tabulate platform-by-platform annotations with MSI confidence levels.

name: cross-platform-ccs-comparison-tims-dtims
description: Use when IM-MS lipidomics data from two ion-mobility technologies (trapped IM and drift-tube IM) must be compared, e.g., to compute mean absolute CCSN2 bias per ionization mode or to decide whether class-adduct-specific CCS correction is needed.

name: cross-platform-classifier-generalization-evaluation
description: Use when a machine-learning peak-quality classifier trained on one LC-MS platform/dataset must be tested on independent datasets from a different platform or ionization mode, and cross-dataset generalization (Accuracy, Pass/Fail F-measure) needs to be quantified.

name: cross-platform-classifier-validation
description: Use when a trained peak-quality classifier must be validated on labeled independent test sets (e.g. ST000695, MTBLS354, MTBLS306) that differ from the development set in platform, matrix, or ionization mode.

name: cross-platform-data-fusion-evaluation
description: Use when multiple separation-platform MS feature tables (e.g., HILIC-MS and CE-MS in ESI positive and ESI negative modes) must be augmented/fused into one mid-level dataset to compare phenotypes, such as inhibitor-treated vs. control Saccharomyces cerevisiae extracts.

name: cross-platform-feature-matching
description: Use when validating a new/in-house HRMS feature-extraction workflow by measuring the fraction of its m/z–RT features recovered by reference tools like MSDIAL or XCMS on identical mzML files of samples with known composition.

name: cross-platform-lcmsms-sample-comparison
description: Use when LC-MS/MS samples were profiled on different instruments (e.g. Q-Exactive Plus vs Q-Exactive Focus) or with different LC gradients, exhibit strong RT shifts or poor feature overlap, and you need to cluster/compare them together.

name: cross-platform-metabolite-overlap-analysis
description: Use when you have near-identical feature tables from two different LC–MS instrument platforms (e.g. Thermo and Waters) and need to annotate metabolites with the PM database and quantify the overlap of reliable annotations across platforms.

name: cross-platform-ms-tool-execution-wine-docker
description: Use when the workflow requires running the Windows-only MZA converter on Linux/macOS (e.g., for converting Agilent .d, Bruker ion mobility .d, or Thermo .raw files to .mza) and the host OS is not Windows.

name: cross-platform-peak-table-comparison
description: Decision support for validating that a containerized LC-MS metabolomics workflow produces identical peak tables when run on different platforms (e.g. macOS with Docker vs Linux HPC with Singularity).

name: cross-platform-quantification-deviation-assessment
description: Use when a designed standard-mixture benchmark (known SB:SA dilution ratios) has been processed with MetaPro run-1 quantification reports (.xlsx) on two or more LC-MS platforms and you must quantify how closely observed log2 fold-changes track the design.

name: cross-polarity-annotation-verification
description: Use when LC/MS datasets were acquired in both positive and negative ESI ion modes, xsAnnotate objects exist for each polarity, and single-mode ion annotations need cross-verification to improve molecular mass annotation rates.

name: cross-polarity-feature-matching
description: Use when LC/MS data were acquired in both positive and negative ion mode and you need to annotate adducts, isotopes, or quasi-molecular ions more reliably by cross-verifying hypotheses across polarities.

name: cross-repository-identifier-mapping
description: Use when input is a metabolomics or proteomics USI string (e.g. mzspec:MASSBANK::accession:... or mzspec:MSV...:file:scan:N) that must be parsed into collection/msRun/indexType/indexNumber fields and mapped to the correct repository or spectral library service.

name: cross-resource-spectrum-comparison
description: Use when spectra from different metabolomics/proteomics resources must be compared or linked unambiguously and no standardized cross-repository spectrum identifier exists; e.g. pairing a metabolomics-extended USI (mzspec:...) with its database-independent SPLASH.

name: cross-run-acquisition-pattern-comparison
description: Use when several Thermo RAW files from nominally identical LC-MS/MS QC or batch acquisitions must be compared scan-by-scan (retention time, TIC, base-peak intensity, ion injection time, charge state) to find underperforming runs.

name: cross-run-ccs-reproducibility-assessment
description: Use when a large batch of IMS-MS runs (e.g. 7106 RapidFire SPE-IMS-MS runs) yields a repeat analyte measurement and you need to quantify CCS variance across runs, or to compare calibration variants (conventional vs. pressure/temperature-corrected single-field) by their %RSD.

name: cross-run-feature-linking
description: Use when multiple LC-MS runs (e.g. replicate measurements or concentration series in mzML/featureXML) must be matched feature-to-feature to build a quantification matrix; the article applies it after feature detection and retention time correction on human plasma data.

name: cross-run-output-comparison
description: Use when you need to demonstrate that repeated executions of a containerized workflow (e.g. Nextflow4MS-DIAL on .mzML LC-MS input) produce identical outputs before trusting the pipeline for downstream metabolomics analysis.

name: cross-sample-component-area-aggregation
description: Use when a GC-MS hit table exported from vendor peak-detection software (e.g. Agilent Unknowns Analysis) contains multiple occurrences of the same tentative compound across samples and per-compound component areas must be collected and standardized.

name: cross-sample-feature-alignment
description: Use when you have peak/feature tables per sample from multidimensional MS acquisitions and need one feature list matched across all study samples, QC pools, and blanks using simultaneous m/z, drift time, and retention time tolerances.

name: cross-sample-feature-grouping
description: Use when you have per-sample deconvolution results from untargeted GC×GC–MS data (e.g. GcDUO Module III output) and need to merge duplicate features into cross-sample consensus features with consensus spectra before annotation or integration.

name: cross-sample-group-difference-estimation
description: Use when running the TIC peak detection stage of AutoTuner and you must supply the Group difference value, the sole parameter estimated through a manual, non-automatable cross-sample comparison rather than statistical inference on raw data.

name: cross-sample-nmr-comparison
description: Use when you have per-sample spin system feature tables (from combined TOCSY/HSQC peak picking) for a sample set and need pairwise sample similarity to drive network-based dereplication or bioactive metabolite prioritization.

name: cross-sample-overlapping-slice-merging
description: Use when building peak groups from LC-MS/MS lipidomics or metabolomics data (e.g., mzML files) where MS/MS scans must be aggregated across samples and assigned to finalized peak groups.

name: cross-sample-peak-alignment
description: Use when you have per-sample peak lists (e.g. m/z values from SIM-stitched DIMS or XCMS feature tables) and need one aligned peak table across all biological and blank samples before filtering or statistics.

name: cross-software-annotation-filtering
description: Use when LipidMatch rule-based annotations on ddMS2-topN feature tables need independent validation against other open-source lipid identification software such as MS-DIAL or Greazy.

name: cross-software-annotation-table-reconciliation
description: Use when you have lipid annotations from two or more open-source lipidomics software aligned to the same features and need to quantify cross-software agreement or benchmark one annotator against the others.

name: cross-software-feature-table-harmonization
description: Use when one raw LC-MS mzML file must be processed independently by MS-DIAL, MZmine3, xcms, and MassCube so their exported feature tables can be matched against a ground-truth list to benchmark peak-detection accuracy.

name: cross-software-phasing-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when you have a replicate series of 1D-NMR spectra (e.g. metabolite mix replicates or Daphnia extract CryoProbe spectra) and must decide which software's automatic phase correction yields the most reproducible phases across the series.

name: cross-solvent-annotation-consistency-analysis
description: Use when evaluating DeepSAT annotation robustness on paired HSQC spectra of identical compounds recorded in different NMR solvents, or when choosing whether solvent changes threaten structure-identification reliability.

name: cross-source-duplicate-reconciliation
description: Use when aggregating molecule entries from multiple public datasets (e.g. AfroDB, ChEBI NPs, BitterDB, AnalytiCon Discovery NPs) and you must detect cross-source duplicates, merge them without losing annotations, and reconcile per-source counts against release-level unique totals.

name: cross-source-metabolite-frequency-filtering
description: Use when you have a merged/harmonized metabolite table from multiple information sources (e.g. an MMS InChIKey-merged list) and need to reduce false positives before pathway enrichment by keeping only compounds supported by ≥2 sources.

name: cross-source-metabolite-harmonization
description: Use when multiple metabolite datasets from different sources (e.g. Metabolomics Workbench studies, HMDB, literature tables) must be merged on a common key and annotated with identifiers and ontology for intercomparison.

name: cross-source-pathway-mapping
description: Use when you need to measure how much metabolite content is shared between pathway definitions from different databases (e.g., KEGG vs Reactome vs WikiPathways) to assess redundancy before enrichment analysis or pathway clustering.

name: cross-species-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when you have de novo sequencing predictions on annotated MS/MS spectra from several species or heterogeneous samples and need a standardized peptide- and amino-acid-level accuracy comparison across models or training datasets.

name: cross-species-benchmark-peptide-precision-evaluation
description: Use when comparing two de novo sequencing models (e.g., two Casanovo variants trained on different training sets) with a controlled cross-species evaluation, or when reporting peptide precision and average precision on held-out species from MSV000090982.

name: cross-species-peptide-overlap-analysis
description: Use when you have unannotated LC-MS/MS tandem mass spectra (e.g. MGF files from serum tryptic digests) from multiple species or individuals and need to quantify shared peptide content — without database search — as a distance for phylogenetic reconstruction or species identification.

name: cross-spectrum-peak-grouping
description: Use when multiple 1D NMR spectra (e.g. 40 wine spectra of 8712 points, or 31 mouse-urine spectra) need their per-spectrum wavelet peaks matched across samples to form a shared feature matrix, avoiding binning.

name: cross-strain-metabolic-distribution-comparison
description: Use when mass spectrometry imaging datasets from multiple mouse strains have been annotated per organ and you need to test whether the organ-specific metabolite distribution pattern is conserved across strains.

name: cross-strain-metabolome-comparison
description: Use when an annotated LC-MS/MS feature table (e.g. from GNPS2 FBMN with ChemWalker and SIRIUS annotations) must be assigned metabolic pathways via KEGG cross-referencing and compared across strains to find common pathways.

name: cross-study-annotation-rate-benchmarking
description: Use when you have publicly available LC/HRMS studies with MSI 1–3 peak annotations plus a tool that produces ranked molecular-formula assignments per peak, and you need to quantify top-hit and top-5-hit recovery rates to compare formula-annotation performance across studies.

name: cross-study-feature-comparison-literature-check
description: Use when a pipeline re-run on a public dataset must be validated against the original publication: you have annotated, quality-filtered features (annotation, fold change, p-value) and need to check which ones the original study did or did not report.

name: cross-study-gene-intersection-filtering
description: Use when pooling RNA-Seq/microarray data from multiple studies (e.g. TCGA + GTEx via PMR) and you must restrict the feature matrix to genes reported in every contributing study, plus drop undersampled organ types and samples lacking metadata.

name: cross-study-metabolite-overlap-classification
description: Use when auditing a merged multi-study metabolite dataset to report the same-name vs different-name split against PubChem title names and to quantify unmerged compounds without the MMS.

name: cross-study-metabolite-overlap-comparison
description: Use when the goal is to reproduce/validate a prior metabolomics finding: paired within-subject measurements across conditions (e.g., venous vs arterial blood over time points) plus a published list of top significant metabolites to compare against.

name: cross-study-significance-pattern-verification
description: Use when an automated GC-MS re-analysis of an already-published dataset must be validated by reproducing the original study's between-treatment significance pattern (e.g., NMDS of compound areas).

name: cross-study-spectral-library-transfer
description: Use when an .msp CSA library built from one study's MS1-only data is available and the goal is to annotate peaks in an independent untargeted LC/HRMS study beyond the compounds already recovered by MS/MS spectral library search.

name: cross-table-merge-by-filename
description: Use when per-RAW-file metadata QC tables (file-based-details TSVs from MetaXtract) must be combined with identification-level results to confirm or refute instrument underperformance signals such as depressed MS2 TIC with preserved MS1 TIC.

name: cross-task-transfer-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when you need to justify a new meta-learning/transfer model by comparing it against SVM, random forest, LeNet, and ANN baselines trained on identical single-cell mass-spectrometry splits, especially when training cell counts are small.

name: cross-tissue-cell-type-labeling
description: Use when you have a per-cell mean marker-intensity matrix from segmented multiplexed IMC (imaging mass cytometry) data spanning multiple imaging regions or patients and need unsupervised single-cell cluster labels that transfer across tissues.

name: cross-tissue-differential-expression-overlap
description: Use when you have per-tissue differential expression results (e.g., MoTrPAC PASS1B 15-tissue rat EET data) and need to measure cross-tissue overlap or tissue-specificity of DE gene sets.

name: cross-tool-annotation-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking tandem MS/MS metabolite annotation: identical spectra splits and compound databases must be run through multiple tools and top-k retrieval rates compared side by side.

name: cross-tool-annotation-comparison
description: Use when the same variant set has been annotated by multiple annotation tools (ANNOVAR, SnpEff, VEP) and you need to quantify agreement on HGVSc, HGVSp, coding impact, or transcript accessions against a clinical reference set.

name: cross-tool-annotation-concordance-analysis
description: Use when you have a table of network-based (MetDNA3 level 3) feature annotations plus independent tool annotations for the same features and need to compute per-tool or all-tools concordance percentages.

name: cross-tool-annotation-concordance-analysis
description: Use when multiple variant annotation tools (ANNOVAR, SnpEff, VEP) have been run on the same VCF and you need to quantify HGVS/coding-impact disagreement, benchmark against ClinVar, or assess ACMG/PVS1 impact.

name: cross-tool-annotation-overlap-comparison
description: Decision support for choosing an annotation tool for MALDI/SM data: run when a user asks whether SpaMTP's annotation covers METASPACE/pySM results on TOF data, or needs per-database overlap statistics between two annotation pipelines.

name: cross-tool-benchmark-comparison
description: Reference for comparing clustering quality of multiple spectral clustering tools on the same MS/MS dataset, using the HyperSpec paper's benchmarking metrics and workflow.

name: cross-tool-benchmark-table-construction
description: Use when evaluating a prediction tool against published baselines on a shared benchmark set, needing a per-tool/per-condition metric table with verifiable reference counts.

name: cross-tool-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when you have cluster assignments from multiple spectrum clustering tools plus peptide-spectrum match identifications, and need to compare clustering purity/completeness or cluster size distributions at equivalent error rates.

name: cross-tool-clustering-fragmentation-comparison
description: Use when comparing multiple spectrum clustering tools' outputs on the same dataset and you need a fragmentation metric: the number of unique clusters a chosen peptide's spectra are split into per tool.

name: cross-tool-dataframe-equality-checking
description: Use when an mzML file has been converted to Parquet by arcMS (convert_mzml_to_parquet()) and you must verify that pandas read_parquet() reproduces exactly the DEIMoS deimos.load() DataFrame from the same mzML.

name: cross-tool-differential-overlap-analysis
description: Use when a pixel × ion feature matrix (e.g., 14,260 pixels × 3,044 ion peaks, AFAD-ESI positive mode) has differential analysis results from one spatial metabolomics tool and you need to cross-validate them against an independent tool's clustering and differential calls.

name: cross-tool-enrichment-performance-comparison
description: Use when choosing among metabolomics pathway enrichment tools on runtime grounds, or when replicating the paper's runtime comparison of EnrichMet vs MetaboAnalystR vs FELLA on a fixed metabolite list.

name: cross-tool-error-frequency-tabulation
description: Use when comparing de novo peptide sequencing predictions (e.g. pNovo 3, SMSNet, PointNovo, Casanovo) against pseudo-ground-truth PSMs and you need to characterize which error types dominate each tool's incorrect predictions.

name: cross-tool-feature-comparison
description: Use when multiple LC-MS processing tools (asari, XCMS, MZmine with wavelet or local-minimum peak detection) report very different feature counts on the same dataset and you must determine whether the extra features are genuine or low-quality non-reproducible peaks.

name: cross-tool-feature-count-comparison
description: Decision support for selecting an LC/MS signal-detection/peak-picking tool: you have raw mzML files, candidate peak-detection algorithms (e.g. mzLearn, XCMS, ASARI), and need objective per-dataset feature counts plus TP/FP rates to compare them.

name: cross-tool-feature-mapping-comparison
description: Use when you need to benchmark a peak-picking/grouping workflow against an established tool like MetaboAnalyst on the same raw NMR spectra, and must quantify differences in feature resolution and overlap of statistically significant features.

name: cross-tool-feature-matching-benchmarking
description: Use when reproducing published untargeted metabolomics feature detection with a different tool and quantifying what fraction of the published (XCMS/CAMERA) features is recovered, separately per ionization mode, from public MetaboLights raw data.

name: cross-tool-file-size-benchmarking
description: Use when choosing between two visualization tools for large ordination datasets: generate equivalent outputs from both on the same samples and metadata, then measure and compare total output file size on disk.

name: cross-tool-formula-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when you have a labeled MS/MS challenge dataset (e.g., CASMI 2022, 304 positive-mode spectra) and need to compare formula-annotation accuracy of two or more tools under identical inputs.

name: cross-tool-formula-annotation-comparison
description: Use when evaluating whether a data-driven formula prediction model (e.g., a formula transformer trained on MS/MS spectra) outperforms a classical tree-based competitor on the same spectra, and you need accuracy, coverage, and concordance metrics on identical inputs.

name: cross-tool-fragmentation-prediction-evaluation
description: Use when comparing MS/MS spectral prediction quality across in silico fragmentation tools (e.g., FIORA vs ICEBERG vs CFM-ID) and assessing generalization to compounds structurally dissimilar from the training set via sqrt-weighted cosine similarity stratified by maximum Tanimoto similarity.

name: cross-tool-integration-consistency-analysis
description: Use when the same MRM acquisition dataset (e.g., 113 Skyline small-molecule test files) has been processed by two tools and you must verify that quantification results (peak areas per transition such as Drug_light/Drug_heavy) agree within a defined correlation threshold.

name: cross-tool-metabolite-prediction-comparison
description: Decision support for choosing among CYP450 SoM or byproduct predictors: when a practitioner has a common evaluation test set (e.g., EBoMD2, the BioTransformer hold-out 13321_2018_324_MOESM6_ESM.sdf, or the HDFAME 60Reactants.

name: cross-tool-parameter-benchmarking
description: Use when two or more parameter-optimization tools (e.g., AutoTuner, IPO) have produced centWave parameter sets for the same raw LC-MS dataset and the analysis goal is to compare how each choice changes feature counts.

name: cross-tool-peak-area-correlation-analysis
description: Use when two or more GC–MS peak-picking or deconvolution tools (e.g. eRah, XCMS centWave, MetAlign) have produced per-sample quantification tables and you need to quantify their agreement by correlating peak areas/intensities per compound across samples.

name: cross-tool-peak-count-benchmarking
description: Use when a novel peak-picking pipeline for untargeted LC/HRMS data needs quantitative benchmarking against MZmine 2, xcms-CAMERA, or MS-DIAL on a shared raw test file.

name: cross-tool-prediction-discrepancy-analysis
description: Use when the same set of MS/MS spectra has been annotated by two independent classifiers (e.g. CANOPUS and MolNetEnhancer) and you need to tabulate per-class disagreement before choosing one tool's output for downstream scoring such as NPClassScore.

name: cross-tool-prediction-performance-comparison
description: Use when a new in silico reactant-prediction or site-of-metabolism tool must be benchmarked against CypReact, ADMET Predictor, or SMARTCyp on the 1632-molecule CYP450 reactant dataset using per-enzyme AUROC.

name: cross-tool-processing-time-comparison
description: Use when comparing the scalability/runtime of MRM quantitation or batch-effect correction tools on an identical large-scale targeted metabolomics dataset.

name: cross-tool-runtime-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantify and compare prediction speed of competing MS/MS spectral prediction tools on the same compound set, including the effect of GPU vs CPU execution.

name: cross-validated-auc-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating BGC classification models on MIBiG-labeled Pfam TSV data and you need cross-validated AUC ROC values to compare machine-learned classifiers against an antiSMASH rule-based baseline.

name: cross-validated-auc-estimation
description: Use when fitting a supervised multi-omics model (e.g. MB-PLS with latent variables) and you need a cross-validated AUC estimate plus tuned hyperparameters like the optimal number of latent variables.

name: cross-validated-auroc-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing supervised multi-omics classifiers (molecular-level vs pathway-level) on semi-synthetic or real labelled data and you need unbiased generalisation performance reported as AUROC across effect sizes.

name: cross-validated-classification-metrics-evaluation
description: Use when 'relevant'/'other'-labeled HR-MS/MS spectra (e.g., SMARTS-filtered MSnLib v6 MGF files split by polarity and collision energy) have MS2DeepScore embeddings and you must train and evaluate classifiers with balanced-accuracy metrics.

name: cross-validated-classifier-performance-evaluation
description: Use when a final, QC-passed LC-MS feature table with sample metadata (e.g., age groups like adolescence vs middle-age) must be turned into a phenotype classifier and its performance quantified via ROC AUC and 5-fold cross-validated accuracy.

name: cross-validated-classifier-training
description: Use when labeled 'relevant' and 'other' HR-MS/MS reference spectra (e.g., MSnLib or in-house libraries) must be trained into binary classifiers whose cross-validated sensitivity and specificity per polarity/CE setup must be quantified.

name: cross-validated-classifier-training
description: Use when you have a manually labeled set of Pass/Fail peaks from an untargeted LC–MS metabolomics dataset and need to train, cross-validate, and statistically select among competing classifiers rather than trust a single model.

name: cross-validated-classifier-tuning
description: Use when a longitudinal metabolomics dataset has a binary outcome label (e.g. recovered vs deceased COVID-19 patients) and you need a supervised classifier whose predictive performance is benchmarked via cross-validated AUC.

name: cross-validated-hyperparameter-grid-search
description: Use when you must choose both a classifier (e.g., Random Forest vs XGBoost) and a feature-set variant (e.g., EI-only vs ESI-only vs combined binned mass spectra) and need fair, cross-validated hyperparameter tuning plus a single held-out metric for the decision.

name: cross-validated-hyperparameter-selection
description: Reference for tuning hyperparameters of the semi-supervised rescoring classifier (e.g. ristretto/percolator SVM c) when rescoring peptide-spectrum matches with MS²Rescore and the train_fdr and model (svm vs lda) must be set alongside a tuned regularization parameter.

name: cross-validated-hyperparameter-tuning
description: Use when training retention-time prediction models on HILIC or RPLC libraries (e.g. Retip training sets with CDK descriptors) and you need tuned models plus an overfitting check comparing training vs test/validation errors.

name: cross-validated-knn-imputation
description: Use when a benchmark requires KNNimpute error rates on data with artificially introduced missing values (10%, 20% or 30% MCAR) but no a priori neighbour count k is given, so k_ must be chosen by cross-validation.

name: cross-validated-latent-variable-selection
description: Use when fitting a PathIntegrate Multi-View MB-PLS (or comparable PLS-based multi-omics model) and the latent-variable count must be tuned to avoid over- or under-fitting before pathway importance is interpreted.

name: cross-validated-model-evaluation
description: Use when you have paired microbial-feature and metabolite-count matrices for the same samples and need an honest estimate of how well a predictive model recovers each metabolite across held-out folds.

name: cross-validated-model-training-and-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking a de novo sequencing model's generalization across species — i.e., annotated MS/MS spectra (MGF) must be split so each organism is held out in turn as a test fold while training on the remaining species.

name: cross-validated-neural-network-training
description: Use when paired microbiome and metabolome count tables are available and the goal is to predict the community metabolome from microbial features with cross-validated SCC evaluation and background-shuffled significance testing.

name: cross-validated-oplsda-score-scoring
description: Use when you have cross-validated supervised model (e.g. OPLS-DA) scores for predefined pairwise class contrasts (carriage vs controls, serovar vs serovar) and need ROC curves, AUC values, and bootstrap CIs to report diagnostic performance.

name: cross-validated-predictive-ability-assessment
description: Use when evaluating a supervised discriminant model (OPLS-DA) fitted to a metabolomics feature table with far more features than samples, to decide whether reported class separation reflects real predictive signal or overfitting.

name: cross-validated-predictive-parameter-ranking
description: Use when a peak table contains many candidate shape/quality features (e.g. duration, height, area, FWHM, tailing factor, asymmetry derivatives) and you must rank which features predict true vs false peaks before fitting a classifier.

name: cross-validated-regularization-parameter-selection
description: Use when fitting a graphical lasso to a high-dimensional feature table (e.g. 90 metabolites quantified by NMR) and you need an unbiased, data-driven choice of the L1 penalty alpha instead of a fixed guess.

name: cross-validated-rmsd-evaluation
description: Decision support for selecting or validating a chemical shift predictor (protein FM, RNA FM, or legacy SVR) when the target atom types are 1H, 13C, 15N and BMRB-assigned shifts plus matching PDB structures are available.

name: cross-validated-scc-evaluation
description: Use when a paired microbiome-metabolome model must be evaluated per metabolite under repeated cross-validation, or when well-predicted metabolites must be counted against an empirical background threshold.

name: cross-validated-spearman-correlation-evaluation
description: Use when comparing metabolite-prediction models (e.g., MiMeNet vs. MelonnPan or NED) on paired microbiome-metabolome datasets and you need per-metabolite SCC plus a count of well-predicted metabolites.

name: cross-validation-auc-evaluation
description: Use when a trained classifier must be validated with 10-fold cross-validation and micro-average AUC, followed by Youden-index threshold optimization and per-metric reporting (accuracy, TPR, FPR, precision, F1).

name: cross-validation-auroc-computation
description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking CypReact's per-enzyme reactant prediction performance: you have the CypReact package, the 1632-molecule reactant dataset, and need cross-validation AUROC per CYP450 enzyme.

name: cross-validation-benchmark-design
description: Use when a claimed annotation-propagation algorithm must be evaluated for true generalization to metabolites lacking seeds — i.e., when you need a held-out benchmark of coverage and Top 1/3/10 correct rates rather than a single-shot annotation run.

name: cross-validation-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when quantifying top-1 and overall retrieval rates of de novo structure predictions on MS2 spectra (e.g. GNPS, GNPS-OK), or when ablating the modified Platt re-ranking step to isolate the RNN's raw ranking power.

name: cross-validation-classifier-evaluation
description: Use when you must reproduce or estimate generalization performance of a per-isoform CYP450 bond-level predictor on EBoMD-style labeled [compound, bond] data, and need externally cross-validated Jaccard scores rather than a single hold-out split.

name: cross-validation-evaluation-data-processing
description: Use when MS/MS spectra plus structure labels (e.g., GNPS cross-validation data) must be scored against database structure candidates to produce a top-k correct-identification curve for a structure identification tool.

name: cross-validation-evaluation-measure-analysis
description: Use when multiple peak-quality metric sets (e.g., M4, M7, M11) must be paired with diverse ML algorithms and statistically compared via cross-validation to identify a -performing classifier.

name: cross-validation-experiment-design
description: Use when fine-tuning a pre-trained retention-time model to a new chromatographic dataset and you need a stable estimate of R2 across folds and seeds rather than a single train/test split.

name: cross-validation-fold-model-fine-tuning
description: Use when reproducing the DeepMet training protocol: you have a pre-trained SMILES language model, a known-metabolite structure set (HMDB), and need per-fold fine-tuned generators whose withheld 10% mimics unknown metabolites.

name: cross-validation-fold-normalization
description: Use when training per-feature-set ML models (e.g., random forest regressors on CCLE omics) where scaling must be fit only on training folds of a 5-fold CV scheme to avoid leakage into held-out metabolite predictions.

name: cross-validation-metabolite-predictability-assessment
description: Use when matched multiomic (CCLE-style) feature tables and a metabolite abundance matrix are available and the goal is to benchmark how well each omics class individually predicts each metabolite via cross-validated ML.

name: cross-validation-model-evaluation
description: Use when comparing versions of an in silico MS/MS spectral prediction model on a shared experimental dataset and you need fold-matched, per-energy-level metrics (Dice, Precision, Recall, Dot Product) with significance testing.

name: cross-validation-performance-estimation
description: Use when a fingerprint-based binary classifier (e.g. the metabolite-likeness SVM over compounds from HMDB, ChEBI, LipidMaps, YMDB vs ZINC non-metabolites) needs an unbiased accuracy estimate before it is applied to score compound databases.

name: cross-validation-performance-evaluation
description: Use when comparing two or more BGC detectors on the same labeled Pfam training matrix and you need a fair, split-identical performance estimate such as mean ROC AUC across folds.

name: cross-validation-performance-reproduction
description: Use when reproducing RT-Transformer-based candidate filtering: given MS-Finder candidate compounds with measured RTs from MoNa/Metabobase and a transfer-learned model, verify counts of correct/erroneous annotations and ranking shifts.

name: cross-validation-rank-statistics-evaluation
description: Use when you hold a table of generative-model outputs with sampling frequencies and want to test whether frequency alone prioritizes withheld cross-validation metabolites or newly released HMDB structures over generated decoys.

name: cross-validation-rsd-precision-assessment
description: Use when a GC-MS (or analogous LC-MS) metabolomics study provides a pooled-QC training block plus an external validation QC set, and you need to measure how well a normalization method controls batch drift via RSD precision.

name: cross-validation-span-selection-comparison
description: Use when normalizing LC-MS metabolomics run-order data with Metanorm and you must decide between GCV and LOOCV smoother selection, or need to demonstrate that downstream differential abundance results are insensitive to that choice.

name: cross-validation-spectral-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking an in silico structure annotation workflow's confidence scoring against known ground-truth reference spectra, comparing merged vs single collision-energy MS/MS performance, or reproducing hop-plot/ROC evaluations.

name: cross-validation-split-sampling-and-median-model-selection
description: Use when training CCS-prediction SVR models on McLean Unified CCS Compendium adduct data ([M-H]-, [M+H]+, [M+Na]+) and you need unbiased split-level performance reporting via a median-RMSEV model rather than a single arbitrary split.

name: cross-validation-topk-accuracy-computation
description: Use when evaluating a structure generator's ability to recover held-out metabolites from exact monoisotopic mass alone, or when comparing sampling-frequency-based structure prioritization against a baseline like AddCarbon.

name: cross-variety-metabolite-localization-comparison
description: Use when two DESI-MSI developmental-gradient datasets (e.g. B73 vs Oaxacan Green roots) already have DIMPLE cluster assignments and the goal is to determine which mass signatures from a source-variety cluster (e.

name: cross-vendor-raw-data-import
description: Use when targeted small-molecule raw data were acquired on an instrument vendor other than the one a Skyline template or method was originally built for, and quantitative extraction must run on Agilent, Bruker, Shimadzu, Thermo, Sciex, or Waters files.

name: cross-version-database-diff-counting
description: Use when auditing a curated database release against its predecessor to count entries with missing fields, incomplete annotations, or newly added information (e.g. chemical structures across MIBiG versions).

name: cross-version-entry-count-verification
description: Use when auditing a MIBiG JSON release to verify that an update met its stated goal of increasing non-minimal entries, or when comparing entry-status composition across MIBiG versions.

name: cross-vocabulary-synonym-scope-annotation
description: Use when compiling a classification dictionary or synonym table for a chemical taxonomy (e.g. ChemOnt OBO terms) that must carry scoped mappings to external vocabularies like ChEBI, LIPID MAPS, or MeSH.

name: crossed-adduct-conflict-annotation
description: Use when building an in-house LC-MS m/z-RT standard library in metScribeR and peaks have been filtered and manually reviewed — to detect conflicting adduct assignments and annotate each adduct with an identification probability prior to exporting the library CSV.

name: crosspeak-correlation-graph-construction
description: Use when peak-picked TOCSY and HSQC peak lists from complex NMR mixtures must be converted into per-sample spin system features (paired 1H/13C resonances) for downstream feature matching or molecular networking.

name: crowdsourcing-annotation-metrics-tabulation
description: Use when a repository update paper reports per-channel curation/contribution counts that must be extracted verbatim, cross-checked against the article text, and assembled into a structured channel-by-counts table.

name: crude-extract-fraction-prioritization
description: Use when a crude natural-product extract has been roughly fractionated and you need to decide which fractions to interpret or isolate from, guided by cytotoxicity, NMR-based SMART 2.0, and MS2-based molecular networking.

name: csa-annotation-aggregation-interpretation
description: Use when an untargeted LC/HRMS study lacks MS2 fragmentation or MS2-library coverage, and you need to annotate peaks by mass spectral similarity of composite spectra and then aggregate/interpret the annotation at the chemical-class level.

name: csa-parameter-spreadsheet-configuration
description: Use when MS1-level mzXML/mzML/netCDF files have already been processed by IDSL.IPA into 'peaklists' and 'peak_alignment' directories and a CSA composite spectra (.msp) library must be generated.

name: csa-spectra-annotation-validation
description: Use when you have exported CSA composite spectra (.msp) from MS1-only LC/HRMS data and need to verify their chemical annotations by mass spectral similarity search against a curated MS/MS library like NIST 2020.

name: csccp-dynamic-programming-solver-execution
description: Use when a targeted molecular weight (e.g. from GAME/examples/MW) must be matched against seed scaffold files (*.cIdx from GAME/examples/Datasets/scaffolds) to enumerate and rank top candidate structures via the DP (-v idp) solver.

name: csccp-solver-cli-operation
description: Use when you need to predict candidate constitutions of an unknown chemical mixture from a high-resolution mass value, given seed scaffold files (*.cIdx), a scaffold/sidechain probability database, and mass precision up to D=5 decimal digits.

name: csccp-structure-prediction-execution
description: Use when a targeted molecular weight from high-resolution mass spectrometry must be matched against a natural-product scaffold database to rank the most probable candidate structures of an unknown mixture.

name: csf-biomarker-association-analysis
description: Use when a metabolite peak-area table has been extracted from LC-MS/MS data and needs to be tested for association with paired CSF AD biomarkers in a subject subset with covariate adjustment.

name: csharp-windows-application-development
description: Reference for embedding a trained deep learning model (e.g. a CNN trained on 25095 annotated EIC plots) into a C# Windows Application that scores vendor LC-MS metabolic features for chromatographic peak quality in metabolomics pipelines.

name: csi-fingerid-fingerprint-prediction
description: Use when an MS2 spectrum (mgf, .ms, or preprocessed SIRIUS workspace) needs a predicted structural fingerprint xF — either to rank candidate structures by modified Platt score or to serve as the blueprint input for MSNovelist de novo generation.

name: csi-fingerid-structure-annotation
description: Use when feature detection is complete (e.g., MZmine feature lists with associated MS2 scans in .mgf for 'Export for SIRIUS') and per-feature in-silico formula, 2D structure, and chemical-class candidates are needed for a knowledge-graph metabolomics annotation stage.

name: csi-fingerprint-prediction
description: Use when you have MS/MS fragmentation spectra (MGF) for chemical features and need predicted molecular fingerprints to compute pairwise chemical distances or build a Qemistree hierarchy.

name: csv-data-frame-io
description: Use when a metabolomics workflow step must read a concentration table from an uploaded .csv (or .xlsx) file, apply an element-wise operation in Python or R, and write the result back as a CSV with identical rows and columns.

name: csv-data-integrity-checking
description: Use when a user receives a DTCCSN2 library or measured-lipid CSV (e.g. U13C_DT_CCS_library.csv) and must confirm its row counts, headers, adduct labels, lipid-class/adduct pairings, and numeric ranges before downstream CCS bias calculation.

name: csv-dataframe-processing
description: Use when the input is a tabular .csv or .xlsx sample-by-metabolite file that must be loaded, parsed, normalized, or reduced to pairwise statistics such as a Pearson/Kendall/Spearman correlation matrix.

name: csv-dataset-annotation
description: Use when a user has a .csv measurement matrix (samples in rows, analytes in columns) of lipids/polar metabolites from (EDTA) plasma or serum, knows the processing conditions, and wants analytes flagged as 'unstable' pre-emptively.

name: csv-output-file-handling
description: Use when a lipid LC-MS/MS workflow needs an in silico-generated transition list for Skyline (or an Excalibur precursor list for DDA orbitrap acquisition) rather than a '.MSP' spectral library.

name: csv-output-formatting
description: Use when a generated lipid spectral library must feed instrument acquisition or targeted-analysis software — i.e. you need an Excalibur precursor list for Orbitrap DDA or a Skyline transition list rather than a '.MSP' library.

name: csv-result-artifact-export
description: Use when running or replicating the iMAP three-step workflow (data-processing -> metabolites-selection -> data-interpretation) and each layer's output — processed data table, selected-metabolites list, pathway results — must be persisted as a CSV artifact for downstream reuse or validation.

name: csv-result-table-generation
description: Use when a scoring/filtering analysis must be tabulated row-per-threshold: e.g. fraction of correct ZODIAC molecular formula annotations among compounds whose score exceeds each cutoff (0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 0.95, 0.99), written as a CSV.

name: csv-summary-generation
description: Use when a repository/dataset metadata table must be summarized into a small CSV with per-category counts, proportional shares of new entries, and percent growth versus a prior version.

name: csv-table-consolidation
description: Use when a metabolomics annotation table (e.g. REname output CSV) contains many redundant putative annotation rows per feature and the goal is a size-reduced table for manual comparison of annotations.

name: csv-table-io
description: Use when a metabolomics processing step (normalization, imputation, scaling) needs a flat .csv or .xlsx table loaded into a DataFrame, or when a completed data frame must be persisted back to CSV for downstream steps or API consumers.

name: csv-tabular-matrix-construction
description: Use when a user needs a blank, sample-by-attribute CSV metadata template generated from their selections of core sample types and additional sample attributes, for local completion and later standardization with SMetaS.

name: csv-xlsx-tabular-parsing
description: Use when an uploaded metabolomics dataset arrives as a .csv or .xlsx table and must be parsed and checked for missing data, non-numeric concentration values, and primary-ID problems before processing.

name: cterminal-residue-frequency-analysis
description: Use when comparing de novo peptide sequencing models for tryptic bias: if predicted peptides from a fine-tuned vs. pretrained transformer model (e.g., Casanovo vs. Casanovone) should be checked for reduced C-terminal K/R enrichment on non-enzymatic spectra.

name: cubic-spline-injection-order-interpolation
description: Use when a large targeted-metabolomics run is split into batches with QC samples injected in acquisition order and you need to remove batch-effect drift from MRM quantitation, using the QC-RLSC approach of MRMQuant.

name: cubic-spline-interpolation
description: Use when a raw 1D NMR spectrum (ppm scale + intensity array) shows a rolling or offset baseline and peak shapes must be preserved while flattening signal-free regions to zero intensity.

name: cubic-spline-regression-on-qc-injection-order
description: Use when untargeted LC-MS peak tables show systematic signal intensity drift over the injection sequence and QC samples are available across the run to model the drift as a smooth function of injection order.

name: culture-dataset-feature-count-comparison
description: Use when a metabolomics parameter-optimization workflow (e.g. AutoTuner) leaves mzDiff unoptimized and you need to justify a fixed mzDiff value by showing its effect on the returned feature table is minimal.

name: cumulative-frequency-distribution-plotting
description: Use when comparing the precision of corrected vs raw LC-MS/GC-MS metabolomics or proteomics feature tables by measuring how many features fall below successive RSD (CV%) thresholds in QC samples.

name: cumulative-single-compound-metabolite-list-construction
description: Use when the goal is to probe how sensitive ORA output is to the composition and size of the differential metabolite list, e.g. to find the list size that maximises detected enriched pathways or to expose local extrema caused by single compounds.

name: cumulative-sum-scaling-normalization
description: Use when BiG-MAP RPKM-normalized gene cluster (MGC/GCF) abundance or expression tables plus sample grouping metadata must be compositionally normalized and tested for differential abundance/expression between conditions.

name: cumulative-variance-component-selection
description: Use when running PCA on a prepared metabolomics X data matrix (DSO) and the number of components is not specified by the user, so the component count must be determined from cumulative explained variance.

name: curated-subcluster-benchmark-matching
description: Use when a sub-cluster prediction method must be benchmarked against curated/verified sub-clusters (e.g. the 109 SubClusterBlast entries) to quantify how many known sub-clusters are recovered and whether two methods agree.

name: curve-fitting-parameter-estimation
description: Use when connecting phenotype-characterizing data (e.g. immunoblot densitometry, qPCR, time-series expression from Tutorial_Data_01.xlsx) to expression trends via linear, polynomial or Michaelis-Menten fits with per-row correlation.

name: cut-vertex-fragmentation-graph-construction
description: Use when scoring a query mass spectrum (e.g. mzML/MGF from MSV000086287) against many candidate molecules and you need a metabolite graph whose fragmentation-graph nodes are computed on demand rather than exhaustively.

name: cutoff-threshold-sweep-performance-evaluation
description: Use when filtering detected chromatographic peaks by quality metrics and you need to choose defensible cutoff thresholds: you have per-peak metric values (sharpness, Gaussian similarity, SNR, peak significance level, TPASR, zigzag index), a ground truth peak list, and must quantify the.

name: cvae-architecture-implementation
description: Use when building or reproducing joint spatial transcriptomics + spatial metabolomics models that require a shared latent embedding across modalities and samples, with batch-label-conditioned decoding and per-spot modality contribution quantification.

name: cvae-vertical-integration-st-sm
description: Use when you have a joint ST-SM AnnData object from paired sections of one sample and need to fuse both modalities into a shared latent embedding, or to test which model components (loss, normalization, decoder sharing) drive integration quality.

name: cwt-based-peak-detection
description: Use when raw LC–MS mzML files must be turned into detected chromatographic peaks (TIC/EIC peaks) before feature correspondence, system suitability checks, or signal-drift evaluation in untargeted metabolomics QC.

name: cwt-based-peak-snr-estimation
description: Use when scoring the quality of an already-detected chromatographic peak (an intensity vector with apex index and left/right boundaries) to decide whether to keep or filter it before downstream peak alignment or annotation in LC/MS metabolomics data.

name: cwt-peak-profile-analysis
description: Use when you have CWT-detected LC/MS chromatographic peaks and need to rank or compare peak quality evaluation metrics, especially when testing which metric distinguishes genuine signal peaks from noise or baseline artifacts.

name: cxsmiles-conversion-and-explicit-hydrogen-addition
description: Use when a compound library of SMILES plus retention times must be prepared as descriptor input for Retip's RT prediction models, i.e., before running getCD() on rcdk-compatible structures.

name: cyanogenic-glycoside-peak-area-quantification
description: Use when pooled-plasma LC-MS feature tables (processed with the R-based MDRB post-processing technique) are available and you must quantify how much of the total plasma peak area is explained by specific identified components, e.g. cyanogenic glycosides of CKXR.

name: cyclic-peptide-fragment-ion-series-interpretation
description: Use when experimental tandem mass spectra of NRP/PK compounds (e.g., desferrioxamine B, pseudacyclin A) must be dereplicated against known building-block sequences using b-ion and a-ion fragment series with defined m/z tolerances.

name: cyclic-peptide-structure-annotation
description: Use when you have 1D/2D NMR (optionally LC-MS/MS) spectra of purified or fractionated natural-product compounds of unknown structural class — e.g. cyclic peptides or swinholide-like macrolides — and need programmatic class-level annotation beyond manual characterization.

name: cyclobranch-annotator-comparator-metrics-derivation
description: Use when benchmarking NRP/PK tandem-MS annotation tools (CycloBranch, NRPro, Dereplicator, Dereplicator+) across CID vs HCD conditions and you need per-tool accuracy deltas, e.g. weighted peak-matched intensity ratios.

name: cyclobranch-sequence-notation-encoding
description: Use when a decomposed NRP/PK building-block sequence must be written in CycloBranch plain-text notation — encoding ring-closing blocks, branch ordering, and terminal modifications — for mass spectra annotation or cross-tool comparison.

name: cyp450-isoform-specific-model-training
description: Use when a training dataset of substrate molecules with bond-of-metabolism (BoM) annotations is available for a specific CYP450 isoform and the goal is a per-isoform classifier that scores each bond as reactive or non-reactive.

name: cyp450-isoform-stratified-benchmarking
description: Use when multiple in silico CYP450 SoM or metabolite predictors must be compared quantitatively per enzyme (1A2, 2A6, 2B6, 2C8, 2C9, 2C19, 2D6, 2E1, 3A4) on a common annotated test set, to quantify relative improvement in Jaccard score.

name: cyp450-metabolism-annotation-parsing
description: Use when an SDF of BoM-annotated CYP450 substrate/molecule records (e.g. EBoMD.sdf or EBoMD2.sdf from the CyProduct repository's Datasets folder) must be parsed to count or cross-check η-η, η-H, or η-SPN BoM statistics and ReactionType labels.

name: cyp450-metabolite-jaccard-comparison
