description: Use when comparing metabolite-prediction tools on human CYP450 enzymes: you have an SDF of known substrates with true metabolite lists, a set of non-reactants, and baseline tool outputs to score with Jaccard.

name: cyp450-metabolite-prediction-benchmarking
description: Use when a new or existing in silico metabolism predictor must be compared against baseline tools on a CYP450 test set, requiring matched predicted-vs-true metabolite sets and precision/recall/Jaccard metrics.

name: cyp450-phasei-phaseii-biotransformation-rule-application
description: Use when you have a compiled chemical list with SMILES/structures and need to enumerate in-silico biotransformation products across hepatic (phase I/II), EC-based, and gut microbial pathways.

name: cyp450-reactant-prediction
description: Use when a query molecule must be classified as a plausible reactant for one or more of the nine major human CYP450 enzymes, and predictions need AUROC-based benchmarking against published baselines (0.83-0.92 CypReact, 0.75 ADMET Predictor, 0.53 SMARTCyp).

name: cytoscape-bioactivity-node-visualization
description: Use when you have run the Bioactive_Molecular_Networks Jupyter notebook and submitted the .MGF plus feature table to GNPS FBMN, and you need to expose, style, and inspect the statistically correlated bioactive candidate nodes inside Cytoscape.

name: cytoscape-network-automation
description: Use when an existing Cytoscape network (e.g. a stringApp PPI network or a DEG gene list) needs to be extended with curated linkset annotations such as compound-target, gene-disease, or gene-pathway associations through reproducible scripted automation.

name: cytoscape-network-export
description: Use when a MEANtools reaction network has been converted to per-substrate DAGs and each DAG must be exported in a Cytoscape-importable format for visualization, inspection, and qualitative pathway assessment.

name: cytoscape-network-format-export
description: Use when you have an aggregated microbe-module x metabolite-module attribution score matrix (e.g. the 8x8 block matrix from MiMeNet consensus biclustering) and need a Cytoscape-loadable network file.

name: cytoscape-network-graphml-annotation
description: Use when a Mass2Motif-annotated molecular network (.graphml or edges/nodes TSV from pyMolNetEnhancer/RMolNetEnhancer) must be inspected in Cytoscape with edge colors for shared motifs and node colors for most-shared motifs per family.

name: cytoscape-network-import
description: Use when a calculated network edge list and node attribute table (source, target, edge-type, node ID columns) must be handed off to Cytoscape or other third-party network analysis/visualization software.

name: cytoscape-network-node-annotation
description: Use when a GNPS FBMN job has produced a molecular network (imported into Cytoscape ≥3.4) and the notebook output table of Pearson correlation scores and corrected p-values per feature must be joined to network nodes to flag significant bioactivity.

name: cytoscape-network-output-generation
description: Use when an NP Analyst run (e.g., on 925-prefraction BioMAP data with triplicate mzML-derived MS features) has finished feature scoring and clustering and the Cytoscape network file plus view/cluster outputs must be produced for inspection.

name: cytoscape-network-visualization
description: Use when LC-MS/MS spectra (e.g. from a MassIVE deposit like MSV000083738) must be clustered into molecular families whose composition — known vs. putatively novel analogues — must be enumerated in a graph layout.

name: cytoscape-network-visualization-styling
description: Use when a Motif_ChemicalClass_Network .graphml (or Mass2Motifs_Edges/Nodes .tsv pair) from pyMolNetEnhancer/RMolNetEnhancer must be visualized in Cytoscape with edges colored by shared Mass2Motifs and nodes colored by CF_subclass chemical classes.

name: cytotoxicity-based-fraction-prioritization
description: Decision support for selecting which roughly-fractionated extract fractions to carry into isolation and dereplication when a table of measured cancer cell cytotoxicity values per fraction is available.

name: d-mpnn-molecular-graph-encoding
description: Use when SMILES strings of metabolites need to be converted into learned, structure-aware molecular vectors (instead of fingerprints/descriptors) to support retention-order prediction or other property-learning tasks on molecules in new chemical spaces.

name: d3-interactive-tree-visualization
description: Use when spectral search matches (per-scan _matches.tsv and per-domain _count_microbe.tsv) need to be turned into a lineage-consistent interactive taxonomic tree HTML for interpreting which microbes may produce the queried metabolite.

name: data-access-performance-timing
description: Use when you must quantify data-access or visualization speed for raw LC-IM-MS spectra stored in .mza files — e.g., benchmarking MZA/HDF5 read-and-plot latency against vendor software on a defined RT window.

name: data-annotation-labeling
description: Use when a table must be subset by a categorical annotation term (e.g. GO terms, cellular localization, signaling pathway) and matched rows need an added category/annotation label while the source table stays unmodified.

name: data-augmentation-for-nmr-spectra
description: Use when training FlavorFormer (or a similar CNN–Transformer classifier) on 1H NMR spectra of flavor mixtures and the labelled training set is too small to achieve the reported test ACC ≈ 98.84 % and TPR ≈ 99.90 %.

name: data-dependent-acquisition-controller-implementation
description: Use when prototyping or modifying a DDA fragmentation strategy (e.g. Top-N, dynamic exclusion variants) for LC-MS/MS metabolomics and you need to encode the precursor-prioritisation logic as a ViMMS 2.0 controller class.

name: data-filtering-query-execution
description: Use when a user has measured lipids/polar metabolites under known pre-analytical conditions and wants analytes flagged or removed as 'unstable' based on literature stability data.

name: data-frame-structure-validation-against-mock-examples
description: Use when feature intensities and metadata have just been imported into R from a patRoon featureGroups/MFsummary object or an MS-DIAL area export, and you must confirm the resulting data frames match the expected featTable/featINFO schema before analysis.

name: data-package-generation-from-metadata
description: Use when preparing a PRIDE/MassIVE submission package (e.g., SDRF-Proteomics .sdrf.tsv) from raw-MS-file sample metadata already managed in MSConnect's SQL-backed database.

name: data-record-count-validation
description: Use when a data descriptor asserts specific file/record counts for a deposited package and you need to reproduce, classify, and verify those counts from the deposit itself.

name: data-reduction-rate-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify how much raw mass spectrometry data a filtering/denoising step removes, and whether retention of relevant signals (e.g. vendor-selected DDA-PASEF precursors) is preserved, as a function of tunable hash parameters.

name: data-to-knowledge-network-mapping
description: Use when you have a GNN-curated reaction network plus MS1 feature table and MS2 spectra, and need to constrain feature-feature edges by modified dot-product MS2 similarity (≥ 0.5) before annotation propagation.

name: database-annotation-scale-comparison
description: Use when you need to compute or restate the fraction of compounds in a large reference collection (e.g. PubChem's >91M compounds as of June 2016) that have received a chemical class annotation from a given system (e.g. MeSH thesaurus vs ClassyFire), and compare two annotation systems on scale.

name: database-annotation-volume-extraction
description: Use when a paper claims that a tool 'has been used to classify/annotate N molecules in <database>' and you need the per-database N values as structured data for adoption-coverage or impact analysis.

name: database-candidate-score-comparison
description: Use when both a de novo MSNovelist prediction and a database search result exist for the same MS2 query spectrum and you must decide which candidate structure better explains the measured spectrum by modified Platt score.

name: database-chemical-list-fusion
description: Use when building a unified chemical inventory from multiple databases and literature sources (e.g., exposome source lists) and you need a deduplicated, structurally annotated parent-chemical list.

name: database-count-verification-and-provenance-tracking
description: Use when a paper reports an aggregate count for a curated reference database (records and unique entities) and you must reproduce the build, reconcile the total, and retain source provenance.

name: database-coverage-quantification
description: Use when you have an integrated multi-source annotation database and need per-database annotation coverage and cross-source overlap statistics for metabolites vs. genes.

name: database-expansion-count-tabulation
description: Use when the goal is to quantify how many novel compounds and reactions a reaction-rule network expansion (e.g., top 500 JN1224min rules, one generation, compounds <600 g/mol) produces from a compound database.

name: database-label-filtering
description: Use when a categorate() result for GC-MS compounds must be narrowed to chemicals meeting user-defined database-membership (LOTUS, KEGG, FEMA, FDA_SPL, reactives), structural-property (MW, Rings, Groups, Atoms, NCharges), or library-group criteria before downstream extraction.

name: database-query-interpretation
description: Use when you have estimated m/z values from LC-MS metabolomics data and need to assign compound identities via m/z matching against HMDB or MassBank at ppm-level tolerances.

name: database-search-baseline-reproduction
description: Use when benchmarking a de novo structure-annotation model against database-search baselines (HSS, SSS, BDC) on EI-MS spectra, or when re-deriving headline metrics like Acc1 = 0.43 or win rate = 0.76 from deposited predictions.

name: database-spectrum-selection-statistics
description: Use when preparing HMDB, GNPS, or CASMI MS/MS spectral datasets for formula-ranking benchmarks and you must quantify how many spectra/metabolites survive the CHONSP, <1500 Da, precursor-type, and >=3-peak selection criteria.

name: database-taxonomy-structuring
description: Use when building or documenting a multiomics database and you need to enumerate its constituent data types (e.g. epigenomics marks), organizational modules, and user-facing functionalities into a structured schema.

name: database-web-scraping
description: Use when a task requires reproducing published counts or distributions (e.g. total curated BGCs, per-class and per-taxon numbers) from a database like MIBiG whose web UI exposes a statistics or repository page.

name: dataset-centering-and-scaling-for-neural-networks
description: Use when training Keras or BRNN neural networks on chemical descriptor matrices for retention time prediction, where features on different scales (e.g., XLogP vs. atom counts vs. pKa) must be centered and scaled first.

name: dataset-count-verification
description: Use when reproducing or auditing a claim that depends on exact dataset frequencies, such as the CyProduct paper's finding that η+η-forming reactions occur in only 4 of 828 η-η BoM records and all 4 are Cyclization.

name: dataset-frequency-ranking-postprocessing
description: Use when a generative model produces multiple candidate molecular graphs per spectrum and you need deterministic top-k predictions with accuracy, MCES-distance, and Tanimoto-similarity metrics on benchmarks like NPLIB1 or MassSpecGym.

name: dataset-growth-quantification
description: Use when a database release report must state how many records were added since the previous version, expressed both as absolute counts (851 new BGCs) and as percentage growth (73% from 1170 to 2021), broken down by class.

name: dataset-size-ablation-analysis
description: Use when fine-tuning a pre-trained ROASMI model with a retraining reference dataset and you want to quantify how many reference compounds are needed for transferability, grouping results by ChemSS and ChrSS.

name: dataset-split-keyed-identifier-mapping
description: Use when generating per-molecule feature or label arrays (e.g., 957-bit substructure vectors from SMILES) that must be keyed and ordered to match NMR2Struct HDF5 label/spectra files and the train/validation/test splitting dictionary.

name: datasetexperiment-container-construction
description: Use when raw measured omics data (samples in rows, variables in columns) must be wrapped together with sample and variable metadata into a struct S4 DatasetExperiment object before being fed to struct model sequences.

name: datasetexperiment-data-container-handling
description: Use when implementing or running struct/structToolbox models in R and the input data must be coerced into the DatasetExperiment format that model_train and model_predict expect.

name: datasetexperiment-object-handling
description: Use when data is held in (or can be loaded as) a struct DatasetExperiment and a multi-step statistical pipeline (e.g. mean centring followed by PCA) must be trained and its predicted outputs extracted.

name: datasetexperiment-training-and-prediction
description: Use when an analysis must train a struct model on a DatasetExperiment object and apply it to data to recover model outputs (scores, loadings, predictions), as in a mean-centring-then-PCA pipeline.

name: db-search-fdr-cluster-validation
description: Use when MS/MS spectra have been clustered (e.g. with MS-Cluster, MaRaCluster, or Falcon) and you need an independent, identification-based purity ground truth to validate a retention-time-based clustering metric such as MS-RT.

name: dbdi-plasma-ionization-in-source-fragment-identification
description: Use when a direct-injection DBDI-MS (or other plasma ionization) dataset has been aligned to a scan-by-feature XIC table and the goal is to flag which features are rivaling ion species (adducts/in-source fragments) of the same compound rather than distinct metabolites.

name: dbscan-density-based-clustering
description: Use when MRM/EIC peak features must be partitioned into groups of chromatograms with similar shapes — e.g., grouping same-transition EICs across samples while leaving low-intensity noise unclustered — as a step toward automated batch manual calibration.

name: dbscan-density-based-clustering
description: Use when you have an unlabeled tabular feature matrix (e.g. 150 samples × 4 iris measurements) and need density-based cluster assignment without pre-specifying k, with noise points flagged as -1.

name: dbscan-eps-minsamples-tuning
description: Use when a HRMS feature table from a dilution/mixing series (e.g., roadway runoff diluted into other water samples) must be grouped into fingerprint clusters, and you need principled eps and min_samples values rather than arbitrary DBSCAN defaults.

name: dd-acquisition-strategy-simulation
description: Use when you need to prototype, compare or optimise MS/MS acquisition strategies in-silico — e.g. benchmarking Top-N against SmartROI/WeightedDEW controllers — before committing to runs on a real Thermo Tribrid Fusion instrument.

name: dd-fragmentation-strategy-prototyping
description: Use when designing or tuning an MS2 fragmentation strategy (ROI-based DDA controllers, TopN baselines, duty cycles) for LC-MS/MS metabolomics and you need in silico simulation of MS1/MS2 schedules on full-scan mzML data.

name: dda-acquisition-mode-classification
description: Use when comparing Thermo RAW-file runs by scan-level acquisition composition (MS2/total scans) using MetaXtract scan-header exports, e.g. diagnosing underperforming DDA HeLa QC runs against reference runs via Figure S3-style proportions.

name: dda-acquisition-variability-analysis
description: Use when DDA LC-MS/MS system suitability data (e.g., SST acylcarnitine mixtures acquired across months, platforms, and operators) needs assessment of MS/MS product ion presence and relative intensity consistency despite stochastic DDA scan triggering.

name: dda-cycle-time-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating how DDA acquisition speed (cycle time) affects feature-extraction depth, or when validating that MS2-recognition rescue in JPA compensates for PP feature loss on DDA mzXML data.

name: dda-dia-feature-table-merging
description: Use when you have paired DDA (pooled QC) and DIA (individual biological sample) mzXML files from an LC-MS untargeted metabolomics run and need one consolidated feature-intensity table plus source-attributed MS2 spectra.

name: dda-dia-paired-file-processing
description: Use when you hold paired vendor raw files (.raw, .d, .wiff) acquired in both DDA and DIA modes on the same instrument (e.g. QE HF-X) and need to compare DDA- vs DIA-based QC metric sensitivity around recorded maintenance events.

name: dda-dia-provenance-fraction-analysis
description: Use when processing combined DDA and DIA-(SWATH) mzXML files (e.g. human urine samples) through DaDIA.R and you need to report what fraction of MS2 spectra originates from each acquisition mode and their quality distribution.

name: dda-duty-cycle-scheduling
description: Use when prototyping or simulating a DDA acquisition strategy for untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics: full-scan mzML input, a duty cycle to define, and a goal of improving coverage of picked peaks over a TopN baseline.

name: dda-fragmentation-coverage-assessment
description: Use when you have MZmine feature tables from a full-scan run and a DDA run of the same strains, plus a RegFilter-generated SPL, and you need to quantify which SPL ions were not fragmented by DDA.

name: dda-metabolomics-dataset-reprocessing
description: Use when you need to assess the sensitivity of a JPA feature-extraction workflow to peak-picking thresholds, e.g., comparing default (ppm=10, snthresh=6) versus tolerant (ppm=30, S/N=3) settings on the same raw mzXML files.

name: dda-ms1-ms2-group-index-construction
description: Use when converting DDA vendor MS data to the Aird format and you need to construct the metadata correlation index that groups MS1 spectra into contiguous blocks with their associated MS2 spectra for fast random access.

name: dda-msms-precursor-spectrum-retrieval
description: Use when a DDA MS/MS dataset has been converted to MZA (HDF5) and you need to pull out the fragmented MS2 spectrum (with m/z, intensity, and ion mobility arrival time where present) for a specific precursor identified in the metadata.

name: dda-msms-spectrum-deconvolution
description: Use when raw DDA LC-MS/MS data (e.g. a Metabolomics WorkBench study such as ST002044) must be converted into deconvolved, unique MS/MS spectra in NIST .msp format for library matching or model training/evaluation.

name: dda-spectra-deconvolution
description: Use when processing centroided DDA LC-MS/MS data (e.g. mzML from a standards mixture or clinical sample) where chimeric spectra must be deconvolved before MS2-based compound identification in R.

name: dda-spectral-deconvolution
description: Use when processing centroided DDA mzML data in which many MS2 spectra are chimeric (multiple ions co-isolated in the isolation window, 'over half' per the paper) and clean, precursor-specific MS2 spectra are needed for downstream library search.

name: dda-target-selection
description: Use when entries from a generated lipid/precursor library must be targeted for DDA on an Orbitrap and an Excalibur-compatible precursor list (.CSV) — not an '.MSP' spectral library — is the required deliverable.

name: dda-vs-dadia-workflow-comparison
description: Decision support for choosing between DDA and DaDIA acquisition when you have paired LC-MS runs of individual biological samples and pooled QC samples and need to compare significant-feature detection, MS2 coverage, and metabolite annotation counts.

name: dda-vs-targeted-fragmentation-comparison
description: Use when evaluating how many ions missed or not fragmented in DDA mode would be captured by a targeted scheduled precursor list derived from full-scan MS1 features.

name: ddac-controller-efficiency-quantification
description: Use when you have mzML files from multiple DDA controllers run on the same sample (e.g. serum/beer extracts) and need to compare scan counts, fragmentation efficiency, or MS1 cycle overhead to validate an acquisition strategy.

name: ddacoverage-and-efficiency-metric-computation
description: Use when you have full-scan mzML peak-picking files plus matching DDA (TopN) controller mzML runs and need to measure how many picked peaks were actually fragmented and how the acquisition compares to the theoretical optimum.

name: ddacoverage-fragmentation-event-matching
description: Use when mzML files from multiple DDA controller injections (e.g., TopN, SmartROI, WeightedDEW with t0 = 15 s and t1 = 120 s) must be scored by how many picked peaks were fragmented, to rank controllers on coverage.

name: ddacoverage-upper-bound-analysis
description: Use when you need to know how many ions an ideal DDA controller could fragment at least once in a given injection — e.g. before designing or evaluating a new DDA method, to quantify headroom above observed TopN coverage.

name: ddda-targeted-peak-picking-consistency-evaluation
description: Use when a batch of DDA-acquired LC-MS vendor files (.wiff, .raw) has been converted to Aird and run through MetaPro Target Search, and you must record per-compound peak-selection consistency prior to manual inspection.

name: ddia-ms2-precursor-deconvolution-context
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS data contain MS2 scans from pooled QC acquisitions whose precursor-ion associations must be reconstructed (especially DIA), before spectral library searching or compound annotation.

name: ddia-workflow-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating whether a hybrid DDA/DIA metabolomic acquisition strategy improves feature detection, quantification, and annotation over conventional DDA or DIA(SWATH) workflows, especially for urine or plasma LC-MS datasets on QqTOF instruments.

name: ddms2-mzml-raw-data-processing
description: Use when vendor LC/GC-HRMS raw data (e.g., Agilent .d) must be converted to centroided ddMS2 mzML and feature-detected with pyOpenMS (10 ppm, 2000 counts) plus MS2 alignment before PFAS feature prioritization.

name: ddms2-spectrum-to-precursor-assignment
description: Use when centroided mzML files acquired under data-dependent ddMS2 must have their MS2 spectra linked to detected MS1 features before PFAS fragment matching, KMD or suspect-screening prioritization.

name: de-bruijn-graph-peptide-assembly
description: Use when a set of de novo MS/MS peptide predictions (multi-enzymatic antibody digests) must be stitched into full-length light/heavy chain contigs without a reference database.

name: de-novo-confidence-score-filtering
description: Use when raw confidence-scored de novo peptide sequencing predictions (e.g. from Casanovo or Novor on antibody MS/MS spectra) must be filtered before assembly, and per-tool precision-score cutoffs are needed.

name: de-novo-confidence-score-threshold-calibration
description: Use when raw de novo peptide predictions from Novor, pNovo 3, DeepNovo, SMSNet, PointNovo or Casanovo must be filtered by their tool-specific confidence scores to reach a target amino-acid-level precision (here 50%) prior to ALPS de Bruijn assembly.

name: de-novo-fatty-acid-synthesis-fraction-quantification
description: Use when analysing U-13C-glucose labelling imzML imaging data (isotopologue series M+0 to M+16 of fatty acids) to estimate de novo synthesis versus uptake fractions and acetyl-CoA pool labelling per pixel or cell.

name: de-novo-generation-metric-computation
description: Use when scoring de novo molecule generation outputs from mass spectra (NPLIB1 or MassSpecGym spectra-to-molecule predictions) to produce accuracy, MCES-distance, and Tanimoto-similarity tables.

name: de-novo-molecular-formula-annotation
description: Use when processing untargeted LC–MS/MS runs (.mzML/.mzXML, centroided, positive ion mode) where precursor and fragmentation spectra must be assigned molecular formulas de novo before structure annotation, or when formula-level results feed CSI:FingerID/COSMIC structure searches.

name: de-novo-molecular-structure-prediction
description: Use when you have a low-resolution MS2 spectrum (e.g., from a miniaturized mass spectrometer) for an unknown small molecule and need de novo structure prediction without a database match.

name: de-novo-peptide-sequencing
description: Use when DDA bottom-up MS/MS spectra (MGF annotated files, immunopeptidomics, metaproteomics, or 'dark proteome' unidentified clusters) must be assigned peptide sequences without a known protein database or to detect variants, PTMs, and foreign peptides.

name: de-novo-prediction-error-classification
description: Use when de novo peptide predictions (pNovo 3, SMSNet, PointNovo, Casanovo) on antibody MS/MS data must be binned into distinct mismatch/error categories against pseudo-ground-truth PSMs, e.g. to explain tool-specific error distributions.

name: de-novo-promoter-prediction
description: Use when predicting operons from shotgun metagenome or whole-genome data where promoters must be inferred de novo from scaftig/gene-prediction files because no functional annotation or experimental promoter data exist.

name: de-novo-recall-evaluation
description: Use when de novo predictions (Novor, pNovo 3, DeepNovo, SMSNet, PointNovo, Casanovo) exist for validated antibody spectra and you must explain recall variation by missing fragment ions, missing cleavage sites, noise factor, or peptide length.

name: de-novo-structure-candidate-ranking
description: Use when an encoder–decoder RNN has produced k candidate SMILES from a predicted molecular formula and structural fingerprint and you must re-rank them to pick the top-1 structure per MS2 query spectrum.

name: de-novo-structure-generation-scoring
description: Use when tandem MS2 spectra must be annotated with de novo SMILES candidates (no spectral-library hit available), and when de novo candidates must be compared to the database (PubChem/KEGG) candidate by modified Platt score.

name: dead-end-metabolite-removal
description: Use when computing chokepoint/bottleneck reactions on an SBML genome-scale metabolic model and you need each bottleneck reaction to be balanced by at least one other producing or consuming reaction.

name: decalin-motif-group-comparison
description: Use when a set of classified natural-product SMILES (e.g. spirotetronate macrolides from NP Atlas) must be split by presence/absence of a structural motif such as decalin and their predicted-potency scores compared between subgroups.

name: decision-boundary-visualization-on-rank-scale
description: Use when comparing discovery regions of reproducibility procedures (e.g., MaRR vs copula mixture model) on paired rank lists, especially to diagnose boundary shape when top signals are near-perfectly correlated and correlation erodes for lower ranks.
tools: idr (copula mixture model, Li et al. 2011)

name: decision-theory-aggregation-function-implementation
description: Use when reconstructing or re-implementing the MS2DECIDE knownness score k: multi-annotated MS/MS features from GNPS, Sirius, and ISDB-LOTUS must be ranked by an expert-modeled, piecewise-linear preference function.

name: decoding-throughput-measurement
description: Use when comparing MS data encoders (ZDPD vs Zlib-only vs other compressors) on m/z arrays and you must quantify decode wall-clock time or MB/s throughput, not just compressed size.

name: deconvoluted-spectrum-network-edge-construction
description: Use when EI GC-MS data has been deconvoluted into individual compound fragmentation spectra (e.g. via MSHub/GNPS auto-deconvolution) and spectrally related compounds must be grouped into molecular networks without precursor-ion masses.

name: deconvolution-output-quality-assessment
description: Use when GC-MS spectral-match annotations carry cosine similarity and balance score columns and you need to select thresholds that minimize top-match FDR, e.g. before building molecular networks or validating deconvolved compound identifications.

name: deconvolved-spectra-quality-assessment
description: Use when you have deconvolved MS2 spectra produced by DecoMetDIA (or another SWATH-MS deconvolution tool) from biological samples and need to quantify how many spectra are annotatable, or to benchmark deconvolution quality against the reported ~90% annotation success rate.

name: decoy-based-fdr-estimation
description: Use when annotating small-molecule LC–MS/MS spectra against a structure database (e.g. PubChem/HMDB) and you must separate correct from incorrect CSI:FingerID hits and estimate FDR, or when calibrating hit scores into posterior-like confidences.

name: decoy-based-fdr-estimation
description: Use when DIA-lipidomics TG annotations need empirical confidence estimation — i.e., after LipidIdentifier target identification and a parallel DecoyIdentifier/allDecoys run, when decoy and target hits must be scored and filtered at a fixed FDR (e.g., 0.1) with standards-based validation.

name: decoy-feature-injection-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether a pathway ranking method degrades gracefully as annotation completeness falls, i.e. when missing/noisy peak features must be simulated via decoy-feature injection into background pathways.

name: decoy-metabolite-set-simulation
description: Use when you must quantify how robustly pathway-ranking methods (mPLAGE vs ORA vs GSEA) behave under missing metabolomics peaks — e.g. annotated peak-feature intensity matrices where you can inject controlled, randomised feature removal and score recovery against known true pathways.

name: decoy-spectra-fdr-estimation
description: Use when evaluating annotation accuracy and FDR of network-based metabolite annotation (e.g. MetDNA3 MRN/SMN/FCN propagation) against decoy MS2 reference spectra on Orbitrap untargeted metabolomics datasets.

name: deep-classifier-metric-evaluation
description: Use when a CNN/sequence classifier trained on TIC-normalized raw MS spectra (e.g. NSCLC, CRLM, RCC, Canine Sarcoma) needs Accuracy/F1 evaluation on a hold-out split plus statistical comparison against a baseline.

name: deep-convolutional-architecture-implementation
description: Use when binary class labels (e.g., pathway presence/absence) must be predicted from 1D waveform signals derived from network auralization, and a very deep 1D convolutional architecture with BCE loss is required.

name: deep-learning-batch-prediction
description: Use when you have a pretrained model plus a set of NMR mixture spectra (e.g. from a Zenodo deposit) and need to predict compound identification and compute ACC/TPR/FPR metrics for the whole dataset in one batch run.

name: deep-learning-hyperparameter-replication
description: Use when comparing model variants that must differ only in one design factor (e.g. single-mode vs. dual-mode training) so observed performance differences can be attributed to that factor rather than hyperparameter drift.

name: deep-learning-input-ablation-analysis
description: Use when a trained deep learning model has uncertain which inputs contribute to performance, and you can define parallel model variants differing only in the input features to compare held-out metrics such as RMSE.

name: deep-learning-model-inference
description: Use when a trained massNet VAE must be applied to MSI spectra (HDF5-converted imzML, 85,062 m/z variables) to obtain latent codes or downstream 2D UMAP class-separation maps.

name: deep-learning-model-training
description: Use when you have a parquet dataset of (molecule, spectrum) pairs with columns such as mol_id, inchi, rdmol, cv_id, and spect, plus an expconfig YAML, and need to fit a GNN spectral prediction model from scratch.

name: deep-learning-model-training-gpu
description: Use when reproducing or extending FIDDLE's formula-identification training: you need to train TCN spectrum-prediction variants and a rescore model on MoNA/NIST Q-TOF MS/MS spectra with GPU acceleration and compare ablation contributions.

name: deep-learning-neural-network-training-h2o

name: deep-learning-nmr-spectrum-reconstruction

name: deep-learning-performance-benchmarking
description: Use when validating a deep-learning classifier on bioactivity-labeled metabolomics samples and comparing its metrics (AUC, accuracy, F1) against classical ML baselines across folds.

name: deep-learning-retention-time-prediction
description: Use when small-molecule ECFP fingerprints plus experimental reverse-phase RT values are available and the goal is to predict LC–MS retention times, compare ML vs. similarity-based baselines at Tanimoto thresholds, or rank candidate metabolite identities by predicted RT.

name: deep-learning-spectral-fingerprint-regeneration
description: Use when a lipidomics pipeline needs a dense theoretical MS2 library covering all chain compositions and C=C double-bond positions, and measured reference spectra are too sparse to support platform-independent annotation.

name: deep-learning-spectral-signal-decoding
description: Use when raw FT-ICR MS transients acquired at low mass resolution (e.g. 64k points, resolution 10,000 at m/z 400) must be decoded into high-resolution spectra (1M points, resolution 160,000 at m/z 400) for MSI or SCMS.

name: deep-learning-test-set-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when a trained NMRQNet CRNN model must be evaluated on a held-out simulated nine-metabolite test set, and per-metabolite accuracy values must be compared against reported benchmarks (92% overall, 0.978-0.995 per metabolite).

name: deep-learning-training-hyperparameter-management
description: Use when training CNN or sequence models on TIC-normalized raw MS spectra (e.g. NSCLC, CRLM, RCC, Canine Sarcoma) where fold-level reproducibility and significance testing against a baseline are required.

name: deep-neural-network-peak-picking
description: Use when a processed 2D or pseudo-3D NMR spectrum contains significantly overlapped cross-peaks that defeat local-maxima picking, and quantitative per-peak intensities, concentrations, or relaxation parameters are needed.

name: deep-neural-network-retention-time-matching
description: Use when labeled feature pairs (m/z, charge, RT, intensity) from aligned LC-MS runs are available and you must decide whether a deep learning direct-matching model outperforms classical ML classifiers (RF, KNN, SVM, LR) on RT alignment quality.

name: deep-neural-network-retention-time-prediction
description: Use when you need to predict LC-MS retention times (RTs) for small molecules from structural features (fingerprints/descriptors), including both retained and non-retained molecules (RT < 300 s), and want accuracy.

name: deep-neural-network-similarity-regression
description: Use when you need to identify unknown metabolites whose MS/MS spectra are not in a database, by scoring structural similarity against known reference compounds instead of direct spectral matching.

name: deep-neural-network-training
description: Use when you need to classify LC-MS spectral peaks as true or false from nontargeted metabolomics data, especially when you have manually reviewed peak examples (e.g., ~1300 training peaks) and peak-extraction features rendered as raster images.

name: defective-run-metrics-matrix-plotting

description: Use when lipid identifications from a LipiDex 2 pipeline run (e.g. .

name: degree-threshold-cluster-pruning

name: dehp-biotransformation-spot-check
description: Use when a BioTransformer metabolite-prediction run over a large chemical list (e.g., the ~20,061-chemical human exposome set) needs a positive-control spot-check before trusting aggregate per-module metabolite counts.

name: deisotoped-ion-library-matching

name: delta-encoding-compression-benchmarking

name: delta-encoding-of-retention-times

name: delta-encoding-of-sorted-spectra
description: Use when a monotonically ordered numeric array (e.g. a centroided m/z list) contains large integers whose adjacent values differ by small, near-constant amounts, and you need a smaller compressed footprint than generic Zlib-only compression.

name: dem-table-visualization-with-volcano-plots-and-heatmaps

name: dendrogram-visualization
description: Use when you have a samples-by-chemical-class relative-abundance matrix (e.g. from ConCISE consensus ClassyFire annotations of ion features) and need to visualize which samples group together, e.g. to test whether toxic and non-toxic strains separate.

name: dendrogram-visualization-of-lipidome-clustering

name: denoising-autoencoder-training

name: denovo-peptide-sequencing-evaluation

name: densenet-ensemble-training-tuning

name: density-based-spectrum-clustering

name: density-matrix-basis-set-simulation

description: Use when ST and SM data come from adjacent or serial tissue sections whose spot coordinate systems differ, and you must learn or apply a rotation/translation plus non-linear distortion before aggregating SM intensities onto ST spots.

name: differential-abundance-analysis
description: Use when comparing taxonomic (species-level) or molecular abundances across two or more condition groups — such as 3xTg versus WT fecal shotgun metagenomic profiles — and you need log-fold changes with FDR-adjusted significance.

name: differential-abundance-analysis-metabolomics
description: Use when you have a group-labelled, CSA-annotated aligned compound matrix (InChIKey/SMILES/formula meta-variables) and need per-compound differential statistics plus chemical-class enrichment (e.g. ChemRICH) between disease and control groups.

name: differential-abundance-comparison-treatment-vs-control
description: Use when HRMS full-scan LC-MS runs from treated vs. control samples need targeted re-extraction of known precursor ion m/z targets and a fold-change/direction comparison against a published result.

name: differential-abundance-log2fc-computation
description: Use when preprocessed LC-MS/MS feature intensity tables and MS/MS spectra must be statistically compared across sample groups (e.g. mushroom type), with per-feature log-2 fold changes extracted after spectral-similarity clustering.

name: differential-abundance-metabolite-analysis
description: Use when you have a metabolomics abundance matrix with disease/control (or mutant/wild-type) group labels and need to flag which named metabolites are differentially abundant — e.g. acd5 vs Col-0 chlorophyll b, D-glucose, proline decreased;

name: differential-abundance-overlap-analysis
description: Use when comparing two or more normalization strategies for metabolomics LC-MS data and you need a downstream functional measure of agreement — overlap of differentially abundant metabolites — rather than QC-RSD or replicate-MAD metrics alone.

name: differential-abundance-testing
description: Use when one or more normalized metabolomics intensity matrices (rows = metabolites/features, columns = sample runs) must be compared for a binary phenotype contrast to detect DAMs and assess normalization-method agreement.

name: differential-abundance-testing-microbiome
description: Use when a disease/control metagenome study requires testing which operon-derived KEGG ortholog pathways differ in abundance between groups, e.g. 74 T2D samples vs 71 healthy controls from mapped gut metagenome reads.

name: differential-correlation-significance-testing
description: Use when comparing whether a feature's Pearson correlation with a user-selected target feature differs significantly between two groups of samples (e.g. tumor vs non-tumor), and a per-feature significance test on the correlation difference is required.

name: differential-expression-plotting
description: Use when an experimental biologist has a gene expression table (e.g. ma_example.csv) from differential expression analysis and needs an MA plot rendered via a web interface instead of R code.

name: differential-feature-cross-referencing
description: Use when you have a list of theoretical biotransformation candidate m/z values and a separate table of dysregulated/DE features from untargeted LC-HRMS data, and need to preannotate which candidates map to observed features.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when a gene expression matrix (e.g., RNA-Seq counts or microarray intensities) has two metadata-defined sample groups and the goal is to flag genes significantly up- or down-regulated between them, as in tumor vs non-tumor LIHC comparison.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when you have a joint ST-SM AnnData with integrated Leiden cluster labels and need cluster-specific marker genes and metabolites (e.g., Imm_4 markers CYP2J2, ACSM2A, Phosphatidylglycerol, PA (24:0/24:1(15Z))).

name: differential-jacobian-ratio-analysis-between-conditions
description: Use when two metabolomic condition subsets (e.g. Cífková et al. 16C control vs 6C stress) are available and the goal is to rank metabolites by changes in their regulatory interaction strength via Jacobian ratios.

name: differential-lipid-abundance-analysis
description: Use when the input is a lipid feature (intensity) matrix plus a phenotype file and the goal is differential abundance and enrichment across lipid classes, chain length, and degree of saturation.

name: differential-lipid-abundance-analysis
description: Use when a targeted lipidomics dataset (Skyline CSV export or numerical matrix with sample-annotation table) must be statistically compared across clinical groups, e.g. HighFat_water vs NormalDiet_water or Cancer vs Benign, with or without confounder correction.

name: differential-lipid-abundance-testing
description: Use when a normalized lipid abundance matrix (from LipidSearch/LIQUID output or Metabolomics Workbench import) is available and the goal is to find differentially abundant lipids between groups defined in a target-file metadata design, optionally with covariates or batch correction.

name: differential-lipidomics-results-interpretation
description: Use when you have a two-group (or multi-group) differential lipidomics comparison and want to know which lipid classes or chain attributes are preferentially enriched among the regulated lipids.

name: differential-metabolite-abundance-analysis
description: Use when joint spatial transcriptomics–metabolomics data have been integrated and clustered by SpatialMETA and you need cluster-defining genes/metabolites plus metabolite pathway enrichment for one sub-cluster vs. the rest.

name: differential-metabolite-abundance-testing
description: Use when a pixel x m/z feature matrix (e.g., 14,260 pixels x 3,044 ions from AFAD-ESI positive-mode mouse brain IMS at 100 um) has region assignments (auto-clusters or manual ROIs) and you need up/downregulated differential metabolites between two regions.

name: differential-metabolite-abundance-testing
description: Use when you have matrices normalized by different strategies (tGAM/rGAM/rLOESS, QC-RLSC, SERFF, TIGER) and need to quantify how the choice of normalization changes the differential abundance hit set.

name: differential-metabolite-annotation-counting
description: Use when a spatial metabolomics feature matrix (pixels × m/z ion peaks) has been pixel-clustered (e.g., UMAP-kmeans) and you must identify metabolites significantly upregulated in one anatomical region versus another, with per-region annotation counts.

name: differential-metabolite-comparison-between-maize-varieties
description: Use when comparing two maize root DESI-MSI datasets whose mass signatures were already extracted along a linear developmental gradient by DIMPLE and you need a conserved/unique partition of pooled m/z peaks per variety.

name: differential-metabolite-detection-across-imputation-methods
description: Decision support for whether missing-value imputation choices materially change the differential-metabolite lists and enriched pathways in an LC-MS untargeted metabolomics feature table, e.g. when a case study applied only one imputation method.

name: differential-metabolite-feature-detection
description: Use when raw MS1 LC-HRMS data from paired treated vs. heat-inactivated control incubations (e.g., 1,021 pesticides in human liver S9) must be feature-detected, aligned, and differentially screened to feed reaction-guided metabolite annotation.

name: differential-network-edge-count-comparison
description: Use when a two-condition metabolomics network has been estimated under alternative lambda/regularization settings and you must tabulate total vs case-specific vs control-specific vs shared edges to judge tuning impact.

name: differential-network-module-agreement-thresholding
description: Use when a DNEA object with estimated two-condition partial correlation networks (e.g. TEDDY metabolomics, 134 metabolites) must be partitioned into metabolic modules and you need to set or adjust the consensus agreement threshold (tau).

name: differential-pathway-activity-t-testing
description: Use when comparing two sample groups (e.g., DM2 vs NGT microarray profiles) to find pathways whose PLAGE-derived activity levels differ significantly, using t statistics calibrated by max-t label permutations.

name: differential-peak-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when a fitted MSI segmentation exists (e.g., spatial shrunken centroids in Cardinal on imzML-derived pig fetus liver/heart data) and you must report which peaks each segment differentially enriches or lacks.

name: differentially-expressed-gene-list-curation
description: Use when you have a ranked differential-expression table (e.g. Mecp2-/y vs. wild-type Purkinje cells) and need a filtered DEG gene list extended with pathway annotations from a curated linkset such as WikiPathways.

name: diffusion-based-annotation-prioritization
description: Use when LC-MS peaks have already been matched to KEGG candidates and clustered, and a context-based prioritized list of compounds is needed to reduce false positives and rank annotations.

name: diffusion-model-checkpoint-inference
description: Use when trained DiffSpectra/DMT checkpoints and multi-modal spectra (IR, Raman, UV-Vis) from QM9S are available and the goal is spectra-conditioned molecular generation with reproducible top-k accuracy metrics.

name: diffusion-model-gradient-computation
description: Use when you need interpretability of a conditioned diffusion generator (e.g. DiffSpectra/DMT): specifically, to determine the temporal order in which spectral evidence drives structural decisions across the 1,000-step denoising trajectory.

name: diffusion-pseudotime-trajectory-inference
description: Use when joint protein-metabolite single-cell data (e.g., co-registered IMC protein and TOF-SIMS/SIMS metabolite matrices from tonsil germinal centers) should be ordered along a maturation trajectory and metabolite trends computed along pseudotime.

name: diffusion-sampler-evaluation
description: Use when you have a trained spectra-conditioned DiffSpectra (DMT) checkpoint and QM9S test spectra (spectra_version ir/raman/uv/allspectra) and need to generate molecules and reproduce accuracy/MCES ablation tables.

name: diffusion-sampler-temperature-sweep
description: Decision support for choosing the noise-scaling temperature τ when generating candidate molecules with a spectra-conditioned diffusion sampler, especially when generated sets look overly deterministic (low τ) or too random (high τ).

name: diffusion-sampling-ablation-comparison
description: Use when reproducing the DiffSpectra 2D-only vs joint 2D/3D ablation: you have the QM9S test spectra and trained checkpoints and need to quantify how the 3D coordinate stream changes exact-structure accuracy and similarity metrics.

name: diffusion-score-prioritization-evaluation
description: Use when LC-MS feature annotation has been produced with a diffusion-prioritization setup (e.g. mWISE over FELLA or RClass networks) and you need entity-level sensitivity/F1 metrics and structure-based Tanimoto comparisons to judge prioritization quality.

name: dilution-factor-parameter-sweep-analysis
description: Use when validating a normalization estimator under dilution: a two-group feature-intensity table with a known true dilution factor (e.g. k=1.5) and varying imbalanced fractions of up-regulated features.

name: dimensional-reduction-pca-analysis
description: Use when the goal is unsupervised dimensional reduction of a tabular feature matrix (e.g., iris 4 morphological features across 3 species) to reveal underlying patterns or produce PC1-PCn score tables with explained-variance ratios.

name: dimensionality-reduction-umap-projection
description: Use when you have MS2DeepScore embedding vectors (e.g. 500-dim per MS/MS spectrum spanning both ionization modes) and need a single 2D chemical-space map, like the Rumex sanguineus UMAP.

name: dimeric-structure-filtering
description: Use when a cleaned structure table contains entries whose SMILES still has a '.' after RDKit parsing and MolVS sanitization, so dimeric entries must be dropped before standardizing to InChI.

name: dims-lcms-case-study-reproduction
description: Decision support for choosing Sample Filtering thresholds in Galaxy-M metabolomics pipelines when planning whether downstream Missing Values Imputation (e.g. KNN) will be needed after filtering removes peaks with missing observations.

name: dims-lcms-peak-list-annotation
description: Use when a peak list that has already been peak-picked, aligned, and filter-cleaned (DIMS SIM-stitched or XCMS-processed) needs metabolite annotation by accurate mass, adduct and isotopic-abundance patterns, and compound-database lookup.

name: dims-transient-fourier-processing
description: Use when the input is direct infusion mass spectrometry (DIMS) FT-ICR transient .dat files organized in selected ion monitoring (SIM) windows, and a peak list per sample is needed before alignment, filtering and PCA.

name: dinosaur-feature-extraction-dia
description: Use when you have raw DIA-MS runs (e.g. single-cell or bulk LC-MS cohorts) that need feature lists containing m/z, charge, RT and intensity columns before ID-free RT alignment with DeepRTAlign.

name: direct-infusion-ms-feature-alignment
description: Use when input is raw .mgf, .mzML or .mzXML spectra from direct injection / plasma ionization (DBDI) MS with no LC separation, and a row-per-feature, column-per-scan DataFrame is needed before imputation or adduct detection.

name: direct-parent-selection-by-feature-weight
description: Use when a compound has multiple candidate ChemOnt categories after category reduction and you need to determine the single direct parent for a taxonomic classification record.

name: direct-peak-integration-assigned-components
description: Use when raw 1D 1H NMR serum/plasma spectra (e.g. Bruker IVDr 600 MHz) must be converted into a per-metabolite concentration/integral table without fitting or deconvolution, relying on SMolESY preprocessing and predefined spin-system bins.

name: directed-acyclic-graph-tree-conversion
description: Use when you have a mass distance network of LC-MS feature pairs (e.g. 13C/12C 1.0034 Da isotope steps, 22.9893 Da Na+ adduct shifts) and need to organize ions into per-compound trees with inferred neutral masses.

name: directed-graph-clustering
description: Use when two or more independently processed LC-MS datasets must be aligned into a Combined Dataset, and pairwise subalignment match tables are available to load into a graph-based clustering step.

name: directed-graph-cycle-removal-to-dag
description: Use when a directed reaction network built from mass-shift annotations contains cycles among metabolites and you need per-initial-metabolite DAGs from which the longest valid reaction path can be extracted.

name: directed-vs-mixed-enrichment-mode-interpretation
description: Use when interpreting ReporterScore/GRSA enrichment results on KO abundance data and you need to decide whether reporter score signs can be read as pathway-level increasing or decreasing trends.

name: direction-of-change-annotation
description: Use when ΔCt qPCR data for metabolic enzyme genes are collected across oncogene-transformed versus control epithelial cells and each gene's direction of change must be tabulated with statistical support.

name: directional-db-mismatch-probability-computation
description: Use when validating whether a structural-comparison tool's double bond position matching is correct, by quantifying mismatch probabilities over high-resolution reference lipid entries from SwissLipids or LIPID MAPS.

name: discoverable-gene-population-background-selection
description: Use when running a hypergeometric over-representation test that compares a metabolite-interacting gene set against GWAS-network genes and you must choose a statistically defensible population size N (the discoverable genes).

name: discrete-diffusion-process-design
description: Use when a generative model must output molecular graphs with a prescribed atom count/type composition (formula-constrained generation), by diffusing and denoising bond-type entries of the adjacency matrix.

name: discrete-graph-diffusion-molecule-sampling
description: Use when a tandem mass spectrum plus an inferred chemical formula must be converted into de novo candidate structures, or when reproducing DiffMS-style top-k accuracy, Tanimoto, and MCES metrics on NPLIB1 or MassSpecGym.

name: discrete-graph-diffusion-training
description: Use when conditional molecular structure generation requires sampling valid, formula-constrained graphs with predefined heavy-atom composition, e.g. de novo generation from mass spectra on NPLIB1 or MassSpecGym benchmarks.

name: discriminating-marker-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when an untargeted LC-MS/MS feature quantification table must be scored for marker-selection performance against a curated ground-truth feature list (e.g. 836 targeted MTBLS733 features).

name: discriminating-marker-selection
description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking the marker-selection stage of an untargeted metabolomics workflow on MTBLS736 (SA vs SB groups), where a ground-truth set of 68 true discriminating markers is available to score sensitivity and specificity.

name: discriminative-metabolite-comparison-across-processing-methods
description: Use when a metabolomics feature table has matched patient/subject metadata and you want to quantify how LMM-based covariate adjustment changes which metabolites pass a VIP > 1 threshold relative to unprocessed data.

name: discriminative-power-roc-evaluation
description: Use when two reproducibility-detection methods must be compared on power/discrimination over simulated rank lists — e.g., MaRR vs. the Li et al. copula mixture model — with empirical FDR checked at alpha = 0.05.

name: disease-classification-model-evaluation
description: Use when a re-trained or pre-trained DeepMSProfiler model must be scored on an independent LC-MS testing set (e.g., MetaboLights MTBLS1129) and its metrics compared against published values.

name: disease-cohort-spectral-match-profiling
description: Use when you have MASST/Fast Search outputs for a spectrum list (e.g., .mgf or USI .csv) and want to know which human body sites or disease cohorts (T2D, IBD, AD) the matching spectra appear in.

name: disease-network-visualization
description: Use when a deep-learning metabolomics run has produced ranked m/z contribution scores (e.g. ensemble_RISE.npy) and the goal is to connect those metabolic signals to proteins and pathways for disease interpretation.

name: disease-prediction-fine-tuning-evaluation
description: Use when fine-tuning a pre-trained metabolomic language model on binary chronic-disease endpoints from UK Biobank NMR metabolomics and benchmarking AUC against ML baselines with paired significance tests.

name: disease-relevance-metabolite-tagging
description: Use when producing the final ROIAL-NMR Result Show tables for a disease-versus-control NMR study and metabolites must be highlighted as disease-relevant against a curated disease list (HMDB-derived).

name: disease-vs-control-cell-comparison
description: Use when single-cell transcriptomics data contain both disease (e.g. AD) and healthy-control cells of the same type (e.g. neurons) and the goal is to identify which predicted metabolites distinguish the two groups.

name: disease-vs-control-metagenome-comparison
description: Use when paired-end gut metagenome reads must be mapped to predicted operon sequences and per-sample KO/pathway differential abundance tested between disease and control cohorts.

name: dissimilarity-matrix-computation-ft-icr-ms
description: Use when you have a normalized FT-ICR MS peak-intensity table with assigned molecular formulas and need pairwise sample dissimilarities (Bray-Curtis, Euclidean, Jaccard) as input to PERMANOVA group testing or NMDS/PCA ordination.

name: dissimilarity-score-density-visualization
description: Use when you have matched-pair dissimilarity scores from a metabolite-identification step and need to verify that a parametric normal-mixture density (EM-fitted) agrees with a non-parametric kernel density estimate.

name: distance-based-similarity-ion-retrieval
description: Use when you have a preprocessed MSI data matrix [X*Y,P] plus peak list [P,1] and need to retrieve colocalized or isotope ion partners by similarity of learned ion-image representations rather than raw spectral correlation.

name: distance-correlation-computation
description: Use when an eigen-analysis-based p-value adjustment method originally defined on Pearson correlations must be re-expressed on distance correlations for metabolomics features, or when Meff estimates need to account for nonlinear dependence structure.

name: distance-distribution-histogram-visualization
description: Use when you have feature vectors (e.g., BiG-SLiCE Euclidean pHMM-domain features) plus known group labels (e.g., curated MIBiG compound/function classes) and need to check — visually and quantitatively — that within-group distances separate from between-group distances.

name: distance-matrix-pca-embedding
description: Use when you must reproduce or validate a LipidSpace-style structural lipid space: a set of lipid species (e.g. a homologous PC series) needs a pairwise structural distance matrix embedded by PCA, or an arc-like sequential PC1/PC2 ordering must be verified.

name: distance-matrix-symmetry-verification
description: Use when assembling an n×n global distance matrix from pairwise dataset comparisons (e.g. 10 comparisons for 5 serum datasets from PXD034932) and you must confirm the metric is symmetric and the diagonal is zero.

name: distance-preservation-scoring-of-embeddings
description: Use when a 2D t-SNE embedding of spectral or feature-distance data must be tuned — choose a perplexity from a grid by comparing each embedding's distance-preservation performance rather than picking a default value.

name: distortion-map-subtraction
description: Use when optical images of macroscopic samples were captured with flatbed scanners or cell phone cameras and target coordinates show moderate distortion or imperfect perspective before MALDI-MS coordinate generation.

name: distributed-hash-computation-spark
description: Use when TimsTOF frames are too large for single-node LSH hashing and you must classify windows as signal/noise via hash collisions across a cluster, then quantify per-frame data reduction.

name: distribution-statistics-verification-against-reported-values
description: Use when reimplementing a model evaluation pipeline and you need to confirm summary metrics like '% of predictions with Tanimoto >= 0.50' or mean similarity match the article's reported numbers.

name: divergent-colorscale-threshold-encoding
description: Use when quantitative pairwise LC–MS/MS similarity matrices (ms2deepscore, modified cosine, spec2vec) must be inspected cell-by-cell around a tunable similarity threshold, especially for small node selections where network views are too coarse.

name: dmodx-residual-variance-profiling
description: Use when processed pooled-QC (QCpool) metabolomics or lipidomics data must be screened for outliers whose behavior is not explained by the main PCA structure, i.e., samples with high residual distance-to-model.

name: dna-adduct-database-tabulation
description: Use when compiling or verifying a curated DNA adduct database (.xlsx plus metadata .docx) from literature-reported and suspected adducts, or when recomputing its descriptive statistics such as mass range and study-design splits.

name: dna-adduct-identifier-harmonization
description: Use when compiling or merging DNA adduct lists from different publications or databases and adduct names, formulas, or structures are inconsistent, duplicated, or ambiguous.

name: dna-adduct-mass-spectrometry-data-parsing
description: Use when LC-HRMS DNA adductomics data must be annotated and experimental MS/MS spectra need comparison against in silico predicted fragments from CFM-ID for DNA adducts.

name: dna-adduct-reference-standard-annotation
description: Use when untargeted HRMS DNA adductomics data must be annotated against experimental MS/MS fragments of purchased reference standards (e.g., N6-Me-dA, 8-oxo-dG, M1-dG), or when reproducing/verifying an experimental-fragments datatable.

name: dna-methylation-epigenomics-analysis
description: Use when annotating methylation latent factors (e.g. MOFA2 factors from MethylationEPIC beta matrices) with biological traits via EWAS atlas enrichment, or when planning CpG-level methylation analysis steps.

name: dnn-architecture-inspection
description: Use when released model files (e.g., HDF5/Keras checkpoints) exist for a paper's DNN and you must reconstruct per-network architecture details — layer shapes, activations, dropout, output sizes — to answer what network design was adopted.

name: dnp-structure-source-dataset-harmonization
description: Use when building a benchmark or reference set that pairs MS/MS spectra (.mgf) with organism-source metadata from the Dictionary of Natural Products, requiring structure harmonization via short InChIKey and taxonomy filtering.

name: docker-container-deployment
description: Use when deploying QC4Metabolomics or its Shiny/R modules (module_Files, module_TrackCmp, module_Contaminants, etc.) on a server or workstation, or when a reproducible demo/test instance of the QC pipeline is needed for mzML-based untargeted metabolomics QC.

name: dockerized-cheminformatics-tool-execution
description: Use when a workflow needs a cheminformatics predictor or parser (e.g., CFM-ID fragment prediction) applied batch-wise to many structures (SMILES/InChI/.mol) and a Docker image of the tool exists.

name: dockerized-classification-service-deployment
description: Use when a workflow needs repeat programmatic NPClassifier calls on many SMILES strings (e.g. batch classifying an NP Atlas structure list tagged bacterial vs fungal) and a local dockerized server is preferred over external APIs.

name: dockerized-instrument-data-pipeline-testing
description: Use when validating that an instrument data pipeline—specifically QC4Metabolomics's continuous Dockerized processing—detects newly acquired mzML files within the expected near-real-time window.

name: dockerized-nmr-workflow-execution
description: Use when raw 1D NMR FID data (Bruker or Agilent/Varian, or nmrML) must be processed through calibration, baseline correction, realignment, and binning via NMRProcFlow deployed as a local Docker web application.

name: dockerized-tool-execution
description: Use when a runtime benchmark must compare prediction tools with heterogeneous installs (CFM-ID via Docker, ICEBERG via its repo, FIORA natively) over an identical compound list, and per-spectrum prediction times must be tabulated.

name: domain-level-score-threshold-calibration
description: Use when comparing BGC detection tools at matched domain-level stringency: you have per-domain prediction scores and labeled calibration data, and need cutoffs at defined FPR/TPR operating points before merging domains into clusters.

name: domain-sequence-similarity-scoring
description: Use when computing pairwise distances between biosynthetic gene clusters at scale and the distance must capture both Pfam domain copy-number differences and domain sequence identity, e.g. for GCF network construction from antiSMASH output.

name: domain-stratified-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a predictor's claimed improvement must be verified per application domain — e.g. testing whether adding a rule-based module (MSRB) helps on foodomics/metabolomics-like molecule sets but not exposomics-like ones.

name: dopamine-metabolite-mapping
description: Use when a haCCA-integrated mouse-brain object (b_predict) already maps MALDI-MSI metabolite intensities onto Visium spot coordinates and you must test whether a gene's spatial expression co-localizes with a specific metabolite such as dopamine or 3-MT.

name: dose-response-curve-fitting
description: Use when metabolomics feature abundances (e.g., LC-MS peak tables) are measured across multiple dose levels of an exposure and you need fitted dose-response curves and per-feature benchmark dose (BMD) values for chemical risk assessment.

name: dose-response-curve-visualization
description: Use when a multiclass metabolomics dataset contains spiked reference metabolites with known dose levels and you must visually verify whether a ranked processing workflow (e.g., HAM+NON+CUT+[CON-RAN] vs KNN+NON+LOG+[VAS-LIN]) preserves the true dose gradient.

name: dose-response-threshold-estimation
description: Use when you need to prioritize chemicals by risk from exposure estimates plus predicted acute toxicity (LD50) data, and no measured chronic reference dose or BMD is available for most compounds.

name: dot-product-fragment-presence-scoring
description: Use when a patRoon or MS-DIAL feature table has been imported into GetFeatistics and each annotated feature needs an automatic Schymanski-style annotation confidence level derived from MS/MS match quality (MoNAScore for patRoon; dot product plus fragment presence for MS-DIAL).

name: dot-product-similarity-scoring
description: Use when you need a conventional cosine/dot-product similarity score between two centroided MS/MS spectra, e.g. as the baseline against which entropy-similarity robustness or library-search performance is compared.

name: dot-product-spectral-library-matching
description: Use when annotating MS2 spectra of LC-MS metabolomic features (e.g. DDA, DIA(SWATH), or DaDIA data on a Bruker Impact II UHR-QqTOF) by spectral library matching, or when binning spectra into high- vs low-quality classes using a dot-product threshold.

name: dot-product-spectral-matching-scoring
description: Use when matching an unknown ESI-MS/MS spectrum against a set of predicted spectra from candidate chemical structures to produce a compound-identification ranking (e.g. CASMI challenge submissions or library search with CFM-ID).

name: dot-product-spectral-scoring
description: Use when dereplicating query MS/MS spectra (with precursor charge, precursor m/z, and peak lists) against accumulated reference library spectra and a peak-level similarity score such as a normalized dot product is needed for identification.

name: dot-product-spectral-similarity-scoring
description: Use when annotating LC-MS/MS or LC-MSn lipid features against an in-silico spectral library (e.g. LipiDex 2 Library Generator output) and you need to score match quality of MS2 and MS3+ spectra before applying identification thresholds.

name: dot-product-spectral-similarity-thresholding
description: Use when consolidating per-sample deconvoluted GC×GC–MS feature lists into cross-sample consensus features, and you need a spectral-similarity rule to merge duplicate/variant detections of the same compound across samples.

name: dotnet-cross-compilation-and-runtime-bundling
description: Use when an R (or other scripting-language) package must execute a compiled .NET/C# vendor library cross-platform, and the wrapper binary must be pre-built and bundled rather than compiled on the user machine.

name: double-bond-position-nomenclature-handling
description: Use when parsing lipid shorthand names that carry double-bond position/geometry annotations (e.g., FA 18:2(9Z,12Z)) and you must verify that a structural similarity computation either counts DB positions or treats all DB matches as mismatches.

name: double-bond-position-recognition
description: Use when you need theoretical MS/MS fragment ions for N-Me derivatized (C═C bond-targeted) unsaturated sterol lipids whose double bond positions must be recognized from molecular structures before spectra generation.

name: double-quantum-shift-matching-tolerance-configuration
description: Use when running the PyINETA matching step on 13C INADEQUATE peak networks: candidate network-to-database assignments must be gated by a double-quantum shift tolerance (DQMT, ppm) in addition to the carbon-shift (CSMT) and connectivity (NCMT) tolerances before scoring.

name: dp-cost-matrix-truncation
description: Use when running the dynamic-programming phase of G.A.M.E. at high mass decimal precision (D=5) on GPU and peak device memory becomes the binding constraint rather than compute time.

name: dplyr-lazy-aggregation-pipelines
description: Use when an HRMS Parquet file converted by arcMS is too large to load fully in RAM (e.g. ~1.9 Gb example) but chromatograms, spectra, or aggregated summaries must be extracted quickly.

name: dpph-bioactivity-label-binning
description: Use when raw DPPH radical-scavenging measurements for wild soybean accessions must be converted into binary class labels for supervised bioactivity prediction, and the article's 0.4/0.6 cutoffs must be reproduced.

name: drift-assessment-from-score-plots
description: Use when you have a post-curation extracted feature data matrix from a LC–MS untargeted metabolomics run that includes pooled/intrastudy QC injections, and you need to verify data quality — outlier detection, QC clustering tightness, and detection of injection-order–related signal drift — using.

name: drift-correction-method-comparison-statistics
description: Use when multiple drift correction or quantification strategies have been applied to the same targeted LC-MS/MS dataset and you need to quantify their agreement (e.g., test whether non-IS strategies mutually correlate at Pearson r > 0.9).

name: drift-correction-strategy-comparison
description: Use when a targeted LC-MS/MS sequence shows intensity drift and multiple drift-correction strategies (IS, QC-based loess, custom/weighted bracketing) have produced concentration tables that must be evaluated for agreement and residual drift.

name: drift-reduction-bias-evaluation
description: Use when comparing drift-correction strategies (IS correction, QC-based correction, bracketing) on a targeted LC-MS/MS sequence to quantify residual bias and confirm drift reduction objectively.

name: drift-time-retention-time-sample-alignment
description: Use when you have multiple GC-IMS spectra loaded into a GCIMSDataset (e.g. threeketones or urine samples) and need them comparable across samples before peak detection and ROI clustering.

name: drift-tube-ccs-reference-matching
description: Use when processing traveling-wave IM-MS (e.g. Waters SYNAPT XS) calibration data (.mzML calibrant files) to derive class-specific power-law calibration parameters anchored to drift-tube CCS references, prior to calibrating unknown TWCCSN2 features.

name: droplet-array-data-processing
description: Use when you have macroMS-exported spectra for a nanoliter droplet array (e.g., bacterial cultures spotted by a liquid handler) and need per-droplet fatty acyl peak-area ratios to classify samples.

name: drug-analog-spectra-filtering
description: Use when converting raw drug-analog matches (from GNPS Drug Library spectra vs. untargeted metabolomics data) into a reliable propagated analog library, i.e., when analog spectra must be filtered to keep only chemically explainable, non-duplicate, exposure-informative MS/MS hits.
tools: GNPS (Global Natural Product Social Molecular Networking)

name: drug-class-metabolite-count-aggregation
description: Use when you have per-drug metabolite annotations plus a drug-class mapping (Supplemental Table 1) and need per-class counts of predicted vs detected metabolites or detection-rate percentages.

name: drug-class-stratified-rate-computation
description: Use when you have per-drug lists of curated metabolite features (m/z and retention time) and BioTransformer 3.0 predictions, and need to report overall plus per-drug-class rates of unpredicted metabolism.

name: drug-combination-synergy-analysis
description: Use when you have ranked top-predictor features (e.g., the top 20 features per metabolite from Metab8D_network.xlsx with 0-8 confidence scores) and want to test whether drugs or drug combinations against those predictors show synergistic Bliss interaction scores.

name: drug-exposure-annotation
description: Use when untargeted metabolomics data (raw LC-MS/MS files, .mgf/.mzML/.mzXML, or MZmine feature tables) must be screened for drug exposures without clinical records, self-reports, or medication tracking.
tools: GNPS (Global Natural Product Social Molecular Networking)

name: drug-exposure-frequency-quantification
description: Use when estimating how often a drug was actually taken in an untargeted metabolomics cohort by tallying parent-drug and metabolite/analog MS/MS hits per sample, matrix (plasma, feces, etc.), or time point.
tools: GNPS (Global Natural Product Social Molecular Networking)

name: drug-exposure-stratification-clustering
description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics cohort (e.g., fecal samples with MS/MS feature tables) has drug annotations and you must derive empirical exposure strata instead of trusting self-reported or record-based medication metadata.

name: drug-like-criteria-molecular-filtering
description: Use when a combinatorially enumerated derivative database (hydrogen-to-R-group substitutions on a drug core template) must be pruned to drug-like, synthesizable candidates before downstream spectrum prediction or ranking.

name: drug-metabolite-time-course-annotation
description: Use when untargeted LC-MS/MS data from a timed (e.g. 0 h vs 72 h, triplicate) microbial incubation of known drugs must be screened for drug analogs and each shared analog classified as microbial vs abiotic.

name: drug-repurposing-hypothesis-classification
description: Use when you have a validated list of essential genes from constraint-based deletion analysis of a metabolic model and a curated drug-target association table, and need to enumerate and label candidate drug-repurposing hypotheses.

name: drug-structure-name-search-pubchem
description: Use when building a curated drug reference library and you need to enumerate drug candidates with canonical structures and cross-references before pulling MS/MS spectra.

name: drug-target-mapping
description: Use when you have an essential-gene list from single-gene deletion analysis of a metabolic model and want to enumerate approved/known drugs targeting those genes and flag which drug-gene hypotheses are novel.

name: drug-target-mapping
description: Use when you have ranked top predictor features from trained metabolite models (e.g. Metab8D_network.xlsx top-20 features) and need to convert them into drug-target / drug-combination hypotheses with synergy scores.

name: drug-tax-structural-class-encoding
description: Use when building CCS prediction inputs for Mol2CCS: molecules are given as SMILES and you must assemble the seven 1-D feature vectors (including the 35-bit Drug Tax structural class encoding) that augment the molecular graph and adduct representation.

name: dso-metabolomics-matrix-handling
description: Use when a cleansed peak table (matrix of samples x peaks) plus sample and metabolite labels and biological/blank class assignments must be packaged for PLS-Toolbox multivariate tools in Galaxy-M.

name: dso-xml-construction-from-peak-matrix
description: Use when an aligned, labeled peak table (e.g. from Galaxy-M's Align Samples or XCMS-Basic-Birmingham-Pipe) must be converted into the DSO XML format consumed by PLS-Toolbox-based cleansing tools.

name: dtccs-library-lookup
description: Use when IM-MS lipidomics data are spiked with fully U13C-labeled yeast extract lipids and measured CCS values must be compared against a reference DTCCSN2 library to quantify CCS bias per lipid class-adduct combination.

name: dtccs-mz-regression-matching
description: Use when processing singly charged TWIM-MS features (m/z, charge state, retention time, arrival time) from a Waters SYNAPT XS-type platform and you must assign each feature to small molecule, lipid, or peptide class before reporting a calibrated TWCCSN2 value.

name: dtccs-n2-value-annotation
description: Use when reviewed drift tube IM-MS results from CCSfind must be committed to a database with DTCCS N2 values, experimental settings, and full mobility spectra retrievable per entry.

name: dtccs-nitrogen-calibration-conversion
description: Use when processing LC-DTIM-MS mzML data with a confirmed primary-ion RT for a targeted molecular formula and single-field CCS calibration coefficients (Tfix, Beta) for nitrogen drift gas are available, and DTCCS(N2) values plus adduct-ion mobility spectra are needed.

name: dtccsn2-library-matching
description: Use when IM-MS lipidomics samples are spiked with U13C-labeled yeast extract and measured CCSN2 values (e.g., TIM-MS) must be bias-assessed or corrected against reference DTCCSN2 values per lipid class-adduct combination.

name: dtw-warping-postprocessing
description: Use when XCMS-flagged misaligned features have been realigned by ncGTW and the realigned profiles must be converted back into XCMS RT warping functions and repositioned peaks for downstream grouping and peak-filling.

name: dual-encoder-feature-fusion
description: Use when you need to predict LC retention times from SMILES/InChI structures under a new chromatographic method and want to jointly exploit both topological graph structure and molecular fingerprints rather than a single descriptor stream.

name: dual-encoder-representation-learning
description: Use when a query (e.g. an MS/MS spectrum) must be matched against a discrete candidate pool (e.g. molecular scaffolds) via embedding-space similarity, rather than by generative or rule-based lookup.

name: dual-isotope-flux-model-comparison
description: Use when HRMS isotopologue distributions from a dual-isotope tracer (e.g., [13C5,15N2]glutamine time course) are available and you must decide whether dual-isotope INST-MFA reduces flux uncertainty versus single- or parallel-label designs.

name: duplicate-detection-and-spectrum-deduplication
description: Use when combining several public MS/MS spectral databases into one curated reference library and you must remove cross-source duplicates (e.g. MoNA vs GNPS, HMDB vs MassBank) without losing provenance.

name: duplicate-lipid-identifier-detection
description: Use when a CSV/TXT lipidomic data matrix is about to be ingested and you must guarantee row identifiers (lipid names) are unique before grouping, zero-variance checks, or statistics run.

name: duplicate-metabolite-deduplication
