description: Use when verifying metabolite coverage from DDA LC-MS/MS organ/serum database sheets where per-sheet lists overlap and a deduplicated union count must be reconciled with a reported unique-metabolite total.

name: duplicate-molecular-species-consolidation
description: Use when a lipidomics concentration matrix (post internal-standard quantification) still contains SPLASH Lipidomix/standard rows and multiple rows for the same molecular species label that must be merged before downstream analysis.

name: duplicate-smiles-collapsing
description: Use when a compound-database m/z match table contains multiple database entries describing the same chemical structure (identical SMILES) and you need one deduplicated putative annotation per structure without discarding true structural isomers.

name: dynamic-exclusion-weight-computation
description: Use when simulating or implementing WeightedDEW ion prioritization for DDA LC-MS/MS: converting MS1 survey-scan intensities plus prior MS2 fragmentation times into a per-ion nonbinary exclusion weight and a per-scan priority ranking.

name: dynamic-exclusion-window-handling
description: Use when implementing or tuning a Top-N DDA controller in ViMMS 2.0 where precursors selected for MS2 must be suppressed from repeated selection via dynamic exclusion (mz_tol / rt_tol windows), or when choosing between Top-N and its dynamically-exclusion-weighted variant WeightedDEWController.

name: dynamic-ppm-binning-peak-alignment
description: Use when centroided .imzML (or .h5ad/.h5mu) MSI data must have peaks aligned across all pixels before lock-mass recalibration, lipid annotation, or quantitation, especially for omics-scale lipidomics.

name: dynamic-programming-shortest-path-optimization
description: Use when a complete LC-MS/MS run has per-spectrum scored candidate lists (e.g. from IOKR, queried from PubChem) plus a trained retention-order model, and you need a joint metabolite assignment consistent with predicted elution order.

name: dynamic-range-compression
description: Use when a metabolomics concentration table (post-normalization, post-imputation) still shows skewed, heavy-tailed distributions that would violate normality assumptions in downstream PCA or group-comparison analyses.

name: early-stage-lung-adenocarcinoma-detection
description: Use when raw LC-MS serum metabolomics data (mzML or .npy) must be classified into lung cancer / benign lung nodule / healthy groups, and the target is early-stage (stage-I) adenocarcinoma detection accuracy.

name: early-stopping-hyperparameter-tuning
description: Use when training a neural ranking/retention model from molecular embeddings where a pairwise binary cross-entropy loss must be tuned and monitored to avoid overfitting on limited reference retention data.

name: early-stopping-model-selection
description: Use when fine-tuning a generative chemical language model on a train fold (e.g., 90% of known metabolites) and you need an automatic, loss-based stopping criterion rather than a fixed number of epochs.

name: ecc-layer-implementation
description: Use when reconstructing SigmaCCS- or Mol2CCS-style CCS predictors from SMILES+adduct inputs, i.e. when the architecture must combine graph-based ECC layers with a parallel dense feature branch.

name: ecdomainminer-biosynthetic-domain-mining
description: Use when building or rebuilding a curated pHMM feature library restricted to biosynthetic protein families (e.g., for BiG-SLiCE feature set 1) from a full Pfam release plus antiSMASH domain models.

name: ecfp-fingerprint-generation
description: Use when you have molecular structures (SMILES strings or SDF files) and need fixed-length ECFP representations as model inputs for in-silico EI mass spectrum prediction with NEIMS or similar fingerprint-based models.

name: ecfp-fingerprint-generation
description: Use when molecules must be featurized as fixed-length count/circular fingerprints to feed a spectral-prediction or molecular ML model, e.g., encoding NIST 2017 library molecules for NEIMS inference.

name: ecfp-molecular-fingerprint-featurization
description: Use when a neural-network or regression model needs a fixed-length molecular representation computed from SMILES/SDF structures, e.g. to predict electron-ionization mass spectra in the NEIMS pipeline.

name: edge-list-construction
description: Use when building gene-gene interaction edge lists for topology-based pathway enrichment, starting from a gene identifier set (e.g. breastcancer2012 row names) and pathway databases such as 'kegg' and 'reactome'.

name: edge-list-export-and-validation
description: Use when a top-prioritized feature from globaltest-based msFeaST testing must be interrogated in network context: extract its k-nearest spectral neighbors as a weighted edge list and verify cross-cluster connectivity.

name: edge-loss-algorithm-selection
description: Use when estimating weighted adjacency matrices for pathway enrichment from a gene-gene edge list whose connected components exceed 1,000 genes, and a tractable block-diagonal adjacency structure is needed for NetGSA.

name: edger-differential-abundance-testing
description: Use when you have an annotated MALDI/MSI m/z intensity matrix plus spatial cluster labels (e.g. tissue regions) and need a reproducible ranked list of m/z peaks that differ significantly between those regions.

name: edited-mrs-sequence-parameter-configuration
description: Use when generating a vendor- and sequence-specific simulated basis set for an edited MRS experiment (MEGA-PRESS, HERMES, HERCULES) and you need to map your scanner acquisition parameters onto MRSCloud's simMRS.json options.

name: edta-free-peak-removal-plasma-nmr
description: Use when input spectra are 1H NMR spectra of EDTA-anticoagulated human plasma (e.g., the 40 MDS-family plasma samples) and the goal is accurate metabolite/lipoprotein quantification with NMRQNet before CRNN fitting.

name: effective-number-of-tests-estimation
description: Use when you have M metabolite features with a features-by-samples matrix (e.g. 761 metabolites x 1054 COPDGene subjects) and need to correct marginal association p-values via an effective-number-of-tests (Meff) estimate instead of raw M.

name: ego-network-subgraph-extraction
description: Use when a single LC-MS/MS feature (node) in the t-SNE overview needs its local neighborhood examined — i.e., the user wants to see which features are adjacent under a given similarity threshold, and optionally expand that neighborhood by regenerating under new constraints.

name: ei-cosine-similarity-spectral-matching
description: Use when networking EI GC-MS fragmentation spectra (e.g. MSHub/GNPS deconvoluted compound spectra) where the molecular ion is absent, so relationships must be inferred from spectral similarity alone.

name: ei-mass-spectrum-embedding-similarity-search
description: Use when query EI mass spectra must be identified against a million-scale in-silico library where exact nearest-neighbor matching is too slow, and recall@1/recall@10 accuracy plus per-query wall time must be benchmarked.

name: ei-mass-spectrum-library-matching
description: Use when measured GC-EI-MS spectra must be matched against a large in-silico spectral library, especially for compounds beyond NIST 2017, and exact nearest-neighbor search over millions of spectra is too slow.

name: ei-mass-spectrum-prediction-model-substitution
description: Use when a PS2MS-style synthetic NPS database already exists and you want to evaluate whether a different in silico EI spectrum predictor (e.g., RASSP) improves or degrades ranked identification of GC/EI-MS queries relative to the NEIMS baseline.

name: ei-mass-spectrum-similarity-scoring
description: Use when a GC/EI-MS analyte's spectrum does not match any known reference library and candidate identities must be ranked against predicted derivative spectra.

name: ei-ms-spectral-transformer-inference
description: Use when you have GC-EI mass spectra (e.g. from an msp file or synthetic NEIMS/RASSP test splits) and need de novo molecular structure reconstruction via the pretrained SpecTUS model without reference spectral libraries.

name: ei-ms-spectrum-encoding
description: Use when preprocessing intensity-binned EI-MS peaks (m/z <= 500, <= 300 peaks) for transformer-based de novo SMILES translation, or when choosing a peak/intensity encoding scheme for a spectral translation model.

name: eic-alignment-across-multiple-ms-files
description: Use when a batch of converted LC-MS files (.aird from TripleTOF .wiff or QE HF .raw) has been Target-Searched in MetaPro against a library with 'mz' and 'rt' columns, and you need consistent automated peak selection per compound across all batch files prior to manual QC inspection.

name: eic-baseline-correction
description: Use when raw LC-MS EICs for targeted metabolites carry a sloping or curved baseline that must be removed before peak detection with MassSpecWavelet in TarMet.

name: eic-coelution-correlation-analysis
description: Use when inspecting a PFAS or other HRMS feature (m/z of interest) in raw ddMS2 mzML data and you need to identify coeluting ions — in-source fragments or adducts — by correlating EICs of all detected features in the same RT region.

name: eic-derivatives-zigzag-index-computation
description: Use when scoring/filtering EICs extracted from LC/MS metabolomics profiles prior to peak detection, especially for EICs with high background signal or only a single peak where the MCQ index is unfair.

name: eic-extraction-accurate-mass
description: Use when you need to visualize and validate prioritized PFAS features in mzML raw data — e.g., extract EICs for suspects or homologue series, correlate coeluting EICs to flag in-source fragments/adducts, or overlay MS2 diagnostic fragments and isotope patterns.

name: eic-extraction-from-mzml
description: Use when starting a metScribeR library-construction run: you have standards_df.csv (common_name, monoisotopic_mass, pos/neg_mode_mzML_file_path) and adduct_df.csv (adduct, change_from_neutral, mode) and need EICs per adduct before find_eic_peaks.

name: eic-extraction-from-mzml
description: Use when raw mzML MS1 spectra and a list of detected features (m/z, rt) must be converted into aligned EIC data matrices — e.g. to train or apply PeakDetective peak-artifact classifiers.

name: eic-image-label-matching
description: Use when raw Orbitrap/QTOF LC-MS data plus a curated set of manually labeled EIC images (double-peak vs single-peak ground truth) are available and peak-detection accuracy must be quantified per software tool.

name: eic-intensity-correlation-grouping
description: Use when an LC/MS peak table contains co-eluting isotopes, adducts and fragments that must be clustered per analyte using EIC intensity correlation across samples rather than retention-time co-elution alone.

name: eic-peak-alignment-grouping
description: Use when you have detected EIC peak lists (retention time, intensity, FWHM per peak) from multiple MRM samples plus estimated RT drifts and need to align/group peaks across samples to support batch manual calibration.

name: eic-peak-clustering-and-model-peak-selection
description: Use when processing centroided SWATH-DIA mzML data where all ions in a wide m/z range are co-fragmented, producing chimeric MS2 spectra that must be relinked to their originating MS1 precursors before compound identification.

name: eic-peak-metric-thresholding
description: Use when constructing a retention-time reference library from replicate LC-MS injections of chemical standard mixtures and you need to decide, per metabolite, whether its EIC peak passes user-specified Std/Blk, retention-time RSD, and intensity thresholds.

name: eic-peak-quality-assessment
description: Use when a feature-extraction step (e.g. DaDIA.R rescued features or significant metabolic features from DDA/DaDIA LC-MS data) yields candidate peaks whose automated detection quality needs validation before downstream annotation or statistical comparison.

name: eic-peak-quality-labeling
description: Use when building or retraining a CNN peak-quality model for LC-MS metabolic feature fidelity, where a corpus of EIC plots must be manually annotated as good or poor quality before training and validation.

name: eic-peak-review-interpretation
description: Use when building an in-house LC-MS RT/m/z metabolite standard library in metScribeR and every peak that passed filtering must be manually assessed for inclusion in the final library.

name: eic-peak-shape-correlation-deconvolution
description: Use when raw LC-MS all-ion fragmentation (AIF) centroid chromatograms are available and parent–fragment ion relationships must be deconvoluted from peak-shape correlation before fragment-library matching or feature annotation.

name: eic-plot-reconstruction-from-features
description: Use when you have a metabolic feature table with m/z and retention-time columns and the corresponding .mzXML or .mzML raw file, and need rendered EIC plots that a CNN-based quality classifier (EVA/pyEVA) can score.

name: eic-quality-index-computation
description: Use when scoring extracted ion chromatogram (EIC) quality prior to peak detection in LC/MS metabolomics workflows, or when benchmarking the MCQ index against alternatives (e.g., the global zigzag index) on normal, high-background, or single-peak EIC profiles.

name: eic-quality-label-counting
description: Use when characterizing the training data behind a peak-quality classifier: parse per-plot good/poor quality labels from manually annotated EIC plots and aggregate counts per project.

name: eic-quality-threshold-classification
description: Use when filtering extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) from LC/MS metabolomics profiles before peak detection — especially when EICs contain high background signals or only a single peak, where the MCQ index scores unfairly and cutoff thresholds must be tuned.

name: eic-reference-selection
description: Use when processing MRM/SRM extracted-ion chromatogram peak tables from multiple samples and a per-transition-group reference trace must be chosen before estimating retention time drifts or grouping EICs.

name: eigengap-cluster-number-estimation
description: Use when you have a fused sample-similarity network (e.g., integrated DNA methylation and metabolomics similarity networks) and need a data-driven estimate of the optimal cluster count before spectral clustering.

name: eigenmetabolite-mutant-ranking
description: Use when you have a metabolomics feature matrix across many mutant lines plus sample metadata, and need to rank mutants on a co-abundance module's eigenmetabolite to nominate lines for validation of a metabolite–gene association.

name: eigenvalue-regularization-transformation
description: Use when a KEGG-derived pathway's normalized Laplacian must be regularized before being embedded in the kernel function of a semi-parametric kernel machine regression, particularly for sparse or disconnected pathway graphs.

name: eigenvalue-variance-explained-interpretation
description: Use when MCA (or a related eigen-decomposition method) has been run on categorical behavioral items and you need to quantify and report how much variation each dimension explains.

name: ejection-time-window-intensity-integration
description: Use when processing full-scan acoustic ejection mass spectrometry (AEMS) data in precursor ion (PI) or neutral loss (NL) mode from SCIEX .wiff/.wiff.scan files and a per-ejection spectrum or quantified signal is needed.

name: ejection-window-delineation
description: Use when you have an AEMS run's ejection-time table plus a TIC trace and must assign each acoustic ejection a bounded detection window with per-ejection peak timing.

name: elastic-net-metabolite-abundance-prediction
description: Use when paired microbiome-metabolome data (samples x taxonomic/functional features, samples x metabolite abundances) is available and per-metabolite Elastic Net linear regression predictions with Spearman correlation evaluation are needed as a benchmark or standalone predictor.

name: elastic-net-penalized-logistic-regression
description: Use when a wide-format feature table (samples in columns, metabolomics features in rows with unique feature identifiers) plus a design file with a binary grouping variable is available, and the goal is penalized feature selection rather than plain significance testing.

name: elastic-net-prediction-imputation
description: Use when targeted metabolomics datasets (e.g., LC/MS FFAs, bile acids) contain left-censored missing values caused by LOD/LOQ (MNAR) and distribution-preserving imputation is needed before univariate or multivariate analyses such as PLS-DA.

name: elastic-net-regularized-modeling
description: Use when a phenotype-grouped metabolomics feature matrix (e.g., CRC vs. PolyP vs. HC serum metabolite intensities) must be turned into a predictive classifier whose discriminatory power is quantified by ROC AUC in train and test pipelines.

name: elastic-net-regularized-regression
description: Use when DDA MS2 spectra are flagged as chimeric (multiple centroids inside the isolation window exceeding the acquisition threshold) and their contribution to the observed mixed spectrum must be untangled via penalized regression.

name: elbo-endpoint-prediction-optimization
description: Use when training a discrete diffusion / Markov bridge generative model whose denoiser must predict the final clean molecular graph at each diffusion step, e.g. MADGEN stage 2, with classifier-free spectrum dropout.

name: electronic-and-chemical-noise-denoising-of-annotated-spectra
description: Use when query MS/MS spectra (e.g. MSP files) contain electronic or chemical noise that lowers entropy similarity against reference library spectra, and the candidate compound's SMILES or molecular formula and adduct are known.

name: electronic-msms-spectrum-denoising
description: Use when evaluating whether electronic noise-ion removal improves or degrades spectral-similarity discrimination (e.g., AUROC of cosine similarity for same vs. different compound pairs), or when deciding whether to include denoising in an MS/MS library preprocessing pipeline.

name: electronic-noise-ion-removal
description: Use when a raw MS/MS spectrum (e.g., from an Orbitrap instrument, loaded from .msp) contains co-occurring 'grass' noise ions with identical intensities that must be stripped before chemical denoising or spectral similarity matching.

name: electronic-resource-inventory-extraction
description: Use when an article claims harmonization/curation from a named number of electronic resources (e.g. 'over 40 electronic resources') and a verifiable, structured source inventory must be extracted from the text.

name: electropherogram-peak-annotation
description: Use when pre-processing targeted full-scan MSI-CE-MS metabolomic data with high migration-time variability (e.g. ~105 s drift), where peak alignment or time-warping tools fail on multiplexed runs and mzML files must be annotated against a targeted mass list.

name: element-composition-restriction
description: Use when ranking candidate structures from HR-MS/MS compound databases (PubChem, ChemSpider) or a user-supplied SDF and isotope signals or prior chemical knowledge imply certain elements must be present, required, or excluded.

name: element-count-aggregation
description: Use when you have a formula-annotated aligned peak table (e.g. from IDSL.UFA) and want to detect homologous chemical-class sub-structure patterns such as polymeric/cyclic chains or fixed-carbon halogenated families (PCBs, PBDEs, Cl-PFTrEAs).

name: element-count-feasibility-verification
description: Use when evaluating whether an element-constrained formula generation space (SIRIUS decomp-style limits) excludes a meaningful share of reference formulae from a spectral dataset such as NPLIB1 before benchmarking de novo formula predictors.

name: element-element-correlation-analysis
description: Use when a pre-processed ICP-MS ionome matrix (e.g. S. cerevisiae mutants profiled across ions like Ca44, K39, Mg25, P31, Zn66 in ppm) must be examined for element-element correlations and relevance networks.

name: elemental-composition-database-filtering
description: Use when MS/MS peak lists fail to yield the correct structure from a composition-restricted candidate database, e.g. isotope ratios indicate Cl and the correct halogenated molecule is absent from candidate sets.

name: elemental-composition-node-labeling
description: Use when constructing metabolite graphs from chemical structures (e.g., a PubChem-derived SDF) as the first stage of the DEREPLICATOR+ fragmentation-graph pipeline before enumerating bond cleavages for spectral dereplication.

name: elemental-composition-parsing
description: Use when you have raw molecular formula strings from a reference dataset (e.g. NPLIB1/canopus_train) and must determine which formulae survive element-count constraints imposed by candidate-generation tools like SIRIUS decomp or MIST-CF.

name: elemental-formula-tracer-atom-enumeration
description: Use when correcting LC-MS isotope-labeling FAM/MDV data for natural abundance and tracer impurity at low resolution, or when building the NRE baseline against which resolution-dependent corrections (MDT/ULS) are compared.

name: elemental-image-background-extraction
description: Use when a 2D LA-ICP-MS elemental image (e.g. a calibrated 56Fe, 55Mn, 63Cu, or 66Zn NumPy array) must be split into tissue and background before quantification or mask-based feature selection.

name: elemental-image-channel-registration-for-spatial-correlation
description: Use when two or more elemental image channels of identical pixel dimensions from a LA-ICP-MS acquisition need quantitative colocalisation statistics, or when a region-of-interest (lasso/rectangle) selection must restrict the coefficient inputs.

name: elemental-image-colormap-comparison
description: Use when preparing elemental images from LA-ICP-MS data for publication or review and you need to show or justify why the default rainbow (Jet) colormap risks misinterpretation versus a perceptually uniform alternative.

name: elution-peak-detection
description: Use when raw centroided LC-MS mzML acquisitions must be preprocessed into feature tables with per-sample elution peaks and m/z–retention-time annotated features, e.g. inside a pcpfm experiment directory.

name: em-algorithm-latent-variable-inference
description: Use when merged GCxGC/TOF-MS peak lists must be assigned to reference library metabolites, and each observed spectrum may match multiple library entries so a latent-variable model with posterior confidence is needed.

name: em-algorithm-parameter-estimation
description: Use when metabolomics feature data must undergo metabolite identification via the hierarchical model with latent variables, and EM convergence behavior of the four parameter estimates must be demonstrated and verified.

name: em-convergence-diagnostics
description: Use when fitting a hierarchical statistical model with an EM algorithm to metabolomics data (e.g., for metabolite identification) and you must verify that all parameter estimates stabilize, e.g. within ~200 EM iterations.

name: em-parameter-density-fitting
description: Use when you have fitted mixture-model parameters (component means, variances, mixing weights) from an EM step and need to check they yield a density consistent with the empirical distribution of the underlying scores.

name: embedding-nearest-neighbor-ranking
description: Use when analyzing preprocessed MSI matrices (e.g. rat brain [X*Y,P] data, 198 x 422 pixels) to retrieve nearest-neighbor ions for a query ion image, especially for low-SNR isotope discovery where PCC/R2 fail.

name: embedding-quality-metric-computation
description: Use when comparing MS/MS-to-embedding prediction quality across spectral variants (individual collision energy, merged, merged+neutral loss) on a test split, or when validating that a trained ChemEmbed CNN reproduces reported embedding-quality numbers.

name: embedding-similarity-retrieval-evaluation
description: Use when you have learned dense representations of ion images from an MSI dataset and need to quantify embedding quality via colocalized-ion retrieval or leave-one-out linear classification.

name: emperor-command-line-visualization-generation
description: Use when you have a PCoA ordination (principal coordinates file) from beta diversity analysis plus a mapping/metadata file (e.g., 5,740 samples, 120 metadata columns) and need interactive 3D metadata-colored visualization.

name: emperor-pca-visualization-preparation
description: Use when you have a per-file chemical annotation matrix (e.g. from GNPS library search over MassIVE/MSV000084206 files) and need unsupervised PCA coordinates formatted for Emperor visualization.

name: empirical-bayes-batch-effect-removal
description: Use when a feature table TSV (e.g. an imputed pcpfm table) shows batch-driven sub-clustering in QAQC PCA plots and sample metadata contains a batch designation field to correct against.

name: empirical-bayes-location-scale-estimation
description: Use when a log2-normalized metabolomics dataset in CSV format (samples in rows, features in columns, batch levels in the first column) shows across-batch signal drift and you need to correct it and compare empirical-Bayes correction models.

name: empirical-bayes-posterior-variance-estimation
description: Use when standardizing exercise (or other condition-induced) log2 fold-changes against within-population expression variability at the gene-by-tissue level, e.g. asking how many genes' 8-week endurance-training effect sizes exceed 2 SD of GTEx expression variance.

name: empirical-compound-annotation
description: Use when an empCpd JSON from a pcpfm experiment has experimental MS2 spectra mapped to features (e.g. moniker 'MS2_mapped') and Level 2 spectral-library annotations are needed against MoNA or user .msp libraries.

name: empirical-compound-grouping
description: Use when a pcpfm/Asari feature table must be pre-annotated into empirical compounds (grouping adducts and isotopologues) before MS1 or MS2 annotation of an LC-MS metabolomics experiment.

name: empirical-compound-json-parsing
description: Use when a khipu preannotation run (JSON output over an LC-MS feature table like ecoli_pos.tsv) must be interpreted per compound — extracting isotope branches per adduct, inferring which isotopologue envelope a compound shows, or matching an inferred neutral mass to a candidate metabolite.

name: empirical-compound-preannotation
description: Use when you have a peak/feature table (m/z, rtime, intensities) from LC-MS metabolomics or isotope-tracing experiments and want to group degenerate ions into empirical compounds before database annotation.

name: empirical-correlation-network-analysis
description: Use when you have a metabolomics data matrix (e.g. plasma GC-TOF-MS peak values with BinBase identifiers for unknowns) and want data-driven metabolite-metabolite edges that do not depend on pathway knowledge or structural annotation.

name: empirical-fdr-estimation
description: Use when you must call reproducible genes from two ranked high-throughput replicate lists with error control at a nominal FDR level (e.g. alpha=0.05) and no parametric assumptions on dependence or signal distribution.

name: empirical-formula-composition-search
description: Use when a processed, aligned peak list (DIMS or LC-MS) with accurate-mass m/z values needs elemental composition assignments before compound-database searches like Single-Peak Search or Peak-Pattern Search.

name: empirical-pvalue-threshold-selection
description: Use when empirical p-values from mb_vip_permtest are available for a multi-assay LC-MS feature matrix (HPOS_/LPOS_/LNEG_ blocks) and significant predictors must be selected at a p-value threshold for counting, comparison against univariate models, or downstream structural clustering.

name: empirical-survival-function-estimation
description: Use when replicate metabolomics data have been reduced to per-metabolite rank pairs across sample pairs and you need a nonparametric estimate of the reproducible proportion pi_1 plus an mFDR-controlled rejection threshold.

name: empty-row-removal-verification
description: Use when irregularly-spaced MALDI/ESI spectral replicates have been mapped onto a theoretical m/z grid with subMALDI (createSpecDF/mapSpectrum) and the row count must be reduced and validated before saving the mapped data frame.

name: end-to-end-representation-module-design-for-ms-classification
description: Use when raw 1D MS spectra (TIC-normalized, m/z-binned at 0.1 Da, e.g. spectrum_dim 12000/9900/15000) must be transformed into multi-channel feature tensors feeding CNN/LSTM/Transformer classifiers, replacing single-channel or hand-crafted feature selection.

name: endogenous-metabolite-subsetting
description: Use when running Met-ID Met-ID/FMP-10 derivatization searches against a parsed HMDB SQLite database and the biological sample is expected to contain only endogenous metabolites, so exogenous and unspecified HMDB records should be excluded from the candidate pool.

name: endogenous-reference-marker-pooling
description: Use when processing untargeted LC/HRMS peaklists from multiple samples or batches where systematic retention time drift must be corrected without spiked standards, using endogenous peaks as retention index markers.

name: energy-based-candidate-scoring
description: Use when you already have per-precursor formula candidate sets (e.g. from SIRIUS decomp with 10 ppm window, RDBE-permissive, down-selected by FastFilter to top 256) and need to pick the most probable formula/adduct from positive-mode MS/MS spectra.

name: enriched-pathway-count-comparison-across-datasets
description: Decision support for choosing between an organism-specific and a reference (non-organism-specific) pathway database set when running ORA on metabolomics data;

name: enrichment-dot-plot-visualization
description: Use when you have a ranked pathway enrichment table (Fisher's Exact Test with Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values) and need a dot plot that highlights the top significantly enriched pathways for figures or validation.

name: enrichment-dotplot-visualization
description: Use when you have a MetSEA/fgsea results table with NES, pval and padj columns (or Fisher enrichment results with Adjusted_P_value) and need a dot plot of -log10(adjusted p-values) to present top enriched pathways.

name: enrichment-odds-ratio-analysis
description: Use when you have ProGeM bottom-up summary output plus high-confidence causal gene assignments (e.g. 227 mQTLs or 562 cis-pQTLs) and need to quantify which criteria (nearest gene, VEP IMPACT, cis-eQTL) enrich for true causal genes.

name: enrichment-result-visualization
description: Use when you have a reporter_score_res object (pathway-level reporter scores with adjusted p-values) from GRSA and need ranked enrichment tables and figures showing which modules are up- or down-enriched per group.

name: enrichment-rmse-method-benchmarking
description: Use when simulated or standard-spiked isotope-labeling data with known ground-truth enrichment are available and you must decide which correction method (modified MDT, modified ULS, original ULS, NRE, FAM) is most accurate for a given tracer/resolution combination.

name: enrichment-rmse-tabulation
description: Use when comparing the accuracy of natural-abundance/resolution-effect correction methods on simulated or experimental isotope-labeling data, where corrected enrichment can be scored against a known theoretical enrichment (e.g. 20% 13C/15N/34S).

name: enrichment-score-computation
description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking GSEA results on the Mootha type 2 diabetes (17 DM2 / 17 NGT / 9 IGT) or airway epithelia smoker datasets, or when validating a pathway-analysis method against published ES values and permutation p-values.

name: ensemble-deep-learning-interpretability
description: Use when a trained ensemble of deep-learning classifiers on raw LC-MS data (mzML or .npy arrays over a retention-time × m/z grid) must be interrogated to reveal which metabolite signals — including unannotated ones — drive class predictions.

name: ensemble-model-fusion-evaluation
description: Use when you have two pretrained spectral prediction baselines (MLP-PD and GNN-PD), a ranking-task training setup, and a candidate-set evaluation (average rank / Rank@K) on spectra-to-candidate annotation.

name: ensemble-model-training-and-prediction
description: Use when a wide-format metabolomics feature table (samples as columns, features as rows with unique identifiers) is paired with a design file assigning samples to class labels (e.g. treatment group) and the goal is supervised classification plus feature ranking.

name: entropy-based-peak-clarity-scoring
description: Decision support for scoring a per-atom modification-site likelihood array Ω from ModiFinder against a known true modification site, when a single metric balancing proximity and ambiguity of the prediction is needed.

name: entropy-based-peak-quality-filtering
description: Use when a feature table derived from CWT peak detection contains irregular, likely noise peaks, and you need a shape-based, parameter-light criterion to discard false positives before chemometric evaluation.

name: entropy-similarity-scoring
description: Use when quantitatively ranking MS/MS spectral matches or measuring denoising benefit — e.g. computing entropy similarity of raw vs. denoised query peaks against reference library spectra for compound annotation.

name: envipat-isotope-fine-structure-computation
description: Use when building a validation/reference peak list for metal-assisted (e.g. Ag-sputtered nanolayer) LDI MSI, where expected Ag-cluster and Ag-adduct masses must be derived from isotope abundances before peak classification.

name: envipat-isotopologue-pattern-prediction
description: Use when building an LC-HRMS benchmark from target molecules with known formulas and RT boundaries: isotopologue patterns must be predicted from SumForm_c entries before chromatographic ROI extraction from centroided mzML files.

name: enzyme-annotation-of-metabolites
description: Use when a pathway-metabolite association table (met_path) for significantly altered metabolites must be extended with gene IDs, EC numbers, and reaction roles, e.g. to infer enzymatic activity of altered metabolites in a species-specific KEGG context.

name: enzyme-metadata-assignment
description: Use when a metabolomics data frame already carries KEGG compound IDs and you need the enzyme orthologies (KO numbers) and genes an organism of interest, e.g. Pseudomonas spp., has to metabolize a compound class such as organic acids.

name: enzyme-specific-cleavage-parameter-configuration
description: Use when MGF-converted antibody MS/MS files from multiple enzymatic digests must be searched against antibody reference sequences to generate trusted PSMs (pseudo-ground truth) for evaluating de novo sequencing predictions.

name: enzyme-specificity-model-evaluation
description: Use when classifying whether query molecules react with specific human CYP450 isoforms and you need per-enzyme AUROC evaluation, cross-validation, or benchmarking against ADMET Predictor/SMARTCyp baselines.

name: enzyme-substrate-pair-scoring
description: Use when you have curated Known enzyme-substrate pairs (plus Random negatives) and need to score them with GNN-SOM + ReactionDecoder and test whether the score distributions separate.

name: epa-chemistry-dashboard-property-extraction
description: Use when a chemical list with CASRNs needs toxicity-relevant properties (log P, BCF, HTS AC50/efficacy) harvested from the EPA Chemistry Dashboard to feed composite prioritization scores such as ToxPi.

name: epidemiological-cohort-analysis
description: Use when the input is an individual-level cohort dataset (exposure biomarkers plus time-to-death and cause-of-death endpoints) and the goal is cause-specific or all-cause mortality hazard ratios per biomarker.

name: epigenomics-inventory-verification
description: Use when a database paper claims a fixed inventory of omics types, histone marks, or internal modules (e.g. 'eight types of omics data sets') and the extracted term list must be reconciled with those reported counts.

name: eps-knee-plot-parameter-tuning
description: Use when running MSS dm.ms_cluster (DBSCAN/OPTICS) on a normalized feature table and the DBSCAN eps and min_samples parameters need to be chosen from the data instead of arbitrary defaults.

name: equal-spacing-mz-binning
description: Use when raw LC-IMS-MS frames (e.g. bruker TDF via OpenTIMS) must be converted into fixed-width m/z windows and equally spaced bins before hashing, window collision analysis, or LSH-based signal classification.

name: equal-variance-t-test-group-comparison
description: Use when comparing lipid abundances of two experimental groups across lipid features (classes, molecular species, or building blocks) and you need p-values, FDR correction, and asterisk-annotated significance per feature.

name: equal-width-binned-pair-sampling
description: Use when a trained spectral-similarity model must be validated against Tanimoto structural similarity across the full similarity range on held-out test spectrum pairs.

name: equivalence-class-unit-testing
description: Use when building or validating a parser that normalizes ion-identity annotation strings from public LC-MS2 spectral libraries (e.g. GNPS-IIMN-PROPOGATED) and you need a concrete check that distinct spellings ('M + H', 'M + H +', '[M + H]+') resolve to one canonical identity.

name: equivalent-carbon-number-rt-conformity-analysis
description: Use when validating a LipidIN LCI retention-order model or auditing any annotated LC-MS/MS lipidomics dataset: you have lipid identities with retention times across glycerophospholipid subclasses and need to quantify conformity to ECN/IUP/ESCN RT rules and reproduce the paper's deviation.

name: equivalent-carbon-number-rule-filtering
description: Use when a lipid MS2 annotation table contains putative lipid identities and inconsistent annotations (violating the ECN rule or feature-peak criteria) must be removed before computing false discovery rates.

name: equivalent-separated-carbon-number-deviation-estimation
description: Use when you have published LC-MS/MS lipidomics datasets with annotated lipid identities and retention times and need to quantify how consistent the ECN, IUP, and ESCN RT rules are across datasets.

name: erah-pipeline-parameter-configuration
description: Use when setting up an eRah (R) processing run on raw GC/MS (GC-TOF or GC-QqQ) chromatogram data and you need to instantiate the parameter objects (setDecPar, setAlPar) and/or the spectral library before running deconvolveComp, alignComp, recMissComp, and identifyComp.

name: error-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when after per-metric/per-sample-group Isolation Forest outlier detection on precursor-ion peak metrics you need heatmaps showing which MS runs deviate on which metric, to localize instrument performance issues (e.g., mass calibration drift, RT instability).

name: error-rate-reduction-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking molecular formula annotation accuracy of SIRIUS versus ZODIAC against a manually validated ground truth across LC-MS/MS datasets such as dendroides, NIST1950, tomato, diatoms, and mice stool.

name: esi-mode-feature-annotation
description: Use when peak-picked, aligned HILIC-IM-MS feature tables from positive and negative ESI modes need lipid species annotation at graded confidence levels (m/z-only up to m/z + RT + CCS).

name: esi-ms2-similarity-scoring
description: Use when identifying small chemical compounds (<3000 Da) from ESI-MS2 query spectra by spectral search against MassBank reference records, especially when comparing QqQ and QqTOF query/target instrument pairings or tuning precision vs recall.

name: esi-ms2-spectral-search
description: Use when scoring query ESI-MS2 peak lists (m/z, intensity pairs) against reference spectra from MassBank and a compound identification decision at a similarity score threshold (0.6) is required.

name: esi-msms-spectral-prediction
description: Use when you need predicted QTOF ESI-MS/MS spectra at 10/20/40 eV for compounds lacking experimental reference spectra, or to benchmark spectral-prediction accuracy (Dice, Dot Product) or MS2C compound identification.

name: essential-fatty-acid-elongation-analysis
description: Use when analysing imzML MALDI imaging data from 13C6-glucose tracer studies of brain/tumour tissue to measure elongation/desaturation of essential fatty acids (20:3, 20:4, 20:5, 22:4, 22:5) and detect branch-specific (omega-3 vs omega-6) labelling.

name: essential-reaction-deletion-analysis
description: Use when an integrated host/virus SBML metabolic model (e.g. iHsaEC21+SARS-CoV-2 or iAB-AMØ-1410 macrophage) needs its host-dependency factors enumerated as reactions whose deletion abolishes the viral biomass objective.

name: estimator-concordance-classification
description: Use when you need to benchmark a new or alternative parameter estimation tool against a gold-standard estimator (e.g. mapbayr vs NONMEM) over simulated PK profiles and quantify agreement with explicit thresholds.

name: eta-eta-bond-canonical-ordering
description: Use when encoding unordered atom-pair bonds (e.g., η-η bonds of metabolism) as feature rows for machine learning, to prevent duplicate encodings of the same bond from inconsistent atom ordering.

name: ete3-phylogenetic-tree-rendering
description: Use when comparing CAMI-format taxonomic profiler outputs (e.g. MetaPhlAn, mOTUs, MetaPhyler, Taxy-Pro) against a ground-truth profile and you need a phylogenetic tree plot showing where abundance errors or missed clades occur.

name: ether-linked-phospholipid-neutrophil-signature-interpretation
description: Use when an XGBoost (or similar tree-based) classifier trained on Ly6G-annotated pixel spectra from co-registered MALDI MSI/IFM data yields feature_importance.csv, and you must identify and biologically interpret the top neutrophil lipids.

name: evaluation-metrics-computation
description: Use when simulated Environment runs over the same chemical set with different controllers (e.g. TopNController, SmartROIController, WeightedDEWController) must be quantitatively compared on fragmentation coverage and intensity.

name: evaluation-metrics-visualization
description: Use when comparing left-censored (MNAR) imputation methods on targeted metabolomics matrices and you need a distribution-level visual metric — plot Procrustes SSE vs. number of missing variables to pick the least-distorting method.

name: evaluation-result-aggregation-from-deposit
description: Use when two annotation pipelines have been evaluated on the same query spectra and you need per-method correctness counts, overlap statistics, and a figure showing which correct annotations are unique to each method.

name: evidence-score-threshold-filtering
description: Use when prioritizing disease-relevant genes from a candidate gene list by requiring strong Open Targets association evidence (score > 0.8), e.g. after mapping rat DE genes to human orthologs.

name: evolutionary-operator-and-population-design
description: Use when optimizing continuous model parameters (e.g. moiety state values) against a non-linear objective like logDifference, where naive scipy optimizers are insufficient and a combined simulated annealing / genetic algorithm with tunable population and operators is needed.

name: ewas-atlas-trait-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when MOFA2 factors computed on Infinium MethylationEPIC DNA methylation data need biological interpretation via CpG-trait enrichment in the EWAS atlas.

name: exact-mass-calculation-from-chemical-formula
description: Use when processing high-resolution GC-CI-MS (e.g. GC-Orbitrap) stable-isotope tracing data and you need theoretical m/z values for a derivatized compound formula or its isotopologues to match detected peaks.

name: exact-mass-difference-adduct-search
description: Use when working with time-resolved DBDI-MS or other direct-injection MS1 feature tables (XICs per scan) where correlated features must be annotated as putative adducts (e.g. [M+O+H]+) or in-source fragments (e.g. [M-H2O+H]+) without chromatographic separation.

name: exact-mass-metabolite-annotation
description: Use when spatial metabolomics peaks (e.g. 401,325 m/z values from an imzML MALDI-TOF dataset) need metabolite name, formula, InChIKey and adduct assignments without METASPACE/pySM, especially for TOF data.

name: exact-mass-mz-matching
description: Use when a GC-MS hit table (columns Component.RT, Component.Area, Base.Peak.MZ, File.Name, Compound.Name, Match.Factor) has been spread by spreadOut() and you need per-sample component areas for a defined chemical list.

name: exact-mass-tolerance-filtering
description: Use when filtering metabolomics annotations against a large structure database (e.g. PubChem) and a narrow mass window plus CCS-based ΔCCS threshold (2.8%) is needed to remove false positives.

name: exact-match-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare MS/MS library-search methods at finding exact library matches, by sweeping top-N cutoffs and measuring true-positive percentage across recall values.

name: exact-mode-spectrum-molecule-scoring
description: Use when you have MGF, mzXML, or mzML spectra with known precursor m/z and want to identify the intact candidate molecule (no variant mass shifts) by scoring fragments against a chemical database such as NPAtlas.

name: exact-monoisotopic-mass-calculation
description: Use when validating or predicting m/z values for derivatization-specific diagnostic ions (e.g. FMP-10 phenolic-hydroxyl and primary-amine fragments reported at 286.122641 and 285.138625) before MS1 mass matching in MALDI-MSI annotation.

name: exact-structure-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when a generative model produces candidate molecular structures (SMILES/coordinates) from spectra and you need to measure how often the exact target structure is recovered and how close near-misses are.

name: exact-structure-matching-metrics
description: Use when you have generated molecular structures (e.g., from a diffusion or autoregressive model) plus ground-truth structures and need exact-match top-k accuracy or MCES similarity scores.

name: example-dataset-retrieval-from-repository
description: Reference for obtaining the ready-made example LC-MS/MS dataset (processed MS/MS spectra, quantification table, and metadata table) shipped with the msFeaST GitHub repository, e.g. when setting up or validating the msFeaST workflow before running it on user-owned data.

name: example-dataset-run-verification
description: Use when a fresh MetaboDirect install or new environment must be validated against the article's example FT-ICR MS datasets, or when a user needs to select a normalization method via test_normalization before the main pipeline.

name: excel-csv-data-ingestion
description: Use when a metabolomics feature table arrives as csv or Excel (e.g., a cancerCell demo table or an XCMS/MS-DIAL/MZmine/Compound Discoverer/Progenesis QI export) and must be parsed with metadata before preprocessing.

name: excel-metabolomics-file-parsing-with-readxl
description: Use when the input is a vendor Excel metabolomics workbook (e.g. metabolon_v1.1_example.xlsx with sheet='OrigScale', or nightingale_v1_example.xlsx) and you need the raw abundance matrix plus sample and feature metadata as separate objects.

name: excel-report-generation
description: Use when a margheRita R analysis produces a result table (identifications, associations, statistics) that must be persisted as an .xlsx workbook with named sheets for sharing or archiving.

name: excel-spreadsheet-generation
description: Use when MALDI-ToF-MS spectra acquired at optically guided target points (mzML files) must be reduced to per-sample ion counts over specified m/z windows and exported as a structured .xlsx spreadsheet.

name: exchange-reaction-flux-enumeration
description: Use when a multi-species community metabolic model (e.g. SBML from PyCoMo) must be interrogated for which metabolites members can exchange and which donor-consumer cross-feeding routes are feasible, independent of a specific abundance profile.

name: exchange-reaction-lower-bound-update
description: Use when a host GEM (e.g., RECON3D in SBML) must be coupled to one or more gut microbiota metabolic models so that microbial metabolite fluxes shift the host model's exchange-reaction lower bounds.

name: execution-log-interpretation
description: Use when a Nextflow4MS-DIAL run (MS-DIAL followed by MS-FLO on .mzML inputs) has completed and you must reconstruct what happened: run duration, per-process timelines, resource allocation, container and parameter provenance from the execution reports and logs.

name: execution-time-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify how fast a tool (e.g. RAIChU drawing biosynthetic pathway diagrams) executes across input categories, and produce a timing table supporting performance comparisons.

name: exercise-de-effect-size-standardization
description: Use when you need to express exercise training-induced differential expression effect sizes in units of human phenotypic or SNP-heritable expression variability (GTEx v8) to identify gene x tissue pairs where exercise can overcome standing or genetic variation.

name: exercise-deg-time-course-trajectory-tracing
description: Use when a trait x tissue gene set needs its direction-of-effect pattern decomposed across the 1-, 2-, 4-, and 8-week MoTrPAC endurance exercise training time points to see when the disease-like shift emerged.

name: exhaustive-grid-search-optimization
description: Use when tuning peak detection parameters for GC-MS metabolomics data (mzML/mzData/NetCDF) and no ground-truth peak list exists, so parameter sets must be ranked by machine-learning peak-quality scores instead of manual curation.

name: exogenous-component-screening
description: Use when you have paired pre-dosing and post-dosing LC-MS/MS feature lists for multiple biological matrices (e.g., plasma, lung, urine, feces) and need to isolate drug/herb-derived exogenous peaks and count prototype vs metabolite components.

name: exorcycle-phase-cycle-equivalence-checking
description: Use when replacing EXORCYCLE phase cycling with a coherence pathway filter in a spatially localized density-matrix MRS simulation (e.g. PRESS/sLASER, MEGA-PRESS, HERMES, HERCULES) and you must demonstrate spectral equivalence before adopting the faster approach.

name: expected-improvement-acquisition-function-implementation
description: Use when reconstructing or extending a Bayesian optimization loop that must pick the next experiment (e.g., an LC-MS gradient) by argmax of Expected Improvement computed from a fitted GP posterior mean and standard deviation.

name: experiment-directory-structure-management
description: Use when setting up or curating the output layout for an LC-MS metabolomics processing run with pcpfm, where .raw/.mzML inputs, Asari feature tables, empirical compound JSON, and QA/QC figures must be organized under one Experiment Directory.

name: experimental-design-dictionary-construction
description: Use when running PALS programmatically on a peak-intensity matrix (e.g. the Rhamnaceae Rhamnus/Ziziphus samples) and sample-factor assignments must be encoded as case/control comparisons before building a DataSource.

name: experimental-design-file-creation
description: Use when preparing an Optimus (KNIME) LC-MS untargeted metabolomics workflow: you have mzXML sample runs (plus blanks) and need the experimental-design CSV that assigns LC-run type and spatial coordinates before feature filtering and quantification.

name: experimental-design-specification-from-target-metadata
description: Use when a lipidomics abundance matrix (LipidSearch/LIQUID output or Metabolomics Workbench data) is loaded with its target-file sample metadata and a differential abundance model must be defined via design matrix and contrasts.

name: experimental-design-to-spectra-mapping
description: Use when you have 1D NMR spectral intensity data plus an experimental-design table recording factor levels per spectrum, and need to visually map design metadata onto spectra (e.g. colored overlays) or export the spectrum-to-factor join for statistics.

name: experimental-design-tracking
description: Use when raw MS files and their sample metadata (LC column info, study factors, project names) already reside in an MSConnect server database and you need a standardized, submission-ready experimental-design data package rather than an ad-hoc sample sheet.

name: experimental-factor-metadata-annotation
description: Use when a filtered NMRProcFlow bucket table must be turned into a samples-by-buckets data matrix whose rows (spectra) carry class-label columns for experimental-factor levels, e.g. before export to MetaboAnalyst 3.0 or BioStatFlow.

name: experimental-vs-simulated-spectra-generalization-testing
description: Use when a model trained solely on simulated spectra (SGNN NMR, Chemprop-IR) must be evaluated on experimental spectral data to measure out-of-distribution generalization and improvement-cycle recovery.

name: experimenthub-resource-fetching
description: Use when a protocol needs a small, citable Thermo Fisher .raw example file for demonstration or testing and the article pins it to an ExperimentHub accession (EH4547) or a MassIVE dataset (MSV000086542).

name: expert-annotation-aggregation
description: Use when multiple human raters have independently labeled the same items (e.g., ion images tagged via TagOff) and you must quantify inter-rater reliability before merging tags into a curated gold standard.

name: expert-annotation-majority-voting
description: Use when multiple independent raters have each scored the same set of files (e.g. qualified/unqualified per instrument run) and you need a reproducible ground-truth label or agreement statistics before training or benchmarking.

name: expert-substructure-ambiguity-refinement
description: Use when ModiFinder MF-R output over a known/unknown analog pair (e.g. Kirromycin-Goldinodox, Naphthomycin A-B) leaves many atoms with high modification-site likelihood, and expert knowledge of gas-phase fragmentation can prune the peak-to-substructure assignments.

name: expert-system-rule-based-filtering
description: Use when you have m/z query results matched against a metabolomic database (e.g., HMDB) and need to filter and rank candidate metabolite annotations under a defined experimental setup (ionization mode, allowed adducts).

name: explained-feature-count-verification
description: Use when rerunning khipu annotation with modified isotope/adduct search patterns and you need to verify that the new run explains more features without inflating the empirical compound count (1,775 ESI+ / 908 ESI- expected on the yeast data).

name: explained-variance-ratio-computation
description: Use when a fitted PCA decomposition must be quantified — after projecting samples onto PCs, to record how much variance each component explains and validate that the component captures the expected share of high-dimensional feature variance.

name: explained-variance-reporting
description: Use when a PCA has been (or will be) fit on Protomix-preprocessed urine spectra (0.1 ppm rectangular bins, TotalArea-normalized) and you need per-component and cumulative explained-variance ratios, e.g. to justify how many PCs to retain for downstream cancer-vs-BHP analyses.

name: exponential-decay-edge-weighting
description: Use when you have a paired transcriptomic-metabolomic dataset (e.g., the tomato Jeon and colleagues 2020 dataset) and need to turn raw Pearson correlation values between transcripts and mass features into weighted edges for network clustering.

name: exponential-decay-function-implementation
description: Use when building or validating kernel functions for relaxation (T1, T2) or diffusion (D) NMR signals before feeding them to regularized numerical inversion (invert()) or multi-exponential fitting (expfit).

name: exposome-compound-detection-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing compound-detection depth of JPA vs conventional peak picking on serially diluted LC-MS exposome standard mixture data (e.g. MTBLS2631 RP(+) mzXML files), to reproduce or re-quantify detection fold-gains per dilution level.

name: exposome-database-compilation
description: Use when the goal is to build a large, deduplicated human exposome chemical inventory from multiple public databases and literature sources, keyed by CASRN with SMILES/InChIKey annotations.

name: exposome-transcriptome-gene-set-association
description: Use when a built multi-omics network (e.g., MetaNet multi1 or co_net objects) contains gene nodes linked to microbial or chemical exposures and you need KEGG/GO over-representation analysis per exposure class.

name: exposome-transcriptome-integration-analysis
description: Use when you need to connect exposure-level features (microbial taxa, chemicals) to host transcriptomic features via cross-layer correlations and compare edge-sign distributions between exposure types.

name: exposure-hazard-quotient-calculation
description: Use when a chemical inventory lacks measured toxicity values and you need a probabilistic exposure-vs-hazard risk score (PrHQ) to rank chemicals for prioritization.

name: exposure-intake-rate-estimation
description: Use when a compiled chemical list (e.g., HExpMetDB's 20,756 human exposome substances) needs predicted population-level exposure/intake values (mg/kg BW per day) from the SEEM consensus model to support exposure- or risk-based chemical prioritization.

name: exposure-source-metadata-filtering
description: Use when curating analog (non-library) MS/MS matches from untargeted metabolomics data and you must drop analogs whose parent drug can plausibly arise endogenously or from the food supply, before propagating spectra into a drug-exposure screening library.
tools: GNPS (Global Natural Product Social Molecular Networking)

name: exposure-toxicity-integration-ranking
description: Use when you hold paired exposure estimates (e.g., SEEM) and in vitro toxicity scores (ToxCast/ToxPi) for a chemical set and need a single risk-based ranking that integrates both dimensions.

name: expression-dataset-exploratory-quality-control
description: Use when a sample-by-gene expression matrix with sample metadata (e.g. organ, tumor status) needs QC before downstream analysis, and samples from the same biological condition must be checked for consistently high pairwise correlations or abnormally low expression.

name: expression-matrix-dependency-analysis
description: Use when you have a numeric expression matrix (feature rows x sample columns) and need pairwise, non-linear dependency scores between features that may not be captured by Pearson or Spearman correlation.

name: expression-matrix-dimension-validation
description: Use when a filtered/assembled expression dataset must be checked against its published dimensions (e.g. 18,212 genes x 7,412 samples for the Hu-cancer-RNASeq-dataset) before MOG analyses.

name: expression-matrix-group-wise-analysis
description: Use when an expression matrix has samples partitioned into two groups (e.g. leaf vs pollen, early vs late stage, tumour vs non-tumour) and the goal is to flag features whose Pearson correlation with a user-selected target feature differs significantly between the groups.

name: expression-matrix-standardization-and-subsetting
description: Use when a raw gene-by-sample expression matrix (e.g., Mootha DM2 or smoker airway epithelium data) must be standardized and subset to ~400 KEGG/Biocarta pathway gene-sets before SVD-based pathway activity computation.

name: external-calibration-concentration-calculation
description: Use when you have a vendor-exported peak-area table (e.g. a MultiQuant 3.0.3 export of peak areas and retention times) for a targeted LC-MS/MS sequence and need per-injection concentrations calibrated against external calibration standards, optionally with drift correction.

name: external-calibration-conversion
description: Use when you have already-integrated targeted LC-MS/MS peak areas (e.g. exported from MultiQuant) plus external calibration curves and need to compute concentrations per compound, optionally after drift correction.

name: external-calibration-quantification-setup
description: Use when a targeted MRM/HRMS metabolomics assay (e.g. Biocrates p180 serum amino acids or arginine/polyamine panels) must yield calibrated concentrations rather than only peak areas, using heavy-labeled internal standards or external calibrants in Skyline.

name: external-cohort-transfer-validation
description: Use when a cross-validated metabolite-prediction model exists and an independent paired microbiome-metabolome cohort is available to test transfer without retraining.

name: external-dataset-model-validation
description: Use when a structural-similarity scoring model trained on one MS/MS dataset (e.g. MetDNA/DIONysus 40V spectra of KEGG compounds) must be evaluated on independent spectra measured on different instruments (e.g. Shimadzu LC-ESI-IT-TOF or Bruker Compact LC-ESI-QTOF) to test generalization.

name: external-instrument-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when validating a spectral-similarity or metabolite-identification model on spectra from an independent instrument or study (external test set), e.g. biomarker spectra from a male infertility study measured on a Bruker Compact LC-ESI-QTOF after training on IT-TOF data.

name: external-qc-pool-validation-analysis
description: Use when a normalization was tuned on in-run pooled QCs and an independent commercial/reference plasma QC pool exists to confirm the method's error generalizes outside the training batches.

name: external-test-result-aggregation
description: Use when evaluating a metabolite identification method with both an internal LOOCV evaluation (e.g. 662 KEGG compounds) and an independent external test set (e.g. male infertility biomarkers), and you need to tabulate identification validity against database-coverage conditions.

name: external-test-set-auc-evaluation
description: Use when a paired microbiome-metabolome dataset has a separate external validation set (e.g. IBD (PRISM) training vs. IBD (External) test) and you must quantify whether derived module features retain disease-predictive information via AUC rather than in-sample cross-validation.

name: external-validation-set-sampling
description: Use when a classifier trained on curated spectra (e.g., BitterMasS) must be evaluated on literature-extracted or laboratory-measured spectra of compounds unseen in training, and per-compound sampling is needed to avoid duplicate-spectrum bias.

name: extracellular-flux-ratio-constraint-setting
description: Reference for imposing extracellular flux ratio constraints from ysi_ratio.csv (e.g. lactate/glucose, lactate/glutamine, glutamate/glutamine) onto constraint-based models during rasIntegration, together with medium.csv nutrient bounds and RAS-derived reaction bounds.

name: extract-priority-score-calculation
description: Use when prioritizing plant/organism extracts for structural novelty after MZmine feature quantification and GNPS FBMN, i.e. when you have a quant table, metadata, and optionally ISDB/timaR, SIRIUS/CANOPUS and MEMO inputs.

name: extract-similarity-scoring
description: Use when a priority-ranked screening of natural extracts requires flagging extracts that are spectral outliers within the set, from an untargeted LC-MS/MS feature-based molecular networking dataset with a MEMO vectorized matrix available.

name: extracted-ion-chromatogram-extraction
description: Use when raw MS data has been converted to .mza and you need intensity-vs-retention-time traces for specific m/z windows (e.g., isotope envelopes) using h5py/numpy rather than vendor libraries.

name: extracted-ion-chromatogram-extraction
description: Use when you hold a Thermo .raw file (e.g. from MassIVE MSV000086542 or ExperimentHub EH4547) and need XIC signal traces around known precursor m/z values — such as spiked-in iRT peptides — without converting to mzML.

name: extracted-ion-chromatogram-isolation-within-tic-peaks
description: Use when raw scan-level metabolomics data (mzML, mzXML, CDF) plus detected TIC peak boundaries are available and centWave parameter estimation—especially the ppm mass-error parameter—requires isolating EICs within each TIC peak's retention-time window.

name: extracted-ion-chromatogram-matching
description: Use when a DDA-detected metabolite feature (from pooled QC samples analyzed in DDA mode) lacks an intensity entry in the feature table of a DIA-analyzed individual biological sample, and its abundance must be recovered from the DIA raw data.

name: extracted-ion-chromatogram-monitoring
description: Use when raw LC–MS injections (e.g., Waters RAW converted to mzML) include system suitability solution and pooled QC samples and you must verify that SSS standards are detected via EICs before/while assessing platform conditioning.

name: extracted-ion-chromatogram-peak-area-tabulation
description: Use when SST mzML data (e.g., six deuterated acylcarnitine standards on UHPLC-HRMS) need EIC peak areas tabulated per analyte across acquisition batches to detect retention-time or method anomalies.

name: extracted-ion-chromatogram-peak-integration
description: Use when vendor raw targeted MS files (SRM/MRM or HRMS) must be inspected as XICs and integrated per compound — with heavy-labeled internal standards — to yield peak areas for calibrated concentration calculation.

name: extracted-ion-chromatogram-peak-quality-assessment
description: Use when you have rescued features from a DaDIA (DDA-rescued-in-DIA) workflow and need to quantify what fraction carry genuine chromatographic peaks versus noise before reporting rescue metrics.

name: extracted-ion-chromatogram-processing
description: Use when processing high-performance thin-layer chromatography coupled with high-resolution mass spectrometry data where extracted ion chromatograms must be clustered to highlight signal (ions of interest) over background ions.

name: extracted-ion-chromatogram-targeted-analysis
description: Use when you must verify how many distinct isomers co-elute under a single precursor m/z, confirm cluster membership of specific isomers (e.g., 2 Da-shifted type E spectra), or validate an annotation such as CCMSLIB00000840365 for m/z 607.32.
tools: GNPS (Global Natural Products Social Molecular Networking)

name: extracted-ion-chromatogram-visualization
description: Use when two XCMS grouping results (different bw) have been screened by ncGTW misalignDetect and the flagged groups in excluGroups need visual confirmation of RT drift via EIC plots.

name: extracted-ion-electropherogram-peak-integration
description: Use when targeted full-scan MSI-CE-MS data in mzML format must be peak-picked and integrated across many multiplexed runs with high migration time variability, and manual preprocessing would be slow or inconsistent.

name: extraction-blank-subtraction-of-features
description: Use when a centroided ddMS2 mzML sample (or custom feature list) is accompanied by a measured extraction blank mzML, and background signals from solvents, labware, or sample preparation must be removed before PFAS feature prioritization.

name: extraction-method-field-verification
description: Use when a retrieval claim about PoDP extraction-method metadata (e.g. 'methanol + cells' finds methanol cell-pellet extractions) must be reproduced and field-level verified against archived Zenodo JSON project documents.

name: exudate-metabolome-class-composition-comparison
description: Use when comparing chemical class/superclass composition of ion features across organism exudates or sample groups, e.g., testing whether coral vs algal exometabolomes differ in organic acid vs organoheterocyclic compound abundance.

name: f-beta-reliability-scoring-of-annotations
description: Use when per-dataset annotation results (target and decoy hits) are available at multiple default FDR thresholds and you need to rank thresholds by a precision-weighted reliability metric or identify the optimal FDR for a sample-type group.

name: f-measure-aggregation-statistics
description: Use when you must quantify how many common feature groups between a reference feature list and target chromatograms are needed for LC-HRMS alignment (MetMatch) to retain full accuracy, via subsampled-run F-measure aggregation.

name: f-measure-calculation
description: Use when evaluating how accurately an LC-HRMS alignment tool (e.g. MetMatch) matches peaks to a reference, from known true-positive and false-positive counts against a ground-truth correspondence.

name: f1-evaluation-of-pathway-ranking
description: Use when comparing pathway ranking methods on metabolomics intensity matrices and you need quantitative robustness evidence (F1, p-value spread) under synthetic missing-feature perturbations rather than a single qualitative run.

name: f1-landscape-optimization
description: Use when tuning mcfNMR runs on artificial 1H,13C HSQC mixtures: an F1 grid over assignment radius (r) and absorption cost/detection threshold (θ) values already exists (from a prior sweep) and you must identify per-setup optima, rank setups by robustness, or quantify F1 degradation as r deviates.

name: f1-score-extraction-and-method-comparison
description: Use when a compound-identification run over 2D 1H,13C HSQC spectra must be scored and compared across methods (MCF grid, MCF-D peak-list variant, MetaboMiner baseline) using F1 metrics.

name: factorization-machine-sgd-training
description: Use when building or retraining an RNA or protein chemical shift prediction model from BMRB assignments paired with PDB structures, and you need an FM (rather than SVR) predictor evaluated by cross-validated RMSD per atom type.

name: failed-descriptor-compound-removal
description: Use when building the Retip feature matrix from SMILES: some compounds fail rCDK descriptor calculation during getCD() and must be auto-removed to yield a complete-case 286-descriptor table.

name: faire-annotation-coverage-assessment
description: Use when auditing a PeakForest compound card or demonstrator compound table to compute identifier-coverage fractions per external chemical bank (ChEBI, PubChem, HMDB, KEGG) and InChIKey completeness.

name: faire-metadata-interoperability
description: Use when a standardized sample-metadata matrix (freetext terms replaced by fixed-vocabulary terms) must be delivered to users and integrated into existing pipelines via CSV export and an API.

name: fallback-default-parameter-handling
description: Use when aggregating GNPS, Sirius, and ISDB-LOTUS annotations and a tool returns no match or only a partial (e.g. score-without-InChI) match, which would otherwise break tanimoto computation.

name: false-annotation-quantification-omics-scale
description: Use when you have untargeted metabolomics feature tables (mzXML from DDA/fullscan plus DDA MS2) and need to identify which features are in-source fragments that could be falsely annotated as metabolites, then quantify their prevalence.

name: false-discovery-rate-curve-analysis
description: Use when matched similarity scores from an MS/MS library search (e.g., 434,287 spectra self-searched against NIST20) must be converted into score-threshold curves to compare algorithms by FDR/TPR.

name: false-discovery-rate-curve-analysis
description: Use when validating a mass spectral database search (e.g. VInSMoC against COCONUT or NPAtlas) by recomputing hit lists across score and P-value cutoffs and plotting false discovery rate curves.

name: false-discovery-rate-empirical-calibration
description: Use when assessing whether a reproducibility-detection procedure controls FDR at the nominal level under rank-dependent correlation decay between replicate pairs, e.g., pi_1 x r_0 simulation grids.

name: false-discovery-rate-estimation-decoy-search
description: Use when benchmarking DEREPLICATOR+ database search identifications (e.g., on SpectraLibrary or GNPS spectra) and you need a target-decoy FDR estimate to define a significance cutoff for recall/precision measurement.

name: false-discovery-rate-estimation-from-confidence-scores
description: Use when ranked in silico structure candidates (e.g., CSI:FingerID hits per compound) must be scored for correctness and an FDR estimated for the top k hits, e.g. to pick a confidence-score threshold such as 0.64 for ~10% FDR.

name: false-discovery-rate-estimation-from-match-scores
description: Use when you have query MS/MS spectra matched to a reference library with a similarity score for each match and need to pick a score cutoff that bounds the fraction of false matches (e.g., below 10%).

name: false-discovery-rate-filtering-of-annotations
description: Use when reporting counts of spectra or unique small molecules annotated by a mass spectral search method (e.g., molDiscovery vs Dereplicator+) and identifications must be filtered at a stated FDR threshold such as 0%.

name: false-discovery-rate-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when a spatial metabolomics or multi-omics analysis tests thousands of m/z peaks, metabolite-gene pairs, or pathways simultaneously and needs FDR-adjusted significance before ranking or reporting hits.

name: false-discovery-rate-qvalue-estimation
description: Use when rescored PSM scores exist and you must compute q-values from target/decoy counts, enforce a 1% training-FDR threshold, and filter lower-rank PSMs before final FDR calculation.

name: false-discovery-rate-threshold-control
description: Use when estimating reproducible metabolites (or features per sample pair) from replicate-rank data and you need the rejection region threshold chosen so empirical FDR is controlled at a specified alpha (e.g., 0.05).

name: false-discovery-rate-threshold-filtering
description: Use when comparing annotation yield between FDR-controlled metabolite annotation methods (e.g., METASPACE-ML vs MSM) across imaging MS datasets, or when confident annotations must be selected at a specified FDR cutoff before counting or fold-change statistics.

name: false-identity-filter-evaluation
description: Use when you have observed vs. model-predicted retention times for candidate metabolites on SMRT or SMRT_Retained test sets and must quantify how many false identities an RT-error threshold removes.

name: false-negative-rate-estimation-for-rt-filtering
description: Use when evaluating or calibrating an RT-based metabolite-annotation filter: you have true vs. RT-Transformer-predicted retention times on a retained test set and need the fraction of molecules within error bounds (e.g. <60 s, <120 s) and the FNR a ±2 SD threshold introduces.

name: false-peak-characterization-from-feature-tables
description: Use when a machine learning peak classifier (DNN or logistic regression) still flags some false positives under more restrictive settings and you need to characterize their peak shapes and parameter distributions to explain covariate shift.

name: false-positive-false-negative-misclassification-assessment
description: Use when validating a colocalization pixel-classification method against ground-truth simulated two-color images spanning full to no colocalization, to estimate misclassification (target ~5%) and subvisual detection ability.

name: false-positive-feature-discrimination
description: Use when a peak table from CWT peak detection (e.g., AriumMS CE-MS or HILIC-MS runs) contains suspected false-positive features and a shape-based, parameter-light noise criterion is needed before augmentation or mid-level data fusion.

name: false-positive-filter-application
description: Use when raw multi-platform untargeted metabolomics data (CE-MS and HILIC-MS of yeast extracts, converted to .mzXML/.mzML) must be filtered of false-positive features after ROI search and feature detection, prior to augmentation.

name: false-positive-rate-assessment
description: Decision support for selecting an MS1/MS2 mass defect tolerance (mmu range) before MDRB matching of unpredictable metabolites to prototypes, when neither coverage nor false-positive burden can be assumed a priori.

name: false-positive-rate-quantification
description: Use when evaluating peak-calling quality on nontargeted LC-MS metabolomics peak lists — specifically when you need the fraction of false positive peaks before/after filtering and true positive retention under 'More Restrictive' vs 'Less Restrictive' MZmine 2 settings.

name: family-wise-error-rate-p-value-adjustment
description: Use when a metabolomics or GWAS-style analysis yields many correlated raw p-values (e.g., per-metabolite t-tests) and you must control FWER at a fixed alpha (e.g., 0.05) while comparing eigen-analysis-based effective-number-of-tests estimators.

name: fast-search-api-query-execution
description: Use when you need to search one or more MS/MS spectra (a single spectrum or an .mgf file from MZmine or a USI .csv/.tsv list) against indexed GNPS/MassIVE, Metabolomics Workbench, Metabolights, and NORMAN data via the Fast Search API.

name: fastica-decomposition
description: Use when the input is a samples x genes expression matrix (e.g., transcriptomic data from tumoral samples) and the goal is to extract independent, interpretable metagene components that are stable across random ICA initializations.

name: fastpfor-bit-level-integer-compression
description: Use when compressing large numeric arrays from mass-spectrometry chromatograms (e.g., MRM retention times) where delta coding plus bit-level integer encoding (FastPFor) followed by ZSTD must shrink file size for fast web-side rendering.

name: fatty-acid-isotopologue-distribution-fitting
description: Use when you have normalized, natural-isotope-corrected isotopologue intensities (M+0..M+16/M+18) for a fatty acid and need the glucose-derived acetyl-CoA labelling fraction p (e.g. per-cell p histograms for ACLYkd vs control).

name: fatty-acid-isotopologue-ion-image-extraction
description: Use when MALDI-AIF imzML datasets contain 13C-labelled fatty acid isotopologues that METASPACE annotations miss, and ion images must be extracted per pixel or ablation mark before isotope-abundance correction and binomial fitting.

name: fatty-acid-nomenclature-validation
description: Use when building or auditing in silico lipid fragmentation libraries to verify fatty acid combination lists, lipid species totals, distinct lipid type counts, and permutation redundancy (e.g. 18:0_20:0 vs 20:0_18:0).

name: fatty-acid-residue-abundance-quantification
description: Use when lipidomic data annotated with individual molecular lipid identifiers (RefMet-compliant or CLASS N:N/M:M format) must be converted into fatty-acid residue counts and ranked/compared across sample groups, e.g. cell-type residue patterns.

name: fatty-acyl-carbon-parity-classification
description: Use when two TG annotation result sets (e.g., DIATAGeR FDR-filtered output vs MS-DIAL annotations on MS-DIAL alignment feature lists from the same DIA lipidomics run) must be compared by fatty-acyl carbon parity to quantify annotation completeness differences.

name: fatty-acyl-composition-parsing
