description: Use when a lipidomics peak table carries fatty acyl compositions (e.g. FA carbon:alkene counts per species) and you need class-level effective carbon number vs. retention time models for Degreaser QC or outlier-identification flagging.

name: fatty-acyl-peak-ratio-calculation
description: Use when MALDI-TOF spectra from macroMS screens (S. cerevisiae colonies or nanoliter droplet arrays) need per-sample fatty acyl ratios, e.g., C16:1/C16 or C16:1/C18:1, to identify colonies or species with shifted fatty acyl profiles.

name: fatty-acyl-residue-extraction-from-lipid-identifiers
description: Use when input is a lipidomics table whose row index contains lipid identifiers such as 'PG 18:1/20:1' or RefMet-compliant names, and the goal is to reprocess analyte-level data into per-sample fatty-acid residue counts or filtered residue tables.

name: fatty-acyl-structural-resolution-matching
description: Use when annotating UHPLC-HRMS/MS features (ddMS2-topN, AIF, or targeted MS/MS from Q-Exactive Orbitrap or Agilent/Bruker/SCIEX Q-TOF) to lipid species where identifications should be resolved to fatty acyl constituent level, not just lipid class or precursor mass.

name: fba-biomass-objective-validation
description: Use when a draft or Reconstructor-generated SBML model has just been built and must be confirmed functional (nonzero biomass flux) prior to gene essentiality or other perturbation analyses.

name: fbmn-compound-match-evaluation
description: Use when you have FBMN annotation results with top-matched compounds and need to quantify how structurally faithful those matches are to the actually analyzed compounds via Tanimoto and MCES scores.

name: fdr-adjusted-statistical-testing
description: Use when a peak-aligned SCMS feature table (e.g., Geena2-aligned at 10 ppm mass tolerance) must be converted into a ranked list of differentially abundant species between two cell phenotypes, with multiple-testing control.

name: fdr-controlled-metabolite-annotation-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing FDR-controlled metabolite annotation methods (e.g., ML vs rule-based scorers) across imaging MS datasets, or when evaluating target/decoy ranking quality via average precision.

name: fdr-estimation-of-spectral-annotations
description: Use when filtering GC-MS deconvoluted spectral matches (with per-match cosine similarity and balance score annotations) and you need to choose joint thresholds that minimize the FDR of the top annotation.

name: fdr-multiple-comparison-correction
description: Use when assigning significance categories to metabolites whose many curve-fitted ROI peaks (SRRMs) each get a p-value, preventing uncorrected p<0.05 calls from inflating identifications in NMR metabolomics.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when thousands of pathway-level importance scores (VIP, MB-VIP, RGCCA loadings, or sparse-DIABLO bootstrap non-zero-loading statistics) must be tested against permutation nulls and converted into pathway detection calls with controlled false discovery rate.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when many features are tested independently (one test per metabolomic feature) and raw p-values must be FDR-adjusted — e.g. reproducing Fig. 3f-style significant-feature counts at FDR <= 0.2 on batch-corrected ST000868 data.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when testing hundreds to thousands of omics features (metabolomics peaks, RNA-seq genes) for group differences in BiomiX-style pipelines and raw p-values must be FDR-corrected before filtering at p.adj thresholds.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when a between-group abundance test on LC-MS feature tables (e.g. 94 samples, 14 lamprey tissues, negative ion mode) yields raw per-feature P values across thousands of mass features, and a significance cutoff must control the false-discovery rate before filtering.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when a metabolomics or multi-omics analysis yields thousands of pairwise correlation P-values (e.g., metabolite-protein Spearman correlations across ~202 shared samples) and edges must be called at FDR < 0.05 with an effect-size cutoff such as |r| > 0.3.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when many gene sets (e.g., GO/KEGG terms) have been tested per ICA metagene Sk vector via hypergeometric overrepresentation or GSEA and p-values must be corrected before calling enriched sets.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when a lipidomic dataset is compared across two or more experimental groups with a test per lipid feature (t-test/ANOVA), and corrected p-values plus significance asterisks are needed.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when many p-values are generated per factor–pair hypothesis (GEE, Spearman correlation, Mann–Whitney/Kruskal–Wallis cluster comparisons, or EWAS atlas over-representation tests) and an FDR-adjusted p-value column must be reported for each tested pair.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when running GetFeatistics significance functions (gentab_P.t.test, one/two-way ANOVA, gentab_lm_long) over many metabolites, where per-feature p-values must be FDR-adjusted before reporting or building volcano plots.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when interpreting over-representation pathway enrichment results from multiple metabolite lists, where p < 0.05 hits exist but only FDR-adjusted values below 0.05 should count as significant pathways.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Decision support for identifying differentially abundant or expressed gene clusters across sample groups when thousands of clusters are tested simultaneously and raw p-values would otherwise inflate false positives.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction-pathway-enrichment
description: Use when per-pathway raw p-values (e.g., from eSPIA impact analysis or gene/metabolite ORA) must be corrected across many pathways, or when p-values from joint gene-metabolite tests need combination before calling significance.

name: fdr-qvalue-rank-assignment
description: Use when a feature table already carries FDR-adjusted p-values (q-values) from feature-wise tests plus multivariate importance ranks (e.g., MUVR RF 'mid' model), and the goal is to pick the most robust metabolic features for downstream identification.

name: fdr-significance-annotation
description: Use when ROIs from disease-vs-control NMR spectra (e.g. serum from lung cancer vs controls) have been scored for trend ('+'/'-') and significance ('*'/'!') and metabolites must be classified into the six ROIAL-NMR categories in the final dataResult table.

name: fdr-target-decoy-cutoff-validation
description: Use when a scored target-decoy TG annotation list (e.g. ResultsTG from ScoreLipids) must be filtered to an empirical FDR (default 0.1) and validated against a standards file.

name: fdr-threshold-based-reproducible-feature-selection
description: Use when you have MS-Metabolomics replicate data (technical or biological replicates, e.g. COPDGene Tech/BioTech/Bio) and need to flag which metabolites and sample pairs are reproducible while controlling FDR.

name: fdr2d-isoline-visualization
description: Use when a metabolomics feature-level results table (mean difference, standard error, p-value, fdr2d per hypothesis) must be visualized as the paper's Figure 8 volcano/tornado pair with fdr2d isolines.

name: fdr2d-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when a metabolomics study (e.g. the 3226 x 57 schisandra Korea-vs-China matrix) requires simultaneous testing of thousands of metabolite null hypotheses under two-dimensional FDR control at levels such as 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, or 0.3.

name: feasible-2-cut-fragmentation-modeling
description: Use when constructing theoretical fragment masses from known chemical structures (e.g., PubChem-derived SDF) to annotate LC-MS/MS spectra during dereplication with DEREPLICATOR+/NPDtools.

name: feature-abundance-matrix-processing
description: Use when a tab-delimited feature abundance table (e.g. from MS-DIAL) requires pre-processing — m/z defect filtering, CV ratio filtering vs QCs, sample/feature quality thresholds, or NA imputation — prior to normalization and statistics in margheRita.

name: feature-alignment-across-polarities
description: Use when LC-HRMS data were acquired in both positive and negative ionization modes and a single combined, aligned feature table spanning both polarities is needed (e.g., patRoon standard-X/solvent-X triplicates).

name: feature-alignment-and-quantification
description: Use when raw centroided LC-MS mzML runs (e.g., from MassIVE accessions like MSV000080560 or MSV000080553) must be converted into an aligned feature quantification table as the first computational stage of untargeted metabolomics or molecular cartography.

name: feature-alignment-metric-computation-precision-recall-f1
description: Use when a feature alignment result (e.g. from G-Aligner, MZmine2, OpenMS, XCMS or local bipartite matching) must be quantitatively scored against manually annotated library-analyte features on benchmark datasets such as TripleTOF 6600, QE HF or MTBLS562.

name: feature-and-sample-missingness-filtering
description: Use when a metabolomics feature data matrix (peak intensities) contains missing values before normalization, and high-missingness features or samples must be removed prior to imputation.

name: feature-annotation-mapping-with-xenobiotic-flags
description: Use when a raw metabolomics workbook (nightingale_v1_example.xlsx, metabolon_v1.1_example.xlsx) must be decomposed into abundance, sample, and feature metadata tables with annotation columns like super_pathway retained unaltered.

name: feature-annotation-qc-granularity
description: Use when building or running untargeted LC-MS/MS QC with Rapid QC-MS and you must annotate reference-standard and external-standard features separately because RS and ES derive from different biological matrices, so each needs its own .msp target library and its own module.

name: feature-based-molecular-annotation
description: Use when you have an aligned MS-Dial feature list with MS/MS deconvolved spectra (e.g. 435 MS-CleanR-filtered PI-mode features) and need to annotate them against open mass spectral libraries.

name: feature-based-molecular-networking
description: Use when you have an aligned feature table (.csv) plus MS2 spectral summary (.mgf) from MZmine/MS-DIAL/XCMS and want a molecular network that groups features by MS2 similarity, or compares MS2-only vs IIN-augmented topology.

name: feature-based-molecular-networking
description: Use when you have MZmine pre-processed LC-MS/MS data exported as a feature table (.csv, peak areas, rows with MS2) plus a paired spectra .mgf, and you need library annotation, cosine scores, paired-peak counts, or molecular networks.

name: feature-based-molecular-networking
description: Use when an LC–MS/MS untargeted metabolomics data set must be processed into a filtered spectral similarity molecular network and benchmarked against GNPS FBMN with paper-equivalent parameters, e.g., MSV000080502.
tools: GNPS (Global Natural Products Social Molecular Networking)

name: feature-based-molecular-networking
description: Use when untargeted LC-MS/MS feature tables need to be organized into molecular subnetworks so that per-node library matches and CANOPUS class predictions can be propagated and scored at the subnetwork level.

name: feature-blank-correction-filtering
description: Use when a sample mzML has a paired extraction blank mzML and detected features must be filtered for background contamination before PFAS prioritization (MD/C-m/C, KMD, suspect screening).

name: feature-blank-filtering
description: Use when raw vendor feature tables (e.g. a sample plus its solvent blanks) contain background features that must be stripped before PFAS annotation, such as an AFFF sample table with tens of thousands of detected features dominated by non-analyte background.

name: feature-cluster-aggregation-analysis
description: Use when a RAMClustR (post-XCMS) clustered object is available and the goal is to evaluate whether aggregating clustered MS features into compound-level spectra lowers quantitative analytical variation versus single-feature measurements.

name: feature-cluster-assignment-tabulation
description: Use when untargeted LC-MS/MS feature tables need grouping by structural similarity: a precomputed pairwise spectral distance matrix is available and the number of clusters k must be chosen from Silhouette-score evaluation.

name: feature-clustering-dendrogram-interpretation
description: Use when a metaboprep Metaboprep object has passed quality_control and you need to inspect the hierarchical clustering of metabolite features (qc_tree) before cutting clusters at a tree_cut_height or reporting QC results in an HTML report.

name: feature-clustering-performance-metrics-reporting
description: Use when evaluating or benchmarking how well competing feature-grouping methods deconvolute MS/MS feature clusters from an XCMS feature table and you need to report MSMS similarity, cluster counts, and singleton percentages in a reproducible comparison table.

name: feature-collection-counting
description: Use when loading an mzMine or XCMS feature table into NeatMS and you need to confirm the expected total number of feature collections before filtering or neural-network labelling.

name: feature-correlation-hierarchical-clustering
description: Use when you have a table of statistically significant features (e.g. permutation p-value < 0.01 from MB-VIP testing) and need to group them into coherent feature sets based on how their intensities co-vary across samples.

name: feature-count-comparison-analysis
description: Reference for quantifying how a parameter tuning approach improves metabolic feature extraction yield, by counting extracted features under tuned vs. default settings and computing the fold increase.

name: feature-count-reconciliation-across-datasets
description: Use when raw mzML/mzXML feature tables must be quality-filtered and the reported before/after feature counts (e.g. dendroides 1,078→784) need to be reproduced or audited.

name: feature-count-reduction-tracking
description: Use when a priorization workflow needs quantified evidence of how intensity-based (2% normalized area) and quantile-based (0.75 cut-off) filters shrink a feature table before computing priority-rank scores.

name: feature-count-reproducibility-assessment
description: Use when the same raw LC-MS dataset (e.g., pooled human plasma mzML files) must be processed by two or more tools to compare feature counts and cross-tool feature correspondence, or to benchmark a new processing tool against XCMS/MZmine.

name: feature-detection-in-mzml-acquisitions
description: Use when raw Thermo .raw or .mzML flow injection MSn files must be turned into per-file feature/compound detections in mzmine, e.g. to count molecules detected in positive-only, negative-only, or both ionization modes.

name: feature-error-range-overlap-clustering
description: Use when you have replicate-comparison output — replicated feature peak lists from technical replicate mzML runs — and need to collapse them into a single list of unique MS features for downstream bioactivity integration.

name: feature-extraction-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify how faithfully an HRMS peak-detection pipeline recovers known analytes, by matching extracted chromatographic peaks against a spiked-chemical list of known composition (e.g., 398 MS-amenable chemicals in ENTACT mixtures).

name: feature-extraction-parameter-translation
description: Use when raw LC-MS-based metabolomics data (any sample type, acquisition mode, or MS vendor) must be processed for feature extraction but default tool parameters would under-extract true positive metabolic features.

name: feature-fidelity-rate-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantify how relaxing peak-picking thresholds (mass tolerance, S/N) changes JPA-PP vs JPA-MR feature counts and the proportion of features with acceptable chromatographic peak shapes.

name: feature-group-count-threshold-analysis
description: Use when you must establish how small a reference feature list can be (relative to a full common-feature list) before retention time shift computation and alignment accuracy of LC-HRMS chromatograms degrade.

name: feature-group-quality-control
description: Use when you need to QC a DeepRTAlign alignment run — i.e., estimate alignment FDR from decoy alignments in information_all.csv and reproduce the post-QC information_target.csv.

name: feature-grouping-across-samples
description: Use when LC-HRMS features must be grouped across replicate sample analyses (e.g. patRoonData 'standard-X'/'solvent-X' triplicate injections) or when feature-group outputs from OpenMS, XCMS and enviPick must be compared and combined on the same dataset.

name: feature-hashing-spectrum-vectorization
description: Use when large collections of high-resolution MS/MS spectra (mzML, mzXML, or MGF peak files) must be converted into compact numeric vectors suitable for approximate similarity searching or indexing without exhaustive pairwise comparisons.

name: feature-image-generation-for-image-registration
description: Use when you have m/z-binned, TIC-normalized serial-section MSI data (e.g. coronal3D_propagated_decoded.h5) and need per-section images with morphological contrast suitable as moving images for affine/B-spline registration to MRI.

name: feature-importance-rank-scoring
description: Use when a wide-format metabolomics feature table plus a design file with class labels are available and the goal is to identify which features differentiate sample groups via random-forest variable importance.

name: feature-intensity-colormap-scaling
description: Use when a molecular map of feature intensities in 'ili is dominated by a few high-intensity spots, neighboring spots overlap, or the color range obscures spatial gradients in the intensity data.

name: feature-intensity-correlation-analysis
description: Use when a candidate match table between two LC-MS feature lists (features described by RT, m/z, and median log10FI per sample) must be quality-checked via intensity-agreement between matched pairs.

name: feature-intensity-correlation-filtering
description: Use when a RowMerger-merged annotation table contains multiple putative annotations per m/z feature and a feature-intensity table is available, so annotations can be ranked by adduct probability, feature correlation, and mass error.

name: feature-intensity-filtering
description: Use when an MZmine 2/3 peak-area quant table produces inflated feature counts (e.g., 727 features) that dilute Inventa's Feature Component (FC), and low-intensity or ubiquitous features must be removed before ranking extracts.

name: feature-intensity-matrix-preparation
description: Use when an actual metabolomics or proteomics dataset must be formatted as a feature/sample intensity matrix as input to pseudoQC's regression-based QC simulation before correction and normalization.

name: feature-intensity-pattern-comparison
description: Use when re-processed LC-MS/MS features (m/z, RT, per-sample intensities) must be matched against a published XCMS/CAMERA feature list to compute detection rates and intensity-pattern agreement, e.g., on MetaboLights datasets like MTBLS1129/MTBLS1130.

name: feature-intensity-sensitivity-specificity-benchmarking
description: Use when you must quantitatively validate that detected metabolite feature intensities are correct against known spike-in ground truth, e.g. precision/recall on repeated spike-in LC-MS measurements in a plasma background.

name: feature-intensity-shift-characterization
description: Use when preparing independently peak-picked XCMS feature tables from two LC-MS metabolomics batches (e.g. MESA reference vs Rotterdam target) for feature correspondence matching, since the matching algorithm operates on per-feature medians of RT, m/z, and FI rather than raw sample-level values.

name: feature-labeling-convention-formatting
description: Use when feature tables from multiple separation groups (HILIC-MS, CE-MS) are being augmented into a single fused feature space and each row must retain its platform-of-origin identity via the 'm/z @Time, Group' label format.

name: feature-level-count-tabulation
description: Use when a JPA-processed feature table contains a 'level' column labeling features as PP or MR, and you need per-level counts to compare feature depth across datasets (e.g., 1 s vs 2 s vs 3 s DDA cycle times) or to quantify MR-rescued features.

name: feature-level-deconvolution-comparison
description: Use when the same DIA-MS/SWATH dataset must be processed through two deconvolution arms (MS2Dec vs CorrDec) and compared feature-by-feature via per-feature MS/MS match scores.

name: feature-lipid-candidate-scoring
description: Use when a feature (defined by m/z and retention time) received multiple lipid identifications from rule-based fragment matching and you must order them, e.g. appending a single top-ranked lipid to a MZmine/MS-DIAL/XCMS feature table.

name: feature-lipid-pair-fragment-matrix-construction
description: Use when you have feature-lipid candidate pairs from MS1 exact-mass matching and corresponding .ms2 spectra (converted from ddMS2-topN or AIF raw files), and need to decide which in silico fragments were observed for each pair so downstream rule-based lipid identification can proceed.

name: feature-lipid-pair-tabulation
description: Use when you have a peak-picked feature table (m/z, retention time, intensities, e.g. from MZmine) and need to enumerate which library lipid species/adducts could explain each feature's precursor m/z before MS/MS validation.

name: feature-list-consistency-evaluation
description: Use when MS1 feature lists from multiple LC-IM-MS replicate runs are available and you need to quantify whether preprocessing (e.g., PreProcessor smoothing) changed replicate-to-replicate detection consistency.

name: feature-list-matching-across-lchrms-tools
description: Use when the same LC-HRMS profile-mode dataset has been processed by several peak-picking tools and you need to quantify which chromatographic features are found in common, missed, or exclusive per tool.

name: feature-mask-generation-from-clustering-bounds
description: Use when an LA-ICP-MS elemental image (e.g., 56Fe in a 1.5 mm TMA core imported as an Agilent MassHunter batch) needs an objective, unsupervised ROI mask without manual threshold tuning, and the input supports automatic image thresholding or multi-level clustering.

name: feature-mass-adduct-error-grouping
description: Use when an annotation table from an untargeted metabolomics workflow contains multiple putative annotation rows per feature that share the same experimental mass, m/z, adduct, and mass error, and downstream comparison or pathway prioritization requires a smaller consolidated table.

name: feature-matching-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when quantifying how accurately a feature alignment method matched features across multiple LC-MS runs, by comparing aligned results against manually annotated library analytes (m/z, RT, area) with F_ACC/A_ACC metrics.

name: feature-matrix-annotation-integration
description: Use when xcms pre-processing (peak picking, grouping, retention-time correction) has produced an XCMSnExp object on LC-MS samples and you need the feature matrix plus its feature and sample metadata bundled into one R object.

name: feature-matrix-construction-from-ms-spectra
description: Use when raw mass spectra stored as variable-length m/z/intensity pairs must be reduced to a fixed-dimensional matrix (TIC filtering + 0.1-Da m/z binning) before feeding CNN/LSTM/Transformer classifiers.

name: feature-matrix-parsing-msi
description: Use when input is an MSI feature matrix (e.g., 14,260 pixels x 3,044 ion peaks from AFAD-ESI positive mode) that must be reshaped so each row is one spatial pixel with X/Y coordinate columns before SMAnalyst QC or clustering.

name: feature-missingness-threshold-categorization
description: Use when a metabolomics feature table (sample-by-feature intensity matrix, e.g. from Sciex MultiQuant export) contains missing values that must be distinguished from true absence before imputation or statistical testing.

name: feature-outlier-detection
description: Use when raw ion-concentration data (e.g. ICP-MS ppm values for Ca44, Cd111, Fe56, K39...) contain extreme readings or unreliable samples that must be flagged before batch correction, standardisation and symbolisation.

name: feature-peak-area-quantification-per-sample
description: Use when processing centroided LC-MS mzML metabolomics data and you need per-sample quantitative peak areas for features that were detected only once on composite (cross-sample) mass tracks, with traceability back to mass tracks.

name: feature-prioritization-interpretation
description: Use when a globaltest-based prioritization on msFeaST spectral-similarity clusters has flagged differential features and you must assess whether their MS2-similarity connectivity supports the statistical call.

name: feature-quantification-table-conversion
description: Use when an OpenMS consensusXML/feature map from UmetaFlow pre-processing must be transformed into a GNPS-upload-ready feature quantification table alongside an MGF and sample metadata.

name: feature-quantification-table-export
description: Use when an LC-MS dataset has been processed into an aligned feature list with MS2 consensus spectra in MZmine (or MS-DIAL/XCMS) and the goal is to run FBMN+IIMN on GNPS — the quantification table plus .mgf and IIN edges must be exported first.

name: feature-quantification-table-generation
description: Use when processing a deposited GC-MS dataset (e.g. MassIVE MSV000084033) through the GNPS MSHub workflow and you need deconvoluted fragmentation spectra plus a per-feature quantification table as exportable artifacts.

name: feature-quantification-table-generation
description: Use when raw LC-HRMS2 DDA metabolomics data (Thermo RAW / mzML / mzXML) must be converted, per sample, into a feature quantification table (m/z, RT, area/intensity) plus MS2 .mgf files for FBMN or ISDB annotation.

name: feature-relabeling-md5-hash
description: Use when preparing fingerprint-bearing MS1 features for qiime qemistree make-hierarchy: raw feature IDs (from MZmine2 feature detection) must become stable tip names that persist across independently processed datasets.

name: feature-selection-quality-control
description: Use when targeted MRM/LC-MSMS or HPLC peak-picked features must be filtered, selected, and QC'd against feature-filter and feature-QC meta-values before calibration and quantitation in a SmartPeak workflow.

name: feature-set-global-testing
description: Use when analyzing LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics feature tables where per-feature tests lose power or multiplicity, and structurally similar features should be jointly tested as groups (clusters) against a two-level group contrast.

name: feature-specific-univariate-p-value-extraction
description: Use when running msFeaST group-wise globaltest on k-medoids spectral-similarity clusters and you need feature-level univariate P-values alongside the Bonferroni-corrected cluster-wise P-values in a single results table.

name: feature-table-assembly
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS metabolomic/lipidomic files (e.g. mzML converted via MSConvert from Multi-ABLE acquisitions) must be turned into a per-feature table before LipidFinder filtering, metID annotation, or EigenMS-style normalization.

name: feature-table-bray-curtis-dissimilarity-computation
description: Use when an aligned GNPS FBMN-style feature abundance table is available and you need a composition-only baseline distance to quantify batch effects (e.g., RT-shift pseudo-F) against MS2/fragmentation-aware methods.

name: feature-table-comparison-across-parameterizations
description: Use when two feature tables were produced from identical raw LC-MS data with different parameter-optimization tools (e.g., AutoTuner vs IPO centWave settings) and you must quantify overlap, subset-specific features, or per-subset MS2 spectra depletion/enrichment.

name: feature-table-curation
description: Use when you have a table of detected drug metabolite features (paired m/z and RT from LC-HRMS) for one or more parent drugs incubated with human liver S9 fraction, plus a corresponding BioTransformer 3.0 predicted-metabolite list, and need to label each feature as predicted or unpredicted (novel).

name: feature-table-export
description: Use when raw positive-ion-mode LC-MS/MS mzML files must be converted into a per-feature CSV (m/z, RT, representative MS2 spectrum) to feed SIRIUS formula/adduct assignment and MVP candidate ranking.

name: feature-table-export-and-qc-inspection
description: Use when you have raw LC–MS mzML data processed with massprocesser into a mass_dataset object and need the feature table plus QC/peak-count checks for downstream tidyMass analysis.

name: feature-table-filtering-by-correlation-and-mz-rt-tolerance
description: Use when an LC-MS metabolite feature table contains suspected in-source fragment features that must be de novo recognized and filtered by correlation and m/z/RT tolerance, e.g. before metabolite annotation from DDA/DIA/fullscan mzXML data.

name: feature-table-generation-from-lc-ms-profiles
description: Use when you have ncGTW realignment output for misaligned XCMS features plus XCMS peak start/end points and widths, and need to convert warping functions back into corrected retention times and a per-feature intensity table across samples.

name: feature-table-interpretation
description: Use when starting from an assembled pcpfm experiment directory containing converted centroided mzML files plus sample-to-file metadata, and feature tables (full and preferred) must be generated via Asari before QC, annotation, or normalization steps.

name: feature-table-matching-across-acquisition-modes
description: Decision support for quantifying coverage overlap between full-scan, RegFilter-scheduled precursor lists, and DDA MS/MS fragmented features in LC-MS/MS metabolomics datasets.

name: feature-table-merging-across-samples
description: Use when per-sample MS-DIAL feature lists (precursor MS1 m/z, RT, MS/MS spectra) must be consolidated into one aligned feature table across many LC-MS/MS samples before classification or multivariate analysis.

name: feature-table-metadata-mapping
description: Use when a feature table must be partitioned by sample class (Blank, QC, Unknown/STD) for background-removal or QC steps, and the experiment's metadata CSV provides the per-sample sample_type annotations.

name: feature-table-mz-rounding
description: Use when comparing LC-MS feature tables from different processing tools (XCMS, MZmine, asari) and you need to quantify whether reported m/z values remain distinguishable at the 5 ppm instrument resolution after rounding to 3 decimal places, e.

name: feature-table-parsing
description: Use when input is a peak-picked feature table (e.g., MZmine/MS-DIAL/XCMS export) with m/z and retention time per feature, and the goal is to prepare it for LipidMatch MS1 precursor matching or to tally annotated features per polarity.

name: feature-table-parsing
description: Use when you have an MZmine3 feature list with representative spectra from positive ion mode LC–MS/MS data and need molecular formula and adduct assignment per feature, or need to reproduce a reported formula/adduct hit rate.

name: feature-table-tic-normalization
description: Use when an Asari-derived feature table (e.g. preferred_Feature_table.tsv) needs per-sample intensity scaling before statistics, especially when per-sample TIC correlates with feature counts or when samples were acquired in multiple batches.

name: feature-table-tsv-io
description: Use when a pcpfm experiment's curated feature intensities must be loaded, filtered, or persisted — every pipeline operation (blank masking, batch correction, imputation, normalization) consumes and emits a TSV feature table under a new moniker.

name: feature-vector-dimension-verification
description: Use when reconstructing or re-implementing GLEAMS' spectrum encoder and you must confirm the concatenated precursor, fragment-bin, and reference-similarity blocks yield the expected 3010 features before feeding the neural network.

name: featuredata-log-transformation-and-imputation
description: Use when raw metabolite peak-intensity data has been arranged into the NormalizeMets 'featuredata' format (samples as rows, metabolites as columns) and needs log transformation plus missing-value imputation before applying NormQcmets, NormScaling, or other normalization functions.

name: featureml-feature-export-visualization
description: Use when PeakBot detection is complete and detected features plus background (wall/background) annotations must be written to featureML/TSV and visually spot-checked.

name: featureml-peak-export-and-annotation
description: Use when PeakBot peak-picking output from LC-HRMS profile-mode chromatograms must be exported as a tsv peak-area table and featureML files for inspection/annotation in TOPPView, or as images for user verification.

name: featurexml-feature-map-serialization
description: Use when a hypothesis-driven feature-assembly stage has accepted a final list of features (mass traces grouped by m/z spacing, co-elution, and SVM isotope-pattern classification) and the results must be written out in featureXML format for downstream TOPP/OpenMS tools.

name: featurexml-format-conversion
description: Use when benchmarking or cross-tool comparison requires converting XCMS/CAMERA feature output into OpenMS featureXML maps with monoisotopic isotope values preserved, so FeatureLinkerUnlabeledQT can link coinciding features and precision/recall can be computed on identical ground truth.

name: feedforward-layer-enumeration
description: Use when you need to reconstruct, verify, or document the layer-by-layer architecture of released HDF5 Keras/TF2 model files (e.g., NPClassifier's three single-task networks) before reimplementation or reuse.

name: few-shot-task-sampling-from-mass-spectrometry-data
description: Use when SCMS metabolomics data yield too few cells per phenotype for conventional deep learning and you need to build N-shot meta-learning tasks (e.g., primary vs metastatic melanoma classification from IGR39/IGR37 single-probe SCMS profiles).

name: few-shot-transfer-learning-comparison
description: Use when few (1-5) labeled single-cell mass spectrometry (SCMS) samples are available for a new cell group and you need to adapt a pre-trained meta-learning classifier and compare it with transfer-learning baselines.

name: fft-based-isotopic-envelope-simulation
description: Use when the input is a metabolite molecular formula (with natural or SIP-enriched isotope abundances) and the goal is a simulated whole-molecule isotopic envelope (M, M+1, M+2, ...) rather than fine structure.

name: fft-based-scalability-processing
description: Use when a deposited GC-MS dataset is too large for direct NNMF auto-deconvolution in MSHub, and the analysis goal is deconvoluted fragmentation spectra at repository scale for molecular networking.

name: fgsea-based-metabolite-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have metabolomics summary statistics (log2FC and p-values per metabolite) and want GSEA-style enrichment over KEGG pathway sets, e.g. reproducing control vs mutant lung cancer MetSEA results.

name: fid-time-domain-preprocessing
description: Use when starting from raw Bruker-formatted FID data (extract_params + extract_fids outputs) and you need to correct the group-delay artifact, suppress residual solvent, and Fourier-transform each FID into a spectrum before phase/baseline steps.

name: fid-time-domain-signal-extraction
description: Use when the input is a directory of raw Bruker 1H-NMR spectra (each sample folder containing 'acqus' and 'fid' files) and you need time-domain FID data plus acquisition parameters as pandas DataFrames before any FID-domain preprocessing.

name: fid-to-spectrum-preprocessing-pipeline
description: Use when starting from raw Bruker NMR acquisition directories (acqus files + FIDs) and a cleaned, phase-corrected, baseline-corrected spectra table (samples × ppm) is needed for metabolomics analysis.

name: fid-truncation-and-binning
description: Use when preparing a binned time-domain FID (e.g., 16,384 complex points) for SAND decomposition, before optimization iterations, to curb overfitting via FID truncation and randomized 70/20/10 train/validation/test subsampling.

name: fiducial-based-image-coregistration-with-penmarks
description: Use when pre- and post-MALDI tiled microscopy images must be stitched and aligned so MALDI ablation marks can be assigned to segmented cells in a SpaceM-style workflow.

name: fiducial-point-geometric-calibration
description: Use when an optical image with three fiducial marks of known instrument coordinates must be registered so detected target pixels can be output as instrument-relative X, Y positions in an MS geometry file.

name: figure-panel-reproduction-from-deposited-data
description: Use when a published figure must be reproduced from deposited deconvoluted GC-MS feature tables that carry sample metadata (e.g., body-location coordinates), and the panel depicts per-feature intensity distributions across spatial locations.

name: figure-reproduction-and-comparison
description: Use when a previously published MS proteomics study has deposited processed results (e.g. PXD037527: DDA/DIA/WWA on Orbitrap Exploris 480) and the goal is to reproduce its figures end-to-end.

name: figure-reproduction-from-corrected-data
description: Use when a target figure reports per-setting counts or effect sizes (e.g. features passing FDR <= 0.2) that must be regenerated from feature-intensity matrices plus batch and phenotype annotation tables.

name: figure-reproduction-from-publication
description: Use when a published NMR metabonomics figure (e.g. a MWAS skyline plot of phenotype-metabolite associations) must be regenerated in R from the authors' package, its vignette SummarizedExperiment data, and documented parameter settings.

name: file-count-aggregation-table
description: Use when you have per-file metadata (raw-file listing with acquisition-mode and instrument annotations, e.g., from a PRIDE PXD identifier) and need a partitioned count table grouped by mode and instrument to audit dataset composition.
tools: ProteomeXchange Consortium via the PRIDE partner repository

name: file-per-line-array-assembly-into-2d-image
description: Use when raw LA-ICP-MS data arrive as generic one-file-per-csv line exports or vendor exports lacking a native importer, and the goal is direct drag-and-drop assembly into a 2D elemental image without preprocessing.

name: file-size-comparison-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing storage efficiency of two text serialization formats (e.g. JSON vs XML) holding the same structured metadata, or when benchmarking a format's size claim such as Aird's JSON-based metadata versus XML equivalents.

name: file-system-format-detection
description: Use when a downloaded metabolomics study from MetaboLights or Metabolomics Workbench arrives in an unknown raw layout and it must be classified into a known format signature before transformation into an analysis-ready standard format.

name: file-volume-measurement-and-ratio-computation
description: Use when evaluating or reporting the storage footprint of MS data formats — e.g., MRM raw vendor files must be compared against converted 32-bit mzML and Aird volumes, or compression ratios must be validated against reported reductions of >60% (vs vendor) and >80% (vs mzML).

name: filename-convention-checking
description: Use when preparing to submit a molecular networking or feature-based molecular networking job to GNPS and a sample-information/metadata table (e.g., 3DMouse_duodenum_metadata.txt from MSV000083437) must be conformance-checked and normalized.

name: filter-comparison-visualization
description: Use when a reaction-network expansion has been generated under multiple filter combinations and you need per-combination counts of annotated compounds/peaks plus a comparison figure (e.g. reproducing Figure 6).

name: filter-efficiency-ranking-across-criteria
description: Use when you have applied multiple rule-based filters to an enumerated compound set and need per-rule elimination counts to identify the most effective criterion and validate filter behavior against a reference (e.g., Figure 2d).

name: filter-rate-statistics-across-molecules
description: Use when you need to quantify how much a retention-time filter narrows a candidate list, by recording each molecule's eliminated-candidate fraction and the mean filter rate over a molecule set.

name: filter-removal-count-comparison
description: Use when you must quantify how many spectra a cleaning pipeline removes with a given filter set versus an ablated filter set (e.g. without repair functions), to justify the filters' added value.

name: filter-summary-qc-accounting
description: Use when you have an mpactr mpactr object after running one or more filters on a Progenesis-format LC-MS/MS peak table and need to record which ions each filter removed or retained, and which mispicked ions were merged.

name: fingerprint-annotation-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when predicted molecular fingerprints (e.g. from IDSL_MINT models on .msp spectra) must be benchmarked against a reference fingerprint database to compute overall and per-lipid-class top-hit annotation accuracy.

name: fingerprint-based-candidate-re-ranking
description: Use when you have multiple candidate structures (de novo SMILES or database hits) for a positive-mode MS2 spectrum and must rank them against a CSI:FingerID-predicted query fingerprint to pick the top candidate.

name: fingerprint-based-retention-time-regression
description: Use when you have small-molecule structures (SDF/molfiles) with computed ECFP fingerprints and experimentally acquired reverse-phase chromatography retention times, and need an ML model that predicts RT in seconds or ranks candidate identities by predicted RT.

name: fingerprint-bit-softmax-classification
description: Use when training or reconstructing a transformer that maps tokenized MS/MS peaks (.msp-derived m/z + intensity tokens) to a fixed-length molecular fingerprint-bit vector, rather than to SMILES text.

name: fingerprint-bit-tokenization-for-seq2seq-targets
description: Use when an .msp reference MS/MS library lacks precomputed `Fingerprint: ` rows, and bit-location descriptor targets must be derived from SMILES/InChI to train the MS/MS-to-fingerprint transformer.

name: fingerprint-conditioned-de-novo-structure-generation
description: Use when a tandem MS2 spectrum has a confidently predicted formula and fingerprint (SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID) but no convincing database candidate, and you want de novo SMILES candidates instead of library lookup.

name: fingerprint-conditioned-molecule-generation
description: Use when generating molecular structures conditioned on an intermediate chemical representation (fingerprint) with a diffusion model, or when scaling decoder pretraining with large fingerprint-structure pools before spectra-conditioned finetuning.

name: fingerprint-cosine-similarity-scoring
description: Use when a predicted Morgan fingerprint bit string from an HSQC spectrum must be compared against reference fingerprints from chemical databases such as PubChem to retrieve, rank, and label (identical/similar) candidate structures.

name: fingerprint-linear-probing-on-mass-spectra
description: Use when you have pre-trained spectral embeddings (e.g. from DreaMS on GeMS HDF5 spectra) and want to test whether the representation space encodes molecular substructure without fine-tuning the encoder.

name: fingerprint-prediction-metrics-evaluation
description: Use when comparing fingerprint-prediction model variants (e.g. low ≤30 eV vs high ≥30 eV collision-energy models vs one combined model) on MS/MS spectra and need structure-disjoint CV with accuracy/F1 metrics.

name: fingerprint-probability-thresholding
description: Use when experimental MS/MS spectra must be turned into discrete fingerprint tokens for finetuning or inference, and a pretrained spectral inference model (MIST) outputs per-bit probabilities {p0,...,p4095} rather than binary fingerprints.

name: fingerprint-random-forest-metabolite-classification
description: Use when evaluating whether a chemical language model's generated molecules are metabolite-like by classifying them against held-out metabolites via fingerprints.

name: fingerprint-retrieval-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when a fine-tuned tandem-MS model outputs molecular fingerprints and you must quantify molecular-structure retrieval quality against MIST/FFN baselines on the CANOPUS benchmark (8,000 spectra, 7,000 unique molecules).

name: fingerprint-scorer-validation
description: Use when tandem MS/MS spectra must be converted into predicted CDK molecular fingerprints via per-bit libSVM models, and candidate compounds ranked by Jaccard similarity against pre-calculated database fingerprints.

name: fingerprint-similarity-metrics
description: Use when scoring de novo generated molecules against known ground-truth structures on a spectral elucidation benchmark, or when quantifying how much an ablation (e.g., 2D-only vs joint 2D&3D diffusion) degrades structural fidelity beyond exact-match accuracy.

name: fingerprint-similarity-scoring
description: Use when ranking candidate compounds for an analyte whose fingerprint has already been predicted from an MS/MS spectrum — score each candidate's 528-digit MACCS/FP3/FP4 fingerprint against the prediction and pick the top-ranked candidate.

name: fingerprint-similarity-scoring
description: Use when ranked candidate lists from cosine-only spectral matching leave the true identity below rank 1 (top-1 < 40%) and fingerprint information is available to integrate for improved ranking.

name: fingerprint-threshold-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when a pipeline binarizes predicted fingerprint probabilities into a fixed-length bit vector via a threshold parameter, and you need to justify the chosen threshold or demonstrate insensitivity by retraining/evaluating across epsilon values.

name: fingerprint-to-molecule-sequence-translation
description: Use when constructing a cross-modal pretraining corpus of fingerprint–molecule pairs and you need a sequence-to-sequence model that maps fingerprint tokens (FP) to SELFIES structures, or when reproducing MS-BART's task ② pretraining objective.

name: fingerprint-token-sequence-generation
description: Use when building a large-scale pretraining corpus of fingerprint–molecule pairs from unlabeled molecular structures, where fingerprints must be expressed as tokens in a unified vocabulary rather than raw bit vectors.

name: fingerprint-variance-thresholding
