description: Use when building the fragment set for a combinatorial bond-breaking MS/MS peak predictor: molecules must be converted from structures into a deterministic fragmentation DAG with formula/mass annotations before probabilistic fragment-distribution modelling.

name: fragmentation-depth-ablation-analysis
description: Use when evaluating how a fragmentation depth parameter (e.g. d=3 vs d=4) changes MS/MS spectrum prediction metrics, or when reproducing reported ablation deltas across metric splits.

name: fragmentation-graph-attribution-analysis
description: Use when you have ICEBERG's per-fragment DAG outputs for held-out test molecules and need to verify that predicted bond breakages (e.g., C-O/C-N vs C-C) and hydrogen-shift peak attributions are chemically plausible.

name: fragmentation-graph-construction
description: Use when dereplicating centroided LC-MS/MS spectra against a database of known metabolite structures and you need to model in-silico fragment ions of candidate metabolites beyond peptidic natural products (e.g., polyketides, terpenes, alkaloids).

name: fragmentation-graph-depth-pruning
description: Use when building theoretical fragment sets from chemical structures (e.g. PubChem-derived SDFs) to annotate MS/MS spectra, and the fragmentation graph must be constrained to feasible fragmentations.

name: fragmentation-graph-feature-engineering
description: Use when predicting ESI-MS/MS spectra for small (≤1000 Da) metabolites from molecular structures and you need ML-learned fragmentation probabilities rather than hand-coded rules, e.g. building an in silico reference spectral library.

name: fragmentation-graph-scoring
description: Use when dereplicating centroided LC-MS/MS spectra (MGF, mzXML, mzML, mzData) against a chemical structure database of natural products, especially non-peptidic classes (polyketides, terpenes, benzenoids, alkaloids, flavonoids) that peptide-only tools like DEREPLICATOR cannot handle.

name: fragmentation-graph-transition-modelling
description: Use when predicting ESI-MS/MS spectra from a compound structure in CFM-ID 4.0, or when modifying ring-cleavage transition probabilities so unstable intermediates do not emit peaks.

name: fragmentation-graph-transition-probability-learning
description: Use when predicting ESI-MS/MS spectra from chemical structures (compound-to-spectrum) or when reproducing CFM-ID 4.0-style ablations on Metlin QTOF [M+H]+/[M-H]- spectra at 10/20/40 eV.

name: fragmentation-pattern-querying-by-mz-difference
description: Use when a mined mineMS2 pattern set must be searched for a specific m/z difference or loss (e.g. 186.079 Da) to recover spectra sharing that fragmentation, including similarities missed by GNPS network edges.

name: fragmentation-pattern-reproducibility-quantification
description: Use when processing GC-MS data deconvoluted with MSHub/GNPS and you need to score deconvolution confidence per compound and discard annotations whose fragmentation patterns are irreproducible across samples.

name: fragmentation-pattern-visualization
description: Use when a GNPS molecular network component (e.g. the 21-spectra fungisporin cluster of P. nordicum) must be visually interpreted with a mineMS2 pattern, showing the exact m/z-difference graph and which component spectra contain it.

name: fragmentation-spectrum-database-matching
description: Use when LC–MS/MS untargeted metabolomics data include acquired fragmentation spectra and candidate annotations from an MS1 database must be ranked by integrating fragment matching with isotope-pattern, mass-accuracy, and adduct evidence.

name: fragmentation-tree-based-candidate-ranking
description: Use when benchmarking metabolite annotation engines on tandem MS/MS spectra: you need the SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID fragmentation-tree baseline ranked candidate lists under the same test splits, compound database and precursor mass tolerance as the ChemDistiller evaluation.

name: fragmentation-tree-computation
description: Use when you have high-resolution MS/MS spectra of small molecules and need to go beyond elemental composition — computing fragment formulas and fragmentation events to rank molecular formulas or feed downstream structure identification.

name: fragmentation-tree-computation
description: Use when a chemical-feature list (MGF with MS1 and MS2 peaks from MZmine2) must be converted into molecular formulas, fragmentation trees, and predicted fingerprints before building a chemical tree with q2-qemistree make-hierarchy.

name: fragmentation-tree-intensity-explanation-analysis
description: Use when reproducing the preprocessing filter that reduced raw feature tables (mzML/mzXML-derived) before ZODIAC molecular formula annotation, and when validating the reported per-dataset feature counts for the five datasets.

name: fragmentation-tree-similarity-scoring
description: Use when reranking SIRIUS top-50 molecular formula candidates across an LC-MS/MS dataset where related compounds should share similar formulas, i.e. building ZODIAC's Bayesian assignment graph.

name: fragmented-bgc-membership-assignment
description: Use when an antiSMASH-derived BGC dataset contains fragmented clusters (partial BGCs on contig edges) that were excluded from GCF model building, and each fragment must be assigned to an existing GCF rather than left unclustered.

name: freetext-term-synonym-mapping
description: Use when sample metadata contains freetext descriptions that must be replaced by terms from a fixed vocabulary, or when a user has confirmed adding a new freetext term absent from an existing vocabulary.

name: frequency-based-scaffold-candidate-aggregation
description: Use when pre-computed ranked scaffold candidate lists (e.g., ranks_msgym_pred.pkl from Zenodo record 17115068) are available for MS/MS test spectra and one predicted scaffold per chemical formula is needed to compute Scaffold Prediction Accuracy (SPA).

name: fret-colocalization-cross-validation
description: Use when colocalization coefficients computed on two-channel CFP/YFP confocal images need independent validation against FRET measurements of the same cell groups, or when interpreting FRET-negative results for large complexes like CRM1 (130 kDa).

name: friedman-nemenyi-multiple-comparison-testing
description: Use when you have repeated (e.g., 10-fold or fivefold CV) F-measure/Accuracy scores for multiple competing models across folds and must rank them and identify statistically significant pairwise winners, such as selecting among 24 classifiers built from peak-quality metric sets M4, M7 and M11.

name: friedman-nemenyi-statistical-classifier-comparison
description: Use when comparing multiple classifiers (e.g. 24 combinations of 3 metric sets and 8 algorithms) on repeated cross-validation folds and you need a statistically justified single model rather than eyeballing metric scatter plots.

name: friedman-nemenyi-statistical-ranking
description: Use when comparing multiple classifier variants (e.g. combinations of metric sets and learning algorithms) evaluated under cross-validation, and you need a statistically defensible selection of the performer rather than eyeballing mean F-measures.

name: frontend-form-selection-handling
description: Use when a user-facing metabolomics submission form must translate checkbox/selection input (core sample types plus additional metadata attributes) into a structured template file for local completion.

name: ft-icr-ms-pairwise-mass-difference-matching
description: Decision support for building ab initio biochemical transformation networks from FT-ICR MS peak tables that already have assigned molecular formulas; triggered when you need putative biotic/abiotic edges (e.g., CH2, N2 gains/losses) per sample.

name: ft-icr-ms-peak-count-summarization-per-sample
description: Use when a filtered FT-ICR MS peak table with assigned molecular formulas has been produced (e.g., by MetaboDirect's data pre-processing step) and you need per-sample counts and assignment-error diagnostics to validate data quality.

name: ft-icr-ms-peak-filtering-by-mz-error-and-isotopes
description: Use when input is a post-formula-assignment FT-ICR MS peak abundance + molecular formula table (e.g. Report.csv) that must be cleaned by m/z range, 13C isotopic peaks, 0.5 ppm formula error, and minimum-sample thresholds before downstream analysis.

name: ft-icr-transient-averaging
description: Use when direct infusion FT-ICR-MS data arrives as multiple transient acquisitions per SIM window per sample and must be averaged before frequency-domain processing.

name: ft-icr-transient-reconstruction
description: Use when you have raw low-resolution FT-ICR transients (e.g., 64k-point MALDI FT-ICR MSI or SCMS acquisitions) and need high-resolution, high-SNR spectra without the acquisition time of full 1M-point transients.

name: ft-spectral-transformation-and-peak-centroid-extraction
description: Use when you need to convert time-domain FT-ICR transients into mass spectra and extract peak intensity lists at defined m/z centroids to quantitatively compare reconstruction methods (deep-learning, linear subspace, standard FT) on MSI data.

name: fticr-ms-normalization-method-selection
description: Use when a direct-injection FT-ICR MS peak abundance table must be normalized before MetaboDirect analysis and the choice of normalization method (e.g., median vs z score) should be data-driven rather than arbitrary.

name: fticr-ms-van-krevelen-visualization
description: Use when you have a filtered FT-ICR MS peak abundance table with assigned molecular formulas plus sample-group metadata, and you need visual overview plots (Van Krevelen, class composition, thermodynamic indices, group overlaps) per group.

name: full-scan-base-peak-identification
description: Use when quantifying how many RegFilter-scheduled precursor-list ions that DDA failed to fragment were nevertheless the highest-intensity (base peak) ions in full-scan MS1, from MZmine feature tables.

name: fully-connected-encoder-with-layernorm-dropout
description: Use when raw one-dimensional mass spectrometry vectors (e.g. spectrum_dim 12000/9900/15000 after 0.1 Da binning and TIC normalization) must be compressed to a dense global embedding before multi-channel convolutional re-encoding.

name: fully-connected-module-design
description: Use when extending a graph neural network (e.g., SigmaCCS-style ECC layers) with tabular molecular features — fingerprints, descriptors, molecule types, instrument type — to improve generalizability of CCS predictions.

name: functional-annotation-of-omics-components
description: Use when you have an ICA-derived metagene (sk vector) of ranked gene weights from cancer omics data and need to identify enriched biological terms or pathways to interpret the component.

name: functional-group-smarts-matching
description: Use when you have recommended SMILES structures (e.g. from Spec2Mol spectra-to-molecule translation) plus ground-truth test structures and need to check scaffold/functional-group presence via RDKit HasSubstructMatch.

name: functional-group-threshold-filtering
description: Use when a large enumerated functional-group list (e.g., 204 groups on a cathinone template) must be screened before combinatorial enumeration so that highly challenging-to-synthesize derivative compounds are excluded from the synthetic database.

name: functional-level-network-representation
description: Use when reconstructing the functional (reactions-based) level of an organism's metabolism from KEGG KGML pathway files, for local pathway-by-pathway or global similarity comparison.

name: functional-pathway-tree-visualization
description: Use when you have a HUMAnN functional-profile matrix (KEGG pathways) plus a LEfSe biomarker result contrasting cohorts (e.g., HMP vs MetaHIT) and need a compact, publication-quality circular tree highlighting enriched pathways.

name: fused-dataset-csv-construction
description: Use when two or more normalized platform-specific metabolomics tables covering the same biological samples must be combined into one dataset with expanded metabolome coverage, or when choosing among concatenative, mid-level, and multi-block fusion strategies.

name: fuzzy-c-means-expression-clustering
description: Use when a multi-time-point gene or KO abundance table needs to be partitioned into expression-pattern clusters (e.g., cardiomyocyte differentiation stages day 0–30) so that pattern-specified GRSA can identify enriched GO/KEGG terms per cluster.

name: fwhm-based-peak-matching
description: Use when per-sample EIC peak lists (retention time, intensity, FWHM) from MRM data must be grouped across samples, and RT drift estimates from chromatogram similarity are available to drive alignment.

name: g-aligner-graph-based-feature-alignment
description: Use when aligning untargeted LC-MS feature lists (m/z, RT, area from each run) across multiple runs where nonlinear RT drifts and naive nearest-neighbor matching degrade accuracy, and when improving OpenMS, MZmine2, or XCMS alignment results.

name: gaba-edited-spectrum-integration
description: Use when you have edited GABA difference spectra simulated at multiple spatial resolutions (e.g. 21×21, 41×41, 101×101 spatial points) and need to quantify GABA signal amplitude at 3 ppm per setting to test resolution convergence.

name: gaims-benchmark-reproduction
description: Decision support for validating isotopologue deconvolution implementations: when you need to check that a new or modified deconvolution/model-ranking pipeline (e.g. moiety_modeling mimicking GAIMS) yields comparable optimization results and model rankings to a published reference.

name: galaxy-compatible-table-output-formatting
description: Use when a SECIMTools analysis step (LASSO/Elastic Net, ANOVA, etc.) must hand its per-feature results to another Galaxy tool or workflow, and the output must be a standard tabular file that any downstream tool can consume.

name: galaxy-workflow-execution
description: Use when you have direct infusion or LC-MS mass spectrometry metabolomics raw files (e.g. Thermo .RAW/.dat transients or vendor LC-MS files) and need to execute the complete published Galaxy-M pipeline in the Galaxy web UI (127.0.0.1:8080) to reproduce published results.

name: galigner-xcms-workflow-integration
description: Use when XCMS feature extraction results (csv feature lists with m/z, RT, area) must be aligned across LC-MS runs more accurately than XCMS's native method, and the gain must be benchmarked against manually annotated library analytes.

name: gam-based-batch-effect-correction
description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics feature table (raw intensities, samples × features, with QC runs and batch labels) shows drift or batch effects and outlier-containing features require robust normalization before differential abundance testing.

name: gam-based-drift-correction-on-qc-samples
description: Use when a MRMhubExperiment holds imported MRM intensity data whose QC-injected features show instrument drift over the run sequence, after normalize_by_istd() and before batch correction.

name: gam-based-robust-normalization
description: Use when an unnormalized metabolomics feature matrix (rows = compounds, columns = sample runs) contains outliers or QC/sample drift, and robust per-metabolite drift and batch-effect correction is needed before downstream DA testing.

name: gam-drift-model-fitting
description: Use when unnormalized LC-MS metabolomics intensity matrices show signal drift over injection order and/or batch effects, and QC-RLSC-style normalization is vulnerable to occasional disproportionately high/low outlier intensities.

name: gam-drift-modeling
description: Use when metabolomics intensity data (runs × compounds, log(e)-transformed, with pooled QC injections, injection order, and batch labels) shows instrument drift or QC-vs-biological-sample discrepancies that must be modeled per compound batchwise before downstream testing.

name: gam-injection-order-drift-modeling
description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics data matrix (samples × peaks) has an injection order vector but no batch label, and you must decide which frequency-domain components carry run-order (batch) drift before removal.

name: gam-model-evaluation-metrics
description: Use when a fit_gam spline has been fitted on RT ordered pairs and you need quantitative accuracy (mean absolute error, per-compound |error| ≤ 0.1 min) on held-out known metabolites before trusting downstream alignment scores.

name: gamma-distribution-concentration-sampling
description: Use when you must synthesize annotated training NMR spectra (e.g., to train a CRNN model like NMRQNet) and need realistic metabolite mixture compositions without measured ground-truth concentrations.

name: gap-filling-database-annotation
description: Use when preparing a MNXref-based gap-filling database for COMMIT community gap filling and you need to tag transport reactions with metabolite permeability to reduce their cost.

name: gap-filling-reaction-set-comparison
description: Use when consensus microbial reconstructions (e.g. Schlaeppi 24-isolate or Bulgarelli 20-isolate communities) have been gap-filled both with and without community composition, and you must quantify whether community-aware gap filling reduced added-reaction set size.

name: gas-phase-ion-protonation-state-handling
description: Use when input is a SMILES structure of a metabolite for in silico CCS prediction or IM-MS annotation, and the relevant gas-phase ion species ([M + H]+ or [M − H]−, plus multiply protonated forms) must be enumerated before conformation generation.

name: gated-gnn-bond-breakage-prediction
description: Use when you need to reconstruct or retrain the Generate stage of ICEBERG — i.e., predict which bonds in a molecular graph break under CID and enumerate candidate fragment subformulae from MAGMa ground-truth fragmentation trees.

name: gaussian-coordinate-perturbation
description: Use when generating pseudo-paired spatial transcriptome / MALDI-MSI benchmark pairs from a single source tissue — e.g. to stress-test coordinate-alignment methods (manual gross, ICP 3D, direct alignment) against realistic inter-section morphology drift.

name: gaussian-curve-fitting-similarity-scoring
description: Use when detected LC/MS chromatographic peaks must be quality-filtered by shape symmetry, e.g. peaks that look Gaussian-like versus zigzag, distorted, or asymmetric profiles after peak detection.

name: gaussian-filter-signal-smoothing
description: Use when you have raw LC-MS ROI intensity arrays (m/z + intensity columns from a mass trace) and need robust chromatographic peak segmentation: smoothing precedes edge detection, never final quantification.

name: gaussian-graphical-model-data-simulation
description: Use when evaluating a kernel or pathway-graph association test via Monte Carlo — you need synthetic correlated data whose covariance encodes a pathway graph under null or alternative hypotheses.

name: gaussian-graphical-model-network-estimation
description: Use when a metabolomics/lipidomics feature table (raw peak intensities) has two condition groups with features outnumbering samples (p >> n) and you need regularized metabolite-metabolite partial correlation networks rather than pathway enrichment.

name: gaussian-graphical-model-resampling
description: Use when estimating partial-correlation metabolite-metabolite networks under p >> n with DNEA, after BIC tuning of lambda, and before getNetworks(), to stabilize edge inclusion via resampling.

name: gaussian-kernel-bandwidth-calibration
description: Use when fitting a semi-parametric kernel machine regression g(Y)=Xβ+h(Z)+ϵ on pathway metabolite features and need a Gaussian kernel whose bandwidth is calibrated from the data.

name: gaussian-kernel-regression-agreement-fitting
description: Use when you have matched per-target log2 peak-area tables from two integration methods (e.g., an open-source R pipeline vs. vendor software such as Xcalibur) and need to quantify whether the automated tool reproduces expert manual integration.

name: gaussian-mixture-model-estimation
description: Use when fitting a calibration curve from calibration-standard injections (per-feature peak_area from a FeatureDB/mzML report) for targeted LC-MS/MS quantitation where a generic linear fit is insufficient.

name: gaussian-noise-injection-at-multiple-sigma-levels
description: Use when benchmarking the noise robustness of computed isotopologue profiles (e.g., single-tracer 13C vs multi-tracer 13C/18O glucose moiety models) and you need simulated replicate datasets at several error magnitudes before renormalization.

name: gaussian-noise-robustness-testing
description: Use when a paired microbiome-metabolome model has been trained in two configurations (full vs. annotated-subset outputs) and you must quantify whether multivariate learning confers robustness to input perturbation before comparing per-metabolite SCCs.

name: gaussian-peak-deconvolution
description: Use when an ion chromatogram's targeted compound peak is coeluted with other peaks (e.g., isomers sharing a transition with close RTs) and per-peak abundances must be separated rather than summed.

name: gaussian-peak-modeling
description: Use when a 1D MS signal (e.g., XIC or ATD extracted from an MZA/HDF5 file via mzapy) contains overlapping or noise-affected peaks that need Gaussian model fitting, peak-parameter estimation, or SNR-based peak quality assessment.

name: gaussian-peak-shape-fitting
description: Use when comparing feature counts from LC-MS processing tools (asari, XCMS, MZmine) and you need an objective peak-quality metric to determine whether extra features are genuinely better coverage or low-quality peaks.

name: gaussian-peak-shape-validation
description: Use when performing untargeted GC × GC–MS peak picking from raw CDF files and false-positive blobs (incomplete peak shapes, sub-threshold S/N) must be discarded before deconvolution by PARAFAC/PARAFAC2.

name: gaussian-process-meta-learning-prior-optimization
description: Use when you must project DNN-predicted retention times to a specific chromatographic method using only ~10 identified molecules with predicted-experimental RT pairs, while also getting credible intervals.

name: gaussian-process-surrogate-regression
description: Use when a sequential optimization loop needs a probabilistic surrogate fitted to small experimental data (e.g., LC gradient parameters vs. separation efficiency) to support acquisition-function-based selection of the next experiment.

name: gaussian-spatial-smoothing-of-msi-data
description: Use when raw MALDI-MSI imzML pixel spectra must be denoised prior to dimensionality reduction/segmentation, and pixel-level noise in the spectral image data needs suppression via Gaussian smoothing as part of the MSIght pre-processing pipeline.

name: gc-ci-hrms-isotope-labeling-data-visualization
description: Use when you have high-resolution GC-CI-MS autoQ integration results and need to visualize summed isotopologue distributions for a specific metabolite (e.g., Gly) across sample groups in a barplot.

name: gc-ci-hrms-isotopologue-integration
description: Use when the input is centroided GC-CI-MS data acquired with isobutane reagent gas (QqQ SIM/NS, GC-qTOF, or GC-Orbitrap mzML) from 13C stable-isotope labeling experiments and all isotopologues of derivatized metabolites need to be quantified.

name: gc-ci-ms-isotopologue-configuration-comparison
description: Use when selecting or benchmarking a GC-CI-MS platform for stable-isotope tracing, e.g. deciding between SIM-mode QqQ and full-scan high-resolution qTOF/Orbitrap for isotopologue quantification.

name: gc-ci-ms-lowresolution-isotopologue-quantification
description: Use when processing low-resolution GC-CI-MS (e.g., QqQ or SIM-mode quadrupole) mzML files for stable-isotope labeling experiments and you need per-isotopologue peak areas for a compound table, as described in the isoSCAN package.

name: gc-cims-dataframe-transformation
description: Use when you have a data frame of isotopologue integration areas from isoSCAN's autoQ and need per-sample percentage-normalized values, or must confirm the transformed frame feeds metBarPlot.

name: gc-gcms-parafac2-deconvolution
description: Use when raw GC×GC–MS data (CDF files) contains overlapping or co-eluting peaks that must be resolved into pure component spectra and elution profiles across a batch of samples, especially when elution profiles shift between samples.

name: gc-ms-deconvolution-feature-table-merging
description: Use when you have deconvoluted GC-MS feature tables from MSHub/GNPS (e.g. GNPS_GC release) from parallel acquisition modes that must be combined and filtered for reliable annotations before spatial or comparative analysis.

name: gc-ms-derivatization-reagent-benchmarking
description: Decision support for choosing between iTIC, fTIC, and mTIC sum-based normalizations in GC-MS metabolomics when derivatization reagent (MSTFA vs MTBSTFA) effects on precision need to be quantified.

name: gc-ms-endogenous-metabolite-rsd-visualization
description: Use when GC-MS metabolomics data with pooled QC samples must be compared across normalization methods (one-to-one ISTD, SERDA, SERRF, one-to-class) and summarized as a median-RSD bar/figure with a CSV table.

name: gc-ms-metabolite-concentration-table-processing
description: Use when you have raw GC/MS metabolomics chromatograms (e.

name: gc-ms-metabolite-data-retrieval
description: Use when starting from a public metabolomics resource entry (e.g., PMR) with GC-MS metabolite accumulation tables plus mutation/condition metadata, and the goal is a metadata-linked MOG project for interactive exploratory analysis.

name: gc-ms-missing-compound-recovery
description: Use when processing GC-EI MS untargeted metabolomics data with eRah and the aligned compound table has missing entries for compounds found in most samples; run after alignComp() and before identification/export.

name: gc-ms-qc-precision-assessment
description: Use when GC-MS peak-area tables from plasma samples plus QC injections must be precision-scored as RSD — e.g. benchmarking derivatization agents (PCF/MTBSTFA/MSTFA), internal-standard schemes, or how QC sampling frequency affects normalization error.

name: gc-ms-quantitative-table-matching
description: Use when processing raw GC–TOF-MS chromatograms (e.g. NetCDF/CDF) from multi-sample untargeted metabolomics and you need per-compound integrated areas that can be validated against peak-picking tables (XCMS centWave ppm=15, peakwidth=c(1,5); MetAlign) for the same compounds.

name: gc-ms-spectral-alignment-across-samples
description: Use when deconvolved GC/MS metabolomics data from multiple samples must be cross-sample aligned to build a compound × sample quantification table, especially when retention indices are unavailable and RT drift plus spectral similarity suffice.

name: gc-ms-spectral-deconvolution
description: Use when raw GC-MS/EI datasets (e.g. a deposited MassIVE dataset such as MSV000084033) contain co-eluting compound fragments that must be separated into deconvoluted spectra before molecular networking or repository-scale analysis.

name: gc-ms-two-dimensional-map-processing
description: Use when the input is GC–MS data (e.g. aroma odor or human breath) represented as a two-dimensional MS map of m/z vs retention time, and the goal is to identify multivariate chemo-/biomarker features at very low concentration levels (down to parts per billion) without peak picking.

name: gcf-centroid-model-construction
description: Use when you have antiSMASH-predicted BGC GenBank files for hundreds of thousands of genomes and need scalable, non-pairwise GCF models (instead of O(n²) pairwise clustering) that can later map new or fragmented BGCs.

name: gcf-genome-based-class-annotation
description: Use when candidate BGCs have been detected by antiSMASH and grouped into GCFs by BiG-SCAPE, and genome-based class labels per GCF are needed for downstream chemical class matching (e.g. NPClassScore in NPLinker).

name: gcf-membership-ranking-and-novelty-assessment
description: Use when one or a few new antiSMASH-annotated BGCs must be assigned to existing GCF models quickly, or when judging whether a BGC is novel versus a member of known biosynthetic families.

name: gcf-molecular-family-link-scoring
description: Use when NPLinker GCF–molecular-family candidate links must be ranked so that PoDP-validated links rise above all-links background, and raw Metcalf scores alone are unreliable because of GCF/MF size dependence.

name: gcf-presence-absence-matrix-construction
description: Use when antiSMASH GenBank BGC predictions across many strains must be converted into a binary GCF presence/absence table (e.g., 363 strains x GCFs) as input for metabologenomic correlation against MS-detected ions.

name: gcf-prevalence-distribution-analysis-across-genomes
description: Use when you have antiSMASH-detected BGCs across many genomes and BiG-SCAPE GCF assignments, and you need to quantify which GCFs are conserved vs rare to prioritize biosynthetic diversity.

name: gcf-versus-phylogeny-discrepancy-analysis
description: Use when BiG-SCAPE GCF clustering may have missed related BGCs — e.g., fragmented assemblies or merged adjacent clusters split a known family — and an evolutionary, query-gene-anchored view is needed to recover them.

name: gcims-delayed-batch-modification
description: Use when all samples in a GCIMSDataset must be transformed identically in batch (e.g. cutting trailing drift-time points) and you want the modification applied lazily via DelayedOperation rather than editing each sample's matrix one by one.

name: gcms-chromatogram-baseline-removal
description: Use when raw GC/MS chromatogram files (e.g. CDF/NetCDF) contain baseline drift and noise that must be removed before compound deconvolution, alignment, or metabolite identification in an untargeted metabolomics pipeline.

name: gcms-chromatogram-noise-filtering
description: Use when raw GC/MS chromatogram files (e.g. NetCDF/CDF from a spike-in or metabolomics experiment) must be baseline-corrected and noise-filtered as the first stage of an eRah untargeted metabolomics pipeline.

name: gcms-component-area-aggregation
description: Use when you have an Agilent Unknowns Analysis (or similar) GC-MS library-hit table and need to pull aggregated component areas for a defined chemical list across all samples in a batch.

name: gcms-data-processing
description: Use when raw GC–MS (or LC–MS) chromatogram data must be converted into marker-feature identifications for metabolomics/chemometrics, and conventional peak picking (e.g. XCMS) is producing false peak detections or unreliable signal acquisition.

name: gcms-deconvolution-feature-scoring
description: Use when a MSHub/GNPS GC-MS deconvolution feature/quantification table must be scored for deconvolution confidence and filtered to discard chimeric or irreproducible compound fragmentation patterns before annotation.

name: gcms-ei-spectral-edge-analysis
description: Use when you have EI molecular networking output (edges table and annotated spectra/consensus spectra) from deconvoluted GC-MS data and need to test whether cosine-similarity edges reflect structural similarity based on chemical class, despite the molecular ion often being absent from EI spectra.

name: gcms-example-dataset-processing
description: Use when the input is raw two-dimensional chromatography–MS data (GC–MS or LC–MS, m/z vs retention time) and the goal is untargeted marker-feature identification while avoiding peak-picking false detections.

name: gcms-hit-table-filtering
description: Use when the input is a raw aggregated GC-MS library-hit CSV from peak detection software (e.g. Agilent Unknowns Analysis) and you must decide which tentative compound identifications to keep before aggregating peak areas across samples.

name: gcms-internal-standard-dose-gradient-analysis
description: Use when a multiclass metabolomic peak table contains internal standards spiked at known levels (e.g. 6/12/25/50 µL classes) and you need to select or validate a NOREVA processing workflow by whether it preserves the true dose gradient.

name: gcms-library-hit-table-parsing
description: Use when a GC-MS vendor output (e.g. Agilent Unknowns Analysis hit table) must be converted into a uafR-compatible data frame with exact column names for downstream spreadOut()/mzExacto() processing.

name: gcms-metabolomics-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when starting from a raw GC/MS metabolomics intensity matrix (e.g., 3226 features x 57 samples) whose columns are sample groups, and a variance-stabilized, centered feature table is needed before metabolite identification or biomarker discovery.

name: gcms-molecular-networking
description: Use when clustering co-eluted EI GC-MS compounds into similarity networks: deconvoluted spectra exist but molecular ions/precursor masses are absent, so edges must come from cosine similarity of fragmentation spectra.

name: gcms-peak-detection-parameter-optimization
description: Use when preprocessing GC-MS metabolomics data (mzML/mzData/NetCDF) with WiPP and needing to select centWave or matchedFilter peak-detection parameters objectively instead of by hand-tuning.

name: gcms-preprocessing-results-analysis
description: Use when you have per-algorithm classified peak-detection tables from a WiPP run and need to measure whether the merged/integrated high-quality peak set exceeds each individual algorithm's high-quality yield.

name: gcms-preprocessing-workflow-configuration
description: Use when preprocessing large-scale GC-MS metabolomics datasets (mzML/mzData/NetCDF) where peak detection parameters for embedded algorithms (centWave, matchedFilter) must be optimised without manual tuning.

name: gcms-quantification-table-generation
description: Use when a GC/MS untargeted metabolomics analysis needs to be finalized into a compound-by-sample quantification table after deconvolution, alignment, and identification, and the workflow must integrate names, match factors, and areas.

name: gcms-query-spectrum-preparation
description: Use when measured EI-MS query spectra (e.g., compounds absent from the NIST 2017 library) must be loaded into FastEI and identified by embedding-based nearest-neighbor search against IN_SILICO_LIBRARY.db.

name: gcms-spectral-deconvolution
description: Use when raw GC/MS chromatograms (netCDF or mzXML) contain co-eluting compounds with extensive EI fragmentation and you need pure compound spectra and integrated areas per sample rather than fragment-ion peak picking.

name: gcms-spectral-library-matching
description: Use when deconvoluted GC-MS spectra are available in a .mgf file (e.g. from GNPS-MSHub auto-deconvolution) and compound identifications are needed via reference-library spectral matching.

name: gcms-spectral-match-filtering
description: Use when top-hit GC-MS spectral match annotations (with cosine similarity and balance score columns) from MSHub/GNPS auto-deconvolution need FDR-controlled filtering, e.g. reproducing Figure 1m,n-style threshold benchmarks.

name: gcms-spectral-matching-analyte-annotation
description: Use when a processed GC-MS peak table (e.g. WiPP's merged high-quality peak set from mzML/mzData/NetCDF inputs) needs analyte identification by spectral matching, and identifications must be benchmarked against analytes confirmed in an original published study.

name: gcms-standardized-compound-area-analysis
description: Use when uafR has produced an aggregated GC-MS compound-area table from Agilent Unknowns Analysis output and the goal is a between-treatment NMDS significance analysis that must match a published result.

name: gcxgc-2dtic-baseline-correction
description: Use when a raw GCxGC chromatogram imported from a NetCDF file as a 2D-TIC matrix shows a steadily increasing baseline that must be removed before multivariate analysis or peak alignment.

name: gcxgc-2dtic-folding
description: Use when raw GCxGC-MS data is provided as a NetCDF/CDF file (e.g. 08GB.cdf from MTBLS) and must be imported and folded into a 2D-TIC object before smoothing, baseline correction, or MPCA.

name: gcxgc-2dtic-object-construction
description: Use when multiple raw GC×GC-MS chromatograms (e.g. NetCDF acquisitions from different samples such as MTBLS09 and MTBLS08) must be combined into one R object before multivariate analysis.

name: gcxgc-2dtic-preprocessing
description: Use when raw GCxGC-MS chromatograms (NetCDF files) contain baseline drift, noise, or retention-time shifts that must be reduced before multivariate analysis such as MPCA of 2D-TIC data.

name: gcxgc-4d-array-data-processing
description: Use when raw GC×GC–TOFMS CDF files must be imported as a 4D array and untargeted peak picking (ROI/blob detection) is needed before deconvolution, alignment, or annotation.

name: gcxgc-4d-tensor-reconstruction
description: Use when a folder of raw CDF/NetCDF files from comprehensive two-dimensional GC–MS must be folded into a structured 4D array (samples × m/z × retention time 1 × retention time 2) as the entry point of the GcDUO workflow.

name: gcxgc-chromatogram-smoothing
description: Use when a 2D-TIC GC×GC chromatogram (e.g., imported from a NetCDF file and baseline-corrected with baseline_corr) still contains noise and must be denoised prior to 2D-COW peak alignment or multivariate analysis.

name: gcxgc-metabolomics-multivariate-analysis
description: Use when GCxGC-MS 2D-TIC chromatograms (e.g., NetCDF imports or bundled MTBLS579 data) have been preprocessed and you need unsupervised multivariate analysis scores/loadings to distinguish sample groups.

name: gcxgc-ms-data-import-and-4d-array-reconstruction
description: Use when raw GC×GC–MS data are supplied as CDF (NetCDF) files and the analysis goal requires building a 4D data array in R with GcDUO as the first step of an untargeted peak-picking/deconvolution pipeline.

name: gcxgc-ms-spectra-cosine-similarity-annotation
description: Use when Module III (deconvolution) has produced consensus spectra ($cor_spectra in DuoResults) for GC × GC–TOFMS features and you need compound identifications from an in-house MSP library before PARAFAC2 data integration.

name: gcxgc-peak-area-quantification-consensus-processing
description: Use when you have GC×GC–MS CDF raw files processed through GcDUO peak picking/annotation and need per-feature peak areas and intensities per sample for quantification or software benchmarking.

name: gcxgc-raw-data-import-cdf
description: Use when raw GC×GC–TOFMS data are stored as CDF/netCDF files and must be folded into a 4D samples × m/z × RT1 × RT2 array before peak picking; requires a known modulation time (e.g., 2.5 s) and acquired m/z range (e.g., 35–440).

name: gcxgc-roi-peak-picking-signal-to-noise-thresholding
description: Use when raw GC×GC–TOFMS CDF files have been imported into a GcDuoObject 4D array and detected features must be extracted sample-by-sample before deconvolution, annotation, or peak-area comparison.

name: gcxgc-roi-selection-inverse-watershed
description: Use when processing raw GC×GC–MS (e.g., CDF files) to detect untargeted features: you need to segment chromatographic matrices into ROIs and filter false-positive peaks by S/N and Gaussian shape before deconvolution.

name: gcxgc-roi-subtensor-extraction
description: Use when processing raw GC × GC–MS CDF files with GcDUO and you need per-peak sub-tensors (from a 4D samples × m/z × RT1 × RT2 array) to feed blind PARAFAC deconvolution.

name: gcxgc-tofms-metabolite-identity-crossmatching
description: Use when two significant metabolite feature lists from GCxGC-TOFMS plasma profiling (named metabolites plus unknown peaks annotated by mass spectrum and retention index) must be matched across studies to classify overlap, direction concordance, and condition-unique features.

name: gcxgc-tofms-peak-area-quantification
description: Use when comparing an open-source GC×GC–MS peak-processing pipeline against a commercial gold standard on serial-dilution QC data, or when validating that extracted peak areas are linearly proportional to analyte concentration.

name: gcxgc-tofms-peak-exclusion-criteria-auditing
description: Use when auditing which GCxGC-TOFMS peaks were excluded from a metabolomics dataset and why — e.g. reconciling an initial peak count (691) against the final metabolite count (195) with per-criterion thresholds.

name: gdb-style-drug-likeness-screening
description: Use when a large enumerated SMILES set of substituted derivatives must be reduced to a drug-like, synthetically tractable candidate database before spectrum prediction, using explicit rule-based filters.

name: gee-association-modeling-for-family-data
description: Use when testing whether latent omics factors (e.g., MOFA factors from buccal DNA methylation and urine metabolomics) or cluster memberships relate to behavioral scores in family/twin data requiring relatedness-adjusted regression.

name: geena2-peak-alignment-10ppm
description: Use when raw single-probe SCMS peak lists exported from Thermo Xcalibur (m/z, retention time, intensity per cell) must be converted into a cell-by-peak matrix with consistent m/z bins before ML phenotype classification.

name: gelatin-standard-concentration-assignment
description: Decision support for quantifying LA-ICP-MS elemental images against gelatin calibration standards: when raw isotope signal maps (55Mn, 56Fe, 63Cu, 66Zn) plus a standard of known concentrations must be converted to μg/g concentration images.

name: genbank-accession-organism-lookup
description: Use when you have PoDP project JSON entries pairing user-created genome labels with NCBI GenBank accession numbers or JGI Genome IDs and need the scientific species/organism names for downstream linking, filtering, or analysis.

name: genbank-coordinate-extraction
description: Use when a candidate BGC of known function is being prepared for deposition into MIBiG and the accession-request stage requires product name(s) plus BGC sequence coordinates, preferentially derived from an NCBI Genbank accession.

name: genbank-feature-parsing
description: Use when the input is antiSMASH GenBank (.gbk) output of a PKS/NRPS BGC (e.g. MIBiG entries) and the goal is to load cluster features into RAIChU for module prediction and visualisation.

name: gender-difference-significant-feature-selection
description: Use when an untargeted LC/MS feature table (m/z, retention time, intensity per sample) has two biological groups, e.g. male vs female urine, and a significant feature list plus full reference list must be derived before mummichog pathway/network analysis.

name: gene-cluster-abundance-benchmarking
description: Use when validating a metagenomic gene-cluster abundance tool against simulated libraries with known abundances, or when choosing a redundancy-filtering cutoff and read-mapping mode for BiG-MAP.

name: gene-cluster-differential-abundance-testing
description: Use when you have RPKM-normalized gene cluster abundance or expression tables plus sample grouping metadata and need to identify MGCs/GCFs significantly differentially abundant or expressed between conditions.

name: gene-cluster-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when you have antiSMASH or gutSMASH cluster predictions from a reference genome collection and paired shotgun metagenomic/metatranscriptomic reads, and need to test which gene clusters differ in abundance or expression between phenotypes (e.g. Crohn's disease vs healthy).

name: gene-cluster-expression-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when BiG-MAP RPKM abundance/expression tables for grouped samples (e.g. healthy vs. caries, CD vs. UC) have been differentially tested and you need a heatmap of significant gene cluster profiles.

name: gene-cluster-family-clustering
description: Use when antiSMASH v4 GenBank BGC predictions (optionally with MIBiG reference BGCs) need to be grouped into gene cluster families or clans, or when a BGC sequence similarity network must be built and clustered.

name: gene-cluster-family-grouping
description: Use when SMASH-predicted gene clusters (antiSMASH or gutSMASH GenBank output folders for a genome collection) contain redundant clusters that must be dereplicated and grouped into GCFs before metagenomic/metatranscriptomic read mapping.

name: gene-cluster-family-method-benchmarking
description: Use when choosing or validating the alignment backend for BiG-SCAPE's DSS index on a growing BGC dataset — e.g. to confirm that Pfam profile-HMM alignment (hmmalign) matches Muscle/MAFFT-based GCF calling while being faster as input BGC count increases.

name: gene-cluster-family-model-distance-querying
description: Use when pre-computed BiG-SLiCE GCF models exist (e.g., the T=900 run yielding 29,955 GCFs) and you need to quantify how close each model is to curated MIBiG v2.0 reference BGCs, or to validate feature-space separation.

name: gene-cluster-family-querying-against-centroid-models
description: Use when you have one or more new antiSMASH-annotated BGCs and an existing BiG-SLiCE SQLite3 result database, and need to rank-match the new BGCs against precomputed GCF models instead of re-clustering.

name: gene-cluster-redundancy-clustering
description: Use when you have antiSMASH/gutSMASH output directories for many genomes and need a nonredundant gene-cluster reference set (and optional GCF assignments) before mapping metagenomic/metatranscriptomic reads.

name: gene-coexpression-network-estimation
description: Use when you need topology-based pathway enrichment on gene expression data (e.g. GEO breast cancer or TCGA prostate cancer matrices) and must first estimate weighted, directed adjacency matrices per pathway from curated interaction databases.

name: gene-disease-association-annotation
description: Use when a Cytoscape network of genes/proteins (e.g. built with a stringApp Disease Query such as query='Rett syndrome', cutoff=0.4, limit=20) needs disease-gene and compound-target annotations added from CyTargetLinker XGMML linksets.

name: gene-disease-association-intersection
description: Use when a list of differentially expressed genes (e.g. sex-consistent F1_M1 / F-1_M-1 states from an 8-week exercise time point) must be prioritized against curated gene-disease associations such as Open Targets.

name: gene-disease-association-mapping
description: Use when the goal is to confirm which genes are shared across a defined panel of intestine-related diseases, or to map specific genes (e.g. STK11, SMAD4/BMPR1A) to named syndromes using GutUDB's disease-gene association data.

name: gene-enzyme-annotation-retrieval
description: Use when a MetENP analysis has already produced significant metabolites mapped to KEGG compound IDs and you need the downstream reaction, gene, and enzyme annotations for those metabolites.

name: gene-essentiality-annotation
description: Use when you have a list of essential genes from single-gene deletion analysis of a metabolic reconstruction and want to map approved drugs onto those targets to prioritize repurposing hypotheses.

name: gene-expression-dataset-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to compare pathway enrichment methods on human disease gene expression datasets by measuring how highly each method ranks known target disease pathways.

name: gene-expression-dataset-loading
description: Reference for retrieving the exact expression datasets (type 2 diabetes from the Whitehead deposit and airway epithelia from AGED) needed to reproduce PLAGE pathway-activity analyses.

name: gene-expression-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when a gene expression or omics matrix (e.g. heatmap_test.csv) with a matching sample-annotation file (e.g. group_info.csv) must be rendered as a clustered, group-annotated heatmap figure.

name: gene-expression-heritability-estimation
description: Use when standardizing cross-species (rat-to-human) differential expression effect sizes against GTEx v8 per-gene, per-tissue expression variability and its genetic component via h_SNP^2.

name: gene-expression-signal-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking pathway enrichment methods on simulated signals: you have a real expression matrix, need ground-truth dysregulated gene groups of varying sizes, and must measure empirical power and type-I error across replicates.

name: gene-expression-standardization-and-matrix-construction
description: Use when expression data must be standardized per gene and pathway-restricted matrices built as input to an SVD-based pathway activity analysis such as PLAGE, or when reproducing metagene results.
tools: PLAGE (Pathway Level Analysis of Gene Expression)

name: gene-gene-interaction-curation
description: Use when performing topology-based pathway enrichment and no pre-built pathway network is available: dataset gene lists (e.g. 2784 breast cancer genes) need gene-gene edges harvested from KEGG/Reactome and assembled into adjacency matrices.

name: gene-identifier-mapping
description: Use when feature names from CCLE omics layers (e.g. RNA splicing Ensemble IDs) must be converted to common gene names or Bigg IDs before matching against Recon3D reactions or SynLethDB SL gene pairs.

name: gene-identifier-mapping
description: Use when pathway node identifiers retrieved from databases like KEGG or Reactome must be matched to the identifiers of your input gene set (e.g. ENTREZID to UNIPROT) before assembling edge lists for topology-based pathway analysis.

name: gene-identifier-standardization
description: Use when raw CCLE/DepMap omics feature matrices mix identifier namespaces (e.g. RNA splicing ensemble IDs, BiggIDs) and feature names must be mapped to common gene names before cross-omics ML training or network output.

name: gene-lipid-class-association
description: Use when a lipid feature abundance matrix plus phenotype file must be linked to lipid classes (via genes) and analysed for differential lipid class, total chain length and hydrocarbon-chain saturation.

name: gene-metabolite-annotation-mapping
description: Use when an XCMS-style feature intensity matrix must be tied to gene function: exact-mass matching of m/z features to HMDB metabolites, removing unannotated features, and testing DAM enrichment among gene-associated metabolite sets.

name: gene-metabolite-association-mining
description: Use when a pseudotargeted metabolomics dataset over a mutant/genotype panel needs to be mined for metabolite-mutation associations, e.g. ranking mutants by module eigenmetabolite to find genes controlling a specific metabolite like glucoraphanin.

name: gene-metabolite-colocalization-analysis
description: Use when haCCA-integrated Data objects (aligned MALDI-MSI features on 10X Visium spots) are available and the goal is to find genes whose spatial pattern co-localizes with specific metabolites.

name: gene-metabolite-enrichment-testing
description: Use when you have a patient-vs-control metabolite z-score matrix and need to convert DAMs into per-gene enrichment scores via gene-metabolite associations before ranking candidate genes.

name: gene-metabolite-ora-vs-espia-comparison
description: Use when you have both gene and metabolite feature tables mapped to KEGG pathway nodes and need to compare topology-aware impact analysis (eSPIA) against ORA, or to reproduce SMART 2.0's IOPA breast cancer result (eSPIA: 2 significant pathways vs ORA: 51 at pFDR < 0.05).

name: gene-metabolite-pathway-membership-mapping
description: Use when an analyte list contains both genes/proteins and metabolites and you need their pathway memberships consolidated from multiple pathway databases before enrichment or clustering analysis.

name: gene-metabolite-pearson-correlation
description: Use when integrating spatial transcriptome and MALDI-MSI data at spot resolution and you need to select gene–metabolite feature pairs whose Pearson correlation on anchor spot pairs will drive CCA-based feature enrichment before ICP alignment.

name: gene-ontology-chord-plot-visualization
description: Use when the input is a GO analysis result table (e.g. chord_example.csv) linking genes to GO terms and the goal is a circos-style chord diagram rendered without programming, via GraphBio's chord plot module.

name: gene-ontology-term-overlap-scoring
description: Use when evaluating whether an integrative clustering (e.g. KLIC vs COCA) better exploits the biological information in multiple omic datasets, by scoring cluster coherence through shared Gene Ontology terms across BP, MF and CC ontologies.

name: gene-pathway-network-extension
description: Use when you have a list of differentially expressed genes (e.g., selected by an absolute log2 fold change cutoff such as > 1) and want to annotate/link them to curated pathway resources (WikiPathways) as a network extension in Cytoscape.

name: gene-prioritization-benchmarking
description: Use when a gene prioritization method must be quantitatively validated against known causative genes — via permutation tests, percentile-of-causative-gene metrics, or ablations of the underlying interaction network.

name: gene-protein-reaction-association-assembly
description: Use when building a draft genome-scale metabolic model from annotated amino-acid FASTA (Type 1) or DIAMOND BLASTp hits (Type 2) and reactions must carry gene-reaction provenance from KEGG annotation.

name: gene-protein-reaction-coverage-assessment
description: Use when a genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. an SBML file such as BioModels MODEL2007210001) must be quality-controlled before or after publication, and GPR coverage, metabolite annotation, or an overall MEMOTE score are needed as evidence of community-standard compliance.

name: gene-set-annotation-construction-from-degenes
description: Use when GWAS summary statistics must be stratified by SNP-heritability enrichment for a gene set (e.g., tissue DE genes from exercise training) and you need to convert a gene list into a partitioned/binary LDSC annotation.

name: gene-set-collection-curation
description: Use when reproducing pathway-level gene-expression analyses (PLAGE, GSEA) that depend on a predefined gene-set collection whose memberships must match a historical KEGG/Biocarta version.

name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when ionomics data (e.g. ICP-MS ion concentrations for haploid S. cerevisiae deletion mutants) have been clustered and you need to identify statistically significant clusters and associated biological processes via GO Slim annotation and GO terms enrichment.

name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when interpreting ICA metagenes (sk vectors) from cancer omics data: you have a ranked gene list per component and need GO/KEGG functional enrichment to name the biological signal.

name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when testing whether a defined gene set (e.g., exercise-responsive DEGs) is enriched for trait/tissue associations in TWAS/S-PrediXcan results across many tissue-by-trait cells, with partial pooling and direction-of-effect testing.

name: gene-set-enrichment-score-ranking
description: Use when the goal is to rank predefined gene-sets (e.g., KEGG or Biocarta pathways) by enrichment score in a two-group comparison and assess their significance by random label permutation.

name: gene-set-overlap-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when two gene sets from independent studies (e.g. metabolite-interacting genes and GWAS trait genes) must be statistically compared for over-represented overlap via a hypergeometric upper-tail test.

name: gene-set-submatrix-decomposition
description: Use when raw gene-expression data must be translated into per-sample, per-pathway activity levels using predefined KEGG/Biocarta gene sets before group comparisons such as diabetic vs. non-diabetic or smoker vs. non-smoker.
tools: PLAGE (Pathway Level Analysis of Gene Expression)

name: gene-set-tissue-specificity-quantification
description: Use when a multi-tissue differential expression study (e.g., MoTrPAC PASS1B rat endurance training, 15 tissues) needs a quantitative measure of DE gene-set overlap and tissue-specificity across tissues.

name: gene-to-reaction-association-mapping
description: Use when experimental protein/gene lists (e.g. host–virus PPI data) must be linked to enzymatic reactions in a constraint-based model whose SBML defines GPR rules, in order to annotate or filter reactions by their catalysing genes.

name: generalized-likelihood-ratio-model-comparison
description: Use when normalizing metabolomics run-order data with pooled QC injections and you must decide, per compound (and batch), whether QC-based drift fits are statistically consistent with biological-sample fits before trusting QC-driven normalization.

name: generative-molecule-diversity-metrics
description: Use when evaluating a diffusion-generated molecular structure set (e.g. 10,000 molecules from DiffSpectra/DMT reverse denoising on QM9S spectra) to detect mode collapse and verify the diversity/accuracy trade-off under temperature sweeps or conditioning ablations.

description: Use when running genome-wide association studies on UK Biobank NMR biomarker concentrations (e.

name: genetic-correlation-matrix-psd-projection
description: Use when a multilevel/Bayesian model needs a correlation matrix among trait- or tissue-level effects (e.g. G_SNP built from GCTA-GRM output) that is empirically not positive semi-definite and would break the sampler.

name: genome-assembly-gene-prediction
description: Use when starting from filtered raw metagenomic or whole-genome shotgun reads (FASTQ) and you need assembled scaftigs plus gene predictions as input for operon or promoter-level prediction.

name: genome-class-to-pathway-cooccurrence-counting
description: Use when you have a set of MIBiG BGCs with SMILES and (sub)classes and need genome-class-to-NPClassifier-pathway match frequencies for scoring BGC-metabolite links.

name: genome-metabolome-link-record-validation
description: Use when auditing archived PoDP project JSONs (Zenodo dumps of the 70 paired datasets) to confirm that genome–metabolome and BGC–MS/MS link records are structurally complete and that totals match published counts (114 BGC–MS/MS links).

name: genome-metabolome-pairwise-co-occurrence-analysis
description: Use when a paired genome-metabolome dataset exists (BGCs called per strain plus MS/MS-derived Mass2Motifs per strain) and the goal is to statistically link sub-clusters or sub-cluster clans (SCCs) to molecular substructures.

name: genome-metadata-counting
description: Use when the task requires reproducing or auditing aggregate counts (projects, MS samples, genomes/metagenomes/MAGs, method counts, BGC–MS/MS links) from PoDP Zenodo JSON archives, or verifying reported PoDP corpus statistics.

name: genome-mining-bgc-detection
description: Use when starting from a raw genome assembly (e.g. a WGS contig such as QZWF01000007) and the goal is to enumerate putative BGC regions and obtain Pfam/subPfam tokenised genes ready for sub-cluster motif querying.

name: genome-pipeline-execution
description: Use when raw bacterial genome sequences (e.g. FASTA) must be converted into predicted BGC regions with product-class and activity annotations, and no Pfam domain TSV is already available.

name: genome-scale-bgc-tool-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing BGC prediction tool performance (counts and prediction-set overlap) across a large genome collection, e.g. reproducing DeepBGC 10926 vs antiSMASH 13865 vs ClusterFinder 62491 on 3376 RefSeq genomes.

name: genome-scale-community-model-construction
description: Use when the input is a set of genome-scale single-organism SBML metabolic models (e.g. AGORA members) and the goal is a reusable, member-attributable community metabolic model for FBA, exchange-metabolite, or cross-feeding analysis.

name: genome-scale-metabolic-model-constraint-editing
description: Use when a human GEM (e.g. RECON3D in SBML/XML) must be updated with flux information from gut microbiota models — i.e. host reactions containing metabolites present in the microbiota model need their lower bounds rewritten.

name: genome-scale-metabolic-model-curation
description: Use when a workflow requires a simulation-ready GEM (e.g., for FVA-based shadow-price extraction) and only a raw published model file such as iJO1366.mat or Yeast-GEM.mat is available.

name: genome-scale-metabolic-model-data-handling
description: Use when a pipeline needs curated GEM files (e.g., .mat models) converted to irreversible, optimized versions as the basis for computing reaction-level shadow prices used as MPI-prediction features.

name: genome-scale-metabolic-model-media-perturbation
description: Use when a constraint-based model pipeline (e.g., SARTRE shadow-price features) must be shown to be insensitive to medium composition — alternate carbon sources or limiting carbon/nitrogen/phosphorus uptake rates — relative to a glucose base model.

name: genome-scale-metabolic-model-quality-assessment
description: Use when a newly constructed or revised genome-scale metabolic model (SBML, e.g. from BioModels) must be checked against community standards such as MEMOTE before publication or reuse in downstream analyses.

name: genome-scale-metabolic-model-shadow-price-analysis
description: Use when predicting metabolite-protein interactions from constraint-based models and you need physiologically grounded metabolite features (shadow prices) instead of, or alongside, chemical fingerprints.

name: genome-scale-metabolic-model-simulation
description: Use when a human GEM (RECON3D or similar, SBML/cobrapy-loadable) must be simulated with the metabolite pool adjusted to gut microbiota fluxes, or when the α-weighted trade-off between host bounds and microbial in-/out-fluxes must be swept.

name: genome-scale-metabolic-model-simulation
description: Use when an SBML-encoded genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. BioModels MODEL2007210001, iHsaEC21, iAB-AMØ-1410) must be loaded, FBA-simulated for host/virus biomass objectives, or FVA-refined so reaction reversibility and flux ranges are determined.

name: genome-scale-metabolic-network-reconstruction
description: Use when annotated protein FASTA, BLASTp/DIAMOND output, or a draft SBML model is available for a bacterial genome and a COBRApy-compatible genome-scale metabolic model (SBML GENRE) is needed for FBA, gene essentiality, or flux sampling analyses.

name: genome-scale-metabolic-network-reconstruction
description: Use when starting from isolate genome assemblies/annotations (e.g., 432 At-SPHERE Arabidopsis root isolate genomes) and you need draft genome-scale metabolic models (SBML) from automated pipelines, or multiple draft reconstructions that must be harmonized, gap-filled, or merged into a consensus.

name: genome-scale-metabolic-reaction-mapping
description: Use when top ML predictor features (e.g. genes from CNV, methylation, transcriptomics, proteomics models) must be anchored to specific reactions in a genome-scale metabolic network like Recon3D to test whether predictors sit near the metabolite they predict.

name: genome-scale-model-curation-and-irreversibility-conversion
description: Use when a constraint-based modeling pipeline needs reaction-level dual values (shadow prices) and requires the model to be converted to an irreversible form with biomass constrained to 90% of its optimum before optimization.

name: genome-set-retrieval-from-ncbi
description: Use when building the raw-genome foundation for a pan-biosynthetic analysis: you need complete (or WGS draft) genomes for a taxon from NCBI, with outgroup genomes, before BGC prediction and GCF clustering.

name: genome-structure-class-pairing-frequency-analysis
description: Use when you need to bridge genome-mining BGC class ontologies (antiSMASH/MIBiG) with structure-based chemical ontologies (NPClassifier/ClassyFire) to derive empirical class-matching score tables for filtering BGC–MS/MS links.

name: genome-wide-association-study-analysis
description: Use when testing whether ukbnmr's removal of technical variation from NMR biomarker data increases genetic association power, or when counting genome-wide significant loci (P < 5e-8) for a metabolomics trait.

name: genomic-proximity-gene-mapping
description: Use when you have a set of sentinel variants (e.g. mQTLs or cis-pQTLs with GRCh37 coordinates) and need to prioritize or validate causal gene assignments based on genomic proximity, LD-overlap, or cis-eQTL targeting.

name: genomic-range-overlap-annotation
description: Use when annotating sentinel (and LD-proxied) variants with positional candidate genes from variant-level data — nearest-gene extraction, LD-range overlap, and biotype filtering around molecular QTL loci.

name: genomic-source-metadata-tabulation
description: Use when you have PoDP project JSON records containing (meta)genome entries with GenBank accession numbers or JGI Genome IDs and need organism names attached per project/genome label for downstream enrichment or filtering.

name: genomic-taxonomy-aggregation
description: Use when you have a BiG-SLiCE output SQLite database plus genome taxonomy annotations (e.g., GTDB 04-RS89) and need per-taxon BGC class proportions or GCF diversity summaries.

name: genomic-variant-qc-validation
description: Use when a raw ClinVar VCF must be cleaned, normalized, and QC-validated to a fixed variant count and clinical-significance composition before it is used as a benchmark for annotation-tool concordance (ANNOVAR, SnpEff, VEP).

name: genomics-metabolomics-link-scoring
