description: Use when a graph (e.g., Pearson-correlation Metabolite CN with |r|>=0.3, p<=0.01) must be converted into fixed-length node/hyperlink signal representations for deep-learning classification, such as predicting pathway presence from metabolomics networks.

name: graph-based-feature-matching
description: Use when two or more independently processed same-method nontargeted LC-MS feature tables (Feature Metadata + Feature Abundances) must be merged into one dataset and features matched across all of them.

name: graph-based-msms-spectral-representation
description: Use when you need to convert an MGF-format MS/MS spectral collection into fragmentation graphs (graphs of m/z differences) so that subsequent frequent-subgraph mining can extract exact fragmentation patterns shared across spectra.

name: graph-based-multidimensional-assignment-matching
description: Use when aligning detected LC–MS features (m/z, RT, area) across multiple runs with nonlinear retention time drift, and accuracy of consensus feature/analyte matching matters more than speed.

name: graph-community-clustering
description: Use when you have peak tables from SAND-decomposed 1D NMR spectra across many samples (e.g. 50 simulated or experimental spectra) and need to group co-occurring peaks into compound-level clusters for automated annotation.

name: graph-community-detection
description: Use when two ICA decompositions of different transcriptomic datasets yield metagene sets that must be matched to assess component reproducibility via RBH graph matching and community metrics.

name: graph-diffusion-decoder-implementation
description: Use when a task requires generating molecular graphs conditioned on a structural input (spectrum embedding or Morgan fingerprint) while preserving a known heavy-atom formula — i.e., rebuilding, training, or finetuning the DiffMS discrete graph-diffusion decoder.

name: graph-diffusion-prioritization
description: Decision support for ranking matched KEGG compound candidates per LC-MS peak when a filtered candidate set exists and network context (KEGG, FELLA or RClass) can break ties among chemically plausible matches.

name: graph-diffusion-score-computation
description: Use when after matching LC-MS peaks to KEGG and filtering candidates, you need a network-context score that propagates evidence from candidate compounds across a graph to prioritize the top three KEGG compounds per peak.

name: graph-diffusion-scoring
description: Use when annotating LC-MS peak lists that have already been mass-matched to KEGG (with the resulting false positives reduced by cluster-based filtering), and a network-context prioritized candidate ranking is needed rather than a plain mass-delta list.

name: graph-distance-normalization-by-diameter
description: Use when computing distance-based scores over atoms of a known compound's 2D molecular graph (e.g. for ModiFinder's Average-distance evaluation) and you need distances comparable across molecules of different sizes.

name: graph-edge-weight-normalization
description: Use when a STRING functional linkage graph or other directed weighted interaction network must be converted into a symmetric weighted adjacency/edge list before label propagation of per-gene metabolomic enrichment scores.

name: graph-embedding-pooling
description: Use when you need to visualize whether a graph neural network's learned molecular representations cluster by compound superclass, or to diagnose per-class spectral prediction quality from per-compound cosine similarity scores.

name: graph-isomorphism-search-confirmation
description: Use when a fingerprint/LSH prefilter yields candidate structures and you must verify actual subgraph isomorphism before reporting substructure search results.

name: graph-laplacian-computation
description: Use when a pathway is represented as a 0/1 symmetric adjacency matrix and you need the regularized normalized Laplacian (D + τI)^(-1/2) L (D + τI)^(-1/2), τ = 1, for kernel regression.

name: graph-laplacian-pseudoinverse-embedding
description: Use when two tandem MS spectra (e.g., MassBank MGF entries) must be aligned via a pair-specific fragment similarity built from all pairwise m/z differences within a tolerance, especially when compounds differ by multiple structural changes.

name: graph-laplacian-regularization
description: Use when testing phenotype–pathway associations on metabolite features mapped onto a sparse or disconnected pathway graph (e.g. KEGG pathways), where ignoring topography or using the unregularized normalized Laplacian loses testing power.

name: graph-layout-visualization
description: Use when a reconstructed structural-level metabolic network (pathways as nodes, edges between pathways sharing at least one non-ubiquitous compound) needs to be rendered as an image for qualitative topology comparison between organisms.

name: graph-modularity-optimization
description: Use when a full-connectivity metabolite similarity network (all pairwise edges retained, no cosine threshold) must be partitioned into communities without a predefined cluster count, as in MCN's community-detection step.

name: graph-neighborhood-non-annotation-counting
description: Use when benchmarking an annotation-propagation method (e.g. ChemWalker vs NAP) and you need to prove that annotations reach network nodes lacking any direct neighbour with a spectral library match.

name: graph-network-assembly-and-validation
description: Use when building or sanity-checking a knowledge-driven reaction network from metabolite databases plus computational reaction prediction, e.g. to expand coverage beyond reported reaction pairs (RPs).

name: graph-neural-network-inference
description: Use when you need to score candidate enzyme–substrate reactions with a trained GNN-SOM model and check whether scores differentiate true (Known) from random pairs via a two-sided Mann-Whitney U test.

name: graph-neural-network-layer-implementation
description: Use when building or validating a GNN layer for 3D molecular point sets (xyz coordinates + atom one-hot features) where embeddings must be provably invariant to atom ordering, translation, and rotation — e.g. as an encoder for MS/MS, RT, or CCS prediction.

name: graph-neural-network-model-evaluation
description: Use when you need to train and compare multiple GNN regression models on the same train/test parquet splits and produce a per-model metrics table (R2, RMSE, MRE) to judge relative performance.

name: graph-neural-network-training
description: Use when reproducing or adapting per-fragment binary classifiers for MS/MS peak prediction where molecules are available as molecular graphs and each of the 1,000 most frequented m/z positions needs a separately trained GNN.

name: graph-neural-network-training
description: Use when building a knowledge-driven metabolic reaction network requires predicting metabolite-metabolite reaction pairs with a GNN, and when ROC/AUC evaluation of that predictor on a held-out test split is needed.

name: graph-neural-network-training
description: Use when you have a curated spectral library csv (Name, SMILES, Precursor_type, CE, Instrument_type) and must train a bond-cleavage GNN and pick architecture/depth via validation spectral_sqrt_cosine.

name: graph-neural-network-training
description: Use when predicting LC retention times for metabolite annotation from molecular structures (InChI/SMILES), especially when transferring a pre-trained model to a new chromatographic method with limited labeled data.

name: graph-parameter-perturbation-reanalysis
description: Use when existing match tables from n>2 LC-MS dataset alignment yield too few matched features under strict clustering, and you want to test relaxed diameter/clique-size settings without recomputing subalignments.

name: graph-regularization-simulation
description: Use when comparing kernel association test power under simulated pathway graphs with varied topology and incomplete knowledge, to judge whether graph regularization (τ = 1) beats unregularized Laplacian or network-agnostic tests.

name: graph-shortest-path-median-analysis
description: Use when characterizing an embedding-based molecular network: you need a single scalar metric describing how many graph edges separate the bulk of unannotated spectra from reference-library nodes, to validate that the network's structure reflects annotation coverage.

name: graph-structure-similarity-index-calculation
description: Use when two KEGG-organism metabolic networks have been reconstructed as a two-level representation (structural graph + functional reaction sets) and a quantitative pathway-by-pathway and whole-metabolism similarity comparison is required.

name: graph-subsetting-with-igraph
description: Use when a curated metabolic reaction network graph must be reduced to metabolites supported by experimental MS1 evidence (e.g. after feature-metabolite matching within 15 ppm m/z and 30% relative RT tolerance), before downstream annotation propagation.

name: graphical-legend-generation-for-biomarkers
description: Use when a GraPhlAn circular taxonomy tree highlights biomarker or background clades and a standalone legend image is needed to map annotations/colors back to clade names.

name: graphlan-circular-cladogram-rendering
description: Use when you need to visualize a phylogeny with thousands of taxa together with per-leaf or per-clade metadata (abundances, functional modules, phenotypes) as a compact circular figure.

name: graphlan-input-file-generation
description: Use when you have MetaPhlAn (v1/v2), HUMAnN, or BIOM-format (v1/v2, e.g. QIIME/mothur 16S) profiles plus optionally a LEfSe result, and need to produce GraPhlAn tree.txt and annot.txt for circular phylogenetic visualization.

name: graphlan-legend-and-annotation-configuration
description: Use when converting LEfSe/MetaPhlAn biomarker results into a GraPhlAn tree plus annotation file and you need controlled highlight levels, background clades/colors, font and clade sizing, and legend rendering.

name: graphlan-tree-annotation-and-rendering
description: Use when LEfSe biomarker results or MetaPhlAn/HUMAnN taxonomic-functional profiles must be rendered as a compact circular cladogram with highlighted sub-trees, sizes mapped to biomarker effect, and legends.

name: graphml-graph-manipulation
description: Use when you have an IIMN graphml file whose nodes are redundant ion-species features (adducts, isotopes, dimers sharing one IIN ID) and you need a collapsed molecular-node graph for downstream analysis or visualization.

name: graphml-network-annotation-with-sirius-predictions
description: Use when you have downloaded a GNPS FBMN/IIMN GraphML network and want to overlay SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID structural and formula predictions onto it for MSI level 2/3 annotation.

name: graphml-network-export
description: Use when a similarity-weighted molecular network (edge weight = spectral similarity score) has been partitioned into Louvain communities and each community must be exported as a pruned, connected GraphML subnetwork for interpretability.

name: graphml-network-export
description: Use when an NP3 MS Workflow analysis has produced pairwise ionization-variant or spectral-similarity links that must be persisted as a reproducible GraphML network for Cytoscape inspection and [M+H]+ representative-ion reporting.

name: graphml-network-export-and-cytoscape-visualization
description: Use when a motif-to-network mapping step (e.g. pyMolNetEnhancer Mass2Motifs_2_Network) has produced an annotated network that must be exported as .graphml and rendered in Cytoscape with node pie charts and edge discrete mappings.

name: graphml-network-export-and-visualization
description: Use when you have a spin system feature similarity matrix from MADByTE and need to produce network graphs (full association, similarity, hybrid) for clustering inspection, dereplication validation, or bioactivity overlay.

name: graphml-network-export-for-cytoscape
description: Use when MS2DeepScore-predicted similarities between tandem mass spectra (including cross-ionization-mode pairs) must be turned into a unified molecular network .graphml file for Cytoscape visualization and cluster inspection.

name: graphml-network-file-generation
description: Use when a Mass2Motif-mapped molecular network (classical GNPS or feature-based) and a chemical class annotation dataframe must be merged into one .graphml file for Cytoscape visualization.

name: graphml-network-simplification
description: Use when a precomputed GNPS molecular network is available as a .graphml file (e.g. pnordicum_ms2_gnps.graphml) and you need clean connected components, cliques or pairs to interpret with fragmentation patterns.

name: graphml-network-visualization
description: Use when a MADByTE run has produced a chemical similarity network from spin-system feature comparisons and you need to inspect compound groupings, identify shared substructures, or spot false-positive connections.

name: gray-code-precursor-mass-encoding
description: Use when reconstructing or reimplementing GLEAMS spectrum featurization: you need to build the exact 3010-feature input vector (Gray-coded precursor mass/m/z, one-hot charge, 2449 fragment bins, 500 reference-spectrum similarities) before applying the pretrained GLEAMS embedding network.

name: gray-vs-white-matter-lipid-biology-interpretation
description: Use when MSI pixels have been assigned brain-region labels (e.g. Waxholm Space atlas) and a lipid annotation table exists, and the goal is to identify which lipid species distinguish white-matter structures (corpus callosum, corticofugal pathway) from gray-matter structures.

name: grayscale-feature-image-conversion
description: Use when serial 2D MSI sections need a single-channel anatomically contrasting image (e.g., to register against T2*-weighted MRI atlas slices) from a high-dimensional hyperspectral data cube or UMAP embedding.

name: grayscale-scatter-plot-rendering
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS feature tables (MS1/MS2 m/z pairs with intensities, e.g. from MS-DIAL output) must be converted into fixed-size grayscale images for image-based deep learning such as CNN bioactivity prediction.

name: greedy-non-overlapping-hypothesis-transfer
description: Use when LC-MS mass traces (with apex positions and FWHM extents) must be aggregated into non-overlapping, isotope-grouped features, and the grouping must resolve competing hypotheses that share traces.

name: greedy-peak-match-selection
description: Use when scoring a modified query spectrum against an unmodified library spectrum where the precursor mass difference implies fragment peak shifts and each peak must be counted at most once in the match.

name: greedy-transitive-spectral-alignment
description: Use when a molecular network component contains multiple MS/MS spectra and you need to compute which peaks correspond across all of them, beyond pairwise matching.

name: greenwood-confidence-interval-computation
description: Use when comparing survival or cumulative-event curves between risk groups (e.g., MetaboRS tertiles) and you need CI bands to judge whether group curves are statistically separated.

name: grid-search-gradient-descent-optimization
description: Use when aligning MRM/SRM chromatograms across samples: EIC peak tables show retention time shifts between acquisitions, and per-sample/per-transition-group drift values must be estimated to enable peak alignment and automatic EIC grouping.

name: grid-search-weight-region-verification
description: Use when tuning or validating the A, B, C weight parameters of the metabCombiner similarity-scoring function for LC-HRMS feature alignment, and you have a training set of shared identified compounds with known true pairings.

name: grins-nus-reconstruction
description: Use when a 3D NMR dataset is non-uniformly sampled (e.g. an NUScon schedule such as 8.8% sampling) and the unmeasured hypercomplex points must be reconstructed before spectral inspection in NMRViewJ.

name: ground-truth-correspondence-matching
description: Use when benchmarking feature-correspondence or RT-alignment tools and you need ground truth: simulated perturbed datasets with known feature mappings let you compute precision/recall per shift magnitude.

name: ground-truth-feature-matching
description: Use when you have an LC-MS feature-detection result on simulated data whose ground truth is known (e.g. from MSSimulator) and you need recall/precision/F-score per noise setting.

name: ground-truth-feature-matching
description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics feature table (e.g. from UmetaFlow/OpenMS on Thermo Q Exactive mzML data) must be validated against a known list of targeted ground-truth features to report detection, quantification and marker-selection performance.

name: ground-truth-formula-matching
description: Use when you have SIRIUS/ZODIAC annotation results plus a ground-truth formula file (spectral library search + manual validation) and need per-dataset accuracy, incorrect-annotation rates, or error-reduction factors.

name: ground-truth-peak-labeling
description: Use when building labeled synthetic benchmark data for signal-vs-noise classification on mass spectrometry raw data, especially when no gold-standard peak-level annotation of real timsTOF data is available.

name: ground-truth-peak-matching
description: Use when evaluating chromatographic peak quality metrics on LC/MS data and no curated reference peak set exists, so a consensus-based ground truth must be derived from multiple independent peak-detection tools before computing TP/Recall/Precision/F-Score.

name: ground-truth-preservation-for-imputation-error-assessment
description: Use when complete source datasets are available and a controlled imputation benchmark is needed — create MCAR-masked replicates at fixed missingness fractions, retaining the complete matrix as the error-assessment reference.

name: ground-truth-reference-peak-extraction
description: Use when preparing a user-defined ground-truth reference feature list (peaks, walls, backgrounds) for training a PeakBot CNN model on LC-HRMS profile-mode chromatograms, and you need accurate RT/mz/borders/mz-deviation values matched to real chromatographic peaks.

name: ground-truth-referenced-spectral-similarity-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking MS/MS denoising or spectral-matching methods on dilution-series data where clean high-concentration reference spectra of the same compounds serve as ground truth.

name: ground-truth-validation-against-podp-links
description: Use when NPOmix (or another co-occurrence classifier) has produced candidate GCF–MS/MS spectrum links and you need a quantified precision estimate against PoDP validated gene–metabolite links as ground truth.

name: group-comparison-statistics
description: Use when comparing a continuous measurement (e.g., metabolite concentration in µg/g tissue) between two small, independent biological subgroups (e.g., phosphoAKT1-high/MYC-low n=14 vs. phosphoAKT1-low/MYC-high n=5) without assuming normality.

name: group-difference-simulation
description: Use when a benchmark dataset with controlled two-group structure and realistic inter-variable covariance is needed to evaluate imputation methods on metabolomics data (e.g., MNAR left-censored missingness tests).

name: group-difference-visualization
description: Use when KEGG pathway abundance profiles must be compared between genotype groups (e.g. 3xTg vs WT fecal metagenomes) to identify and visualize enriched vs depleted pathways with effect direction and significance.

name: group-label-informed-metabolomics-statistics
description: Use when comparing missing-value imputation methods on metabolomics data with known two-group labels, and you need label-informed metrics (t-test p-value correlation, PLS-Procrustes SSE) rather than only reconstruction error.

name: group-labeled-supervised-feature-screening
description: Use when the input is a metabolite intensity matrix (samples × metabolites, e.g., 234 samples × 113 metabolites) with sample-group labels and the goal is to select the subset of metabolites predictive of the phenotype.

name: group-pair-discrimination-modeling
description: Use when a metabolomics feature table with two or more phenotype groups needs binary discrimination models per group pair (e.g. CRC vs polyp vs healthy controls) using pre-selected metabolite features.

name: grouped-bar-abundance-visualization
description: Use when you have a superclass-by-organism relative abundance table from ConCISE consensus annotations and need a grouped bar chart to visually compare chemical-class composition across exudate source organisms.

name: grouped-barchart-reproduction-from-fraction-tables
description: Use when per-dataset fraction values for several adduct classes (Na+, K+, 13C, DHB or CHCA matrix adducts) must be assembled across multiple MALDI-MSI datasets and rendered as a grouped bar chart to compare platforms.

name: grouped-boxplot-visualization-of-diversity-metrics
description: Use when FT-ICR MS peak tables with assigned molecular formulas have per-sample abundance-based diversity (Shannon, Gini-Simpson, Chao1) and functional diversity (Rao's quadratic entropy) values that must be compared across user-defined sample groups.

name: grouped-composition-plot-generation
description: Use when you have a filtered peak/formula table from FT-ICR MS with per-sample abundances, assigned molecular formulas, and metadata grouping variables, and you need an overview of molecular composition and thermodynamic descriptors per group.

name: grouped-cross-validation-of-image-classifiers
description: Use when validating image classifiers on expert-tagged ion images drawn from multiple datasets, where images from the same source dataset must stay in a single fold to avoid leakage.

name: grouped-metabolite-data-serialization
description: Use when a metabolomics matrix contains samples from multiple experimental conditions (e.g., 6C and 16C) and separate per-condition covariance/Jacobian analysis is planned with MInfer.

name: grouping-accuracy-evaluation-against-standard-mixture
description: Decision support for validating that an LC/MS feature-grouping or compound-spectrum extraction step correctly co-assigns features from known standards before trusting it on unlabeled samples.

name: growth-curve-visualization
description: Use when a multi-generation reaction-network expansion must be characterized by exponential compound/reaction growth per generation and by runtime benchmarks that identify when expansion becomes computationally intractable.

name: growth-yield-constraint-maintenance-in-sampling
description: Use when sampling the feasible flux region of a constraint-based model where biomass output must be non-zero, so sampled FFD solutions reflect proliferating cells rather than zero-growth artifacts.

name: gsmn-quality-metrics-reporting
description: Use when a newly reconstructed GSMN (e.g. from AuReMe draft reconstruction plus orthology mapping) needs its global size metrics tallied and compared with published networks to demonstrate completeness before curation.

name: gtex-expression-covariate-residualization
description: Use when you need human-expression-variability-normalized effect sizes for cross-species DE comparisons, e.g. dividing exercise log2FCs by GTEx per-gene, per-tissue standard deviations.

name: gut-metabolomics-differential-analysis
description: Use when a GNPS-derived intensity matrix plus molecular-family annotation table must be compared between two sample groups (case vs control, e.g. >30 vs <10 plant-based foods/week) to find significantly changing metabolite sets at p<=0.05.

name: gut-microbial-biotransformation-prediction
description: Use when a curated parent-chemical list (SMILES/structures, ~20,000 exposome chemicals) needs microbiome-mediated metabolite prediction and per-module counts as part of a biotransformation metabolite database build.

name: gut-microbiota-human-gem-integration
description: Use when a human GEM (e.g. RECON3D) loaded in cobrapy must be updated with in- and out-fluxes aggregated from one or more user-provided gut microbiota GEMs, to study the pool of metabolites exchanged between gut microbes and human cells.

name: gut-microbiota-human-metabolic-interaction-modeling
description: Use when a human GEM (e.g. RECON3D in cobrapy/SBML form) must be modified to reflect metabolite in- and out-fluxes from selected gut microbes, or when the α-weighted trade-off between host-scaled bounds and microbiota flux-scaled bounds must be swept and recorded.

name: gwas-catalog-network-gene-set-construction
description: Use when a metabolomics-only (standalone, unpaired) dataset needs to be compared against GWAS evidence: you must extract disease- or trait-anchored gene sets (e.g. cardiovascular disease, kidney/urine) from the GWAS Catalog network before running a hypergeometric enrichment test.

name: gwas-locus-ld-block-annotation
description: Use when you need to annotate GWAS/mQTL sentinel loci with candidate causal genes via LD-block annotation, or when benchmarking phenotype-agnostic annotation tools like SNiPA against a reference causal gene set.

name: gwas-network-construction
description: Use when constructing genomic gene-set networks from GWAS Catalog studies, or when extracting disease/trait-specific GWAS subnetworks to serve as genomic gene sets for hypergeometric over-representation testing against metabolic gene sets.

name: gwas-network-node-classification
description: Use when you have metGWAS 1.0 intersection gene sets from a hypergeometric comparison of metabolic and genomic gene sets and need to trace whether each gene is a primary keyword node or a first-neighbour node in the GWAS subnetwork.

name: gwas-summary-statistics-harmonization
description: Use when estimating causal relationships between a metabolite (from mGWAS summary statistics) and a phenotype (from comparable GWAS data) via two-sample Mendelian randomization, e.g. testing L-Cystathionine against type 2 diabetes.

name: gwas-summary-statistics-processing
description: Use when published GWAS summary statistics for multiple traits must be harmonized into LDSC-format annotations (e.g., SNPs within 100kb of sex-consistent 8-week DE genes per tissue) to estimate heritability enrichment per trait x tissue.

name: gzip-tsv-parsing
description: Use when a large .tsv.gz table is distributed via a Zenodo deposit (e.g. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.5607264) and must be loaded for row-level counting, deduplication, or validation of reported dataset totals.

name: halogen-element-formula-expansion
description: Use when MS/MS spectra may contain halogen-containing metabolites (F, Cl, Br, I) and the default FSA CHONSP reference list of 928,369 formulas is too narrow to rank the correct candidate formula.

name: halogen-isotope-pattern-recognition
description: Use when MS/MS isotope ratios suggest halogens (e.g. chlorine M+2 patterns) or when default MAGMa candidate retrieval limited to C,H,N,O,P,S returns no plausible candidates for a challenge peak mass.

name: halogenated-compound-database-retrieval
description: Use when a CASMI-style MS/MS challenge has a precursor elemental composition containing halogens (F, Cl, Br) and the default CHNOPS-only PubChem candidate database would miss the correct structure.

name: harmonic-mean-pvalue-aggregation
description: Use when a gene-set or enrichment analysis yields multiple correlated subtest p-values (e.g. Bonferroni-adjusted fgsea() results per trait×tissue pair) that must be combined into one FWER-controlled test statistic.

name: harrell-c-statistic-survival-discrimination
description: Use when comparing the predictive ability of two or more risk scores for a censored time-to-event endpoint (e.g. 5- and 10-year all-cause mortality) and rank discrimination (C-statistic) is the required performance measure.

name: hash-block-truncation
description: Use when generating or validating a SPLASH identifier for a mass spectrum and the fourth (hash) block must be computed from the canonical ion:intensity representation, or when checking an existing SPLASH's hash block.

name: hash-table-bisection-lookup-optimization
description: Use when implementing a large-scale MS2 spectral matching routine (e.g., matching measured peaks to millions of theoretical lipid fragment m/z values within a ppm tolerance) and naive pairwise comparison is too slow.

name: hazard-ratio-confidence-interval-extraction
description: Use when reproducing or extending the biomarker-outcome association table (e.g. Table 3 of the Deelen et al. metabolic mortality profile): each of 14 NMR biomarkers (e.g. GlycA, PUFA/FA) must yield an HR, 95% CI, and P per cause-of-death endpoint.

name: hcc-cirrhosis-differential-abundance-analysis
description: Use when a final high-quality peak table from WiPP's result integration step on the HCC vs cirrhosis plasma GC-MS dataset is available and the goal is to identify features significantly different between the two conditions.

name: hcd-fragmentation-pattern-modeling
description: Use when building or verifying an in-silico lipid MS/MS reference library, or when reproducing the rule-based fragmentation spectra behind the CalicoLipids library deposited under MetaboLights MTBLS3097.

name: hdbscan-density-clustering-of-msi-pixels
description: Use when UMAP-embedded MALDI MSI pixels (e.g., from imzML data) must be grouped into spectrally coherent clusters without a predefined cluster count — e.g., for automated matrix/off-tissue pixel detection, tissue segmentation, or flagging sample outliers in multi-sample datasets.

name: hdbscan-unsupervised-clustering-of-spectral-data
description: Use when you have pixel spectra from registered MALDI MSI data (optionally masked to a cell-type region such as Ly6G+ neutrophils) and need to discover the number of molecularly distinct clusters without pre-specifying k.

name: hdf5-binary-spectra-serialization
description: Use when building a repository-scale corpus of raw MS/MS spectra (e.g. from mzML/mzXML experiments in MassIVE GNPS) that must be stored compactly and streamed efficiently for neural network training.

name: hdf5-chemdb-record-access
description: Use when you need to query ChemDistiller's pre-compiled compound databases in HDF5 (*.h5) format for candidate compounds matching an MS1 precursor m/z within a ppm tolerance, rather than rebuilding formula/fragment predictions from scratch.

name: hdf5-jagged-array-storage-design
description: Use when converting multidimensional MS data (LC-MS, LC-IM-MS with DIA/alternative activation) from vendor raw formats or mzML into a language-agnostic binary structure so spectra can be read in Python or R without vendor libraries.

name: hdf5-large-scale-graph-serialization
description: Decision support for persisting tens of millions of MS/MS spectra or nearest-neighbor graph structures (nodes, edges, similarity scores) when flat text or MGF files become impractical.

name: hdf5-mass-spectrometry-data-loading
description: Use when raw MSI data has been exported from SCiLS lab as imzML and must be converted to HDF5 for deep learning analysis, or when a trained model requires loading labeled spectral matrices (normal/tumor) with tens of thousands of m/z variables.

name: hdf5-model-loading
description: Use when a task requires inspecting, reconstructing, or serving NPClassifier's pretrained Pathway/Superclass/Class networks and the models must first be fetched and loaded from HDF5 files.

name: hdf5-ms-spectra-access
description: Use when a workflow needs programmatic access to raw LC-MS/LC-IM-MS spectra (e.g., XIC extraction, mobility plots, ML feature engineering) and vendor raw-file libraries are unavailable, Windows-bound, or too slow to iterate against.

name: hdf5-msi-data-loading
description: Use when raw MSI data is in imzML format exported from SCiLS lab and must be converted/loaded into HDF5 (via Python h5py) for pixel-wise classification or benchmarking on withheld test spectra.

name: hdf5-mza-file-access
description: Use when raw MS/IMS data has been converted to MZA (HDF5) and you need programmatic access to spectra, metadata headers, or ion mobility arrival-time arrays from Python or R.

name: hdf5-prediction-results-analysis
description: Use when NMR2Struct inference (nmr_infer or nmr_infer_single_spectrum) has produced an hdf5 predictions file and you need to compute exact-match accuracy, e.g. benchmarking the 106 experimental spectra against the 69.6% simulated baseline.

name: hdf5-spectra-storage
description: Use when raw LC/LC-IM-MS vendor files (.d, .raw, mzML) must be converted to a vendor-neutral format readable with generic HDF5 libraries (h5py, rhdf5) for downstream analysis or ML feature engineering.

name: hdf5-spectra-subset-storage
description: Use when a mined or filtered collection of tandem mass spectra (e.g. hundreds of millions of peak lists from .mzML files) must be persisted in a compact, deep-learning-ready binary format with per-spectrum LC–MS/MS metadata such as instrument type.

name: hdf5-spectral-data-loading
description: Use when the input is a GeMS or DreaMS Zenodo HDF5 deposit of MS/MS spectra (e.g., the GeMS-A10 subset for pre-training analyses) and spectra plus metadata must be read into PyTorch/numpy pipelines.

name: hdf5-spectral-dataset-serialization
description: Use when you need to store or exchange large mined MS/MS collections (millions of tandem mass spectra with LC–MS/MS metadata) in a compact binary format optimized for deep-learning training or downstream clustering/deduplication.

name: hdf5-spectrometry-table-io
description: Use when an analysis pipeline must pass large high-dimensional MS peak or feature tables between DEIMoS stages (thresholding, peak detection, alignment, CCS calibration) and persistent HDF5 intermediates/finals are needed.

name: hdf5-spectrum-array-access
description: Use when raw MS data has been converted to .mza format and a script must read individual spectra (m/z, intensity, IM arrival time, retention time) directly from the HDF5 structure in Python or R.

name: he-msi-affine-image-registration
description: Use when raw imzML MSI data and a matching high-resolution H&E image must be spatially aligned (affine plus B-spline refinement) before overlaying ion images on tissue histology.

name: heatmap-relevance-matrix-visualization
description: Use when a trained TransExION model has scored a query-reference MS/MS spectrum pair and you must explain WHICH product-ion links drove the similarity, e.g. to trace an oxygen (+15.99 Da) or CH2 (-14.02 Da) modification between analogues.

name: heavy-atom-count-stratified-model-evaluation
description: Use when a structure-generation model (e.g., a transformer producing SMILES) has been run over a test set and you need to quantify exact-match accuracy both overall and per molecular size class (heavy-atom count) to detect size-dependent degradation.

name: heavy-atom-formula-constrained-generation
description: Use when generating candidate molecular structures from a tandem mass spectrum where the chemical formula (heavy-atom composition) is already known or inferred (e.g., via SIRIUS or MIST), and atom counts must be preserved exactly in every generated candidate.

name: heavy-atom-skeleton-extraction
description: Use when you have a molecular structure (e.g. SDF/MolBlock from a spectral library entry such as NIST20) and need the heavy-atom-only graph as input to combinatorial bond-breaking or fragmentation-DAG generation.

name: held-out-classification-performance-evaluation
description: Use when a labeled categorical class label (e.g. UCI wine quality ratings) must be predicted on unseen samples and you need train/test-disjoint accuracy and F1 for a tuned pre-processing + feature-selection + estimator pipeline.

name: held-out-lipid-species-validation-splitting
description: Use when judging whether a trained lipid MS2 annotation model learned transferable fragmentation patterns — i.e., testing on spectra of lipid species completely held out from training rather than re-scoring training or random validation spectra.

name: henderson-hasselbalch-pka-shift-computation
description: Use when simulating 1H NMR spectra at a target pH different from the standard pH0 = 7.4 and you need per-peak or per-cluster ppm shifts derived from δL, δHL and HMDB 5.0 pKa values.

name: hepatocellular-carcinoma-early-recurrence-prediction
description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking HCC early-recurrence classifiers from aligned LC-MS feature intensities, and when testing whether aligned MS features outperform peptide- or protein-level classifiers.

name: hereditary-polyposis-syndrome-gene-annotation
description: Use when a gene-disease mapping for the nine main intestine-related diseases (colon cancer, colorectal cancer, bleeding of the colon, rectal cancer, constipation, diarrhea, ileus, inflammatory bowel disease, small intestine cancer) must be annotated with etiologic syndrome-level exemplars.

name: heterogeneity-assessment-i2
description: Use when reproducing or conducting a classical meta-analysis on per-study effect sizes and standard errors, and you must decide per compound between fixed-effect and random-effects (DerSimonian-Laird) models based on an I² heterogeneity threshold.

name: heterologous-recombination-rate-extraction
description: Use when a manuscript's Results section reports heterologous recombination assay percentages and event fractions per genotype that must be compiled into a machine-readable table to test whether double mutants show a synergistic elevation of heterologous recombination.

name: heuristic-string-vertex-labeling
description: Use when building MS-relevant topological features from fragment graphs where vertex ordering from a structure reader is arbitrary — i.e., when identical rooted subgraphs must map to identical feature vectors regardless of input atom indexing.

name: hgvs-nomenclature-concordance-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking variant annotation tools against a curated clinical database (e.g., ClinVar two-star variants) to measure HGVS nomenclature and coding-impact concordance, or when discordant annotations must be stratified by variant type.

name: hgvs-nomenclature-string-matching
description: Use when you must quantify how concordant HGVSc/HGVSp nomenclature strings from variant annotation tools (ANNOVAR, SnpEff, VEP) are against a curated clinical reference such as ClinVar two-star variants.

name: hgvs-nomenclature-syntax-validation
description: Use when tool-generated HGVS strings disagree with a trusted reference (e.g. ClinVar two-star variants) and you must attribute each mismatch to missing (NA) values, shifted position or variant type, or non-preferred/unknown HGVS syntax.

name: hidden-layer-activation-extraction
description: Use when you need to quantify how a trained deep classifier (e.g., DenseNet121 on raw LC-MS .npy spectra) progressively removes batch-related information layer-by-layer, and to visualise hidden-layer embeddings.

name: hidden-markov-model-bgc-detection
description: Use when benchmarking HMM-based BGC detectors against alternative predictors on genomes with known validated BGCs, or when reproducing domain-level ROC/AUC comparisons such as ClusterFinder (AUC 0.847) vs DeepBGC (AUC 0.923).

name: hidden-qc-drift-assessment
description: Use when evaluating whether a synthetic-QC drift-correction approach (e.g. mzLearn) is an adequate substitute for experimental QC samples: when you must compare normalization strategies on the same feature matrix without exposing QC samples during correction.

name: hierarchical-average-linkage-clustering
description: Use when m ≥ 3 lipidomes have been placed in a common structural space and you need a global lipidome-level relationship model (dendrogram) from their pairwise Hausdorff distances.

name: hierarchical-batch-merge-orchestration
description: Use when a large-scale metabolomics study spans multiple acquisition batches (e.g. 96-well plates across many days) with inter-batch replicate pairs embedded, and between-batch unwanted variation must be removed via RUV-III in a hierarchical merge design.

name: hierarchical-batch-merging-structure-comparison
description: Use when hRUV-normalising a large-scale metabolomics cohort (e.g. BioHEART-CT plasma batches) and you must justify the choice of negative-control metabolites or the hierarchical merging design rather than accepting defaults.

name: hierarchical-centroid-distance-linkage
description: Decision support for clustering a wide-formatted metabolomics feature table (samples as columns, metabolomics features as rows) to visualize group structure via a clustered heatmap with dendrograms.

name: hierarchical-clustering-dendrogram-construction
description: Use when you have a full pairwise similarity-index matrix (Ssim, Psim, PsimW, Csim) for a set of organisms and want to test whether index-based groupings reproduce known evolutionary or phylogenetic structure.

name: hierarchical-clustering-of-expression-matrix
description: Use when input is a gene expression matrix CSV (e.g. heatmap_test.csv) plus a sample annotation CSV (e.g. group_info.csv) and the goal is a clustered, group-annotated heatmap figure.

name: hierarchical-clustering-of-msms-spectra
description: Use when a set of curated MS/MS spectra (e.g., NIST 17 or MoNA entries) carries instrument type and collision-energy metadata and the goal is to determine whether spectral similarity is driven by acquisition conditions (HCD, QqQ, Q-TOF, IT) rather than by the underlying compounds.

name: hierarchical-clustering-visualization
description: Use when you have a line-aggregated, z-score-standardised ionome profile (e.g. ICP-MS ion concentrations across yeast knockout mutants) and need to group elements by similarity and display element-element structure as a clustered heat map.

name: hierarchical-dendrogram-height-cutting
description: Use when a metabolomics feature matrix contains highly correlated metabolites and you need a reduced set of approximately independent representative features via hierarchical clustering with a fixed tree-cut height.

name: hierarchical-latent-variable-modeling
description: Use when metabolomics feature data must be assigned to metabolites under a probabilistic model containing latent variables, and EM-based estimation of component means, variances, and mixing proportions is required.

name: hierarchical-library-querying
description: Use when benchmarking or performing lipid annotation of raw/benchmark MS2 spectra where recall@Top-20, coverage of chain compositions and C=C positional isomers, and false-positive control via relative RT rules are the goals.

name: hierarchical-linkage-clustering
description: Use when you have a scored feature-pair matrix (e.g. normalized microbe-metabolite attribution scores) and need to group each feature axis into modules with shared interaction patterns before aggregating scores at module level.

name: hierarchical-lipid-library-level-truncation
description: Use when benchmarking how much recall a deep-learning-regenerated (5th-level) lipid fragment library adds over a truncated 1st–4th-level or MS-DIAL public library, using a dataset with a known reference lipid list.

name: hierarchical-metabolite-classification-mapping
description: Use when a metabolomics input table contains raw or non-standardized metabolite names (e.g. from a Metabolomics Workbench study) and downstream class-level enrichment analysis requires RefMet main_class/sub_class/super_class annotations.

name: hierarchical-protein-sequence-clustering
description: Use when you need finer-than-domain resolution for BGC feature vectors: input is a set of protein sequences (e.g., RP15 representatives) and a curated pHMM library of core biosynthetic domains, and generic Pfam-level features are too coarse for GCF clustering.

name: hierarchical-spectral-clustering
description: Use when millions of MS/MS spectra (e.g., from mzML peak files) have already been embedded with GLEAMS and the goal is to detect spectrum clusters of spectra generated by the same peptide, as in the 669M-spectrum MassIVE-KB analysis.

name: hierarchical-unwanted-variation-normalisation
description: Use when a large-scale metabolomics matrix spans multiple 96-well plates/batches with embedded replicate structure (pooled QC, short replicates, batch replicates) and you must correct signal drift and inter-batch unwanted variation while retaining biological signal.

name: hierarchy-level-class-label-prediction
description: Use when you have a natural product SMILES string and need automated hierarchical structural classification into Pathway/Superclass/Class labels without rule-based systems like ClassyFire.

name: high-dimensional-data-reduction-visualization
description: Use when a numeric feature matrix (e.g. 150 samples x 4 morphological iris measurements, or high-dimensional omics columns) should be projected onto principal components to identify unsupervised patterns and visualize sample structure.

name: high-mass-reference-peak-frame-definition
description: Reference for full-scan AEMS spectra where a persistent high-intensity baseline obscures weak analyte peaks, and you need to define shot-event frames from high-mass anchor peaks.

name: high-resolution-lcms-mdv-correction
description: Use when LC-MS isotope-labeling FAM data (XLSX columns of isotopologue fractions) from Orbitrap or similar high-resolution analyzers need natural-abundance/impurity correction at a known nominal resolution (e.g. 140,000 or 280,000).

name: high-resolution-spectrum-mz-binning
description: Use when peak files (mzML, mzXML, or MGF) of MS/MS spectra must be vectorized for fast similarity searching or clustering, and exhaustive pairwise spectrum comparison is infeasible (e.g. millions of spectra).

name: high-similarity-pair-thresholding
description: Use when you have a precomputed GNPS molecular network (e.g. a .graphml file where vertices are MS/MS spectra and edges carry a pairwise modified-cosine similarity score) and need to isolate pairs of spectra whose similarity exceeds a chosen cutoff such as 0.9.

name: high-throughput-mass-spectrometry-workflow-execution
description: Use when timing how fast rtmsEcho processes a full 384-well MRM AEMS plate (<5 transitions) and the measured wall-clock duration must be validated against the reported <2 s benchmark.

name: high-throughput-plate-workflow-execution
description: Use when validating or benchmarking rtmsEcho's end-to-end plate-level processing throughput, e.g. timing a full 384-well plate AEMS run in full-scan precursor ion (PI) mode to check the <30 s claim.

name: highly-connected-subgraph-community-detection
description: Use when a CAMERA xsAnnotate pseudospectrum from findIsotopes/groupFWHM is suspected to mix features of co-eluting analytes and needs to be separated into distinct compound spectra.

name: highs-lp-solver-via-scipy-interface
description: Use when a spectral mixture reconstruction has been cast as a minimum cost flow LP on the mcfNMR network (compound hubs, peak nodes, capacity-limited mixture nodes, absorption sink) and must be solved to optimality to obtain flow assignments and concentration factors.

name: hilbert-transform-fid-reconstruction
description: Use when a 1D frequency-domain NMR spectrum has been partitioned into frequency bins and each bin must be converted into complex time-domain FID data for downstream time-domain modeling.

name: hilic-chromatography-rt-modeling
description: Use when you need to predict HILIC retention times for lipid species (class/subclass + fatty acid sum composition level) from an experimental HILIC-IM-MS lipid database, or to reproduce/reference RT prediction metrics like MAE 0.11 min.

name: hilic-lipid-rt-database-mapping
description: Use when HILIC-IM-MS lipidomics runs were acquired under a modified gradient or a different column length (100, 50, or 30 mm Kinetex HILIC) than the reference database, and measured lipid RTs must be rescaled to the reference RT scale for identification.

name: hilic-positive-mode-data-processing
description: Use when you have raw mzML files from HILIC positive-mode serum/plasma LC/MS studies (ideally multiple studies) and need a feature matrix suitable for downstream ML: signal detection without manual parameters, cross-study alignment, RT drift correction, and filtering to reproducible features.

name: hilic-retention-time-prediction
description: Use when annotating untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics features (e.g. HILIC plasma spectra) and you need predicted retention times to rank or exclude candidate structures from in silico or library MS/MS matches.

name: hilic-retention-time-prediction
description: Use when HILIC-IM-MS lipidomics features have measured retention times and you need to match them against predicted HILIC retention times for lipid classes that lack experimental RT entries, or when regenerating/extending the LiPydomics RT prediction models.

name: hilic-rplc-complementary-annotation
description: Use when cleaned features from complementary HILIC and RPLC LC-MS modes must be annotated against in-house metabolite databases and reduced to non-redundant MSI level 2 identifications.

name: hilic-rplc-dataset-handling
description: Use when fitting or evaluating retention time models that must be run separately per chromatographic mode (HILIC vs RPLC) on metabolomics RT training sets, or when comparing coverage statistics across modes.

name: hilic-versus-rplc-descriptor-mechanism-interpretation
description: Use when you have fitted Retip Keras RT-prediction models (HILIC and/or RPLC descriptor tables from Retip getCD() plus ChemAxon pKa) and need to rank descriptor importances to explain retention mechanisms per chromatographic mode.

name: histogram-visualization-of-sequence-features
description: Use when you have a set of protein/peptide sequences (e.g. 'Peptide sequence.fasta.txt' from the HORDB figshare deposit) and need to characterize and visualize the distribution of a per-sequence numeric feature such as amino-acid length.

name: histology-image-binarization-and-foreground-extraction
description: Use when preparing an H&E histology image (e.g. .tif/.imzML workflow inputs) for co-registration to MALDI-MSI data: you must isolate tissue from background before affine or B-spline registration.

name: histology-morphology-alignment-assessment
description: Use when spatial metabolomics cluster maps (pixels labeled by graph-based clustering) must be visually or expert-assessed against an H&E-stained tissue image to confirm that preprocessing (e.g., SMQVP noise/background removal) recovered true neuroanatomical structure.

name: hlb-distribution-statistics
description: Use when a table of IFS-predicted biotransformation half-lives exists for an exposome chemical inventory and you need population-level distribution statistics (count predicted, median HLB, fraction below 12 h) and spot-check validation.

name: hmdb-annotation-lookup-automation
description: Use when you have a list of standalone metabolite identifiers (e.g., plasma lipidome metabolites) and need their metabolite-interacting protein/gene annotations from HMDB to construct a metabolic gene set for over-representation analysis.

name: hmdb-annotation-of-pathway-metabolites
description: Use when MetaboAnalyst pathway_results.csv rows must be filtered to FDR ≤ 0.05 and each selected KEGG pathway's metabolites need resolving to HMDB IDs for downstream gene-set mapping in metGWAS 1.0.

name: hmdb-chemical-shift-parsing
description: Use when building a reference metabolite library from HMDB NMR assignments — i.e., extracting per-metabolite chemical shift peaks (ppm) and SRRM multiplet regions needed for spectral region-of-interest (ROI) matching in untargeted NMR metabolomics.

name: hmdb-compound-mass-retrieval
description: Use when an MS1 metabolite-annotation workflow needs a reference library of monoisotopic compound masses retrieved from public HMDB to match query m/z values (neutral mass plus adduct shift) against.

name: hmdb-concentration-data-parsing
description: Use when preparing MetAssimulo 2.0 simulations and you need human metabolite concentration ranges (mean and SD) drawn from HMDB 5.0 to populate the Input/parameters.txt file.

name: hmdb-data-ingestion
description: Use when a metabolomics annotation workflow needs a local, reproducible reference database of compounds plus experimental MS2 spectra built from an HMDB release, rather than querying HMDB online.

name: hmdb-metabolite-annotation-mapping
description: Use when you have a metabolite list (e.g. HMDB IDs from urine, blood, or CSF) and need per-peak values of delta_L, delta_HL, pKa and pH0 to drive Henderson-Hasselbalch peak-shift simulation.

name: hmdb-metabolite-database-querying
description: Use when you have user-defined proton NMR spectral ROIs (e.g., 0.5–4.5 ppm biofluid regions) and need to identify candidate metabolites by matching HMDB chemical shift peaks and SRRMs, avoiding over-identification in crowded spectra.

name: hmdb-protein-interaction-retrieval
description: Use when a metabolomics result has been annotated with HMDB IDs and you must build the metabolite-interacting gene set (UniProt IDs → current human gene symbols) that metGWAS 1.0 needs for its hypergeometric over-representation test.

name: hmdb-reference-database-querying
description: Use when an annotation step needs candidate metabolites with exact masses and formulas from HMDB 5.0, e.g. to feed m/z-based matching of chromatographic peaks via matchMz/Mass2MzParam.

name: hmdb-smiles-dataset-preparation
description: Use when preparing HMDB-derived SMILES datasets in the {SMILES String: [[Question, Answer], ...]} format so each metabolite yields a molecular graph and image that downstream GNN/CNN encoders can encode for MetaboliteChat training.

name: hmdb-spectral-database-matching
description: Use when untargeted 1H NMR spectra have user-defined ROIs (e.g. 0.5-4.5 ppm curve-fitted peaks) and metabolites must be identified by matching HMDB chemical shifts and SRRMs within those ROIs rather than by whole-spectrum database search.

name: hmdb-standard-id-lookup
description: Use when a metabolomics matrix's columns are raw metabolite names (e.g., plasma_breast_cancer.csv) that must be converted to standard HMDB IDs before pathway mapping or PDS-score computation in Lilikoi.

name: hmdb-structure-database-parsing
description: Use when annotating MALDI-MSI m/z features against a derivatizing matrix (e.g. FMP-10) and you need HMDB/LIPID MAPS structures filtered to compounds bearing matrix-reactive functional groups.

name: hmdb-subclass-annotation-mapping
description: Use when you have a list of metabolite annotations uniquely captured by METASPACE-ML at the 10% FDR threshold (split by animal vs. plant datasets) and need to identify which HMDB chemical taxonomy subclasses are significantly overrepresented.

name: hmdb-version-diff-prospective-evaluation
description: Use when a structure-generating model predates a database version bump (e.g., HMDB v4→v5) and you want to test whether its sampling frequency ranks newly added, previously unknown metabolites above other generated molecules.

name: hmm-based-bgc-prediction
description: Use when benchmarking a deep-learning BGC detector against a probabilistic HMM baseline, or when training ClusterFinder on Pfam TSV training data with in_cluster labels.

name: hmm-profile-database-construction
description: Use when you need to rebuild or customize the biosynthetic pHMM reference library (feature set 1) that BiG-SLiCE uses to project BGCs into Euclidean feature space, e.g. after a Pfam release update.

name: hmmer-pfam-domain-detection
description: Use when antiSMASH GenBank BGC outputs must be assigned conserved protein domains before BGC similarity networking (BiG-SCAPE), or when per-domain-type alignments are needed for GCF/clan clustering or CORASON-style analysis.

name: hnsw-approximate-nearest-neighbor-search
description: Use when searching a large library (millions) of spectral embeddings for nearest neighbors where exact search (e.g., weighted cosine similarity via faiss.IndexFlatL2) is too slow and approximate search accuracy loss is acceptable.

name: hold-out-test-set-performance-evaluation
description: Use when comparing model variants on a small, tic-normalized mass spectrometry feature matrix (e.g., spectrum_dim=12000, 2 classes) and you need unbiased per-model Accuracy/F1 plus fold-level significance testing against baselines.

name: holdout-test-set-evaluation
description: Use when running an ablation study where model variants must be trained on the full training set (no k-fold splitting) and compared on the same independent hold-out test set to quantify incremental gains from each module.

name: homologous-series-eic-visualization
description: Use when prioritized PFAS features from non-target LC/GC-HRMS mzML data must be visually verified, homologous series EICs must be extrapolated from repeating units (e.g., CF2), or coeluting adduct/in-source-fragment ions must be flagged.

name: homologous-series-matching
description: Use when processing untargeted LC-HRMS/MS data (e.g. aqueous film forming foam or environmental samples) to discover PFAS homologous series and assign per-compound confidence levels beyond a small targeted PFOA/PFOS panel.

name: homologue-annotation-count-verification
description: Use when reproducing a published homologue-series annotation run on an LC-MS peak table (mz/rt/intensity columns) and a specific annotated-peak count must be matched as validation.

name: homologue-id-annotation-of-features
description: Use when a metabolomics peak table with mz/rt/intensity columns needs homologue series grouping — e.g. recurring methylene-repeat or step-mass families — and each feature should receive a homologue_id annotation.

name: homologue-series-assignment
description: Use when two or more homologueDiscoverer detection runs (e.g. targeted mz_steps = c(44.02628) plus untargeted mz_min = 10 / mz_max = 20) share peaks and you must keep only non-overlapping series before pushing to the series database (sdb).

name: hop-plot-visualization
description: Use when you have per-compound ranked hit scores from structure annotation tools plus a known correct structure per query, and you need ROC/hop-plot curves and AUC to judge score separation quality.

name: hose-code-stereoaware-model-application
description: Use when you need predicted 1H chemical-shift distributions across a large compound library to quantify what fraction of molecules contain deshielded (>~2.5 ppm quadrant) protons, e.g., to validate NMR platform coverage.

name: host-virus-integrated-metabolic-modeling
description: Use when quantifying host cell and viral growth rates from an integrated host-pathogen genome-scale metabolic model in SBML format, or when reproducing the reported FBA growth values for SARS-CoV-2-infected epithelial and macrophage models.

name: hotelling-ellipse-clustering-assessment
description: Use when 1H NMR metabonomic datasets (e.g. FGENTCARD plasma, 506 experimental + 10 QC samples, δ 0.80–1.60 ppm) need QC clustering verified before association analysis.

name: housekeeping-peak-rt-deviation-modeling
description: Use when targeted LC–MS peak extraction shows run-to-run retention time drift and QC runs with annotated housekeeping compounds are available to model per-run RT deviations.

name: hpc-parallel-bioinformatics-workflow-execution
description: Use when a BGC-clustering pipeline must scale to ~10^6 clusters from hundreds of thousands of genomes/MAGs within days on a multi-core server, requiring a non-pairwise (near-linear) approach instead of O(n^2) pairwise comparison.

name: hpc-slurm-resource-allocation
description: Use when running a containerized Nextflow LC-MS metabolomics pipeline (MS-DIAL/MS-FLO) on an SLURM-managed HPC cluster such as HiPerGator, and local Docker execution is insufficient or reproducibility must be demonstrated cross-platform.

name: hptlc-hrms-spectral-data-parsing
description: Use when you have mzXML-format spectral files from HPTLC-HRMS experiments and need to load the raw spectra into R as the first step before extracted ion chromatogram (EIC) clustering or other downstream analysis.

name: hr-msms-spectrum-merging
description: Use when multiple HR-MS/MS spectra of the same precursor/compound exist and must be consolidated into one representative spectrum before in silico fragmentation scoring.

name: hresims-mass-error-validation
description: Use when structural annotations retrieved from the ENPKG knowledge graph (e.g., Sachem Tanimoto ≥ 0.8 similarity hits among confident annotations) must be confirmed against the accurate-mass HRESIMS data of an isolated compound before targeted isolation.

name: hrms-chemical-formula-prediction
description: Use when you already have an aligned HRMS feature table (.csv of m/z and retention-time pairs) and need formula assignments, isotopic scores, and MS/MS-based compound identification for each feature.

name: hrms-data-extraction-benchmarking
description: Use when a Shinyscreen or MSnbase-based mzML extraction/prescreening workload runs too slowly serially and you need to quantify wall-clock speedup from registering a future parallel backend.

name: hrms-data-format-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking mass spectrometry data storage formats (Parquet, mzML, mz5, mzMLb, HDF5) for conversion speed, file size, or read/query latency on Waters UNIFI (HD)MSE or mzML-derived HRMS data.

name: hrms-eic-extraction-from-mzml
description: Use when you have raw HRMS peak data in mzML plus a validated compound list (CSV) of target or suspect masses, and you need EICs, MS2 scans, and per-peak quality flags before full identification.

name: hrms-feature-clustering
description: Use when a pre-processed HRMS feature table (e.g., Agilent .csv export, features x samples) needs grouping by abundance-trend similarity — e.g., to flag candidate transformation products across a time course or isolate contaminant source fingerprints from dilution/mixing series.

name: hrms-feature-extraction-peak-picking
description: Use when raw LC-HRMS data in .mzML format must be converted into a curated chromatographic peak/feature list, e.g. for ENTACT-style mixtures of known MS-amenable chemicals or non-targeted analysis workflows.

name: hrms-feature-list-overlap-analysis
description: Use when you have feature lists (m/z–RT pairs with peak areas) from one HRMS peak-picking tool and equivalent lists from comparison tools run on identical .mzML files of known-composition standards, and need a cross-platform overlap fraction to validate extraction performance.

name: hrms-feature-table-export
description: Use when starting from vendor- or converted- HRMS raw files in .mzML format and the goal is a non-targeted feature list (m/z–retention time pairs) prior to annotation, clustering, or export to CSV.

name: hrms-feature-table-processing
description: Use when a non-target LC/GC-HRMS feature list (e.g. external_feature_list.xlsx from FeatureFinding with its mzML file) must be prioritized for PFAS by reducing matrix features using the MD/C-m/C data-reduction dimensions.

name: hrms-low-energy-mslevel-filtering
description: Use when you have HRMS data in Apache Parquet format (from arcMS/HDMSE conversion) and need to extract an EIC, TIC or MS spectrum for a specific m/z window or scan subset without loading the full file into memory.

name: hrms-target-and-suspect-screening-initialisation
description: Use when starting a Shinyscreen HRMS workflow from a YAML config plus a compound or mass list CSV, and a validated compound_table.csv with precursor masses is needed before extraction/prescreening.

name: hrmsms-spectral-data-parsing
description: Reference for preparing MetFrag2.2 input spectra: merging duplicate HR-MS/MS records, dropping spectra that contain only the precursor peak, and supplying parameter files, candidate lists and spectral data to MetFrag or its R/CLI variants.

name: hruv-normalisation-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when hRUV-normalised metabolomics data must be robustness-checked against alternative negative-control metabolite selections or alternative hierarchical batch-merging (tree) designs.

name: hsqc-carbon-shift-annotation
description: Use when peak-picked TOCSY and HSQC tables from the same sample are available and spin system sub-graphs must be converted into (1H, 13C) features for dereplication or similarity networking.

name: hsqc-spectral-input-processing
description: Use when you have measured 1H-13C HSQC spectra (normal or multiplicity edited) and want to run DeepSAT structure annotation against large chemical databases like PubChem.

name: hsqc-spectral-peak-annotation
description: Use when a trained DeepSAT model has already predicted fingerprints/classes from a 1H-13C HSQC spectrum and you need to attribute the prediction to specific spectral peaks or substructures, e.g. quercetin's A-ring HSQC peaks.

name: hsqc-spectrum-candidate-ranking
description: Use when you have a query HSQC spectrum and a set of candidate structures sampled by MMST, and need to score/rank candidates to reproduce Figure 3d-style top-1 success rates per molecular-weight bin.

name: hsqc-spectrum-input-preparation
description: Reference for formatting 1H-13C HSQC peak lists or spectral images as DeepSAT inputs, including multiplicity-edited HSQC handling, before running the pretrained multi-task CNN for structure annotation.

name: hsqc-spectrum-structure-identification
description: Use when the input consists of query 1H-13C HSQC or multiplicity-edited HSQC peak lists/spectra and the goal is top-k small-molecule identification or annotation (fingerprint cosine similarity) against large structure databases such as the Moliverse library (n=143,467).

name: html-document-rendering
description: Use when a completed maplet pipeline container (SummarizedExperiment-derived object saved as .RDS) must be turned into a shareable report documenting every executed function, its arguments, and its embedded plots/statistics tables.

name: html5-interactive-controller-implementation
description: Use when building a web-browser 3D visualization of PCoA-embedded microbial community samples where visual features (sphere size, transparency, color, visibility) must be driven interactively by metadata categories or gradient values.

name: http-api-record-caching
description: Use when you need KEGG or PubChem metabolite records repeatedly during identifier mapping, and remote HTTP fetching must be throttled by a persistent local cache to avoid timeouts from excessive calls.

name: http-download-scripting
