name: in-silico-lipid-library-search
description: Use when per-feature lipid annotations are needed for Thermo mzML lipidomics data via MS/MS spectral matching in MAVEN2 against the CalicoLipids and MS-DIAL in-silico libraries scored by hypergeometric score.

name: in-silico-mass-spectral-library-construction
description: Use when an experimental spectral library (e.g., NIST 2017 with only 0.27 million EI spectra) lacks coverage and you need large-scale predicted spectra from molecular structures to support compound identification by spectrum matching.

name: in-silico-mass-spectrum-generation
description: Use when you need to predict an MS/MS spectrum for a small molecule lacking library spectra — e.g. a metabolite, gut-microbiome compound, or any structure whose experimental CID-MS/MS spectrum is absent — and you can afford quantum-chemistry MD.

name: in-silico-metabolism-tool-orchestration
description: Use when benchmarking or comparing in silico metabolism prediction software on a common substrate set, e.g. to reproduce baseline precision/recall/Jaccard ranges before evaluating a new predictor.

name: in-silico-metabolite-annotation
description: Use when you have .mgf MS/MS spectra (e.g. [M+H]+ adducts, parent masses 100–1500 Da, ≥6 fragments) and need candidate molecular formula/structure annotations for dereplication.

name: in-silico-metabolite-biotransformation-generation
description: Use when a knowledge-driven metabolic reaction network built from KEGG, MetaCyc, and HMDB is too sparse, and putative metabolites/reaction pairs absent from those databases are needed to improve annotation coverage and topological connectivity.

name: in-silico-msms-annotation
description: Use when untargeted LC-MS/MS data in .mzML format contains features that cannot be annotated by spectral matching alone, and per-feature chemical structures, formulas, and chemical classes must be assigned and ranked.

name: in-silico-msms-fragment-prediction
description: Use when building a spectral library for adductomics or metabolomics where reference standards are unavailable and in silico MS/MS fragments are needed for each structure entry.

name: in-silico-msms-fragmentation-enumeration
description: Use when annotating a tandem MS spectrum against candidate molecules whose structures are known, and you need pre-calculated fragmentation patterns or per-candidate fragment scores to rank metabolite annotations.

name: in-silico-msms-spectral-prediction
description: Use when validating putative unknown metabolite annotations from LC-MS untargeted metabolomics (e.g., KGMN/MetDNA2 unknown peaks in NIST urine data) where no spectral library match or chemical standard exists and computational fragmentation support is needed.

name: in-silico-msms-spectral-prediction
description: Use when you need simulated MS/MS spectra for compounds lacking reference library entries, or when benchmarking fragmentation-prediction quality across NIST/MS-DIAL, MSnLib, and CASMI test sets.

name: in-silico-msms-spectrum-prediction
description: Use when a large set of candidate metabolite structures needs predicted ESI tandem mass spectra in both ionization modes so experimental MS/MS spectra can be matched to structures without experimental reference libraries.

name: in-silico-single-gene-deletion-analysis
description: Use when you have a metabolic model (e.g., a Reconstructor-generated SBML GENRE like NCGM2.S1.xml) and need to identify which genes are essential versus non-essential for biomass production.

name: in-silico-spectra-exclusion
description: Use when compiling a training set from public libraries (MoNA, GNPS, LipidMaps) while a separate annotation reference (NIST 20, LipidBlast) will score the evaluation set, to prevent overlap.

name: in-silico-spectral-library-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing two or more in-silico lipid fragmentation libraries by enumerating per-class and per-adduct library entry counts and feature annotation counts to reveal coverage gaps such as classes unique to one library.

name: in-silico-spectrum-validation
description: Use when you need to benchmark a machine-learned (e.g., NEIMS) EI-MS predictor against experimental spectra before trusting its outputs for library building or matching.

name: in-silico-structure-annotation-integration
description: Use when a GNPS molecular network (classical or feature-based) contains nodes lacking chemical class labels and you have tab-separated annotation tables with Scan and SMILES columns from library hits, NAP, or DEREPLICATOR to propagate ClassyFire taxonomy onto the network.

name: in-silico-structure-classification-evaluation
description: Use when a ConCISE consensus annotation run must be validated: compare consensus superclass/class/subclass assignments against GNPS-reported compound identities to compute true positive rates and check the >95% criterion.

name: in-silico-substructure-fragmentation
description: Use when you need to rank candidate molecules for an unknown metabolite from accurate-mass MS/MS peak lists without reference spectra, e.g. candidate lists from PubChem for CASMI-style contests or untargeted LC-MS identification.

name: in-silico-tryptic-digestion
description: Use when a simulated gold-standard LC-MS/MS dataset is needed: a known FASTA proteome must be converted into a finite, size-controlled peptide list so that identification recovery (PSMs at 1% q-value) can be measured against ground truth.

name: in-source-fragment-and-adduct-annotation
description: Use when working with untargeted, time-resolved direct-injection (e.g. DBDI-FT-ICR-MS) MS data lacking chromatographic separation, and multiple ion species from one analyte (adducts/in-source fragments) must be putatively identified.

name: in-source-fragment-annotation
description: Use when processing raw LC-MS (mzML or Bruker .d) nontargeted metabolomics data and you need to collapse features into groups annotated as isotopes, adducts, or in-source fragments to remove false-positive features.

name: in-source-fragment-correlation-clustering
description: Use when input is full-scan (MS1-only) LC-MS data in mzML/mzXML — e.g., files from GNPS/MassIVE lacking MS/MS — and the goal is to generate pseudo MS/MS spectra from in-source fragments for library-based structural annotation.

name: in-source-fragment-identification-lcms
description: Use when an LC-MS/MS metabolomics feature table contains spurious features suspected to be in-source fragments, and you need to flag ISF features and their precursor-fragment relationships from mzXML/feature-table inputs.

name: in-source-fragment-matching-to-msms
description: Use when annotating LC/HRMS peaks from MS1-only or DDA/DIA untargeted metabolomics data where MS2 fragmentation spectra are absent or sparse, and you want to leverage in-source fragments within composite spectra as surrogates for MS/MS library matches.

name: in-source-fragment-recognition
description: Use when processing untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics data (e.g. DDA/DIA/fullscan mzXML from NIST plasma-style acquisitions) where ISF features may be misannotated as real metabolites.

name: in-source-fragment-rule-matching
description: Use when per-sample MGF clean consensus spectra from LC–MS/MS contain multiple ionization variants of one precursor (in-source fragments, adducts, dimers) that must be collapsed to a single [M + H]+ ion entity before molecular networking.

name: in-source-spectrum-reconstruction
description: Use when a RAMClustR-clustered feature table (post-XCMS MS and idMS/MS features with cluster memberships and a feature-by-sample abundance matrix) must be converted into deconvoluted spectra for spectral matching or annotation.

name: inadequate-connectivity-simulation
description: Use when building or extending a reference database of metabolite 13C-13C connectivity networks (INADEQUATE-style) from public chemical shift data (BMRB), or when computing per-compound ambiguity (CA/CT) to weight downstream compound annotation confidence.

name: inadequate-nmr-pipeline-execution
description: Use when you have INADEQUATE 13C-13C NMR spectra from isotope-labeled metabolomics samples (e.g. 13C-labeled amino acid feeding studies) and need automated compound annotation plus fragment information for unknowns.

name: inadequate-spectral-database-search
description: Use when you have filtered networks of picked peaks from an INADEQUATE NMR spectrum (e.g. from PyINETA's cluster/find steps) and need to identify which metabolites from a simulated INADEQUATE database produced them.

name: inadequate-spectral-peak-picking
description: Use when you have an INADEQUATE spectrum (with chemical-shift referencing) and need to extract peak positions and areas where a single intensity threshold cannot separate overlapping 13C-13C correlations.

name: inchi-annotation-counting
description: Use when you have an mzmine-processed FBMN feature table with MS/MS spectra and need to benchmark how many features get an InChI from GNPS strict vs iterative weighted analog search.

name: inchi-generation-from-structures
description: Use when raw natural-product structure tables (e.g. smiles.tsv.gz, nominal.tsv.gz) hold SMILES identifiers or compound names, and a standardized InChI column is required for downstream harmonization or database upload.

name: inchi-key-based-structure-unification
description: Use when curating or merging chemical structure collections from multiple provenance where duplicate/same-core molecules must be de-duplicated into one canonical entry while retaining stereochemical variants.

name: inchi-key-molecule-deduplication
description: Use when preparing query and reference libraries for spectral database lookup: overlapping molecules between sides would inflate recall, so InChI-key-based disjointness must be asserted before ranking.

name: inchi-smiles-annotation-checking
description: Use when imported MS/MS spectra (MGF, msp, mzML, mzXML, JSON) carry inconsistent, wrongly labeled, or missing structure annotations (InChI, SMILES, InChIKey) or ionmode/adduct/charge fields that must be cleaned before scoring.

name: inchi-to-smiles-structure-normalization
description: Use when reference .msp blocks lack precomputed Fingerprint rows and contain only InChI: entries (or SMILES needing canonicalization), and dash-separated bit-location targets are required for IDSL_MINT transformer decoder training.

name: inchikey-annotation-aggregation
description: Use when you have matched annotations from a spectra search (e.g. CSA spectra searched against an .msp library) on an aligned peak table and need to consolidate them per compound (InChIKey) and identify annotations beyond those recovered by MS/MS library searches.

name: inchikey-annotation-based-spectrum-selection
description: Use when a cleaned MS/MS library must be split into training spectra with structural identifiers (InChIKeys) and query spectra without them, or when a deduplicated per-molecule reference set is needed.

name: inchikey-based-compound-grouping
description: Use when an MGF-format MS/MS library (e.g. MassSpecGym.mgf) must be grouped by underlying compound identity to compute intra-compound spectral similarity or de-duplicate spectra before model training or benchmarking.

name: inchikey-based-database-querying
description: Use when you hold a merged metabolite table keyed on unique InChIKeys and need to populate per-metabolite attributes (name descriptors, MW, formula, database IDs) for downstream interstudy comparability checks.

name: inchikey-based-dataset-merging
description: Use when multiple metabolomics datasets with heterogeneous metabolite identifiers (names, HMDB, KEGG, PubChem CIDs, CAS) must be merged and intercompared, and a systematic InChIKey-based harmonization with curation is required.

name: inchikey-based-spectral-lookup
description: Use when building an in-house m/z–RT metabolite standard library in metScribeR and the standards dataframe contains an inchiKey column, so public MS/MS spectra from MoNA should be merged into the exported library.

name: inchikey-based-spectrum-holdout-splitting
description: Use when building or benchmarking a spectral similarity model (Spec2Vec, cosine) on GNPS-style MS/MS libraries and you must guarantee that query compounds never appear in the training library, i.e. unknown-compound (structural-analogue) search evaluation.

name: inchikey-based-structure-matching
description: Use when benchmarking structure prediction or annotation pipelines where candidate and reference structures must be compared exactly at the connectivity level, e.g., scoring BAM derivatives against known suspects.

name: inchikey-block-comparison
description: Use when a candidate list retrieved from PubChem, ChemSpider, KEGG, or a user-supplied SDF contains stereoisomeric duplicates (shared first InChIKey block) that would otherwise inflate candidate counts and split score mass across chemically equivalent entries.

name: inchikey-canonical-smiles-resolution
description: Use when building a per-compound dataset from many spectra entries and you must deduplicate compounds and standardize structures (e.g. resolving canonical SMILES from InChIKeys before merging MS/MS spectra).

name: inchikey-canonicalization-verification
description: Use when a compound database ships structure files (.mol/.cdxml) plus identifier columns that must be regenerated and validated, or when checking whether deposited SMILES/InChI/InChIKey fields are populated and canonical.

name: inchikey-compound-deduplication
description: Use when merging MS/MS spectral reference libraries (NIST20, Agilent METLIN, GNPS, MSDIAL) and you need to quantify and remove cross-library duplicate compounds before building a combined database or reference file.

name: inchikey-compound-identifier-handling
description: Reference for pipelines that must merge MS/MS spectra from the same compound across collision energies or align predicted fingerprints with candidate compound lists drawn from MetaboQuest/PubChem.

name: inchikey-connectivity-block-label-matching
description: Use when you need ground-truth same/different-compound labels to benchmark spectral similarity scores (cosine, entropy) on MS/MS library pairs, and both spectra carry InChIKey annotations plus precursor m/z metadata.

name: inchikey-derivation-from-chemical-identifiers
description: Use when MS/MS library spectra (e.g. GNPS ALL_GNPS.json, 154,820 spectra) lack InChIKey annotations but carry compound name, molecular formula, or parent mass that can be resolved against PubChem.

name: inchikey-exact-match-accuracy-computation
description: Use when evaluating de novo structure elucidation output (SELFIES/SMILES candidates from a spectrum-conditioned model) and you need the fraction of predictions whose full InChIKey string exactly equals the reference molecule's InChIKey.

name: inchikey-exact-match-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking de novo structure elucidation from mass spectra on MassSpecGym/NPLIB1 test folds and you need Top-1/Top-10 exact-identity accuracy over full InChIKey strings for generated molecule sets.

name: inchikey-identifier-overlap-analysis
description: Use when integrating two or more mass spectral libraries (e.g., .MGF, .MSP, .JSON exports) and you need the fraction of compounds present in multiple sources, per-library compound/spectrum counts, and single-library exclusivity.

name: inchikey-molecule-indexing
description: Use when annotated MS/MS spectra (InChIKey/SMILES metadata) must be grouped at the compound level, e.g. to prevent spectra of the same molecule from leaking across model train/validation/test splits.

name: inchikey-protonation-layer-interpretation
description: Use when a merged metabolite table contains multiple InChIKeys that share the same 14-character molecular-skeleton prefix (e.g. palmitate vs. palmitic acid) and entries must be reduced to one non-conjugated compound per pair.

name: inchikey-scaffold-dataset-split-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking C2MS (compound-to-spectrum) models like FraGNNet, ICEBERG, GrAFF-MS, MassFormer, NEIMS, or Precursor-Only on MS/MS prediction or retrieval tasks and you need generalization-controlled splits with spectral similarity metrics.

name: inchikey-set-difference-analysis
description: Use when you have InChIKey or SMILES lists from a new library and several existing open/commercial spectral libraries and need to quantify which compounds are novel.

name: inchikey-short-key-structure-matching
description: Use when building a benchmarking or dereplication set that must join a curated structure table (e.g. DNP-derived) to an MS/MS spectral library (e.g. GNPS-derived) at the level of unique parent structures rather than individual stereoisomers.

name: inchikey-skeleton-matching
description: Use when building a ground-truth set of known BGC–spectrum links: you have MIBiG BGC records with structural annotations and GNPS library spectra with InChIKey annotations, but no direct spectral link, and need a chirality-insensitive structural join.

name: inchikey-skeleton-prefix-matching
description: Use when merging metabolite datasets that report heterogeneous non-systematic identifiers and need a systematic key to collapse conjugated base/acid pairs or duplicate entries before manual curation.

name: inchikey-smiles-compound-deduplication
description: Use when a curated MS/MS library needs unique-compound counts for reporting or validation, and each spectrum carries structure metadata (InChIKey or SMILES) that can serve as the de-duplication key.

name: inchikey-stereoisomer-filtering
description: Use when candidate lists retrieved from PubChem, ChemSpider or KEGG contain multiple stereoisomers sharing a first InChIKey block, and scores must be assigned per unique connectivity before ranking Top 1/3/5.

name: inchikey-structure-dereplication
description: Use when preparing a candidate structure database (e.g. DNP, UNPD, GNPS libraries) for ISDB spectral matching, where duplicate structures and stereoisomers would otherwise inflate candidate ranking lists.

name: inchikey-structure-hashing
description: Use when a spectral or metabolite library (e.g., GNPS .mgf entries with structural identifiers) needs unique structural keys so duplicate structures and stereoisomers can be collapsed before benchmarking or annotation.

name: inchikey-unique-count-aggregation
description: Use when ms1-id annotations from multiple LC-MS modes must be reduced to unique-metabolite counts (distinct InChIKey strings) per mode and pooled, e.g. to benchmark annotation yield on a public cohort dataset.

name: independent-dataset-generalizability-evaluation
description: Use when a retention-order or molecular-property model has been trained on one reference set (e.g., dataset_87) and you must quantify whether its performance transfers to unseen chromatographic runs before trusting it for annotation.

name: independent-dataset-validation-reporting
description: Use when a new feature-clustering method must be validated against established tools (e.g. CAMERA) on a dataset independent of the one used to develop the method, with clustering-quality metrics reported in a reproducible table.

name: infant-vs-adult-microbiome-sample-interpretation
description: Use when exploratory ordination of a large combined microbiome PCoA (thousands of samples, dozens of metadata columns) must reveal infant-vs-adult age differences via gradient or discrete metadata coloring.

name: infonce-contrastive-alignment
description: Use when pre-training a spectral encoder on multi-modal spectra (IR, Raman, UV-Vis) whose embeddings must be aligned with 3D structural embeddings for downstream spectra-conditioned molecular generation.

name: information-gain-feature-selection
description: Use when a high-dimensional per-instance feature table (here, 473 CDK-derived bond features over 679 Zaretzki-derived substrates) must be reduced before training a classifier, and the retained dimensionality should be learned per class via internal cross-validation rather than fixed a priori.

name: injection-sequence-pre-interpolation
description: Use when a randomized LC/GC-MS sample list must be converted into an instrument injection sequence where QC samples are evenly interspersed and QC wells stay confined to a dedicated plate column.

name: inorganic-and-mixture-compound-filtering
description: Use when a merged multi-source chemical inventory (e.g., fused EPA HPV, EINECS, CHEMINV, Tox21, pesticide, and exposome lists) must be cleaned of non-single-organic entries and deduplicated into a unique CASRN-keyed set.

name: inorganic-compound-formula-keyed-classification
description: Decision support for classifying inorganic, organometallic, or carbon-exception compounds (cyanides, CO, CO2, carbon disulfide) when structural-rule-based taxonomy categories are needed rather than name- or text-based labels.

name: input-output-kernel-regression-scoring
description: Use when GNPS molecular networking spectra must be linked to candidate biosynthetic gene clusters with a supervised kernel-regression score, or when reproducing the IOKR top-n ranking and AUC benchmarks (Table 3) against a randomised baseline.

name: insilico-formula-annotation-sirius
description: Use when MS/MS peak lists (e.g., from a microbeMASST batch search) lack library matches and you need tentative molecular formula and compound-class assignments; applied to spectra with parent mass < 850 Da.

name: insilico-lipid-library-search
description: Use when a positive-ion LC-HRMS lipidomics peak list contains unannotated precursor m/z values and you need additional lipid annotations beyond MSI level 1/2 spectral matches, as MSI level 3 accurate-mass-only assignments.

name: insilico-ms2-annotation-sirius-canopus
description: Use when you have MZmine-processed features with associated MS2 scans (mzML / mgf spectra) from LC-HRMS2 DDA data in positive and/or negative ionization mode and want per-feature in-silico candidate structures, formulas, and chemical classes to merge with ISDB spectral matches and taxonomic.

name: insilico-msms-annotation-sirius
description: Use when MS2 .mzML features lack spectral-library matches and candidate metabolite structures must be ranked via SIRIUS in silico fragmentation with the 'all' (orbitrap) database inside the MAW containers.

name: insilico-spectral-library-construction
description: Use when you have a set of predicted or known metabolite structures plus a corpus of experimental MS/MS spectra and need to measure annotation gains from expanding the reference library.

name: insilico-vs-experimental-spectrum-comparison
description: Use when a spectral library candidate has CFM-ID (or similar) in silico fragments and a matching experimental tandem HRMS/MS spectrum, and you must quantify/visualize fragment overlap to validate predicted fragments before using them for compound annotation.

name: inst-mfa-output-processing
description: Use when INCA INST-MFA 'fit' objects (flux upper/lower CI bounds) exist for two or more isotope labeling designs and the goal is to compare flux confidence-interval widths and measurement counts across designs.

name: instrument-acquisition-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing acquisition controllers on real LC-MS/MS runs and you need to quantify MS2 efficiency (peaks fragmented / MS2 scans), scan counts, or per-cycle MS1 scan-plus-processing overhead from mzML files.

name: instrument-context-stratified-comparison-orbitrap-fticr
description: Use when comparing annotation counts between METASPACE-ML and MSM on imaging mass spectrometry datasets grouped by instrument (Orbitrap, FT-ICR) or sample type (animal, plant) at fixed FDR cutoffs of 5% and 10%.

name: instrument-controller-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when multiple DDA acquisition controllers (e.g., TopN, SmartROI, WeightedDEW with specific t0/t1 parameters) must be ranked by how many picked peaks they fragment, against a computed optimal, on the same complex sample injections.

name: instrument-drift-timeline-visualization
description: Use when long-term pooled-QC injections (e.g., MetNexs long-term QC pool) tracked per instrument show suspected calibration drift, intermittent calibrant-signal loss, or degrading peak shape, and the goal is to plot deviations versus analysis time to date and diagnose the malfunction.

name: instrument-family-group-statistics
description: Use when analyzing multi-vendor DIA raw cohorts (e.g., PRIDE-deposited .raw/.d/.wiff files) with DIA-NN and you need per-instrument-type protein ID counts and group medians.

name: instrument-format-file-io
description: Use when input is raw/profile-mode LC-IM-MS data in an instrument format such as Agilent .d or UIMF, and the output must remain in the same instrument format without overwriting the original file.

name: instrument-format-preserving-ms-file-writing
description: Use when you have preprocessed (smoothed, demultiplexed, spike-removed) LC-IM-MS TOF spectra and need to save them in the original instrument's file format for downstream processing.

name: instrument-metadata-based-task-routing
description: Use when a mixed batch of raw MS files from multiple instruments (e.g., Orbitrap Astral, timsTOF Ultra, Orbitrap Exploris 480) spans DDA, WWA, and DIA acquisition modes and each file must be sent to the matching search engine automatically.

name: instrument-parameter-auto-reading-from-raw-exports
description: Use when raw vendor LA-ICP-MS exports (Agilent .b batch directories, Perkin Elmer Elan 'XL', Thermo Qtegra exports, or text image/file-per-line files) are imported into Pew2 and instrument parameters such as MS acquisition time must be applied to the image configuration without manual.

name: instrument-parameter-qc-inspection
description: Use when you hold a raw LC-IM-MS file (e.g., Agilent .d) and need the instrument settings and parameters used for the acquisition — electric field strength, pressure, temperature, voltages — to check instrument performance relative to the collected data.

name: instrument-performance-benchmarking
description: Use when you have paired full-scan and DDA-controller mzML files (e.g. serum QCA / beer QCB injections) and need to quantify how many picked peaks were actually fragmented versus the theoretical optimum for those injections.

name: instrument-platform-partitioning
description: Use when raw-file-level metadata from a ProteomeXchange/PRIDE deposition (e.g., PXD037527) must be grouped and counted by acquisition mode (DDA/WWA/DIA) and instrument platform to characterize dataset composition, throughput, or search-tool routing (e.g., DIA-NN for DIA files).
tools: ProteomeXchange Consortium via the PRIDE partner repository

name: instrument-qc-metric-aggregation
description: Use when QCing Thermo RAW LC-MS/MS runs (e.g. HeLa digest standards) and you need to compare scan-level acquisition metrics across files to flag underperforming batches before searching.

name: instrument-specific-collision-energy-mapping
description: Use when evaluating a QTOF-trained MS/MS spectral prediction model (e.g. CFM-ID 4.0 trained on Metlin QTOF data) against Orbitrap MS/MS query spectra, such as the CASMI 2016 category 3 dataset of 208 Orbitrap spectra.

name: instrument-specific-mass-accuracy-handling-qtof-vs-orbitrap
description: Use when refining formula candidates from MS/MS data whose precursor m/z and instrument type (Q-TOF or Orbitrap) are known, and candidate formulas must fall within the correct ppm tolerance of the precursor mass.

name: instrument-specific-model-checkpoint-selection
description: Use when running FIDDLE formula prediction or reproducing benchmark accuracies on MS/MS spectra whose instrument type (Orbitrap vs Q-TOF) is known, so the matching pre-trained weights are loaded.

name: instrument-specific-model-inference
description: Use when MS/MS spectra (MGF with title, precursor_mz, precursor_type, collision_energy) originate from a known instrument type (Q-TOF or Orbitrap) and formula predictions must use the matching pre-trained FIDDLE weights and mass tolerance.

name: instrument-specific-mz-tolerance-selection
description: Use when filtering MASST candidate matches for a synthesized compound's MS/MS spectrum and the precursor m/z tolerance must be set per instrument class (0.01 for Orbitrap-derived data, 0.02 for Q-ToF-derived data).

name: instrument-specific-ppm-tolerance-matching
description: Use when annotating MS2 fragment peaks with subformulae of a candidate precursor formula and no fragmentation tree is desired; instrument type (Ion Trap, Q-ToF, Orbitrap/FTICR) determines the ppm tolerance.

name: instrument-stability-quality-assessment-msi
description: Use when a spatial metabolomics peak table (pixels × m/z ion intensities) must be checked for stable acquisition before downstream analysis, by testing whether manually or lasso-delineated off-tissue background regions yield mutually consistent spectra.

name: instrument-type-spectra-annotation
description: Use when building MS/MS training corpora where spectra come from mixed instrument sources and you need to tag each spectrum with collision-cell vs IT instrument type and energy before merging, binning, or model training.

name: instrument-underperformance-confirmation
description: Use when a Thermo RAW run shows depressed acquisition-side QC signals (e.g. reduced MS2 TIC with preserved MS1 TIC) and you need identification-count evidence from MaxQuant-style searches to confirm the underperformance.

name: instrument-vendor-classification
description: Use when you need to stratify repository studies by acquisition instrument vendor (e.g., Bruker vs Agilent/Varian) or by sample type from raw NMR data available in Metabolomics Workbench.

name: instrument-vendor-metadata-inventory
description: Use when reproducing repository-level survey counts (e.g., Figure 3 of the CloMet paper) or auditing which instrument vendors appear in raw data of a public metabolomics repository's study catalog.

name: instrument-vendor-software-concentration-comparison
description: Use when raw targeted SRM/MRM data (e.g., Waters Xevo TQ-S .raw files from a Biocrates AbsoluteIDQ p180 plate) already have vendor-software quantification results and you need to verify that an open-source pipeline reproduces those concentrations.

name: instrumental-data-type-categorisation
description: Use when curating or classifying a metabolomics software catalogue and each tool must be labelled with its instrumental data type (LC-MS, GC-MS, NMR) and major functionality under a fixed controlled vocabulary.

name: instrumental-shift-quantification
description: Use when preparing raw LC-MS-based metabolomics data for feature extraction and you need an automatically measured instrumental shift value rather than a manually guessed retention-time drift tolerance.

name: integrated-discrimination-improvement-reclassification
description: Use when two nested or competing risk scores must be compared for predictive value of 5- or 10-year mortality (or similar survival endpoints), and you need C-statistic differences with SEs/P values plus IDI with SEs/P values.

name: integrated-gradients-attribution-computation
description: Use when a trained transformer model has produced lipid token predictions on MS2 spectra and you need per-peak interpretability: attributing each predicted lipid token back to specific m/z peaks to compare them against known fragment annotations.

name: integrated-spectrum-fingerprint-ranking
description: Use when an analyte's GC/EI-MS spectrum matches no known reference spectra and a ranked list of putative NPS identities must be produced from an enumerated synthetic database.

name: integrative-clustering-method-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing integrative clustering algorithms across multiple omic data layers, especially when some layers are noisy or have different cluster separability, and you need ARI-based benchmark tables.

name: integrative-omics-pathway-analysis
description: Use when you have matched gene-expression and metabolomics data from a phenotype study and need to identify significantly perturbed pathways (pFDR < 0.05) using over-representation, topology, and combined p-value evidence.

name: intensity-dependent-missing-value-simulation
description: Use when preparing augmented ion-image pairs from a preprocessed MSI matrix ([X*Y,P]) for DeepION ISO-mode isotope-ion representation training and the missing values must depend on ion intensity.

name: intensity-jitter-parameterization
description: Use when preparing a binned training corpus for MS2DeepScore (or a similar Siamese spectral-embedding model) and you need stochastic intensity variability applied to the square-root-transformed, 10,000-bin spectra between 10 and 1000 m/z.

name: intensity-matrix-preprocessing-and-imputation
description: Use when a peak-intensity matrix (rows = peak features, columns = samples, with a group line or experimental_design dict) contains zero intensities or unnormalised scale, and must be prepared for PALS pathway activity scoring.

name: intensity-normalization-to-unit-scale
description: Use when stacked peak plots from an MZmine 2 aligned peak list must be converted to unit-maximum, fixed-size 64x64 raster images to feed an image-based DNN peak classifier.

name: intensity-peak-noise-injection
description: Use when a ViMMS ChemicalMixtureCreator-generated chemical dataset needs realistic intensity fluctuation (and optionally random RT jitter) applied via pluggable noise classes before running simulated acquisition.

name: intensity-ratio-based-isotope-filtering
description: Use when annotating LC/MS pseudospectra where isotope peaks must be flagged and charge states deduced from isotope spacing, and candidate isotope pairs need an intensity-ratio plausibility check.

name: intensity-scale-sweep-simulation
description: Use when you need labeled synthetic MS windows with known ground-truth peaks at multiple intensity scales to benchmark signal/noise classification methods where real-data ground truth is unavailable.

name: intensity-scaling-visualization
description: Use when MS/MS spectra (e.g. from an MGF file such as iPRG2012.mgf) need intensity de-emphasis of overly intense peaks and downstream rendering as static publication figures or interactive web plots.

name: intensity-threshold-background-segmentation
description: Use when a spatial metabolomics peak table (X/Y pixel coordinates plus m/z intensity columns) contains off-tissue background pixels that degrade clustering, and a total-intensity threshold must be derived or applied to segment tissue from background.

name: intensity-threshold-baseline-comparison
description: Use when a binary signal/noise classifier (e.g. LSH on mass-spectrometry windows) needs a ROC-based comparison against intensity/SNR threshold filtering on labeled synthetic windows with per-panel intensity settings.

name: intensity-threshold-peak-localization
description: Use when you need to locate peak clusters in simulated (or preprocessed) 1D 1H, 2D J-Res, or 2D COSY 1H NMR spectra before further modeling, using only a user-supplied intensity cutoff.

name: intensity-weighted-gaussian-mz-density-estimation
description: Use when reconstructing or tuning the mass trace detection stage of LC-MS feature finding from centroided mzML data, specifically when deciding which nearby peaks belong to a seeded trace along the m/z axis.

name: intensity-weighted-positional-encoding
description: Use when reimplementing or extending the IDSL_MINT MS2Fingerprint transformer — specifically when encoding .msp MS/MS peak lists (m/z + intensity pairs) as transformer input sequences with intensity-aware positional embeddings.

name: intensity-weighted-spectral-peak-matching
description: Use when annotating a tandem MS spectrum by candidate retrieval: you have an experimental MS/MS peak list (m/z, intensity) and candidate molecules whose theoretical fragmentation patterns must be matched and scored.

name: intensity-weighted-spectrum-vector-scoring
description: Use when comparing MS/MS query spectra against a library (e.g. cleaned AllPositive GNPS dataset) and peak-based cosine scores underperform, or when you need similarity scores that track structural similarity across instruments and conditions.

name: inter-batch-replicate-utility-assessment
description: Decision support for choosing negative-control metabolites and hierarchical batch-merging designs before finalising hRUV normalisation of large-scale metabolomics batches.

name: inter-batch-sample-partitioning-for-plate-design
description: Use when a cohort of samples (e.g. hundreds of samples spanning 2-, 3-, and 4-category strata like treatment/placebo, gender, age group) must be partitioned into multiple 96-well plates so each plate's group distribution mirrors the full cohort, prior to intra-batch block randomization.

name: inter-batch-variation-assessment
description: Use when you have LC-MS or SRM proteomics runs with pooled QC injections interspersed at a fixed interval (e.g. every 5, 6, or 8 subject samples) and you need to measure and report how much unwanted inter-batch variation remains, before versus after batch correction such as QC-RFSC.

name: inter-laboratory-ccs-variation-analysis
description: Use when comparing TWIMS (or DTIM) CCS values measured in-house against literature CCS values for the same metabolite/adduct ([M + H]+ or [M − H]−), or when validating that predicted CCS values agree with experimental ones within the ~±3% experimental variation band.

name: inter-rater-agreement-statistics
description: Use when multiple independent annotators have labeled the same set of items (e.g. qualified/unqualified QC calls per file) and you need reproducibility statistics and consensus labels before training a supervised model.

name: interactive-dashboard-plotting
description: Use when mzML/mzXML files from untargeted MS-based metabolomics runs are being added incrementally (or a whole batch needs retrospective review) and extracted diagnostic values — observed m/z, retention time, intensity, peak shape, calibrant signal — must be plotted interactively so acquisition.

name: interactive-datatable-construction
description: Use when publishing curated chemical or spectral tables (e.g., fragment ions with m/z, intensity, precursor, collision energy) as an interactive, searchable HTML datatable for public repositories.

name: interactive-filtering-effect-visualization
description: Use when you need to visually communicate to end users how successive feature-intensity filtering steps shrink a feature table, e.g. per-sample HTML plots of the intensity-based, quantile-based, and sequential filtering effects after running Inventa on MZmine output.

name: interactive-html-report-generation
description: Use when a patRoon NTA/TP-screening workflow in R has finished and the resulting suspects, TP components and annotations must be delivered as a single interactive HTML document (report.html) for review.

name: interactive-selection-dialog-gui-logic
description: Use when a boolean ROI mask must be derived from an LA-ICP-MS elemental image (e.g. a 2D NumPy array of a 56Fe pancreatic adenocarcinoma tissue microarray core) by automatic thresholding, and the mask must optionally be combined with or restricted to a previously selected region.

name: interactive-umap-plot-generation
description: Use when you have 500-dimensional MS2DeepScore embedding vectors for tandem mass spectra and need to visually explore chemical space, especially to check whether positive and negative ionization mode spectra of the same compound cluster together.

name: intergenic-distance-clustering
description: Use when you have a gene prediction .tab file with coordinates and strands, and need to group adjacent same-strand genes into proximal clusters (proximons) as a precursor to operon definition.

name: interior-point-local-refinement
description: Decision support for tuning or implementing SAND's per-bin decomposition when sampled MCMC peak parameters need periodic deterministic polishing before emitting a peak table.

name: intermediate-fragment-persistence-weight-zeroing
description: Use when implementing or modifying the CFM-ID 4.0 fragmentation graph for ESI-MS/MS spectral prediction, specifically to remodel ring cleavages as sequential one-bond breaks while suppressing unstable intermediate fragment peaks.

name: internal-standard-area-standardization
description: Use when raw integrated component areas (Component.Area) from GC-MS samples must be normalized against internal or external standards before downstream analyses such as NMDS, PCA, or ANOSIM.

name: internal-standard-based-ccs-bias-correction
description: Use when IM-MS lipidomics measurements (e.g., TIM-MS) are spiked with U13C-labeled yeast lipids and CCSN2 values show bias against the DTCCSN2 library that must be corrected per lipid class-adduct combination.

name: internal-standard-based-lipid-normalization
description: Use when a lipidomics experiment (LipidSearch/LIQUID output or Metabolomics Workbench data) includes internal lipid standards and per-lipid absolute concentrations are needed before differential abundance analysis.

name: internal-standard-based-migration-time-prediction
description: Use when pre-processing targeted full-scan MSI-CE-MS multiplexed data (mzML) where high migration time variability from nonlinear electroosmotic flow changes prevents peak alignment, and analyte migration times must be predicted per run from internal-standard landmarks.

name: internal-standard-based-sample-correction
description: Use when a metabolomics feature table contains samples spiked with one or more internal standards and unwanted sample-to-sample variation (e.g., from extraction or injection variability) must be corrected before statistical analysis or reporting.

name: internal-standard-calibration
description: Use when GC-MS component areas aggregated by uafR's mzExacto() must be normalized relative to a known internal standard (e.g. tetradecane) or external-standard calibration curves before PCA/NMDS/machine-learning analyses.

name: internal-standard-calibration-design
description: Use when a mass-spectrometry metabolomics study requires absolute concentrations of selected metabolites (e.g., oleic, arachidonic, docosahexaenoic acids, creatine) to validate untargeted profiling between molecularly defined tumor subgroups.

name: internal-standard-class-mapping
description: Use when a lipidomics data matrix contains raw peak areas or peak heights plus internal standard rows with known concentrations, and species-level concentrations per lipid class are needed.

name: internal-standard-correction
description: Use when a targeted LC-MS/MS peak-area table contains measured analogue internal-standard transitions for each compound and intensity drift over the injection sequence must be corrected before external-calibration quantification.

name: internal-standard-drift-trend-analysis
description: Use when a raw-file series (e.g. Thermo .raw from a Thermo acquisition sequence) has been processed through MS-DIAL against an .msp IS library and you need to detect gradual drift in internal standard RT, intensity, or Δm/z across specimens.

name: internal-standard-dropout-threshold-logic
description: Use when a specimen-level 'Warning' flag must be assigned in Rapid QC-MS based on IS intensity dropouts relative to a user-defined threshold or on per-IS QC designations.

name: internal-standard-failure-notification-rule-implementation
description: Use when implementing or configuring automated notification logic in Rapid QC-MS that must alert designated researchers whenever a newly acquired raw file's internal standard quality metrics violate user-defined IS Configurations criteria.

name: internal-standard-mapping-for-quantification
description: Use when a targeted metabolomics dataset contains calibration points, QC samples, and internal standard intensities, and the goal is absolute analyte concentrations rather than relative feature intensities.

name: internal-standard-normalization-benchmarking
description: Use when you have GC-MS peak-intensity tables with pool QC samples (and ideally an independent external validation QC set) and need to quantify which normalization — sum-based iTIC/fTIC/mTIC, SERRF, or SERDA — minimizes technical variation.

name: internal-standard-pass-fail-evaluation
description: Use when acquiring large untargeted LC-MS/MS runs (e.g., Thermo RAW files with a sequence .csv and an .msp internal-standard library) and you need automatic, per-specimen Pass/Fail/Warn status for every internal standard target as soon as mzML-converted data arrive.

name: internal-standard-qc-flagging
description: Use when implementing or re-implementing per-internal-standard QC status assignment for LC-MS/MS specimens, where each IS target needs Pass/Warn/Fail flags from RT and m/z deviation thresholds and missing-peak detection.

name: internal-standard-qc-metabolite-normalization
description: Use when the metabolitedata frame flags internal standards or QC metabolites (e.g. IS==1) and the goal is metabolite-level normalization of featuredata via a single standard (is), nomis, ccmn, or RUV-based methods (ruv2, ruvrand, ruvrandclust).

name: internal-standard-ratio-normalization
description: Use when raw peak areas from a targeted LC-MS method with stable isotope labeled internal standards must be converted to compound/IS ratios before quality assessment, batch correction or outlier detection.

name: internal-standard-recovery-normalization
description: Use when lipidomics quantification output (e.g. LipidSearch or LIQUID tables) contains spiked internal lipid standards and the goal is a normalized, absolute concentration matrix per lipid and sample.

name: internal-standard-response-normalization
description: Use when processing targeted LC-MS(/MS), CE-, GC-MS, HPLC, or FIA-MS injections where each transition or component is paired with an internal standard and per-feature peak areas must be ratio-normalized before calibration or quantitation.

name: internal-standard-retention-time-correction
description: Use when running MetaPro Target Search on Aird-converted DDA LC-MS batches (TripleTOF 6600 .wiff or Q Exactive HF .

name: internal-standard-scoring
description: Use when processing targeted LC-MS/MS MRM quantitation data (e.g. SmartPeak FeatureDB.csv from the 5500 QTRAP RapidRIP tutorial) and you want a per-compound IS quality score computed from tailing, asymmetry, and height-ratio metrics before quantitation reporting.

name: internal-standard-selection-rsdqc-ranking
description: Use when a targeted LC-MS metabolomics experiment contains multiple candidate internal standards and you need to assign each compound a suitable IS, using the lowest-RSDQC criterion on batch-corrected compound/IS ratios.

name: internal-standard-signal-adequacy-checking
description: Use when preprocessing targeted full-scan MSI-CE-MS runs where peak annotation depends on internal standards (or other reliable landmark peaks) with sufficient signal-to-noise; verify IS signal adequacy before trusting peak areas or reference ranges.

name: internal-standard-validation
description: Use when a GC-MS experiment includes known internal or external standards and automated component-area extraction must be verified for accuracy before compound quantification is trusted.

name: internal-test-set-evaluation
description: Use when retraining or evaluating the BitterMasS Random Forest classifier on subsets of combined MassBank spectra and you need held-out precision/recall comparable to the paper's internal test set (precision = 0.83, recall = 0.90).

name: interquartile-range-threshold-filtering
description: Use when you have multiple stochastic predictions (e.g., MC-dropout embeddings) per compound pair and must decide which similarity scores are reliable enough to use downstream, or quantify the error-vs-retrieval tradeoff.

name: intestinal-disease-gene-set-verification
description: Use when a task requires confirming which genes (e.g. STK11, CFTR, BMPR1A, SMAD4, NOTCH1, PKD1, MLH1, MSH2, APC, MEFV) are associated with multiple intestinal diseases in GutUDB.

name: intra-batch-drift-adjustment-of-targeted-metabolomics
description: Use when a targeted metabolomics run sequence shows run-order-dependent signal drift within a batch/plate (visible in pooled QC or replicate traces over run order) and drift must be removed before between-batch correction.

name: intra-batch-injection-order-randomization
description: Use when a batch's samples must be ordered for LC/GC-MS injection such that treatment/placebo or other randomized dimensions never cluster (e.g., no three consecutive samples of the same group) after inter-batch balancing has been done.

name: intra-interbatch-drift-assessment
description: Use when monitoring a specific compound's intensity across long-term QC injections spanning multiple batches to quantify drift that occurs within a batch versus between batches.

name: intra-subclass-unsaturation-parallelism-checking
description: Decision support for ranking candidate lipid annotations in LC-MS/MS data when multiple isobaric chain-composition assignments exist within one subclass and only retention order can discriminate them.

name: intraclass-correlation-coefficient-analysis
description: Use when two or more simulated or experimentally acquired MRS basis sets (e.g. MRSCloud vs FID-A, MRSCloud vs MARSS, MRSCloud vs LCModel .basis, or 21/41/101 spatial-point runs) must be compared metabolite-by-metabolite for agreement.

name: inverse-differential-jacobian-interaction-validation
description: Use when two metabolomic conditions are to be compared for differential metabolite-metabolite interaction identification, especially when validating against a curated model (e.g. BioModels BIOM0000000070) and scoring precision/sensitivity/specificity.

name: inverse-gamma-variance-regularization
description: Use when per-gene expression variances estimated from limited samples (e.g., GTEx v8 tissue subsets) are too noisy to standardize effect sizes, and you need Empirical-Bayes posterior mean variances under an inverse-gamma conjugate prior.

name: inverse-sd-decoy-weighting
description: Use when estimating per-annotation false discovery rates in imaging mass spectrometry where decoys were generated by SD-sampling of ion similarities, and each decoy carries a standard-deviation value that should modulate its decoy weight.

name: inverted-comparison-orientation-correction
description: Use when pooling fold-changes from multiple metabolomics studies where some reports give the inverted ratio (control/case instead of case/control), and a case-vs-control-consistent combined estimate per compound is required.

name: iokr-kernel-regression-link-scoring
description: Use when you have paired microbial genome-mining (AntiSMASH BGC/GCF) and metabolomics (GNPS spectral) data loaded in NPLinker and need a kernel-regression score to rank candidate BGC–spectrum links, e.g. against a validated link subset.

name: iokr-link-prediction-scoring
description: Use when ranking candidate GCF-to-molecular-family links in NPLinker output and you want to combine the standardised strain correlation score with IOKR scores to improve the rank of validated links.

name: ion-adduct-abundance-quantification
description: Use when you have per-dataset IIMN/FBMN-IIN output (feature quantification table plus IIN edges CSVs) from MZmine-processed LC-MS/MS datasets and need relative adduct percentages per dataset or per sample-type group.

name: ion-adduct-annotation
description: Use when IM-MS data contains adduct types (e.g. [M−H]−, [M+H]+, [M+Na]+, or uncommon dimers like [2M+H]+ / [2M−H]−) for which CCS predictions are needed to filter or annotate candidate structures.

name: ion-adduct-annotation-propagation-statistics
description: Use when a dataset has been processed through the MZmine metaCorrelate IIMN workflow and you need to measure how much annotation improves by propagating library matches to neighboring ion identity nodes.

name: ion-arrival-time-field-regression
description: Use when IMS-MS data were acquired in stepped-field DTIMS mode (e.g., Agilent 6560 with multiple electric fields per ion) and per-ion CCS values must be computed from arrival-time vs P/V regressions rather than single-field calibration.

name: ion-charge-state-assignment
description: Use when an aligned multi-sample feature table (with m/z, drift time, and retention time dimensions) needs isotopic signature detection and charge-state annotation, as required before identifications rely on isotopic evidence.

name: ion-chromatogram-background-estimation
description: Use when processing LC-MS/MS MRM ion chromatograms where a background intensity level is needed to define smoothing windows or section extents prior to peak detection and quantitation.

name: ion-chromatogram-peak-abundance-quantitation
description: Use when MRM ion chromatograms contain coeluted peaks (2–3 isomers sharing one chromatogram) and per-compound peak abundances must be computed automatically rather than attributed wholly to one targeted compound.

name: ion-feature-matrix-processing
description: Use when input is a pixel-by-ion feature matrix from an imaging mass spectrometry run (CSV with X/Y pixel coordinates plus per-pixel ion intensities) and noise ions must be removed during quality control before metabolite annotation or spatial pattern analysis.

name: ion-form-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when you have a curated LC-MS peak benchmark (e.g. Demo_MetDNA2_NIST_urine_pos) and need to compare rule-based isotope/adduct annotation (CAMERA) against knowledge-guided network-based ion form assignment (KGMN, MetDNA2Vis).

name: ion-identity-annotation-parsing
description: Use when a feature quantification table, IIN edges file, or GNPS library (e.g., GNPS-IIMN-PROPOGATED) contains ion-identity annotation strings with inconsistent spellings or ordering that must be normalized before grouping, counting, or comparing adduct abundances.

name: ion-identity-network-construction
description: Use when you have an aligned LC-MS/MS feature list with consensus MS2 spectra and redundant unconnected nodes (adducts/isotopes of one compound), and you want MS1 ion-identity edges to propagate annotations in GNPS FBMN.

name: ion-identity-network-group-counting
description: Use when the analysis goal is to reproduce or verify the graph-level statistics of a GNPS FBMN job (feature count, IIN group count, node count, singleton count, edge count) from the deposited MZmine quant table and GNPS job ID.

name: ion-identity-network-node-collapsing
description: Use when an aligned feature table plus IIN graphml (ion groups keyed by shared IIN ID) is available and the goal is to reduce feature redundancy by merging ion-species nodes of the same compound into single representative molecular nodes.

name: ion-identity-network-statistics-aggregation
description: Use when you have IIMN (FBMN-IIN) outputs across multiple LC-MS datasets and need to summarize and compare the relative abundance of ion species/adducts per dataset or sample type.

name: ion-identity-network-supplementary-edge-integration
description: Use when you have an aligned feature list (feature quantification .csv + MS2 .mgf) plus IIN supplementary edge files and want to compare MS2-only FBMN against IIMN, or to merge redundant adduct/isotope subnetworks of the same compound.

name: ion-image-correlation-analysis
description: Use when an rMSIproc peak matrix has matrix-related clusters (e.g. silver 'Ag1' annotation) whose S1 spectral and S2 morphological similarity scores fall below the user-specified threshold, so co-localized endogenous ions may be hiding inside the cluster.

name: ion-image-hotspot-truncation
description: Use when raw MALDI-MSI pixel-by-ion matrices contain extreme intensity spikes (matrix crystal hotspots) that must be capped before self-supervised ion-image representation learning or any downstream similarity measurement.

name: ion-image-preprocessing-for-cnn-inference
description: Use when ion images (e.g. from METASPACE gold standard GS.tar.gz or the 353 DHB matrix-cluster formulas) must be converted into the fixed-size RGB input expected by a pretrained ResNet-50 CNN for off-sample/on-sample classification.

name: ion-image-representation-learning
description: Use when MSI pixel-by-ion matrices (e.g. [X*Y,P] shape, 198x422 rat brain images) must be converted into dense ion-image representations for colocalized-ion or isotope-ion search without manual annotation.

name: ion-image-spatial-correlation-analysis
description: Use when evaluating spectral/spatial fidelity of MSI reconstruction methods (e.g. MEISTER, FT, linear subspace) against a clean ground-truth dataset with known peak centroids.

name: ion-intensity-spectrum-parsing
description: Use when input records are raw mass spectra (m/z / intensity pairs) that must be converted into the ion:intensity single-line format or Spectrum objects before SPLASH generation or similarity work.

name: ion-list-sorting-and-canonicalization
description: Use when a raw spectrum (e.g. a MassBank PR100026-style ion list such as '138.0641:71.59 195.0815:261.7') must be converted into the deterministic canonical ion:intensity string that feeds SPLASH hashing, similarity search, or cross-database comparison.

name: ion-mobility-adduct-dataset-partitioning
description: Use when a CCS prediction model must be built or reproduced per ion species — e.g. splitting McLean CCS Compendium measurements into [M−H]−, [M+H]+ and [M+Na]+ subsets for SVR regression and reporting median relative error and RMSEV.

name: ion-mobility-arrival-time-correction
description: Use when working with traveling-wave IMS-MS data (SLIM-based IMS or Waters Synapt) where arrival times from feature files must be adjusted for instrument-specific delays before fitting CCS calibration functions.

name: ion-mobility-arrival-time-metrics
description: Use when raw MS data from LC-IMS-MS acquisitions (or any run with IMS separation) must be quality-controlled by computing arrival-time or 1/K0 errors for auto-tracked or user-specified precursor ions.

name: ion-mobility-arrival-time-peak-detection
description: Use when you have drift tube IM-MS mzML data, a confirmed retention time for a molecular formula's primary ion, and single-field CCS calibration coefficients (Tfix, Beta) with a known drift gas, and you need IM peaks and DTCCS(N2) values for adduct ion species.

name: ion-mobility-bin-index-preservation
description: Use when converting profile-mode HDMSE/ion-mobility mass spectrometry data (mzML or Waters UNIFI) to a columnar format and the drift-time dimensions (bin, dt) must survive the conversion for later IMS trace or CCS analysis.

name: ion-mobility-calibration-curve-fitting
description: Use when converting ion arrival times from single-field RapidFire-DTIMS-MS, SLIM-based IMS, Waters Synapt TWIMS, or Bruker timsTOF into CCS values using a calibrant such as Agilent tune-mix; not needed for stepped-field DTIMS.

name: ion-mobility-calibration-plotting
description: Use when calibrating drift/arrival times to collision cross section (CCS) for TWIMS or SLIM IMS-MS data stored in MZA (HDF5) format, and when a fitted-calibration plot is needed for QC.

name: ion-mobility-ccs-calibration
description: Use when you have IMS-MS arrival-time/feature data (e.g. UIMF frame metadata plus Features_csv tables) and need to convert drift or arrival times into calibrated CCS values, choosing among single-field, stepped-field, or traveling-wave calibration methods.

name: ion-mobility-ccs-experimental-comparison
description: Use when per-conformer or Boltzmann-averaged CCS values (e.g., from HPCCS trajectory calculations) need to be validated against TWIMS experimental CCS references, or when ranking conformers to find the one matching the measured CCS.

name: ion-mobility-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when raw multidimensional MS data (e.g., Agilent .d or SLIM-MS LC-IM-MS runs) has been converted to .mza and you need to visualize mobility distributions or benchmark non-vendor rendering speed of an ion mobility heatmap.

name: ion-mobility-intensity-thresholding
description: Use when loading mzML-derived LC-IMS-MS/MS data onto a common m/z, drift time, retention time, intensity grid and the 3D signal span must be reduced to make local-maximum peak detection tractable.

name: ion-mobility-lipidomics-quality-control
description: Use when LC-IM-MS lipidomics measurements (e.g. trapped IM-MS or DTIM-MS) are spiked with fully U13C-labeled yeast lipids and CCS bias against a DTCCSN2 reference must be quantified or corrected per lipid class-adduct combination.

name: ion-mobility-mass-spectrometry-data-processing
description: Use when processing high-dimensional LC-IMS-MS/MS (e.g. Agilent 6560, Bruker, Waters) data where m/z, drift time, and retention time must be jointly leveraged for feature detection, alignment, and CCS-calibrated characterization.

name: ion-mobility-mass-spectrometry-peak-detection
description: Use when processing high-dimensional LC-IMS-MS/MS metabolomics data (e.g., mzML from Waters Synapt G2Si, Bruker timsTOF, or Agilent 6560) where peak detection across m/z, drift time, and retention time dimensions is needed before feature alignment or CCS calibration.

name: ion-mobility-mode-and-drift-tube-classification
description: Use when assembling or auditing a lipid CCS reference database from multiple experimental ion-mobility collections and you must classify entries by ionization mode and drift-tube type to report coverage totals.

name: ion-mobility-ms-acquisition-parameter-interpretation
description: Use when a raw instrument-format IM-MS acquisition file (e.g. Agilent .d) needs its acquisition settings extracted for quality assessment of instrument performance relative to the collected data.

name: ion-mobility-ms-data-processing
description: Use when analyzing high-dimensional TWIM-MS data from mixed multiomic samples (small molecules, lipids, peptides) on a Waters SYNAPT XS where calibrated CCS values and biomolecular class assignments are needed for features without prior identification, as when a feature table derived from a NIST.

name: ion-mobility-ms-lipid-dataset-harmonization
description: Use when lipid CCS values from one IM platform (e.g., negative-mode TIMS from Vasilopoulou et al. or Tsugawa et al.) must be calibrated toward reference values from another platform (DT) before pooled error metrics like MDRE are computed.

name: ion-mobility-separation-profile-matching
description: Use when LC-IMS-MS/MS data contain MS1 precursor peaks and MS2 fragment peaks and fragments must be attributed to precursors by co-elution/co-drift rather than retention time alone.

name: ion-mobility-spectrum-conversion
description: Use when raw IM-MS data (Agilent .d, Bruker TimsTOF .d, Thermo .raw, or mzML) must be converted to a cross-platform HDF5 structure for Python/R access, especially when the ion mobility dimension must be preserved.

name: ion-mode-database-partitioning
description: Use when preparing or validating an organ-specific metabolite database for MSI annotation, where measured m/z values must be matched against theoretical adduct m/z per ionization mode and per organ.

name: ion-mode-feature-counting
description: Use when you have UPLC-HRMS peak lists acquired in both positive and negative ESI modes and need a non-targeted count of genuine sample components per mode, reconciled against background-subtracted totals.

name: ion-mode-partition-analysis
description: Use when a metabolomics paper reports ion-mode-specific or organ-specific metabolite counts (e.g. positive/negative mode totals, deduplicated unique-metabolite totals) and a companion database file must be counted and reconciled against those claims.

name: ion-mode-specific-database-validation
description: Use when annotating features in a preprocessed AFADESI-MSI dataset with MSIannotator and you must confirm that the imported Database (from Organ specific metabolite database.xlsx, e.g. Sheet4 = liver) matches the detection mode of MSIdata before running MSIannotator.m.

name: ion-mode-stratified-accuracy-computation
description: Use when evaluating formula-prediction tools (FIDDLE, SIRIUS, BUDDY, MIST-CF) on held-out MS/MS benchmark spectra and you need ion-mode-resolved top-k accuracy comparable to Fig. 5 of the FIDDLE paper.

name: ion-mode-stratified-analysis
description: Use when comparing predicted versus experimental MS/MS spectra acquired under both positive and negative ionization modes, so that mean cosine similarity and significance tests are reported per mode rather than pooled.

name: ion-of-interest-vs-background-partitioning
description: Use when HPTLC-HRMS data contains many EICs mixing analyte ions with background ions and the goal is to partition ion tracks into interesting vs background clusters before structure elucidation.

name: ion-peak-metric-csv-reporting
description: Use when extracted precursor-ion peak metrics (mass error, RT error, arrival time error) for auto-tracked and user-specified ions need to be packaged into CSV reports and JPG/PDF figures for operator inspection and batch tracking.

name: ion-species-mz-transformation
description: Use when reference and target LC-HRMS feature lists contain the same metabolites detected as different ion species/adducts, and peak matching fails or must be tested against an adduct swap.

name: ion-species-rule-matching
description: Use when LC/MS peak lists (e.g. XCMS feature tables) contain co-eluting features whose m/z differences match known adducts or losses and you need to reduce feature redundancy and identify quasi-molecular ions.

name: ion-species-spectrum-aggregation
description: Use when building or extending MS/MS spectral libraries from feature-based molecular networking outputs, specifically to propagate a high-confidence library match (cosine >0.9) to other ion species (adducts, multimers, in-source fragments) of the same compound.

name: ionic-compound-exclusion
description: Use when curating large molecule sets (SDF/SMILES from databases like NIST, ChEMBL, HMDB) before spectrum prediction, and neutral-only compounds are required for EI-MS library building.

name: ionisation-mode-metadata-filtering
description: Use when importing an annotated MS/MS spectral library (e.g. GNPS MGF) and the downstream model or pipeline requires spectra restricted to one ionisation mode and valid metadata such as ionmode and precursor m/z.

name: ionization-mode-count-tabulation
description: Use when a results-section text or figure reports metabolite/peak counts per ionisation mode (e.g. positive and negative ESI) and the counts must be extracted, consistency-checked against a stated total, and tabulated.

name: ionization-mode-feature-count-comparison
description: Use when raw untargeted metabolomics LC-MS/MS data must be processed with two distinct peak-picking parameter sets (e.g., AutoTuner- vs. IPO-derived centWave parameters) and downstream feature-table differences need to be quantified per ionization mode.

name: ionization-mode-filtering
description: Use when assembling curated training libraries (library.csv) or benchmark query CSVs from NIST'17, MS-DIAL, or MSnLib spectra and entries carry heterogeneous precursor types that must be reduced to the modes used by the model.

name: ionization-mode-inference
