name: isotopic-pattern-prediction-for-lipids
description: Use when MSI lipidomics ion images contain same-class lipid species differing by one double bond (e.g., PC 38:3 vs PC 38:2, PE 38:3 vs PE 38:4) whose monoisotopic signals are inflated by the M+2 isotopologue of the more unsaturated isobar.

name: isotopic-pattern-similarity-scoring
description: Use when annotating ion peaks from an imaging MS feature matrix (e.g., 14,260 pixels x 3,044 ions) against a metabolite library and you need isotopic-pattern similarity as one of the multi-evidence scores for candidate ranking.

name: isotopic-peak-pair-detection
description: Use when a pixel x m/z feature matrix from an imaging mass spectrometry run (e.g., AFAD-ESI positive mode) must be classified into isotopic peak pairs and adduct ion pairs ([M+H]+, [M+K]+, [M+Na]+, [M+NH4]+, [M+H-H2O]+) before metabolite annotation.

name: isotopic-peak-pair-identification
description: Use when you have a preprocessed spatial metabolomics peak table (X/Y pixel coordinates plus m/z ion columns) and need to quantify what fraction of ions are isotopic peaks or flag ion pairs whose spatial intensity patterns co-vary.

name: isotopic-profile-theoretical-vs-experimental-matching
description: Use when annotating untargeted LC/HRMS peaks (mzXML, mzML, netCDF) with molecular formulas from only MS1-level data, especially when database-dependent tools (MetDNA, SIRIUS, ZODIAC) risk missing exposome compounds absent from biochemical databases.

name: isotopic-signature-detection
description: Use when the input is a DEIMoS-aligned multi-sample feature table (e.g. example_alignment.h5) in an N-dimensional space (m/z, drift time, retention time) and the goal is to glean ion charge state or identification evidence from isotopic signatures.

name: isotopic-species-quantification-from-hsqc
description: Use when a pseudo-2D (e.g. 1H-13C HSQC) isotope-labeling NMR series must be decomposed into individual isotopic species and their relative abundances quantified, especially with overlapping peaks.

name: isotopic-subnetwork-partitioning
description: Use when you have a preprocessed LC-MS feature table (e.g. asari 1.9.2 TSV with feature ID, m/z, rtime, intensities) and need to group adduct/isotope-related features into empirical compounds with inferred neutral M0 masses, without prior formulas.

name: isotopic-trace-peak-shape-filtering
description: Use when filtering raw FeatureFinderMetabo output from centroided ddMS2 mzML data to remove spurious or poorly shaped features before blank correction and PFAS prioritization.

name: isotopically-labeled-lipid-library-qc
description: Use when a workflow imports U13C_DT_CCS_library.csv from the FelinaHildebrand/MobiLipid repository and must confirm the 377-value, 162-lipid-species, 15-class curation is intact before internal standardization.

name: isotopically-nonstationary-metabolic-flux-analysis
description: Use when time-course stable-isotope labeling data (e.g., [13C5,15N2] glutamate 0-8 h sampling) have been processed into natural-abundance-corrected isotopologue distributions and fluxes with confidence intervals are needed.

name: isotopologue-12c-13c-peak-handling
description: Use when grouping co-eluting MS1 peaks into CSA clusters from IDSL.IPA peaklists/peak_alignment directories and you must decide whether an m/z-shifted neighbor is a genuine 12C/13C isotopologue of the seed peak.

name: isotopologue-abundance-normalization
description: Use when tracer quantification output (e.g. from TarMet's isotope tracer assay on 13C6-glucose samples) provides raw isotopologue peak areas (M+1, M+2, ...) and you need per-metabolite fractional labeling to check pathway-position labeling patterns.

name: isotopologue-adduct-annotation
description: Use when processing centroid-mode AIF LC–MS metabolomics chromatograms and you need to assign isotopologues, adducts, and in-source fragments across features, especially when focusing on a statistically significant subset rather than the full dataset.

name: isotopologue-chromatographic-peak-extraction
description: Use when generating a benchmark dataset from user-provided molecules with known composition and retention-time boundaries, requiring isotopologue-level peak extraction from mzML files before NPP reliability assessment.

name: isotopologue-correction-method-comparison
description: Use when comparing how isotope-correction schemes (MDT, ULS, NRE) perform on FAM/MDV data for labeled metabolites at a stated nominal instrument resolution (e.g. 140,000 or 280,000 Orbitrap), or when choosing MDT vs ULS for a tracer/compound class.

name: isotopologue-deconvolution-model-selection
description: Use when MS-measured isotopologue timecourses (single or multiple isotope tracers, e.g. 13C UDP-GlcNAc SIRM data) must be deconvoluted into moiety abundances and the -fitting deconvolution model must be chosen from several plausible models.

name: isotopologue-distribution-fitting
description: Use when HRMS data from a transient stable-isotope labeling time course (e.g., [13C5,15N2]glutamine or [U-13C6]glucose) must be converted to isotopologue distributions and used to estimate metabolic fluxes.

name: isotopologue-distribution-normalization
description: Use when single-cell isotope-tracing data (SpaceM spatiomolecular anndata objects, per-cell ion intensities for fatty acids like palmitate C16:0 and oleate C18:1) must be converted to corrected, normalized isotopologue fractions before binomial-fitting uptake estimates.

name: isotopologue-distribution-simulation
description: Use when you have a list of molecular formulae and need their monoisotopic masses plus theoretical isotopologue patterns (including adducts and multiply charged species) to target ions in LC-IM-MS or MS data.

name: isotopologue-envelope-extraction
description: Use when khipu has preannotated untargeted metabolomics or stable isotope tracing data (e.g. U-13C E. coli, 548 empCpds from 3,602 asari features) and you need to extract per-compound isotope-index envelopes for downstream labeling analysis.

name: isotopologue-fractional-abundance-correction
description: Use when LC-MS data from isotope labeling experiments (FAM vectors per compound/sample, e.g. XLSX input) must be corrected for natural abundance, tracer isotopic impurity, and resolution effects before deriving MDVs and enrichment.

name: isotopologue-intensity-forward-calculation
description: Use when a measured MS isotopologue profile of a multi-moiety metabolite (e.g. single-tracer 13C UDP-GlcNAc timecourses or multi-tracer 13C/18O data) must be reconstructed from moiety state fractional abundances, i.e. computing I_x,calc per isotopologue mass shift from a moiety model.

name: isotopologue-intensity-simulation-from-moiety-models
description: Use when you need Monte Carlo benchmarking of how measurement noise propagates through moiety-model-derived isotopologue profiles — e.g. comparing 13C-only vs 13C/18O glucose multi-tracer error behavior at defined sigma levels.

name: isotopologue-ion-image-extraction-from-imzml
description: Use when MALDI imaging data are stored as imzML and you need ion images for all isotopologues of specific molecules (e.g. fatty acids 20:3, 20:4, 20:5, 22:4, 22:5) from an ion list, rather than only the annotated natural-abundance peaks from METASPACE.

name: isotopologue-ion-pairing
description: Use when processing untargeted LC/HRMS (mzXML, mzML, netCDF) data where redundant isotope peaks inflate peak lists and only carbon-containing compound signals (12C monoisotopic isotopologues) should be retained.

name: isotopologue-labelling-visualization-of-metabolic-flux
description: Use when TarMet has produced a peak-area table of 13C isotopologues for labelled samples (e.g. MRC5 cells labelled 5 or 60 min with 13C6-glucose) and the goal is to visualize labelling patterns across metabolites and assess parallel-sample consistency.

name: isotopologue-mass-difference-calculation
description: Use when building a resolution-dependent isotopologue correction matrix for a compound formula at a given nominal instrument resolution, and you must decide which same-nominal-mass isotopologs (e.g. 17O vs 15N/13C contributions) can be resolved and which correction-matrix columns to zero.

name: isotopologue-mass-shift-detection
description: Use when pairwise LC/MS feature tables from an isotope-supplemented condition (e.g. 13C6-leucine) and an unlabeled control must be compared to find labeled features via a specific mass shift, or to test whether particular lipids derive from a labeled precursor.

name: isotopologue-pairing-assessment
description: Use when processing untargeted LC/HRMS mzXML/mzML/netCDF data with IDSL.IPA and you need to suppress redundant isotope/adduct-like peaks by pairing 12C and 13C signals within each scan, or when troubleshooting why peaks were excluded by nIsoPair/RCS thresholds.

name: isotopologue-pairing-quality-threshold-evaluation
description: Use when comparing IDSL.IPA peak lists (e.g. 20,253 peaks for MTBLS1684 file 003.d) against MZmine 2, xcms-CAMERA or MS-DIAL output and you must attribute missing peaks to isotopologue pairing or peak quality thresholds.

name: isotopologue-pattern-interpretation
description: Use when a preprocessed feature table contains unexplained ion groups whose members differ by isotope or adduct mass shifts (e.g. 1.0034 Da 13C/12C, 22.9893 Da Na+), or when annotating U-13C-labeled tracing samples.

name: isotopologue-pattern-matching
description: Use when performing targeted LC-MS stable-isotope-tracer or isotopologue analysis: you have defined target metabolites, extracted M+H isotopologue EICs per sample, and need to score observed isotope patterns against theoretical patterns at the MS resolution.

name: isotopologue-peak-quantification
description: Use when you have EICs for a targeted isotopologue across multiple tracer samples (e.g. 13C6-glucose labelling) and need retention-time-aligned peak areas per sample for isotopologue quantification.

name: isotopologue-peak-selection-targeted-ms
description: Use when quantifying a targeted metabolite and its isotopologues from LC-MS EICs where multiple peaks are detected per isotopologue and the correct target peak must be chosen via isotope-pattern similarity.

name: isotopologue-ppm-error-verification
description: Use when processing high-resolution (Orbitrap) centroided GC-MS mzML files with isoSCAN autoQ in stable-isotope labeling experiments and you must confirm that the integrated isotopologue peaks correspond to the predicted m/z values within the allowed mass error before reporting enrichment.

name: isotopologue-profile-normalization
description: Use when mass spectrometry isotopologue profiles (e.g. 13C UDP-GlcNAc timecourses) must be reconstructed from moiety state fractional abundances, or when validating deconvolution outputs against measured isotopologue distributions.

name: isotopologue-quantification
description: Use when centWave-processed LC-MS chromatograms of known target metabolites must be quantified per adduct (M+H, M+Na, M+K) with isotopologue-level confidence, including isotope tracer assays.

name: isotopologue-ratio-quality-assessment
description: Use when assessing peak-abundance quality of XCMS or MZmine 2 pre-processing output against an mzRAPP benchmark — i.e. quantifying what fraction of matched peaks show degenerated isotopologue ratios.

name: isotopologue-timecourse-parameter-optimization
description: Use when you need to solve the boundary-value inverse problem of fitting moiety model parameters to MS-measured isotopologue timecourse data, and/or to select among multiple plausible moiety models via AICc.

name: isotopologue-to-nmol-13c-unit-conversion
description: Use when isotopologue distributions from a [U-13C6]glucose or similar tracer HRMS time course have already been natural-abundance corrected (NACorrectionFxnII) and the goal is to express enrichment as nmol of 13C-labeled molecules formed per time point for kinetic clustering or precursor-product.

name: isotopologue-trace-confirmation
description: Use when building LC-IM-MS (drift tube IM-MS) databases from profile mzML files for a list of molecular formulae, and candidate primary-ion m/z traces must be confirmed by isotopologue matching after RT peak picking.

name: isotopomer-distribution-comparison
description: Use when two isotopomer distributions for the same metabolite are available — one from a classical NMR multiplet fit over a restricted isotopomer subset and one from the deep-learning fit over all possible isotopomers — and their agreement must be quantified.

name: istd-normalization-rsd-calculation
description: Use when peak-area tables from GC-MS amino acid analysis must be ISTD-normalized one-to-one and precision summarized as average RSD to compare derivatization agents (PCF, MTBSTFA, MSTFA) across plasma sample sets.

name: iterative-module-assignment-wgcna
description: Use when a large metabolite abundance matrix (peak-area feature table, metabolites × samples) must be partitioned into co-accumulation modules and hub metabolites, and group-based DAM comparison is impractical.

name: iterative-threshold-convergence-estimation
description: Use when processing raw LC/MS mzML files where signal-detection thresholds cannot be set manually and must be learned from the data itself until convergence.

name: iteratively-reweighted-pls-baseline-fitting
description: Use when 1H-NMR spectra (rows = samples, columns = chemical shifts in ppm) still show baseline drift after internal referencing — e.

name: iupac-name-feature-parsing
description: Use when input compounds carry only IUPAC names (no structure strings) and structural features must still be extracted for taxonomy classification, or when name-parsing must be validated against OPSIN-converted structures.

name: j-coupled-spin-system-discrepancy-interpretation
description: Use when comparing two simulated MRS metabolite basis sets (e.g. MRSCloud vs MARSS) and some metabolites show larger basis-function discrepancies than others, requiring judgment on whether differences stem from complex J-coupling spin systems rather than simulation error.

name: j-coupling-multiplet-structure-analysis
description: Use when 1D or pseudo-2D NMR spectra (1H, 13C, 15N, 31P, etc.) contain multiplet signals whose chemical shift, intensity, area, linewidth, and J coupling constants must be quantified, including overlapping peaks.

name: j-coupling-spin-system-parameterization
description: Use when building metabolite basis functions for MRS fitting (e.g., PRESS, MEGA-PRESS, HERMES, HERCULES) and the spin-system Hamiltonians — J-coupling values and chemical shifts per metabolite — must be specified before density-matrix simulation.

name: jaccard-analyte-overlap-scoring
description: Use when a pathway enrichment result table contains many overlapping enriched pathways (within or across pathway databases) and you need to quantify and cluster their analyte-membership redundancy before interpretation.

name: jaccard-co-occurrence-filtering
description: Use when a KNN classifier has returned candidate GCF labels for MS/MS spectra from paired genome-metabolome samples and predictions must be pruned by biosynthetic co-occurrence before computing precision or prioritizing links.

name: jaccard-coefficient-edge-filtering
description: Use when you have a network representation of the GWAS Catalog gene sets and need to prune non-significant study-study edges and extract disease/trait-specific subnetworks for downstream over-representation analysis.

name: jaccard-cooccurrence-filtering-of-bgc-msms-links
description: Use when NPOmix KNN classification has produced candidate gene cluster family (GCF)-to-MS/MS spectrum links and you need a post-hoc confidence filter scored against PoDP-validated gene-metabolite links.

name: jaccard-cooccurrence-link-validation
description: Use when NPOmix KNN votes have produced candidate GCF assignments for query MS/MS spectra and you must score link confidence (e.g. top-1 precision, Jaccard co-occurrence threshold) before accepting a spectrum-to-GCF link.

name: jaccard-index-component-counting
description: Use when you need pairwise structural similarity of lipid species from molecular graphs, e.g., to verify MCS/Jaccard overlap counts for structurally similar lipids or to quantify how double-bond position information changes lipid-lipid distances.

name: jaccard-index-metabolic-reaction-comparison
description: Use when comparing the metabolisms of two organisms selected from the KEGG database quantitatively: KGML files are available, reaction sets per pathway can be reconstructed, and global similarity indexes (Psim, PsimW, Csim) are the desired output.

name: jaccard-mask-overlap-evaluation
description: Use when an IFM image has been warped into the MALDI MSI frame (e.g. via ANTs SyNRA in msiFlow's msi_if_registration_flow) and you need a quantitative overlap metric to validate registration accuracy.

name: jaccard-maximum-common-subgraph-similarity
description: Use when lipid species names must be compared by molecular structure rather than exact name matching, e.g. to build structural distance matrices across heterogeneous lipidomes from csv/xlsx or mzTab-M lipidomics tables.

name: jaccard-ordination-health-status
description: Use when MASST matches of synthesized compounds have been joined to ReDU sample metadata (biospecimen/tissue, health phenotype) and you need to test whether sample groups cluster by health status or tissue based on shared detected conjugates.

name: jaccard-overlap-scoring-of-peak-sets
description: Use when a set of significant 1D NMR peaks (ppm values) has been clustered by Pearson correlation and you must rank HMDB metabolite matches by how well their expected peak patterns overlap the cluster.

name: jaccard-peak-overlap-scoring
description: Use when ranking candidate compounds for an unknown GC/EI-MS analyte where cosine spectrum similarity alone leaves the true compound below rank 1, and DeepEI-predicted fingerprints (msp-merged) are available for the analyte and enumerated candidates.

name: jaccard-reaction-set-overlap-analysis
description: Use when comparing the reaction content of corresponding KEGG reference pathways in two organisms, and you need a normalized per-pathway similarity in [0,1] computed over reaction sets or multisets.

name: jaccard-score-cross-validation
description: Use when evaluating a sparse-positive molecular site-of-metabolism classifier (e.g. ~5% reactive bonds) where accuracy is mis and per-class/isoform Jaccard scores from external cross-validation are the appropriate metric.

name: jaccard-score-metric-computation
description: Use when evaluating a bond- or site-level predictor whose output is a set of predicted locations (e.g., BoMX−Y pairs or SoMs) per molecule, and you need a single per-class score that penalizes false positives and false negatives symmetrically.

name: jaccard-set-similarity-on-reaction-sets
description: Use when two organisms' metabolisms have been reconstructed from KEGG KGML into per-pathway reaction sets and you need quantitative local and global functional similarity between them.

name: jaccard-similarity-computation
description: Use when scoring isomer-pair MS/MS similarity from multi-collision-energy spectra (e.g., NCE 1–100%) to build I/N-ratio-based identification criteria, or when comparing Jaccard vs dot product/entropy sensitivity-specificity on spectral libraries like CQMD.

name: jaccard-similarity-computation
description: Use when quantifying metabolite-content overlap between pathway pairs — e.g., building a pairwise Jaccard redundancy matrix across KEGG, Reactome, and WikiPathways pathways stored in RaMP to identify which database pairs show the largest overlap.

name: jaccard-similarity-index-computation
description: Use when the goal is to quantify how similar the metabolisms of two (or more) KEGG organisms are, either locally (per reference pathway) or globally (whole metabolism), e.

name: jaccard-similarity-matrix-computation
description: Use when you have binary gene membership sets (e.g., per-tissue DE gene lists from the MoTrPAC rat EET study) and need to measure how concordant or tissue-specific the sets are across conditions or tissues.

name: jaccard-similarity-scoring-multi-collision-energy-fragments
description: Use when query MS/MS spectra are acquired at multiple collision energies and must be matched to multi-CE reference spectra (e.g. Exploris 480 queries vs. CQMD Exploris 120 references) to call metabolite identifications under Figure 2 cutoff criteria.

name: jaccard-similarity-scoring-of-longitudinal-fragment-profiles
description: Use when annotating metabolites from MS/MS spectra acquired at multiple distinct collision energies (e.g. 13 CEs or stepped NCE 20/40/60%), where cross-sectional scoring misranks isomers with similar predominant fragments.

name: jaccard-similarity-scoring-of-molecular-structures
description: Use when benchmarking spectral similarity or alignment algorithms and a per-pair structural similarity ground truth is needed for compound pairs with known SMILES from GNPS library metadata or MassBank records.

name: jaccard-similarity-spectrum-scoring
description: Use when experimental and reference MS/MS spectra are available at multiple collision energies (e.g., stepped NCE 20/40/60%) and you must identify metabolites or quantify correct-match rates against an isomer-rich library.

name: jackknife-resampling-visualization
description: Use when QIIME principal coordinates files from replicate (jackknifed) beta diversity analyses plus a metadata mapping file must be rendered as per-sample confidence ellipsoids in an interactive 3D PCoA visualization.

name: jacobian-matrix-computation-from-metabolic-interaction-networks
description: Use when a metabolomics study has preprocessed concentration data, a defined interaction network, and the goal is to quantify metabolite interactions via Jacobian matrices for specific conditions (e.g., 6C vs 16C).

name: jacobian-matrix-network-inference
description: Use when raw metabolomic data or MetaboAnalyst-derived metabolite inputs need to be converted into a network of dynamic metabolite interactions via Jacobian matrix computation, with topology metrics.

name: java-algorithm-implementation
description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking a published peak-list alignment (or similar MS data-processing) algorithm in Java, where the method must be re-implemented from the paper's description and evaluated against known ground-truth tables.

name: java-module-development
description: Use when a new MS data-processing step (e.g., the RANSAC peak list alignment) must be added to MZmine 2 as a Java module, or when building the framework from source is required.

name: java-scientific-computing
description: Use when implementing statistical analyses (e.g. B-spline mutual information, hierarchical clustering, Pearson/Spearman correlations) in Java on numeric expression matrices, or when reusing MOG's Java analysis modules.

name: java-webapp-module-development
description: Use when a scientific data infrastructure (e.g., spectral or metadata databases) must be implemented or extended as a Java Web application with REST endpoints, a Web interface, and a Maven/Tomcat build-deploy chain.

name: javascript-implementation-of-bioinformatics-algorithms
description: Use when a pairwise distance matrix (e.g., compareMS2 distances between LC-MS/MS datasets) must be converted into a rooted phylogenetic tree in Newick format, or when porting a clustering/phylogenetics algorithm into a JavaScript/Electron GUI.

name: jcamp-data-point-extraction
description: Use when the input is a JCAMP-DX (or mzML-converted-to-JCAMP-DX) spectrum file whose data table of x/y pairs must be parsed out before peak-picking, plotting, or writing a peaks list.

name: jcamp-dx-data-type-block-classification
description: Use when you need to automatically determine the spectra type (NMR, IR, MS, UV/VIS, XRD, CV, LC/MS) of an uploaded JCAMP-DX file before routing it to the correct conversion or analysis path in the chem-spectra-app backend.

name: jcamp-file-conversion
description: Use when input spectra are in mzML, proprietary RAW/FID, Bruker zip, or other non-JCAMP-DX formats and must be normalized to open JCAMP-DX (IR, MS, 1H/13C NMR) for ELN storage, editing, or image generation.

name: jcamp-peak-table-composition
description: Use when detected peak positions must be converted into an annotated peak table/label file (e.g. IR wavenumbers with bracketed vw/w/m/s/vs intensity labels) for export as JCAMP-DX metadata or ELN transfer.

name: jcamp-spectrum-parsing
description: Use when the input is a JCAMP-DX spectrum (or a file already converted to JCAMP-DX, e.g. mzML converted via pymzML) and the x/y data points must be extracted as the basis for peak picking, annotation, or peaks output.

name: jit-warmup-outlier-exclusion
description: Use when benchmarking spectrum_utils or other Numba-compiled Python spectral-processing pipelines against baselines (pymzML, pyOpenMS) and you need to remove first-call JIT compilation overhead before comparing per-spectrum runtimes.

name: joined-chromatogram-preparation-for-multivariate-analysis

name: joint-2d-topology-3d-geometry-denoising

name: joint-distribution-visualization
description: Use when comparing a spectral predictor's quality metric (e.g., cosine similarity) against a coverage-type covariate (annotated peak-intensity fraction) across two benchmark datasets to expose a bounding relationship and annotation-rate differences.

name: joint-embedding-similarity-ranking
description: Use when you have a query tandem MS spectrum plus a candidate molecule list (e.g. PubChem candidates in cand_dict.pkl) and need to rank candidates by structural match, reporting rank@k metrics such as rank@5 and rank@20.

name: joint-pathway-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when a curated metabolite-protein subnetwork (e.g. from PIUMet Steiner forest analysis of high-contribution m/z peaks) must be mapped onto metabolic pathways to find disease-relevant pathways.

name: jpa-feature-level-stratification-pp-mr
description: Use when an aligned JPA feature table must be quality-checked by extraction level — e.g. comparing quantitative precision of MS2-recognition (MR) rescued features vs conventional peak-picking (PP) features across replicate samples before statistical analysis.

name: jres-skyline-projection-generation

name: json-conversion-directive-semantics-implementation

name: json-lipid-database-schema-authoring

description: Use when submitting, curating, or consuming MIBiG 2.0 BGC entries in JSON annotation format, or before sideloading a MIBiG annotation file into the customised antiSMASH 5 BGC-page module.

name: json-schema-validation-of-metabolomics-metadata
description: Use when tabular experimental metadata (Excel/CSV) has been extracted to JSON via MESSES and must be checked against the Experiment Description Specification, a PDS, or custom JSON schema before conversion to mwTab.

name: json-schema-validation-testing
description: Use when auditing or reproducing the automated test coverage of a Python package that validates extracted JSON against JSON schemas (Experiment Description Specification, Protocol Dependent Schema, format-specific schemas), or when establishing a >90% coverage baseline for schema-validation code.

name: json-serialization-of-chemont-annotations
description: Use when a chemical classification pipeline must expose ChemOnt annotations (category IDs, textual descriptions, per-compound results) in a machine-readable JSON payload for downstream programmatic access.

name: json-to-xml-format-conversion
description: Use when quantifying the storage-size penalty of XML vs JSON for the same metadata content, e.g. to justify a JSON-based index format like Aird's AirdMetaData.json or to benchmark format verbosity.

name: jsonized-data-modification-handling
description: Use when a tagged spreadsheet extraction must apply #modify directives to rename or revalue data, or when already-produced MESSES JSON records need name/value modification or lineage rendering rather than a fresh extraction.

name: jsonized-format-download-qc
description: Use when auditing the download integrity and parseability of a large batch of Metabolomics Workbench analyses (e.g. all 1891 analyses) in the JSONized format, to identify blank/un-downloadable and un-parseable entries for curation.

name: jsonschema-metadata-validation
description: Use when a MESSES 'extract' step has produced JSONized metadata from tagged tabular data (Excel/CSV) and it must be checked for errors and schema compliance before running 'convert' toward Metabolomics Workbench deposition.

name: jupyter-notebook-end-to-end-execution
description: Use when the task is to reproduce or rerun a published ICA decomposition of cancer omics data via the review's companion notebook rather than reimplementing ICA from scratch.

name: jupyter-notebook-reproducible-execution
description: Use when a companion repository (e.g. bittremieux/GNPS_GC) provides example notebooks and workflow output files (edges, annotated spectra tables), and the goal is to re-run the analysis to validate a published figure or table.

name: jupyter-notebook-workflow-execution
description: Use when a computational workflow is distributed as a self-documented .ipynb notebook (e.g. CCS prediction, metabolomics filtering) that must be run end-to-end in Jupyter Lab, Jupyter Notebook, or Google Colab with all packages installed per its requirements file.

name: k-fold-cross-validation-of-deep-models
description: Use when training a deep learning model on high-dimensional spectra (e.g., 85,062 m/z variables) and you need to demonstrate that optimization converges stably rather than depending on a lucky train/validation split.

name: k-fold-cross-validation-training
description: Use when training deep learning (ResNet50, DenseNet121, LSTM, Transformer) or traditional ML classifiers on TIC-normalized MS spectra and you need fold-level performance estimates plus paired statistical comparison of an augmentation module against baselines.

name: k-means-clustering-of-labeling-kinetics
description: Use when NA-corrected isotopologue distributions from a stable-isotope time course (e.g., [U-13C6]glucose 0–32 h lipidomics) have been converted to molar 13C quantities and species must be grouped by labeling kinetics.

name: k-means-clustering-outlier-score-heuristics
description: Use when estimating the mass error (ppm) centWave parameter from extracted-ion chromatograms of detected TIC peaks in raw untargeted metabolomics data (mzML, mzXML, CDF), needing to separate true-feature ppm values from noise-derived ppm values.

name: k-medoids-cluster-context-analysis
description: Use when a differential feature flagged by globaltest-based statistical testing of msFeaST feature groups needs its connectivity context quantified — e.

name: k-medoids-feature-grouping
description: Use when you have an LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics feature table with associated MS/MS spectra and need to aggregate features into structurally similar groups before feature-set (group-wise) statistical testing.

name: k-medoids-partitioning
description: Use when an LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics workflow needs structurally similar features grouped together — i.e., a pairwise spectral (dis)similarity distance matrix is available and a feature-grouping proxy for downstream feature-set testing must be generated.

name: k-medoids-spectral-feature-clustering
description: Use when processing untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics feature tables paired with MS/MS peak lists and you need structurally similar features grouped so clusters can serve as feature sets in group-wise statistical testing.

name: kaplan-meier-curve-visualization
description: Use when metabolomics samples have survival times and event indicators and you need to visually validate risk-group stratification from a fitted Cox-PH or Cox-nnet model on pathway deregulation score (PDS) features.

name: kaplan-meier-survival-curve-estimation
description: Use when the input is a survival table with sample IDs, survival times, censoring status, and group labels (like surv_example.csv) and the goal is a publication-ready survival curve figure per group.

name: kaplan-meier-survival-stratification
description: Use when patient-level metadata includes overall survival time/event and predicted risk groups (e.g. VAE embeddings or IMDC classes) and you must test whether groups separate by OS via KM curves and log-rank p-values.

name: kappa-sharpness-parameter-tuning
description: Use when running Magnetstein on a 1H NMR mixture where default parameters underperform — e.g., a ~1:10 two-component mixture, spectra with contaminant peaks, or low-field benchtop spectra — and per-component RE/AvRE must be optimized.

name: kegg-api-orthology-retrieval
description: Use when a metabolomics data frame of KEGG compound identifiers contains significant metabolites (e.g. adjusted p <= 0.05) and you need the enzyme orthologies and genes an organism has for metabolizing those compounds.

name: kegg-biocarta-geneset-mapping
description: Use when a microarray-style expression matrix must be partitioned into predefined pathway gene sets (KEGG/Biocarta) before computing pathway activity scores or differential pathway rankings.

name: kegg-compound-hierarchy-annotation
description: Use when a metabolomics count data frame has KEGG compound identifiers and downstream statistics, bar plots, or volcano plots need per-metabolite class/subclass metadata from the KEGG hierarchy.

name: kegg-compound-identifier-mapping
description: Use when extracting or anchoring layer-1 metabolic-reaction-network (KMRN) subnetworks in MetDNA2Vis and you must specify centric metabolites by KEGG compound IDs (C00082) or extended unknown IDs (KeggExd000923) with is_unknown_annotation = TRUE.

name: kegg-compound-identifier-matching
description: Use when a list of lipid annotations (e.g. shorthand notations like PC 16:0_18:2) must be matched to KEGG compound IDs — or ChEBI/LION identifiers — as a prerequisite for pathway (KEGG, Reactome) or ontology-based lipidome analysis.

name: kegg-compound-matching
description: Use when you have an untargeted LC-MS peak list (m/z, retention time, intensity) and need to map each peak to candidate KEGG compounds via adduct/fragment-aware m/z matching before annotation prioritization.

name: kegg-compound-pathway-mapping
description: Use when you have an annotation matrix pairing peak IDs with KEGG (Cxxxxx) or ChEBI IDs and need to build peak-to-pathway membership tables for metabolite-set activity scoring with PALS.

name: kegg-compound-reference-mapping
description: Use when an untargeted LC-MS feature/peak list must be assigned initial KEGG compound candidates by m/z matching before any biological-context scoring, or when reproducing mWISE's matching stage to benchmark annotators against KEGG-only databases.

name: kegg-database-matching
description: Use when starting an mWISE annotation run on unannotated LC-MS peak lists (m/z features) and you need KEGG compound candidates before applying the cluster-based filter and diffusion scoring.

name: kegg-gene-to-modelseed-reaction-mapping
description: Use when the input is an annotated amino acid FASTA (Type 1) and the goal is a KEGG-annotation-based draft GENRE whose reactions are traceable to genes via ModelSEED reaction IDs.

name: kegg-identifier-based-compound-classification
description: Use when a metabolomics count data frame contains KEGG compound identifiers and each feature needs hierarchical class/subclass metadata attached before statistical testing or figure faceting.

name: kegg-kgml-pathway-data-retrieval
description: Use when the goal is to automatically reconstruct a metabolic network for one or two KEGG organisms from KEGG database information, requiring organism-specific KGML downloads and parsing of compounds and reactions.

name: kegg-kgml-reaction-extraction
description: Use when building the functional level of a KEGG-based metabolic network for an organism: you need, per reference pathway, the set or multiset of reactions (and compounds) that MetNet compares between two organisms.

name: kegg-metabolite-database-searching
description: Use when you have preprocessed LC/MS feature tables (m/z per feature, e.g. from apLCMS cdf.to.ftr or XCMS centWave) and need to quantify how many features can be matched to known metabolites via KEGG.

name: kegg-module-annotation-mapping
description: Use when a large phylogeny (thousands of taxa, e.g. PhyloXML) must be annotated per leaf with KEGG module presence/absence or genome-size metadata as external rings in a circular cladogram.

name: kegg-module-enrichment-interpretation
description: Use when you have a full (unprefiltered) KO/compound abundance table plus sample metadata with grouping, and need threshold-free, multi-group or longitudinal KEGG pathway/module enrichment rather than single-list over-representation.

name: kegg-organism-network-structural-comparison
description: Use when you have reconstructed the two-level metabolic networks of two KEGG organisms and need to compare their structural level — pathway connectivity through shared non-ubiquitous compounds — pathway by pathway or globally.

name: kegg-ortholog-functional-annotation
description: Use when raw paired-end metagenome reads must be converted into per-sample KEGG ortholog (KO) abundance profiles using predicted operon sequences as the alignment reference, e.g. for disease-vs-control pathway association testing.

name: kegg-ortholog-hierarchical-rendering
description: Use when you have a HUMAnN-derived KEGG functional profile matrix plus a LEfSe biomarker result and need a publication-quality circular functional tree highlighting pathways enriched in contrasting sample cohorts.

name: kegg-pathway-abundance-profiling
description: Use when you have raw fecal shallow shotgun metagenomics sequencing data (e.g. the n=666 3xTg/WT Sacrifice cohort deposit on Qiita) and need per-sample KEGG pathway abundances plus genotype-level enrichment/depletion calls.

name: kegg-pathway-accessibility-quantification
description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics experiment (e.g. MetaboLights MTBLS136 split by assay type) needs its assay-specific chemical bias quantified as a count or proportion of KEGG human pathways reachable for ORA.

name: kegg-pathway-adjacency-construction
description: Use when a KEGG organism code is available and the goal is a graph-based (topological) representation of its metabolism — pathways as nodes, shared-compound relations as edges — for later comparison or visualization.

name: kegg-pathway-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when standalone metabolomics data must be linked to disease/phenotype GWAS results by testing whether metabolite-interacting genes from KEGG pathways are over-represented in GWAS gene networks.

name: kegg-pathway-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when a metabolite list (KEGG compound IDs converted via MetaboAnalyst ID Conversion) must be mapped to KEGG pathways to find where the selected metabolites occur and ranked by occurrence count.

name: kegg-pathway-enrichment-interpretation
description: Use when a differential metabolomics experiment (e.g., control vs mutant lung cancer) yields a metabolite list or ranked statistics and you must identify significantly enriched KEGG pathways and prioritize them by biological impact.

name: kegg-pathway-graph-construction
description: Use when preparing pathway-level kernel association tests (e.g., PaIRKAT) on metabolomics data where each metabolite must be assigned to a KEGG pathway graph with reaction-derived topology.

name: kegg-pathway-id-resolution
description: Use when a metabolomics feature table contains non-standard identifiers (e.g., RI-coded names from GC retention time) that must be converted to standard compound IDs before KEGG pathway enrichment in MeTEor.

name: kegg-pathway-library-construction
description: Use when rebuilding or refreshing metabolomics pathway-analysis libraries from KEGG, or when verifying reported library counts (e.g. ~130 species, ~3700 RaMP-DB pathways) after a knowledgebase update.

name: kegg-pathway-map-url-generation
description: Use when a metabolomics workflow has converted compound identifiers (e.g. HMDB IDs) to KEGG IDs via MetaboAnalyst ID Conversion and needs ranked pathway enrichment plus interactive pathway-map links highlighting the query metabolites.

name: kegg-pathway-mapping
description: Use when a table of significant metabolites carrying KEGG compound IDs must be associated with KEGG pathways for a chosen species and ranked by enrichment p-value, as in the MetENP ST000915 workflow.

name: kegg-pathway-mapping
description: Use when an annotated feature table from LC-MS/MS metabolomics (e.g., GNPS2 FBMN with ChemWalker/SIRIUS annotations) needs KEGG compound-to-pathway assignment and cross-strain pathway comparison.

name: kegg-pathway-metabolite-retrieval
description: Use when MetaboAnalyst outputs ('name_map.csv' and 'pathway_results.csv') are available and KEGG pathways with FDR ≤ 0.05 must be populated with their member metabolites annotated as HMDB IDs.

name: kegg-pathway-network-mapping
description: Use when building species-specific metabolic networks from KEGG layouts and NCBI-RefSeq annotations and refining them with empirical metabolomics data to flag missing or disconnected reactions.

name: kegg-pathway-set-filtering
description: Use when assembling pathway sets from KEGG (or Reactome/BioCyc) as ORA input for metabolomics data, to exclude pathways with fewer than 3 compounds from the over-representation analysis.

name: kegg-pathway-set-property-characterization
description: Use when deciding between the KEGG organism-specific human compound-only pathway set (261 pathways, mean size 30) and the KEGG reference compound-only set (377 pathways, mean size 45) for ORA on metabolomics data, and you need quantitative evidence of how much more/larger pathways in one set drive.

name: kegg-pathway-similarity-index-computation
description: Use when two KEGG organisms' metabolic networks have been reconstructed from KGML files and you need quantitative pairwise comparison scores (SimPi, SimSi, Psim, PsimW, Csim) in [0,1].

name: kegg-pathway-topology-retrieval
description: Use when a multi-omics (gene + metabolite) pathway analysis needs the underlying KEGG pathway graph topology — node types, compound/gene identifiers, and gene–metabolite interactions — as input, e.g. to run eSPIA in the SMART 2.0 IOPA module.

name: kegg-pathway-visualization-overlay
description: Use when a metabolomics analysis needs a visual, pathway-level rendering of metabolite abundance changes on the canonical KEGG diagram after metabolites have been mapped to KEGG pathway IDs.

name: kegg-rclass-reaction-pair-retrieval
description: Use when reconstructing the KMRN layer of KGMN or any metabolic reaction network that needs curated known metabolite nodes and reactant-pair reaction edges from KEGG RCLASS as a knowledge seed.

name: kegg-reaction-gap-tabulation
description: Use when a metabolomics-driven network-refinement study reports reaction gaps against a reference metabolic database (e.g. KEGG) and these must be normalized into a per-reaction table with pathway class, species, and literature-support flags.

name: kegg-reaction-gene-retrieval
description: Use when a metabolite enrichment table (e.g. MetENP met_path output for a study like ST000915) has associated KEGG pathways and you need the underlying genes, reactions, EC enzymes, and each metabolite's reactant/product role.

name: kegg-reaction-network-mapping
description: Use when an untargeted LC-MS/MS peak table (MS1 m/z, RT, MS2 spectra) has seed 'known' peaks matched against a standard spectral library and you must annotate reaction-paired unknown peaks via a KEGG-style metabolic reaction network.

name: kegg-rest-api-querying
description: Use when a pathway-metabolite association table (met_path) already exists and you need gene IDs, EC numbers, reaction IDs, and reactant/product roles for the metabolites in those pathways.

name: kegg-rpair-edge-derivation
description: Use when building biochemical (substrate-product) reaction networks from a metabolite identifier list and the identifiers may be common database names or synonyms rather than KEGG compound IDs, with no pathway annotation required.

name: kegg-smpdb-pathway-set-enrichment
description: Use when you have sex-stratified (or group-stratified) differential metabolite tables and need to identify which biological pathways are enriched in one group versus another, mirroring the ferroptosis/bile-acid (male) and glutathione/cAMP/cGMP-PKG (female) CRC results.

name: keggrest-api-queries
description: Use when a metabolomics workflow yields compound IDs that must be linked to KEGG pathways and visualized on interactive pathway maps — e.g., the pathway enrichment step of MeTEor after metabolite ID conversion.

name: kendrick-mass-defect-homologous-series-detection
description: Use when MS1 feature lists (m/z, RT, carbon count) from LC- or GC-HRMS runs of PFAS-contaminated samples must be reduced by detecting fluorinated homologous series, e.g. CF2- or CF2O-based, prior to annotation.

name: kendrick-mass-defect-series-detection
description: Use when a blank-filtered LC-HRMS feature table from PFAS samples (e.g. AFFF) must be grouped into homologous series based on CF2-normalized Kendrick mass defect and RT-order logic, beyond suspect-list exact mass matching.

name: keras-deep-learning-model-construction

name: keras-model-summary-inspection
description: Use when a pretrained .h5 model must be replicated or audited and its architecture (layer names, shapes, parameter counts) needs to be verified programmatically.

name: keras-neural-network-hyperparameter-tuning

name: keras-tensorflow-model-compilation
description: Use when building or modifying a Keras/TensorFlow classification model — e.g. extending massNet's two-class normal/tumor output layer to K>1 classes via softmax and categorical cross-entropy.

name: keras-two-branch-neural-network-implementation

name: kernel-density-estimation

name: kernel-density-fold-change-estimation

name: kernel-density-pvalue-estimation

name: kernel-machine-score-test-power-estimation

name: kernel-machine-score-testing

name: kernel-score-test-statistic-computation

name: kinetic-equation-integration-into-flux-calculation
description: Use when running MetaboPAC's kinetic-equations approach on time-course relative-abundance (concMatrix/timeVec) data and a subset of kinetic terms for the reaction network are known a priori, so fluxes needed for penalty calculation must be inferred from metabolite rates of change.

name: kmd-homologous-series-analysis

name: kmeans-partitioning-cluster-assignment

name: kmeans-pixel-clustering-msi

name: kmeans-spatial-segmentation

name: kmeans-subcluster-family-clustering
description: Use when a large set of predicted sub-clusters (e.g. 108,085 PRESTO-STAT sub-clusters from 60,028 antiSMASH-DB BGCs) must be organised into related families and higher-level clans.

name: kmeans-subgroup-count-reconciliation

name: kmeans-voronoi-inverted-index-construction

name: knn-correlation-based-neighbor-imputation
description: Use when metabolomics datasets contain missing values (from LOD/MNAR or MAR mechanisms) and you need a correlation-distance KNN baseline imputation to benchmark against, or to reproduce KNN-CR arms in the paper's RMSE and MLCI evaluation workflows.

name: ko-abundance-statistical-testing

name: kruskal-wallis-differential-abundance-testing

name: lc-ms-feature-detection
description: Use when you have triplicate LC-HRMS data (e.g. standard-X/solvent-X) acquired in both positive and negative ionization modes and need a single aligned feature table spanning both polarities.

name: lc-ms-feature-detection
description: Use when raw centroided LC-MS1 spectra (e.g. mzML files from Metabolomics Workbench accessions like ST002796/ST002798) must be converted into a quantified MS1 feature table as the precursor step to MS2 deconvolution, DB searching, or pathway analysis.

name: lc-ms-feature-detection
description: Use when starting from raw LC-MS files (mzML or Bruker timsTOF .d/TDF2 DDA-PASEF) and you need nontargeted peak detection with 100% signal coverage, edge-bounded peak segments, and feature quality metadata.

name: lc-ms-feature-detection
description: Use when starting from centroided mzML (or Thermo .raw) acquisitions and an experiment directory with sample-name-to-file-path metadata, and you need feature tables (m/z + retention time per feature) for downstream QC, normalization, or annotation.

name: lc-ms-feature-detection
description: Use when centroided mzML LC-MS/MS runs (e.g. QTOF or Orbitrap spatial-mapping datasets) must be converted into a feature quantification matrix as the entry point of an Optimus/'ili cartography analysis.

name: lc-ms-feature-detection
description: Use when raw UHPLC-HRMS2 DDA data (Thermo RAW converted to mzXML/mzML) must be converted into a per-sample feature quantification table plus per-feature MS2 spectra (.mgf), before structural annotation or FBMN.

name: lc-ms-feature-detection-and-alignment
description: Use when raw LC-MS metabolomics data (e.g. MTBLS146 maternal plasma files in ~/GalaxyM-TestData/LCMS_DATA) must be converted from vendor spectra into a peak/feature table aligned across biological, blank and QC samples before filtering or PCA.

name: lc-ms-feature-detection-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating or comparing LC-MS metabolomics feature-detection tools on data with known ground truth, or when tuning FeatureFinderMetabo parameters under varying detector noise, mass error (e.g. 10 ppm vs 40 ppm), and distorted elution profiles.

name: lc-ms-feature-detection-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating or comparing LC-MS metabolomics feature-detection tools against a manually verified/certified reference feature list, or when reproducing the asari vs XCMS/MZmine benchmark counts.

name: lc-ms-feature-detection-centwave
description: Use when starting from centroid-mode mzML raw LC–MS files and per-sample chromatographic/spectral peaks must be located and converted into (retention time, m/z) features for downstream feature matrices.

name: lc-ms-feature-extraction
description: Use when starting from publicly deposited LC–MS/MS mzML raw files (e.g. Metabolomics Workbench) and you need chromatographic features with linked representative MS2 spectra as a feature table for downstream annotation.

name: lc-ms-feature-extraction
description: Use when processing raw mzXML LC-MS metabolomics or exposomics data (DDA mode) where low-abundant or bad-shape features are missed by conventional peak picking and deeper feature coverage is needed.

name: lc-ms-feature-extraction-openms
description: Use when raw mzML LC-MS runs (e.g. MTBLS562, QE_HF, TripleTOF_6600 benchmark datasets) must be converted into per-run feature lists (m/z, RT, area) for downstream alignment or for reproducing an OpenMS-based baseline.

name: lc-ms-feature-filtering
description: Use when a PATBS-processed LC-MS feature table with m/z, MS1/MS2, and retention information must be filtered to link in vivo metabolites to prototypes, especially when metabolites follow unpredictable (non-obvious) metabolic pathways.

name: lc-ms-feature-finding
description: Use when raw LC-HRMS data (e.g., a standard mixture vs. blank solvent, each in triplicate) must be converted to features grouped across analyses, especially to compare feature-finding algorithms or build a consensus feature list.

name: lc-ms-feature-grouping-analysis
description: Use when LC-MS peak data has been grouped by XCMS at two RT-window (bw) resolutions and you need to identify which peak groups (features) are misaligned before realignment.

name: lc-ms-feature-grouping-metacorrelate
description: Use when processing aligned LC-MS/MS feature lists where redundant ion species of the same compound must be connected before uploading to GNPS feature-based molecular networking with IIMN enabled.

name: lc-ms-feature-matching-across-platforms
description: Use when two or more LC-MS feature tables of the same or near-identical features were acquired on different mass spectrometry platforms and you need to test annotation robustness by comparing metabolite annotations against the same plant-specific MS database.

name: lc-ms-feature-matching-between-datasets
description: Use when two LC–MS feature tables (XCMS peak-picked, post-QC, each with RT, m/z, and FI medians per feature) must be matched across batches or cohorts, and Step 1 candidate matching leaves features in clusters with multiple matches requiring unique correspondence.

name: lc-ms-feature-matrix-missing-value-imputation
description: Use when a peak-intensity profile table from LC-MS or SRM-MS metabolomics/proteomics contains missing values that must be filled before applying the 80% rule-based peak filter, QC-RFSC drift correction, or multivariate statistics in statTarget.

name: lc-ms-feature-mz-annotation
description: Use when you have a pre-processed MS1 feature table (m/z + retention time) and a compound reference database with exact masses and RTs, and retention times are only partially transferable between labs or methods.

name: lc-ms-feature-pair-classifier-training
description: Use when labeled feature-pair data from aligned LC-MS runs (attributes: m/z, charge, RT, intensity) are available and the goal is to train or benchmark classifiers, e.g. testing whether a DNN outperforms RF/KNN/SVM/LR by AUC.

name: lc-ms-feature-quality-filtering
description: Use when raw mzML/mzXML LC-MS/MS files must be quality-filtered into feature tables prior to SIRIUS/ZODIAC formula annotation, or when reported per-dataset feature counts before and after filtering must be reproduced.

name: lc-ms-feature-quality-flagging
description: Use when a preprocessed LC-MS peak table (e.g. MS-DIAL output) must be quality-controlled before statistics: features detected in <70% of QC samples or with RSD ≥ 0.2 / D-ratio ≥ 0.4 need flagging.

name: lc-ms-feature-quality-metric-computation
description: Use when you have an XCMS peak-picked LC–MS untargeted metabolomics run (with pooled QC samples) and need numeric per-peak quality metrics to feed peak-quality classifiers or flag low-quality integrations.

name: lc-ms-feature-quantification
description: Use when centroided LC/MS data (mzML/mzXML) from multiple biological groups must be converted into a feature table (m/z, retention time, group-wise intensities) for comparative metabolomics.

name: lc-ms-feature-quantification-processing
description: Use when you have mzML LC–MS/MS runs needing feature detection, quantification, filtering, and level-2 putative compound annotation, or when MS/MS spectra must be exported (MGF/MAT) for GNPS, Sirius, or MS-FINDER dereplication.

name: lc-ms-feature-row-tabulation
description: Use when comparing alignment algorithms (RANSAC vs Join) on LC-MS peak lists and row counts are needed to explain why one aligner degrades on high-feature-count fractions.

name: lc-ms-feature-statistical-testing
description: Use when the input is a preprocessed MetaboSet object (or imputed feature abundance matrix with group labels) and the goal is per-feature group comparisons — selecting which molecular features differ between two or more study groups with multiplicity-corrected p-values.

name: lc-ms-feature-table-annotation
description: Use when you have a feature/peak table with accurate m/z, RT, and intensities from a fixed LC-MS assay (e.g., HILIC- or CSH-Q Exactive HF) plus a same-condition in-house m/z+RT library, and MS/MS spectra are absent, sparse, or not required for level 2 annotation.

name: lc-ms-feature-table-batch-correction
description: Use when a PCPFM-derived feature table (TSV) exhibits batch-driven sub-clustering in QAQC PCA plots and sample metadata contains a batch designation field, and missing/uncommon features have already been removed or imputed.

name: lc-ms-feature-table-cleaning
description: Use when you have a processed LC-MS untargeted metabolomics feature table (features x samples) with missing values in QC and biological samples, and you need a cleaned, imputed, normalized intensity table before statistical analysis.

name: lc-ms-feature-table-formatting-and-filtering
description: Use when peak-picked LC-HRMS feature tables from two untargeted metabolomics data sets must be cleaned and formatted before feature pair alignment with metabCombiner.

name: lc-ms-feature-table-generation
description: Use when raw LC–MS metabolomics data (netCDF/mzXML vendor files) must be converted into a sample-by-feature table via XCMS peak identification, RT correction, and grouping, prior to peak-quality labeling or MetaClean classification.

name: lc-ms-feature-table-ingestion
description: Use when starting an mpactR workflow with an exported peak table (e.g. Progenesis CSV with compound, m/z, retention time, and raw abundance columns) and a companion sample metadata CSV that must be loaded into a single R object before applying filters.

name: lc-ms-feature-table-processing
description: Use when you have an LC-MS feature table (samples × metabolite features in negative ion mode) plus tissue/group labels, and need to test whether a specific tissue (e.g., buccal gland) separates from others in PCA.

name: lc-ms-feature-table-processing
description: Use when you have an Asari feature table (preferred_Feature_table.tsv or full_feature_table.tsv) from an LC-MS experiment and need QC curation or grouping of features into empirical compounds (empCpds) before MS1/MS2 annotation.

name: lc-ms-feature-table-quality-filtering
description: Use when a processed LC–MS peak/feature table still contains missing values and you must remove noisy features by MV thresholds before imputation, differential analysis, and pathway enrichment in the tidyMass framework.

name: lc-ms-homologue-series-detection
description: Use when given an LC-MS feature/peak table (mz, rt, intensity) and the goal is to group features into homologue series defined by repeating mass increments (e.g. 44.02628 Da C2H4O) with correlated retention-time steps.

name: lc-ms-intensity-matrix-reconstruction
description: Use when an XCMS-derived peak intensity matrix (retention time, m/z, peak intensity) shows batch or injection-order drift (visible intensity drift over run order, dispersed QCSs) and the corrected intensity matrix must be rebuilt without batch labels.

name: lc-ms-intensity-noise-modeling
description: Use when simulating synthetic LC-MS/MS peaks in mzML and noise standard deviation must scale with signal intensity (e.g. reproducing SMITER's noise model or validating a replacement injector).

name: lc-ms-isotope-feature-grouping
description: Use when raw LC-MS data (mzML or Bruker .d) has been feature-detected and aligned, and isotope/adduct/ISF peak groups must be annotated to remove false-positive features before statistics.

name: lc-ms-maintenance-event-alignment
description: Use when you have time-ordered DIA and paired DDA QC runs from a monitored instrument with maintenance-event timestamps, and need to determine whether DIA-based QC metrics (e.g. MS2 intensity) respond more sensitively than DDA metrics (e.g. MS1 area) to system status changes.

name: lc-ms-mass-trace-detection
description: Use when the input is centroided LC-MS data (mzML) and the goal is sensitive detection of mass traces (co-eluting signals of the same ion) as the precursor step to feature assembly and label-free metabolite quantification.

name: lc-ms-metabolic-feature-extraction
description: Use when raw LC-MS mzML/mzXML files (Orbitrap or Q-TOF, MS1-only or DDA) must be turned into metabolic features plus pseudo MS/MS spectra before spectral library annotation.

name: lc-ms-metabolic-feature-fidelity-assessment
description: Use when a feature table contains suspect LC-MS features whose EIC shapes may be false positives, and you need automated good/poor peak-quality classification before downstream statistical analysis.

name: lc-ms-metabolite-chromatogram-parsing
description: Use when raw LC-MS MRM data are supplied as mzML files (e.g. from an Agilent 1290 Infinity II UHPLC coupled to an Agilent 6495 QQQ-MS) and chromatograms per metabolite, per sample must be extracted for preprocessing.

name: lc-ms-metabolomics-batch-correction
description: Use when an unnormalized LC-MS metabolomics data matrix (rows = compounds, columns = samples) shows signal drift over acquisition order and batch effects that QC-only or non-robust normalization fails to fix, especially with outlier-contaminated features.

name: lc-ms-metabolomics-data-normalization
description: Use when an unnormalized LC-MS metabolomics matrix (compounds x runs) shows signal drift, batch effects, or occasional disproportionately high/low outlier intensities that deteriorate QC-based normalization, and you need batch-aware robust correction with QC-sample representativeness checking.

name: lc-ms-metabolomics-data-processing
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS metabolomics data in .mzML (or .abf) format must be processed reproducibly via MS-DIAL and MS-FLO, and peak tables with retrospective provenance reports are needed.

name: lc-ms-metabolomics-peak-filtering
description: Use when a detected chromatographic peak list from LC/MS metabolomics data must be quality-filtered before downstream statistical analysis, and true positives can be validated against a ground-truth peak list.

name: lc-ms-metabolomics-training-data-preparation
description: Use when building a deep-learning peak-quality classifier for LC-MS feature lists and you need labeled EIC plot images spanning diverse sample types, LC and MS conditions, with each plot manually inspected to assign good or poor quality labels.

name: lc-ms-mrm-preprocessing
description: Use when raw MRM-mode LC-QQQ-MS data (e.g. mzML files from an Agilent 6495 QQQ-MS) must be processed into quality-scored chromatographic peak reports without manual peak review.

name: lc-ms-ms-feature-abundance-normalization
description: Use when a margheRita mRList from MS-Dial LC-MS/MS profiling (e.g. the Urine dataset) has passed QC/filtering and sample abundances must be normalized, with PQN or log/reference methods.

name: lc-ms-ms-gc-ms-network-comparison
description: Use when you have MCNs derived from multiple mass-spectrometry data types (e.g. LC-MS/MS and EI GC-MS) and need to assess whether network-level properties such as modularity or scale-free degree behaviour are consistent across platforms.

name: lc-ms-ms-quality-control-job-configuration
description: Use when Thermo Orbitrap .raw files are being written during an active LC-MS/MS run and you need near-real-time QC (instrument sensitivity, retention time shifts, mass accuracy) against a sequence .csv and library .msp.

name: lc-ms-ms2-feature-recognition
description: Use when processing DDA LC-MS metabolomics mzXML files where conventional peak picking (XCMS-style) misses low-abundance or bad peak-shape features, and you want to quantify or recover those lost features via their MS2 spectra.

name: lc-ms-mz-to-pathway-mapping
description: Use when LC-MS peak lists of m/z features (optionally with MS2-annotated compound names from pooled-QC spectra) need to be interpreted as pathway-level biology, e.g. identifying pathways changed between treatment groups in untargeted metabolomics.

name: lc-ms-noise-threshold-setting
description: Use when processing LC-MS mzML files of authentic metabolite standards in metScribeR and a background noise level must be chosen from the noise plot before peak finding and filtering.

name: lc-ms-noise-zigzag-assessment
description: Use when processing LC/MS profile data (e.g. Agilent HPLC–Q-TOF Premier) where extracted ion chromatograms must be quality-scored and filtered prior to CWT-based chromatographic peak detection, or when detected peaks need to be ranked by sharpness, peak significance level, or zigzag index to.

name: lc-ms-peak-annotation-counting
description: Use when an LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics dataset (e.g., in vitro S9 incubation peak tables with MS2 spectra) has been annotated with KGMN and you must report per-mode known/unknown peak counts.

name: lc-ms-peak-annotation-prioritization
description: Use when untargeted LC-MS peak lists (mass-to-charge ratios with adducts/fragments) need to be annotated to KEGG compounds and a small prioritized proposal per peak is required, especially when standard annotation tools like xMSannotator underperform.

name: lc-ms-peak-area-column-validation
description: Use when importing tab-delimited peak-integrated metabolomics data into mzQuality and you need to verify the presence of mandatory columns (aliquot, compound, area, type, injection_time, batch) before downstream quality analysis.

name: lc-ms-peak-area-extraction
description: Use when the analysis goal is to obtain quantitative peak-area values for specific metabolites (e.g. phenylacetyl-carnitine) from raw LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics files rather than relying on pre-computed feature tables.

name: lc-ms-peak-area-normalization
description: Use when MultiQuant-exported peak areas and RTs from a targeted LC-MS/MS sequence show intensity drift and a compound needs IS correction, QC-based drift correction, custom bracketing, or weighted bracketing before external-calibration quantification.

name: lc-ms-peak-detection-and-feature-alignment
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS chromatogram files (e.g., beer extracts in positive and negative ionization modes) must be converted into a bag-of-fragments matrix with MS2 features as rows and MS2 spectra as columns before LDA inference.

name: lc-ms-peak-detection-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating or reproducing peak-detection accuracy on Orbitrap/QTOF LC-MS raw files against a manually labeled EIC ground-truth set, or comparing MassCube with MS-DIAL, MZmine3, and xcms.

name: lc-ms-peak-integration-quality-prediction
description: Use when an XCMS-processed untargeted LC–MS feature table (e.g., from Metabolomics Workbench ST000726/ST000695-style data) contains poorly integrated peaks you need to flag automatically, and RSD < 30% QC filtering alone is insufficient.

name: lc-ms-peak-picking-and-grouping
description: Use when starting from raw mzML (or similar vendor) LC–MS files for untargeted metabolomics and a feature intensity table (metabolic features × samples) must be constructed before statistical analysis, annotation or QC.

name: lc-ms-peak-picking-bounding-box-extraction
description: Use when you have full-scan mzML peak lists plus mzML files from DDA (TopN) controller injections and need per-sample coverage (peaks fragmented) and efficiency metrics for LC-MS/MS metabolomics.

name: lc-ms-peak-quality-classification
description: Use when you have non-filtered MZmine 2 peak lists from nontargeted LC-MS metabolomics data and need to separate true spectral features from random false noise peaks prior to downstream analysis.

name: lc-ms-peak-quality-classification
description: Use when an untargeted LC-MS metabolomics feature table produced by XCMS contains poorly integrated peaks that would propagate to downstream analyses, and automated Pass/Fail peak-quality classification is needed instead of manual expert assessment.

name: lc-ms-peak-quality-filtering
description: Use when processing raw mzML files of LC-MS metabolite standards to decide which adduct peaks (per EIC) are high-quality enough for RT/m/z library inclusion, and when benchmarking automated filtering against manual Good/Bad Peak labels.

name: lc-ms-peak-raster-image-generation
description: Use when non-targeted LC-MS peak lists (e.g., MZmine 2 mzXML-derived features) must be transformed into per-peak raster images to feed an image-based CNN for true/false peak classification.

name: lc-ms-peak-screening-and-identification
description: Use when performing semi-targeted LC-MS metabolomics analysis in MetaPro after peak integration, to apply quality-screening criteria and library-based peak identification using HMDB/METLIN-style spectral matching.

name: lc-ms-peak-shape-distortion-correction
description: Use when ncGTW realignment has distorted peak shapes (broadened or narrowed peaks) in XCMS-flagged misaligned features, and corrected warping functions plus relocated peak positions are needed to return results to XCMS.

name: lc-ms-peak-sharpness-and-significance-evaluation
description: Use when you have candidate chromatographic peaks detected from LC/MS EICs (e.

name: lc-ms-peak-table-quantification
description: Use when raw LC-MS metabolomics data (.mzML or .abf) needs to be converted into a quantified peak table with peak detection, alignment, and filtering; especially when reproducibility across runs, containerization, or HPC execution is required.

name: lc-ms-performance-quality-classification
description: Use when evaluating whether DIA raw files (from Orbitrap, TripleTOF, or timsTOF series instruments) show degraded LC or MS performance, or when binary qualified/unqualified labels must be predicted from extracted QC metrics rather than inspected manually.

name: lc-ms-pooled-qc-rsd-filtering
description: Use when an LC–MS feature table contains pooled quality-control (QC) sample injections and noisy, low-reproducibility peaks must be removed with a simple, unsupervised reproducibility filter before statistical analysis or classifier training.

name: lc-ms-qc-based-normalization
description: Use when an unnormalized LC-MS metabolomics intensity matrix (e.g., runs x metabolites with QC annotations and batch labels) shows signal drift, batch effects, or outliers that degrade replicate concordance and downstream differential abundance testing.

name: lc-ms-qc-consensus-labeling
description: Use when multi-rater quality annotations of LC-MS files (e.g., qualified/unqualified per metric or per file) must be collapsed to a single consensus label and reproducibility (observed agreement) must be quantified per instrument.

name: lc-ms-qc-rsd-calculation
description: Use when a targeted LC-MS peak table (tab-delimited with aliquot, compound, area, type, injection_time, batch columns) contains pooled QC samples (SQC/LQC) and you need a per-compound QC-reproducibility metric for compound filtering.

name: lc-ms-qc-rule-implementation
description: Use when a dashboard or QC pipeline needs to escalate per-internal-standard QC results into a specimen-level 'Warning' label using Rapid QC-MS's dropout-threshold and IS-Warn-fraction rule.

name: lc-ms-qc-sample-pca-visualization
description: Use when a targeted LC-MS metabolomics study was measured in multiple batches and you need to verify, via PCA of sample types and batches, whether pooled QC (SQC) samples become aligned and centered across batches after batch correction.

name: lc-ms-qualified-prediction
description: Use when a DIA-MS raw file (.raw/.d/.wiff) from Orbitrap, TripleTOF, or timsTOF instruments must be assessed for LC/MS run quality and receive an automated qualified/unqualified prediction.

name: lc-ms-quality-control-metric-extraction
description: Use when Thermo .raw files are being acquired across a specimen sequence and per-specimen IS-derived RT, intensity, and Δm/z values must be tabulated to expose acute QC failures or gradual drift over hours, days, months, or years.

name: lc-ms-quantification-linear-quadratic-modeling
description: Use when processing already-integrated targeted LC-MS/MS peak-area data (calibration standards plus samples) and you need per-compound automated calibration-curve regression without manual model/level tuning.

name: lc-ms-raster-image-representation
description: Use when raw LC-MS peak groups (e.g. MZmine 2 extracted features from nontargeted metabolomics runs) must be represented as images to train or apply a DNN-based true/false peak classifier.

name: lc-ms-raw-data-peak-picking
description: Use when raw LC-MS mzXML files (e.g., DDA data from an exposome or metabolomics mixture) need conventional XCMS peak picking as a feature table before JPA's MS2-recognition or targeted-list extraction steps.

name: lc-ms-raw-file-batch-processing
description: Use when a study deposits or generates hundreds to thousands of vendor LC-MS raw files spanning multiple acquisition modes and instruments, and the goal is fully autonomous, mode-conditional identification without manual per-file intervention.

name: lc-ms-raw-spectra-processing
description: Use when starting from raw LC-MS1/MS2 spectral files (e.g. mzML/CDF vendor conversions of untargeted metabolomics or exposomics runs, including pooled-QC SWATH-DIA acquisitions) and you need feature detection, quantification, and MS2 deconvolution before annotation or statistics.

name: lc-ms-reference-metabolite-validation
description: Use when a raw mzXML/mzML standard-mixture file and its extracted library table must be screened so that only metabolite peaks passing Std/Blk ratio, RT RSD, and intensity thresholds enter the validated reference library.

name: lc-ms-retention-time-alignment
description: Use when aligned LC-MS feature tables across many runs show retention time drift (e.g., tens of seconds in RPLC negative mode) and features must be mapped to a common RT scale before statistical analysis or phenotype prediction.

name: lc-ms-retention-time-alignment
description: Use when you have per-run feature lists (m/z, charge, RT, intensity) from Dinosaur, OpenMS, MaxQuant, XICFinder or TXT/CSV, need to align corresponding features/peptides across many LC-MS runs, or compare against MBR-based tools.

name: lc-ms-retention-time-alignment
description: Use when XCMS-class single-warping-function alignment has produced misaligned feature groups in LC-MS profiles — detected by ncGTW's p-value-based misalignment detection — and the goal is compound-specific realignment before re-grouping and peak-filling.

name: lc-ms-retention-time-benchmarking
description: Use when you have metabolite standard peak lists from both a manual vendor tool (e.g. MassHunter) and a semiautomated RT assignment pipeline (e.g. metScribeR) and need to quantify RT assignment accuracy for library quality control.

name: lc-ms-retention-time-drift-correction
description: Use when aligning peak lists from multiple LC-MS samples whose retention times drift nonlinearly, and a naive join-by-m/z/RT tolerance fails; requires per-sample peak lists plus m/z and RT thresholds.

name: lc-ms-retention-time-precision-analysis
description: Use when replicate LC-MS runs of chemical standards are available (e.g. each standard mixture evaluated three times) and you need to quantify retention time reproducibility or filter peaks by an RSD threshold before accepting a metabolite as validated.

name: lc-ms-retention-time-tracking
description: Use when a longitudinal series of DIA raw files (.wiff/.raw/.d) from a fixed instrument must be quantified consistently and per-precursor retention-time/intensity stability (CV) needs to be summarized over time.

name: lc-ms-roi-detection
description: Use when raw LC/MS mzML files must be mined for peaks without a pre-existing peak list — e.g. recovering signals an XCMS run missed, or benchmarking how many unique (non-degenerate) peaks a deep-learning detector adds over a conventional peak-picker.

name: lc-ms-roi-signal-segmentation
description: Use when raw LC-MS mzML or Bruker .d files contain noisy MS1 mass traces that must be cut into chromatographic peak segments without biasing final peak parameters, or when a peak detector must achieve complete signal coverage over each ROI.

name: lc-ms-rt-mz-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when raw LC-MS data (.npy/.mzML) has been classified by a trained DeepMSProfiler ensemble and you need per-class importance heatmaps on the 341×341 RT×m/z grid, e.g. for unknown-metabolite biomarker inspection.

name: lc-ms-run-simulation
description: Use when you need gold-standard synthetic mzML datasets with known ground truth — e.g. to benchmark quantification algorithms, test mass-accuracy (ppm) sensitivity, or predict co-elution/co-fragmentation before real MS experiments.

name: lc-ms-semi-targeted-peak-detection
description: Use when the goal is to reproduce automated semi-targeted quantification of predefined analytes and internal standards from vendor DDA LC-MS files (Thermo .raw, SCIEX .wiff) without a spectral library or manual curation.

name: lc-ms-serum-metabolomics-classification
description: Use when the task is to classify raw untargeted LC-MS serum samples (mzML or .npy) into tri-class disease labels — healthy / lung nodule / lung cancer — or to reproduce the 0.961 early-stage lung adenocarcinoma accuracy via a pre-trained ensemble model.

name: lc-ms-signal-drift-correction
description: Use when a preprocessed LC-MS peak table (e.g. MS-DIAL Excel export) contains pooled QC samples measured across the run and features show systematic intensity drift with injection order that must be corrected before statistical analysis.

name: lc-ms-signal-drift-evaluation
description: Use when untargeted LC–MS data in mzML format contains pooled/intrastudy QC injections acquired over time and you need to detect, visualize, or correct time-dependent signal drift before downstream statistical analysis.

name: lc-ms-simulated-data-metrics
description: Use when evaluating a feature-matching workflow on synthetic LC-MS metabolomics data where the true correspondences between reference and target feature tables are known by construction, and a match-correctness fraction must be reported.

name: lc-ms-spectra-file-handling
description: Use when loading untargeted LC-MS metabolomics data (feature table plus MS2 fragmentation spectra) into an annotation pipeline and deciding between .mgf and .mzML spectral file formats.

name: lc-ms-spike-in-reference-matching
description: Use when you have repeated spike-in LC-MS measurements (e.g. human plasma background) plus a ground-truth list of reference analytes, and need to quantify detection sensitivity/specificity or verify the >95% claim.

name: lc-ms-system-suitability-testing
description: Use when LC-HRMS acquisitions (mzML of a spiked SST standard mixture) must be checked for system suitability — retention-time stability, EIC peak areas, or MS/MS product-ion/neutral-loss behavior — before collecting study data.

name: lc-ms-targeted-metabolomics-qc-outlier-detection
description: Use when evaluating targeted LC-MS metabolomics peak tables (tab-delimited with aliquot, compound, area, type, injection_time, batch columns) to identify mis-injections and pooled-QC outliers before batch correction or statistical analysis.

name: lc-ms-time-series-feature-extraction
description: Use when a time-course LC-MS peak table (sample rows, feature columns, time-point labels such as T0–T48) has been scanned by NOREVA's workflow ranking and you must extract a known rhythmic metabolite's trace from top- and bottom-ranked workflow outputs to visually validate processing quality.

name: lc-ms-vendor-software-benchmarking
description: Use when peak areas from an automated integrator must be validated against an experienced analyst's vendor-software (e.g., Xcalibur) peak areas using correlation, regression, and reproducibility metrics.

name: lc-ms-vs-afadesi-msi-adduct-difference-evaluation
