description: Use when building or extending a metabolite annotation database for AFADESI-MSI data: metabolites identified by LC-MS/MS in tissue extracts must be re-represented as the adduct ions actually formed during ambient MSI desorption before m/z matching can be done.

name: lc-ms-workflow-execution
description: Use when raw LC-MS data (.mzML or .abf) must be processed reproducibly end-to-end — peak detection through filtering, alignment, and contaminant removal — on a Unix-like machine, container, or HPC/SLURM cluster.

name: lc-ms1-feature-detection-and-quantification
description: Use when starting from raw, centroided LC-MS1 spectra (e.g. mzML files) and you need peak picking, peak alignment, gap filling, and peak annotation to produce a full MS1 feature table for quantification or dilution-series correlation analysis.

name: lc-ms2-feature-annotation
description: Use when a crude natural product or metabolomics extract has been acquired by LC-MS2 and you need to prioritize which molecular features to fractionate or isolate based on spectral similarity and dereplication.

name: lc-ms2-fragment-matching
description: Use when LC-MS2 data from fractionated natural-product extracts must be dereplicated against a reference compound (e.g. swinholide A) to prioritize fractions and annotate known or structural-hybrid macrolides.

name: lc-ms2-molecular-networking-interpretation
description: Use when LC-MS/MS data from fractionated crude natural-product extracts (e.g. marine cyanobacterial Symploca fractions) must be clustered by MS2 similarity to prioritize which fractions to isolate and annotate.

name: lc-msms-annotation-accuracy-assessment
description: Use when a processed LC-MS/MS feature table with SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID annotations must be checked against known expected compounds (e.g. actinomycete secondary metabolites or commercial standards) to report detection and annotation accuracy fractions.

name: lc-msms-annotation-yield-comparison
description: Use when comparing annotation coverage of unsupervised motif-based substructure discovery (MS2LDA Mass2Motifs) against spectral library matching (Mass Bank/NIST) on the same MS/MS spectra.

name: lc-msms-chromatogram-simulation
description: Use when the goal is to generate a gold-standard synthetic mzML for LC-MS/MS (peptides, nucleosides, or lipids defined by chemical formulas) and benchmark it against a real run, e.g. reproducing a 140-min proteomics gradient simulation.

name: lc-msms-consensus-spectra-processing
description: Use when a multi-sample LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics data set (e.g. MSV000080502 Euphorbia dendroides extract) must be turned into clean consensus spectra with ionization variants (in-source fragments, adducts, dimers) merged into one representative [M+H]+ ion.

name: lc-msms-dda-run-simulation
description: Use when a gold-standard LC-MS/MS dataset with known ground truth is needed to benchmark peptide identification pipelines, test search/rescoring algorithms, or predict co-elution and co-fragmentation before running real MS experiments.

name: lc-msms-feature-alignment
description: Use when aligning per-sample precursor (MS1) and fragment (MS2) m/z/intensity feature lists exported from MS-DIAL across many LC-MS/MS samples into one feature table for downstream multivariate or machine-learning analysis.

name: lc-msms-feature-annotation-msi-level3
description: Use when mzML files and OpenMS-annotated featureXML adduct information are available and you need to attach SIRIUS molecular formula and CSI:FingerID structural identifications (MSI level 3) to detected LC-MS/MS features.

name: lc-msms-feature-based-molecular-networking-processing
description: Use when the analysis goal is to detect, align, quantify and dereplicate LC-MS/MS features from natural product extract fractions in order to generate an MS/MS-annotated feature table for downstream bioactivity-correlation mapping (e.g., antiviral screening).

name: lc-msms-feature-count-validation
description: Use when running the specXplore importing pipeline on .mgf MS/MS feature lists (e.g. wheat or urine exposome data) and you need a scale sanity check — wall-clock preprocessing time and post-processing feature count — before opening the dashboard session.

name: lc-msms-feature-detection
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS runs in .mzML or .mzXML format from untargeted metabolomics experiments must be converted into features (precursor ion, adduct, isotope peaks) with merged fragmentation spectra per feature before de novo formula and structure annotation.

name: lc-msms-feature-detection-and-alignment
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS files from bioassay-guided fractionation must be converted into a feature-level table aligned across fractions before Pearson correlation scoring and GNPS FBMN.

name: lc-msms-feature-mz-rt-matching
description: Use when a preprocessed margheRita mRList (MS-Dial-exported features with m/z, retention time and MS/MS spectra) must be matched against a reference spectral library to produce feature-metabolite associations up to level-1 confidence.

name: lc-msms-feature-network-edge-overlay
description: Use when a globaltest-prioritized LC-MS/MS differential feature must be inspected in its spectral-similarity network context — e.g. to check whether its strongest neighbors (top-30 edges) reach beyond its small k-medoid cluster.

name: lc-msms-feature-quantification
description: Use when raw LC–MS/MS runs (e.g. mzML/MGF per sample) must be turned into per-feature relative abundances that support bioactivity correlation scoring or fraction-based prioritization of bioactive natural products.

name: lc-msms-feature-quantification-table-transposition
description: Use when an aligned LC-MS/MS feature table (row ID, row m/z, row retention time, peak area) has been exported and bioassay values per fraction have been added, and feature-wise correlation scoring requires features-as-rows orientation.

name: lc-msms-feature-set-data-integration
description: Use when a completed msFeaST pipeline has produced embedding coordinates, k-medoids cluster labels, and globaltest statistics per feature, and these must be joined on the m/z–retention-time feature key and serialized into the msFeaST_Dashboard_bundle.html-compatible .json schema.

name: lc-msms-feature-spectra-preprocessing
description: Use when an LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics dataset (e.g. a Kathib et al. 2024 feature table with quantification, metadata, and MS/MS spectra) must be prepared for msFeaST spectral similarity computation.

name: lc-msms-feature-table-filtering
description: Use when you have a Progenesis-format LC-MS/MS peak table plus sample metadata and need to correct mispicked isotope peaks, remove solvent-blank/media background, CV-filter technical replicates, or drop in-source fragments.

name: lc-msms-feature-table-import-progenesis
description: Use when you have tandem MS/MS pre-processed feature tables exported in Progenesis format (a peak table CSV plus a sample metadata CSV) and need to load them into R as an mpactr object for quality filtering.

name: lc-msms-feature-table-ingestion
description: Use when starting a margheRita workflow from MS-Dial-exported LC-MS/MS feature tables and sample metadata, before any filtering, normalization, annotation or statistics can run.

name: lc-msms-feature-table-processing
description: Use when starting from raw LC-MS/MS feature abundance tables, sample group metadata, and MS/MS peak lists (e.g., the Pleurotus eryngii 0% vs 80% olive mill solid waste contrast) and needing a cleaned, msFeaST-ready data bundle.

name: lc-msms-fingerprint-image-generation
description: Use when raw untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics data (MS1/MS2 m/z–intensity pairs from MS-DIAL) must be encoded as 2D grayscale fingerprint images as CNN input for bioactivity classification without compound annotation.

name: lc-msms-ground-truth-evaluation
description: Use when you have MS/MS spectra of a compound set whose molecular formulas/structures were validated by spectral library search and manual inspection, and you need to quantify annotation accuracy of a formula- or structure-annotation tool.

name: lc-msms-identification-count-verification
description: Use when a paper reports a total unique-metabolite count from DDA LC-MS/MS and an accompanying organ/mode-specific database file (e.g. an .xlsx workbook with per-organ sheets) that must be reconciled against that count.

name: lc-msms-metadata-parsing
description: Use when constructing a large unannotated MS/MS corpus from raw metabolomics repository files (MassIVE GNPS .mzML/.mzXML) and you need per-spectrum LC–MS/MS metadata preserved alongside peak lists for downstream ML.

name: lc-msms-mzml-data-parsing
description: Use when an mzML file contains MS2 scans from a simulated co-eluting peptide mixture and the goal is per-scan peak extraction plus annotation against theoretical fragment ions to quantify chimeric spectra.

name: lc-msms-peak-coverage-evaluation-from-fullscan-data
description: Use when the goal is to quantify DDA coverage (proportion of MS1 ions fragmented) for SmartROI or WeightedDEW controller settings by simulating LC-MS/MS injections from full-scan mzML data in ViMMS.

name: lc-msms-peak-picking-mzmine
description: Use when raw full-scan LC-MS/MS mzML files (e.g. serum QCA or beer QCB extract injections) must be converted into picked-peak RT/mz bounding boxes so that DDA controller coverage of picked peaks can be tabulated.

name: lc-msms-simulation-environment-orchestration
description: Use when a prepared chemical list (e.g. from ChemicalMixtureCreator) must be subjected to a simulated fragmentation strategy (Top-N DDA, DIA, SmartROI, WeightedDEW) and the resulting scans exported as an mzML file.

name: lc-msms-spectra-fingerprinting
description: Use when comparing chemodiverse metabolomics samples with poor feature overlap, strong retention time shifts, or data acquired across different LC methods or mass spectrometers (Q-ToF vs Orbitrap), where feature alignment is impractical.

name: lc-msms-spectral-clustering
description: Use when you have per-sample MGF MS2 spectra from LC–MS/MS feature detection (e.g. MSV000080502) and need to group them into clean consensus spectra, merging duplicates of the same ion yet keeping distinct isomers of the same m/z (e.g. 11 isomers of m/z 589.31) separated.

name: lc-msms-spectral-clustering-parameter-tuning
description: Use when an LC-MS/MS dataset (mzML/mzXML/mgf uploaded to MassIVE) must be molecular-networked and the practitioner needs to know how clustering and tolerance settings affect node counts and annotation yield for a compound class of interest.

name: lc-msms-spectral-library-matching
description: Use when you have an aligned LC-MS/MS feature table (e.g. from MS-Dial after MS-CleanR filtering) and need to annotate detected features by matching their MS/MS spectra against a spectral library.

name: lc-msms-spectral-preprocessing
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS spectra from paired genome–metabolome samples (e.g. PoDP bacterial/fungal strains or cryptic features from MZmine) must be deconvoluted, aligned, and converted into MS/MS fingerprints for NPOmix KNN linking of spectra to biosynthetic gene clusters.

name: lc-msms-untargeted-metabolomics
description: Use when analyzing LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics feature tables with MS/MS spectra, where the goal is to group features by spectral similarity and statistically prioritize feature groups across sample conditions.

name: lc-msms-untargeted-metabolomics-data-processing
description: Use when an agent must reproduce or extend KGMN annotation of known and unknown metabolites from untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics output (e.g., NIST human urine positive/negative mode) and quantify how far annotation expands beyond seed metabolites.

name: lc-msms-untargeted-metabolomics-processing
description: Use when raw LC–MS/MS untargeted metabolomics files (e.g. mzML from a Bruker Impac II qQToF or similar) plus a Metadata Table describing samples/sample groups must be converted into quantified, cleaned consensus spectra, library annotations, and a filtered SSMN.

name: lc-msms-workflow-result-integration
description: Use when raw PSM tables from LC-MS/MS peptide searches must be filtered (unique peptides, unique monoisotopic mass, >=5 peptides/protein) to confirm putative MSI identifications or replicate Figure 4-style filtering cascades.

name: lc-retention-time-layer-ordering
description: Use when a complete LC-MS/MS run yields multiple MS/MS spectra with associated retention times and scored candidate lists from an MS/MS-based predictor like IOKR, and the goal is to jointly identify a set of metabolites by combining MS/MS-based scores with predicted retention order.

name: lc-srm-chromatogram-peak-integration
description: Use when vendor raw LC-SRM/LC-MS files must be converted into quantified analyte concentrations via scheduled SRM transition extraction, peak picking, and isotope-dilution or external calibration in Skyline.

name: lchrms-annotation-extraction
description: Use when a recurring unassigned LC-HRMS peak (e.g. a specific m/z in positive mode, such as m/z 247.1441 in NIST plasma) must be resolved to a metabolite annotation and its MSI confidence level across instruments.

name: lchrms-peak-picking-pipeline-execution
description: Use when raw LC-HRMS profile-mode chromatograms must be converted into chromatographic feature lists, or when comparing peak-picking tools (PeakBot vs XCMS, MS-Dial, peakOnly) on a shared dataset such as the PHM porcine hepatic microsome data.

name: lcms-adduct-annotation
description: Use when geoRge's PuInc_seeker and basepeak_finder have produced labeled base-peak m/z values on an XCMS feature table and you need putative metabolite identities with adduct assignments in negative-ion LC/MS.

name: lcms-alignment-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking the m/z offset detection accuracy of an LC-HRMS alignment tool by injecting known m/z shifts into a reference feature list and comparing imposed versus detected offsets.

name: lcms-annotation-workflow-execution
description: Use when you have a filtered peak list from an LC-MS assay with m/z, RT and adduct/fragment information, and need a KEGG-based, context-prioritized compound annotation per peak rather than a simple mass matching.

name: lcms-compound-spectra-extraction
description: Use when you have an XCMS feature table from UPLC/ESI-QTOFMS data (positive and negative ion mode) and need to group co-eluting, adduct, and isotope features into per-analyte compound spectra before compound identification.

name: lcms-cross-dataset-feature-matching
description: Use when two or more independently processed same-method nontargeted LC-MS datasets must be aligned to form a complete dataset, and you need pairwise Source→Target subalignment match tables.

name: lcms-data-ingestion
description: Use when a Thermo .raw or .mzML LC-MS data file needs to be loaded into lcmsWorld for 3D visualization, especially as the first load of a file that has no cached .lcms conversion yet.

name: lcms-data-quality-control-assessment
description: Use when running or monitoring large LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics analyses (e.g. Thermo Orbitrap acquisition sequences) and you need per-specimen QC status (Pass/Fail/Warn) for internal standards within minutes of each raw file being written.

name: lcms-demo-data-loading
description: Use when validating or demonstrating MetaboReport end-to-end without user-supplied data — e.g. reproducing the File S5 example HTML report or testing that preprocessing, statistics, visualisation and reporting modules communicate via new_app_state().

name: lcms-eic-extraction
description: Use when building an in-house LC-MS metabolite standard reference library from mzML files and per-adduct EICs must be generated at expected m/z values before peak finding, peak-quality filtering, or RT assignment.

name: lcms-eic-extraction
description: Use when raw LC/MS mzML files and a generic peak list (mz, rt columns, e.g. from XCMS) must be converted into per-peak EIC matrices to feed peak-classification or reintegration models.

name: lcms-extracted-ion-chromatogram-metric-implementation
description: Use when you have LC/MS or UPLC/MS profile intensity profiles (extracted ion chromatograms) and need to score each EIC or detected peak's quality with quantitative metrics, or to filter out high-background / single-peak / spike / zigzag noise before time-consuming peak detection processing.

name: lcms-feature-alignment-across-datasets
description: Use when two or more independently processed, same-method nontargeted LC-MS feature datasets — each a merged Feature Metadata + Feature Abundances table — must be combined into one aligned feature set with overlapping features matched.

name: lcms-feature-alignment-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking feature alignment methods (e.g. G-Aligner, MZmine2, OpenMS, XCMS) on mzML-derived feature lists against a manually annotated ground truth of library analytes.

name: lcms-feature-annotation
description: Use when a peak table from untargeted LC-MS metabolomics needs putative compound-level annotations from m/z values, especially when candidates must be prioritized against KEGG context networks rather than by m/z match alone.

name: lcms-feature-annotation-against-hmdb
description: Use when a MultiABLER-generated feature table of metabolomic or lipidomic peaks needs compound-level annotation and lipid-versus-metabolite labels before downstream statistical analysis such as sPLS or rCCA.

name: lcms-feature-annotation-table-generation
description: Use when each sample has a minimal metadata file with its originating taxon plus MZmine-processed LC-MS/MS DDA feature MS2 spectra, and you need per-feature structural annotations reranked by taxonomy and chemical consistency.

name: lcms-feature-correlation-clustering
description: Use when a preprocessed LC-MS feature abundance matrix contains multiple features per metabolite (adducts, isotopes) that need grouping, or when redundant correlated features must be collapsed before statistical analysis.

name: lcms-feature-correspondence-matching-across-tools
description: Use when benchmarking feature detection/quantification of LC-MS processing tools on a dilution or mixing-ratio dataset, where feature tables from multiple tools must be matched and ranked by correlation of peak areas to known abundances.

name: lcms-feature-correspondence-metrics-computation
description: Use when two LC–MS metabolomics feature tables have been matched (e.g. via M2S) and you need a quantitative validation of match quality — fraction of correctly matched annotated features, counts of wrong matches, and annotated features outside thresholds.

name: lcms-feature-detection-and-alignment
description: Use when you have raw centroided LC-MS runs (mzXML/mzML) from a spatially mapped sample set and need a per-run feature table aligned across all runs to build intensity maps or heat maps.

name: lcms-feature-detection-and-quantification
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics data (Thermo RAW, Agilent, Bruker, or mzML files) must be converted into a table of metabolic features with alignment, adduct annotation, and quantification, and you need benchmarkable detection/quantification rates.

name: lcms-feature-detection-benchmarking
description: Use when multiple LC-MS data processing tools must be compared for feature detection consistency, or when reported feature counts (e.g. 10,901 XCMS vs 42,099 MZmine features on 184 pooled HZV029 plasma samples) need to be reproduced.

name: lcms-feature-detection-parameterization
description: Use when processing raw LC-MS/MS DDA metabolomics files (positive and/or negative ionization) with MZmine in a sample-centric workflow, where parameterization and feature filtering must be fixed before RDF/KG integration.

name: lcms-feature-extraction-parameterization
description: Use when raw LC-MS-based metabolomics data must be processed for feature extraction and default software parameters underperform, or when you need data-driven values for mass tolerance, peak height, peak width, or instrumental shift.

name: lcms-feature-filtering
description: Use when an MZmine-exported full-scan feature table (.csv with row ID, row m/z, row retention time, per-sample peak areas) must be reduced to biologically consistent ions before MS/MS targeted acquisition.

name: lcms-feature-grouping
description: Use when you have a feature table from LC-MS untargeted metabolomics or stable isotope tracing and need to group degenerate ions (isotopes/adducts) into empirical compounds with inferred neutral masses, without prior formula knowledge.

name: lcms-feature-grouping-graph-partitioning
description: Use when an xsAnnotate object has already been grouped by retention time (groupFWHM) and isotopes (findIsotopes), but compound spectra may still contain features of two or more closely co-eluting compounds.

name: lcms-feature-grouping-retention-time-coelution
description: Use when processing raw LC/MS feature lists (e.g. from XCMS) where multiple m/z features originate from a single metabolite and you need to reduce feature-list redundancy before adduct or isotope annotation.

name: lcms-feature-intensity-ratio-computation
description: Use when XCMS peak-picked LC/MS data contains labeled and unlabeled biologically equivalent samples (e.g., 12C vs 13C glucose) and you need fold-change intensities of enriched features versus a control condition.

name: lcms-feature-intensity-rsd-calculation
description: Use when an aligned LC-MS feature table with replicate sample-intensity columns and a 'level' column (PP/MR) is available, and quantitative precision of rescued MR features must be benchmarked against conventional peak-picked PP features.

name: lcms-feature-intensity-ttesting
description: Use when you have a feature-intensity matrix from LC/MS preprocessing (apLCMS or XCMS) plus batch and phenotype labels, and need to test each feature for between-group differences after batch-effect correction.

name: lcms-feature-list-perturbation
description: Use when validating or calibrating an LC-HRMS feature-matching/alignment tool where ground truth is unknown: perturb a processed reference feature list (m/z + retention time) with known shifts and score recovery (F-measure, ppm discrepancy).

name: lcms-feature-matching
description: Use when integrating two similar untargeted LC–MS metabolomics feature tables (e.g. two batches or two cohorts peak-picked with XCMS) that need feature-level correspondence based solely on RT, MZ, and FI values.

name: lcms-feature-matrix-construction
description: Use when raw LC-MS mass spectra must be converted into a fixed-dimension 2D feature matrix (m/z bins × RT windows) for feeding CNN/LSTM/Transformer classifiers, and spectrum_dim differs per dataset (e.g. 12000 NSCLC/CRLM, 9900 RCC, 15000 Canine Sarcoma).

name: lcms-feature-pair-alignment-reduction
description: Use when metabCombiner has produced a scored combined table after fit_gam and calcScores, and conflicting or low-scoring FPAs must be pruned to form the final reduced table before downstream statistics.

name: lcms-feature-pair-screening-deuterium-labelling
description: Use when LC/MS peak data from a stable-isotope feeding experiment (processed with XCMS and CAMERA) must be screened for label-shifted feature pairs to enumerate putative metabolites of the fed precursor.

name: lcms-feature-percentage-computation
description: Use when analyzing how capillary voltage, ion energy, or collision energy settings change the number and percentage of ISF features detected relative to real metabolic features in LC-MS feature tables.

name: lcms-feature-quality-filtering
description: Use when an extracted LC–MS feature matrix (mzML-derived peaks, TidyMS Data Container, MZmine/XCMS output) needs cleaning before statistical analysis and you have pooled/intrastudy QC, blank, and study samples to drive reproducibility and background filters.

name: lcms-feature-quantification-peak-area-extraction
description: Use when LC-MS data contain a dilution/mixing series with known composition ratios (e.g. BM21 plasma–vegetable juice dilutions) and you need to compare peak-area quantification quality across processing tools like asari vs XCMS.

name: lcms-feature-rescue-from-dda-in-dia
description: Use when DIA (SWATH) feature tables of individual biological samples lack metabolic features that were confidently detected in the pooled-QC DDA run, and their intensities must be recovered from the DIA raw data.

name: lcms-feature-table-analysis
description: Use when processing LC/MS feature tables from untargeted metabolomics where features must be grouped into compound spectra and annotated with ion species to cut feature count before statistical analysis or compound identification.

name: lcms-feature-table-annotation
description: Use when you have a tab-delimited feature table (feature ID, m/z, rtime, intensities) from LC-MS data — e.g. from asari v1.9.2 — and need to group degenerate ions into empirical compounds and infer neutral masses before database annotation, including stable isotope tracing.

name: lcms-feature-table-annotation
description: Use when apLCMS- or XCMS-generated feature tables (m/z, RT, intensity columns) from LC/MS metabolomics data acquired in negative ion mode need KEGG metabolite annotation via adduct matching, e.g. to compare annotation/matching rates across preprocessing methods.

name: lcms-feature-table-filtering
description: Use when an LC/MS untargeted metabolomics feature table must be turned into the two input lists (significant m/z features and reference list of all detected features) that mummichog requires for pathway/network activity prediction.

name: lcms-feature-table-filtering
description: Use when a feature table with mz, rt, and group-defined intensity columns is available and features enriched between two conditions (e.g. hacl-1 vs WT) must be isolated with intensity, significance, and fold-change cutoffs.

name: lcms-feature-table-import
description: Use when you have raw mzML files plus an mzMine- or XCMS-derived feature table CSV/TSV and need to bring both into a single NeatMS Experiment for downstream peak labelling.

name: lcms-feature-table-interpretation
description: Use when you have an LC-MS feature table (from XCMS mzXML extraction or a custom csv from MS-DIAL/MZmine2) and need to identify which features are in-source fragments of which precursor ions.

name: lcms-feature-table-parsing
description: Use when feature tables from multiple LC-MS processing tools must be parsed and unified for cross-tool comparison or per-feature rescoring, e.g. recomputing peak-shape fitness scores on the Yeast2021 dataset.

name: lcms-feature-table-processing
description: Use when raw LC-MS(/MS) files from a serially diluted sample set must be preprocessed in MZmine into aligned full-scan feature tables (.csv with row ID, row m/z, row retention time, peak areas) suitable for downstream regression-based feature selection.

name: lcms-feature-to-compound-spectrum-assignment
description: Reference for grouping LC/MS peaks detected by XCMS into per-analyte compound spectra when you need to de-redundant a feature list and know which features co-elute with a compound.

name: lcms-feature-to-metabolite-mapping
description: Use when a cleaned LC-MS feature table (mass_dataset object) needs metabolite annotations, and database-level identifications (MSI level 2) must be produced by matching m/z and retention time.

name: lcms-file-level-quality-filtering
description: Use when building training corpora from repository-scale LC-MS/MS deposits (e.g. MassIVE GNPS .mzML/.mzXML experiments) and you need to drop low-quality files before spectrum-level QC.

name: lcms-glycan-identification-reporting
description: Use when the goal is to identify fluorescently labeled N-linked glycans from LC-MS/MS data acquired on an Orbitrap (or MALDI-TOF) instrument, replacing manual analyst peak picking with automated MS1/MS2 searching and Excel reporting.

name: lcms-homologue-series-detection
description: Use when a pre-processed LC-MS peak table (m/z, rt, intensity columns, e.g. the mtbls1358 dataset) should be annotated with homologue series IDs — e.g. to find polymer/PEG-like repeating-unit ladders or compare targeted vs untargeted detection runs.

name: lcms-injection-list-formatting
description: Use when preparing flow-injection MSn acquisition for a Thermo Orbitrap ID-X and you have plate-based metadata (unique sample id, plate_id, well_location) that must become an Xcalibur import sequence.

name: lcms-intensity-normalization-comparison
description: Use when an LC/MS ion-feature matrix (>150 samples) has QC injections that can be withheld, and the goal is to test whether data-driven synthetic-QC drift correction matches experimental-QC normalization.

name: lcms-intensity-rank-sorting
description: Use when processing raw LC-MS-based metabolomics data in R to derive universal feature-extraction parameters via rank-ordered intensity profiles and zone-of-interest structures, prior to tools like MS-DIAL or XCMS CentWave.

name: lcms-isotope-label-detection
description: Use when you have XCMS-processed untargeted LC/MS feature data from paired unlabeled vs. labeled samples (e.g. CELL_Glc12 vs CELL_Glc13) and need to flag isotopically enriched features and their base-peak isotope assignments.

name: lcms-isotope-pattern-mapping
description: Use when an LC-MS untargeted feature table (ids, rel.ids, mzs, RTs, Ints) has been feature-clustered and isotope peaks must be grouped into isotope-pattern units before IPA annotation.

name: lcms-isotopologue-pattern-detection
description: Use when you have a table of significant features whose column headers encode AssayName_RTsec_m/z, and you need to group isotopologues and adducts into structural clusters across multi-assay LC-MS metabolomics data.

name: lcms-lipidomics-data-reprocessing
description: Use when reprocessing publicly deposited LC-MS lipidomics raw files (Thermo .raw, e.g. MSV000091033 Nile rat plasma) to reproduce or re-annotate reported lipid feature counts and identifications.

name: lcms-mass-track-extraction-from-mzml
description: Use when centroided mzML LC-MS files must be converted into per-sample mass tracks (full-RT intensity vectors per unique m/z) and aligned into a MassGrid before peak picking or annotation.

name: lcms-metabolite-detection-counting
description: Use when a study has a list of predicted metabolites from a tool like BioTransformer and an LC-HRMS detection list from postincubation samples, and the goal is to compute the number (or percentage) of predictions that were actually observed.

name: lcms-metabolite-library-benchmarking
description: Use when quantifying the computational and manual effort of an LC-MS metabolite library construction workflow (e.g., metScribeR on mzML standard files) against a manual peak-picking baseline, to report per-standard effort and total time savings.

name: lcms-metabolomics-data-preprocessing
description: Use when an LC-MS metabolomics feature table (XCMS/MZmine2/SIEVE/Skyline output) with pooled QC samples injected at fixed intervals shows injection-order signal drift and needs drift correction before statistical analysis.

name: lcms-metadata-table-curation
description: Use when preparing a GNPS molecular networking (METABOLOMICS-SNETS-V2) or library-search job from LC-MS/MS data and a sample metadata table must be collated, standardized, and attached so the analysis is publishable and reproducible.

name: lcms-missing-value-imputation
description: Use when a non-targeted LC-MS peak table stored as a notame MetaboSet still contains NA values in its exprs matrix after drift correction, quality flagging, and QC removal, and those gaps must be filled before statistical analysis.

name: lcms-ms-map-image-conversion
description: Use when raw LC–MS data (m/z vs retention time) must be converted into NPFimg's MS-map image format to enable marker feature identification and produce a marker feature table without peak picking.

name: lcms-ms1-bayesian-annotation
description: Use when a clustered MS1 feature table (intensities across samples) from LC-MS untargeted metabolomics needs compound and adduct annotations with statistically rigorous probability estimates, especially when MS2 spectra or prior experiment knowledge should be integrated.

name: lcms-ms1-signal-detection
description: Use when you have raw LC/MS untargeted metabolomics data in mzML format (e.g., HILIC positive-mode serum studies) and need to detect metabolite signals without user-set parameters, QC samples, or manual threshold tuning.

name: lcms-ms1-signal-matching-across-scans
description: Use when starting nontargeted LC-MS feature detection from raw MS1 scans (mzML or Bruker timsTOF .d) and you need 100% signal coverage rather than peak-shape-filtered peak picking.

name: lcms-multi-dataset-alignment
description: Use when two or more nontargeted LC-MS feature tables (Feature Metadata + Feature Abundances) from independently processed but same-method datasets must be merged into one complete dataset, and existing pairwise alignment tools do not fully meet the need.

name: lcms-noise-and-background-modeling
description: Use when EICs extracted from LC/MS profile data (e.g. Agilent HPLC Q-TOF metabolomics runs) show high background signals or contain only a single peak, and a quality score is needed to filter bad EICs prior to time-consuming peak detection.

name: lcms-peak-annotation-prioritization
description: Use when you have a filtered LC-MS peak table (signal-bearing features, 80% rule applied) and need a biologically prioritized KEGG compound annotation list that outperforms mass-only matching, e.g. reproducing mWISE vs xMSannotator sensitivity benchmarks.

name: lcms-peak-artifact-classification
description: Use when raw mzML files and an XCMS peak list need peak-level curation — i.e., detected peaks must be scored as artifacts vs. true peaks with minimal manual labeling (e.g., <100 peaks) before downstream statistics.

name: lcms-peak-classification-metrics-comparison
description: Use when evaluating whether a machine learning peak filter (deep neural network or logistic regression) removes false LC-MS peaks without losing true positives, by comparing ROC curves, AUC, TPR/FPR, and retained false peaks across training, test, and independent cohorts.

name: lcms-peak-classification-scoring
description: Use when nontargeted LC-MS peak lists (e.g. from MZmine 2 centWave extraction) contain a large fraction of false noise peaks and you need to classify and filter peak groups using peak-shape information.

name: lcms-peak-curation
description: Use when you have raw mzML files plus an XCMS-generated peak list (m/z and rt columns) and need to remove artifact peaks — e.g. replicate, blank, or spiked-standard metabolomics data where peak quality determines downstream statistics.

name: lcms-peak-detection-parameterization
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS data (converted to mzML) from a Multi-ABLE extraction must be converted into a processed, aligned peak table with adduct annotations before downstream filtering, normalization, or joint metabolomic–lipidomic analysis.

name: lcms-peak-detection-preprocessing
description: Use when raw LC/MS profile data (e.g. NetCDF/CDF files from Metabolomics Workbench) were acquired in multiple batches and consistent feature detection/quantification across batches is required before downstream analysis.

name: lcms-peak-feature-extraction
description: Use when raw nontargeted LC-MS metabolomics data (e.g., human plasma HILIC runs) must be converted into peak lists/peak groups before ML-based true vs false peak filtering.

name: lcms-peak-filling
description: Use when an XCMS xcmsSet has missing peaks after grouping and you need filled feature intensities, especially for features flagged misaligned by ncGTW, to compare CV before vs after realignment.

name: lcms-peak-image-rasterization
description: Use when nontargeted LC-MS peak lists from MZmine 2 must be converted into fixed-size 64x64 raster images so a deep neural network can classify candidate peaks as true or false.

name: lcms-peak-integration-evaluation
description: Use when targeted LC-MS data (e.g., HRMS full-scan or SRM runs from instruments like the Waters Synapt G2 HDMS) must have known small-molecule targets extracted as ion chromatograms, peak-picked, and integrated for quantification or between-group comparison.

name: lcms-peak-list-alignment
description: Use when a set of peak lists from multiple LC-MS samples (e.g., 20 synthetic lipidomic samples derived from a seed sample) must be merged into an aligned peak list, especially when random non-linear RT shifts are present.

name: lcms-peak-quality-classification
description: Use when unaligned or aligned mzMine2/XCMS feature tables must be labelled and filtered to remove false-positive MS1 peaks before downstream statistical analysis of large-scale LC-MS metabolomics data.

name: lcms-peak-quality-feature-engineering
description: Use when detected chromatographic peaks from LC/MS metabolomics data must be classified as good or bad, and single-metric cutoff filtering is insufficient — combine multiple peak quality metrics as ML features.

name: lcms-peak-table-automated-transfer
description: Use when running the Nextflow4MS-DIAL pipeline on .mzML LC-HRMS input and you need MS-DIAL's peak table to flow into MS-FLO automatically without manual file copying or manual re-parameterization between the two tools.

name: lcms-peak-table-generation
description: Use when starting from raw .mzML (or .abf) LC-HRMS metabolomics files and you need a reproducible, containerized peak-detection/alignment pipeline that yields a filtered MS-DIAL plus MS-FLO peak table (.tsv).

name: lcms-processing-software-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing the computational efficiency (CPU time, memory, scaling with sample number) of LC-MS metabolomics processing tools on centroided mzML datasets, or when validating claims that a new tool scales better than established ones like XCMS.

name: lcms-qc-normalization-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing the computational cost of QC sample-based normalization methods on targeted (e.g., 53-compound) vs untargeted (e.g., 8913-feature) metabolomics matrices, or when deciding which normalization method is feasible for high-throughput use.

name: lcms-quality-metric-interpretation
description: Use when targeted LC–MS peak integration output must be quality-filtered: peaks carry computed metrics (AUC, max intensity, POP, SNR, bell-curve similarity) and 'Good'/'Bad'/'Ambiguous' calls must be evaluated or reproduced.

name: lcms-raw-data-autotuning-benchmark
description: Use when raw LC-MS metabolomics data must be processed and you need to decide which auto-tuning method (Paramounter, AutoTuner, or IPO) yields the most true positive features before committing to a peak-picking parameter set.

name: lcms-raw-data-import
description: Use when raw vendor or open-format LC-MS files need to be loaded into MZmine 2 before peak picking, or when designing a processing pipeline that must import MS data without precision loss from resampling.

name: lcms-raw-data-parameter-measurement
description: Use when starting an untargeted LC-MS metabolomics workflow with raw spectra and you need data-driven values for mass tolerance, peak height, peak width, or instrumental shift instead of relying on vendor defaults or manual tuning.

name: lcms-raw-data-reading-mzml
description: Use when you have raw LC-MS mzML files (e.g., pooled/intrastudy QC, blanks, and study plasma samples) that must be ingested by TidyMS to extract spectral features for a quality-control or data-curation pipeline.

name: lcms-raw-file-format-conversion
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS files (e.g. Orbitrap .raw) must be converted to mzXML so the GlyKAn AZ app's MS1 Peak ID / MS2 Peak Confirmation tabs can ingest them.

name: lcms-raw-spectra-preprocessing-to-npy
description: Use when starting from raw LC-MS metabolomics files (e.g. mzML from MetaboLights studies such as MTBLS1129) that must be auto-converted to .npy arrays for end-to-end deep-learning classification with DeepMSProfiler.

name: lcms-replicate-retention-time-analysis
description: Use when you have three or more replicate mzXML/mzML injections of a chemical-standard mixture (e.g. from comparing HILIC LC-MS mobile phases) and need per-peak quality metrics, validated peaks, and replicate-consistent retention times.

name: lcms-retention-time-bounding-box-matching
description: Use when you have full-scan mzML peak-picked bounding boxes (min/max RT and m/z) plus a TopN mzML schedule and need the upper bound on fragmentable peaks for a single injection.

name: lcms-scan-timing-analysis
description: Use when comparing DDA acquisition controllers' scan overhead — e.g. mzML files from full-scan, TopN, SmartROI, and WeightedDEW runs need inter-scan start-time deltas converted into MS1 scan-plus-processing timings to verify controller processing overhead.

name: lcms-signal-patch-partitioning
description: Use when raw LC/MS data in mzML format must be converted to an MS1 ion-feature table (median rt, m/z, normalized intensities) and no QC samples or user-tuned peak-detection thresholds are available.

name: lcms-spectral-metadata-serialization
description: Use when a curated PeakForest compound/spectrum collection (JSON/CSV peak lists with chromatography and ionization metadata) must be exported for MassBank/MoNA submission or consumed by tools like MS-DIAL and NIST MSsearch.

name: lcms-standard-blank-intensity-ratio-filtering
description: Use when building or validating a retention-time reference library from chemical standard mixtures measured in triplicate LC-MS runs and peaks must pass blank-vs-standard (Std/Blk), RSD, and intensity thresholds before recording.

name: lcms-structural-cluster-linking
description: Use when you have statistically significant features from untargeted multi-assay LC-MS metabolomics datasets and want to group them into structural clusters based on retention time and mass-to-charge ratio, enabling putative annotation.

name: lcms-system-suitability-assessment
description: Use when raw LC–MS mzML files from a plasma reference material batch (e.g., NIST candidate RM 8231 or SRM 1950, MTBLS1919 deposit) must be checked for system suitability using the five SSS standard compounds and pooled/intrastudy QC injections.

name: lcms-system-suitability-assessment
description: Use when evaluating UHPLC-HRMS acquisition performance prior to data collection — e.g., assessing RT stability, peak areas, or MS/MS product ion consistency of an SST standard mixture acquired over months by multiple operators.

name: lcms-target-list-parsing
description: Use when a targeted LC–MS metabolomics/lipidomics analysis needs a compound target table (identifier, name, m/z, expected RT, polarity) converted into TARDIS' expected data frame input.

name: lcms-targeted-peak-integration
description: Use when raw targeted LC–MS runs (e.g., mzML) must be integrated per target list/retention-time list, producing per-target AUC and quality metrics (AUC, Max. Int., SNR, bell-curve similarity, points over the peak) for large cohorts.

name: lcms-total-ion-current-qc-computation
description: Use when MetaXtract scan-header tables from Thermo RAW files contain a 'Total Ion Current' column for MS1/MS2 and you need search-free run-level QC: comparing UP vs reference HeLa QC runs or gating runs by MS2/MS1 TIC ratio.

name: lcms-universal-parameter-measurement
description: Use when raw LC-MS metabolomics data must be processed with feature-extraction software (MS-DIAL, XCMS CentWave, AutoTuner, IPO) and default parameter sets would discard true-positive metabolic features.

name: lcms-xsannotate-object-handling
description: Use when LC/MS peak tables from positive and negative ESI ion-mode runs must be annotated jointly, or when single-polarity CAMERA annotations need cross-mode verification to recover molecular mass assignments.

name: lcmsms-annotation-record-structuring
description: Use when LC-MS/MS spectra acquired on a biological matrix (e.g. human urine) must be imported into PeakForest via its prefilled XLSX template, and template columns must be mapped onto chemical-compound and spectral entities.

name: lcmsms-feature-table-construction
description: Use when MS-DIAL-aligned peak intensity data (profile MS1, centroid MS/MS) from many LC-MS/MS samples must be merged into feature tables via similarity-based equivalence rules for downstream ML bioactivity prediction.

name: lcmsms-fragmentation-image-encoding
description: Use when you have MS-DIAL-preprocessed LC-MS/MS feature tables with precursor (MS1) and fragment (MS2) m/z pairs plus intensities and need fixed-size image inputs for CNN-based bioactivity prediction of complex metabolomics extracts.

name: lcmsms-run-identification-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when you have per-spectrum scored candidate molecule lists from an LC-MS/MS run plus a retention-order predictor, and you need to measure whether integrating the two improves the percentage of correctly identified molecular structures.

name: lcss-optional-parameter-usage
description: Use when you need the health/safety (LCSS) annotation content for a single PubChem compound record, organized by the LCSS table of contents, as a JSON payload from PUG-View.

name: ld-block-locus-partitioning
description: Use when counting independent genetic association signals from PLINK2 GWAS summary statistics, e.g. comparing genome-wide significant locus counts between pre- and post-QC versions of NMR biomarker data.

name: ld-clumping-of-instrument-variants
description: Use when running a two-sample Mendelian randomization analysis (e.g. an mGWAS metabolite as exposure against a GWAS outcome such as finn-b-E4_DM2) and the selected instrument SNPs need pruning of correlated variants before harmonization.

name: ld50-to-bmd10-uncertainty-factor-derivation
description: Use when ranking thousands of exposome chemicals by risk and only predicted LD50 toxicity (no measured reference dose) is available, requiring LD50-to-BMD10 conversion with uncertainty factors.

name: lda-coherence-scoring-and-convergence-checking
description: Use when training an LDA topic model over bag-of-words BGC (sub)Pfam tokenisations (e.g. iPRESTO PRESTO-TOP) and you must verify topic quality (u_mass coherence) and training convergence before using the motifs downstream.

name: lda-topic-model-inference-on-mass-spectra
description: Use when you have a corpus of unlabelled MS2 spectra (e.g. ~1,000 MS peaks per sample per ionization mode from complex mixtures) and want unsupervised discovery of conserved fragment/neutral-loss substructures plus per-spectrum motif loadings.

name: lda-topic-model-visualization
description: Use when you have a trained LDA topic model over MS/MS fragmentation data (e.g., ms2lda.bin with motifset.json) and need interactive exploration of inferred topics and their fragment/neutral-loss terms before structural characterization.

name: lda-topic-modeling-of-bgc-domain-combinations
description: Use when you have antiSMASH-predicted BGCs tokenised into (sub)Pfam domain combinations and need unsupervised discovery of sub-cluster motifs without relying on gene order.

name: lda-topic-multitask-head-training
description: Use when training or evaluating ESP's MLP/GNN base models where spectral-peak dependencies and topic-structured co-occurrence should be exploited — e.g. flags like disable_mt_lda=False, mt_lda_weight, correlation_mat_rank appear in the config.

name: leading-digit-distribution-comparison-statistics
description: Use when importing a lipidome quantity table (csv/xlsx, pivot or flat, or mzTab-M) and you need a global QC verdict on whether quantitative values plausibly span several orders of magnitude before downstream analysis.

name: learning-curve-performance-analysis
description: Use when planning or justifying a custom AnnoMe/MS2DeepScore classifier training run and you must decide whether your number of annotated 'relevant'-class reference spectra is sufficient or can be trimmed.

name: learning-curve-visualization
description: Use when quantifying how much target-system training data a RankSVM or SVR retention-order predictor needs, by sweeping target-system training percentages and plotting accuracy curves for single-system vs multi-system regimes.

name: learning-curve-visualization
description: Use when you need to show how model performance (precision, recall) scales with training-set size — e.g., to justify a dataset's size or demonstrate diminishing returns on a spectral classification task.

name: least-square-spectral-alignment
description: Use when overlaid 1D 1H NMR spectra show uncontrolled chemical shift variations between spectra in specific ppm areas, and peaks must be re-aligned before binning or statistical analysis of metabolomics data.

name: least-squares-curve-fitting
description: Use when a 1D signal (e.g., an extracted ion chromatogram or arrival time distribution from MZA/HDF5 data) contains Gaussian-shaped peaks whose centers, heights, and widths must be quantified, not just located.

name: leave-class-out-cross-validation
description: Use when evaluating whether a BGC detection model can extrapolate to unseen product classes, i.e. when the goal is leave-class-out validation across the six non-hybrid MIBiG classes rather than standard cross-validation on seen classes.

name: leave-one-out-cross-validation-evaluation
description: Use when a database-backed MS/MS identification method needs unbiased performance estimates on a closed compound set — e.g. 662 KEGG spectra scored by deep neural network structural similarity.

name: lefse-biomarker-annotation
description: Use when you have a LEfSe-format abundance matrix (from merged MetaPhlAn or HUMAnN profiles) plus a LEfSe result file and need to render a GraPhlAn circular tree that highlights biomarker clades.

name: lefse-output-to-graphlan-conversion
description: Use when you have MetaPhlAn/LEfSe (or HUMAnN) input and result files and need to generate publication-quality circular cladograms highlighting LEfSe biomarker clades with LDA-mapped clade sizes and shaded background classes.

name: left-censored-metabolomics-imputation
description: Use when targeted metabolomics datasets contain left-censored missing values caused by LOD/LOQ (MNAR) and a robust imputation method is needed before univariate t-tests, PLS-DA, or differential-variable detection.

name: left-censored-missing-value-imputation
description: Use when a targeted metabolomics (LC/MS or GC/MS) data matrix contains left-censored MNAR missing values caused by LOD/LOQ, and prediction-based imputation bounded by the censoring point is needed before downstream univariate or multivariate analysis.

name: leiden-community-detection-on-cell-graphs
description: Use when you have a per-cell mean marker-intensity matrix from multiplexed IMC protein imaging and need single-cell cluster/cell-type assignments across multiple imaging regions or patients.

name: leiden-single-cell-lipid-clustering
description: Use when you have a cross-annotated single-cell SCMS peak matrix (e.g. peak_data_sc_regional_decode.imzML) and need to partition cells into lipid-chemistry clusters before mapping those cluster dictionaries onto tissue MSI pixels.

name: levenshtein-fuzzy-name-matching
description: Use when a metabolomics feature table has free-text or non-standard metabolite column names that must be converted to standard HMDB IDs before pathway mapping, and exact/synonym lookups leave names unmapped.

name: library-composition-verification
description: Use when you have downloaded a public MS/MS library (e.g. from github.com/QizhiSu/MS-libraries) and must confirm its entry counts per polarity match the reported composition before feeding it to MS-DIAL identification.

name: library-entry-validation-against-vignette
description: Reference for building and quality-checking MetaboAnnotatoR fragment library entries from experimental MS/MS spectra (including MassBank .msp records) when a trusted reference entry from the package vignettes is available for comparison.

name: library-match-score-based-representative-selection
description: Use when an ion identity molecular network (IIMN graphml) contains multiple ion-species nodes sharing one IIN ID and you must collapse them to one representative neutral-molecule (M) node before writing the reduced network.

name: library-reliability-comparison-across-databases
description: Use when a task asks to reproduce or verify library-level spectral-rating reliability statistics — e.g. the fraction of library spectra with average user match ratings below 2.5 stars — across multiple spectral libraries.

name: libsvm-bit-prediction-training
description: Use when you need to train or swap per-bit libSVM classifiers that predict molecular fingerprints from tandem MS spectra within ChemDistiller's FingerScorer scoring pipeline.

name: lightgbm-classifier-tuning
description: Use when a lipid (or other small-feature) biomarker panel must be validated as a classifier across independent clinical cohorts, with accuracy and ROC curve reporting.

name: likelihood-array-postprocessing-threshold-and-power-scaling
description: Use when a ModiFinder per-atom likelihood array Ω has been computed and must be cleaned/sharpened prior to evaluation (e.g. Average-distance scoring) or visualization, to suppress low-confidence atoms and emphasize top candidates.

name: limit-of-detection-data-handling
description: Use when a metabolomics data matrix contains missing values that arise from a known limit of detection (MNAR below-LOD missingness) combined with random missingness, and downstream statistical testing requires accurate imputation.

name: limit-of-detection-estimation
description: Use when a wide-format feature intensity table includes blank samples in its companion design file and features must be flagged/filtered against a blank-derived limit of detection before downstream statistics.

name: limit-of-detection-region-shading
description: Use when reproducing single-dataset imputation comparisons (e.g., Figure 6-style plots) where missing values are partly MNAR below a detection limit and below-LOD imputation accuracy must be inspected visually.

name: limited-labeled-pathway-evaluation
description: Use when comparing a pathway/hyperlink prediction model against a baseline (e.g. CHESHIRE) under artificially limited labeled-pathway conditions on metabolite correlation networks, to mimic organisms with sparse pathway knowledge.

name: limma-differential-abundance-analysis
description: Use when a metabolomics/proteomics feature table (e.g. ST000284) has study covariates (batch, sex, age, etc.) that may confound group comparisons, and you need covariate-adjusted differential abundance results to compare against unadjusted t-test/ANOVA calls.

name: limma-differential-abundance-modeling
description: Use when a normalized MultiABLER feature table plus sample metadata are available and the goal is group-level differential expression of lipids or metabolites, such as genotype contrasts in mouse arterial tissue.

name: limma-linear-model-fitting
description: Use when a normalised metabolite abundance matrix (metabolites × samples) is paired with a sample-level binary phenotype such as hypertension status, and per-metabolite differential-abundance hits with adjusted p-values are required.

name: linear-baseline-scaling-mean-median
description: Use when a metabolomics feature table (samples × features, e.g. the imputed cancerCell demo table from MetaboReport) shows sample-to-sample variation that should be reduced by per-sample scaling, and a simple mean- or median-intensity baseline is acceptable.

name: linear-combination-decomposition-of-fragment-ion-peaks
description: Use when SWATH-MS-based untargeted metabolomics data contain coeluted, unresolved chromatographic peaks of fragment ions in multiplexed MS/MS spectra that must be separated into metabolite-specific MS2 spectra.

name: linear-discriminant-analysis-classification
description: Use when a SpaceM spatio-molecular matrix (MORPHnMOL.csv) contains single-cell metabolite intensities plus fluorescence channels for two or more morphologically distinguishable cell types, and the goal is to test whether metabolic profiles alone predict cell type.

name: linear-dynamic-range-validation
description: Use when processing lipidomics peak tables (e.g., LipiDex 2 Peak Finder/Spectral Searcher results) where quantitation confidence must be validated against a dilution-series-derived linear dynamic range before downstream statistics.

name: linear-mixed-effects-model-fitting
description: Use when paired or repeated clinical metabolomics samples (e.g. VAT/SAT tissue pairs from 59 CRC patients) contain subject-specific variation that confounds metabolite signals and you need to readjust per-metabolite abundances before PCA or PLS-DA.

name: linear-mixed-effects-model-fitting-for-metabolite-stability
description: Use when NMR metabolomics concentrations are available for blood samples exposed to varying pre-/postcentrifugation delays across tube types and you must quantify how fast each metabolite changes (time to 20% concentration change).

name: linear-mixed-effects-modeling-of-protein-abundances
description: Use when protein-level abundance matrices from twin/pair-related or longitudinally repeated DIA (SWATH) measurements must be decomposed into heritable, environmental, and longitudinal variance components.

name: linear-mixed-model-prediction
description: Use when NMR-quantified plasma/serum metabolite concentrations are available at multiple controlled pre- or postcentrifugation delay time points (e.g. 2, 4, 6, 8 h) and per-parameter concentration changes must be predicted or a stability time point (20% change) must be located.

name: linear-model-bound-fitting
description: Use when candidate peak boundaries from a sliding-window TIC/chromatogram peak detection must be sharpened before downstream parameter estimation, and per-peak scan bounds with an explicit fit-quality criterion (R2 >= 0.8) are needed.

name: linear-model-design-matrix-specification
description: Use when a lipidomics dataset has grouped samples plus a potential confounding clinical variable (e.g. Race, batch, age) and you need a covariate-adjusted group contrast rather than a plain two-group comparison.

name: linear-model-diagnostic-assessment
description: Use when a series of Thermo .raw system-suitability or QC files (e.g. the ~12 h longitudinal FGCZ Orbitrap series) contains an iRT peptide mix (Biognosys) and you need to verify that retention times remain highly linear and comparable across instruments and time.

name: linear-model-differential-abundance-analysis
description: Use when a peak-value feature matrix (samples x features) from 1D NMR spectra must be tested for features associated with a continuous dose, ordinal diet level, or multi-group factor, with multiple-testing correction.

name: linear-model-group-comparison
description: Use when you have a peak-based feature/sample matrix from speaq 2.0 (e.g. from BuildFeatureMatrix on Winedata) plus class metadata and need a per-feature significance test between two groups.

name: linear-nonlinear-model-comparison
description: Use when a metabolomics feature table spans several dose levels of a compound (e.g. four etomoxir doses on BT549 cells) and the goal is fitted dose-response curves plus per-feature benchmark dose (BMD) values for risk assessment.

name: linear-program-formulation-with-capacity-constraints
description: Use when a target HSQC NMR spectrum must be reconstructed as a union of library compound spectra scaled by concentration factors, with joint capacity constraints preventing over-assignment of shared peaks.

name: linear-quadratic-regression-model-fitting
description: Use when you have a concentration-series calibration data set (e.g., narcotics standards) plus a test sample of unknown concentration, and need fitted linear/quadratic calibration curves with adjusted R2 and per-analyte relative errors.

name: linear-regression-baseline-benchmarking
description: Use when validating a learned predictor for an auxiliary molecular property (RT or CCS) by demonstrating it beats a trivial univariate regression baseline on identical data splits, e.g. reproducing Fig. 5-style parity plots.

name: linear-regression-ccs-correction-fitting
description: Use when TIM-MS or DTIM-MS lipidomics CCS values show class-specific bias against a DTCCSN2 reference library and at least 3 U13C-labeled lipids per lipid class-adduct combination are available for regression.

name: linear-regression-feature-screening
description: Use when an untargeted LC-MS feature table (m/z rows, samples as columns) must be screened for features significantly altered by a binary condition, with batch-corrected vs raw comparisons.

name: linear-regression-fitting-of-computational-scaling
description: Use when benchmark timing measurements exist for a tool's runtime across varying input file sizes or parameter counts, and you must verify a claimed linear scaling relationship quantitatively.

name: linear-regression-intercept-verification
description: Use when a series of spectra contains compounds spiked at known graded amounts (e.g., 0/20/40/60/80 uL) and you must confirm linear amplitude response plus a nonzero intercept from endogenous matrix content.

name: linear-regression-model-fitting
description: Use when IM-MS lipidomics data (e.g., TIMCCSN2 values from a Bruker timsTOF Pro) are spiked with U13C-labeled lipids and a DTCCSN2 reference library exists, and CCS biases must be corrected per lipid class-adduct combination via linear regression.

name: linear-regression-model-fitting
description: Use when calibrating single-field DTIMS-MS data with external calibrants (e.g. Agilent tune-mix): feature tables provide measured arrival times and a reference CCS list (TuneMix-CCS.txt) provides known CCS values, and a linear Ω″-vs-time calibration curve is needed.

name: linear-regression-r2-computation
description: Use when two GC–MS preprocessing tools have produced per-sample compound/feature quantification tables for the same samples and compounds, and you need a numeric per-compound agreement metric (R²) to validate that a new method (e.g., eRah) reproduces established quantification.

name: linear-regression-two-stage-batch-fitting
description: Use when a log2-scaled LC-MS metabolomics matrix (.csv, samples in rows, features in columns, batch levels in the first column) shows across-batch signal drift — e.

name: linearized-power-function-ccs-regression
description: Use when converting arrival-time measurements from single-field DTIMS or traveling-wave/SLIM IMS-MS into CCS values and the calibrant-to-analyte relationship is non-linear — e.g. SLIM helium data calibrated with TAA/tune-mix references where a quadratic poly fit underperforms.

name: linearized-power-function-fitting
description: Use when calibrating TWIMS-MS arrival times to CCS (e.g. SLIM-based IMS or Waters Synapt) using reference calibrants such as Agilent tune-mix, and a power-law relationship (rather than polynomial) is desired for the calibration function.

name: link-prediction-precision-evaluation
description: Use when NPOmix candidate BGC-GCF/MS-MS links exist for paired genome-MS/MS samples and you need to quantify precision against validated PoDP links, optionally filtered by a Jaccard co-occurrence threshold.

name: link-rank-comparison-table-reproduction
description: Use when benchmarking a BGC–MS/MS linking method (e.g. NPClassScore vs Metcalf-only) against a set of experimentally validated links from the PoDP, and you must report per-link retention and rank changes at a fixed score cut-off.

name: link-reduction-percentage-calculation
description: Use when you need to quantify the pruning effect of NPClassScore class matching on candidate BGC-MS/MS links per GCF in paired genome-metabolome datasets after Metcalf scoring, and to validate reported reduction percentages.

name: linker-translation-output-parsing
description: Use when a run of lipid abbreviations through the LipidLynxX Linker yields per-lipid cross-reference identifier columns and you must quantify coverage against LION, KEGG, ChEBI, Rhea, and UniProtKB, or find which lipid classes fail to map.

name: lipid-abundance-normalization-principal-components
description: Use when comparing multiple heterogeneous lipidomes where raw abundances must be added to a structural (PCA-based) lipid space model without low-abundant lipid species dominating the structural comparison.

name: lipid-acyl-chain-labeling-analysis
description: Use when HRMS lipidomics data from a 13C labeling time course contains a resolved lipid molecular species (e.g., PC(36:4)) whose precursor isotopologue distribution must be decomposed into per-acyl-chain (18:1, 18:2, 18:3) labeling using MS2 fragment spectra.

name: lipid-adduct-annotation-maldi-msi
description: Use when a MALDI-MSI peak list (e.g. imzML or exported intensity CSV from SCiLS/MSiReader) contains unassigned high-abundance ions whose pairwise mass differences match known matrix adducts, and you need to flag them as matrix-adduct duplicates rather than distinct metabolite signals.

name: lipid-annotation-agreement-disagreement-analysis
description: Use when aligning lipid annotations between two spectral libraries (e.g., CalicoLipids and MS-DIAL) and a per-library score cutoff is needed to separate authentic from spurious identifications.

name: lipid-annotation-candidate-filtering
description: Use when you must narrow a LipidBlast-style candidate list from precursor m/z matches for lipidomics queries and want multidimensional (RT, CCS) re-ranking with recall metrics.

name: lipid-annotation-conversion
description: Use when lipid shorthand annotations from heterogeneous software (e.g. MS-DIAL, LipidSearch, MZmine2) or databases (LIPID MAPS, SwissLipids, HMDB, RefMet) must be unified, level-equalized, or linked to LION/KEGG/ChEBI/Rhea/UniProtKB identifiers.

name: lipid-annotation-count-comparison
description: Use when evaluating whether PNNL PreProcessor preprocessing improves lipid annotation yield in a replicate LC-DT IM-MS lipidomics workflow, or when reproducing a reported annotation-count improvement between two processing conditions on the same deposited MSV000087295 lists.

name: lipid-annotation-count-reconciliation
description: Use when auditing or reproducing published lipidomics annotation counts from a supplemental annotation workbook — e.g., recounting LipidMatch negative-mode identifications on Red Cross plasma (210 lipid ions, 159 features, 15 lipid types) from Additional file 3 Table S4.

name: lipid-annotation-counting
description: Use when reproducing published lipidomics annotation counts from a LipidMatch/MS-DIAL/Greazy annotation workbook (e.g. Additional file 3) or validating counts of unique lipid ions, features, and lipid types per polarity.

name: lipid-annotation-fdr-estimation
description: Use when you have MS/MS feature tables from LC-MS lipidomics (e.g., RBL-2H3, mixture, human sera, zebrafish) and need to quantify annotation confidence via an estimated FDR against the LipidIN theoretical library.

name: lipid-annotation-level-equalization
description: Use when two or more lipidomics annotation lists report lipids at mixed structural levels (e.g. PC 38:4 vs PC 16:0_20:4 vs PC(16:0/20:4)) and you need to cross-match or merge them at a shared level.

name: lipid-annotation-lipid-maps-search
description: Use when you have a TIC-normalized peak list of m/z values from MALDI FT-ICR mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) data and need to assign putative lipid identities before regional or differential analysis.

name: lipid-annotation-qc-evaluation
description: Use when lipid structure records (e.g., LIPID MAPS or SwissLipids exports at the highest structural resolution level) must be checked for correct double bond position encoding, or when the plausibility of double bond annotations in a lipid database must be quantified.

name: lipid-annotation-style-curation
description: Use when a task requires enumerating which lipid identification software or lipid databases have predefined annotation input styles, or when building/validating a converter's style catalog from JSON rule configurations.

name: lipid-annotation-table-querying
description: Use when you have annotation lists from Lipid Annotator for original vs. preprocessed LC-IM-MS replicates and need per-replicate detection/annotation counts for a specific lipid feature.

name: lipid-annotation-threshold-filtering
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS lipidomics feature annotations must be filtered by RBP score thresholds and compared between two fragmentation libraries to reproduce annotation counts and agreement statistics.

name: lipid-annotation-verification
description: Use when LC/MS feature tables contain enriched lipid features with tentative acyl-chain annotations whose biosynthetic origin is unknown and isotope-labeled precursor (e.g., 13C6-leucine) versus unlabeled control data are available to test incorporation.

name: lipid-building-block-submatrix-generation
description: Use when an uploaded lipidomic data matrix is at the molecular-species level (e.g., 'PC 16:0_18:1') and a chain-level (lipid building block) sub-matrix is required for downstream analysis.

name: lipid-ccs-database-assembly
description: Reference for building or auditing an experimental lipid CCS/m/z reference database from cleaned per-instrument CCS collections (DTIM, TWIM, TIMS) when per-field totals must be verified against reported row counts.

name: lipid-ccs-prediction
description: Use when annotating lipid metabolites from ion-mobility MS data where candidate structures from PubChem must be ranked or filtered using measured/predicted CCS values, and a lipid-superclass [M−H]− training set is available or desired.

name: lipid-ccs-prediction-model-training
description: Use when a curated lipid CCS training table (e.g., the 6394-measurement LiPydomics dataset) with one-hot lipid class, fatty acid modifier, and adduct features plus sum composition and m/z must be used to fit and evaluate an SVR CCS predictor.

name: lipid-ccs-reference-library-validation
description: Use when building or auditing a DTCCSN2 library of U13C-labeled lipids for internal standardization in LC-IM-MS lipidomics, or when verifying that a supplied library (e.g. U13C_DT_CCS_library.csv) meets stated quality criteria.

name: lipid-chain-length-unsaturation-inference
description: Use when lipid molecule name strings (e.g. from Metabolomics Workbench study ST001111, Skyline CSV exports, or numerical matrices) need class/chain/unsaturation annotations, or when entries such as full-chemical-name ceramides fail to parse and must be renamed via RegEx before annotation.

name: lipid-class-abundance-profiling
description: Use when profiling lipidomics abundance data and you need sample-level or group-level composition summaries at the lipid-class level rather than per lipid species, e.g. to compare class percentages across samples in a multi-group dataset.

name: lipid-class-adduct-ccs-regression-correction
description: Use when LC-IM-MS lipidomics samples are spiked with fully U13C-labeled yeast extract lipids, measured CCS values exist per lipid class/adduct, and TIMCCSN2-vs-DTCCSN2 bias needs correction via lipid class- and adduct-specific linear regression.

name: lipid-class-adduct-enumeration
description: Use when building a reference in-silico lipid fragmentation library for LC-MS/MS spectral matching, or when verifying locally generated msp lipid libraries against the deposited MTBLS3097 reference.

name: lipid-class-adduct-filtering
description: Use when a measured IM-MS lipidomics table (File, LipidClass, LipidSpecies, Adduct, Label, CCS) must be matched against the U13C_DT_CCS_library.csv DTCCSN2 library and invalid or nomenclature-mismatched class-adduct pairs must be excluded before CCS bias calculation.

name: lipid-class-adduct-parameter-selection
description: Use when building an in silico lipid spectral library with LSG and you must decide which lipid class(es), fatty-acid compositions, and adduct(s) to include for LC-MS/MS identification.

name: lipid-class-adduct-subset-resampling
description: Use when measured IM-MS lipidomics data (.csv with File, LipidClass, LipidSpecies, Adduct, Label, CCS columns) contains heavy (U13C-labeled) lipids and CCSN2 values need class- and adduct-specific correction against a DTCCSN2 reference library.

name: lipid-class-aggregation-from-molecular-species
description: Use when the input is a molecular-species-level lipidomic data matrix (rows = lipid species in LIPID MAPS shorthand notation, columns = samples) and a lipid-class-level (LCL) matrix is needed for downstream class-level statistics.

name: lipid-class-and-fatty-acid-enumeration
description: Use when an LC-MS/MS lipid identification workflow needs a custom, on-demand in silico spectral library covering specified lipid classes, fatty acid compositions, and adducts, rather than a fixed pre-built library.

name: lipid-class-annotation-against-metlin-hmdb
description: Use when a peak-aligned, TIC-normalized SCMS feature table from two cell phenotypes (e.g., primary vs metastatic melanoma, ± drug treatment) needs differential lipid species filtered at fold change ≥ 2.0 and FDR-adjusted p ≤ 0.05 and annotated to lipid classes.

name: lipid-class-annotation-from-names
description: Use when lipid feature identifiers are name strings (e.g. from a Skyline export or Metabolomics Workbench study like ST001111) and you need class/chain/unsaturation annotations, including renaming full-chemical-name ceramides to shorthand.

name: lipid-class-annotation-level-matching
description: Use when a per-lipid LipidLynxX Linker cross-reference table must be scored for identifier coverage against integration databases, and class-level gaps (e.g. which of the 131 lipids lack LION/KEGG/ChEBI IDs) need to be summarized.

name: lipid-class-annotation-visualization
description: Use when you have lsea enrichment results (e.g., ranked by logFC from a two-group lipidomics contrast) and need to render class-level or chain-length enrichment plots.

name: lipid-class-chain-annotation-inference
description: Use when importing lipidomics matrices, Skyline exports, or Metabolomics Workbench studies into lipidr and you need lipid class/chain annotations parsed from molecule names, or need to detect unparseable names.

name: lipid-class-enrichment-interpretation
description: Use when interpreting S2IsoMEr bootstrapping ORA/MSEA output tables of lipid-class terms (HMDB sub_class, LION) from MS1 imaging or single-cell metabolomics comparisons of conditions, e.g. fatty-acid-treated vs untreated HepaRG cells.

name: lipid-class-enrichment-visualization
description: Use when a differential-expression table of lipid species (with p-values) is available and the goal is to identify which lipid classes or lipid sets are enriched among up- or down-regulated species, and to visualize those enrichments per class.

name: lipid-class-frequency-thresholding
description: Use when compiling a reference MS/MS training library from a public spectral database (e.g. LipidMaps-derived .msp blocks) and you must decide which compound classes have enough spectra to support a data-centric model.

name: lipid-class-grouped-linear-modeling
description: Use when you have a LipiDex 2 pipeline peak table with lipid identifications, retention times, and fatty acyl compositions, and need a class-aware RT QC model to flag likely incorrect identifications.

name: lipid-class-library-composition-analysis
description: Use when comparing lipid-class/adduct coverage across in-silico lipidomics libraries (MAVEN2, MS-DIAL, CalicoLipids) to find classes present in only one library.

name: lipid-class-matched-ccs-model-training
description: Use when a metabolomics annotation workflow needs CCS-based false-positive filtering for lipid/lipid-like [M-H]- candidates, requiring a training set restricted to the same molecular superclass as the targets.
tools: PubChem (Identifier Exchange Service, PyPubChem, Biopython Entrez)

name: lipid-class-over-representation-analysis
description: Use when a differential expression result table (e.g., the deSp_multiGroup output from a multi-group lipidomics analysis) contains significant lipid species that should be tested for over-representation in lipid characteristics such as lipid class.

name: lipid-class-prefix-parsing
description: Use when a feature table of lipid identifications (e.g., Additional file 3 Table S4 LipidMatch annotations) lacks an explicit class column and you need distinct lipid ion, feature, or lipid-type counts to verify reported numbers.

name: lipid-class-regulation-pattern-interpretation
description: Use when a lipidomics dataset with sample group annotations (e.g. cancer vs benign, cancer vs metastasis) has been differential-analyzed with lipidr and you need to summarize which lipid classes show consistent regulation.

name: lipid-class-stratified-benchmarking
description: Use when you have predicted molecular fingerprints for a set of extracted MS/MS spectra and need to quantify annotation accuracy overall and per chemical class (e.g., lipid classes) against a reference database.

name: lipid-class-subclass-classification
description: Use when an annotated m/z feature table (e.g. an all_IsomerNames-style metadata column from a spatial metabolomics experiment) holds multi-isomer lipid annotation strings that need standardising into common lipid categories and classes.

name: lipid-class-subnetwork-interpretation
description: Use when MS/MS networking of differential metabolomics features (e.g., >1000 enriched features) must be resolved into lipid-class subnetworks such as N-acyl ethanolamide families for biological interpretation.

name: lipid-class-template-construction
description: Use when a discovery lipidomics study targets lipid classes not in a prebuilt database such as LipidBlast or Lipid Maps — e.g. glycolipids, lipopeptides, sphingomyelin, FAHFA, ornithine lipids — or requires fragmentation patterns for unique MSn methods.

name: lipid-common-name-decoding
description: Use when input lipid identifiers are common/RefMet names (e.g. 'octadecatrienoic acid', 'linolenic acid', 'linoleyl palmitate') rather than CLASS N:N/M:M shorthand, and you need carbon:double-bond residues.

name: lipid-component-accuracy-metric-computation
description: Use when evaluating LipiDetective transformer predictions on labeled test MS2 spectra and you need a finer-grained accuracy metric than whole-species match rate, e.g. to show performance when full species predictions are partly wrong.

name: lipid-compound-class-annotation-from-spectral-matches
description: Use when MS2Query (or a similar library-matching tool) has returned per-spectrum matches for complex-mixture metabolomics data and you must check whether annotations agree with the expected compound class (e.g., lipids in plasma).

name: lipid-correlation-network-reconstruction
