description: Use when you have a targeted-lipidomics abundance matrix (lipid species such as PI, PC, PE, PS, PG and AA-containing species as rows; e.g. 0.01/1 U/mL thrombin, 1/5 µg/mL CRP plus unstimulated control as columns) and need to test class-level depletion claims and co-regulation structure.

name: lipid-database-accession-linking
description: Use when lipid shorthand annotations (e.g. PC 16:0_18:2, MS-DIAL/LipidSearch-style abbreviations, DHA-style aliases) must be cross-matched to LIPID MAPS, SwissLipids, or PubChem accession IDs for cross-database comparison or systems biology integration.

name: lipid-database-structure-retrieval
description: Use when a structural-space or structural-similarity analysis needs molecular graphs for named lipid species (e.g., PC 12:0/[12-24,26]:0 series) and only species names/SMILES-free identifiers are available.

name: lipid-double-bond-position-extraction
description: Use when lipid structure records carry explicit double bond positions on fatty acyl chains and you must quantify how often two arbitrary chains share no double bond at the same position under forward (carbonyl) and backward (omega) numbering, or need a reference-database ground truth for.

name: lipid-feature-abundance-comparison
description: Use when LC/MS feature tables from two or more biological groups (e.g., WT vs hacl-1 mutant on OP50 vs cyclopropane-deficient JW1653-1 diets) must be compared to find features enriched in one genotype that additionally depend on the bacterial diet.

name: lipid-feature-annotation-against-lipidpioneer
description: Use when lipid features from traveling-wave IM-MS (m/z, charge, retention time, arrival time) have been class-assigned and CCS-calibrated and you need database-backed validation of exact mass and CCS against curated lipid reference values.

name: lipid-feature-count-reconciliation
description: Use when a LipiDex 2 (or similar) discovery lipidomics run has Peak Finder and Spectral Searcher outputs plus Degreaser QC filtering results, and you must report how feature counts and identification rate changed after filtering.

name: lipid-feature-importance-ranking
description: Use when you have MALDI MSI peak data co-registered with an IFM segmentation mask (e.g. thresholded Ly6G marker) and need to rank which lipids (m/z features) classify marker-positive vs marker-negative pixels.

name: lipid-feature-importance-selection
description: Use when LipidIN-annotated lipid feature tables from patient cohorts (e.g., breast cancer vs. healthy plasma LC-MS lipidomics, Supplementary Data 9) are available and a small diagnostic panel with cross-cohort generalization is needed.

name: lipid-feature-normalization
description: Use when a lipid feature/abundance matrix plus a phenotype file must be normalized (mstus) and decomposed via lipidr into lipid class, chain length, and saturation features before differential lipid analysis in MOI.

name: lipid-feature-one-hot-encoding
description: Use when training or applying lipid CCS prediction models that need tabular lipid measurements (lipid class, fatty acid sum composition, adduct, m/z) converted to a fixed-width numeric feature matrix for scikit-learn estimators.

name: lipid-feature-qc-filtering
description: Use when a lipidomics peak table (e.g. from Compound Discoverer 3.3 .cdResult) contains adduct peaks, dimers, or identifications failing QC evidence such as >30% RSD in QC samples, and must be filtered before quantitation.

name: lipid-feature-quality-control
description: Use when raw peak lists from MSI sections or single-cell SCMS runs contain mass-shifted duplicate m/z peaks, and you need to retain only mutually observed, low-occurrence-filtered lipid features for downstream annotation or clustering.

name: lipid-feature-sequential-forward-selection
description: Use when a lipidomics abundance table is annotated with sample-associated study variables (e.g., BMI, tissue, condition) and you need the lipid subset that distinguishes each variable.

name: lipid-fingerprint-regeneration
description: Use when MS2 library search (EQ) plus LCI filtering leaves low-confidence or unannotated LC-MS/MS lipid features that need recall boosting via regenerated fingerprint spectra from a pre-trained deep-learning model.

name: lipid-fluorescence-correlation-in-steatosis-model
description: Use when a per-cell SpaceM matrix (MORPHnMOL.csv) containing normalized lipid intensities plus microscopy-derived fluorescence such as LD540 must be screened for lipids that positively or negatively mark a steatotic (lipid-droplet-rich) cell subpopulation.

name: lipid-fragment-annotation-matching
description: Use when you have per-peak attribution scores from a deep learning lipidomics model and need to verify that top-attributed m/z values correspond to known, interpretable lipid fragments rather than spurious spectral features.

name: lipid-fragment-intensity-ranking
description: Use when a single feature (defined by m/z and retention time) has multiple co-eluting lipid candidates with similar m/z values and you must decide which identification to report as the primary annotation.

name: lipid-fragment-library-matching
description: Use when annotating lipid features from all-ion fragmentation (AIF) LC–MS lipidomics datasets (e.g., human serum Lipid+ or Lipid− modes) that require parent–fragment matching against curated lipid fragment libraries rather than generic MS/MS spectral search.

name: lipid-fragment-mass-probability-computation
description: Use when designing or auditing a targeted lipidomics PRM/MRM assay: you must decide how many MS/MS fragments (and which tolerance, e.g. ±0.5 Da vs ±2.5 ppm) are needed so that target lipids cannot be confused with decoys within the sample lipidome background.

name: lipid-fragment-mz-matching
description: Use when feature tables paired with .ms2 tandem MS files are available and lipid identifications must be assigned by matching observed fragment m/z values to in silico library fragments of candidate lipids from MS1 exact-mass matching.

name: lipid-identification-confidence-tiering
description: Use when a peak-picked, aligned HILIC-IM-MS feature table must be annotated with lipid identifications whose confidence is graded by how many dimensions (m/z, retention time, CCS) agree within defined tolerances.

name: lipid-identification-filter-status-validation
description: Use when LipiDex 2 Degreaser automated threshold filtering has flagged lipid identifications for removal and a mass spectrometrist must manually validate those statuses via QC plots, or when reproducing a manual-validation QC count against reported totals.

name: lipid-identification-level-assignment
description: Use when downstream interpretation needs to distinguish how structurally resolved a lipid annotation is — e.g. separating class-level IDs from fatty-acyl-constituent IDs after fragment matching.

name: lipid-identifier-converter-inventory
description: Use when building a converter or mapping table for lipid annotation identifiers and you need the definitive list of source software/database notation styles and their JSON rule files.

name: lipid-identifier-cross-mapping
description: Use when lipid annotation lists from tools like MS-DIAL, LipidSearch, or LipidBlast must be converted to a common identifier scheme or cross-mapped to LIPID MAPS, SwissLipids, PubChem, KEGG, ChEBI, or LION IDs for dataset compilation or meta-analysis.

name: lipid-identifier-cross-matching
description: Use when two or more lipidomics annotation lists report lipids at different structural annotation levels (e.g. PC 16:0/18:2 vs PC 16:0_18:2 vs PC 34:2) and they must be compiled or compared at a shared level.

name: lipid-identifier-parsing
description: Use when a processed lipidomics table (lipid identifiers as vertical index, samples as columns) needs its analyte names decomposed into fatty acid residues such as 18:1 or 20:4, whether names follow the generic 'CLASS N:N/M:M' form, isomer-group form, or RefMet nomenclature.

name: lipid-ion-annotation-in-mass-spectrometry-imaging
description: Use when you have a list of up- or down-regulated ion m/z values from an MSI experiment (e.g. rMSIKeyIon 'ions' output) and need putative metabolite identifications against HMDB with common positive-mode adducts at a defined ppm tolerance.

name: lipid-isomer-ambiguity-handling
description: Use when lipid identifiers contain unresolved mass-isomer groups such as 'TAG 48:2 total (14:0/16:0/18:2)(14:0/16:1/18:1)(16:0/16:1/16:1)', and residue extraction must account for or discard isobaric uncertainty.

name: lipid-knowledge-base-inventory-verification
description: Use when a targeted lipidomics assay design must be validated against the tool's claimed knowledge-base scope, e.g. LipidCreator transition lists built from head-group, fatty-acyl, and adduct rules need per-class inventory tallies compared to a reported 61+ classes / 10^12-molecule coverage.

name: lipid-mass-difference-matching
description: Use when you have a peak list (plain-text CSV from SCiLS/MSiReader, imzML processed with Cardinal, or a simple mass list) from MALDI-MSI data and need to identify which peaks are metabolite–matrix or salt adducts rather than genuine metabolite ions.

name: lipid-mass-library-construction
description: Use when deisotoped MSI ion features must be assigned putative lipid identities via accurate-mass matching, requiring a generated in silico lipid m/z library for the chosen positive or negative ionisation mode.

name: lipid-metabolite-class-categorization
description: Use when a set of lipids and/or polar metabolites measured from blood samples must be grouped into compound classes before querying pre-analytical stability in ALISTER's Sample search mode.

name: lipid-metabolite-network-extraction
description: Use when you have a MultiABLER-normalized feature table from concurrently acquired LC-MS/MS metabolomics and lipidomics data and need to identify correlated lipid-metabolite pairs, network structure, or the effect of normalization on cross-omics correlation via rCCA/sPLS.

name: lipid-metabolite-nomenclature-matching
description: Use when a user's metabolomics/lipidomics dataset (samples as rows, analytes as columns) contains analyte names that must be reconciled with a curated stability database before stability assessment or data filtering.

name: lipid-molecular-species-level-data-analysis
description: Use when a lipidomic intensity matrix must be analyzed at the lipid molecular species level and a validated supervised discrimination model (PLS-DA) with score, loading, and validation outputs is required.

name: lipid-ms2-spectral-identification
description: Use when preprocessed MS2 lipid spectra (HDF5 2xN m/z/intensity arrays, or mzML for prediction) must be assigned molecular lipid species by a learned fragmentation model instead of spectral-library database matching.

name: lipid-ms2-spectral-library-annotation
description: Use when annotating lipid MS/MS spectra from LC-MS/MS lipidomics data (Thermo .raw, SCIEX .wiff, Bruker/Agilent .d, .mzML) and benchmarking annotation recall against tools like MS-DIAL or LipidMatch.

name: lipid-msi-quantitative-image-visualization
description: Use when ion images from qMSI lipidomics exports (Cardinal HDF5, imzML via LipidQMap) must be reshaped to 2-D maps and compared pixel-wise, e.g. raw vs corrected isobar images on timsTOF fleX TIMS data.

name: lipid-name-abbreviation
description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics annotation list contains long lipid compound names and redundant putative entries that must be shortened to LMSD-style abbreviations and deduplicated.

name: lipid-name-parsing-standardization
description: Use when lipidomics tables (csv/xlsx, flat or pivot, or mzTab-M) contain lipid names from different sources or dialects that must be mapped to standardized shorthand identifiers before computing structural distances, PCA projections, or per-sample quantity statistics.

name: lipid-name-regex-parsing
description: Use when lipidomics molecule names (e.g. from Metabolomics Workbench study ST001111 or Skyline exports) need class, chain-length, and unsaturation annotations inferred from name strings, and some names fail pattern matching.

name: lipid-nomenclature-carbon-double-bond-notation-parsing
description: Use when a lipidomic data table carries lipid identifiers like 'PG 18:1/20:1' or 'PE(P-40:6)' and the goal is to extract fatty-acyl residues (carbon:double-bond notation) and retain only residues meeting carbon-count or saturation criteria.

name: lipid-nomenclature-parsing
description: Use when lipidomics data tables contain lipid species names in mixed dialects (e.g., LIPID MAPS, SwissLipids, shorthand like PC 18:0_16:1) that must be parsed and standardized before structural comparison, PCA, or feature analysis.

name: lipid-nomenclature-parsing
description: Use when an uploaded lipidomic data matrix is keyed by molecular-species identifiers (e.g. 'PC 16:0_18:1') and chain-level lipid building block sub-matrices must be generated for downstream class/species/building-block analyses.

name: lipid-nomenclature-parsing
description: Use when lipid identifiers come from mixed sources (e.g. MS-DIAL, LipidSearch, LIPID MAPS, SwissLipids) in inconsistent notation styles and must be decomposed and cross-compared at a common structural level.

name: lipid-nomenclature-standardisation
description: Use when an annotated m/z feature table contains raw lipid annotation strings (e.g. multi-isomer entries in an all_IsomerNames-style column) that must be collapsed into standard lipid categories and subclasses before downstream statistics.

name: lipid-ontology-enrichment
description: Use when the input is a set of FDR-controlled METASPACE formula-adduct annotations from imaging MS (MS1-only data where isomers/isobars cannot be resolved) and the goal is overrepresentation of lipid-ontology (LION) terms.

name: lipid-ontology-enrichment-analysis

name: lipid-ontology-id-mapping
description: Use when a lipid annotation list (e.g. abbreviations like PC 16:0_18:2) needs identifiers for downstream ontology (LION), pathway (KEGG, Rhea), or network/interaction (UniProtKB, ChEBI) analysis.

name: lipid-precursor-exact-mass-matching
description: Use when you have a peak-picked feature table (e.g., MZmine CSV with m/z, RT, intensities) and in silico lipid precursor libraries, and need candidate lipid/adduct assignments per feature before MS/MS fragment confirmation.

name: lipid-precursor-list-export

name: lipid-precursor-mass-computation
description: Use when designing targeted lipidomics PRM/MRM assays: you need to compute monoisotopic precursor m/z and diagnostic fragment masses from lipid class definitions, fatty acyl chains, and adducts, or generate transition lists for Skyline.

name: lipid-quantification-qc-curve-validation
