name: lipid-refmet-analyte-class-mapping
description: Use when a user-supplied analyte list or uploaded measurement table must be matched to ALISTER's stability database — e.

name: lipid-residue-extraction
description: Use when you have a processed lipidomics table (one lipid identifier per row, one sample per column, e.g. from pandas.read_excel) and need to reprocess analyte annotations into per-sample fatty acid residue abundances rather than individual molecular lipid levels.

name: lipid-retention-time-rule-implementation
description: Use when you have annotated lipid identities paired with LC-MS retention times in one or more datasets and want to quantify conformity of the ECN/IUP/ESCN relative RT ordering rules.

name: lipid-rt-ecn-regression-modeling
description: Use when a lipid feature table with identifications, retention times, and fatty acyl compositions needs per-class RT plausibility checks or filtering of likely incorrect identifications.

name: lipid-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a LipidSigR differential-expression output table of lipid species and want to test whether a priori-defined lipid sets (e.g., lipid classes like Cer, TAG, PC O-) show statistically significant, concordant differences between two biological states (e.g., phenotypes).

name: lipid-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when a lipidomics dataset (Skyline export, numerical matrix, or Metabolomics Workbench file) has been differentially analyzed with lipidr and you need to know which lipid classes or chain characteristics are enriched in the regulated lipids.

name: lipid-shorthand-name-parsing
description: Use when lipid identifiers arrive as heterogeneous shorthand names (LIPID MAPS, SwissLipids, or search-engine dialects from LipidXplorer, LDA, MS-DIAL) and must be converted to a canonical, machine-comparable structure before distance computation or structural comparison.

name: lipid-shorthand-nomenclature-tokenization
description: Use when labeled lipid species strings (e.g. from HDF5 'lipid_species' attributes) must be decomposed into headgroup/fatty-acyl/adduct tokens for seq2seq training, per-component accuracy scoring, or token-level prediction comparison.

name: lipid-shorthand-notation-parsing
description: Use when an uploaded lipidomic matrix or lipid-name list contains vendor shorthand (e.g., PE(P-34:1), sphingoid bases like d16:1, placeholders like 0:0) that must be normalized before LipidOne 2.0 analysis.

name: lipid-shorthand-token-reassembly
description: Use when running LipiDetective prediction on MS2 spectra and you have raw decoded token sequences (headgroup, fatty-acid chain, adduct, end-of-sequence tokens from the 1,032-token vocabulary) that must be converted to lipid shorthand notation strings with confidence values.

name: lipid-species-annotation-parsing
description: Use when raw lipid identification/quantification files from LipidSearch or LIQUID (or a Metabolomics Workbench experiment) must be converted into a structured table of lipid class, chain length, and double-bond strata before normalization or differential analysis.

name: lipid-species-boundary-filtering
description: Use when preprocessing vendor lipidomics output (e.g., LipidSearch or LIQUID tables) whose lipid species names must be validated against class-specific carbon-atom and double-bond limits before downstream normalization or statistical analysis.

name: lipid-species-enumeration-fatty-acyl-chain-space
description: Use when a lipidomics identification module needs a comprehensive predicted lipid database spanning class and composition space beyond available experimental CCS/RT collections, especially for HILIC-IM-MS workflows.

name: lipid-species-parsing-lipid-maps-classification
description: Use when a lipid abundance matrix lacks structured annotations (class, chain composition) and you need to decompose lipid species names before normalization, statistical analysis, or plotting.

name: lipid-spectra-library-formatting
description: Use when a completed Lipid Spectrum Generator run (lipids enumerated by class and fatty-acid composition, spectra per adduct) must be written out as a '.MSP' spectral library for downstream LC-MS/MS lipid identification.

name: lipid-spectral-library-generation
description: Use when constructing a reference spectral library for lipid identification in liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) and experimental library entries are missing or need custom lipid classes/adducts.

name: lipid-spectrum-generator-export-configuration
description: Use when a downstream acquisition or analysis workflow (e.g. Skyline transition lists for targeted MS, or Excalibur precursor lists for Orbitrap DDA) needs lipid species generated by class, fatty-acid composition, and adduct in an importable file format.

name: lipid-sphingolipid-fatty-acid-pathway-flux-analysis
description: Use when comparing flux distributions between host-optimal and virus-optimal objectives in an integrated host–virus genome-scale metabolic model, especially to quantify pathway-level (lipid, sphingolipid, fatty acid) flux perturbations caused by maximal viral growth.

name: lipid-structural-distance-matrix-computation
description: Use when lipid species names have been parsed/standardized (e.g., via Goslin) and a pairwise structural distance/similarity matrix between all distinct lipid species is required for downstream PCA, lipidome comparison, or dendrogram clustering.

name: lipid-structural-feature-encoding
description: Use when preparing structured inputs for the WMYn reverse-lipidomics model: lipid annotations (head group, chain length, degree of unsaturation per fatty acyl chain) must be converted into the feature representation the network consumes before MS2 fingerprint regeneration.

name: lipid-structural-feature-encoding
description: Use when lipid species must be turned into the specialized 26-feature structural vector (lipid class, fatty acid modifier, sum composition) before fitting or applying LiPydomics CCS/HILIC retention time prediction models.

name: lipid-structural-level-mapping-lcl-lms-lbb
description: Use when an uploaded lipidomic data matrix is annotated at molecular-species level (e.g., PC 34:1, TG 52:2 shorthand) and statistical or pathway analyses must be run per lipid class, per molecular species, or per acyl/alkyl building block.

name: lipid-structure-distance-computation-mcs-jaccard
description: Use when pairwise structural distances or similarities between lipid species must be derived from their molecular structures (e.g., to build a structural space PCA model, an arc-shaped lipid ordering, or lipidome-level similarity), rather than from exact name matches or abundances.

name: lipid-structure-maximum-common-subgraph-comparison
description: Use when pairwise structural similarity between lipid species must be quantified from molecular graphs — e.g. building a lipid distance matrix, constructing a lipid space model, or testing whether counting double-bond positions changes the overlap between two fatty acids.

name: lipid-subclass-recall-benchmarking
description: Use when a published lipidomics dataset reports a known set of lipids (e.g. 2704 lipids in the mouse aging-associated lipidome atlas) and you must quantify how many are recovered by a spectral-library search.

name: lipid-transition-list-generation
description: Use when designing targeted lipidomics assays in Skyline or stand-alone LipidCreator that need user-defined target lists and fragment libraries for PRM and MRM experiments across multiple lipid classes.

name: lipid-transition-response-regression
description: Use when targeted SRM/PRM peak areas exported from Skyline for LipidCreator-computed transitions must be checked for linearity against analyte amount, e.g. verifying PUFA-PL ion signatures in a human platelet lipid matrix before releasing a transition list as an assay.

name: lipid-transition-spectral-library-export
description: Use when a targeted lipidomics workflow needs a Skyline-consumable spectral library from computed lipid transitions — e.g., exporting CE-optimized platelet lipid-mediator transition lists as .blib for spectral matching.

name: lipid-type-classification-tallying
description: Use when you have a feature-level annotation workbook (e.g. Additional file 3, Table S4) from LipidMatch, MS-DIAL, and Greazy and need to count unique lipid ions, features, and lipid types for a given polarity such as positive-mode IE-ddMS2-top5 data.

name: lipid-type-composition-auditing
description: Use when you need to quantify or verify the composition of an in silico lipid fragmentation library — e.g., counting lipid species, lipid types, fatty acid combinations, or class/adduct coverage from a library distribution.

name: lipidblast-in-silico-spectral-matching
description: Use when annotating lipid-class features in untargeted AIF LC–MS/MS datasets where no experimental MS/MS spectra are available and in-silico coverage of lipids is needed.

name: lipidmaps-classification-mapping
description: Use when importing lipid identification/quantification tables (LipidSearch or LIQUID outputs, or Metabolomics Workbench experiments) and each lipid species name must be decomposed into class, chain length, and double-bond strata.

name: lipidmaps-database-record-parsing
description: Use when input records are lipid database entries with explicit double-bond positions on carbon chains and you need to extract per-chain double-bond position sets in both carbonyl-forward and methyl-end (ω) counting directions for pairwise comparison.

name: lipidmaps-lmsd-mass-matching
description: Use when a MultiABLER-processed LC-MS/MS feature table needs feature annotation, and lipid versus metabolite classification must be assigned by m/z matching against HMDB and LipidMaps reference mass databases.

name: lipidmaps-reference-download
description: Use when the goal is to quantify overlap between CMM 3.0's in-house oxidized lipid library and public lipid databases, or to establish whether CMM-exclusive oxidized lipid annotations are genuinely novel.

name: lipidome-distance-matrix-serialization
description: Use when a multi-lipidome dataset must be reduced to a single pairwise distance matrix relating all lipidomes structurally, as the basis for hierarchical clustering or QC of large-scale lipidomics studies.

name: lipidome-hausdorff-distance-computation
description: Use when you have two or more lipidomes (e.g., csv/xlsx or mzTab-M tables with lipid species abundances) and need a global structural comparison relating all lipidomes, rather than only exact lipid-name matching.

name: lipidome-pca-projection-visualization
description: Use when lipidome samples must be placed into a shared structural space: an n x n lipid-species distance matrix is available and per-lipidome coordinates plus reportable projection figures are the deliverable.

name: lipidomic-data-matrix-reshaping
description: Use when an uploaded lipidomic matrix is at molecular-species level (rows like PC, PE, TG species) but the target analysis is at the lipid class (LCL) or building block (LBB) structural level.

name: lipidomic-feature-group-statistics
description: Use when a lipidomic data matrix with experimental group assignments must be tested per lipid feature (class, molecular species, or building-block level) to flag significant group differences with significance asterisks.

name: lipidomic-feature-table-preprocessing
description: Use when raw lipidomic or metabolomic peak-intensity feature tables (e.g. MetaboLights S-BSST1038/S-BSST1039 exports) need filtering, imputation, log-transformation, and EigenMS normalization before downstream limma or ClassifyR analysis.

name: lipidomics-annotation-accounting
description: Use when reproducing or auditing lipid annotation counts for an untargeted MS/MS study (e.g. ST002044) where library-match results must be merged with deep-learning fingerprint predictions under explicit Tanimoto and spectral-entropy cutoffs.

name: lipidomics-annotation-appending
description: Use when a feature table (m/z + retention time peaks) contains multiple co-eluting lipid candidates with similar m/z values, and you must rank candidate identifications and append final lipid annotations to the table.

name: lipidomics-annotation-table-summarization
description: Use when comparing which lipid classes and adduct forms are enumerated or annotated across two or more in-silico lipid libraries, and you need to identify classes unique to a single library (e.g., OxPC only in MS-DIAL, CE only in CalicoLipids).

name: lipidomics-batch-effect-correction
description: Use when a lipidomics abundance matrix (LipidSearch/LIQUID output or Metabolomics Workbench data) spans multiple acquisition batches and the user wants corrected values feeding the differential lipid abundance analysis (MA/volcano plots).

name: lipidomics-ccs-correction-application
description: Use when raw negative-mode TIMS CCS measurements from constituent datasets (e.g. Vasilopoulou et al., Tsugawa et al.) must be linearly calibrated toward DT reference CCS values and the post-correction MDRE reported.

name: lipidomics-cross-reference-count-validation
description: Use when a lipid annotation list must be linked to LION ontology, KEGG compound, ChEBI entity, Rhea reaction, or UniProtKB protein identifiers and the output needs to be tabulated and validated against reported match counts.

name: lipidomics-data-import-from-skyline-exports
description: Use when targeted lipidomics measurements have been exported from Skyline as a CSV file and need to be loaded into R for lipidr-based quality control, normalization, summarization, or differential analysis.

name: lipidomics-data-integration
description: Use when a list of lipid annotations (e.g. shorthand notations like PC 16:0_18:2) must be mapped to ontology/pathway/reaction IDs (LION, KEGG, ChEBI, Rhea, UniProtKB) and coverage gaps per lipid class must be assessed.

name: lipidomics-data-table-import-flat-pivot-csv-xlsx
description: Use when the input is a lipidomics abundance table (csv, xlsx, or mzTab-M) with lipid species names in row-wise or column-wise (pivot) orientation that must be loaded and its heterogeneous lipid nomenclature standardized.

name: lipidomics-database-construction-sqlite
description: Use when building a broad-coverage lipid identification database from scratch — enumerating lipid species by class, chain length (10–30 carbons, even/odd) and unsaturation (0–6) — to back IM-MS/HILIC lipid identification with predicted CCS and RT values.

name: lipidomics-database-coverage-mapping
description: Use when auditing which lipid annotation formats / source tools a converter supports, or when compiling a reference table of lipid identification software vs. lipid database notation styles.

name: lipidomics-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when a preprocessed lipidomics data matrix (from LipidSearch/LIQUID outputs or a Metabolomics Workbench experiment) is loaded in the ADViSELipidomics Shiny app and you need unsupervised/supervised dimension reduction, sample clustering, or interactive exploratory visualizations.

name: lipidomics-feature-count-benchmarking
description: Use when you have identifications from ≥2 lipid annotation software appended to the same MZmine feature table and need to compare annotation coverage and cross-software corroboration per polarity.

name: lipidomics-feature-importance-analysis
description: Use when a lipidomics abundance table (csv/xlsx, flat or pivot, or mzTab-M) with attached study variables must be reduced to the lipid subset that explains each variable.

name: lipidomics-feature-set-overlap-analysis
description: Use when you have LC-MS/MS lipidomics feature annotations from two spectral libraries and need to quantify annotation overlap, library agreement on lipid class/composition/adduct, or reproduce per-instrument identification counts.

name: lipidomics-feature-table-prefiltering
description: Use when raw vendor lipidomics identification/quantification tables (LipidSearch or LIQUID outputs) or Metabolomics Workbench experiments must be imported, pre-filtered, and lipid species decomposed into class/chain/double-bond strata.

name: lipidomics-identification-count-tabulation
description: Use when you have aligned, peak-picked IM-MS lipidomics feature tables (one per ESI mode) and need lipid annotations ranked by confidence tier, with per-tier identification counts comparable to the paper's Figure 6J pattern.

name: lipidomics-internal-standard-quantification
description: Use when a raw lipidomics matrix contains peak area/height intensities plus an internal standard table with known concentrations, and the goal is a concentration matrix per molecular species.

name: lipidomics-library-coverage-benchmarking
description: Use when reproducing or verifying library-composition claims for a lipid identification tool, or comparing the number of lipid types/species covered across open-source lipidomics software.

name: lipidomics-metadata-annotation
description: Use when a lipidomics matrix (numerical matrix, Skyline CSV export, or Metabolomics Workbench file) contains lipid molecule name strings that need class, chain-length, and double-bond annotations, or when some names fail pattern matching.

name: lipidomics-msms-slice-formation-in-mz-rt-space
description: Use when processing LC-MS/MS lipidomics or metabolomics mzML data where MS/MS scans must be linked to quantified MS1 peak groups across multiple samples.

name: lipidomics-msms-spectral-matching
description: Use when in-house Thermo lipidomics mzML files need per-feature MS/MS-based lipid annotations via library spectral matching, or when comparing alternative in-silico lipid libraries.

name: lipidomics-multivariate-pca-analysis
description: Use when a lipidomics dataset (Skyline export, numerical matrix, or Metabolomics Workbench study such as ST001111) has been imported as a LipidomicsExperiment and you need PCA scores plots for quality control, outlier detection, or pattern discovery.

name: lipidomics-multivariate-statistical-analysis
description: Use when you have an annotated lipidomics feature table (e.g. thousands of m/z features across replicate strain/treatment groups, such as Par, Dap2, Dal2, Van4) and need PCA/PLS-DA clustering plus per-feature fold-change statistics to compare lipidomes.

name: lipidomics-peak-table-filtering
description: Use when you have a chromatographic peak table from Compound Discoverer (v3.3 .cdResult or .csv) plus lipid identifications and want to remove adduct peaks, in-source fragments, dimers, and redundant unidentified features correlated with identified lipids before downstream statistics.

name: lipidomics-precursor-ion-targeting
description: Use when specific lipid species must be confirmed or quantified as precursor-ion targets in HRMS full-scan lipidomics data (e.g., Waters Synapt G2 HDMS runs of FASN-inhibitor treated vs. control cells) rather than discovered by untargeted feature finding.

name: lipidomics-qc-filtering
description: Use when downstream of LipiDex 2 Peak Finder and Spectrum Searcher results you need to remove spurious/redundant lipid identifications and unidentified features using automated lipid-specific QC thresholds before statistical analysis.

name: lipidomics-qc-threshold-evaluation
description: Use when reprocessing LC-MS/MS lipidomics peak tables (e.g., Compound Discoverer .cdResult-derived identifications) and you must validate automated filter decisions on lipid identifications using RSD, RT, and spectral-match evidence, with or without manual curation.

name: lipidomics-quality-control-reporting
description: Use when lipidome quantity tables (csv/xlsx pivot or flat, or mzTab-M) have been imported and you must verify that lipid intensity values follow the expected -digit reciprocal distribution before downstream analysis.

name: lipidomics-query-throughput-reproduction
description: Use when reproducing or verifying claims that spectral-library query time is independent of library size, or when benchmarking MS/MS search engines (LipidIN EQ vs Flash Entropy Search) for per-query latency.

name: lipidomics-residue-table-aggregation
description: Use when you have a final lipidomic abundance table (lipid species as row index, samples as columns) and need per-residue fatty acid abundances aggregated across replicate groups for cross-sample or cross-cell-type comparison.

name: lipidomics-spectrum-classification
description: Use when you have raw untargeted LC-MS lipidomics spectra (mzML or npy per sample) with class labels (e.g. 928 CCLE cell lines across 23 cancer types) and need end-to-end disease-type classification without peak picking or annotation.

name: lipidomics-spectrum-quality-control
description: Use when raw lipid MS2 spectra (e.g. from phospholipid standard measurements or profile-mode mzML) must be cleaned, normalized, and filtered before deep-learning training or downstream identification in tools like LipiDetective.

name: lipidomics-table-reprocessing
description: Use when a processed lipidomics table (lipid names as index, samples as columns) contains analyte identifiers in 'CLASS N:N/M:M' or RefMet form and you need per-sample fatty acid residue counts.

name: lipidomics-time-course-data-processing
description: Use when analyzing LC-MS/MS lipidomics feature tables from a stable-isotope labeling time course (e.g., [U-13C6]glucose 0-32 h) and you need isotopologue distributions, natural abundance correction, or clustering of labeling kinetics.

name: lipidomics-tissue-type-separation-analysis
description: Use when you have paired tissue lipidomics samples (e.g., SAT and VAT from the same patients), patient metadata for fixed/random effects, and you need to verify that LMM adjustment improves tissue-type separation in PCA.

name: lipidr-workflow-execution
description: Use when a Metabolomics Workbench lipidomics study (e.g., ST001111, measure="Area") has been imported as a LipidomicsExperiment and you need to run multivariate quality control such as PCA to detect outlier samples.

name: lipidsearch-output-import
description: Use when the input consists of LipidSearch output files (identification + quantification, with an accompanying target file) that must be loaded into ADViSELipidomics, pre-filtered, and parsed into lipid class/chain/double-bond strata.

name: lipidsearch-output-preprocessing
description: Use when the input is a LipidSearch (or LIQUID) lipid identification/quantification output and the goal is a cleaned, LIPID MAPS-parsed concentration matrix ready for exploratory or statistical lipidomics analysis.

name: lipidspecies-lipidmaps-annotation-parsing
description: Use when lipid quantification matrices arrive as LipidSearch or LIQUID vendor outputs (or a Metabolomics Workbench experiment download) and lipid species names must be decomposed into LIPID MAPS-compliant structural information before analysis.

name: lipoprotein-edta-cluster-simulation
description: Use when no public annotated NMR spectra database exists and synthetic labeled 1H plasma training spectra with realistic lipoprotein/EDTA clusters are needed to train a quantification model such as CRNN.

name: lipoprotein-subclass-quantification
description: Use when 1H NMR human plasma spectra (CSV with chemical shifts in the first column and one column per sample) need decomposition into metabolite and lipoprotein-cluster concentrations via NMRQNet's CRNN initial fitting.

name: liputils-exported-api-usage
description: Use when a lipidomics table with RefMet-compliant lipid names as the row index must be reprocessed into residue counts, or when residues must be kept/discarded by predicates such as saturated() and max_carbon(residue, n) cutoffs.

name: list-only-ion-fraction-quantification
description: Use when MZmine full-scan and DDA MS/MS feature tables plus a RegFilter SPL exist and you need to quantify coverage losses — e.g. 'what fraction of list-only ions were MS1 base peaks that DDA failed to fragment?'

name: literature-component-subtractive-scoring
description: Use when prioritizing natural extracts for chemical novelty and you need a literature-coverage score per taxon, computed independently of spectral data, from reported compound counts in LOTUS for species, genus, and family.

name: literature-database-curation
description: Use when compiling or updating a small-molecule/bioadduct annotation database from published sources, or when reproducing an overlap comparison between a new curated database and prior databases to report added entries and excluded entries with rationale.

name: literature-support-status-curation
description: Use when MINNO boundary-flux analysis has flagged reactions missing from the KEGG database and you must classify each as publication-supported (e.g. the six confirmed B. burgdorferi purine reactions) or homology-backed.

name: litsearchr-keyword-extraction
description: Use when annotating a discriminant MOFA (or DIABLO) factor: once PubMed abstracts have been retrieved for the factor's top omics contributors, litsearchr text-mining converts those abstracts into a biologically interpretable keyword list.

name: live-cell-time-lapse-kinetics-fitting
description: Use when a background-corrected two-color (e.g. CFP/YFP) live-cell time-lapse confocal series is available and you need time-resolved colocalization proportions plus a fitted dissociation rate after a perturbation such as LMB.

name: living-data-continuous-reanalysis
description: Use when quantifying how many spectral library matches a deposited public MS/MS dataset gains over time as community reference libraries are updated, or when validating 'living data' growth claims against reported reference points.

name: llm-prompt-based-metabolite-annotation
description: Use when a targeted or untargeted LC-MS peak table contains m/z features that HMDB/MassBank matching in SMART 2.0 cannot assign (e.g., heroin, nimetazepam), and database lookup fails for narcotics-like compounds.

name: lme4-random-intercept-specification
description: Use when metabolomics profiles contain repeated measurements or clustered samples from the same patients/subjects (e.g. paired tissue types) and subject-specific variation must be absorbed before PLS-DA/OPLS-DA.

name: lmm-processed-vs-original-data-contrast
description: Use when you have discriminative feature lists (VIP > 1) from PLS-DA run on both LMM- and M0-processed metabolomics matrices and need to quantify shared vs. uniquely selected metabolites between processing strategies.

name: lobov-validation-accuracy-interpretation
description: Use when projected Nightingale Health 1H-NMR surrogate scores (e.g. diabetes, high hscrp) need their discriminative performance (ROC AUC) and Platt-calibrated metrics (ECE/MCE/logLoss) validated against MiMIR's published LOBOV reference accuracies.

name: local-fdr-estimation
description: Use when you must reject null hypotheses for thousands of metabolite features at explicit fdr2d cutoffs (e.g. 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3) and need reproducible per-level rejection counts.

name: local-maxima-apex-selection
description: Use when you must define integration limits for targeted LC–MS chromatographic peaks from RT/intensity vectors of extracted ion chromatograms, given a target list with expected retention times.

name: local-maxima-peak-detection-parameter-matching
description: Use when validating or reimplementing asari's chromatographic peak calling on composite mass tracks, e.g. to recompute snr and cSelectivity from export/cmap.pickle and compare against full_Feature_table.tsv values.

name: local-maximum-peak-detection
description: Use when you need to locate and quantify discrete peaks in a 1D intensity array (such as an extracted ion chromatogram from MZA data) and can validate detections against known or ground-truth peak positions and heights.

name: local-minima-detection-between-ejections
description: Use when you have an AEMS run with a per-ejection time table and a TIC trace, and need to assign each ejection a bounded detection window (min_time, peak_time, max_time) before peak integration or quantification.

name: locality-sensitive-hashing-reference-matching
description: Use when timsTOF/TDF raw DDA-PASEF frames must be screened for peptide isotope patterns without a classical peak-picking pipeline, e.g., to match vendor-selected precursors from a .d folder via hashed averagine references.

name: locality-sensitive-hashing-window-collision-classification
description: Use when raw Bruker TDF/timsTOF frames (e.g. DDA-PASEF) must be strongly reduced (≥50% of data points) before downstream processing while preserving vendor-selected precursor peaks, with tunable (m,n) hash parameters.

name: lock-mass-spectral-recalibration
description: Use when imported centroided .imzML lipid MSI files exhibit m/z drift across pixels and you need mass-axis stabilization before dynamic binning, lipid annotation, or quantitation in pmol/mm².

name: loess-baseline-smoothing
description: Use when MALDI-MS or ESI-MS spectra carry an irregular, drifting baseline that must be estimated with LOESS and subtracted before peak detection or replicate comparison, and the data must remain accessible as plain data frames.

name: loess-batch-correction-of-lc-ms-feature-tables
description: Use when a QC-filtered LC-MS feature table contains pooled/intrastudy QC injections in run order and time-related signal drift must be removed from study-sample intensities before normalization or statistical analysis.

name: loess-drift-modeling
description: Use when pooled/intrastudy QC samples in an LC–MS batch (e.g., mzML files from MetaboLights MTBLS1919) show time-related systematic variance — signal drift along PC1 of a PCA score plot — that must be modeled and removed over injection order.

name: loess-drift-trend-fitting
description: Use when MRM sample files contain QC samples and systematic signal drift across injection order must be corrected per compound, e.g. BQC regression slope != 0 before correction.

name: loess-spline-eic-smoothing
description: Use when deconvolving MS1-only LC/HRMS data with IDSL.CSA: you need Pearson correlation coefficients between co-eluting peaks' EICs to be robust to noise and irregular sampling before grouping ions into CSA composite spectra clusters.

name: log-fold-change-pooling
description: Use when contributing studies report only aggregate statistics (fold-change plus sample size, no raw data) and a per-compound combined effect direction and magnitude must be derived.

name: log-hazard-ratio-weight-computation
description: Use when building a weighted additive biomarker risk score from published Cox meta-analysis HRs (e.g., 14 Nightingale NMR biomarkers for all-cause mortality) and you need score weights plus a per-unit score HR.

name: log-likelihood-implementation
description: Use when a metabolomics matrix has missing values below a known limit of detection (LOD), so observed values are left-truncated, and maximum-likelihood (mu, sigma^2) estimates are needed as standardization parameters for KNN-TN imputation.

name: log-likelihood-ratio-spectrum-scoring
description: Use when tandem mass spectra must be matched to candidate molecules from a structure database (e.g., PubChem, DNP) with calibrated FDR, rather than heuristic peak-count scores like MetFrag or EPIC.

name: log-log-linear-regression-calibration
description: Use when calibrating traveling-wave ion mobility drift-time measurements to CCS values (e.g., Waters Synapt G2Si LC-IMS-MS/MS data) where the drift time is not directly CCS-proportional and requires nonlinear-to-linear transformation before regression.

name: log-normal-kernel-dissociation-profile-modeling
description: Use when building targeted lipidomics assays that need per-fragment collision energy optimization from CE-dependent relative intensity measurements on QExactive HF or QTOF instruments.

name: log-normal-prior-parameter-estimation
description: Use when building ZODIAC-style weighted assignment graphs from SIRIUS top-50 formula candidates and fragmentation trees, and you need data-driven prior parameters (mu, sigma^2, tau) for similarity-based Bayesian reranking.

name: log-odds-score-normalization
description: Use when ranking candidate molecular formulas from high-resolution MS1 isotope patterns, where measured peak intensities must be compared to theoretical patterns with both absolute (σ_abs = 0.01) and relative (σ_rel = 0.08) noise terms.

name: log-rank-significance-testing
description: Use when comparing overall survival distributions between predicted risk groups (e.g. VAE-derived or IMDC-defined) on held-out patient cohorts and needing a significance p-value.

name: log-scale-plot-annotation
description: Use when the task is to graphically summarize two-dimensional FDR (fdr2d) multiple-testing results for metabolomics biomarker discovery as volcano/tornado scatter plots with fdr2d isolines overlaid.

name: log-space-abundance-back-transformation
description: Use when applying notame's correct_drift() to LC-MS feature abundances: you log-transform the exprs matrix, fit a smooth.spline to QC samples across injection order, correct in log space, then must convert the corrected matrix back to linear intensities for output.

name: log-transform-intensity-preprocessing
description: Use when metabolomics feature intensities are on a raw linear scale and are about to be fed into Metanorm's robust normalization methods, which expect log-transformed inputs.

name: log-transform-robust-scaling-of-retention-times
description: Use when preparing RT pairs (e.g. DNN predictions from SMRT vs experimental PredRet RTs) for GP-based projection or regression fitting, so skewed RTs are transformed to a comparable scale.

name: log-transformation-for-normality
description: Use when metabolomics abundance data (e.g. myocardial infarction, atherothrombotic, or African Race metabolite matrices) are skewed before KNN-TN imputation or distribution-based simulation of missing values.

name: log-transformation-of-feature-abundances
description: Use when a raw metabolomics data matrix in the featuredata format (unique sample names as row names, unique metabolite names as column names) has skewed positive intensities needing log transformation, or when a NormalizeMets normalization call such as NormQcsamples should log-transform its output.

name: log-transformation-with-column-scaling
description: Use when a raw GC/MS intensity matrix (e.g., metabolites x samples) shows skewed feature abundance distributions and must be preprocessed for metabolite identification or biomarker discovery.

name: log2-error-tolerance-accuracy-assessment
description: Use when evaluating accuracy of inferred response factors or absolute concentrations against known true values, particularly for comparing MetaboPAC against negative control baselines like random or constant response factors.

name: log2-fold-change-calculation
description: Use when you have a MetaPro-exported run-1 quantification report (.xlsx) from a benchmark mixture with designed SB:SA dilution ratios (e.g. 1/16 to 16/1 plus Gm controls) and need to verify quantification accuracy per platform.

name: log2-fold-change-computation
description: Use when you have an LC-MS/MS feature abundance table with group metadata and need per-feature effect sizes (log-2 fold changes) to overlay with globaltest cluster-wise P-values for feature prioritization.

name: log2-fold-change-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when an annotated lipidomics feature table has two strain/condition groups to compare and you need per-feature log2 fold-change statistics and a heat map to spot lipid class-level abundance patterns.

name: log2-intensity-standardisation
description: Use when feeding raw peak-intensity CSV matrices into PLAGE/ORA/GSEA pathway-activity scoring, since mPLAGE requires imputed, log2-scaled, zero-mean/unit-variance intensities before SVD decomposition.

name: log2-intensity-transformation
description: Use when a raw metabolite abundance matrix (e.g. AUC peak areas integrated in MultiQuant from LC-MS/MS runs) must be placed on an additive scale before within-batch signal-drift correction or RUV-III batch adjustment in the hRUV pipeline.

name: log2-intensity-transformation
description: Use when a raw LC/MS metabolomics feature table (e.g. moDC Dataset S1) with missing values and untransformed intensities must be normalized before mummichog QC filtering and reference-list construction.

name: log2fold-change-thresholding
description: Use when you have a batch-corrected LC-MS feature table from a two-group dietary/condition contrast and need a statistically defensible list of differentially abundant metabolites with a volcano plot.

name: logfc-rank-based-enrichment-testing
description: Use when you have two-group differential-expression results for lipids (e.g. cancer vs benign tissue) and want to test whether specific lipid classes, total chain lengths, or unsaturation patterns are preferentially enriched.

name: logistic-regression-model-fitting
description: Use when a labeled set of true/false LC-MS peaks has been scored with tabular peak group parameters (e.g., medRelFWHM) and you need an interpretable classifier or parameter ranking via logistic regression with forward selection.

name: logistic-regression-peak-filtering
description: Use when filtering MZmine 2 peak lists from nontargeted LC-MS metabolomics data and you need an interpretable, tabular-feature classifier that scores peak groups as true vs false without converting peaks to raster images.

name: logp-polarity-grouping-of-compounds
description: Use when evaluating formula-prediction output on a held-out test set and you need per-compound-property breakdowns (LogP polarity, mass range, chemical superclass) of top-k accuracy rather than a single pooled score.

name: long-format-ms-spectra-table-construction
description: Use when raw vendor HRMS acquisitions (Waters UNIFI (HD)MSE, or Thermo RAW converted to mzML) must be turned into an open, compact long-format table (rt, scanid, mslevel, mz, intensity, plus bin/dt for ion mobility) for downstream querying in R or Python.

name: long-term-qc-pool-monitoring
description: Use when you have repeated injections of a long-term QC pool (mzML/mzXML from untargeted MS metabolomics) and need to detect slow m/z, RT, intensity or peak-shape drift over batches, e.g. flagging m/z deviations > 20 ppm.

name: long-term-qc-pool-retrospective-analysis
description: Use when untargeted MS metabolomics data (mzML from pooled QC injections) must be retro-inspected across batches for systematic m/z offsets, calibrant intensity loss, or tailing/asymmetry degradation on a specific instrument such as a Waters Synapt.

name: longest-common-subcluster-detection
description: Use when comparing complete vs fragmented (or merged) BGCs — e.g. metagenome or pan-genome assemblies — where a purely global Pfam-domain alignment would misalign non-corresponding genes, and pairwise distances must reflect the shared subcluster.

name: longest-path-extraction-in-metabolic-networks
description: Use when a directed reaction network of correlated metabolite-transcript mass shifts has been converted into per-substrate DAGs and you need to report the longest valid reaction path from each initial metabolite as a candidate pathway.

name: longevity-mutant-phenotype-annotation
description: Use when MutMap SNP-index analysis of EMS-mutagenised long-lived non-CID suppressor strains has produced candidate gene calls and you must assign each causal nonsense mutation (e.g. gst-13, mtk-1, nsy-1, smg-1, smg-2, sur-2, rcd-1) to specific EMS strain numbers.

name: longitudinal-cv-statistics-computation
description: Use when you have a run-by-feature intensity/RT matrix from repeated longitudinal DIA injections (e.g., a 31-day WMLD DIA series) and need to quantify per-precursor detection stability via CV statistics.

name: longitudinal-fragment-profile-construction
description: Use when you have multi-collision-energy MS/MS spectra per reference compound (e.g. 13 NCEs and stepped NCE 20/40/60%) and need per-fragment intensity vectors across the CE series before similarity scoring.

name: longitudinal-gradient-normalization
description: Use when 2D DESI-MSI ion-intensity images of a linear developmental axis (e.g., maize root tip-to-mature gradient) must be projected to normalized 1D linescans and clustered by enrichment pattern.

name: longitudinal-intensity-trend-visualization
description: Use when a series of mzML files (e.g. pooled QC injections spanning weeks) needs per-compound intensity timelines to reveal drift, degradation, or sensitivity loss across batches.

name: longitudinal-metabolomics-data-analysis
description: Use when analyzing metabolite abundance tables collected across developmental stages or time points (e.g., 1H-NMR metabolite concentrations from sequential cell populations) to reduce dimensionality and identify cell-specific metabolic subnetworks.

name: longitudinal-metabolomics-outcome-prediction
description: Use when a longitudinal metabolomics dataset has a binary outcome label (e.g., recovered vs deceased COVID-19 categories) and the goal is outcome prediction with ROC/AUC evaluation and feature-importance inspection.

name: longitudinal-mixed-effects-regression
description: Use when a metabolomics intensity table must be regressed per metabolite on study-design covariates, especially longitudinal/repeated-measures designs needing mixed effects, or intensities censored at detection limits.

name: longitudinal-network-comparison
description: Use when a longitudinal abundance table and a pre-built co-occurrence network are available and the goal is to test whether per-sample subnetwork topology at later timepoints diverges from a baseline timepoint.

name: longitudinal-omics-regression-testing
description: Use when feature abundance data (KO table or compound table with KEGG C numbers) are paired with a continuous or time-point metadata variable and you need threshold-free pathway-level enrichment along that variable.

name: longitudinal-stage-sample-labeling
description: Use when an NMR-derived metabolite table spans multiple differentiation stages (hESC, EB, Rosette, hNPC, Neuron) and samples must be tagged with stage labels before normalization/PCA.

name: longitudinal-system-suitability-monitoring
description: Use when a series of Thermo Orbitrap autoQC/system-suitability .raw files is available across time or instruments and you must verify retention-time linearity (iRT calibration slope, intercept, R²) without converting to mzML.

name: loocv-result-aggregation
description: Use when validating a known-to-unknown metabolite identification method by LOOCV plus an external test set, specifically to determine whether identification is valid when a structure-related metabolite exists in the database.

name: lookup-rank-metrics-computation
description: Use when you have two non-overlapping (by inchi_key) spectral libraries — a query library and a main library with (mass, intensity) spectra — and need top-k lookup error/recall metrics for predicted versus experimental EI-MS spectra.

name: loopless-fva-solution-inspection
description: Use when a PyCoMo/COBRApy community model (SBML) predicts exchange or cross-feeding fluxes absent from the original member-model analysis and you suspect an internal loop; compare standard vs. loopless FVA to flag them.

name: lorentzian-peak-synthesis-from-reference-library
description: Use when training an NMR metabolite identification/quantification model (e.g., CRNN) but no annotated spectra database is available, and synthetic 1H plasma training spectra with known metabolite concentrations must be simulated.

name: loss-of-function-impact-annotation
description: Use when comparing predicted coding-impact calls across annotation tools against ClinVar high-review-status variants, or when LoF/PVS1 misassignment is expected to drive ACMG classification changes.

name: lotus-compound-report-count-retrieval
description: Use when computing Inventa's Literature Component (LC) requires per-taxon compound report counts from LOTUS at the species, genus, and family levels for each sample in a GNPS-format metadata table.

name: lotus-reference-provenance-filtering
description: Use when you need to extract only referenced structure–organism pairs attributable to the LOTUS initiative from Wikidata, or reproduce LOTUS' reference/provenance validation filters on candidate occurrence pairs.

name: lotus-taxon-reported-class-subtraction
description: Use when prioritizing natural extracts for chemical novelty and you need to flag CANOPUS/NPClassifier-predicted chemical classes that are absent from literature reports for the extract's species and genus.

name: louvain-community-detection
description: Use when a weighted metabolite similarity network (e.g. GNPS/MassIVE cosine-similarity edges) must be partitioned into communities without preset cluster counts, to reconstruct MCN structure or quantify singleton reduction.

name: louvain-community-detection-on-molecular-networks
description: Use when a scored NP Analyst network (nodes = MS features/samples, edges = bioactivity-weighted associations) needs partitioning into communities for Compound Activity Mapping visualization and prioritization of bioactive MS features.

name: louvain-graph-clustering
description: Use when a spatial metabolomics peak table (pixels x ion intensities with X/Y coordinates) needs to be segmented into spatial tissue regions whose alignment with histology (e.g. H&E) must be assessed, or when comparing preprocessing impact on clustering.

name: louvain-graph-community-clustering
description: Use when you have an all-pairs spectral similarity matrix (e.g., Spec2Vec or modified cosine over ~95,320 positive-ionization MS/MS spectra) and need to decompose the molecular network into well-connected communities for downstream structural clustering analysis.

name: louvain-partition-consumption
description: Use when a molecular network already has Louvain community labels (e.g., from a spectral-similarity edge list) and you need interpretable, cycle-free per-cluster subnetworks that preserve connectivity of every assigned metabolite.

name: low-abundance-compound-annotation
description: Use when the urine feature table contains low-abundance peaks lacking MS/MS fragmentation but with accurate mass and retention time that fall within condition-matched in-house library tolerance windows for m/z and RT.

name: low-field-benchtop-nmr-mixture-quantification
description: Use when a mixture spectrum comes from a low-field benchtop 1H NMR spectrometer (e.g. Magritek 43 MHz) with nearly complete peak overlap, or when peak-picking quantification has failed on overlapping signals.

name: low-rank-matrix-factorization-pytorch
description: Use when enhancing an MLP or GNN spectral predictor so co-occurring spectral-peak dependencies are learned, by adding a rank-limited (e.g. correlation_mat_rank=100) mixing matrix and an auxiliary LDA topic-distribution head.

name: low-resolution-ms2-spectrum-peak-annotation
description: Use when a low-resolution MS2 spectrum (e.g., from a miniaturized mass spectrometer) has top fragmentation peaks that need structural annotation, and no library match or negative standard is available.

name: low-resolution-msn-spectrum-interpretation
description: Use when MS2 spectra from a miniaturized/low-resolution ion trap instrument must be converted into candidate molecular structures without a library match, e.g. on-site identification of drug-class substances.

name: low-resolution-peak-list-handling
description: Use when the input is a low-resolution tandem MSn spectrum from a miniaturized mass spectrometer (peak list by ion intensity) and you need clean, size-limited peak lists for de novo structure prediction with TeFT.

name: low-resolution-peak-selection-and-averaging
description: Use when handling low-resolution MSn peak lists from a miniaturized mass spectrometer that will feed fragmentation-tree-based de novo structure prediction (e.g., TeFT), and you need to select, cap, and error-correct peaks.

name: low-variance-metabolite-flagging
description: Use when an uploaded .csv or .xlsx metabolomics table has been parsed (primary ID, group/factor, and metabolite concentration columns identified) and metabolite columns must be screened for near-constant values before imputation and normalization.

name: lowess-residual-scaler-fitting
description: Use when aligning two independently processed same-method nontargeted LC-MS datasets whose RT and m/z drift between runs, and Source features must be scaled to a Target dataset before match identification.

name: lowess-retention-time-calibration-to-reference-sample
description: Use when aligned per-sample mass tracks (from centroided mzML files) show retention time drift across samples in a study and must be mapped to a common reference sample before aggregating into composite mass tracks.

name: lrms-hrms-resolution-coverage-interpretation
description: Use when choosing between or interpreting results from LRMS (QqQ SIM/NS) and HRMS (qTOF, GC-Orbitrap) acquisition for stable-isotope tracing, or when tabulating instrument-specific isotopologue coverage and isotope ratio fidelity.

name: lsh-hash-collision-signal-classification
description: Use when raw TimsTOF LC-IMS-MS frames (e.g., DDA-PASEF precursor frames from a .d folder) must be denoised or reduced in size while retaining true peptide signal, and intensity thresholding is inadequate.

name: lsh-parameter-sweep-evaluation
description: Use when tuning (m,n) AND/OR-connective settings of an LSH signal/noise classifier on TimsTOF LC-IMS-MS frames, to quantify false-positive/false-negative rates or the data-reduction vs. retained-precursor trade-off.

name: lsh-random-projection-clustering
description: Use when a large mass spectra collection (e.g., millions of LC-MS/MS spectra from GeMS/MassIVE GNPS) contains redundant similar spectra and you need near-duplicate clusters in linear time before capping or subsampling.

name: lsh-scalability-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify how an MS raw-data processing implementation (e.g. LSH classification of TimsTOF frames) scales with parallelism before committing it to large-scale pipelines.

name: lstm-detector-training
description: Use when training a deep learning BGC detector from labeled Pfam TSV training examples (MIBiG positives vs. artificial negatives) and you need cross-validated AUC comparison to an HMM baseline like ClusterFinder.

name: lstm-sequence-detection-inference
description: Use when you have bacterial genome FASTA files and need domain-level BGC detection scores with reduced false positives, especially to detect novel BGC classes that HMM-based tools like ClusterFinder miss.

name: lstm-sequence-model-training
description: Use when training a BGC detection model on Pfam TSV gene features with pfam2vec embeddings, or when reproducing leave-class-out validation AUCs comparing DeepBGC against ClusterFinder.

name: ly6g-ifm-mask-based-roi-extraction
description: Use when registered MALDI MSI and immunofluorescence microscopy (IFM) data are available with a segmented cell-type marker mask (e.g. Ly6G for neutrophils) and the goal is to isolate that cell population's pixel spectra for ROI-restricted downstream analysis.

name: m2s-penalty-score-matching
description: Use when combining two separately peak-picked untargeted LC–MS metabolomics datasets (e.g. two batches or two cohorts) that have already gone through QC and peak-picking, and you need feature-level correspondence using only RT, m/z, and FI values.

name: ma-plot-visualization
description: Use when an experimental biologist needs to visualize gene expression changes across thousands of genes as an MA plot from a CSV expression table, without writing R code.

name: ma-volcano-plot-visualization
description: Use when a lipidomics differential analysis (LipidSearch/LIQUID outputs or Metabolomics Workbench data) has already been fitted under a defined experimental design and comparison, and differentially abundant lipids must be depicted with MA and Volcano plots.

name: maccs-and-morgan-fingerprint-computation
description: Use when scoring de novo molecular structure predictions from tandem MS spectra — e.g. evaluating TeFT candidates on the 660-spectrum GNPS/HMDB(5.0)/MoNA test set — by comparing predicted vs. real structures at Tanimoto 1.0, 0.9, and 0.8 thresholds.

name: machine-learning-analyte-discrimination
description: Use when GC–MS or LC–MS chromatography–MS data must be mined for multivariate chemo-/biomarker marker features at very low (parts-per-billion) analyte concentrations and conventional peak picking is undesirable, e.g., untargeted metabolomics of aroma odor or human breath samples.

name: machine-learning-classifier-training
description: Use when building or retraining a classifier (e.g., random forest peak-reporting model) from tabulated feature/quality scores plus curated 0/1/2 expert labels, with F1-validated hyperparameter tuning.

name: machine-learning-metric-evaluation-roc-f1
description: Use when a pixel-wise classifier trained on labeled mass spectra (e.g., massNet or SVM on MALDI FT-ICR MSI data) must be benchmarked on a withheld test set with accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, ROC, and runtime.

name: machine-learning-model-evaluation
description: Use when you have a labeled peak-quality development set and multiple metric-set × ML-algorithm candidate classifiers, and must choose one global classifier with statistically defensible evidence before deploying it on independent datasets.

name: machine-learning-peak-classification
description: Use when preprocessing batches of MRM-mode LC-MS raw data (mzML) where chromatographic peaks must be detected, scored, and automatically accepted/rejected without manual peak review.

name: machine-learning-peak-filtering-evaluation
description: Use when you have TARDIS-extracted peak quality metrics for targeted LC–MS peaks (with Good/Bad/Ambiguous labels) across one or more biofluid matrices and want to train or reproduce a random-forest peak-quality classifier or assess its filtering reliability.

name: machine-learning-performance-aggregation
description: Use when evaluating a multi-model, multi-class prediction tool (e.g. one model per CYP450 enzyme) and you need per-class cross-validation AUROC plus an aggregate average to compare against reported benchmarks (0.83-0.92 for CypReact vs 0.75 ADMET Predictor and 0.53 SMARTCyp).

name: machine-readable-parameter-serialization
description: Use when extracting processing parameter sets from supplementary tables or software documentation of a multi-platform metabolomics workflow (e.g., five CE-MS and HILIC-MS methods) and they must be persisted as structured, method-keyed records.

name: machine-readable-peak-list-export
description: Use when a spectrum has already been located via a USI (GNPS task, MassBank accession, MetaboLights/Workbench dataset, ProteomeXchange scan) and the underlying peak list must be retrieved as structured data for downstream scripts or reproducible reporting.

name: machine-replicate-averaging
description: Use when an LC/MS metabolomics feature table contains machine-replicate injections per sample and a consensus feature intensity table is needed before pathway/network analysis with mummichog.

name: macro-averaged-multiclass-metrics-computation
description: Use when scoring multi-class classifiers (e.g., 12-class Canine Sarcoma) on a fixed independent hold-out test set, where per-class performance must be averaged equally via macro-averaged Accuracy and F1-Score.

name: macrocycle-topology-scoring-bias-correction
description: Use when two candidate molecules (e.g., a linear molecule and its cyclic macro-topology variant) receive the same VInSMoC peak count score and raw scores alone are mis for selecting the correct topology.

name: macrolide-planar-structure-elucidation
description: Use when a fractionated marine natural product extract yields an unannotated macrolide candidate and you need a planar structure from 1D/2D NMR plus LC-MS2 molecular networking rather than full de novo stereochemical assignment.

name: macrolide-structure-elucidation-from-1d-2d-nmr
description: Use when a fractionated marine cyanobacterial (Symploca) extract contains cytotoxic, SMART 2.0-predicted macrolide/polyketide fractions and you need to resolve planar structures of swinholide-like compounds from NMR plus LC-MS2 data.

name: macroms-geometry-file-interoperability
description: Use when converting target positions picked from flatbed-scanner or cell-phone optical images into macroMS geometry files for MALDI-TOF acquisition, or when quantifying targeting accuracy in micrometers from geometry/ablation-mark file pairs.

name: macroms-spectrum-data-analysis
description: Use when you have macroMS-exported mass spectra (peak areas per target location) from a high-throughput screen — e.g., a 5 × 50 nanoliter droplet array — and need per-sample ratios and grouped statistics (mean ± std) to distinguish sample classes.

name: mad-outlier-robust-dispersion-estimation
description: Use when benchmarking normalization approaches (e.g., tGAM, rGAM, rLOESS, SERFF, TIGER, QC-RLSC, QC-RSC) on metabolomics data containing replicate sample pairs run in different batches, to identify which method harmonizes intensities across batches.

name: magma-substructure-annotation
description: Use when bootstrapping training data for ICEBERG's Generate module from labeled NIST spectra: enumerate fragment substructures for each molecule and assign peaks within 20 ppm mass tolerance using the minimal MAGMa heuristic score.

name: maize-root-developmental-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when DESI-MSI data from maize root sections sampled along a linear developmental axis needs to be grouped into enrichment clusters and compared across varieties.

name: maize-root-spatial-metabolomics
description: Use when you have DESI-MSI hyperspectral images of maize (or other linearly organized) tissue sections and need to identify mass signatures enriched at specific positions along a developmental gradient or in specific cell layers, and to annotate unknown m/z values.

name: maize-root-zone-annotation
description: Use when DESI-MSI mass signatures from linear maize-root developmental gradients need zone-level localization labels (e.g., meristem-localized Cluster 1) or when comparing signature localization between varieties such as B73 and Oaxacan Green.

name: majority-vote-ensemble-aggregation
description: Use when several independently trained classifiers (e.g., LDA, NN, SVM across different random seeds) each produce per-spectrum MS/MS predictions that must be merged into one binary 'relevant'/'other' label.

name: majority-vote-ensemble-classification
description: Use when you need to prioritize novel HR-MS/MS spectra by a compound class of interest — e.g., flagging putative prenylated flavonoids in plant extracts — using curated 'relevant'/'other' reference spectra.

name: majority-xor-binary-spectrum-encoding
description: Use when you have quantized peak m/z and intensity vectors from preprocessed MS/MS spectra and need compact binary high-dimensional representations (HVs) for fast GPU distance computation in spectral clustering pipelines like HyperSpec.

name: maldi-ablation-mark-detection-in-post-maldi-microscopy
description: Use when processing MALDI-imaging mass spectrometry data of cultured cells where per-cell metabolite assignment requires detecting laser ablation marks in post-MALDI microscopy and linking them to segmented cells.

name: maldi-fticr-ion-image-extraction
description: Use when raw imzML/HDF5 FT-ICR MSI data (e.g., tens of thousands of m/z variables) contains a specific candidate m/z (e.g., 400.9546) whose spatial pattern must be rendered as an ion image and compared against histology-annotated tumor regions.

name: maldi-imaging-data-processing
description: Use when raw MALDI-imaging data (*.RAW, *.UDP, *.imzML, *.ibd) plus tiled pre-/post-MALDI microscopy tiles with out.txt coordinates must be converted into a per-cell spatio-molecular matrix via the SpaceM pipeline.

name: maldi-imaging-isotopologue-extraction
description: Use when you have MALDI-AIF imzML data (e.g. 600-1600 m/z, negative mode) from 13C-labelled tissue and need spatial isotopologue ion images for fatty acids rather than METASPACE's natural-abundance-only annotations.

name: maldi-imaging-pixelwise-isotope-tracing
description: Use when MALDI imaging data from 13C6-glucose-labeled tissue must be analyzed per pixel instead of per cell, to recover spatial maps of isotopologue distributions and binomial-fitted labelling probability p for fatty acids.

name: maldi-imaging-pixelwise-isotopologue-normalization
description: Use when processing MALDI imaging mass spectrometry isotope-tracing data (imzML files, e.g. 13C6-glucose-labelled tissue) at pixel rather than single-cell level, to obtain corrected, normalized isotopologue distributions for fatty acids per pixel.

name: maldi-intensity-data-frame-organization
description: Use when raw MALDI-MS or ESI-MS spectra with mismatched, irregularly-spaced m/z grids must be organized into one m/z-by-replicate data frame before smoothing, baseline correction, peak detection, or normalization (e.g., rel_TIC).

name: maldi-matrix-cluster-modeling
description: Use when annotating MALDI-imaging datasets where matrix cluster ions (e.g., from 2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid) may pollute annotations, and a predicted list of matrix cluster formulas is needed to match recognized off-sample signals.

name: maldi-metabolite-annotation-via-metaspace
description: Use when raw MALDI-imaging MS acquisitions (.RAW, .UDP, .imzML, .ibd) from cultured-cell experiments must be metabolite-annotated before per-cell spatio-molecular analysis with SpaceM.

name: maldi-msi-coordinate-matrix-construction
description: Use when two spatial datasets (e.g. 10X Visium/BMKMANU S1000 transcriptome and MALDI-MSI) are stored as .h5ad files with feature matrices in .X and spot coordinates in obsm['spatial'] and must be packaged for haCCA alignment.

name: maldi-msi-group-comparison-statistics
description: Use when you have segmented, ROI-annotated MSI pixel-intensity data from two sample groups and need per-lipid fold-change/p-value statistics per tissue region with volcano plots.

name: maldi-msi-ifm-registration-data-handling
description: Use when raw MALDI MSI and IFM images of consecutive tissue sections must be spatially aligned to assign lipid spectra to marker-defined cell populations, e.g. before extracting Ly6G+ pixel spectra for downstream UMAP/HDBSCAN heterogeneity clustering.

name: maldi-msi-spectral-preprocessing
description: Use when raw vendor MALDI MSI files must be converted into a reproducible, quality-controlled peak list (e.g. imzML output with QC visualisations) before segmentation, registration or statistical analysis.

name: maldi-msi-spot-alignment
description: Use when integrating paired or pseudo-paired 10X Visium (.h5ad) and MALDI-MSI (.h5ad) spatial datasets that share no spots or features and need morphological/feature-based spatial alignment before cross-modality label transfer.

name: maldi-spectral-replicate-averaging
description: Use when a MALDI-MS data frame holds multiple replicate intensity columns (e.g. matrix blanks or technical replicates) on a shared m/z grid and you need one averaged intensity column before subtraction, normalization, or plotting.

name: maldi-tof-spectral-ion-count-extraction
description: Use when MALDI-TOF spectra have been acquired over a library or array of targets (e.g., 749 yeast SSM colonies or nL droplet arrays) and per-target ion intensities at specific fatty acyl m/z values must be tabulated and ratio-ranked.

name: maldi-tof-spectral-peak-detection
description: Use when you have a permethylated released N-glycan MALDI-TOF spectrum (e.g., Super-DHB matrix) and need to assign glycan identities to detected peaks by accurate-mass search against a glycan mass database, replacing manual peak-by-peak analysis.

name: maldi-tof-target-positioning
description: Use when you have an optical image (flatbed scanner or cell phone camera) of a macroscopic sample plate with detected target positions and need instrument-relative X, Y coordinates for MALDI-TOF spectra acquisition at selected locations.

name: maldim-spectral-baseline-correction
description: Use when raw MALDI spectra (m/z + intensity data frames) show an irregular baseline and you need combined baseline correction plus peak detection without masking data into S3/S4 objects.

name: maml-1d-cnn-backbone-selection
description: Use when building a MAML meta-learning classifier for single-cell mass spectrometry (SCMS) metabolomics data and you must decide which 1D-CNN backbone to adopt before full-scale meta-training with limited cells.

name: manders-costes-threshold-colocalisation-analysis
description: Decision support for quantifying spatial correlation between two LA-ICP-MS elemental images (e.g. 55Mn vs 66Zn) when reporting colocalisation coefficients such as Manders, Li ICQ, or Pearson R.

name: mann-whitney-u-group-comparison
description: Use when comparing two groups (e.g. COPD vs control, mild vs severe COVID-19) on pathway-score or molecular-level matrices to estimate what fraction of features separates groups under controlled effect sizes.

name: mann-whitney-u-hypothesis-testing
description: Use when comparing ion concentrations between two regions of interest in an MSI peak matrix where undetected (null) peaks would otherwise invalidate parametric testing and must be discarded before the test.

name: mann-whitney-u-pvalue-reproduction
description: Use when validating or benchmarking how undetected MS peaks (null values) affect Mann-Whitney U p-values in ion filtering between two clusters of mass-specimaging intensities, e.g. testing rMSIKeyIon's TestIonSelect behavior.

name: mann-whitney-u-test-statistics
description: Reference for testing whether median feature intensities differ across outcome categories (correct vs incorrect vs no annotation) when you need a nonparametric, rank-based significance test rather than a parametric t-test.

name: manual-annotation-concordance-comparison
description: Use when validating an automated GC-MS processing pipeline (e.g. uafR) against published results by reproducing compound counts and statistical patterns (ANOSIM/NMDS) from a study that used traditional manual peak annotation.

name: manual-annotation-ground-truth-matching
description: Use when benchmarking feature alignment or detection methods on public LC–MS metabolomics datasets (e.g., MTBLS562, QE_HF, TripleTOF_6600) where a manual annotation of library analytes is available to serve as ground truth.

name: manual-landmark-affine-transform-selection
description: Use when MSIght's automated affine registration of an MSI image to an H&E stain fails—e.g., when phase cross correlation does not minimize SSD sufficiently and tissue masks do not overlap—requiring manual landmark placement.

name: manual-web-service-metabolite-query
description: Use when metabolite identifiers are retention-index-style codes (e.g., RI1150.81) or other non-standard names that must be converted to standard database identifiers before KEGG pathway mapping, and no API is available.

name: manually-annotated-analyte-matching
description: Use when evaluating feature-alignment accuracy against a gold standard of manually annotated library analytes with m/z, RT and area information across benchmark LC–MS metabolomics datasets.

name: many-to-many-match-result-extraction
description: Use when a matchMz()/matchSpectra() call has returned a Matched result object and the many-to-many peak-to-compound matches must be converted into a tabular annotation table (one row per match, NA for unmatched) for CSV export or downstream QC.

name: map-bayesian-estimation
description: Use when individual PK parameters (CL, V, etas) must be estimated from patient TDM concentrations given a user-defined population PK model, or when validating/replicating NONMEM MAP-BE results in R for MIPD workflows.

name: map-bayesian-estimation-of-individual-pk-parameters
description: Use when individual PK parameters (CL, V, ETA) must be estimated from sparse TDM concentration data given a published population PK model, e.g., for model-informed precision dosing (MIPD) or therapeutic drug monitoring in R.

name: mapping-rate-aggregation-statistics
description: Use when you need to measure how consistently MetaFetcheR resolves metabolite identifiers across the five supported small-compound databases, e.g. to validate a populated PostgreSQL cache or compare mapping quality per source database.

name: mapping-rate-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantify how completely a metabolite identifier mapper fills HMDB/ChEBI/PubChem/KEGG/LIPID MAPS fields on a sparse identifier table, and compare that rate against a reference tool's reported rate.

name: mapping-rate-qc-comparison
description: Use when running Lilikoi's lilikoi.metab_to_pathway on a metabolomics dataset and you need to verify the metabolite-name-to-HMDB mapping rate against a reported benchmark (e.g., 182/227 plasma, ~80%) before downstream PDS computation.

name: marginal-false-discovery-rate-estimation
description: Use when you have two (or three) replicate rank lists over the same n genes and need an error-controlled call set of reproducible signals without parametric assumptions on the dependence structure of reproducible genes.
tools: Python (NumPy/pandas implementation of the closed-form MaRR estimator)

name: marginal-versus-partial-correlation-network-comparison
description: Use when you need to explain or quantify why Pearson-correlation metabolite networks are denser than GLASSO-based partial correlation networks built from the same peak-intensity table, e.g. reproducing the DNEA paper's MetaBox2 vs DNEA edge-count comparison (576 vs 172 edges).

name: marine-cyanobacterial-extract-fractionation-context
