description: Reference for ingesting MS/MS library files (msp, mzML, mzXML, MGF, JSON, metabolomics-USI) into matchms and running default-filter preprocessing with automatic YAML/report logging before library searching or ML training.

name: mass-spectral-library-matching
description: Use when the goal is to identify an unknown small molecule from its EI mass spectrum by ranking candidates in a spectral reference library (e.g., NIST 2017) and reporting recall@10.

name: mass-spectral-library-matching
description: Use when a structurally characterized Mass2Motif (or other fragment/loss set) needs putative annotation or validation against curated MS/MS spectral libraries before transferring annotations to new datasets.

name: mass-spectral-library-matching-cleanup
description: Use when raw GNPS FBMN spectral match annotation tables (from MZmine2/MZmine3 feature tables of LC-HRMS/MS runs) need cleaning against defined match-quality thresholds before computing annotation rates or feeding downstream prioritization.

name: mass-spectral-library-msp-io
description: Use when input is a mass spectral library file in .msp format whose records need loading into a Python tool, enrichment with metadata (SMILES, InChI, CAS), or export back to .msp after annotation.

name: mass-spectral-library-preprocessing
description: Use when raw spectral library entries (e.g., GNPS JSON/MGF libraries) lack structural annotations like InChIKeys, or have inconsistent metadata (ionmode, charge, compound name, formula, parent mass), and structure-based analyses are planned.

name: mass-spectral-library-retrieval
description: Use when querying mass spectra against a large spectral library (e.g. MoNA-hosted MassBank, GNPS, HMDB, ReSpect, FiehnLib entries) and you need to shrink the candidate set before running a full NIST cosine similarity search.

name: mass-spectral-library-search-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing the query-time scaling of spectral library search modules (e.g., linear-time hash-table/bisection methods vs entropy-similarity search) across MassBank libraries of growing size.

name: mass-spectral-library-search-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing the runtime scalability of MS2 spectral library search methods (e.g., ML-based analogue search vs score-based search with precursor preselection) on a fixed query set and library.

name: mass-spectral-main-peak-extraction
description: Use when you need a coarse theoretical isotopic envelope (main peaks at integer neutron differences from the monoisotopic mass) for a metabolite with a known chemical formula or a peptide precursor, rather than the full isotopic fine structure.

name: mass-spectral-molecular-network-annotation-merging
description: Use when a GNPS molecular network already has mapped Mass2Motifs and a chemical class annotation dataframe is available, and the two annotation layers must be combined into one Cytoscape-ready network artifact.

name: mass-spectral-molecular-network-motif-mapping
description: Use when you have GNPS molecular network outputs (graphml, clustered MGF, edges/nodes files) plus an MS2LDA experiment and need to link substructure motifs to network nodes/edges for annotation and visualization.

name: mass-spectral-peak-alignment
description: Use when you have per-sample DIMS peak lists (e.g. SIM-stitched FT-ICR m/z peaks from MTBLS79 cow/sheep heart samples plus QC and blank) and need a cross-sample aligned matrix before replicate/blank/sample filtering and PCA.

name: mass-spectral-peak-binning
description: Use when raw mass spectral peak lists (m/z, intensity) must be converted into fixed-length numeric feature vectors for a classifier, or when spectra from different acquisition modes (EI-MS vs ESI-MS/MS) must be projected onto a common m/z scale for training or comparison.

name: mass-spectral-peak-binning
description: Use when filtered MS/MS peak lists must be turned into fixed-width numeric vectors (10,000 bins over 10–1000 m/z) to feed the MS2DeepScore base network or to build 200-dimensional spectrum embeddings.

name: mass-spectral-peak-embedding-with-formula-assignment
description: Use when you have tandem mass spectra (e.g., MassSpecGym or NPLIB1/CANOPUS-format entries) with a known or inferrable chemical formula and need de novo candidate molecular structures ranked by sampling frequency.

name: mass-spectral-peak-overlap-detection
description: Use when a matrix-annotation score (e.g. spectral S1 or morphological S2 in rMSIcleanup) falls below the user threshold and overlapped or isobaric peaks may share the same ion image as matrix-related ions, risking misclassification.

name: mass-spectral-peak-picking
description: Use when raw LC-HRMS files (e.g., Thermo Orbitrap ID-X, MS1 scan range m/z 100–1000 at 60,000 resolution) must be converted into m/z and retention-time feature lists for differential comparison of preincubation and postincubation samples.
tools: Thermo Scientific Orbitrap ID-X Tribrid mass spectrometer

name: mass-spectral-ranking-metric-analysis
description: Use when ranked candidate lists (e.g., the top-100 ranked compounds PS2MS yields per analyte) exist for the same test substances under two or more similarity metrics, and you must quantify which metric puts the true compound at rank 1.

name: mass-spectral-similarity-metric-selection
description: Use when you have predicted spectra and ground-truth library spectra for the same molecules and need to score similarity directly (cosine similarity ratios) or via augmented-library matching with recall@10.

name: mass-spectral-similarity-network-construction
description: Use when building metabolomic networks from GC-TOF-MS (or similar) feature spectra where many molecular features lack structural annotation and you want to connect unknowns to identified metabolites via spectral similarity.

name: mass-spectral-similarity-networking
description: Use when metabolites in a measured feature table (e.g. GC-TOF-MS metabolites with BinBase identifiers) lack structural annotation or KEGG/PubChem mappings, and you need network edges connecting them via mass spectra.

name: mass-spectral-similarity-prediction
description: Use when MS/MS spectra in MGF/h5py format must be scored against a spectral library (e.g., GNPS/MassBank) to retrieve structural analogues, or when similarity scores must reflect subtle structural modifications.

name: mass-spectral-similarity-search
description: Use when you have a query .msp spectra file (e.g. unique CSA spectra variants exported for one study) and a reference .msp library (e.g. CSA or MS/MS library from another study), and you want to annotate compounds by spectral similarity.

name: mass-spectral-similarity-searching
description: Use when msp or .mgf spectra files (e.g., CSA composite spectra exported from MS1-only data, or DDA/DIA spectra) need compound-level annotations against a reference MS/MS library such as NIST 2020.

name: mass-spectrometry-acquisition-metadata-handling
description: Use when a study provides proprietary Thermo .raw files plus a sample-metadata CSV and centroided mzML inputs are required for downstream LC-MS preprocessing (e.g., Asari in pcpfm).

name: mass-spectrometry-adduct-annotation
description: Use when an LC/MS feature table contains multiple features per analyte (isotope/adduct/fragment series) and you must assign quasi-molecular ion species, charge states, or neutral losses to reduce feature-list redundancy before statistical analysis or compound identification.

name: mass-spectrometry-adduct-identification
description: Use when annotating MALDI-MSI peaks where suspected matrix or salt adducts (e.g., DHB) may inflate peak counts or cause false-positive metabolite identifications from exact mass alone.

name: mass-spectrometry-annotation-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking annotation propagation on a molecular network: you need to quantify whether annotations reach nodes not directly connected to spectral library matches, not just first neighbours.

name: mass-spectrometry-annotation-file-parsing
description: Use when you have SIRIUS/ZODIAC annotation output files plus ground-truth formula lists (e.g. from MassIVE MSV000080502, MSV000081364) and need to reproduce or extend the molecular formula accuracy benchmark.

name: mass-spectrometry-annotation-rank-metric-computation
description: Use when evaluating spectral annotation models on a candidate set and you need average rank / Rank@K metrics, or relative improvement percentages (e.g. 23.7% and 37.2%) against baselines.

name: mass-spectrometry-area-integration
description: Use when processing full-scan AEMS spectra (precursor ion or neutral loss modes) from 384- or 1536-well plates where persistent high-intensity baseline signals obscure weaker, less well-defined analyte peaks that need quantification.

name: mass-spectrometry-array-decompression
description: Use when raw vendor MS files (e.g. SCIEX .wiff/.wiff.scan) contain compressed binary m/z and intensity arrays that must be decompressed and reassembled into usable spectra before peak integration or quantification.

name: mass-spectrometry-batch-search
description: Use when you have a set of MS/MS spectra (a .mgf file from MZmine or a list of USIs in .csv/.tsv) and need to find matching datasets and taxa in public metabolomics repositories.

name: mass-spectrometry-benchmark-claim-extraction
description: Use when a metabolomics/mass-spectrometry paper or abstract states numeric performance claims (runtimes, speedup factors, latency, accuracy, memory overhead) that must be tabulated and traced verbatim to source text.

name: mass-spectrometry-benchmark-metric-tabulation
description: Decision support for quantifying how scaffold retrieval error limits spectra-conditioned molecular generation, when per-condition metric tables for both an oracle scaffold retriever (lookup table) and a predictive contrastive retriever are available alongside SPA values.

name: mass-spectrometry-centroided-spectra-visualization
description: Use when the input is a Thermo Fisher Scientific raw Orbitrap file and you need to inspect or plot centroided MS/MS scans, a total ion chromatogram over MS1 scans, or extracted ion chromatograms directly from R.

name: mass-spectrometry-chromatogram-visualization
description: Use when the input is a Thermo Fisher Scientific .raw file (e.g. 20181113_010_autoQC01.raw) and the goal is to plot extracted ion chromatograms for target masses, inspect fragment-ion traces, or derive retention times for RT/iRT calibration.

name: mass-spectrometry-clustering-threshold-tuning
description: Use when tuning or comparing spectral clustering quality on MS/MS peak lists (MGF), e.g. to verify a tool achieves MaRaCluster-level quality on datasets like PXD000561 using clustered spectra ratio, incorrect clustering ratio, and completeness.

name: mass-spectrometry-comparison-parameter-configuration
description: Use when raw or converted tandem MS/MS datasets (e.g. MGF files such as the PXD034932 serum datasets with ~42,629–47,626 spectra each) must be compared pairwise and suitable compareMS2 parameters like m/z windows and spectral similarity thresholds need to be estimated and set.

name: mass-spectrometry-correction-matrix-construction
description: Use when correcting FAM to MDV for natural abundance and tracer impurity on a high-resolution analyzer (e.g., Orbitrap at nominal resolution 100,000–280,000) where same-nominal-mass isotopologs may be resolved and full correction matrices are no longer justified.

name: mass-spectrometry-data-classification
description: Use when raw, TIC-normalized mass spectrometry feature vectors (e.g., spectrum_dim 9900–15000 from m/z binning at 0.1 Da and 10 s RT windows) must be classified, and multi-channel representation learning should be compared against single-channel baselines.

name: mass-spectrometry-data-cleaning
description: Use when importing raw MS/MS spectra (mgf, mzML, mzXML, msp, JSON, USI) whose metadata may be inconsistent, wrongly labeled, or incorrect, and a harmonized, filter-cleaned spectrum set is needed downstream.

name: mass-spectrometry-data-compression
description: Use when converting vendor MS files (SCIEX, Thermo, Agilent; DDA, DIA/SWATH, PRM, PASEF) into a computation-oriented format where decoding speed and m/z storage size matter, or when benchmarking ZDPD against Zlib-only compression.

name: mass-spectrometry-data-frame-construction
description: Use when you have multiple raw spectral replicates with irregularly spaced m/z values that must be placed on a shared, regularly spaced m/z grid before normalization, averaging, or replicate-wise comparison.

name: mass-spectrometry-data-parsing
description: Use when you hold GNPS molecular networking outputs (consensus .mgf + edge table) for a dataset such as MSV000083437 and need to reproduce, audit, or re-score the pairwise spectral similarity underlying network edges.

name: mass-spectrometry-data-postprocessing
description: Use when mzML MS2 features already have raw spectral matches and SIRIUS/MetFrag candidate lists and you must merge them, apply score thresholds, and prioritize one annotated candidate per feature.

name: mass-spectrometry-data-preprocessing
description: Use when raw vendor LC-MS files (Thermo .RAW, or other vendor formats/.mzXML) from a high-resolution instrument must be turned into centroided mzML and a cross-sample LC-MS feature table, or when reproducible, trackable feature detection is required.

name: mass-spectrometry-data-preprocessing-for-bioactivity-workflow
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS files of bioassay-guided fractionation fractions must be converted into the GNPS FBMN feature quantification table (features_quantification_matrix.csv) and its .MGF MS/MS summary before bioactivity scoring.

name: mass-spectrometry-data-structure-validation
description: Use when scripting against OpenMS from Python — after building/installing pyOpenMS and before writing mzML-loading or quantitation workflows, to confirm MSExperiment/FeatureMap objects work in Python.

name: mass-spectrometry-dataset-preprocessing
description: Use when preparing MS/MS spectra (e.g., NPLIB1, NIST20, biomols, CASMI2022) for formula inference: candidate sets from mass decomposition are too large for exhaustive scoring and must be ranked/filtered before model training or evaluation.

name: mass-spectrometry-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when a public LC-MS/MS dataset (e.g., a MassIVE accession such as MSV000078577) must be obtained from a repository to run dereplication, spectral library search, or continuous reanalysis against reference libraries.

name: mass-spectrometry-dda-scoring-reimplementation
description: Use when reimplementing or evaluating DDA precursor-prioritization scoring: MS1 survey-scan ions with known prior fragmentation times (tf) need nonbinary dynamic-exclusion weights and a top-N MS2 target list per scan.

name: mass-spectrometry-dereplication
description: Use when you have a feature quantification table and an .MGF MS/MS summary from LC-MS/MS fractionation and must prioritize or annotate molecules before investing in purification.

name: mass-spectrometry-detection-statistics-aggregation
description: Use when raw Thermo .raw / .mzML flow injection acquisitions have been processed into per-file feature lists and you need to summarize how many unique compounds were detected exclusively in positive mode, exclusively in negative mode, or in both ionization modes.

name: mass-spectrometry-dia-acquisition-simulation
description: Use when the analysis goal is to simulate data-independent acquisition (e.g. all-ion-fragmentation or SWATH-style) over a chemical mixture, rather than Top-N DDA precursor selection, and the input is a set of generated or mzML-derived chemical objects.

name: mass-spectrometry-eic-processing
description: Use when raw targeted LC-MS peak tables contain EICs whose retention-time shifts vary across samples and the goal is to compute per-sample peak areas for a specific isotopologue for downstream metabolite quantification.

name: mass-spectrometry-error-rate-estimation
description: Use when quantifying how many spectra in a mass spectral library have missing or incorrect structure annotations, by re-deriving SMILES from compound names and comparing against original annotations.

name: mass-spectrometry-feature-annotation-evaluation
description: Use when an xsAnnotate/CAMERA peak list (e.g. faahKO or MM39) must be checked for correct isotope cluster membership and charge states, or when benchmarking a reimplementation of CAMERA's findIsotopes logic.

name: mass-spectrometry-feature-annotation-parsing
description: Use when deposited LC-HRMS feature tables need to be parsed, joined with sample metadata or a drug-class mapping, and aggregated into per-feature or per-class counts of unpredicted metabolites.

name: mass-spectrometry-feature-annotation-qc
description: Use when untargeted MS/MS feature tables (e.g., a GNPS FBMN task with canopus_summary.tsv and Node_info.tsv) need consensus chemical-class coverage and per-subnetwork consensus-score QC metrics.

name: mass-spectrometry-feature-based-molecular-networking
description: Use when a reanalysis of public metabolomics data (e.g. GNPS-MassIVE MSV000081832) needs molecular families grouped by MS/MS fragmentation similarity and tested for differential activity between phenotypes such as healthy vs caries samples.

name: mass-spectrometry-feature-detection
description: Use when starting from raw LC-MS/MS files and the analysis goal is an untargeted metabolomics workflow requiring an MGF of MS1/MS2 entries plus a feature table of MS1 peak areas per sample as inputs to fingerprinting or networking tools.

name: mass-spectrometry-feature-importance-analysis
description: Use when a pretreated SCMS feature matrix (m/z peaks per single cell) and a trained classifier exist and you need to rank essential metabolite peaks for discriminating primary vs metastatic melanoma cell phenotypes.

name: mass-spectrometry-feature-mass-matching
description: Use when an LC-MS2-annotated active extract needs its detected features (e.g. HRESIMS m/z 465.3002, 495.2754) matched to compounds in ChEMBL with reported activity against a target organism such as T. cruzi (CHEMBL368).

name: mass-spectrometry-feature-retention-curation
description: Use when a GNPS molecular networking job has produced .mgf and edges files and you need to select a subset of spectra (e.g. SPF-unique) before batch MASST searching.

name: mass-spectrometry-feature-table-import
description: Use when starting a Qemistree workflow: untargeted MS data (mzXML, mzML or mzDATA) has been pre-processed in MZmine2 into an MGF and a quant/biom feature table that must be loaded as QIIME 2 artifacts before fragmentation-tree computation or hierarchy building.

name: mass-spectrometry-feature-table-processing
description: Use when you have GNPS FBMN output (DBResult/Node_info files), a CANOPUS canopus_summary.tsv, and need putative ClassyFire or NPClassifier annotations per ion feature for clustering or comparative metabolomics.

name: mass-spectrometry-feature-table-statistics
description: Use when a feature quantification table with ion-identity annotations is available and you need to test whether specific adduct species (e.g. [M+Na]+, [M+NH4]+) change abundance across infusion conditions or sample types.

name: mass-spectrometry-feature-tracking
description: Use when MZmine full-scan (.csv) feature tables and DDA MS/MS tables are available and the goal is to quantify which targeted-list ions were detected in MS1 but lacked MS2 fragmentation.

name: mass-spectrometry-file-format-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing read/decode performance of MS data formats (Aird, mzML) on the same MRM or DIA datasets, or when deciding whether converting vendor data to Aird will pay off in loading/rendering speed.

name: mass-spectrometry-file-format-conversion
description: Use when a mass spectrometry input file is not JCAMP-DX (e.g. mzML or vendor RAW) and downstream ChemSpectra/ELN processing requires the standardized JCAMP-DX representation of the spectral data.

name: mass-spectrometry-file-format-conversion
description: Use when raw vendor MS files (e.g., Thermo .raw, Agilent or Bruker .d) must be converted to an open format like .mza, mzMLb, mzML or mz5, or when benchmarking conversion speed across MS formats.

name: mass-spectrometry-file-ingest-pipeline
description: Use when new instrument acquisition files (mzML, mzXML, mzData) must flow continuously from an instrument PC into a QC-metrics database and dashboard with no manual file handling.

name: mass-spectrometry-file-level-feature-summarization
description: Use when a collection of public LC-MS/MS files (e.g. those indexed in ReDU / MassIVE MSV000084206) needs an unsupervised, file-level overview of chemical content, or when PCA score plots colored by sample information are needed to explore repository-scale chemical annotations.

name: mass-spectrometry-format-comparative-analysis
description: Use when evaluating or comparing MS data formats (mzML, mzMLb, imzML, vendor RAW, mzPeak) across trade-off dimensions such as file size, data access speed, metadata support, interoperability, and long-term archival durability.

name: mass-spectrometry-format-conversion
description: Use when the input is an LC-MS data file in .mzML or Thermo .raw format and the goal is to parse it into flat per-spectrum records (spectrum_id, rt, mz, intensity) for downstream viewing, tabulation, or reuse without a GUI.

name: mass-spectrometry-formula-prediction
description: Use when given a positive-mode MS2 spectrum (or batch of converted vendor raw files) with an observed precursor m/z and you need a ranked list of candidate precursor molecular formulas scored by candidate score.

name: mass-spectrometry-formula-representation
description: Use when a neural model over formula candidates (e.g., the MIST-CF Formula Transformer or FastFilter) needs a fixed-dimensional, permutation-ordered numeric encoding of integer element counts rather than learned embeddings.

name: mass-spectrometry-fragment-annotation
description: Use when tandem MS/MS spectra from a low-resolution miniaturized mass spectrometer contain unannotated fragment peaks (e.g. nominal m/z 262 and 249) whose molecular formulas or structures must be predicted and cross-validated.

name: mass-spectrometry-fragmentation-algorithm-implementation
description: Use when you must enumerate all single- and double-bond-cleavage fragments of small molecules (0–2000 Da) from a structure database so tandem mass spectra can be matched against millions of candidate structures.

name: mass-spectrometry-fragmentation-graph-serialization
description: Use when building theoretical fragment sets from chemical structure databases (e.g., PubChem-derived SDF/MGF inputs) for DEREPLICATOR+ spectral annotation of LC-MS/MS natural product data.

name: mass-spectrometry-fragmentation-motif-visualization
description: Use when a trained topic model over MS/MS fragmentation data (Mass2Motifs assigned to spectra) needs interactive visual exploration before motif characterization, e.g. filtering motifs by degree prior to biochemical interpretation.

name: mass-spectrometry-fragmentation-scoring
description: Use when evaluating small-molecule identification accuracy of a mass spectral database-search method on spectra with known true structures, such as benchmarking top-1/3/5/10 accuracy on the PNNL lipid library against LMSD compounds.

name: mass-spectrometry-fragmentation-spectrum-processing
description: Use when you have paired genome + LC-MS/MS samples and need to turn raw fragmentation spectra (GNPS job output or cryptic spectra) into per-sample MS/MS fingerprints for BGC linking or benchmarking.

name: mass-spectrometry-image-linescan-projection
description: Use when you have 2D DESI-MSI hyperspectral images of a tissue with an approximate linear developmental gradient (e.g., maize root tip) and need to assign mass signatures to developmental enrichment clusters.

name: mass-spectrometry-image-segmentation
description: Use when a peak-picked MSI dataset (e.g., imzML loaded into Cardinal as a processed MSImagingExperiment) must be partitioned into chemically homogeneous tissue segments without class labels, and the expected number of segments is known from a reference figure or must be selected by scanning.

name: mass-spectrometry-imaging-classification
description: Use when raw MALDI MSI spectra (e.g. imzML/HDF5 with tens of thousands of m/z variables) must be classified into tissue classes (normal vs tumor) with per-pixel probabilities, and the probabilistic outputs must be mapped back into image space to localize classification uncertainty such as at tumor.

name: mass-spectrometry-imaging-clustering
description: Use when imzML MSI pixel spectra need unsupervised segmentation into tissue clusters, especially when t-SNE embedding parameters (perplexity, learning rate, iterations) must be tuned and compared via Silhouette score.

name: mass-spectrometry-imaging-data-processing
description: Use when you have DESI-MSI imzML/NetCDF (cdf) pixel spectra from elongating root sections arranged along a linear developmental gradient and need to identify metabolite mass signatures and group them by developmental enrichment pattern.

name: mass-spectrometry-imaging-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when pixel-wise peak features from one or multiple MALDI MSI samples must be jointly projected into a low-dimensional embedding (UMAP) and density-clustered (HDBSCAN) for segmentation or sample-outlier flagging.

name: mass-spectrometry-imaging-peak-table-processing
description: Use when a spatial metabolomics peak table matrix (pixels x m/z ion peaks with X/Y coordinates) contains background pixels and randomly distributed noise ions that must be detected and filtered before spatial pattern recognition or clustering.

name: mass-spectrometry-imaging-preprocessing
description: Use when raw DESI-MSI root-imaging data (NetCDF .cdf or MATLAB workspace .mat files) must be converted into per-sample mass signature lists before gradient clustering or cross-replicate comparison.

name: mass-spectrometry-imaging-signal-preprocessing
description: Use when raw MALDI-MSI imzML pixel spectra must be made comparable across a tissue section (TIC normalization), denoised, and background-corrected before clustering or segmentation with MSIght.

name: mass-spectrometry-imaging-spectra-embedding
description: Use when a trained massNet-style VAE over high-dimensional MALDI MSI spectra (e.g., 85,062 m/z variables) exists and you need to inspect its 5-D latent space or check normal-vs-tumor separability in a 2D UMAP map.

name: mass-spectrometry-intensity-encoding
description: Use when converting vendor MRM/MS raw files to a compact, computation-oriented binary format and file size or fast web-side rendering of hundreds of chromatograms is the goal.

name: mass-spectrometry-intensity-filtering
description: Use when MS/MS spectra contain many low-intensity noise peaks — e.g. prior to peak annotation, library comparison, or spectrum visualization — and you need to restrict peaks to a fraction of the base peak intensity and cap their number.

name: mass-spectrometry-ionization-mechanism-interpretation
description: Decision support for choosing an ionization source (EI 70 eV, EI 15 eV, CI-methane, CI-isobutane) when designing or interpreting GC-MS isotopologue detection for 13C/15N labeling experiments.

name: mass-spectrometry-library-downloading
description: Use when you need to quantify the adduct/ion-species composition of public LC-MS2 spectral libraries (MoNA, GNPS) or need those raw library entries as inputs for an ion-species bias analysis.

name: mass-spectrometry-library-matching
description: Use when untargeted metabolomics MS/MS peak annotations yield too many candidate structures per formula (isomers), and predicted retention times from an HILIC or RPLC Retip model can be used to exclude unlikely candidates in MS-FINDER compound identification.

name: mass-spectrometry-library-matching
description: Use when you have a set of unannotated MS/MS consensus spectra (e.g., an .mgf from MZmine or GNPS molecular networking) and need to identify which ones match metabolites from a specific taxonomic domain such as microbes.

name: mass-spectrometry-lipidomics-validation
description: Use when a targeted lipidomics transition list (PRM/SRM) has been generated in silico — e.g., LipidCreator-computed fragment masses for defined fatty acyl combinations — and you must confirm the computed ion signatures yield linear instrument response before deploying the assay.

name: mass-spectrometry-mass-peak-matching
description: Use when you have a target molecular weight (1–5 decimal digits) from a high-resolution mass spectrum of an unknown natural-product mixture and need to rank candidate structures from seed scaffolds (.cIdx files).

name: mass-spectrometry-match-table-compilation
description: Use when you have MASST search results (per-compound job/USI identifiers) for a panel of reference tandem MS spectra and must aggregate them into a per-compound match table with deduplicated file counts.

name: mass-spectrometry-match-thresholding
description: Use when a MASST or GNPS search result table of candidate spectral matches for a synthesized compound's MS/MS spectrum must be filtered to trusted matches before phenotypic association analysis.

name: mass-spectrometry-metadata-extraction
description: Use when Thermo RAW files (e.g. downloaded from PRIDE accessions) need instrument-, run-, and scan-level metadata extracted into structured TSV/CSV tables for QC, repository submission, or batch annotation workflows.

name: mass-spectrometry-metadata-extraction
description: Use when input contains mzspec:/mzdraft: USI strings that must be split into collection, msRun, indexType, indexNumber fields and mapped to the correct metabolomics data repository or spectral library service.

name: mass-spectrometry-metadata-harmonization
description: Use when a public MS/MS spectral library (e.g. GNPS, MassBank, MoNA) has inconsistent or missing metadata — compound-name-only annotations, mismatching SMILES/InChI/InChIKey, wrong adducts or parent masses — and must be cleaned reproducibly.

name: mass-spectrometry-metadata-integration
description: Use when a GNPS molecular networking job must be tied back to sample context: uploading a standardized metadata table with the LC-MS/MS files and classifying network nodes by sample origin (e.g., lung tissue vs. cultured isolates).

name: mass-spectrometry-molecular-networking
description: Use when an untargeted tandem MS dataset has been processed with GNPS feature-based molecular networking and in silico annotations (e.g., CANOPUS summaries) are available, and consensus chemical classifications must be propagated across subnetworks.

name: mass-spectrometry-mz-binning
description: Use when raw NetCDF/CDF files from comprehensive 2D GC–MS runs must be folded into a sample-by-m/z-by-RT2-by-RT1 array and the m/z axis must be rounded and aligned to the acquired fragment range before peak picking or deconvolution.

name: mass-spectrometry-mz-deviation-tracking
description: Use when tracking the long-term QC pool on a Waters Synapt instrument and you need to compute per-injection m/z deviations (ppm) from target m/z values and flag deviations > 20 ppm as serious analytical problems.

name: mass-spectrometry-noise-injection
description: Use when generating a synthetic mzML with SMITER and the simulated run must carry a realistic baseline intensity noise, e.g. to compare simulated vs. real TIC noise profiles as in the 24-nucleoside-standard validation.

name: mass-spectrometry-novelty-prioritization
description: Use when a feature-based molecular networking (FBMN) experiment produces multiannotated MS/MS features and you need to prioritize putatively novel natural products by ranking features with a knownness score instead of relying on single-tool annotation ranks.

name: mass-spectrometry-parameter-spreadsheet-configuration
description: Use when you have IDSL.IPA-generated 'peaklists' and 'peak_alignment' directories from LC/HRMS MS1 data and need to run CSA correlation-based deconvolution by filling and submitting the IDSL.CSA parameter spreadsheet.

name: mass-spectrometry-peak-area-extraction
description: Use when you have macroMS-exported per-target mass spectra (peak areas at known m/z values) and need per-sample quantitative features, such as fatty acyl ratios, for comparing groups of samples.

name: mass-spectrometry-peak-list-processing
description: Use when raw MS/MS spectra (mzML, mzXML, msp, MGF, JSON, or metabolomics-USI) contain inconsistent metadata, noisy peaks, or incompatible intensity scales and must be cleaned, filtered, and normalized before similarity scoring.

name: mass-spectrometry-peak-metrics-extraction
description: Use when batch LC-MS, LC-IMS-MS, DDA/DIA, or direct-infusion raw MS data (Agilent 'd', Thermo '.raw', Bruker 'd', or mzML) needs precursor-ion QC metrics and error reports without omics-specific identification pipelines.

name: mass-spectrometry-qc-tabulation

name: mass-spectrometry-raw-file-conversion

name: mass-spectrometry-sample-traceability

name: mass-spectrometry-seasonality-analysis

name: mass-spectrometry-transient-signal-simulation

name: mass-spectrometry-transition-pair-counting

name: mass-spectrum-matching-speed-profiling

name: mass-spectrum-peak-count-verification

name: mass-tolerance-configuration

name: mass-tolerance-library-filtering

name: mass-tolerance-parameter-tuning

name: mass-transformation-mapping

name: mass-weight-tolerance-filtering

description: Use when pre-processing raw multi-vendor MALDI MSI data (vendor formats converted to imzML) where matrix/spray pixels would contaminate peak lists, and the sample must be segmented into tissue vs. matrix regions automatically without manual ROI drawing.

name: matrix-region-detection-in-maldi-msi
description: Use when pre-processing MALDI MSI (e.g. t-MALDI-2) imzML data and a binary mask separating matrix/off-tissue pixels from tissue-covered pixels must be generated automatically, without manually defined matrix peak lists.

name: matrix-related-peak-annotation
description: Use when an MSI peak matrix contains matrix-related signals (e.g. Agn+ cluster peaks in Ag-sputtered AgLDI data) that must be annotated and removed, and simple blank subtraction is insufficient because of ion suppression, adducts, or isobaric peaks.

name: matrix-row-expansion-and-aggregation
description: Use when the input is a molecular-species (LMS) intensity matrix whose row identifiers are LIPID MAPS shorthand names (e.g. 'PC 16:0_18:1') and a chain-level (LBB) matrix is required for downstream statistics or pathway analysis.

name: matrix-specific-component-profiling
description: Use when you have paired pre-dosing (blank) and post-dosing LC-MS/MS acquisitions for multiple mouse biological matrices (e.g., plasma, lung, urine, feces) and need to count and classify dosage-related exogenous components per matrix.

name: matrix-wise-metabolite-count-verification
description: Use when a metabolite-bridging or characterization pipeline reports an overall characterization rate and you must confirm per-matrix counts (e.g., 66/222/30/40) reconcile with the claimed total and percent improvement.

name: maven-peak-group-detection
description: Use when raw mzML LC-MS/MS metabolomics or lipidomics samples need peak detection and grouping into peak groups with associated MS/MS scans, rather than a precomputed feature table.

name: maximal-clique-subcluster-extraction
description: Use when tokenised BGCs (each gene as a (sub)Pfam domain combination, original gene order retained) must be grouped into sub-clusters via gene co-localisation and adjacency statistics.

name: maximum-common-substructure-computation
description: Use when a study needs compound-level structural similarity ground truth to benchmark spectral alignment or spectral similarity scores (e.g., modified cosine, SIMILE p-values) against chemical structure.

name: maximum-difference-redundancy-fragment-filtering
description: Use when enumerating candidate molecular formulas from LC-MS/MS fragment peaks with FSA and fragment formulas resolve to multiple maximum-difference-redundancy (MDR) combinations, and you must set MaxComb to control which fragments are dropped before scoring precursor candidates with Eq. 4.

name: maximum-flow-warping-estimation
description: Use when XCMS-corrected retention times remain misaligned for specific detected feature groups (e.g., flagged by ncGTW misalignment detection) and compound-specific, per-feature warping functions are needed instead of one global per-sample warp.

name: maximum-marginal-topk-ranking-of-molecular-annotations
description: Use when a ready-to-identify dataset contains candidate structures with MS/MS scores and ROASMI retention-order probabilities P_ij, and you need top-k ranked annotations per peak, especially for isomers with similar fragmentation or peaks lacking informative spectra.

name: maximum-rank-reproducibility-fdr-procedure
description: Use when you have ranked lists from replicate RNA-seq (or other high-throughput) experiments and need to identify reproducible signals with controlled false discovery rate, without parametric assumptions on dependence structures.

name: maximum-rank-statistic-computation
description: Use when two gene rank lists from replicate high-throughput experiments (e.g., SEQC RNA-seq comparisons of 43,919 transcripts) must be converted to per-gene maximum rank statistics M_g = max(R_gx, R_gy) as input to MaRR thresholding and mFDR estimation.
tools: Python (NumPy/pandas implementation of the closed-form MaRR estimator)

name: maximum-rank-statistic-implementation
description: Use when a replicate-pair metabolomics (or other high-dimensional biological) dataset needs a nonparametric estimate of the proportion of reproducible metabolites (pi_1) plus a data-driven rejection threshold controlling mFDR at level alpha.

name: maximum-rank-statistic-threshold-estimation
description: Use when you have two replicate rank lists (e.g., RNA-seq gene rankings from technical or biological replicates such as SEQC platform data) and need to detect the reproducible-to-irreproducible change point with FDR control, without parametric copula assumptions.

name: maximum-spanning-tree-extraction
description: Use when a weighted molecular network has been partitioned into Louvain communities and each cluster must be reduced to an interpretable, fully connected subnetwork without dropping any member nodes.

name: maximum-weight-spanning-tree-reconstruction
description: Use when a weighted molecular similarity graph built from tandem MS spectra edges must be re-connected so that every metabolite keeps its relationship instead of being fractured by a fixed cosine-0.7 cutoff.

name: maximum-weight-spectral-matching
description: Use when comparing pairs or sets of MS/MS tandem spectra — e.g. from MassBank or molecular networking datasets — where compounds have multiple delocalized structural differences and cosine-based scores fail, and significance estimation (p-values) is needed.

name: mb-pls-multiview-model-fitting
description: Use when two or more omics datasets (e.g. metabolomics and proteomics) measured on the same samples have been transformed to pathway-level scores and you need a predictive, integrative multi-view model that ranks pathways and omics-layer contributions.

name: mb-pls-significant-feature-counting
description: Use when you have fitted a multi-block PLS model over concatenated HPOS/LPOS/LNEG feature tables, obtained per-feature empirical p-values from an MB-VIP permutation test, and need to count significant predictors per block and quantify reduction vs univariate models.

name: mb-vip-feature-importance-scoring
description: Use when a fitted MamsiPls MB-PLS model (e.g., on HPOS/LPOS/LNEG LC-MS feature tables) needs per-feature importance scores and empirical p-values to identify which predictors drive the predicted outcome.

name: mb-vip-permutation-significance-testing
description: Use when an MB-PLS model (e.g. MamsiPls on multi-assay serum LC-MS intensity tables) has been fitted and you need per-feature statistical significance for feature selection before structural/correlation clustering, rather than relying on raw VIP scores alone.

name: mca-behavioral-factor-association-analysis
description: Use when you have latent factors from multi-omics data (e.g. MOFA factors), sample cluster memberships (e.g. SNF clusters), and behavioral dimension scores from MCA, and need cohort-aware association testing with multiple-testing correction.

name: mcar-missforest-imputation
description: Use when a metabolomics concentration table (CSV/XLSX) has missing entries whose per-group, per-metabolite missingness percentage classifies them as MCAR, and statistically rigorous imputation (missForest, KNN, mean, or median) is required before normalization or PCA.

name: mces-analog-retrieval-auc-evaluation
description: Use when comparing spectral similarity measures (embedding cosine similarity, MS2DeepScore, spectral entropy, dot-product variants) on molecular analog retrieval, needing AUROC curves stratified by MCES distance thresholds on paired MS/MS spectra.

name: mces-graph-distance-evaluation
description: Use when scoring de novo structure-elucidation outputs (SELFIES/SMILES candidates from spectra) against reference molecules and you need a structural-graph distance in addition to exact-match and fingerprint-similarity metrics, e.g. filling MCES columns of benchmark comparison tables.

name: mces-leakage-filtering-against-test-fold
description: Use when building an auxiliary pretraining corpus (e.g. fingerprint-molecule pairs from unlabeled PubChem molecules) that must not leak structures from held-out benchmark test sets such as MassSpecGym test folds or NPLIB1.

name: mces-structural-similarity-scoring
description: Use when evaluating FBMN or library-matching annotation quality: you have compound pairs (e.g., top-10 matches per query with SMILES) and need structural similarity scores to judge whether matches are identical, structural isomers, or dissimilar.

name: mcf-configuration-parameter-selection
description: Use when a target 2D 1H,13C HSQC spectrum (grid or peak-list csv.gz) must be mapped against a compound library (e.g. 501-compound MetaboMiner/Wishart HMDB library) with mcfNMR, and values for assignment_radius, detection_threshold, and fit mode must be configured.

name: mcia-multi-omics-integration
description: Use when two or more omics feature matrices (e.g. genes, proteins, lipids/metabolomics) share a sample set with a phenotype of interest and the goal is data-driven cross-omics integration to differentiate samples by phenotype.

name: mclean-compendium-sampled-split-generation
description: Use when benchmarking multiple CCS prediction tools (e.g., CCSP 2.0, CCSbase, AllCCS, DeepCCS) on the McLean Compendium and you need reproducible, tool-shared random test splits with aggregate median MRE/RMSE metrics.

name: mcmc-based-peak-parameter-estimation
description: Use when 1D NMR spectra (especially highly overlapped metabolomics spectra) must be deconvoluted into peak tables with accurate peak parameters rather than fitted in the frequency domain.

name: mcmc-convergence-diagnostics
description: Use when fitting Stan hierarchical/binomial multilevel models (e.g., PrediXcan-DEG enrichment or proportion-positive direction-of-effect models) and you must verify chain convergence before extracting marginal posterior means or 95% posterior-mass flags.

name: mcmc-convergence-diagnostics
description: Use when running a Gibbs sampler over a candidate-assignment network (e.g., ZODIAC reranking SIRIUS formula candidates) and you must set chain count, burn-in, sampling epochs, and verify the chains have stabilized before trusting posterior marginals.

name: mdv-nonnegative-regression-solving
description: Use when a fractional-abundance vector (FAM) from an LC-MS isotope labeling experiment must be converted to a corrected, non-negative MDV and isotopic enrichment via an already-built total correction matrix (MDT and/or ULS).

name: mean-centring-of-omics-feature-data
description: Use when a DatasetExperiment object from the struct framework needs per-column (feature) mean centring before downstream steps like PCA, or when implementing a custom centring model via set_obj_method.

name: mean-percentage-error-calculation-across-time-points
description: Use when validating delay-prediction models for NMR metabolomics data: you have fitted linear mixed models of metabolite change over pre-/post-centrifugation delays and need to score prediction accuracy against measured time-point values.

name: media-blank-background-component-removal
description: Use when a Progenesis-format peak table contains blank groups (solvent or media blanks) and features overrepresented in those blanks must be identified and removed to correct between-sample carryover and contamination.

name: median-aggregation-across-candidate-sets
description: Use when comparing candidate structure sets for the same spectra — e.g. whether the incorrect de novo prediction is as chemically close to the truth as the incorrect database candidate.

name: median-fold-change-normalization
description: Use when computing median fold change normalization factors from a metabolomics feature intensity table, or when demonstrating median FC bias against kernel-density MDFC under imbalanced up-/down-regulated feature fractions.

name: median-imputation-with-missing-indicators
description: Use when a descriptor/fingerprint feature matrix contains NaNs from tool failures (e.g., alvaDesc not generating some of the 5,666 descriptors) before fitting tree- or neural-network-based retention time regressors.

name: median-log2foldchange-computation
description: Use when comparing untargeted metabolomics peak matrices between two condition groups and a per-feature effect size is needed before significance filtering (e.g., |log2FC| > 0.5, p.adj < 0.1).

name: median-normalization-of-omics-counts
description: Decision support for choosing and applying a sample-scaling normalization (median vs EigenMS/NOMIS/CRMN) on MultiABLER-processed LC-MS/MS feature tables from metabolomic or lipidomic experiments.

name: median-normalization-of-omics-feature-tables
description: Use when a MultiABLER-derived metabolomic or lipidomic feature table needs sample-level intensity scaling so that all samples share the same median intensity before joint downstream analyses.

name: median-rank-statistic-computation
description: Use when you have IDSL.IPA-generated individual peak lists plus an aligned peak table and need to summarize which molecular formula hits from IDSL.UFA are reproducibly ranked near the top across samples before downstream reporting or MS/MS cross-checking.

name: median-relative-error-computation
description: Use when a collection of corrected/predicted CCS measurements with reference values needs its central accuracy quantified as a median relative error (MDRE), or when validating a calibration by reproducing a reported MDRE.

name: median-similarity-threshold-calibration
description: Use when you must simulate lower-quality fragmentation spectra from biological samples on clean reference MS/MS spectra and need an objective, similarity-based calibration of the noise level instead of arbitrary noise parameters.

name: median-spectrum-computation-per-region
description: Use when you have a spatial metabolomics peak table (pixels × m/z ions) with manually or lasso-delineated regions and need one representative spectrum per region before computing region-pair metrics like Pearson correlation.

name: median-squared-prediction-error-computation
description: Use when you need an outlier-sensitivity benchmark for normalization methods on simulated single-feature drift data where the true drift is known, e.g. comparing QC-RLSC, QC-RSC, rLOESS, rGAM, and tGAM across 0, 1, 2, or 4 injected outliers.

name: median-statistics-summarization-across-datasets
description: Use when two annotation methods (e.g. METASPACE-ML vs MSM) have been run on many imaging MS datasets and you need per-group median annotation-count gains and log2 fold-changes at fixed FDR cutoffs (5% and 10%).

name: median-threshold-outlier-filtering
description: Use when a CWT peak-detection step has produced ROI feature regions with intensity profiles from LC-MS/CE-MS metabolomics runs and noise features must be removed before feature integration and data augmentation.

name: medium-exchange-metabolite-matching
description: Use when building a multi-species community metabolic model in PyCoMo and you must define which substrates the community can take up, or link exchange metabolites across member models to enable cross-feeding.

name: medoid-representative-selection
description: Use when a redundant set of antiSMASH/gutSMASH gene-cluster GenBank outputs must be deduplicated before metagenomic read mapping, to avoid ambiguous mapping of reads to near-identical clusters.

name: meiotic-recombination-focus-count-extraction
description: Use when reproducing reported TOP-3::HA (or related recombination-marker) focus counts per nucleus across C. elegans germline zones 2–4 from published Results text, e.g. for the rtel-1 sensitized background.

name: meiotic-recombination-genotype-annotation
description: Use when a paper reports heterologous recombination event counts or percentages across meiotic genotypes and you need a genotype-indexed table to compare mutant rates or test synergy of BTR-complex alleles.

name: melanoma-phenotype-classification
description: Use when you have few-shot labeled single-cell mass spectrometry (SCMS) metabolomic feature vectors from melanoma cell pairs (untreated or drug-treated) and need rapid phenotype classification plus selection of essential m/z species.

name: melanoma-primary-vs-metastatic-classification
description: Use when you have pretreated SCMS metabolomics feature data (e.g., dataset.csv) from a primary/metastatic melanoma cell pair, PCA fails to discriminate the phenotypes, and only limited cells are available for training a classifier.

name: memo-matrix-alignment-across-instrument-platforms
description: Use when samples were acquired on different LC-MS/MS platforms or LC methods, or with strong RT shift/poor feature overlap, and you need sample-level clustering without prior feature alignment.

name: memo-matrix-alignment-across-samples
description: Use when LC-MS/MS samples lack a prior RT-based feature alignment — e.g. chemodiverse datasets, strong RT shifts, or different LC/MS platforms — and you need comparable sample-by-word vectors from raw MS2 spectra (.mgf).

name: memo-matrix-samplewise-normalization
description: Use when MEMO MS2 fingerprints have been aligned into a matrix of chemodiverse samples (e.g. the 1,600-plant-extract T. cruzi dataset) and you need comparable sample vectors prior to UMAP/TMAP embedding or cluster membership verification.

name: memote-metric-interpretation
description: Use when a genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. an SBML GEM from BioModels) must be quality-checked against community standards, with metrics like GPR coverage, metabolite InChI/annotation completeness, and stoichiometric consistency.

name: memote-model-quality-assessment
description: Use when genome-scale metabolic reconstructions (e.g. consensus or gap-filled SBML/MATLAB COBRA models) must be quality-assessed against standardized tests after reconstruction or gap filling, to report score, consistency, and GPR coverage.

name: mendelian-randomization-instrument-selection-from-mgwas
description: Use when estimating a causal relationship between a metabolite and a phenotype by integrating mGWAS data with comparable phenotype GWAS data via two-sample Mendelian randomization.

name: merge-efficacy-quantification
description: Use when you have just applied a metabolite-merging strategy (e.g. MMS) to a combined multi-study dataset and need to report the merge's efficacy — counts of name-consistency and of compounds that would not have merged by name alone.

name: merged-fragmentation-spectrum-construction
description: Use when processing LC-MS/MS runs (mzML/mzXML) where a feature (precursor ion) was fragmented at multiple collision energies and you need a single consolidated MS/MS spectrum per feature before formula and structure annotation.

name: merged-vs-unmerged-enrichment-comparison
description: Use when you hold two versions of a metabolite list — one harmonized/merged (e.g., via MMS InChIKey merging) and one unmerged — and need to quantify how harmonization changes which pathways reach significance (FDR < 0.05).

name: mesh-ontology-sample-grouping
description: Use when sample metadata from many GC/MS metabolomics studies is free-text, inconsistent, or riddled with domain-specific acronyms, and the goal is to run ontologically grouped differential analysis (OGDA) or phylogenetic-organization queries across studies.

name: mesh-taxonomy-mapping-analysis
description: Decision support for benchmarking a manual chemical classification system's coverage (e.g. MeSH over PubChem) against an automated, structure-based classifier such as ClassyFire before choosing an annotation pipeline.

name: messaging-api-alert-dispatch-configuration
description: Use when setting up semi-autonomous QC during Thermo LC-MS/MS acquisition, so researchers are alerted minutes after a raw file fails internal standard acceptance criteria in IS Configurations.

name: messes-cli-workflow-execution
description: Use when a metabolomics dataset exists as messy tabular spreadsheets (Excel/CSV) tagged per the MESSES tagging system and must be transformed into Metabolomics Workbench mwTab format via the extract-validate-convert pipeline.

name: messes-json-validation-workflow-execution
description: Use when a JSONized metadata representation has been produced by the MESSES extract step from tagged CSV/Excel tabular data and must be checked against a JSON Schema before the convert step to a deposition format.

name: messes-record-recoding-and-header-collation
description: Use when a validated MESSES JSONized metadata file must be transformed into mwTab JSON via conversion directives, and you need the value_type-driven semantics (str/matrix/section) plus recoding fields (override, code, record_id) and structural fields (for_each/test, headers, collate.

name: meta-learning-model-adaptation
description: Use when SCMS single-cell metabolomic peak tables are limited (1–10 adaptation samples per class) and a meta-trained model must be transferred via few-shot gradient descent to classify new cell groups (e.g., drug-treated IGR39/IGR37 or WM115/WM266-4 melanoma cells) as primary vs metastatic.

name: metabcombiner-intersection-mode-alignment
description: Use when evaluating LC-MS multi-dataset alignment tools — i.e., when feature tables from independently processed same-method datasets must be aligned and compared on overlapping Annotation_IDs and spurious matches.

name: metaboanalyst-data-matrix-formatting
description: Use when a processed 1D NMR bucket table (ppm-interval buckets after signal-to-noise filtering) must be converted into a samples-by-buckets CSV that online statistics tools like MetaboAnalyst 3.0 or BioStatFlow can ingest directly.

name: metaboanalyst-differential-abundance-analysis
description: Use when comparing a MetaboAnalyst-based NMR peak-grouping and differential analysis pipeline against an alternative peak-based workflow (e.g. speaq 2.0) on the same peak list, or when a lower-resolution grouped feature table is acceptable for between-group testing.

name: metaboanalyst-input-table-construction
description: Use when a binned NMR bucket-intensity matrix (rows = samples, columns = Bin.SpectraPoint buckets) plus sample class labels must be converted into MetaboAnalyst- or Workflows4Metabolomics-ready files.

name: metaboanalyst-statistical-analysis-workflow
description: Use when a public NMR/untargeted metabolomics data set (e.g., a MetaboLights study id) has been converted to an analysis-ready csv with class labels, and the goal is classification/discrimination analysis with ROC-AUC comparison between defined groups.

name: metabolic-biomarker-risk-scoring
description: Use when NMR metabolomics biomarker measurements (e.g., Nightingale platform) plus survival data are available and you must build a weighted mortality risk score and test whether it outperforms conventional risk factors in a held-out validation cohort.

name: metabolic-biomarker-score-construction
description: Use when mortality-associated metabolic biomarkers and their meta-analysis hazard ratios are available and you need to reproduce a weighted, per-unit risk score plus age/sex stratified consistency checks.

name: metabolic-compound-overlap-graph-construction
description: Use when building the structural (graph-based) level of a KEGG organism's metabolic network from pathway KGML files, where pathways must be connected via shared non-ubiquitous compounds rather than reactions.

name: metabolic-correlation-network-analysis
description: Use when you have a table of metabolite measurements plus sample trait metadata and want to group metabolites into correlation modules (accounting for interaction topology) and test whether modules associate with traits like tumor_normal or gender.

name: metabolic-distance-phylogenetic-correlation
description: Use when you have draft GEMs of related isolates from multiple reconstruction pipelines and need to know whether structural differences between the models track organism phylogeny rather than pipeline artifacts.

name: metabolic-exchange-reaction-analysis
description: Use when gap-filled community GEMs (e.g., Matlab workspaces from run_iterative_gap_filling.m) are available and the goal is to map which metabolites members secrete/uptake and derive helper/beneficiary dependency calls.

name: metabolic-feature-association-testing
description: Use when a metabolome-wide association (partial correlation or GLM) between a metabolic feature and a phenotype such as BMI needs confidence intervals or robustness validation by resampling, with confounders like Age, Gender, T2D adjusted.

name: metabolic-flux-estimation-from-transcriptomics
description: Use when single-cell (or bulk) RNA-seq count matrices are available and the goal is cell-type-resolved metabolic flux, metabolite concentration changes, or comparing flux landscapes (e.g., cancer vs stromal, AD vs control).

name: metabolic-flux-scaling-interpretation
description: Use when you have a human GEM paired with microbiota-derived aggregated in-/out-fluxes (fi, fo) and need to characterize how the α mixing weight scales the resulting exchange-reaction lower bounds across [0, 1].

name: metabolic-gene-mrna-expression-profiling
description: Use when ΔCt qPCR expression data (e.g. Taqman Custom Array raw values) for a fixed panel of metabolic genes must be converted into a gene × cell-line table of statistically supported direction-of-change calls versus a baseline control line.

name: metabolic-gene-set-construction
description: Use when you have a disease-associated or otherwise annotated metabolite list already carrying HMDB IDs and need to derive a metabolite-interacting gene set as input to over-representation analysis.

name: metabolic-gene-set-cross-referencing
description: Use when prioritizing candidate causal genes at molecular QTL loci by identifying sentinel-proximal genes already implicated in a trait-relevant molecular phenotype (e.g. metabolism) across curated annotation databases.

name: metabolic-gene-set-scoring
description: Use when prioritizing candidate causal genes at a molecular QTL (mQTL) by testing whether genes local to the sentinel variant are annotated as metabolism-related in GO, KEGG (hsa01100), Orphanet (ORPHA:68367), Reactome (R-HSA-1430728) or MGI (MP:0005266).

name: metabolic-geneset-to-gwas-subnetwork-comparison
description: Use when you have a metabolic gene set (metabolite-interacting genes) and a GWAS trait/disease subnetwork gene set and need the over-representation P-value of their intersection.

name: metabolic-model-boundary-reaction-identification
description: Use when a gut microbiota metabolic model (SBML) has been loaded into cobrapy and you need per-metabolite boundary in/out fluxes from FBA to constrain a human GEM's exchange reactions with M2R.

name: metabolic-model-gene-reaction-association-mapping
description: Use when you have an essential-gene list from single-gene deletion of a COBRApy/Reconstructor model and need to intersect it with DrugBank targets to enumerate drug-hypothesis counts (e.g. 7 known inhibitors, 13 untested).

name: metabolic-model-memote-quality-assessment
description: Use when you have draft or gap-filled SBML metabolic models (e.g., COBRApy/Reconstructor output with ModelSEED-consistent naming) and need standardized quality benchmarking scores to judge reconstruction quality.

name: metabolic-model-response-factor-inference
description: Use when you have time-course relative-abundance GC-MS metabolomics data (concMatrix + timeVec), a stoichiometric matrix with concentration/flux bounds, and need standard-free inference of absolute concentrations or response factors.

name: metabolic-model-reversible-to-irreversible-conversion
description: Use when a cell-relative SBML model produced by rasIntegration must be split so that reversible reactions are represented as separate forward and reverse reactions before sampling or RAS t-tests.

name: metabolic-module-factor-graph-construction
description: Use when a transcriptomics matrix (gene x cell) must be converted to cell-wise metabolic reaction fluxes via scFEA's module-wise neural networks coupled by a metabolite-by-module stoichiometry (factor-graph) constraint.

name: metabolic-module-graph-partitioning
description: Use when you need to reproduce or verify the composition of a curated metabolic module map (e.g. scFEA's M171 human metabolic map): counting reaction modules, super modules, intermediate substrates, genes, enzymes, transporters, reactions and metabolites.

name: metabolic-module-identification
description: Use when a DNEA object contains estimated condition networks and you need to partition metabolites into interconnected sub networks (metabolic modules) before enrichment analysis.

name: metabolic-network-adjacency-matrix-serialisation
description: Use when reconstructing MetNet's structural level from KEGG KGML pathway data and you need a pathway-by-pathway adjacency matrix capturing shared-compound connections for organism comparison.

name: metabolic-network-gap-filling
description: Use when building a GSMN from a newly annotated genome of an emerging model organism whose biochemical knowledge is incomplete and requires orthology mapping plus manual gap-filling.

name: metabolic-network-module-activity-analysis
description: Reference for reproducing mummichog network module activity predictions (e.g. the moDC YF17D activation network of 60 metabolites, 19 un-annotated) from a significant-m/z list plus a full reference feature list.

name: metabolic-network-module-extraction
description: Use when you have an untargeted metabolomics feature table (m/z, retention time, p-value) with a significant vs reference feature split, and need pathway/network-level activity or predicted metabolite networks without doing MS/MS identification.

name: metabolic-network-reconstruction
description: Use when building or verifying the KGMN layer-1 reaction network from KEGG metabolites and BioTransformer predictions, or when checking KMRN scale (unknown metabolites, edges, biotransformation types) against reported figures.

name: metabolic-network-reconstruction-from-kegg
description: Use when the goal is to reconstruct organism-specific metabolic networks from KEGG organisms for downstream comparison (pairwise similarity indexes or multi-organism clustering), starting only from KEGG organism codes.

name: metabolic-network-visualization-export
description: Use when metabolite association networks (biochemical, structural, spectral, or empirical edges) have been calculated and need interactive thresholding, node attribute mapping, or export to CSV/SVG/Cytoscape for interpretation.

name: metabolic-pathway-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have an unfiltered KO/gene/compound abundance table plus sample metadata (categorical groups, multiple time points, or a continuous variable) and need pathway-level enrichment with high sensitivity.

name: metabolic-pathway-enrichment-testing
description: Use when a list of differentially abundant metabolites must be interpreted functionally via ORA against KEGG, Reactome, or BioCyc compound sets, and background-set/parameter choices must be controlled.

name: metabolic-pathway-enrichment-visualization
description: Use when a list of significant metabolites (e.g. Log2FC > 1.5, adj-p < 0.05) from HFD or other treatment comparisons needs mapping to KEGG pathways to identify which metabolic functions are over-represented.

name: metabolic-pathway-hypothesis-reconstruction
description: Use when a paired transcriptomic-metabolomic dataset is available and the goal is unsupervised, de novo reconstruction of a specialized metabolite biosynthetic pathway without prior knowledge of a 'bait' compound or enzyme.

name: metabolic-pathway-prediction-evaluation
description: Use when you need to quantify and statistically validate how much of a reference set of experimentally characterized biosynthetic reactions a computational reaction-rule predictor (e.g., MEANtools/RetroRules rules) can anticipate.

name: metabolic-pathway-reconstruction
description: Use when you have the KEGG code of one or more organisms and a pathway list (organismList.txt / pathwayList.txt) and need per-pathway reaction sets for the functional level of the network.

name: metabolic-reaction-iteration
description: Use when labeled Metabolite CNs are too sparse to train a pathway predictor and only a subset of known chemical reactions (hyperlinks) is available to imitate the organism's metabolic activity and generate artificial networks.

name: metabolic-reaction-network-curation
description: Use when building or expanding a knowledge-driven metabolic reaction network from KEGG/MetaCyc/HMDB records with predicted reaction pairs, or when verifying curated MRN metabolite/reaction-pair counts.

name: metabolic-reaction-rule-catalog-construction
description: Use when constructing the predictable-metabolite matching rule set for a mass spectrometry bridging analysis — i.e., you need to enumerate metabolic transformation products of prototypes and score m/z and MS2 similarity for each candidate metabolite-prototype pair.

name: metabolic-reaction-site-extraction
description: Use when you have a PathModel knowledge base (.lp) with molecules as atom/bond predicates and known reactions, and need reaction sites (biochemical transformations) to drive analogical inference of new reactions or metabolite structures.

name: metabolic-reconstruction-merging
description: Use when multiple automatically generated draft GEMs for the same isolates (e.g. from KBase, CarveMe, RAVEN 2.0, AuReMe) must be merged into a single consensus model and compared against curated reference models.

name: metabolic-state-annotation-in-hepatocytes
description: Use when a SpaceM spatio-molecular matrix (MORPHnMOL.csv) of single-cell metabolic profiles must be partitioned into unsupervised metabolic states and per-condition state proportions quantified, e.g. CTRL vs +FA vs +FA+IL17A vs +FA+IL17A+TPCA1 NAFLD/NASH cultures.

name: metabolic-state-marker-stability-assessment
description: Use when a SpaceM spatio-molecular matrix (MORPHnMOL.csv) contains ablation marks that co-sampled neighboring cells and you must quantify whether excluding them changes metabolic-state clustering, marker significance, or cell type classification accuracy.

name: metabolic-subnetwork-module-detection
description: Use when interpreting an LC/MS feature table (m/z, rtime, p-value) via network-level analysis: matching features to tentative metabolites and scoring metabolic subnetwork modules instead of relying on confirmed metabolite IDs.

name: metabolic-time-course-quantification-from-pseudo-2d-nmr
description: Use when you have a series of 1D NMR spectra (acquired individually or as a pseudo-2D experiment) from a metabolic time course — e.g. real-time glycolysis monitoring on 31P or 1H — and need fitted intensities, areas, chemical shifts, linewidths, and coupling constants per signal per time point.

name: metabolic-transformation-deduplication
description: Use when you have reactions encoded as reactant-product links over atom/bond predicates (e.g. sterol_pwy.lp, MAA_pwy.lp) and need distinct molecular transformations rather than per-reaction sites.

name: metabolights-dataset-retrieval
description: Reference for retrieving a named public MS dataset (PXD/IPX/MTBLS/XCMS accession) from ProteomeXchange or Metabolights to obtain native vendor files for compression or format-conversion experiments.

name: metabolism-prediction-model-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating or comparing reactant-prediction performance for CYP450 enzymes (CYP1A2, 2A6, 2B6, 2C8, 2C9, 2C19, 2D6, 2E1, 3A4) on molecule-enzyme pairs with binary reactant labels, using AUROC as the metric.

name: metabolite-abundance-extraction-from-vendor-worksheets
description: Use when source metabolomics data arrive as vendor worksheets (e.g. Metabolon Excel 'OrigScale' sheet or Nightingale Health .xlsx) and you need the abundance matrix, sample metadata, and metabolite metadata as separate tab-delimited datasets.

name: metabolite-abundance-significance-verification
description: Use when a preprocessed metabolite measurement matrix has two labeled groups (e.g. MYC-high vs AKT1-high prostate cancer) and you need per-metabolite significance calls (pval, adj_pval, dm) to confirm a published significance pattern.

name: metabolite-adduct-annotation
description: Use when processing raw centroided LC-MS/MS mzML data through UmetaFlow and features must carry adduct/charge information before feature linking, re-quantification, or GNPS export.

name: metabolite-adduct-annotation
description: Use when you have a preprocessed MSI dataset (measured m/z in the first column) and an organ/mode-matched metabolite database with theoretical adduct m/z values, and need metabolite/adduct annotations.

name: metabolite-adduct-form-enumeration
description: Use when constructing a metabolite database for mass spectrometry imaging that must contain the adduct ions actually formed under AFADESI-MSI rather than the LC-MS adduct forms, given a metabolite list per organ and ionization mode.

name: metabolite-annotation-against-plant-ms-database
description: Use when LC–MS peak/feature tables (e.g. matched Thermo and Waters feature tables) need compound annotation in a plant metabolomics context, and cross-platform annotation robustness must be quantified.

name: metabolite-annotation-agreement-validation
description: Use when you have M2S (or similar RT/mz/FI-based) match tables linking two LC-MS feature tables and independent metabolite annotations, and you need a ground-truth estimate of match correctness.

name: metabolite-annotation-api-querying
description: Use when a downstream application (e.g. HMDB or a custom pipeline) needs to fetch compound annotations programmatically from CMM 3.0 — i.e. given a list of metabolite exact masses and adduct forms, you must query ceumass.eps.uspceu.

name: metabolite-annotation-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating or benchmarking LC-MS untargeted metabolomics peak-annotation methods against a curated ground-truth feature set, or when reproducing the KGMN vs MetDNA1 accuracy/coverage comparison on the 242-metabolite urine benchmark.

name: metabolite-annotation-benchmarking
description: Use when candidate metabolite annotations must be filtered by predicted-vs-observed retention time agreement and you need an objective threshold chosen via ROC analysis on a labeled test set.

name: metabolite-annotation-benchmarking
description: Use when ranked candidate annotation lists exist for MS/MS spectra and you need to quantify annotation quality (precision/recall/F1 with correct-at-rank-1 as TP) or measure the impact of a re-ranking strategy such as taxonomically informed scoring.

name: metabolite-annotation-candidate-filtering
description: Use when a high-resolution MS metabolite annotation workflow yields too many exact-mass candidates (e.g. 43–13,984 per compound within 10 ppm) and measured or predictable ion-mobility CCS values are available to prune them.

name: metabolite-annotation-class-categorization
description: Use when starting from a raw GCxGC-TOFMS detected-peak list (e.g. 691 peaks) and you must document exclusion criteria, missing-value replacement rules, and the annotation-class breakdown of retained metabolites.

name: metabolite-annotation-class-filtering
description: Use when assembling a curated set of known metabolites from HMDB-classified SMILES to train or evaluate a chemical language model and you need to exclude merely predicted/expected annotations and lipid-like molecules.

name: metabolite-annotation-confidence-level-assignment
description: Use when an unassigned LC-HRMS signal (e.g. a recurrent m/z feature observed on multiple platforms such as Orbitrap Fusion and Q-ToF Impact II) has been characterized by HRMS/MS and needs a metabolite annotation with an explicit MSI confidence level.

name: metabolite-annotation-confidence-level-matching
description: Use when validating network-derived (e.g., MetDNA3 level 3) metabolite annotations by testing concordance with independent tools such as CFM-ID, MetFrag, MS-FINDER, and SIRIUS on feature-matched annotations.

name: metabolite-annotation-confidence-leveling
description: Use when input is MS1-only full-scan LC-MS data (mzML/mzXML, e.g. from Metabolomics Workbench) lacking MS/MS acquisition, and the goal is metabolite annotations at MSI level 2/3 confidence with per-mode counts.

name: metabolite-annotation-corroboration
description: Use when a KGMN or MetDNA2 annotation run produced putatively annotated unknown peaks (e.g. from NIST urine) that cannot be validated against spectral libraries or standards, and independent in silico MS/MS support is needed.

name: metabolite-annotation-coverage-analysis
description: Use when you need to quantify how much of a known metabolite set a network-based annotation pipeline recovers (coverage, Top 1/3/10 correct rate, Top 3 FDR) by hiding a fraction of known annotations and testing their recovery from seed metabolites.

name: metabolite-annotation-cross-referencing
description: Use when an annotated feature table (e.g. FBMN + ChemWalker + SIRIUS output for actinomycete strains such as BRA006, BRA010, BRA177) needs KEGG compound mapping, pathway assignment, and cross-strain pathway comparison.

name: metabolite-annotation-cross-validation
description: Use when evaluating whether generated candidate structures plus predicted MS/MS spectra improve exact-structure assignment of held-out metabolites over accurate-mass prioritization alone.

name: metabolite-annotation-database-mapping
description: Use when METASPACE-annotated spatial or single-cell metabolomics data must be linked to metabolite/lipid set terms for overrepresentation or set enrichment analysis while accounting for isomeric and isobaric candidate ambiguity.

name: metabolite-annotation-fdr-filtering
description: Use when MALDI-imaging datasets must be re-annotated with a specific formula list (e.g., matrix clusters) against a metabolite database and a controlled FDR cutoff is needed before image classification.

name: metabolite-annotation-fdr-filtering

name: metabolite-annotation-gain-quantification

name: metabolite-annotation-hmdb-metlin-matching
description: Use when a shortlist of tumor-co-localized m/z peaks (Pearson r ≥ 0.7 against a massNet tumor-class prediction map) needs tentative molecular formula and adduct assignment via exact-mass search of HMDB and METLIN.

name: metabolite-annotation-level-assignment
description: Use when a filtered/normalized margheRita mRList object derived from MS-Dial output needs feature-metabolite annotation, and MS/MS spectra for features are available for matching against the RPShort positive-mode spectral library.

name: metabolite-annotation-mapping
description: Use when untargeted LC-MS/MS features (from MZmine2 output: feature table + MGF spectra) need molecular formulas, fingerprints, and chemical-taxonomy annotations attached to a chemical tree so annotated molecules can be traced across samples.

name: metabolite-annotation-msi-confidence-levels
description: Use when LC-MS untargeted metabolomics features (e.g. a cleaned mass_dataset object from tidyMass) need metabolite identification against curated in-house databases with standardized MSI confidence-level reporting.

name: metabolite-annotation-network-reconstruction
description: Use when an LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics peak table with MS2 spectra contains annotated known metabolites (seeded from standard spectral libraries) that must be propagated to reaction-paired, spectrally similar unknown peaks via KGMN.

name: metabolite-annotation-precision-recall-computation
description: Decision support for choosing the most reliable FDR threshold when analyzing METASPACE-ML annotation results: per-dataset target and decoy annotation tables are available and reliability must be compared across default FDR thresholds.

name: metabolite-annotation-propagation-benchmarking
description: Use when you must quantify how the connectivity/edge density of a knowledge-driven metabolite network (MRN vs SMN vs FCN) changes annotation accuracy, estimated FDR, and propagation specificity, with decoy MS2 spectra as negative controls.

name: metabolite-annotation-scoring
description: Use when a plant metabolomics LC-MS/MS peak needs a reproducible annotation score: e.g. a peak defined by m/z (e.g. 385.1118 in negative mode) plus RT (e.g. 1.27 min) whose MS/MS spectrum should be scored against a plant-specific metabolite database.

name: metabolite-annotation-scoring
description: Use when mzML files from spiked-standard experiments (e.g., standards in water or yeast backgrounds) have been searched against a spectral library and you must rank annotations by score and select the -performing scoring method and threshold.

name: metabolite-annotation-source-tracking
description: Use when building or auditing a plant-specific MS1 annotation database from multiple source libraries (KEGG, KNApSAcK, PlantCyc) and you need per-source retained counts after filtering out non-plant metabolites.

name: metabolite-annotation-strategy-comparison

name: metabolite-annotation-table-generation

name: metabolite-annotation-verification
description: Use when a genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. an SBML file from BioModels) must be assessed against community standards for metabolite/reaction annotation coverage and GPR completeness before publication or reuse.

name: metabolite-annotation-with-metdna

name: metabolite-attribute-coverage-quantification

name: metabolite-auc-threshold-verification
