name: metabolite-background-set-reduction-simulation
description: Use when evaluating the robustness of over-representation analysis results to the composition of the background/reference compound set, e.g. when the assay-specific background may be incomplete or when reporting how SEP proportions change as the background shrinks.

name: metabolite-basis-function-alignment
description: Use when you have a simulated MRS metabolite basis set and an experimentally acquired LCModel basis set and need to validate simulation fidelity per metabolite via ICCs.

name: metabolite-batch-association-regression

name: metabolite-calibration-curve-quantification

name: metabolite-candidate-annotation-filtering

name: metabolite-candidate-filtering

name: metabolite-candidate-filtering-lcms
description: Use when LC/MS feature tables (XCMS/CAMERA xsAnnotate results) must be reduced to a short list of metabolite candidates by applying label-shift, RT-window and detectability filters.

name: metabolite-candidate-graph-construction

name: metabolite-candidate-prioritization

name: metabolite-candidate-ranking

name: metabolite-candidate-ranking-kegg-database

name: metabolite-candidate-ranking-with-tie-breaking

name: metabolite-candidate-reranking

name: metabolite-candidate-score-normalization

name: metabolite-candidate-shift-alignment

name: metabolite-candidate-top10-ranking-evaluation

name: metabolite-coexpression-network-analysis

name: metabolite-competition-ratio-calculation

name: metabolite-correlation-distance-clustering

name: metabolite-database-compound-curation

name: metabolomics-feature-cutoff-sensitivity-sweep

name: metabolomics-feature-differential-analysis

name: metabolomics-feature-extraction-mzmine
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS files (e.g., MassIVE accession MSV000080673) must be converted into a per-sample feature table with extracted MS/MS spectra before spectral library matching of drugs or metabolites.

name: metabolomics-feature-filtering-and-imputation
description: Use when you have a raw feature table from LC-MS or DIMS peak detection/alignment (e.g. XCMS output) that must be cleaned of low-quality, blank-derived or non-reproducible peaks and made statistics-ready via imputation and normalization.

name: metabolomics-feature-group-tabulation

name: metabolomics-feature-importance-ranking

name: metabolomics-feature-intensity-table-processing

name: metabolomics-feature-matrix-pca-analysis

name: metabolomics-feature-network-analysis

name: metabolomics-feature-normalization-scaling
description: Use when a preprocessed metabolomics or proteomics feature table (after missing-value imputation) still contains features on incomparable numeric scales and the goal is normalized data for downstream EDA or statistical analysis in POMAShiny/POMA.

name: metabolomics-feature-quality-control
description: Use when starting from a raw LC/MS feature table (m/z, retention time, intensity per sample class) that must be QC-filtered before pathway or network activity analysis such as mummichog.

name: metabolomics-feature-quality-filtering
description: Use when a feature-by-sample metabolomics intensity table must be filtered to retain only high-quality features before computing normalization factors, and per-feature failure reasons are needed.

name: metabolomics-feature-requantification
description: Use when an untargeted LC-MS/MS feature table from OpenMS pre-processing contains missing values across samples and a complete quantification matrix is needed for statistical analysis, marker selection, or benchmarking detection/quantification rates.

name: metabolomics-feature-scaling
description: Use when a normalized metabolomics feature table (mass features x samples) must be brought onto a comparable scale prior to statistical analysis or visualization, and a choice among centering/scaling variants is needed.

name: metabolomics-feature-scoring

name: metabolomics-feature-scoring-and-basketing

name: metabolomics-feature-statistical-testing
description: Use when you have an aligned, quantified feature table (uncorrected or batch-corrected apLCMS/XCMS/two-stage output) and two labeled sample groups (e.g. oak vs wine yeast cell types) and need to count significant features at a stated FDR cutoff such as 0.2.

name: metabolomics-feature-table-clustering
description: Use when a wide formatted metabolomics feature table (samples as columns, features as rows) plus a companion design file need unsupervised hierarchical clustering with dendrograms and pairwise distance output.

name: metabolomics-feature-table-comparison
description: Use when two untargeted LC-MS metabolomics feature tables (samples x features with RT, m/z, and optionally FI medians) must be matched, and match counts/quality should be compared against metabCombiner.

name: metabolomics-feature-table-construction

name: metabolomics-feature-table-construction
description: Use when converting eRah deconvolved GC/MS (e.g. GC–TOF EI) chromatograms across multiple samples into a compound-by-sample area table, and compounds must be grouped across samples (alignment) and missing entries recovered before downstream quantification.

name: metabolomics-feature-table-differential-abundance-testing

name: metabolomics-feature-table-generation

name: metabolomics-feature-table-generation

name: metabolomics-feature-table-matching

name: metabolomics-feature-table-mgf-preparation

name: metabolomics-feature-table-parsing

name: metabolomics-feature-table-processing

name: metabolomics-feature-table-wrangling

name: metabolomics-figure-s10-reproduction

name: metabolomics-file-schedule-monitoring

name: metabolomics-qcpool-series-monitoring
description: Use when a targeted metabolomics or lipidomics study has pooled QC samples (QCpool) measured at regular intervals across one or more sequences, and you need to detect signal drift, background/carryover effects or out-of-control injections before downstream missing-value handling and outlier removal.

name: metabolomics-quality-control-boxplot-visualization
description: Use when a MetaboDiff MultiAssayExperiment object (Metabolon®-style metabolite measurements) has been imputed and vsn-normalized and you must visually verify near-constant variance and comparable per-sample distributions before differential analysis.

name: metabolomics-quality-control-cv-analysis
description: Use when a 1H-NMR or metabonomic dataset contains QC replicate samples and you must quantify analytical reproducibility per metabolic feature, or decide which features to retain via CV < 0.30 / CV < 0.15 filtering.

name: metabolomics-quality-control-filtering
description: Use when raw platform-exported metabolomics data (e.g. Metabolon OrigScale xlsx, Nightingale NMR, Olink, SomaLogic adat) must be QC'd, filtered on missingness/outlier thresholds, and summarized before association analysis.

name: metabolomics-quality-control-monitoring
description: Use when untargeted MS-based metabolomics files (mzML, mzXML, mzData) are being acquired or already acquired and you need to monitor QC parameters such as m/z deviation, retention time deviation, intensity drift, calibration offset, or contaminant levels in (near) real time or retrospectively.

name: metabolomics-quality-correction-workflow
description: Use when an Asari preferred_Feature_table.tsv from a pcpfm experiment shows per-sample TIC differences driven by feature counts, or samples span multiple batches, and the table must be normalized/batch-corrected before downstream analysis.

name: metabolomics-quality-parameter-extraction
description: Use when acquired or archived untargeted MS metabolomics files (mzML, mzXML, mzData) must be summarized into per-file quality metrics — RT and m/z deviations, intensity drift, peak shape — for real-time or retrospective QC.

name: metabolomics-quantification-report-processing
description: Use when a MetaPro run-1 quantification export (.xlsx) is available for a benchmark mixture design with known SB:SA dilution ratios (1/16 to 16/1) and you need to verify that observed log2 fold changes track the designed values before manual peak inspection.

name: metabolomics-quantitative-results-extraction
description: Use when a source card asks to reproduce reported metabolomics counts (peaks/identifications per ionisation mode) from a paper's Results text and supplementary figures, and the deliverable is a validated summary table rather than re-processed spectra.

name: metabolomics-raw-data-preprocessing
description: Use when raw targeted LC–MS runs from public repositories (e.g., MetaboLights MTBLS8735, potentially from different vendors) must be integrated against a target list and QC-clustered PCA is the exploratory endpoint.

name: metabolomics-raw-data-reprocessing
description: Use when raw LC–MS mzML files (e.g. from MetaboLights MTBLS1919) must be converted into a curated, QC-controlled feature matrix for untargeted metabolomics, rather than analyzed with manual or GUI tools.

name: metabolomics-raw-data-retrieval-from-repository
description: Use when a metabolomics analysis must start from publicly deposited raw spectra — e.g., reproducing a SWATH-DIA benchmark that requires the raw mzML files of a Metabolomics Workbench study plus its MS1 feature table.

name: metabolomics-regression-modelling
description: Use when a metabolomics intensity table plus sample metadata and a model formula require per-metabolite regression — fixed-effects lm, longitudinal mixed-effects (lmer), or Tobit for censored detection-limit values.

name: metabolomics-replicate-precision-assessment
description: Use when you have an aligned feature table from JPA's peak.alignment step with replicate sample-intensity columns and need to quantify analytical precision of peak-picked (PP) versus MS2-recognized (MR) features before statistical testing.

name: metabolomics-replicate-qc-evaluation
description: Use when raw LC-MS spectra from a serial dilution series (known dilution design, replicate tubes) are available and you need to validate that a spectra-processing workflow quantifies features proportionally to concentration.

name: metabolomics-replicate-reproducibility-quantification
description: Use when high-dimensional metabolomics (or similar omics) data contain technical or biological replicate samples and you need to identify reproducible metabolites/sample pairs and compare replicate layers, e.g. Tech vs BioTech vs Bio COPDGene datasets.

name: metabolomics-replicate-variability-assessment
description: Use when comparing normalisation strategies for multi-batch, large-scale metabolomics matrices (e.g. BioHEART-CT plasma data) by measuring replicate SD per metabolite across pooled QC, short replicate, and batch replicate sets.

name: metabolomics-repository-data-access
description: Use when a spectrum of interest lives in a metabolomics repository (e.

name: metabolomics-repository-data-conversion
description: Use when a study from MetaboLights or Metabolomics Workbench (e.g. an NMR study like MTBLS563 with Bruker fid/acqu files) must be transformed into an analysis-ready format before statistical analysis or ROC/AUC evaluation.

name: metabolomics-repository-quality-control
description: Use when you need to quantify validation errors across a corpus of mwTab files from the Metabolomics Workbench (e.g. schema violations, null section items, inconsistent SUBJECT_SAMPLE_FACTORS sample IDs) to guide repository curation.

name: metabolomics-repository-routing
description: Use when input consists of USI strings from metabolomics resources (MassBank, MOTIFDB, GNPS tasks/libraries, MSV/PXD/MetaboLights/Workbench accessions) that must be decomposed and mapped to the correct data service.

name: metabolomics-repository-study-retrieval
description: Use when a study ID from MetaboLights or Metabolomics Workbench is available and the raw/NMR acquisition files need to be fetched, harmonized into a standardized directory format, and made ready-to-use for data analysis platforms.

name: metabolomics-reproducibility-simulation
description: Use when validating that the MaRR procedure controls FDR at a nominal level, achieves high discriminative power, and estimates the reproducible-signal proportion (pi_1) without substantial bias under simulated bivariate Normal metabolomics settings.

name: metabolomics-results-export-csv
description: Use when MS-DIAL has finished annotating internal standard, reference standard, and external standard features for a Thermo raw file and the aligned results must be written to disk as CSV inputs for the Rapid QC-MS dashboard.

name: metabolomics-sample-fingerprint-generation
description: Use when you have LC-MS/MS samples (e.g. an MZmine-exported aligned feature table plus a GNPS FBMN-exported .mgf spectra file) and need a retention-time-agnostic sample-vs-sample comparison matrix built from MS2 peak/loss occurrence counts.

name: metabolomics-sample-group-statistics
description: Use when an xcms or .mskFT feature table with mz, rt and group-defined intensity columns must be statistically compared across biological groups to find enriched features.

name: metabolomics-sample-metadata-handling
description: Use when building or validating the sample metadata/sequence file for a pcpfm experiment — e.g. assigning Type (STD/BLANK/QC/Unknown) and Batch fields from an instrument sequence file, or preparing metadata that batch correction will consume via --by_batch.

name: metabolomics-sample-metadata-mapping
description: Use when a binned NMR data matrix (rows = bucket intensities over Bin.SpectraPoint spectral points per sample) must be annotated with sample class labels from sample metadata before export to MetaboAnalyst or Workflows4Metabolomics.

name: metabolomics-sample-normalization-factor-calculation
description: Use when you have a feature intensity table (features in rows, samples in columns) from untargeted metabolomics and need per-sample normalization factors that reflect relative sample concentrations, reducing intragroup variation.

name: metabolomics-sample-subset-removal-from-multiassayexperiment
description: Use when a metabolomics MultiAssayExperiment object (post kNN imputation) shows a distinct outlier cluster in sample-sample clustering that should be excluded before normalization.

name: metabolomics-sample-table-construction
description: Use when the input is a directory of raw Bruker NMR spectra in the original Bruker directory format (per-sample 'acqus' files and 'fid' binary traces) and you need one-row-per-sample parameter and FID tables before any FID-to-spectrum preprocessing.

name: metabolomics-sample-vectorization
description: Use when comparing large ensembles of LC-MS/MS samples (e.g. 1,920 plant extracts / 906,509 MS/MS spectra) that are chemodiverse, have strong RT shifts, or were acquired across different LC or MS platforms (Q-ToF vs Orbitrap).

name: metabolomics-signal-drift-correction
description: Use when a metabolomics or proteomics feature intensity table (e.

name: metabolomics-signal-normalization
description: Use when raw or pre-processed clinical metabolomics matrices (e.g. log2-transformed lipid or GC-TOF MS profiles from paired patient samples like CRC VAT/SAT) show subject-driven variation that obscures group differences.

name: metabolomics-significance-table-construction
description: Use when starting from a metabolite names/concentration matrix with sample metadata and you need to determine which metabolites are significantly altered between comparison groups before class or pathway enrichment.

name: metabolomics-significant-feature-counting
description: Use when you have an LC/MS feature-intensity matrix plus batch and phenotype annotations and need per-preprocessing-setting counts of differentially abundant features at FDR <= 0.2 after empirical-Bayes batch correction.

name: metabolomics-simulation-data-generation
description: Use when benchmarking sample-normalization estimators on metabolomics data where ground truth is needed — e.g., testing whether MDFC stays unbiased under imbalanced up/down-regulation while median FC is expected to be biased.

name: metabolomics-software-pipeline-categorization
description: Use when auditing a metabolomics software bundle (e.g. MetumpX-bin) to enumerate its packaged tools, categorize them by pipeline stage, and verify the count against claims in a paper abstract or README.

name: metabolomics-software-usage-ranking-extraction
description: Use when a task asks which freely available metabolomics software tools were most widely used per data type/functionality, or when reproducing the survey-based usage claims (e.g. XCMS 70% of LC-MS respondents) from the Spicer et al. 2017 review.

name: metabolomics-spectra-disease-classification
description: Use when the input is raw untargeted LC-MS metabolomic data (.npy or mzML per sample) with a disease-label file, and the goal is multi-class disease-state prediction while removing batch/hospital effects.

name: metabolomics-spectra-matrix-export
description: Use when a set of calibrated 1D 1H NMR spectra (Bruker/Agilent FID, Bruker 1r files, or nmrML) has been baseline-corrected and realigned across selected ppm areas in NMRProcFlow and a spectral data matrix must be produced for statistical analysis.

name: metabolomics-spectra-qc-reporting
description: Use when a metabolomics pipeline holds MS2 peak lists for public spectra and must decide, before compound identification, which spectra are reliable enough to carry into MS2 spectral comparison and annotation.

name: metabolomics-spectra-rank-annotation
description: Use when a per-spectrum feature table with formula-rank labels (R1 vs R2+) is available from FSA output and the goal is to test which spectral features discriminate correct from incorrect rank#1 formula annotations.

name: metabolomics-spectral-data-cleaning
description: Use when an integrated spectral library (.MSP/.MGF/.JSON/.CSV) contains spectra with sparse peak lists, and low-information spectra must be dropped via a minimum-peak-count filter before library harmonization or search.

name: metabolomics-spectral-matrix-reduction
description: Use when you have preprocessed, window-selected 1H-NMR spectra (spectra_df with samples as rows and chemical shifts as columns) and need to reduce dimensionality for multivariate analysis such as PCA.

name: metabolomics-spectrum-processing
description: Use when an MS/MS spectrum (e.g., a GNPS spectral-library entry referenced by USI) must be processed — noise/precursor peak removal, intensity filtering and scaling — and rendered as a static annotated spectrum figure.

name: metabolomics-standard-library-matching
description: Use when untargeted LC-MS/MS peak tables with MS2 spectra (per ionization mode) need seed annotations of known metabolites to launch knowledge-guided multi-layer network (KGMN) propagation to unknowns.

name: metabolomics-statistical-hypothesis-testing
description: Use when you have the grouped molecular feature table from OUKS step 8 (Grouping.R) plus a metadata.csv defining two sample groups, and you need hypothesis testing, fold changes, CV-based biomarker selection, and ROC/UMAP/t-SNE outputs.

name: metabolomics-statistical-testing
description: Use when metabolomics count data (e.g. c57_nos2KO_mouse_countDF) must be tested for per-metabolite differences between two groups (e.g. Mock vs Strep) with BH-adjusted p-values and fold-change output for downstream plotting.

name: metabolomics-statistics-subsetting
description: Use when a metabolomics data frame with KEGG compound IDs has been statistically tested (e.g. omu_summary student's t-test with BH adjustment) and only metabolites of interest (e.g. adjusted p <= 0.05) should be carried into KEGG enzyme/gene annotation.

name: metabolomics-study-data-acquisition
description: Use when a public metabolomics study's raw LC-MS/MS files must be fetched (e.g. Metabolomics WorkBench ST002044) and converted into deduplicated MS/MS .msp spectra per ESI+ / ESI− mode for downstream modeling or library matching.

name: metabolomics-substructure-annotation-validation
description: Use when you have automatically annotated Mass2Motifs via spectral matching and need to measure how many match manually characterized substructure labels, especially when neutral losses had to be omitted because spectral-matching tools do not support them.

name: metabolomics-summary-statistics-visualization
description: Use when a preprocessed metabolomics feature/sample table needs exploratory visualisation and summary statistics, and the results must be packaged into a self-contained HTML report for a lab or core facility project.

name: metabolomics-supervised-modeling-reporting
description: Use when GCxGC-TOFMS metabolite feature tables (e.g. 195 metabolites from plasma) carry sample-class labels such as S. Typhi carriage, S. Paratyphi A carriage, and non-carriage controls, and the goal is supervised discrimination with significance testing and ROC-validated latent biomarkers.

name: metabolomics-table-csv-roundtrip
description: Use when the input is a metabolomics concentration table in .csv or .xlsx with mixed metadata and measurement columns, and it must be parsed, normalized, or transformed and exported as CSV for downstream statistical analysis.

name: metabolomics-table-export
description: Use when a Metaboseek comparative analysis (e.g. hacl-1 vs WT exo-metabolome) has produced a filtered feature table with fold-change, intensity, and significance columns that must be persisted as a .csv deliverable.

name: metabolomics-table-missing-data-threshold-detection
description: Use when a freshly imported .csv or .xlsx metabolomics table must be checked for processing-readiness before imputation or normalization, especially when groups may contain too many missing values.

name: metabolomics-tabular-data-import
description: Use when starting an mzQuality workflow from a tab-delimited peak-integrated table (e.g. from SCIEX OS dMRM integration) containing aliquot, compound, area, type, injection_time, and batch columns, and a SummarizedExperiment must be built before analysis.

name: metabolomics-throughput-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing automated preprocessing wall-clock time against a manual vendor-software baseline for a large targeted metabolomic data set (e.g., thousands of MSI-CE-MS serum samples) to quantify speedup.

name: metabolomics-tool-category-mapping
description: Use when curating or ranking metabolomics software for a workflow: you need to place a tool into a data-type/functionality category, check whether it counts as 'most widely used' (≥50 Web of Science citations or Metabolomics Society survey use), or build structured claim records.

name: metabolomics-tool-comparison-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking LC-MS metabolomics feature-detection tools (asari vs XCMS vs MZmine) against certified/verified feature lists such as the 402 Thermo-verified features on HZV029, 314 Chen et al. certified features on Yeast2021, or 643 certified E. coli features.

name: metabolomics-tsne-dimension-reduction
description: Use when starting a differential metabolomic analysis in MetaboDiff and you need to check, before group comparisons, whether samples (e.g. tumor vs normal) separate metabolome-wide along the first two principal components.

name: metabolomics-univariate-group-comparison
description: Use when you have a normalized two-group or three-group metabolomics/proteomics feature table (e.g. POMA SummarizedExperiment from a preprocessed ST000284-style study) and need per-feature significance testing with multiple-testing correction.

name: metabolomics-validation-metric-compilation
description: Use when reproducing or auditing a published metabolomics tool's validation claims from per-compound supplementary tables of LC-MS/MS results, e.g. expected-feature detection, SIRIUS formula and CSI:FingerID annotation accuracy.

name: metabolomics-variance-adjustment
description: Use when clinical metabolomics matrices (e.g. log2-transformed lipid/metabolite features from GC-TOF MS or UPLC-QTOF MS) still show subject-specific variance and outliers after standard pre-processing, and normalization should account for patient metadata before downstream multivariate analysis.

name: metabolomics-violin-plot-visualization
description: Use when quality-controlling targeted LC-MS peak-area data: comparing per-batch distributions of QC samples, or evaluating pre- vs post-batch-correction variation before relying on corrected ratios.

name: metabolomics-weighted-meta-analysis
description: Use when combining results across metabolomics studies where raw data or standard deviations are unavailable, and only P-values, fold-changes, trend labels, and per-study sample sizes (n) are reported.

name: metabolomics-workbench-and-metabolights-data-retrieval
description: Use when a reproducibility, benchmarking, or reanalysis task cites public study accessions (ST* from Metabolomics Workbench, MTBLS* from MetaboLights) or Zenodo deposits and requires the raw MS1 LC/HRMS files, parameter spreadsheets, IPDBs, or MSI 1-3 annotation lists behind them.

name: metabolomics-workbench-data-acquisition
description: Use when a downstream analysis (network construction, partial-correlation estimation, differential network analysis) requires a real metabolomics dataset, and publicly available study data such as the TEDDY IA/T1D metabolomics measurements can be pulled from the Metabolomics Workbench.

name: metabolomics-workbench-data-retrieval
description: Use when a pipeline must fetch a metabolomics dataset (metabolite names/concentrations plus metadata) for a specific Metabolomics Workbench study ID (e.g. ST000915, ST001308, ST001140) as the entry point of an enrichment workflow.

name: metabolomics-workbench-data-retrieval
description: Use when an analysis needs the deposited ST003991 feature tables, m/z–RT paired entries, or per-drug metabolite annotations underlying PharmMet DB, e.g. to reproduce class-level or reaction-type counts from 1114 S9-incubated drugs.
tools: NIH Common Fund’s National Metabolomics Data Repository (Metabolomics Workbench), Study ID ST003991

name: metabolomics-workbench-data-retrieval
description: Use when a workflow needs to download specific study/analysis data from the Metabolomics Workbench REST interface (e.g. paired mwTab and JSON files for cross-format comparison) rather than manually browsing the site.

name: metabolomics-workbench-dataset-access
description: Use when a metabolomics analysis needs a publicly available example study — e.g. the ST000284 three-group or ST000336 two-group targeted metabolomics datasets — to feed POMAShiny/POMA workflows such as group-comparison tests or covariate-adjusted (ANCOVA/limma) comparisons.

name: metabolomics-workbench-dataset-reanalysis
description: Use when the goal is to retrieve and reanalyze a public Metabolomics Workbench lipidomics study (e.g. ST001111) in R with lipidr, performing differential or multivariate analysis on public lipid intensity data.

name: metabolomics-workbench-deposition-preparation
description: Use when raw MS or NMR experimental metadata sits in messy spreadsheets (Excel/CSV) and the goal is a Metabolomics Workbench deposition in mwTab format.

name: metabolomics-workbench-experiment-description-conformance
description: Use when tabular data has already been extracted into MESSES JSON and must be checked for conformance to the Experiment Description Specification and PD schema before mwTab conversion.

name: metabolomics-workbench-rest-batch-retrieval
description: Use when you need a complete, current inventory of Metabolomics Workbench analyses retrieved via REST (e.g. 1891 analyses at the 19 Nov 2020 snapshot) and per-format download/parse failure counts for curation or FAIRness assessment.

name: metabolomics-workflow-benchmark-reproduction
description: Use when you need to benchmark wall-clock run time of metabolomics normalization methods (e.g. tGAM vs TIGER/SERFF) across targeted and untargeted datasets under a fixed parallelization setting.

name: metabolomics-workflow-comparison
description: Use when comparing the structural complexity of two LC-MS metabolomics workflows — e.g. counting processes and user-facing configuration parameters from a Nextflow repo against a paper-reported baseline such as Metaboigniter's 20+ processes and 200+ parameters.

name: metabolomics-workflow-configuration
description: Use when setting up an untargeted LC-MS/MS processing run (raw or mzML inputs, blanks/QC present, positive or negative ionization) and you must decide which UmetaFlow steps to enable and how to list samples.

name: metabolomics-workflow-containerization
description: Use when an LC-MS metabolomics pipeline must chain MS-DIAL peak-table generation to MS-FLO quality filtering reproducibly, or when reproducibility in LC-MS data processing is compromised by uncontainerized downloadable tools like MS-DIAL, MZmine, or xcms.

name: metabolomics-workflow-execution
description: Use when processing raw nontargeted LC-MS data (mzML or Bruker .d) from acquisition to a grouped, ISF-annotated feature table, e.g. when reproducing adduct/ISF grouping counts on the Metabolome Atlas mouse-brain dataset.

name: metabolomics-workflow-step-classification
description: Use when curating or reproducing a catalogue of metabolomics R/Bioconductor packages that must be classified by workflow step (data processing, biostatistics, annotation/identification, network/pathway analysis) and repository (CRAN, Bioconductor, GitHub).

name: metabolomics-workflow-tool-mapping
description: Use when choosing or comparing metabolomics analysis toolkits: the input is textual tool inventories or feature lists from framework documentation/articles, and the goal is a structured overlap/unique-tool comparison rather than running the tools.

name: metabolomics-workstation-provisioning
description: Use when a clean Ubuntu 18.04 environment must be equipped with multiple untargeted metabolomics MS tools and manual per-tool dependency resolution is impractical; MetumpX automates this.

name: metabolomics-zero-intensity-imputation
description: Use when a peak intensity matrix (rows = peak features, columns = samples with a group line) contains zero values that must be imputed before log-2 transformation and pathway-activity scoring, and imputation must respect experimental factors.

name: metabolon-data-import
description: Use when the input is a Metabolon-platform metabolomics export (Excel worksheet such as 'OrigScale') that must be loaded into R as a Metaboprep object with sample/feature annotation before quality_control can be run.

name: metabonic-feature-clinical-variable-testing
description: Use when a SummarizedExperiment of metabolomic feature intensities plus clinical metadata (phenotype + confounders) must be screened feature-by-feature for phenotype associations with rank-based, confounder-adjusted statistics and FDR control.

name: metaboset-exprs-matrix-manipulation
description: Reference for when working with preprocessed LC-MS metabolomics data inside the notame R package and needing to extract, transform, or export the feature abundance matrix held by a MetaboSet object.

name: metaboset-object-data-handling
description: Use when loading or manipulating preprocessed LC-MS metabolomics data inside the notame workflow: constructing, reading, or passing a MetaboSet object (e.g. full_data.RData) through preprocessing or modeling steps.

name: metaboset-object-preprocessing
description: Use when starting from a preprocessed LC-MS metabolomics peak table (MS-DIAL Excel export) and you need a quality-controlled, drift-corrected, imputed feature-by-sample abundance matrix in R.

name: metacyc-pathway-curation
description: Use when building a PathModel input knowledge base from MetaCyc pathway entries, encoding metabolite structures and enzymatic reactions as ASP facts for pathway inference.

name: metadata-attribute-column-mapping
description: Use when a user must supply per-sample natural-language metadata for metabolomics submissions and needs a template CSV whose columns exactly match the selected sample types and attributes before SMetaS standardization.

name: metadata-augmented-compound-ranking
description: Use when ranking candidate structures retrieved from a spectral database against an experimental MS/MS spectrum and optional metadata (e.g. compound citation frequency) is available to boost identification accuracy beyond spectrum-only dot-product scoring.

name: metadata-category-header-processing
description: Use when freetext sample metadata strings (e.g., organism, cell line, tissue headers) must be mapped to constrained vocabulary terms via synonym matching and typographical fixing with n-grams/nearest neighbors.

name: metadata-conformant-peak-table-import
description: Use when raw tandem MS/MS data have already been preprocessed by a peak-picking tool (e.g. Progenesis) and you need to load the resulting peak table plus a sample-metadata file into R as an mpactr object before running filters.

name: metadata-curation-for-spectra
description: Use when a .msp mass spectral library file has records missing metadata such as SMILES, InChI, InChIKey, formula, or CAS number, and those identifiers must be fetched or derived before downstream annotation.

name: metadata-driven-point-recoloring
description: Use when a QIIME PCoA plot of beta-diversity ordination must be recolored or its points shown/hidden per arbitrary metadata column (categorical, gradient, or MIxS standard) for exploratory visual analysis of large microbial community datasets.

name: metadata-driven-sample-grouping
description: Use when an expression dataset carries sample metadata (organ, tumor/non-tumor status, disease stage) and analyses — correlation QC, Mann–Whitney U tests, outlier screening — must be stratified by biological condition rather than run across all samples pooled.

name: metadata-driven-visual-property-mapping
description: Use when a QIIME principal coordinates file and metadata mapping file must be rendered as a 3D PCoA plot whose sphere size, transparency, or coloring changes as a function of metadata categories (e.g. body site).

name: metadata-gradient-coloring-of-microbiome-plots
description: Use when you have a QIIME principal coordinates file plus a metadata mapping file (e.g., thousands of samples with dozens of columns) and need exploratory 3D ordination plots colored by a continuous metadata gradient or categorical variable.

name: metadata-ring-annotation
description: Use when you have a large phylogeny (thousands of leaf taxa, e.g., a 3,737-taxon PhyloPhlAn tree in PhyloXML format) plus per-leaf genome metadata (module presence/absence, continuous values like genome size) that must be overlaid as external rings on a circular cladogram.

name: metadata-stratified-sample-clustering
description: Use when a multi-batch untargeted metabolomics peak-area table (e.g., brain, serum, liver, cecal content, feces from 3xTg and 5xFAD mouse cohorts) must be checked for batch/cohort clustering before differential analysis is pooled across studies.

name: metadata-to-feature-mapping
description: Use when you have mzmine feature lists from .raw/.mzML flow injection acquisitions plus a cleaned metadata sheet and need to map each feature to its compound ID (e.g. to reproduce coverage counts like 30,008 unique molecules across ionization modes).

name: metadata-versus-peak-change-differentiation
description: Use when running a matchms SpectrumProcessor library-cleaning pipeline (e.g. on the GNPS public library) and you need a per-filter breakdown of how many spectra were deleted, had metadata changed, or had peak information changed.

name: metadata-vocabulary-extension
description: Use when a user has confirmed a freetext sample-metadata term that is absent from an existing SMetaS vocabulary and the tf-idf/nearest-neighbors matching models must be rebuilt to recognize it.

name: metadata-vocabulary-standardization
description: Use when sample metadata records contain inconsistent, freetext descriptor terms that must be mapped to fixed vocabularies before database integration, cross-study comparison, or ontological parent aggregation.

name: metadata-vocabulary-substring-matching
description: Use when a sample metadata table (e.g., a CSV of freetext fields like zeroTimeEvent, drugName, drugDoseUnit) contains non-numeric freetext strings that must be mapped to fixed, ontology-derived vocabularies for FAIR reuse.

name: metagene-gene-weight-inspection
description: Use when a PLAGE/SVD pathway activity result is significant (e.g. current vs never smokers, p < 0.0001) and you need to identify which pathway genes dominate the first metagene w by absolute weight ranking.

name: metagene-metasample-matrix-extraction
description: Use when a cancer omics dataset (e.g. transcriptome, methylome, proteome) must be decomposed into metagene and metasample components via ICA and the resulting matrices exported as artifacts.

name: metagene-reproducibility-assessment
description: Use when you must decide which matrix factorization method yields the most reproducible metagene/source signatures, by cross-comparing decompositions (ICA-vs-ICA, ICA-vs-PCA, ICA-vs-NMF, PCA-vs-NMF) of one shared data matrix.

name: metagenomic-abundance-table-conversion
description: Use when you have a taxonomy- or function-annotated abundance table (MetaPhlAn/LEfSe/HUMAnN text output or BIOM v1/v2 file, e.g. from QIIME or mothur 16S studies) and need GraPhlAn input files for circular visualization.

name: metagenomic-bgc-annotation
description: Use when you have assembled genomes or metagenomes (e.g., 40 cyanobacterial samples from the PoDP) and need annotated BGC GenBank files plus a BGC-BGC similarity matrix to link metabolites to gene clusters.

name: metagenomic-biomarker-visualization
description: Use when you have LEfSe biomarker results and a MetaPhlAn (or HUMAnN) abundance profile and need a publication-quality circular cladogram highlighting discriminatory taxa with metadata overlays.

name: metagenomic-functional-annotation
description: Use when you have shotgun metagenomics sequencing data (e.g. FASTQ from fecal samples) and need functional pathway enrichment comparisons between groups rather than only taxonomic composition.

name: metagenomic-gene-cluster-mining
description: Use when starting from microbial genome assemblies and needing predicted MGCs/BGCs reduced to representative GCFs as mapping targets for metagenomic or metatranscriptomic abundance analysis.

name: metagenomic-gene-prediction
description: Use when shotgun metagenomic reads or scaftigs (FASTA) lack gene annotations and gene coordinates are required as input for operon/proximon prediction (e.g. MetaRon 'ago' or 'op' mode).

name: metagenomic-profiler-versus-ground-truth-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking a taxonomic profiler against a known ground truth (e.g. CAMI marmgCAMI2_short_read_sample_0) and you need clade-level presence/absence discordance beyond F1 or UniFrac scores.

name: metagenomic-protein-database-construction
description: Use when analyzing metaproteomics tandem MS/MS spectra against metagenome-derived protein databases (metapeptide or non-redundant environmental FASTA), or when benchmarking database search vs de novo peptide-detection counts.

name: metagenomic-read-alignment-to-operons
description: Use when you have predicted operon sequences from metagenomic shotgun samples and raw paired-end reads, and need per-sample pathway/KO abundances to compare disease versus control groups.

name: metagenomic-read-mapping-abundance-profiling
description: Use when you have predicted MGC/BGC regions from antiSMASH/gutSMASH genomes plus shotgun metagenomic or metatranscriptomic reads (e.g., SRA accessions) and need RPKM abundance profiles and phenotype-differential cluster statistics.

name: metagenomic-read-simulation

name: metagenomic-sample-metadata-stratification
description: Use when a Qiita-deposited fecal shotgun metagenomics feature table (n=666 paired SPF fecal samples) with metadata fields genotype/study/sex/cohort must be subset (e.g., Sacrifice cohort, per-study) before PERMANOVA or beta-diversity testing.

name: metagenomic-scaffold-sequence-processing
description: Use when input is metagenomic shotgun data or pre-assembled scaftigs with gene predictions (.tab from Prodigal or MetaGeneMark) and the goal is de novo operon prediction without functional or experimental information.

name: metagenomic-short-read-assembly
description: Use when the input is unassembled paired-end shotgun FASTQ reads (e.g. Illumina HiSeq from SRA studies such as SRP029211 or SRP008047) and scaftigs must be generated before gene and operon prediction.

name: metagenomic-taxonomic-cladogram-visualization
description: Use when you need to visualize taxonomic biomarkers contrasting metagenomic cohorts (e.g., LEfSe output on MetaPhlAn profiles) as a compact circular cladogram with highlighted, sized, and colored clades.

name: metagenomic-taxonomic-profile-comparison
description: Use when two or more taxonomic profilers report identical or near-identical single-value metric scores (e.g., UniFrac) against a gold standard and you must determine whether their taxonomic profiles actually differ per taxon.

name: metagenomic-taxonomic-profile-conversion
description: Use when you have a LEfSe-format abundance matrix (from merged MetaPhlAn profiles) and/or a LEfSe biomarker result file and need to render them as a GraPhlAn circular phylogeny with clade-size and ring annotations.

name: metagenomic-taxonomy-tree-annotation
description: Use when you have a MetaPhlAn/LEfSe-style abundance table or a BIOM-format 16S table (e.g., from QIIME or mothur, such as a saliva microbiome profile) and need a compact circular taxonomy tree highlighting biomarker clades.

name: metal-adduct-fragmentation-analysis
description: Use when molecular networks contain ion variants annotated as [M+Na]+ (or other metal adducts) that fail to link to their [M+H]+ counterparts under conventional similarity-threshold networks, and you need to verify whether the connectivity method recovers the true metabolite relationship.

name: metaproteome-peptide-count-benchmarking
description: Use when asked to reproduce or compare peptide-detection counts for de novo vs database-search proteomics tools on metaproteomics spectra (e.g., Fig. 4a-b reference values) against metapeptide or environmental protein FASTA databases.

name: metaspace-annotation-cross-referencing
description: Use when annotating MALDI-MSI peaks by exact m/z (e.g. via METASPACE) and you need to test whether some annotated ions are actually matrix adducts like [M + (DHB-H2O) + H]+ or [M + DHB + Na]+ of other peaks in the same spectrum.

name: metatranscriptomic-expression-profiling
description: Use when metatranscriptomic (RNA-seq) reads from a microbiome cohort must be mapped against gutSMASH/antiSMASH-predicted gene cluster sequences to obtain per-sample MGC/GCF expression profiles and detect clusters differentially expressed between conditions (e.g. Crohn's disease vs healthy).

name: metcalf-co-occurrence-score-thresholding
description: Use when a paired genomics–metabolomics dataset (e.g. PoDP accessions MSV000084950, MSV000084771, or a Crüsemann et al. Streptomyces/Salinispora set) has been loaded into NPLinker and candidate BGC-GCF–to–spectrum links must be ranked and filtered by co-occurrence prior to class-based refinement.

name: metcalf-co-occurrence-scoring
description: Use when generating an initial set of candidate gene cluster family (GCF) to MS/MS spectrum links from paired genome–metabolome data before applying class-based filtering such as NPClassScore.

name: metcalf-strain-correlation-scoring
description: Use when linking AntiSMASH/BigScape-derived GCFs to GNPS molecular families by strain co-occurrence, or when raw Metcalf scores must be standardised against a null to compare links across GCFs and MFs of different sizes.

name: metfrag-annotation-score-averaging
description: Use when you have MetFrag candidate scores for each node in a spectral molecular network plus spectral cosine similarity between connected nodes, and you need to build a weighted graph for ChemWalker random-walk propagation.

name: metfrag-batch-input-configuration
description: Use when a validated compound list from HRMS suspect/target screening contains molecular formula and/or SMILES entries that must be converted into a MetFrag-consumable candidate file with computed precursor ion masses.

name: metfrag-commandline-batch-execution
description: Use when you need to score many tandem mass spectra against pre-retrieved candidate lists (e.g. SDF/PubChem snapshot SDFs for ~102 compounds) and compute candidate ranks in a scripted, reproducible batch run.

name: metfrag-scoring-weight-configuration
description: Use when ranking candidate structures from HR-MS/MS spectra with MetFrag2.2 and you need to set or verify the ωFrag, ωRT and ωRefs weights (summing to 1) against validation datasets.

name: metfusion-fusion-weight-function-implementation
description: Use when building the weighted molecular-network graph for ChemWalker propagation: you have MetFrag in silico fragmentation results for candidates of each network node, pairwise spectral cosine scores from library matching or network edges, and structural (chemical) similarity between candidate.

name: metfusion-weighted-graph-construction
description: Decision support for building a ChemWalker-style weighted graph when you have a spectral network plus in silico fragmentation candidate lists (MetFrag results) and need edge weights that fuse spectral and structural similarity before random-walk propagation.

name: method-coverage-count-computation
description: Use when a multi-platform metabolomics study reports a standards table with per-method detection flags (checkmark/cross plus RT/MT ± sd) and you must quantify how many metabolites each method or method combination covers.

name: method-parameterized-spectra-transformation
description: Use when a 1H-NMR spectra DataFrame (columns = chemical shifts in ppm, rows = samples) shows baseline distortions from incomplete relaxation, pulse sequence imperfections, magnetic field inhomogeneities, solvent effects, phase errors, or macromolecules.

name: methylation-probe-variability-filtering
description: Use when a buccal DNA methylation matrix (Infinium MethylationEPIC betas) must be reduced to its most variable autosomal probes as a preprocessing view for unsupervised multi-omics integration.

name: metid-databaseclass-object-construction
description: Use when you need to compile or extend a plant-specific MS1/MS2 annotation database from public spectral libraries (MoNA, MassBank, ReSpect, PlaSMA, NIST, GNPS) and MS1 sources (KEGG, KNApSAcK, PlantCyc) for use in MetMiner/tidyMass.

name: metid-identify-api-annotation

name: metmatch-alignment-configuration

name: metnet-command-line-execution
description: Use when two KEGG organisms must be automatically reconstructed and compared without GUI interaction, e.g. in batch pipelines or reproducible scripts, using MetNet's two-level representation.

name: metric-clustering-normalization
description: Use when multiple peak quality metrics computed on curated good/bad LC/MS peaks must be brought to a common scale, clustered across representative peaks, and ranked by maximum F-Score to identify which metrics are most discriminative.

name: metric-robustness-comparison-across-chromatogram-scenarios
description: Use when evaluating whether a chromatogram quality metric (e.g. MCQ, zigzag index, sharpness, SNR) is fair across EICs with high background signals, single-peak EICs, or zigzag-contaminated profiles, and you need an evidence-based robustness verdict per scenario.

name: mgf-and-tsv-benchmark-dataset-export

name: mgf-file-parsing
description: Use when you need per-dataset tandem mass spectrum counts from MGF files, e.g. to reproduce or verify a compareMS2 quality-control figure or sanity-check that MGF conversion preserved all spectra.

name: mgf-ms2-spectra-loading-and-filtering

name: mgf-msms-data-qc-validation
description: Use when preparing MGF files and feature tables from MZmine2 pre-processing as QIIME 2 artifacts, before compute-fragmentation-trees, and when checking that make-hierarchy outputs (rooted Phylogeny, filtered hashed table, feature data columns) are correctly formed.

name: mgf-msms-feature-import-qiime2
description: Use when starting a Qemistree/QIIME 2 metabolomics workflow with pre-processed LC-MS/MS feature data: you have an MGF file (MS1 + MS2 peaks) from feature detection and need it as a QIIME 2 artifact to run SIRIUS/ZODIAC/CSI:FingerID steps.

name: mgf-msp-library-format-conversion
description: Use when building an MS-DIAL identification library from multiple public tandem-MS sources in mixed formats (msp and mgf) that need polarity separation and structure-field harmonization.

name: mgf-spectra-export
description: Use when a Spectra::Spectra object has been filtered or normalized (e.g., via filterSpectriPy/normalize_intensities) and the resulting peak lists must be written out as an MGF file for storage or downstream annotation workflows.

name: mgf-spectra-export
description: Use when starting from Thermo RAW (or mzML/mzXML) LC-HRMS2 DDA files that must be converted into a feature quantification table plus per-feature MS2 .mgf spectra for each sample individually, before annotation or molecular networking.

name: mgf-spectra-file-handling
description: Use when LC-MS/MS acquisitions (e.g. serum or food/feed samples) are exported as MGF files and the goal is direct tandem-spectrum comparison — phylogenetics, species identification, or dataset QC — before any database search.

name: mgf-spectra-file-parsing
description: Use when an NPLinker-based integrative omics workflow needs MS/MS spectra read from a GNPS molecular networking MGF file, e.g. as the input for CANOPUS class prediction on spectra below 850 Da.

name: mgf-spectra-fragment-filtering
description: Use when assembling experimental MS/MS benchmarking sets from GNPS or third-party .mgf spectral libraries, and noisy, oversized, or adduct-mixed spectra must be normalized before annotation-tool evaluation.

name: mgf-spectra-handling

name: mgf-spectra-import

name: mgf-spectra-noise-filtering-and-preprocessing
description: Use when raw MGF tandem MS/MS spectra contain low-abundance noise peaks or crowded m/z regions and need deterministic cleaning (intensity and m/z cutoffs, 3-Da de-clustering) before pair-based spectral similarity modeling.

name: mgf-spectra-parsing
description: Use when you have MGF peak lists of tandem MS2 spectra (e.g. from ProteomeXchange PXD034932) and need pairwise spectral similarities or the compareMS2 set-level distance S/D between datasets.

name: mgf-spectra-reading
description: Use when the input is an MGF peak list file (e.g. iPRG2012.mgf) whose spectra must be loaded into Python for downstream processing or benchmarking with spectrum_utils, pymzML, or pyOpenMS.

name: mgf-spectral-data-handling

name: mgf-spectral-data-import

name: mgf-spectral-data-import
description: Use when the input is a .mgf file of MS/MS feature spectra (unique feature identifier, precursor m/z, m/z–intensity tuples) that must be loaded into Python and preprocessed before specXplore similarity or dashboard work.

name: mgf-spectral-file-preparation

name: mgf-spectral-file-processing

name: mgf-spectrum-batch-search
description: Use when you have a single .mgf file of consensus MS/MS spectra (e.g., from MZmine molecular networking) and need to determine which spectra match microbial metabolomes in GNPS/MassIVE-indexed data.

name: mgf-spectrum-field-parsing
description: Use when input is an MGF tandem mass spectrometry file whose spectra must be parsed into FIDDLE's required 'precursor_mz' and 'precursor_type' fields before candidate formula generation.

name: mgf-spectrum-import

name: mgf-spectrum-parsing
description: Use when tandem MS/MS data are provided as MGF peak lists (e.g. from a ProteomeXchange/PRIDE deposit such as PXD034932) and spectra must be read with precursor m/z for direct spectral comparison or parameter estimation.

name: mgf-spectrum-parsing

name: mgf-spectrum-parsing

name: mhc-class-i-immunopeptidomics-dataset-analysis

description: Use when you have a set of MIBiG BGC records with associated natural products and need to validate that a visualisation/prediction tool reproduces each annotated structure, or to systematically flag database records whose linked structure (e.

description: Use when building chemical-class-matching tables that bridge genome-based BGC classes (e.g. from MIBiG 2.0 JSON) to structure-based NPClassifier pathway terms for a BGC-metabolite linking analysis.

name: mibig-json-data-parsing
description: Use when you need structured MIBiG biosynthetic gene cluster annotations in machine-readable form — e.g. to count annotated compounds/A-domains, build substrate-SMILES maps, or harvest training data for ML predictors.

name: mibig-json-data-parsing
description: Use when a study needs MIBiG BGC entries as a structured reference set — e.g. assessing novelty of candidate BGCs, homology searches against known clusters, or pathway design inputs.

name: mibig-metadata-parsing
description: Use when building a validated ground-truth table of known BGC-spectrum pairs from MIBiG structural annotations and GNPS library spectra, e.g. to benchmark metabologenomic link scoring methods.

name: mibig-reference-cluster-group-curation

name: microarray-expression-data-processing

description: Use when a paired microbiome/metabolomics study needs a genotype- or treatment-level test of community composition from a compositional feature table (e.

description: Use when you need to render LEfSe biomarker results as a compact circular phylogenetic cladogram, e.g., highlighting taxonomic clades enriched in one cohort (HMP) versus another (MetaHIT) from MetaPhlAn taxonomic profiles.

name: microbiome-cutotype-stratification

name: microbiome-metabolome-integrative-analysis

name: minimum-cost-flow-network-construction

name: minimum-cost-flow-optimization
description: Use when you have 2D 1H,13C HSQC NMR spectra of a mixture (grid data or peak lists) and a compound library, and need to identify/quantify constituents without peak-picking the mixture spectrum.

name: minimum-cost-flow-spectral-fitting
description: Use when you need to identify and quantify compounds in 2D 1H,13C HSQC NMR mixture spectra against a compound library, especially when peak-picking the mixture is undesirable or peaks overlap/shift due to sample-matrix effects.

name: minimum-fraction-single-value-imputation
description: Use when a metabolomics feature table (e.g., the cancerCell demo dataset) contains NA/NaN intensities and simple single-value replacement — constant 1, 1/5 of the feature minimum, or column mean/median — is acceptable before downstream statistics.

name: minimum-intensity-scalar-imputation
description: Use when a pcpfm/Asari feature table (e.g. preferred_drop_missing TSV) contains missing entries after removal of uncommon features and the table must be complete for downstream statistical analysis.

name: minimum-shift-baseline-removal-implementation
description: Use when implementing or modifying the SAND adaptive binning stage on 1D high-resolution metabolomics NMR spectra and each binned region (nominal 0.002 ppm buckets) needs intensity offsets removed before raised-cosine banding and inverse Fourier processing.

name: minimum-spanning-tree-construction-over-spectra
description: Reference for constructing an MST over MS/MS spectra whose pairwise modified cosine similarity scores are known, when a deterministic ordering of spectra is needed for transitive peak alignment within a molecular network component.

name: minimum-spanning-tree-spectra-ordering
description: Use when you have a molecular network component's MS/MS spectra (GNPS2 task/component or USIs) and need a deterministic ordering for transitive multiple-spectrum alignment in MMSA.

name: minimum-spanning-tree-spectral-alignment
description: Use when a molecular networking component (a molecular family of related MS/MS spectra, e.g. ~80 rhamnolipid spectra or an albicidin analog family) needs its common fragments and modification-site shifts aligned across all members, beyond pairwise spectral comparison.

name: mipack-metabolite-annotation
description: Use when a processed, aligned peak list from the Galaxy-M DIMS SIM-stitch pipeline (calibrated m/z values with blank/replicate filtering already applied) needs metabolite annotation as the final analysis step of the workflow.

name: mirna-target-interaction-retrieval
description: Use when integrating miRNA data with other omics (genes, isoforms, proteins, lipids) in MOI and you need to annotate putative miRNA-mRNA regulatory connections among the loaded feature matrices before downstream analysis.

name: mirror-match-spectral-comparison
description: Use when an LC-MS/MS feature annotated against the GNPS Drug Library must be linked across sample contexts — e.g. confirming that an incubation-derived drug analog matches a fecal-sample feature — and when distinguishing true microbial transformation products from abiotic or ion-form artifacts.
tools: GNPS (Global Natural Product Social Molecular Networking)

name: mirror-plot-cosine-similarity-spectral-matching
description: Use when an experimental MS/MS spectrum must be compared against a spectral library match (or another dataset spectrum) and the deliverable is a publication-ready mirror plot with a quantified cosine similarity and highlighted matching peaks.

name: mirror-plot-spectrum-comparison
description: Use when two USI-resolvable tandem MS spectra (e.g. GNPS/MassBank/MassIVE library or task spectra) must be compared side-by-side, with matched peaks highlighted and a cosine similarity score for the pair.

name: mirror-plot-spectrum-visualization
description: Use when consensus/deconvolved MS2 spectra have been searched against reference databases and you need visual verification of top-scoring compound matches, or when compiling annotated features for a QC case study.

name: mirror-spectrum-plot-visualization
description: Use when two MS/MS spectra need to be compared visually (e.g. a library spectrum vs. an unknown query spectrum from GNPS), to assess peak-by-peak similarity, including annotated peptide fragment ions (a/b/y).

name: mis-injection-detection-from-is-areas
description: Use when reviewing targeted LC-MS metabolomics data from multiple batches and study samples must be screened for mis-injections or low/high total IS-area outliers before compound-level reporting and batch correction, with flagged samples excluded from further calculations.

name: misaligned-feature-truth-label-interpretation
description: Use when ncGTW has flagged potentially misaligned feature groups from XCMS output and you must decide which flagged features are genuine misalignments worth keeping, using CV improvement from ncGTW-guided peak-filling as the truth signal.

name: misalignment-detection-input-preparation
description: Use when raw LC-MS profiles (e.g. mzXML) must be preprocessed by XCMS into two grouping objects — one at large bw, one near RT sampling resolution — so ncGTW can detect misaligned features.

name: mispicked-ion-peak-merging
description: Use when a Progenesis-format peak table from LC-MS/MS pre-processing shows split isotope/adduct features, and you need to identify or merge mispicked ions before downstream blank/replicate filtering.

name: missed-atom-error-matrix-analysis
description: Use when comparing whether a formula-identification model trained on one instrument type (Q-TOF vs Orbitrap) generalizes to the other, using identical compound sets and per-formula missed-atom counts as the error metric.

name: missing-cleavage-site-detection
description: Use when annotating validated peptide-spectrum matches (e.g. MGF spectra from PRIDE/MassIVE with pseudo-ground-truth PSMs filtered at 1% FDR) to quantify missing fragment ions before evaluating de novo sequencing recall.

name: missing-data-tolerant-meta-analysis-computation
description: Use when combining published fold-changes and P-values across metabolomics studies that report only overall statistics (no raw data, error, or variance), with incomplete/missing values per compound.

name: missing-feature-perturbation-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing pathway-ranking methods (PLAGE/mPLAGE, ORA, GSEA) for robustness to missing peaks in metabolomics feature tables, by synthetically injecting known missingness levels (20/40/60/80%) over many seeded replicates.

name: missing-metabolite-abundance-filtering
description: Use when mapping metabolite identifiers to model identifiers (e.g. via metsEngroVsMetabolomics.csv) before computing mass-action-law substrate-product propensity scores, and you must decide which reactions can be scored given missing abundance measurements.

name: missing-observation-zero-padding
description: Use when per-dataset clusterings (label vectors c_m with K_m clusters each) cover different subsets of N observations and must be stacked into a single binary K̄×N matrix before Cluster-Of-Clusters Analysis.

name: missing-peak-apex-estimation
description: Use when XCMS peak-filling left a flagged feature undetected in one or more samples and the ncGTW realignment warping functions must supply an apex position and rigidly aligned peak boundaries for those missing peaks before results are handed back to XCMS.

name: missing-peak-classification-metabolomics
description: Use when a processed LC-HRMS feature/peak table (e.g. MZmine 2 aligned or unaligned csv output) must be assessed for which benchmark peaks are absent and why, as part of NPP reliability assessment.

name: missing-reaction-gap-flagging
description: Use when KEGG+RefSeq-derived organism-specific networks (e.g. Borrelia) leave activity without an annotated reaction — boundary fluxes indicate flux through a node pair absent from KEGG.

name: missing-reaction-table-annotation
description: Use when MINNO's boundary-flux analysis has produced a set of candidate missing reactions from KEGG and each candidate must be triaged into 'literature-supported' versus 'NCBI-RefSeq homology' evidence categories before network refinement.

name: missing-value-artificial-mask-generation
description: Use when you have one or more fully observed datasets (continuous, categorical, or mixed-type) and need controlled artificial missingness benchmarks to evaluate imputation methods against known ground truth.

name: missing-value-cutoff-application-metabolomics
description: Use when a metabolite-by-sample measurement table contains missing values and metabolites must be filtered by a missingness cutoff before imputation and downstream differential analysis.

name: missing-value-filtering-and-imputation
description: Use when preparing expert-inspected or DIA-NN-derived QC feature tables (with many NA entries across DIA files) for machine learning, before training the LC/MS qualified-vs-unqualified classifiers.

name: missing-value-filtering-metabolomics-intensities
description: Use when a metabolomics abundance table (e.g., a Metabolomics Workbench study retrieved with getmwstudies) contains missing intensity values that would break per-metabolite t-test/ANOVA computation before enrichment analysis.

name: missing-value-filtering-qc-thresholds
description: Use when a processed LC-MS feature table contains missing values and you must decide which features to drop before statistical analysis, following the tidyMass CRC case-study criteria.

name: missing-value-handling-in-harmonized-metabolite-tables
description: Use when assembling an InChIKey-keyed attribute table from CTS queries and some attributes come back empty — decide whether to record blanks or impute, and validate the table schema.

name: missing-value-imputation-and-normalization
description: Use when a preprocessed metabolomics peak-intensity/concentration matrix (CSV with a SampleID/group sample table) still contains missing values or batch/intensity artifacts and needs cleaning before statistical metabolite selection.

name: missing-value-imputation-config-comparison
description: Decision support for choosing a Sample Filtering threshold (x-out-of-n biological samples) in Galaxy-M pipelines and predicting whether Missing Values Imputation (e.g. KNN) will be needed downstream.

name: missing-value-imputation-feature-table
description: Use when a LC-MS feature table (e.g. preferred_drop_missing TSV) still contains missing values after removal of rare features and a complete table is required for downstream statistics or annotation.

name: missing-value-imputation-knn
description: Use when a metabolomics featuredata matrix (log-transformed peak intensities) still contains missing values that must be filled before normalization functions such as NormScaling can be run.

name: missing-value-imputation-method-comparison
description: Use when a cleaned LC-MS feature table (mass_dataset object) still contains missing values and you need to assess whether the choice of imputation method changes the differential-metabolite and pathway-enrichment conclusions between study groups.

name: missing-value-iterative-imputation
description: Use when an n x p data matrix contains missing values (e.g. 10-30% removed completely at random) mixing continuous and categorical variables, and non-linear relations or complex interactions are suspected.

name: missing-value-knn-imputation
description: Use when a metabolomics metabolite-by-sample matrix (e.g., plasma_breast_cancer.csv from Lilikoi) contains missing intensity values that must be filled before pathway transformation, feature selection, or machine learning classification.

name: missing-value-pattern-simulation
description: Use when augmenting MSI ion images for contrastive/self-supervised training and you need augmented views that mimic the missing-value artifacts of MS ion detection, as in DeepION's T_COL or T_ISO transforms.

name: missing-value-prefiltering-before-statistical-activities
description: Use when dispatching a statistical activity (t-test, U-test, ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis) or other computation onto a chart/column in Instant Clue and the underlying dataset may contain missing values that the activity cannot handle.

name: missing-value-probabilistic-pca-imputation
description: Use when a metabolomics abundance matrix (e.g., tomato pericarp metabolic profiles from seasons 2001, 2003, 2004) contains missing metabolite measurements that would corrupt downstream pairwise Pearson correlation computation.

name: missing-value-quantification-spatial-metabolomics
description: Use when a peak table matrix (pixels x m/z ion columns with X/Y coordinates) must be checked for missing/undetected signals before noise ion filtering or clustering, e.g. to validate a preprocessed AFADESI dataset's quality.

name: missing-value-ratio-computation
description: Use when a spatial metabolomics feature matrix (pixels × m/z ion intensities, e.g. 14,260 pixels × 3,044 ions) needs quality assessment of detection completeness, or when deciding which pixels/ions to retain before preprocessing.

name: missing-value-requantification-of-consensus-features
description: Use when an untargeted LC-MS/MS pre-processing consensus map contains consensus features with missing intensity values in some sample files, and complete quantification is needed for statistical analysis.

name: missing-value-versus-absent-data-handling
description: Use when a targeted MS-based metabolomics or lipidomics QCpool data set (Sciex MultiQuant txt exports) contains features that are absent in some QCpool injections, and you must decide whether to impute, flag, or drop them without losing relevant biological information.

name: missing-value-zero-fraction-filtering
description: Use when an LC/MS feature table (e.g. apLCMS or XCMS output on a dataset like ST000868) contains missing/zero values and a two-group comparison (e.g. cell-type t-test at FDR <= 0.2) requires removing sparse features before testing.

name: missing-versus-absent-data-discrimination
description: Use when a metabolomics intensity table contains features with intermittent missing signals and you must decide which are real zeros versus missing data before imputation or filtering.

name: missingness-based-sample-feature-exclusion
description: Use when raw un/targeted metabolomics sample-by-feature matrices (e.g. Metabolon or Nightingale exports) need preanalysis cleaning by dropping samples and metabolites above missingness thresholds before downstream analysis.

name: mixed-effects-metabolomics-data-processing
description: Use when clinical metabolomics data (e.g. GC-TOF MS or UPLC-QTOF MS feature tables, log2-transformed) contain subject-specific biological variation that should be modeled and removed prior to multivariate analyses such as PLS-DA/OPLS-DA.

name: mixed-gaussian-lorentzian-lineshape-fitting
description: Use when quantitative parameters (intensity, area, chemical shift, linewidth, J coupling constants) must be extracted from 1D or pseudo-2D NMR spectra of multiplets whose lineshape is neither purely Gaussian nor purely Lorentzian.

name: mixed-identifier-type-mapping
description: Use when a metabolomics meta-analysis input table mixes identifier types (common name, InChIKey, SMILES) for the same compounds, inflating unique-ID counts and masking duplicate votes across studies.

name: mixed-ionization-mode-feature-set-combination
description: Use when HRMS data were acquired in both positive and negative ionization modes and the goal is a single aligned feature table combining both polarities, rather than processing each mode independently.

name: mixed-model-based-delay-impact-prediction
description: Use when sample cohorts carry variable pre- and postcentrifugation processing delays and you need to predict, per metabolite (NMR-quantified serum/plasma), which concentrations shift and by how much before running downstream analyses.

name: mixed-type-categorical-dummy-coding
description: Use when benchmarking imputation methods on mixed-type or categorical-only data (e.g. the Children's Hospital data with 48 continuous and 76 categorical variables) and a numeric-only baseline such as KNNimpute must also handle categorical entries.

name: mixed-type-imputation-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing imputation methods on continuous-only, categorical-only, or mixed-type datasets with artificially introduced missing values (10%, 20%, 30% MCAR), to locate where missForest's relative error reduction over the strongest baseline is largest.

name: mixed-type-missing-value-imputation
description: Use when a data matrix mixes continuous and categorical variables (e.g. gene expression plus nominal annotations) and contains missing values needing imputation without parametric distributional assumptions.

name: mixed-type-variable-handling
description: Use when an n x p matrix with missing entries mixes continuous and categorical columns (e.g. gene expression plus binary/nominal traits) and a non-parametric, type-aware imputation is needed without test-set error estimation.

name: mixs-metadata-standards-handling
description: Use when you have a QIIME principal coordinates file plus a metadata mapping file with per-sample MIxS or GSC-standard columns and want to visually recolor or hide/show 3D PCoA points according to an arbitrary metadata category.

name: mixture-component-identification
description: Use when given one or more 1H NMR spectra of flavor mixtures (known or undisclosed compositions) and a pretrained FlavorFormer model, to produce per-spectrum component predictions and compute ACC, TPR, and FPR against a ground-truth formulation or standards library.

name: ml-based-source-apportionment-modeling

name: ml-benchmark-comparison-mass-spectrometry
description: Use when comparing a proposed deep learning model (e.g., MSMCE-ResNet50) against single-channel baselines and traditional ML classifiers (SVM, logistic regression, Random Forest, XGBoost) on binned, TIC-normalized MS data such as NSCLC spectra.

name: ml-classification-metric-evaluation
description: Use when you have an XCMS-derived feature table of extracted ion chromatogram peaks with expert Pass/Fail quality labels and need to select and benchmark a machine learning classifier that flags low-quality peak integrations.

name: mlp-peak-embedding-encoding
description: Use when MS/MS peak lists (m/z, intensity pairs) must be tokenized into variable-length per-peak embeddings so that a downstream generator can attend to individual peaks via cross-attention rather than to a pooled spectrum vector.

name: mmd-loss-batch-correction
description: Use when integrating joint ST/SM spot-level AnnData across multiple samples (e.g. human ccRCC, GBM, mouse brain) and batch effects from different samples must be corrected within a CVAE latent space rather than by feature-level scaling.

name: mmff-conformer-minimization
description: Use when preparing 3D molecular structures for CCS or other geometry-dependent ML prediction: after ETKDG conformer generation and before converting SMILES-derived molecules into graph matrices.

name: mnar-half-minimum-imputation
description: Use when a metabolomics concentration table (.csv/.xlsx) contains missing peak values that cluster within whole groups per metabolite — indicating values below the detection limit (MNAR) — and those values should be filled with zero or half the minimum observed concentration.

name: mnar-mar-missingness-injection
description: Decision support for benchmarking imputation methods on complete metabolomics matrices when you need missing values reflecting both MNAR (below-LOD) and MAR mechanisms, e.g. 15% missingness with more MNAR than MAR.

name: mnar-mar-missingness-mechanism-simulation
description: Decision support for comparing imputation methods when missing values may arise from MNAR (metabolite below detection limit) and/or MAR (technical issues), and controlled simulations are needed to separate mechanism effects.

name: mnar-missing-data-evaluation
description: Use when complete (pre-missingness) metabolomics data plus group labels are available and several MNAR imputation methods must be ranked by how well they preserve univariate and supervised multivariate group-difference structure.

name: mnar-missing-data-simulation
description: Use when you have a complete (or near-complete) metabolomics data matrix, e.g. data_sim.csv or real_data.csv, and need to simulate left-censored MNAR missingness to evaluate imputation accuracy, distribution preservation, or statistical sensitivity.

name: mnar-vs-mar-missingness-classification

name: mnv-normalization-and-repeat-shifting

name: mnxref-identifier-translation

name: mobile-phase-constraint-validation

name: mobile-phase-score-computation

name: modality-contribution-angular-similarity-analysis

name: modality-contribution-interpretation

name: modality-weighted-spatial-clustering

name: model-sequence-composition-with-plus-operator

name: model-training-time-benchmarking
description: Use when deciding whether to merge multi-collision-energy MS/MS spectra before CNN training, by comparing wall-clock epoch times between spectral-representation variants.

name: modification-site-edge-counting

name: modification-site-likelihood-distribution-interpretation
description: Use when a ModiFinder prediction has produced a per-atom likelihood array Ω for the known compound and you need to collapse it into a single evaluation score that rewards peaked, site-concentrated distributions over diffuse, ambiguous ones.

name: modification-site-likelihood-scoring

name: modification-tolerant-spectral-library-search

name: molecular-mass-filtering

name: molecular-mass-mz-consistency-checking
description: Use when curating a CCS or metabolomics reference table where each row carries a structure identifier (InChI/SMILES), an adduct type, a listed theoretical m/z, and an m/z tolerance window for structural validation.

name: molecular-network-analog-prioritization
description: Use when a molecular network (e.g., GNPS) contains an unannotated node adjacent to library hits of a related metabolite, and the structural site of modification between the analogs must be localized from MS/MS spectra.

name: molecular-network-annotation-propagation
description: Use when you have GNPS molecular networking outputs (edges and annotated spectra/MGF tables) and want to label nodes and edges with chemical class or MS2LDA Mass2Motif information to interpret network organization.

name: molecular-network-annotation-propagation
description: Use when you have a GNPS-style molecular network with per-spectrum candidate annotations and sparse spectral library matches (e.g. only ~10% seed nodes) and need annotations on nodes without any library match.
tools: GNPS (Global Natural Products Social Molecular Networking)

name: molecular-network-chemical-class-annotation
description: Use when you have a GNPS molecular networking output (classical or feature-based) plus SMILES annotations (library hits, NAP, DEREPLICATOR) and want ClassyFire chemical class labels mapped onto the network graph.

name: molecular-network-cluster-consistency-reweighting
description: Use when candidate MS2 annotation lists (e.g., ISDB-LOTUS spectral matches) need to be reweighted using the chemical consistency of the molecular-network cluster a feature belongs to.

name: molecular-network-cluster-visualization
description: Use when a set of identified spectra (PSMs/compound–spectrum matches) must be expanded to related spectra via GNPS molecular network clusters, with variants grouped into families and rendered as network graphs.

name: molecular-network-component-analysis
description: Use when a GNPS molecular network component (e.g. a 21-spectra cluster) contains unknown spectra that pairwise similarity alone cannot structurally explain, and you want the mined fragmentation pattern with highest support and precision over that component.

name: molecular-network-construction
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS data (mzXML/mzML) must be organized into a molecular network to group related spectra, detect analog mass shifts (e.g. -41 Da stenothricin analogs), or dereplicate known metabolites.

name: molecular-network-construction
description: Use when building molecular networks from clustered LC–MS/MS consensus spectra (per-sample MGF files) to represent ionization variants of the same precursor as one [M+H]+ ion entity for dereplication and bioactivity ranking.

name: molecular-network-construction
description: Use when you have a large extract library (e.g., thousands of MGF MS/MS spectra) and want to cluster spectra into molecular families using a learned spectral similarity (TransExION) instead of GNPS cosine networking.

name: molecular-network-construction-from-similarity-scores
description: Use when you have all-pairs spectral similarity scores (Spec2Vec, cosine, or modified cosine) over a positive-ionization MS/MS dataset and want to cluster spectra into molecular networks whose edges reflect structural (Tanimoto) similarity.

name: molecular-network-construction-ms2-spectra
description: Use when a differential LC/MS feature table plus centroided MS/MS raw data are available and structurally related differential features need to be grouped by MS2 spectral similarity into subnetworks for class-level annotation.

name: molecular-network-edge-filtering
