description: Use when preparing a filtered .mgf input for microbeMASST batch search from a deposited GNPS molecular networking job, and you need spectra unique to one condition (e.g. SPF) excluding GF-linked spectra.

name: molecular-network-edge-filtering
description: Use when you have a full pairwise MS2DeepScore similarity matrix over spectra from both ionization modes and need to build a sparse, Cytoscape-ready molecular network of cross- and within-mode clusters.

name: molecular-network-edge-redirect-deduplication
description: Use when you have an IIMN graphml with many ion-species nodes sharing a common IIN ID (adducts/isotopes/in-source fragments of one compound) and need a collapsed molecular-node network without redundant edges.

name: molecular-network-graph-construction
description: Use when a molecular network's spectral library matches need candidate-structure-aware edge weights before random-walk annotation propagation, and MetFrag candidate scores plus cosine similarities are available.

name: molecular-network-graphml-export
description: Use when a GNPS molecular networking job on deconvoluted EI GC-MS spectra (or MS2-based GNPS networks) has finished and you need the graphml network file to map Mass2Motifs/chemical classes and visualize in Cytoscape.

name: molecular-network-mass2motif-mapping
description: Use when a GNPS molecular network job output and an ms2lda.org LDA experiment summary (Mass2Motif probability/overlap scores) are available and the goal is to attach shared-substructure (Mass2Motif) annotations per node and per molecular family.

name: molecular-network-modularity-computation
description: Use when you have MCN network structures (from molecular_communities repository outputs) for LC-MS/MS or EI GC-MS datasets and need to quantify community structure via modularity and power-law degree behavior.

name: molecular-network-motif-annotation
description: Use when you have both a GNPS molecular networking job output and an MS2LDA experiment summary (motif-document probabilities and overlap relations) and need to annotate network nodes and edges with shared Mass2Motifs for Cytoscape visualization.

name: molecular-network-node-annotation-mapping
description: Use when a GNPS molecular network has node-level structural annotations (SMILES from GNPS library hits, NAP, or DEREPLICATOR) and you need per-family chemical class consensus scores across the ClassyFire ontology.

name: molecular-network-visualization
description: Use when an LC-MS/MS feature-based molecular network from GNPS needs to be visualized with bioactivity (or other node-level attribute) overlays to prioritize candidate molecules.

name: molecular-network-visualization
description: Reference for inspecting the NP3 MS Workflow step-10 filtered SSMN in Cytoscape after clustering, cleaning, IVAMN [M+H]+ selection, and damped pruning have produced the final molecular network.
tools: GNPS (Global Natural Products Social Molecular Networking)

name: molecular-network-visualization-preparation
description: Use when a spin system correlation/similarity matrix from MADByTE's correlation_matrix_generation step must be converted into network graph edges, pruned, and exported as graphML for Gephi visualization.

name: molecular-network-vs-pattern-occurrence-comparison
description: Use when MS/MS spectra suspected to share a structural motif (e.g. a common neutral loss such as tryptophan loss 186.079) are NOT all connected in a GNPS molecular network and you need a graph-pattern-based similarity check.

name: molecular-networking-annotation-rate-evaluation
description: Use when you have a molecular network–derived set of anchor–suspect spectrum pairs with known SMILES for anchors, and you need to quantify how many suspects a rule-based annotator correctly recovers.

name: molecular-networking-dereplication
description: Use when LC-MS/MS data of a bioactive fractionated natural extract is available (feature quantification table plus per-fraction bioassay values) and the goal is to dereplicate molecules via molecular networking and highlight bioactive candidates prior to isolation.

name: molecular-networking-family-spectra-extraction
description: Use when an analysis needs the complete set of MS/MS spectra belonging to one molecular networking component (Task ID + component number, or a list of USIs) as input to multiple spectral alignment rather than single-spectrum inspection.

name: molecular-networking-fbmn-annotation
description: Use when you have MZmine-exported feature quantification tables (.csv) and .mgf fragmentation spectra — especially ions present only in a scheduled precursor list and never fragmented by DDA — that need multi-level annotation.

name: molecular-networking-genome-mining-integration
description: Use when validated BGC–metabolite links must be scored or benchmarked — e.g. PoDP JSON metadata with MIBiG IDs, MS/MS URLs (GNPS-MassIVE or MetaboLights), and genome labels are available and a candidate link ranking is needed.

name: molecular-networking-input-preparation
description: Use when MSHub deconvolution output (per-compound fragmentation/abundance table) must be annotated with balance scores and filtered before being used as GNPS molecular networking input.

name: molecular-networking-link-verification
description: Use when validating an MCN molecular network against a conventional similarity-threshold network by checking whether specific ion pairs (e.g. [M+Na]+/[M+H]+ adduct variants of the same metabolite) are connected only in the MCN graph.

name: molecular-networking-node-classification
description: Use when you have a GNPS feature-based molecular networking job (Node_info.tsv), CANOPUS in silico class predictions (canopus_summary.tsv), and spectral library match data, and need consensus chemical class annotations for ion features across subnetworks.

name: molecular-networking-subnetwork-propagation
description: Use when you have GNPS feature-based molecular networking output plus a CANOPUS canopus_summary.tsv and node info with library spectral matches, and need to propagate chemical class annotations to unannotated subnetwork members.

name: molecular-property-regression-from-spectra
description: Use when raw MS/MS peak lists must be converted to continuous molecular property values (e.g. QED, synthetic accessibility, Bertz complexity) and spectrum-to-structure reference libraries are unavailable.

name: molecular-representation-training-cross-validation
description: Use when comparing candidate molecular representations (RDKit-normalized descriptors, Morgan counts, D-MPNN, hybrid embeddings) for retention-order prediction, via 5-fold cross-validation on a reference training set followed by independent-dataset generalizability testing.

name: molecular-smiles-feature-preparation
description: Use when raw SMILES strings and adduct labels ([M+H]+, [M+Na]+, [M-H]-) must be transformed into graph representations (node, adjacency, edge matrices or adduct graphs) with 3D coordinates before training or evaluating GNN CCS prediction models.

name: molecular-species-submatrix-extraction
description: Use when a lipidomic intensity matrix needs to be reduced to the molecular-species (LMS) level before LipidOne 2.0 statistical or pathway analysis and it still contains missing or '0' entries that must be imputed per-row.

name: molecular-species-to-chain-decomposition
description: Use when a molecular-species intensity matrix (row IDs like 'PC 16:0_18:1') must be converted to chain-level building-block rows for statistical or pathway analysis at the LBB level.

name: molecular-structural-similarity-networking
description: Use when a metabolomic dataset (e.g. GC-TOF-MS feature table with BinBase identifiers) contains metabolites with no known biochemical intermediates or missing KEGG annotations, producing sparse disconnected biochemical networks that need structural edges.

name: molecular-structure-candidate-ranking
description: Use when a preprocessed low-resolution GC-EI-MS spectrum (intensity-binned, threshold-filtered, m/z ≤ 500, ≤ 300 peaks) must be translated de novo into a ranked list of candidate SMILES structures without a reference database.

name: molecular-structure-clustering-visualization
description: Use when you need to demonstrate that graph-neural-network-learned molecular representations (e.g., 16-dim pooled node attributes) reflect chemical structure, by visualizing their 2D UMAP embedding colored by ring number or molecular class.

name: molecular-structure-database-search
description: Use when you have tandem mass spectra (e.g., positive-mode [M+H]+) whose true structures are absent from spectral libraries and you must search them against a large molecular structure database (LMSD, PubChem, DNP).

name: molecular-structure-feature-augmentation
description: Use when a per-MZ-position peak classifier built on 2D-only molecular embeddings (mol2vec or graph features) underperforms and you want to test whether 3D conformer-derived structure features lift per-bin F1.

name: molecular-structure-filtering-by-mass-and-elements
description: Use when preparing large molecular structure databases (SDF/SMILES) as inputs for in-silico EI-MS spectrum prediction, and unreasonable molecules (heavy, exotic-element, ionic, high-LogP, or duplicate structures) must be excluded first.

name: molecular-structure-fingerprinting
description: Use when you need to test whether per-compound spectral prediction accuracy depends on how structurally similar each test compound is to the training set, e.g. via maximum Bulk Tanimoto similarity on RDKit fingerprints.

name: molecular-structure-generation-from-spectra
description: Use when you need de novo small-molecule structure candidates from unannotated tandem mass spectra, conditioned on chemical formula metadata, without a reference spectral library — e.g. MassSpecGym or NPLIB1-style test folds.

name: molecular-structure-representation-translation
description: Use when you have four MS/MS spectra files ([M+H]+ and [M-H]- at 35% and 130% NCE) with spectra embeddings and need de-novo SMILES structures reconstructed by a pre-trained decoder.

name: molecular-topology-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when you have generated candidate molecules (2D topology from a diffusion or generative model) paired with known reference structures and need to quantify exact-match and similarity-based elucidation accuracy.

name: molecular-trait-functional-diversity-calculation
description: Use when a sum-normalized FT-ICR MS peak table with assigned molecular formulas must be summarized as per-sample functional diversity (Rao's Q) grouped by experimental conditions such as phage treatment or incubation condition.

name: molecular-variant-mass-shift-annotation
description: Use when a GNPS-format mass spectral dataset (MGF/mzXML/mzML) has been searched with VInSMoC variable mode and the goal is to explain precursor-vs-molecule mass differences as known chemical mass shifts and quantify FDR across score thresholds.

name: molecular-vs-pathway-level-model-comparison
description: Use when you must decide whether pathway transformation before multi-omics integration (ssPA + MB-PLS) degrades predictive performance relative to modelling raw molecule abundances, e.g. on COPDgene plasma metabolomics/proteomics/transcriptomics.

name: molecular-weight-and-metal-atom-filtering
description: Use when a chemical list is about to be processed with fragment- or descriptor-based QSAR models (e.g., IFS biotransformation half-life prediction) and must first be screened for metals or MW > 1,000.

name: molecular-weight-descriptor-calculation
description: Reference for building the seven one-dimensional feature vectors that Mol2CCS feeds alongside the 3-D molecular graph, when SMILES, adduct and instrument metadata are available per record.

name: molecular-weight-descriptor-calculation
description: Reference for quantifying whether two molecular benchmark sets differ in structural complexity via the Ertl-Schuffenhauer synthetic accessibility score and molecular weight.

name: molecular-weight-regression-scoring
description: Use when a 1H-13C HSQC spectrum (normal or multiplicity-edited) must yield a predicted molecular weight via DeepSAT's pretrained CNN regression head, and the result must be validated against the paper's R-squared benchmarks.

name: molecule-frequency-ranking
description: Use when a generative model (e.g. DiffMS's graph diffusion decoder) outputs many sampled molecular structures per mass spectrum and you need a deterministic ranked candidate list for top-k (k=1,10) elucidation evaluation.

name: molecule-gcf-pair-tail-validation
description: Use when binary presence/absence GCF and ion tables from 363 strains have been correlated and you must validate that known molecule–GCF pairs (e.g. 9 detoxin/rimosamide-type pairs) rank in the rightmost tail, or choose between BiG-SCAPE mode/cutoff settings.

name: molecule-graph-preprocessing
description: Use when a RASSP pipeline stage (forward_train.py, forward_evaluate_pipeline.py, run_rassp.py) needs molecules converted from parquet columns (inchi, smiles, rdmol blobs) into per-atom feature matrices, adjacency matrices, enumerated subformulae/subsets, and power-scaled spectra tensors.

name: molecule-identifier-mapping-to-pathway-databases
description: Use when molecular abundance matrices (e.g. metabolite names, ChEBI, UniProt or ENSEMBL columns) must be converted to the identifier vocabulary of a pathway database (Reactome, KEGG, PathBank) before ssPA scoring or any pathway-based multi-omics integration.

name: molecule-level-data-partitioning
description: Use when training or benchmarking spectral similarity/spectrum embedding models on GNPS-derived spectra (e.g. 210,407 spectra, 184,698 annotated) and spectrum-level splits would leak identical molecules across train and test.

name: molecule-provenance-based-subset-selection
description: Use when a merged multi-source chemical collection contains a source whose entries need an extra QC gate, and the subset must first be isolated by provenance (present only in that one source) before applying per-molecule property filters.

name: molecule-search-space-magnitude-estimation
description: Use when explaining size-dependent accuracy trends in structure prediction: accuracy is tabulated by heavy-atom bin and needs to be juxtaposed against the combinatorial molecule-count growth at that size.

name: molecule-structure-decoding-selfies
description: Use when a generative model outputs molecule representations as SELFIES token sequences (possibly beam-sampled) and you must convert them to valid SMILES, then score Top-1/Top-10 accuracy by InChIKey, minimum MCES distance, and maximum Tanimoto similarity.

name: molecule-structure-enumeration
description: Use when you have an annotated anchor molecule (SMILES) paired with an unannotated suspect via a precursor mass difference, and need candidate structures ranked by biotransformation likelihood.

name: molecule-substructure-search-implementation
description: Use when building a chemical search backend on a non-relational store (e.g. MongoDB) and you need exact substructure matching over large molecule collections without a dedicated cheminformatics search engine.

name: molfile-structure-parsing
description: Use when a curated compound database (e.g. a .xlsx of DNA adducts) must be populated or validated with SMILES/InChI/InChIKey from structure files, or when regenerating identifiers from deposited .mol files for entry-by-entry comparison.

name: mona-spectral-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when a study requires the openly deposited mass spectra used to develop and validate SPLASH identifiers, e.g. to regenerate SPLASHes or reproduce the 53.25-million-spectrum hash-collision test.

name: monascore-cutoff-classification
description: Use when a pre-processed feature table from patRoon or MS-DIAL needs annotation confidence levels (Schymanski scheme) assigned per feature, or when annotations must be graded before downstream QC filtering/statistics.

name: mongo-database-result-storage
description: Use when Pickaxe expansion runs must be persisted as compounds/reactions in a database (rather than .tsv files) and later queried to tabulate per-database counts for validation against published results.

name: mongodb-bitwise-query-filtering
description: Use when a molecule collection is stored in MongoDB and you need to answer substructure queries by filtering on precomputed fingerprint bits, then confirming candidates with graph pattern matching.

name: mongodb-compound-database-querying
description: Use when a Pickaxe network expansion (e.g. two-generation EcoCyc expansion with top 50 JN1224min rules) has stored its generated compounds and reactions in MongoDB and you must quantify per-filter annotation counts.

name: mongodb-network-results-storage
description: Use when running Pickaxe network expansions (e.g. YMDB one-generation expansion with top 500 JN1224min rules) whose results must be persisted in a database for downstream analysis notebooks instead of flat files.

name: mongodb-reaction-network-querying
description: Reference for practitioners whose Pickaxe network-expansion run has written results into a MongoDB collection and who need to load, query, or iterate those reactions/compounds in Python for downstream analysis or filtering.

name: monoisotopic-basepeak-assignment
description: Use when an XCMS-derived feature table already contains putatively labeled features (PuInc_seeker output) and each labeled feature needs a monoisotopic base peak assigned before adduct/database queries.

name: monoisotopic-exact-mass-calculation
description: Use when you need theoretical monoisotopic masses or isotope distributions (M, M+1, M+2) for element-count molecular formulas (e.g., C3H8O2) in MS method development or adduct m/z prediction.

name: monoisotopic-mass-calculation
description: Use when enumerating formula candidates from elemental compositions (e.g., a 16-element ECS of C, H, As, B, Br, Cl, F, I, K, N, Na, O, P, S, Se, Si) and monoisotopic masses must be recorded per candidate to build or reuse an IPDB for LC/HRMS formula annotation.

name: monoisotopic-mass-calculation
description: Use when a fragment set from a bond-breaking DAG must be converted to predicted peak masses — enumerate formulae {f_n^{-j},...,f_n^{j}} per fragment and compute exact monoisotopic masses for spectrum construction or formula annotation.

name: monoisotopic-mass-calculation
description: Use when you need theoretical monoisotopic masses for B/Y/internal glycan fragments of a new N-linked glycan not already in a database, to support MS1/MS2 peak identification from LC-MS/MS data.

name: monoisotopic-mass-calculation
description: Use when a fragment-tree or de novo method predicts candidate molecular formulas and you must verify them against independently measured high-resolution MS m/z values using a sub-0.01 Da mass-error criterion.

name: monoisotopic-mass-calculation
description: Use when compiling a DNA adduct database or mass spectral library and you need charged monoisotopic masses for adduct ions, including deoxyribose-loss fragments, from molecular formulas.

name: monoisotopic-mass-computation-for-metabolites
description: Use when a differential MS1 feature table contains dysregulated m/z peaks, no reference-standard spectra are available, and a library of parent structures plus biotransformation reaction rules can be exploited to compute theoretical candidate masses for preannotation.

name: monoisotopic-mass-computation-from-structure
description: Use when you need to verify or predict the theoretical m/z of a derivatized metabolite from its chemical structure — e.g., confirming that Met-ID hits for FMP-10-derivatized dopamine (1A, 2A, 2B) correspond to expected [M+H]+ ions within a 5 ppm mass-error window.

name: monoisotopic-mass-conversion-from-mz
description: Use when LC-MS/MS precursor or fragment m/z values must be converted to neutral monoisotopic masses before formula enumeration or adduct-aware mass matching (as FSA does against PubChem-derived formula lists).

name: monoisotopic-mass-conversion-with-adduct-correction
description: Use when raw MS/MS spectra (e.g. centroided with msconvert) must be cleaned before formula ranking: m/z peaks need adduct-corrected monoisotopic mass conversion and spurious fragment removal prior to feeding FSA.

name: monoisotopic-mass-range-computation
description: Use when building or auditing a DNA adduct reference database and you need to verify the monoisotopic mass span of its entries, or when you need to confirm a newly added set of potential adducts does not change the reported mass range.

name: monoisotopic-mass-uniqueness-filtering
description: Use when converting MSFragger/FragPipe PSM results into a confident MALDI-MSI peptide imaging list: peptides with non-unique monoisotopic masses cannot be distinguished in an untargeted MS image and must be dropped before mapping peptides to proteins.

name: monoisotopic-parent-mass-computation
description: Use when spectra carry a structure annotation plus adduct and precursor m/z but the parent mass may be wrong (e.

name: monoisotopic-peak-identification-by-intensity-stepping
description: Use when a target feature in an AIF LC-MS feature table may be an isotopologue rather than the monoisotopic mass, i.e. before running the fragment-library candidate search on m/z that must first be corrected to M+0.

name: monte-carlo-dropout-inference
description: Use when MS2DeepScore Tanimoto predictions must carry per-pair uncertainty, or when uncertain predictions need to be filtered out to lower RMSE at the cost of retrieval rate.

name: monte-carlo-false-discovery-rate-evaluation
description: Use when validating that a reproducibility-detection procedure (e.g., MaRR) controls the False Discovery Rate at a nominal level (e.g., 0.05), and when quantifying discriminative power and bias of an estimated signal proportion over many simulated replicates.

name: monte-carlo-missingness-simulation
description: Use when you have complete reference datasets with known values and need to quantify imputation error (NRMSE/PFC) by injecting artificial missingness completely at random at 10–30% rates, or to check whether a method's internal error estimate tracks the true imputation error.

name: monte-carlo-null-distribution-sampling
description: Use when testing whether the Pearson correlation between two fluorescence channels (e.g., CFP/YFP or red/green from a Zeiss LSM 510) exceeds random overlap, and adjacent pixel intensities are spatially correlated by texture or the PSF so pixel-level scrambling would be invalid.

name: monte-carlo-pvalue-aggregation
description: Use when benchmarking how robustly ORA, mPLAGE, and GSEA rank a known-significant pathway under synthetic noise — e.g. decoy features injected at 0%–1000% levels in a PALS-format peak-intensity and KEGG annotation matrix.

name: monte-carlo-rank-data-simulation
description: Use when validating or benchmarking reproducibility procedures (MaRR, copula mixture model) on synthetic replicate data where ground truth pi1 and r0 are known and empirical FDR/power must be measured.

name: monte-carlo-replicate-aggregation
description: Use when a simulation step contains randomisation — such as randomly selecting f% of compounds for isobaric or identical-formula replacement — and the resulting metric (e.g. pathway loss/gain rate) must be reported with a stable central estimate and uncertainty.

name: monte-carlo-replicate-dataset-averaging
description: Use when you have computed (noise-free) relative isotopologue intensities from a moiety model (single 13C tracer or 13C/18O multi-tracer) and need to quantify how additive measurement error at multiple sigma levels propagates into summed isotopologue totals prior to renormalization.

name: monte-carlo-resampling-analysis
description: Use when you have raw mass-spectrometry samples (e.g. MTBLS157 culture data) and need to determine how many samples are required for stable AutoTuner parameter estimates, via CV-vs-sample-size resampling.

name: monte-carlo-result-aggregation
description: Use when a simulation study produces per-replicate, per-pathway test calls (e.g., NetGSA REHE vs REML power runs) and you need per-method empirical power estimated across replicates and summarized as mean +/- SE within defined effect-size bins.

name: monte-carlo-simulation-study-design
description: Use when validating that a proposed statistical test (e.g., a kernel score test) maintains nominal size, by estimating empirical type I error rates via Monte Carlo replication under simulated null data.

name: morgan-fingerprint-bit-decoding
description: Use when the goal is to turn raw 1H-13C HSQC peak lists (normal or multiplicity-edited) into a machine-comparable structural fingerprint (6144-bit Morgan string, radius 0-2) plus molecular weight and superclass probabilities for library-wide similarity searching.

name: morgan-fingerprint-computation
description: Use when building a large-scale pretraining corpus of fingerprint–molecule pairs from unlabeled molecules (e.g. MassSpecGym's 4M molecules), or when spectra must be converted into an experimental-condition-invariant token representation.

name: morgan-fingerprint-computation
description: Use when you have multiple structural annotations per MS/MS feature from several tools and need to quantify structural consensus between tool pairs via Tanimoto similarity for downstream prioritization.

name: morgan-fingerprint-encoder-training
description: Use when preprocessing MassSpecGym spectra/candidate files into fingerprint training inputs and training a fingerprint-view encoder inside a multiview contrastive (CMC-style) model for molecule–spectrum retrieval.

name: morgan-fingerprint-encoding
description: Use when a deep-learning RT-prediction model requires a fixed-length substructure descriptor for each molecule — e.g. to complement a molecular-graph encoder with the 2048D Morgan fingerprint stream described in the RT-Transformer pipeline.

name: morgan-fingerprint-generation
description: Use when ranked structural candidate lists (SMILES) must be scored against ground-truth SMILES for GC-EI-MS spectra, and you need top-k accuracy or SpecTUS-vs-database-search win rates via Morgan-fingerprint Tanimoto similarity.

name: morgan-fingerprint-generation
description: Use when you have a predicted Morgan fingerprint bit string from a DeepSAT HSQC prediction and need to retrieve, rank, and annotate candidate molecular structures from databases like PubChem by fingerprint cosine similarity.

name: morgan-fingerprint-prediction-from-msms
description: Use when raw tandem MS/MS spectra must be converted to 4,096-bit Morgan fingerprints for molecular-structure retrieval from PubChem, or when benchmarking fingerprint-based retrieval against MIST on the CANOPUS benchmark.

name: morgan-fingerprint-tanimoto-similarity-scoring
description: Use when evaluating ranked SMILES candidate lists from spectra-to-structure inference (e.g. SpecTUS top-1/top-10 predictions) where exact-match Acc1/Acc10 alone is too harsh and partial structural similarity must be quantified.

name: morphological-population-filtering
description: Use when macroMS has detected candidate targets in an optical image (flatbed scanner or cell phone camera) and the raw region list must be filtered by per-region area, circularity, and nearest-neighbor distance before MS targeting.

name: mortality-covariate-handling
description: Use when constructing or comparing weighted mortality risk scores from longitudinal cohort data where age must serve as the Cox time scale rather than a covariate, and weights must be trained on an independent training cohort.

name: motif-annotation-agreement-comparison
description: Use when you have Mass2Motif pseudo-spectra with expert manual substructure annotations and want to test whether automated spectral-matching annotation agrees with them, e.g. reproducing the 19/19 positive-mode beer motif result.

name: motif-count-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when a run of MS2LDA (or any LDA-style motif decomposition) over an MGF spectral corpus must be validated against a published motif count and a training-time envelope, e.g. 5,670 GNPS spectra yielding 500 Mass2Motifs.

name: motif-degree-filtering-in-metabolomics
description: Use when an LDA/MS2LDA run has produced a large motif set (e.g., 300 Mass2Motifs per file) and only motifs recurring across many spectra should be carried into structural or annotation steps.

name: motif-document-threshold-filtering
description: Use when an MS2LDA summary of motif-document relations must be filtered before mapping Mass2Motifs onto a molecular network, or when setting Experimental Options in the ms2lda.org app so downstream summaries are thresholded consistently.

name: motif-occurrence-counting-across-bgc-datasets
description: Use when you have a trained sub-cluster motif library (e.g. PRESTO-TOP motifs annotated with substructures) and a large BGC dataset, and need per-motif occurrence counts, degree statistics, and BGC class distributions.

name: mouse-brain-spatial-data-processing
description: Use when integrating 10X Visium spatial transcriptome (.h5ad) with MALDI-MSI metabolome data from mouse-brain (or ICC tumor) sections that share no spots or features, and spot-to-spot cluster-label transfer accuracy must be quantified.

name: mouse-fecal-metabolomics-data-handling
description: Use when a metabolomics analysis needs a ready-to-use mouse fecal sample count dataset with treatment-factor metadata for testing omu workflows or reproducing the paper's figures.

name: moving-average-parameter-selection
description: Use when raw profile-mode LC-IM-MS TOF data (e.g., Agilent 6560 IM-QTOF .d files) shows poorly defined low-abundance peaks and you must choose user-specified smoothing point counts for the IM and LC dimensions of a multidimensional moving average.

name: moving-window-interpolation-baseline-correction
description: Use when raw multi-platform CE-MS/HILIC-MS data converted to mzXML or mzML has been ROI-searched and false-positive-filtered in AriumMS, and retained ROIs still carry baseline drift that must be removed before feature detection and integration.

name: mqtl-reference-causal-gene-set-evaluation
description: Use when you have a curated molecular QTL reference set with known causal genes and need to quantify how many true positives a prioritization tool recovers and how many false positives it introduces.

name: mr-spectral-line-broadening
description: Use when comparing density-matrix-simulated basis functions (e.g., MRSCloud unedited PRESS TE 30 ms output) against an experimentally acquired LCModel phantom basis file and linewidth mismatch must be removed before spectral agreement metrics.

name: mrgsolve-pk-model-implementation
description: Use when an individual PK parameter estimation (MAP-BE) task requires coding a population PK model in mrgsolve, e.g. a two-compartment model with IIV on CL and V1 and a mixed residual error model.

name: mrlist-object-construction
description: Use when MS-Dial-derived LC-MS/MS feature abundances (m/z, retention times, MS/MS spectra) and sample metadata must be ingested into margheRita as a single mRList object before preprocessing or metabolite identification.

name: mrlist-object-handling-metabolomics
description: Use when an mRList built from MS-Dial tab-delimited feature and sample-annotation files lacks a 'reference' column in mRList$metab_ann and probabilistic quotient normalization (PQN) is required on filtered LC-MS/MS metabolomic profiles.

name: mrm-abundance-table-manipulation
description: Use when a targeted MRM dataset contains QC samples per batch and you need to reduce systematic injection-order drift in compound abundances, e.g. before downstream statistical or pathway analysis.

name: mrm-chromatogram-parsing-from-mzml
description: Use when raw LC-QQQ-MS data are provided as mzML files and per-metabolite quantifier/qualifier MRM chromatograms must be extracted per sample before peak picking and quality scoring.

name: mrm-chromatogram-processing
description: Use when MRM/SRM chromatograms from multiple samples must have their extracted-ion chromatogram peaks aligned and grouped so that per-transition peaks across samples can be reviewed and calibrated in batch.

name: mrm-chromatogram-quantitation
description: Use when processing LC-MRM-MS targeted metabolomics data (e.g., bile-acid or phospholipid panels) where vendor raw files or mzML files plus a method file of targeted compounds must be converted into per-sample peak abundances, handling coeluted isomers and batch effects.

name: mrm-chromatogram-reference-sample-alignment
description: Use when preprocessing MRM-mode LC-MS raw data (mzML) whose chromatograms drift in retention time between samples, and peak picking or peak scoring requires RT-normalized traces before metabolite quantification.

name: mrm-experiment-quantifier-signal-selection
description: Use when a processed MRMhubExperiment exists and downstream INTEGRATOR/QUANT workflows need one quantifier value per feature per analysis in the MRMhub long exchange format.

name: mrm-feature-metavalue-extraction
description: Use when an MRM peak-picking workflow has produced OpenMS FeatureMaps and you need to flatten feature meta-values (peak_area, logSN, RT, quality) into a tidy per-compound CSV for internal-standard scoring or quantitation.

name: mrm-ion-chromatogram-smoothing
description: Use when MRM sample files (mzML, MRM) must be preprocessed so that each ion chromatogram's peaks are detectable and traceable before peak detection, coelution deconvolution, and absolute quantitation in MRMQuant.

name: mrm-metabolomics-data-preprocessing
description: Use when preprocessing batches of MRM-mode LC-QQQ-MS chromatograms (mzML raw data) into per-analyte peak intensity tables with automatic accept/reject peak decisions, especially when manual peak review is too slow or is to be benchmarked.

name: mrm-peak-alignment
description: Use when processing multiple MRM/SRM samples whose EIC peak tables show retention time shifts between runs, and peaks must be aligned or EICs grouped automatically before manual inspection.

name: mrm-peak-area-extraction
description: Use when analyzing multiple reaction monitoring (MRM) mass spectrometry data where peak areas must be extracted per transition across a file batch, or when cross-checking automated peak picking against manual integration for quantification accuracy.

name: mrm-peak-group-validation
description: Use when processing MRM peak/EIC feature lists that require grouping of chromatograms with similar shapes across samples, e.g. before batch manual peak inspection or when validating that EICs of one peptide transition co-cluster and noise stays unclustered.

name: mrm-storage-format-benchmarking
description: Use when converting MRM datasets to Aird, vendor, and mzML formats and you need to measure per-dataset file-volume ratios to justify a compressed storage/computation-oriented format choice.

name: mrm-targeted-metabolomics-peak-processing
description: Use when an MRM ion chromatogram contains coeluted peaks (e.g., 2–3 isomers sharing one transition, such as PC 34:3 isomers at RTs 4.72, 4.84, and 4.92 min) and per-compound abundances must be separated automatically.

name: mrm-transition-xic-extraction
description: Use when processing AEMS MRM raw data from 384- or 1536-well plates where each well/ejection maps to one or more mass transitions and you need per-transition peak areas, baseline correction, and shot-to-peak association in the rtmsEcho/rtms R framework.

name: mrmhub-status-flag-verification
description: Reference for checking that a processing step in a mrmhub MRMhubExperiment actually mutated the intended variable and its is_* status flag before downstream QC or reporting.

name: mrmr-feature-selection
description: Use when building predictive classifiers from high-dimensional LC-MS matrices (hundreds to thousands of aligned features, peptides, or proteins) and you need to reduce dimensionality to a fixed-size top-N feature set (e.g., top 200) prior to SVM training and cross-validated AUC evaluation.

name: mrs-basis-set-simulation
description: Use when a vendor-specific, sequence-specific (PRESS/sLASER, unedited or MEGA/HERMES/HERCULES edited) metabolite basis set is needed for LCModel-style fitting at 3T and no experimentally acquired basis set is available.

name: mrs-metabolite-spectra-pairwise-comparison
description: Use when two sets of simulated MRS metabolite basis functions (e.g., from MRSCloud and FID-A under PRESS at TE 30/68 ms) must be validated for agreement per metabolite using ICC and NRMS thresholds.

name: ms-annotation-confidence-level-assignment
description: Use when labelling MS-based annotation tools or annotation results by confidence level (Schymanski Level 4/3/2a) during curation of a metabolomics tool catalogue or annotation pipeline.

name: ms-backend-object-integration
description: Use when an R analysis must read peak (m/z, intensity) data that lives as a Python object in the shared reticulate session, and copying the full dataset into R should be avoided.

name: ms-chromatogram-plotting-ggplot2
description: Use when prescreened HRMS extraction tables containing compound metadata, extracted-ion chromatogram (EIC) traces and MS2 scans need to be rendered as inspection-quality chromatogram and spectrum plots for quality control.

name: ms-data-access-runtime-benchmarking
description: Decision support for choosing an MS data-access route: use when you must quantify how long XIC extraction takes from .mza/HDF5 files across a full LC-MS run versus vendor library access.

name: ms-data-precision-control
description: Use when storing, converting, or compressing MS m/z arrays and you must fix a controlled-precision loss level (ppm target) before quantization, e.g. converting vendor/mzML data to an integer-based format like Aird or evaluating ZDPD-style compression.

name: ms-dial-feature-extraction-workflow
description: Use when raw LC-MS-based metabolomics data must be converted into a metabolic feature table and software-specific extraction parameters need to be set automatically rather than guessed with MS-DIAL defaults.

name: ms-dial-output-parsing
description: Use when you have run Nextflow4MS-DIAL (or pulled its results folder) and need to quantify the MS-DIAL peak table—e.g., total peaks, true-positive counts, or percentages—for the 10-sample MTBLS733 dataset.

name: ms-dial-spectral-library-parsing
description: Use when a public .msp-format spectral library (MS-DIAL) must be mined for compounds with RT or CCS annotations, e.g. to build training sets for retention-time or CCS predictors that NIST'17 cannot supply.

name: ms-feature-activity-scoring
description: Use when you have processed MS feature data (MZmine 2 or GNPS outputs, mzML-derived peak lists) for an extract library plus bioassay results, and need to score which features match the biological profile for prioritization or dereplication.

name: ms-feature-adduct-fragment-interpretaion
description: Use when NP Analyst (or equivalent Compound Activity Mapping) output shows several distinct m/z features with similar Activity and Cluster Scores sharing one retention time, indicating adduct/fragment/multiply-charged stripes of one molecule.

name: ms-feature-annotation-table-generation
description: Use when you have a GNPS feature-based molecular networking task with CANOPUS in silico class predictions (canopus_summary.tsv) and node/library-match info (Node_info.tsv), and need per-feature chemical consensus annotations.

name: ms-feature-metadata-annotation
description: Use when a direct-injection MS dataset lacks chromatographic separation and features must be grouped as adducts/in-source fragments of one analyte via time-profile correlation plus exact mass differences.

name: ms-feature-network-community-analysis
description: Use when you have extract/fraction-level bioassay results (e.g., BioMAP inhibition profiles) plus replicate LC-MS feature lists and need to map which MS features drive activity and which prefractions cluster together.

name: ms-feature-retention-time-stripe-grouping
description: Use when an NP Analyst community contains multiple strong-Activity-Score MS features that cluster at the same retention time in the community view's RT vs m/z plot, suggesting adducts/fragments of one molecule rather than distinct compounds.

name: ms-feature-table-filtering
description: Use when an aligned feature quantification matrix (features_quantification_matrix.csv from MZmine2 or Optimus) contains many features lacking MS/MS scans and must be reduced to MS/MS-backed rows before GNPS FBMN or bioactivity correlation.

name: ms-file-analysis-table-parsing
description: Use when per-file analysis rows for transferred MS data (e.g. task_001/per_file_analysis_table) need to be rolled up into a QC summary of PSM, peptide and protein group counts at a given FDR filter, posted to a dashboard.

name: ms-file-size-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when choosing an open mass spectrometry file format for storing converted vendor raw data and you need an empirical file-size comparison across formats like MZA, mz5, mzXML, mzML and mzMLb.

name: ms-file-storage-size-quantification
description: Use when both original raw MS-files and preprocessed counterparts of the same dataset exist in a deposit (e.g. MassIVE MSV000087295) and the goal is to numerically verify a claim that preprocessing reduces file size.

name: ms-finder-rt-similarity-filtering
description: Use when MS/MS spectral matching or in silico MS/MS annotation leaves many isomeric structure candidates and predicted LC retention times (from Retip) are available to rank or exclude candidates in MS-FINDER 3.30+.

name: ms-finder-spectral-library-format-preparation
description: Use when building an RT-annotated structure library for MS-FINDER ≥3.24 to rank/exclude isomer candidates in untargeted MS/MS annotation, starting from SMILES sets from HMDB, DrugBank, FooDB, STOFF-IDENT and other Retiplib databases.

name: ms-imaging-ion-image-extraction
description: Use when input is MS1-only imaging MS data in imzML/ibd format (e.g., MALDI-Orbitrap mouse liver on METASPACE) and the goal is structural annotation via pseudo MS/MS built from spatially correlated in-source fragments.

name: ms-instrument-type-comparison
description: Use when comparing a predictor's per-spectrum accuracy across MS/MS instrument types (Q-TOF vs. Orbitrap) or strata such as LogP polarity, precursor mass bins, or chemical superclass, to locate where a model underperforms.

name: ms-low-intensity-threshold-filtering
description: Use when raw LC-IM-MS or LC-DT IM-MS TOF profile-mode data (Agilent .d or UIMF) contains a large background of low-count points that inflate file size and degrade downstream feature finding or lipid annotation.

name: ms-marker-feature-visualization
description: Use when a GC–MS run has been processed with NPFimg (2D m/z–retention-time map, no conventional peak picking) and the identified multivariate marker features for analytes such as aroma odor or human breath metabolites need to be rendered on the original MS map for inspection or reporting.

name: ms-ms-spectra-alignment-shifted-unshifted-peak-matching
description: Use when you have MS/MS spectra of a known compound and a structural analog (same adduct, one modification site) and need to classify matching/shifted/unshifted fragment peaks to localize where the structural modification occurs.

name: ms-peak-list-conversion-to-magma-format
description: Use when starting from flat CASMI-style MS/MS peak lists (precursor plus fragment m/z values at one or more collision energies) that must be loaded into MAGMa command-line or via the www.emetabolomics.org/magma web interface for candidate annotation.

name: ms-quality-control-metric-analysis
description: Use when raw MS runs from a batch need omics-agnostic QC: you want to flag anomalous runs by tracking mass error, RT error, or arrival time error for auto-tracked or user-specified precursor ions rather than relying on spectral-match counts.

name: ms-quality-control-metric-heatmap-generation
description: Use when a batch of raw MS runs (LC-MS, LC-IMS-MS, or direct infusion) has been processed through PeakQC's Isolation Forest anomaly detection on peak metrics and you need a compact visual report of which runs and which ions/metrics are defective.

name: ms-rt-purity-scoring
description: Use when clustering tandem mass spectra (e.g. from PXD023047 with MS-Cluster, Falcon, or MaRaCluster) and you need a per-cluster purity score that does not depend on FDR-controlled database-search identifications, or when validating an MS-RT purity score against a DB-Search reference.

name: ms-signal-characterization-without-peak-picking
description: Use when raw 2D chromatography–MS data (GC–MS or LC–MS maps of m/z vs retention time) must be comprehensively characterized and marker features identified and visualized, and conventional peak picking is either unavailable, unreliable (prone to false peak detections), or undesired — e.

name: ms-spectra-clustering-runtime-profiling
description: Decision support for profiling spectrum preprocessing as a runtime bottleneck before choosing or optimizing an MS/MS spectral clustering tool; triggered when MGF-converted PRIDE data are available and per-stage timings are needed.

name: ms-spectra-metadata-roundtrip-validation
description: Use when Python matchms.Spectrum objects produced by an upstream rspec_to_pyspec conversion must be rebuilt as R Spectra::Spectra objects, and you must prove no loss in peaks data or metadata.

name: ms-spectrum-preprocessing
description: Use when tandem MS test spectra (e.g. NPLIB1, MassSpecGym) must be downloaded, processed into peak lists, and prepared as input for formula annotation tools or de novo structure generation.

name: ms1-accurate-mass-glycan-searching
description: Use when you have LC-MS/MS data of fluorescent-labeled N-linked glycans (OrbiTrap mzXML) plus a list of candidate glycan names and theoretical masses, and need to find which glycans are present at which retention times.

name: ms1-annotation-reproducibility-across-acquisition-modes
description: Use when benchmarking or reproducing ms1-id annotation yield across LC-MS acquisition modes on the NIST fecal dataset (MSV000095787), comparing DDA MS/MS against MS1-only full-scan annotation.

name: ms1-candidate-mass-matching
description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics workflow needs candidate metabolite annotations for MS1 peaks: given a list of monoisotopic m/z values, an ionization mode, and a set of allowed adducts, to produce a ranked candidate list.

name: ms1-eic-correlation-within-rt-window
description: Use when annotating untargeted AIF LC–MS features in MetaboAnnotatoR, to determine which isotopologue (M+0 … M+3) a target feature corresponds to before running the candidate fragment search.

name: ms1-feature-correlation-clustering
description: Use when you have an unclustered MS1 feature table with per-sample intensities (e.g., ExampleDatasets/README/df_test_pos_not_clustered.csv) and need to consolidate features from the same metabolite into single rows before ipaPy2 annotation.

name: ms1-feature-ion-species-annotation
description: Use when an aligned feature list from LC-MS/MS metabolomics must be grouped into ion species (adducts, isotopes, multimers) per molecule, or when relative ion-formation percentages per adduct must be computed and compared across datasets.

name: ms1-feature-metabolite-mass-matching
description: Use when starting MetDNA3/MrnAnnoAlgo3 annotation: you have a curated MRN (igraph), an MS1 feature table, and seed metabolite annotations, and must constrain the network before reaction mapping and MS2-similarity propagation.

name: ms1-feature-relationship-annotation
description: Use when you have a clustered MS1 feature table (pandas dataframe with ids, rel.ids, mzs, RTs, Int columns) and need to collapse isotope peaks into isotope pattern units before adduct computation or IPA annotation.

name: ms1-feature-table-processing
description: Use when a raw vendor MS1 feature table (sample plus ≥3 solvent-blank feature tables) must be de-noised prior to exact mass matching, mass defect filtering, or homologous-series detection for PFAS.

name: ms1-feature-table-qc-summarization
description: Use when a pre-processed LC-MS/MS peak/feature table (e.g., Progenesis export such as PTY087I2) plus sample metadata must be QC-filtered and summarized into per-filter pass/fail ion counts before downstream analysis.

name: ms1-ion-abundance-ranking
description: Use when a QC batch in PeakQC lacks user-specified target ions and you need the software to pick abundant, frequently detected MS1 ions per sample group as auto-tracked QC targets.

name: ms1-ion-feature-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when raw mzLearn output (a feature table of median rt/m/z-defined signals with normalized intensities) must be standardized and split into X_Pretrain_*/X_Finetune_* CSVs before VAE training.

name: ms1-low-collision-energy-filtering
description: Use when computing TIC, EIC, or MS1 spectra from arcMS-converted Parquet files containing both low and high energy (HDMSE) scans and only precursor (MS1) signal should be aggregated.

name: ms1-ms2-database-integration
description: Use when building or extending a plant metabolomics annotation pipeline that needs both MS1 exact-mass tables and MS2 spectral libraries merged into a single search database, e.g. for MetMiner/metID-based compound annotation.

name: ms1-ms2-feature-correspondence
description: Use when processing raw LC–MS/MS runs where per-sample MS1 peaks must be linked to their acquired MS2 spectra before any clustering, spectral merging, or bioactivity correlation — the article's Preprocessing step extracts MS2 spectra and determines MS1–MS2 correspondence per sample.

name: ms1-ms2-feature-result-merging
description: Use when you have SIRIUS (.json) outputs and spectral dereplication results (spectral_results.csv) for .mzML-derived features and need to combine them with the MS1DATA.csv feature table to obtain ranked final candidates per feature.

name: ms1-ms2-median-ratio-analysis
description: Use when comparing HeLa Pierce QC RAW runs to a reference set to diagnose whether peptide-identification loss stems from MS1 TIC decline or an MS2 isolation/fragment-transmission failure.

name: ms1-peak-deconvolution
description: Use when processing LC/HRMS untargeted metabolomics datasets where peaks lack MS2 spectra or available MS2 libraries poorly cover the chemical space, and chemical annotation must be recovered from MS1-only data.

name: ms1-peak-intensity-extraction
description: Use when high-resolution MS/MS or MS1 data need precursor and isotope peak abundances extracted after preprocessing, as input to isotope pattern-based molecular formula deduction (e.g. SIRIUS).

name: ms1-precursor-candidate-screening
description: Use when annotating tandem MS spectra and you need the initial MS1 precursor m/z candidate screen (e.g. 20 ppm delta_mz window) against a compound database in HDF5 format, or when measuring candidates per peak.

name: ms1-scan-filtering
description: Use when the goal is to restrict spectral access to MS1-level scans of a Thermo Fisher .raw file (e.g. building a base-peak table, TIC, or XIC) and the input is a proprietary Orbitrap raw file readable by rawR.

name: ms1-scan-priority-ranking-construction
description: Use when an mzML full-scan dataset plus a prior TopN MS1/MS2 scan schedule must be turned into a per-scan ranked MS2 fragmentation priority list via weighted (nonbinary) ion intensities.

name: ms1-signal-detection-pipeline-execution
description: Use when raw LC/MS data in mzML format needs automated MS1 peak detection and alignment without user-set parameters or QC samples, or when benchmarking signal counts/TP-FP rates against XCMS/ASARI.

name: ms1-spectrum-extraction
description: Use when validating a ZODIAC/SIRIUS-annotated molecular formula for a single LC-MS feature by comparing its measured MS1 isotope pattern (M, M+1, M+2, ...) against a simulated pattern from the elemental composition.

name: ms1-time-mz-image-generation
description: Use when raw MS files (Agilent 'd', Thermo '.raw', Bruker 'd', or mzML) must be screened for global batch quality via MS1-derived time-versus-m/z images and PCA, before or alongside targeted peak-metric QC.

name: ms1-time-mz-image-principal-component-analysis
description: Use when you have a batch of MS runs (Thermo .raw, Agilent .d, Bruker .d, or mzML; LC-MS, LC-IMS-MS, or direct infusion) and need an omics-agnostic, MS1-based global quality check to flag defective runs or group-separating trends before deeper metrics analysis.

name: ms1-time-vs-mz-image-rendering
description: Use when assessing global quality of a batch of untargeted MS runs (LC-MS, LC-IMS-MS, direct infusion, DDA/DIA) before detailed peak-metric QC, and you need a fast, identification-free representation per sample.

name: ms2-adduct-base-peak-specification
description: Use when extracting a layer-3 MS2-similarity subnetwork with retrieveSubNetwork3 and you must declare which peaks serve as base peaks and their adduct identities before merging subnetworks.

name: ms2-annotation-evaluation
description: Use when a new spectral library's practical value must be quantified as added annotations (unique matches, total count deltas) on a public LC-MS/MS dataset, e.g. drug-incubated bacterial cultures.

name: ms2-annotation-peak-count-restriction
description: Use when you must quantify the marginal contribution of MS2 peak information to de novo formula annotation accuracy — e.g., reproducing an Np peak-ablation sweep or benchmarking MS1-only versus MS2-conditioned formula prediction on spectra with subformula annotations.

name: ms2-chimeric-spectrum-detection
description: Use when processing DDA LC-MS/MS data where multiple centroids fall inside an MS2 isolation window and contamination-ion fragments must be removed from co-isolated chimeric spectra before compound identification.

name: ms2-compound-annotation-filtering
description: Use when untargeted LC-MS/MS data (DDA or DIA, with MS2 spectra from pooled QC samples) needs compound-level annotation with fragment-level evidence, and noisy/blank-contaminated features must be filtered before annotation.

name: ms2-cosine-similarity-networking
description: Use when you have GNPS feature-based molecular networking spectral matches (mzML/mzXML-derived feature tables plus paired MS/MS spectra) and need a library-match-only chemical tree to compare sample chemistries against fingerprint-predicted or tree-agnostic metrics.

name: ms2-cosine-similarity-scoring
description: Use when a user-provided tissue MS2 spectrum (e.g. exported from mzML) must be quantitatively compared against Met-ID's MS2 database of FMP-10-derivatized chemical standards and scored with cosine similarity.

name: ms2-embedding-generation
description: Use when labeled 'relevant' and 'other' MS/MS spectra (e.g. MSnLib libraries, in-house BOKU database, wheat ear extract) must be converted into MS2DeepScore embeddings as classifier input features.

name: ms2-event-to-peak-coverage-classification
description: Use when you have an mzML file containing MS2 fragmentation events plus picked-peak bounding boxes (m/z and RT min/max, e.g. exported from MZmine2) and need per-peak coverage flags to quantify fragmentation-controller coverage.

name: ms2-filtered-functional-interpretation
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS data (DDA or SWATH-DIA mzML) have been processed to MS1 feature tables plus MS2 compound identifications, and the goal is to test whether MS2-informed functional analysis yields more significant pathways than MS1-only enrichment.

name: ms2-fingerprint-distance-matrix-construction
description: Use when samples were acquired under different LC methods (e.g. C18 vs C18 RT-shift) or show poor feature overlap, and you need RT-agnostic sample distances from MS2 spectra instead of an aligned feature table.

name: ms2-fingerprint-generation
description: Use when LC-MS/MS samples must be compared in a retention-time-agnostic way, e.g. across chemodiverse samples, different LC methods, or different mass spectrometers (Q-Exactive Orbitrap vs Maxis II Q-TOF), from MS2 peak lists such as MGF.

name: ms2-fingerprint-sample-metrics-interpretation
description: Use when an LC-MS/MS dataset shows an acquisition-batch split (e.g., RT shift or MS sensitivity drift around a run date) and you must test whether MS2-fingerprint MEMO matrices mitigate it relative to feature-table PCoA.

name: ms2-fingerprint-vectorization
description: Use when metabolomics samples cannot be compared by RT-aligned features — chemodiverse samples with poor feature overlap, strong RT shifts, different LC gradients, or different MS instruments (e.g. Maxis Q-ToF vs Q-Exactive Orbitrap) — and a sample-level MS2 fingerprint matrix is needed.

name: ms2-fragment-isotopologue-quantification
description: Use when HRMS MS2 spectra are available for individual lipid isotopologues (e.g., M0 vs M6 of PC(36:4)) and acyl-chain-specific 13C labeling, not just precursor-level MID, is required.

name: ms2-fragment-mass-difference-matching
description: Use when centroided ddMS2 mzML data (ideally one collision energy per precursor) and a completed FeatureFinding feature list are available, and features must be separated into PFAS-like analytes vs. matrix components using MS2 evidence.

name: ms2-fragment-one-to-one-matching
description: Use when bridging prototype compounds to candidate metabolites from PATBS-processed LC-MS feature tables where MS1 mass-defect screening (±100 amu / ±25 mmu) is insufficient and MS2 fragment-level corroboration is needed.

name: ms2-fragment-peak-annotation
description: Use when you have an MS1-identified glycan–RT pair from LC-MS/MS (Orbitrap or MALDI-TOF) data in mzXML format and need to confirm the glycan identity by annotating its MS2 fragment peaks.

name: ms2-fragment-similarity-scoring
description: Use when bridging in vivo metabolite features to in vitro TCM prototype components from LC-MS feature lists, and you need similarity-of-MS2-fragment evidence combined with m/z and mass-defect scoring to assign metabolites to prototypes.

name: ms2-fragment-spectrum-comparison
description: Use when a m/z peak in a MALDI-MSI dataset (e.g., mouse brain imzML data acquired with DHB matrix) is suspected to be a matrix adduct of a known lipid, and a deposited on-tissue MS2 spectrum is available to verify the fragment-ion series against the parent ion.

name: ms2-fragmentation-event-to-peak-matching
description: Use when raw mzML injections from a TopN DDA controller and full-scan mzML of the same serum (QCA) or beer (QCB) extracts are available, and you must measure what fraction of picked peaks received MS2 fragmentation events.

name: ms2-metadata-harmonization
description: Use when MS/MS library entries (e.g. GNPS .msp downloads) contain inconsistent or missing metadata — mismatched SMILES/InChI/InChIKey, salt-form annotations, molar-mass-vs-monoisotopic parent mass errors, or wrong adducts — and must be cleaned reproducibly.

name: ms2-molecular-formula-elucidation
description: Use when MZmine 'Export for SIRIUS' .mgf files (feature MS1 isotopic patterns + MS2 spectra) need per-feature molecular formula and 2D structure candidates within a 10 ppm parent-mass tolerance, e.g. to later cross-check against ISDB-LOTUS spectral annotations.

name: ms2-molecular-networking-annotation
description: Use when you have LC-MS2 peak lists from a fractionated natural product extract and need to prioritize fractions for isolation or compare unknowns against reference compounds (e.g., swinholide A) via spectral similarity networks.

name: ms2-ms3-fragment-peak-annotation
description: Use when a LC-MS lipidomics pipeline has already produced MS2 and MS3+ spectral matches (e.g. from LipiDex 2 Spectrum Searcher) and fragment-level peak assignments are needed to validate or annotate chromatographic features.

name: ms2-peak-intensity-normalization
description: Use when replicate-grouped, deconvolved MS2 spectra (e.g., DDA or SWATH-DIA output) must be merged into one consensus spectrum per MS1 peak and fragment intensities need normalization before MSP export.

name: ms2-peak-mass-decomposition
description: Use when annotating MS2 fragment peaks with chemical subformulae for a candidate precursor formula and you want to avoid costly fragmentation tree computation (e.g. as input features for formula scoring models like MIST-CF).

name: ms2-peak-neutral-loss-counting
description: Use when you have LC-MS/MS peak lists (e.g. .mgf) and need to vectorize samples without feature alignment — especially for chemodiverse samples with poor feature overlap or strong RT shifts.

name: ms2-precursor-coisolation-analysis
description: Use when you have a simulated (e.g., SMITER-generated mzML) or real complex-mixture dataset and must estimate how many distinct peptides co-fragment within each MS2 spectrum before committing to a real MS experiment.

name: ms2-product-ion-mass-difference-alignment
description: Use when comparing a query MS/MS spectrum against reference library spectra to find structural analogues, and you need to explain which query–reference product-ion pairs (including mass-shifted ones like +15.99 Da) drive the similarity score.

name: ms2-recognition-feature-rescue
description: Use when processing DDA LC-MS mzXML data in which conventional peak picking (XCMS.featureTable with snthresh=6, prefilter=c(3,100)) has already run but low-intensity or poorly shaped peaks with detectable MS2 spectra were missed.

name: ms2-representative-spectra-selection
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS mzML files contain multiple MS2 scans per chromatographic feature and you need one representative MS2 spectrum per feature (m/z, RT) to feed formula assignment or ML-based annotation.

name: ms2-scan-content-quality-checking
description: Use when a vendor-format raw LC-MS/MS file (e.g., from GNPS-MassIVE dataset MSV000083437) has been converted to .mzXML or .mzML and must be confirmed readable and MS2-scan-containing before molecular networking upload.

name: ms2-scan-parameter-scheduling
description: Use when you need to simulate or prototype a Top-N DDA acquisition method in ViMMS 2.0 — i.e. you have simulated chemicals or mzML-derived ROIs and must decide which MS1 precursors get fragmented in which MS2 scans at each point in the run.

name: ms2-scan-proportion-computation
description: Use when QC-comparing the MS1/MS2 acquisition balance across Thermo RAW runs — e.g., diagnosing underperforming HeLa QC runs from MetaXtract scan-header CSVs where only the Scan Mode column is required.

name: ms2-scan-to-feature-association
description: Use when you have LC/MS data with detected molecular features (feature table from xcms) plus centroided MS/MS scans, and you need to associate each MS2 spectrum with the correct feature to enable MS/MS spectral similarity or networking.

name: ms2-similarity-network-annotation
description: Use when annotating untargeted LC-MS/MS features beyond spectral-library hits by propagating annotations through a knowledge-guided MS2 similarity network connecting reaction-paired metabolites with similar MS/MS spectra.

name: ms2-similarity-network-tool-comparison
description: Use when a feature table carries network-propagated level 3 annotations (e.g. MetDNA3 output on Orbitrap data) and you need to quantify how many annotations independent in-silico tools support.

name: ms2-spectra-construction-from-peak-lists
description: Use when you have raw MS2 peak lists (paired m/z and intensity vectors) with known precursor m/z values and need to assemble them into Spectra objects for comparison or conversion, rather than reading from mzML/MGF files.

name: ms2-spectra-de-novo-structure-generation
description: Use when you have positive-mode MS2 spectra (MGF or SIRIUS .ms) with no library match, need de novo candidate structures, or want to evaluate whether de novo candidates rival database-search annotations.

name: ms2-spectra-deconvolution
description: Use when raw DDA or SWATH-DIA MS/MS spectra contain co-eluting or chimeric fragment ions that must be reassigned to their precursor ions before compound annotation or functional interpretation.

name: ms2-spectra-preprocessing
description: Use when starting the MAW workflow on raw untargeted tandem MS data in .mzML format and you need MS2 pre-processing plus spectral dereplication outputs that feed SIRIUS or MetFrag candidate generation.

name: ms2-spectra-retrieval-and-representative-selection
description: Use when you have raw HRMS data (mzML) plus a compound or mass list and need first-look prescreening: retrieve EICs and MS2 scans within an m/z tolerance, QC each MS1 parent, and pick a representative MS2 spectrum.

name: ms2-spectra-source-attribution
description: Use when combining MS2 spectra from paired DDA and DIA-(SWATH) acquisitions of the same sample set and you need each spectrum record in the exported MGF labeled with its DDA or DIA provenance.

name: ms2-spectral-clustering
description: Use when tens of millions of MS/MS spectra (tens to hundreds of GB) must be merged into consensus spectra before peptide identification and CPU-only clustering tools like MS-Cluster, spectra-cluster, or MaRaCluster are too slow.

name: ms2-spectral-clustering-and-cleaning
description: Use when processing raw LC–MS/MS untargeted metabolomics data (e.g. mzML/MGF per-sample MS2 files from a feature-detection step) and you need to consolidate redundant MS2 spectra into clean consensus spectra for downstream molecular networking, library identification, and bioactivity correlation.

name: ms2-spectral-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when repeated MS/MS acquisitions in DDA metabolomics data must be de-duplicated by clustering, and the clustering quality (purity vs completeness N10) of Falcon, MaRaCluster, or MS-Cluster must be compared without metabolite ground truth.

name: ms2-spectral-database-curation-characterization
description: Use when a local annotation tool ships a built-in MS2 spectral library (e.g. Met-ID's FMP-10 database) and you must quantify its contents — number of derivatized forms, parent standards, CID energy range — before trusting downstream identifications.

name: ms2-spectral-entropy-similarity-networking
description: Use when LC-HRMS MS2 peak lists exist for enzymatic-assay-derived candidate metabolites and their parent xenobiotics, and candidates must be assigned to parents by spectral similarity rather than reference-library matching.

name: ms2-spectral-library-aggregation-across-public-databases
description: Use when building or auditing a compound-identification spectral library that must merge spectra from many public MS2 sources with deduplication and unique-compound counting.

name: ms2-spectral-library-annotation
description: Use when MS1 features from an LC-MS metabolomics/exposomics run (e.g., urine RP(+) DDA mzXML data) need compound-level identification by matching DDA MS2 spectra against an in-house .msp standard library.

name: ms2-spectral-library-annotation
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS (DDA or DIA) spectra have been processed to features and you need compound-level annotation of MS2 peaks via spectral library matching.

name: ms2-spectral-library-annotation-rate-analysis
description: Use when you have FBMN/IIMN outputs (feature table .csv, .mgf MS2 summary, IIN edge .csv files) and need to compute annotation rates and the gain from propagating spectral library matches over ion identity neighbors.

name: ms2-spectral-library-matching
description: Use when annotating untargeted LC-MS metabolomics peaks where MS2 spectra (.mgf or .mzML) are available alongside an m/z feature table and metabolite-level annotation confidence is required.

name: ms2-spectral-library-matching
description: Use when tissue MS2 spectra (e.g. from mzML files) need to be compared against reference MS2 spectra of chemical standards — such as FMP-10-derivatized neurotransmitters — to annotate on-tissue metabolites or quantify bin-size sensitivity of similarity scores.

name: ms2-spectral-library-matching
description: Use when centroided LC-MS/MS mzML data (DDA or SWATH-DIA) has yielded consensus MS2 spectra per MS1 feature and compounds must be identified by spectral library matching using MS2, MS1, retention-time and isotope similarity.

name: ms2-spectral-library-matching
description: Use when mapped empirical compounds carry experimental MS2 spectra and putative identifications need reference-library support; i.e., after map_ms2 has associated empCpds with MS2 peaks and Level 1 (MS1) annotation is insufficient.

name: ms2-spectral-library-matching
description: Use when untargeted metabolomics LC-MS/MS data (e.g., xcms peak-derived spectra or MZmine-exported MGF files) needs compound-level MS2 annotation against a reference spectral library such as HMDB.

name: ms2-spectral-library-search
description: Use when an LC-MS/MS lipidomics feature has a measured MS2 peak list (m/z + intensity + precursor m/z) and the goal is library-based annotation of lipid species, chain composition, or C=C double-bond position.

name: ms2-spectral-match-annotation-prioritization
description: Use when you have a Qemistree hierarchy and merged feature data and need chemical class labels (e.g., acyl-carnitines, flavonoids) to trace class-specific subtrees against sample metadata.

name: ms2-spectral-quality-assessment
description: Use when you need to quantify how 'good' tandem MS spectra are—e.g. comparing DDA vs DIA(SWATH) vs DaDIA MS2 quality—by scoring each spectrum against a standard spectral library.

name: ms2-spectral-similarity-network-analysis
description: Use when an aligned LC-MS/MS feature table (.csv), consensus MS2 spectra (.mgf), and ion-identity supplementary edges are available and network connectivity or feature redundancy across adducts and isotopes is the bottleneck.

name: ms2-spectral-similarity-scoring
description: Use when you have an experimental MS2 peak list (m/z, intensity pairs) and need a per-pair similarity score against reference metabolite spectra to support compound identification.

name: ms2-spectral-similarity-scoring
description: Use when you have MS1 features with MS2 spectra and a reaction-linked feature-pair table, and must filter network edges by spectral similarity before metabolite annotation propagation.

name: ms2-spectral-vectorization-memo
description: Use when you need to compare metabolomics samples by their overall MS2 fragmentation content rather than aligned features — e.g. chemodiverse samples with poor feature overlap, strong RT shifts, or different LC/MS methods — or to flag spectrally dissimilar extracts for novelty prioritization.

name: ms2-spectrum-annotation
description: Use when centroided ddMS2 mzML data must be inspected at the spectrum level — e.g., to verify whether PFAS diagnostic fragments or fragment mass differences were detected for a prioritized feature before assigning a suspect hit.

name: ms2-spectrum-clustering
description: Use when processing raw MS2 peak lists (e.g. .mzXML) for classic molecular networking and a reduced set of representative consensus spectra is needed instead of redundant duplicate scans.

name: ms2-spectrum-clustering-mgf-generation
description: Use when a processed LC-MS/MS feature table (OpenMS consensusXML) must be exported for GNPS Feature-Based Molecular Networking or Ion Identity Molecular Networking, i.e. you need an MGF plus quantification and metadata files for a GNPS upload.

name: ms2-spectrum-count-normalization
description: Use when comparing untargeted metabolomics feature tables produced with different centWave parameter sets (AutoTuner- vs IPO-derived) and you need to test whether a feature subset is depleted for MS2 spectra after controlling for subset size.

name: ms2-spectrum-input-encoding
description: Use when raw or profile MS2 spectra (mzML for prediction, HDF5 for training) must be converted into peak-embedding plus positional-encoding input sequences for a transformer that predicts lipid species tokens.

name: ms2-spectrum-mgf-loading
description: Use when starting a mineMS2 analysis from raw MGF spectra (e.g. pnordicum_ms2_spectra.mgf) plus a TSV metadata file, before discretizeMzDifferences.

name: ms2-spectrum-peak-merging
description: Use when multiple ESI-MS2 records of the same compound exist under different CID collision energies (e.g. 10–50 V) and a single reference spectrum per compound is needed for spectral similarity search.

name: ms2-spectrum-peak-normalization
description: Use when MS2 spectra in .mzML format must be normalized and low-intensity peaks filtered prior to cosine-similarity dereplication against spectral databases like GNPS, HMDB, or MassBank.

name: ms2-spectrum-peak-selection-and-deconvolution
description: Use when MS2 spectra come from a miniaturized, low-resolution mass spectrometer and must be reduced to a compact, error-corrected peak list before feeding a de novo structure-prediction model such as TeFT.

name: ms2-spectrum-preprocessing
description: Use when raw MS/MS peak files (mzML, mzXML, or MGF) must be cleaned and normalized before spectrum clustering or similarity computation, e.g. prior to falcon DBSCAN clustering of proteomics spectra.

name: ms2-spectrum-processing-in-python
description: Use when each sample's LC-MS/MS DDA features (from MZmine feature detection) need structural annotation in Python via spectral matching to a large in silico MS2 database with organism-level reweighting.

name: ms2-spectrum-quality-assessment
description: Use when raw MS2 peak lists must be vetted for compound-identification reliability before being trusted in a metabolite annotation or identification workflow.

name: ms2-spectrum-quality-criteria-checking
description: Use when building a large-scale MS/MS training corpus (e.g. from GeMS-style mining of 250,000 LC–MS/MS experiments) and redundant or low-quality spectra must be filtered into nested quality tiers.

name: ms2-spectrum-quality-filtering
description: Use when building IIMN-based propagated spectral libraries from ion identity networks where only high-confident, high-quality MS2 consensus spectra should become library entries.

name: ms2-spectrum-similarity-networking
description: Use when LC-HRMS/PRM spectra from biotransformation assays (e.g. human liver S9 incubations of pesticides) contain metabolites with no reference library spectra, and top-down annotation is needed via spectral similarity clustering.

name: ms2-spectrum-subformula-assignment
description: Use when performing database-independent, de novo chemical formula assignment from MS/MS spectra where fragmentation trees (SIRIUS) are too slow or unavailable, and you need peak-to-subformula mappings to feed an energy-based formula scorer.

name: ms2-spectrum-visualization
description: Use when you have prescreened HRMS extraction output (compound/precursor metadata, EIC traces, MS2 spectral scans) and need visual QC panels per compound, as in Shinyscreen's visualisation stage.

name: ms2deep-score-embedding-generation
description: Use when HR-MS/MS spectra (e.g., MGF inference spectra of Glycyrrhiza uralensis root or Paulownia tomentosa fruit extracts) need MS2DeepScore structure-informed embeddings as classifier input in AnnoMe.

name: ms2deepscore-candidate-preselection-and-reranking
description: Use when annotating MS2 query spectra against a large library (e.g. GNPS) and both exact matches and analogues are needed, with a fast, scalable alternative to modified cosine score-based searching.

name: ms2deepscore-embedding-generation
description: Use when a set of HR-MS/MS spectra (e.g. MSnLib MGF files plus in-house BOKU database spectra, or inference extracts) must be converted into MS2DeepScore structure-informed embeddings before AnnoMe classifier training or prediction.

name: ms2deepscore-pretrained-model-inference
description: Use when MS/MS spectra in .mgf format need pairwise spectral similarity scores and no suitable MS/MS library search target exists, so pretrained machine-learned scoring (ms2deepscore via MS2Query) is required.

name: ms2deepscore-similarity-scoring
description: Use when ranking GNPS-style MS2 library spectra against query spectra without precursor m/z preselection, e.g. selecting top-2000 candidates for random-forest re-ranking or comparing spectral similarity methods for exact-match benchmarking.

name: ms2deepscore-similarity-scoring
description: Use when tandem MS/MS spectra must be compared across ionization modes (e.g., a Rutin positive-mode vs negative-mode pair), or when cosine (0.0) and modified cosine (0.3) scores underreport true chemical similarity of structurally identical compounds.

name: ms2deepscore-similarity-thresholding
description: Use when exploring LC-MS/MS feature connectivity around a node of interest in specXplore and you need to regenerate the local edge overlay under new threshold or connectivity-limitation constraints.

name: ms2lda-mass2motif-mapping
description: Use when annotated MS1/MS2 peak features should be grouped into GNPS FBMN Molecular Families and MS2LDA Mass2Motif metabolite sets for PLAGE-based activity scoring in PALS.

name: ms2lda-mass2motif-threshold-filtering
description: Use when MS2LDA motif summary tables (e.g. MotifFS2.csv) must be thresholded prior to mapping ring/tail-type Mass2Motifs onto GNPS molecular network nodes and edges.

name: ms2lda-motif-assignment-verification
description: Use when a GNPS molecular network job has a paired MS2LDA experiment and you must confirm that substructure motifs (e.g., flavonoid motifs 130, 86, 149) are correctly and completely assigned to network nodes before downstream class-distribution analysis.

name: ms2lda-motif-probability-filtering
description: Use when annotating a GNPS classical or feature-based molecular network with MS2LDA Mass2Motifs and you need to control which motif-document relations (motif probability and overlap scores) pass into the network mapping.

name: ms2lda-motif-summary-parsing
description: Use when a Mass2Motifs_2_Network (classical or feature-based) workflow requires an MS2LDA job's motif summary file and the ms2lda.org export times out, or when motif-document relations must be filtered by prob/overlap thresholds before network mapping.

name: ms2lda-pipeline-execution
description: Use when an mzML/mzXML MS/MS dataset must be decomposed into recurring substructure motifs (Mass2Motifs) without prior compound identification, and stage-wise runtimes need benchmarking.

name: ms2query-library-search-runtime-profiling
description: Use when benchmarking specXplore preprocessing on .mgf LC–MS/MS feature lists to measure MS2Query search time, pairwise similarity time (ms2deepscore/modified cosine/spec2vec), and output feature counts per dataset.

name: msconvert-peakpicking-filter-configuration
description: Use when vendor-format raw LC-MS/MS files (e.g., Thermo, Waters, Agilent, Bruker, SCIEX) must be converted to an open format (.mzXML/.mzML/.mgf) before uploading to GNPS-MassIVE for molecular networking.

name: msdial-annotation-scoring
description: Use when a pre-processed MS-DIAL or patRoon untargeted metabolomics feature table with metabolite annotations needs one confidence level per feature, written out as annoLevels.csv.
