name: msdial-area-export-import
description: Use when untargeted metabolomics feature data has been processed in MS-DIAL and needs to be brought into GetFeatistics as featTable/featINFO for QC filtering, annotation confidence assignment, and statistics.

name: msdial-feature-extraction
description: Use when raw LC-MS metabolomics data need to be converted into a metabolite feature table via MS-DIAL and you want data-derived parameters rather than MS-DIAL defaults to maximize the number of true positive features.

name: msdial-feature-table-parsing
description: Use when an MS-DIAL output peak list from the CSH-Q Exactive HF lipidomics assay contains positive-ionization precursor m/z values that lack MS/MS-based annotation and need lipid hits assigned by accurate mass alone.

name: msdial-peak-detection-parameter-configuration
description: Use when preparing an LC-HRMS metabolomics run with Nextflow4MS-DIAL: mzML (or .abf) files must be processed through MS-DIAL v4.48 with parameter sets matched to the original study (e.g. Li et al. 2018 / MTBLS733) and the resulting peak table handed to MS-FLO.

name: msdial-raw-data-processing
description: Use when raw MS1 LC-HRMS files from case/control incubation experiments (e.g., human liver S9 fractions with vs. without active enzyme) must be converted into an aligned feature-intensity matrix and filtered to differentially expressed metabolites.

name: mse-error-metric-computation
description: Use when simulated or spiked data sets have known ground-truth metabolite concentrations and you must quantify how well a deconvolution/quantification method (e.g. SAND, CRAFT, peak intensity, numerical integration) recovers them.

name: mse-lambda-proportion-estimation

name: msflo-artifact-flagging-and-alignment
description: Use when you have a raw MS-DIAL peak table (from .mzML or .abf LC-HRMS metabolomics files) and need to flag duplicates/adducts/isotopes, align peaks, and remove contaminant ions before statistical analysis.

name: msflo-duplicate-adduct-isotope-flagging
description: Use when MS-DIAL peak tables (from .mzML LC-HRMS runs) must be cleaned and optimized before downstream analysis — specifically for duplicate/adduct/isotope flagging, alignment and contaminant ion removal via MS-FLO.

name: msgf-peptide-assignment-tabulation

name: msi-annotation-confidence-assessment
description: Use when evaluating ms1-id annotation results on MALDI-MS imaging imzML/ibd data — e.g. deciding which annotations are trustworthy, comparing scaled vs non-scaled GNPS library searches, or validating against spotted standards.

name: msi-annotation-fdr-filtering

description: Use when significant m/z hits from statistical analysis (e.g. a t-test on DI-MS/LC-MS peak tables) need putative metabolite annotations with MSI confidence levels after a compound-database m/z search.

name: msi-annotation-level-classification
description: Use when a feature table with database annotation matches (annotate_tbl) needs per-feature MSI confidence levels — e.g. to separate metabolites with m/z+RT+MS2 support from those with m/z-only matches before reporting or filtering.

name: msi-annotation-level-classification

name: msi-ce-ms-data-preprocessing

name: msi-ce-ms-migration-index-annotation

name: msi-ce-ms-peak-annotation
description: Use when pre-processing targeted full-scan multiplexed MSI-CE-MS mzML runs where large migration-time variability makes standard alignment tools unsuitable and metabolite peaks must be annotated, integrated, and assigned to serial injection positions.

name: msi-ce-ms-sample-position-assignment

name: msi-composite-image-upsampling

name: msi-confidence-level-annotation
description: Use when annotating untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics spectra (e.g. urine on HILIC/CSH Q Exactive HF) with tiered MSI confidence levels 1-3, or when quantifying the annotated vs unannotated fraction of MS/MS spectra.

name: msi-confidence-level-annotation-interpretation

name: msi-data-preprocessing
description: Use when raw .imzML/.ibd MSI pixel data (e.g. test_POS from MetaboLights MTBLS487) must be converted into a filtered, deisotoped ion feature table before lipid annotation at a chosen ppm.annotate tolerance.

name: msi-data-quality-benchmarking

name: msi-he-image-overlay-compositing

name: msi-hyperspectral-spectra-loading

name: msi-intensity-normalisation-and-pareto-scaling
description: Use when an imzML-derived, annotated MSI feature table (e.g. image.norm.csv from massPix) must be prepared as input for PCA or clustering, and pixel-to-pixel intensity variation needs correction before scaling.

name: msi-intensity-normalization

name: msi-ion-image-augmentation

name: msi-ion-image-extraction-and-overlay-visualization

name: msi-level1-authentic-standard-validation

name: msi-metabolite-annotation

name: msi-metabolite-database-interpretation
description: Use when metabolite annotations from ambient MSI (e.g., AFADESI-MSI of mouse body sections) must be organized into per-organ membership/enrichment sets and compared across organs, ionization modes, or mouse strains.

name: msi-mz-matching

name: msi-pca-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when you have a centroid-mode MSI peak matrix (e.g. rMSIproc .zip format) and need dimensionality reduction to visually compare data quality before and after a peak-removal step such as matrix-related signal removal.

name: msi-peak-filtering-pooling

name: msi-peak-matrix-processing

name: msi-peak-pair-mass-difference-calculation

name: msi-peak-picked-intensity-analysis

name: msi-peak-picking-alignment

name: msi-peak-table-import-msimat

name: msi-pixel-to-spot-binning

name: msi-principal-component-analysis

name: msi-spatial-colocalization-analysis

name: msi-spatial-visualization

name: msi-specific-data-augmentation-design
description: Use when training a self-supervised contrastive encoder (e.g., SimSiam with ResNet18 backbone) on MSI ion images and you must generate augmented view pairs whose noise model matches the Poisson-distributed ion abundance and random/intensity-dependent missing patterns of MSI data.

name: msi-spectrum-binary-classification-inference
description: Use when you have raw MALDI FT-ICR MSI spectra (e.g., 85,062 m/z variables) with ground-truth normal/tumor labels and a trained massNet model, and need probabilistic binary pixel-level classification plus ROC AUC, accuracy, confusion matrix, and runtime.

name: msi-to-mri-multimodal-image-registration
description: Use when many misaligned serial MSI tissue sections (e.g., H5-serialized 3D MSI like coronal3D_propagated_decoded.h5) must be aligned to a reference MRI/atlas for volumetric reconstruction and per-brain-region profiling.

name: msi-transcriptome-integrated-data-interpretation
description: Use when an integrated spatial transcriptome/MALDI-MSI object (haCCA b_predict with X feature matrix and D spatial matrix) is available and the goal is to test whether a gene's spatial expression distribution overlaps a specific metabolite's intensity distribution.

name: msi-validation-list-curation
description: Use when a matrix-related peak-annotation method for AgLDI/silver-nanolayer MSI needs a ground-truth list to validate classification performance, or when Table 2-style theoretical Ag peak masses must be reproduced.

name: msiflow-workflow-configuration-and-execution
description: Use when MALDI MSI (optionally multimodal with IFM) data must be processed through an automated, reproducible workflow — e.g. pixel-wise statistical comparison of lipid intensities between infected and control groups within tissue ROIs.

name: mslevel-collision-energy-annotation
description: Use when converting Waters UNIFI (HD)MSE or mzML profile-mode data to Parquet/HDF5 with arcMS and you need to preserve and exploit the low vs high collision energy (MS1/MS2) distinction for filtering and chromatogram/spectrum queries.

name: msml-model-training-on-qtof-spectra
description: Use when training CFM-ID 4.0's learned (MSML) predictor on QTOF ESI-MS/MS spectra at 10/20/40 eV, or when benchmarking in silico compound identification (MS2C) on CASMI 2016 category-3 Orbitrap/QTOF data.

name: msml-neural-network-retraining
description: Use when observed MS/MS spectra come from a non-QTOF instrument (e.g. Orbitrap HCD) and the stock CFM-ID 4.0 QTOF-trained MSML model must be recalibrated before in silico spectral prediction and candidate ranking.

name: msms-based-compound-candidate-ranking
description: Use when feature groups retaining MS/MS peak lists and formula candidates (e.g. from GenForm/SIRIUS) need compound identification by ranking database candidates against MS/MS peaks.

name: msms-candidate-penalty-scoring
description: Use when you have MS/MS (or MSn) peak lists with a precursor elemental composition and need to rank candidate structures from a chemical database without reference spectra.

name: msms-clustering-parameter-sweep-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking tandem-MS clustering tools on untargeted metabolomics spectra (Orbitrap or qTof mzML/MGF) and you need purity/N10 trade-off curves across tool parameter settings rather than a single clustering run.

name: msms-confidence-score-modeling
description: Use when ranking top-k candidate molecular formulas generated from tandem mass spectra requires a learned confidence score, e.g. training a rescore model on Orbitrap or Q-TOF MS/MS features.

name: msms-cosine-similarity-evaluation
description: Use when a set of predicted MS/MS spectra (MGF/PKL from 3DMolMS or baselines) must be quantitatively scored against experimental Agilent Q-TOF PCDL/NIST20 spectra, per compound and per ion mode ([M+H]+, [M-H]-).

name: msms-cosine-similarity-fingerprinting
description: Use when a query MS/MS spectrum (reference spectrum from GNPS or a cryptic spectrum from a paired genome-MS/MS sample) must be converted into a similarity fingerprint so it can be matched to biosynthetic gene cluster families via the NPOmix KNN classifier.

name: msms-cosine-similarity-library-matching
description: Use when untargeted LC–MS/MS feature tables carry acquired MS2 spectra for a subset of features and you want per-annotation posterior probabilities that exploit the fragmentation pattern, not just MS1 peak masses and adducts.

name: msms-coverage-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when LC-HRMS/MS workflow needs to measure how many true chromatographic peaks receive MS/MS coverage before and after applying an exclusion list generated from background (wall) annotations, and the result must be compared against published baseline counts (Supplementary Table S2).

name: msms-dataset-batch-processing
description: Use when benchmarking formula assignment across multiple qualified MS/MS datasets — e.g. computing rank#1/top-3/top-5 accuracy and total processing time for SIRIUS, Buddy, or FSA on identical spectra and hardware.

name: msms-dereplication
description: Use when raw or identified tandem MS (MS/MS) data from public repositories (e.g., MassIVE) needs compound-level annotations via exact spectral library search, or when tracking identification growth across library updates ('living data' reanalysis).

name: msms-dilution-series-entropy-similarity-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing denoising algorithms (e.g. Spectral Denoising vs MS Reduce, 1% base-peak thresholding, DNL) on serial-dilution MS/MS data against ground-truth reference spectra, to measure annotation gains and false negatives.

name: msms-embedding-prediction
description: Use when annotating MSP-format MS/MS spectra (MSP files with or without SMILES) for a chosen polarity whose features have precursor masses and known adducts, and you need top-N candidate compound IDs from embeddings rather than spectral-library dot-product matching.

name: msms-entropy-similarity-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantify agreement between a noisy/denoised query MS/MS spectrum and a clean reference spectrum (e.g., validating electronic+chemical denoising of .msp spectra) or to score spectral matches in Denoising Search.

name: msms-exclusion-list-generation
description: Use when PeakBot has annotated walls/background signals in blank or background LC-HRMS samples and you need a targeted DDA exclusion list to boost MS/MS coverage of true chromatographic peaks in subsequent runs.

name: msms-feature-preprocessing
description: Use when a .mgf file of MS/MS feature spectra (e.g. wheat or urine metabolome LC–MS/MS with <1000–<4000 features) must be turned into a specXplore session data object with pairwise similarity matrices before t-SNE or dashboard exploration.

name: msms-fingerprint-prediction-evaluation
description: Use when a study has MS/MS spectra left unannotated by spectral library search (e.g. IDSL.CSA vs NIST 20/LipidBlast) and you need to quantify annotation gains from predicted-fingerprint structure matching.

name: msms-formula-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when you have ranked candidate molecular formulas per MS/MS spectrum (from FSA or a comparable ranker) and need to quantify rank#1 accuracy, top-5 accuracy, and per-spectrum runtime against known metabolite ground truth.

name: msms-fragment-annotation
description: Use when you need theoretical MS/MS fragment ions for derivatized unsaturated sterols (or other C=C-containing molecules) to support matching of LC-IM-MS/MS features against a reference lipid database.

name: msms-fragment-bag-of-words-corpus-construction
description: Use when raw MS2 spectra (e.g. from beer-extract or other complex-mixture LC-MS/MS runs) must be converted into the fragment-and-neutral-loss bag-of-words documents that LDA/MS2LDA topic modeling consumes.

name: msms-fragment-binning-and-factorization
description: Use when comparing MS/MS spectra of several features from an .mgf file to see which fragment m/z values and neutral losses they share in one heatmap view.

name: msms-fragment-data-extraction
description: Use when UNIFI-exported .xlsx MS/MS spectra of reference standards need to be converted into a fragment datatable stratified by standard and collision energy (20/40/60 eV).

name: msms-fragment-ion-overlap-quantification
description: Use when LC–MS/MS spectra (.mgf) are embedded via an ms2deepscore similarity matrix and you need to characterize how much of the fragmentation signal is shared among spectra in a dense local neighborhood around a feature of interest.

name: msms-fragment-ion-prediction
description: Use when public/commercial MS/MS libraries lack spectra for a compound class (e.g., <50 acylcarnitine structures) and MSI level 2 annotation requires predicted fragment ions.

name: msms-fragment-lfp-similarity-scoring
description: Use when you have chained MS/MS fragment ion-intensity profiles of two (or more) isomeric compounds across multiple collision energies and need per-fragment similarity scores to distinguish them.

name: msms-fragment-library-generation
description: Reference for building or extending metabolite fragment libraries when new experimental MS/MS spectra (e.g. MassBank records such as MSBNK-RIKEN-PR100295 for Pantothenic acid [M+H]+) must be converted into scored .csv entries for MetaboAnnotatoR.

name: msms-fragment-library-searching
description: Use when an aligned feature table contains m/z and retention-time pairs whose monoisotopic precursor masses need compound-level annotation via MS/MS spectral matching against an online MassBank library.

name: msms-fragment-mass-enumeration
description: Use when building targeted PRM/MRM or DIA assays for lipids and you must enumerate precursor-to-fragment transitions (m/z, adduct, charge) for lipid classes rather than measuring them experimentally.

name: msms-fragment-overlap-analysis
description: Decision support for whether CFM-ID predicted fragments can back annotation of DNA adducts in HRMS adductomics when experimental MS/MS spectra exist only for a subset (e.g. 15 of 582) of database entries.

name: msms-fragment-pattern-search
description: Use when you have centroided LC/MS data (mzML) with a feature table and MS2 scans, and a known diagnostic product ion (e.g., m/z 333.0592) to screen for structurally related features across many spectra.

name: msms-fragment-peak-matching
description: Use when annotating an LC-MS/MS peak (e.g. negative-mode peak M386T77, m/z 385.1118, RT 1.27 min) by matching its fragment peaks to a candidate metabolite's reference fragments within a 10 ppm tolerance to obtain an MS/MS score.

name: msms-fragment-profile-matching
description: Use when untargeted LC-MS/MS data are acquired at multiple collision energies (e.g., stepped NCE 20/40/60%) and isomers with similar substructures must be distinguished, so a single cross-sectional spectrum match is insufficient.

name: msms-fragment-screening
description: Use when a blank-filtered LC-HRMS/MS feature table (e.g. AFFF samples) needs PFAS candidate flagging via MS/MS fragment matching, especially for precursor ions whose exact masses match nothing in the EPA catalogued PFAS list.

name: msms-fragment-simulation-for-n-me-derivatized-sterols
description: Use when building a spectral library or 4D identification database for N-Me derivatized unsaturated sterol lipids, and theoretical fragment ions matching N-Me fragmentation patterns are needed for LC-IM-MS/MS annotation.

name: msms-fragmentation-candidate-ranking
description: Use when a challenge provides MS/MS peak lists (possibly merged across collision energies) with a known elemental composition, and candidate structures must be retrieved from PubChem and ranked without reference spectra.

name: msms-fragmentation-depth-sweep
description: Use when you need to assess how deeply MAGMa breadth-first fragmentation (depth 2 vs 3 vs 4) affects ModiFinder's shifted-peak annotation coverage and MF-O evaluation scores on an MS/MS analog pair benchmark.

name: msms-fragmentation-pattern-annotation
description: Use when a GNPS molecular network (MS/MS spectra as vertices, modified-cosine edges) must be interpreted by mapping mineMS2-mined fragmentation patterns onto its components and exporting for Cytoscape.

name: msms-fragmentation-pattern-matching-to-network-components
description: Use when you have a mined mineMS2 pattern library plus a GNPS molecular network (components of similar MS/MS spectra) and need to identify which patterns specifically explain each network component.

name: msms-hypergeometric-score-histogram-analysis
description: Use when you have per-feature MS/MS spectral match scores from searching lipid annotations against two or more spectral libraries (e.g., CalicoLipids vs MS-DIAL) and need library-specific score cutoffs to separate authentic from spurious identifications.

name: msms-intensity-coincidence-analysis

name: msms-intensity-coverage-filtering
description: Use when curating raw MS/MS spectral libraries (NIST'17, MS-DIAL, MSnLib .mgf/.msp entries) into training-ready data for in silico fragmentation models and uncurated spectra must be quality-controlled by fragment-to-peak matching criteria.

name: msms-intensity-normalization-to-unit-sum
description: Use when a centroided MS/MS spectrum has been cleaned (peaks merged within +/- 0.05 Da, noise-filtered) and you need intensities as a probability distribution for spectral entropy or entropy-similarity calculations.

name: msms-intensity-weighting
description: Use when a centroided, normalized MS/MS peak list must be intensity-weighted prior to entropy similarity computation and the spectrum's entropy (or ion richness) is unknown or low (S < 3).

name: msms-library-count-verification
description: Use when a deposited MS/MS reference library (MGF or matchms-readable format) carries reported totals of spectra and unique compounds that must be independently verified against the Zenodo archive before downstream use or benchmarking.

name: msms-library-matching
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS feature tables from lipidomics experiments (e.g. Thermo .raw, SCIEX .wiff, .mzML inputs) need MS2 library-search annotation against a theoretical spectral library covering lipid chain compositions and C=C double-bond positions.

name: msms-longitudinal-fragment-profiling-scoring
description: Use when annotating metabolites from MS/MS spectra acquired at multiple distinct collision energies (e.g., stepped NCE 20/40/60%) and you need per-candidate similarity ranking plus ROC-derived identification thresholds.

name: msms-metadata-harmonization
description: Use when a raw or merged MS/MS spectral library in MGF format contains inconsistent metadata fields, missing precursor m/z or ionization mode, or annotations whose parent mass/adduct contradict the precursor m/z and SMILES.

name: msms-modified-cosine-similarity-scoring

name: msms-noise-ion-simulation

name: msms-pairwise-similarity-computation
description: Use when you have MS/MS spectra (MGF files) from a spectral library or extract library and need pairwise similarity scores that reflect structural relatedness, e.g., to build a molecular network or find structural analogues beyond cosine-based matching.

name: msms-pattern-interpretation
description: Use when a GNPS molecular network component or spectral cluster needs a chemical interpretation, and MS/MS spectra (e.g., LC-HRMS .mgf with metadata) can be mined for shared, graph-structured m/z differences.

name: msms-peak-filtering
description: Use when raw MS/MS peak sets from spectra in a molecular network component must be preprocessed before MMSA multiple spectral alignment, e.g. to reduce noise and outlier intensity effects prior to consensus peak identification.

name: msms-peak-formula-annotation-matching
description: Use when comparing predicted formula annotations against expert-curated peak annotations on held-out MS/MS spectra (e.g., NIST20 scaffold-split test set) to score formula-level agreement of C2MS models such as FraGNNet, GrAFF-MS, or ICEBERG.

name: msms-peak-fragment-matching

name: msms-peak-intensity-coverage-analysis

description: Use when a raw MS/MS spectrum loaded from an MGF file must have low relative-intensity peaks removed via matchms, and you need the retained and filtered-out peak lists for inspection.

name: msms-peak-list-format-conversion
description: Use when raw MS/MS contest or experiment peak lists (precursor m/z plus fragment m/z-intensity pairs, possibly at several collision energies) must be restructured into MAGMa hierarchical input files before in silico candidate annotation.

name: msms-peak-list-processing
description: Use when LC-MS/MS runs in mzML or mzXML format must be converted into cleaned, feature-merged peak lists feeding molecular formula determination or structure annotation with SIRIUS 4 / COSMIC.

name: msms-peak-list-scoring

name: msms-precursor-mass-filtering
description: Use when cleaning raw MS/MS spectra prior to formula identification — e.g., converting m/z to monoisotopic Da via adduct correction and removing spurious precursor-adjacent and contamination peaks.

name: msms-precursor-mass-matching

name: msms-product-ion-intensity-normalization

name: msms-product-ion-quantification

name: msms-similarity-network-cluster-visualization

name: msms-similarity-scoring

name: msms-spectra-database-searching

name: msms-spectra-merging-and-renormalization
description: Use when two centroided MS/MS peak lists (m/z, intensity) must be combined into a merged spectrum AB to compute spectral entropy similarity, e.g. for library matching or compound identification scoring.

name: msms-spectra-merging-by-inchikey
description: Use when building a training set from MS/MS spectral libraries (e.g. NIST 17, MoNA) where the same compound appears in multiple spectra at different collision energies or instrument types, and a single unified input vector per compound is needed.

description: Use when several trained spectrum-prediction checkpoints (fragment-level and binned-vocabulary models) must be scored on identical held-out datasets to produce a fair, per-model accuracy table.

name: multi-model-machine-learning-comparison
description: Use when you must select a regression model for retention time prediction from several candidates and need quantitative comparison of training/test/validation errors and true-positive coverage within ±1 min windows to justify the choice.

name: multi-module-heterogeneity-quantification
description: Use when you have spot-level multi-module spatial data (transcript, metabolite, morphology) integrated by haCCA and need to demonstrate that the integrated view captures more heterogeneity than any single modality.

name: multi-omic-pathway-database-querying
description: Use when a paired spatial metabolomics + transcriptomics dataset (e.g. integrated Seurat object with MALDI and Visium assays) has per-cluster differential metabolite and gene results and you need regional pathway enrichment.

name: multi-omic-wnn-integration
description: Use when a paired SM (e.g. MALDI-TOF imzML) and ST (e.g. 10X Visium) dataset has been mapped onto common spatial units (spots/pixels) and unimodal clustering of one assay misses metabolically defined populations.

name: multi-omics-data-integration
description: Use when you have >=2 molecular abundance matrices measured on the same individuals and need a predictive, pathway-level multi-omics model that ranks pathways and quantifies each omics layer's contribution.

name: multi-omics-data-preprocessing
description: Use when raw DepMap/CCLE omics feature tables (CNV, mutations, methylation, histone PTMs, RNA, miRNA, lncRNA, proteomics, phosphoproteomics) must be cleaned and normalized before training per-metabolite ML models.

name: multi-omics-data-zero-filtering
description: Use when two or more omics abundance matrices must be harmonized before cross-omics correlation or network analysis, and raw matrices contain many zero (unmeasured) entries that would distort Spearman correlations.

name: multi-omics-de-count-validation
description: Use when processing concurrently generated untargeted metabolomic and lipidomic LC-MS/MS feature tables (e.g. from the Multi-ABLE method) through filtering, imputation, EigenMS normalization, and limma differential expression, then verifying reported DE feature counts at adjusted p < 0.05.

name: multi-omics-factor-analysis
description: Use when two or more standardized omics matrices (e.g. top-10%-most-variable DNAm beta values and creatinine-normalized urine metabolite intensities) need to be integrated into shared latent factors without a priori labels.

name: multi-omics-factor-literature-annotation
description: Use when a discriminant MOFA/DIABLO factor from BiomiX needs biological interpretation and you want literature-grounded annotation of its multi-omics contributor features via PubMed abstracts.

name: multi-omics-feature-importance-aggregation
description: Use when per-metabolite model feature importances exist across multiple omics feature sets (e.g., 9 feature sets x 225 metabolites) and the goal is a global, cross-omics top-regulator ranking.

name: multi-omics-integration-baseline-comparison
description: Use when a new multi-modal integration embedding (e.g., fused spatial transcriptomics + spatial metabolomics latent space) must be fairly ranked against published integration methods on the same AnnData inputs.

name: multi-omics-integration-embedding-quality-metrics
description: Use when comparing integration methods (e.g., SpatialMETA, totalVI, SpatialGLUE, MISO, Seurat v5 BNN, Stabmap, spaMultiVAE) on paired ST-SM samples and you need quantitative, ranked evidence of which method's joint embedding preserves spatial biology.

name: multi-omics-integrative-clustering
description: Use when you have independent clusterings (or per-dataset kernels) over the same set of observations from M omic platforms and need a single global clustering that down-weights noisy datasets, e.g. pan-cancer subtyping or transcriptional module discovery.

name: multi-omics-network-fusion
description: Use when two or more standardized sample-by-feature omics tables (e.g. buccal DNA methylation betas and urine metabolomics intensities) must be integrated into a fused sample similarity network to identify subject subgroups per cohort.

name: multi-omics-pathway-score-classification
description: Use when you have two or more molecular omics matrices measured on the same samples with an outcome label (e.g. COVID vs non-COVID or mild vs severe) and want predictive, interpretable multi-omics integration at the pathway level.

name: multi-omics-pathway-transformation
description: Use when you have two or more molecular abundance matrices (e.g. log-transformed metabolite and protein values with ChEBI/UniProt/Gene Symbol IDs) measured on the same individuals and need interpretable, pathway-level features for predictive multi-omics modelling.

name: multi-omics-predictive-modelling
description: Use when you have two or more omics data matrices measured on the same individuals (e.g. COPDgene plasma proteomics/metabolomics or the Su et al. 2020 COVID-19 data) and need supervised prediction plus pathway-level interpretation of the outcome.

name: multi-omics-regulation-classification
description: Use when you have paired transcriptomics and intracellular metabolomics data mapped onto a stoichiometric model and want to determine, per reaction, whether flux variation follows substrate abundance (metabolic), enzyme expression (transcriptional), both, or neither.

name: multi-omics-unit-variance-standardisation
description: Use when molecular abundance matrices from different omics layers (e.g. ChEBI-annotated metabolomics, UniProt proteomics, ENSEMBL transcriptomics) must be brought to a common scale prior to single-sample pathway analysis or pathway-based multi-omics model fitting.

name: multi-panel-figure-arrangement-cowplot
description: Use when separate ggplot2 plot objects (e.g. MS1 EIC trace, MS2 EIC trace, representative MS2 spectrum for one compound) must be vertically stacked into one publication-quality panel and exported to a PDF report.

name: multi-pipeline-draft-model-normalization
description: Use when draft GEMs from multiple reconstruction tools must be structurally compared or merged into a consensus, and reaction/metabolite/gene identifiers are in incompatible, self-defined namespaces (SBML from different pipelines).

name: multi-platform-data-augmentation
description: Use when you have feature tables from multiple separation methods (e.g., HILIC-Orbitrap MS in ESI+ and ESI− plus CE-Orbitrap MS) that need to be combined into one augmented multi-platform dataset for joint target/suspect counting or chemometric evaluation.

name: multi-platform-metabolomics-augmentation-analysis
description: Use when raw metabolomics data were acquired across multiple separation platforms (e.g., HILIC-MS plus CE-MS with different BGEs/ionization modes) and you need one augmented feature table and regulation-call matrix instead of separate per-platform results.

name: multi-platform-metabolomics-data-fusion
description: Use when two or more normalized platform-specific metabolomics tables (e.g., an MS table and an NMR table) cover the same biological samples and you need expanded metabolome coverage in one fused feature table.

name: multi-relation-edge-integration
description: Use when four metabolite association edge lists (biochemical, structural, spectral, correlation) must be combined into a single network and overlapping edges between the same metabolite pairs need type-resolved deduplication.

name: multi-sample-outlier-detection-via-spectral-similarity
description: Use when pre-processing a multi-sample MALDI MSI dataset and you need to automatically detect samples whose spectra deviate from the spectral similarity expected across samples before downstream analysis.

name: multi-score-adjacency-comparison
description: Use when mgf LC–MS/MS feature spectra need a quantitative heatmap readout of ms2deepscore similarities with modified cosine and spec2vec adjacency overlays to guide local threshold adjustment or replace network views for small node selections.

name: multi-seed-benchmark-aggregation
description: Use when a benchmark comparison (e.g., spectrum-prediction cosine scores across multiple models and data splits) must be repeated over multiple random seeds and reported as mean ± std to demonstrate stability of a claim.

name: multi-seed-ensemble-variance-estimation
description: Use when training a RankNet-type pairwise retention-order model where single-seed predictions are noisy, and you need an interpretable uncertainty estimate (prediction variance) to mark distinguishable vs indistinguishable molecular pairs.

name: multi-site-derivatization-mass-accounting
description: Use when annotating MALDI-MSI peaks from a derivatizing matrix (e.g. FMP-10) and the analyte has multiple taggable functional groups, so single- and double-derivatized species (forms A and B) must be mass-predicted separately.

name: multi-software-lipid-annotation-corroboration-analysis
description: Use when a MZmine feature table has been annotated by multiple lipid identification tools (e.g., LipidMatch, MS-DIAL, Greazy) and you need to measure cross-software agreement of fatty acyl constituent assignments per polarity.

name: multi-source-annotation-fusion
description: Use when you have per-feature candidate lists from several spectral/compound annotation sources and must reduce them to a single, source-supported chemical structure (SMILES) per feature for downstream network or reporting steps.

name: multi-source-chemical-set-intersection
description: Use when several spectral libraries (e.g., .MGF, .MSP files from GNPS, MoNA, MassBank, MS-Dial) have been harmonized and you need to know what fraction of unique compounds is shared vs. exclusive to each source.

name: multi-spectrum-fragmentation-overlap-assessment
description: Use when several MS/MS spectra from an .mgf file (e.g. a feature group of interest) must be compared for shared fragment m/z bins and neutral losses, beyond what a single mirror plot or pairwise similarity score can reveal.

name: multi-task-loss-debugging
description: Use when training or restoring ESP MLP/GNN models with multi-task LDA topic prediction and peak-correlation label mixing enabled, and forward/backward passes or output shapes must be validated.

name: multi-tissue-metabolomics-group-comparison
description: Use when a metabolomics feature table has many biological groups (e.g. 14 tissues) and the goal is to identify features dramatically enriched in one group versus all others at a strict FDR threshold (e.g. P<0.001, >1000-fold change).

name: multi-tool-annotation-comparison
description: Use when two or more annotation tools (e.g. mWISE and xMSannotator) must be compared on identical LC-MS peak lists with known compound ground truth, to rank tools by sensitivity, F1, and structural closeness of proposals.

name: multi-tool-annotation-table-construction
description: Use when you have multi-annotated tandem MS/MS features — GNPS FBMN, Sirius 6 structure_identifications.tsv, and ISDB-LOTUS/CFM-ID results — and need per-feature match scores and cross-tool structural similarity indicators for prioritization.

name: multi-tool-export-format-normalization
description: Use when a metabolomics feature table exported from XCMS, MS-DIAL, MZmine, Compound Discoverer, or Progenesis QI must be loaded into MetaboReport and needs tool-specific header conventions normalized into the features-in-rows/samples-in-columns csv layout.

name: multi-tool-performance-comparison
description: Use when comparing computational efficiency (runtime, memory) of network-construction implementations across R packages on identical inputs, or when validating performance claims for a new package against established baselines.

name: multi-tool-prediction-overlap-analysis
description: Use when you need to compare BGC prediction counts and set overlap between DeepBGC, antiSMASH, and ClusterFinder on a common genome panel to expose differences in detection stringency.

name: multi-tracer-sirm-dataset-deconvolution
description: Use when MS isotopologue profiles from single- or multi-isotope SIRM experiments must be decomposed into moiety abundances (e.

name: multiassayexperiment-data-preprocessing
description: Use when starting from a raw table of metabolite measurements plus metabolite (rowData) and sample (colData) metadata, and you need a clean, normalized MultiAssayExperiment object before differential metabolomic testing.

name: multiassayexperiment-data-slot-management
description: Use when building or evolving a MetaboDiff MultiAssayExperiment object and you need to track raw, knn-imputed, and variance-stabilized assay slots side-by-side for QC or downstream differential analysis.

name: multiassayexperiment-metadata-extraction
description: Use when a MetaboDiff analysis is stored in a MultiAssayExperiment object and you need colData group labels or the t-test results stored in the metadata slot to identify differentially abundant metabolites.

name: multiassayexperiment-statistics-extraction
description: Use when a MetaboDiff analysis has produced a MultiAssayExperiment object and you need the per-metabolite p-values, Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values, and difference-in-means (dm) for downstream tables or volcano plots.

name: multiblock-pls-regression-modeling
description: Use when you have two or more sample-aligned LC-MS feature-intensity tables (e.g. HPOS/LPOS/LNEG or multi-assay serum assays) and a numeric outcome (continuous bilirubin levels or encoded biological sex) to predict jointly across blocks.

name: multicriteria-processing-workflow-ranking
description: Use when a metabolomics peak table (e.g., MTBLS656 plasma time-course LC-MS data with T0–T48 labels) must be processed and the optimal combination of filtering/imputation, QCS correction, transformation, and normalization methods is unknown and study-dependent.

name: multidimensional-assignment-optimization
description: Use when aligning untargeted LC-MS feature lists (m/z, RT, area CSVs) across multiple runs with nonlinear RT drift, where nearest-neighbor or bipartite matching yields ambiguous or inaccurate consensus features and a global non-centric optimum is needed.

name: multidimensional-feature-matching
description: Use when aligning detected features across LC-IMS-MS/MS samples where m/z, drift time, and retention time must all be matched to achieve high-confidence feature correspondence between samples.

name: multidimensional-local-maximum-peak-picking
description: Use when raw LC-IMS-MS/MS data (mzML) has been loaded into a common m/z, drift time, retention time, intensity grid and you need to locate ion peaks in 3D without sequential 1D/2D processing that would yield only ~13% cross-sample intersection.

name: multidimensional-nmr-processing
description: Use when input is a time-domain multi-dimensional NMR FID dataset (possibly NUS-sampled, e.g. an NUScon Protein A HNCACB with 8.8% sampling schedule) and the goal is a processed, reconstructed 3D spectrum in NV format.

name: multidimensional-peak-detection
description: Use when detecting features in high-dimensional LC-IMS-MS/MS data (e.g. example_data.h5 from an Agilent 6560) and you need to leverage the full m/z–drift time–retention time space simultaneously rather than processing dimension-by-dimension.

name: multigroup-anova-hypothesis-testing
description: Use when a numerical measurement column has more than two groups (e.g. a 'Condition' column) and the goal is a multi-group comparison — either ANOVA (parametric) or Kruskal-Wallis (non-parametric) — with the p-value annotated on the chart.

name: multilabel-neural-network-training
description: Use when MS/MS spectra (binned peak vectors) must be mapped to a full compound fingerprint vector simultaneously, or when a per-digit/per-block multi-model setup is undesirable.

name: multilayer-metabolic-subnetwork-retrieval
description: Use when you have completed KGMN network reconstruction (reconstructNetwork1/2/3) on MetDNA2 output and need to extract, inspect, or merge the three-layer subnetwork for a specific peak pair or centric metabolite (e.g. M182T541–M262T526).

name: multimatrix-outlier-detection-machine-learning
description: Use when a set of natural extracts needs prioritization for spectral dissimilarity: a MEMO vectorized dissimilarity matrix (e.g. Celastraceae_memomatrix.csv) is available and the Similarity Component of Inventa's priority rank must be computed from MS2 spectral fingerprints.

name: multimetric-pattern-ranking
description: Use when you have mined fragmentation patterns from an MS/MS collection and a GNPS molecular network, and need to select which patterns explain each detected component.

name: multimodal-image-overlay-visualization
description: Use when an MSI composite/cluster image must be upscaled to match the pixel dimensions of a co-registered H&E stain for side-by-side or overlay visualization, and an interpolation method must be chosen.

name: multimodal-molecule-featurisation-for-llm-training
description: Use when SMILES strings from a metabolite instruction-tuning dataset (e.g. HMDB-derived JSON keyed {SMILES String: [[Question, Answer], ...]}) must be featurised into molecular graphs and molecular images before GNN/CNN encoding for LLM training.

name: multimodal-msi-ifm-image-registration
description: Use when consecutive tissue sections have been measured by MALDI MSI and stained/IFM-imaged, and the IFM cell-type masks (e.g., urothelium markers) must be warped into the MSI pixel frame to assign lipids to cell populations.

name: multimodal-registration-preprocessing-of-3d-msi
description: Use when you have a reconstructed multi-section 3D MSI dataset whose serial sections are misaligned and you need contrast-rich 'feature' images to register them to an MRI/atlas (e.g. rat brain coronal/sagittal sections).

name: multimodal-spectra-image-rendering
description: Use when an already-processed 2D or pseudo-3D NMR spectrum needs interactive contour visualization, a pseudo-3D surface-mesh rendering, or exported publication-style images of both without any local software installation.

name: multimodal-transformer-fine-tuning
description: Use when a pre-trained MMST model fails to correctly predict structures for a set of molecules (out-of-distribution chemical space, e.g. PubChem sets) and analogues plus simulated spectra can be generated to recover predictions.

name: multimode-elution-profile-alignment
description: Use when processing a batch of GC×GC–MS samples in GcDUO where a feature's retention-2 elution profile shifts between samples and you need per-sample peak areas/intensities without forcing rigid tri-linearity.

name: multinomial-distribution-isotopologue-sampling
description: Use when a user-defined chemical formula (e.g., glucose, penicillin) needs theoretical isotopic fine structures at a specified SIP atom% enrichment, especially where FFT-based envelope methods miss fine structure.

name: multinomial-isotopologue-distribution-computation
description: Use when correcting measured fractional abundances of isotopologs (FAM) to mass distribution vectors (MDV) and you need the theoretical natural-abundance + isotopic-impurity correction matrix for a compound of known formula and a specified tracer (e.g., U-13C6 glucose).

name: multiomic-class-assignment-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when you need to quantify class-assignment accuracy of a CCS calibration tool on multiomic TWIM-MS data (NIST SRM 1950, CCS Compendium references) or compare that accuracy against IMSCal and a single power law calibration.

name: multiomic-feature-annotation
description: Use when a traveling-wave IM-MS feature table (m/z, charge, retention time, arrival time) contains unidentified small-molecule, lipid, and peptide features from a mixed multiomic mixture and class-specific TWCCSN2 values are needed without prior identification.

name: multiomic-feature-classification
description: Use when you have singly charged feature arrival times from TWIM-MS (e.g., Waters SYNAPT XS) with computed class-specific TWCCSN2 calibration parameters, and you must assign each unknown feature to a biomolecular class without prior identification.

name: multiomic-feature-importance-comparison
description: Use when top features from models trained on one dataset (e.g. CCLE-trained metabolite predictors) must be validated in an independent dataset by comparing their feature-importance distribution against that of the full feature set.

name: multiomic-feature-metabolite-overlap-quantification
description: Use when validating ML metabolite models: given top predictor features per metabolite (e.g. from Metab8D_network.xlsx) and the Recon3D model, to compute the fraction of predictors mapping to the metabolite's reactions or one-step neighbors.

name: multiomic-feature-table-processing
description: Use when you have singly charged features from Waters SYNAPT XS traveling-wave IM-MS data spanning small molecules, lipids, and peptides, and need class-assigned calibrated CCS values without prior identification.

name: multiomic-power-law-curve-selection
description: Use when processing multiomic TWIM-MS data on Waters instruments where unknown features must be assigned to small molecule, lipid, or peptide calibrations and calibrated CCS values computed without prior identification.

name: multiomics-feature-set-benchmarking
description: Use when a study has matched multiomic feature tables and a metabolite abundance matrix for the same samples (e.g. CCLE cell lines), and the goal is to determine which omics class most accurately predicts metabolomic variation.

name: multipartite-graph-construction-from-feature-lists
description: Use when aligning features across multiple LC-MS runs from CSV feature tables (m/z, RT, area columns) where nearest-neighbor matching is insufficient and all potential inter-run correspondences must be jointly considered in a graph structure.

name: multiple-comparison-significance-filtering
description: Use when you have a binary presence/absence detection matrix across cohort samples and need to identify statistically significant co-detection pairs (e.g., parent compounds vs. their CMDN-annotated metabolites) among many tested pairs.

name: multiple-correspondence-analysis
description: Use when behavioral questionnaire items are categorical (e.g., CBCL item scores) and you need to reduce them to a few underlying dimensions and quantify per-dimension explained variance.

name: multiple-kernel-learning-clustering
description: Use when several omic data layers over the same N samples have been converted to per-layer N x N kernel/consensus matrices and you need an integrative clustering whose per-dataset weights reveal which layers carry the cluster structure.

name: multiple-regression-egfr-creatinine-association
description: Use when a targeted LC-MS metabolomics feature (e.g. creatinine) must be validated against an external clinical trait (CKD-EPI/eGFR, clinical routine creatinine) to check whether batch correction improves the biological signal.

name: multiple-testing-adjustment-metabolomics
description: Use when a metabolomics abundance matrix (metabolites x samples, control vs mutant groups) yields per-metabolite p-values, or when Fisher's Exact Test pathway hits must be judged against an adjusted p-value cutoff of 0.05.

name: multiple-testing-bh-correction
description: Use when thousands of genes are tested simultaneously for differential expression between sample groups (e.g. tumor vs non-tumor) and raw Mann–Whitney U or other per-gene P-values must be corrected for multiple testing before filtering.

name: multiple-testing-bonferroni-correction
description: Use when calling significant parent–adduct ion pairs from massdiff/corrPairsMSI output — i.e. when each candidate pair's Pearson p-value must be judged against a family-wise threshold to avoid false adduct calls.

name: multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when a feature-by-feature univariate test (e.g. t-test or Wilcoxon rank-sum between tumor and normal groups) has been run on many metabolomics features and p-values must be adjusted before reporting differential metabolites or rendering volcano plots.

name: multiple-testing-correction-fdr
description: Use when a metabolomics or proteomics feature table (CSV) has been tested feature-by-feature (t-test/ANOVA, or covariate-adjusted limma/ANCOVA models) and the resulting raw p-values must be FDR-corrected to define significant feature sets.

name: multiple-testing-correction-function-implementation
description: Use when you need Meff estimates for eigen-analysis-based multiple testing correction: you have M correlated tests (e.g., metabolites) and a Pearson correlation matrix, and must compute effective numbers of tests for p-value adjustment as in DisCo P-ad.

name: multiple-testing-correction-simulation
description: Use when evaluating whether an alternative correlation matrix (e.g., Spearman's rank correlation) improves or matches eigen-analysis-based Meff estimates in a simulation scenario such as a small sample size (n=100).

name: multiple-testing-correction-statistics
description: Use when comparing two cell groups (e.g. +FA benign vs +FA+IL17A inflammatory steatotic hepatocytes) across hundreds of metabolites in a per-cell matrix and uncorrected p-values would inflate false positives.

name: multiple-testing-fdr-control
description: Use when a pathway-level test yields one p-value per pathway across many tested pathways (e.g., NetGSA, DEGraph, CAMERA, Pathway-Express) and you must adjust for multiplicity with FDR q-values before calling pathways dysregulated.

name: multiple-testing-fdr-correction
description: Use when a limma linear model has been fit per metabolite across a large-scale metabolomics cohort (e.g. BioHEART-CT plasma samples) and you need adjusted p-values to call significant hypertension-associated metabolites.

name: multiple-testing-fdr-correction
description: Use when testing many metabolite classes/subclasses simultaneously for overrepresentation among a subset of annotations (e.g. METASPACE-ML-exclusive hits) and you need multiplicity-controlled q-values rather than raw p-values.

name: multiple-testing-fdr-correction
description: Use when testing thousands of metabolic features or dozens of KEGG pathways for significance (e.g., volcano-plot differential testing with Log2FC > 1.5, or hypergeometric MSEA), where uncorrected p-values would yield inflated false positives.

name: multiple-testing-p-value-adjustment
description: Use when you run univariate statistical tests (t-test, ANOVA, Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis) over each metabolite/protein feature of a preprocessed feature matrix and need p-values adjusted for the large number of simultaneous tests.

name: multiple-testing-padjust-correction
description: Use when a metabolite abundance table (e.g. from Metabolomics Workbench study ST000915) has been tested per metabolite between two groups and raw p-values must be adjusted before calling significantly altered metabolites.

name: multiple-testing-pvalue-correction
description: Use when a feature-by-sample quantification table (e.g., from MZmine2 with row ID, row m/z, row retention time, peak area) is annotated with bioassay values per LC-MS/MS fraction and per-feature correlation significance is needed before mapping onto molecular networks.

name: multipletesting-bonferroni-correction
description: Use when many spatial correlation tests (e.g. Pearson tests over all parent–adduct ion pairs from massdiff objects) are run simultaneously and per-pair p-values must be thresholded to avoid false-positive adduct assignments.

name: multiplexed-injection-peak-spacing-analysis
description: Use when annotating peaks in multiplexed MSI-CE-MS data where serial injections produce evenly spaced peak segments, and MTI-predicted migration times need confirmation or reanalysis of mis-annotated segments.

name: multiplexed-protein-image-processing
description: Use when raw IMC ROI image stacks (multi-channel, metal-isotope antibody channels) from the scSpaMet raw data deposit need noise removal and intensity normalization before segmentation, registration, or VAE joint embedding.

name: multiplexed-spectrum-deconvolution
description: Use when SWATH-MS-based untargeted metabolomics yields multiplexed MS/MS spectra with co-eluted, unresolved fragment-ion chromatographic peaks that must be deconvolved into metabolite-specific MS2 spectra.

name: multiprocess-cpu-parallel-preprocessing
description: Use when large collections of raw MGF MS/MS spectra must be parsed and preprocessed (precursor-peak removal, peak filtering, L2 normalization) before clustering, and preprocessing time is a bottleneck.

name: multisample-ion-correlation-analysis
description: Use when processing multisample DIA-MS/SWATH acquisitions where coeluting low-abundance compounds produce mixed fragment spectra, and quantitative ion correlations across samples can be exploited to separate them.

name: multitask-neural-network-training
description: Use when paired microbiome-metabolome data (e.g. samples x microbial features plus samples x 8848 metabolite features) are available and metabolites should be predicted jointly rather than one-by-one, especially when many metabolites are unannotated.

name: multithreaded-wall-clock-timing-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking a parallel raw-data-processing implementation (e.g. LSH signal classification on MS1 TimsTOF frames) to quantify how wall-clock time changes with thread count and find the point where speedups saturate.

name: multivariate-adjustment-direction-of-effect-analysis
description: Use when biomarker effect estimates may change sign after multivariate adjustment for correlated immune-metabolic covariates, and you must reproduce or verify direction-of-effect changes (e.g., sign flips for XXL-VLDL-L or isoleucine) alongside partial-correlation structure.

name: multivariate-anova-across-metabolite-columns
description: Use when the input is a preprocessed metabolomics concentration table (samples as rows, metabolite columns, a group/factor column) and per-metabolite significance testing across two or more sample groups is the goal.

name: multivariate-biomarker-feature-extraction
description: Use when input is two-dimensional MS map data (m/z vs retention time) from GC–MS or LC–MS and the goal is to identify and visualize multivariate marker features without conventional peak picking, e.g. untargeted metabolomics of aroma odor or human breath.

name: multivariate-chemomarker-feature-identification
description: Use when raw two-dimensional MS maps (m/z vs retention time) from GC–MS or LC–MS must be characterized, analytes discriminated, and multivariate chemo-/biomarker features identified and visualized without a peak picking stage.

name: multivariate-feature-standardization
description: Use when a numerical feature matrix has columns on heterogeneous scales (e.g. iris-like morphological measurements) and PCA, clustering or another scikit-learn-based activity is about to be run on the raw columns.

name: multivariate-gaussian-simulation
description: Use when you need controlled simulated data that preserves the empirical multivariate correlation structure of a real metabolite abundance matrix (e.g., to compute permutation-based effective number of tests, Meff0, across sample sizes n=100/500/1000).

name: multivariate-linear-regression-model-training
description: Use when you have an assembled experimental lipid database (e.g., m/z, CCS, HILIC retention time entries across lipid classes) with gaps in chemical space and need to train regression models to predict CCS or HILIC retention times for unseen lipid species.

name: multivariate-metabolomics-feature-prioritization
description: Use when both feature-wise tests (with FDR-adjusted q-values) and a multivariate importance model (e.g., MUVR RF ranks) have already been produced for the same feature table, and the goal is to prioritize features for metabolite identification.

name: multivariate-model-validation
description: Use when a supervised multivariate model (e.g. OPLS-DA) has separated sample classes (carriage vs controls) and you must quantify its diagnostic performance with ROC AUC values and confidence intervals.

name: multivariate-normal-data-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking missing-value imputation methods on high-dimensional metabolomics-like matrices and you need replicated simulated data with known true values, specified correlation structure, and controlled MNAR/MAR missingness for RMSE evaluation.

name: multivariate-normal-sampling
description: Use when a benchmark needs a fully-observed synthetic data matrix with realistic covariance and group structure, e.g., to evaluate imputation methods under controlled MNAR masking before injecting missing values.

name: multivariate-ordination-input-preparation
description: Use when you have an aggregated peak-area table from GC-MS library hits (e.g. mzExacto output) and need standardized, statistically comparable component areas for downstream ordination or modeling.

name: multivariate-ordination-visualization
description: Use when a standardized GC-MS compound-area matrix (areas relative to internal/external standards) must be ordinated with NMDS and the between-treatment significance pattern checked against a published manual-peak-annotation analysis.

name: multivariate-outlier-detection
description: Use when a post-curation feature data matrix plus pooled/intrastudy QC injections are available and you need to verify curation quality, spot outliers, QC clustering, or time-related signal drift before statistical analysis.

name: multivariate-qc-plot-visualization
description: Use when a metabolomics/lipidomics sequence contains regularly injected QCpool samples and you must identify outlying or out-of-control samples that univariate plots miss, before outlier removal in the QComics sequential workflow.

name: multivariate-scores-plot-visualization
description: Use when a feature table has vastly more features than samples and you need to assess whether a supervised classifier (OPLS-DA) overfits by comparing in-sample R²Y against cross-validated Q²Y with a scores plot.

name: multivariate-statistical-analysis
description: Use when a pre-processed (batch-corrected, log-transformed, standardised) ICP-MS ionome table of ion concentrations needs exploratory multivariate analysis: variance decomposition, element-element correlation networks, or clustered correlation heat maps.

name: multivariate-statistical-plotting
description: Use when you have a raw and a QC-RFSC-corrected metabolomics/proteomics intensity matrix and need PCA score plots to visually verify tighter QC-sample clustering or restored biological group separation (e.g. Figure 3B/3C style).

name: multivariate-vs-univariate-diagnostic-performance-comparison
description: Use when a supervised multivariate model (e.g. OPLS-DA) is claimed to outperform single markers, and per-feature AUCs plus the model-level AUC are available for a head-to-head ROC comparison.

name: multiview-contrastive-learning-for-metabolite-annotation
description: Use when ranking candidate molecular structures for MS/MS query spectra on MassSpecGym-style data, particularly when multiple spectra per molecule are available to build a consensus-spectrum view.

name: multiview-contrastive-model-inference
description: Use when you have preprocessed MS/MS spectra (formSpec with subformula labels or binnedSpec) plus a candidate molecule list (by mass or formula) and need ranked candidate structures using the pretrained MVP checkpoint.

name: mummichog-metabolite-set-library-assembly
description: Use when rebuilding, updating, or locally reproducing MetaboAnalyst/MetaboAnalystR compound, pathway, or metabolite-set libraries (e.g. after an HMDB release), or when verifying reported library scale metrics.

name: mummichog-network-activity-prediction
description: Use when you have two m/z feature lists — a significant list selected by univariate statistics and a reference list of all detected features — and need to infer pathway/module activity without metabolite identification.

name: mummichog-pathway-activity-prediction
description: Use when you have an LC-MS peak table (m/z features) and optionally an MS2-annotated compound list from untargeted metabolomics, and need pathway-level functional interpretation without requiring full compound identification upfront.

name: mummichog-pathway-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have LC-MS1 feature tables (from raw mzML processing) and/or MS2-based compound identifications and need pathway enrichment/functional interpretation of untargeted metabolomics data.

name: munkres-optimal-domain-matching
description: Use when computing pairwise distances between biosynthetic gene clusters with differing numbers of Pfam domains per type, and you need an optimal, non-quadratic one-to-one domain assignment to score sequence similarity and copy-number differences.

name: murcko-histogram-disjoint-scaffold-splitting
description: Use when fine-tuning or evaluating spectral models (DreaMS, MIST, MS2DeepScore) on paired spectrum–structure data and you must guarantee no training molecule shares a Murcko scaffold with test molecules.

name: murcko-scaffold-extraction
description: Use when evaluating de-novo structure recommendations from MS/MS spectra: to verify that generated SMILES recover the key molecular substructures (Murcko scaffolds and functional groups) of the ground-truth test compounds.

name: murcko-scaffold-extraction
description: Use when a de novo MS/MS generation pipeline requires per-molecule scaffold identities: building an oracle scaffold lookup table, constructing the scaffold candidate set for contrastive retrieval, or checking scaffold coverage.

name: murcko-scaffold-stratified-train-test-splitting
description: Use when preparing CCSBase (16,989 raw CCS values, 22 datasets, 6,744 distinct molecules) or METLIN-CCS dumps for model benchmarking and you need train/test splits that keep scaffold space shared across both partitions.

name: mutual-information-estimation
description: Use when you need a non-linear similarity measure between pairs of expression features (e.g., gene rows x sample columns in a numeric matrix) where Pearson/Spearman correlation is insufficient.

name: mutual-information-multimodal-matching
description: Use when consecutive tissue sections were measured by MALDI MSI and IFM and the cell-marker masks from microscopy must be warped into the MSI pixel frame without manual landmarks.

name: mutual-rank-correlation-analysis
description: Use when integrating paired transcriptomic–metabolomic datasets (e.g., tomato samples from Jeon 2020) to find mass features correlated with biosynthetic genes without a prior 'bait', before clustering mass feature–transcript networks.

name: mutual-top-k-edge-filtering
description: Use when you have many MS/MS spectra (mzXML/mzML) and need to build a molecular network of related consensus spectra, keeping only the strongest mutual spectrum-to-spectrum matches rather than the full all-vs-all graph.

name: mwas-skyline-plot-visualization
description: Use when MWAS results (association/p-value matrix for a phenotype such as BMI) are available for 1H NMR metabonomic data and you need to visualize which spectral regions (ppm windows) carry significant associations.

name: mwtab-conversion-example-reproduction
description: Use when a validated MESSES JSON representation must be converted to mwTab JSON deposition format, or when reproduction of the documented conversion_directives examples is required to verify directive semantics.

name: mwtab-format-conversion
description: Use when a messy tabular metabolomics dataset (Excel/CSV, e.g. MS or NMR experiment metadata) must be transformed into mwTab format for Metabolomics Workbench deposition after MESSES extract and validate steps.

name: mwtab-format-metadata-validation
description: Use when a tabular metabolomics dataset has already been extracted to MESSES JSON and must be checked for schema conformance before mwTab conversion and Metabolomics Workbench deposition.

name: mwtab-format-parsing
description: Use when input files are Metabolomics Workbench mwTab-format or JSONized analysis files (or ANxxxxxx analysis IDs) that must be tokenized into MWTabFile objects, converted between formats, or schema-validated.

name: mwtab-json-structure-mapping
description: Use when a validated MESSES JSON representation of tagged experimental metadata (MS or NMR) must be transformed into mwTab JSON deposition format, using conversion directives with value_type str, matrix, or section.

name: mwtab-jsonized-roundtrip-consistency-comparison
description: Use when auditing Metabolomics Workbench analyses that have both 'mwTab' and JSON data files, to determine which pairs are consistent and which mismatch, and to catalog the affected analysis IDs.

name: mysql-database-loading
description: Reference for recreating the RaMP MySQL schema locally: you have parsed HMDB/KEGG/Reactome/WikiPathways source data into SQL files and need a populated MySQL instance queryable via RMySQL.

name: mysql-relational-database-querying
description: Use when an analysis needs structured pathway/analyte membership data stored in a MySQL dump (e.g., RaMP's inst/extdata dump) and must be queried programmatically in R for batch queries or overlap computations.

name: mz-axis-binning-uniform-dimension
description: Use when raw SpiderMass mass spectra (m/z, intensity pairs) have variable lengths and must become a fixed-dimension feature matrix (0.1-Da bins, TIC >= 1e4) for deep model input.

name: mz-bin-discretization
description: Use when building training targets for per-fragment or per-bin MS/MS prediction models from multiple experimental spectra per compound, or when a presence/absence (binary) peak representation at 0.01 m/z resolution is required instead of raw intensities.

name: mz-bin-discretization-of-mass-spectra
description: Use when a training spectrum (or predicted output) must be represented as a dense per-bin intensity vector — e.g. to regress spectra directly from ECFP features in the NEIMS forward-prediction MLP.

name: mz-binning-peak-alignment
description: Use when mass spectra from separate MSI/SCMS acquisitions (e.g. imzML peak lists) must be compared across runs but mass shift between instruments or sections may misalign nominal features — bin before matching, clustering, or cross-annotation.

name: mz-channel-variation-filtering
description: Use when deconvolving untargeted GC × GC–MS blobs (e.g., from CDF files loaded into a GcDUO object) where PARAFAC must be run on a reduced m/z dimension because full m/z ranges (e.g., 35–440) are dominated by uninformative channels.

name: mz-data-extraction-from-hdf5
description: Use when spectra from a converted MZA (HDF5) file need to be read programmatically — e.g., extracting per-scan m/z and intensity arrays from Arrays_mz/Arrays_intensity, or loading mzbins and Full_mz_array for ion mobility data — as the first step before calibration or peak finding.

name: mz-database-annotation
description: Use when a metabolomics analysis has produced a list of significant m/z values (e.g. t-test hits such as 264, 308, 441, 561 m/z) that need putative compound identities and MSI confidence-level assignment.

name: mz-decimal-precision-binning
description: Use when processed matchms Spectrum objects must be turned into Word2Vec documents for Spec2Vec training, i.e. after metadata cleaning and peak filtering but before training the Word2Vec model with gensim.

name: mz-decimal-precision-formatting
description: Use when a spectrum must be converted from a raw ion list or 'm/z:intensity' string into the canonical single-line form (integer intensities 0–100, 6-decimal m/z, zero-intensity ions kept) before hashing it to a SPLASH identifier.

name: mz-decimal-truncation-binning
description: Use when building or reproducing LipiDetective's transformer input encoding: MS2 peak lists (m/z + intensity) from base-peak-normalized spectra must be converted to embedding tokens with m/z precision fixed by config decimal_accuracy.

name: mz-difference-count-matrix-construction
description: Use when aligning two tandem MS (MS/MS) spectra whose fragment ion m/z values do not coincide exactly and whose precursor neutral losses differ, requiring a pair-specific similarity measure between fragment ions.

name: mz-difference-edge-label-interpretation
description: Use when fragmentation-graph patterns from mineMS2 must be chemically annotated: each edge label is a discretized m/z difference (14–200 Da) whose candidate neutral formulas must be generated and interpreted.

name: mz-dimension-cube-linking
description: Use when filtered per-group feature tables from different separation platforms (e.g., HILIC-MS ESI+/ESI- and CE-MS via the nanoCEasy interface) must be fused into a single augmented 'm/z @Time, Group' feature space for joint chemometric evaluation.

name: mz-error-feature-contribution-quantification
description: Use when a trained METASPACE-ML GBDT ranking model and its candidate-annotation feature matrix are available and the goal is to attribute the prediction score back to individual ion features, especially to check whether rho_spectral or the m/z error features dominate target-decoy separation.

name: mz-feature-significance-testing
description: Use when a raw untargeted metabolomics feature table of thousands of spectral features (e.g. 5,707 or 7,995 peaks) must be reduced to a significant list for downstream pathway/network analysis, and feature selection is the upstream step.

name: mz-feature-to-metabolite-matching
description: Use when you have an untargeted LC/MS feature table (m/z, retention time, p-value) and need to map m/z features to candidate metabolites — including ambiguous one-to-many matches — as input to pathway/network activity prediction.

name: mz-integer-quantization
description: Use when preparing m/z array data for lossless integer-based compression (e.g. ZDPD, ZDVB, Stack-ZDPD) or when a controlled-precision integer representation of m/z values must be derived from floating-point spectra.

name: mz-intensity-alignment
description: Use when replicate mass spectra have non-identical, irregularly-spaced m/z values and must be placed into one comparable data frame (m/z column plus per-replicate intensity columns) before averaging, normalization, or subtraction.

name: mz-intensity-dataframe-manipulation
description: Use when handling irregularly-spaced MALDI-MS or ESI-MS replicate spectra as plain R data frames — m/z in column 1, intensities in adjacent columns — for blank subtraction, replicate averaging, or pre-processing without S3/S4 wrappers.

name: mz-intensity-range-integration
description: Use when you have MALDI-ToF-MS spectra (e.g., Bruker .fid converted to mzML) acquired at many target points and need total ion counts for specific m/z ranges per sample for screening.

name: mz-matching-threshold-tuning
description: Use when merging two peak-picked untargeted LC–MS metabolomics feature tables (e.g., from XCMS) where datasets were processed identically but run in different batches or cohorts, and you must decide RT, MZ, and FI tolerance windows before aligning features.

name: mz-offset-histogram-detection
description: Use when LC-HRMS feature lists (m/z + retention time) from different measurement sequences or batches need correction for systematic m/z shifts relative to a reference before alignment.

name: mz-peak-count-threshold-filtering
description: Use when curating spectra for a model with fixed input capacities (e.g. peak counts or SMILES length) and you must exclude out-of-range records from test libraries such as NIST, SWGDRUG, Cayman, or MONA.

name: mz-peak-spatial-colocalisation-analysis
description: Use when a spatial metabolomics image (e.g. imzML MALDI dataset) must be segmented into anatomical regions and m/z peaks assigned to those regions — e.g. urothelium/lamina propria/muscle in the murine bladder — with significant DEMs reported.

name: mz-range-bin-interval-construction
description: Use when MS/MS spectra (already filtered: <0.1% max-intensity peaks removed, ≤1000 peaks, square-root transformed intensities) must be converted into fixed-width numerical vectors as input to the MS2DeepScore base network.

name: mz-ratio-filtered-metabolite-structure-prediction
description: Use when an unknown metabolite peak (e.g., m/z = 270.3 from metabolomic profiling of the MAA pathway) needs a candidate structure inferred from known reactions, atom/bond encodings, and mass constraints.

name: mz-retention-time-annotation-handling
description: Use when a targeted LC–MS metabolomics or lipidomics workflow starts from a user-authored target file (.xlsx/.csv) that must be parsed into a data frame with identifier, name, m/z, expected RT and ion polarity before peak integration.

name: mz-retention-time-peak-matching
description: Use when LC-MS metabolomics data (mzXML, .raw, .d) must be screened for a predefined target list of known compounds using their m/z and retention times with explicit tolerances, and S/N ratios per target are required.

name: mz-rt-ccs-tolerance-filtering
description: Use when analyzing aligned, peak-picked HILIC-IM-MS feature tables (positive/negative ESI) and every feature must receive a lipid annotation at the highest confidence level supported by m/z, retention time, and CCS agreement.

name: mz-rt-correspondence-matching
description: Use when multiple per-sample peak lists from LC-MS runs must be merged into a single master peak list by matching peaks within user-defined m/z and retention-time tolerances, e.g. for benchmarking alignment methods.

name: mz-rt-molecular-annotation
description: Use when detected LC-MS features need putative compound identities (MSI level 2), e.g. annotating rosmarinic acid, urocanate, or sphingosines before spatial mapping in 'ili.

name: mz-rt-pair-alignment
description: Use when two or more HRMS feature lists (m/z–RT pairs with peak areas, e.g., exported from MSS, MSDIAL, or XCMS on the same .mzML files) must be matched by proximity in retention-time and m/z space to compute shared-feature counts or overlap fractions.

name: mz-rt-pair-matching-in-qc-samples
description: Use when monitoring specific compounds (e.g. tryptophan, calibrant, contaminants) in pooled/long-term QC samples across batches, or when you need per-file intensity/RT/peak-shape diagnostics from untargeted metabolomics acquisitions.

name: mz-rt-shift-correspondence-matching
description: Use when multiple LC-HRMS metabolomics files exhibit m/z and retention time shifts relative to a reference chromatogram and corresponding ions of metabolites must be aligned into one data matrix.

name: mz-rt-targeted-feature-verification
description: Use when a comparative statistical result flags specific m/z values (e.g. hacl-1-enriched features) and you must confirm the raw chromatographic evidence — presence/absence and intensity in each genotype/diet group — by direct EIC inspection at known m/z and RT.

name: mz-spacing-error-model-scoring
description: Use when mass traces from LC-MS metabolomics data must be grouped into isotope features, and candidate trace sets must be judged by whether their pairwise m/z distances fit a metabolite isotope-spacing error model.

name: mz-spacing-regression-modeling
description: Use when you need to build reference isotope-pattern models — linear m/z-spacing functions or SVM training data — from theoretical formula enumerations instead of measured spectra.

name: mz-to-mass-adduct-conversion
description: Use when a mass spectral search tool needs to compare experimental precursor m/z or theoretical fragment m/z to molecule masses and the ion mode and maximum absolute charge must be chosen to define the [M+H]+/[M-H]- conversion.

name: mz-tolerance-based-ion-matching
description: Use when verifying that ions on a curated scheduled precursor list are present as detected MS1 features in an independent feature table, and when counting features shared with a DDA fragmented-precursor set.

name: mz-tolerance-peak-pooling-across-varieties
description: Use when two or more DESI-MSI mass-signature peak lists (e.g., DIMPLE-processed replicate roots per variety) must be merged at a fixed m/z tolerance and split into conserved vs. variety-unique signature partitions.

name: mz-value-compound-matching-within-ppm-tolerance
description: Use when you have already produced positive/negative-mode m/z peak tables (e.g. XCMS or MetaboAnalyst export) and need putative MSI level 2 identities for individual m/z values within a set ppm tolerance.

name: mz-window-eic-filtering
description: Use when you need an EIC (or targeted ion trace) for a specific m/z window from a large Parquet-converted HRMS file and want on-disk, zero-copy filtering rather than full in-memory loading.

name: mza-converted-ms-data-processing
description: Use when raw vendor MS files (Agilent .d, Thermo .raw, Bruker .d, or mzML) must be converted with MZA and processed through PeakQC's MS1 QC pipeline for omics-agnostic batch quality assessment.

name: mza-file-structure-validation
description: Reference for verifying the structure of an MZA file after conversion from Agilent .d, Bruker ion mobility .d, Thermo .raw, or mzML, before consuming it with h5py or rhdf5.

name: mza-hdf5-raw-data-access
description: Use when multidimensional MS data have already been converted to the MZA format and you need to retrieve raw spectra (1D m/z and intensity arrays) by scan number directly through generic HDF5 libraries like h5py or rhdf5.

name: mza-raw-data-extraction
description: Use when raw MS data in vendor formats (Agilent .d, Bruker TIMS .d, Thermo .raw, mzML) has been converted to MZA (.h5/HDF5) and arrays such as MS1 spectra, TIC, XICs, or arrival time distributions must be extracted programmatically.

name: mzdiff-parameter-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when a centWave (XCMS/MZmine2) metabolomics workflow leaves mzDiff unoptimized and you need to quantify how mzDiff variation affects the downstream feature table.

name: mzmine-adap-chromatogram-processing
description: Use when raw LC-HRMS files from the PharmMet DB study (Metabolomics Workbench ST003991) must be converted into MS1-derived m/z/RT feature tables to support 0-hour vs 24-hour drug-metabolite feature detection.
tools: Thermo Scientific Orbitrap ID-X Tribrid mass spectrometer

name: mzmine-csv-and-mgf-export-configuration
description: Use when raw fractionated LC-MS/MS files have been feature-detected, deconvoluted and aligned in MZmine2 (v2.31) and a feature table plus MS/MS spectra must be exported for GNPS FBMN or bioactive molecular networking.

name: mzmine-feature-list-export
description: Use when MZmine has produced an aligned feature list across samples and the next step is uploading to GNPS for FBMN or IIMN, or when supplementary IIN edge files are needed to connect adducts/isotopes of the same molecule.

name: mzmine-feature-list-processing
description: Use when you have MZmine2 self-extracted untargeted feature lists (CSV with m/z, RT, area columns) from multiple LC–MS runs and need more accurate multi-run feature alignment than MZmine2's built-in alignment provides.

name: mzmine-feature-spectra-integration
description: Use when MS2 spectra were generated by an external feature-based tool such as MZmine or MS-DIAL and exported as MGF (e.g. MZmine-GNPS_AG_test_GNPS.mgf), and you need them as matchSpectra() query input in R.

name: mzmine-feature-table-import
