description: Use when the input is a MZmine join-aligned feature table (.csv, produced with m/z tolerance 40 ppm and RT tolerance 0.2 min) plus its corresponding GNPS FBMN .mgf spectra file, and the goal is to build a MEMO MS2 fingerprint matrix from the aligned samples (e.g. MSV000083306 demo data).

name: mzmine-feature-table-processing
description: Use when the input is an MZmine 2/3-exported quantitative feature table and sample metadata and you need to load, normalize, and reduce the feature set (e.g., 727 → 104 → 26 for Pristimera indica roots) prior to computing Inventa components.

name: mzmine-peak-list-parsing
description: Use when the input is an MZmine 2 aligned peak list (from 'More Restrictive' or 'Less Restrictive' extraction) that must be decomposed into candidate peak groups with sample-level intensity profiles and RT window boundaries before filtering or classification.

name: mzmine-peak-picking-and-msms-extraction
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS challenge or study data arrives as mzML files and you need discrete, exported MS/MS spectra (e.g., an MGF-style set) as input for formula or structure annotation tools like MIST-CF or SIRIUS.

name: mzmine-workflow-configuration
description: Use when building a sample-centric LC-HRMS2 feature detection pipeline on UHPLC-MS2 DDA data (mzML/mzXML inputs) that must yield a per-sample feature table and MS2 .mgf export for FBMN, ISDB, or KG integration.

name: mzmine3-workflow-configuration
description: Use when raw LC–MS/MS mzML files need feature extraction and per-feature representative MS2 spectra before formula/adduct assignment and molecular candidate ranking.

name: mzml-centroided-peak-import
description: Use when raw metabolomics data are supplied as individual centroided mzML files (or per-replicate peak-list CSVs) and a deduplicated list of unique MS features is needed for downstream Compound Activity Mapping or bioactivity integration.

name: mzml-dataset-subset-sampling
description: Use when benchmarking the computational performance or scalability of LC-MS metabolomics data processing tools, and you need study-size-varied inputs from a fixed centroided mzML corpus rather than a single fixed-size run.

name: mzml-feature-annotation
description: Use when mzML lipidomics runs need per-feature MS/MS-based lipid identifications, especially when comparing candidate annotations from multiple in-silico fragmentation libraries.

name: mzml-feature-extraction-parsing
description: Use when raw LC–MS data in mzML format must be turned into extracted feature lists (m/z, RT, area CSV per run) so that feature alignment tools like G-Aligner, or its evaluation against manual annotations, can be run.

name: mzml-feature-table-ingestion
description: Use when you have raw LC-MS mzML files plus an aligned or unaligned feature table CSV (from mzMine2, XCMS, etc.) and need to load both into NeatMS before peak prediction or filtering.

name: mzml-file-generation
description: Use when a ground-truth LC-MS/MS dataset with known molecule identities, abundances, and retention times is needed to benchmark quantification or identification algorithms before running real MS experiments.

name: mzml-file-ingestion-and-scheduling
description: Use when an instrument PC writes vendor raw files that must be automatically converted to mzML, picked up by a monitoring daemon, and queued for QC processing without manual intervention.

name: mzml-file-loading-and-grid-construction
description: Use when raw LC-IMS-MS/MS acquisitions in mzML(.gz) format (e.g. Agilent 6560 Ion Mobility LC/Q-TOF deposits such as MSV000091746) must be converted into DEIMoS's common N-dimensional grid before peak detection or other downstream steps.

name: mzml-file-parsing
description: Use when raw acquisition output from DDA controllers (full-scan, TopN, SmartROI, WeightedDEW) is available as mzML files and scan counts, precursor events, or inter-scan timing metrics must be extracted before efficiency or timing analysis.

name: mzml-file-processing-pipeline-configuration
description: Use when raw HRMS instrument files in mzML format must be extracted against a compound or mass list with configured m/z/RT tolerances and MS1/MS2 intensity thresholds, especially when serial vs parallel wall-clock timing must be compared.

name: mzml-jcamp-dx-data-interpretation
description: Use when the input is an mzML (MS) file that must be brought into JCAMP-DX form so it can undergo the ChemSpectra standardized processing, editing, and peak-output workflow.

name: mzml-output-generation
description: Use when you need a synthetic mzML gold-standard for benchmarking MS algorithms, predicting co-elution/co-fragmentation, or simulating runs for arbitrary biomolecules given only chemical formulas.

name: mzml-parsing-for-targeted-lc-im-ms-analysis
description: Use when you have a profile-mode mzML file from LC-DTIM-MS plus a list of molecular formulae and want to target their predicted ion species for peak picking, isotopologue confirmation, and CCS database entry building.

name: mzml-parsing-noise-filtering
description: Use when parsing mzML files of authentic metabolite standards for in-house RT/m/z library construction and you need to determine and apply a background noise level before extracting adduct EICs.

name: mzml-peak-feature-annotation
description: Use when vendor .raw files need to be converted to mzML and matched against a .msp library to tabulate internal standard RT, intensity, and mass-accuracy metrics per specimen during QC.

name: mzml-processing-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking a tool that parses LC-IM-MS mzML files: you have runtime measurements at multiple file sizes (e.g. 460–1083 MB) or formula counts (e.g. 15–38 s per added formula) and need to verify linear scaling and absolute runtime criteria.

name: mzml-raw-data-parsing
description: Use when raw LC/GC-HRMS data must be read from vendor-independent mzML files (centroided, DDA/ddMS2) into Python via pyOpenMS as the entry point for feature finding or feature prioritization workflows.

name: mzml-scan-event-parsing
description: Use when you need to quantify what fraction of picked peaks a DDA controller actually fragmented: i.e. when you have mzML files from TopN injections and peak bounding boxes (min/max RT and m/z) from MZmine2-style peak picking.

name: mzml-scan-import-parsing
description: Use when starting an HRMS non-targeted analysis from vendor-neutral raw files (.mzML) in Python and you need scan-level metadata (m/z–intensity scans) before chromatographic peak detection with mssmain.peak_pick.

name: mzml-scan-parsing
description: Use when the input is an mzML file from an LC-MS/MS injection and the analysis needs MS2 fragmentation events (precursor m/z + RT) or MS1/MS2 scan schedules, e.g. to score DDA controller coverage of picked peaks.

name: mzml-spectra-conversion-configuration
description: Use when proprietary vendor LC-MS metabolomics raw files must be converted to open .mzML or .abf format and staged in data/raw_data/ before running Nextflow4MS-DIAL.

name: mzml-spectra-import-and-denoising
description: Use when acquired Orbitrap ID-X MSn raw files (or mzML) must be converted into clean spectra before building an MSn spectral library, e.g. signals at each MSn level need to be denoised and background artifacts removed.

name: mzml-spectra-parsing
description: Use when raw HRMS non-targeted analysis data in .mzML format must be converted into Python-readable scan metadata prior to feature extraction (e.g., mssmain.peak_pick) or when validating MSS on samples like EPA ENTACT mixtures #505, #506, #508.

name: mzml-spectral-data-loading
description: Use when raw MS/MS peak files are in mzML format and need to be read into memory as spectra objects before embedding, spectral clustering, or similarity computation.

name: mzml-spectral-data-parsing
description: Use when raw profile LC-DTIM-MS data in mzML format must be parsed and searched for predicted primary-ion m/z species from molecular formulae prior to RT-dimension peak picking.

name: mzml-spectral-parsing
description: Use when starting from raw untargeted LC/MS runs in mzML format and you need a zero-parameter MS1 signal-detection entry point that feeds downstream drift correction and feature-table generation.

name: mzml-spectrum-import
description: Use when MS2 spectra from MALDI-MSI tissue measurements are supplied as mzML files and need to be loaded for downstream binning, cosine-similarity comparison against Met-ID's FMP-10 standard spectra, or MS2-based metabolite identification.

name: mzml-spectrum-parsing-and-metadata-extraction
description: Use when converting vendor-raw or mzML MS data (Agilent .d, Bruker IM .d, Thermo .raw, mzML) into an HDF5-based structure so spectra can be read in Python/R without Windows-bound vendor libraries.

name: mzml-spectrum-upload-and-parsing
description: Use when raw tandem mass spectra are stored in mzML, mzXML, or MGF files and must be ingested into the npanalysis.org platform as parsed 'Mass Spectrum' data before running VInSMoC search tasks.

name: mzml-spectrum-xml-parsing
description: Use when the input is a .mzML LC-MS data file (or a Thermo .raw file needing the analogous pathway) and the goal is to recover per-spectrum records — spectrum_id, rt, m/z and intensity peak lists — into a flat tabular form.

name: mzml-to-jcamp-conversion
description: Reference for converting MS spectra stored in mzML or vendor RAW format into JCAMP-DX before visualization, peak detection, or ELN transfer with ChemSpectra/Chemotion.

name: mzml-to-npy-conversion
description: Use when raw untargeted LC-MS metabolomics data arrive as mzML files and the goal is end-to-end DeepMSProfiler analysis, which requires .npy spectral arrays plus a datalist mapping each spectrum to its disease/cancer-type label.

name: mzrt-molecular-annotation
description: Use when an aligned LC-MS feature quantification matrix exists and detected consensus features must be putatively identified by mz-RT matching against a molecule list (e.g., GNPS MS/MS matches or a manually built CSV).

name: mztab-feature-report-parsing
description: Use when you have run a SmartPeak (CLI or GUI) workflow over mzML injections and exported feature reports, and you need to read those tables in Python to score peak integration correctness or extract quantitative features.

name: mztab-m-format-export
description: Use when a processed metabolomics feature table held as a mass_dataset object must be shared with, or ingested by, external tools that require the mzTab-M data structure.

name: mzxml-metric-parsing
description: Use when raw DIA files (.raw/.d/.wiff from Orbitrap, TripleTOF, or timsTOF Pro instruments) must be converted to mzXML and mined for the iDIA-QC QC metrics per file.

name: mzxml-raw-data-parsing
description: Use when the input is raw LC-HRMS measurement data in mzXML format and the analysis goal requires extracting per-scan m/z and retention-time information (e.g., before peak picking with MetMatch's MassSpecWavelet, Gaussian correlation, or Savitzky-Golay algorithms).

name: n-linked-glycan-retention-time-matching
description: Use when LC-MS/MS data from released, labeled N-glycans (mzXML from Orbitrap or MALDI-TOF instruments) must be identified and validated against a reference set of manually annotated glycan-RT pairs.

name: n-methyl-derivatized-lipid-msms-simulation
description: Use when generating theoretical fragment-ion information (m/z and relative intensity) for N-Me derivatized unsaturated sterol lipids to build a fragment ion prediction component of a 4D sterol lipid database.

name: naive-baseline-classifier-comparison
description: Use when a binary classifier's precision/recall must be shown to exceed what the class proportions alone would achieve, e.g. reporting an internal test set for a spectral bitterness classifier.

name: nalkylpyridinium-sulfonate-ri-calibration
description: Use when retention times of features measured in one lab must be matched to reference compounds annotated in another (e.g. HPLC vs UHPLC), so annotation should rely on m/z plus retention index rather than raw RT.

name: nanobind-wrapper-generation
description: Use when a C++ library needs Python scripting access to its core data structures and algorithms for rapid prototyping, and the binding layer is nanobind.

name: nap-webserver-baseline-comparison
description: Use when reproducing or validating performance claims for annotation propagation: you have a molecular spectral network (e.g. NIST 555-spectra benchmark) and need to compare measured ChemWalker runtime/scalability against the NAP webserver baseline.

name: narcotic-concentration-quantification
description: Use when a standard concentration series (e.g., narcotics at multiple ppb levels) plus a test sample of known target concentration (e.g., 500 ppb) is available and concentrations must be quantified via calibration-curve regression in R.

name: narcotics-lcms-data-analysis
description: Use when analyzing LC-MS data for a panel of known narcotic or other targeted compounds with known m/z and retention times, and per-target detection plus signal-to-noise quantification is required.

name: narcotics-mz-peak-identification
description: Use when metabolomics m/z peaks (e.g., the 12 SMART 2.0 narcotics: amphetamine, ketamine, cocaine, heroin, delta9-THC, nimetazepam, FM2) need candidate compound identities and database-only matching (HMDB/MassBank via SMART 2.

name: narcotics-peak-annotation
description: Use when you have estimated m/z values from untargeted LC-MS metabolomics peaks and need to annotate candidate compounds by exact-mass matching to HMDB or MassBank at ppm-level tolerances.

name: natural-abundance-correction
description: Use when you have unscaled isotopologue distribution tables (MIDs) from XCMS-pre-processed HRMS isotope-labeling experiments and need natural-abundance-corrected MIDs and average labeling values before flux analysis or clustering.

name: natural-extract-novelty-prioritization
description: Decision support for selecting which extracts from an untargeted metabolomics set to send for phytochemical isolation when the goal is maximizing novelty of discovered natural products.

name: natural-isotope-abundance-correction
description: Use when isotopologue ion intensities of 13C6-glucose-labelled fatty acids (e.g. palmitate C16, stearate/oleate C18) are extracted per cell or per pixel from imzML-derived ion images and must be freed of natural-abundance 13C signal before binomial fitting.

name: natural-product-analog-identification
description: Use when you need to prioritize potential structural analogs of a known bioactive compound (e.g., the anti-L. donovani triterpene isoiguesterin) among confident structural annotations of a natural product extract stored in an RDF knowledge graph.

name: natural-product-analogue-family-verification
description: Use when a manually annotated molecular network family must be validated against known reference compounds (e.g. MIBiG accessions) to confirm that discovered analogues belong to a specific biosynthetic class.

name: natural-product-annotation
description: Use when annotating GNPS tandem MS spectra (e.g., the ~8 million spectra of the GNPS microbial repository) with known natural-product structures, or when pairing MS identifications with genome-mining data to confirm molecule-to-BGC links.

name: natural-product-annotation-of-cyanobacterial-extracts
description: Use when a roughly fractionated natural-product extract has paired 1D NMR and LC-MS2 data per fraction and the goal is to prioritize fractions and assign natural-product classes (NP classes) to known and new metabolites without full isolation-first dereplication.

name: natural-product-biosynthesis-visualization
description: Use when you have a PKS, NRPS, RiPP, or terpene BGC (e.g., an antiSMASH prediction or MIBiG entry) and need a module-resolution pathway diagram with drawn intermediates and products, rather than only a scaffold prediction.

name: natural-product-compound-annotation-from-feature-groups
description: Use when a NP Analyst community lacks a single dominant bioactive MS feature but contains multiple high Activity-Score features that may represent adducts/fragments of the same molecule; group them by retention time to dereplicate constituent compounds.

name: natural-product-database-inventory-counting
description: Use when verifying or reporting dataset-scale statistics for the NPDB scaffold release of G.A.M.E., e.g. validating that a downloaded deposit contains the expected number of curated natural products and scaffold index files.

name: natural-product-dataset-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing GPU vs CPU runtimes of the CSCCP dynamic-programming solver across natural-product mixture datasets, or when reproducing the reported ~20.72 s vs 324.16 s runtime at D=5 mass precision.

name: natural-product-identification-benchmarking
description: Reference for evaluating NMR-based structure annotation tools on measured natural product HSQC spectra, especially when testing performance under changed solvent conditions (methanol-d4 vs chloroform-d) or comparing against NMRshiftDB shift-search baselines.

name: natural-product-isolation-prioritization
description: Use when a crude natural product extract (e.g., marine cyanobacterial LC-MS2 data) must be fractionated and you need to decide which fractions to pursue based on MS2 molecular networking, cytotoxicity, and NMR mixture analysis signals.

name: natural-product-likeness-score-filtering
description: Use when curating a natural products collection that includes predicted NPs from SuperNatural II and you must decide which SuperNatural II-only molecules qualify as genuine or plausible predicted NPs before adding them to the database.

name: natural-product-msms-data-processing
description: Use when given MS/MS spectra of two structurally related natural products (known + unknown analog) with 2D structures, and the goal is to localize the modification site on the known molecule or reproduce benchmark analog-pair analyses.

name: natural-product-msms-dereplication
description: Use when query tandem MS/MS spectra from natural-product extracts (e.g., MassIVE deposits of S. roseosporus or Streptomyces sp. DSM5940) must be matched against reference MS/MS library spectra, especially to find analogs whose peaks are shifted by a constant mass delta.

name: natural-product-nmr-spectral-classification
description: Use when you have 1D NMR spectra of crude extracts, fractions, or purified natural products (e.g., Symploca fractions, cyclic-peptide case-study spectra) and need rapid NP class-level annotation, prioritization, or benchmarking against the 'atomic sort' method.

name: natural-product-prioritization-ranking
description: Use when you have an MZmine FBMN quantitative table (.csv) plus an MGF of tandem mass spectra and need to prioritize features by novelty — e.g., to surface unreported NPs or rank candidate annotations in an alkaloid/plant extract.

name: natural-product-scaffold-clustering
description: Use when you have 1H, TOCSY and HSQC spectra for a panel of reference natural products or extract fractions and need to determine which compounds share structural scaffolds versus remain unconnected singletons in a chemical similarity network.

name: natural-product-structure-annotation
description: Use when molecular networking or analog library search (GNPS) surfaces an unknown MS/MS spectrum with a structurally related library hit, and the modification site on the known structure must be localized to annotate the new natural product.

name: natural-product-structure-classification
description: Use when you have SMILES strings for natural products (e.g. NP Atlas entries tagged bacterial vs fungal) and need pathway/superclass/class labels to aggregate counts or compare biosynthetic distributions across organism groups.

name: natural-product-structure-comparison
description: Use when you have antiSMASH annotations of PKS, NRPS, or NRPS/PKS hybrid BGCs and need to validate RAIChU-predicted product structures against characterised natural product structures, classifying any mismatches.

name: natural-product-structure-elucidation
description: Use when predicting mixture constituents from high-resolution MS molecular weights of natural products (e.g. Cuscuta chinensis, Ophiopogon japonicus, Polygonum multiflorum, Angelica sp.) using scaffold databases with sidechain probabilities.

name: natural-product-structure-fragment-matching
description: Use when a cryptic MS/MS spectrum absent from the GNPS library must be connected to a candidate structure and its biosynthetic gene cluster via predicted-fragment fingerprints.

name: natural-product-structure-informatics
description: Use when you need ground-truth linkages between gene clusters and MS2 spectra for evaluating linking algorithms, and both MIBiG BGC annotations and GNPS library InChIKeys are available but the two databases contain no direct cross-references.

name: natural-product-structure-library-curation
description: Use when benchmarking or running spectral library searches against natural product structures and you must merge community structure databases (DNP, GNPS) into one searchable reference set with ground-truth annotations.

name: natural-products-atlas-identifier-matching
description: Use when annotated MIBiG BGC entries need cross-references to chemical structure/spectral databases (Natural Products Atlas, GNPS, PubChem) based on matching compound names and structures.

name: natural-products-database-dereplication
description: Use when filtered MS/MS spectra ([M+H]+ adducts, >=6 fragments, 500 most intense peaks, parent masses 100-1,500 Da) from specialized metabolites need annotation against a natural products structural database before any taxonomic re-ranking.

name: natural-products-database-harmonization
description: Use when merging structure-organism pair records from multiple NP electronic resources (e.g. KNApSAcK, NAPRALERT, NPAtlas, PubChem, GBIF) and you need standardized chemical, biological and reference levels plus validated retention before open release.

name: natural-products-database-quality-verification
description: Use when a published database paper reports aggregate counts (e.g. retained structure-organism pairs, unique structures, organisms) and the deposited dataset (Zenodo deposit, TSV table) is available to reproduce them.

name: natural-products-database-querying
description: Use when a research question requires counts or inventories of reported natural products per taxon (family/genus/species) from a structured NP database dump, or when chemical-class coverage of a clade must be benchmarked against a larger kingdom-wide set.

name: natural-products-source-count-aggregation
description: Use when you need to reproduce or audit COCONUT's dataset statistics for a specific release — i.e., reconstruct Table 1 per-source counts and verify them against reported totals of unique flat and stereochemistry-preserving NPs.

name: natural-products-structure-dataset-processing
description: Use when you need predicted 1H chemical shifts for a batch of known natural product structures (e.g. Natural Products Atlas SMILES/MOL files) to compute shielded/deshielded signal statistics or build an in silico reference spectral library.

name: ncbi-refseq-homology-verification
description: Use when MINNO or a similar flux-based workflow flags reactions as absent from the KEGG database and each candidate must be classified as literature-supported or RefSeq-homology-supported before being added to the network.

name: ncbi-taxonomy-resolution
description: Use when a CAMI-format taxonomic profile contains taxIDs that must be attached to an NCBI taxonomy tree (e.g., to annotate nodes with percentage abundances or emit a Newick tree for downstream plotting).

name: near-duplicate-spectra-detection
description: Use when curating or benchmarking an MS/MS spectral library (e.g. an MGF file) and you need to quantify or remove spectra that are near-duplicates of another spectrum of the same compound, as a data-quality or train/test-leakage check.

name: nearest-neighbor-description-similarity-analysis
description: Use when a trained protein/domain embedding must be validated for functional coherence, e.g. checking that pfam2vec vectors place domains with related Pfam descriptions close together in cosine space.

name: nearest-neighbor-freetext-term-mapping
description: Use when freetext sample metadata strings must be coerced into a fixed, pre-determined vocabulary via synonym matching and typographical fixing, e.g. curating metabolomics metadata headers.

name: nearest-neighbor-outlier-alignment
description: Use when two adjacent spatial sections (e.g. 10X Visium spatial transcriptome and MALDI-MSI) have already undergone manual gross and ICP alignment, but residual spot-to-spot distances must be minimized before feature-based integration.

name: nearest-neighbor-search-comparison-profiling
description: Use when benchmarking whether ANN indexing (feature hashing + Voronoi inverted index) avoids exhaustive pairwise spectrum comparison at scale, e.g. on millions of MS/MS spectra from proteomics PRIDE datasets.

name: nearest-neighbor-spectrum-similarity-searching
description: Use when clustering very large tandem MS/MS datasets (e.g. 25 million spectra from a human draft proteome) where exhaustive pairwise spectrum comparison is quadratically expensive and an approximate sparse distance matrix suffices.

name: nearest-spd-matrix-projection
description: Use when an empirical M-by-M pairwise distance-correlation matrix of metabolite features must be made non-negative-definite before eigen-analysis-based effective-number-of-tests (Meff) correction in a MWAS multiple-testing pipeline.

name: nef-constraint-file-processing
description: Use when you have a NEF-format constraint file (deposited chemical shifts, distance/dihedral restraints) for a protein or nucleic acid and need to run or reproduce an NMR structure calculation in NMRFx without a pre-existing project.

name: nef-format-conversion
description: Use when an archival BMRB NMR-STAR entry must be syntax-validated and its chemical shift loop and restraint saveframes (NOE distances, dihedral angles) converted to the NEF interchange format for OneDep/wwPDB deposition with IUPAC atom nomenclature preserved.

name: negative-control-classification-evaluation
description: Use when a trained MS/MS classifier's false-positive rate must be quantified: i.e., when a curated ground-truth set of known non-target (negative-control) compound spectra is available and the fraction correctly assigned to the 'other' class needs to be reported per ion mode.

name: negative-control-metabolite-selection
description: Use when applying hRUV/RUV-III normalisation to large-scale metabolomics data and you must decide which metabolites serve as negative controls — e.g. selecting all metabolites vs. ranking non-differentially expressed metabolites by p-values per batch for a response variable such as hypertension.

name: negative-control-statistical-comparison
description: Use when you must show that a computational inference method (e.g., MetaboPAC's heuristic penalty-function optimization of response factors) significantly outperforms negative control methods across graded conditions such as percKnownKinetics = [0 20 40 60 80 100].

name: negative-correlation-filtering
description: Use when a correlation network built from abundance data carries both positive and negative edges, and the analysis goal (e.g., sample-specific subnetworks or topological comparison) requires retaining only co-occurrence (positive) edges.

name: negative-ion-mode-lc-ms-data-interpretation
description: Use when you have a negative-ion-mode LC-MS feature table with tissue/group labels (e.g. 94 samples across 14 tissues) and need to determine whether a specific tissue separates from the others in PCA space.

name: negative-mode-adduct-enforcement
description: Use when running mummichog on negative-ion-mode LC/MS feature tables (e.g. mzXML-derived yeast mutant vs wild-type data) and the predicted metabolites must be constrained to deprotonated M−H[−] species.

name: negative-mode-ionization-rule-filtering
description: Use when converting a catalogued SMILES list (e.g., the EPA CompTox PFAS list) into a predicted MS/MS fragment library for negative-mode PFAS annotation and you must drop structures incapable of forming [M−H]−.

name: negative-mode-tandem-ms-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking a small molecule database search tool (e.g., molDiscovery) on negative-ion-mode tandem mass spectra against a structure database such as DNP, especially to quantify the penalty of using a positive-mode-trained fragmentation model.

name: neighbor-definition-shift-modeling
description: Use when two peak-picked LC–MS feature tables (RT, m/z, FI per feature) must be matched across datasets and you need a robustly determined expected shift at each reference feature's RT before applying residual-threshold matching.

name: neighbor-section-morphological-disagreement-modeling
description: Use when creating pseudo-paired spatial transcriptome / MALDI-MSI benchmark datasets from spatial transcriptome matrices, so that spot-to-spot integration methods can be evaluated under realistic neighbor-section morphological disagreement.

name: neims-spectrum-prediction
description: Use when you need EI mass spectra for molecules lacking measured spectra — e.g., building an in-silico library from SMILES/SDF sets like f-NIST (255,821) and ChEMBL 28 to expand coverage beyond the 0.27M compounds in NIST 2017.

name: neme-mass-error-statistics
description: Use when validating molecular formula annotations from IDSL.UFA (or any MS1 isotopic-profile matching tool) by quantifying monoisotopic mass error in mDa against authentic reference standards.

name: nested-cross-validation-benchmarking
description: Use when you must compare several hyperparameter-tuned regressors on one labeled dataset (e.g. 80,038 SMRT retention times with alvaDesc descriptors/fingerprints) and need an unbiased error estimate without validation-set leakage.

name: nested-cross-validation-model-evaluation
description: Use when comparing several ML regressors (e.g. DNN, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) on a labeled dataset where hyperparameter tuning must be separated from performance estimation to avoid optimistic bias.

name: nested-json-table-hierarchy-construction
description: Use when messy, arbitrarily organized Excel/CSV spreadsheet data must be turned into clean, well-structured JSONized metadata via a tag layer of #export, #automate, and #modify directives.

name: netcdf-2dtic-import
description: Use when raw comprehensive two-dimensional gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC×GC-MS) data is stored in NetCDF format and must be converted into a 2D-TIC matrix for smoothing, baseline correction, peak alignment, or MPCA in R.

name: netcdf-chromatogram-matrix-handling
description: Use when raw GC×GC-MS chromatograms are stored in NetCDF files and must be loaded into R as 2D-TIC chromatogram matrices via RGCxGC's read_chrom to begin preprocessing and multivariate analysis.

name: netgsa-subnetwork-enrichment-testing
description: Use when two-condition metabolomics networks have been estimated with DNEA (glasso partial correlations + clusterNet consensus clustering) and you need to determine which metabolic subnetworks are differentially enriched between groups.

name: netmhcpan-binder-fraction-estimation
description: Use when you have deduplicated peptide sequence sets from MHC class I immunopeptidomics (e.g. Casanovo de novo vs Tide at 1% FDR) and need binder fractions to compare their immunological plausibility.

name: network-based-annotation-propagation
description: Use when you have MS1/MS2 untargeted metabolomics feature tables plus a set of known/seed metabolite annotations, and need to extend annotations to unknown features via network propagation rather than spectral-library matching alone.

name: network-centrality-visualization
description: Use when a differential metabolomics hit list (e.g., absolute fold change >= 1 and adjusted p < 0.05) needs hub-metabolite prioritization via betweenness centrality on a KEGG pathway network.

name: network-cluster-comparison-analysis
description: Use when untargeted metabolomics spectral data have already been networked with a fixed cosine similarity cutoff (e.g., 0.7) and you need to identify metabolite pairs or families split across separate clusters that per-metabolite connectivity optimization would reconnect.

name: network-composition-summarization
description: Use when a task asks to reproduce or verify reported composition statistics of a metabolic module network (e.g., 171 modules, 22 super modules, 66 intermediate substrates in Figure 1 of the scFEA/FLUXestimator paper) from its module-gene and stoichiometry files.

name: network-consensus-clustering
description: Use when a DNEA object contains estimated condition-specific networks (post-getNetworks) and you need to partition metabolites into highly interconnected subnetworks for downstream NetGSA enrichment testing.

name: network-count-figure-reproduction
description: Use when validating a rule-based reaction network expansion against published counts — e.g. reproducing Pickaxe Figure 4 trends for the YMDB (Version 2.0) expansion filtered by similarity cutoffs (0.4/0.5/0.8) or by similarity sampling of 2000 compounds.

name: network-coverage-scoring
description: Use when annotating metabolites from filtered INADEQUATE peak networks: after clustering and network finding, each candidate network must be scored against simulated database entries via hit and coverage scores before annotation.

name: network-cutoff-filtering
description: Use when a BGC sequence similarity network with pairwise Jaccard/Domain Sequence Similarity/Adjacency distances must be filtered at a hard cutoff to define GCFs, and optionally a second-layer clan cutoff for GCCs.

name: network-data-export
description: Use when preparing gene-gene interaction networks for topology-based pathway enrichment (NetGSA) and input gene identifiers must be matched to pathway database edges without manual curation.

name: network-edge-list-export
description: Use when MetaMapR network calculations (KEGG RPAIR, Tanimoto >0.7 structural, cosine >0.7 spectral, or Spearman/FDR <0.05 correlation edges) must be persisted as .csv edge lists and node attributes for downstream network analysis.

name: network-edge-priority-resolution
description: Use when merging multiple MetaMapR edge lists (KEGG RPAIR biochemical, PubChem Tanimoto structural, mass spectral cosine, empirical Spearman) into one network and duplicate node pairs carry more than one edge type.

name: network-edge-threshold-filtering
description: Use when a GGM/marginal-correlation network over metabolomics data is too dense to interpret, and edges must be filtered by an absolute correlation cutoff (e.g., |r| or |pcor| >= 0.2).

name: network-extension-with-linksets
description: Use when a Cytoscape network (e.g. a stringApp Disease Query PPI) needs to be enriched with compound-target, gene-disease, gene-pathway, or transcription-factor interactions from pre-built XGMML linksets, reproducibly via command line or R/Python.

name: network-graphics-export
description: Use when a combined metabolic network edge list (source, target, edge-type) and node attribute table exist and must be handed off to Cytoscape or exported as publication-quality SVG/PNG network graphics.

name: network-inference
description: Use when ICP-MS ion-concentration data (e.g. haploid S. cerevisiae deletion-mutant ionomes) have been normalised/symbolised and you need element-element or mutant-mutant network extraction plus correlation analysis.

name: network-label-propagation
description: Use when a patient-level per-gene score vector (e.g., metabolomic enrichment) needs to be smoothed/ranked over a protein interaction network so that neighborhood signal can implicate genes lacking direct annotation.

name: network-modularity-and-clustering-analysis
description: Use when two ICA decompositions (metagene/sk weight vectors) from different transcriptomic datasets must be matched to assess reproducibility of independent components via a graph of 'orthologous' metagenes.

name: network-module-detection-keystone-classification
description: Use when a co-occurrence network (e.g. MetaNet c_net_build output at r_threshold=0.6, p=0.05) needs community decomposition and hub/connector classification, such as microbial species networks from abundance tables.

name: network-neighborhood-metabolic-annotation
description: Use when per-patient metPropagate LPA propagated scores and Exomiser-Phenotype candidate scores (Exomiser-filtered lists of ~281-609 genes) must be merged to boost causative-gene ranks for suspected IEM patients.

name: network-neighbourhood-tracing
description: Use when the intersecting genes from a hypergeometric metabolic/GWAS comparison need to be attributed to primary keyword nodes versus first-neighbour nodes of a GWAS Catalog network to interpret where the signal arises.

name: network-node-motif-frequency-counting
description: Use when a motif-mapped molecular network (.graphml or Mass2Motifs_Nodes/Edges TSVs from pyMolNetEnhancer) is available and you need per-motif node frequencies and counts of annotated motifs across the network.

name: network-partition-export
description: Use when a full-connectivity metabolite similarity network (all pairwise cosine edges retained, no threshold) needs to be partitioned into molecular communities without a predefined community count.

name: network-propagation-score-ranking
description: Use when a single patient's untargeted metabolomics yields DAMs (|z| >= 2) plus an Exomiser-filtered candidate gene list, and genes must be ranked by metabolomics-derived scores propagated across a STRING protein interaction network.

name: network-scale-verification
description: Use when a KGMN-style analysis requires rebuilding network layer 1 (KMRN) from KEGG and BioTransformer and you must confirm the reconstruction matches the published network scale before downstream subnetwork retrieval.

name: network-statistics-computation
description: Use when you have FT-ICR MS peak abundance data with assigned molecular formulas and need to construct transformation networks from mass differences and summarize network metrics.

name: network-table-spreadsheet-generation
description: Use when a trained per-metabolite model set (e.g. scikit-learn Random Forest Regressor models over nine feature sets) must be converted into a consolidated network spreadsheet with control-based confidence scores.

name: network-threshold-tuning-and-simplification
description: Use when pairwise MS/MS spectrum similarities for molecular features must be converted into a graph and weak edges removed to reveal subnetworks of related metabolites (e.g., N-acyl GPEs, GLEAs, NAEs).

name: network-topological-index-computation
description: Use when per-condition or per-sample subnetworks have been extracted from a co-occurrence network and you need global topological indices compared against a baseline to detect fragmentation or restructuring under exposure or other treatments.

name: network-topology-annotation-propagation
description: Use when an FBMN molecular network has spectral pairing (GNPS/GNPS2 library) matches for only a subset of nodes and the remaining MS/MS spectra still need chemical annotations.

name: network-topology-comparison
description: Use when you need to validate an alternative spectral similarity metric by reproducing a published molecular network and checking that known compound-family sub-networks are recovered with matching topology.

name: network-topology-comparison-analysis
description: Use when you must decide which knowledge-driven network topology (metabolic reaction network vs. spectral or fully connected network) to adopt for MS2-based annotation propagation, by quantifying accuracy, FDR, and specificity trade-offs.

name: network-topology-hub-identification
description: Use when significant metabolites from a case-control metabolomics comparison must be placed in a chemical-chemical interaction network to identify hub (high-degree/central) metabolites.

name: network-topology-validation
description: Use when building or filtering MetDNA3 feature/metadata reaction networks and you must verify intermediate graph sizes (node/edge counts) against published reference values before recursive annotation propagation.

name: network-visualization-styling
description: Use when a network has just been extended in Cytoscape (e.g. via 'cytargetlinker extend') and needs the CyTargetLinker visual style, a force-directed layout, and node-type-specific coloring before export or figure production.

name: networking-parameter-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when re-running or reproducing a GNPS METABOLOMICS-SNETS-V2 molecular networking job on a public dataset (e.g. MassIVE MSV000083381) and you need to characterize how clustering or tolerance parameters alter node counts and library annotations.

name: neural-mass-spectrum-prediction
description: Use when you need to predict EI mass spectra from molecular structures (SMILES/SDF/InChI) or augment a spectral reference library (e.g., NIST, MassBank, Wiley) with predicted spectra for molecules absent from the library.

name: neural-network-annotation-evaluation
description: Use when comparing annotation models (e.g. ESP vs MLP/GNN baselines) on mass spectra candidate sets and you must reproduce or verify reported average-rank improvements such as 23.7%/37.2%.

name: neural-network-architecture-reconstruction
description: Use when a paper describes a network's architecture concretely (layer count, hidden dimensions, output activation) and the goal is to reimplement, train, and validate it from the described spec and released codebase.

name: neural-network-batch-creation
description: Use when a manually labelled LC-MS peak experiment exists and you need balanced train/test/validation batches to retrain or fine-tune the NeatMS neural network classifier.

name: neural-network-flux-balance-modeling
description: Use when a single-cell count matrix (genes x cells, raw or normalized counts) needs cell-wise reaction-rate (fluxome) prediction and metabolite-variation estimates, e.g., comparing glucose-glutamine flux among cancer, myeloid, and T cells in tumor microenvironment data.

name: neural-network-flux-estimation
description: Use when single-cell (or bulk) transcriptomics data must be converted to cell-wise metabolic flux estimates using a flux-balance-constrained neural network, e.g. rebuilding the scFEA factor-graph solver or reproducing its loss convergence.

name: neural-network-hyperparameter-tuning
description: Use when preparing a MiMeNet run on paired microbial/metabolite count CSVs and you must fix the MLP architecture (number of layers, layer size, L2 penalty, dropout rate) via a JSON net_params file for shared or per-partition tuning.

name: neural-network-inference-probability-thresholding
description: Use when an aligned or unaligned MZmine/XCMS feature table must be scored against raw mzML data so that false-positive MS1 peaks reported by the processing pipeline can be filtered by confidence label.

name: neural-network-model-inference
description: Use when you need per-molecule mass spectra predictions in milliseconds (e.g., to augment a spectral library with synthetic spectra for millions of candidate molecules) and have SMILES/SDF inputs plus the pretrained NEIMS weights.

name: neural-network-peak-classification
description: Use when you have non-filtered MZmine 2 peak lists from nontargeted LC-MS data (e.g. HILIC plasma metabolomics) and need to filter false spectral peaks while preserving true positive features, beyond what centWave or local minimum search quality filters achieve.

name: neural-network-regression-inference
description: Use when RT predictions are needed for large structure libraries (e.g. 320,919 SMILES from public databases) using a pre-trained neural network on molecular descriptors, with centering/scaling before inference.

name: neural-network-spectra-formula-re-ranking
description: Use when you have held-out tandem MS spectra (e.g. NPLIB1, CASMI 2022), precomputed SIRIUS formula candidates, and need to compare neural re-ranking architectures by top-1 accuracy.

name: neural-network-survival-modeling
description: Use when you have metabolomics data mapped to pathway-level PDS features plus patient survival times/events and want to fit or compare a neural-network-based survival model (Cox-nnet) against a Cox-PH baseline.

name: neural-network-weight-matrix-attribution
description: Use when a trained MiMeNet multi-layer perceptron model set is available and you need to attribute microbe-metabolite interaction scores from network weights, e.g. to identify significant microbes (like the 163 significant microbes on the IBD PRISM dataset) tied to well-predicted metabolites.

name: neural-spectrum-prediction-mode-configuration
description: Use when a neural mass-spectra prediction model must be configured with forward-only, reverse-only, or bidirectional output heads, or when comparing prediction modes by library-matching recall on EI spectra.

name: neutral-lipid-species-annotation
description: Use when per-cell lipid intensity columns from a MALDI-IMS single-cell metabolomics matrix (e.g. SpaceM MORPHnMOL.csv) must be annotated as candidate lipid species and scored against a microscopy-derived lipid droplet marker such as LD540.

name: neutral-loss-annotation-visualization
description: Use when MS/MS spectra of multiple features (from an .mgf file, e.g. feature_id-keyed MZmine3 output) need a single overview of fragment-ion overlap and neutral-loss sharing for a feature or feature group of interest.

name: neutral-loss-computation
description: Use when converting processed MS/MS spectra into Spec2Vec/SpectrumDocument word tokens and neutral losses must be represented as words alongside peak words for Word2Vec model training.

name: neutral-loss-extraction-from-msms-spectra
description: Use when raw MS2 fragmentation spectra (e.g., XCMS/mzMatch-preprocessed peaks paired via RMassBank, or MGF spectra such as the 5,670-spectrum GNPS set) must be converted into bag-of-fragments documents with neutral losses before LDA topic modeling.

name: neutral-loss-feature-calculation
description: Use when converting a merged MS/MS peak list (m/z–intensity pairs with a known precursor m/z) into a feature representation that captures loss information for ANN fingerprint prediction.

name: neutral-loss-formula-annotation
description: Use when MS/MS spectra have been converted to fragmentation graphs of m/z differences and pattern edges need chemical interpretation, e.g. annotating a valine-like loss in GNPS network components.

name: neutral-loss-node-generation
description: Use when constructing fragmentation DAGs from molecule–spectrum pairs where fragment nodes already carry 20 ppm peak assignments and observed neutral losses must be represented as explicit graph nodes linking fragment pairs.

name: neutral-loss-omission-in-spectral-matching
description: Use when decomposing external reference MS2 spectra (Mass Bank, GNPS) with pre-characterized Mass2Motifs and running motif-based spectral library matching, since loss fields are unsupported by matching tools.

name: neutral-loss-peak-calculation
description: Use when per-compound MS/MS spectra spanning multiple collision energies (from MSP-derived data) must be transformed into a single enhanced spectrum containing fragment ions plus neutral-loss peaks in binarized (0/1) form before CNN-based metabolite identification.

name: neutral-loss-removal-from-pseudo-spectra
description: Use when Mass2Motif pseudo-spectra containing both fragment and neutral-loss entries must be fed to a spectral-matching-based annotation tool (e.g. MS2Analyzer-style matching) that only accepts fragments.

name: neutral-loss-spectrum-combination
description: Use when comparing parent and TP MS/MS fragment spectra (m/z–intensity peak lists) to score similarity for TP componentization, and equal neutral losses or a constant mass shift between fragments should contribute to the score.

name: neutral-loss-spectrum-derivation
description: Use when preparing paired query-reference MS/MS inputs for TransExION: neutral-loss representations must be built alongside original-spectrum representations from MGF/h5py peak lists.

name: neutral-mass-derivation-from-adduct-annotations
description: Use when cleaning MS/MS spectral libraries (MGF format) where adduct metadata must yield chemically coherent neutral masses, especially when [M]+ or [M]− adducts are annotated with a reported charge of zero.

name: neutral-mass-regression-inference
description: Use when a mass distance network of LC-MS features (e.g. from asari-preprocessed feature tables like ecoli_pos.tsv) has been converted into a 2-tier adduct/isotope tree and the neutral M0 mass of each empirical compound must be recovered.

name: newick-tree-filtering-and-pruning
description: Use when you have microbeMASST/microbeMASST-style batch search outputs (_matches.tsv, _count_microbe.tsv) plus NCBI lineage Newick/JSON taxon data and need a lineage-consistent taxonomic tree showing which microbes may produce a queried metabolite.

name: newick-tree-format-serialization
description: Use when a phylogenetic analysis has produced a species-level distance matrix (e.g. from averaged compareMS2 pairwise spectra comparisons) and the reconstructed topology must be exported as a Newick (.nwk) file for downstream inspection or validation.

name: newick-tree-serialization
description: Use when a symmetric pairwise distance matrix over tandem MS datasets has been computed (e.g., by compareMS2) and a rooted, ultrametric tree in Newick format is the required output for phylogenetic display or downstream tooling.

name: newman-spectral-split-subnetwork-identification
description: Use when running mummichog module analysis on a significant m/z feature list and you need to partition the matched-metabolite subnetworks into structural modules for activity scoring against a permuted null.

name: newton-raphson-numeric-optimization
description: Use when estimating parameters (e.g. mean and SD) of a truncated normal distribution via maximum likelihood on left-truncated metabolomics data, where missing values below the LOD require iterative numeric optimization.

name: nextflow-execution-report-interpretation
description: Use when a Nextflow workflow (e.g., LC-MS metabolomics processing) has finished or failed and you must audit what ran, with which container/parameters, on which resources, or verify cross-platform reproducibility.

name: nextflow-pipeline-configuration
description: Use when you have raw .mzML or .abf LC-MS metabolomics files, need to run the MS-DIAL → MS-FLO workflow, and must set up container profiles, parameter files, and resource allocations for local or HPC execution.

name: nextflow-pipeline-structure-analysis
description: Use when you need to quantify a Nextflow workflow's structural complexity — enumerate every process in main.nf and count user-facing parameters in conf/*.config to compare pipelines' complexity.

name: nextflow-provenance-capture
description: Use when a Nextflow workflow run (e.g. containerized MS-DIAL/MS-FLO processing of .mzML LC-MS data) must yield retrospective provenance artifacts — execution reports, timeline, and logs — documenting runtime, resources, and data derivation.

name: nextflow-workflow-execution
description: Use when you need to execute an end-to-end untargeted LC-HRMS metabolomics feature-detection workflow reproducibly from raw .mzML files, with containerized software (MS-DIAL + MS-FLO) under Nextflow on a local machine or HPC (SLURM).

name: nextflow-workflow-execution
description: Use when a multi-omics analysis (e.g. metabolomics CSV, methylation betas, CBCL behavioral items) must be run end-to-end through a reproducible, containerized Nextflow pipeline rather than ad-hoc scripts.

name: nightingale-nmr-metabolomics-data-import
description: Use when the input is a Nightingale Health NMR metabolomics dataset (e.g. ALSPAC_F24) that must be loaded into metaboprep before sample/metabolite QC summaries and threshold-based filtering can be performed.

name: nist-compatible-msp-file-generation
description: Use when predicted retention times must be exported into NIST-format .msp spectral files so downstream tools like MS-DIAL or MS-FINDER can apply RT-window filtering or Gaussian RT similarity scoring to candidate structures.

name: nist-cosine-similarity-scoring
description: Use when a reduced candidate set of mass spectra (e.g. grouped by SPLASH second-block value) must be scored and ranked against a query spectrum to quantify search-space reduction versus similarity-based recall.

name: nist-msp-spectral-export
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS data (e.g., from an untargeted metabolomics study like ST002044 on Metabolomics WorkBench) must be converted into unique, deconvoluted MS/MS spectra in .msp format, split by ESI+ and ESI− modes.

name: nist-spectral-library-annotation-processing
description: Reference for exporting spectra from the NIST20 MS/MS spectral library and cleaning expert-curated formula annotations (10 ppm mass consistency, glycan/peptide removal) before evaluating formula-annotation precision/recall or retrieval.

name: nist-srm-1950-plasma-qc-pool-handling
description: Decision support for organizing NIST SRM 1950 plasma QC-pool sample sets — 112 specimens, 40 QC pools, 10 blanks — prior to DEIMoS feature detection and cross-sample alignment.

name: nist20-benchmark-result-extraction
description: Use when a published Table 1-style results table reports mean and standard deviation performance over multiple random seeds for two model variants (e.g., fragmentation depth ablations) on NIST20, and a delta/ablation summary is needed.

name: nist20-overlap-removal
description: Use when building pretraining corpora from large compound libraries (e.g. ~30M ZINC20 SMILES) that will later be paired with a model finetuned on NIST 20 experimental EI-MS spectra, to prevent train/test leakage.

name: nmds-ordination-of-compound-abundance-data
description: Use when a standardized sample-by-compound area table from uafR GC-MS processing is available and the goal is ordination plus a between-treatment significance test of compound composition, e.g. reproducing a published result.

name: nmds-ordination-visualization
description: Use when a normalized peak-intensity table (peaks with assigned molecular formulas) plus sample grouping metadata need ordination to visually test whether treatment groups separate, and when PERMANOVA significance must be interpreted against ordination plots.

name: nmf-lipid-dictionary-learning
description: Use when single-cell MS spectra from isolated cells must be mapped onto tissue MALDI MSI pixel data to infer where cell subpopulations contribute chemically across a tissue section or 3D reconstruction.

name: nmr-automated-phase-correction
description: Use when raw Bruker time-domain FID data (`fid` or `ser`) must be turned into a correctly phased 2D spectrum without manual phasing, e.g. batch or autonomous processing of many spectra.

name: nmr-automatic-peak-picking-threshold-detection
description: Use when a 1D 1H or 13C NMR spectrum (JCAMP-DX) must be reduced to a picked peak list — e.g. as the first step before integration, coupling constant calculation, multiplicity assignment, or automated transfer of signals to an ELN.

name: nmr-baseline-correction
description: Use when a raw 1D NMR spectrum (ppm scale and intensity array) shows a curved or offset baseline that must be subtracted prior to multivariate statistical analysis, and dense peak regions risk being over-corrected by a naive spline fit.

name: nmr-baseline-correction
description: Use when raw 1D 1H NMR spectra (Bruker or Agilent/Varian FID, or Bruker 1r files) show baseline distortion from macromolecules in extracts or an intense peak dominating less intense neighboring ones, before alignment or binning.

name: nmr-baseline-region-objective-definition
description: Use when automatically phasing a series of 1D-NMR spectra and a phase-corrected reference spectrum exists: baseline-only edge regions (>10.0 ppm and <−0.5 ppm) can be used to define an optimisation objective for zero/first-order phase (ph0/ph1).

name: nmr-binned-matrix-reshaping
description: Use when a binned NMR matrix (rows of bucket intensities over Bin.SpectraPoint per sample) must be converted into MetaboAnalyst CSV or Workflows4Metabolomics .TABULAR input files for downstream statistical analysis.

name: nmr-biomarker-hazard-ratio-estimation
description: Use when UK Biobank NMR biomarker concentrations (original or ukbnmr remove_technical_variation output) must be tested for association with incident disease endpoints via per-SD Cox models adjusted for age and sex.

name: nmr-biomarker-log-transformation-with-zero-offset
description: Use when preparing the 107 non-derived UK Biobank NMR biomarker concentrations for robust regression-based removal of technical variation and some biomarkers contain exact 0 values.

name: nmr-biomarker-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when raw NMR metabolomics biomarker concentrations (e.g., 226 Nightingale Health platform measures in EDTA plasma/serum) contain zeroes marking values below the detection limit and must be made analysis-ready for per-cohort Cox survival models.

name: nmr-biomarker-ratio-recomputation
description: Use when you have post-QC UK Biobank NMR biomarker data produced by remove_technical_variation() and need the derived composites (61), original ratios (81), or extended ratios (76) recomputed from adjusted non-derived biomarkers rather than directly adjusted.

name: nmr-bucket-snr-filtering
description: Use when a 1D 1H/13C NMR spectra processing pipeline has produced a bucket table (ppm intervals × per-spectrum intensities) and noisy, low-intensity buckets must be removed before statistical analysis.

name: nmr-bucket-table-export
description: Use when a processed 1D NMR bucket table (ppm-interval buckets per spectrum) must be handed off, without intermediate file conversions, to online statistical tools such as MetaboAnalyst 3.0 or BioStatFlow.

name: nmr-chemical-shift-axis-plotting
description: Use when MWAS results from 1H NMR metabonomic data need to be visualized as a skyline plot against chemical shift (ppm), e.g. reproducing paper figures like the BMI association plot over the δ 0.80–1.60 ppm lipid region.

name: nmr-chemical-shift-binning
description: Use when preparing a 13C NMR peak list (comma-separated carbon ppm shifts) as model input for the NMR2Struct multitask spectrum-to-structure CNN/transformer pipeline.

name: nmr-chemical-shift-curation
description: Use when building or extending a metabolite NMR chemical-shift reference library for ROI-based metabolite identification, e.g., swapping the HMDB source for BMRB assignments to drop into ROIAL-NMR.

name: nmr-chemical-shift-database-construction
description: Use when a ROI-based NMR metabolite identification tool needs reference chemical shift and J-coupling (SRRM) libraries, and you must derive them from HMDB records and organize them by biological sample type.

name: nmr-chemical-shift-drift-assessment
description: Use when a series of 1D-NMR spectra (e.g. a Daphnia magna extract series) shows chemical-shift drift between spectra and you need to quantify misalignment against a user-selected reference within a chosen spectral region before and after segmental alignment.

name: nmr-chemical-shift-library-searching
description: Use when a query HSQC spectrum (list of 1H/13C shift pairs) must be identified or annotated by peak-shift matching against a reference library, or when reproducing the SMART 2.0 / NMRShiftDB baseline of a DeepSAT benchmark.

name: nmr-chemical-shift-ph-dependence-modeling
description: Use when simulating 1D or 2D metabolomic 1H NMR spectra at a target pH different from the standard pH0 (usually 7.4) and you must reposition peaks that shift with pH.

name: nmr-chemical-shift-prediction
description: Use when you need predicted 1H NMR shifts across a compound structure library (e.g., SMILES/SDF from the Natural Products Atlas) to assess dereplication coverage or classify shielded vs. deshielded resonances.

name: nmr-concentration-calibration
description: Use when a series of 1D NMR spectra (individual, pseudo-2D, or tabulated text files) has been fitted and fitted signal areas must be converted to mM concentrations and time courses with uncertainties.

name: nmr-coupling-constant-calculation
description: Use when a one-dimensional 1H NMR spectrum (JCAMP-DX) has been loaded and peak-picked, and per-peak coupling constants and multiplicity labels must be derived automatically from the splitting pattern.

name: nmr-cross-peak-overlap-resolution
description: Use when a processed 2D or pseudo-3D NMR spectrum contains significantly overlapped cross-peaks that prevent straightforward peak picking, and quantitatively analyzable individual components (positions, line shapes, intensities) are needed.

name: nmr-data-format-parsing
description: Use when raw 1D 1H NMR spectra in Bruker IVDr format (600 MHz) must be loaded and made ppm-addressable before spectral calibration to the glucose anomeric proton at 5.233 ppm.

name: nmr-dataset-retrieval-from-metabolomics-repositories
description: Use when a task requires acquiring public NMR metabolomics data sets from MetaboLights or Metabolomics Workbench, or when raw repository file-system formats must be converted into analysis-ready formats for MetaboAnalyst or Workflows4Metabolomics.

name: nmr-doublet-signal-interpretation
description: Use when 1H NMR plasma spectra (e.g. FGENTCARD metabo_SE SummarizedExperiment) contain unassigned peaks linked to a phenotype and you need a metabolite assignment via driver-signal correlation.

name: nmr-feature-differential-analysis
description: Use when you have a speaq 2.0 peak-picked/grouped feature matrix (samples x features) plus class metadata for 1D NMR spectra, and you need to find features that significantly differ between two classes (e.g. red vs white wines).

name: nmr-feature-matrix-construction
description: Use when raw 1D NMR spectra must be reduced to a feature matrix of peak groups for downstream statistics (PCA, differential analysis), and binning would lose information.

name: nmr-fid-batch-processing
description: Use when comparing processing speed of NMR software on a batch of 1D 1H-NMR FIDs requiring identical parameters (e.g., zero-filling to 131072 points, 0.3 Hz exponential line broadening, FT, automated phase correction), or when scripting batch NMR pre-processing in Python.

name: nmr-fid-group-delay-correction
description: Use when raw Bruker FIDs (time-domain, complex) carry a DSP digital-filter group delay recorded in the acqus parameters and you need phase-corrected FIDs prior to apodization, zero filling, and Fourier transform.

name: nmr-fid-visualization
description: Use when raw Bruker 'fid' files have just been extracted into a pandas DataFrame (one row per sample) and you need a sanity check that FID traces loaded correctly before group delay removal or Fourier transform.

name: nmr-fit-uncertainty-estimation
description: Use when 1D or pseudo-2D NMR spectra contain overlapping multiplet peaks (e.g. a triplet plus a quadruplet) or low signal-to-noise, and you need quantitative parameters with reported uncertainty rather than simple integration.

name: nmr-fourier-transform-processing
description: Use when raw Bruker time-domain 2D NMR FID data (`fid` or `ser`) must be converted to a phased 2D spectrum via the automated chain: zero-filling, apodization, water suppression, Fourier transformation, phase correction.

name: nmr-gradient-decay-curve-fitting
description: Use when the input is a pseudo-3D NMR series (e.g., pulsed-field-gradient DOSY, or T1/T2/titration/kinetics series of 2D planes) and per-component parameters such as diffusion coefficient D must be extracted, especially when peaks overlap.

name: nmr-hsqc-spectral-library-matching
description: Use when you have HSQC mixture spectra (grid spectra or peak lists) and a compound spectral library (e.g. 501-metabolite MetaboMiner library), and need to detect constituent compounds and estimate concentrations without peak-picking the mixture.

name: nmr-input-vector-preparation-for-cnn-transformer
description: Use when raw 1H NMR spectra (ppm, intensity pairs) and/or 13C chemical-shift lists must be turned into the fixed-length concatenated input vectors expected by the NMR2Struct spectrum-to-structure model before training or single-spectrum inference.

name: nmr-ir-ms-spectra-type-mapping
description: Use when a batch of spectra files (JCAMP-DX, mzML, Bruker, RAW, FID, BagIt or ZIP) must be automatically classified as NMR, IR, MS or unknown before further conversion or rendering.

name: nmr-jcamp-dx-block-parsing
description: Use when a 1H or 13C NMR input file is in JCAMP-DX (.jdx) format and the spectrum must be loaded block-by-block before peak detection or multiplicity analysis, as done in ChemSpectra's NMR workflow.

name: nmr-jres-tissue-distribution-quantification
description: Use when quantifying how metabolites derived from a 13C-labeled amino acid diet are distributed across multiple tissues from integrated 13C-JRES spectra, to assign each compound an enrichment pattern (liver-enriched, liver-depleted, co-enriched).

name: nmr-library-component-matching
description: Use when a mixture 1H NMR spectrum must be deconvolved against reference component spectra and peaks overlap almost completely, lineshapes are distorted, or peaks are shifted — e.g., low-field benchtop (Magritek 43 MHz) data where peak-picking tools fail.

name: nmr-match-ratio-scoring
description: Use when candidate metabolites have been matched to one or more user-defined NMR spectral ROIs and you must filter out metabolites whose SRRMs mostly lie outside the analyzed regions before categorization.

name: nmr-metabolite-assignment
description: Use when 1H-NMR spectra (e.g. plasma metabonomic profiles) yield unassigned peaks linked to a phenotype and you need metabolite-level assignment via co-correlation of ppm signals.

name: nmr-metabolite-distribution-visualization
description: Use when a CSV/TSV of Nightingale 1H-NMR metabolite concentrations (with optional phenotype columns) needs initial inspection: distribution checks, missingness overview, and comparison against the BBMRI-nl reference.

name: nmr-metabolite-identification
description: Use when raw 1H-NMR spectra from cell extracts (e.g., hESC-derived neural stages acquired on a Bruker Avance 800 MHz with cryoprobe) must be converted into a per-sample list of identified metabolites for quantification or pathway analysis.
tools: Bruker Avance 800 MHz NMR spectrometer with cryoprobe

name: nmr-metabolite-integral-pca
description: Use when 1D ¹H NMR plasma/serum spectra have already been processed with SMolESY-select into a metabolite-integral matrix (22 metabolites × N samples), and the goal is exploratory biomarker discovery via dimension reduction rather than fitting/deconvolution-based profiling.

name: nmr-metabolite-phenotype-correlation-computation
description: Use when a matrix of projected metabolic scores (e.g., mortality, MetaboAge, T2D, COVID-severity surrogates) must be correlated with metabolites or phenotypes, or when event prediction over time (Kaplan-Meier) is required.

name: nmr-metabolite-trend-categorization
description: Use when candidate metabolites from ROIs in 1H NMR spectra (e.g. a 0.5-4.5 ppm serum region) must be filtered by match ratio, significance, HMDB concentration, and disease relevance, then sorted into an output table for a disease-vs-control comparison.

name: nmr-metabolomics-biomarker-annotation
description: Use when many mutually correlated candidate biomarkers (e.g. 226 NMR metabolic measures) must be pruned to a subset independently associated with a survival endpoint, using repeated meta-analytic forward-backward selection.

name: nmr-metabolomics-class-discrimination-roc-analysis
description: Use when re-analyzing a public NMR metabolomics study (MetaboLights or Metabolomics Workbench study id) to reproduce reported binary class-discrimination AUCs, e.g. disease vs control groups with labels such as bacterial, viral, control.

name: nmr-metabolomics-data-refitting-from-deposited-tables
description: Use when deposited delay-experiment data tables must be re-analyzed to reproduce or extend metabolite stability time points (20% change threshold) for EDTA plasma, LiHep plasma, or serum from pre-/postcentrifugation delays.

name: nmr-metabolomics-feature-processing
description: Use when input is a raw NMR metabolomics table with sample IDs and metabolite columns containing missing values, and you need an imputed, label-annotated matrix for disease-prediction fine-tuning or AUC evaluation.

name: nmr-metabolomics-phenotype-association-count-extraction
description: Use when the goal is to quantify how many 1H-NMR metabolomics features associate with a clinical endpoint and tabulate surrogate-model performance (AUC, LOBOV, calibration deltas) for a cohort such as LLS_PAROFFs against a reference like BBMRI-nl.

name: nmr-metabolomics-surrogate-score-calibration
description: Use when projected 1H-NMR surrogate scores (e.g. 'high hscrp') from MiMIR need recalibration to a desired cohort, and calibration gain must be quantified on a held-out fraction of samples.

name: nmr-metabolomics-surrogate-validation
description: Use when projected surrogate scores (e.g. diabetes, mortality, MetaboAge-adjacent clinical surrogates) from Nightingale Health 1H-NMR metabolomics must be quality-checked against available phenotypes and published LOBOV AUC references.

name: nmr-metabolomics-table-verification
description: Reference for validating PyINETA INADEQUATE network results against a published table: compare constructed-network, matched-network, and compound counts to the paper's reported values.

name: nmr-metabolomics-validation-cohort-analysis
description: Use when NMR metabolomics samples have known pre- or postcentrifugation delays and you need to test whether delay-prediction models (fit on a training cohort) robustly predict concentrations in an independent validation cohort, with a 10% MPE accuracy threshold.

name: nmr-metabonomic-dataset-loading
description: Use when starting an MWASTools-based metabonomic analysis or vignette-style reproducibility task that needs a ready-made plasma 1H NMR dataset with annotated QC samples.

name: nmr-mixture-deconvolution-penalty-tuning
description: Use when a 1H NMR mixture spectrum must be quantified against library component spectra despite overlapping peaks, unexpected shifts (e.g. different solvents or temperature), low-field benchtop acquisition, or distorted lineshapes from poor shimming.

name: nmr-mixture-dereplication-via-network-matching
description: Use when you have TOCSY and HSQC spectra for a sample set of microbial extracts/prefractions and need to dereplicate known compound families (e.g., novobiocin in prefractions 1565C/1565D) or group samples into regions of related chemical space.

name: nmr-mixture-quantification
description: Use when 1H NMR mixture spectra contain overlapping peaks, shifted resonances (e.g., 36.7 °C sample vs 22.27 °C library), lineshape distortions from inhomogeneous fields, or low-field benchtop resolution, and relative molar proportions of components are needed.

name: nmr-mixture-spectra-cnn-training
description: Use when the goal is compound identification in NMR spectra of mixtures and you have (or can generate) superposed, noise-augmented NMR spectral pairs to train a CNN classifier.

name: nmr-moving-average-smoothing-filter
description: Use when processing 1D 1H NMR serum/plasma spectra (e.g. Bruker IVDr 600 MHz acquisitions) where targeted low-concentration metabolite spin systems are obscured by noise and need a standardized 11-point moving-average denoising before pattern-based assignment.

name: nmr-multiplicity-assignment-from-splitting-pattern
description: Use when processing 1D 1H NMR spectra (e.g. JCAMP-DX from ChemSpectra/Chemotion ELN) and you need automatic peak picking plus coupling constant calculation and multiplicity assignment for the detected signals.

name: nmr-outlier-plate-detection
description: Use when processing UK Biobank NMR biomarker data after regression-based technical-covariate adjustment, when a small number of 96-well shipment plates show unexplained plate-level shifts across a swathe of biomarkers and their samples should be set to missing.

name: nmr-parameter-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when an mcfNMR run has produced F1 scores over scanned (r, theta) combinations for multiple MCF setups and you need to determine parameter robustness and optimal (r, theta) settings per setup.

name: nmr-peak-list-based-mcf-variant-execution
description: Use when the target spectrum is available as a pre-picked peak list (csv with 1H, 13C, optional weights) and you want compound identification that is robust to matrix-induced peak shifts, e.g. pH-disturbed plasma samples like N907.

name: nmr-peak-network-matching
description: Use when you have filtered peak networks from an INADEQUATE NMR spectrum and need to identify metabolites by matching each network to a simulated INADEQUATE database using CSMT, NCMT, and DQMT thresholds.

name: nmr-peak-pairing-between-spectra
description: Use when experimental mixture NMR spectra and pure-component reference spectra are both available and you need to measure how far the same compound's peaks shift between mixtures, e.g. to derive or validate a chemical shift tolerance interval in ppm.

name: nmr-peak-picking
description: Use when a 1D 1H/13C NMR spectrum (JCAMP-DX, or Bruker/FID after conversion) must be reduced to a machine-readable list of detected signal positions and intensities under a default or user-defined threshold.

name: nmr-peak-picking-and-multiplicity-assignment
description: Use when a series of 1D or pseudo-2D NMR spectra (1H, 13C, 31P, 15N) must be quantified and each signal of interest needs peak positions and multiplicity defined before multiplet-model fitting, especially with overlapping peaks.

name: nmr-peak-regrouping-with-ppm-distance
description: Use when peak grouping of 1D NMR spectra (e.g., the wine dataset processed with speaq 2.0) has produced suspect groups, indicated by a low mean silhouette value despite a high average peak SNR.

name: nmr-phase-angle-statistics-visualization
description: Use when comparing automatic phase correction algorithms (e.g. MetaboLabPy baseline-based, MetaboLab apk5, TopSpin apk0.noe, MNova) on replicate NMR series and you need a quantitative within-series phase-consistency benchmark plus comparison figures.

name: nmr-plasma-biomarker-extraction
description: Use when a relative-concentration matrix (e.g. 40 MDS family plasma samples x 38 metabolites from NMRQNet) needs group-difference biomarker calls between patient and control groups via PCA, OPLS-DA, and t-tests.

name: nmr-preprocessing-pipeline-interfacing
description: Use when raw Bruker 1H-NMR metabolomics data (acqus parameters + FIDs, e.g. a Zenodo NMRDataset zip) must be converted into a sample x bin intensity table for multivariate analysis such as PCA.

name: nmr-processing-time-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to compare wall-clock processing speed of NMR software (MetaboLabPy, MNova, TopSpin, MetaboLab scripting) on a defined batch of 1D 1H-NMR spectra with fixed processing parameters.

name: nmr-pulse-sequence-signal-modeling
description: Use when building or validating forward signal models for 1D/2D NMR relaxation or diffusion experiments (T1/T2 relaxation, PFG diffusion) prior to multi-exponential fitting or regularized numerical inversion.

name: nmr-quantification-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when simulated 1D NMR spectra with known ground-truth peak parameters are available and you need to quantify how a perturbation (e.g., zero-order phase distortion) or preprocessing choice degrades peak parameter estimation relative to a phased baseline.

name: nmr-raw-data-availability-assessment
description: Use when you need to quantify how many publicly available studies in a metabolomics repository (e.g. Metabolomics Workbench) use NMR, involve Homo sapiens, or expose raw vendor acquisition files, broken down by sample type or instrument vendor.

name: nmr-raw-spectral-file-parsing
description: Use when raw NMR-based metabolomics files (acqu/acqus, fid, 1r) from MetaboLights or Metabolomics Workbench studies must be reconstructed into a sample-by-spectral-point matrix and binned to exactly 1000 columns.

name: nmr-reference-spectrum-retrieval
description: Use when you need reference-like 1D 1H NMR spectra for blood/urine/CSF and no suitable experimental spectra are available, or when benchmarking spectral algorithms against simulated-vs-real comparisons.

name: nmr-reference-spectrum-retrieval-from-hmdb
description: Use when building simulated 1H NMR case-vs-control spectra from known metabolites, or when detected peak ppm values must be queried against a reference metabolite database such as HMDB.

name: nmr-referencing-calibration
description: Use when a raw 1D 1H NMR spectrum of serum/plasma (e.g. Bruker IVDr 600 MHz format) must be ppm-calibrated before metabolite assignment, integration, or cross-sample comparison.

name: nmr-region-of-interest-metabolite-identification
description: Use when you have 1D proton NMR spectra of biological samples (serum, saliva, urine, CSF, sweat, tissues) with pre-determined ROIs, trends, and significance levels, and need to identify which HMDB metabolites explain those ROI patterns.

name: nmr-signal-calibration-glucose-anomeric
description: Use when 1D 1H NMR spectra of serum or plasma are about to enter a spin-system assignment workflow and must first be referenced to a common chemical-shift axis, e.g. before running SMolESY-select or comparing spectral windows across samples.

name: nmr-signal-substructure-correlation
description: Use when interpreting a trained DeepSAT HSQC model: you need to verify that specific HSQC peaks drive predicted chemical fingerprints or structure classes by masking spectral regions and measuring attribution changes.

name: nmr-simulated-spectra-generation
description: Use when you need controlled benchmark spectra with known ground truth — e.g., to validate SAND quantification (~0.9 correlation), cluster recovery (~74%), or robustness to 0.2 rad phase distortion.

name: nmr-solvent-residual-signal-removal
description: Use when you hold a pandas DataFrame of FIDs (grpd_df) that has already been through group-delay correction, and dominant residual solvent decays must be removed before apodization and Fourier transform in a 1H-NMR metabolomics pipeline.

name: nmr-solvent-suppression
description: Use when processing raw Bruker 2D FID data (fid/ser) from aqueous samples where the dominant solvent peak must be suppressed automatically before Fourier transformation and phase correction.

name: nmr-spectra-compound-identification
