description: Use when you need to identify known compounds in flavor/food mixture samples from 1H NMR spectra rather than run full spectral deconvolution, or when you want to test whether a trained classifier generalizes to unseen compounds by retraining on a reduced standard set.

name: nmr-spectra-dataframe-processing
description: Use when Fourier-transformed 1H-NMR spectra are held as a pandas DataFrame (samples × ppm) and need per-spectrum phase correction or further Protomix preprocessing before statistical analysis.

name: nmr-spectra-file-import
description: Use when raw 1D 1H/13C NMR FID data from Bruker or Agilent/Varian instruments (Bruker folder structure with 1r files), or spectra in nmrML format, must be loaded into NMRProcFlow before baseline correction, alignment, or binning.

name: nmr-spectra-format-conversion
description: Use when raw NMR metabolomics data pulled from MetaboLights or Metabolomics Workbench must be reshaped from repository-specific layouts (.fid, .mzXML, .CNX, .nmrML, .TABULAR, Bruker directories) into an analysis-ready standard format.

name: nmr-spectra-grouping-correction
description: Use when peak-picked, already-grouped NMR spectra contain suspicious peak groups — e.g., a group with a low mean silhouette value (~0.25) but a high average SNR — and the groups must be reassigned before building the feature matrix.

name: nmr-spectra-integral-binning
description: Use when a preprocessed, window-selected NMR spectra matrix (spectra_df, samples x chemical shift points) is still too high-dimensional for multivariate statistics and you need a bucketed feature table with one integrated intensity per fixed ppm bin, while coarsely tolerating residual peak shifts.

name: nmr-spectra-intelligent-binning
description: Use when bucketing aligned, baseline-corrected 1D 1H NMR spectra into a sample x bucket intensity matrix and peak-shift artifacts or information loss from equally sized bins are a concern.

name: nmr-spectra-ppm-shifting
description: Use when raw 1D 1H NMR spectra of serum/plasma (e.g. 600 MHz Bruker IVDr) show uncalibrated chemical-shift axes and a glucose-referenced, reproducible ppm scale is required before metabolite assignment.

name: nmr-spectra-preprocessing
description: Use when a series of raw 1D-NMR metabolomics spectra must be transformed into an aligned, scaled, variance-stabilised matrix ready for multivariate statistical analysis or metabolic tracer data analysis.

name: nmr-spectra-referencing-shifting
description: Reference for aligning chemical shifts of raw INADEQUATE spectra (via basic shifting) before PyINETA peak picking, when input spectra have not yet been referenced and picked_peaks.csv coordinates must fall on the correct chemical-shift axis.

name: nmr-spectra-series-shift-export
description: Use when a series of 1D-NMR spectra shows chemical-shift variability that must be corrected before multivariate statistical analysis, and per-spectrum optimum shifts need to be computed and exported.

name: nmr-spectra-viewer-grouping
description: Use when you have a set of 1D 1H or 13C NMR spectra plus an experimental-design table recording factor levels per spectrum, and you need spectra rendered overlaid or stacked, colored by factor level.

name: nmr-spectra-visual-inspection
description: Use when raw 1D NMR spectra (FID from Bruker or Agilent/Varian) need to be visually explored — e.g. to locate a reference resonance for ppm calibration, check alignment, or compare spectra grouped by experimental factor.

name: nmr-spectra-wavelet-peak-detection
description: Use when raw 1D NMR spectra (e.g. 40 wine spectra × 8712 ppm points, or 31 urine spectra) must be reduced to a feature matrix of peaks, avoiding binning's information loss and user-dependent bin boundaries.

name: nmr-spectra-webgl-contour-visualization
description: Use when an already-processed 2D or pseudo-3D NMR spectrum needs interactive contour or 3D surface-mesh rendering that is architecture- and OS-independent, with no installation required.

name: nmr-spectral-adaptive-binning
description: Use when a 1D frequency-domain (ppm-axis) metabolomics NMR spectrum must be partitioned into frequency bins and converted into per-bin time-domain FIDs for time-domain deconvolution or peak-table generation.

name: nmr-spectral-assignment
description: Use when analyzing 1D 1H NMR spectra of serum/plasma samples (e.g. IVDr 600 MHz acquisition) to assign and quantify specific metabolite spin systems via spectral-window binning rather than full spectral deconvolution.

name: nmr-spectral-binning-and-normalization-chaining
description: Use when you have phase-corrected, baseline-corrected, peak-aligned 1H-NMR spectra (e.g. Protomix spectra_df from Bruker FID processing) and need a binned, normalized sample-by-bin matrix as input to PCA or similar statistical analysis.

name: nmr-spectral-data-augmentation
description: Use when you need to construct an augmented training/validation/test set of NMR spectral pairs from a small flavor-standard spectral database, or need pseudo-mixture spectra (e.g., augmented F10) to benchmark a component-identification model.

name: nmr-spectral-data-augmentation
description: Use when training deep-learning metabolite identification/quantification models (e.g. CRNN in NMRQNet) but no public annotated NMR spectra database exists and training spectra must be synthesized from a metabolite reference spectral library.

name: nmr-spectral-data-io
description: Use when input is raw or already processed 1D ¹H NMR serum/plasma spectra (e.g. Bruker IVDr 600 MHz acquisitions from MetaboLights MTBLS395) that must be read into memory, normalized to a common chemical-shift reference, or smoothed to recover low-abundance metabolite signals.

name: nmr-spectral-deconvolution
description: Use when 1D NMR spectra (e.g., urine metabolomics FIDs) have heavily overlapping peaks that bin-based integration cannot resolve, and the goal is an automated peak table for quantification, spike-in linearity checks, or correlation-network annotation.

name: nmr-spectral-encoder-feature-concatenation
description: Use when building or reproducing an end-to-end spectrum-to-structure model whose input is concatenated 1H/13C NMR spectra and whose downstream head is a pretrained transformer generating SMILES.

name: nmr-spectral-global-shift-correction
description: Use when a CRNN reconstruction of a 1H NMR plasma spectrum is misaligned relative to the target spectrum and metabolite candidates must be aligned before local quantification optimization.

name: nmr-spectral-inference
description: Use when given 1H NMR spectral data of a flavor mixture and a standards library, and the goal is to predict the mixture's component list and quantify identification accuracy (ACC/TPR/FPR).

name: nmr-spectral-noise-augmentation
description: Use when training a supervised NMR mixture-identification model and labeled experimental mixture spectra are too scarce — synthesize realistic mixtures from measured pure-compound 1H NMR spectra with variability simulation.

name: nmr-spectral-noise-region-selection
description: Use when a raw 1D NMR spectrum (ppm scale plus intensity array) has a distorted baseline and you need baseline points selected only in signal-free regions before spline fitting and subtraction.

name: nmr-spectral-peak-coordinate-matching
description: Use when a target NMR mixture spectrum and a library of compound spectra are both available as coordinate/weight tables (csv with '1H', '13C', optional 'weights' columns) and the goal is compound identification plus concentration estimation by optimal spectral fitting.

name: nmr-spectral-peak-detection
description: Use when the input is a simulated (e.g. MetAssimulo 2.0) or real 1D 1H, 2D J-Res or COSY NMR spectrum and you need to identify peak positions/clusters before downstream analysis such as mixture spectrum simulation or metabolite quantification.

name: nmr-spectral-peak-grouping
description: Use when raw 1D 1H NMR spectra (spectra matrix + ppm vector) must be summarized into features with minimal information loss, especially when shifts or multiplet structure would make binning/bucketing lossy.

name: nmr-spectral-peak-picking
description: Use when you have a processed, frequency-domain 2D NMR spectrum (after Fourier transformation, phasing, baseline correction) and need a peak list of cross-peak positions and intensities via local maxima detection.

name: nmr-spectral-phase-and-baseline-preprocessing
description: Use when raw 1D 1H NMR spectra of serum/plasma (e.g. Bruker IVDr 600 MHz, MTBLS395-style data) must be ppm-calibrated and baseline-suppressed before metabolite assignment or integration.

name: nmr-spectral-phase-correction
description: Use when processing a series of 1D-NMR spectra (e.g. metabolomics profiles) whose baselines show phasing/roll, and a manually phase-corrected reference spectrum is available to seed automated ph0/ph1 optimisation.

name: nmr-spectral-preprocessing
description: Use when raw 1H NMR spectra (e.g. EDTA, heparin, or citrate anticoagulated plasma) must be cleaned and formatted into the NMRQNet CSV layout prior to CRNN identification or quantification.

name: nmr-spectral-processing
description: Use when raw Bruker fid/ser time-domain NMR FID data needs processing into a phased, baseline-corrected spectrum without installing software, or when NUS 2D/pseudo-3D/3D data requires direct-FT or iterative SMILE reconstruction.

name: nmr-spectral-realignment
description: Use when overlaid/stacked 1D 1H NMR spectra show uncontrolled chemical shift variations between spectra after ppm-scale calibration, i.e. peaks of the same metabolite drift across the spectral dimension.

name: nmr-spectral-recalibration-glucose-anomeric-proton
description: Use when raw 1D 1H NMR spectra from Bruker IVDr 600 MHz serum/plasma cohorts show ppm drift that must be corrected before metabolite assignment, bin-based integration, or cross-sample comparison.

name: nmr-spectral-reconstruction-error-evaluation
description: Use when you have raw 1H NMR spectra (csv with chemical shifts in column 1, one column per sample) plus a method's reconstructed spectra and want a per-sample fidelity metric, especially to expose regional reconstruction failure.

name: nmr-spectral-reconstruction-mse-optimization
description: Use when refining per-metabolite concentration and chemical-shift-position estimates from an initial NMR spectral fitting (e.g., CRNN output) so the reconstructed 1H NMR spectrum minimizes MSE against the original plasma spectrum.

name: nmr-spectral-reproducibility-assessment
description: Use when 1H-NMR metabonomic features must be validated for analytical reproducibility via QC-sample CVs, or when deciding whether to filter metabolic features at CV < 0.30 (biomarker discovery) or CV < 0.15 (quantification).

name: nmr-spectral-residual-minimization
description: Use when refining per-metabolite concentration and position estimates after an initial deep-learning (CRNN) NMR spectral fit, when reconstruction residuals must be locally minimized via MSE.

name: nmr-spectral-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to verify that a fully automated NMR metabolite-assignment pipeline (SMolESY-select) is fast enough for high-throughput processing of standard 1D 1H NMR serum spectra, e.g. an external cohort like MTBLS395.

name: nmr-spectral-segmental-alignment
description: Use when a series of 1D-NMR spectra (e.g. a metabolomics sample set) shows chemical-shift drift within a spectral region and peaks must be aligned to a reference spectrum before multivariate statistical analysis.

name: nmr-spectral-zero-filling-apodization
description: Use when starting from raw Bruker time-domain FID files (fid or ser) and an unprocessed 2D or pseudo-3D NMR spectrum is needed; triggers include 'free induction decay' input and no phased spectrum yet.

name: nmr-spectrum-inference-decoding
description: Use when you have a trained multitask spectrum-to-structure checkpoint and simulated 1H/13C NMR spectra (concatenated 28000-point 1H grid plus 80-bin 13C shifts) and need SMILES structure predictions without molecular formula input.

name: nmr-spectrum-phase-and-baseline-correction
description: Use when you have Fourier-transformed 1H-NMR spectra (e.g. Protomix spectra_df from 10000-point zero-filled FIDs) that still show phase errors and baseline offsets before referencing, binning, or normalization.

name: nmr-spectrum-probability-measure-representation
description: Use when quantifying components of 1H NMR mixture spectra that suffer from overlapping peaks, shifted resonances, low resolution, or distorted lineshapes where peak-based deconvolution methods fail.

name: nmr-spectrum-simulation
description: Use when you need synthetic metabolomic 1H NMR spectra (1D, 2D J-Res, or 2D COSY) of urine, blood, or CSF mixtures — e.g. for benchmarking spectral processing algorithms or reproducing paper comparisons against real spectra.

name: nmr-spin-system-feature-construction
description: Use when you have 2D NMR (TOCSY + HSQC) peak data from complex natural product mixtures and need discrete, comparable spin system features to drive sample-to-sample similarity networks.

name: nmr-spin-system-pattern-search
description: Use when you need to assign metabolite signals in calibrated 1D 1H NMR serum/plasma spectra to a curated metabolite panel by matching spin-system patterns inside spectral windows derived from a large cohort.

name: nmr-star-entry-sequence-extraction
description: Use when starting from a BMRB accession (or a local NMR-STAR entry) and you need the protein entity sequence in FASTA format to run BLAST-based cross-linking of BMRB archive data to external public databases.

name: nmr-star-file-parsing
description: Use when a task requires reading, validating, or extracting saveframes and loops (e.g., the assigned Atom_chem_shift chemical shift loop, NOE/dihedral restraint saveframes) from a BMRB entry in NMR-STAR format.

name: nmr-star-schema-validation
description: Use when input is an archival BMRB NMR-STAR entry file that must be parsed, validated against the NMR-STAR 3.2 schema, or converted (e.g., to NEF) before deposition or downstream analysis.

name: nmr-structure-annotation
description: Use when you have 1H-13C HSQC (optionally multiplicity edited) NMR peak lists from a small natural product or metabolite and need to retrieve candidate structures or nearest known compounds from large chemical databases rather than limited NMR spectral libraries.

name: nmr-structure-calculation
description: Use when you have NEF files containing NMR constraints for proteins and need to generate an ensemble of ranked structural conformers via torsion-angle dynamics.

name: nmr-study-file-validation
description: Use when a study downloaded from MetaboLights or Metabolomics Workbench has been converted to CloMet's internal standard (a_ / i_ / m_ / s_ / audit metadata files with per-sample experiment directories holding acqu, acqus, fid) and you must decide whether it is usable downstream.

name: nmr-time-domain-fid-processing
description: Use when raw Bruker time-domain FID files (`fid` or `ser`) must be turned into inspectable, phased 2D spectra and no manually tuned processing parameters are available or desired.

name: nmr-tocsy-hsqc-spin-system-construction
description: Use when you have paired TOCSY and HSQC spectra for multiple complex natural products extract/prefraction samples and need shared spin system features to cluster samples or dereplicate known scaffolds.

name: nmr-voigt-lineshape-fitting
description: Use when processed 2D/pseudo-3D NMR spectra contain overlapping cross-peaks requiring per-peak quantitative parameters (amplitudes, widths, relaxation T1/T2, concentrations) that simple peak picking cannot resolve.

name: nmr-wine-spectra-multivariate-analysis
description: Use when a peak-based NMR feature matrix (e.g. from speaq 2.0 peak picking and grouping) is available and the goal is to test whether samples separate by a known class label such as wine colour via PCA.

name: nnmf-fragmentation-factorization
description: Use when deposited GC-MS datasets contain co-eluting compounds whose fragmentation spectra must be auto-deconvoluted (e.g. breathomics or volatilome data) before repository-scale GNPS molecular networking analysis.

name: node-attribute-mapping
description: Use when a calculated metabolic network edge list must be linked back to per-metabolite measurements or annotations before export to Cytoscape, especially when numeric node IDs were assigned by row order of the uploaded data.

name: node-attribute-masking-perturbation-analysis
description: Use when you need to determine which node attributes of a trained GNN (e.g. SigmaCCS CCS predictions) most affect prediction accuracy by perturbing each input feature and measuring the resulting performance drop.

name: node-centrality-network-analysis
description: Use when you have two processed abundance matrices (e.g., metabolite and protein feature tables across the same samples) and need to build a correlation-based network and identify hub nodes via centrality metrics.

name: noise-factor-computation-across-datasets
description: Use when evaluating how noisy spectra and missing fragmentation ions affect de novo peptide sequencing, by annotating MGF spectra against validated PSMs and computing per-dataset noise factors.

name: noise-ion-filtering
description: Use when preprocessing a pixel × m/z feature matrix (X/Y coordinate columns plus ion intensity columns) to remove spatially random, likely non-biological ions before metabolite annotation, UMAP-kmeans/Seurat pixel clustering, SpaGene co-expression analysis, or differential analysis.

name: noise-ion-score-filtering
description: Use when preprocessing a spatial metabolomics peak table matrix (pixels x ions with X/Y coordinates) to remove randomly distributed noise ions that would interfere with spatial pattern recognition or downstream clustering.

name: noise-ion-statistics
description: Use when calibrating an electronic ('grass') noise filter for high-resolution MS/MS data: you need an empirical, instrument-specific intensity-coincidence threshold rather than a fixed base-peak-height cutoff.

name: noise-model-function-implementation
description: Use when implementing, reproducing, or validating SMITER's intensity-specific chromatographic peak-noise model — i.e., when you need sigma as a function of signal intensity for synthetic mzML generation or noise-model comparison.

name: noise-peak-filtering
description: Use when MS/MS spectra read from an MGF or mzML file need low-intensity noise peaks removed and peak counts capped before plotting, spectrum comparison, or downstream processing.

name: noise-peak-injection-calibration
description: Use when you need to degrade reference MS/MS spectra (mzML/mzXML-derived peak lists) to match lower biological-sample quality before evaluating structure-annotation confidence scores.

name: noise-peak-quantification
description: Use when you have validated MS/MS spectra with known ground-truth peptides plus de novo predictions, and need to characterize noise levels, missing cleavage-site ions, or their effect on peptide recall.

name: noise-perturbation-error-grid-analysis
description: Decision support for determining at which added-error levels simulated single-tracer or multi-tracer isotopologue datasets remain usable for moiety model selection, e.g. when extending robustness evaluation beyond sigma in {0.001, 0.01, 0.1}.

name: noise-perturbation-robustness-testing
description: Use when you need to test whether a structure-annotation or scoring method degrades gracefully under degraded spectral quality — e.g. added noise levels, differing collision energies, or merged-versus-single spectra — and want ROC/hop-plot metrics as evidence.

name: noise-robustness-evaluation-of-eics
description: Use when LC/MS metabolomics extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) must be scored or filtered for quality — especially EICs with high background signals or only a single peak, where the MCQ index cannot fairly evaluate them.

name: noiseless-time-course-simulation-for-model-benchmarking
description: Use when establishing an upper-bound accuracy baseline for methods that infer absolute concentrations from relative abundance time-course data, before testing noisy or sparse regimes.

name: noisy-spectra-filtering
description: Use when building a curated MS2 training set from reference-standard or raw lipid spectra and noisy profiles must be excluded before model training or spectral storage.

name: non-enzymatic-psm-dataset-splitting
description: Use when fine-tuning or benchmarking a de novo sequencing model on non-tryptic/non-enzymatic spectra, and you need annotated MGF training/validation/test splits rather than tryptic MassIVE-KB data.

name: non-mwtab-response-handling-csv-json-text
description: Use when downloading Metabolomics Workbench REST responses (csv, json, or text) that cannot be parsed into mwTab format and need to be captured as raw payload via MWRESTFile.

name: non-specific-digest-database-search
description: Use when analyzing MHC class I immunopeptidomics (non-enzymatic) DDA spectra and you need a database-search reference peptide set at 1% FDR to compare against de novo sequencing predictions.

name: non-systematic-identifier-mapping
description: Use when metabolite entries from merged studies carry non-systematic identifiers (CAS, HMDB, KEGG, etc.) instead of InChIKeys and a systematic, structure-based key is needed for dataset merging.

name: nonlinear-threshold-definition
description: Use when a two-dataset LC-MS metabolomics feature correspondence already contains unique matches (post Step 2) but the plain box thresholds in RT, m/z, and FI are too tight for features under large local shift trends, so candidate matches need to be re-scored and poor matches deleted.

name: nonmem-map-estimation-execution
description: Use when replicating or benchmarking individual parameter estimation in NONMEM for simulated PK profiles, especially to cross-check mapbayr or another open-source MAP-BE tool on the same model-profile pairs.

name: nonmem-mapbayr-concordance-analysis
description: Use when validating an open-source MAP-BE implementation (e.g. mapbayr) against NONMEM on simulated PK profiles, especially when discrepancies arise from estimated lag time, infusion duration, or models with large IIV (omega^2 > 1).

name: nonnegative-least-squares-tissue-fitting
description: Decision support for mapping single-cell-derived chemical dictionaries onto tissue MSI pixels — use when you have cross-annotated SCMS clusters and a shared lipid feature matrix with a tissue pixel matrix and want per-cluster spatial contribution maps.

name: nonparametric-hypothesis-testing
description: Use when two independent score distributions (e.g., Known vs Random enzyme-substrate pairs scored via MEANtools createGnnSom) must be compared nonparametrically, with reported statistics available for validation.

name: nonparametric-rank-based-testing
description: Use when the target (metadata) design is a two- or three-group metabolomics/proteomics comparison whose features fail parametric assumptions, and per-feature p-values plus FDR adjustment are needed.

name: nonparametric-significance-testing
description: Use when two MS/MS prediction models yield per-compound cosine-similarity scores against the same experimental Q-TOF test set and you must claim one significantly outperforms the other per ion mode ([M+H]+, [M-H]-).

name: nonparametric-significance-testing-mann-whitney
description: Use when comparing a gene's expression distributions between two independent, unpaired sample groups (e.g. LIHC tumor vs non-tumor) from an expression matrix and metadata, without assuming normality of expression values.

name: nonparametric-u-test-group-comparison
description: Use when a numerical column has exactly two categorical groups (e.g. Condition), the data may violate parametric assumptions, and an interactive p-value for the two-group comparison is needed on a chart.

name: noreva-workflow-performance-ranking
description: Use when a multiclass or time-course metabolomic peak table (e.g. GC-MS quadrupole MTBLS6 fetal calf serum with spiked aspartic acid and malic acid at 6/12/25/50 µL) must be processed by an optimized workflow chosen from thousands of stage combinations.

name: noreva-workflow-scan-configuration
description: Use when the input is a time-course metabolomic peak table (e.g. MTBLS656 plasma samples labelled T0–T48) and the goal is to identify the study-specific optimal processing workflow by exhaustively scoring all S1–S4 method combinations.

name: normal-density-scoring-candidates
description: Use when a MetFrag2.2 run has user-supplied reference standard retention times plus measured RT of the unknown, and candidates should be ranked using the log P vs RT correlation term (Eq. 9-10).

name: normal-mixture-density-evaluation
description: Use when dissimilarity scores from matched metabolite pairs have been fitted with a normal mixture via the EM algorithm and you must validate the fitted component means, variances, and mixing proportions against a non-parametric density estimate.

name: normalization-benchmark-heatmap-visualization
description: Decision support for choosing a normalization method before running the MetaboDirect pipeline on peak abundance tables with assigned molecular formulas — trigger when the pipeline's normalization step must be justified per dataset.

name: normalization-factor-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to test whether a normalization-factor estimator stays unbiased when the fraction of up-regulated features is imbalanced, e.g. validating MDFC-like estimators against median FC or other MAFFIN norm methods.

name: normalization-method-benchmarking
description: Use when several normalization methods (e.g., tGAM/rGAM/rLOESS vs QC-RLSC, QC-RSC, SERFF, TIGER) must be compared on a batched metabolomics dataset to decide which recovers signal, using DAM overlap, p-value correlation, and replicate MAD concordance rather than QC-RSD reduction or DAM counts as.

name: normalization-method-comparative-assessment
description: Use when a metabolomics featuredata matrix is subject to unwanted variation (batch/matrix effects) and several candidate normalization methods must be implemented, assessed, and compared before choosing one.

name: normalized-abundance-statistics
description: Use when a targeted metabolomics workflow has produced normalized abundances for compounds across replicate injections or QC samples, and you need to report per-compound and average variability (STD) to benchmark a quantitation tool or deconvolution setting.

name: normalized-dot-product-reference-features
description: Use when encoding MS/MS spectra as neural-network input features and you need a fixed-size, comparable similarity block (500 dot products against reference spectra) alongside precursor Gray codes and binned fragment intensities.

name: normalized-dot-product-spectrum-scoring
description: Use when query MS/MS spectra must be dereplicated against reference library spectra (e.g., GNPS community libraries), or when putative analogs must be found via modification-tolerant peak matching around a precursor mass difference delta.

name: normalized-root-mean-square-difference-analysis
description: Use when two implementations of the same spectral simulation (or two paired sets of metabolite basis functions) must be numerically compared per metabolite to demonstrate equivalence, e.g., validating an accelerated simulator against a reference codebase.

name: novel-metabolite-classification
description: Use when a detected feature table (paired m/z and RT values from LC-HRMS) must be split into metabolites that were predicted by an in silico tool versus those detected only postincubation with no predicted m/z match.

name: novel-metabolite-formula-annotation
description: Use when annotating molecular formulas de novo from tandem MS spectra without spectral/structure databases, or when claiming a molecular formula is novel (absent from PubChem/ChemSpider).

name: novelty-filtering-against-pubchem
description: Use when COSMIC or CSI:FingerID annotations must be reduced to compounds never reported before, e.g. before ranking 'truly novel' bile acid conjugates or HMDB-absent metabolites.

name: np-producer-organism-fraction-analysis
description: Use when analyzing a natural products dataset with recorded producing organisms and you need per-category producer fractions (e.g., plants ~65%, animals ~0.5%) plus cross-category production overlap counts.

name: np3-shifted-cosine-similarity
description: Use when clustering or de-replicating MS2 consensus spectra from LC–MS/MS untargeted metabolomics (e.g. per-sample MGFs from NP3 preprocessing) so that redundant spectra of the same ion merge while isomers stay separate.

name: npclassifier-chemical-class-annotation
description: Use when you have standardized InChIKeys for compounds from one or more OMSLs (e.g. FragHub 'standardize lib' files) and need chemical-class labels — pathway, superclass, class — for class-distribution tables, library comparisons, or coloring t-SNE/fingerprint-based chemical-space plots.

name: npclassifier-chemical-class-mapping
description: Use when compound–organism records need to be assigned to NPClassifier chemical classes and class-level censuses (distinct class counts, class coverage fractions per family) must be computed or validated.

name: npclassifier-chemical-classification-matching
description: Use when filtering predicted/machine-generated NP structures (e.g. a vendor or combinatorial source mixed with curated NPs) using NP-likeness score, NPclassifier class assignments, or sugar-moiety flags as retention criteria.

name: npclassifier-class-accuracy-assessment
description: Use when reproducing or validating DeepSAT's reported structure-class performance (Top-1 accuracy 90.4% normal / 90.8% edited HSQC) on HSQC test spectra with ground-truth NPClassifier classes.

name: npclassifier-compound-taxonomy-assignment
description: Use when per-feature SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID candidate structures (2D SMILES) from LC-MS/MS DDA metabolomics data must be classified into natural-product chemical classes to enrich the knowledge graph for downstream SPARQL querying.

name: npclassifier-superclass-probability-prediction
description: Use when the only input is a 1H-13C HSQC spectrum (normal or multiplicity-edited) and you need predicted NPClassifier superclass labels/probabilities for a compound whose authentic NMR reference is absent from spectral libraries.

name: npclassscore-class-matching-filtering
description: Use when NPLinker co-occurrence (standardised Metcalf) scoring yields long candidate BGC-GCF to MS/MS spectrum link lists and you need to filter or prioritise links using chemical-class agreement, e.g. on paired PoDP genomics–metabolomics datasets.

name: npclassscore-scoring-table-generation
description: Use when building or updating the NPClassScore scoring tables needed by NPLinker, i.e. you must bridge genome-based BGC classes to structure-based chemical classes using experimentally validated MIBiG BGC–product pairs.

name: npeaks-multiple-match-cluster-evaluation
description: Use when an M2S-style matching of two untargeted LC-MS metabolomics feature lists (matched on RT, m/z, FI) leaves clusters of multiple candidate matches, and you need to gauge match quality via the unique-to-multiple-match ratio and npeaks differences.

name: npfimg-marker-feature-identification
description: Use when processing GC–MS or LC–MS chromatography–mass spectrometry data as a two-dimensional MS map (m/z vs retention time) to identify and visualize multivariate chemo-/biomarker features without conventional peak picking.

name: npp-output-import-xcms

name: nrp-sequence-topology-classification

description: Use when an orphan metabolite's known substructures (e.g. sugars, methylaminosugars, halogenated aromatics) must be matched to a candidate BGC region in a genome assembly that antiSMASH annotates but BGC databases lack.

name: orthology-based-reaction-annotation-transfer
description: Use when building a draft GSMN for a species with a genome annotation but no dedicated metabolic model, using curated reference algal/plant networks as orthology donors (e.g., A. thaliana, G. sulphuraria, E. siliculosus → C. crispus).

name: osf-deposit-data-retrieval
description: Use when a published paper states that its 'input and output data are available on OSF' and downstream reproduction or benchmarking requires those exact files (e.g. annotation outputs, benchmarking datasets) before any local computation can start.

name: otsu-threshold-image-segmentation
description: Use when an LA-ICP-MS elemental image (2D delimited text / NumPy export) needs tissue/background segmentation via automatic image thresholding, e.g. Otsu, median binary filter, or multi-level k-means.

name: out-of-bag-error-estimation
description: Use when imputing a masked n x p matrix with missForest and you need an imputation error estimate (NRMSE for continuous, PFC for categorical variables) without a test set of true values.

name: out-of-memory-spectral-data-processing
description: Use when raw MSI spectra (e.g. imzML or Analyze 7.5 files) are too large to fit in memory, and pre-processing (normalize, smooth, reduceBaseline, peakPick) or PCA must be run on the full dataset.

name: outlier-cluster-filtering-of-metabolite-measurements
description: Use when sample-level outliers distort the metabolite measurement table — e.g. the outlier heatmap shows samples grouping into a distinct k-means cluster that should be removed prior to normalization or differential testing.

name: outlier-identification-from-drift-plots
description: Use when QC-based drift correction (e.g. QC-RLSC) leaves suspicious non-monotonic intensity excursions in biological (non-QC) samples, and you need to locate and remove outlier features before normalization.

name: outlier-injection-benchmarking
description: Use when you must quantify whether outlier counts or magnitudes degrade QC-based normalization methods (e.g., QC-RLSC, QC-RSC) relative to robust alternatives (rLOESS, rGAM, tGAM) on data with a known drift pattern.

name: outlier-injection-robustness-assessment
description: Use when benchmarking outlier robustness of QC-based LC-MS metabolomics normalization methods on simulated data where ground-truth drift is known and outliers can be injected at controlled counts and magnitudes.

name: outlier-sample-removal-from-experiment
description: Use when a lipidomics experiment (e.g. Metabolomics Workbench study imported into R) must be quality-controlled before differential or multivariate analysis, and suspect samples must be identified and dropped.

name: outlier-trimming-quantile-statistics
description: Use when matched peak-area tables from two peak-detection tools on the same LC-HRMS dataset (e.g. PeakBot profile-mode vs XCMS centroid-mode on the PHM dataset) need an agreement metric, and a small fraction of features with too dissimilar areas must be excluded before reporting correlation.

name: output-file-size-comparison-analysis
description: Use when two alternative tools visualize or transform the same large dataset and you must quantify scalability by timing load performance and comparing output file sizes, e.g. EMPeror (26 MB) versus KiNG (1.85 GB) for PCoA plots.

name: output-folder-organization-for-qc-reports
description: Use when per-ion peak metrics for auto-tracked and user-specified ions have already been extracted and must be reported as CSV summaries plus JPG/PDF figures organized per ion and per metric for operator inspection.

name: over-representation-analysis-fishers-exact-test
description: Use when you have a query set of metabolite/lipid identifiers and a pathway-to-feature mapping table, and need to identify which pathways are over-represented at adjusted p-value < 0.05.

name: over-representation-analysis-kegg
description: Use when you have a precomputed list of significant gene-expression or metabolite identifiers (e.g., KEGG IDs) and want to test whether KEGG pathways are over-represented, optionally feeding p-values into eSPIA or Pbine.

name: over-representation-analysis-of-go-terms
description: Use when you have a gene list associated with an exposure or network module (e.g. chemical-exposome-linked gene nodes from a MetaNet co_net object) and need enriched GO biological functions.

name: over-representation-analysis-of-kegg-pathways
description: Use when a list of genes significantly associated with an exposure layer (e.g., microbial or chemical exposome nodes in a MetaNet multi-omics network) needs pathway-level functional interpretation via KEGG or GO over-representation testing.

name: over-representation-pathway-analysis
description: Use when a SpaMTP-integrated Seurat object has per-cluster differentially expressed metabolites (FindAllDEMs) and genes, and you need region-level pathway enrichment (e.g. lesioned vs intact striatum).

name: overfitting-assessment-via-error-differences
description: Use when several regression models (e.g. RF, BRNN, XGBoost, LightGBM, Keras) have been fit on the same training data with 80:20 splits and you must decide which model generalizes by comparing [test-training] and [validation-training] MAE gaps rather than raw test-set metrics alone.

name: overfitting-control-in-mcmc-spectral-modeling
description: Use when fitting time-domain 1D NMR FID data (e.g., 16,384 complex points) with an MCMC or iterative peak-decomposition model and you need to infer a reasonable number of peaks without overfitting.

name: overfitting-diagnosis-high-dimensional-feature-tables
description: Use when fitting supervised discriminant models (e.g. OPLS-DA in the ropls package) to high-dimensional LC-MS/MS feature tables (thousands of features, hundreds of samples) and you must verify whether reported class separation generalizes.

name: overfitting-pipeline-comparison
description: Use when a metabolomics predictive model (e.g., RF or elastic net on selected metabolites) must be validated with a train-vs-test AUC comparison to quantify overfitting, as in iMAP's new model-building module.

name: overlap-statistics-aggregation
description: Use when validating a new HRMS peak-picking workflow against established open-source tools (MSDIAL, XCMS) by matching m/z–RT feature pairs across pipelines on samples of known composition and reporting overlap fractions.

name: overlapping-cluster-detection
description: Use when you have pairwise Pearson correlations between transcripts and mass features across samples and need overlapping (non-partitional) network clusters, since a mass feature can belong to multiple candidate biosynthetic pathways.

name: overlapping-peak-deconvolution
description: Use when 1D or pseudo-2D NMR spectra contain overlapping multiplet signals (e.g. a triplet and quadruplet, or overlapping ADP/ATP peaks) and accurate peak parameters must be recovered by model-based fitting rather than integration.

name: overlapping-peak-detection
description: Use when annotating matrix-related peaks (e.g. Agn+ clusters with formula 'Ag1') in MSI peak matrices and a cluster's similarity scores S1/S2 fall below the user threshold, indicating a possibly co-isolated endogenous peak.

name: overlapping-window-coverage-design
description: Use when preparing raw timsTOF frames (Bruker TDF data accessed via OpenTIMS/pyproteolizard-data) for LSH-based signal classification and you must choose window lengths, inter-set offsets, and bin widths before hashing.

name: overrepresentation-analysis-single-cell-metabolomics
description: Use when you have MS1-only metabolite annotations (e.g., METASPACE annotations at FDR <= 0.1) from a single-cell or spatial metabolomics experiment and need ORA that accounts for isomeric/isobaric identification ambiguity.

name: oxidized-fatty-acid-notation
description: Use when lipid abbreviation inputs (e.g. oxidized fatty-acid shorthand like HETE, PONPC) fail to convert to LipidLynxX IDs and you need to add a new input style via a rule-based JSON alias configuration file.

name: oxidized-lipid-class-identification
description: Use when annotating ddMS2-topN or AIF UHPLC-HRMS/MS features that may derive from oxidized fatty acids or other oxidized lipids absent from standard libraries like LipidBlast (26 classes) — e.g. features matching precursor m/z of O/OH/OOH or aldehyde/carboxylic-acid FA species.

name: oxidized-lipid-library-search
description: Use when precursor accurate masses from oxidized phospholipid screening need annotation against oxidized lipids not present in public databases such as LIPID MAPS.

name: oxidized-pc-species-identifier-mapping
description: Use when a fixed sample of oxidized PC species retrieved from CMM 3.0 (via its RESTful API) must be checked for presence/absence in a public reference like LIPID MAPS to quantify novel, non-overlapping oxidized lipids.

name: p-value-combination-weighted-fisher
description: Use when individual metabolomics studies report only P-values and fold-changes (no raw data, SD, or variance) and a combined significance per metabolite across studies is needed.

name: p-value-comparison-table-compilation
description: Use when benchmarking group-level metabolite pathway enrichment tools on a shared metabolite list and you need a side-by-side comparison of each tool's top significant pathway and its enrichment P value.

name: p-value-distribution-aggregation
description: Use when comparing robustness of pathway ranking methods on metabolomics peak data by repeating an analysis over multiple random feature-removal replicates and summarising each method's p-value distribution as mean and variance.

name: p-value-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when a pathway overrepresentation analysis produces a table of raw per-pathway p-values from Fisher's exact test (or Fisher's-method combined metabolite/gene p-values) and they must be corrected for multiple testing before ranking or cutoff filtering.

name: p-value-verification-against-publication-text
description: Use when extracting reported model significance values (e.g. OPLS-DA p-values) from a metabolomics paper's text/figures and validating each against its verbatim source span before writing to a results table.

name: package-manager-automation
description: Use when a clean Ubuntu 18.04 environment needs a metabolomics software stack installed and manually resolving each tool's dependencies would be error-prone or time-consuming.

name: paga-trajectory-inference
description: Use when you have clustered single-cell metabolic profiles (e.g. a Leiden-partitioned AnnData built from a SpaceM spatio-molecular matrix like MORPHnMOL.csv) and need to infer connectivity/relationships between metabolic states and embed them coherently with UMAP.

name: pagerank-representative-ion-selection
description: Use when clean consensus spectra from an LC–MS/MS untargeted metabolomics run contain multiple ionization variants (in-source fragments, adducts, dimers) of one precursor that must be deconvoluted to a single protonated [M+H]+ entity per variant group.

name: paired-adipose-tissue-lipidomics-context
description: Use when two feature-selection lists (e.g. VIP > 1 metabolites from PLS-DA under two processing strategies such as LMM vs M0) must be compared to quantify shared and uniquely identified discriminative metabolites.

name: paired-coefficient-of-variation-comparison
description: Use when two peak-integration approaches must be quantitatively compared on log2 peak areas per target, and replicate QC data are available to compute per-target CVs for a paired significance test.

name: paired-nonparametric-method-comparison
description: Use when two or more metabolomics normalization methods must be compared on identical GC-MS feature-intensity data with paired per-metabolite precision (RSD) values, to decide which method yields the highest coverage of compounds passing a <30% RSD threshold.

name: paired-omics-bgc-spectrum-link-validation
description: Use when a paired omics (genome + metabolomics) dataset contains curated validated genome-metabolome links and you must quantify how many survive Metcalf and NPClassScore filtering, or verify prioritisation/rank improvements of known links.

name: paired-omics-data-retrieval
description: Use when a linking or benchmarking analysis needs paired genome+LC-MS/MS samples with validated BGC–metabolite links, e.g. from the PoDP or a GNPS job task, to build fingerprints or evaluate precision/recall.

name: paired-omics-dataset-configuration
description: Use when a paired genome–metabolome dataset with a Paired Omics Data Platform (PoDP) accession (e.g. MSV000078836, MSV000084950, MSV000084771) must be assembled in NPLinker for BGC–MS/MS spectrum linking.

name: paired-omics-dataset-curation
description: Use when building a genome-mining workflow that needs matched genome (or metagenome) and metabolome data for the same samples, e.g., to train or query NPOmix against PoDP paired datasets.

name: paired-omics-fingerprint-vector-analysis
description: Use when you have paired genome/metagenome + LC-MS/MS samples and need to link MS/MS spectra (GNPS reference or cryptic) to biosynthetic gene clusters with confidence scores.

name: paired-omics-metadata-retrieval
description: Use when an analysis needs systematically curated BGC–metabolite linkages: e.g. assembling validated paired datasets for NPLinker scoring, benchmarking link-ranking algorithms, or finding projects by genus, extraction method, or metadata ontology terms.

name: paired-omics-precision-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when NPOmix KNN predictions (GCF labels assigned to query MS/MS spectra) must be scored against validated BGC-metabolite links from MIBiG/PoDP to report top-1 and top-10 precision.

name: paired-omics-project-filtering
description: Use when the analysis goal is to find PoDP projects by extraction or sample-preparation metadata (e.g. projects that used methanol to extract cell pellets) via keyword search over project documents.

name: paired-t-test-metabolite-screening
description: Use when comparing replicate metabolite intensities measured on the same cultures at two time points (e.g. 0 h vs 72 h extracellular samples) and you must flag which metabolites show significant change before computing boundary fluxes.

name: paired-ttest-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when two spectral-processing variants were applied to the same compounds/samples and you need a statistically grounded per-compound comparison of paired scores (e.g., matching scores with vs. without PerformDDADeconvolution).

name: paired-wilcoxon-error-testing
description: Use when two or more imputation methods have been run on the same masked datasets across repeated simulations (e.g. 10–30% MCAR values), yielding paired per-simulation error rates (NRMSE/PFC) that need significance testing against a reference method.

name: paired-wilcoxon-rank-testing
description: Use when comparing two related sets of continuous error scores (e.g., DLM vs. naive k-NN relative RT errors on the same validation molecules, or errors of molecules with vs. without a >=threshold Tanimoto-similar training counterpart) and you need a distribution-free significance test.

name: paired-wilcoxon-significance-testing
description: Use when comparing paired per-fold performance metrics (Accuracy or macro F1-Score) of a MSMCE-integrated model vs. its baseline from 6-fold stratified cross-validation to establish statistical significance.

name: pairwise-cell-transition-network-comparison
description: Use when you have a longitudinal metabolomics matrix (e.g., NMR-derived concentrations across ordered developmental stages) and need to identify which metabolites or subnetworks are associated with each specific cell-state transition rather than the whole trajectory.

name: pairwise-chain-overlap-probability-computation
description: Use when validating double bond position conventions in a lipid structure database: enumerate chains from fully resolved records (explicit double bond positions), pairwise-compare forward and omega-direction position sets, and check the complete-mismatch probability against the >= 73% threshold.

name: pairwise-comparative-metabolomics
description: Use when you have centroided LC/MS data (mzML/mzXML) from two sample groups — e.g. hacl-1 vs. wildtype C. elegans, or 13C6-leucine-supplemented vs. unlabeled controls — and need to identify features enriched in one group or carrying isotope-label mass shifts.

name: pairwise-compound-similarity-classification
description: Use when you have FBMN/MSnLib annotation matches (top-10 matched compounds per query) as SMILES pairs and need to quantify and threshold their structural similarity via Tanimoto and MCES scores.

name: pairwise-contrast-pvalue-computation
description: Use when you have a wide-format feature table (features as rows, samples as columns) plus a design file mapping samples to treatment groups, and you need per-feature pairwise group contrast p-values and binary significance flags.

name: pairwise-correlation-computation
description: Use when you have a processed samples-by-metabolites table (post Viime imputation/normalization/transformation/scaling) and need to explore correlated behavior of metabolites, e.g. to build a metabolite network diagram whose edges encode signed correlation strength.

name: pairwise-dam-overlap-analysis
description: Use when several normalization methods have been applied to the same metabolomics dataset and you need to quantify consistency of their differential abundance calls (e.g. DAM overlap and p-value similarity across methods).

name: pairwise-distance-matrix-construction
description: Use when you have processed MS/MS spectra per LC-MS/MS feature and need a square pairwise spectral-similarity matrix as input for k-medoids clustering or feature-set testing in msFeaST.

name: pairwise-distance-matrix-tabulation
description: Use when you have peak-listed LC-MS/MS (MGF) datasets for multiple samples and need a quantitative pairwise similarity/distance matrix without peptide identification or spectral annotation.

name: pairwise-feature-correlation-analysis
description: Use when a Compound Discoverer (v3.3) peak table retains adduct, dimer, or in-source-fragment features co-eluting with identified lipids and pairwise correlation filtering is needed to reduce spurious unidentified peaks.

name: pairwise-group-comparison-statistics
description: Use when a pre-processed (missing-value-handled, log-transformed, pareto-scaled) targeted or untargeted metabolomics feature table must be compared across sample groups to identify features with statistically significant and practically relevant abundance changes.

name: pairwise-interaction-agreement-statistics
description: Use when two independent methods (e.g., SMETANA and COMMIT) have predicted metabolite exchanges over the same gap-filled community member models and you need to quantify how much their pairwise interaction predictions agree, including shared metabolites.

name: pairwise-mass-difference-histogram-analysis
description: Use when you have peak-mass lists from MALDI-MSI datasets (e.g. SCiLS/MSiReader CSV exports or peakBinned Cardinal imzML) and need to find which peaks are matrix- or salt-adduct partners of parent ions.

name: pairwise-metabolite-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you have a QC-filtered, per-cell anndata object of normalized isotopologue-derived relative uptake fractions and need to test whether uptake of individual fatty acids co-varies across single cells (e.g. control/normoxic liver cancer cells).

name: pairwise-metabolite-overlap-venn-upset-visualization
description: Use when you have a filtered FT-ICR MS peak/formula table with assigned molecular formulas and sample-grouping metadata, and you need to quantify and visualize which molecular formulas are shared or unique between user-defined sample groups.

name: pairwise-mz-distance-matrix-construction
description: Use when annotating isotope peaks and charge states within grouped LC/MS compound spectra (pseudospectra) from an xsAnnotate/CAMERA peak table, e.g. features from faahKO or MM39-style mixtures where spacing near 1.0033/z must be identified.

name: pairwise-ranking-model-evaluation
description: Use when you have an unretrained pairwise ranking model (e.g., ROASMI ensemble) and one or more independent datasets with experimental elution orders, and need to quantify cross-dataset generalizability via rank score, accuracy, and Spearman correlation.

name: pairwise-result-set-comparison
description: Use when you have top-hit annotation lists from multiple scorer/filter configurations (e.g. fingerprint, fragprint, totalscore scorers with element, formula, or InChI filters) and need to quantify whether they retrieve the same or distinct candidate subsets per spectrum.

name: pairwise-similarity-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when several normalization outputs (e.g. tGAM, rGAM, rLOESS, QC-RLSC, SERFF, TIGER) of the same LC-MS metabolomics matrix must be compared, to visualize cross-method agreement via pairwise Spearman correlation heatmaps alongside DAM overlap percentages.

name: pairwise-similarity-matrix-computation
description: Use when you need to score every pair of MS/MS peak lists (m/z and intensity values with precursor metadata) against each other with entropy similarity instead of dot-product similarity, e.g. to build a library-search similarity matrix.

name: pairwise-similarity-network-construction
description: Use when you need to cluster a moderate-sized set of annotated BGCs (e.g. 92 MIBiG v1.3 curated groups) into GCFs by exhaustive pairwise comparison, and need non-convex clusters that partitional Euclidean-space methods may miss.

name: pairwise-spectral-overlap-quantification
description: Use when you need pairwise similarity/distance between complete MS/MS datasets (e.g. for phylogenetics, QC, or species identification) without peptide identification or spectral libraries.

name: pairwise-spectral-similarity-matrix-analysis
description: Use when exploring an MS/MS feature set via its pairwise spectral similarity matrix — e.g. you have a .mgf-derived specXplore session object and want threshold-tunable local network views, heatmaps, and clustering overlays rather than fixed molecular networking output.

name: pairwise-spectral-similarity-scoring
description: Use when a set of MS/MS feature spectra (e.g. .mgf with feature_id, precursor m/z, m/z-intensity tuples) must be converted into pairwise similarity matrices to drive downstream embedding, network, or heatmap visualizations.

name: pairwise-superkingdom-overlap-computation
description: Use when a COCONUT snapshot contains organism annotations and the goal is to quantify NP production per taxonomic category and the pairwise sharing of NPs between superkingdoms.

name: pairwise-welch-t-test-group-comparison
description: Use when an imputed MetaboSet from LC–MS metabolomics has two or more sample groups in the Group annotation and you need per-feature univariate statistics — e.g. ANOVA_P_FDR-selected features for post-hoc pairwise testing, or direct two-group comparisons.

name: pan-cancer-subtyping-replication
description: Use when reproducing the Hoadley et al. (2014) multiplatform cancer subtyping with klic/coca, or when integrative clustering of five omic layers (copy number, methylation, miRNA, mRNA, protein) with per-dataset kernel weights is needed.

name: pandas-data-container-curation
description: Use when raw LC-MS data (mzML) have already yielded an extracted data matrix and you need a reproducible, scripted sequence of feature-filtering and correction steps (Rt filter, blank filter, RSD filter, LOESS batch correction) curated as an ordered Pipeline over a DataContainer.

name: pandas-dataframe-wrangling
description: Use when a published supplementary lipidomics table (e.g. a srep44503 Excel sheet, one analyte per row, one sample per column) must be reformatted for downstream residue extraction with liputils.

name: panorama-deposit-data-retrieval-for-targeted-analysis
description: Use when a publication states its Skyline documents and raw LC-MS data were shared via Panorama and you need the underlying SRM/HRMS vendor files to reproduce, validate, or extend the targeted metabolomics analysis.

name: parafac-tensor-deconvolution-gcxgc-ms
description: Use when raw GC × GC–MS data (e.g., CDF files folded into a 4D samples × m/z × RT1 × RT2 array) contain overlapping peaks that must be deconvoluted into pure chemical signals without prior knowledge of sample composition.

name: parallel-batch-processing-of-large-metabolomics-studies
description: Use when an untargeted LC/HRMS study has hundreds or thousands of sample files (e.g. 499–1,649 mzML/mzXML runs) and sequential peak-picking would be too slow; you need to parallelize peak detection and m/z-slice alignment across threads.

name: parallel-compute-scaling-profiling
description: Use when comparing computational cost or parallel-scaling behavior of competing normalization/analysis methods (e.g., Metanorm's QC-RLSC/QC-RSC/rLOESS/rGAM/tGAM vs TIGER or SERFF) on the same data sets.

name: parallel-extraction-performance-measurement
description: Use when you must quantify whether Shinyscreen's mzML extraction and prescreening steps are accelerated by parallel backends — i.e. you have multiple vendor-neutral mzML files, a compound list, and need a reproducible serial vs parallel timing comparison with a speedup ratio.

name: parallel-high-throughput-normalization
description: Reference for normalizing large-scale LC-MS metabolomics datasets (e.g. ~8913 untargeted features or ~53 targeted compounds across hundreds of samples) where single-threaded QC-based normalization would be too slow.

name: parallel-scaling-behavior-visualization
description: Use when a multicore-capable implementation must be benchmarked for thread scalability — e.g. you need to know whether wall-clock time keeps decreasing or saturates as threads increase from 1 to 32 on real raw-data subsets.

name: parameter-configuration-counting
description: Use when a task asks to quantify the structural complexity of a Nextflow workflow by enumerating its processes and user-facing parameters and comparing those counts against a published baseline (e.g., Metaboigniter's >20 processes / >200 parameters).

name: parameter-distribution-histogram-visualization
description: Use when you have a set of recognized (e.g., off-sample-flagged) matrix cluster ion formulas and a predicted formula-to-parameter lookup table, and need to visualize which combinatorial parameter values dominate the clusters.

name: parameter-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when a published pipeline result (e.g., DIMPLE peak counts per B73 root) must be stress-tested by re-running preprocessing at altered thresholds to report percent changes relative to the default-parameter baseline.

name: parameter-setting-comparison-of-feature-tables
description: Use when multiple apLCMS parameter settings (or apLCMS/XCMS vs a two-stage batch-aware pipeline) have produced feature tables for a two-group design, and you need to count features significant at FDR <= 0.2 per setting.

name: parameter-spreadsheet-workflow-configuration
description: Use when processing raw untargeted LC/HRMS files (mzXML, mzML, netCDF) with IDSL.IPA and you must set data/output locations, peak-detection and recursive mass correction options (PARAM0019-PARAM0020) before calling IPA_workflow.

name: parameter-stability-visualization
description: Use when you must decide how many samples are sufficient for stable parameter estimation, by tabulating CV across random subsets and plotting CV vs. sample size against an acceptance threshold (e.g. CV <= 0.1).

name: parameter-sweep-analysis
description: Use when you must quantify how a feature-detection algorithm's recall, precision, and F-score degrade as detector noise, mass error (10 and 40 ppm), or elution-profile distortion is swept on simulated LC-MS data with a known ground truth.

name: parameter-sweep-analysis
description: Use when a model's update rule contains an explicit mixing/weighting parameter (e.g. α∈[0,1] blending host-model bounds with aggregated microbiota fluxes) and you need the sensitivity of derived bounds or fluxes across that range.

name: parameter-sweep-analysis
description: Use when you have an aligned post-XCMS feature intensity table and need to justify a choice of RAMClustR's sigma_t (retention-time sigma) and sigma_r (correlational sigma) values by evaluating cluster quality across a grid of combinations instead of accepting defaults blindly.

name: parameter-trace-plot-visualization
description: Use when you have logged per-iteration parameter values from an EM algorithm (e.g., component means, variances, mixing proportions for metabolite identification) and need to verify or demonstrate that the algorithm converged.

name: parameter-uncertainty-estimation
description: Use when fitting 1D/pseudo-2D NMR spectra where quantitative signal parameters and their standard-deviation uncertainties are required, especially to decide whether to fit whole multiplets versus independent peaks.

name: parametric-t-test-anova-analysis
description: Use when you have a preprocessed, normalized feature matrix with group labels (two groups or more) and need per-feature classical significance testing with multiple-testing correction across the many tests.

name: parametric-time-warping-of-spectral-regions
description: Use when overlaid 1D 1H NMR spectra show uncontrolled chemical shift variations in a ppm area containing intertwined peaks, and Least-Square realignment cannot resolve the shifts.

name: parametric-umap-embedding-of-msi-data
description: Use when you have a reconstructed, m/z-binned and TIC-normalized serial-section MSI dataset (e.g. coronal3D_propagated_decoded.h5) and need anatomically contrasted 2D feature images to co-register against MRI atlas slices.

name: paramounter-to-msdial-parameter-translation
description: Use when raw LC-MS metabolomics files must be processed in MS-DIAL but software-specific extraction parameters are unknown, and you want to measure them from the data itself rather than relying on default parameters.

name: params-yml-omics-pipeline-configuration
description: Use when a raw feature count matrix plus phenotype file must be filtered, normalized (e.g. quantile), and batch-corrected (ComBat/SVA) as a standalone pre-processing step before downstream omics analysis with MOI.

name: parent-adduct-spatial-colocalization-correlation
description: Use when you have an msimat MSI peak table and a set of candidate parent–adduct mass-difference pairs (from diffGetPeaks/adductMatch) and need to filter them by pixel-intensity correlation before counting adduct abundance.

name: parent-drug-formula-annotation
description: Use when a peak-picked mzML file from LC-HRMS/MS is available for a drug of interest whose exact molecular formula is known, and in silico metabolite prediction (e.g., with MetIDfyR) is the goal.

name: parent-drug-to-feature-mapping
description: Use when analyzing deposited ST003991 feature tables from PharmMet DB where individual LC-HRMS features must be attributed to a specific incubated drug and then aggregated by therapeutic class to quantify unpredicted metabolites.

name: parent-fragment-ion-linking
description: Use when processing centroid-mode all-ion fragmentation (AIF) LC-MS chromatograms already peak-picked with xcms/RAMClustR and you need to assemble a pseudo-MS/MS spectrum for a specific target feature before fragment library matching.

name: parent-mass-window-filtering
description: Use when assembling or curating MS/MS spectral libraries from .mgf entries and you need to discard ions outside the mass range typical of natural-product metabolites before dereplication or benchmarking.

name: parent-suspect-screening
description: Use when you have patRoon feature groups from classical NTA feature finding and a target list of parent compounds whose transformation products you want to predict and screen in a patRoon 2.0 TP workflow.

name: parent-tp-feature-componentization
description: Use when confirmed parent suspect-screening hits (e.g. carbamazepine, benzotriazole) and mass-matched TP features must be grouped into parent/TP components before reporting in an NTA workflow.

name: pareto-scaled-multivariate-image-analysis
description: Use when imzML-derived pixel-by-m/z data (e.g. image.norm.csv with lipid annotations, m/z and TIC-normalised intensities) must be classified into tissue regions such as cerebellum white matter, granular and molecular layers.

name: pareto-scaling-data-normalization
description: Use when you have a peak-based feature/sample/peak-value matrix from NMR spectra (e.g. speaq 2.0 output) and need to equalize variable influence before PCA or multivariate statistics.

name: pareto-scaling-metabolomics-matrix
description: Use when a peak-based feature matrix has been built with speaq 2.0 (BuildFeatureMatrix) and a univariate test such as red-vs-white linear-model differential analysis requires column scaling as a pre-statistics step.

name: parity-plot-visualization
description: Use when a trained FIORA model checkpoint and annotated compound sets (RT and CCS labels) are available and you need to quantify/visualize regression accuracy of RT/CCS predictions against simple baselines on held-out splits.

name: parquet-columnar-spectra-conversion
description: Use when proprietary vendor HRMS data (Waters UNIFI (HD)MSE, or Thermo RAW converted to mzML) must be stored compactly, queried fast, or shared across R and Python.

name: parquet-columnar-spectral-storage
description: Use when Thermo RAW spectral peak data must be converted to scalable, analysis-ready arrays for downstream ML/QC workflows, joining per-scan spectra to scan-header metadata via scan numbers.

name: parquet-on-disk-query-timing-measurement
description: Use when you need to benchmark read/query performance of Parquet-stored HRMS (MSE/HDMSE) data against other formats (mzML, mz5, mzMLb), measuring query wall time and output data volume from on-disk Arrow datasets.

name: parsimonious-flux-balance-analysis-gap-filling
description: Use when a draft SBML GENRE fails to produce biomass under defined media conditions and reactions must be added from a universal reaction database (universal.pickle) to restore growth.

name: partial-correlation-analysis-of-biomarkers
description: Use when testing whether a metabolic biomarker panel adds predictive value beyond conventional risk factors, or when the question is whether risk-factor information is already captured by correlated metabolites (e.g. lipids measured by both clinical chemistry and NMR).

name: partial-correlation-confounder-adjustment
description: Use when testing metabolite–phenotype associations in a metabolomics dataset (e.g. plasma 1H NMR features vs BMI) while adjusting for epidemiological confounders such as age, gender or disease status, and a rank-based univariate model with pFDR control is needed.

name: partial-correlation-covariate-adjustment
description: Use when testing whether a specific metabolite feature (e.g. a Level 1-annotated carnitine peak from untargeted metabolomics) is associated with a continuous clinical biomarker in a human cohort subset, and demographic covariates (age, sex, BMI) must be held constant.

name: partial-correlation-edge-extraction
description: Use when a fitted GLASSO/GraphLassoCV precision matrix is available and you need an edge list of partial correlations to build a sparse metabolite network.

name: partial-correlation-edge-filtering
description: Use when a DNEA (or Filigree) GLASSO network has been estimated for two experimental groups and the raw edge list is too dense for interpretation — edges must be filtered by partial correlation strength or percentile.

name: partial-layer-freezing-transfer-learning
description: Use when a small labeled cohort (e.g. CheckMate025 ccRCC baseline serum metabolomics, 543/149/149 split) must be fine-tuned from the mzLearn 2,736-feature pre-trained VAE and naive full retraining would overfit or destroy pre-trained representations.

name: partition-coefficient-descriptor-retrieval
description: Use when a QSAR half-life prediction step (e.g., IFS per Arnot et al. 2014) requires log Kow and log Koa inputs for a chemical list, and descriptors must be fetched before filtering and prediction.

name: patbs-background-subtraction
description: Use when raw UPLC-HRMS peak lists in positive and negative ESI modes contain background/blank ions that must be removed to enumerate genuine in vitro sample components (prototypes) before annotating identities and ranking abundances.

name: pathogenicity-downgrade-rate-analysis
description: Use when a variant-annotation pipeline (ANNOVAR/SnpEff/VEP on ClinVar two-star variants) needs its clinical impact assessed, specifically to quantify PLP downgrades caused by incorrect PVS1 interpretations.

name: pathway-activity-level-computation-via-svd
description: Use when gene expression data (e.g., 43 type 2 diabetes samples) must be converted into per-sample activity levels for ~400 predefined KEGG/Biocarta pathways and correlated with a continuous phenotype such as OGTT glucose.

name: pathway-activity-level-scoring
description: Use when you have a peak-intensity matrix plus peak-to-compound annotations (KEGG/ChEBI IDs) or fragmentation-based metabolite sets (GNPS Molecular Families, Mass2Motifs) and need to rank metabolite sets by activity between a case and control group.

name: pathway-activity-score-computation-kernel-pca
description: Use when you have one or more standardised, log-transformed molecular abundance matrices (metabolomics with ChEBI/KEGG IDs, proteomics or RNA-seq with UniProt/ENSEMBL or gene symbols) and need per-sample pathway-level feature scores to feed supervised multi-omics integration models.

name: pathway-activity-scoring
description: Use when a peak-feature intensity matrix (samples as columns, group row) plus a peak-to-compound annotation table is available and pathway-level ranking of significantly changing metabolite sets is the analysis goal.

name: pathway-annotation-gmt-formatting
description: Use when a metabolite set enrichment analysis (MetSEA/GSEA) step requires pathway-to-metabolite annotations in a specific file format and the source annotations are only available as a table, KEGG dump, or API response.

name: pathway-annotation-of-hijacked-metabolic-pathways
description: Use when you must annotate host metabolic reactions — identified as viral-PPI, chokepoint/bottleneck, or essential-reaction intersections — with their metabolic pathway membership in iHsaEC21 to catalogue SARS-CoV-2-hijacked pathways.

name: pathway-association-pvalue-calculation
description: Use when per-metabolite partial residuals from null covariate regressions and a regularized graph kernel matrix (τ = 1) are available and pathway-level association p-values against a phenotype are required.

name: pathway-background-set-comparison
description: Use when performing over-representation analysis on metabolomics data and you must decide whether the background/reference compound set should be assay-specific or a database-wide organism set, or must quantify that choice's effect on p-values and SEP counts.

name: pathway-coexpression-coordination-quantification
description: Use when you have expression profiles plus predefined KEGG/Biocarta gene-sets and need to measure pathway-wide expression coordination, or to test whether GSEA's top-ranked sets are merely coordinately expressed rather than differentially active between groups.

name: pathway-database-comparison-kegg-reactome
description: Use when choosing between KEGG and Reactome as the pathway source for pathway-transformed multi-omics models, or when quantifying database-specific pathway sizes and molecule-to-pathway identifier coverage.

name: pathway-database-concordance-analysis
description: Use when you need to assess whether ORA conclusions on metabolomics datasets are robust to the choice of pathway database, e.g. comparing KEGG vs Reactome vs BioCyc significantly enriched pathway (SEP) sets.

name: pathway-database-interaction-retrieval
description: Use when a topology-based pathway analysis needs gene-gene interaction (edge) lists pulled from pathway databases like KEGG or Reactome for a user-supplied gene identifier set, instead of hand-curated network files.

name: pathway-database-redundancy-analysis
description: Use when you need to measure the extent of shared metabolite content between pathways drawn from multiple source databases (KEGG, Reactome, WikiPathways) hosted in a RaMP MySQL instance, e.g. to assess cross-database pathway redundancy.

name: pathway-deregulation-score-computation
description: Use when raw metabolite-level abundance data (e.g., named metabolites or HMDB ids) must be transformed into personalized pathway-based features before feature selection, machine learning classification, or Cox-PH/Cox-nnet prognosis prediction.

name: pathway-deregulation-scoring
description: Use when a raw metabolite measurement table (e.g. metabolite-by-sample CSV with a phenotype Label column) must be converted into individual patient-level pathway features for classification modeling.

name: pathway-dysregulation-scoring
description: Use when a metabolomics abundance matrix (metabolites as features) must be converted into a pathway-level feature matrix before feature selection or disease classification in Lilikoi v2.0.

name: pathway-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when an untargeted LC/MS feature table (m/z, retention time, p-value) plus a significant-vs-reference feature split needs pathway-level interpretation, and metabolite identification is not yet available.

name: pathway-enrichment-analysis-fishers-exact-test
description: Use when an untargeted LC/MS metabolomics run yields two m/z feature lists — a significant list and a reference list — and you need pathway-level biological activity without prior metabolite identification.

name: pathway-enrichment-annotation
description: Use when a differential analysis or MOFA factor yields a significant feature list (e.g. |log2FC|>0.5, p.adj<0.1 peaks or top factor contributors) that must be interpreted via biological process enrichment and literature annotation.

name: pathway-enrichment-fishers-exact-test-with-gamma-null-modeling
description: Use when analyzing untargeted LC/MS metabolomics feature tables (significant vs reference m/z lists) to identify which metabolic pathways are enriched without prior metabolite identification.

name: pathway-enrichment-of-annotated-metabolites
description: Use when a cleaned LC-MS feature table already carries level-2 metabolite annotations and the goal is to identify enriched metabolic pathways from differential-metabolite lists in the tidyMass pipeline.

name: pathway-enrichment-result-comparison
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS data (DDA or SWATH-DIA, e.g. mzML from Metabolomics Workbench ST002796/ST002798) has been processed to MS1 features plus MS2 compound IDs and the goal is to test whether MS2 filtering yields more significant mummichog pathways than MS1 alone.

name: pathway-enrichment-results-visualization
description: Use when you have sex-specific (or group-specific) differential metabolite tables from a massstat differential-analysis step and need to identify which KEGG/SMPDB pathways are enriched in one group but not another.

name: pathway-enrichment-testing
description: Use when testing whether entire pathways are enriched/dysregulated from gene expression data by incorporating pathway topology (gene-gene interactions), or when benchmarking enrichment methods' statistical power and type-I error in simulations.

name: pathway-enrichment-tool-comparison
description: Use when you have a standardized metabolite list (e.g. HMDB-mapped names) and need to benchmark which pathways different group-level enrichment methods rank as most significant.

name: pathway-fdr-significance-filtering
description: Use when metabolite pathway over-representation output (e.g. MetaboAnalyst 'pathway_results.csv') must be reduced to significant pathways and their constituent metabolites converted from KEGG IDs to HMDB IDs.

name: pathway-feature-mapping-kegg-ids
description: Use when metabolomics or multiomics feature tables carry KEGG IDs and you need to place features on KEGG pathway gene/compound nodes (with topology) before ORA or perturbation impact analysis such as eSPIA.

name: pathway-gene-set-mapping-kegg-biocarta
description: Use when a genes-by-samples expression matrix (e.g., microarray) must be decomposed into predefined KEGG/Biocarta pathway gene sets (~400 pathways and complexes) as input to SVD-based pathway activity analysis.

name: pathway-geneset-curation-kegg-biocarta
description: Use when a gene expression analysis needs a predefined gene-set universe (KEGG, Biocarta pathways and complexes) to quantify pathway activity or compute enrichment scores from gene rankings.

name: pathway-graph-kernel-smoothing
description: Use when metabolites map onto a pathway graph (e.g., KEGG edges from the KEGG reaction database) that is sparse or disconnected, and you want to incorporate that graph topology into a kernel machine association test via a regularized normalized Laplacian.

name: pathway-graph-simulation-edge-permutation
description: Use when you need to evaluate robustness or statistical power of pathway-structured association tests (e.g. kernel machine tests on Laplacian-derived pathway kernels) under controlled amounts of incorrect or incomplete pathway graph knowledge.

name: pathway-graph-topology-analysis
description: Use when testing phenotype–pathway associations from metabolomics data where metabolites can be mapped to a pathway graph (e.g., KEGG reaction edges) and the graph's topography should inform the kernel.

name: pathway-hyperlink-classification-training
description: Use when labeled pathway sets (positives from TomatoCyc, negatives from MetaCyc plus random sampling) must be classified from metabolite correlation network waveforms, or when reproducing NetAurHPD-style AUC benchmarks.

name: pathway-impact-plot-visualization
description: Use when you have ORA enrichment results (adjusted Fisher's exact-test p-values on KEGG pathways) plus a significant metabolite list, and need to prioritize pathways by network topology impact rather than p-value rank alone.

name: pathway-importance-scoring
description: Use when you have fitted a pathway-level multi-omics model (PathIntegrate MB-PLS/Single-View or DIABLO on ssPA-transformed data) and need ranked pathway importance statistics with permutation-tested significance or detection AUCs.

name: pathway-level-clustering
description: Use when you have a PDS score matrix (0–1 pathway deregulation scores) restricted to Lilikoi-selected pathway features and want to check whether pathway-level profiles visually separate phenotype classes before or after classification modeling.

name: pathway-level-feature-selection
description: Use when you have a per-sample pathway score matrix (e.g., Lilikoi PDS matrix built by lilikoi.PDSfun) and need to pick the most significant pathway features before running a classification or prognosis model in Lilikoi v2.0.

name: pathway-level-vs-molecular-level-signal-detection-benchmarking
