description: Use when you need to empirically justify a pathway-transformation step by comparing pathway-level versus molecular-level univariate detection power on injected-signal simulations spanning effect sizes 0–1.

name: pathway-loss-gain-rate-quantification
description: Use when you need to stress-test the stability of an ORA-derived list of significantly enriched metabolomics pathways against compound annotation errors, e.g. measuring how many baseline pathways (p <= 0.1) are lost or falsely gained at a given simulated misidentification rate.

name: pathway-metabolite-mapping
description: Use when annotating m/z features from preprocessed organ-specific MSI data (e.g. AFADESI-MSI in positive/negative mode) and tracing which metabolic pathways are altered across multiple organs, such as liver, brain, and kidney.

name: pathway-network-construction
description: Use when a metabolomics feature list must be mapped to pathway database identifiers (KEGG compound IDs) to enable pathway-based network construction or enrichment, and when you need to quantify how many features are actually annotatable.

name: pathway-ora-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when interpreting metabolomics data with ORA and you need to know how sensitive the significant-pathway result is to the background set, the DA-metabolite list construction (e.g. BH FDR q <= 0.05 vs p-value ordering), or the pathway database (KEGG, Reactome, BioCyc).

name: pathway-over-representation-analysis
description: Use when a standalone metabolomics dataset (e.g., a table of 56 named urine metabolites) needs pathway-level interpretation via over-representation testing before downstream metabolite-gene set comparison.

name: pathway-over-representation-analysis
description: Use when you have a curated list of dysregulated metabolites (e.g., Log2FC > 1.5, BH-adj p < 0.05) from LC–MS metabolomics and want to identify over-represented biological pathways such as lipid or amino-acid metabolism.

name: pathway-overrepresentation-analysis
description: Use when you have a list of metabolites and/or genes of interest and need statistically adjusted pathway overrepresentation p-values from the RaMP relational database (KEGG, Reactome, WikiPathways, HMDB annotations).

name: pathway-overrepresentation-clustering
description: Use when a Fisher's enrichment result table (fishers_df) contains many overlapping significant pathways across KEGG, Reactome, WikiPathways, and HMDB, and you need to reduce redundancy into non-overlapping pathway clusters.

name: pathway-ranking-robustness-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating how stable pathway rankings from a metabolomics tool remain when a large fraction of peak features is randomly removed, and you need a quantitative robustness metric (F1) to compare competing ranking methods.

name: pathway-reporter-score-aggregation
description: Use when you have a feature abundance table (KO numbers, gene symbols, or KEGG C numbers) with sample metadata and need threshold-free, pathway/module-level enrichment with directionality across two-group, multi-group, or longitudinal designs.

name: pathway-set-intersection-analysis
description: Use when a metabolomics dataset contains multiple analytical assays (e.

name: pathway-set-overlap-coefficient-analysis
description: Use when choosing between candidate pathway databases or pathway sets for ORA and you need to know whether differing enrichment counts stem from genuinely different biology or merely from set size/overlap differences.

name: pathway-step-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a pathway-prediction run (e.g., MEANtools reaction anticipation on the Jeon 2020 tomato paired-omics dataset) must be scored against published pathway steps.

name: pathway-topology-analysis-espia
description: Use when a multiomics (gene expression + metabolomics) study needs pathway-level significance that accounts for pathway topology over KEGG, beyond simple over-representation of differentially abundant features.

name: pathway-topology-betweenness-analysis
description: Use when you have a standalone list of metabolite names (e.g. 56 urine metabolites from a metabolomics-GWAS case study) and need KEGG pathway over-representation P-values, FDR, and pathway-impact scores to connect them to disease GWAS genes.

name: pathway-topology-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a two-condition gene expression matrix (e.g., breastcancer2012: 520 subjects × 2784 genes) and need topology-aware pathway enrichment against KEGG/Reactome interaction networks on ordinary hardware.

name: pathway-waveform-aggregation-from-metabolite-signals
description: Use when you have node-level waveforms from network auralization of a metabolite correlation network and need one representative signal per metabolic pathway (hyperlink) before training the M5 classifier.

name: pathway-zscore-aggregation
description: Use when you have a full (unprefiltered) KO, gene, or compound abundance table plus sample metadata and need threshold-free pathway enrichment with permutation-calibrated reporter scores.

name: patient-metadata-driven-metabolite-modeling
description: Use when clinical metabolomics data (e.g., GC-TOF MS lipid profiles) contain patient metadata and subject-specific biological variation should be readjusted before multivariate analyses like PLS-DA, OPLS-DA, or PCA.

name: patient-metadata-fixed-effects-modeling
description: Use when a metabolomics feature matrix has paired or repeated measurements per patient plus subject metadata, and residual inter-individual variation masks biological group separation (e.g. SAT vs VAT) prior to PCA or PLS-DA.

name: patroon-feature-table-import
description: Use when patRoon featureGroups and MFsummary outputs must be brought into GetFeatistics as featTable/featINFO data frames for pooled-QC filtering, annotation grading, regression modelling, or plotting.

name: patroon-featuregroups-import
description: Use when starting an untargeted metabolomics analysis whose features were extracted and annotated with patRoon, and the data must be converted into GetFeatistics' featTable/featINFO structures before pooled-QC filtration or regression modelling.

name: pattern-component-overlap-analysis
description: Use when you have mined mineMS2 fragmentation patterns and a GNPS molecular network whose detected components (groups of similar MS/MS spectra) need interpretation, and you want to know which pattern explains each component.

name: pattern-occurrence-mapping-to-spectra
description: Use when you have mined fragmentation patterns (mineMS2 pattern set) and need to find which patterns contain a specific m/z difference or loss and which spectra share them, especially to flag spectra that are not connected in a GNPS molecular network.

name: pattern-support-precision-evaluation
description: Use when a GNPS molecular network component of MS/MS spectra must be explained by one dominant fragmentation pattern, and candidate mineMS2 patterns need support/precision scoring over the component.

name: pattern-to-component-mapping
description: Use when you have mined mineMS2 patterns, identified which pattern explains each GNPS molecular network component, and need to transfer that annotation onto the network object and export it for visualization.

name: pc-outlier-visualization
description: Use when a Metaboprep object's QC run needs PCA-based sample outlier identification and PC plots for the HTML QC report — e.g. flagging samples beyond ±5 SD on informative PCs under pc_outlier_sd=5.

name: pc1-pc2-scores-plotting
description: Use when a matrix of relative concentration values for the 22 SMolESY-select metabolites (e.g. serum samples from MTBLS395) is available and you need PCA-based visualization/ biomarker-pattern comparison against a whole-1H NMR-profile approach.

name: pca-based-drift-diagnostics
description: Use when a feature matrix contains ordered pooled/intrastudy QC injections and you need to quantify or visually assess signal drift, or to verify that LOESS batch correction reduced time-related systematic variance.

name: pca-based-sample-outlier-detection
description: Use when a raw metabolite-by-sample matrix (e.g. Nightingale NMR or Metabolon UPLC-MS/MS export) is being QC-filtered in metaboprep and samples with abnormal multivariate metabolite profiles must be flagged via PCA scores at a user-defined SD cutoff.

name: pca-based-tissue-region-classification
description: Use when you have a preprocessed, TIC-normalised MSI feature matrix (imzML-derived lipid intensities) and want to spatially separate tissue regions with high spectral similarity via principal components analysis and interpret driving lipids from PC loadings.

name: pca-batch-effect-assessment
description: Use when you need to judge whether a metabolomics normalization method (e.g. tGAM, QC-RLSC) removed batch effects before/after correction, or to spot subpar normalization.

name: pca-batch-effect-visualization
description: Use when a raw feature table with periodic pooled QC injections (e.g. every 5–8 samples) has been drift-corrected and you need to demonstrate batch-effect removal before downstream statistics.

name: pca-class-separation-statistical-testing
description: Decision support for statistically evaluating whether metabolomic sample groups separate in a PCA scores plot when no univariate statistics or graphical diagnostics are available in the workflow.

name: pca-data-quality-tracking
description: Use when a pooled/intrastudy QC-injected LC-MS batch (e.g. NIST candidate RM 8231 / SRM 1950 plasma in mzML with a Pandas feature table) must be checked for drift, outliers, or group separation via PCA score plots.

name: pca-dimension-reduction-metabolomics
description: Use when the analysis goal is unsupervised exploration of a samples x metabolites (or proteins) matrix — e.g. the ST000284 targeted metabolomics three-group study — to reduce its dimensions and visualize sample separation before supervised modelling.

name: pca-dimension-reduction-plotting
description: Use when a metabolomics data frame plus demographic/metadata table is loaded in R and you need unsupervised sample-embedding plots (PCA, t-SNE) or a confounder/source-of-variation assessment before classification.

name: pca-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when a metabolomics or 'omics feature table (samples × metabolites, e.g. 90 NMR-quantified metabolites across 3–8 biological replicates per cell population) needs unbiased dimensionality reduction and unsupervised visualization of sample-group clustering.

name: pca-dimensionality-reduction-of-binned-spectral-features
description: Use when you have ≥30 MS/MS spectra per compound from spectral libraries (e.g. NIST 17, MoNA) with instrument-type and collision-energy metadata and want to inspect whether spectra cluster by acquisition conditions before training a fingerprint model.

name: pca-embedding-visualization
description: Use when a trained deep metabolomics model (e.g. DenseNet121 on raw LC-MS .npy spectra) must be inspected layer-by-layer to show how hidden representations shed batch information and gain disease-class information.

name: pca-glasso-network-overlay
description: Use when high-dimensional longitudinal metabolomics data (e.g., NMR-derived metabolite concentrations across developmental stages) must be decomposed into transition-specific covariance subnetworks linking metabolites to specific cell-type transitions.

name: pca-hotelling-t2-outlier-detection
description: Use when a metabolomics/lipidomics data table with QCpool samples measured at regular sequence intervals must be screened for outlying samples before downstream analysis, i.e. during the 'removal of outlying samples' step of a multistep QC protocol.

name: pca-input-feature-scaling
description: Use when a raw metabolite concentration/intensity table (e.g., 90 metabolites from integrated NMR peak areas across hESC→EB→Rosette→hNPC→Neuron stages) must be scaled before PCA so features contribute comparably to components.

name: pca-loading-biomarker-prioritization
description: Use when an untargeted DI-MS or LC-MS peak table has been normalized in MetaboShiny (filtered, normalized, transformed, scaled) and you need to rank which m/z values separate a disease group from controls before annotating candidates.

name: pca-loading-interpretation-for-bmi-variance
description: Use when you have simulated or measured 1D 1H NMR spectra of blood mixtures tied to a continuous outcome such as BMI, and need to determine which principal component captures the outcome-related variance and which metabolites drive it.

name: pca-loadings-and-explained-variance-interpretation
description: Use when a small, feature-rich metabolomics or omics table (samples x metabolites) needs unbiased dimensionality reduction and you must inspect per-component loadings, sample scores, and explained variance to judge which components capture significant variance.

name: pca-loadings-lipid-interpretation
description: Use when mass spectrometry imaging data (imzML) has been extracted, deisotoped, annotated and TIC-normalised, and the goal is to separate spatially co-located tissue regions (e.g. cerebellum layers) or interpret which lipids drive each principal component.

name: pca-model-parameter-configuration
description: Use when building a struct model object in R (e.g. PCA from struct/structToolbox) and you need a typed, documented, scalar-constrained parameter such as number_components, accessible via P$number_components and param_obj(P,'number_components').

name: pca-ordination-procrustes-analysis
description: Use when comparing imputed vs original data matrices to quantify distortion of the observation/sample distribution, e.g., benchmarking MNAR imputation methods (GSimp, QRILC, kNN-TN) across graded missingness levels.

name: pca-outlier-detection-and-missing-value-replacement
description: Use when curating or reproducing QC filtering of GCxGC-TOFMS plasma metabolite peak tables — specifically when deciding which detected peaks to exclude (run-order drift, QC deviation, PCA outliers) and which metabolites need missing-value replacement, as in the 691→195 peak filter.

name: pca-outlier-screening
description: Use when you have a matrix of NMR-estimated metabolite relative concentrations across plasma samples (e.g. NMRQNet CSV output) and need to detect outlier samples prior to supervised group-difference modeling (OPLS-DA, t-tests).

name: pca-quality-control-of-nmr-spectra
description: Use when QC of a large-scale 1H NMR metabonomic dataset (e.g. plasma spectra with pooled QC replicates) is required before metabolome-wide association analysis, to verify analytical reproducibility and absence of batch effects.

name: pca-quality-control-tightness-evaluation
description: Use when a corrected metabolomics feature matrix (e.g., post-WaveICA or WaveICA 2.0) must be scored for batch effect removal quality and pooled QCS injections are available to benchmark clustering tightness.

name: pca-score-based-mid-level-fusion
description: Use when two or more platform-specific metabolomics datasets (e.g., MS and NMR CSV tables) covering the same samples must be combined into one integrated table and raw column concatenation would duplicate correlated metabolite information across platforms.

name: pca-score-extraction
description: Use when multivariate data in a struct DatasetExperiment needs mean centring followed by PCA, and you must extract principal-component scores (e.g. number_components = 2) as the pipeline output.

name: pca-score-plot-visualization
description: Use when a LipidomicsExperiment (e.g. imported from Metabolomics Workbench study ST001111 with measure="Area") needs unsupervised quality control, and samples with significantly large dispersion in the PCA scores plot must be identified as outliers before further analysis.

name: pca-score-plot-visualization
description: Use when a grouped NMR peak feature matrix (samples × peaks) must be checked for class structure: Pareto-scale and mean-center it, run PCA, and inspect the PC1–PC2 score plot colored by wine color for red vs white/rosé separation.

name: pca-score-plot-visualization
description: Use when a targeted LC–MS preprocessing run (e.g., TARDIS AUC table) needs a global quality check, and you want to confirm QC runs cluster tightly before downstream statistics.

name: pca-score-plot-visualization-of-multi-tissue-data
description: Use when you have untargeted metabolomics peak-area tables with many zero-count features across multiple tissues and need to check whether samples cluster by study, cohort, genotype, or tissue before downstream stratified analyses.

name: pca-scores-interpretation-metabolomics
description: Use when you have a peak-value feature matrix from 1D NMR metabolomics spectra and need to visually assess whether experimental groups (e.g., diet concentrations) separate before or alongside differential analysis.

name: pca-scores-loadings-export
description: Use when you have SMolESY-select relative concentration values for the 22 SMolESY-select metabolites and want to verify whether PCA of the panel recapitulates the biomarker signal seen when analysing the full 1H NMR profile.

name: pca-scores-significance-testing
description: Use when a cleaned, class-labelled X data matrix (DSO with row/column labels and biological/blank class labels) is ready and you need PCA with per-component statistical evidence of class separation rather than visual scores plots.

name: pca-scree-biplot-generation
description: Use when FT-ICR MS metabolomic samples with assigned molecular formulas need ordination-based group discrimination assessment, complementing PERMANOVA and NMDS, using normalized peak intensities or molecular class composition vectors.

name: pca-tsne-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when the input is an imzML MSI dataset whose high-dimensional pixel spectra must be reduced to a 2D embedding (PCA→t-SNE) for clustering-based tissue segmentation and hyperparameter comparison.

name: pca-variance-explanation-lipidomics
description: Use when an annotated lipidomics feature table (e.g., 3647 features across replicate groups like Par, Dap2, Dal2, Van4) must be reduced to a few components to test whether strain or condition clusters separate before downstream PLS-DA or fold-change analyses.

name: pcc-r2-similarity-baseline-comparison
description: Use when evaluating a learned ion-image representation for isotope or colocalized ion discovery in MSI and you need the established SIM-based baselines (Pearson correlation coefficient and R2) computed on identical query ions for direct comparison.

name: pcoa-ordination-of-chemical-dissimilarity-matrices
description: Use when you already have (or can compute) sample-by-sample dissimilarity matrices from LC-MS/MS data — e.g. a GNPS/MZmine feature table, aligned MS2 fingerprints, or MEMO matrices — and need to check for batch splits (e.

name: pcoa-ordination-of-metabolomics-distance-matrices
description: Use when you have a beta diversity or phylogenetic distance matrix computed from an LC-MS/MS metabolomics feature table and need 2D/3D ordination plots to compare clustering by sample metadata (e.g. chromatographic batch).

name: pcoa-ordination-of-metabolomics-samples
description: Use when you have an aligned MS2 fingerprint similarity matrix (e.g., from MEMO, built by counting MS2 peaks and neutral losses to the precursor) and need PCoA ordination plus PERMANOVA pseudo-F/p-values for grouping factors.

name: pcoa-ordination-plot-generation
description: Use when you have a QIIME principal coordinates (PCoA) file and a metadata mapping file and need an interactive, shareable 3D ordination of thousands of microbial community samples, optionally overlaid with biplot or procrustes layers.

name: pcoa-ordination-visualization
description: Use when you have a QIIME principal coordinates file and a metadata mapping file (e.g. thousands of samples, many metadata columns) and need an exploratory 3D ordination visualization colored by sample metadata.

name: pcoa-plot-reproduction-from-deposited-files
description: Use when you have a deposited QIIME principal coordinates file and mapping file (e.g. the 5,740-sample, 120-column combined dataset) and need to rebuild a PCoA 3D plot or benchmark visualization loading performance.

name: pcoa-plot-visualization
description: Use when you have a QIIME principal coordinates file plus a metadata mapping file and need to explore microbial community beta diversity clustering in an interactive 3D plot, color or resize points per metadata category, or share the visualization in a web browser.

name: pcoa-visualization-embedding
description: Decision support for embedding interactive 3D principal coordinates plots of QIIME beta diversity PCoA output and metadata mapping files into a web page or email for sharing.

name: pcoa-visualization-generation
description: Use when a QIIME principal coordinates file plus a metadata mapping file must be turned into an interactive 3D ordination plot with discrete or gradient coloring, especially for large datasets (thousands of samples) that must be shared or loaded quickly.

name: pcr-gold-standard-external-validation
description: Use when two reproducibility methods disagree on top-k gene sets for SEQC RNA-seq replicate comparisons and an independent qPCR/Taqman gold standard is available to judge which method's sets are more biologically relevant.

name: pdac-metabolomics-recurrence-analysis
description: Use when input data are per-study aggregate statistics (p-values and fold-changes) for metabolites across multiple PDAC studies, and the goal is to rank compounds by recurrence with consistent up/down trend directions rather than pooled effect sizes.

name: pdb-provenance-classification
description: Use when a deposit contains a mixed collection of .pdb 3D structure files and each file must be attributed to its original source (experimental PDB entries vs AlphaFold DB predictions) and counted per category.

name: pdf-figure-export-of-qc-diagnostics
description: Use when a PeakQC QC run has completed over a batch of MS runs (Thermo .raw, Agilent/Bruker 'd', mzML) and the resulting PCA projection and diagnostic figures need to be saved as PDF/JPG reports for QC inspection.

name: pdf-report-generation-for-ms-quality-control
description: Use when prescreened HRMS extraction results (compound/precursor metadata, EIC traces, representative MS2 spectra) must be rendered into per-compound figure panels and aggregated into a PDF QC report.

name: peak-abundance-table-preparation
description: Use when direct-injection FT-ICR MS data have already been formula-assigned but still need peak filtering and a normalization-method choice before running the MetaboDirect pipeline on datasets like the bacterium-phage (36 samples) or S. fallax (4 samples) examples.

name: peak-alignment-and-formula-ranking-interpretation
description: Use when you have IDSL.IPA peaklists and an aligned peak table processed by IDSL.UFA with a candidate IPDB, and need to quantify formula-annotation performance (top-hit and top-five-hit recovery) against known MSI 1-3 annotations.

name: peak-alignment-summary-statistics
description: Use when you have per-file IDSL.UFA formula annotation peaklists plus an IDSL.IPA aligned peak table and need one summarized, ranked formula annotation per peak across all samples.

name: peak-area-correlation-analysis
description: Use when a matched feature table with peak areas from PeakBot and XCMS (e.g. from a PHM tool comparison) must be compared: regression R2, trimming of dissimilar features, and derivation of the profile-to-centroid median area factor.

name: peak-area-integration
description: Use when GC × GC–MS deconvoluted features must be quantified across all samples — the annotated peaks from GcDUO's module III need area/intensity values, not just detection and annotation.

name: peak-area-integration
description: Use when processing AEMS MRM raw data (XIC points per mass transition and ejection/well) to produce a baseline-corrected area table, e.g. mrm_areas.csv, for shot-to-peak quantification.

name: peak-area-quantification
description: Use when you have a referenced 2D 13C INADEQUATE spectrum and need to detect peaks and quantify their areas with a multi-threshold sweep, before network filtering and metabolite matching.

name: peak-area-to-concentration-conversion
description: Use when the input is a lipidomic peak-area/peak-height matrix whose rows include internal standard species and a companion standards table (Standard/Class/Conc.) exists, and the goal is a per-species concentration matrix.

name: peak-artifact-classification
description: Use when you have raw mzML files plus a detected peak list (mz, rt columns, e.g. from XCMS) and need to separate genuine metabolite peaks from artifacts without large manually annotated training sets.

name: peak-based-parameter-estimation
description: Use when starting from raw untargeted metabolomics data (.mzML, .mzXML, or .CDF from qTOF, orbitrap, or FT-ICR instruments) and needing dataset-specific centWave peak-picking and XCMS grouping parameters before feature-table generation.

name: peak-boundary-eic-extraction
description: Use when comparing feature tables from LC-MS processing tools and you must judge whether extra reported features are genuine or low-quality, by recomputing a shape-fitness score on the EIC around each reported peak boundary.

name: peak-bounding-box-coverage-evaluation
description: Use when an acquisition controller's simulated or real MS2 scan schedule (mzML with MS1/MS2 events) must be scored by how many chromatographic peaks it actually fragmented, rather than counting MS2 scans.

name: peak-bounding-box-matching
description: Use when you have an mzML run containing MS2 fragmentation events plus an exported MZmine2 picked-peak bounding-box list for a corresponding full-scan run, and need per-peak coverage flags to score a fragmentation controller.

name: peak-correlation-network-analysis
description: Use when annotating ion forms and relationships among untargeted LC-MS metabolic features (e.g., NIST urine positive-mode peak tables) where conventional isotope/adduct rule grouping (CAMERA) misses in-source fragments and neutral losses.

name: peak-count-accounting-across-filter-steps
description: Decision support for choosing a Sample Filtering percentage in Galaxy-M: re-run the DIMS (100% threshold) and LC-MS (80% threshold) pipelines over MTBLS79 and MTBLS146 data, and record per-step peak removals before deciding whether Missing Values Imputation (e.g. KNN) is required.

name: peak-count-comparison-analysis
description: Use when GC-MS peak picking has been run with multiple embedded algorithms (e.g. centWave and matchedFilter) via WiPP and you need to quantify whether the integrated result set yields larger high-quality peak coverage than either algorithm alone.

name: peak-count-metrics-computation
description: Use when re-running or validating DIMPLE preprocessing under altered parameters (e.g., ppm mass tolerance or background-enrichment threshold) and you need average peak counts per root plus percent-change metrics versus defaults.

name: peak-count-scoring-of-spectrum-molecule-matches
description: Use when scoring query mass spectra (MGF, mzXML, or mzML) against candidate molecules in VInSMoC and you need the raw peak count score that determines which spectrum-molecule couples exceed the minimum score reporting threshold.

name: peak-cselectivity-fraction-calculation
description: Use when validating or re-implementing asari peak quality metrics on extracted ion chromatograms, or when assessing whether a chromatographic peak in a composite mass track is selective (cSelectivity up to 1.0) versus contaminated by co-eluting signal.

name: peak-detection-accuracy-metric-computation
description: Use when a custom-trained PeakBot CNN model must be quantitatively evaluated — verify peak/background classification accuracy exceeds 0.99 and that train-vs-validation loss/metric gaps stay below 5%.

name: peak-detection-and-integration-pipelining
description: Use when processing raw AEMS acquisitions from 384- or 1536-well plates in MRM or full-scan mode (PI/NL) where vendor software cannot automate shot-to-peak association, integration, and area quantification at high throughput.

name: peak-detection-ground-truth-validation
description: Use when you need to verify that a peak-finding routine (e.g. mzapy.peaks.find_peaks_1d_localmax or find_peaks_1d_gauss) detects the correct number of peaks with accurate x positions and heights before trusting it on real MS data.

name: peak-detection-sensitivity-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify how correctly reported chromatographic peaks depend on training data set choice (e.g., HILIC vs reversed-phase vs combined) and ML algorithm (NNet, RF, SVM, XGB) for automated LC-MRM-MS preprocessing.

name: peak-detection-signal-to-noise-thresholding
description: Use when raw GC×GC–MS CDF files must be converted into detected peak features, and you need to control detection sensitivity via first- and second-dimension signal-to-noise thresholds (e.g. benchmarking detection rates like the 27 fruitybeer peaks).

name: peak-filling-gap-imputation
description: Use when a speaq 2.0 peak-based workflow has produced grouped peak lists from 1D NMR spectra and some spectra lack a peak in groups present in other spectra, requiring gap filling before building the feature matrix.

name: peak-group-parameter-extraction
description: Use when MZmine 2 non-filtered peak lists from LC-MS metabolomics data must be converted into numeric peak shape features (e.g., medRelFWHM) for training or applying true/false peak classifiers such as logistic regression or Random Forest.

name: peak-grouping-overlap-quantification
description: Use when two homologue-series annotation runs over the same peak table (e.g. untargeted vs targeted detectHomologues, or HD vs nontarget) must be compared for grouped-peak overlap and exact-series correspondence, especially on complex datasets like MTBLS1358.

name: peak-height-normalization-and-thresholding
description: Use when raw MS/MS peak lists must be cleaned and scaled before formula ranking — converting m/z to monoisotopic Da via adduct correction, normalizing all peak heights to 100, and discarding peaks whose normalized height is below 0.5.

name: peak-integration-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when an automated CE-MS/MSI-CE-MS peak annotation or integration pipeline must be validated, i.e., you have a ground-truth annotation/peak-area table or expert manual preprocessing results to compare against quantitatively.

name: peak-integration-of-srm-chromatograms
description: Use when raw targeted SRM/MRM vendor files (e.g., Waters Xevo TQ-S from a Biocrates AbsoluteIDQ p180 plate) must be integrated and converted to concentrations with an open-source tool.

name: peak-intensity-coverage-annotation
description: Use when evaluating FIORA (or similar) spectral predictions against CASMI challenge data and you need to quantify annotated intensity coverage, enforce the paper's annotation filters, and verify cosine ≤ sqrt(coverage) per spectrum.

name: peak-intensity-l2-normalization
description: Use when MS/MS peak lists (e.g., parsed from MGF) must be intensity-normalized before spectral similarity comparison or clustering, and raw base-peak intensity scales vary across spectra.

name: peak-intensity-missing-value-filtering
description: Use when preparing a raw LC-MS feature/peak intensity table for downstream annotation or prioritization and many features have zero or missing intensities across samples.

name: peak-intensity-normalization
description: Use when MS/MS spectra (m/z + intensity peak lists from MSP/MGF metabolomics library files) must be intensity-normalized and de-weighted before computing spectral-entropy similarity between spectrum pairs.

name: peak-intensity-scaling
description: Use when pseudo MS/MS spectra reconstructed from MS1-only data (in-source fragments) must be matched against GNPS/MoNA/NIST-style reference MS/MS libraries, since in-source fragments skew toward low m/z and low collision energies relative to reference spectra.

name: peak-intensity-sqrt-transformation
description: Use when preprocessing MS/MS spectra (from mzML, mzXML, or MGF peak files) for cosine-similarity comparison or clustering, and dominant high-intensity peaks would otherwise skew the similarity measure.

name: peak-intensity-thresholding
description: Use when curating a mass spectral library (.MSP, .MGF, .JSON) in FragHub and you need to drop sparse or low-intensity spectra before writing the final unified library.

name: peak-intensity-weighting
description: Use when scoring similarity between two ESI-MS2 peak lists (m/z, intensity pairs) for compound identification against MassBank-style reference spectra, or when comparing exponent choices (m=0.5/n=2 vs m=0.6/n=3) at a 0.6 score threshold.

name: peak-intensity-weighting-of-spectral-tokens
description: Use when reconstructing Spec2Vec similarity scores from a trained Word2Vec model: processed MS/MS spectra must be converted into peak/loss word documents and embedded into fixed-length vectors via intensity-weighted summation.

name: peak-label-csv-export
description: Use when an aligned or unaligned MZmine/XCMS feature table must be labelled as High_quality, Low_quality, or Noise by the pretrained NeatMS model and exported to CSV for downstream use.

name: peak-label-filtering-for-classification-rates
description: Use when computing true-/false-positive classification rates or ROC curves for signal-vs-noise classification (e.g. LSH vs. intensity thresholding) on labeled synthetic windows that contain a 'noise_2' peak class.

name: peak-list-alignment
description: Use when combining detected peak lists from multiple LC-MS samples into one master peak list in MZmine 2 and retention times drift non-linearly between samples, forcing a choice between the Join and RANSAC aligners.

name: peak-list-alignment-precision-recall-analysis
description: Use when comparing peak list alignment algorithms on LC-MS feature tables where a 'ground truth' alignment table exists, and you need precision/recall metrics to decide which aligner (e.g., RANSAC vs Join) performs better on specific dataset fractions.

name: peak-list-mz-tolerance-matching
description: Use when an experimental MS2 peak list must be compared against database reference spectra (e.g., MassBank records) to score spectral similarity for metabolite annotation.

name: peak-list-parquet-export
description: Use when Thermo .RAW files must be converted into columnar (Parquet) spectral peak lists for downstream machine learning, secondary analysis, or QC — e.g. when per-scan m/z, intensity, noise, baseline and charge arrays are needed.

name: peak-list-parsing
description: Use when you need the underlying peak list (m/z and intensity pairs) of a specific MS/MS spectrum held in GNPS, MassIVE, MassBank, MS2LDA, MetaboLights, or Metabolomics Workbench, identified by a metabolomics USI such as mzspec:MSV000082791:(-)-epigallocatechin:scan:2.

name: peak-list-row-filtering-msms-annotated-features
description: Use when preparing a feature table exported from MZmine2 or Optimus for bioactive molecular networking: Step 1 requires a features_quantification_matrix.csv limited to features with an acquired MS/MS scan.

name: peak-list-spectra-parsing
description: Use when LC-MS/MS tandem mass spectra are provided as peak-list files (e.g., MGF) that must be loaded and parsed as unannotated spectra for direct pairwise comparison, dot-product distributions, or distance-matrix computation in compareMS2.

name: peak-list-spectrum-filtering
description: Use when raw or converted MS2 peak lists (e.g., .mzXML/.mgf files) are about to be clustered, library-searched, or networked in GNPS and need the standard GNPS spectrum cleaning filters applied.

name: peak-list-tabulation
description: Use when an MGF-imported MS/MS spectrum has been filtered (e.g. select_by_mz with mz_from=0, mz_to=1000) and the retained peaks must be written to a tabular file like filtered_peaks_mz.csv for inspection or validation.

name: peak-matching-within-mass-tolerance
description: Use when two entropy-normalized MS/MS spectra (intensity sums = 1, low-abundance ions already removed) must be ion-matched within 0.05 Da to form a merged spectrum for Shannon-entropy similarity scoring.

name: peak-mz-intensity-pair-extraction
description: Use when you have an LC-MS data file in .mzml format and need to parse it into per-spectrum records (spectrum_id, rt, and paired m/z/intensity peak arrays) for tabular downstream use rather than 3D viewing.

name: peak-overlap-statistics-computation
description: Use when generating augmented training instances from user-provided reference features and decoy/background signals for PeakBot's CNN peak-picking model training.

name: peak-parameter-recovery-validation
description: Use when validating that a peak-finding/peak-fitting function recovers correct peak positions, intensities, and widths — e.g. testing find_peaks_1d_gauss on synthetic 1D signals before applying it to real chromatographic or IMS data.

name: peak-picking-algorithm-reimplementation
description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking LC-HRMS chromatographic peak picking from MetMatch, comparing MassSpecWavelet vs. Gaussian-correlation vs. Savitzky-Golay runtimes, or porting MetMatch's Section 2.4 peak-picking logic to another language.

name: peak-picking-and-peak-list-generation
description: Use when raw vendor MALDI MSI data must be converted into a centroided peak list with peak filtering, alignment, matrix pixel removal, normalisation, outlier detection and de-isotoping before segmentation or ROI-level analysis.

name: peak-picking-from-fullscan-mzml
description: Reference for turning untargeted metabolomics LC-MS/MS full-scan mzML data (e.g. serum or beer extract injections) into per-peak bounding boxes of min/max RT and m/z to define which ions any DDA strategy could fragment.

name: peak-picking-from-profile-spectra
description: Use when raw profile-mode MS2 spectra (e.g. from lipid standard measurements stored in mzML) must be converted to centroided peaks prior to normalization, filtering, and HDF5 storage for spectral model training.

name: peak-picking-parameter-optimization
description: Use when raw untargeted metabolomics MS files (mzML, mzXML, CDF) must be peak-picked with centWave in XCMS or MZmine2, but no universal parameter set applies and manual/iterative tuning (e.g. IPO on HPC) is too slow or noisy.

name: peak-picking-parameter-optimization
description: Use when preprocessing large-scale GC-MS metabolomics raw data (mzML, mzData or NetCDF) where reliable peak detection is the bottleneck and per-algorithm peak-picking parameters need automated optimisation rather than manual tuning.

name: peak-picking-parameter-tuning
description: Use when raw LC-MS mzXML files are being processed with XCMS.featureTable and you need to test how changing mass tolerance or S/N thresholds changes feature counts and peak-shape fidelity.

name: peak-presence-threshold-classification
description: Use when you need in silico MS/MS spectra for small molecules from SMILES as binary peak-present/absent calls on a discretized m/z grid, e.g. to build in silico libraries or benchmark against CFM-ID/3DMolMS.

name: peak-property-table-preparation
description: Use when building a SMITER simulation and you need to turn a list of identified peptides with retention times and intensities (e.g. from a database search at 1% FDR) into the peak-properties csv/dict format SMITER expects.

name: peak-quality-classifier-selection
description: Use when you have cross-validation performance scores (e.g. Pass/Fail F-measure, Accuracy) for multiple candidate classifiers (algorithm × peak-quality metric set combinations) and must pick a single classifier with statistical justification rather than eyeballing averages.

name: peak-quality-metric-calculation
description: Use when an untargeted LC-MS peak table has been generated with XCMS (peak-picking, retention time correction, grouping across samples and pooled QCs) and you need quantitative, per-peak integration-quality features to train or apply the MetaClean peak-quality classifier.

name: peak-quality-metric-computation
description: Use when integrating targeted LC–MS peaks from RT/intensity ion chromatograms and you need per-target quality metrics (AUC, Max. Int., custom S/N, bell-curve similarity, points over the peak) to filter or QC peaks across large run collections.

name: peak-quality-post-processing-filtering
description: Use when a raw mzML HRMS file has been peak-picked (e.g., mssmain.peak_pick) and the resulting feature list contains noisy, split, or replicate peaks that must be filtered before background subtraction, clustering, or feature export.

name: peak-quality-score-feature-engineering
description: Use when building or retraining ML models for peak picking/peak reporting on LC-QQQ-MS MRM data (mzML) and you need the quality-score features that automRm derives from quantifier and qualifier traces.

name: peak-quality-threshold-counting
description: Use when comparing feature tables from multiple LC-MS processing tools (e.g. asari, XCMS, MZmine) on the same raw data and you need to determine whether differences in reported feature counts reflect genuine coverage or low-quality peaks.

name: peak-record-unique-identifier-assignment
description: Use when a raw Agilent Unknowns Analysis CSV (columns Component.RT, Component.Area, Base.Peak.MZ, File.Name, Compound.Name, Match.Factor) must be expanded into one uniquely-identified record per datapoint before compound extraction or annotation.

name: peak-recovery-quantification
description: Use when evaluating automated annotation of metabolomics NMR spectra: simulated mixtures with known ground-truth peak assignments are available and you need a per-compound recovery ratio for clustered SAND-decomposed peaks.

name: peak-resolvability-assessment-at-given-resolution
description: Use when processing high-resolution GC-CI-MS stable-isotope labeling data and you need to know which isotopologue m/z values of a derivatized formula can be distinguished at the instrument's resolution setting before quantifying them.

name: peak-sample-filtering-threshold-analysis
description: Decision support for choosing a Sample Filtering threshold in a Galaxy-M DIMS or LC-MS workflow, when you need to anticipate whether Missing Values Imputation (e.g. KNN) will be required afterwards.

name: peak-scoring-function-evaluation
description: Use when optimising GC-MS peak-picking parameters (e.g. centWave or matchedFilter) without ground truth: each candidate parameter set's detected peaks can be classified by a trained peak-quality SVM and ranked by an aggregate quality score.

name: peak-shape-asymmetry-monitoring
description: Use when a long-term LC-MS QC pool is tracked over weeks/months and you need to flag progressive column degradation from changing tailing factor or asymmetry factor of user-defined tracked compounds.

name: peak-shape-characterization
description: Use when processing raw untargeted LC/HRMS data (mzXML, mzML, netCDF) and each detected extracted ion chromatogram peak must be characterized by shape metrics (nIsoPair, RCS, RPW, S/N) to decide whether it passes quality thresholds.

name: peak-shape-manual-annotation
description: Use when an automated feature-detection output (mzLearn, XCMS, ASARI) must be scored for accuracy and you need peak-shape-based ground-truth labels for true-positive and false-positive rates.

name: peak-shape-quality-assessment
description: Use when a targeted MRM workflow (e.g. SmartPeak/OpenMS) has produced a FeatureDB CSV of sample types and meta-values such as peak_area, logSN, and RT and you need per-compound internal-standard quality scores before quantitative reporting.

name: peak-shape-raster-image-generation
description: Use when you have MZmine 2-extracted LC-MS peak groups (e.g., from human plasma HILIC LC-MS data) and need to represent each peak's shape across samples as a raster image for image-based deep learning peak classification.

name: peak-splitting-annotation
description: Use when SAND output peak tables contain multiple fitted peaks per compound (split peaks, e.g., around 7.3 and 7.95 ppm in the simulated benchmark) and peaks must be mapped back to their compound of origin for accurate quantification.

name: peak-table-matrix-parsing
description: Use when input is a spatial metabolomics peak table matrix (e.g. the AFADESI mouse brain table with 53,812 pixels x 2,654 ion peaks) that must be loaded and split into pixel coordinates and ion intensity columns before SMQVP analysis.

name: peak-table-metrics-comparison-across-pipelines
description: Use when benchmarking peak-picking/alignment pipelines on identical mzML/mzXML cohorts and you need defensible sensitivity, specificity, speed, and overlap numbers, such as IPA vs MS-DIAL on 499-sample studies.

name: peak-table-processing-stage-modeling
description: Use when a metabolomic peak table must be processed and you need to enumerate or reason about which ordered combinations of imputation, QCS-correction, transformation and normalization methods are applicable to the data scenario (with QCSs, with ISs, or neither).

name: peak-table-quality-checking
description: Use when you have an integrated, time-aligned, imputed peak table from untargeted LC-MS metabolomics and need to filter peaks for quality checking and account for technical variation prior to downstream grouping or statistics.

name: peak-table-sample-type-partitioning
description: Use when a tab-delimited peak-integrated table (columns aliquot, compound, area, type, injection_time, batch) from targeted LC-MS dMRM measurements must be split by sample type (QC, blank, study) so that per-compound RSD of QC area ratios and blank-derived background signal (e-score) can be.

name: peak-to-known-standard-matching
description: Use when an HRMS feature list from .mzML data of mixed chemical standards with known composition needs reliability validation by matching detected peaks to the spiked standard list and computing extraction accuracy.

name: peak-to-multiplicity-table-assembly
description: Use when a 1H NMR spectrum (e.g. JCAMP-DX) has been loaded and peak-picked with a threshold, and you need per-peak coupling constants and multiplicity labels assembled into a structured CSV table.

name: peakforest-data-model-entity-mapping
description: Use when a batch compound list must be loaded into a local PeakForest database and each template row's metadata (common name, InChI, InChIKey, etc.) must be mapped to the chemical compound entity before validation and database ingestion.

name: peaklist-alignment-across-samples
description: Use when per-sample IDSL.IPA peaklists (m/z–RT pairs from mzXML/mzML/netCDF HRMS files) must be RT-corrected and cross-referenced into one aligned table for a population-scale untargeted LC/HRMS study.

name: peaklist-deisotoping
description: Use when a peak-picked LC-MS peak list contains multiple co-eluting peaks differing by ~1 Da isotopic spacing that should be grouped into single deisotoped features before alignment across samples.

name: peaklist-gap-filling
description: Use when a peak list has been deisotoped and aligned across multiple raw LC-MS data files, but individual samples are missing detections for peaks found in other samples, blocking normalization and export.

name: pearson-correlation-analysis
description: Use when evaluating a spectral similarity metric against structural (Tanimoto) ground truth on MS/MS library testing pairs — e.g. mergedGNPS — to reproduce or compare correlation coefficients across multiple scoring methods.

name: pearson-correlation-analysis-of-biological-duplicate-pairs
description: Use when blinded biological replicate (duplicate) samples are embedded in a large metabolomics cohort and you need to quantify sample-level reproducibility via per-pair Pearson r across all metabolite features, e.g. 102 duplicate pairs in a 4104-sample T2D GC-MS plasma study.

name: pearson-correlation-analysis-of-ion-intensities
description: Use when you need to verify background-region signal stability in a spatial metabolomics peak table, e.g. before background noise removal, by checking that pairwise Pearson correlations of region spectra exceed 0.9.

name: pearson-correlation-and-rmsd-analysis
description: Use when validating that automated RT assignments match manual RT assignments, e.g. comparing metScribeR-derived RTs against manually assigned MassHunter RTs on authentic metabolite standards.

name: pearson-correlation-bioactivity-scoring
description: Use when you have a bioassay-annotated feature quantification table (e.g. features_quantification_matrix_edited_bioactivity.

name: pearson-correlation-coefficient-computation
description: Use when you have an expression matrix (e.g. Hu-cancer-RNASeq-dataset genes x samples) and need Pearson correlations of each feature with a selected feature, with or without two-group significance testing.

name: pearson-correlation-computation
description: Use when you need to verify that a targeted-lipidomics assay produces a linear response — e.g., after importing Skyline peak-area results for a transition list and fitting response-versus-amount regressions per lipid class.

name: pearson-correlation-feature-association
description: Use when an untargeted lipidomics feature table has few biological groups (e.g. resistant vs parent strains, ~4 replicates each) and you need a feature-level association ranking to complement multivariate PCA/PLS-DA cluster separation.

name: pearson-correlation-feature-collapsing
description: Use when a two-condition metabolomics feature table contains redundant or highly correlated metabolites (e.g. |Pearson r| > 0.7) or co-classed compounds (e.g. BCAAs, fatty acids) that should be collapsed into single nodes before joint network estimation.

name: pearson-correlation-feature-mask-analysis
description: Use when a registered multimodal MSI dataset has a thresholded binary pixel annotation (e.g. Ly6G IFM segmentation mask) and the goal is to identify the molecular signature — such as ether-linked PCs like PC O-36:4 — of a specific cell population.

name: pearson-correlation-feature-ranking
description: Use when you have a trained VAE/latent-space MSI classifier (e.g. massNet Code layer output) plus decoded per-m/z spatial images and a pixel-level class-probability map, and need to identify which m/z peaks drive tumor delineation.

name: pearson-correlation-meta-analysis
description: Use when the same feature/gene pairs have Pearson correlation coefficients measured across multiple independent studies (each with its own sample size) and they must be combined into a single estimate with fixed or random effects weighting.

name: pearson-correlation-of-alignment-functions
description: Use when comparing or validating the retention-time shift correction produced by MetMatch against an independent alignment (e.g., XCMS) on LC-HRMS feature lists, to confirm both tools recovered consistent non-linear Rt shifts.

name: pearson-correlation-of-pathway-activity-with-clinical-phenotype
description: Use when you have a gene expression matrix paired with a continuous clinical variable (e.g. 1-hour OGTT blood glucose) and need to test which of ~400 predefined KEGG/Biocarta pathways' activity levels correlate with the phenotype.

name: pearson-correlation-of-peak-areas
description: Use when validating a GC×GC–TOFMS peak-picking/quantification workflow against reference software using paired peak-area tables, especially with a serial dilution series (e.g. 1 ppm Breath Mix QC) where both correlation and dilution linearity must be shown.

name: pearson-correlation-of-peak-areas-to-mixing-ratios
description: Use when evaluating metabolomics peak-area quantification accuracy on a dilution/mixing series with known expected ratios, especially comparing two processing tools' feature tables.

name: pearson-correlation-significance-testing-by-random-shuffling
description: Use when two co-registered LA-ICP-MS elemental images (identical pixel dimensions) require quantification of spatial colocalisation, and a significance probability for the observed Pearson R is needed beyond the raw correlation coefficient.

name: pearson-correlation-spectral-similarity-assessment
description: Use when you have generated a simulated 1D or 2D metabolomic 1H NMR spectrum (urine, blood, or CSF) and need an objective, scalar measure of its resemblance to a real experimental spectrum before using the simulation for algorithm development or validation.

name: pearson-correlation-testing
description: Use when interpreting discriminant MOFA (or DIABLO) factors by testing their association with clinical metadata — numeric features via Pearson correlation, binary features via Wilcoxon — inside the BiomiX R pipeline.

name: pearson-correlation-testing-of-ion-pairs
description: Use when an annotated massdiff object of matched adduct ion pairs has been generated from MSI peak data and the candidate parent–adduct pairs must be tested for spatial co-localization before being accepted as true adducts.

name: pearson-correlation-validation
description: Use when a newly proposed clustering evaluation metric must be validated against an established ground-truth evaluation on a dataset where reference results exist, via Pearson correlation.

name: penalized-likelihood-density-ratio-fitting
description: Use when many metabolite hypotheses are tested simultaneously and raw p-value FDR is inflated: you have observed t statistics (z1), log standard errors (z2), and np permutations of null statistics, and need a calibrated local fdr2d threshold for biomarker discovery.

name: penalty-function-heuristic-optimization
description: Use when relative-abundance time-course GC-MS metabolomics data lack chemical standards and you can supply a stoichiometric matrix plus some fraction of known kinetic terms, to infer response factors via soft-constraint penalty minimization.

name: penicillium-spectral-library-processing
description: Use when a collection of MS/MS spectra (e.g. the 51 P. nordicum .mgf spectra with pnordicum_ms2_info.tsv metadata) must be converted into fragmentation graphs of m/z differences and mined for closed frequent fragmentation patterns.

name: peptide-activity-field-filtering
description: Use when you have a tabular HORDB peptide hormone information table (from the figshare deposit 10.6084/m9.figshare.c.5522241) and need to filter rows by an exact string in the activity field to validate a reported entry count.

name: peptide-binding-affinity-prediction-context-analysis
description: Use when reproducing or interpreting benchmark results on PSM rescoring features for immunopeptidomics, e.g. judging whether binding-affinity, ΔRT, or spectral features from tools like inSPIRE, DeepRescore, or MHCquant actually improve identifications.

name: peptide-bond-graph-annotation
description: Use when an input SMILES of an NRP or PK siderophore (e.g. pseudacyclin A, desferrioxamine B retrieved from PubChem) must be decomposed into building-block sequences with topology classification for CycloBranch mass spectra annotation.

name: peptide-database-search-execution
description: Use when MGF-converted MS/MS spectra (e.g. enzymatic antibody digests) need reference peptide identifications from a known protein database, to serve as pseudo-ground truth or benchmark labels for downstream tool evaluation.

name: peptide-database-search-parameterization
description: Use when a simulated proteomics run must be seeded with real identifications: you have a public MS/MS deposit (PRIDE/ProteomeXchange) and need a 1% FDR peptide list with retention times as simulation input.

name: peptide-feature-class-assignment
description: Use when processing traveling-wave IM-MS feature tables (m/z, charge, retention time, arrival time) from multiomic experiments where peptide features such as ADH or enolase digests and polyalanine peptides must receive class-matched CCS calibration without prior identification.

name: peptide-filtering-for-assembly-input
description: Use when raw de novo peptide predictions (e.g. from Novor, pNovo 3, DeepNovo, SMSNet, PointNovo, Casanovo) must be quality-filtered before de Bruijn assembly of antibody sequences with ALPS.

name: peptide-fragment-ion-annotation
description: Use when a molecular family of tandem mass spectra contains a shared core scaffold with variable modifications — e.

name: peptide-fragment-ion-annotation
description: Use when a specific scan in a Thermo .raw file has an assigned PSM (peptide + charge) and you must verify it by annotating the y-/b-ion series against fragment m/z values and comparing signal intensity to noise estimates.

name: peptide-fragment-ion-isotopic-annotation
description: Use when validating PSMs from proteomic stable isotope probing data: you have an observed MS2 scan (mzML/FT2) for a known peptide sequence and need to confirm theoretical b/y ion peaks align with observed peaks at a specified 13C enrichment level.

name: peptide-fragmentation-search-configuration
description: Use when the query mass spectra (MGF, mzXML, or mzML) originate from generalized peptides or the analysis aims to identify peptide-derived molecules, and a VInSMoC task must be set to Peptide fragmentation mode with the correct ion mode and scoring thresholds.

name: peptide-fragmentation-simulation
description: Use when you need a gold-standard synthetic proteomics mzML — e.g. to benchmark search/scoring algorithms, predict co-elution/co-fragmentation, or compare simulated vs. real TIC behavior for a peptide list on a defined gradient length.

name: peptide-ground-truth-label-mapping
description: Use when evaluating spectrum clustering results on data with known peptide identifications, needing per-cluster peptide label assignment to compute incorrectly-clustered fraction and completeness.

name: peptide-hormone-family-classification
description: Use when the input is a peptide-hormone table (e.g. HORDB's xlsx) needing family assignment under UniProt protein classification criteria, with per-family frequency counts and a family-size distribution plot.

name: peptide-identification-count-tabulation
description: Use when QC runs on the same sample (e.g. Pierce HeLa Protein Digest Standard) show depressed MS2 TIC or scan counts in MetaXtract metadata and you must confirm underperformance by comparing per-run peptide identification counts.

name: peptide-identification-matching
description: Use when peptide IDs from a search engine must be attached to RT-aligned feature groups (DeepRTAlign output) to compare aligned-peptide counts and quantification accuracy against MBR-based workflows like MaxQuant MBR or MSFragger MBR.

name: peptide-isotope-envelope-simulation
description: Use when a peptide amino-acid sequence needs a theoretical isotopic peak envelope at natural abundance (1.07% 13C) or a user-defined SIP enrichment level (e.g., 50% 13C) for visualization or SIP-PSM validation.

name: peptide-label-consistency-assessment
description: Use when spectrum clustering results (cluster assignments per MS/MS spectrum) must be validated against peptide-spectrum match labels to measure cluster purity, e.g. tuning thresholds to ~1% incorrectly clustered spectra.

name: peptide-label-propagation-across-clusters
description: Use when spectra are already embedded (32-dimensional GLEAMS vectors) and clustered (GLEAMS_cluster.npy, minimum cluster size 2), a subset carries peptide identifications such as MSGF+ PSMs at 1% FDR, and the goal is to label unassigned spectra in pure clusters.

name: peptide-length-accuracy-analysis
description: Use when de novo peptide predictions for antibody MS/MS spectra have been validated and you need to quantify whether long peptides are predicted less accurately and how missing fragment ions amplify that loss.

name: peptide-monoisotopic-mass-computation
description: Use when a predicted peptide sequence from de novo sequencing (e.g. Casanovo transformer output) must be checked against the observed precursor m/z within precursor_mass_tol across the isotope_error_range, or when beams must be pruned during decoding.

name: peptide-mz-image-extraction-from-imzml
description: Use when you have an imzML MALDI-MSI dataset plus an LC-MS/MS-confirmed peptide list and need per-protein spatial ion images co-registered to H&E histology.

name: peptide-physicochemical-property-calculation
description: Use when you have peptide hormone sequences in FASTA format from HORDB (figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.c.5522241) and need to reproduce or audit net charge, hydrophobic fraction, and length, or characterize hydrophobicity profiles (e.g. the 20-40% hydrophobic residue range).

name: peptide-physicochemical-property-calculation
description: Use when a curated peptide precursor panel has been filtered by inclusion criteria (1% FDR, consistency, no missed cleavage, length 7–15 aa, Skyline transition inspection) and needs GRAVY/length characterization.

name: peptide-precision-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when you must benchmark de novo sequencing tools on annotated MS/MS spectra across multiple species, holding out whole species to test cross-species generalization with peptide-level precision.

name: peptide-precision-recall-threshold-selection
description: Use when de novo peptide predictions from multiple sequencing tools (each reporting its own confidence score) must be filtered before assembly, and no absolute score cutoff is available because each tool calculates confidence differently.

name: peptide-precursor-inclusion-filtering
description: Use when a large DIA-quantified precursor list (e.g., from a spectral library like 110,126 precursors) must be filtered down to a small, manually verifiable panel of high-quality peptide precursors for targeted assay development.

name: peptide-precursor-mass-tolerance-assessment
description: Use when validating de novo sequencing predictions (e.g., Casanovo output on annotated MGF benchmark spectra) and you need a precursor mass-accuracy metric independent of peptide identity accuracy.

name: peptide-psm-filtering-from-fragpipe-output
description: Use when MSFragger/FragPipe PSM tables (searched at 1% protein FDR) must be filtered to confident peptide/protein sets before generating MALDI-MS peptide images in MSIght.

name: peptide-retention-time-peak-picking
description: Use when the input is a Thermo Fisher Orbitrap .raw file (e.g., 20181113_010_autoQC01.raw) containing iRT peptide runs and the goal is calibration-grade retention times for iRT regression, i.e., fitting rt = a + b * iRT-score.

name: peptide-sequence-adjacent-swap-perturbation
description: Use when rescoring peptide-spectrum matches with predicted-fragment-intensity features and you need a stability feature that distinguishes a peptide from its adjacent-residue-swap neighbours.

name: peptide-sequence-length-distribution-analysis
description: Use when you have a peptide FASTA file (e.g. 'Peptide sequence.fasta.txt' from the HORDB figshare deposit) and need to quantify or validate the sequence-length distribution of peptide hormones against the ~10 aa mode reported in Fig. 10.

name: peptide-sequence-mismatch-alignment-msms
description: Use when evaluating de novo sequencing output against pseudo-ground-truth PSMs (e.g. MS-GF+/X!Tandem at 1% FDR) and you need the relative frequency of mismatch categories such as >6 wrongly assigned amino acids or last-3-AA inversions.

name: peptide-set-overlap-analysis
description: Use when you have two peptide identification result sets — e.g. de novo mzTab predictions and a database-search PSM list at a stated FDR — and must quantify their overlap and per-set properties.

name: peptide-spectrum-match-fdr-summarization
description: Use when raw LC-MS files have been searched by a peptide/protein identification engine (e.g., FragPipe/MSFragger or DIA-NN) and you need per-file identification counts at a chosen FDR threshold for QC, throughput reporting, or result aggregation.

name: peptide-spectrum-match-filtering
description: Use when you need to select a defined subset of identified spectra (e.g. one peptide/charge, such as VATVSIPR charge 2 from P00761) from MassIVE/PRIDE identifications before joining them to spectrum clustering results.

name: peptide-spectrum-match-table-preparation
description: Use when building a ground-truth identification table (per-scan peptide assignments) to evaluate MS/MS clustering quality via DB-search-based purity, e.g. for PXD021518 or PXD023047 proteomics data.

name: peptide-spectrum-match-training-data-compilation
description: Use when a neural spectral-embedding model (e.g. GLEAMS) needs a labeled peptide-spectrum-match training corpus and no pre-packaged training set exists, requiring assembly from MassIVE-KB library metadata and raw spectra retrieval.

name: peptide-spectrum-matching
description: Use when raw centroided MS/MS spectra need to be assigned peptide identities by searching them against a protein reference database, e.g. after converting public tandem MS data into a standardized open format.

name: peptide-spectrum-search-fdr-filtering
description: Use when a synthetic (SMITER-generated) mzML must be quality-checked by searching it against the source proteome and reporting a 1% q-value PSM identification rate per peptide-set size.

name: peptide-structural-annotation-from-fragmentation
description: Use when MS/MS spectra suspected of sharing a structural motif (e.g. a residue-specific neutral loss) are NOT linked in a GNPS molecular network and you need exact m/z-difference patterns to annotate them.

name: peptidoform-prediction-feature-annotation
description: Use when raw search-engine PSM identifications (e.g. mzIdentML from X!Tandem, MaxQuant, or PEAKS) must be enriched with predicted-peptidoform features before semi-supervised rescoring, especially for non-tryptic immunopeptidomics data.

name: per-adduct-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you have SigmaCCS-predicted CCS values for [M+H]+, [M+Na]+, or [M-H]- adducts and an independently calculated CCS database (e.g., ISiCLE/PNNL) and need to quantify per-adduct agreement.

name: per-atom-attribution-heatmap-averaging
description: Use when you have a trained diffusion-based generative model over molecules and spectra, and you want to attribute which spectral patches influence which atom-type decisions at each stage of the denoising trajectory.

name: per-atom-type-rmsd-mae-evaluation
description: Use when a predicted-vs-experimental chemical shift comparison must be quantified per atom class (e.g. backbone 1H, 13C, 15N) to benchmark a prediction model like NMRFx's against an established predictor.

name: per-class-bgc-similarity-tuning
description: Use when tuning BiG-SCAPE pairwise distance weights per BGC class, e.g. when JI/AI/DSS combinations must be optimized against MIBiG compound structural distances for classes like RiPPs or PKS/NRP hybrids.

name: per-class-precision-recall-f1-computation
description: Use when you have a multiclass confusion matrix or class-level prediction counts and need to identify which class labels (e.g. NPClassifier superclasses) a model like DeepSAT predicts worst.

name: per-cohort-z-score-scaling
description: Use when a matrix of Nightingale NMR metabolic biomarker concentrations contains below-detection-limit zeroes and must be log-transformed and z-scaled within each study before cohort-level survival or meta-analysis.

name: per-component-concentration-position-refinement
description: Use when an initial CRNN-based spectral decomposition of 1H NMR plasma spectra leaves residual error and individual metabolite components need concentration scaling and peak-position adjustment to lower the per-metabolite reconstruction MSE.

name: per-compound-majority-vote-aggregation
description: Use when a compound-level decision must be derived from multiple per-spectrum classifier outputs (e.g. EI-MS and ESI-MS/MS spectra of the same compound) and a single bitter/nonbitter label is required for precision/recall evaluation.

name: per-compound-match-table-compilation
description: Use when you have parsed MASST match records for a library of synthesized compounds and need to compile per-compound counts of matched public files and total matches, then reconcile totals against reported figures.

name: per-compound-spectrum-merging
description: Use when training spectra-presence predictors from multiple spectra per compound and each compound needs one canonical binary target spectrum rather than intensity-level prediction across varying collision energies.

name: per-database-count-tabulation
description: Reference for adoptions/usage volumes of a chemical classification tool across named chemical databases (DrugBank, HMDB, ChEBI, PubChem, LIPID MAPS) — e.g. building an impact or adoption table for a classifier.

name: per-dataset-entry-tabulation
description: Use when reconstructing the provenance composition of COCONUT (or a similarly aggregated NP database) from published per-source counts and validating aggregated totals against reported flat/stereo release numbers.

name: per-dataset-metrics-table-assembly
description: Use when evaluating a pairwise retention-order model over many independent RPLC datasets and you must compute per-dataset accuracy, Spearman, and rank score for model vs. fingerprint baseline, then assemble into a comparison table.

name: per-dataset-summary-table-assembly
description: Use when you have run parameter tuning plus feature extraction on multiple LC-MS datasets (different sample types, acquisition modes, or MS vendors) and need one consolidated table recording each dataset's metadata and extracted-feature count to judge robustness across conditions.

name: per-feature-drift-quality-assessment
description: Use when a preprocessed LC-MS feature abundance matrix contains QC samples spread across injection order and features show systematic intensity drift that must be corrected and assessed per feature before imputation or statistics.

name: per-feature-indicator-table-construction
description: Use when FBMN/GNPS annotation coverage is incomplete (missing InChIs or no matches per feature) and you need per-feature GNPS cosine/tanimoto indicators to feed MS2DECIDE's K_estimation aggregation.

name: per-feature-linear-regression-modeling
description: Use when a full-scan feature table was acquired across a serial dilution series (e.g. 1.0, 0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 0.0625 mg/mL) and you must select biologically consistent ions by their linear intensity-vs-concentration response.

name: per-file-processing-timing-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify per-file processing cost of QC4Metabolomics — e.g. estimating how many mzML files the pipeline can handle per hour or planning acquisition scheduling around module latency.

name: per-formula-off-sample-frequency-analysis
description: Use when you have per-ion-image off-sample predictions across multiple datasets and want to know which molecular formulae are classified off-sample in a majority of datasets, e.g., to flag matrix-cluster contamination like DHB cluster ions.

name: per-gcf-histogram-visualisation
description: Use when you need to quantify and visualise how a link-scoring or filtering step (e.g. NPClassScore at a 0.25 cut-off) changes the per-GCF distribution of candidate BGC–MS/MS links, e.g. counting GCFs with ≤10 or ≤25 candidate links.

name: per-group-qc-criteria-merge
description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics feature table contains multiple pooled QC groups (separate pooled QC prepared per sample group) and features should be kept if they pass QC criteria in at least one QC pool.

name: per-injection-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when a SmartPeak CLI or GUI run has completed across a sequence of injections and you need per-injection wall-clock timings to quantify automated throughput and verify speed-up versus a manual processing baseline.

name: per-ionization-mode-statistical-aggregation
description: Use when a CCS bias table (per lipid species-adduct, in %) has been computed against a reference CCS library and you need a single quality-control metric per ionization mode (positive vs negative).

name: per-library-median-spectra-computation
description: Use when a newly integrated or existing mass spectral library collection must be characterized before integration — e.g., reporting how many spectra each compound contributes and which chemical classes dominate across GNPS, MassBank, MoNA, and MS-Dial-VS17.

name: per-metabolite-ttest-significance-testing
description: Use when a metabolomics abundance table (e.g., from Metabolomics Workbench) must be reduced to significantly altered metabolites between two groups before enrichment scoring.

name: per-molecule-performance-aggregation
description: Use when you have mzRAPP benchmark (Benchmark.csv) and NPP tool outputs (e.g. XCMS unaligned/aligned CSVs) already matched into comparison_data and need stage-wise per-molecule metrics with uncertainty bounds rather than single point estimates.

name: per-molecule-sampling-count-tracking
description: Use when preparing training pairs for a Siamese spectral similarity model (e.g., MS2DeepScore) and you must avoid bias from uneven Tanimoto-score coverage or over-sampled molecules in a spectral library.

name: per-mz-bin-classifier-training
description: Use when building or reproducing MS/MS spectral prediction models that predict peak presence per m/z bin (F1-scored binary classification) instead of full-spectrum intensity regression, as in the SingleFrag approach.

name: per-mz-position-fragment-classifier-training
description: Use when you need to predict MS/MS peak presence per m/z bin from molecule structures (SMILES), or to retrain/augment per-bin classifiers — e.g. adding 3D features to a mol2vec-based classifier.

name: per-peak-flag-table-export
description: Use when you have an mzML file with MS2 fragmentation events and a MZmine2-exported picked-peak list with RT and m/z min/max, and need per-peak DDA coverage flags.

name: per-plate-group-distribution-verification
description: Use when a stratified inter-batch balancing run (e.g., across gender, treatment/placebo, and age-group dimensions) has produced a plate-assignment table and you must confirm each plate's group proportions match the overall cohort ratio before exporting worksheets.

name: per-project-aggregation-of-annotations
description: Use when a training or evaluation dataset for EIC peak-quality annotation spans multiple LC-MS metabolomics projects and you need per-project good/poor label counts to verify dataset balance before CNN training.

name: per-reaction-fraction-computation
description: Use when metabolite annotations are tagged with BioTransformer reaction types and you need detected-vs-predicted counts and detection fractions per biotransformation (oxidation, glucuronidation, etc.).
tools: NIH Common Fund’s National Metabolomics Data Repository (Metabolomics Workbench)

name: per-record-annotation-quality-reporting
description: Use when an annotated .msp spectral library must be checked per record that SMILES, InChI, InChIKey, or CAS number metadata are well-formed before export or downstream use.

name: per-sample-rmse-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a new metabolite identification/quantification method's output reconstructions must be validated against an established tool on identical 1H NMR spectra, to demonstrate lower per-sample reconstruction error.

name: per-spectrum-runtime-measurement
description: Use when evaluating or comparing FSA formula-ranking throughput across reference-list scopes or datasets, where rank#1/top-5 accuracy must be reported alongside an average seconds-per-spectrum runtime metric.

name: per-spectrum-runtime-statistics
description: Use when comparing computational efficiency of spectrum-processing libraries on the same spectra (e.g. iPRG2012.mgf): identical steps must be timed per spectrum and first-call JIT outliers excluded before computing speedup.

name: per-subclass-annotation-stratification
description: Use when comparing MS2 annotation tools (LipidIN EQ+LCI, MS-DIAL, LipidSearch, Spectral Entropy, LipidMatch) on the same benchmark spectra and you need the reported ~70% vs >90% recall@Top-20 reproduced and broken down by lipid subclass.

name: per-superclass-statistical-aggregation
description: Use when you have per-compound cosine-similarity scores from spectral prediction evaluation and need to check whether prediction quality is uniform across compound classes rather than only reporting a global median.

name: per-tool-installation-status-tracking
description: Use when installing the MetumpX toolset on Ubuntu 18.04 and you need to capture, per selected tool, whether dependency resolution and installation succeeded or failed from the installer's on-screen dialogue and logs.

name: per-tool-percentage-tabulation
description: Use when comparing tool-generated HGVS annotations (HGVSc/HGVSp) against a reference standard such as ClinVar and you need to quantify, per tool and per field, what fraction of mismatches are missing values, position/variant-type shifts, or non-preferred syntax.

name: per-tool-performance-tabulation
description: Use when comparing in silico metabolism predictors on a common test set (e.g., EBoMD2, 60Reactants.sdf, or BioTransformer's hold-out SDF) and you need per-tool, per-enzyme Jaccard matrices to compute relative improvement margins.

name: per-year-performance-table-generation
description: Use when reproducing a baseline comparison across multiple harvest years (2001/2003/2004) where a trained baseline (CHESHIRE, threshold=0.5) must be tabulated against reported method results (NetAurHPD) per training-fraction session.

name: percentage-change-recomputation
description: Use when validating or recomputing a reported percent change in annotation or feature counts between two replicate groups (e.g., original vs PNNL PreProcessor-preprocessed LC-DT IM-MS lipid annotations) from deposited feature/annotation lists.

name: percentage-delta-verification
description: Decision support for validating reported benchmark deltas — e.g., checking that a recomputed +6.3 pp improvement in correct molecular formula assignment and a 792→541 drop in wrongly assigned formulas reproduce from deposited source data.

name: percentage-gain-consistency-verification
description: Use when consolidating before/after optimization metrics (GSI, feature counts, MS/MS spectra, annotated compounds) across multiple studies and you must verify each reported percentage gain is arithmetically consistent with the absolute counts.

name: percentage-improvement-verification
description: Use when an article claims a relative percentage improvement of one model over baselines (e.g. ESP vs MLP/GNN average rank) and the claim must be independently verified from the reported metric values.

name: percentile-based-baseline-correction
description: Use when smoothing MRM ion chromatograms (especially with dynamic dwell time) where baseline/background intensity must be estimated per-section from raw RT-intensity pairs before peak tip detection or peak quantitation.

name: percentile-based-common-feature-filtering
