description: Use when a pcpfm feature table contains rare/uncommon features that should not influence per-sample normalization factors, or when 'removal of uncommon features' is needed before QC, normalization, or batch correction.

name: perceptually-uniform-colormap-selection
description: Use when rendering LA-ICP-MS elemental images (e.g., 66Zn, 55Mn, 56Fe ion images) for publication or presentation, or when auditing existing figures for colormap-induced perceptual artifacts.

name: percolator-fdr-post-processing
description: Use when database-search engine output (Tide, Comet, MSGF+ PSMs) must be converted into an FDR-controlled unique peptide list — e.g. to benchmark de novo sequencing results like Casanovo's against a reference search at matched confidence.

name: performance-speedup-computation
description: Use when comparing file-format read performance for MRM mass-spectrometry data, or when validating that Aird conversion delivers the reported ~33x full-file and ~2.5x single-chromatogram speedups over mzML.

name: permanova-group-comparison-testing
description: Use when FT-ICR MS peak-intensity data with assigned molecular formulas have been normalized and grouped by treatment metadata, and you need a significance test of between-group differences in metabolite composition that complements ordination.

name: permanova-group-significance-testing
description: Use when testing whether compositional (beta-diversity) distances separate predefined sample groups — e.g. genotype or sex in SPF mouse metagenomics — and you need a per-factor pseudo-F and p-value rather than abundance-level tests.

name: permanova-group-significance-testing
description: Use when a sample metadata column (e.g., chromatographic batch) must be tested against beta diversity of a metabolomics feature table, especially to quantify how much a Qemistree chemical hierarchy attenuates batch-driven separation.

name: permanova-pseudo-f-hypothesis-testing
description: Use when a precomputed sample-sample distance matrix (MEMO, Qemistree UniFrac, CSCS, or feature-table Bray-Curtis) must be tested for group effects — e.g. 'experiment' (C18 vs C18 RT-shift, Q-Exactive vs Maxis II Q-TOF) vs 'composition' — via PERMANOVA pseudo-F.

name: permethylated-n-glycan-mass-assignment
description: Use when you have a permethylated N-glycan MALDI-TOF spectrum (e.g., PNGase-F released, HILIC SPE enriched, permethylated with DMSO/NaOH/CH3I, mixed with Super-DHB matrix) and a glycan name/theoretical-mass (Da) database, and need to call which glycans are present by accurate mass matching.

name: permutation-based-family-wise-error-estimation
description: Use when you need a gold-standard family-wise error rate benchmark (Meff0 = alpha / alpha_f0) to calibrate or validate eigen-analysis or distance-correlation-based p-value adjustment procedures for high-dimensional metabolomics association testing.

name: permutation-based-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when comparing pathway activity levels between two sample groups with per-pathway t statistics and a family-wise error correction is needed for many correlated pathway tests.

name: permutation-based-pathway-significance-testing
description: Use when a gene-by-sample matrix has been converted to pathway activity levels for ~400 KEGG/Biocarta gene-sets and you need empirical p-values for phenotype associations without parametric distributional assumptions.

name: permutation-based-prioritization-benchmarking
description: Use when you have a ranked per-patient candidate gene list with a known causative gene and need to quantify whether the prioritization rate exceeds chance, e.g. reproducing metPropagate's 92% top-20th-percentile rate.

name: permutation-based-pvalue-estimation
description: Use when testing many predefined gene-sets (~400 KEGG/Biocarta pathways) for differential activity between two sample groups and you need a multiple-testing-aware empirical p-value without parametric assumptions on small microarray cohorts.

name: permutation-based-significance-testing
description: Use when a pathway-level importance statistic (MB-VIP, VIP, RGCCA loading relevance, bootstrap non-zero-loading count) needs a p-value, and no closed-form null exists because the statistic comes from a fitted multivariate model (MB-PLS, PLS, DIABLO).

name: permutation-based-significance-testing
description: Use when comparing mean pathway activity levels between two sample groups (e.g., diabetic vs. non-diabetic, current vs. never smokers) and you need a p-value that controls for multiple testing across ~400 pathways.

name: permutation-cross-validation-design
description: Use when validating a supervised PLS-DA discriminant model built on lipid molecular species (LMS) intensity data and you need permutation-based cross-validation statistics (Accuracy, R2Y, Q2Y) per PLS component to assess classification robustness.

name: permutation-null-approximation
description: Use when testing many metabolite hypotheses (e.g., biomarker discovery) and a standard single-statistic FDR is inflated; input includes observed t statistics (z1) with their log standard errors (z2) plus permutation-based null statistics.

name: permutation-null-distribution-significance-testing
description: Use when pairwise MS/MS spectral alignments (e.g. from SIMILE max-weight matching) need p-value-based significance calls so candidate compound pairs can be ranked and compared against cosine-based scoring.

name: permutation-null-pvalue-gamma-modeling
description: Use when enrichment p-values from Fisher's exact tests on network module/pathway hits need a permutation-estimated null because the small-of overlap-corrected overlap count is non-standard.

name: permutation-null-sampling
description: Use when pathway activity levels (e.g. the first metacompound/SVD singular vector per metabolite set) have been computed and calibrated p-values are needed that account for noise and missing peaks in metabolomics intensity data, for comparisons like Stage_1/Control.

name: permutation-significance-testing
description: Use when correlating metabolomics-derived substructure motifs (Mass2Motifs) with genome-mined sub-cluster features across a paired genome-metabolome strain panel, and you need p-values that account for non-independence of closely related strains.

name: permutation-significance-testing
description: Use when you have trained the SARTRE random forest classifier (e.g. on stitch_yeast with shadow-price or 128-bit fingerprint features) and need to verify that observed AUC/metrics are statistically significant rather than artifacts of label structure or feature information.

name: permutation-test-model-validation
description: Use when a supervised classifier (OPLS-DA, RF) fitted on a feature table where features vastly outnumber samples reports high training fit (R²Y) and you must establish whether it generalizes, via k-fold CV and permutation testing.

name: permutation-testing-empirical-pvalue-estimation
description: Use when a fitted multiblock PLS model (e.g. MamsiPls on multi-assay LC-MS feature tables) needs statistically defensible per-feature significance, and MB-VIP scores alone cannot distinguish signal from chance.

name: permutation-testing-feature-significance
description: Use when you have a fitted MB-PLS model over multiple LC-MS assay blocks (e.g. HPOS/LPOS/LNEG) and need statistically defensible feature significance beyond raw MB-VIP magnitudes before biomarker annotation or structural search.

name: perplexity-hyperparameter-grid-tuning
description: Use when a 2D t-SNE embedding of spectral features is needed in an LC-MS/MS untargeted metabolomics pipeline and the pairwise feature distance/similarity matrix (e.g. MS2DeepScore) is already available, so perplexity must be chosen objectively rather than by default.

name: perplexity-parameter-tuning
description: Use when computing the specXplore t-SNE overview embedding from an ms2deepscore pairwise similarity matrix (e.g. wheat <1000 or urine <4000 features) and a perplexity value must be chosen before exporting tsne_embedding.csv.

name: perspective-transformation-matrix-estimation
description: Use when optical images of macroscopic (>300 μm) targets are distorted by camera lenses or scanner mechanics and accurate spatial coordinates are needed for optically guided MALDI-TOF MS targeting.

name: pesticide-metabolite-candidate-enumeration

name: pfas-mdc-mc-feature-classification

name: pfas-msms-feature-annotation

name: precursor-mass-window-filtering
description: Use when annotating unassigned query MS/MS spectra against a reference library: before Denoising Search scoring, filter library entries whose precursor m/z or molecular formula mass lies outside the instrument's precursor mass accuracy window.

name: precursor-mz-candidate-filtering
description: Use when matching unknown query MS/MS spectra against a large spectral library (e.g., ~76,000–95,000 AllPositive/GNPS spectra) and full pairwise scoring would be too slow: filter candidates by precursor m/z before computing similarity scores.

name: precursor-mz-candidate-retrieval
description: Use when you have an MS/MS analyte precursor mass and need a putative compound candidate list from a metabolite database for annotation or fingerprint-score ranking.

name: precursor-mz-charge-filtering
description: Use when dereplicating natural products by matching query MS/MS spectra against a reference spectral library and candidate library entries must be restricted by precursor charge state, precursor m/z tolerance, matched-peak count, and match score.

name: precursor-mz-charge-matching
description: Use when confirming N-linked glycan identifications from LC-MS/MS mzXML data: an MS1 output Excel file lists candidate glycan-RT pairs, and the MS2 fragment scan for the matching precursor m/z and charge must be located for fragment annotation.

name: precursor-mz-difference-histogramming
description: Use when you hold two MGF peak-list files (e.g., serum tandem mass spectra from ProteomeXchange PXD034932) and want to visualize spectral similarity as a function of precursor m/z difference to inspect charge states, mass accuracy, and isotope errors without a database search.

name: precursor-mz-mobility-charge-matching
description: Use when detected isotope patterns from DDA-PASEF TDF/TIMS data must be validated against vendor-selected precursor lists, e.g. to measure how many of the N=6902 Bruker-selected peptides an LSH pipeline recovers.

name: precursor-mz-pairing-with-ppm-tolerance
description: Use when you need candidate spectrum pairs from an MS/MS library whose precursor m/z agree within ~10 ppm, to build same-vs-different-compound labels for AUROC evaluation of spectral similarity scoring.

name: precursor-mz-tolerance-based-retrieval
description: Use when evaluating whether a spectral similarity metric (embeddings, supervised models, or 44 classical measures) retrieves the correct molecular structure from a spectral library, with candidates restricted by precursor m/z tolerance such as 10 ppm.

name: precursor-mz-tolerance-grouping
description: Use when raw MS2 peak lists (.mzXML/.mzML/.mgf) from multiple LC-MS files must be collapsed into consensus spectra to build GNPS molecular network nodes, or when choosing a Minimum Cluster Size for a dataset.

name: precursor-peak-metric-extraction
description: Use when raw MS files (Agilent 'd', Thermo '.raw', Bruker 'd', or mzML; LC-MS, LC-IMS-MS, DDA/DIA, direct infusion) need automated QC of precursor-ion peak metrics without identification-based scoring, e.g. batch-level metabolomics QC.

name: precursor-peak-removal
description: Use when a USI-loaded or MGF-loaded MS/MS spectrum (e.g. mzspec:PXD004732:...:scan:41840 or iPRG2012.mgf) still contains the precursor ion peak and must be cleaned before fragment annotation, noise filtering, or plotting.

name: precursor-product-ion-intensity-normalization
description: Use when MS-DIAL result tables contain raw precursor and fragment ion intensities that must be converted to comparable 0–1 scales before rendering MS1×MS2 grayscale fingerprint images for CNN input.

name: precursor-tolerant-open-search
description: Use when annotating pseudo MS/MS spectra (MGF) reconstructed from MS1-only LC-MS or imaging MS data, where each spectrum contains multiple ion forms (e.g. [M+H]+, adducts, multimers) rather than a single true precursor.

name: precursor-tolerant-reverse-spectral-matching
description: Use when annotating full-scan MS data (MS1-only mzML/mzXML/imzML or pseudo MS/MS mgf) against a reference MS/MS library, especially when the true precursor m/z is unknown or multiple adducts/multimers must be matched at once.

name: predicate-based-residue-index-filtering
description: Use when a liputils-produced residue count table (residues as DataFrame index, samples as columns) must be subset by chain-length and unsaturation, e.g. restricting to residues ≤30 carbons because low-resolution compounds like PE(P-40:6)/PE(O-40:7) are ambiguous.

name: predicted-lipid-database-matching
description: Use when aligned, peak-picked HILIC-IM-MS feature tables (positive and/or negative ESI) must be annotated with lipid identities at graded confidence levels using m/z, retention time, and CCS matching.

name: predicted-metabolite-set-matching
description: Use when a structure-based metabolism predictor (e.g. CyProduct, GLORY, BioTransformer, ADMET Predictor) has produced predicted metabolite lists and you need a quantitative comparison against known true metabolites.

name: predicted-metabolite-set-stability-assessment
description: Use when you have mummichog's two input lists (significant m/z features selected by a cutoff and the full reference feature list) and need to know whether the predicted activity network is robust to the cutoff choice, e.g. for sensitivity analysis of the ~60-metabolite moDC prediction.

name: predicted-vs-annotated-metabolite-validation
description: Use when benchmarking mummichog metabolite prediction against a published, experimentally annotated metabolite list for the same MS dataset, e.g. the human urine set of Roux et al. 2012 with a BioCyc model.

name: predicted-vs-groundtruth-scatter-visualization
description: Use when a supervised or heuristic spectral similarity metric must be visually benchmarked against a structural ground truth (Daylight Tanimoto) on MS/MS query–reference pairs, and a scatter point cloud plus Pearson r are the reporting format.

name: predicted-vs-purified-bioactivity-concordance-analysis
description: Use when a compound isolated via NP Analyst-guided mass-guided fractionation must be confirmed as the predominant active component by comparing its measured bioassay (BioMAP) profile against the aggregated activity profile of the bioactive community's member prefractions.

name: predicted-vs-true-similarity-correlation-analysis
description: Use when a trained MS2DeepScore model must be validated on held-out test pairs, especially to check whether cross-ionization-mode Tanimoto predictions correlate with ground-truth structural similarity.

name: prediction-accuracy-curve-analysis
description: Use when you have per-spectrum embedding-quality estimates (predicted MSE from an embedding evaluator) and a similarity prediction error metric, and want to quantify how much accuracy improves as the highest-uncertainty spectra are removed.

name: prediction-accuracy-statistics
description: Decision support for judging whether computationally predicted collision cross sections agree with experimental TWIMS CCS values within ±3%, per metabolite or per adduct state.

name: prediction-error-aggregation-across-simulation-runs
description: Use when benchmarking normalization methods on in-silico metabolomics data with known ground-truth drift and injected outliers, and per-run squared prediction errors must be aggregated into median estimates.

name: prediction-error-metric-aggregation
description: Use when a benchmark produces per-split error metrics (e.g. MRE and RMSE over 101 random 70:30 splits) and you need robust median-based rankings of multiple prediction tools per adduct class.

name: prediction-error-metric-computation
description: Use when several prediction tools are being benchmarked on the same randomly sampled test sets and you need per-tool error rankings (MRE/RMSE) aggregated across iterations, e.g. evaluating CCS predictors on ion-mobility test data stratified by adduct type.

name: prediction-error-quantification
description: Use when RTs predicted under one chromatographic method (e.g., the METLIN SMRT reverse-phase method) must be made comparable with retention times measured under other independent experimental LC-MS methods, and when a median absolute error (in seconds) must be reported to validate the projection.

name: prediction-error-threshold-coverage-evaluation
description: Use when you have paired true vs. predicted retention times for a held-out test set and need to quantify model coverage at error cutoffs and the FDR impact of an RT-based candidate filter.

name: prediction-pipeline-grid-search-tuning
description: Use when a labeled data set (e.g. a quality rating treated as a categorical class label) must be turned into a class-prediction estimator whose pre-processing, feature selection and estimator settings need joint optimization.

name: prediction-probability-interval-analysis
description: Use when a pretrained classifier (e.g. pSCNN on NMR spectral pairs) must be stress-tested against a bounded input perturbation to determine the tolerable variation interval for confident (probability > 0.5) predictions.

name: prediction-stability-delta-scoring
description: Use when rescoring immunopeptidomics or other PSMs with predicted fragment-ion intensities and you need to detect sequences whose spectral-angle fit is unstable under adjacent-residue swaps, as in inSPIRE-style rescoring.

name: prediction-strategy-comparison-across-tools
description: Use when chemical structures are known for a set of compounds with EI-MS or ESI-MS/MS positive-mode spectra and sensory bitter/nonbitter labels, and both a structure-based and a spectrum-based predictor must be compared.

name: prediction-vs-verified-structure-comparison
description: Use when G.A.M.E. predictions from csccp-solver-cli (--dec 5, -r 3) exist for the Cuscuta chinensis, Ophiopogon japonicus, Polygonum multiflorum or Angelica sp. datasets and you must confirm the expected verified compounds (5, 7, 7, 45 constitutions) were recovered.

name: predictive-interval-quantification-for-rt-projections
description: Use when predicted RTs from a DNN (e.g. trained on SMRT) must be projected onto a target chromatographic method with few (~10) identified molecules and probabilistic intervals are needed to score candidate metabolites.

name: predictive-model-auc-evaluation
description: Use when a tuned supervised classifier (e.g. SKlearn random forest on pathway scores) has been trained with nested cross-validation and you must quantify held-out predictive performance as AUC, especially to compare against a molecular-level concatenated baseline.

name: predictive-model-overfitting-assessment
description: Use when building a metabolomics classifier (e.g. random forest on feature-selected metabolites) and you need to measure how much train-set-only validation (OOB error) underestimates generalization error versus a stratified held-out test set.

name: predret-dataset-preprocessing
description: Use when loading PredRet retention time data from multiple LC systems via a config.json file and you need per-system cleaning (duplicate RTs, small-RT noise, >5% spread outliers) before order prediction or cross-system comparison.

name: prefect-workflow-orchestration
description: Use when batch harmonizing multi-source compound metadata sheets — e.g. plate_id/well_location tables from natural-product and drug libraries — into a standardized template with structural descriptors.

name: prefraction-activity-community-prioritization
description: Use when a prefractionated extract library has per-prefraction bioassay results plus processed MS feature data (GNPS graphML or MZmine 2 peak lists), and the goal is to identify which MS feature drives the activity of a bioactive community and dereplicate it against known compound profiles.

name: prenylated-flavonoid-spectral-benchmarking
description: Use when a ground-truth prenylated flavonoid MS/MS test set is available and you need a head-to-head comparison of AnnoMe's custom classifiers versus SIRIUS compound-class predictions.

name: prenylated-flavonoid-spectrum-annotation
description: Use when you need to count or prioritize putative prenylated flavonoid spectra in HR-MS/MS inference datasets (e.g., MGF files from Glycyrrhiza uralensis root or Paulownia tomentosa fruit extracts) using custom-trained spectrum classifiers.

name: preprocessed-vs-original-feature-comparison
description: Use when evaluating whether raw-data preprocessing (multidimensional smoothing, spike removal) changes low-abundance feature detectability across LC-IM-MS replicates, using annotation lists from original vs PreProcessor-generated MS-files.

name: preprocessing-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when validating that a specXplore preprocessing run of .mgf MS/MS data (e.g. wheat or urine datasets) completes within the published runtime envelope and yields the expected number of features after processing.

name: preprocessing-file-pairing-original-vs-preprocessed
description: Use when a MassIVE deposit pairs original raw LC-IM-MS files with PreProcessor-generated counterparts (suffix _MA-d3-c3-Min20_SR) and you must quantify preprocessing storage savings as a preprocessed/original byte-size ratio.

name: preprocessing-parameter-recording
description: Use when a notame preprocessing pipeline has produced a feature-by-sample abundance matrix and you must capture the exact transformation, PQN and center/scale settings before writing the transformed matrix onward.

name: presence-absence-matrix-construction-from-tokenised-genes
description: Use when you have a large set of predicted statistical sub-clusters (e.g. PRESTO-STAT output from antiSMASH-DB BGCs) and need to organise related ones into hierarchical families/clans via a binary gene-content representation.

name: press-localization-parameter-configuration
description: Use when a vendor-, sequence-, and field-strength-specific (3T PRESS) metabolite basis set must be simulated in MATLAB, or when validating simulated basis functions against release FID-A or phantom-measured (LCModel) basis sets.

name: pressure-temperature-corrected-ccs-calibration
description: Use when single-field DTIMS CCS values for the same ion vary across many runs (e.g. large RapidFire SPE-IMS-MS batches) and per-run pressure/temperature fluctuations are suspected of inflating %RSD.

name: presto-stat-subcluster-detection
description: Use when a biosynthetic gene cluster dataset (e.g. tokenised antiSMASH BGCs) needs statistical sub-cluster prediction whose performance must be benchmarked against experimentally verified SubClusterBlast sub-clusters using an overlap-fraction criterion.

name: presto-top-motif-matching
description: Use when tokenised BGCs (antiSMASH-predicted clusters with detected (sub)Pfams) need unsupervised sub-cluster motif discovery, or when validating predicted sub-clusters against curated SubClusterBlast/MIBiG references via overlap fractions.

name: pretrained-cross-modal-model-inference
description: Use when you have preprocessed consensus MS/MS spectra plus candidate molecule lists (retrieved by mass tolerance) and need to annotate spectra by ranking candidates with a pretrained joint-embedding model.

name: pretrained-deep-neural-network-inference-msms
description: Use when an unknown metabolite's MS/MS spectrum (e.g., from Shimadzu LC-ESI-IT-TOF or Bruker Compact LC-ESI-QTOF) must be matched to candidate structures in a known-spectra database rather than via direct library match.

name: pretrained-gnn-cnn-checkpoint-integration
description: Use when SMILES-derived molecular graphs and molecular images must be encoded by pretrained GNN/CNN encoders before training the projection layer that connects to the LLaMA model.

name: pretrained-gnn-inference
description: Use when building the 4D derivatized sterol lipid database where predicted retention times must complement fragment ion and CCS predictions, and molecular structures (RDKit-parsable) are available for inference with the pretrained GNN.

name: pretrained-metabolic-score-projection
description: Use when you have a Nightingale Health 1H-NMR metabolomics matrix (CSV/TSV with example-matching column names) and need per-sample values for MiMIR's 24 pre-trained metabolic scores/surrogates.

name: pretrained-resnet-backbone-adaptation
description: Use when building a self-supervised representation model for ion images (MSI) where a pretrained CNN backbone must be converted into a twin shared-parameter encoder feeding projection/prediction MLPs and a SimSiam-style contrastive loss with stop-gradient.

name: pretraining-dataset-scaling-ablation
description: Use when you must quantify whether scaling a decoder pretraining corpus (fingerprint-to-molecule pairs) improves downstream de novo structure generation, and you can pretrain/finetune at multiple corpus sizes on a held-out benchmark.

name: pride-dataset-batch-processing
description: Use when a benchmark or QC task requires annotating a batch of publicly deposited Thermo RAW files from PRIDE (e.g. the most recent N files from a given year) via an automated, reproducible pipeline.

name: pride-dataset-mgf-conversion
description: Use when raw files from a PRIDE accession such as PXD000561 must be fetched and converted from vendor format to MGF (ThermoRawFileParser) before spectral clustering or CPU/GPU clustering benchmarks.

name: pride-repository-raw-file-retrieval
description: Use when RAW files deposited in a public repository such as PRIDE must be fetched automatically by accession (e.g. PXD060351) and annotated with acquisition metadata in a reproducible, containerizable batch pipeline.

name: primary-id-uniqueness-check
description: Use when a freshly uploaded .csv or .xlsx metabolomics table must be validated for threshold-exceeding missing data, non-numeric concentration entries, or a missing/non-unique primary ID before imputation and normalization.

name: primary-literature-confirmation-mapping
description: Use when a metabolic network reconstruction (e.g. from KEGG/NCBI-RefSeq mapping in MINNO) has yielded predicted missing reactions and each candidate needs an evidence label — primary-literature confirmation vs homology support — before downstream use.

name: primate-serum-tryptic-digest-sample-annotation
description: Use when multiple MS/MS datasets (e.g. MGF files of tryptic digests from primate sera, four individuals per species) must be assigned to species/group labels so pairwise spectral similarities can be averaged at the species level.

name: primate-topology-validation-against-reference-cladistics
description: Use when LC-MS/MS tandem mass spectra (e.g. MGF files of tryptic digests) are available for multiple individuals per species and the goal is a species-level phylogeny validated against known primate cladistics.

name: principal-component-analysis-of-scms-feature-matrices
description: Use when you have a pretreated SCMS metabolomics feature table (single cells x metabolic species, noise/background-subtracted, TIC-normalized, peak-aligned) and want an unsupervised first check of phenotype separability before supervised classification.

name: principal-component-chemical-space-analysis
description: Use when ML retention-time models must be shown to generalize across compound libraries, by checking that training, test, and validation sets (e.g. HILIC 880/143/377 and RPLC 398/96/358 compounds) co-occupy chemical space.

name: principal-component-loadings-export
description: Use when a fitted m_prcomp MPCA model on 2D-TIC GCxGC chromatograms (e.g., MTBLS579) needs its scores matrix or PC loadings exported as numeric CSV files for downstream use or validation.

name: principal-component-score-extraction
description: Use when the analysis goal is quality control of a 1H NMR plasma metabonomic dataset — e.g. detecting batch effects or confirming run reproducibility by inspecting PCA score plots of QC samples.

name: principal-components-analysis
description: Use when a line-aggregated, z-score standardised ionome dataset (ion concentrations from ICP-MS experiments) needs exploratory multivariate analysis to reveal the dominant sources of variation across elements/samples.

name: principal-curve-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when a metabolite-by-sample measurement matrix (e.g. plasma_breast_cancer.csv) must be converted into a pathway-by-sample PDS matrix to enable personalized, patient-level pathway classification modeling.

name: principal-curve-projection
description: Use when you have a metabolite abundance matrix (e.g., metabolite names or HMDB ids × samples) and need to reduce it to pathway-level features via PDS projection before feature selection or ML classification.

name: priority-rank-table-generation
description: Use when you have a table of fractions or candidate samples with measured potency/cytotoxicity values and need to rank them so the most potent entries guide which material proceeds to isolation or deeper analysis.

name: prm-assay-validation-verification
description: Use when designing or auditing a targeted lipidomics PRM/SRM assay and you must decide how many MS/MS fragments per lipid are needed for unambiguous identification within a background lipidome.

name: prm-targeted-scan-interval-verification
description: Use when a Thermo .raw file is claimed to be PRM/targeted and you must confirm regularly spaced MS2 scans for a precursor (e.g. FTMS + c NSI Full ms2 487.2567@hcd27.00) via scan-index deltas.

name: probabilistic-fragment-distribution-modeling
description: Use when predicting an MS/MS spectrum from a known molecular structure (C2MS), especially when high mass accuracy, formula annotations, and fragment-level interpretability matter for library augmentation.

name: probabilistic-fragmentation-model-training
description: Use when training or retraining a learned fragmentation model for tandem mass spectral database search, or when scoring candidate molecule-spectrum pairs and estimating target-decoy FDR for small molecule identification.

name: probabilistic-graph-integration-of-retention-order-and-msms-scores
description: Use when you have per-peak MS/MS candidate scores and pairwise ROASMI P_ij retention-order probabilities and need to rank candidate structures for each detected peak, e.g. to distinguish isomers or annotate peaks lacking usable MS/MS spectra.

name: probabilistic-log-rank-model-fitting
description: Use when you have molDiscovery fragment-peak matches on training molecules with reference spectra and want to learn or visualize how fragment log-ranks depend on bond type and parent-molecule log rank.

name: probabilistic-pca-data-completion
description: Use when a metabolite profiles matrix (e.g. tomato pericarp metabolic profiles for the 2001, 2003 and 2004 harvesting seasons) contains missing values that must be completed before downstream correlation-network construction or other pairwise analyses.

name: probabilistic-pixel-classification
description: Use when raw MALDI-MSI pixel spectra (e.g. HDF5-format FT-ICR MSI with tens of thousands of m/z variables) must be classified normal vs tumor per pixel with probabilistic scores, and spatially mapped uncertainty at tumor margins is the target output.

name: probabilistic-quotient-normalization
description: Use when an mRList of MS-Dial-derived Urine or similar LC-MS/MS feature abundances has been filtered (m/z, NA, CV vs QC) and needs PQN, but mRList$metab_ann lacks the 'reference' column.

name: probabilistic-quotient-normalization
description: Use when a metabolomics feature table shows unwanted sample-to-sample variation (e.g. dilution or total-signal differences) and a normalization robust to a few dominant metabolite changes is needed before statistical analysis.

name: probabilistic-quotient-normalization
description: Use when preprocessing a feature-abundance matrix from non-targeted LC-MS metabolomics and samples need to be normalized against a reference (e.g. QC pool) before multivariate analysis.

name: probability-thresholding-and-component-ranking
description: Use when a trained pSCNN model has produced inclusion probabilities for N mixture–compound spectral pairs and you must convert these probabilities into a thresholded, descending-rank list of candidate components of an NMR mixture.

name: probability-weighted-fragment-spectral-aggregation
description: Use when you have a per-fragment probability distribution (atom subsets or chemical subformulae) with exact atomic-composition masses and need to render it as a summed mass spectrum at a specified bin resolution.

name: processing-parameter-traceability
description: Use when a metabolomics pipeline must remain reproducible and auditable — i.e., each raw-data-processing, cleaning, or QC step's parameters need to be stored alongside the processed feature table so prior steps can be traced.

name: processing-report-generation
description: Use when a matchms library-cleaning pipeline has been run (e.g. on the GNPS public library of 500,569 spectra) and you need a per-filter accounting of removals/repairs to quantify repair-function impact or audit the cleaning run.

name: processing-report-generation-and-filter-impact-summarization
description: Use when running a matchms spectrum-cleaning pipeline (e.g. on a GNPS, MassBank, or MoNA .msp/.MGF/JSON library) and you need machine-readable provenance: a rerunnable YAML of all filter settings plus a per-filter impact report.

name: processing-report-interpreting-per-filter-spectrum-changes
description: Use when auditing or reproducing a matchms SpectrumProcessor/Pipeline cleaning run (e.g. on GNPS, MassBank, or MoNA libraries): you need to verify which filters ran in the fixed global order and how many spectra each filter removed or modified.

name: processing-time-metrics-computation
description: Use when a task requires quantifying computational plus manual effort of a semi-automated LC-MS library-building workflow and comparing it against a manual per-compound baseline to derive a fold-reduction metric.

name: processing-time-scaling-analysis
description: Use when evaluating whether TurboPutative's RESTful API workflow can handle a planned metabolomics annotation dataset, or when comparing end-to-end runtime scaling of a web-based annotation-processing pipeline across input sizes.

name: processor-pipeline-architecture-design
description: Use when raw LC–MS mzML files must be curated into a quality-controlled feature matrix and you need a reusable, versioned sequence of filtering/correction processors rather than ad-hoc scripts.

name: procrustes-coordinate-comparison-visualization
description: Use when two principal coordinates ordinations of the same samples (e.g., QIIME PCoA files from a procrustes comparison) must be visualized together, or when biplot taxa arrows/jackknifed beta diversity layers should be overlaid on a 3D PCoA plot.

name: procrustes-sample-distribution-comparison
description: Use when comparing imputed vs. original metabolomics data matrices to verify that supervised group-separation structure (e.g., case/control labels like rep(c(0,1), each=80)) was preserved after missing-value imputation.

name: profile-based-graphical-time-warping
description: Use when XCMS preprocessing leaves suspected misaligned feature groups whose RT drift differs across m/z bins or samples, and single per-sample warping functions cannot correct them.

name: profile-hmm-domain-alignment
description: Use when computing BiG-SCAPE's Domain Sequence Similarity (DSS) index, or when many antiSMASH-predicted domain sequences must be aligned per Pfam domain type against profile HMMs instead of running all-versus-all sequence alignment between BGC pairs.

name: profile-mode-hrms-data-handling
description: Use when raw profile-mode HRMS files (Waters UNIFI MSE/HDMSE exports or mzML) must be converted to a compact columnar format while retaining ion-mobility dimensions, and later queried, filtered or aggregated with Apache Arrow.

name: profile-mode-lc-hrms-data-processing
description: Use when raw mzXML/mzML LC-HRMS profile-mode data must be converted into fixed-size (32 scans x 128 m/z) standardized areas around every local maximum, prior to CNN peak classification.

name: profile-versus-centroid-mode-area-comparison
description: Use when a matched feature table with peak areas from two peak-picking tools (e.g. PeakBot and XCMS) is available and the goal is to quantify correlation (R2) and the systematic profile-versus-centroid area scaling factor.

name: profiler-metric-tie-verification
description: Use when two or more taxonomic profilers report an identical benchmarking score (e.g., UniFrac) on a sample and you need to determine whether the underlying taxonomic profiles actually differ at specific clades.

name: proforma-peptide-spectrum-annotation
description: Use when an MS/MS spectrum corresponds to a known peptide sequence and peaks must be labeled as fragment ions (e.g. a, b, y series, including modified residues such as oxidized methionine) for publication-quality figures.

name: proforma-peptidoform-parsing
description: Use when an MS/MS spectrum must be peak-annotated against a known peptide sequence supplied as a ProForma 2.0 string (optionally with PTMs), e.g. to build a fragment-annotation table for a USI-resolved spectrum.

name: progenesis-peak-table-import
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS pre-processing output is a Progenesis-format peak table CSV that must be joined with sample metadata (Injection, Sample_Code, Biological_Group) before applying mpactR filters.

name: programmatic-nmr-data-export
description: Use when a task requires programmatically retrieving a specific BMRB accession (e.g., BMRB entry 17074) and exporting its assigned per-atom chemical shift records into a structured tabular file for downstream analysis.

name: programmatic-pdf-report-generation
description: Use when tabulated MassQL query results (peak intensities per query per mzML file) need to be rendered into per-query visualization PDFs and summary csv tables for system suitability assessment of UHPLC-HRMS acquisitions.

name: progressive-module-ablation-training
description: Use when a multi-component representation module (e.g. Encoder + Channel Embedding + Channel Concatenation) needs a quantitative per-component contribution analysis on raw TIC-normalized mass spectrometry spectra.

name: project-json-genome-label-extraction
description: Use when PoDP project JSON (e.g., from the monthly Zenodo archive) must be parsed to enumerate genome entries by genome label and resolve their organism names from public genome identifiers.

name: prokaryotic-gene-prediction
description: Use when starting from assembled prokaryotic or metagenomic scaftigs (e.g. IDBA output) and gene coordinates/labels are needed downstream for operon, proximon, or promoter-based prediction.

name: prominence-based-peak-finding
description: Use when raw LC-MS ROI/mass-trace intensity arrays must be split into discrete chromatographic peak segments with edge boundaries, without smoothing biasing the reported peak shapes.

name: promoter-prediction-integration
description: Use when predicting operons from metagenomic or whole-genome shotgun data where scaftigs and gene predictions (.tab from Prodigal or MetaGeneMark) exist and promoter evidence is needed to delimit operon boundaries.

name: proportion-overlap-score-computation
description: Use when curating large batches of public METASPACE imaging mass spectrometry datasets and you must exclude non-centroided or noisy datasets via a pixel-overlap heuristic before model training or benchmarking.

name: prosit-predicted-spectrum-interpretation
description: Use when PSMs carry both an observed fragment-ion intensity vector and a Prosit/MS2PIP-predicted intensity vector, and you need a per-peptide confidence signal for immunopeptidomics-style rescoring.

name: prospective-retrospective-scenario-classification
description: Use when a metabolomics or lipidomics blood-sample stability question must be mapped to an app workflow: decide whether the user is planning a future sample collection or assessing already-collected (e.g. biobank) samples, and which search mode follows.

name: protein-fasta-kegg-annotation-mapping
description: Use when starting from an annotated protein .fasta file for a bacterial strain with no existing reconstruction and you need a draft GENRE that can be loaded into COBRApy for downstream flux analysis.

name: protein-hmm-alignment
description: Use when you need to assign Pfam-domain architecture to protein sequences — e.g., aligning representative BGC proteins against biosynthetic domain pHMMs before hierarchical clade clustering or feature-vector construction.

name: protein-identification-count-aggregation
description: Use when DIA raw files (.raw/.d/.wiff) have been searched with DIA-NN against a spectral library and you need per-file protein identification counts plus medians aggregated by instrument family (e.g., TripleTOF vs Orbitrap vs timsTOF Pro).

name: protein-inference-fdr-control
description: Use when spectra have been searched against a protein database and you need to infer proteins from peptide identifications and control false discovery rate before exporting novel protein-coding gene annotations.

name: protein-interaction-evidence-extraction
description: Use when the research question asks whether two specific proteins physically interact and the source text describes named assays (e.g. yeast two-hybrid, co-IP) with figure/supplement locators that must be tabulated per assay.

name: protein-interaction-network-seeding
description: Use when a patient's differentially abundant metabolites (DAMs) fail to directly enrich the causative gene's metabolite set, and you need network propagation over protein-protein interactions to recover candidate genes from metabolomic enrichment scores.

name: protein-metabolite-integrative-embedding-analysis
description: Use when you have a segmented single-cell feature matrix with per-cell protein marker intensities and metabolite intensities of very different dimensionality/variability (e.g., ~25 protein vs ~200 metabolic markers) and need a joint latent representation.

name: protein-nucleolar-compartment-proportion-measurement
description: Use when live-cell, two-color confocal time-lapse images (e.g., Rev-CFP/YFP-CRM1 in HeLa cells) must be converted into time-resolved proportions of each protein within a subnuclear compartment, or when a drug perturbation (e.

name: protein-peptide-mapping-confidence-scoring
description: Use when raw MSFragger/FragPipe PSM tables (e.g., searched against a proteome like Mus musculus at 1% protein FDR) must be filtered into a confident peptide/protein set for validating MSI peptide identifications.

name: protein-sequence-alignment-analogy-application
description: Use when aligning pairs of fragmentation (MS/MS) spectra that contain multiple delocalized structural differences, where cosine-based similarity fails and a biologically-meaningful alignment with p-value estimation is required.

name: protein-sequence-alignment-diamond
description: Use when the input is an annotated amino acid .fasta file (Type 1 input) and KEGG-based gene annotations are needed to seed a draft genome-scale metabolic network reconstruction.

name: protein-sequence-extraction-from-genbank
description: Use when you have antiSMASH/gutSMASH output directories in GenBank format and need the predicted gene-cluster protein sequences as input for MASH MinHash redundancy filtering or BiG-SCAPE GCF grouping in BiG-MAP.

name: protein-structure-superposition
description: Use when you have computed NMR structure ensembles (from NMRFx torsion-angle calculation on NEF constraint files) that need to be aligned and validated against experimentally confirmed PDB structures, or when aggregating per-protein quality statistics for comparison against published tables.

name: protein-wise-peptide-image-aggregation
description: Use when you have a filtered LC-MS/MS peptide list mapped to proteins and per-peptide m/z ion images from an imzML MSI dataset that must be summed gene-wise and overlaid on registered histology.

name: proteogenomics-novel-annotation-discovery
description: Use when you have large collections of public tandem MS spectra (e.g. tens of millions) and want to identify peptides supporting novel protein-coding gene annotations beyond an existing genome annotation such as GENCODE.

name: proteome-first-peptide-annotation
description: Use when you have large collections of unidentified MS/MS spectra (e.g. GLEAMS clusters) and want proteome-anchored de novo peptide assignments plus variant-enrichment evidence for single-mismatch predictions.

name: proteomeexchange-dataset-acquisition
description: Use when a protocol cites a ProteomeXchange identifier (e.g. PXD034932) or OSF/PRIDE link as the data source and the tandem mass spectra must be downloaded as MGF files before any spectral comparison.

name: proteomeexchange-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when a benchmark or reproduction task needs raw tandem mass spectra for a published study and the paper cites a ProteomeXchange/PRIDE identifier such as PXD034932, so the five serum LC-MS/MS datasets can be fetched before compareMS2.

name: proteomexchange-vendor-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when a benchmark or conversion study needs original vendor RAW files, and the article supplies ProteomeXchange/MetaboLights accession IDs (e.g. PXD021390, PXD018139, IPX0001509000, MTBLS2119, XCMS1197236) that must be fetched.

name: proteomic-benchmark-reproducibility
description: Use when reproducing or auditing the QC/FDR estimation of LC-MS feature alignment output — i.e., you have information_all.csv (pre-QC, target+decoy) and need to verify FDR <= 0.01 at the retained score cutoff or recompute decoy-based alignment FDR.

name: proteomic-metabolomic-benchmark-reproduction
description: Use when benchmarking peak-list alignment algorithms on LC-MS peak lists with known ground-truth alignments, or when reproducing the reported RANSAC vs Join aligner precision/recall comparison.

name: proteomic-quantification-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when comparing proteomics workflows (e.g., MaxQuant MBR vs DeepRTAlign alignment with MSFragger identification) on a benchmark mixture and you must show that identification gains preserve quantitative accuracy.

name: proteomics-benchmark-result-aggregation
description: Use when comparing peptide-level de novo sequencing performance of multiple tools (e.g., Casanovo vs PointNovo, DeepNovo, Novor) on a shared annotated MS/MS benchmark such as the nine-species dataset MassIVE MSV000090982.

name: proteomics-database-search-identification
description: Use when you have vendor .raw proteomics spectra (e.g. PXD021518, PXD023047) and need FDR-controlled peptide/spectrum identifications as ground truth for evaluating MS/MS clustering.

name: proteomics-dataset-file-subsampling
description: Use when benchmarking MS/MS clustering tools (MS-Cluster, Falcon) across dataset sizes: create random file-level subsamples at fixed fractions from a large qToF dataset such as MSV000081981.

name: proteomics-dataset-metadata-parsing
description: Use when a proteomics dataset has a ProteomeXchange/PRIDE identifier (e.g. PXD037527) and you need per-file counts partitioned by acquisition mode (DDA, WWA, DIA) and instrument platform (e.g. Orbitrap Astral, timsTOF Ultra, Orbitrap Exploris 480).

name: proteomics-dataset-subset-sampling
description: Use when evaluating the computational scalability (runtime, memory) of a spectrum clustering or search tool across progressively larger subsets of a mass spectrometry dataset.

name: proteomics-dda-dia-workflow-dispatch
description: Use when a large batch of raw LC-MS files carries mixed acquisition modes (DDA, DIA, or WWA) and metadata, and each file must be dispatched automatically to the matching search engine.

name: proteomics-fdr-controlled-search-evaluation
description: Use when converting spectrum-spectrum matches from an open modification spectral library search into confident identifications, e.g. estimating FDR via target–decoy decoys appended 1:1 and grouping SSMs by charge-normalized precursor mass difference before filtering.

name: proteomics-identification-mapping
description: Use when clustering quality of MS/MS spectral clustering must be quantified against known peptide identifications, e.g., sweeping HyperSpec parameters like HD quantization level Q or dimension D and assembling a metric table per parameter value.

name: proteomics-intensity-normalization
description: Use when a published metabolomics or proteomics feature intensity table lacks sufficient real QC samples and you need signal correction/normalization with simulated QC data, or when benchmarking linear vs nonlinear regression for correction.

name: proteomics-psm-label-pairing
description: Use when spectra have PSM peptide identifications (e.g., Mascot or MSGF+ results at 1% FDR) and you need positive/negative spectrum pairs to train or evaluate a spectral embedding on an independent dataset such as the phosphoproteomics PXD015943 study.

name: proteomics-qc-metrics-aggregation
description: Use when raw MS data files (e.g., Thermo Orbitrap or Bruker timsTOF output) have been transferred from an instrument control computer to a server, and you need an automated per-upload QC summary of identification counts.

name: proteomics-qc-sample-simulation
description: Use when a metabolomics or proteomics feature/sample intensity matrix lacks measured pooled-QC injections and drift correction/normalization still requires QC-reference signal profiles.

name: proteomics-raw-file-conversion
description: Use when starting from vendor RAW files (e.g. HEK293 data downloaded from PRIDE project PXD001468) that must be converted to MGF before open spectral library searching with ANN-SoLo.

name: proteomics-raw-file-conversion
description: Use when the input consists of vendor raw mass-spectrometry files (e.g. Thermo .raw downloaded from PRIDE) and a downstream clustering or search tool requires open peak list formats like MGF, mzML, or mzXML.

name: proteomics-repository-data-retrieval
description: Use when an analysis needs raw spectra or spectral libraries identified only by repository accession numbers (e.g. MassIVE MSV000078492, PRIDE PXD001468/PXD009861) and they must be downloaded and combined into a searchable library.

name: proteomics-repository-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when a downstream analysis (e.g. de novo sequencing with Novor, Casanovo, PointNovo) needs raw antibody MS/MS data in an open text format and the data must be fetched from PRIDE or MassIVE.

name: proteomics-visualization-panel-generation
description: Use when processed proteomics results (e.g., deposited dataset PXD037527 from DDA, DIA, or WWA acquisition on an Orbitrap Exploris 480) must be converted into figure panels and checked for concordance with a published manuscript figure.

name: proteowizard-msconvert-conversion
description: Use when raw vendor files (Thermo .raw, Agilent/Bruker .d) must be converted to open formats like mzML, mzXML, mz5 or mzMLb for downstream storage-size or access benchmarks against MZA.

name: proteowizard-msconvert-parameterization
description: Use when the input consists of vendor Thermo RAW LC-HRMS2 files (negative or positive ionization mode) that must be converted to open formats before MZmine processing or repository upload.

name: protocol-dependent-schema-validation
description: Use when a MESSES-extracted JSON must be checked against the Protocol Dependent Schema and a target deposition format (mwTab) before running the convert step.

name: protonated-molecular-ion-protomer-construction
description: Use when preparing a small molecule (<~205 Da in the benchmark) for CID-MS/MS spectrum prediction and all plausible protonation sites/protomers must be enumerated and optimized before running collision trajectories.

name: protonation-site-protomer-enumeration
description: Use when preparing a small molecule (<205 Da or larger) for CID-MS/MS spectrum prediction from structure alone, and the exact protonation site in ESI is unknown: enumerate every candidate protomer/tautomer at heteroatom sites and simulate each independently before comparing to the experimental.

name: prototype-metabolite-annotation
description: Use when non-targeted LC-MS/MS feature lists from dosed vs. blank biological matrices (e.g., mouse plasma, lung, urine, feces) must be annotated as prototypes or metabolites of a known herbal prototype component set.

name: proximon-operon-prediction
description: Use when you have scaffold/contig-level gene predictions (from Prodigal or MetaGeneMark) and need to cluster adjacent same-strand genes into proximons based on intergenic distance before operon prediction.

name: pscnn-inclusion-probability-prediction
description: Use when a single NMR mixture spectrum must be decomposed into its constituent compounds against a library of known compound NMR spectra, especially when chemical shift variation and peak overlapping complicate matching.

name: psd-eigenvalue-verification
description: Use when a similarity/co-clustering matrix must be certified as a kernel: after aggregating H re-sampled co-clustering matrices into a consensus matrix, check all eigenvalues are >= 0 before kernel learning.

name: pseudo-3d-nmr-series-peak-fitting
description: Use when a pseudo-3D NMR dataset (a series of 2D planes at varying gradient strength, relaxation delay, titration point, or time point) needs per-cross-peak intensities and decay-parameter fitting, especially with overlapping peaks.

name: pseudo-bulk-aggregation-of-single-cell-maldi-data
description: Use when single-cell MALDI-MS isotope tracing data (e.g. 13C-SpaceM anndata objects with per-cell isotopologue fractions M+0..M+16) must be collapsed per condition to compare with bulk LC-MS or to visualize condition-level shifts.

name: pseudo-bulk-differential-metabolite-expression
description: Use when a MALDI/imaging-MS spatial metabolomics dataset (e.g. imzML converted to a SpaMTP Seurat object) has been segmented into clusters (e.g. urothelium, lamina propria, muscle) and you need significantly differentially expressed m/z peaks between those clusters.

name: pseudo-bulk-pooling-of-spatial-metabolite-intensities
description: Use when you have an annotated m/z intensity matrix with tissue-cluster labels (e.g. urothelium, muscle, adventitial layer) and need to identify metabolite peaks that vary between spatial regions via differential expression testing.

name: pseudo-ground-truth-comparison-database-search
description: Use when evaluating de novo peptide sequencing tools on antibody MS/MS data and no authoritative reference sequences exist — a database search against the known antibody sequences provides the pseudo-ground-truth PSMs needed to compute precision, recall and error-type distributions.

name: pseudo-ground-truth-peptide-matching
description: Use when de novo sequencing predictions on antibody MS/MS data must be scored for accuracy or filtered against reference peptides from database search, e.g. to set confidence thresholds at 50% AA precision before ALPS assembly.

name: pseudo-lipid-header-construction
description: Use when an LMS-level (molecular species) intensity matrix must be decomposed into chain-level lipid building block rows for downstream LBB-level statistics or pathway analysis, preserving total sample signal.

name: pseudo-maldi-msi-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking a spatial-transcriptome/MALDI-MSI integration method and no real paired metabolome data exist — split features of a 10X Visium mouse-brain section into two pseudo-sections and perturb coordinates with Gaussian translation to mimic neighboring-section morphology.

name: pseudo-ms2-spectrum-reconstruction
description: Use when input is centroid-mode SWATH-DIA mzML with sequential variable-size MS2 windows (e.g., 10 windows, 1.0 m/z overlap, ~0.9 s cycle time) and pseudo-MS2 spectra must be reconstructed per MS1 feature.

name: pseudo-msms-fragment-library-matching
description: Use when annotating features from AIF LC–MS/MS data by ranking library candidates per feature using m/z error and fragment matching against pseudo-MS/MS spectra.

name: pseudo-msms-spectral-matching
description: Use when MS1-only data (mzML/mzXML/imzML or pseudo MS/MS .mgf) must be structurally annotated or annotation propagated across molecular networks via spectral similarity, as in MASST-style cross-matching.

name: pseudo-msms-spectrum-cleaning
description: Use when pseudo MS/MS spectra generated by ms1-id from MS1-only LC-MS data contain extra ion forms above the feature's precursor m/z and must be prepared for modified cosine molecular networking or library matching.

name: pseudo-msms-spectrum-generation
description: Use when input is MS1-only data — mzML/mzXML LC-MS runs or imzML imaging acquisitions — and structural (level 2/3) annotation requires pseudo MS/MS spectra built from correlated in-source fragments.

name: pseudo-msms-spectrum-generation-from-in-source-fragments
description: Use when input is MS1-only full-scan data (mzML, mzXML, or imzML) containing in-source fragments and the goal is structural (level 2/3) annotation without real MS/MS spectra — e.g. reanalysis of public repository LC-MS or MS imaging files.

name: pseudo-msms-spectrum-reconstruction-from-aif
description: Use when processing centroid-mode LC-MS AIF (DIA) chromatograms where the analyst needs a pseudo-MS/MS spectrum for a subset of features of interest, e.g. features reaching statistical significance in an untargeted metabolomics experiment.

name: pseudo-paired-omics-data-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating or benchmarking a spatial omics integration method (e.g. haCCA) that claims to outperform morphological alignment (STUtility, ICP) on data where no true shared spots exist, by building a pseudo-paired dataset with a known ground truth for label transfer.

name: pseudo-siamese-cnn-inference-on-nmr-spectra
description: Use when you have NMR spectral pairs of mixture components with chemical shift variation and need to identify mixture components, or to test how much ppm-level shift a trained pSCNN model tolerates.

name: pseudobulk-spectrum-construction
description: Use when analyzing MSI data with hundreds-to-thousands of peaks per pixel, where untargeted analysis of the full pixel-level mass spectrum is intractable and a per-pixel pooled spectrum is needed.

name: pseudoinverse-underdetermined-system-computation
description: Use when time-course relative-abundance metabolomics data must be converted into flux profiles for penalty calculation, and the stoichiometric system S·v = dx/dt is underdetermined without fluxomics measurements.

name: pseudotargeted-metabolomics-data-processing
description: Use when the input is a plant pseudotargeted LC-MS metabolomics abundance table (e.g. Arabidopsis mutant panel with mutant IDs mapped to metabolite columns) and the goal is data cleaning, metabolite annotation, or gene-mutant–metabolite association mining such as hub-metabolite WGCNA.

name: psm-false-discovery-rate-control
description: Use when PSMs from a spectral library or database search (e.g., ANN-SoLo, MS-GF+) must be filtered to a 1% FDR before counting identifications, propagating peptide labels, or building training resources.

name: psm-fdr-filtering
description: Use when MS/MS spectra (e.g. MGF files) must be converted into trusted peptide identifications via database search to serve as ground truth for evaluating de novo sequencing output, or whenever PSMs must be FDR-controlled.

name: psm-fdr-filtering
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS spectra (e.g. an mzML from a PRIDE/ProteomeXchange deposit) must be converted into a confident, FDR-controlled peptide identification list with retention times.

name: psm-fdr-filtering
description: Use when proteomics raw MS/MS data has been searched against a reference proteome with MS-GF+ and a target-decoy identified-PSM table filtered at 1% FDR is needed as an external evaluation reference for spectrum clustering.

name: psm-fdr-identification-mapping
description: Use when evaluating the purity of spectrum clustering results: you have per-spectrum cluster labels from a clustering tool and need to attach 1%-FDR PSM peptide identifications (e.g., from MS-GF+ via MassIVE RMSV000000091.3) to compute the fraction of incorrectly clustered spectra.

name: psm-peptide-protein-group-summarization
description: Use when raw MS files (e.g., from Orbitrap Astral, timsTOF Ultra, or Orbitrap Exploris 480) have been transferred to storage and you need an automated QC summary of identification counts per file.

name: psm-rescoring-literature-extraction
description: Use when a review or benchmark article reports multiple tool-specific PSM rescoring results (DDA/timsTOF conditions, predictor architectures, feature sets) that must be parsed into a comparable finding/tool/condition table.

name: psm-scoring-function-comparison
description: Use when selecting or validating a scoring function for peptide-spectrum matches in proteomic SIP data, or when quantifying how well each scoring function separates true matches from decoys as 13C labeling fraction varies across enrichment levels.

name: psm-target-decoy-classification
description: Use when unfiltered database-search PSMs need post-processing to improve identification sensitivity — e.g., immunopeptidomics or metaproteomics where features like MS²PIP fragment-intensity or DeepLC retention-time predictions must be folded into a final score.

name: pubchem-annotation-data-classification
description: Decision support for choosing between PUG-View and PUG-REST (or FTP/other backends) when retrieving PubChem annotation data, computed properties, bulk synonyms, or ExternalTableName tabular content.

name: pubchem-annotation-lookup
description: Use when a compound list for amanida meta-analysis contains inconsistent names/synonyms and each entry must be keyed to one unambiguous compound with PubChem CID, InChIKey, KEGG, ChEBI, HMDB, and DrugBank identifiers.

name: pubchem-annotation-retrieval
description: Use when you need programmatic access to the full annotation content of a PubChem record — e.g. a Compound Summary for CID 1983, a Substance record SID 46506142, or an Assay AID 1259416 — as JSON.

name: pubchem-api-throttling
description: Use when writing or calling a WebConverter that queries a webservice enforcing a programmatic access-rate limit (e.g. PubChem's ~5 requests/second), inside MSMetaEnhancer's asynchronous annotation loop.

name: pubchem-candidate-retrieval
description: Decision support for building candidate molecule sets from PubChem when annotating MS/MS or MSn spectra by in silico generated substructures, given only a precursor m/z (and optionally a known elemental composition) and no reference spectra.

name: pubchem-cid-and-exact-mass-retrieval
description: Use when processing an Agilent Unknowns Analysis GC-MS CSV (columns Component.RT, Component.Area, Base.Peak.MZ, File.Name, Compound.Name, Match.Factor) and per-compound PubChem CIDs, exact masses, and names are needed to build the spread database.

name: pubchem-cid-compound-linkage
description: Use when building SQL-format compound database entries from reviewed CCSfind results and each molecular formula entry needs a PubChem CID cross-reference alongside its DTCCS N2 value, EICs and full IM spectra.

name: pubchem-compound-database-processing
description: Use when you need to measure or justify database pruning for MS1 candidate retrieval in PubChem, e.g. comparing ppm-scale mass tolerances (--delta_mz) against absolute Da windows before annotation.

name: pubchem-compound-lookup
description: Use when GNPS (or similar) MS/MS library spectra lack InChIKey annotations but their metadata contains compound names, molecular formulas, and/or parent masses usable for compound lookup.

name: pubchem-compound-name-annotation-derivation
description: Use when a mass spectral library entry (e.g. from the GNPS public library) carries only a compound name in its annotation and lacks SMILES/InChI/InChIKey, and you want to repair rather than remove that spectrum.

name: pubchem-compound-retrieval
description: Use when an ion-mobility metabolomics workflow has a target m/z with an adduct type (e.g. [M+H]+, [M−H]−, [M+Na]+) and needs candidate structures from PubChem to predict and filter CCS values.

name: pubchem-database-candidate-retrieval
description: Use when ranking unknowns from HR-MS/MS spectra requires candidate structures from a large open compound database: you have a precursor m/z (e.g. 199.0428) and need PubChem candidates for fragmentation-based scoring.

name: pubchem-entrez-candidate-querying
description: Use when building an annotation-candidate list for a target analyte of known exact mass — e.g. gathering PubChem structures for downstream CCS prediction and ΔCCS filtering.

name: pubchem-fingerprint-extraction
description: Use when you need to convert normalized InChIKey identifiers from OMSL compound records (e.g., FragHub's standardized .mgf/.msp/.csv/.xml output for GNPS, MoNA, MassBank, MS-Dial) into PubChem fingerprint feature vectors for downstream dimensionality-reduction or chemical-space mapping.

name: pubchem-formula-based-candidate-querying
description: Use when annotating an LC-MS analyte whose molecular formula is known and candidate lists must be filtered before ranking candidates using fingerprint prediction methods like MetFID.

name: pubchem-formula-based-candidate-retrieval
description: Use when you have a measured precursor molecular formula plus an observed LC retention time and need to enumerate and prune isomeric candidate structures to reduce metabolite-annotation ambiguity.

name: pubchem-formula-reference-construction
description: Use when setting up or recalibrating FSA's reference formula list — e.g. rebuilding the CHONSP-only list of 928,369 PubChem formulas, or extending it to 2,613,203 formulas that include halogens (F, Cl, Br, I) for halogen-containing metabolite searches.

name: pubchem-heading-url-encoding
description: Use when you need one annotation type (identified by heading name) for all PubChem records via PUG-View, especially when the heading contains URL-incompatible characters (e.g. '/'), or when results must be paginated or filtered by source.

name: pubchem-interface-limitation-analysis
description: Use when designing a programmatic data-retrieval plan against PubChem and you need to decide whether a target data category (annotations, computed compound properties, bulk synonyms, ExternalTableName tables) is served by PUG-View, PUG-REST, both, or neither, and to identify fallback routes (FTP.

name: pubchem-kegg-profile-enrichment
description: Use when a GC-MS hit table (Component.RT, Component.Area, Base.Peak.MZ, File.Name, Compound.Name, Match.Factor) has yielded compound names and you need PubChem/KEGG traits, pathways, and source-coverage diagnostics for every published chemical.

name: pubchem-mass-based-candidate-querying
description: Use when an unannotated IM-MS feature (e.g. [M-H]- at m/z 155.0093) has an experimentally measured CCS and you need all plausible PubChem structures within a 10 ppm exact-mass window to filter by predicted ΔCCS.

name: pubchem-name-to-structure-lookup
description: Use when a metadata sheet for a plate-based small-molecule collection lacks a structure field (SMILES/InChI) for some rows but retains compound names, and standardized structures are needed downstream.

name: pubchem-patent-pubmed-count-retrieval
description: Use when performing MetFrag2.2 candidate ranking from HR-MS/MS spectra and reference/patent/literature counts must be fetched per candidate structure from PubChem and ChemSpider web services to enrich the score beyond in silico fragmentation alone.

name: pubchem-record-identifier-handling
description: Use when a task requires retrieving PubChem annotations for one specific record via PUG-View and you must correctly encode the record identifier (e.g., CID), the output format, and an optional heading parameter into a request URL.

name: pubchem-snapshot-candidate-list-processing
description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking candidate ranking on a fixed compound dataset against historical database snapshots, e.g. quantifying how PubChem growth (338 vs 2508 average candidates per compound) degrades MetFrag ranks.

name: pubchem-structure-linkage
description: Use when a curated biosynthetic gene cluster repository or compound annotation table needs link-outs to chemical structure or spectral databases, and compound name/structure fields are available for matching.

name: pubchem-structure-lookup-validation
description: Use when library spectra carry only a compound name (no SMILES), or when validating existing SMILES/InChI/InChIKey annotations against each other in a mass spectral library cleaning pipeline.

name: pubchem-title-name-matching
description: Use when a merged metabolomics dataset (e.g., 391 urinary asthma metabolites) has been assembled via InChIKeys and you must quantify name consistency against PubChem title names or estimate name-only merge failures.

name: public-data-deposit-retrieval
description: Use when a question asks how many PoDP projects match a List-tab keyword query (e.g., 'Streptomyces | Salinispora' → 18 projects) and you must retrieve the archived Zenodo JSON snapshot and filter it locally.

name: public-dataset-overdetection-screening
description: Use when curating propagated drug-analog MS/MS matches and needing to remove signals whose detection is too widespread across public metabolomics data to plausibly reflect real drug exposure.

name: public-lipidomics-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when the analysis target is a public lipidomics study identified by a Metabolomics Workbench study ID (e.g. ST001111) and you need to download it into R for inspection or reanalysis.

name: public-mass-spectrometry-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when an analysis must start from a large public untargeted metabolomics network (e.g., the ~8.4M-node GNPS/MassIVE molecular network with cosine-similarity edges) rather than locally acquired MS/MS files.

name: public-massive-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when a benchmark requires a real public metabolomics dataset: the article reanalyzes the group1_B* MS2 files of MSV000096589 (drug-incubated bacterial cultures) to test library annotation gains.

name: public-metabolomics-repository-querying
description: Use when you have an MS/MS feature from an animal model (e.g. phenylacetyl-carnitine at m/z 280.153) and want to find which public human/mouse/rat datasets detect it, across which tissues and disease states.

name: public-proteomics-data-retrieval
description: Use when a study specifies a public accession (PRIDE project, MassIVE reanalysis, or Zenodo DOI) and the analysis requires the underlying raw spectra, PSMs, or result files; e.g. clustering 25 million MS/MS spectra from PXD000561.

name: public-repository-data-harvesting-massive
description: Use when a repository-scale chemical annotation table over public tandem MS files is needed, i.e., when a downstream analysis requires a compound-by-file binary matrix rather than running new GNPS library search jobs.

name: publication-ready-figure-export
description: Use when a figure produced by a GraphBio module (heatmap, volcano, MA, ROC, chord, network, etc.) needs to be saved in a downloadable image format with publication-appropriate dimensions and resolution rather than only viewed on screen.

name: published-statistics-reproduction-verification
description: Use when a workflow requires validating that a live metabolomics database's coverage statistics (number of experimental and predicted metabolites) match the values reported in a publication.

name: pubmed-literature-factor-interpretation
description: Use when a MOFA (or, in BiomiX ≥2.5, DIABLO) integration has produced latent factors and you need to biologically interpret discriminant factors by linking their top contributing features to published literature, clinical variables, and pathways.

name: pubmed-query-construction
description: Use when a discriminant MOFA factor from a multi-omics integration has contributor feature lists (genes, metabolites, CpG probes) and you need literature evidence to interpret the factor via PubMed abstracts.

name: pug-view-bulk-annotation-retrieval
description: Use when you need one annotation type (e.g. Viscosity, LogP) for all PubChem records and the heading name is supplied with no record identifier in the request URL.

name: pug-view-request-url-construction
description: Use when programmatic access to PubChem annotation/summary data is needed — e.g., LCSS chemical-safety sections or historical record versions — rather than computed compound properties.

name: pug-view-url-construction
description: Use when a task requires programmatic retrieval of PubChem chemical annotations (e.g., solubility, LCSS, experimental properties) for one or a few record identifiers via PUG-View, and you need to formulate the correct REST request URL.

name: purine-metabolism-pathway-interpretation
description: Use when annotated LC-MS/MS feature tables (GNPS2 FBMN with ChemWalker propagation and SIRIUS annotations) need KEGG pathway assignment and cross-strain pathway comparison, e.g. testing whether purine metabolism is shared but with strain-specific intermediates.

name: putative-annotation-table-processing
description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics dataset contains massive numbers of putative annotation entries (e.g., hundreds of candidate metabolites) that must be classified by origin (peptides, drugs, nutrients, plants, etc.) or reduced in redundancy.

name: putative-identity-ranking-by-rt-error
description: Use when accurate-mass search (e.g., 10 ppm) returns multiple putative candidates for a feature's m/z and an experimentally acquired RT is available, so candidates must be ranked or filtered using predicted-vs-observed retention time error.

name: putative-incorporation-feature-detection
description: Use when an XCMS feature table has biologically equivalent unlabeled vs stable-isotope-labeled LC/MS sample classes (e.g., 12C vs 13C glucose) and you must flag features that are new or higher-intensity in labeled samples.

name: putative-label-flagging-statistics
description: Use when you have paired unlabeled/labeled replicate sample classes (e.g., 12C vs 13C glucose) in an XCMS xcmsSet and need to identify which features show isotopic enrichment before basepeak assignment or database querying.

name: putative-metabolite-annotation
description: Use when statistically significant LC-MS features (e.g. MB-VIP permutation p < 0.01) must be assigned putative metabolite identities by grouping them into structural clusters (m/z/RT) and matching to known adducts, isotopologues, and fragments in HMDB or literature.

name: putative-metabolite-annotation-msi-level-2

name: quantile-cutoff-variable-selection
description: Use when building an imputation evaluation benchmark that requires MNAR left-censored missingness injected into a scaled data matrix at controlled missing-proportion levels.

name: quantile-normalization-of-omics-matrices
description: Use when raw metabolite-sample matrices (e.g., plasma_breast_cancer.csv) show sample-to-sample distribution shifts before pathway transformation or machine learning.

name: quantile-normalization-of-sample-distributions
description: Use when an imputed metabolomics feature table (samples × metabolite features) shows sample-to-sample intensity distribution shifts to remove before statistical analysis, and simple per-sample scaling is insufficient.

name: quantile-rank-evaluation
description: Use when scoring how well a gene-ranking method (e.g., metPropagate, Exomiser, or a combined score) recovers a known causative gene, by testing whether it lands in the top 20th percentile of a patient's candidate gene list and comparing per-patient counts across methods.

name: quantitative-elemental-image-production
description: Reference for producing concentration-calibrated LA-ICP-MS images (e.g. 55Mn, 56Fe, 63Cu, 66Zn in tissue sections) when gelatin standards with known concentrations are available and raw vendor batch data must be turned into quantified images.

name: quantitative-ion-intensity-interpretation
description: Use when GC-CI-MS stable-isotope labeling data must be scored quantitatively — e.g., comparing [M+H]+ intensity across reagent gases or judging isotopologue detectability on QqQ SIM, narrow-window scan, qTOF, or Orbitrap platforms.

name: quantitative-msi-concentration-mapping
description: Use when centroided .imzML lipid imaging data must be converted from raw ion intensities to absolute concentrations (pmol/mm²), and class-specific internal standards were co-sprayed onto the tissue for calibration.

name: quantitative-nmr-fit-table-generation
description: Use when quantitative per-cross-peak parameters (amplitude, center frequency, width) or cross-peak-specific relaxation values from T1/T2 pseudo-3D series are needed from 2D NMR spectra, especially where peaks overlap.

name: quantitative-nmr-trueness-metric-compilation
description: Use when benchmarking quantitative NMR mixture analysis tools on spectra of graded difficulty (overlap, contaminants, low-field benchtop, lineshape distortion, peak shifts) and you need a per-experiment trueness gap table.

name: quantitative-peak-integration-review
description: Use when quantitative peak areas or concentrations for targeted small-molecule metabolites (SRM, MRM, or HRMS-extracted transitions) must be validated or corrected in Skyline before reporting, e.g. polarity-switched purine/pyrimidine panels, Biocrates p180 amino acids, or polyamine assays.

name: quantitative-results-reconciliation
description: Use when a deposited Skyline small-molecule document template and reference quantitative results exist and raw data from a different MS vendor (Agilent, Bruker, Shimadzu, Thermo vs. the original Sciex/Waters) must be shown to yield consistent quantitative values.

name: quantitative-structure-retention-relationship-modeling
description: Use when you need to predict reverse-phase LC-MS retention times from molecular structures (e.g., molfiles/SDF, PubChem numbers) or rank/filter putative annotations from accurate-mass search by predicted RT, and you have structural fingerprints as model inputs.

name: quantum-chemistry-ccs-computation
description: Use when you need to compute CCS values from SMILES structures for metabolites (or other small molecules) whose experimental CCS is unavailable, or when benchmarking in silico CCS against TWIMS-measured values for structural annotation.

name: quasi-molecular-ion-identification
description: Decision support for annotating ion species (adducts, neutral losses, cluster ions) in grouped LC/MS compound spectra and revealing quasi-molecular ions to reduce feature-list redundancy.

name: query-gene-guided-bgc-family-retrieval
