description: Use when a single anchor gene defines a BGC family of interest and GCF clustering (BiG-SCAPE distance cutoffs) has omitted fragmented or merged assemblies from the family; needs evolutionary ordering of related clusters.

name: questionnaire-item-missing-data-imputation
description: Use when a questionnaire item matrix (e.g., parent-rated ASEBA CBCL externalizing behavior items per child) contains missing entries that must be filled before downstream factor extraction such as multiple correspondence analysis.

name: queue-based-graph-traversal-identifier-filling
description: Use when a metabolite table (e.g. HMDB IDs) has sparse/empty identifier fields across databases (KEGG, PubChem, ChEBI, LIPID MAPS, METLIN) that must be resolved for pathway enrichment analysis.

name: queue-based-resolution-algorithm-implementation
description: Use when a metabolomics dataset contains sparse primary identifiers (e.g. HMDB, KEGG, PubChem) and you must map them to identifiers of other small-compound databases, resolving empty/ambiguous returns by exhaustive re-iteration.

name: quinolone-metabolite-annotation
description: Use when an untargeted LC-MS/MS dataset (e.g., GNPS-MassIVE MSV000083359) contains MS2 spectra from biological tissue plus microbial isolates and the goal is to recover a specific molecular family, such as Pseudomonas quinolones, and map its nodes to sample metadata.

name: quinonemethide-triterpene-annotation-retrieval
description: Use when an active extract's LC-MS/MS features are already annotated in the ENPKG knowledge graph and you need to recover known bioactive compounds (e.g. anti-T. cruzi activity in ChEMBL, target CHEMBL368) without re-isolation or re-screening.

name: r-backend-script-execution-for-metabolomics
description: Use when a metabolomics feature table (e.g., 113 metabolites x 234 CRC/polyp/healthy serum samples) must be processed through iMAP modules reproducibly via R scripts rather than the web interface, e.g., to rank metabolites by SVM importance.

name: r-based-metabolomics-data-processing
description: Use when raw Thermo Vanquish UHPLC / Orbitrap ID-X LC-HRMS runs have already been processed into MZmine 2.53 feature tables and you need to annotate candidate drug metabolites by comparing 0-hour preincubation and 24-hour postincubation samples in R.

name: r-based-nmr-data-processing
description: Use when processing 1D NMR spectra in R (peak picking, grouping, feature-matrix construction) or when peak groups look wrong and you need silhouette-based detection plus regroupR correction on a dataset like the wine spectra.

name: r-based-non-target-analysis-workflow-orchestration
description: Use when processing LC- or GC-HRMS mzML data for environmental non-target screening and you need one R-based pipeline covering feature extraction, blank/replicate/intensity filtering, and formula/compound annotation with swappable algorithms.

name: r-batch-workflow-execution
description: Use when a raw batch of LC-MS/MS MRM data files (mzML) must be transformed end-to-end into a processed quantitative report (peakinfo.xlsx) via a single scripted R entry point like process_batch().

name: r-bioconductor-lipidomics-workflow
description: Use when a lipidomics dataset (Skyline CSV export, numerical lipid-by-sample matrix, or Metabolomics Workbench study) needs QC, normalization, differential or multivariate analysis with lipid class/chain annotations in R.

name: r-bioconductor-metabolomics-preprocessing
description: Use when raw LC-MS profile files (e.g. mzXML) must be converted into XCMS peak-grouping objects with two bw settings before ncGTW misalignment detection can be run.

name: r-bioconductor-package-workflow
description: Use when an XCMS feature table (m/z, retention time, peak intensity) needs grouping into compound spectra and ion-species annotation to cut feature-list redundancy in untargeted metabolomics.

name: r-bioconductor-programming
description: Use when a computational pipeline must be implemented, installed, or benchmarked in R — e.g. reproducing NetGSA REHE vs REML runtime comparisons or assembling weighted, directed pathway adjacency matrices with prepareAdjMat.

name: r-caret-machine-learning-pipeline-construction
description: Use when you have a labeled feature matrix (e.g., expert Pass/Fail-labeled LC-MS peaks) and need to train, cross-validate, and statistically rank several caret classification algorithms across candidate feature sets.

name: r-chemometric-modeling
description: Use when processing a batch of GC×GC–MS samples where a feature has been detected in more than one sample and you need its second-dimension elution profile to vary per sample while its mass spectrum is fixed to a library spectrum.

name: r-cluster-analysis-scripting
description: Use when per-dataset cluster label vectors (possibly different K_m per dataset) must be summarised into a binary cluster-membership matrix before consensus/COCA-style integrative clustering.

name: r-csharp-system2-wrapper-interoperability
description: Use when an R package must read proprietary vendor binary formats (e.g. Thermo Fisher .raw Orbitrap files) for which no native R parser exists, by delegating queries to a vendor-provided .NET/C# API.

name: r-data-frame-aggregation
description: Use when a gene or metabolite pathway-annotation table carries a source-database label (KEGG, Reactome, HMDB, WikiPathways) and you must quantify how many analytes are unique to each database versus shared across all four.

name: r-data-frame-na-manipulation
description: Use when you have a complete (NA-free) scaled data matrix and need to simulate missing-not-at-random, left-censored values at controlled missing proportions (e.g., 0.1–0.8) for benchmarking imputation methods.

name: r-data-serialization
description: Use when an R workflow built with struct or structToolbox must be checkpointed or shared — e.g. a populated DatasetExperiment or a trained model sequence needs to be reloaded later without re-running preprocessing or training.

name: r-dataframe-wrangling
description: Use when you hold a UK Biobank NMR biomarker table output by remove_technical_variation() and need the 61 composite biomarkers and 81+76 ratios recovered from adjusted non-derived components rather than adjusted directly.

name: r-datatable-pipeline-orchestration
description: Reference for implementing chained R data-processing functions where the output of one stage (a data.table) feeds the next, e.g. building an LC-HRMS benchmark from raw mzML files.

name: r-dotnet-system2-interop-wrapping
description: Use when an R workflow must read spectra, TIC/XIC chromatograms, or file headers directly from Thermo Fisher .raw Orbitrap files without converting them to mzML, and a vendor API wrapper executable is or can be built.

name: r-function-implementation
description: Use when a lipid annotation column (e.g. an all_IsomerNames-style metadata column with multi-isomer entries) must be simplified into standard lipid nomenclature as a filter step in the SpaMTP refinement workflow.

name: r-geneset-pvalue-computation
description: Use when a metabolite-interacting gene set and a GWAS trait/disease subnetwork have already been generated (metGWAS 1.0 Modules 2 and 3) and you need the over-representation P-value of their overlap.

name: r-html-report-rendering
description: Use when a metaboprep object has completed the quality_control pipeline and you must produce an HTML disclosure report summarizing quality metrics, filtering steps, and batch-variable influence for a cohort.

name: r-kernel-jupyter-notebook-execution
description: Use when executing the Bioactive_Molecular_Networks Step 2 Jupyter notebook that computes Pearson correlation scores/p-values in R, or when Jupyter reports no R kernel available.

name: r-matrix-linear-algebra
description: Use when a PaIRKAT-style kernel machine association test needs a pathway's normalized Laplacian regularized via its eigenspectrum (τ=1) to dampen noisy graph components before building the kernel matrix, e.g. on KEGG metabolite pathway graphs.

name: r-metabolomics-package-workflow-execution
description: Use when metabolomics data must be processed and analyzed in R via the MInfer package, e.g. preparing conditions, generating covariance matrices (num_tp = 1), and calculating Jacobians of metabolite interactions.

name: r-metabolomics-scripting
description: Use when raw GC/MS chromatograms (e.g. GC-TOF MS plasma or gcspikelite spike-in data) must be deconvolved, aligned across samples, recovered for missing compounds, and identified by spectral library matching entirely within an R workflow.

name: r-object-serialization
description: Use when an R-based ML pipeline trains a model (e.g. a caret random forest on 80/20-split quality-score data) that must be persisted to disk and reused by a downstream processing function such as automRm::process_batch().

name: r-object-serialization-rds
description: Use when raw LC-MS samples have been pre-processed in xcms (peak picking, grouping, retention-time correction) and the quantitative feature matrix, feature annotations, and sample metadata must be combined into one coherent R object for downstream analysis or archiving.

name: r-package-batch-data-processing
description: Use when you have GC-CI-MS mzML files from 13C stable-isotope-labeling experiments and need to quantify isotopologue peak areas for derivatized metabolite formulas across a batch of samples.

name: r-package-biocmanager-installation
description: Use when a workflow requires the JPA R package or its xcms/MSnbase dependencies and they are not yet installed in the R environment (R >= 4.0.0).

name: r-package-catalogue-extraction
description: Use when building or updating a structured inventory of R packages for metabolomics, where each package must be attributed to a repository (CRAN, Bioconductor, GitHub) and a workflow step (data processing, biostatistics, annotation, pathway analysis).

name: r-package-data-handling
description: Use when a metabolite count data frame (e.g., c57_nos2KO_mouse_countDF) has KEGG compound numbers and you need per-metabolite compound class and subclass metadata attached before statistics or plotting.

name: r-package-data-ingestion
description: Use when importing targeted LC-MS peak-integrated tables into mzQuality: the input is a tab-delimited file (or SummarizedExperiment) with required columns aliquot, compound, area, type, injection_time, batch, compound_is and area_is that must be format-checked before QC.

name: r-package-data-normalization
description: Use when a metabolomics feature matrix (.csv, samples in rows, features in columns, batch levels in first column) shows samples clustering by batch (e.g. PCA groups by run order) and across-batch signal drift must be corrected and compared across statistical models.

name: r-package-data-pipeline-execution
description: Use when a task requires reproducing mzQuality's internal-standard recommendation in R from peak-integrated targeted LC-MS data, or validating that the recommended IS is the one minimizing QC-sample variability (RSDQC).

name: r-package-demo-dataset-handling
description: Use when a Lilikoi v2.0 analysis run needs a known-good metabolomics input and paired phenotype metadata, e.g. to demo or smoke-test PCA/t-SNE/SOV, feature selection, or classification modules before applying them to user data.

name: r-package-dependency-parsing
description: Use when a catalogue of R metabolomics packages (from CRAN, Bioconductor and GitHub) is available and you need to quantify how other packages depend on them, e.g. to reproduce a reverse-dependency network figure.

name: r-package-example-data-loading
description: Use when reproducing the RGCxGC vignette/MPCA workflow on the MTBLS579 MetaboLights dataset and you need the preprocessed 2D-TIC chromatograms already packaged as MTBLS.rda instead of re-importing raw NetCDF chromatograms.

name: r-package-example-data-processing
description: Use when a stable-isotope HRMS feature table (e.g., XCMS output) must be converted into isotopologue distributions with natural abundance correction for downstream INST-MFA or labeling time-course interpretation.

name: r-package-extdata-data-loading
description: Use when reproducing the EnrichMet runtime benchmark or any example pathway-enrichment run that requires the package's built-in 94-metabolite dataset and its summary-statistics table.

name: r-package-feature-selection-execution
description: Use when a metabolomics data matrix (samples × metabolites) with group labels needs automated feature selection — e.g., recovering a confirmed/rejected metabolite set like the 39-metabolite CRC serum signature — before building a predictive model.

name: r-package-function-export-and-example-data-execution
description: Use when a study plan requires invoking a specific exported R function from an installed package on the package's own example data to reproduce or validate a reported annotation outcome before applying the function to new data.

name: r-package-function-implementation
description: Use when a geoRge result object of labeled base-peak m/z values (s2 from basepeak_finder) must be mapped to putative metabolites in a database with explicit adduct annotations (e.g. -H, +Cl).

name: r-package-function-implementation
description: Use when reconstructing or re-implementing an R package function whose statistical mechanism must be validated against a synthetic fixture — here, a three-parameter MSI ion filter with null-signal segregation.

name: r-package-function-implementation
description: Use when writing, extending, or contributing a function to an R/Bioconductor package such as maplet, or when reconstructing one of its data-loading functions (e.g. MetaboLights or Metabolomics Workbench loaders) inside a reproducible pipeline.

name: r-package-function-reimplementation
description: Use when a pipeline step depends on an R package function whose internals must be reproduced locally — e.g. annotating LC-MS/MS features against HMDB V5.0 and LMSD with metID when metID itself cannot be installed or wrapped.

name: r-package-high-throughput-computation
description: Use when metabolomics normalization must run on large feature matrices (e.g. FAME: 8913 features, 618 runs, 9 batches) within practical wall-clock time, or when benchmarking method runtimes and parallel scaling across 1–6 compute cores.

name: r-package-metabolomics-workflow-execution
description: Use when running a personalized pathway-based metabolomics classification or prognosis pipeline in R on metabolite-level data that must be converted to pathway-level features.

name: r-package-metabolomics-workflow-execution
description: Use when raw LC-MS mzXML files (e.g., serial-diluted urine MTBLS2631) must be processed with JPA in R to count PP vs. MR features and compute a per-sample MS2-based feature rescue percentage.

name: r-package-normalization-pipeline-execution
description: Use when an unnormalized LC-MS metabolomics intensity matrix (rows = compounds, columns = samples) must be drift/batch-corrected via QC-based normalization, with diagnostic plots to verify performance.

name: r-package-pipeline-execution
description: Use when an LC-MS feature table must be processed through an R package's ordered pipeline functions (e.g. MS1 feature extraction, MS2 annotation, then ISF level 3→2→1 identification) rather than a single function call.

name: r-package-scripting
description: Use when the task requires reproducing or adapting a published R/Bioconductor package workflow by scripting its exported functions against bundled example data rather than reimplementing the method.

name: r-package-scripting-for-formula-annotation
description: Use when you need to assign elemental-composition (molecular formula) candidates to MS1 peaks from untargeted LC/HRMS files (mzXML/mzML/netCDF) at population scale using reproducible R scripts rather than GUI peak-picking tools.

name: r-package-storage-object-processing
description: Use when a previously started metScribeR analysis exists as a saved storage object (storage_object.RDS or storage_object_initial) and you need to continue peak review, run find_adduct_conflicts, or export the library without reprocessing mzML files.

name: r-package-timing-profiling
description: Use when benchmarking the run time of R-based metabolomics normalization methods across feature-count and sample-count scales, and you need wall-clock timings per method under fixed core allocations.

name: r-package-vignette-execution
description: Use when an R package (e.g. Aerith) ships an .Rmd vignette that demonstrates its core functions, and the goal is to execute that vignette to reproduce documented outputs such as simulated isotopic envelopes or PSM scoring examples.

name: r-package-vignette-reproduction
description: Use when validating an R package's documented behavior by executing its vignette workflow — specifically, confirming that TARDIS screening-mode EIC diagnostic plots (five EICs per image for QC runs) appear in the output folder before committing to full peak detection.

name: r-package-vignette-reproduction
description: Use when verifying an installed R package against its published vignette: you have the package name (e.g. GetFeatistics), its bundled mock/example data, and the vignette URL, and the goal is to reproduce the documented workflow rather than analyze new data.

name: r-package-workflow-execution
description: Use when reproducing a published R-package analysis from raw tabular data (e.g. log2-scaled metabolomics intensities with batch levels in the first column) into diagnostic plots (PCA, scree) plus per-sample coordinate CSVs.

name: r-package-workflow-execution
description: Use when an agent must run an R-based metabolomics pre-processing pipeline on an MS-DIAL feature abundance table plus sample annotation file, and reproduce documented filter counts (e.g. 548/604 kept after m/z filtering, 303/539 after CV-ratio filtering).

name: r-package-workflow-execution
description: Use when running an R-based LC/HRMS pipeline such as IDSL.IPA where a single workflow function consumes a parameter spreadsheet (xlsx) pointing at raw MS1 data and output directories.

name: r-package-workflow-execution
description: Use when reproducing or auditing KGMN subnetwork reconstruction from MetDNA2 output (e.g., the 06_visualization folder of Demo_MetDNA2_NIST_urine_pos) with the MetDNA2Vis/SpectraTools R packages.

name: r-package-workflow-scripting
description: Use when LC/GC-HRMS data must be processed end-to-end in R — feature finding, grouping, filtering, annotation — and you want to run or compare several algorithms under one consistent programmatic interface.

name: r-package-workflow-scripting
description: Use when peak-integrated dMRM metabolomics data (tab-delimited table with aliquot, compound, area, type, injection_time, batch columns) must be QC-assessed and batch-corrected via scripted R commands rather than vendor software.

name: r-pipeline-end-to-end-execution
description: Use when processing DDA mzXML files from pooled QC samples together with DIA mzXML files from individual biological samples and you need a single R script to extract features, rescue DDA-unique features, and annotate metabolites end-to-end.

name: r-python-dataframe-bridge-integration
description: Use when a Python-based metabolomics pipeline (pandas DataFrames) must call R statistical routines — e.g. running the multivariate ANOVA + Tukey post-hoc test on metabolite concentration tables in Viime.

name: r-runtime-and-memory-profiling
description: Use when benchmarking an R network-construction function (e.g. MetaNet's c_net_calculate) across a series of feature sizes to characterize runtime and memory scaling against stated performance targets.

name: r-s4-class-definition-with-struct-templates
description: Use when implementing a new statistical method as an R object from struct's class-based templates, e.g. a mean-centring or PCA model, so its inputs, outputs, and model_train/model_predict methods are standardized and pipeline-composable.

name: r-s4-object-data-structuring
description: Use when implementing or reconstructing an R Bioconductor workflow (e.g. DNEA) that must hold unnormalized peak intensity data, group labels, hyperparameters, and feature aggregation metadata in typed S4 objects with defined slots.

name: r-script-pipeline-execution
description: Use when a user has sentinel and proxy variant files plus a VEP output for molecular QTL loci and needs to run the ProGeM R script pipeline to prioritize candidate causal genes.

name: r-script-workflow-execution
description: Use when a script-based R tool must be executed on a batch of raw data files — e.g. converting vendor MSI-CE-MS files to mzML, filling an Excel parameter template, and running the project-file R script to automate preprocessing at scale.

name: r-scripting-for-enumeration-counting
description: Use when a metabolomic processing study requires exhaustively enumerating or counting candidate pipelines from stage-wise method sets — e.g., reproducing NOREVA's 5,904 (QCS), 48 (IS), and 1,968 (no-QCS/no-IS) workflow totals before performance assessment in S5.

name: r-shiny-dashboard-design
description: Use when building or adapting a Shiny dashboard that must display instrument quality metrics from mzML/mzXML/mzData files as they are acquired (or retrospectively), with database-mediated separation between file ingestion and web presentation.

name: r-spectra-package-spectra-processing
description: Use when untargeted MS2 .mzML features must be annotated by spectral matching against GNPS, HMDB, or MassBank, requiring threshold-based dereplication with cosine similarity scoring.

name: r-squared-goodness-of-fit-verification
description: Use when comparing quantification outputs from two MRM analysis tools (e.g. MRMPro vs. Skyline) across a common dilution/file series and you need a numeric goodness-of-fit (R-squared) check of peak area vs. concentration curves against reference thresholds.

name: r-statistical-function-implementation
description: Use when a paper defines a statistical test rule (e.g., a density-ratio FDR surface) that must be turned into a reusable R function and validated against reported rejection counts.

name: r-statistical-programming
description: Use when reconstructing or reproducing MetENP's R-based metabolite/pathway enrichment workflow, e.g. running hypergeometric metabolite class enrichment or sourcing MetENP analysis scripts in an R session.

name: r-statistical-programming
description: Use when categorical behavioral item data (e.g., parent-rated CBCL externalizing items) or paired omics matrices need unsupervised factor extraction and variance reporting inside a Nextflow-pipeline R environment.

name: r-summarizedexperiment-container-introspection
description: Use when you have a saved maplet pipeline container (.rds, read via readRDS) and need to recover what the pipeline did — function order, arguments, and per-step outputs — e.g. to auto-generate a report or audit reproducibility.

name: r-tree-multidimensional-feature-basketing
description: Use when replicate mzML-derived feature lists must be aligned across analytical runs where RT and m/z vary — or extended to 3D ion-mobility data where features must remain distinct if separated only by drift time/CCS.

name: r-web-tool-interactive-execution
description: Use when a published R/Shiny web tool must be run interactively (via its web URL or locally from GitHub) to generate simulated pooled-QC sample data from a feature/sample intensity matrix for correction and normalization.

name: r6-object-data-access
description: Use when an mpactR R6 object exists (after import_data) and you need to retrieve the raw or filtered Progenesis-format peak table, verify sample metadata columns, extract CV values from filter_cv, or compute group means.

name: r6-reference-semantics-data-updating
description: Use when chaining multiple mpactr filters (mispicked, group, cv, insource) on one imported Progenesis peak table and you must decide whether each filter mutates the mpactR object in place or leaves the original intact via copy_object.

name: r6-reference-semantics-feature-table-filtering
description: Use when building or reviewing an mpactr pipeline where successive filters (filter_mispicked_ions, filter_cv, filter_insource_ions, filter_group) must either mutate the shared R6 mpactr object in place or leave the original peak table untouched for downstream QC and comparison.

name: raichu-pathway-visualisation
description: Use when you have antiSMASH annotations for a PKS, NRPS, or hybrid PKS/NRPS BGC and need a module-resolution depiction of the biosynthetic pathway or the predicted end-product structure.

name: raised-cosine-apodization-filtering
description: Use when partitioning a 1D frequency-domain metabolomics NMR spectrum (ppm axis) into frequency bins inside SAND's adaptive binning stage, where each bin must be windowed at its edges to suppress spectral leakage prior to conversion to per-bin time-domain FIDs.

name: ramclustr-correlation-spectrum-assembly
description: Use when reconstructing an in-source fragment pseudo-MS/MS spectrum from centroided AIF LC–MS chromatograms processed with xcms/RAMClustR — e.g. when annotating isotopologues, adducts, or in-source fragments from AIF datasets where no targeted MS/MS acquisition exists.

name: random-baseline-simulation-for-site-localization
description: Decision support for benchmarking modification site-localization methods on MS/MS analog pairs, when top-1 accuracy would be mis and a proximity+ambiguity-balanced null baseline is needed.

name: random-chance-baseline-performance-evaluation
description: Use when a trained Pass/Fail or other binary classifier's test-set performance must be shown to exceed chance before it is trusted for real filtering decisions.

name: random-effects-heterogeneity-estimation
description: Use when the same gene pairs have Pearson correlation coefficients measured in multiple studies, each with its own sample size, and you need pooled fixed and random effects estimates with a heterogeneity statistic.

name: random-forest-classification
description: Use when metabolomics or proteomics feature tables (CSV features + target/metadata files, e.g. ST000284 or ST000336) need exploratory visualization and quality checks before statistical analysis.

name: random-forest-classifier-training
description: Use when you have experimental EI-MS or ESI-MS/MS spectra of labeled bitter/non-bitter compounds and need to train, select, and evaluate a Random Forest against XGBoost and a naive baseline.

name: random-forest-classifier-training
description: Use when a quality-controlled LC-MS feature table with sample metadata (e.g. age group, sex, brain region) is available and the goal is metabolome-informed phenotype prediction via a random forest with feature selection and ROC-AUC / cross-validation evaluation.

name: random-forest-classifier-training
description: Use when a labeled, high-dimensional lipid feature table (e.g., annotated by LipidIN, such as Supplementary Data 9 breast cancer cohorts) needs feature ranking and biomarker panel selection for patient-vs-healthy classification.

name: random-forest-classifier-training
description: Use when a metabolomics intensity matrix (e.g., 234 samples, 113 metabolites, 3 phenotype groups) must be split into train/test sets, modeled with random forest, and validated via ROC AUC against a held-out test set.

name: random-forest-classifier-tuning
description: Use when a binary-classification outcome is being predicted from pathway-transformed multi-omics abundance data (e.g. Su et al. COVID-19 mild vs moderate/severe metabolomics/proteomics scores) and an interpretable pathway-level model with feature selection is required.

name: random-forest-cross-validated-classification
description: Use when you need a supervised classification baseline on peak-aligned metabolomics feature tables (e.g., cosine-similarity or spectral-entropy similarity tables) with labeled bioactivity groups, reported as accuracy, precision, recall, F1, and ROC AUC.

name: random-forest-feature-importance-analysis
description: Use when a trained random forest (e.g. scikit-learn) combines multiple candidate-scoring features and you must determine which feature contributes most to ranking performance.

name: random-forest-feature-importance-extraction
description: Use when trained random forest regression models (e.g. per-metabolite models over CCLE multiomics features) need their feature importances ranked, top-k features extracted, and robustness-confidence scores computed.

name: random-forest-iterative-imputation
description: Use when an n x p matrix with 10–30% of values removed completely at random contains mixed variable types (continuous + categorical) and a non-parametric imputation is needed, or when nonlinear relations/complex interactions are suspected.

name: random-forest-learning-curve-analysis
description: Use when you must show how a spectral classifier's precision and recall change as the training set is grown from small to full size, e.g. to justify a data-collection effort or reproduce a published learning curve.

name: random-forest-matrix-completion
description: Use when a preprocessed LC-MS MetaboSet object still contains NA values in exprs and a statistically sound fill-in (random forest, per Kokla et al.) is needed before feature-wise tests or multivariate models.

name: random-forest-metabolomics-classification
description: Use when the analysis goal is supervised classification of metabolomics samples into class labels (e.g., treatment groups from a design file) and identification of which features differentiate those classes.

name: random-forest-missing-value-imputation
description: Use when a behavioral item matrix (e.g. ASEBA CBCL parent-rated externalizing items) contains missing item responses and a completed matrix is required before factor extraction such as multiple correspondence analysis.

name: random-forest-model-evaluation
description: Use when a metabolomics feature table with phenotype labels (e.g. CRC, polyp, healthy controls) needs supervised classification and validation of predictive performance via random forest OOB error rates.

name: random-forest-oob-error-estimation
description: Use when running missForest on data with artificially or naturally missing values and you need an imputation error estimate without holding out a test set, e.g. to report NRMSE/PFC reliability per simulation run.

name: random-forest-peak-quality-classification
description: Use when TARDIS-integrated targeted LC–MS peaks across biofluid matrices (stool, saliva, urine) have labeled quality classes and you need to reproduce or evaluate the RF 'Bad'-peak classifier and its variable-importance ranking.

name: random-forest-peak-quality-scoring
description: Use when peaks have already been detected from .mzML HRMS scans with mssmain.peak_pick and you need to filter out poor-quality features (peak splitting, insufficient scan numbers, high baseline noise) using a pre-trained ML model.

name: random-forest-regression-model-fitting
description: Use when a large-scale LC-MS metabolomics or proteomics feature table contains repeatedly injected pooled QC samples interleaved with biological samples (e.g. QC after every 5–8 injections) and per-feature intensities drift with injection order or vary across batches.

name: random-forest-regression-model-training
description: Use when you have matched multi-omics and metabolite abundance matrices across samples (e.g. CCLE cancer cell lines) and need cross-validated, per-target regression to identify which feature set most accurately predicts each metabolite.

name: random-forest-retention-time-prediction
description: Use when experimental MS1 features must be matched to MRN metabolites with a relative RT tolerance (30%) in addition to m/z, and only a subset of metabolites (seed annotations) have observed retention times to learn from.

name: random-forest-spectrum-pair-reranking
description: Use when building or reproducing an MS2Query-style analogue search pipeline where MS2Deepscore preselection must be re-ranked to place the analogue or exact match at the top.

name: random-forest-variable-importance-ranking
description: Use when a preprocessed, imputed LC-MS MetaboSet feature table with a class label (e.g. group column) is available and you need supervised, model-based identification of the most interesting molecular features rather than univariate feature-wise tests.

name: random-identifier-sampling
description: Use when you need to quantify how reliably MetaFetcheR resolves identifiers for a given compound database — e.g. to reproduce the Supplementary Tables S2-S6 quality test before trusting mapping output.

name: random-intercept-paired-data-modeling
description: Use when metabolomics data contain paired/repeated samples per subject (e.g. VAT and SAT lipid profiles from the same 59 CRC patients) and per-metabolite variance or outliers must be reduced using subject metadata.

name: random-matrix-theory-threshold-estimation
description: Use when you have a computed correlation matrix (e.g. occor.r from omics features) and must pick a defensible r_threshold for building a co-occurrence network instead of choosing a cutoff arbitrarily.

name: random-projection-locality-sensitive-hashing-implementation
description: Use when you need to tune or characterize the collision probability P(m,n)([x_i,x_j]) of an LSH scheme as a function of pair similarity, e.g. to pick (m,n) settings like (32,16), (64,32) or (32,32) for signal/noise classification.

name: random-projection-tree-index-construction
description: Use when performing open modification spectral library searching against large libraries (e.g. NIST human HCD or MassIVE-KB), where exhaustive shifted-dot-product comparison of every query against all library spectra is too slow and a limited candidate set suffices.

name: random-reaction-removal-perturbation
description: Use when you need to benchmark a gap-filling approach (e.g., COMMIT vs. individual gap filling) by injecting controlled corruption—randomly removed reactions—into published species models and scoring recovery by precision and recall.

name: random-value-imputation-with-minimum-scaling
description: Use when an MS-DIAL-derived feature abundance table in an untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics workflow contains NA values that must be filled before normalization or statistical testing, and low-abundance-proportional imputation is desired.

name: random-walk-annotation-propagation
description: Use when molecular networking (e.g. GNPS) leaves most nodes unannotated because NAP only propagates library matches to first neighbors, and you need walking probabilities for candidate structures not directly connected to any spectral match.

name: random-walk-runtime-profiling
description: Use when you need to benchmark runtime, memory and scalability of random-walk annotation propagation (e.g. ChemWalker vs NAP) on a molecular network benchmark, or validate performance claims about a propagation tool.

name: random-walk-seed-node-analysis
description: Use when annotating GNPS molecular networks where only ~10% of nodes have spectral library matches and you need annotations on nodes lacking a direct edge to any matched seed node.

name: randomised-baseline-auc-evaluation
description: Use when a newly trained link-scoring function (e.g. IOKR on paired MIBiG/GNPS BGC-spectrum data) must be compared to a randomised baseline to quantify whether it ranks true links above chance, especially at low top-n.

name: randomised-simulation-repetition-averaging
description: Use when an in-silico simulation involves randomisation — e.g. randomly removing compounds from the ORA background set or simulating metabolite misidentification — and stable mean-effect estimates with uncertainty are needed.

name: randomization-output-tabular-aggregation
description: Use when you have a randomized sample injection sequence with categorical dimensions (e.g. treatment, gender, age group) and need to quantify consecutive same-category runs to validate randomization behavior against published expectations.

name: randomized-replicate-selection-in-r
description: Use when planning multi-plate/multi-batch metabolomics acquisition and you need an embedded replicate layout (pooled QC, short within-row replicates, batch replicates) before running samples.

name: rank-aggregation-across-prioritization-tools
description: Use when candidate gene lists from Exomiser variant filtering and metPropagate LPA propagation are available and you suspect either single-tool ranking is biased — e.g. metPropagate over-ranking genes with many metabolic first-degree STRING neighbors.

name: rank-aggregation-evaluation
description: Use when a molecule has multiple query spectra (e.g. three collision-energy levels) and you must choose between consensus-spectrum annotation versus aggregating per-spectrum candidate rankings, with rank@1 as the decision metric.

name: rank-at-1-metric-comparison
description: Decision support for comparing candidate-ranking tools (e.g. JESTR vs SIRIUS vs CFM-ID) when each tool outputs a ranked candidate list per query spectrum and you need a single, interpretable top-1 accuracy figure plus a percent-improvement delta on matched test subsets.

name: rank-at-k-metric-computation
description: Reference for evaluating molecular retrieval models on MassSpecGym when you have per-query ranked candidate lists and need rank@1 scores under the by-mass and by-formula candidate conditions.

name: rank-based-ensemble-label-derivation
description: Use when training a ranking-based ensemble over spectral predictions and you need per-formula candidate sets, dMLP/dGNN labels, and SMAPE-derived importance weights from training data alone.

name: rank-based-gene-set-enrichment
description: Use when a paired spatial metabolomics–transcriptomics Seurat object has per-cluster differential metabolite (FindAllDEMs) and gene (DEG) results, and you need region-level pathway enrichment statistics.

name: rank-based-gsea-enrichment-of-ms-features
description: Use when you have a ranked list of LC-MS features (e.g. fold-change-ordered m/z peaks from high- vs low-glucose islet comparisons) with MS2-annotated compounds, and need pathway-level enrichment via mummichog's GSEA scoring in MetaboAnalystR.

name: rank-based-inverse-normal-transformation
description: Use when a metabolite abundance table (e.g., SMART narcotics or breast cancer demonstrative data) shows high variance and non-normally distributed metabolite abundances that would compromise downstream association or classification analysis.

name: rank-based-method-comparison
description: Use when several imputation/substitution methods (e.g., GSimp, HM, QRILC, kNN-TN) must be compared fairly on left-censored MNAR missing values across varying numbers of missing variables, and NRMSE values alone need aggregation into a single comparable metric.

name: rank-based-reproducibility-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking reproducibility methods on rank lists — specifically when generating synthetic replicate rank datasets to contrast the MaRR decision boundary with a parametric competitor's boundary on the rank plane.
tools: idr (copula mixture model, Li et al. 2011)

name: rank-correlation-analysis
description: Use when two chromatographic systems (or instruments) share measured molecules and you need to decide whether rank/order-based models can pool training data better than absolute retention-time models.

name: rank-correlation-statistics
description: Use when two chemical prioritization/ranking schemes (e.g., risk index vs. PrHQ) cover overlapping substances and you need to quantify whether their rank orders agree via a Pearson correlation coefficient.

name: rank-distribution-statistics
description: Use when you have ranked candidate lists (suspect rankings) from BAM for anchor-suspect pairs and need to measure ranking accuracy — e.g. average rank of the correct structure and the proportion ranked at position 1–5 — to benchmark GNN-SOM's site-of-metabolism ranking.

name: rank-distribution-visualization
description: Use when BAM has produced ranked candidate derivative lists for anchor–suspect pairs from a global molecular network and you need to quantify and visualize where the correct suspect lands in each ranking.

name: rank-frequency-summarization-of-annotations
description: Use when per-file formula annotation peaklists (from IDSL.IPA/IDSL.UFA) must be collapsed into one annotated aligned peak table, and formulas per peak must be ranked across all samples by detection frequency and median rank.

name: rank-reproducibility-verification-against-published-values
description: Use when a reimplementation or rerun of an aggregation/prioritization pipeline (GNPS + Sirius + ISDB-LOTUS indicators) must be validated by reproducing specific per-feature ranks reported in a publication.

name: rank-score-distribution-visualization
description: Use when you need to benchmark a retention-order predictor's generalizability across many independent RPLC datasets and present the rank-score distribution against a fingerprint baseline.

name: rank-statistic-null-distribution-derivation
description: Use when ranks of features (e.g. genes) are available from two or more independent replicate experiments and you need the theoretical null CDF of the maximum rank statistic to estimate pi1 or assign marginal FDRs to reproducible features.

name: rank-statistic-simulation-generation
description: Use when benchmarking a rank-based reproducibility method under realistic correlation decay — e.g., testing whether MaRR maintains FDR, power, and low bias when correlation between replicate pairs decreases with rank.

name: rank-sum-selection-scoring
description: Use when you have both feature-wise test results with FDR-adjusted p-values and multivariate model (e.g., RF 'mid' model) importance ranks, and you need one ordered shortlist of robust features for metabolite identification.

name: ranked-gene-list-overlap-analysis
description: Use when two reproducibility-assessment methods have each declared top-k reproducible transcripts from replicate rank lists and an external gold-standard subset (e.g., 1129 Taqman PCR transcripts) is available to judge which method's method-specific genes are more biologically relevant.

name: ranknet-pairwise-loss-implementation
description: Use when training a retention-order model from pairwise elution comparisons of molecular pairs rather than absolute RT regression, e.g. when chromatographic RTs are non-replicable across methods but relative elution orders are consistent.

name: ranknet-retention-prediction
description: Use when you need to retrain ROASMI on a user-defined RPLC reference set (e.g. dataset_83/dataset_84) and predict pair-wise retention scores to rank candidate molecules for small-molecule identification.

name: ranksvm-learning-curve-experiment
description: Use when quantifying how much labeled retention time data from the target chromatographic system is needed, or when comparing single-system training against training on all heterogeneous LC systems at varying target-data fractions.

name: ranksvm-pairwise-order-training
description: Use when you have retention time measurements from one or more LC systems and need to predict elution order from molecular structure, especially when retention times are on incomparable scales across systems so pairwise preferences within a system are the only consistent supervision.

name: ransac-alignment-performance-comparison
description: Decision support for choosing between RANSAC and Join aligners in MZmine when aligning peak lists across LC-MS fractions, especially when feature counts exceed thousands of rows and alignment quality must be quantified.

name: ransac-obi-warp-retention-time-coarse-registration
description: Use when aligning features across multiple LC-MS runs whose retention times drift nonlinearly (e.g. due to column temperature, aging, contamination) and a coarse RT correction is needed before feature matching.

name: ransac-peaklist-alignment
description: Use when multiple deisotoped peak lists from LC-MS runs must be aligned across samples to build a consistent feature table, especially when retention-time drift or non-linear sample variability degrades simpler join-based alignment.

name: ransac-robust-model-fitting
description: Use when aligning LC-MS peak lists across samples where spurious peak correspondences (outliers) would corrupt a single least-squares fit, and a robust random-sampling model fit with m/z and RT tolerance windows is needed.

name: ransac-robust-regression-alignment
description: Use when aligning LC-MS peak lists across sample batches with random non-linear RT deviations, and you must not tolerate spurious row correspondences (precision/recall critical).

name: ras-score-integration-into-model-bounds
description: Use when per-cell-line FPKM transcriptomics have been converted to normalized RAS scores and you must constrain a stoichiometric model's reaction bounds to build cell-relative models for flux sampling.

name: ras-score-normalization-across-cell-lines
description: Use when per-reaction RAS scores have been generated from GPR rules and an RNA-seq file (e.g. FPKM_Breast_forMarea.tsv) for multiple cell lines and must be rescaled — e.g. before imposing RAS constraints on cell-relative SBML models or running the RAS t-test.

name: rassp-element-constraint-filtering
description: Use when preparing large SMILES libraries (e.g. scraped ZINC20 lists) as input for RASSP synthetic spectra generation, and you must restrict compounds to those RASSP can convert into EI-MS spectra.

name: rassp-model-inference
description: Use when you have a list of small-molecule InChI/SMILES strings and need predicted EI mass spectra, or want to reproduce the RASSP forward prediction pipeline on sample molecules before downstream library matching.

name: rat-oral-ld50-prediction
description: Use when a large compiled chemical list (with QSAR-ready SMILES and CASRNs, e.g. from HExpMetDB) lacks acute mammalian toxicity values and rat oral LD50 predictions are needed for hazard or risk-prioritization.

name: ratio-of-change-curve-computation
description: Use when paired longitudinal DIA/DDA QC injections must be summarized as ratio-of-change curves around recorded maintenance-event timestamps to compare fault-detection sensitivity of DIA vs DDA metrics.

name: raw-file-batch-processing
description: Use when RAW files from public repositories (e.g., PRIDE accessions such as PXD060351) must be bulk-downloaded and annotated with acquisition metadata in structured TSV/CSV outputs without a GUI.

name: raw-file-chromatogram-extraction
description: Use when the input is a Thermo Fisher .raw file (e.g. 20181113_010_autoQC01.raw) and target XIC traces or full TIC/BPC are needed directly in R without converting to mzML via ProteoWizard.

name: raw-file-format-conversion-to-mzml
description: Use when processing newly written instrument raw files (e.g. Thermo RAW) that must be converted to mzML before feature extraction, QC metric computation, or dashboard reporting.

name: raw-file-metadata-extraction
description: Use when input is one or more Thermo Fisher .RAW files and the goal is to obtain structured, analysis-ready metadata (LC-MS method, scan headers, TIC, base-peak intensity, ion injection time, charge state) without running a database search — e.

name: raw-file-metadata-qc-signal-interpretation
description: Use when RAW files from nominally identical runs (e.g. Pierce HeLa Protein Digest Standard QC) must be compared for instrument performance using acquisition-side signals alone, before or instead of database search results.

name: raw-file-runtime-measurement
description: Use when benchmarking MetaXtract's per-RAW-file wall-clock runtime in the PRIDE Snakemake workflow, to reproduce or validate the ~40 s/file reference performance before scaling to large batches.

name: raw-file-scan-extraction
description: Use when the analysis goal is per-scan inspection of Thermo Orbitrap raw files — e.g. building a base-peak table for all MS1-level scans, reconstructing a scan index with MSOrder and rtinseconds, or extracting centroided m/z–intensity vectors for a specific scan — in R without converting to mzML.

name: raw-file-scan-header-extraction
description: Use when you have Thermo .RAW mass spectrometry files and need structured scan-header tables (TIC, Scan Start Time, Base Peak Intensity) for search-free QC, method troubleshooting, FAIR metadata export, or machine-learning feature extraction.

name: raw-file-scan-index-extraction
description: Use when the input is a Thermo Fisher Scientific Orbitrap .raw file (e.g., 20181113_010_autoQC01.raw) and you must enumerate, filter, or select scans (MS1-only or targeted MS2) before per-scan spectral extraction or PRM acquisition verification.

name: raw-file-spectral-data-extraction
description: Use when raw Thermo Fisher Orbitrap .raw files must be read directly in R for spectra, chromatograms, or XICs without prior conversion to mzML via ProteoWizard.

name: raw-file-spectrum-reader-invocation
description: Use when analysis needs spectral or chromatographic data read directly from a proprietary Thermo Orbitrap .raw file in R, without prior mzML conversion via ProteoWizard/MSconvert.

name: raw-file-to-mzml-format-conversion
description: Use when input acquisitions are proprietary Thermo .raw files and downstream tools (e.g. Asari) require .mzML; skip entirely when .mzML files are already provided.

name: raw-lc-ims-ms-frame-data-access
description: Use when raw Bruker .d TimsTOF PRO data (TDF format) must be read frame-by-frame in Python/C++ to obtain recorded mass axes, scans and intensities before any windowing or LSH computation.

name: raw-lcms-data-processing
description: Use when raw LC-MS metabolomics files must be converted into extracted metabolic feature lists and software-specific parameters (mzdiff, peak height, peak width) need to be measured from the data itself rather than left at vendor defaults.

name: raw-lcms-peak-picking
description: Use when starting from raw LC-MS/MS files of an untargeted metabolomics study (e.g. Metabolomics WorkBench ST002044) and you need unique MS/MS spectra in NIST .msp format per ESI+/ESI− mode as input for library search or fingerprint prediction.

name: raw-lcms-profile-parsing
description: Use when starting from raw LC-MS-based metabolomics data (e.g., vendor profile or centroided intensity profiles) and you need to construct the rank-based intensity sorted structure and zone of interest before any feature extraction program such as MS-DIAL, XCMS, MZmine, or OpenMS runs.

name: raw-mass-spectrometry-file-conversion
description: Use when you have instrument-vendor raw MS/MS files that must be converted to .mzXML/.mzML/.mgf before uploading to GNPS-MassIVE or submitting a molecular networking job.

name: raw-mass-spectrometry-file-conversion
description: Use when vendor RAW LC-HRMS2/MS2 DDA files (e.g., Thermo .RAW from plant-extract or metabolomics runs) must be converted to an open format (mzML/mzXML) before MZmine processing or repository upload.

name: raw-mass-spectrometry-file-import
description: Use when raw vendor LC-HRMS files must be converted into m/z and retention-time feature lists in MZmine (ADAP chromatogram builder) before 0-hour vs 24-hour differential metabolite detection.
tools: Thermo Scientific Orbitrap ID-X Tribrid mass spectrometer

name: raw-metabolomics-quality-control-filtering
description: Use when raw mzML/mzXML/CDF/qTOF, Orbitrap or FT-ICR data must be processed into a features table and QC filtering is needed to remove noise-inflating features before or after XCMS/MZmine2 centWave processing.

name: raw-ms-data-decoding-and-management
description: Use when starting an untargeted LC-MS metabolomics pipeline from raw vendor data — e.g. a 100+ GB Astral MS file or a Bruker timsTOF DDA-PASEF .d directory — and scans must be loaded once and reused across feature detection, gap filling, and alignment.

name: raw-ms-data-format-conversion
description: Use when raw MS data from LC, LC-IM-MS, or LC-SLIM-MS experiments is locked in Agilent '.d', Bruker TIMS, or Thermo '.raw' formats and downstream Python/R analysis needs cross-platform, lossless access to spectra arrays.

name: raw-ms-data-format-conversion
description: Use when raw vendor LC–MS acquisition files (Waters RAW) must be converted to open centroided mzML before loading into TidyMS/pyopenms for QC pipelines such as system conditioning or system suitability checks.

name: raw-ms-data-handling
description: Use when raw multidimensional LC-MS/LC-IM-MS data (e.g. .d, .raw) must be converted to an open format for feature engineering, machine learning, or visualization outside vendor Windows-bound software.

name: raw-ms-data-import
description: Use when the input consists of raw MS acquisition files (vendor-native directories/files or mzML) from infusion, LC-MS, LC-IMS-MS, DDA, or DIA experiments and the goal is to load them into PeakQC for automated omics-agnostic quality control.

name: raw-ms-data-ingestion-vendor-formats
description: Use when the input consists of raw, unconverted MS files in vendor formats (Agilent 'd', Thermo '.raw', Bruker 'd', or mzML) from LC-MS, LC-IMS-MS, DDA/DIA, or direct infusion acquisitions that need to enter an automated QC pipeline.

name: raw-msms-file-format-conversion
description: Use when raw MS/MS files from proteomics repositories (PRIDE, MassIVE) are vendor-proprietary and must be reformatted to an open, parseable format (MGF) before feeding de novo sequencing tools such as Novor.

name: raw-mzml-data-ingestion
description: Use when starting from raw LC-MS mzML files and an untargeted metabolomics feature table (rows = metabolic features, columns = samples) must be generated before any statistics or annotation, following the tidyMass CRC case-study workflow.

name: raw-profile-mode-spectra-processing
description: Use when raw profile-mode LC-IM-MS TOF spectra (e.g., Agilent MassHunter .d from an Agilent 6560 in All Ions mode) show poorly defined low-abundance peaks and smoothing must precede feature finding or lipid annotation.

name: raw-scan-extraction-with-rt-window
description: Use when a targeted GC-CI-MS stable-isotope-labelling run needs its raw scan data inspected at a specific compound's retention time — e.

name: raw-spectra-mzml-processing
description: Use when raw LC-MS spectra in centroid mzML format (e.g. from a Metabolomics Workbench deposit such as ST002796) need MS1 feature detection, alignment, gap filling and annotation before quantification or compound identification.

name: raw-spectra-noise-filtering-and-peak-alignment
description: Use when starting from raw instrument files (.mzML, .mzXML, .CDF) from untargeted metabolomics experiments and you need a cross-sample aligned features table rather than per-file peak lists.

name: raw-spectra-peaklist-extraction
description: Use when native Thermo RAW files must be converted into per-scan indexed MS1/MS2 peak-list Parquet files (m/z, intensity, and extended MS2 arrays) that can be joined to scan-header metadata by scan number.

name: raw-to-mzml-conversion
description: Use when input data are vendor-specific instrument raw files (e.g., .raw from Thermo instruments) that must be converted to open-source .mzML before MassQL queries or MassQLab workflows can be applied.

name: rawfilereader-api-invocation
description: Use when LC-MS input data is in Thermo vendor .raw format and needs to be ingested (or converted to .lcms) for visualization or scan-level extraction, e.g. enumerating scan number, retention time, and base peak intensity per scan.

name: rcdk-molecular-structure-parsing
description: Use when you need to generate predicted MS/MS fragment libraries from a list of SMILES structures — e.g. building substructure-to-fragment mappings for non-targeted PFAS annotation when no experimental MS/MS spectra exist for the candidates.

name: rclr-feature-transformation
description: Use when a sparse, zero-inflated metabolomics feature table (e.g. peak areas from GNPS/MassIVE deposits) must be made compositional-ready for PCA-based QC or PLS-DA classification across tissues, cohorts, and genotype/colonization groups.

name: rclr-log-ratio-transformation-of-peak-areas
description: Use when per-tissue untargeted metabolomics peak-area tables contain many zero-count features and the goal is compositional-aware ordination (e.g., PCA score plots) of samples across conditions.

name: rcpp-cpp-score-function-implementation
description: Use when scoring peptide-spectrum matches from SIP proteomics data against theoretical spectra, or when implementing high-performance spectral similarity scorers in C++ exposed to R via Rcpp.

name: rcpp-performance-implementation
description: Use when an existing pure-R metabolomics algorithm (e.g., DecoMetDIA-style SWATH-DIA EIC clustering and decomposition) is too slow at scale and the analysis goal is a fast, parallelized re-implementation behind an R interface.

name: rdata-object-loading
description: Use when running the metGWAS 1.0 R workflow: the workflow scripts require the two .RData objects (GWAS network and HMDB gene list) to be present in the R session before any hypergeometric comparison can run.

name: rdata-object-manipulation
description: Use when an analysis pipeline distributes its inputs/outputs as R .RData objects (e.g., GWASnetwork_discoverableGenesOnly_2021_10_14.RData) that must be loaded into R, filtered, and re-saved before downstream statistical comparison.

name: rdbe-constrained-fragment-formula-filtering
description: Use when annotating MS2 fragment peaks with chemical subformulae for a candidate molecular formula (e.g., MIST-CF pipeline) and you need a fast, tree-free peak-to-formula assignment instead of SIRIUS fragmentation tree computation.

name: rdf-knowledge-graph-construction
description: Use when per-sample LC-MS/MS DDA metabolomics results (feature tables, MS2 spectra, taxonomic metadata) must be integrated across datasets without RT-based feature alignment, e.g. merging batches acquired under different conditions into one queryable graph.

name: rdf-semantic-graph-navigation
description: Use when processed metabolomics features are already integrated as RDF (e.g. ENPKG .ttl in GraphDB) and you need to answer questions spanning annotations, taxonomy, and external knowledge bases like Wikidata, LOTUS or ChEMBL.

name: rdkit-ecfp-fingerprint-generation
description: Use when training data are NIST .msp MS/MS blocks with SMILES: or InChI: rows but no dash-separated Fingerprint: bit-location entries, and decoder targets must be derived for supervised fingerprint prediction.

name: rdkit-molecular-graph-manipulation
description: Use when you have derivatized sterol lipid structures (e.g., N-Me tagged C═C bonds) and need theoretical fragment-ion m/z and relative-intensity predictions for building an MS/MS spectral database.

name: rdkit-molecular-property-filtering
description: Use when a large enumerated set of derivative SMILES must be reduced by rule-based structural filters (ring count, drug-like property criteria, synthetic-accessibility score) before downstream spectrum prediction.

name: rdkit-molecular-scaffold-extraction
description: Use when you need to derive ground-truth core scaffolds from molecular SMILES/graphs (e.g., msgym.pkl, canopus.pkl) to build an oracle scaffold lookup table or to score scaffold retrieval accuracy (SPA) per dataset.

name: rdkit-molecular-similarity-computation
description: Use when a metabolomics annotation workflow must consolidate multiple top-scoring candidate structures per MS2 feature into a single final candidate using structural similarity comparisons rather than spectral scores alone.

name: rdkit-molecule-preprocessing
description: Use when a metabolite or chemical structure dataset arrives as raw SMILES strings that need cleanup (salt stripping, charge neutralization, element/token filtering) before training or evaluating a chemical language model.

name: rdkit-molecule-structure-validation
description: Use when a generative model (e.g. DiffMS discrete graph diffusion) has produced a pool of sampled molecules per spectrum and you must filter out invalid or disconnected structures before ranking or evaluation.

name: rdkit-smiles-parsing-and-descriptor-calculation
description: Use when raw database structures (SDF from ChEMBL 28/HMDB 5.0, NEIMS training splits from NIST 2017) must be converted to SMILES and filtered by mass, element composition, ionic state, and LogP before building a spectral library.

name: rdkit-structure-parsing
description: Use when library spectra carry structure annotations in more than one format (SMILES, InChI, InChIKey) that must be parsed, checked for mutual consistency, or repaired against a stored parent mass before downstream matching.

name: rdkit-substructure-matching
description: Use when assembling structurally related compound pairs (e.g., from MS/MS libraries) where the heavier compound must contain the lighter compound as a substructure and exactly one bond links the matched and unmatched atoms.

name: rdkit-substructure-search
description: Use when you have Spec2Mol-recommended SMILES and ground-truth structures from an MS/MS test set and need to quantify recovery of key substructures (scaffolds, functional groups) in the recommendations.

name: reactant-product-classification
description: Use when a pathway-metabolite association table (met_path) exists with KEGG reaction IDs and you must determine each metabolite's role (reactant vs product) in its reaction for mechanistic annotation.

name: reaction-activity-score-computation-from-gpr-rules
description: Use when transcriptomics data (e.g. an FPKM table per cell line) must be converted into per-reaction scores via the GPR rules of a specific metabolic model (ENGRO2, Recon3D subset) to feed downstream RAS integration, t-tests or concordance analysis.

name: reaction-activity-score-computation-from-transcriptomics
description: Use when you have a SBML metabolic model with GPR rules and a gene-level transcriptomics table (e.g. FPKM values for breast cancer cell lines) and need reaction-level expression scores for constraint-based flux analysis or multi-omics flux-regulation classification.

name: reaction-activity-score-statistical-testing
description: Use when comparing transcriptomics-derived RAS scores and sampled-flux FFD significance across sample pairs to identify reactions whose flux variation is concordant with substrate-availability (metabolic) versus enzyme-expression (transcriptional) regulation in a constraint-based model such as.

name: reaction-activity-score-statistics
description: Use when a concordance table of Cohen's kappa and Pearson correlation scores (RPS vs RAS, RPS vs FFD) exists and reactions with statistically significant RPS–FFD concordance must be identified after multiple-comparison correction.

name: reaction-based-pseudo-ms1-annotation
description: Use when you need to annotate untargeted LC-HRMS MS1 features from biotransformation assays (e.g., human liver S9 incubations of xenobiotics) using reaction rules and a curated metabolite database, rather than spectral-library 'bottom-up' matching.

name: reaction-based-pseudomolecular-candidate-filtering
description: Use when LC-HRMS feature tables from S9 incubation or cohort samples contain a known parent xenobiotic (e.g., a pesticide) and you must enumerate reaction-derived metabolite candidates via mass-shift rules before MS2 spectral-network annotation.

name: reaction-center-extraction
description: Use when you need a library of reaction-center-based biotransformation rules derived from a curated reaction dataset (e.g. RetroRules or KEGG reactions with SMILES-annotated metabolites) to drive rule-based derivative generation.

name: reaction-center-identification-on-anchor-molecule
description: Use when you have a known anchor molecule (SMILES) with high spectral similarity to an unknown suspect spectrum, a set of generated derivative candidates, and need to rank them by likely reaction-center likelihood.

name: reaction-center-substructure-matching
description: Use when you have an anchor molecule SMILES, a precursor mass difference to a suspect molecule, and a reaction dataset (RetroRules/KEGG/MetaCyc) from which biotransformation operators should be extracted and matched.

name: reaction-database-integration
description: Use when building a knowledge-layer metabolic reaction network for annotation propagation and the available reaction databases are too sparse (e.g., only ~14,974 reported reaction pairs) to connect metabolites.

name: reaction-evidence-source-categorization
description: Decision support for classifying newly inferred missing metabolic reactions (e.g. purine/pyrimidine gaps in Borrelia) into literature-backed versus homology-backed evidence categories.

name: reaction-feasibility-prediction
description: Use when you have Pickaxe-generated novel reactions in a MongoDB database and need to exclude reactions with unfavorable physiology or unlikely catalytic transformation before downstream pathway design or metabolomics annotation.

name: reaction-feasibility-scoring
description: Use when a Pickaxe-generated network expansion (e.g. EcoCyc <600 Da compounds, top 50 JN1224min rules, two generations) yields too many candidate compounds for unannotated metabolomics peaks and you need to prune reactions by enzymatic feasibility with DeepRFC.

name: reaction-matching-across-draft-reconstructions
description: Use when merging automatically generated draft GEMs from heterogeneous pipelines (KBase, CarveMe, RAVEN 2.0, AuReMe/Pathway Tools) whose metabolite/reaction/gene identifiers differ, to build a consensus reconstruction via MNXref translation and cosine-similarity reaction matching.

name: reaction-network-filtering
description: Use when a Pickaxe network expansion explodes (e.g. 13.7 M reactions from KEGG) and you must constrain compounds/reactions before the next generation, for metabolomics peak annotation, thermodynamic feasibility screening, or targeted compound discovery.

name: reaction-network-generation-benchmarking
description: Use when running multi-generation network expansions (e.g., 100-rule ruleset on YMDB) and you need to measure exponential compound/reaction growth and per-generation runtime to identify tractability limits.

name: reaction-network-on-the-fly-pruning
description: Use when running a Pickaxe/MINE-Database network expansion and you need to prune the growing network on-the-fly with property, similarity, metabolomics, or thermodynamics filters before the next rule-application generation.

name: reaction-pair-classification
description: Use when you must curate or expand a metabolic reaction network by predicting RP vs non-RP relationships between metabolites, and you have labeled reaction pairs from knowledge databases plus a defined held-out test set for ROC evaluation.

name: reaction-propensity-score-computation
description: Use when you need to predict how differences in substrate availability translate into differences in metabolic fluxes from intracellular metabolomics data and an irreversible stoichiometric model, to discriminate metabolically regulated reactions in INTEGRATE.

name: reaction-rule-based-network-expansion
description: Use when you need to enumerate predicted promiscuous-enzyme reactions and novel compounds from a compound database (KEGG, EcoCyc, YMDB) or metabolite list, e.g. for pathway design or metabolomics peak annotation.

name: reaction-rule-based-pathway-prediction
description: Use when you have a paired transcriptomic–metabolomic dataset and want to anticipate biosynthetic reaction steps and candidate enzymes de novo, without a known 'bait' compound or enzyme.

name: reaction-rule-mass-shift-annotation
description: Use when integrating unlabeled metabolome mass features with reaction-rule-based pathway prediction: you need neutral-mass candidates per m/z feature and mass shifts attached to RetroRules reaction rules before filtering by correlated enzymes.

name: reaction-rule-matching-validation
description: Use when validating that MEANtools' reaction-rule prediction (strict RetroRules dataset) anticipates known experimentally characterized biochemical reactions, or when reproducing reported coverage percentages and chi-square significance for reaction-rule databases.

name: reaction-rule-network-construction
description: Use when transcript-metabolite correlated mass-shift associations must be turned into a directed reaction network, resolved into per-substrate acyclic DAGs, and mined for the longest valid reaction path starting from each initial metabolite.

name: reaction-ruleset-selection-from-metacyc
description: Use when setting up a Pickaxe/MINE-Database network expansion and you must choose which reaction ruleset and rule subset (e.g., top 500 vs. top 50 JN1224min rules) to apply to a starting compound set.

name: reaction-thermodynamics-filtering
description: Use when a Pickaxe-generated reaction network contains too many chemically implausible reactions and you need to prune them by computed ΔG and DeepRFC feasibility predictions before downstream analysis or storage.

name: reaction-type-classification
description: Use when counting or categorizing BoM records by ReactionType in an annotated SDF dataset (e.g., EBoMD.sdf), or when verifying reported reaction-category frequencies such as η+η-forming Cyclization counts.

name: reaction-type-count-aggregation
description: Use when metabolite annotation tables carry BioTransformer reaction-type tags (oxidation, glucuronidation, hydrolysis, etc.) and you need detected-vs-predicted counts and detection fractions per biotransformation reaction, as for PharmMet DB Study ST003991.

name: reactive-moiety-target-filtering
description: Use when annotating MALDI-MSI or LC-MS features acquired with a derivatizing matrix (e.g. FMP-10), where the candidate target list must be restricted to metabolites containing moieties the matrix reacts with (e.g. phenolic hydroxyls, primary/secondary amines).

name: reactome-neo4j-pathway-query
description: Use when annotated peak features carry ChEBI (or KEGG COMPOUND) IDs and metabolite sets must be drawn from Reactome pathways for Homo sapiens or other supported species, rather than KEGG.

name: recalibrant-series-quality-evaluation
description: Use when a CHO-assigned molecular formula dataframe (from MFAssignCHO or MFAssign) is available and the mass spectrum shows systematic mass error that must be corrected via RecalList/Recal internal recalibration.

name: recall-at-k-benchmark-computation
description: Use when benchmarking MS/MS lipid annotation performance of two or more tools (e.g., LipidIN EQ+LCI vs. MS-DIAL/LipidMatch) on identical spectra, and you need a top-k ranked-candidate recall metric stratified by lipid subclass.

name: recall-at-k-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when comparing spectrum-identification methods on a query test set against a large spectral library and you need rank-based accuracy (recall@k) plus throughput (spectra/second) metrics.

name: recall-at-k-evaluation
description: Use when a query set of replicate mass spectra must be identified against a reference library and you need a rank-based accuracy metric (e.g. recall@10) to judge library augmentation or matching quality.

name: recall-at-k-metric-computation
description: Use when evaluating spectral library matching where the correct reference spectrum's rank must be summarized as recall@k (e.g., recall@10) over a query set, such as comparing forward vs bidirectional NEIMS prediction modes.

name: recall-comparison-visualization
description: Use when a ground-truth list of reported lipids (e.g. 2704 lipids from an aging-associated lipidome atlas) exists and you must quantify and plot how recall differs between spectral library levels or annotation backends.

name: recall-metric-evaluation
description: Use when you have precursor m/z-matched candidate lists plus orthogonal predictions (GNN-RT retention time, SigmaCCS CCS) and need to measure whether adding dimensions improves correct-molecule ranking via Recall@k.

name: recall-metric-evaluation-spectrum-identification
description: Use when benchmarking a spectrum-to-library identification method on measured EI-MS spectra and you must report recall@k accuracy and per-query matching time against a similarity-search baseline such as WCS.

name: recall-precision-benchmarking
description: Use when a spectral dereplication tool must be quantitatively evaluated against spectra of known compounds, e.g. computing rank-1 recall/precision at a stated FDR cutoff like 3%.

name: recall-tanimoto-curve-analysis
description: Use when comparing MS2 spectral library-search or analogue-search methods and you need a recall-versus-structural-similarity benchmark on a GNPS-derived analogues test set.

name: recall-true-positive-curve-analysis
description: Use when comparing spectral library search or ranking methods (e.g. MS2Query vs MS2Deepscore, cosine, modified cosine) on a labeled test set where each query has a known exact-match ground truth and you need a recall-vs-true-positive-rate benchmark.

name: recap-fragment-tree-construction
description: Use when you need to rank candidate molecule structures predicted from low-resolution MSn spectra (e.g., MS2 peaks from a miniaturized mass spectrometer) by comparing simulated SMILES fragment trees against experimental fragmentation trees.

name: reciprocal-best-hit-matching
description: Use when two ICA decompositions (e.g., of two cancer omics transcriptomic datasets) each yield metagene sk vectors and you need to assess component reproducibility by matching metagenes across the two decompositions.

name: recognition-accuracy-benchmarking-against-standard-ground-truth
description: Use when you need to quantify how accurately an ISF-detection pipeline assigns ISF levels to features, and you have metabolite-standard injections that provide known ISF relationships as ground truth.

name: recombination-foci-quantification
description: Use when reproducing or verifying reported per-nucleus recombination foci counts (GFP::RMH-1, GFP::MSH-5) across germline zones (2–4) for BTR-complex genotypes such as gfp::rmh-1, top-3-ZnF, and rmh-2; top-3-ZnF::ha from a Results text.

name: reconstruction-error-evaluation-mae
description: Use when training a joint multi-branch VAE (e.g., protein + metabolite single-cell features) and you need a quantitative reconstruction metric to validate the shared latent embedding against single-modality baselines.

name: reconstruction-fidelity-correlation-evaluation
description: Use when a deep-learning or subspace reconstruction of FT-ICR MSI transients must be quantitatively compared to standard FT or linear-subspace baselines on simulated data with known ground truth, via peak and spatial correlation scores.

name: reconstruction-quality-evaluation-vae
description: Use when a trained ConditionalVAESTSM (or similar CVAE) model must be scored on reconstruction of ST gene expression and SM mass-spectrometry intensity profiles, latent embedding quality, and modality fusion, e.g. during ablation or tool benchmarking.

name: record-version-parameter-encoding
description: Reference for retrieving historical versions of PubChem substance (SID) or assay (AID) records when the current annotation is insufficient and an earlier depositor-provided record version is needed.

name: recursive-derivative-enumeration-from-drug-template
description: Use when a GC/EI-MS analyte spectrum matches no reference library and you need to enumerate plausible derivatives of a known drug core to populate a searchable synthetic database.

name: recursive-feature-elimination-analysis
description: Use when you have trained CCSP 2.0 linear-kernel SVR models per adduct type ([M−H]−, [M+H]+, [M+Na]+) and want to know which of the 1613 Mordred descriptors RFE retained, or which descriptor classes drive CCS predictions.

name: recursive-feature-elimination-descriptor-selection
description: Use when you have a large 2D molecular descriptor matrix (e.g. 1613 Mordred descriptors for [M-H]-, [M+H]+ or [M+Na]+ ions) and need to shrink it to a compact SVR-performing subset via recursive feature elimination, stopping when RMSECV increases.

name: recursive-feature-elimination-model-simplification
description: Use when a high-dimensional descriptor matrix (e.g., 1613 Mordred descriptors) must be reduced to a minimal predictive feature subset for regression, with the stopping point determined by cross-validated RMSE rather than a fixed feature count.

name: recursive-mass-correction
description: Use when processing raw LC/HRMS files (e.g. Thermo 003.d, mzXML/mzML/netCDF) with IDSL.IPA and you need to quantify or prune false-positive chromatographic peaks produced by the initial peak-detection pass.

name: red-algae-comparative-genomics
description: Use when a newly sequenced or emerging model organism (e.g. red alga C. crispus) lacks a GSMN and you need to build one from genome annotation plus orthology to existing algal/plant networks, then compare its size to other algal GSMNs.

name: redu-metadata-aggregation-for-spectral-matches
description: Use when you have a set of MS/MS spectra that have already been batch-searched against public GNPS/MassIVE, Metabolomics Workbench, Metabolights, and NORMAN data via the Fast Search API, and you need to determine in which body sites (stool, blood, oral cavity, breast milk, urine, brain) and.

name: redu-metadata-stratification
description: Use when you have a table of matched public spectra (e.g. MASST hits for synthesized conjugated bile acids) with ReDU metadata attached and need to test whether detections are enriched in specific tissues (fecal vs blood/liver) or health phenotypes (IBD vs healthy).

name: reduced-collision-cross-section-correction
description: Use when calibrating single-field DTIMS-MS arrival times to CCS and calibrant and sample runs differ in pressure/temperature, requiring charge-state, reduced-mass, and P/T correction before linear fitting.

name: redundant-annotation-collapsing
description: Use when a metabolomics feature table contains many putative annotation rows per feature (e.g., the abbreviated table output by TurboPutative REname) and rows must be consolidated before manual comparison or pathway-level prioritization of metabolites.

name: redundant-annotation-filtering-by-score
description: Use when a feature table has been annotated against multiple metabolite databases in tidyMass/metID and duplicate or conflicting compound assignments must be reconciled before downstream statistical analysis.

name: redundant-annotation-grouping-by-abbreviated-name-and-mass
description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics annotation table contains many putative compound name variants for the same metabolite and redundant entries must be collapsed for downstream pathway analysis.

name: redundant-subcluster-removal
description: Use when a large collection of PRESTO-STAT statistical sub-clusters (e.g. 108,085 from 60,028 non-redundant antiSMASH-DB BGCs) must be de-replicated and organised into hierarchical sub-cluster families and clans.

name: reference-based-feature-alignment
