description: Use when per-sample detected feature tables (e.g., key 'A' from example_alignment.h5) show coordinate drift between LC-IMS-MS/MS samples and features must be matched across samples before downstream quantification.

name: reference-baseline-based-phase-correction
description: Use when processing a series of 1D-NMR metabolomics spectra (e.g. replicate mixtures or extract series in MetaboLabPy 0.9.66) where within-series phase consistency across replicates matters, or when comparing against apk0.noe/apk5/MNova phasing.

name: reference-bgc-dataset-integration
description: Use when constructing BGC sequence similarity networks from genome-mining output and you need experimentally characterized reference clusters (e.g. MIBiG) mixed into the same clustering run to assign functions to novel GCFs.

name: reference-causal-gene-set-matching
description: Use when you have prioritized candidate causal gene lists per sentinel variant and a curated reference set of true positive causal genes, and need per-component sensitivity (fraction of reference loci recovered) and specificity (true positives per candidate assignment).

name: reference-database-compound-identifier-mapping
description: Use when constructing or validating the compound input for HRMS prescreening: mapping compound names, formulas or SMILES (or precursor m/z for non-targets) to adduct-specific precursor ion masses and confirming identifiers against PubChemLite.

name: reference-database-name-matching
description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics compound/annotation list needs biological-origin labels (nutrient, drug, microbiota-dependent metabolite, natural product/plant, halogenated, peptide-like) derived purely from compound names and synonyms rather than from spectra or structures.

name: reference-database-row-count-validation
description: Use when reproducing or auditing the assembled experimental lipid CCS reference database (SQLite) and its row counts — per-mode (positive/negative), per-drift-tube-type (DTIM/TWIM/TIMS), and per-lipid-class coverage.

name: reference-deposit-comparison
description: Use when a locally regenerated preprocessed MS-file (e.g., a '_SR' saturation-repair output in Agilent .d profile mode) must be validated against the authors' deposited preprocessed file in a public deposit such as MassIVE MSV000087295.

name: reference-feature-list-matching
description: Use when multiple LC-HRMS data files from different metabolomics experiments must be matched to a reference feature list so corresponding ions across batches can be compared, e.g. after XCMS feature extraction with observed m/z and retention time shifts.

name: reference-free-multiple-profile-alignment
description: Use when XCMS peak grouping has flagged feature groups as misaligned (features whose RT drift differs across m/z bins or with run-order-dependent drift) and the per-sample corrected RTs must be replaced with compound-specific warping functions before re-grouping or peak-filling.

name: reference-gene-set-validation
description: Use when a candidate causal gene prioritization tool needs quantitative validation against expert-curated mQTL/pQTL reference gene assignments (e.g., Supplementary Table S1) to estimate sensitivity and specificity.

name: reference-ion-metric-comparison
description: Use when precursor-ion peak metrics have already been extracted and you need to package them as CSV reports and JPG/PDF figures that visualize each ion metric across a batch of MS runs for operator inspection.

name: reference-library-count-validation
description: Use when a GNPS GC-MS library search will be run against the freely available released reference library and the spectra/standards counts must be verified as 19,808 spectra for 19,708 standards before matching deconvoluted .mgf features.

name: reference-library-spectrum-matching
description: Use when a 1H NMR mixture spectrum must be decomposed into molar proportions of known library components (e.g., BCAAs leucine/isoleucine/valine), especially with overlapping, shifted, or distorted peaks.

name: reference-material-bias-assessment
description: Use when a quantification pipeline has been applied to a certified reference material (e.g., NIST SRM-1950) with known reference concentrations and you must report per-analyte percent bias and mean bias to validate the method.

name: reference-patent-count-scoring
description: Use when ranking tandem-MS candidate lists whose in silico fragmentation scores alone (HR-MS/MS only) leave the correct compound outside the Top 1, and reference/patent/retention metadata can be retrieved per candidate.

name: reference-pathway-to-organism-pathway-mapping
description: Use when reconstructing the functional level of a metabolic network from KEGG: you have an organism KEGG code (e.g. hsa, ptr) and need per-reference-pathway reaction sets for set/multiset comparison.

name: reference-sample-group-initialization
description: Use when you have per-sample extracted-ion chromatogram (EIC) peak lists (RT, intensity, FWHM) for MRM data plus estimated RT drifts, and need to seed alignment groups from a reference sample before cross-sample peak matching.

name: reference-sample-sum-scaling
description: Use when an uploaded metabolite concentration table (.csv or .xlsx) has per-sample totals that differ due to loading or volume differences, and consistent per-sample measurement values are needed before Viime's transformation, scaling, and PCA steps.

name: reference-specimen-qc-comparison
description: Use when a Rapid QC-MS run includes a reference specimen and a prior library of high-confidence RS annotations (.msp) exists, and you need to quantify current RT shifts and mass accuracy drift versus previous analyses.

name: reference-spectra-library-validation
description: Use when a curated reference spectral library is available and you need to demonstrate that a proposed spectral-networking scheme (e.g. MCN vs. conventional thresholded molecular networking) produces valid, structurally meaningful connections before applying it to untargeted data.

name: reference-spectrum-mplus-peak-extraction
description: Use when an analyte's GC/EI-MS spectrum matched no reference library entry and enumerated derivative candidates must be narrowed by molecular mass before spectrum/fingerprint similarity ranking.

name: reference-spectrum-selection
description: Use when a series of 1D-NMR spectra shows chemical-shift drift and MetaboLabPy's segmental alignment is about to be run on a user-selected spectral region, requiring a reference spectrum to be designated.

name: reference-standards-validation-analysis
description: Use when validating formula-annotation accuracy on authentic reference standards (e.g., the MSV000088661 dataset) and you need quantitative NEME (mDa) and isotopic profile cosine similarity (PCS %) metrics to compare against published benchmarks.

name: reference-table-regeneration-verification
description: Use when a paper publishes a scored/ranked table (e.g. Table 3 of MS2DECIDE) whose inputs (per-compound annotation indicators and the scoring function) are deposited in a public repo, and the goal is to reproduce and verify it.

name: reference-table-validation
description: Use when a paper claims a ranking result (e.g., one method placing 6 unreported compounds in the top 10 of a 95-compound library) and you must verify it by re-deriving the rank table from primary tool outputs.

name: reference-value-verification-of-model-predictions
description: Use when a published model yields concrete numeric reference values (e.g., 20%-change stability time points in EDTA/LiHep/serum) that a recomputation from source data must reproduce, or when validating that a re-implementation matches reported anchors.

name: reference-vector-normalization
description: Use when metabolomics samples differ in total abundance due to physical quantity differences (e.g., tissue mass, sample volume) and a per-sample reference vector such as weight or volume is available to normalize against.

name: reference-vs-target-ion-list-preparation
description: Use when aligning untargeted LC-HRMS metabolomics batches where the same metabolites may be detected as different ion species (e.g., A1 vs. A2 adducts) and features must be matched across m/z and retention time shifts.

name: refmet-metabolite-class-counting
description: Use when a metabolomics dataset already has RefMet class annotations and per-metabolite significance calls, and you need per-class (main/sub/super) enrichment p-values and enrichment scores.

name: refmet-nomenclature-conversion
description: Use when metabolite feature names from a Metabolomics Workbench study (or custom dataset) are unstandardized and must be normalized via RefMet before mapping to KEGG compound IDs and computing enrichment.

name: refmet-nomenclature-mapping
description: Use when lipid identifiers in a processed lipidomic table are RefMet-compliant textual names (e.g. 'FA(18:3)', 'octadecatrienoic acid') rather than the generic 'CLASS N:N/M:M' format, and you need per-residue carbon:double-bond strings.

name: refmet-nomenclature-mapping
description: Use when metabolite identifiers in a study's metabolite table are non-standard (free-text names) and must be harmonized to RefMet and KEGG compound IDs before counting significant metabolites or mapping to KEGG pathways.

name: refscore-based-candidate-filtering
description: Use when a mass deviation query against PubChem (e.g., 10 ppm with 0.002 Da absolute minimum) returns very large candidate sets (challenges 1, 2, and 14) for MAGMa penalty-score ranking, and candidate-list reduction by compound reliability is desired.

name: refseq-ensembl-transcript-set-concordance
description: Decision support for choosing annotation tools or transcript sources: when you must know which transcripts ANNOVAR, SnpEff, or VEP actually cover on RefSeq vs Ensembl, and how much their transcript identifier sets overlap.

name: refseq-gene-annotation-integration
description: Use when building a species-specific metabolic network for an organism whose KEGG map lacks complete reaction coverage, by combining NCBI-RefSeq gene annotations with the 66 base KEGG pathway layouts shipped in MINNO.

name: regex-based-column-value-validation
description: Use when parsing mwTab METABOLITES sections and needing to detect standardized fields (e.g. pubchem_id, inchi_key, kegg_id, hmdb_id, retention_time) regardless of column-name variants or value formats.

name: regex-based-non-lipid-name-normalization
description: Use when a putative metabolite annotation table contains compound names that fail lipid parsing (Goslin) but still need standardized abbreviations so that redundant or equivalent entries can be collapsed.

name: region-specific-lipid-differential-analysis
description: Use when you have a registered 3D MSI volume with propagated anatomical atlas labels and need region-specific lipid enrichment tables (e.g. myelin lipids elevated in corpus callosum) from mass-spectrometry imaging data.

name: registration-resolution-comparison-analysis
description: Use when an MSI composite/cluster image must be resampled to H&E image dimensions for co-registration and the interpolation algorithm choice (nearest, bilinear, bicubic, Lanczos) must be evaluated or justified.

name: regression-adjusted-r2-batch-association-scoring
description: Use when a log2-scaled metabolomics matrix (samples as rows, batch labels in the first column) has been corrected by multiple batch-effect models and you need a quantitative, comparable metric of residual metabolite-vs-batch association to select the model.

name: regression-based-dataset-correction-normalization
description: Use when a metabolomics or proteomics feature/sample intensity matrix lacks actual pooled-QC samples and you need simulated QC data to perform regression-based correction and normalization of the dataset.

name: regression-based-ion-filtering
description: Use when you have an MZmine full-scan MS1 feature table (.

name: regression-coefficient-reporting
description: Use when a fitted metabolite-pathway regression in Lilikoi v2.0 must be documented as a coefficient table with significance calls (P < 0.05) for metabolites mapped to a selected pathway.

name: regression-coefficient-verification
description: Use when reproducing a published linear calibration/regression whose reported coefficients, slope/intercept, and R-squared must be re-derived from raw-derived tabular data and compared against stated values.

name: regression-error-metrics-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating a retention time prediction model's test-set performance in seconds against experimental LC retention times, e.g. SMRT benchmark splits or transfer-learning datasets.

name: regression-error-metrics-evaluation
description: Use when trained regressors (e.g., RT prediction from molecular descriptors) must be validated on a held-out test set and compared via RMSE, R2, MAE, and an error-within-threshold fraction.

name: regression-error-metrics-evaluation
description: Use when a trained regression model (e.g., CCS or HILIC RT prediction from one-hot lipid class/fatty acid/adduct features) must be scored and its error metrics verified against published MAE/MDAE/RMSE/MDRE values.

name: regression-method-performance-comparison
description: Use when simulated or pooled QC samples must be applied for signal correction and normalization of a metabolomics or proteomics dataset, and the goal is to decide whether a nonlinear regressor outperforms linear ones.

name: regression-metric-evaluation-r2-mae
description: Use when comparing regression model variants (e.g. 3DMolMS-TL vs a from-scratch model vs ALLCCS/DeepCCS baselines) on held-out experimental CCS measurements, where performance must be quantified with R² and MAE rather than spectral cosine similarity.

name: regression-metrics-computation
description: Use when scoring trained CCS prediction models (SigmaCCS, GraphCCS, Mol2CCS) on test-split parquet files and you need R2, RMSE, and MRE tabulated per model and per database (CCSBase, METLIN-CCS, or combined).

name: regression-model-selection-qc-correction
description: Use when designing a QC-based signal correction pipeline and needing to choose which regression algorithm should model signal drift from serially injected QC samples across candidate models.

name: regression-model-summary-interpretation
description: Use when a GetFeatistics workflow has produced regression-model summary tables (e.g. summary_regression_models from get_targeted_elaboration, or fixed-effects/mixed-effects/Tobit model output) and they must be read, validated, or reported.

name: regression-model-training-validation
description: Use when a clustered HRMS feature table from a dilution/mixing experiment (e.g., roadway runoff diluted into other water samples) must be turned into a predictive regression model for source tracking and apportionment of unknown mixtures.

name: regression-model-validation-metrics
description: Use when scoring an SVR or similar regression model's predictive accuracy with MRE, RMSE and R2 under cross-validation and test-set validation, and checking per-adduct median relative errors against a ≤2% target.

name: regression-performance-metric-computation
description: Decision support for comparing predicted CCS values against experimental references across training regimes (train-METLIN-test-METLIN, train-CCSBase-test-CCSBase, cross-dataset), and for testing whether a confidence-model filter improves error metrics.

name: regression-r2-evaluation
description: Use when comparing a fine-tuned regression model against a baseline across many small external datasets and you need a distribution of R2 scores (not a single point estimate) plus a stability criterion, as in RT-Transformer transfer to 41 PredRet datasets.

name: regression-slope-correlation-analysis
description: Use when quantification estimates (e.g. deconvoluted 1D NMR peak tables) must be judged against known ground-truth concentrations on simulated or spiked datasets, using slope k and Pearson correlation as accuracy metrics.

name: regressor-ensemble-blending
description: Use when several base regressors have been trained on molecular fingerprints/descriptors for RT prediction and you need a stacked 'blender' that combines their predictions to minimize median absolute error under nested CV.

name: regular-expression-compound-classification
description: Use when a putative-annotation compound list from untargeted metabolomics needs origin labels (nutrient, drug, MDM, natural product/plant) via reference-list matching plus regex rules, as in Tagger.

name: regularization-coefficient-ablation-study
description: Use when you need to attribute normalization performance to individual components of a multi-term adversarial loss (e.g. RALPS's d_lambda, g_lambda, v_lambda) via scenario-based ablation with fixed shared hyperparameters.

name: regularization-effect-quantification
description: Use when you need to quantify the embedding-space discrimination effect of JESTR's candidate-based regularization — i.e. measure whether candidate regularization reduces average target-candidate cosine similarity in a joint embedding space.

name: regularization-parameter-edge-weighting
description: Use when estimating a DNEA partial-correlation network for two experimental metabolomics groups and you need per-edge regularization weighting derived from stability-selection probabilities rather than a single global lambda.

name: regularized-normalized-laplacian-standardization
description: Use when a pathway's connectivity is sparse or disjoint and you need a regularized graph representation for a kernel machine score test on metabolomics associations.

name: regularized-regression-model-fitting
description: Use when a targeted metabolomics feature table (e.g. ST000284 three-group study) with class metadata must be fitted with LASSO/ridge/elastic-net classifiers and accuracy must be measured on held-out test samples, not the full dataset.

name: relational-database-schema-migration
description: Use when a repository's data currently lives in static HTML pages or flat files and must be migrated into a relational schema (PostgreSQL) with an API layer so downstream clients can query/filter entries by metadata.

name: relative-abundance-comparison-across-profilers
description: Use when benchmarking CAMI-style taxonomic profiles where single-value metrics (F1 score, L1 norm, UniFrac) look equivalent across profilers, and you need to see which clades at class/phylum rank drive abundance differences versus ground truth.

name: relative-abundance-normalization
description: Use when comparing raw taxonomic profiler profile files (e.g., CAMI profile_submissions and gold-standard profiles) whose relative abundances must be recomputed against the NCBI taxdump before ranking tools by error metrics like the L1 norm.

name: relative-abundance-threshold-background-removal
description: Use when a Progenesis-format LC-MS/MS peak table includes solvent blank or media blank sample groups and features overrepresented in those blanks (e.g. carryover) must be identified and removed before downstream analysis.

name: relative-abundance-time-course-data-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking an inference method like MetaboPAC that needs ground-truth absolute concentrations — simulate relative-abundance time-course GC-MS-style data from a known metabolic model with controlled noise, sampling frequency, and response-factor distributions.

name: relative-betweenness-normalization
description: Use when building a pathway-metabolite interaction network from significant metabolites and you need to rank hub metabolites (e.g. pyruvate, pyruvic acid, arachidonic acid) by normalized centrality rather than raw betweenness values.

name: relative-error-accuracy-comparison
description: Decision support for choosing between retention-time prediction models on an LC-MS small-molecule dataset when the metrics of interest are mean and median relative error and a head-to-head accuracy ranking is needed.

name: relative-error-concentration-assessment
description: Use when estimated mixture proportions (e.g. πi from Magnetstein's optimal-transport deconvolution) must be scored against gravimetrically known ground-truth composition, or when comparing quantifiers like Magnetstein, MANIQ, and ACD/TP on the same mixture.

name: relative-error-metrics-computation
description: Use when evaluating predicted vs. measured retention times from a chromatographic RT-prediction model (e.g. GNN-RT), to quantify accuracy as mean/median relative error.

name: relative-increase-computation
description: Use when replicate-level LC-IM-MS MS1 feature lists exist for two conditions (original vs PreProcessor-smoothed) and the goal is to quantify a relative percentage gain in features consistently detected across 3 replicates, e.g. the 70.7% smoothing increase for NIST SRM 1950 plasma.

name: relative-intensity-noise-thresholding
description: Use when a raw MS/MS spectrum (e.g. from an Orbitrap instrument, .msp format) contains co-occurring 'grass' electronic noise ions that must be removed before precursor-formula-dependent chemical denoising or spectral matching.

name: relative-intensity-threshold-filtering
description: Use when raw MS/MS spectra from MSP files must be de-noised before model input, e.g. dropping peaks with intensity below 1% of the base peak while retaining precursor-mass-window consistency.

name: relative-performance-stratification-by-variable-type
description: Use when you have per-simulation NRMSE or PFC error tables for missForest and compared imputation methods across datasets that differ in variable-type composition (continuous-only, categorical-only, mixed) and in artificially introduced missingness, and you need to locate where the largest.

name: relative-retention-time-classification
description: Use when LC-MS/MS lipidomics annotations from MS2 library search contain false positives, and chromatographic retention-order information (relative RT across lipid subclasses) is available to filter or extend them.

name: relative-standard-deviation-qc-metrics
description: Use when you need to quantify residual intensity drift in LC/MS untargeted metabolomics after normalization, by computing per-feature RSD across withheld QC sample injections on a multi-sample feature matrix.

name: relative-standard-deviation-quality-assessment
description: Use when you have raw or signal-drift-corrected LC/GC-MS metabolomics or proteomics feature tables with repeated pooled QC injections and need a quantitative precision metric (e.g. % peaks within 15% or 30% RSD) to judge correction performance.

name: relevance-network-extraction
description: Use when a pre-processed ionome dataset (line-aggregated z-score ion profiles from ICP-MS, e.g. 14 ions across yeast knockout mutants) needs element-element correlation network analysis.

name: reliability-diagram-construction
description: Use when projected surrogate scores (e.g. 'high hscrp') from Nightingale Health 1H-NMR metabolomics must be checked for calibration against binarized phenotypes, using reliability diagrams plus ECE/MCE and log-loss deltas.

name: repeated-cross-validation-accuracy-estimation
description: Use when comparing normalization methods on metabolomics abundance data by supervised classification performance — e.g. predicting hypertension status from BioHEART-CT plasma metabolite abundances — where a repeated, averaged CV accuracy estimate is needed per method.

name: repeated-cross-validation-benchmarking
description: Use when a labeled metabolomics or other small-n feature matrix must be benchmarked across several classifiers, and a stable estimate of held-out performance (accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1) under repeated k-fold cross-validation is needed.

name: repeated-double-cross-validation-variable-selection
description: Use when a preprocessed, imputed LC-MS metabolomics feature table (MetaboSet object) with a known class label (e.g. a 'group' column) is available and the goal is supervised ranking of molecular features into minimal-optimal vs. all-relevant subsets.

name: repeated-kfold-cross-validation-splitting
description: Use when a log2-transformed metabolomics data matrix must be split into paired training/test sets so prediction performance (accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity) can be estimated and averaged over multiple resampled partitions.

name: repeated-measures-anova-on-longitudinal-metabolomics
description: Use when metabolomics values are measured repeatedly within the same subjects (e.g., venous vs arterial conditions or multiple time points) and the goal is to rank metabolites by ANOVA significance for feature selection.

name: repeated-stratified-cross-validation-evaluation
description: Use when a labeled single-cell feature matrix (e.g., the SpaceM MORPHnMOL.csv spatio-molecular matrix with 88 metabolite intensity columns and fluorescence-derived cell-type labels) must be scored with an honest accuracy estimate before claiming a prediction benchmark.

name: repetitive-alignment-batch-orchestration
description: Use when you must determine the minimum reference feature-list size (e.g. common feature groups between reference and target chromatograms) needed for reliable retention-time alignment, requiring systematic repetition of an alignment workflow across subsampled inputs.

name: replicate-averaging-and-ranking-of-expression-measurements
description: Use when replicate rank lists (e.g., the six SEQC RNA-seq replicate comparisons) must be reduced to per-gene average scores and ranks to test whether a reproducibility method's top-k sets are enriched for gold-standard genes such as the 1129 SEQC Taqman PCR transcripts.

name: replicate-based-unwanted-variation-estimation
description: Use when large-scale metabolomics batches contain embedded sample replicates (pooled QC, short replicates, batch replicates) and unwanted variation within and between batches must be estimated with RUV-III.

name: replicate-consensus-annotation-filtering
description: Use when comparing annotation counts between two LC-IM-MS replicate groups (e.g. original vs preprocessed MS-files) and you need a per-replicate consensus cutoff instead of per-file totals.

name: replicate-consensus-spectrum-assembly
description: Use when replicate DDA or SWATH-DIA MS2 spectral files have been deconvoluted (DecoID-style regression for DDA, DecoMetDIA-style C++/Rcpp for DIA) and must be consolidated into per-feature consensus spectra with precursor-fragment associations and compound annotations.

name: replicate-consistency-annotation-checking
description: Use when triplicate LC-IM-MS replicate annotation lists must be cross-checked to verify that smoothing/preprocessing improves consistent detection of low-abundance annotated features.

name: replicate-cross-correlation-evaluation
description: Use when you have a multi-batch metabolomics feature matrix with replicate reference samples (e.g. pooled or NIST 1950 SRM samples) present in each batch and need to quantify whether a normalization removed batch effects.

name: replicate-design-construction-for-metabolomics
description: Use when planning a multi-plate, multi-day targeted metabolomics run (e.g., >1,000 plasma samples over 44 days) where signal drift and inter-plate batch effects must be estimable from embedded replicates before normalisation.

name: replicate-feature-consistency-checking
description: Use when features have been detected per-sample (e.g. in positive and negative ionization mode LC-IMS-MS/MS data) from study samples acquired in triplicate and you need to downselect only those features reproducibly observed in all replicate injections.

name: replicate-group-clustering-regularization
description: Use when normalizing multi-batch untargeted metabolomics data (e.g. flow-injection MS) where reference samples such as pooled study samples or NIST 1950 SRM are present in every batch and their biological similarity must be preserved during batch-effect removal.

name: replicate-reproducibility-estimation-mass-spectrometry
description: Use when MS-metabolomics data contain biological or technical replicate samples and you need a nonparametric, FDR-controlled measure of which metabolites and sample pairs are reproducible, or when comparing pre-processing pipelines.

name: replicate-retention-time-rsd-assessment
description: Use when building or validating a retention-time reference library from chemical-standard mixtures measured in replicate LC-MS (e.g. three HILIC injections per mixture), and you must decide which analytes' retention times are reproducible enough to record.

name: replicate-rsd-quality-control
description: Use when QC filtering lipidomics feature tables (e.g. LipiDex 2 Peak Finder/Spectrum Searcher results) where replicate quality control samples were injected and features with >30% RSD should be flagged for removal.

name: replicate-run-metabolite-annotation
description: Use when you have merged peak lists from replicate GCxGC/TOF-MS runs (e.g. two runs of a 35-compound mixture) and need metabolite identification with a posterior confidence measure per metabolite, ranked by posterior probability.

name: replicate-series-phase-consistency-analysis
description: Use when a series of replicate 1D-NMR spectra (e.g. metabolite mix replicates or Daphnia extract CryoProbe spectra) must be phased automatically and you need to compare which algorithm gives the most reproducible phases.

name: reported-count-reconciliation
description: Use when a paper reports aggregate counts for a curated resource (e.g. total entries, novel additions, taxonomic coverage) and you must verify them directly from the released data files rather than trusting the text.

name: reported-count-reproduction-from-deposited-data
description: Use when a paper reports a database-overlap count and a significance test (e.g., 132 of 374 structures in LOTUS, chi-square 32.353) backed by a deposited dataset, and you must verify it independently.

name: reported-count-verification-against-reference-values
description: Use when a reported finding is a count of parameters grouped by sample type (EDTA plasma, serum, LiHep plasma) and delay type (pre- vs postcentrifugation) and you need to verify it against the PRIMA Panel stability time point data.

name: reported-metric-verification
description: Use when a paper reports aggregate counts (e.g., 5159 unique lipid ions, 1401 features, 26 lipid types) that must be verified by recounting them from the underlying per-feature annotation workbook in its supplementary files.

name: reported-results-extraction-from-manuscript
description: Use when a manuscript reports paired before/after optimization metrics across multiple biological studies (e.g. GSI, feature counts, annotations) and you need a machine-readable, arithmetic-consistency-checked results table.

name: reported-table-count-reproduction
description: Use when a paper reports exact per-method counts of significant features (e.g., significant metabolites at FWER alpha=0.05 in Table 3/Table S1) and you must verify those counts by re-executing the analysis from the released data and code.

name: reported-total-consistency-checking
description: Use when a paper reports exact counts of workflow/method combinations (e.g., 5,904/48/1,968 NOREVA workflows under QCS, IS, and neither conditions) and you must reproduce them by re-enumerating the underlying combinatorial space.

name: reporter-score-statistics
description: Use when a KO/gene/compound abundance table plus metadata (two-group, multi-group, continuous covariate, or longitudinal) needs pathway-level enrichment, and threshold-free aggregation with reporter scores is preferred over cutoff-based hypergeometric-style tests.

name: reporter-score-taxonomic-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a species-level microbial abundance table plus sample metadata and want threshold-free, hierarchical enrichment of taxa (e.g., genera) across group contrasts instead of pathway/KO enrichment.

name: repository-composition-statistics
description: Use when a curated reference database (e.g. MIBiG) has released a new version and you must report how many entries were added, how they distribute across predefined classes (including hybrids and 'Other'), and the proportional share of dominant classes.

name: repository-dataset-aggregation
description: Use when a paper reports aggregate statistics about a curated database release (total entries, newly added entries, phyla/kingdom coverage) and the underlying versioned data are available in a public repository, so the numbers can be recomputed and checked.

name: repository-growth-metric-verification
description: Use when a database-release paper reports divergent growth numbers per contribution channel (e.g. submission forms vs. curated events vs. classrooms) and these need to be reconciled into a verifiable per-channel table.

name: repository-package-classification
description: Use when a dependency edge list or package list of metabolomics R software lacks per-package repository labels and the analysis goal requires comparing CRAN-, Bioconductor-, and GitHub-hosted packages.

name: repository-scale-tandem-ms-cohort-analysis
description: Use when you need to reanalyze public tandem MS (MS/MS) files at repository scale as cohorts — e.g. compute PCA of per-file GNPS chemical annotations from the ReDU/MSV000084206 identification database — rather than analyzing one dataset in isolation.

name: repository-wide-data-corpus-auditing
description: Use when you need to quality-control a whole repository's holdings rather than one file — e.g. counting how many Metabolomics Workbench analyses fail to download or fail mwTab/JSON parsing at a given snapshot date.

name: reproducibility-assessment-high-throughput-rank-lists
description: Use when you have gene rank lists (e.g., from RNA-seq SEQC-style replicate experiments) from three replicates and need to quantify reproducibility, estimate pi1, and call reproducible genes with FDR control.

name: reproducibility-feature-documentation
description: Use when you need to characterize how reproducible and how complex a pipeline is (process count, parameter count, containerization) and compare it against a published baseline such as Metaboigniter's 20+ processes and 200+ parameters.

name: reproducibility-scatter-plot-visualization
description: Use when you have MaRR-classified reproducible/irreproducible metabolites and per-metabolite RSD values and need to show graphically whether a conventional CV/RSD cutoff (e.g., 25%) separates the two classes.

name: reproducibility-signal-detection-under-decaying-correlation
description: Use when assessing reproducibility of high-dimensional replicate experiments (e.g., MS-metabolomics feature tables with metabolites x replicate sample pairs) where replicate correlation decays with rank, and FDR-controlled, power-assessed detection of reproducible signals is needed.

name: reproducibility-statistic-comparison
description: Use when reproducing cross-laboratory lipid identification overlap statistics from a lab-by-lipid identification matrix, e.g. counting how many of 31 laboratories reported each SRM 1950 lipid and validating the ≥5-lab subset against a published value.

name: reproducibility-threshold-topk-set-extraction
description: Use when replicate rank lists have already been scored by MaRR and a competing method, and you need per-method top-k gene sets of equal size to compare against an external benchmark.

name: reproducible-vs-irreproducible-component-data-generation
description: Use when benchmarking a reproducibility method (e.g., MaRR) on synthetic data with a known ground-truth proportion of reproducible signals, under settings calibrated to real MS-Metabolomics replicate data.

name: request-timestamp-logging
description: Use when annotating spectra via web converters against rate-limited public APIs (e.g. PubChem ~5 req/s) and you need to record, log, or test the spacing of issued requests.

name: resampling-based-cluster-aggregation
description: Use when building kernel matrices from omic data layers via repeated resampled base clusterings, or when verifying that a consensus matrix is PSD before feeding it to kernel-based integrative clustering.

name: resampling-based-correction-function-generation
description: Use when IM-MS lipidomics CCS values need class- and adduct-specific correction and ≥3 U13C-labeled lipids of a lipid class-adduct combination (e.g., PC [M+H]+) are detected in measured data.

name: rescaled-intensity-difference-computation
description: Use when benchmarking metabolomics normalization methods on replicate runs (especially between-batch replicates) and you need a robust concordance metric that avoids favoring any method, as an alternative to QC-sample RSD or differential-abundance-count benchmarks.

name: rescoring-tool-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a review or paper reports multiple PSM rescoring benchmark results that must be reconciled into a structured comparison, especially when findings appear contradictory across tools or acquisition conditions (DDA vs timsTOF, RNN vs transformer predictors).

name: rescued-feature-identification
description: Use when quantifying how many features from a DDA feature list are recovered in DaDIA combined data and when validating rescued features by EIC peak-shape inspection before trusting rescue metrics.

name: residual-based-covariate-adjustment
description: Use when a pathway-level kernel association test (PaIRKAT) must be run on metabolomics data that are confounded by clinical covariates, so covariate effects must be removed from each metabolite before computing kernel quadratic-form statistics.

name: residual-based-peak-parameter-initialization
description: Use when initializing peak parameters for SAND's per-bin time-domain decomposition of 1D NMR spectra so the hybrid optimizer starts from data-driven seeds rather than arbitrary guesses.

name: residual-discordance-fraction-derivation
description: Use when comparing binary molecular subgroups (e.g., phosphoAKT1-high or MYC-high from k-means clustering) against SNP-array alteration calls (10q/PTEN loss, 8q/MYC gain) and you need the fraction of altered cases within each subgroup denominator.

name: residual-error-model-specification
description: Use when coding a population PK model in mrgsolve for MAP-BE with mapbayr and observations require a combined proportional (e.g. 0.05) and additive (e.g. 0.1) residual error structure on predicted concentrations.

name: residual-mad-normalization
description: Use when matching two untargeted LC–MS metabolomics feature tables: residuals from an estimated inter-dataset RT/mz/FI shift must be normalized robustly (median + F×MAD) before scoring or threshold tightening.

name: residual-standard-error-weighting
description: Use when aligning two same-method nontargeted LC-MS datasets (Source→Target) whose RT/mz drift must be modeled per feature dimension, and candidate matches must be filtered with a dataset-specific RSE-scaled tolerance rather than fixed ppm/RT windows.

name: residue-abundance-percent-change-analysis
description: Use when a lipidomics dataset with individual molecular lipid annotations (e.g., from Metabolomics Workbench) must be converted to fatty acid residue counts and compared as per-residue percentage changes between experimental groups or conditions.

name: residue-abundance-rank-verification
description: Use when lipidomic abundance tables from hepatocyte cell models (PHH, HLC, HepG2 and their media) must be converted to fatty acid residue counts and checked for cell-type-specific rank patterns.

name: residue-formula-monoisotopic-mass-calculation
description: Use when converting a SMILES structure into building-block sequences and each residue's formula/mass is needed for CycloBranch export, especially when blocks like Put (amine-terminated, oxygen-free) break the standard water-elimination convention.

name: resnet-transfer-learning-inference
description: Use when ion images from METASPACE-style imaging MS datasets must be classified as off-sample vs on-sample with a pretrained ResNet-50, or when reproducing the paper's off-sample frequency counts over DESI datasets.

name: resolution-dependent-isotope-correction
description: Use when correcting LC-MS isotope labeling data (13C, 2H, 15N, 18O, or 34S tracers) acquired on Orbitrap-class analyzers where resolution-dependent isotopolog overlap makes combinatorial correction (IsoCor-style NRE) inaccurate.

name: resource-count-verification
description: Use when a paper claims a dataset was harmonized from a numeric minimum of source resources (e.g. 'over 40 electronic resources') and you must audit that claim by enumerating the resources into an inventory.

name: response-factor-error-binning-analysis
description: Use when evaluating accuracy of inferred absolute concentration scaling factors (response factors) from relative abundance GC-MS time-course data, by binning per-metabolite errors against known ground truth and comparing to negative controls.

name: response-factor-negative-control-simulation
description: Decision support for validating response factor inference on GC-MS relative abundance data when no published comparator method exists, by simulating random and constant response factor baselines.

name: response-factor-normalization-of-abundances
description: Use when time-course metabolomics data provide only relative abundances (no fluxomics measurements) but a stoichiometric matrix and time vector exist, and flux profiles are needed for MetaboPAC's penalty calculation.

name: response-factor-optimization-with-known-kinetics
description: Use when metabolomics time-course data are relative abundances only, a stoichiometric model with known kinetic equations for some metabolites is available, and absolute concentrations must be inferred standard-free.

name: rest-api-data-retrieval
description: Use when a scientific database exposes REST Web services with an OpenAPI (v3.0) spec and you need programmatic, filterable retrieval of records (compounds, spectra) into a tabular dataset.

name: rest-api-endpoint-exposure
description: Use when standardized sample metadata produced by the SMetaS freetext-transformation pipeline must be consumed programmatically by downstream pipelines or database frontends, in parallel with a standardized CSV export.

name: rest-api-json-response-handling
description: Use when a downstream analysis consumes data retrieved from a REST-style endpoint that returns JSON documents — e.g. chemical annotation records from PUG-View, whose response follows the PUG-View annotation content model (the same model as the ASNT/ASNB formats).

name: rest-api-pagination-looping
description: Use when a PUG-View bulk request must fetch one annotation heading (e.g. Viscosity, LogP) for all records with no record identifier in the URL, and the response reports TotalPages > 1 requiring paged retrieval.

name: rest-api-parameter-documentation
description: Use when a paper documents a REST API (e.g. PUG-View) with concrete example request URLs in its Construction And Content section, and you must reconstruct machine-readable URL templates, identifier-type constraints, and output-format rules.

name: rest-api-querying-pubchem
description: Use when metabolite names (or non-systematic identifiers such as CAS numbers, HMDB, KEGG or LIPID MAPS IDs) reported in a source metabolomics dataset must be converted to systematic InChIKeys for cross-dataset merging, as in MMS Step 1.

name: rest-api-spectral-record-retrieval
description: Use when a recurrent LC-HRMS feature in a biological matrix (e.g., NIST plasma) needs its deposited spectrum/compound records retrieved programmatically from PeakForest rather than copied manually from an article.

name: rest-query-parameter-encoding
description: Use when you need annotations for exactly one PubChem record limited to a single (sub)heading (e.g. 'Solubility') via PUG-View, rather than the full annotation content for that record.

name: rest-url-construction
description: Use when you need to retrieve a specific annotation for a given PubChem compound record through PUG-View but must first know how to form the request URL.

name: rest-url-parameter-validation
description: Use when you need to fetch Metabolomics Workbench study/analysis data programmatically via its REST interface and must construct valid REST request URLs from key-value parameters (e.g. study ID and analysis ID) rather than hard-coding endpoint strings.

name: rest-web-service-data-export
description: Use when a laboratory needs to move locally curated PeakForest spectral records (peak lists, chromatography and ionization metadata) out of the database for reuse by external tools or submission to international repositories.

name: restful-api-batch-annotation
description: Use when a fixed list of metabolites with known exact monoisotopic masses and adduct forms must be annotated programmatically via the CMM 3.0 RESTful API and the HMDB-sourced results verified against public HMDB records.

name: restful-api-bmrb-entry-retrieval
description: Use when a workflow needs a specific archived BMRB entry fetched programmatically (by entry_id) in NMR-STAR or JSON format, without manual browser download, as input for parsing or chemical-shift extraction.

name: restful-api-implementation-for-bgc-metadata
description: Use when building or extending a REST-like API that serves structured BGC annotation metadata from a relational database backend for a repository-style web front end.

name: restful-api-metabolite-count-extraction
description: Use when you need programmatic counts of experimental vs predicted metabolites in a metabolomic database, or when integrating CMM 3.0 annotation queries into a pipeline rather than using the web UI.

name: restful-api-workflow-automation
description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics putative-annotation table (e.g., compound-name/mass TSV) must be processed headlessly — via TurboPutative's RESTful API — inside an automated pipeline, or when benchmarking runtime scaling with input row count.

name: restful-repository-data-retrieval
description: Use when a corpus of mwTab-format MS or NMR dataset files must be fetched from Metabolomics Workbench (e.g., for validator sweeps or curation audits) via the MW REST interface rather than manual download.

name: restful-url-construction
description: Use when you need to programmatically fetch full PubChem annotation/summary content for a specific CID, SID, or AID record and must formulate a valid PUG-View request URL.

name: restraint-data-format-conversion
description: Use when an archival BMRB NMR-STAR entry must be validated, its chemical shift loop and restraint saveframes extracted, and its tables emitted as a NEF file (converted.nef) conformant with the NEF specification.

name: restricted-likelihood-pathway-testing
description: Use when performing topology-based pathway enrichment on gene-level expression data (e.g., 2784 genes, 520 subjects) where standard NetGSA is computationally expensive and you need efficient REHE-based testing.

name: result-count-verification
description: Use when a reported PoDP List-tab search result count (e.g. 18 projects for 'Streptomyces | Salinispora') must be independently reproduced from the Zenodo JSON archive of project records.

name: retention-index-based-peak-refinement
description: Use when annotating consensus spectra from GC × GC–MS deconvolution and an MSP library provides Kovats retention indices for compounds, so that cosine-similarity matches can be refined or disambiguated by RT-to-RI conversion.

name: retention-index-constrained-compound-identification
description: Use when a GcDUO DuoResults object contains detected peak spectra and an MSP spectral library (optionally with Kovats RI values) is available, and each feature must be assigned a compound identity with a confidence threshold.

name: retention-index-database-matching
description: Use when retention times are only partially transferable between labs/chromatographic systems and features must be annotated by m/z plus retention index instead of raw RT, given a set of retention-index standard compounds and a reference database with exact mass and index values.

name: retention-index-error-computation
description: Use when annotating features from an mRList object against a margheRita spectral library (e.g. RPShort positive mode) and you need per-match ppm, retention-time, and retention-index errors to support level-1 identifications.

name: retention-index-log-interpolation
description: Use when aligned per-sample peaklists (m/z–RT pairs) from multiple LC/HRMS samples or batches show systematic RT drift, and no external RT standard ladder is available — indigenous recurring peaks serve as the reference markers.

name: retention-index-metabolite-annotation
description: Use when metabolite features are named by retention-index codes (RI<value> format) from GC-based metabolomics and standard identifiers are required before KEGG pathway enrichment or compound mapping.

name: retention-index-unit-error-flagging
description: Use when auditing METABOLITES section headers and value series in mwTab files to detect retention-index columns labeled with time units (e.g. minutes) or other logical-format mismatches against standardized fields like pubchem_id, inchi_key, hmdb_id.

name: retention-migration-time-transcription
description: Use when a supplementary DOCX table reports per-method RT/MT ± sd and checkmark/cross detection flags for standard analytes and these must be converted into a machine-readable coverage matrix for verifying multi-platform metabolite coverage claims.

name: retention-order-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when evaluating whether molecular fingerprint representation (counting vs binary, Min-Max vs Tanimoto kernel) affects pairwise retention order accuracy in a single-system RankSVM setting.

name: retention-order-correlation-analysis
description: Use when multiple paired RPLC retention datasets (e.g., from RepoRT, PredRet, Metabolome Workbench, MetaboLights) share compounds and you need to test whether eluent pH or other configuration attributes explain retention-order replicability.

name: retention-order-integrated-metabolite-identification
description: Use when you already have per-spectrum scored candidate molecule lists from an MS/MS predictor (e.g. IOKR) plus retention times for a complete LC-MS/MS run, and want to jointly identify the whole metabolite set using retention order constraints.

name: retention-order-model-training
description: Use when you need to train or fine-tune a retention-order prediction model from RT data of a reference compound set (e.g. dataset_87), producing pairwise P_ij elution probabilities for candidate small molecules in an RPLC system with eluent pH ~2.7.

name: retention-order-pairwise-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when you must quantify how accurately a retention-order model ranks pairs of molecules for specific chromatographic systems (e.g. Eawag_XBridgeC18, FEM_long, RIKEN), and compare single-system versus pooled multi-system training regimes.

name: retention-order-prediction-selfsupervision
description: Use when training MS/MS spectral encoders on large unannotated LC-MS/MS collections (e.g., GeMS mined from MassIVE GNPS) and you want representations that cluster by molecular structure without supervised labels.

name: retention-order-probability-sourcing-from-roasmi-predictions
description: Use when ready-to-identify datasets carry candidate molecular pairs with ROASMI retention scores and you must exclude indistinguishable pairs or infer elution order for identification.

name: retention-order-ranking-model-training
description: Use when you have paired compound-retention data (SMILES + retention times/retention order) from an RPLC reference set and need to train, cross-validate, or retrain a retention-order prediction model or compare molecular representations.

name: retention-order-score-integration
description: Use when a full LC-MS/MS run yields one scored candidate list per spectrum (e.g. from IOKR over PubChem) and a RankSVM retention-order predictor is available, and per-spectrum top hits must be made jointly consistent in elution order.

name: retention-order-supervised-training-pipeline
description: Use when raw reference retention-time records (e.g. dataset_83 for the default RPLC retraining setup) must be converted into pairwise elution-order training data with D-MPNN molecular embeddings for retraining or building a RankNet retention model.

name: retention-score-integrated-candidate-reranking
description: Use when ready-to-identify candidate lists from MS/MS tools (e.g. SIRIUS or MS-DIAL outputs as CSV) exist for RPLC-MS/MS peaks and retention-order scores should be integrated to improve top-k accuracy.

name: retention-time-agnostic-memo-matrix-merging
description: Use when new LC-MS/MS samples must be added to an existing metabolomics sample-comparison matrix despite different LC gradients (e.g. 40 min vs 8 min) or different MS instruments (QE-Plus vs QE-Focus).

name: retention-time-agnostic-sample-comparison
description: Use when comparing LC-MS/MS samples with poor feature overlap, strong RT shifts, samples acquired on different LC methods or MS platforms (e.g. Maxis Q-ToF vs Q-Exactive Orbitrap), or over long time periods where feature-table metrics inherit acquisition-batch artifacts.

name: retention-time-alignment
description: Use when processing a batch of MRM mzML files (e.g. HILIC 1a/1b, MTBLS429, MTBLS897) whose metabolite peaks shift in RT between samples, and peak boundaries must be aligned before peak picking and ML-based peak reporting.

name: retention-time-alignment
description: Use when two LC-MS feature lists — an in vitro prototype list and an in vivo metabolite list, each with retention time and accurate m/z per component — must be bridged by RT and m/z matching.

name: retention-time-alignment
description: Use when LC-MS targeted metabolomics EICs show retention-time drift between samples or replicate groups and the same isotopologue peak must be matched across samples before peak-area integration.

name: retention-time-alignment
description: Use when raw LC/MS mzML files from multiple injections are being converted into EIC data matrices for downstream peak scoring, and retention-time drift between runs could misalign the 60-datapoint chromatographic windows for the same peak.

name: retention-time-alignment-and-feature-linking
description: Use when multiple LC-MS/MS or DIA/SWATH maps must be made comparable — after feature detection and database searching, before protein inference — so peptide quantities refer to the same molecular feature in every run.

name: retention-time-alignment-comparison
description: Use when you have an MZmine-exported full-scan (MS1) feature table and a RegFilter-generated SPL .csv for the same LC-MS run and need to quantify what fraction of targeted precursor ions exist as DDA MS1 features or were actually fragmented in DDA.

name: retention-time-alignment-of-lc-ms-runs
description: Use when multiple mzML runs (e.g. a spike-in series with randomized technical triplicates on an Acquity/Synapt HDMS instrument) show retention-time drift that would break feature correspondence prior to linking feature maps.

name: retention-time-alignment-parameters
description: Use when preparing raw LC/MS mzXML data (e.g. MetaboLights MTBLS213) as an XCMS xcmsSet for isotopologue-pair detection with geoRge, where feature quality is determined by peak picking, alignment and grouping parameters.

name: retention-time-ambiguity-analysis
description: Use when a metabolite standard or adduct in a metScribeR EIC review shows more than one manually labeled 'good' peak at different retention times, and ambiguous entries must be flagged or removed from the final RT/m/z library.

name: retention-time-axis-construction
description: Use when raw GCxGC-MS acquisition data arrives as a NetCDF (.cdf) file and you must build the two-dimensional retention-time axis (first dimension vs modulation-period second dimension) before smoothing, baseline correction, alignment, or MPCA.

name: retention-time-based-cluster-purity-evaluation
description: Use when you need to assess how well a tool clusters MS/MS spectra from metabolomics datasets (qToF or Orbitrap, e.g. MSV000081981 or MSV000093033) without ground-truth identifications, or when benchmarking clustering purity against a database-search-based evaluation.

name: retention-time-candidate-filtering
description: Use when a formula-based database retrieval (e.g. PubChem isomeric candidates by exact molecular formula, or MS-Finder candidate lists) must be narrowed using a measured liquid-chromatography retention time for the unknown molecule.

name: retention-time-candidate-filtering-msfinder
description: Use when MS-FINDER compound identification returns many isomeric candidate structures per formula and you have predicted RTs (Retip) plus experimental RTs to exclude candidates that are chromatographically implausible.

name: retention-time-chromatogram-parameterisation
description: Use when building synthetic chemical datasets for ViMMS 2.0 simulations and the generated chemicals need controlled retention-time, intensity and chromatogram shapes (e.g. Gaussian peaks) alongside formula-derived m/z values, rather than chemicals extracted from existing mzML files.

name: retention-time-coarse-alignment
description: Use when LC-MS feature tables from multiple runs show RT drift that must be removed before aligning features, as the preprocessing stage of DeepRTAlign's deep-learning correspondence workflow.

name: retention-time-coelution-overlap-analysis
description: Use when a large set of peptides with overlapping simulated/measured retention times is planned or simulated and you must predict chimeric-spectrum burden (2+ peptides selected for fragmentation simultaneously) before a real MS experiment.

name: retention-time-confirmation-against-standards
description: Use when assigning highest-confidence (MSI level 1) compound identities from LC-MS/MS peak lists by matching precursor mass, retention time, and MS/MS fragments against an in-house authentic-standard spectral library.

name: retention-time-correction-via-retention-index-markers
description: Use when an untargeted LC/HRMS dataset (mzML/mzXML from hundreds of samples or multiple batches) shows systematic retention-time drift that must be removed before peak alignment or peak annotation.

name: retention-time-correlation-analysis
description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics feature table contains multiple putative annotations per feature (shared monoisotopic mass and adduct variants) and a single most-probable annotation per feature must be selected using adduct probability, feature-intensity correlations, and mass error.

name: retention-time-database-construction
description: Use when you need a reference set of predicted retention times for known metabolites (e.g. HMDB entries) to pair with m/z filtering and RT-based candidate ranking in untargeted metabolomics where MS/MS spectra are unavailable.

name: retention-time-descriptor-regression-modeling
description: Use when you have SMILES/InChI structures or a compound list with measured LC retention times (HILIC or reversed-phase) and need RT predictions or descriptor-importance rankings to filter annotation candidates.

name: retention-time-deviation-analysis
description: Use when you need to quantify retention time stability of monitored compounds in a long-term QC pool (e.g. MetNexs) across LC-MS batches, comparing short-term within-batch deviations against interbatch offsets using QC4Metabolomics.

name: retention-time-deviation-scoring-against-expected-rt
description: Use when preprocessing LC-QQQ-MS MRM batch data (mzML) and you need to score candidate chromatographic peaks by their deviation from expected RT, including alignment-corrected deviation, for downstream ML peak classification.

name: retention-time-direction-filtering
description: Use when TP components have been generated by patRoon componentization (parents linked to TP features) from LC-HRMS data in mixed positive/negative ionization, and you must prioritize which parent/TP pairs are chemically plausible by chromatographic retention-time direction.

name: retention-time-distance-clustering
description: Use when GC–MS untargeted metabolomics samples have been deconvolved independently (e.g. via eRah's deconvolveComp) and the same compound must be matched across samples to produce one row per unique compound with per-sample areas.

name: retention-time-distribution-pattern-recognition
description: Use when running semi-targeted Target Search over multiple batches of DDA-acquired LC-MS files (e.g., TripleTOF .wiff or QE HF .raw converted to Aird) and you need automated, consistent peak selection before manual inspection.

name: retention-time-drift-alignment
description: Use when targeted LC–MS peak integration shows RT shifts between runs and you have QC runs plus a target list containing housekeeping peaks whose RT deviations can anchor the alignment.

name: retention-time-drift-correction
description: Use when per-sample detected feature tables must be aligned to a reference sample and coordinates drift between acquisitions (e.g. LC-IMS-MS/MS runs from Bruker or Waters instruments).

name: retention-time-drift-correction
description: Use when integrating multiple untargeted LC/MS serum studies (e.g., HILIC positive-mode mzML files) whose RT and intensity drifts from batch effects and run order prevent cross-study feature alignment.

name: retention-time-drift-correction
description: Use when MRM chromatographic peak lists from multiple samples show retention time shifts that must be corrected before peak alignment or EIC grouping, and per-sample RT drift values need to be estimated from chromatogram shapes.

name: retention-time-drift-correction
description: Use when per-sample LC/HRMS peaklists (m/z–RT pairs) from a multi-sample or multi-batch study show systematic RT drift and peaks must be aligned before cross-referencing or building an intensity matrix.

name: retention-time-drift-correction-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating or comparing LC–MS feature alignment algorithms (e.g. G-Aligner, MZmine2, OpenMS, XCMS, local bipartite matching) on datasets with nonlinear RT drift, especially when a manually annotated feature list is available as ground truth.

name: retention-time-drift-detection
description: Use when historical or incoming LC-MS system suitability mzML files must be screened for batch-clustered retention time shifts or EIC patterns inconsistent with the intended chromatographic method (e.g., an F5 method run on a BEH Amide column) prior to data collection.

name: retention-time-drift-registration
description: Use when aligning features across multiple LC–MS runs whose RTs drift nonlinearly due to chromatogram condition changes (column temperature, aging, contamination), as the first stage before feature matching.

name: retention-time-drift-threshold-logic
description: Use when coding or auditing per-target QC decision rules for internal standards in untargeted LC-MS/MS runs processed by Rapid QC-MS, and the paper's 66%/80% fractional warning thresholds must be reproduced exactly.

name: retention-time-drift-tolerance-setting
description: Use when matching two untargeted LC–MS metabolomics feature tables whose RT, MZ, and FI values drift between experiments, and you must choose initial match thresholds before Step 2 uniqueness resolution.

name: retention-time-error-metric-computation
description: Use when evaluating LC–MS RT prediction models (e.g. METLIN SMRT 25% hold-out molecules with experimental vs DLM-predicted RT in seconds) and you must report per-molecule relative errors and decide whether to exclude non-retained compounds (RT < ~60 s).

name: retention-time-error-metric-extraction
description: Decision support for comparing retention-time prediction accuracy across candidate models when multiple methods have been evaluated on the METLIN SMRT dataset and you need to rank mean/median relative error.

name: retention-time-error-threshold-optimization
description: Use when candidate compounds from untargeted metabolomics have RT-Transformer-predicted vs observed RTs and you must choose an RT-error cutoff to discard false identities without losing true ones.

name: retention-time-feature-engineering
description: Use when building molecular feature inputs (descriptors and/or fingerprints) for RT regressors on compounds with SMILES/SDF structures and RT labels, and you must handle missing descriptors and collinear features.

name: retention-time-filtered-annotation-ranking
description: Use when you have m/z-matched candidate annotation lists (e.g. from LipidBlast or similar) plus measured retention times, and you need to improve Recall@1/Recall@k of the correct identification by adding orthogonal RT or CCS evidence.

name: retention-time-filtration
description: Use when a CAMERA/XCMS LC/MS feature list contains early-eluting contaminants (e.g. under the 45 s exclusion used for Arabidopsis rosette extracts) or when you must bound candidate metabolites by RT and accommodate retention-time shifts caused by isotope labeling.

name: retention-time-fwhm-window-matching
description: Use when you have a peak table (Compound Discoverer 3.3 .cdResult or .csv) with a mix of lipid-identified and unidentified features and need to classify unidentified features as adducts, in-source fragments, or dimers.

name: retention-time-integer-quantization
description: Use when converting vendor MRM chromatogram files (e.g. from Xcalibur or SCIEX OS) into the Aird format and storage size or web-side rendering speed for hundreds of chromatograms is the bottleneck.

name: retention-time-interval-encoding
description: Use when converting the retention times of top MS1 signals (e.g., from BAGO's findTopSignals on mzML/mzXML data) into a bounded separation-efficiency score to serve as the objective for LC gradient optimization.

name: retention-time-library-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify how faithfully an automated LC-MS peak-quality filter reproduces manual quality labeling of standard peaks, using precision, recall, F1, and misclassification counts.

name: retention-time-logp-modeling
description: Use when LC/MS HR-MS/MS candidates must be re-ranked using measured retention times on a reverse-phase column and reference-standard RTs are available to fit the log P correlation.

name: retention-time-map-alignment
description: Use when multiple centroided LC-MS mzML maps must be brought onto a common retention-time scale (e.g. before FeatureLinkerUnlabeledKD consensus grouping) and RT drift between runs would break cross-sample feature matching.

name: retention-time-misalignment-detection
description: Use when you have two XCMS grouping results (one with an RT window near the RT sampling resolution, one with the expected maximal RT drift) and need to identify which peak groups are misaligned before realignment.

name: retention-time-model-filtering
description: Use when lipid identifications from the LipiDex 2 Peak Finder and Spectral Searcher pipeline need QC filtering based on retention-time plausibility, i.e. removing identifications whose measured RT deviates substantially from the ECN-predicted RT for their lipid class.

name: retention-time-mz-matrix-resampling
description: Use when raw profile-mode mzXML/mzML LC-HRMS chromatograms must be converted into fixed-size (rt x mz) candidate-peak areas before CNN-based peak-apex classification, e.g. as the preprocessing step of PeakBot peak picking.

name: retention-time-mz-scatter-visualization
description: Use when a scored NP Analyst feature network (nodes = MS features/samples, edges = bioactivity-weighted associations) needs to be divided into communities and rendered as network graphML, rt vs m/z scatter plots, and community views for prioritizing bioactive MS features.

name: retention-time-order-validation
description: Use when a candidate PFAS homologous series (features grouped by matching CF2-normalized Kendrick mass defect and CF2-unit mass differences) needs confirmation that chromatographic retention time follows the expected order along the series.

name: retention-time-pairing-from-adjacent-chromatographic-peaks
description: Use when building pairwise training data from a reference retention-time dataset (e.g., 'dataset_83') where ordered molecule pairs (Ci eluting before Cj) are needed to train a ranking model like RankNet.

name: retention-time-peak-assignment-per-formula
description: Use when confirmed LC-IM-MS peak detections must be linked to specific molecular formulae with assigned RT values, e.g. after peak picking mzML-derived ion traces and before building SQL-format database entries.

name: retention-time-peak-boundary-assessment
description: Use when building an LC-MS metabolite RT library from mzML files of authentic standards and you must decide which detected EIC peaks have valid boundaries and RTs worth exporting.

name: retention-time-peak-picking
description: Use when a targeted, formula-driven workflow needs to extract monoisotopic primary-ion m/z traces (optionally multiply charged) from LC-IM-MS mzML data and pick chromatographic peaks in the RT dimension, rather than performing untargeted feature detection.

name: retention-time-piecewise-linear-calibration
description: Use when lipid features were separated on a modified HILIC gradient or a non-reference Kinetex HILIC column (e.g. 50 mm or 30 mm instead of 100 mm), and their measured RTs must be mapped to the reference database RTs (23 lipid classes carry HILIC RTs) before identification.

name: retention-time-precision-statistics
description: Use when system suitability testing must report chromatographic reproducibility: retention times of SST standard compounds are available per acquisition file across multiple runs, platforms, or operators, and RSD summaries are needed.

name: retention-time-prediction-error-analysis
description: Use when you have true vs. predicted retention times for a fixed test set of molecules (e.g. SMRT) and need error-distribution coverage statistics and a ±2 SD exclusion-threshold false negative rate.

name: retention-time-prediction-error-analysis
description: Use when you have a trained RT prediction model (e.g., a DLM on the METLIN SMRT dataset) plus predicted-vs-experimental RT for a validation split, and want to test whether structurally similar training-set counterparts reduce prediction error.

name: retention-time-prediction-feature-evaluation
description: Decision support for choosing or validating a retention time predictor (e.g. DeepLC, Prosit-derived RT, RTPredict) whose ΔRT error will serve as a rescoring feature in Percolator-style PSM rescoring.

name: retention-time-prediction-fine-tuning
description: Use when predicting liquid chromatography retention times for a new chromatographic method from molecular structures (InChI/SMILES), especially with limited labeled data where training a retention-time model from scratch is infeasible.

name: retention-time-prediction-from-chemical-descriptors
description: Use when SMILES structures need predicted retention times (HILIC or RPLC) to rank or filter candidate structures in untargeted metabolomics, or when batch-predicting RTs for a large compound database.

name: retention-time-prediction-inference
description: Use when you have a molecular formula (e.g. from PubChem PUG REST) with multiple isomeric candidate SMILES and one observed retention time under an SMRT-type chromatographic method, and need to prune inconsistent candidates.

name: retention-time-prediction-integration
description: Use when building multidimensional (4D) LC-IM-MS/MS identification databases where computationally predicted retention times must be supplied for candidate molecules lacking experimental RT measurements, e.g. derivatized sterol lipid entries.

name: retention-time-prediction-model-inference
description: Use when you have SMILES/InChI structures or a compound descriptor table and need predicted retention times for HILIC or reversed-phase LC-MS runs to filter isomer candidates, rank unknowns, or remove unlikely annotations in metabolomics workflows.

name: retention-time-prediction-modeling
description: Use when you need to predict retention times for compounds from SMILES/structures to complement MS/MS spectral matching, or to benchmark a learned RT predictor against a logP-based linear regression baseline.

name: retention-time-prior-integration
description: Use when the MS1 database contains RT entries (e.g. '30;60' elution ranges) for compounds, and LC-MS feature annotations must be filtered or reweighted by whether the feature's measured retention time falls within that expected range.

name: retention-time-projection-across-chromatographic-methods
description: Use when you have deep-learning-predicted RTs on one chromatographic method and need them transformed onto the time scale of other experimental reverse-phase methods (ECMs) to compute projection errors or rank candidates.

name: retention-time-projection-between-chromatographic-methods
description: Use when predicted RTs from a machine learning model must be projected to a specific chromatographic method for which only ~10 experimentally identified molecules (predicted-vs-experimental RT pairs) are available, and confidence intervals on the projections are needed.

name: retention-time-projection-meta-learning
description: Use when you have a small set (10–50 molecules) of paired predicted/experimental RTs for a target chromatographic method and need to map DNN-predicted RTs onto that method's scale with 95% prediction intervals.

name: retention-time-projection-regression
description: Use when you have DLM-predicted RTs, a molecule library with accurate masses (e.g. HMDB), and experimental RTs from a target chromatographic method, and you need to rank/filter candidate identities from 10 ppm accurate-mass search results.

name: retention-time-range-configuration-for-virtual-runs
description: Use when executing a simulated LC-MS/MS acquisition in ViMMS 2.0 and you must bind the mass spectrometer and controller in an Environment and define the simulated RT window before env.run().

name: retention-time-reference-library-construction
description: Use when building a metabolite reference library from chemical standard injections in LC-MS: replicate mzXML/mzML files of standard mixtures are available and validated retention times per analyte must be extracted and tabulated.

name: retention-time-regression-model-training
description: Use when experimental retention times are available for a compound library (e.g. 880 HILIC compounds from MoNA or 398 RPLC compounds from RIKEN PlaSMA) and the goal is a descriptor-based RT prediction model to filter false-positive annotations.

name: retention-time-regression-model-training
description: Use when you have small-molecule structures with measured LC retention times (e.g. a METLIN SMRT-style dataset) and need an accurate data-driven retention time regression model for structural identification support.

name: retention-time-regression-modeling
description: Use when authentic standards are unavailable and LC-HRMS annotations (e.g. CMDN-annotated metabolites with accurate m/z and RT) need chromatographic plausibility checks by predicting RT from SMILES/InChIKey structures.

name: retention-time-regression-training
description: Use when you have a large set of molecules with experimental retention times (e.g., SMRT reversed-phase LC-MS data) plus alvaDesc fingerprints/descriptors and need to train or compare RT prediction regressors.

name: retention-time-rsd-computation-across-replicates
description: Use when validating LC-MS reference analytes from >=3 replicate runs (e.g. HILIC standard mixtures in mzML/mzXML) and you must quantify retention-time reproducibility per analyte against a user-specified threshold c (default 15%).

name: retention-time-scheduled-method-export
description: Use when a second-round targeted MS method (SRM/MRM) must be built from measured retention times observed in a first-pass Skyline analysis, e.g. refining an arginine/polyamine pathway assay after initial unscheduled acquisition.

name: retention-time-score-evaluation
description: Use when scoring metabolite annotations from MS/MS spectra in negative mode where retention time is available, e.g. verifying that a candidate like 1-O-beta-D-glucopyranosyl sinapate at RT 1.27 min receives the expected RT score of 1.

name: retention-time-search-frame-restriction
description: Use when re-detecting peaks from LC-HRMS mzXML chromatograms for a known reference feature list, and narrowed m/z + retention-time search windows are available or can be derived per feature.

name: retention-time-shift-and-noise-thresholding
description: Use when a targeted or suspect HRMS prescreening run has produced EICs and MS2 scans per compound and you must pass/fail each parent point against experimental m/z error, RT error, and MS1/MS2 intensity thresholds before further identification.

name: retention-time-shift-correction
description: Use when aligning XCMS-derived feature lists or target chromatograms from different LC-HRMS batches where retention times are shifted (e.g. 7–52 s or -9 to -24 s ranges) and m/z deviates slightly (e.g. -3.4 ppm) relative to a reference.

name: retention-time-shift-correction-isotope-labelling
description: Use when isotope-labelling experiments (deuterium- or 13C-labelled substrates) shift chromatographic retention times, and m/z-difference-based substrate-metabolite discovery would otherwise miss the labelled peak pair.

name: retention-time-shift-interpretation
description: Use when annotating reaction-derived xenobiotic metabolites from LC-HRMS feature tables and you need to attach RT-shift metadata and biotransformation labels to metabolite network nodes, or use RT consistency as a validation channel.

name: retention-time-shift-modeling
description: Use when two untargeted LC–MS metabolomics feature tables (samples × features with RT, m/z, and FI medians per feature) must be matched feature-by-feature despite inter-dataset retention-time shifts, e.g. for batch combination or multicohort integration.

name: retention-time-shift-quantification
description: Use when a sequence of LC-MS/MS acquisitions must be monitored for RT drift, e.g. to confirm each specimen's RT against IS/RS/ES m/z-RT windows written live by the Python Watchdog watcher.

name: retention-time-shift-simulation
description: Use when you need to stress-test an LC-MS RT alignment tool against ground-truth correspondences, or to determine at what RT-shift variability an aligner's precision and recall degrade.

name: retention-time-spline-fitting
description: Use when a pair of untargeted LC-MS metabolomics data sets acquired under different gradient elution methods must be combined and RT drift must be corrected before ranking feature pair alignments by mapped retention time.

name: retention-time-stability-assessment
description: Use when a metabolomics/lipidomics feature table contains repeated pooled-QC injections and you need to verify retention time precision (RSD < 2%) before trusting chromatographic alignment across the sequence.

name: retention-time-tolerance-sensitivity-analysis
