description: Use when peak lists from multiple LC-MS samples have been aligned with configurable retention-time (RT) tolerance parameters and you need to test whether the aligner's precision/recall holds across tolerance settings and feature-row counts, or to identify dataset fractions where one aligner.

name: retention-time-tolerance-sweep
description: Use when comparing peak-list alignment algorithms on LC-MS peak lists with known ground-truth correspondences, and you need a tolerance sweep (e.g., 5/20/50 s RT) scored by precision and recall.

name: retention-time-trend-chain-extension
description: Use when running untargeted homologue series detection on LC-MS peak tables and candidate series have reached three members, so their RT step trends must be learned to constrain further chain extension.

name: retention-time-warping-function-substitution
description: Use when XCMS grouping has flagged features as misaligned and ncGTW has produced per-sample warping functions, and you want more accurate peak-filling (integration of missing peaks) than the default single-warping-function XCMS alignment provides.

name: retention-time-window-aggregation
description: Use when raw LC-MS profile spectra must be converted to a fixed-size 2D intensity matrix (m/z x RT windows) as input to CNN/LSTM/Transformer classifiers, and the m/z and RT dimensions vary between acquisitions.

name: retention-time-window-based-peak-grouping
description: Use when processing LC–MS/MS mzXML files of released N-glycans where multiple peaks share the same m/z and need to be separated and counted as distinct isomer peaks within a fixed retention-time window.

name: retention-time-window-encoding
description: Use when converting MZmine 2 aligned peak groups (m/z and retention-time windows plus per-sample peak shapes) into the standardized 64x64 pixel raster images that feed the image-based deep neural network for true/false peak classification.

name: retention-time-window-extraction
description: Use when confirming a candidate glycan identified in MS1 by pulling the MS2 fragmentation scans in a narrow window around the glycan's MS1 retention time (MS1 RT minus 0.1 min) from an mzXML-derived LC-MS/MS run.

name: retention-time-window-filtering
description: Use when a raw LC-IM-MS dataset has been converted to .mza and the analysis target is a narrow chromatographic region (e.g., a 0.5 min RT window) whose spectra must be isolated before mobility or m/z visualization.

name: retention-time-window-matching
description: Use when evaluating MS/MS spectral clustering (msCluster, Falcon, MaRaCluster) on metabolomics or proteomics LC-MS data that lacks annotated peptide/molecule labels, by exploiting precursor m/z and RT consistency instead of database identifications.

name: retention-time-window-matching
description: Use when you have an Agilent Unknowns Analysis GC-MS hit table with Component.RT, Component.Area, Base.Peak.MZ, File.Name, Compound.Name, and Match.Factor columns and need per-sample areas for user-specified chemicals.

name: retention-time-window-pair-filtering
description: Use when a non-targeted LC-MS peak table (e.g. MS-DIAL export) needs same-metabolite feature grouping, and you must constrain which feature pairs are considered correlated by a retention-time window before graph clustering.

name: retention-time-zscore-annotation-ranking
description: Use when annotating small molecules with only m/z and retention times (no MS/MS spectra), and you need to rank a mass-filtered candidate list using RT predictions projected to your chromatographic method from ~10 identified molecules.

name: reticulate-cross-language-execution
description: Use when an R-based Spectra workflow needs Python-only MS routines (matchms similarity scores, filters like normalize_intensities), or when a Python routine must operate on R MS data without exporting files.

name: reticulate-cross-language-object-mapping
description: Use when an R-based Spectra workflow must hand MS2 peak data (mz/intensity matrices plus spectra variables like msLevel, precursorMz, rtime) to Python matchms functions, or matchms results must be returned to R, without intermediate file serialization.

name: reticulate-python-session-management
description: Use when an R workflow must configure a Python environment (py_require, RETICULATE_PYTHON) or reference a live Python MS object such as a matchms.Spectrum from R instead of importing a static copy of the peak data.

name: retip-chem-space-visualization
description: Use when you have SMILES-annotated training/test/validation compound sets for a chromatographic method and need to assess structural coverage before trusting RT-prediction generalization.

name: retrieval-rate-benchmark-computation
description: Use when benchmarking a metabolite annotation engine against MetFrag, CFM-ID or CSI:FingerID: you have tandem MS/MS test spectra with known structures and ranked candidate lists per tool, and need top-1/top-k retrieval rates for side-by-side comparison.

name: retrieval-recall-evaluation
description: Use when you need to quantify how well a spectrum-identifier or bucketing key reduces a mass spectral search space while preserving similarity-based recall, using the SPLASH second-block scheme and NIST cosine scoring.

name: retrometabolic-reaction-presence-quantification
description: Use when you have a reference set of characterized biochemical reaction IDs and want to quantify how many are anticipated by RetroRules reaction-rule predictions in MEANtools, with a statistical significance test.

name: retrospective-annotation-evaluation
description: Use when initial MAGMa annotation rankings leave specific MS/MS peaks unexplained or correct candidates rank poorly, and you need to retrospectively test whether a more permissive fragmentation depth or mass tolerance resolves the miss.

name: retrospective-challenge-benchmark-analysis
description: Use when a benchmark-contest solution set (e.g. CASMI challenges with known ground-truth molecules) must be re-analyzed after the fact to isolate the effect of a ranking or filtering parameter on correct-candidate rank.

name: reverse-cosine-spectrum-search
description: Use when pseudo MS/MS spectra reconstructed from MS1-only data must be annotated against a reference MS/MS library but contain fragment peaks not present in the reference spectra (in-source fragments of adducts, multimers, co-eluting species).

name: reverse-dependency-degree-computation
description: Use when you have a dependency-network edge list of R packages annotated by hosting repository (CRAN, Bioconductor, GitHub) and need reverse-dependency connectivity metrics per repository.

name: reverse-dependency-network-construction
description: Use when a catalogued list of R packages (e.g. metabolomics packages from CRAN, Bioconductor and GitHub) is available and you need to know which other packages depend on them, to compare connectivity across repositories.

name: reverse-spectral-library-search
description: Use when you have MS1-only LC-MS or imaging MS data (mzML/mzXML or imzML) that lack DDA MS/MS files, and you want level 2/3 structural metabolite annotations by leveraging in/post-source fragment ions against an indexed MS/MS library.

name: reversed-phase-liquid-chromatography-data-comparison
description: Use when you have paired RPLC datasets (two analytical runs or configurations sharing detected compounds) with retention order data and configuration metadata (eluent pH, organic-phase modifier/percentage, temperature), and need to identify which chromatographic factor drives retention-order.

name: rf-pulse-time-evolution-operator-computation
description: Use when simulating MRS metabolite basis sets with repeated shaped pulses (e.g. PRESS/MEGA-PRESS/HERMES/HERCULES with editTp 14 ms or 20 ms) and per-sample propagator recalculation is the dominant runtime cost.

name: rgb-principal-component-image-compositing
description: Use when you have a centroided MSI peak matrix (e.g. rMSIproc .zip) and need an exploratory, per-pixel spatial visualization of dominant variance sources — e.g. to compare data quality before vs after peak filtering or cleaning.

name: rhamnolipid-fragment-mz-annotation
description: Use when a molecular-networking component of rhamnolipid or homologous lipid MS/MS spectra (positive mode, [M+Na]+ fragments) must be interpreted by annotating diagnostic fragment peaks and checking which shifted homolog peaks the MMSA multiple alignment failed to capture.

name: rhea-reaction-protein-linkage
description: Use when an experimentally annotated lipid list (e.g. 131 shorthand lipid abbreviations) must be linked to biochemical reactions (Rhea) and protein entries (UniProtKB) to enable downstream pathway/network integration.

name: ridge-penalized-cox-proportional-hazards-modeling
description: Use when metabolomics samples have patient survival times and event indicators and the goal is prognosis prediction from pathway-level features (e.g., 67 NCI breast tumor samples × 536 metabolites reduced to PDS features).

name: riemann-sum-peak-area-approximation
description: Use when a detected mass trace in centroided LC-MS data has been bounded around its chromatographic apex and you need a robust feature-level intensity from the summed peak signals.

name: right-tailed-fisher-exact-enrichment-testing
description: Use when you have a list of metabolites of interest, a collection of pathway compound sets, and a background set, and need per-pathway enrichment p-values to identify significantly enriched pathways (SEPs).

name: ring-cleavage-fragmentation-implementation
description: Use when modifying or extending CFM-ID-style fragmentation graphs to model ring cleavage, or when predicted MS/MS spectra must exclude chemically unstable ring-cleavage intermediate fragments.

name: rise-perturbation-saliency-mapping
description: Use when you have a trained CNN ensemble on raw LC-MS .npy grids (e.g. 341×341 RT×m/z arrays) and need per-class metabolite contribution heatmaps or to test whether unannotated metabolite signals carry classification-relevant information.

name: rise-saliency-heatmap-generation
description: Use when you have a trained DeepMSProfiler ensemble (e.g., 10 DenseNet121 runs on raw .npy LC-MS spectra) and need to visualize which metabolite signal regions contribute to each class (cancer/nodule/healthy) before network mapping.

name: risk-index-computation
description: Use when prioritizing chemicals that have both exposure estimates (e.g., SEEM) and predicted toxicity data (e.g., ToxPi scores from ToxCast), and you need a combined risk-based ranking.

name: rmse-accuracy-benchmarking-across-correction-methods
description: Use when you have simulated or spike-in labeled metabolite data with known theoretical enrichment and need to quantify which natural-abundance/resolution correction method (MDT, ULS, NRE/IsoCor, uncorrected FAM) recovers enrichment most accurately.

name: rmse-aggregation-across-scenarios
description: Use when comparing multiple Meff estimation methods across a factorial grid of simulation scenarios against a gold standard, to quantify which method/matrix combination (e.g., DisCo vs PrsCo) yields the lowest RMSE per cell.

name: rmse-correlation-method-benchmarking
description: Use when multiple NMR spectral deconvolution/quantification methods must be compared on identical spectra and a manual-annotation reference exists, so reconstruction quality can be scored with RMSE and Pearson correlation per metabolite cluster.

name: rmse-imputation-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing imputation algorithms for metabolomics or other high-dimensional data with missing values arising from both below-limit-of-detection (MNAR) and random technical loss (MAR), and you need a quantitative RMSE ranking.

name: rna-chemical-shift-prediction
description: Use when assigned RNA chemical shifts and a 3D RNA structure (PDB coordinates) are available and per-atom-type predicted shifts for 1H, 13C, or 15N are needed, e.g. for assignment validation or NMR structure assessment.

name: rna-seq-dataset-curation

name: rna-seq-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when raw RNA-seq data (SRA run accessions or FASTQ files) or a gene/miRNA/isoform count matrix must be turned into a ranked list of differentially expressed features between phenotypes (e.g. TNBC vs other BC subtypes) as part of a multi-omics workflow.

name: rna-seq-replicate-reproducibility-analysis
description: Use when you have read counts or rank lists for the same transcript/gene set from two replicate RNA-seq experiments (within-lab or between-lab, e.g. SEQC comparisons) and need to quantify reproducibility with error control at a target mFDR such as alpha = 0.01.
tools: Python (NumPy/pandas implementation of the closed-form MaRR estimator)

name: rna-seq-sample-outlier-detection
description: Use when an RNA-Seq or expression dataset with sample metadata (condition, organ, tumor status) needs a QC pass to confirm that within-condition samples are consistent and to flag outlier samples before differential expression analysis.

name: rnn-language-model-training-on-smiles
description: Use when a set of preprocessed, canonicalized SMILES is ready and you need to train one or more RNN generators per train/test fold (e.g. DeepMet-style pre-training then HMDB fine-tuning with early stopping).

name: rnn-sequence-probability-scoring
description: Use when you need to isolate the contribution of the modified Platt re-ranking step by ranking MSNovelist de novo candidates purely by RNN decoder sequence probability on MS2 spectra (GNPS or GNPS-OK), e.g. for ablation or benchmarking.

name: ro-crate-fair-digital-object-packaging

name: robust-additive-model-fitting
description: Use when a raw metabolomics intensity matrix (compounds x samples, run-ordered) contains QC injections and shows signal drift, batch effects, or occasional extreme intensities that would bias QC-sample-based smoothers like QC-RLSC or QC-RSC.

name: robust-gam-signal-drift-correction
description: Use when an unnormalized LC-MS metabolomics intensity matrix shows signal drift or batch effects over run order, contains occasional disproportionately high/low metabolite intensities (outliers), and QC plus replicate samples are available to guide and evaluate normalization.

name: robust-linear-regression-residual-backtransformation
description: Use when raw UK Biobank NMR metabolomics field data shows technical variation attributable to sample degradation time, shipping plate well position, or spectrometer drift, and corrected biomarker concentrations are needed before genetic or epidemiological analysis.

name: robust-regression-biweight-reweighting
description: Use when normalizing metabolomics intensity data exhibiting signal drift over injection order and occasional outlying compound intensities (outliers) that would deteriorate QC-based normalization and downstream differential abundance testing.

name: robust-smoother-fitting-loess-rlm
description: Use when a metabolomics acquisition shows run-order-dependent signal drift within a batch, and a metabolite-by-sample log2 intensity matrix with run-order annotations is available to fit a drift correction smoother.

name: roc-auc-average-precision-evaluation
description: Use when comparing gene-cluster detection methods (e.g., a trained deep-learning detector vs. ClusterFinder HMMs) on genomes with known BGC annotations and you need area-under-ROC-curve and average-precision metrics over bootstrap resamples.

name: roc-auc-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when two or more BGC detectors must be quantitatively compared on labeled positives (e.g., 65 experimentally validated BGCs or MIBiG clusters) and negative regions, using per-domain or per-cluster prediction scores.

name: roc-auc-blind-validation-evaluation
description: Use when a binary classifier (e.g., qualified vs unqualified LC or MS QC labels from DIA features) must be evaluated on held-out blinded data and reported as a single ROC AUC per model.

name: roc-auc-curve-computation
description: Use when evaluating a binary bioactivity classifier (e.g., DPPH high vs low activity) that outputs class probabilities, and you need ROC-AUC plus accuracy/precision/recall/F1 to compare CNN vs Random Forest baselines.

name: roc-auc-evaluation
description: Use when a trained formula-prediction model emits multiple candidate formulas per spectrum and you need to quantify how well a confidence score discriminates correct from incorrect candidates (ROC AUC) on a held-out MS/MS test split.

name: roc-auc-evaluation-clinical-biomarker
description: Use when a trained MS-feature-based classifier (e.g., HCC early-recurrence SVM) must be independently tested on a held-out cohort to reproduce or report a ROC/AUC generalization metric.

name: roc-auc-evaluation-of-surrogate-scores
description: Use when metabolomics-based surrogate scores (e.g. for diabetes) have been projected from Nightingale Health 1H-NMR metabolomics and the corresponding binary phenotypic variables are available to benchmark local AUCs against LOBOV reference performance.

name: roc-auc-metabolite-retrieval-assessment
description: Use when you have a set of generated structures with sampling frequencies and need to quantify how well that frequency signal retrieves withheld or newly-discovered metabolites (ROC AUC, enrichment, hypergeometric p-value).

name: roc-auc-metric-computation
description: Use when a trained classifier (e.g. massNet's sigmoid output layer) emits per-spectrum class probabilities for labeled normal/tumor MSI spectra and you must report ROC AUC, confusion matrix, accuracy, and runtime.

name: roc-auc-model-evaluation
description: Use when a longitudinal metabolomics dataset has a two-class outcome label (e.g. COVID-19 recovered vs. deceased) and the goal is classifier performance quantified by ROC/AUC plus feature-importance ranking.

name: roc-auc-model-validation
description: Use when a labeled metabolomics feature table (e.g. 234 CRC/PolyP/HC serum samples) must be split into train/test sets, modeled with RF and elastic net, and its discriminative power reported as ROC AUC values.

name: roc-auc-performance-evaluation
description: Use when you have a list of candidate structures filtered by predicted-vs-experimental ΔCCS and a known set of true annotations, and need to quantify threshold-dependent discrimination via ROC AUC.

name: roc-auc-performance-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating a binary LC-MS peak classifier that emits true/false peak probability scores, by computing ROC/AUC on held-out calibration and test sets or by tracing performance versus training-set size.

name: roc-auc-ranking-analysis
description: Use when you have per-feature ROC AUC values (e.g. one AUC per metabolite with 95% CIs from an OPLS-DA model) and need to verify that a multivariate pattern or panel outperforms every individual feature.

name: roc-based-filtering-evaluation
description: Use when an annotation-filtering step (e.g., ΔCCS 2.8% threshold at varying ppm mass tolerances) must be quantified as retained-correct-annotation vs. filtered-candidate trade-offs across mass windows.

name: roc-criterion-threshold-application
description: Use when similarity scores from longitudinal fragment profiling (multi-collision-energy MS/MS matched against an in-house spectral library) must be converted into identification calls via ROC-derived thresholds, or when verifying match rates under a loosened criterion.
tools: Jaccard similarity algorithm (optimized for longitudinal profiling)

name: roc-curve-analysis
description: Use when a binary filter (e.g. RT-error agreement) must be tuned to a threshold that maximizes true-positive retention while quantifying false-identity removal, with ROC curves built via scikit-learn.

name: roc-curve-auc-analysis
description: Use when you have per-compound ranked candidate structure lists with a known correct structure and want to quantify whether a score (e.g. COSMIC confidence score or tool hit score) separates correct from incorrect annotations.

name: roc-curve-auc-evaluation
description: Use when a supervised classification model (e.g. OPLS-DA in SIMCA) produces cross-validated scores that must be converted into ROC curves and AUC values with bootstrap confidence intervals to report diagnostic performance.

name: roc-curve-computation
description: Use when two binary signal/noise classifiers on labeled synthetic mass-spectrometry windows (e.g., LSH vs. intensity thresholding) must be compared by receiver operating characteristic performance.

name: roc-curve-evaluation
description: Use when a trained binary classifier on metabolite reaction-pair (RP vs. non-RP) predictions needs held-out performance evaluation via ROC analysis, threshold selection, and AUC reporting.

name: roc-curve-performance-evaluation
description: Use when multiple peak-curation strategies (e.g., active-learning scores, CV-of-QC-peak-area filters, NeatMS) must be ranked by how well their scores separate manually annotated true peaks from artifacts.

name: roc-curve-visualization
description: Use when two weighted risk scores must be compared for predictive accuracy of a time-to-event outcome with right censoring — e.g. biomarker vs conventional scores for 5-/10-year all-cause mortality in a cohort like FINRISK 1997.

name: roc-curve-visualization
description: Use when a binary lipid-biomarker classifier (e.g., LightGBM on RF-selected featured lipids) has produced predicted probabilities for case/control cohorts and you must quantify and visualize discrimination per cohort, as in reproducing Fig. 5c.

name: roc-cutoff-based-match-calling
description: Use when query MS/MS spectra (e.g. Exploris 480, 150 CP and 134 CN modes) must be scored against a multi-collision-energy reference library and a binary match/no-match decision is needed using validated Figure 2 cutoff thresholds.

name: roc-endpoint-annotation-rate-analysis
description: Use when you have confidence-scored structure candidates from multiple spectral conditions (e.g. 10/20/40 eV, merged) and need to benchmark how many correct hits each condition recovers at a given annotation rate threshold.

name: roc-precision-recall-curve-analysis
description: Use when comparing NMR preprocessing/summarization methods (peak-picking-then-grouping vs binning vs alignment+binning) on case-vs-control spectra and you need ROC and Precision-Recall curves as the performance metric.

name: roc-separation-evaluation-binary-variables

name: roc-threshold-optimization
description: Use when a trained binary classifier outputs probability scores for LC-MS peak groups and you need to characterize discriminative performance and pick an operating point.

name: roc-threshold-optimization
description: Use when candidate identities from accurate mass search (e.g. 10 ppm HMDB search) must be filtered or ranked by predicted-vs-experimental RT error, and you need an objective error-threshold choice.

name: roc-threshold-optimization-for-spectral-matching
description: Use when establishing identification criteria (similarity-score thresholds) for MS/MS spectral matching of isomer pairs, e.g., computing I/N-ratio ROC cutoffs and sensitivity/specificity across CP, CN, AP, AN ionization modes in a spectral database like CQMD.

name: roc-threshold-sensitivity-specificity-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking spectral similarity algorithms on isomer vs non-isomer pairs across multiple collision energies (13 individual NCEs or stepped NCE 20/40/60%) and you need threshold-based sensitivity/specificity figures to set identification criteria.

name: roi-based-targeted-metabolite-fitting

name: rolling-window-modulation-segmentation

name: rplc-dataset-benchmark-evaluation

name: s3-object-class-validation
description: Use when rawrr::readSpectrum or rawrr::readChromatogram has returned objects from a Thermo Fisher .raw file and you must confirm their class (rawrrSpectrum, rawrrSpectrumSet, rawrrChromatogram(Set)) and internal integrity before analysis or reporting.

name: s3-object-design-for-mass-spectrometry-data
description: Use when implementing an R package or pipeline that reads Thermo Fisher Orbitrap .raw files via the vendor RawFileReader API and must parse exchanged m/z/intensity tuples and scan headers into validated S3 objects for downstream R analysis.

name: s3-object-parsing-from-file-io
description: Use when an R workflow shells out to rawrr.exe (or another vendor-API wrapper) that writes spectral or chromatographic results to a temporary location on disk, and those files must be read back and structured into typed S3 objects for downstream analysis or plotting.

name: s4-class-implementation-in-r
description: Use when building an R data object that must hold a feature × sample metabolomics expression matrix together with sample and variable metadata that remain dimension-consistent whenever samples or features are removed.

name: s4-object-construction-in-r
description: Use when measured omics data (samples in rows, variables in columns) plus its sample metadata and variable metadata must be assembled into a single validated S4 object in R/struct for downstream model_train/model_predict workflows.

name: s4-object-oriented-programming-in-r
description: Use when implementing new statistical methods (e.g. mean centring, PCA) as reusable R objects whose inputs, outputs and documentation must be standardized and composable into pipelines.

name: s4-slot-parameter-access
description: Use when implementing a new struct model object in R (e.g. a PCA or mean-centring template) and you need parameters defined as entity objects with metadata, then read back via P$number_components or param_obj(P,'number_components')$description.

name: s9-incubation-metabolomics-group-comparison
description: Use when raw MS1 LC-HRMS data from enzymatic (S9) incubation experiments with matched heat-inactivated controls need differential feature screening to isolate biotransformation-derived metabolites.

name: saga-boundary-value-inverse-problem-optimization
description: Use when fitting a nonlinear moiety/deconvolution model to mass spectrometry isotopologue profiles (e.g. UDP-GlcNAc 13C timecourses) requires solving a boundary-value inverse problem where local optimizers are unreliable and many perturbation models must be compared.

name: saga-genetic-algorithm-fitting
description: Use when deconvoluting MS-measured isotopologue profiles (single or multiple isotope tracers, e.g. 13C UDP-GlcNAc timecourses) into moiety abundances, or when fitting parameters of a moiety model that requires stochastic global optimization.

name: saga-hybrid-optimization-implementation
description: Use when optimizing parameters of moiety models against mass spectrometry isotopologue timecourses (e.g., 13C UDP-GlcNAc data) where the nonlinear deconvolution problem requires a hybrid GA/annealing search rather than a single optimizer.

name: saga-stochastic-global-optimization-replicated-runs
description: Use when fitting a stochastic global optimizer (SAGA) to isotopologue/moiety model parameters and you need parameter uncertainty, i.e. distributions over repeated runs rather than one -fit value.

name: salmon-quantification-ingestion
description: Use when RNA-seq transcript-level quantification files (Salmon quant.sf) are available and the goal is isoform-level differential expression plus isoform switch detection and functional annotation, as in the MOI isoform sub-workflow.

name: salmonella-carriage-class-comparison-mapping
description: Use when reproducing or auditing class-comparison p-values from supervised OPLS-DA models of GCxGC-TOFMS plasma metabolite profiles — specifically the five comparisons (p = 0.0031, 2.8e-06, 3.1e-05, 3.7e-04, 0.07) reported in Table 1 of the carriage study.

name: salt-ion-smiles-disambiguation
description: Use when a library spectrum's SMILES is a salt (e.g. 'C1=NC2=NC=NC(=C2N1)N.Cl'), the parent mass is ambiguous, and you want to keep the spectrum rather than discard it during annotation repair.

name: salt-stripping-and-neutralization
description: Use when a compound metadata table (template-format columns with structure fields such as SMILES) contains salts, counter-ions or unneutralized molecules that must be harmonized before descriptor computation and database lookups.

name: salt-stripping-fragment-parent
description: Use when standardizing SMILES annotations attached to MS/MS spectra and records may contain salts, solvates, or counterion components that must be stripped to a single fragment parent before further structure harmonization.

name: sam-to-sorted-bam-processing
description: Use when metagenomic/metatranscriptomic FASTQ reads have been aligned to representative gene cluster (MGC/GCF) reference sequences with Bowtie2 and the resulting SAM output must be converted to leftmost-coordinate-sorted BAM for downstream counting and RPKM/coverage computation.

name: same-superclass-specificity-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking network-propagation annotation (e.g. MetDNA3/MrnAnnoAlgo3) across alternative knowledge-driven topologies, to test whether higher connectivity improves or degrades propagation specificity and decoy-based accuracy/FDR.

name: sample-annotation-integration
description: Use when the input is a metabolomics dataset downloaded from Metabolomics Workbench or MetaboLights (processed data matrix plus sample/metabolite annotation tables) and it must be assembled into a single annotated container for maplet statistical pipelines.

name: sample-annotation-integration
description: Use when a lipidomics dataset (Skyline CSV export or numerical matrix) needs its clinical/group metadata merged in before normalization, de_analysis, or plotting — e.g. linking diet groups to Skyline-exported samples.

name: sample-by-feature-matrix-construction
description: Use when raw NMR metabolomics data (fid, 1r, acqu/acqus files) from a repository study must be converted into a binned sample-by-variable matrix with a fixed spectral resolution (1000 columns) for tools like MetaboAnalyst.

name: sample-class-mapping-for-qc-filters
description: Use when a feature table from LC-MS untargeted metabolomics must be curated with QC filters (RSD, D-ratio, blank subtraction, LOESS drift correction) and sample types are not yet encoded as classes.

name: sample-clustering-analysis
description: Use when a SummarizedExperiment of preprocessed lipid abundances (from LipidSearch, LIQUID, or Metabolomics Workbench input) needs unsupervised sample grouping as part of an exploratory lipidomics analysis, e.

name: sample-coordinate-table-export
description: Use when dbnorm's unsupervised diagnostics (PCA/scree plots) have been run on log2-scaled metabolomics data and you need the numeric per-sample PC scores exported to CSV to document or validate batch-effect clustering, e.g. samples colored by analytical batch levels.

name: sample-design-metadata-annotation
description: Use when you have a wide-format metabolomics feature table (samples as columns, features as rows) and need to attach sample-class annotations (e.g. blank vs treatment group) from a design file before running QC or statistics.

name: sample-filtering-threshold-tuning
description: Use when an aligned X data matrix (peaks × samples) from DIMS or LC-MS processing contains sparse peaks, and low-prevalence features must be removed before normalization, imputation, and statistical analysis.

name: sample-group-annotation-of-heatmap-columns
description: Use when input is an omics/gene expression matrix CSV (e.g. heatmap_test.csv) plus a sample-group annotation CSV (e.g. group_info.csv) and the goal is a publication-ready clustered heatmap with columns annotated by sample group.

name: sample-group-colored-batch-qc-visualization
description: Use when a batch of raw MS runs (LC-MS, LC-IMS-MS, or direct infusion; DDA or DIA) needs an omics-agnostic global QC overview, and you want a PCA view of MS1-derived time-vs-m/z images colored by sample group to spot batch outliers or group-separating trends.

name: sample-group-ion-frequency-analysis
description: Use when QC of MS1 data is needed but no user-specified target/reference ions exist, so abundant ions that recur per sample group must be selected automatically for tracking.

name: sample-group-outlier-detection
description: Use when a batch of raw MS runs (Thermo .raw, Agilent 'd', Bruker 'd', mzML) has been processed to extract peak metrics (mass error, retention time error, arrival time error) for auto-tracked and user-specified ions and you need to flag which individual runs are anomalous per sample group.

name: sample-group-scatter-plot-visualization
description: Use when a wide-format metabolomics feature table with a sample-design file (treatment groups) needs per-sample visualization in PC space to reveal group clustering or separation.

name: sample-grouping-annotation-plotting
description: Use when you have a vsn-normalized MultiAssayExperiment (MetaboDiff 'met' object) and need an unsupervised check of whether sample groups separate metabolome-wide, before any differential testing.

name: sample-id-unique-assignment
description: Use when generating acquisition sequence files from a plate-based metadata sheet where multiple wells or plates could collide on identifiers, and downstream Xcalibur file names must be unambiguous.

name: sample-information-table-normalization
description: Use when preparing a sample-information/metadata table (e.g. 3DMouse_duodenum_metadata.txt from MSV000083437) before uploading to MassIVE or submitting a GNPS networking job, to guarantee schema conformance.

name: sample-level-data-normalization
description: Use when raw metabolomics concentration matrices (e.g., introgression-line tomato pericarp profiles) are loaded and must be normalized per sample and per metabolite before missing-value imputation and pairwise Pearson correlation networks.

name: sample-level-outlier-filtering-metabolomics
description: Use when a Nightingale-format 1H-NMR metabolomics matrix (CSV/TSV) must be quality-controlled per sample before computing metaboAge, surrogate clinical variables, or published clinical scores with MiMIR.

name: sample-metadata-attachment
description: Use when data arrive as two separate CSVs (a features matrix and a target/metadata file) that must be combined into one covariate-annotated analysis object (e.g. MSnSet) before preprocessing or statistics.

name: sample-metadata-derivation-from-column-headers
description: Use when a metabolomics feature table (csv or Excel, features in rows / samples in columns) originates from XCMS, MS-DIAL, MZmine, Compound Discoverer, or Progenesis QI and sample metadata must be attached before upload to MetaboReport.

name: sample-metadata-extraction-from-metabolomics-sheets
description: Use when the input is a platform vendor metabolomics workbook or export (Excel sheets such as Metabolon 'OrigScale', Nightingale v1) and the sample annotation (batch, sample_id, run_day) must be separated from raw abundance data for downstream QC.

name: sample-metadata-graph-storage
description: Use when sample metadata records from SMetaS/MetaS need relationships beyond tabular columns — e.g. co-culture links — that a fixed 'is a' table cannot express as first-class relations.

name: sample-metadata-interoperability-analysis
description: Use when evaluating how metabolomics repositories or metadata standardizers (e.g., ReDU, MetaboLights, Metabolomics Workbench, SMetaS) design sample-level metadata fields, to judge whether programmatic meta-analysis via string equality is feasible.

name: sample-metadata-standardization
description: Use when a metabolomics study's sample metadata is freetext (e.g. zeroTimeEvent, drugName, drugDoseUnit columns) and terms must be mapped to fixed vocabularies, with the output feeding a study submission, repository deposit, or downstream pipeline.

name: sample-metadata-stratification-gf-vs-spf
description: Use when you have a GNPS molecular networking job (spectra .mgf plus edges file) with sample metadata distinguishing treatment groups and need to retain spectra from one group while removing spectra network-connected to another.

name: sample-metadata-table-construction
description: Use when preparing a GNPS FBMN/IIMN upload from UmetaFlow outputs and the quantification table needs a matching sample metadata file derived from `dataset.tsv`.

name: sample-metadata-template-generation
description: Use when a metabolomics submission workflow needs a blank sample-metadata template (one row per sample, one column per selected attribute) for users to fill with freetext terms prior to vocabulary standardization.

name: sample-outlier-flagging-sd-threshold
description: Use when a raw metabolomics data matrix (e.g. Metabolon OrigScale sheet or dummy_data.csv) needs sample-level outlier detection before analysis, and PCA-based SD-threshold flagging of samples on top PCs is desired.

name: sample-quality-control-outlier-detection
description: Use when a lipidomics experiment (e.g. a LipidomicsExperiment from Metabolomics Workbench or Skyline export) needs QC screening before downstream analysis and suspect samples must be identified and removed.

name: sample-quality-metric-computation
description: Use when raw (un)targeted metabolomics data (e.g. Nightingale NMR or Metabolon exports) must be characterized with sample- and feature-level QC metrics before applying user-defined exclusion thresholds.

name: sample-row-alignment-across-datasets
description: Use when two or more normalized, transformed, and scaled metabolomics tables — one per analytical platform — must be merged into a single integrated dataset in Viime and the sample rows need to correspond to the same biological samples across the merged blocks.

name: sample-sequence-distribution-verification
description: Use when an intra-batch randomized injection sequence has just been generated (block randomization or optimized block randomization) and must be checked for consecutive same-group runs and even group distribution before LC/GC-MS injection.

name: sample-similarity-network-construction
description: Use when multi-omics feature tables for the same samples (e.g., methylation betas and metabolite intensities) must be integrated into a single sample-by-sample similarity network to identify subject subgroups via clustering.

name: sample-size-scaling-curve-analysis
description: Use when you need to quantify how a data-processing tool's CPU time and memory scale with sample number, or to benchmark one metabolomics pipeline against another (e.g. asari vs XCMS) on identical subsets of a public dataset.

name: sample-size-weighted-effect-combination
description: Use when the same feature pairs have Pearson correlation coefficients measured in multiple studies, each with its own sample size, and a single combined fixed/random-effects estimate per pair is needed.

name: sample-size-weighted-meta-analysis
description: Use when contributing studies report only aggregate statistics (p-value, fold-change, sample size) per compound and you need to combine them into a single combined p-value, fold-change, and regulation direction per compound.

name: sample-specific-cluster-identification-msi
description: Use when pre-processing a multi-sample MALDI MSI dataset and you need to automatically flag samples whose spectra deviate from the multi-sample spectral similarity structure, without manual inspection.

name: sample-wise-matrix-normalization
description: Use when MEMO MS2 fingerprint matrices built from different MS platforms or acquisition batches must be made comparable prior to distance computation, PCoA ordination, or PERMANOVA testing.

name: sample-wise-metabolomics-data-organization
description: Use when ingesting an externally published LC-MS2 dataset (e.g., MSV000093464 from MassIVE) whose .mzML, .mgf, feature quantification tables, and metadata must be organized per sample before ENPKG graph building.
tools: Open Tree of Life (ott3.5) taxo enhancer

name: sample-wise-metabolomics-workflow-reproducibility
description: Use when a task requires regenerating or validating the ENPKG knowledge graph from deposited LC-MS/MS DDA data (e.g. MassIVE MSV000087728), or when reproducing sample-level feature detection, annotation, and RDF integration figures.

name: sample-wise-scaling-normalization
description: Use when a log-transformed, missing-value-imputed metabolomics featuredata matrix (samples as rows, metabolites as columns) needs sample-wise scaling normalization, or when one of sum, median, mean, or reference-vector normalization is required.

name: sampling-area-overlap-normalization-to-per-cell-molecular-assignment
description: Use when MALDI-imaging MS data (.imzML/.ibd/.RAW/.UDP) from a laser-ablation experiment on cultured cells must be converted into per-cell molecular profiles, i.e. when ablation marks must be linked to segmented cells to build a spatio-molecular matrix.

name: sampling-frequency-perturbation-testing
description: Use when a concentration-inference method validated on dense, noiseless time-course metabolomics data must be stress-tested against realistic acquisition conditions — i.e., fewer sampled timepoints and noisy relative-abundance measurements with defined CoV.

name: sampling-temperature-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when you need to test whether a generative molecular-structure decoder's reported benchmark metrics depend on the sampling temperature hyperparameter, e.g. reproducing Table 8 of the MS-BART paper.

name: satterthwaite-moment-matching
description: Use when a kernel machine score test needs a null p-value: the quadratic-form statistic Q's null distribution must be approximated by Satterthwaite moment-matching as a scaled chi-square c·χ²_ν.

name: saturated-peak-exclusion
description: Use when fitting standard-curve regressions (constant/linear/quadratic) or QC-RLSC batch-effect corrections in MRMQuant, and some calibration points or BQC peaks may be saturated with unreliable abundances.

name: saturation-repair-peak-reconstruction
description: Use when LC-IM-MS raw/profile-level data (e.g. Agilent .d TOF files) contain high-abundance ions with truncated intensity profiles due to detector saturation, and accurate isotopic distributions or monoisotopic peak heights are needed downstream.

name: savitzky-golay-chromatogram-smoothing
description: Use when targeted LC–MS ion chromatograms (RT and intensity vectors) are noisy and peak borders must be located reliably before integration, as in TARDIS's targeted peak border detection workflow.

name: savitzky-golay-peak-smoothing
description: Use when you need to smooth noisy extracted ion chromatograms from mzXML/mzML LC-MS metabolomics data before peak detection and per-peak quality metrics (MCQ, asymmetry factor, FWHM) are computed.

name: savitzky-golay-smoothing-of-chromatographic-signals
description: Use when EICs extracted from mzML/mzXML LC-MS standard-mixture runs contain baseline drift or jagged peaks that must be corrected and smoothed before computing per-peak quality metrics like MCQ, max intensity, or asymmetry factor.

name: sbml-genome-scale-model-interrogation
description: Use when input is an SBML genome-scale metabolic model (possibly virus-integrated) and the goal is structural/dynamical analysis — chokepoints, bottlenecks, essential reactions, FVA flux bounds, or PPI-to-enzyme mapping for drug-target prediction.

name: sbml-metabolic-model-loading
description: Use when the input is an SBML genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. iHsaEC21 or the macrophage iAB-AMØ-1410 SARS-CoV-2 integrated models) that must be parsed and instantiated in Python before FBA/FVA/bottleneck analyses.

name: sbml-model-conversion-and-validation
description: Use when member models carry fixed lower/upper flux bounds that must scale with community member abundance, or when a COBRApy community model must be saved/loaded as SBML and remain fully reusable.

name: sbml-model-export
description: Use when a Reconstructor reconstruction (from FASTA, BLASTp hits, or an existing SBML) is complete or gap-filled and needs to be written out as a portable SBML GENRE for benchmarking or downstream COBRApy analysis.

name: sbml-model-flux-bound-refinement
description: Use when an SBML genome-scale metabolic model has default or inconsistent reaction bounds and downstream analyses (chokepoints, reversibility, bottlenecks) require bounds updated to steady-state FVA-computed ranges.

name: sbml-model-input-output
description: Use when a genome-scale community metabolic model built with PyCoMo (e.g. the three-species biogas model of D. vulgaris, M. hungatei, M. barkeri) must be persisted to, or reloaded from, an SBML file for sharing, reuse, or downstream COBRA analysis.

name: sbml-model-io-with-cobrapy
description: Use when you need to turn an annotated amino acid .fasta (or BLASTp output) into an SBML metabolic model and immediately interrogate it with COBRApy tools such as FBA or single_gene_deletion.

name: sbml-model-loading-and-analysis
description: Use when a compartmentalized community metabolic model (SBML from PyCoMo, e.g. the biogas community of D. vulgaris, M. hungatei, M. barkeri) must be reloaded and analysed for exchange fluxes or cross-feeding via COBRApy.

name: sbml-model-validation
description: Use when an SBML genome-scale metabolic model (e.g. from BioModels) must be assessed against community standards for annotation completeness, GPR coverage, and stoichiometric consistency before publication or reuse.

name: scaffold-based-dataset-splitting
description: Use when evaluating MS/MS spectral-prediction or retrieval models on NIST20-like datasets and you need a split that prevents highly similar scaffold-mates from leaking into the test set, making generalization across chemical classes a fair test.

name: scaffold-conditioned-de-novo-graph-generation
description: Use when you have an MS/MS spectrum plus a candidate scaffold (predicted or oracle) and need to generate full candidate molecular structures for top-k accuracy or Tanimoto-based evaluation.

name: scaffold-conditioned-markov-bridge-training
description: Use when building a spectra-conditioned de novo molecule generator whose output must contain a fixed Murcko scaffold subgraph, e.g. training on NIST23, CANOPUS, or MassSpecGym-style pickles of canonical SMILES and normalized MS/MS spectra.

name: scaffold-prediction-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating a mass-spectrometry scaffold retriever (e.g., contrastive-ranking models on NIST23, CANOPUS, or MassSpecGym pkl datasets) and you need a per-dataset accuracy for how often the true core scaffold is retrieved from ranked candidates.

name: scaffold-sidechain-combinatorial-search
description: Use when you have a target molecular weight (up to five decimal digits) from a mass spectrum of an unknown natural-product mixture and a scaffold database with sidechain probabilities, and need ranked candidate structures.

name: scaftig-length-filtering
description: Use when running MetaRon's 'ago' mode after IDBA assembly of paired-end shotgun reads, to discard scaftigs ≤ 500 bp prior to prodigal/MetaGeneMark gene prediction and proximon/operon identification.

name: scalability-curve-visualization
description: Use when you need to demonstrate or verify that a method's time and memory consumption increase approximately linearly with the number of spots/samples, e.g. reproducing efficiency figures for a VAE-based integration model.

name: scaled-t-likelihood-outlier-accommodation
description: Use when metabolomics intensities show run-order signal drift plus occasional extreme high/low outliers that would corrupt QC-sample-based normalization, or when pooled QC samples may be unrepresentative of biological samples.

name: scaling-method-selection-multivariate-data
description: Use when fitting a multivariate discriminant model (e.g., KODAMA-based PLS-DA) on a lipidomic intensity matrix at the lipid molecular species (LMS) level and a scaling scheme among Autoscaling, Pareto, or None must be chosen before validation.

name: scaling-normalization-of-metabolite-abundance-matrices
description: Use when a log-transformed featuredata matrix (samples as rows, metabolites as columns) shows sample-wide intensity differences—e.g. dilution or loading effects—and no QC samples or internal standards are needed for correction.

name: scan-filter-string-parsing
description: Use when a Thermo Fisher .raw file has been indexed via rawrr::readIndex and you need to classify scans by their filter string — e.g. to isolate targeted MS2 scans for a precursor like 487.2567@hcd27.00 and compute inter-scan deltas.

name: scan-frequency-quality-assessment
description: Use when Thermo RAW-derived .FT1/.FT2 SIP data need a pre-search QC pass: confirming mass-range coverage, TIC continuity, and whether precursor m/z distributions show the mass shifts expected from isotope labeling.

name: scan-number-metadata-linkage
description: Use when Thermo Fisher RAW files must yield per-scan peak arrays (m/z, intensity, resolution, noise, charge) that join to scan-header metadata by scan number for downstream or ML analysis.

name: scanorama-multi-omics-batch-correction
description: Use when assigning single-cell cluster/cell-type labels to per-cell IMC protein intensity tables spanning multiple imaging regions or patients, where batch effects must be removed before Leiden clustering.

name: scanpy-neighbor-graph-embedding
description: Use when spot-level feature matrices (transcript, metabolite, or fused multi-module) from a spatial omics pipeline are available and the goal is to quantify cluster counts or heterogeneity per view in an embedded space.

name: scatter-plot-confidence-interval-estimation
description: Use when you have paired chromatographic datasets with a per-pair agreement score (e.g. CCRS) and a continuous per-pair difference attribute (ΔpH, ΔF, Δtemperature), and you need to test and visualize whether that attribute explains replicability.

name: scc-gene-sharing-relatedness-validation
description: Use when validating hierarchical K-means grouping of predicted biosynthetic sub-clusters into sub-cluster families (SCFs) and clans (SCCs), where correctness is judged by gene-sharing relatedness within clans.

name: scheduled-precursor-list-construction
description: Use when a user has an MZmine-exported full-scan feature table (.csv with row ID, row m/z, row retention time, per-sample Peak area) from a dilution series and wants to build a targeted precursor list for scheduled fragmentation of ions missed in DDA mode.

name: schymanski-identification-level-assignment
description: Use when patRoon suspect screening or formula/compound annotation results (e.g. from MetFrag/SIRIUS/GenForm on LC-HRMS features) need automatic, reproducible Schymanski 1-5 confidence level assignment.

name: scib-integration-benchmark-scoring
description: Use when two or more integration methods (e.g. SpatialMETA, Seurat RPCA/CCA, scVI, scANVI, totalVI, Stabmap, scPoli, spaVAE, PCA) have produced latent embeddings of the same joint ST-SM AnnData and a fair, metric-based ranking of batch correction vs. biological conservation is needed.

name: scib-metric-aggregation-and-ranking
description: Use when you have joint embeddings from multiple integration methods (e.g. SpatialMETA, totalVI, MISO, SpatialGLUE) on the same ST-SM samples and need to quantitatively rank their integration quality.

name: scientific-figure-export
description: Use when rendering elemental images (e.g. 66Zn, 56Fe, 55Mn) for publication or interpretation, where colormap choice and scale/color bar accuracy must reflect laser and calibration parameters.

name: scientific-figure-export-jpg-pdf
description: Use when a mass-spectrometry QC pipeline (PeakQC/IonToolPack) must render per-sample or per-metric diagnostic plots to image files for reporting or archival, or when heatmap-style error summaries of anomalous MS runs and metrics are needed alongside CSV outputs.

name: scientific-task-formulation
description: Use when a research question must be converted into a concrete computational task with named tools, input formats (e.g. mzML, isotope-labeled LC-MS data), and verifiable outputs before any analysis is attempted.

name: scientific-task-formulation
description: Use when a research question about feature co-association (e.g., CLR scoring of MI networks to discount promiscuous features) must be formulated as a bounded, computable procedure with defined inputs, tools, and outputs before implementation.

name: scms-cell-phenotype-meta-learning-training
description: Use when SCMS metabolomics data (e.g., Single-probe profiles of melanoma cell pairs) are too limited for conventional deep learning and the goal is few-shot primary/metastatic cell phenotype classification via meta-learning.

name: scms-feature-matrix-construction
description: Use when raw single-probe SCMS spectra from cell experiments must be converted into a cleaned, normalized, aligned feature table (e.g., dataset.csv with cells × metabolite species) before machine learning classification or meta-learning.

name: scms-lipidomics-fold-change-analysis
description: Use when a peak-aligned, TIC-normalized SCMS lipid/metabolomics feature table must be screened for species differing between two cell phenotypes (e.g., primary vs metastatic) under control and drug-treated conditions to nominate biomarker candidates.

name: scms-noise-background-subtraction
description: Use when raw single-cell peak lists exported from Thermo Xcalibur must be denoised, debackgrounded, and TIC-normalized before peak alignment or PCA/machine-learning analysis of SCMS data.

name: scms-peak-ablation-significance-testing
description: Use when you have a trained meta-learning classifier (MetaPhenotype) on pretreated SCMS feature tables and need to select the small number of m/z species critical for phenotype classification, e.g. to overlay as bold dots on volcano plots.

name: score-distribution-summary-statistics
description: Use when a prediction tool outputs per-pair scores for a known-positive set and a random-negative set, and you must confirm the score separates the two distributions with medians/means and a U test.

name: score-distribution-visualization
description: Use when validating PSMs from proteomic SIP database search outputs (e.g., Sipros searches of .FT2 spectra) by comparing experimental and theoretical isotope envelopes, or when selecting a scoring function for partially 13C-labeled PSMs.

name: score-loading-plot-visualization
description: Use when a case-control lipidomic dataset has been scaled and fitted with a PLS-DA model and you need to visualize sample separation (score plot), variable contribution (loading plot), and cross-validated Accuracy/R2Y/Q2Y for the first five components.

name: score-normalization-to-unit-range
description: Use when combining annotation scores from multiple MS/MS annotation tools with an external additive term (e.g., taxonomic-distance bonuses) whose weights were optimized on a 0–1 score scale; without normalization the tools' incomparable score ranges dominate or are dominated by the added term.

name: score-percentile-threshold-analysis
description: Use when evaluating whether combining genomic–metabolomic link scoring functions (e.g. IOKR, standardised Metcalf/correlation) yields more validated links than individual scores, using percentile thresholds and pooled Fisher-style significance tests.

name: score-plot-interpretation-of-pca-results
description: Use when PCA has been run on a pretreated SCMS metabolomics feature table (e.g., single-cell peak matrices after TIC normalization and peak alignment) and you must assess cluster separation between phenotypes from the score plot.

name: score-table-csv-export
description: Use when an all-vs-all matchms Scores object (CosineGreedy over pre-filtered MGF spectra) must be reduced to a tabular record of significant pairs, skipping self-comparisons and keeping only pairs with at least 20 matching peaks.

name: scores-and-loadings-matrix-extraction
description: Use when an MPCA model has been fitted with m_prcomp on preprocessed two-dimensional chromatogram data and the score matrix or principal-component loading values must be exported as numeric CSVs rather than viewed as plots.

name: scoring-term-table-export
description: Use when a candidate list retrieved from PubChem/ChemSpider must be ranked with reference and patent information, i.e. when S_C_PCR and S_C_CCR scoring terms must be computed, max-normalized, and exported as a TSV for MetFrag scoring.

name: scoring-weight-parameter-optimization
description: Use when tuning metabCombiner's similarity-scoring weights (A for m/z, B for mapped retention time, C for abundance) before finalizing the combined feature table, using a training table of identified compounds shared between two datasets.

name: scree-plot-generation
description: Use when an SVD-based PCA has been fit on a centered (and optionally scaled) wide-format metabolomics feature matrix and you need to summarize explained variability per principal component as a plot for output alongside PCA scores and loadings.

name: screening-mode-diagnostic-plotting
description: Use when setting up a targeted LC-MS metabolomics/lipidomics assay in TARDIS and you need to verify, before peak detection, that each target's peak is actually visible within its expected m/z and RT window in QC runs.

name: screening-outcome-data-extraction
