description: Use when you have pixel-level DESI-MSI data over a tissue axis (e.g., .cdf or Matlab workspace files) and need per-sample m/z signature lists plus a pooled replicate-level unique signature set.

name: significance-asterisk-annotation
description: Use when bar-chart group comparisons of lipid features (classes, molecular species, or building blocks) need statistical significance encoded as asterisks, or when reproducing the barplot_statistics.csv output of LipidOne 2.0.

name: significance-flag-generation
description: Use when a wide-format metabolomics feature table plus a design file mapping samples to treatment groups needs per-feature ANOVA contrasts reduced to binary significance flags for downstream reporting or filtering.

name: significant-enriched-pathway-quantification
description: Use when running ORA perturbation simulations (background-set reduction, metabolite misidentification, DA-list changes) and you need a robust metric of how many enriched pathways are gained or lost across datasets.

name: significant-pathway-count-tabulation
description: Use when running right-tailed Fisher's exact ORA (scipy.stats.fisher_exact) on multiple candidate metabolite-of-interest lists or correction/alpha settings and you need to tabulate SEP counts to show how those choices affect enrichment outcomes.

name: silhouette-based-optimal-cluster-count-selection
description: Use when a table of statistically significant features (e.g. MB-VIP permutation p-value < 0.01) must be partitioned into correlation-based clusters and the cluster count k is unknown and must be chosen objectively.

name: silhouette-cluster-validation
description: Use when a pairwise spectral similarity/distance matrix exists (e.g. from MS2DeepScore or MS2/MS similarity) and you must choose how many k-medoids clusters to group LC-MS/MS features into, with no prior label or target K.

name: silhouette-score-cluster-evaluation
description: Use when selecting unsupervised segmentation parameters (e.g., t-SNE perplexity, learning rate, iteration count) or comparing search strategies, and an internal cluster-quality metric is needed to rank k-means segmentations of MSI pixel data.

name: silico-spectral-library-matching
description: Use when an unannotated empirical tandem MS spectrum must be matched against candidate molecules whose predicted spectra are available, and ranking accuracy (Top-1/Top-5/Top-10) or annotation confidence is the goal.

name: silver-cluster-mass-annotation
description: Use when building or validating a silver-cluster peak list for AgLDI MSI experiments — e.g. to benchmark rMSIcleanup's peak classification algorithm against a chemically defined set of positive and negative silver-related peaks.

name: silver-isotope-pattern-matching
description: Use when an Ag-sputtered AgLDI mass spectrometry imaging peak matrix contains unassigned low-m/z peaks that must be classified as matrix-related (Ag clusters/adducts) versus endogenous signals via isotopic-pattern matching.

name: sim-based-isotope-baseline-comparison
description: Use when you need to validate or contextualize isotope-pair identifications in MSI by comparing them against PCC and R2 SIM-based baselines from METASPACE and the rMSI package, including cases where baselines fail.

name: sim-stitch-direct-infusion-peak-picking
description: Use when processing direct infusion mass spectrometry (DIMS) FT-ICR data stored as .dat transient files organized in SIM windows (e.g. MTBLS79 DIMS_DATA) and you need a calibrated, stitched peak list across samples.

name: sim-window-mass-calibration-and-stitching
description: Use when processing FT-ICR direct infusion MS transients stored as Thermo .RAW/.dat files that have already been summed and apodized per SIM window, and the next step is calibrated m/z peak lists across all windows.

name: simd-accelerated-integer-compression
description: Use when compressing ordered, near-uniformly spaced numeric arrays (e.g. m/z values from MS spectra in mzML/vendor-converted data) where controllable precision (e.g. 3 dp for 10 ppm, 5 dp for 0.1 ppm) is acceptable and both size and decode speed matter.

name: similarity-algorithm-benchmarking
description: Use when you must compare spectral similarity metrics head-to-head on a spectral library search — e.g., deciding whether entropy similarity beats dot product or 40+ alternatives on NIST20/MassBank-style MS/MS spectra.

name: similarity-matrix-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when a local, quantitative read-out of the raw pairwise similarity matrix is needed around selected features — e.g. to tune similarity thresholds or complement partial network views of LC-MS/MS feature data.

name: similarity-matrix-to-distance-conversion
description: Use when a pairwise similarity matrix from unannotated tandem mass spectra comparisons (e.g. compareMS2 dot products) must be inverted into distances and aggregated per species to build a phylogenetic tree or quantify shared peptide content.

name: similarity-score-comparison-visualization
description: Use when you need to benchmark cross-language spectral similarity scoring on the same peak lists — comparing R Spectra cosine/dot-product scores against Python matchms scores — or to visualize score agreement per spectrum pair.

name: similarity-score-threshold-classification
description: Use when you must label each peak in an rMSIproc peak matrix as matrix-related or not, using isotope-pattern-based similarity scores (S1, S2) and a user threshold to separate matrix clusters from endogenous ions.

name: similarity-threshold-annotation-classification
description: Use when a predicted Morgan fingerprint bit string from an HSQC-based predictor must be compared against fingerprints of candidate structures from chemical databases such as PubChem to produce ranked, thresholded annotation results.

name: simpleitk-bspline-nonlinear-registration
description: Use when an initial affine (or manually landmarked) H&E-to-MSI alignment leaves residual local mismatch between the H&E foreground and the MSI tissue mask that must be corrected with a non-linear transform before overlaying histology onto mass spectrometry imaging data.

name: sims-spectral-total-ion-normalization
description: Use when raw TOF-SIMS (3D-SMF) pixel-by-peak intensity matrices must be normalized per pixel prior to pixel clustering or other downstream pixel-level metabolomic analysis.

name: simsiam-based-self-supervised-pipeline-integration
description: Use when you need low-dimensional, annotation-free representations of ion images from an MSI matrix for downstream colocalized-ion or isotope-ion identification tasks.

name: simsiam-contrastive-loss-implementation
description: Use when training a self-supervised encoder on ion images from mass spectrometry imaging, where two augmented views of each ion image must be mapped to representation vectors and collapse must be prevented via a stop-gradient contrastive loss.

name: simulated-annealing-temperature-schedule-configuration
description: Use when optimizing boundary-value inverse problems such as moiety model parameters, where genetic algorithm operators must be combined with an annealing temperature schedule to balance exploration and convergence.

name: simulated-data-validation
description: Use when you need an annotation-free accuracy estimate of a feature-matching method: simulate two LC–MS feature tables with known true pairs, run matching, and score match correctness, retention (e.g. 2682/2728), and precision (99.6%).

name: simulated-isotopologue-data-generation
description: Use when you need to assess how noise magnitude affects moiety model selection — e.g., tabulating whether the generating model ranks first by AICc as added-error sigma varies, or defining data-quality requirements for simulated 13C SIRM isotopologue datasets.

name: simulated-isotopologue-fam-generation
description: Use when benchmarking isotopic-enrichment correction methods (MDT, ULS, NRE/IsoCor, FAM-only) against a known ground-truth enrichment, requiring simulated labeled and unlabeled FAM inputs at a specified nominal resolution (e.g., 140,000).

name: simulated-measurement-noise-modeling
description: Use when benchmarking an annotation or ranking pipeline where true reference values exist but no real measured masses are available; noise must mimic instrument accuracy.

name: simulated-metabolomics-data-generation
description: Use when benchmarking or validating imputation algorithms on metabolomics data and ground-truth values are needed to compute RMSE/MLCI, or when a controlled MNAR+LOD/MAR missingness setting must be reproduced.

name: simulated-metagenome-read-generation
description: Use when a benchmark requires realistic paired-end shotgun reads from known reference genomes so pipeline outputs (e.g., operons) can be scored against curated per-genome truth annotations.

name: simulated-multi-omics-dataset-generation
description: Use when benchmarking integrative clustering methods on multi-dataset omic data and you need ground-truth labels across settings like similar datasets, noisy variables (sparse k-means variant), and datasets with different noise levels.

name: simulated-multidataset-clustering-generation
description: Use when benchmarking KLIC/COCA-style integrative consensus clustering on synthetic data with known true labels — e.g. to quantify ARI gains of combining kernels versus single-dataset clustering and to inspect learned kernel weights.

name: simulated-mzml-export
description: Use when a ViMMS 2.0 Environment run (TopNController DDA or AIF DIA simulation over generated chemicals) has finished and the resulting scan list must be persisted as a well-formed mzML document for downstream evaluation.

name: simulated-nmr-spectral-dataset-construction
description: Use when you need a ground-truth-controlled benchmark to compare NMR spectra processing methods (binning, alignment like CluPA/icoshift, or peak-based approaches) where real spectra lack known per-peak labels.

name: simulated-spectra-ground-truth-comparison
description: Use when evaluating quantification accuracy of NMR spectral deconvolution methods on simulated spectra where ground-truth metabolite concentrations are known and methods can be regressed against truth.

name: simulated-time-course-metabolomics-data-handling
description: Use when benchmarking inference of absolute concentrations from relative abundance time-course GC-MS data and ground-truth response factors are needed that cannot be measured experimentally.

name: simulated-transient-signal-generation
description: Use when evaluating or training a spectral reconstruction model (e.g. MEISTER-style deep-learning reconstruction) and controlled simulated MSI transients with known ground truth are needed.

name: simulated-versus-experimental-nmr-generalization-evaluation
description: Use when a model trained on simulated 1H and/or 13C NMR spectra must be evaluated on real experimental spectra, and the simulated-to-experimental accuracy gap needs to be quantified (e.g., top-15 exact-match rate ~33.0% vs 69.6% simulated).

name: simulation-benchmark-method-comparison
description: Use when you have simulated or sub-sampled high-dimensional metabolomics p-values plus competing correlation matrices (e.g., Pearson vs distance correlation) and need to benchmark eigen-analysis-based Meff estimation methods against a gold standard by RMSE.

name: simulation-dataset-generation
description: Reference for constructing a synthetic, fully observed metabolomics dataset with realistic covariance and simulated group differences when no complete ground-truth data exist for benchmarking imputation methods.

name: simulation-replicate-aggregation-power-tabulation
description: Use when estimating empirical power of a kernel machine score test (e.g., PaIRKAT with τ = 1) over repeated simulations in which a design factor—fraction of incorrect pathway edges or number of pathway metabolites—is systematically varied.

name: simulation-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when you must quantify how fast SMITER can synthesize a proteome-scale synthetic mzML (tens of thousands of peptides, thousands of MS2 scans) or verify that a simulated run meets a runtime and scan-count budget.

name: simulation-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when an MRS basis-set simulation pipeline has been accelerated (e.g. coherence filtering instead of EXORCYCLE phase cycling) and you need to quantify runtime savings while demonstrating spectral equivalence against a reference implementation.

name: simulation-study-reproduction
description: Use when a task requires reproducing or validating published kernel-association-test power results, specifically PaIRKAT's power-vs-SNR curves over graph-structure and pathway-knowledge scenarios.

name: single-cell-differential-abundance-testing
description: Use when you have a per-cell metabolomics matrix (e.g. MORPHnMOL.csv) with condition metadata and need to rank features by abundance shift between two cell populations, such as inflammatory vs benign steatotic states.

name: single-cell-feature-prevalence-filtering
description: Use when a single-cell SCMS peak matrix (e.g. imzML-derived peak lists of thousands of cells) contains sparse or noise-only m/z features, and you need prevalence-based pruning before clustering or cross-annotation.

name: single-cell-isotope-tracing-data-analysis
description: Use when MALDI imaging MS data paired with microscopy segmentation has been acquired after 13C6-glucose labelling and the goal is per-cell fatty-acid isotopologue distributions and uptake/synthesis fractions.

name: single-cell-isotopologue-data-normalization
description: Use when processing SpaceM single-cell MALDI imaging output (spatiomolecular adata per well) into quality-controlled, per-cell fatty acid isotopologue distributions ready for binomial labelling fits.

name: single-cell-leiden-clustering
description: Use when a per-cell spatio-molecular matrix (e.g. MORPHnMOL.csv with 29,738 hepatocytes across +FA, +FA+IL17A, +FA+IL17A+TPCA1 conditions) must be partitioned into discrete metabolic states without labels.

name: single-cell-metabolic-flux-estimation
description: Use when a single-cell expression matrix (rows = genes, columns = cells, raw or normalized counts, e.g. Melissa_full.csv) needs cell-wise predicted metabolic flux and metabolite variation outputs from the human M171 module model.

name: single-cell-metabolic-state-clustering
description: Use when a per-cell spatio-molecular matrix (normalized single-cell metabolomes with microscopy-derived phenotypic properties) needs to be partitioned into metabolic states, or when assessing whether such state assignments are robust to cell-filtering choices such as excluding co-sampling ablation.

name: single-cell-metabolomics-hierarchical-clustering
description: Use when you have pretreated SCMS single-cell metabolomics feature matrices (e.g., primary/metastatic melanoma cell pairs, untreated or vemurafenib-treated) and want a label-free baseline check of phenotype separability before training a classifier.

name: single-cell-metabolomics-matrix-preparation
description: Use when a raw single-cell metabolomics dataset (e.g. METASPACE annotations or an .rds single-cell matrix) must be reshaped into a metabolites-by-cells input matrix with condition labels before running S2IsoMEr ORA/MSEA.

name: single-cell-multiomic-joint-embedding
description: Use when a per-cell feature matrix contains paired protein and metabolite intensity blocks of unequal feature size and you need a joint low-dimensional embedding to compare reconstruction against single-modality VAE baselines.

name: single-cell-protein-feature-matrix-analysis
description: Use when a co-registered protein (IMC) and metabolite (TOF-SIMS) single-cell feature table is available and the goal is cell-population identification plus trajectory/pseudotime analysis of differentiation paths.

name: single-cell-protein-intensity-normalization
description: Use when you have a per-cell mean marker-intensity feature matrix from IMC single-cell segmentation spanning multiple imaging regions or patients, and you need comparable, normalized features for unsupervised cell-type clustering.

name: single-cell-proteomics-clustering
description: Use when you have a per-cell mean marker-intensity feature matrix from single-cell segmentation of multiplexed IMC protein images (multiple imaging regions or patients) and need to label every segmented cell with a cell-type cluster.

name: single-cell-proteomics-data-interpretation
description: Use when processed single-cell proteomics results (e.g., a ProteomeXchange dataset such as PXD037527) must be turned into reproducible figure panels that reproduce or match panels from a published study.

name: single-cell-proteomics-sample-metadata-mapping
description: Use when you have per-run feature lists (m/z, charge, RT, intensity) from single-cell DIA-MS runs and need to associate each feature file with its cell/sample identity before cohort-wide RT alignment and alignment-vs-identification benchmarking.

name: single-cell-quality-control-filtering
description: Use when single-cell readouts derived from SpaceM ablation-mark aggregation (h5ad/anndata objects) need QC prior to correlation, isotopologue, or uptake-fraction analysis, to remove poorly segmented or low-signal cells.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-imputation
description: Use when a sparse single-cell RNA-seq count matrix (especially 10x data, genes x cells) must be imputed before feeding the scFEA/FLUXestimator neural-network flux estimation on the M171 or Glucose-Glutamine module networks.

name: single-cell-spatial-map-visualization
description: Use when per-cell intensities and centroid coordinates are already extracted (notebook 04) and the goal is to visualize local metabolite competition or expression as a spatial map per imaging region relative to landmarks like CD31+ vessels.

name: single-cell-transcriptomics-predictive-modeling
description: Use when you have a trained multi-omics predictor's ranked top features and need to check whether those features show elevated feature importance in an independent dataset (bulk NCI60 or single-cell transcriptomics) beyond chance.

name: single-field-ccs-calibration
description: Use when you have single-field RapidFire-DTIMS-MS (or similar DTIMS) feature files plus IMS frame-metadata from many runs and need calibrated per-run CCS values, e.g. tracking CCS variance of a compound like protonated rotenone across thousands of SPE-IMS-MS plant-extract runs.

name: single-field-dtims-arrival-time-calibration
description: Use when calibrating single-field DTIMS arrival/drift times to CCS via external calibrants (Agilent tune-mix with known CCS values), especially when calibrant and sample runs differ in pressure/temperature.

name: single-sample-pathway-analysis-scoring
description: Use when molecular-level omics matrices need a common, interpretable scale for supervised integration — e.g. before fitting MB-PLS or a sklearn classifier on multi-omics COPDgene or COVID-19 data — to exploit coordinated pathway-level signals in low signal-to-noise scenarios.

name: single-step-ruv-batch-correction
description: Use when a multi-batch metabolomics abundance matrix (e.g. BioHEART-CT targeted metabolomics) contains embedded intra-batch and inter-batch replicates and you need a baseline batch-correction with RUV-III, or to benchmark against hierarchical normalisation.

name: single-thread-runtime-profiling
description: Use when comparing query speed of spectral-search modules across libraries of varying size, or when reproducing the LipidIN EQ (~2.3 µs/query, 10M-spectrum library) vs Flash Entropy (0.14 s/MS2, 1M library) timing claims under controlled single-thread CPU conditions.

name: single-tracer-13c-model-implementation
description: Use when reconstructing or replicating how the moiety_modeling package computes calculated relative isotopologue intensities (Ix,calc) from moiety state fractional abundances for a 13C single-tracer isotopologue profile.

name: single-versus-multi-tracer-deconvolution-comparison
description: Decision support for choosing between single- and multi-tracer SIRM isotopologue designs: when you need to know at what added-error standard deviation (σ) model selection via AICc ranking breaks down, or must assess data-quality requirements before measuring multi-tracer datasets.

name: sinusoidal-feature-embedding-implementation
description: Use when featurizing integer element counts of a chemical formula candidate into a fixed-length, non-negative vector for a neural scorer — e.g., before the Formula Transformer in MIST-CF or when replicating SCARF-style sinusoidal formula embeddings.

name: sinusoidal-phase-optimization
description: Use when AEMS .wiff raw data lacks explicit per-ejection timestamps and peaks from 384-well plate acoustic shots must be associated with ejection times before MRM or full-scan peak integration.

name: sip-labeled-psm-spectral-validation
description: Use when validating database-search PSM outputs from proteomic SIP experiments — e.g. unlabeled peptides at natural 13C abundance (~1.07%) or partially/fully 13C-labeled peptides (e.g. ~52%) — where theoretical fragment annotations must be visually confirmed on observed MS2 spectra.

name: sirius-baseline-comparison-evaluation
description: Use when a new MS/MS annotation or property-prediction model (e.g. fingerprint retrieval, fluorine detection, similarity) must be evaluated head-to-head against the established SIRIUS-based method on the same labeled test spectra.

name: sirius-classyfire-class-annotation
description: Use when ground-truth-labeled MS/MS spectra (e.g., prenylated flavonoid test sets from the AnnoMe repo) need an independent compound-class baseline from SIRIUS ClassyFire for comparison against user-defined classifiers.

name: sirius-commandline-workflow
description: Use when an MZmine3 feature table with representative MS/MS spectra must receive molecular formula and adduct annotations before downstream candidate retrieval, especially for positive-ion-mode metabolomics data where the original study provides no processed spectra.

name: sirius-formula-annotation
description: Use when you have deconvolved (or DDA) MS2 spectra from SWATH-MS untargeted metabolomics and need to assign molecular formulas to precursor/fragment peaks, or when benchmarking annotation success rate of DecoMetDIA output.

name: sirius-formula-candidate-enumeration
description: Use when you have an exact precursor mass from MS/MS data and need a database-independent candidate formula set (RDBE-plausible, C/H/N/O/P/S/Cl/Br/F elemental space) to score and re-rank with a downstream model.

name: sirius-formula-decomposition
description: Use when you have positive-mode MS/MS spectra (e.g., mzML exports) with an MS1 precursor exact mass and need a database-independent candidate formula list to feed MIST-CF scoring, or when benchmarking against SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID as in Table 2 of the MIST-CF paper.

name: sirius-in-silico-compound-annotation
description: Use when MS2 .mzML features remain structurally unannotated after spectral database dereplication (GNPS/HMDB/MassBank .rda matching) and ranked candidate structures with formulas and compound classes are needed per feature.

name: sirius-in-silico-compound-class-prediction
description: Use when unannotated MS/MS spectra from an untargeted metabolomics dataset sit inside a biologically coherent molecular-network subnetwork (e.g., a carnitine subnetwork) and need putative compound-class or structural assignment without a GNPS library match.

name: sirius-in-silico-formula-annotation
description: Use when molecular network nodes (e.g., from GNPS2 FBMN on MZmine .mgf/.csv inputs) have no spectral library match and no ChemWalker propagation, and a molecular-formula-level annotation is still needed.

name: sirius-molecular-formula-annotation
description: Use when you need a baseline formula/structure annotation rate for MS/MS query spectra (e.g., GMN anchor–suspect pairs) against a defined structure database such as bioDB.

name: site-localization-evaluation-scoring
description: Use when a ModiFinder run has produced a per-atom modification-site likelihood array and you need a single comparable quality score, or when benchmarking site-localization accuracy across depth settings or parameter sweeps.

name: site-of-metabolism-prediction-ranking
description: Use when enumerating ranked candidate structures for a suspect molecule: after PROXIMAL2 has generated derivatives from an anchor molecule by applying biotransformation rules, and you need to order them by reaction-center likelihood.

name: site-of-metabolism-ranking
description: Use when BAM/PROXIMAL2 has generated multiple candidate derivatives for an anchor-suspect pair and you must rank them by enzymatic plausibility before evaluating exact InChIKey matches.

name: skewness-based-sign-detection
description: Use when independent component analysis (e.g. sklearn FastICA or fastICA with icasso stabilisation) has been run on a samples x genes expression matrix and component signs must be fixed so each source's heaviest distribution tail is positive.

name: sklearn-predictive-model-cross-validation
description: Use when a pathway-transformed (ssPA) multi-omics matrix with outcome labels is available and a cross-validated classification performance metric (AUROC/AUC) plus a ranked pathway importance list is required from an SKlearn-compatible model.

name: skyline-diagonal-peak-cluster-detection-jres-cosy
description: Use when simulating 2D metabolomic 1H NMR spectra (J-Res or COSY) in MetAssimulo 2.0 and you need to locate each metabolite's peak clusters on skyline or diagonal projections so pH-driven peak shifts (equation 3, δL, δHL, pH0, pKa) can be applied per cluster rather than per 1D peak.

name: skyline-document-template-reuse
description: Use when new targeted metabolomics raw files (e.g. Sciex, Waters, Agilent, Bruker, Shimadzu, or Thermo data) need to be processed with the exact transition list, retention-time windows, and calibrated quantification of an already-validated Skyline small-molecule assay template rather than rebuilt.

name: skyline-lipidomic-data-export
description: Use when Skyline holds a LipidCreator transition list for targeted PRM/MRM lipid measurements and peak areas must be exported (e.g., 433 plasma lipids in triplicate) for QC filtering or reference-material correlation.

name: skyline-small-molecule-data-processing
description: Use when raw LC-SRM/LC-MS vendor files for targeted small-molecule assays (e.g., arginine/polyamine panel with heavy-labeled internal standards) must be imported, peak-picked, RT-scheduled, and calibrated into concentrations.

name: skyline-small-molecule-document-setup
description: Use when starting a new Skyline project for small molecules — e.g. lipid precursors (DAG 30:0, DAG 32:0), amino acid panels (Biocrates p180), or polyamine targets — and you need the document's transition settings, extraction mode, and molecule inputs configured before importing raw data.

name: skyline-spectral-library-import-validation
description: Use when targeted lipidomics transitions (e.g. platelet lipid mediators) need an in silico .blib spectral library consumable by Skyline for DIA/spectral-matching method validation.

name: skyline-targeted-metabolomics-document-building
description: Use when a targeted small-molecule or metabolite assay (SRM/MRM or HRMS) needs a vendor-independent Skyline document — e.g. a transition list plus SCIEX 5500 raw files with rapid positive/negative polarity switching — to yield integrated peak areas and calibrated concentrations.

name: skyline-transition-inspectability-checking
description: Use when curating a targeted peptide precursor panel from DIA-NN-derived quantification of retrospective DIA files, and only precursors whose transitions can be manually peak-shape-inspected in Skyline should be kept.

name: skyline-transition-list-formatting
description: Use when a targeted LC-MS/MS workflow (e.g. Skyline) needs an in silico lipid transition list, and LSG's default '.MSP' spectral-library export does not match the acquisition software's required input format.

name: slice-wise-maximum-detection-sweep
description: Use when peak-picking a 13C INADEQUATE spectrum where overlapping or weak peaks are missed by a single intensity cutoff, and you need slice-wise threshold sweeps with merge tolerances.

name: sliding-window-signal-analysis
description: Use when processing raw untargeted metabolomics data (.mzML, .mzXML, .mzData, .CDF from qTOF, orbitrap, or FT-ICR instruments) to detect TIC peaks per sample and derive dataset-specific peak-picking parameters in a single inference step rather than iterative parameter sweeping.

name: slurm-hpc-job-submission
description: Use when LC-HRMS metabolomics data (mzML or abf) is too large for a local machine — e.g., more than a handful of samples — and execution should be moved to a SLURM-managed HPC cluster with the Nextflow4MS-DIAL singularity profile.

name: sm-intensity-aggregation-onto-st-spots
description: Use when SM and ST are measured on adjacent/serial tissue sections with mismatched spot grids, and integration requires metabolite intensities aggregated onto ST spots before CVAE-based vertical integration.

name: sm-intensity-normalization-assessment
description: Use when tuning SpatialMETA's ConditionalVAESTSM for vertical integration of ST with SM mass-spectrometry intensities and you must decide between Gaussian vs MSE SM loss, SM normalization on/off, and shared vs independent decoders.

name: small-molecule-ccs-verification-against-compendium
description: Use when a TWIM-MS feature list contains small-molecule features (singly charged, m/z < 550) whose calibrated TWCCSN2 values need validation against drift-tube reference CCS values before feature identification.

name: small-molecule-database-search-configuration
description: Use when tandem mass spectra (e.g., from GNPS) must be searched against a structure database such as the Dictionary of Natural Products or PubChem, and search configuration decisions — database redundancy, fragmentation model scope, ionization mode — must be made and validated.

name: small-molecule-identification-benchmarking
description: Use when tandem MS/MS spectra (e.g., from GNPS or MoNA spectral libraries) must be searched against molecular structure databases (DNP, MoNA DB, PubChem) and identification accuracy of multiple search methods must be compared via top-k accuracy.

name: small-molecule-mass-shift-computation
description: Use when you know only a parent drug's molecular formula (e.g. diclofenac C14H11Cl2NO2) and need a list of phase I/II metabolite formulas with exact masses to search against LC-HRMS/MS (mzML) data.

name: small-molecule-mrm-quantification-comparison
description: Use when two MRM quantification tools (e.g. MRMPro and Skyline) must be compared on the same small-molecule MRM acquisition files, and per-transition peak-area correlations (R-square vs concentration) quantify agreement.

name: small-molecule-nmr-data-handling
description: Use when the task requires retrieving a metabolite or biological small-molecule NMR entry (spectra, time-domain data, or assigned chemical shifts) from BMRB and converting its NMR-STAR record into a tabular shift table.

name: small-molecule-spectral-library-import-and-matching
description: Decision support for building small-molecule identification/confirmation workflows in Skyline when candidate metabolite targets need spectral confirmation against public fragmentation libraries rather than in-house spectral libraries.

name: small-molecule-srm-transition-list-import
description: Use when the input is a custom small-molecule SRM transition list (e.g., purine/pyrimidine targets with heavy internal standards) and raw LC-SRM files from polarity-switching acquisitions on instruments like a SCIEX 5500.

name: small-molecule-structure-database-preparation
description: Use when tandem mass spectra (e.g., from GNPS/MassIVE datasets like MSV000079450) must be searched against known molecular structure databases and no prepared structure-DB target set is yet available.

name: small-molecule-structure-descriptor-calculation
description: Use when you have SMILES (or equivalent 2D structure) representations for small-molecule databases like HMDB, DrugBank, FooDB, or STOFF and need quantitative molecular descriptors to feed an RT-prediction or QSAR-style machine learning model.

name: small-molecule-structure-lookup-in-lotus
description: Use when you have measured m/z mass features that need putative structure annotations, or a set of known substrate/product structures (e.g. the 374 characterized biosynthetic structures) whose presence/absence in LOTUS must be tabulated.

name: small-molecule-targeted-extraction-hrms
description: Use when you have HRMS full-scan LC-MS raw files (e.g., Waters Synapt G2 HDMS) for treated vs. control samples and a list of small-molecule precursor ions with measured m/z and retention times whose peak areas you need to extract and compare.

name: small-molecule-targeted-quantification
description: Use when you have vendor raw LC-MS data (e.g. Sciex, Waters, Agilent, Bruker, Shimadzu, Thermo) for known small-molecule targets (p180 amino acids, polyamines, purine/pyrimidines, HRMS lipids) and need calibrated peak-area quantification with a transition list and retention-time scheduling.

name: small-molecule-transition-list-authoring
description: Use when building a targeted SRM/MRM or HRMS assay for small molecules or metabolites — e.g. arginine/polyamine or Biocrates p180-style panels — where a transition list with heavy internal standards must be defined, optimized, and exported as a scheduled acquisition method.

name: small-vs-large-database-benchmarking

name: spatial-metabolomics-cluster-mapping
description: Use when you have a spatial metabolomics peak table (pixels x ion intensities with X/Y coordinates) and need to assess whether preprocessing (e.g. SMQVP noise/background removal) improves spatial segmentation relative to H&E tissue morphology.

name: spatial-metabolomics-feature-evaluation
description: Use when a trained machine-learning annotation or scoring model (e.g., GBDT over ion features) exists and you need per-feature contribution/importance ratios to explain target-decoy separation, or to justify re-weighting or re-defining scoring features.

name: spatial-metabolomics-feature-matrix-processing
description: Use when the input is an IMS feature matrix CSV (pixel X/Y coordinates plus ion-intensity columns) that needs QC, isotope/adduct pair identification, metabolite annotation against a custom LC-MS/MS library, or ROI-based differential testing.

name: spatial-metabolomics-horizontal-integration
description: Use when multiple spatial metabolomics samples from the same tissue type (e.g., ccRCC MSI metabolite intensity matrices) must be integrated into a shared latent space and benchmarked against existing horizontal integration methods.

name: spatial-metabolomics-pattern-visualization
description: Use when an IMS feature matrix (pixel coordinates + ion intensities) has been clustered by spatial co-expression and the patterns must be mapped back onto tissue pixels to identify region-enriched expression patterns.

name: spatial-metabolomics-peak-table-processing
description: Use when a spatial metabolomics peak table matrix (X/Y pixel coordinates + ion intensity columns) contains background pixels that must be removed prior to clustering or downstream spatial analysis.

name: spatial-metabolomics-pixel-clustering
description: Use when you have a spatial metabolomics feature matrix (rows = pixels with X/Y coordinates, columns = m/z ion intensities) and need to segment the tissue section into spatial regions or compare them to anatomical references.

name: spatial-metabolomics-pixel-region-classification
description: Use when working with an AFADESI- or MALDI-style spatial metabolomics peak table (pixels x m/z ions) and you need to partition pixels into user-defined tissue vs. background regions to assess acquisition quality or tissue-enriched ion expression.

name: spatial-metabolomics-quality-control
description: Use when a spatial metabolomics feature matrix (pixels × m/z ion intensities, e.g., MALDI/DESI imaging MS) must be QC-assessed and noise-filtered before annotation, clustering, or differential analysis.

name: spatial-metabolomics-transcriptomics-alignment
description: Use when you hold paired SM (imzML, e.g. MALDI-TOF) and ST (e.g. 10X Visium) measurements from the same or adjacent tissue section and need metabolite signals mapped onto ST spots for joint clustering or WNN integration.

name: spatial-molecular-cartography-visualization
description: Use when LC–MS runs were acquired across spatially arranged samples (e.g. swabs of a 96-well plate, plant surfaces, keypads) and the goal is a molecular intensity map localized onto an image or 3D model of the sampled surface.

name: spatial-neighborhood-computation-from-cell-centroids
description: Use when per-cell intensity tables and centroid coordinates are available and the goal is to quantify neighborhood-dependent behavior (e.g., metabolite competition between tumor cells and T-cells) as a function of proximity to CD31+ endothelial cells or cell-cell contact.

name: spatial-omics-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when a joint spatial transcriptomics-metabolomics embedding must be quantitatively compared against competing integration tools, requiring metric computation and a ranked overall-score table.

name: spatial-omics-benchmark-generation
description: Use when no real paired spatial-omics sections exist but a ground-truth reference is needed to evaluate spot-to-spot integration or label transfer methods such as haCCA against morphological alignment baselines like STUtility.

name: spatial-pattern-annotation-against-brain-anatomy
description: Use when a spatial metabolomics feature matrix (pixel × ion intensities, e.g. AFAD-ESI+ 100 um mouse brain section) has been ion-clustered and clusters must be labeled/validated against anatomical regions like cortex or tissue edges.

name: spatial-pearson-correlation-of-ion-images
description: Use when a peak table from spatial metabolomics data (pixels x m/z) contains mass-difference pairs matching known adducts (M+H, M+K, M+Na) and you must confirm which pairs co-localize spatially before assigning adduct annotations.

name: spatial-prediction-map-reconstruction
description: Use when you have per-pixel probabilistic class scores from a trained classifier applied to mass spectrometry imaging data and need to map predicted labels and classification uncertainty back into image space to inspect tumor-margin heterogeneity.

name: spatial-randomness-quadrat-testing
description: Use when a spatial metabolomics feature matrix (pixel X/Y coordinates + per-pixel ion intensities, e.g. 14,260 pixels x 3,044 ions from an AFAD-ESI(+) mouse brain IMS section) must be QC-filtered of noise ions before annotation or spatial pattern analysis.

name: spatial-region-differential-analyte-interpretation
description: Use when an integrated SpaMTP Seurat object (paired SM/ST assays) already has per-cluster differential metabolites and genes, and the goal is region-level pathway enrichment or pathway-network interpretation across spatial regions.

name: spatial-segment-tstatistic-extraction
description: Use when you have a fitted Cardinal segmentation of an MSI tissue section (e.g. imzML-derived peak data from pig fetus liver/heart sections) and need ranked lists of peaks enriched or absent in each spatial segment.

name: spatial-shrunken-centroids-pixel-clustering
description: Use when you have a pixel-by-ion feature matrix from imaging MS (e.g., 14,260 pixels x 3,044 ion peaks) and need anatomically meaningful pixel clusters or region-of-interest definitions to benchmark or replace web-tool clustering.

name: spatial-transcriptome-background-plotting
description: Use when haCCA integration has produced a b_predict object whose MALDI-MSI metabolite features sit on transcriptome spot coordinates and you need to visualise a metabolite against the spot background to co-localise it with a gene.

name: spatial-transcriptome-clustering-comparison
description: Use when you have haCCA-integrated multi-module spatial data (morphology + transcripts + metabolites) plus matched transcript-only or metabolite-only matrices and want to test whether integration yields more clusters and higher heterogeneity.

name: spatial-transcriptome-data-splitting
description: Use when you need to benchmark a spatial transcriptome-to-MALDI-MSI integration method (e.g. haCCA) against a known ground truth but lack true paired sections, by constructing pseudo-paired data from a single spatial transcriptome.

name: spatial-transcriptome-msi-alignment-benchmarking
description: Use when two neighboring tissue sections have been profiled with spatial transcriptomics (e.g. 10X Visium .h5ad) and MALDI-MSI, you lack shared spots/features, and you must decide which spot-to-spot alignment method maximizes label transfer fidelity.

name: spatial-transcriptome-peak-integration
description: Use when you hold paired spatial transcriptome and MALDI-MSI data from the same or neighboring tissue section (no shared spots or features) and need spot-to-spot integration to map gene expression onto biomolecule profiles.

name: spatially-aware-distance-computation
description: Use when segmenting a peak-picked MSI dataset (e.g., the pig fetus dataset with 28,016 non-background pixels and 10,200 mass features) and you must select the number of tissue segments from pixel intensities rather than assign pre-defined class labels.

name: spatio-molecular-matrix-analysis
description: Use when you have a per-cell spatio-molecular matrix (MORPHnMOL.csv) from SpaceM and need to identify metabolic states, rank differential metabolites between conditions, or classify cell types from single-cell metabolomes.

name: spatio-molecular-matrix-generation-for-single-cell-metabolomics
description: Use when assigning MALDI-imaging MS metabolite intensities to individual cultured cells from tiled pre/post-MALDI microscopy plus imzML/ibd data, to produce a per-cell normalized metabolic and morphological feature matrix.

name: spearman-agreement-statistics
description: Use when validating that an experimentally derived isotopic ratio metric (e.g. R13C from LC/HRMS peaklists) agrees with theory computed from molecular formulas across a benchmark set of authentic standards.

name: spearman-correlation-analysis
description: Use when two processed abundance matrices (e.g., metabolomics and proteomics from the same samples) must be integrated via pairwise Spearman correlations to construct a metabolite-protein network and identify hub nodes.

name: spearman-correlation-analysis
description: Use when ranking metabolic features (e.g. from 1H NMR metabonomic profiles) against a continuous phenotype such as BMI while adjusting for epidemiological confounders like Age, Gender, or T2D, and when bootstrap confidence intervals are needed to validate the associations.

name: spearman-correlation-analysis-of-peak-areas
description: Use when two peak-integration approaches have produced matched per-target peak-area tables (e.g., log2 AUC per target per run) and you must demonstrate their quantitative agreement via rank correlation, regression, and precision (CV) benchmarking.

name: spearman-correlation-computation
description: Use when evaluating a retention-order prediction model (e.g. ROASMI, Morgan_count fingerprints) against experimental elution orders on multiple RPLC datasets, where per-dataset rank agreement must be aggregated into an average rank score.

name: spearman-correlation-edge-filtering
description: Use when building metabolite-metabolite network edges from measured concentrations or peak intensities (e.g., GC-TOF-MS plasma metabolite data across samples) and biochemical pathway or structural annotations are missing, so empirical co-variation is the only available association signal.

name: spearman-correlation-edge-filtering
description: Use when building omics co-occurrence or multi-omics networks from a feature (species/metabolite/gene) abundance table in MetaNet, and you need defensible correlation thresholds instead of an arbitrary similarity cutoff before downstream topology, module, or keystone analyses.

name: spearman-correlation-heatmap-clustering
description: Use when several normalization variants (e.g., tGAM, rGAM, rLOESS, QC-RLSC, QC-RSC, SERFF, TIGER) have been applied to the same dataset and you need to visualize how similarly they rank metabolites by differential abundance signal.

name: spearman-correlation-omics-behavioral-factors
description: Use when relating continuous multi-omics factor loadings (e.g., MOFA factors from methylation/metabolomics) to behavioral dimension scores in a cohort where no family structure needs modeling, and a rank-based association measure is preferred.

name: spearman-correlation-performance-assessment
description: Use when a paired microbiome-metabolome model (e.g. MiMeNet, MelonnPan, NED) has been trained and cross-validated and you need per-metabolite SCC values plus a shuffled-data empirical background to declare which metabolites are well-predicted.

name: spearman-correlation-prediction-evaluation
description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking metabolite abundance prediction from paired microbiome-metabolome count data and per-metabolite SCC values, mean SCC, and well-predicted metabolite counts are needed.

name: spearman-correlation-threshold-derivation
description: Use when you need an objective, dataset-specific significance threshold for per-metabolite prediction correlations in a paired microbiome-metabolome regression task, rather than an arbitrary fixed SCC cutoff.

name: spearman-injection-order-analysis
description: Use when a quantified concentration table from a targeted LC-MS/MS sequence (e.g. porcine plasma) must be checked for residual injection-order drift after applying a drift-correction strategy, or when comparing correction strategies for compound-specific residual drift.

name: spearman-rank-correlation-analysis
description: Use when a per-cell matrix (e.g. MORPHnMOL.csv from a SpaceM scAnalysis run) contains both normalized lipid intensities and microscopy-derived fluorescence such as LD540, and the goal is to find lipids positively or negatively correlated with that readout across single cells.

name: spearman-rank-correlation-statistics
description: Use when testing whether detected LC/HRMS peaks from an aligned peak table (IDSL.IPA, MS-DIAL, etc.) are significantly associated with a continuous or ordinal phenotype (e.g. birth weight) in a cohort.

name: spec2vec-spectral-embedding-scoring
description: Use when comparing large collections of positive-ionization MS/MS spectra (e.g. GNPS libraries, ~95k spectra) where cosine or modified cosine poorly reflects structural similarity, or when scalable all-pairs analogue search / molecular networking is needed.

name: specialized-metabolism-pathway-curation
description: Use when a MEANtools/ClusterONE analysis of paired transcriptomic-metabolomic data (e.g., Jeon 2020 tomato) yields FCs and you need to assign known pathway genes to clusters and check cluster stability.

name: species-and-sample-type-metadata-extraction
description: Use when the analysis goal is to stratify a public metabolomics repository catalog by measurement technique (e.g. NMR), species (e.g. human), and sample type (e.g. blood plasma/serum) to answer 'how many studies match X?' questions.

name: species-chemical-profile-clustering
description: Use when you have ConCISE consensus annotations for ion features from multiple species/conditions and want to test whether consensus chemical-class profiles (relative production per class) group samples by phenotype or toxicity.

name: species-coverage-verification
description: Use when building or auditing the scope statement of a multiomics resource and you need to confirm that the listed species, tissue subtypes, cell lines, and gene counts match the values reported in the source article or repository metadata.

name: species-genus-novelty-scoring
description: Use when prioritizing natural extracts by chemical novelty: you have CANOPUS NPC class predictions for a feature table and literature-reported compounds/classes for the taxa, and need to flag classes new to species or genus.

name: species-level-taxonomic-profiling
description: Use when you have paired-end shallow shotgun metagenomic reads (e.g., fecal samples from the SPF Sacrifice cohort, n=666) plus genotype metadata, and you need species-level taxonomic profiles to run differential abundance testing (e.g., ANCOM-BC2) between 3xTg and WT mice.

name: species-level-taxonomy-lineage-completion
description: Use when a natural products database stores organism/origin information as heterogeneous free text and you need one accepted scientific name per row with complete taxonomy down to the species level.

name: species-specific-reaction-annotation
description: Use when a metabolomics differential table already has KEGG compound IDs for significant metabolites and you need species-specific reaction-to-pathway associations before computing pathway enrichment p-values.

name: specimen-level-qc-warning-assignment
description: Use when implementing or reproducing Rapid QC-MS's specimen-level QC logic — specifically assigning a dashboard Specimen Table 'Warning' label from IS intensity dropouts and per-IS 'Warn' flags rather than raw-file-level or instrument-level alerts.

name: spectra-annotation-benchmark-tabulation
description: Use when benchmarking how many experimental peaks each tool annotates in high-resolution MS/MS spectra of NRPs or PK siderophores, or when comparing annotator accuracy across CID and HCD fragmentation conditions.

name: spectra-annotation-validation-without-repair
description: Use when you need a counterfactual baseline of how many spectra a require/remove-only cleaning pass discards, to quantify the rescue effect of repair functions (e.g. repair reduces removals from 83,843 to 31,758 on GNPS).

name: spectra-candidate-ranking-evaluation
description: Use when you must rank candidate molecular structures for tandem mass spectra from a structure prediction model and compare that ranking against established tools (SIRIUS4, MetFrag) with statistical significance testing.

name: spectra-chemical-class-annotation-comparison
description: Use when two or more chemical-class annotation tools (e.g., CANOPUS vs MolNetEnhancer) have been run on the same GNPS molecular networking spectra and you need to quantify per-ontology-category agreement or discrepancy before choosing class-based link filtering thresholds.

name: spectra-conditioned-molecular-diffusion-generation
description: Use when you need to generate/elucidate unknown molecular structures from multi-modal spectral data (IR, Raman, UV-Vis) as a conditional generation task rather than retrieval against a finite library.

name: spectra-conditioned-molecule-generation
description: Use when you must recover an unknown molecule's exact structure from simulated or measured multi-modal spectra (IR, Raman, UV-Vis), especially when 3D conformation matters and single-spectrum methods are insufficient.

name: spectra-level-motif-prevalence-rendering
description: Use when a trained MS2LDA model (ms2lda.bin) with an inferred Mass2Motif set (motifset.json) must be made explorable interactively, e.g. to pick biochemically relevant motifs before further characterization.

name: spectra-merging-same-energy-and-all-energies
description: Use when raw vendor/open-format MSn data has been denoised and annotated in mzmine and replicate fragmentation spectra must be merged into consensus library entries at the same collision energy or across energies, including pseudo-MS2 collapse of MSn trees.

name: spectra-metadata-factor-level-join
description: Use when 1D NMR spectral intensity data must be annotated with experimental-design metadata — i.e. spectrum IDs need to be tagged with factor levels so spectra can be grouped and colored by condition in an overlay or stacked viewer figure.

name: spectra-metadata-field-retention
description: Use when query spectra come from an external feature-based tool (MZmine, MS-DIAL) as an exported MGF file and feature identifiers must survive import for later join-back of matchSpectra annotation results.

name: spectra-metadata-variable-mapping
description: Use when translating R Spectra::Spectra objects to Python matchms.Spectrum objects and spectra metadata (MS level, precursor m/z, retention times, arbitrary annotations) must be renamed/reformatted to matchms conventions.

name: spectra-molecule-joint-embedding
description: Use when annotating untargeted metabolomics spectra by ranking a candidate molecule list (e.g. PubChem candidates keyed by InChIKey) for a query spectrum with no reference spectrum match, and you have pretrained spectra/molecule embedding weights available.

name: spectra-overlay-visualization-by-factor-level
description: Use when 1D NMR spectral intensity data (e.g. Bruker 1r-derived spectra) must be visualized grouped or colored by experimental-factor levels, bridging experimental design and downstream statistical analyses.

name: spectra-quality-filtering
description: Use when building or cleaning a homemade MS/MS spectral library from MetaPro batch QC inspection results and you need to keep only inspected-and-passed spectra grouped per compound with full acquisition metadata.

name: spectra-search-throughput-measurement
description: Use when comparing the runtime scalability of MS2 library search methods (e.g. MS2Query vs matchms modified cosine) on a fixed query-vs-library task, and wall-clock throughput in spectra/minute is the metric of interest.

name: spectra-server-service-operation
description: Use when an input spectrum is not already in JCAMP-DX (mzML MS, proprietary RAW, FID, Bruker, BagIt) and it must be standardized server-side to JCAMP-DX before visualization, editing, or transfer of signals to an ELN.

name: spectra-similarity-scoring
description: Use when experimental MS2 spectra extracted from an xcms result (e.g. from a mzML file) must be matched against reference fragment spectra from a CompDb/HMDB or similar library to assign compound identities to chromatographic peaks.

name: spectra-to-document-conversion
description: Use when preparing preprocessed MS/MS spectra (e.g. cleaned MGF/GNPS library spectra) as input for training a Word2Vec/Spec2Vec model or for scoring spectra with a pre-trained Spec2Vec model.

name: spectra-to-molecule-finetuning-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating de novo molecular structure generation from tandem mass spectra on NPLIB1/MassSpecGym, especially after pretraining the fingerprint-to-molecule diffusion decoder, to quantify downstream accuracy and structural similarity.

name: spectra-url-field-completeness-checking
description: Use when auditing PoDP project JSON records (from Zenodo archives or the paired-data-form app) to verify that link records are structurally complete before tabulating or downstream linking analyses.

name: spectra-viewer-interactive-processing
description: Use when raw 1D NMR FID spectra (Bruker or Varian/Agilent, or nmrML) from metabolomics experiments need interactive visual inspection and processing steps that require expert visual judgement, such as baseline distortion assessment or alignment checks.

name: spectral-agreement-icc-benchmarking
description: Use when validating that an accelerated or reimplemented MRS basis-set simulation produces metabolite basis functions statistically equivalent to a reference baseline, requiring per-metabolite ICC thresholds before acceptance.

name: spectral-alignment-algorithm-reconstruction
description: Use when fragment ion matches must be computed between spectra from a pair-specific similarity matrix and you need the maximum weight matching (matching matrix M) prior to significance testing.

name: spectral-alignment-method-benchmarking
description: Decision support for choosing a 1H NMR spectra summarization or alignment method: when shifted spectra need objective comparison of peak-based vs alignment-plus-binning workflows using classification performance (ROC/PRC).

name: spectral-alignment-significance-estimation
description: Use when fragmentation-spectra alignments (e.g. from a max-weight matching over a SIMILE similarity matrix S and spec_ids) must be ranked by p-value or judged significant, rather than treated as uninterpretable intermediate similarity scores.

name: spectral-alignment-visualization-and-svg-export
description: Use when an MMSA alignment JSON (from a GNPS2 task ID/USI/FBMN input) must be inspected interactively — verifying consensus peak sets shared across a molecular family's MS/MS spectra — or exported as a high-resolution SVG figure for reporting.

name: spectral-annotation-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantitatively benchmark MS/MS annotation tools (ISDB-DNP, MS-Finder, Sirius) and tune taxonomically informed re-ranking weights on a labeled benchmark set of identified molecules.

name: spectral-annotation-coverage-filtering
description: Use when applying NPClassScore to a paired genomics–metabolomics dataset and you need to determine which spectra lack CANOPUS or MolNetEnhancer ClassyFire superclass predictions, so candidate links based on unannotated spectra can be filtered out.

name: spectral-annotation-formatting
description: Use when detected peak positions from IR spectra (or shared peak lists from NMR/MS/IR) must be converted into bracketed annotation strings for a peak table or labels file, such as an IR_peak_labels.txt output.

name: spectral-annotation-performance-analysis
description: Use when ranked candidate annotation lists from annotation tools must be scored against known ground-truth structures to quantify whether a re-ranking strategy improves precision, recall and F1.

name: spectral-annotation-rank-metrics-computation
description: Use when evaluating metabolite spectral annotation models on candidate sets — you need average rank and Rank@K (k=1..20) to compare models like ESP, MLP-PD, and GNN-PD on the same test spectra.

name: spectral-annotation-ranking-evaluation
description: Use when a pretrained mass-spectra annotation model must be scored on candidate sets from PubChem, and when average rank and Rank@K curves are needed to compare models or candidate-set designs.

name: spectral-assignment-tuning
description: Use when a 2D 1H,13C HSQC mixture-spectrum reconstruction pipeline shows parameter sensitivity: you must choose assignment_radius and detection_threshold values, compare single-pass vs incremental MCF variants, or validate that F1 scores remain stable over a plausible parameter grid.

name: spectral-attribute-support-assessment
description: Use when you must decide which R package to adopt for reading or writing mass-spectral libraries in NIST msp / MoNA msp / GNPS mgf dialects, or when compiling a package capability matrix for spectral-file format support.

name: spectral-basis-function-grid-alignment
description: Use when two MRS basis sets (e.g., an MRSCloud-simulated set and a reference set such as MARSS or LCModel) must be compared metabolite-by-metabolite and their basis functions first need to be placed on a shared spectral grid.

name: spectral-basis-set-comparison
description: Use when you have a simulated MRS basis set and a phantom-acquired or vendor-provided basis set for the same sequence/field (e.g., 3T PRESS TE 30 ms) and need per-metabolite agreement metrics such as ICCs.

name: spectral-benchmark-table-compilation
description: Use when reproducing or extending the MassSpecGym molecule-retrieval benchmark: you have pretrained spectra-to-candidate models, MassSpecGym spectra and candidate datasets, and need per-view rank@1 values aggregated into a comparison table.

name: spectral-bin-assignment-mapping
description: Use when you have calibrated 1D 1H NMR serum/plasma spectra from a Bruker IVDr 600 MHz spectrometer and need to map 24 predefined spin-system bins to metabolite signals in a 22-metabolite panel.

name: spectral-binning-and-totalarea-normalization
description: Use when aligned, window-selected spectra (spectra_df rows indexed by ppm) must be converted to a fixed feature table for statistical analysis or classification, e.g. after Icoshift alignment in a Protomix 1H-NMR metabolomics pipeline.

name: spectral-binning-uniform-bucketing
description: Use when per-sample NMR spectral data (e.g. 1r processed spectra from fid/acqu(ac)us acquisitions) must be reduced from full spectral resolution to a fixed-width bucketed feature table (exactly 1000 data columns) for downstream analysis tools.

name: spectral-bucket-intensity-reshaping
description: Use when a processed 1D NMR bucket table from NMRProcFlow must be handed off to an online statistical tool (MetaboAnalyst 3.0 / BioStatFlow) and you need a ready-to-import samples-by-buckets matrix with experimental-factor class labels.

name: spectral-bucket-table-processing
description: Use when you have a matrix of processed 1D 1H NMR spectra (ppm scale x samples) from NMRProcFlow/NMRspec and need to reduce them to a bucket table with adaptive intervals and SNR-based quality filtering.

name: spectral-bucket-variable-labelling
description: Use when a binned NMR bucket intensity matrix (rows of bucket intensities over Bin.SpectraPoint spectral points per sample) plus sample class metadata must be converted into MetaboAnalyst or Workflow4Metabolomics input files.

name: spectral-classifier-ensemble-training
description: Use when a curated set of annotated and labeled HR-MS/MS spectra of compounds of interest ('relevant') and others ('other') is available and you need a trained ensemble that classifies new MGF spectra into 'relevant' vs 'other' for natural-product prioritization.

name: spectral-cluster-annotation-mapping
description: Use when upstream msFeaST result tables (embeddings, k-medoids cluster labels, globaltest statistics, contrast mappings) must be joined per feature and serialized into the schema expected by the msFeaST_Dashboard_bundle.html interactive dashboard.

name: spectral-cluster-marking-and-filtering
description: Use when reconstructing or validating peak-detection code for simulated 1D 1H, 2D J-Res or COSY metabolomic NMR spectra where peaks must be localized as clusters above a user-defined intensity threshold before downstream spectral simulation.

name: spectral-cluster-medoid-selection
description: Use when you have GLEAMS cluster assignments (GLEAMS_cluster.npy) and medoid indexes (GLEAMS_cluster_medoids.npy) and need to pick one representative spectrum per cluster of previously unidentified spectra for downstream search/annotation.

name: spectral-clustering-assignment
description: Use when a fused sample-by-sample similarity network (e.g., from SNF over methylation and metabolomics distance matrices) must be partitioned into subgroups, with cluster labels retained per sample and cohort.

name: spectral-clustering-completeness-quantification
description: Use when benchmarking MS/MS clustering tools (msCluster, Falcon, MaRaCluster) on mzML/MGF-derived spectra and you need to report how many spectra end up in usable clusters (N10) and the overall clustered fraction.

name: spectral-clustering-consensus-spectrum-generation
description: Use when you have per-sample MGF MS2 files from untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics (e.g., MSV000080502 Euphorbia dendroides data) and need to collapse redundant MS2 scans into clean consensus spectra for GNPS/Tremolo library identification.

name: spectral-clustering-quality-evaluation
description: Use when comparing spectral clustering outputs of MS/MS spectra (e.g., MGF-derived clusters with charge 2-3 precursors) against peptide assignments to quantify completeness, incorrect clustering ratio, and clustered spectra ratio.

name: spectral-clustering-tool-configuration
description: Use when profiling the runtime breakdown of CPU-only spectral clustering tools on large MS/MS data sets (e.g. PXD000561 MGF files) to quantify the preprocessing bottleneck before benchmarking a faster method such as HyperSpec.

name: spectral-conditional-molecule-generation
description: Use when you have simulated or measured molecular spectra (IR, Raman, UV-Vis, or all jointly) and need de novo molecular structure elucidation evaluated by top-1/top-10 exact match rather than retrieval from a fixed library.

name: spectral-constraint-optimization
description: Use when a batch of GC×GC–MS samples has already been peak-picked and annotated (consensus spectra available from GcDUO module III) and you need sample-wise peak areas/intensities that account for between-sample retention-time shifts, i.e. module V data integration.

name: spectral-contrast-angle-computation
description: Use when you have peptide sequences with both observed and Prosit-predicted fragment-ion intensity vectors and need a similarity or sequence-stability feature for PSM rescoring.

name: spectral-correlation-coefficient-analysis
description: Use when a series of 1D-NMR spectra (e.g. Daphnia magna extracts) shows chemical-shift drift and you need to measure alignment improvement via Pearson correlation against a chosen reference spectrum in a spectral region.

name: spectral-cosine-similarity-evaluation
description: Use when you have predicted MS/MS spectra (e.g. MGF from 3DMolMS pred_msms) paired with experimental test spectra (PKL/MGF) and need per-compound cosine similarity scores stratified by ion mode or collision energy.

name: spectral-cosine-similarity-ranking
description: Use when an experimental MS/MS spectrum is unannotated but a candidate compound list exists (e.g. from precursor mass) and in silico predicted spectra are available to score each candidate for identification.

name: spectral-cosine-similarity-scoring
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS metabolomics spectra (e.g. deposited mzML/MassIVE MSV000083738) must be grouped into molecular families by spectral similarity, or when correlating those families to BiG-SCAPE-derived GCFs.

name: spectral-cosine-similarity-scoring
description: Use when benchmarking in silico MS/MS spectral predictions (e.g., from FIORA, CFM-ID v4, or ICEBERG) against reference spectra in mgf/msp libraries such as NIST'17/MS-DIAL, MSnLib, or CASMI 2016/2022 challenge sets.

name: spectral-cosine-similarity-scoring-of-structural-permutations
description: Decision support for benchmarking modification-site localization when a simulated in-silico fragmentation alternative to ModiFinder's likelihood scoring is needed, using MS2-unknown plus an S-known structure with a known modification substructure.

name: spectral-cosine-similarity-thresholding
description: Use when a deconvoluted GNPS GC-MS feature table must be cleaned before interpretation — e.g. to select reliably annotated, reproducible features prior to spatial mapping, differential analysis, or figure reproduction.

name: spectral-coverage-fraction-calculation
description: Use when you have counts of merged MS/MS spectra and of MSI level 1/2 compound annotations for an untargeted metabolomics assay (e.g. urinary HILIC-Q Exactive HF data) and need to report the fraction of spectra covered and the unannotated remainder before applying in silico annotation.

name: spectral-cross-correlation-scoring
description: Use when an observed MS2 spectrum (e.g. .FT2 scans extracted by Raxport) must be scored against a theoretical peptide fragment spectrum to validate or rank PSMs from proteomic SIP database searches.

name: spectral-data-augmentation
description: Use when training an MS2DeepScore-style Siamese model and you need to augment binned spectra (10,000 equal-width bins over 10–1000 m/z, square-root transformed intensities) to improve robustness.

name: spectral-data-augmentation-gaussian-noise
description: Use when training a deep learning model on MS/MS spectra from an instrument type with limited training data (e.g., Q-TOF) and top-1 formula prediction accuracy is near zero without augmentation.

name: spectral-data-cleaning-with-matchms
description: Use when raw MGF/mzML spectra are about to be matched against a spectral library (e.g. with MS2Query or modified cosine), and peak lists and metadata still need harmonization and noise filtering.

name: spectral-data-conditioned-molecule-generation-evaluation
description: Use when a checkpoint of a spectra-conditioned molecular generator (e.g. DiffSpectra with SpecFormer + DMT) must be benchmarked on spectral input, producing accuracy, FCD and RMSD metrics comparable to paper ablations.

name: spectral-data-conversion-raw-to-mzml
