description: Use when a peak has been putatively annotated as an unknown metabolite by KGMN/MetDNA2 (e.g. in NIST human urine data) and you need independent support for the annotation via in silico MS/MS fragmentation rather than library matching.

name: spectral-similarity-scoring
description: Use when an unannotated MS/MS spectrum may be a modified form of a library compound — e.g. precursor/fragment shifts consistent with methylation (+14 Da), acetylation (+42 Da), hydroxylation (+16 Da), or phosphorylation (+80 Da) — and plain library matching failed to assign it.

name: spectral-similarity-scoring-cosine-entropy
description: Use when you have MS-DIAL-aligned peak tables from untargeted LC-MS/MS runs and need to decide whether detected features across samples are equivalent (merge) or distinct (new entry) before building a feature table.

name: spectral-similarity-scoring-cosine-jaccard
description: Use when a GC/EI-MS query spectrum (e.g., from SWGDRUG or NIST) has no matching reference entry and must be ranked against a set of predicted candidate spectra to produce a top-k identification list.

name: spectral-similarity-threshold-network-isolation
description: Use when a specXplore session object (ms2deepscore similarity matrix + t-SNE embedding) exists for an LC–MS/MS dataset and you need the densely connected subnetwork around a feature (e.g. Procyanidin-A2) isolated by similarity thresholds for fragmentation-overlap analysis.

name: spectral-statistics-aggregation
description: Use when you have paired peak lists from mixture NMR spectra and their pure-component references (ppm axis) and need to quantify chemical shift deviation statistics or derive a tolerance interval for peak-pairing.

name: spectral-threshold-level-tuning
description: Use when a processed 2D or pseudo-3D NMR spectrum needs publication-quality contour rendering or 3D surface visualization, and the contour threshold/levels must be matched to the spectrum's intensity range.

name: spectral-tool-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing formula assignment tools (e.g., FSA vs SIRIUS vs Buddy) on identical MS/MS datasets and you need paired rank-1/top-3/top-5 accuracy plus total and per-spectrum runtime to quantify accuracy-speed trade-offs.

name: spectral-training-data-balancing
description: Use when preparing training pairs for a Siamese spectral similarity model (e.g. MS2DeepScore) where biased pair selection over Tanimoto score ranges or molecule frequencies would skew model training.

name: spectral-vector-binning
description: Use when spectra must be transformed into fixed-dimensional numeric vectors (e.g. to build an ANN index or compute coarse cosine similarities) prior to spectral library candidate selection or similarity search.

name: spectral-word-embedding-vector-aggregation
description: Use when you have a trained Spec2Vec Word2Vec model and processed spectra as peak/loss word documents, and need pairwise spectral similarity scores for library matching or molecular networking.

name: spectrogram-deconvolution-error-correction
description: Use when low-resolution MSn spectra from a miniaturized mass spectrometer feed de novo fragment-tree or formula prediction and raw mass errors would corrupt constraints such as the <500 Da cutoff or ten-element formula search.

name: spectrometer-drift-time-binning
description: Use when UK Biobank NMR biomarker concentrations still show within-spectrometer drift over time after correction for sample degradation time, plate row (A-H), and plate column (1-12), and must be adjusted via date-binned robust regression.

name: spectroscopy-data-file-management
description: Use when ingesting or storing spectroscopic data (1H/13C NMR, IR, MS) from JCAMP-DX or Bruker files and a FAIR-compliant three-file artifact set per spectrum is required.

name: spectrum-cluster-consensus-assignment
description: Use when a large collection of unidentified MS/MS spectra has been clustered (e.g. 3.4M GLEAMS clusters) and the goal is cluster-level peptide assignments plus enrichment statistics for variant-consistent mismatches.

name: spectrum-clustering-parameter-sweep
description: Use when comparing spectrum-clustering tools on large-scale MS/MS peak-list data and you need per-tool cluster-quality metrics (clustered fraction, incorrect clustering, completeness) reproduced against a paper's reported comparison.

name: spectrum-clustering-quality-evaluation
description: Use when comparing spectrum clustering results from multiple tools on a labeled MS/MS dataset and you need purity (incorrectly clustered fraction), cluster size distribution, completeness, or data-volume reduction at a comparable operating point.

name: spectrum-compound-grouping
description: Use when curating a homemade MS/MS spectral library from checked MetaPro batch QC inspection overviews and reviewed spectra need to be accumulated per metabolite with acquisition metadata.

name: spectrum-conditioned-denoising-trajectory-analysis
description: Use when you need to expose the elucidation order inside a diffusion-based structure generator, e.g. testing whether broad atom semantics are established before simple bonds and then complex functional groups.

name: spectrum-conditioned-generative-sampling
description: Use when you have trained DMT checkpoints and multi-modal spectra (IR/Raman/UV-Vis) and need to generate de novo 3D molecular structures via spectra-conditioned diffusion sampling, then score exact-match accuracy.

name: spectrum-cross-attention-conditioning
description: Use when training or adapting a Markov-bridge molecular generator in which a fully connected (scaffold + molecule) graph must be conditioned on normalized MS/MS peak lists, and the spectrum should influence each layer of generation.

name: spectrum-database-search-annotation
description: Use when MS/MS (MS2) spectra must be annotated by searching a candidate structure database with SIRIUS4 or MetFrag, producing ranked candidate lists and similarity scores for baseline comparison.

name: spectrum-disjoint-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating structure annotation methods against spectral library search baselines on independent tandem MS/MS query data (e.g., medium-noise QTOF), requiring a spectrum-disjoint setup and FDR-controlled comparison at 5% FDR.

name: spectrum-embedding-extraction-from-transformer
description: Use when you need internal model states — embeddings, attention weights, predictions — from a trained LipiDetective transformer over preprocessed tandem MS2 lipid spectra, to feed interpretability or validation analyses.

name: spectrum-formula-keyed-lookup-table-construction
description: Use when constructing MADGEN's oracle retrieval setting: you have processed spectra datasets (e.g. msgym.pkl or canopus.pkl) with canonical SMILES and chemical formulas and need a per-entry correct-scaffold table keyed by spectrum and formula.

name: spectrum-identifier-block-verification
description: Use when you have a known peak list (ion:intensity pairs) and a published SPLASH, and need to verify, reproduce, or cross-check its fourth hash block or the full identifier.

name: spectrum-identifier-schema-validation
description: Decision support for identifiers presented as mzspec/mzdraft colon-delimited strings whose collection segment must be matched against known metabolomics and proteomics resources (GNPS, MassIVE, MetaboLights, Metabolomics Workbench, MassBank, MS2LDA) before spectra can be retrieved.

name: spectrum-identity-clustering-quality-evaluation
description: Use when GLEAMS embeddings of a large MS/MS dataset (e.g., MassIVE-KB peak files) have been hierarchically clustered and you must quantify clustering quality and label-propagation yield.

name: spectrum-intensity-filtering-and-noise-removal
description: Use when a raw MS/MS spectrum (e.g. loaded via USI from a public resource like GNPS) contains precursor peaks, off-range m/z values, and low-intensity noise peaks that must be cleaned before computational analysis or visualization.

name: spectrum-intensity-filtering-and-scaling
description: Use when raw MS/MS spectra (e.g. from an MGF file like iPRG2012.mgf) contain precursor peaks and low-intensity noise that must be removed and intensities normalized before spectral library searching, comparison, or plotting.

name: spectrum-intensity-normalization
description: Use when raw library spectra (e.g. MGF from GNPS or matchms-loaded entries) must be cleaned before training or scoring — e.g. noisy low-intensity peaks and unbounded peak counts would otherwise dominate model input.

name: spectrum-intensity-normalization
description: Use when spectra loaded from MGF, mzML, mzXML, msp, JSON, or USI carry raw (instrument-dependent) peak intensities and you need comparable relative intensities before peak filtering or before computing cosine-based similarity scores between reference and query spectra.

name: spectrum-metadata-extraction
description: Use when raw mass spectra must be read from msp, mzML, mzXML, MGF, JSON, or USI files and their per-spectrum peak counts and metadata fields need to be extracted into structured records before filtering or similarity scoring.

name: spectrum-metadata-validation
description: Use when a public or private MS/MS spectral library (e.g. GNPS .msp/MGF exports) contains unstandardized metadata and annotated structures, and spectra with inconsistent annotations must be removed before library searching or machine-learning training.

name: spectrum-molecule-match-scoring
description: Use when experimental LC-MS/MS spectra (MGF, mzXML, or mzML) must be searched against a chemical database (e.g. NPAtlas, PubChem, COCONUT) to identify known molecules or previously unreported variants, especially when precursor mass deltas suggest molecular variants.

name: spectrum-molecule-match-significance-estimation
description: Use when a variable- or exact-mode VInSMoC search (e.g. GNPS spectra vs COCONUT/PubChem/NPAtlas) reports hits per scan and you must quantify which spectrum–molecule matches are statistically significant and estimate false discovery rates.

name: spectrum-molecule-score-ranking
description: Use when tandem MS spectra (MGF, mzXML, or mzML) must be scored against a chemical database of candidate molecules and ranked per scan to produce top-k identification accuracy, including benchmarking against baseline tools like Dereplicator+ and molDiscovery.

name: spectrum-motif-decomposition-and-loading-analysis
description: Use when you have information-rich MS2 spectra (e.g. ~1,000 MS1 peaks per sample, ramped or stepped collision energy) from a complex mixture and want unsupervised substructure discovery without prior compound identification.

name: spectrum-mz-intensity-quantization-to-hypervectors
description: Use when preprocessed MGF spectra (precursor-filtered, L2-normalized, ≤50 peaks) must be converted into compact binary representations for fast pairwise distance computation on GPU.

name: spectrum-pair-data-augmentation
description: Use when training MS2DeepScore (or a similar Siamese spectral model) on annotated MS/MS spectra and you need to expand limited spectral data into diverse training pairs with Tanimoto-score labels.

name: spectrum-pairwise-similarity-scoring
description: Use when you have filtered/normalized spectra and need all-pairs spectral similarity scores (e.g. cosine scores with matching-peak counts) to identify related spectra or build network edges.

name: spectrum-peak-embedding-encoding
description: Use when preparing MS2 spectra (HDF5 or preprocessed arrays) as model input for LipiDetective or a similar transformer-based lipid identifier: converting raw peak lists into fixed-length embedded sequences with m/z-precision-aware vocabularies, intensity-by-ordering encoding, and label tokenization.

name: spectrum-peak-threshold-inspection
description: Use when raw MS/MS spectra (MGF, mzML, msp, JSON) contain low-abundance noise peaks and you need to reproduce or audit exactly which peaks a relative-intensity cutoff removes before similarity scoring.

name: spectrum-prediction-inference-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify and compare the computational cost (per-molecule prediction time) of a learned mass spectral prediction model against published quantum-chemical or CFM-EI baselines.

name: spectrum-preprocessing-denoising
description: Use when raw GNPS-derived MGF MS/MS spectra must be normalized and denoised before feeding a spectral-similarity model such as TransExION, Cosine, Spec2Vec, or MS2DeepScore.

name: spectrum-processing-benchmark-timing
description: Use when comparing the computational efficiency of Python mass-spectrometry processing libraries (e.g., spectrum_utils vs pymzML vs pyOpenMS) on a common spectral dataset such as an MGF file.

name: spectrum-processing-chain-assembly
description: Use when raw MS/MS spectra (e.g. from an iPRG2012 MGF file or a USI-resolvable online resource) need to be cleaned and normalized before downstream analysis such as deep neural network processing, peptide fragmentation annotation, or spectrum plotting.

name: spectrum-processing-pipeline-implementation
description: Use when prototyping a Python MS/MS preprocessing pipeline (m/z windowing, precursor and noise-peak removal, intensity filtering/scaling) on spectra loaded from MGF or mzML, or when benchmarking processing runtimes across spectrum_utils, pymzML, and pyOpenMS.

name: spectrum-quality-assessment
description: Use when an MGF/mzML/msp MS/MS collection contains sparse or noisy spectra — e.g. fewer than ~10 peaks above a relative-intensity threshold — and you must flag or drop low-quality spectra before library cleaning or spectral similarity comparison.

name: spectrum-quality-filtering
description: Use when an integrated OMSL (e.g. .MSP or .MGF files from GNPS, MoNA, MassBank) must be cleaned before export, and spectra with too few peaks or weak high-intensity peaks should be removed.

name: spectrum-quality-statistics
description: Use when validated peptide-spectrum matches and de novo predictions are available and you must quantify missing fragment ions, noise-peak prevalence, or quality-dependent peptide recall per tool.

name: spectrum-similarity-ranking
description: Use when you have a real MS/MS test spectrum plus candidate molecules (e.g. a 50-compound PubChem set built by Tanimoto similarity) and must rank candidates by spectral similarity to compute Top-1/3/5 identification accuracy.

name: spectrum-string-parsing
description: Use when the input is a mass spectrum given as a single-line 'm/z:intensity ion:intensity ...' string (e.g. MassBank PR100026-style records) that must be canonicalized before SPLASH generation or validation.

name: spectrum-structure-based-class-annotation

name: spectrum-technique-descriptor-lookup

name: spectrum-to-fingerprint-deep-learning-inference

name: spectrum-to-formula-transformer-inference

name: spectrum-type-mapping-table-csv-export

name: spectrum-usi-retrieval-from-online-repositories

name: spectrum-utils-figure-rendering

name: spectrum-vector-nearest-neighbor-indexing
description: Use when pairwise spectral similarity must be computed for large MS/MS datasets (millions of spectra) where exhaustive all-vs-all comparison within a precursor mass tolerance is computationally infeasible.

name: spectrum-visualization-parameter-tuning
description: Use when a tandem MS spectrum must be turned into a publication-ready figure with controlled m/z range, intensity zoom, sizing, grid, and peak-annotation settings, and exported in vector/raster/machine-readable formats.

name: specxplore-importing-pipeline-execution

name: speedup-ratio-calculation

description: Use when raw LA-ICP-MS elemental images (Agilent MassHunter batches, Perkin Elmer Elan .

name: spike-in-concentration-linearity-analysis

name: spike-in-linearity-analysis

name: spiked-standard-qc-validation-metabolomics

description: Use when a dataset contains spiked metabolite standards (e.g., 81 standards in a P. pastoris extract) and you need to quantify true-peak recall against XCMS-detected features.

name: splash-identifier-structure-verification
description: Use when a mass spectrum in single-line 'ion:intensity' representation (e.g. MassBank PR100026 caffeine) has a published SPLASH and you need to verify the identifier's blocks are reproducible from the spectrum.

name: spreadsheet-sheet-schema-verification

name: spreadsheet-tabular-data-extraction

description: Use when FDR must be estimated for open modification search SSMs whose mass shifts span many values: group matches by charge-normalized mass difference, estimate decoy/target FDR per group, and merge groups with fewer than 20 SSMs.

name: sssr-ring-perception-analysis
description: Use when a rule-based drug-like filter must be applied to an enumerated derivative SMILES set and per-ring-count screening (messy rings, >7 smallest sets of smallest rings) is one of the filtering criteria.

name: stability-plateau-detection
description: Use when applying ICA (e.g. FastICA) to a transcriptomic expression matrix and you must decide the decomposition order (number of components) from component reproducibility across restarts rather than an arbitrary choice.

name: stability-results-csv-export
description: Use when a completed ALISTER query (Sample search, Analyte search, Data filtering mode, or Protocol search) needs a persistent, citable record of stability classifications for reporting or downstream filtering.

name: stability-selection-edge-probability-estimation
description: Use when building differential metabolomics/lipidomics networks (p >> n, two conditions) and you need robust edge retention before GLASSO network estimation, e.g. TEDDY case-vs-control data with 134 metabolites and unbalanced groups.

name: stability-selection-edge-resampling
description: Use when building differential metabolomics networks with DNEA/Filigree where features outnumber samples (p >> n), and only resampling-stable edges should be retained after lambda tuning or approximation.

name: stabilized-ica-decomposition
description: Use when a samples-by-features cancer omics matrix (transcriptome, methylome, proteome, or single-cell) needs to be decomposed into independent, reproducible metagene/source components, or when ICA must be compared against PCA/NMF.

name: stable-isotope-dilution-calibration
description: Use when targeted LC-SRM or HRMS chromatograms contain stable-isotope-labeled internal standards for each analyte and the goal is absolute concentration (µM, nmol/g, µmol/mmol creatinine) rather than relative peak-area comparison.

name: stable-isotope-enrichment-parameterization
description: Use when simulating theoretical isotopic envelopes or fine structures of a user-defined peptide sequence or chemical formula under arbitrary SIP labeling percentages (partial 13C/15N incorporation), not just natural abundance.

name: stable-isotope-fractional-labelling-calculation
description: Use when quantified 13C isotopologue peak areas from a stable isotope tracer experiment (e.g., 13C6-glucose) are available and the goal is fractional labelling per metabolite to check pathway labelling patterns across parallel samples.

name: stable-isotope-label-pair-detection
description: Use when you have an XCMS-processed XCMSet with paired unlabeled/labeled sample groups (e.g., 12C vs 13C glucose) and need to find feature pairs showing shifted m/z and enrichment-consistent intensity changes.

name: stable-isotope-labeling-data-quantification
description: Use when GC-CI-MS raw centroided files from a stable-isotope labelling study (e.g. 13C-glucose or 13C-arginine tracing) need automatic isotopologue quantification for derivatized central-carbon or polyamine metabolites.

name: stable-isotope-labeling-detection-in-lcms-metabolomics
description: Use when untargeted LC/MS data from a stable isotope-labeling experiment (e.g. 12C vs 13C glucose) has been processed with XCMS and you need to enumerate features whose isotopic distribution shifts between unlabeled and labeled samples.

name: stable-isotope-labeling-feature-detection
description: Use when analyzing untargeted LC/MS peak tables from stable isotope-labeling experiments (e.g. 12C/13C glucose pairs in XCMS output) to find putatively labeled features and annotate them against a metabolite database.

name: stable-isotope-lc-ms-annotation
description: Use when you have XCMS-processed untargeted LC/MS data from paired unlabeled/labeled tracer experiments (e.g., 12C vs 13C glucose) and need to detect isotopically enriched features and annotate their base peaks.

name: stable-isotope-lcms-labeling-data-processing
description: Use when LC-MS data from a stable isotope labeling experiment (13C, 2H, 15N, 18O, or 34S tracer) are given as FAM column vectors in XLSX form and must be resolution-corrected to MDV and per-compound enrichment.

name: stable-isotope-lipidomics-compound-annotation
description: Use when HRMS lipidomics feature tables from a stable-isotope ([U-13C6] tracer) time course must be matched to lipid species and converted to isotope-corrected labeled quantities, e.g., to cluster PC/DAG species by labeling kinetics.

name: stable-isotope-probing-peptide-analysis
description: Use when analyzing proteomic stable isotope probing (SIP) data: you have peptide sequences with partially 13C-labeled spectra, need simulated isotopic envelopes at user-defined enrichment levels, or must validate database-search PSM outputs.

name: stable-isotope-tracer-mz-series-calculation
description: Use when defining target lists for targeted LC-MS metabolite quantification or stable-isotope tracer assays: you have a molecular formula plus adduct and need isotope-pattern m/z windows or per-isotopologue m/z series for up to N tracer atoms.

name: stable-isotope-tracing-spectra-evaluation
description: Use when selecting an ionization method/reagent gas for GC-MS isotopologue detection in stable-isotope labeling experiments, or when [M+H]+ molecular ions fragment excessively under the current source settings.

name: stacked-chromatogram-plotting
description: Use when non-targeted LC-MS peak lists (e.g. from MZmine 2 centWave extraction) must be transformed into image representations so a CNN can score peaks as true vs false.

name: stage-applicability-constraint-verification
description: Use when enumerating candidate metabolomic data-processing workflows and needing to constrain stage combinations to the dataset scenario (with QCSs, with ISs, or without both).

name: stage-specific-metabolic-biomarker-identification
description: Use when longitudinal or staged metabolomics data (e.g., NMR concentration matrices across sequential cell states) must be distilled into per-stage biomarker subnetworks, and pairwise transition-specific metabolite signatures are the goal.

name: standard-annotation-purity-comparison
description: Use when validating a metabolomics MS/MS clustering purity metric (e.g., MS-RT) against ground-truth manual annotations of chemical standards, where a standard-library dataset with known compound identities is available and FDR-controlled database search identifications are not.

name: standard-curve-regression-fitting
description: Use when converting detected MRM peak abundances from standard samples (e.g. 14 standards spanning 0.025–500 mol/mL) into calibration curves for absolute concentration calculation.

name: standard-over-blank-intensity-ratio-analysis
description: Use when three-replicate LC-MS runs of chemical standards (mzML/mzXML) must be screened for blank contamination and reproducibility, i.e. deciding which metabolites are validated or excluded by Std/Blk, RSD, and intensity cutoffs.

name: standard-row-filtering
description: Use when a lipidomic peak-area or peak-height matrix contains internal standard rows (e.g. SPLASH Lipidomix species) that must be removed after class-specific conversion to concentration, and species duplicates consolidated.

name: standardization-scaling-methods
description: Use when raw ICP-MS ionomics concentrations have already been log-transformed and batch-corrected and line-level z-score profiles are needed for PCA, hierarchical clustering, or relevance network extraction.

name: standardized-linear-regression-modeling
description: Use when simulating metabolomic spectra whose concentrations must correlate with a continuous biological variable (e.g. BMI, age) rather than a discrete case-control label.

name: standards-library-inventory-summarization
description: Use when you have an inventory table of metabolite standards with chemical class and ionization mode columns and need mode-level metabolite counts plus per-class composition percentages.

name: static-formula-library-construction
description: Use when building or benchmarking a C2MS model that predicts spectra from a fixed formula vocabulary, or when quantifying how the breadth of a model's formula support (e.g. GrAFF-MS ~10,000 formulae vs FraGNNet's learned fragment distribution) affects formula annotation on held-out NIST20 spectra.

name: static-spectrum-plot-rendering
description: Use when the goal is a static, publication-quality annotated MS/MS spectrum figure from a USI-addressed proteomics or metabolomics spectrum, e.g. replicating Figure 1A of the spectrum_utils paper.

name: statis-compromise-matrix-analysis
description: Use when you have multiple draft GEMs of the same isolate set (e.g. 432 At-SPHERE genomes reconstructed by four pipelines) and need to quantify structural differences and test their biological relevance against phylogeny.

name: statistical-accuracy-assessment-omics
description: Use when evaluating whether signal drift correction (e.g. QC-RFSC) actually improved differential feature calling or precision in LC-MS metabolomics/proteomics data.

name: statistical-data-verification
description: Use when a task asks to reproduce or verify published statistical claims from the IonFlow yeast ionomics case study (unchanged-profile fraction, ion correlations, network centrality extremes, enrichment results) against a re-executed pipeline.

name: statistical-hypothesis-testing-on-importance-distributions
description: Use when you have trained per-target random forest models (e.g., one per metabolite via 5-fold CV) and need to statistically test whether a pre-selected subset of top features is more important than the full feature set in independent validation data.

name: statistical-model-performance-comparison
description: Use when a log2-transformed metabolomics matrix (samples in rows, features in columns, batch labels in the first column) shows batch clustering (e.g. PCA by batch order) and several batch-correction models must be compared to pick the -fitting one.

name: statistical-model-residual-batch-effect-assessment
description: Use when after applying a batch correction model (ber, parametric/non-parametric ComBat, bagging ber or lowess) to a log2-scaled metabolomics matrix, you must decide whether residual intensity differences across analytical batches (e.

name: statistical-outlier-detection
description: Use when a metabolomics or proteomics dataset has been loaded into POMAShiny (target + features CSV), missing values imputed and data normalized, and samples must be screened for statistical outliers before statistical analysis.

name: statistical-power-bias-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating whether a reproducibility-detection method (e.g., MaRR maximal rank statistic) controls FDR, achieves high power, and estimates the proportion of reproducible signals without bias under simulated replicate data.

name: statistical-power-curve-estimation
description: Use when comparing association-test power between graph-regularized kernel tests (PaIRKAT, regularized normalized Laplacian), an unregularized normalized Laplacian kernel, and a kernel test ignoring network information across signal-to-noise-ratio levels.

name: statistical-power-estimation
description: Use when evaluating whether a revised pathway enrichment implementation (e.g., NetGSA REHE) retains power and type-I error control under simulated dysregulation before trusting its pathway-level calls.

name: statistical-reproducibility-verification
description: Use when a published finding reports concrete numerical outputs (e.g. rejection counts at fdr2d levels 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3) that must be re-derived from raw processed data to confirm reproducibility.

name: statistical-results-table-aggregation
description: Use when both per-feature statistics with FDR q-values and a multivariate importance ranking (e.g., MUVR RF 'mid' model ranks) exist for the same features, and a single combined ordering is needed to prioritize features for metabolite identification.

name: statistical-sensitivity-tpr-evaluation
description: Use when comparing imputation methods (e.g., GSimp vs QRILC vs kNN-TN) on left-censored/MNAR metabolomics data by measuring degradation of t-test statistical sensitivity, not just imputation accuracy.

name: statistical-significance-threshold-filtering
description: Use when you have per-study P-values and fold-changes combined into global statistics via amanida and need to select metabolites that pass a significance cutoff (combined P < 0.05) and/or an effect-size cutoff (e.g. fold-change < 1.5–2) for reporting.

name: statistically-significant-peak-selection
description: Use when a peak-based NMR feature matrix from speaq 2.0 has been produced and you must isolate which grouped peaks differ significantly between conditions (e.g. onion-intake vs control mice) before metabolite identification.

name: std-propagation-for-flux-ratios
description: Use when you have triplicate 0 h and 72 h extracellular metabolomics intensity/concentration measurements in species and medium samples and need to assign uncertainty to per-metabolite boundary fluxes from the MINNO eq 1 estimator (e.g. purine/pyrimidine fluxes in Borrelia cultures).

name: steatosis-inflammation-metabolic-state-comparison
description: Use when single-cell metabolomics data (e.g. a SpaceM MORPHnMOL.csv matrix) must be split by culture condition (e.g. +FA vs +FA+IL17A) and tested for differential metabolite abundance or metabolic state occupancy shifts.

name: stein-dot-product-spectrum-ranking
description: Use when comparing predicted EI-MS spectra against a library of candidate spectra and you need top-k lookup error rate or recall (e.g. recall-at-10), ranking by weighted Stein dot product.

name: steiner-forest-network-reconstruction
description: Use when raw LC-MS spectral peaks have been ranked by deep-learning feature attribution (e.g., ensemble RISE contribution scores) and the goal is to link those m/z signals to hidden metabolites, proteins, and disease pathways via network propagation.

name: stepped-field-dtims-ccs-calculation
description: Use when computing CCS values from stepped-field DTIMS-MS acquisitions (e.g., Agilent 6560 tune-mix infusion data) where ions are measured across multiple electric fields and per-field arrival times and frame metadata are available.

name: stepwise-count-reconciliation-with-paper-reports
description: Use when reproducing a paper's filtering cascade on its deposited data and you need to verify each intermediate count (peptides/proteins remaining per filter) matches the reported figure or supplemental table.

name: stepwise-forward-backward-biomarker-selection
description: Use when many candidate biomarkers are individually associated with survival but are highly correlated, and you must select a reduced subset that remains independently significant after mutual adjustment.

name: stereochemistry-preserving-molecule-merging
description: Use when merging molecular structures from multiple NP data sources into a non-redundant catalog where entries must be unified by stereochemistry-insensitive identity but original stereoisomers must remain retrievable under the parent entry.

name: sterol-fragmentation-pattern-modeling
description: Use when you need theoretical MS/MS fragment ions for N-Me derivatized unsaturated sterol lipids whose C=C double bond positions are known, e.g. to build a searchable fragment ion database for isomer-level sterolomics.

name: stitch-database-retrieval
description: Use when you have a list of significant metabolites (e.g. control vs mutant lung cancer metabolites with |fold change| ≥ 1 and adjusted p < 0.05) and need chemical-chemical interaction edges to build a network and identify hub metabolites like Xanthine.

name: stitch-network-construction-filtering
description: Use when metabolite-level pathway analysis needs network topology (betweenness centrality / pathway impact) built on STITCH chemical-chemical interactions, e.g. to prioritize pathways beyond ORA p-values.

name: stl-model-rendering
description: Use when an Optimus-produced feature-intensity table ('ili_input.csv from mzML-derived output) with sample x/y/z coordinates and spot radii must be visualized as a molecular map on a 3D object represented by an STL model.

name: stochastic-denoising-parameter-ablation
description: Use when evaluating a diffusion-based molecular generator (e.g. DiffSpectra/DMT) and you need to quantify how sampling noise level affects the trade-off between structural diversity (unique atom types, bond types, SMILES) and elucidation accuracy (top-1/top-10).

name: stochastic-hill-climbing-parameter-search
description: Use when per-metabolite spectral fits from an initial CRNN/deep-learning quantification still leave elevated residuals between reconstructed and original NMR spectra, and small per-component concentration/position corrections should be searched greedily.

name: stocsy-pseudospectrum-generation
description: Use when an MWAS on metabonomic 1H NMR spectra (e.g. plasma spectra vs BMI) flags unassigned ppm signals and you need to identify the underlying metabolite by correlating all spectral variables against a driver ppm.

name: stoichiometric-mass-balance-constraint-modeling
description: Use when you have relative-abundance (not absolute) time-course metabolomics data for an intracellular metabolic network with a known stoichiometric matrix and need to infer response factors / absolute concentrations without chemical standards.

name: stoichiometric-mass-balance-flux-solving
description: Use when time-course relative-abundance metabolomics data (concMatrix/timeVec) and a stoichiometric matrix are available but fluxomics measurements are not, and flux profiles v must be reconstructed for penalty-based optimization of response factors.

name: stoichiometry-matrix-parsing
description: Use when a task requires reconstructing the structure of the scFEA human metabolic map from its CSV model files — counting reaction modules, super modules, and intermediate substrates, or tallying genes/enzymes/transporters per module.

name: stop-gradient-anti-collapse-training
description: Use when training a self-supervised contrastive encoder on augmented ion-image pairs from mass spectrometry imaging data and representations are collapsing to trivial constants.

name: strain-identifier-mapping
description: Use when GCF–spectrum link scoring requires strain co-occurrence vectors but genome/molecule objects carry heterogeneous identifiers (antiSMASH BGC ids, GNPS spectrum ids, mzXML filenames) that must first be reconciled to a shared strain namespace.

name: stratified-cross-validation
description: Use when training a CNN classifier on grayscale molecular fingerprint images with imbalanced or skewed high/low bioactivity labels (normalized DPPH < 0.4 low, > 0.6 high) and you need stable fold-balanced metrics like AUC.

name: stratified-cross-validation-experiment-design
description: Use when comparing classifier variants (e.g., MSMCE-integrated vs. baseline ResNet50) on a labeled MS dataset and you need fair fold-shared training, fixed hold-out evaluation, and statistical significance (p < 0.05) for accuracy/F1 differences.

name: stratified-molecule-subampling-per-chromatographic-method
description: Use when validating few-shot RT projection to a chromatographic method with limited identified molecules — e.g. testing meta-learned GP projections at 10, 20, 25, 30, 40, 50 training points.

name: stratified-random-test-set-sampling
description: Decision support for comparing CCS prediction algorithms on a common footing: when benchmarking CCSP 2.0, CCSbase, AllCCS or DeepCCS against the same 463 McLean CCS Compendium measurements, or designing stratified hold-out splits for IM-MS regression evaluation.

name: stratified-summary-statistics
description: Use when you have paired CCS (or other instrument-reported quantity) measurements from two methods/software for the same compounds and need per-stratum (mode, acquisition setting) average absolute relative bias summaries and a tabulated output.

name: stratified-train-test-split-metabolomics
description: Use when building predictive models (e.g. RF or elastic-net classifiers) from a metabolite-by-sample intensity table with class labels, and you need class-proportioned train/test separation before feature selection and AUC evaluation.

name: stratified-train-test-split-optimization
description: Use when authentic analytical standards are unavailable for CMDN-annotated metabolites and chromatographic plausibility must be validated by predicting LC-HRMS retention times from molecular structure (SMILES/InChIKey).

name: striatal-cluster-map-comparison
description: Use when you have co-registered spatial metabolomics (MALDI-TOF/imzML) and spatial transcriptomics (e.g. 10X Visium) data on the same tissue section and need to test whether multi-omic integration recovers spatial populations that unimodal clustering misses.

name: string-functional-network-mapping
description: Use when per-gene enrichment scores (e.g., linear_msea_genebig_allpeaks_combined.csv) must be propagated over the STRING functional network to rank WES candidate genes for a single patient.

name: struct-model-train-apply-workflow
description: Use when a DatasetExperiment object needs a multi-step statistical pipeline (e.g. mean centring followed by PCA) executed via struct's model_train/model_predict and outputs extracted with predicted()/output accessors.

name: struct-template-class-definition
description: Use when building struct class-based template objects in R and you need a model parameter (such as number_components for PCA) to be a single constrained, self-documenting scalar slot.

name: structural-analogue-library-matching
description: Use when unknown query spectra must be matched to a large spectral library (e.g. GNPS ALL_GNPS.json) to detect highly related molecules via Spec2Vec similarity scores.

name: structural-analogue-retrieval-evaluation
description: Use when MS/MS spectra must be searched against a spectral library to retrieve structural analogues and compared to baseline similarity measures via precision-recall curves at Tanimoto cut-offs from 0.6 to 0.9.

name: structural-annotation-evaluation
description: Use when a metabolomics workflow has processed samples containing compounds of known identity (e.g. actinomycete extracts or commercial standards) and you must quantify how accurately formulas, structures, and spectral matches were annotated.

name: structural-descriptor-calculation
description: Use when a compound metadata sheet (template columns: unique sample id, plate_id, well_location, name, structure fields) must be standardized and enriched with SMILES/InChI/InChIKey/logP/monoisotopic mass before spectral library generation or database cross-referencing.

name: structural-key-annotation-extraction
description: Use when building annotation records for taxonomy categories or compounds that must be defined by unambiguous, computable structural keys (elemental composition, formula, oxyanions) parsed from a ChemOnt OBO file, as ClassyFire does for its inorganic branch.

name: structural-ordering-robustness-comparison-across-embeddings
description: Use when you must confirm that relative positions of a chosen lipid series in a graph-based structural space remain stable after recomputation within a larger background lipidome, e.g. reproducing the arc-like PC ordering.

name: structural-relatedness-assessment-of-spectral-clusters
description: Use when a spectral similarity network (e.g., an MCN output) must be validated against reference spectra with known structural classes, to check that community/cluster assignments group structurally related molecules together.

name: structural-similarity-metabolite-ranking
description: Use when you have acquired tandem MS/MS spectra of unknown metabolites (e.g. from Shimadzu LC-ESI-IT-TOF or Bruker Compact LC-ESI-QTOF) and need to identify them by ranking known database metabolites (e.g. KEGG) by structural similarity rather than exact spectral match.

name: structural-similarity-scoring
description: Use when identifying an unknown metabolite whose MS/MS spectrum lacks an exact match in a database, but structurally related known metabolites (e.g. KEGG entries) exist whose spectra can anchor similarity scoring.

name: structure-annotation-benchmark-metrics-computation
description: Use when you have held-out 1H-13C HSQC query spectra (normal or multiplicity edited) with ground-truth structures and need to score/reproduce Top-1 identification rates, annotation rates at cosine > 0.8, and precision/recall/F1@k against SMART 2.0 or NMRShiftDB shift-search baselines.

name: structure-annotation-rank-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking a candidate-ranking score for MS/MS structure annotation against known-correct structures (e.g., CASMI 2016 contest data), to quantify separation via AUC, FDR-level hit counts, and mean rank of correct hits.

name: structure-annotation-validation
description: Use when MS/MS library entries carry structural annotations (SMILES/InChI/InChIKey) whose consistency against adduct, precursor m/z, parent mass and ionmode must be checked or repaired before library searching or ML training.

name: structure-candidate-ranking
description: Use when untargeted metabolomics spectra (mzML/mzXML, positive ion mode) cannot be matched to spectral libraries and you need ranked, confidence-scored structure annotations from a structure database such as HMDB or a combinatorial candidate set.

name: structure-candidate-ranking-comparison
description: Use when you have MS/MS spectra of compounds already assigned at MSI confidence level 1 via authentic standards and need to measure how often an in silico annotator (CSI:FingerID) ranks the true structure first or in the top 3.

name: structure-database-size-validation
description: Use when enumerating a combinatorial search database (e.g. amino-acid conjugates of bile acid scaffolds) and you must confirm the enumerated structure count matches the expected database size before downstream annotation.

name: structure-deduplication-by-inchikey-layer
description: Use when building a non-redundant structural dataset from spectral library entries (e.g. GNPS .mgf) where duplicate structures and stereoisomers must be collapsed to unique first-layer InChIKeys.

name: structure-disjoint-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when re-evaluating formula or structure identification tools (e.g. SIRIUS 4 / CSI:FingerID) on a public challenge dataset such as CASMI 2016 and a fair, training-independent estimate of top-1/top-k identification rates is needed.

name: structure-disjoint-cross-validation
description: Use when evaluating MS/MS-to-fingerprint prediction models (MetFID-style ANNs) where multiple spectra of the same compound exist across collision energies or instruments, and naive random splits would leak structural identity.

name: structure-disjoint-dataset-splitting
description: Use when training or benchmarking spectral similarity or library-matching models (e.g. MS2Deepscore, Spec2Vec) on annotated spectral libraries like GNPS, where spectra of the same or closely related compounds must not appear in both train and test splits.

name: structure-disjoint-model-evaluation
description: Use when assessing whether a metabolite annotation or fingerprint-prediction model generalizes beyond its training compounds, e.g. before publishing accuracy claims for an MS/MS spectrum predictor.

name: structure-file-inventory-verification
description: Use when a data record asserts a specific number and provenance split of structure files (e.g. .pdb files from PDB vs AlphaFold DB) in a deposit and the deposit contents must be enumerated and reconciled against that statement.

name: structure-modification-class-shift-analysis
description: Use when you need to test if a structure-based classifier's predictions are causally driven by specific functional groups, by modifying those groups in a known molecule and observing label changes.

name: structure-organism-pair-curation
description: Use when a structure database's organism/biological-source field is free text and needs detection of scientific names, synonym resolution, and backbone-standardized taxonomy before metabolite annotation or scoring.

name: structure-organism-pair-export-formatting
description: Use when a validated structure-organism-reference table (e.g. LOTUS table.tsv.gz from Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.5794106) must be converted into Wikidata upsert records for batch upload.

name: structure-prediction-evaluation
description: Use when scoring de novo structure predictions from tandem MS2 spectra against known ground-truth SMILES, requiring exact-match, Tanimoto>0.9, and Tanimoto>0.8 recovery rates on a held-out spectral test set.

name: structure-related-metabolite-database-matching
description: Use when you must identify an unknown metabolite from an MS/MS spectrum but the exact compound is absent from spectral databases, and structurally related known metabolites (e.g. KEGG entries) are available to anchor the search.

name: structure-standardization-and-cleaning
description: Use when raw compound sets from sources like MoNA, MassBank, Metabolomics Workbench, RIKEN, or the Pathogen Box carry mixed SMILES (salts, metal-containing entries) that must be cleaned before computing CDK descriptors for PCA or RT modeling.

name: structured-comparison-table-construction
description: Use when an article makes comparative claims about multiple formats or methods (e.g. mzML vs vendor RAW vs mzPeak) across explicit trade-off dimensions, and the goal is a machine-readable, quote-backed comparison table.

name: structured-csv-output-generation
description: Use when you have batch-processed MSThunder outputs from multiple water sample groups (influent, effluent, surface, source, tap water) and need a consolidated, deduplicated pollutant inventory with sample assignments for reporting or validation.

name: structured-data-tabulation
description: Use when an article asserts a count of harmonized or curated source resources (e.g. 'over 40 electronic resources') and a structured, count-verified inventory of those sources must be extracted from the text.

name: structured-error-report-generation
description: Use when a lipidomic data matrix (CSV/TXT) must be checked before upload to Lipid One 2.0, and issues such as duplicate lipid names, all-zero rows, or invalid group labels must be reported explicitly.

name: structured-findings-tabulation
description: Use when a review article reports multiple named empirical benchmark results with distinct tool-condition pairings (e.g. DeepRescore, inSPIRE, MHCquant, MSBooster, Prosit, Percolator) and they must be captured as a machine-readable findings table.

name: structured-json-record-construction
description: Use when you have loaded spectrums from an MGF-formatted file via matchms.importing.load_from_mgf and need a structured, verifiable JSON record of each spectrum's peaks and metadata before downstream filtering or scoring.

name: structured-output-matrix-construction
description: Decision support for comparing tool coverage across multiple software suites or toolkits — e.g., when the research question asks which analytical tools (ANOVA, PCA, LASSO, blank feature filtering) appear in all, some, or exactly one of several Galaxy metabolomics frameworks.

name: structured-record-construction
description: Use when a task requires turning qualitative findings from a review article (e.g. tool usage rankings from the Weber et al. 2016 Metabolomics Society survey) into a machine-readable record set with a uniform schema.

name: structured-results-table-authoring
description: Use when a research question requires comparing multiple methods or configurations reported in an article (e.g., reagent gases or ionization techniques) and the findings are scattered across Results text, figures, and supplementary figures.

name: structured-table-construction
description: Use when a repository manifest or setup script must be enumerated into a structured table of tool names plus pipeline-stage categories, and the resulting count must be compared against counts stated in the paper's abstract or revision history.

name: student-t-test-metabolomics
description: Use when an LC/MS untargeted metabolomics feature table (m/z, retention time, intensity per sample) must be reduced to a significant feature list by univariate statistics before mummichog pathway analysis.

name: students-t-test-class-comparison
description: Use when PCA sample scores from a preprocessed metabolomics data matrix (DSO) are available and you need per-component evidence of whether biological and blank (or other) sample classes are statistically separated.

name: study-design-evidence-classification
description: Use when auditing or rebuilding a DNA adduct database table where each literature-derived entry must carry a study-design label (in vitro/in vivo/human) plus source/genotoxicant and detection-technique fields.

name: study-design-stratification-of-adduct-entries
description: Use when a DNA adductomics database (.xlsx with metadata) must be profiled or validated by stratum — study design, identification technique, genotoxicant class, source, or precursor mass range.

name: study-id-based-repository-data-access
description: Use when a ready-to-use NMR metabolomics data set from MetaboLights or Metabolomics Workbench is needed and only the study identifier (e.g. an MTBLS or Metabolomics Workbench study id) is available, and the raw repository file system is non-standard.

name: study-identifier-based-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when a task requires re-analyzing a publicly deposited NMR metabolomics study (e.g. MTBLS563) and you have its repository study id but the raw download lacks a standardized file-system layout.

name: study-size-gamma-weight-assignment
description: Use when combining per-study overall P-values from metabolomics studies where only P-value and fold-change (not variance or raw data) are reported, and each study's participant count (n) is available as the sole basis for weighting.

name: stutility-landscape-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking a spatial multi-omics integration workflow (e.g., spatial transcriptome + MALDI-MSI) against a morphology-only alignment baseline such as STUtility on same-section or neighboring-section data.

name: subalignment-match-table-construction
description: Use when two or more same-method, independently processed nontargeted LC-MS feature tables (Feature Metadata + Feature Abundances) must be aligned, and pairwise Source-to-Target feature matches must be identified and ranked.

name: subclass-abundance-quantification
description: Use when you have MAW's merged candidate results for a metabolomics dataset (e.g. file_id_mergedResults-with-one-Candidates.csv) and need to quantify and plot which chemical subclasses dominate the classified top-ranked annotations.

name: subcluster-family-and-clan-grouping
description: Use when you have a large set of predicted sub-clusters (e.g. 108,085 PRESTO-STAT sub-clusters from tens of thousands of BGCs) and need to organise them into families and clans for redundancy removal and relatedness assessment.

name: subcluster-motif-probability-filtering
description: Use when querying tokenised BGCs (bags of (sub)Pfam domain combinations) against trained LDA sub-cluster motifs and you must decide which gene-to-motif assignments count as real sub-cluster predictions versus noise.

name: subcluster-motif-querying
description: Use when you have antiSMASH-predicted BGCs tokenised with (sub)Pfam domains and need to identify which PRESTO-TOP sub-cluster motifs they match, e.g. to nominate a candidate BGC for an orphan metabolite.

name: subcluster-overlap-calculation
description: Use when validating predicted biosynthetic sub-clusters against a curated set of experimentally verified sub-clusters by quantifying per-sub-cluster gene overlap fractions against a defined cut-off.

name: subcluster-size-occurrence-distribution-validation
description: Use when a PRESTO-STAT run on tokenised antiSMASH-DB BGCs has produced a sub-cluster table and you must verify the detection count and the size and BGC-occurrence distributions reproduce the reported benchmarks.

name: subclusterblast-validation-overlap-analysis
description: Use when an unsupervised sub-cluster prediction model (e.g. PRESTO-TOP topics trained on tokenised BGCs) must be benchmarked against experimentally verified sub-clusters such as the 109 SubClusterBlast entries.

name: subformula-enumeration-from-precursor-formula
description: Use when annotating MS2 peaks from a tandem mass spectrum against a candidate molecular formula, e.g. de novo formula ranking with MIST-CF, and no fragmentation tree is required.

name: subformula-loss-annotation
description: Use when a peak list has already passed electronic denoising and a precursor formula (from SMILES+adduct or formula) is known, and remaining fragment ions must be classified as plausible subformula losses vs chemical noise.

name: subformula-loss-chemical-denoising
description: Use when MS/MS spectra contain chemical noise ions — e.g. co-isolated contaminants or artificially generated chemical noise — and the precursor molecular formula and adduct are known, so fragments lacking chemically plausible subformula losses can be removed before spectral matching.

name: subformula-loss-chemical-plausibility-filtering
description: Use when cleaning MS/MS spectra of chemical noise ions with a known or predicted precursor molecular formula (SMILES or formula) and adduct, so fragments unexplainable by plausible subformula losses can be discarded before spectral matching.

name: subformula-loss-mass-tolerance-retuning
description: Use when adapting the Spectral Denoising / Denoising Search pipeline to MS/MS data from a non-Orbitrap high-resolution analyzer, where the Orbitrap-calibrated electronic-noise rule (fewer than four ions at ±0.1% relative intensity) and mass tolerances may not transfer.

name: subgroup-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when a user-defined gene panel (e.g., 26 IFN-induced genes) should partition samples into activity-score-positive/negative subgroups, and per-subgroup differential expression plus pathway exploration (EnrichR/GSEA) is the analysis goal.

name: subgroup-fdr-filtering
description: Use when filtering open-search SSMs (e.g. shifted dot product matches with large precursor mass shifts) where a single global FDR would be inflated or underpowered for modified peptides; requires target and decoy SSM counts per mass-difference group.

name: subgroup-fdr-stratification
description: Reference for controlling FDR in open searches where modifications shift precursor masses and a single global target-decoy FDR would underestimate error rates.

name: subject-sample-factor-consistency-checking
description: Use when validating mwTab-format files from Metabolomics Workbench studies: run this check on every parsed MWTabFile to detect blank/missing sample IDs or factors and sample IDs in SUBJECT_SAMPLE_FACTORS that do not appear in the _DATA blocks.

name: subject-sample-factors-metadata-verification
description: Use when Metabolomics Workbench analyses are available in both 'mwTab' and JSON formats and you must verify whether SUBJECT_SAMPLE_FACTORS entries (and related section/item content) agree between the two parsed representations.

name: sublevel-phmm-construction
description: Use when building a BiG-SLiCE feature space that needs finer resolution than the 293 core biosynthetic pHMMs, i.e. when sub-clade-level domain fingerprinting of BGCs is required.

name: submodular-reference-spectra-selection
description: Use when a learned spectral encoder (e.g. GLEAMS) needs a small, diverse reference-spectrum set for pairwise similarity features, and the training corpus (~200,000 downsampled MS/MS spectra) is too large to compare against exhaustively.

name: subnetwork-extraction-and-node-coloring
description: Use when a GNPS molecular networking job is complete and a specific molecular family (a connected cluster of MS2 consensus spectra) must be isolated and its nodes classified by sample origin, e.g., lung tissue vs. microbial isolates in MSV000083359.

name: subnetwork-node-count-tabulation
description: Use when a GNPS molecular networking job has completed and you need to quantify how a parameter sweep (Minimum Consensus Cluster Size, PIMT/FIMT tolerance, filter settings) changes the node/spectrum composition of a specific subnetwork.

name: subpfam-hmm-construction-from-msa-clades
description: Use when standard Pfam pHMMs are too coarse for downstream BGC tokenisation and per-clade subfamily-level pHMMs are needed from existing Pfam MSAs.

name: subsample-pvalue-aggregation
description: Use when comparing statistical testing methods whose p-values are indistinguishable on the full cohort (here, >1,000 complete cases), and differences in power need to be exposed by evaluating averaged p-values over random subsamples of controlled smaller sizes.

name: subspace-permutation-processing-strategies
description: Use when evaluating whether multidimensional (N-dim) feature detection improves sensitivity over staged lower-dimensional processing on LC-IMS-MS/MS data, or when comparing a DEIMoS pipeline to MS-DIAL-style (m/z versus RT followed by DT) approaches.

name: substance-assay-annotation-retrieval
description: Use when a workflow needs the full set of third-party chemical annotations or assay descriptions for a specific PubChem SID or AID, and the required data are not exposed by other PubChem programmatic access routes.

name: substrate-frequency-tabulation
description: Use when you need to count and tabulate NRPS A-domain substrate annotations (e.g. per-substrate frequencies, unique substrate totals) from structured biosynthetic gene cluster records such as MIBiG JSON entries.

name: substrate-metabolite-pair-annotation
description: Use when you need to convert a site-of-metabolism (SoM) dataset into atom-pair BoM annotations, or when reproducing/verifying the 2262-record EBoMD annotation counts (828 η-η, 1348 η-H, 86 η-SPN).

name: substrate-selectivity-evidence-code-extraction
description: Use when reproducing or auditing how the MIBiG JSON schema encodes evidence for A-domain/NRPS substrate selectivity — e.g. enumerating the evidence codes the schema permits for substrate annotations.

name: substructure-annotation-of-molecular-families
description: Use when molecular families in a GNPS molecular network have no or few spectral library matches but MS2LDA motif data, NAP/DEREPLICATOR in silico annotations, and ClassyFire classification are available, and you need level-3 class or substructure-level annotation.

name: substructure-fingerprint-prediction
description: Use when untargeted LC-MS/MS chemical features (MGF with MS1+MS2 peaks imported as MassSpectrometryFeatures) need predicted molecular fingerprints to build a Qemistree chemical hierarchy, rather than relying on sparse spectral library matches.

name: substructure-motif-frequency-analysis
description: Use when you have a GNPS molecular network and MS2LDA Mass2Motifs and need to quantify motif frequency across molecular families to find substructural diversity or common substructures linking known and unknown compounds.

name: substructure-penalty-scoring
description: Use when annotating MS/MS or MSn spectra where no informative reference spectra exist and candidate structures (e.g. from PubChem) must be ranked by how well they explain observed fragment peaks.

name: substructure-presence-vector-construction
description: Use when you have a molecule as a SMILES string and need the substructure presence representation (957 SMART-defined fragments) required to train or run inference with the substructure-to-structure transformer.

name: substructure-scaffold-retention-assessment
description: Use when you have multiple SMILES predictions per molecule plus ground-truth SMILES (e.g., processed_predictions.h5 from an NMR2Struct test-set run) and want to characterize the chemical proximity of wrong predictions via Tanimoto similarity.

name: subsystem-restricted-model-evaluation
description: Use when you need to test whether a constraint-based MPI predictor (SARTRE) generalizes to metabolite-protein pairs from metabolic subsystems that were excluded from training, or to assess subsystem-level accuracy drops.

name: subvisual-colocalization-detection-verification
description: Use when reproducing the Costes colocalization validation on simulated red/green image pairs, or when verifying that an automated colocalization method detects subvisually obvious overlap and quantifies false positives/negatives.

name: sum-based-normalization-comparison-tic
description: Use when you have raw peak-intensity tables (e.g. xlsx) from pooled QC injections and must decide among iTIC, fTIC, and mTIC sum-based scaling before adopting ML-based normalizers like SERDA/SERRF.

name: sum-formula-enumeration-heuristic-filtering
description: Use when building reference metabolite isotope-pattern models for feature-hypothesis validation in LC-MS data (e.g. FeatureFinderMetabo), requiring enumerated sum formulas and theoretical isotope patterns as training material.

name: sum-normalized-intensity-table-handling
description: Use when raw FT-ICR MS peak abundances with assigned molecular formulas must be normalized before chemodiversity or statistical analysis, and the normalization method itself must be chosen empirically rather than fixed a priori.

name: sum-of-ranks-method-comparison
description: Use when comparing two or more imputation configurations (e.g., lo=-Inf/hi='min' vs LOQ- or 10%-quantile upper bounds) across a gradient of missingness levels and a single robust aggregate ranking is needed.

name: summarized-experiment-object-manipulation
description: Use when a metabonomic dataset must be filtered (e.g. CV_th = 0.30 reproducibility filter) while keeping the feature matrix and associated metadata coherently stored in a single SummarizedExperiment container that downstream MWASTools functions expect.

name: summarizedexperiment-container-assembly
description: Use when a maplet pipeline needs a starting container: you have an intensity matrix (e.g. from MetaboLights/Metabolomics Workbench or a raw CSV) plus annotation tables and must bind them into one SummarizedExperiment .rds.

name: summarizedexperiment-container-wrangling
description: Use when building reproducible metabolomics (or other omics) pipelines in R where intermediate results, applied steps, and parameters must be retraced end-to-end from a single serialized object.

name: summarizedexperiment-data-handling
description: Use when metabolomics/1H-NMR data must be loaded into R as a SummarizedExperiment (metabo_SE) so MWASTools functions can operate on feature intensities and clinical metadata together.

name: summarizedexperiment-data-structuring
description: Use when vendor lipid quantification output (LipidSearch or LIQUID, or Metabolomics Workbench data) has been parsed, boundary-filtered, and internal-standard normalized, and needs to be packaged with sample metadata into a standard Bioconductor container for downstream analysis.

name: summarizedexperiment-object-construction
description: Use when a mass_dataset object (from tidyMass processing or the massdataset interoperability vignette) must be handed off to tools that require a SummarizedExperiment data structure.

name: summarizedexperiment-slot-population
description: Use when measured omics data (e.g. a 150x4 measurements data.frame such as Fisher's iris data) must be wrapped with its sample_meta and variable_meta into a struct DatasetExperiment object for downstream struct/structToolbox model pipelines.

name: summary-statistics-comparison-across-models
description: Use when you need to quantify and contrast the breadth of predicted formula distributions from two spectrum-prediction models on a shared held-out test set, e.

name: summary-statistics-compilation
description: Use when reproducing or tabulating feature/annotation throughput statistics of a reaction-guided metabolomics workflow (DMS, RCS, SSN layers) over LC-HRMS data from enzymatic biotransformation assays.

name: summary-statistics-computation
description: Use when a per-compound prediction table (e.g., MAIP scores keyed to SMILES) must be split into annotated subgroups and summarized as group sizes, means, and observed ranges to test a structure–activity correlation.

name: summary-statistics-table-generation
description: Use when you have batch-predicted 1H chemical shifts for a large compound library and need to report proportions of molecules passing a signal-deshielding threshold (e.g. ≥10% deshielded signals) into a summary statistics table.

name: summary-statistics-table-generation
description: Use when a ranked candidate list has been produced for each anchor–suspect pair and you need to quantify ranking accuracy via average correct-suspect rank and the proportion of cases where the true suspect is ranked first.

name: summary-table-assembly
description: Use when a task requires pulling exact reported numbers (e.g. 518 total metabolites, 313 positive-mode, 205 negative-mode) out of a Results-section text or figure legend and packaging them into a machine-readable summary table.

name: sunburst-hierarchy-visualization
description: Use when MAW's final per-feature candidates (e.g. file_id_mergedResults-with-one-Candidates.csv) carry CANOPUS/ClassyFire class assignments and the goal is a hierarchical sunburst plus subclass abundance percentages.

name: super-sampled-standardized-area-extraction
description: Use when raw profile-mode LC-HRMS chromatograms (mzXML/mzML) must be converted into fixed-size rt x m/z candidate areas around local maxima before CNN peak classification, or when reproducing PeakBot's candidate-generation stage.

name: superclass-relative-abundance-computation-across-organisms
description: Use when a ConCISE consensus annotation file (from a GNPS feature-based molecular networking task plus CANOPUS canopus_summary.tsv) must be summarized into superclass-relative-abundance profiles that are compared across organisms or sample sources.

name: supervised-classifier-training-multiple-algorithms
description: Use when you have a pathway deregulation score (PDS) matrix and phenotype labels and need to build and compare multiple classification models with cross-validated performance metrics.

name: supervised-multivariate-modeling-lc-ms-metabolomics
description: Use when a preprocessed, imputed LC-MS feature table (e.g. a notame MetaboSet loaded from full_data.RData) with a class label such as 'group' needs supervised multivariate modeling to rank molecular features.

name: supervised-siamese-spectral-embedding-training
description: Use when building a spectral similarity predictor from annotated tandem MS libraries (e.g. GNPS ALL_GNPS.mgf) where spectral similarity must proxy chemical structural similarity, and no test structure may leak into training.

name: supplemental-table-reproduction
description: Use when a paper publishes shared pipeline outputs (e.g., DIMPLE mass-signature lists) plus a numeric supplemental table, and the goal is to independently re-derive and validate those exact counts.

name: supplementary-data-reproduction
description: Use when a task requires reproducing a deposited trend table or figure showing how MS parameters (e.g. capillary voltage, ion energy, collision energy) change the number and percentage of ISF features relative to real metabolic features.

name: supplementary-document-table-parsing
description: Use when a paper's quantitative claim (e.g. how many of 36 standard metabolites are covered by HILIC ESI+, HILIC ESI−, CE alkaline/acidic anion and CE cation methods) exists only as a table inside an electronic supplementary file that must be transcribed to structured data.

name: supplementary-table-cross-verification
description: Reference for validating that a curated inventory of tool- or database-specific lipid annotation styles is complete and correctly attributed against a paper's supplementary file and repository configuration files.

name: supplementary-table-data-extraction
description: Use when claims in a paper (ROC AUC benchmarks, metabolite counts, concordance categories) must be verified against numeric values locked in supplementary tables supplied as .docx/.xlsx, rather than re-derived from raw data.

name: supplementary-table-data-extraction
description: Use when reproducing or auditing validation numbers (expected-feature detection rate, formula/structure annotation accuracy) that appear only in supplementary tables rather than the main text, e.g. Tables S9–S11 of the UmetaFlow paper.

name: supplementary-table-data-extraction
description: Use when a paper's main text defers quantitative results to supplementary tables (e.g., Supplementary Tables 6/7/8/11 in the GNPS SI) and the goal is to reproduce or verify a reported number from those tables.

name: supplementary-table-data-extraction
description: Use when Supplementary Tables contain curated entity lists with database cross-references (e.g. MetaCyc-indexed vs. orphan metabolites) that must be merged into one dataset and validated against reported indexation statistics.

name: supplementary-table-data-extraction
description: Use when a validation task requires comparing article-reported intermediate precision or agreement metrics (CVs, median Pearson r) against values recomputed from supplementary replicate data tables.

name: supplementary-table-fdr-validation
description: Use when a reimplementation of METASPACE-ML FDR estimation (weighted target-decoy ranking with Laplace correction) produces per-ion FDR values that must be checked against the paper's published Supplementary Data 10 scores/FDR table.

name: supplementary-table-range-verification
description: Use when a pipeline reproduces a paper's result table (e.g. pairwise overlap matrices from annotation runs) and you need a quantitative acceptance check against the ranges published in supplementary tables before trusting the reproduction.

name: supplementary-table-reaction-extraction
description: Use when a paper reports reaction gaps (e.g., 18 missing KEGG reactions across Borrelia species) only in supplementary tables, and you need a machine-readable per-reaction table annotated with pathway class, species, and literature-support flags.

name: supplementary-table-reproduction
description: Use when a paper's key quantitative result lives in a supplementary table or figure (e.g. class-matching score tables built from MIBiG 2.0) and the goal is to rebuild it independently from raw public data and verify it against the published supplement.

name: supplementary-table-result-verification
description: Use when benchmarking candidate gene prioritization output against a reference causal gene set, or when reproducing/validating enrichment statistics (odds ratios with 95% CIs) against published supplementary tables such as ProGeM's Table S7.

name: support-vector-regression-hyperparameter-tuning
description: Use when building SVR regression models from molecular descriptor tables and you need systematic hyperparameter (C, epsilon) selection via cross-validation plus descriptor reduction before validation.

name: support-vector-regression-model-training
description: Use when you need to build or rebuild a CCS prediction model for a specific adduct type or molecular class — e.g. when published CCSP 2.0 models ([M−H]−, [M+H]+, [M+Na]+) do not cover your ions, or when you have a unique experimental CCS training set to fit.

name: surrogate-pooled-qc-feature-coverage-assessment
description: Use when a metabolomics feature matrix includes pooled/surrogate QC injections run alongside study samples, and you must determine which features a QC-based drift-correction model (e.g. lowess) cannot correct because they are absent from QC injections.

name: survey-result-extraction
description: Use when a task asks to reproduce or verify specific tool-usage rankings or percentages reported from a community survey (e.g. the Metabolomics Society survey) within a full-text article.

name: survival-curve-estimation-from-metabolic-scores
description: Use when the analysis goal is examining how a projected metabolomics-based score (e.g., mortality score) predicts events over time, and the dataset contains samples with both a projected score and event/time endpoint data.

name: survival-function-mse-estimation
description: Use when two ranked lists of features (e.g., 43,919 SEQC transcripts ranked by read count) need a nonparametric reproducibility assessment, and a critical threshold N-hat controlling mFDR at a chosen alpha (0.05 or 0.01) must be derived from maximum rank statistics.
tools: Python (NumPy/pandas implementation of the closed-form MaRR estimator)

name: survival-function-mse-minimization
description: Use when you have per-experiment rank lists (rank 1 = most extreme) from two replicate high-throughput experiments and need a tuning-parameter-free estimate of the number of reproducible genes (k-hat/pi1-hat) without parametric assumptions on the dependence structure.

name: survival-meta-analysis-heterogeneity-assessment
description: Use when you have per-cohort Cox model summary statistics (lnHR and SE) for many candidate biomarkers and must pool them across cohorts while quantifying between-cohort heterogeneity (I2, P(het)) and selecting an independent biomarker set.

name: suspect-ranking-evaluation
description: Use when ranked candidate lists (e.g. BAM suspect rankings) must be scored for how accurately the correct structure is placed, or when a rank-distribution histogram and top-k hit rates need to be computed and visualized.

name: sva-combat-batch-effect-correction
description: Use when a raw gene/miRNA/isoform count matrix from an RNA-seq workflow (e.g. Salmon quantification) shows batch structure — samples processed in multiple batches or confounded runs — and must be batch-corrected before differential expression analysis.

name: svd-based-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when a wide-format metabolomics feature matrix (samples as columns, unique feature IDs as rows) plus a design file mapping samples to groups needs ordination, group separation assessment, or feature-weight inspection.

name: svd-based-matrix-inversion-stabilization
description: Use when converting an estimated covariance matrix of metabolite abundances into a Jacobian matrix in R and the linear system is ill-conditioned or noisy, requiring SVD-stabilized solving across replicate estimates.

name: svd-metagene-eigenvalue-analysis
description: Use when you have gene expression matrices over groups (e.g. 17 DM2/17 NGT/9 IGT diabetes samples or 75 airway epithelium smoker samples) and need to check whether gene-set enrichment rankings reflect coordinate expression strength rather than consistent group differences.

name: svd-pathway-activity-decomposition
description: Use when peak-intensity matrices with compound annotations (KEGG/ChEBI IDs) must be converted to pathway-level activity scores, especially when noise and missing peaks make ORA/GSEA unreliable.

name: svg-figure-generation
description: Use when you need to programmatically draw a biosynthetic gene cluster (e.g. a MIBiG modular PKS/NRPS entry) as a spaghetti diagram with a vertically aligned backbone, exported to an .svg file.

name: svm-classification-hypertension-status
description: Use when you need to quantify how much biological signal a normalisation method preserves — e.g. comparing hRUV variants, ratio, SVR, SERRF, or RLSC on their cross-validated accuracy for a binary clinical outcome such as hypertension status.

name: svm-classifier-training
description: Use when you have a sample-by-analyte intensity matrix (aligned MS features, peptides, or proteins) with binary labels (e.g., HCC early recurrence) and need to build and compare predictive classifiers via cross-validated AUC.

name: svm-classifier-training
description: Use when a curated, expert-labeled set of representative good and bad chromatographic peaks exists and you want a single combined classifier for peak quality filtering instead of varying individual metric cutoff thresholds.

name: svm-classifier-training-on-msi-spectra
description: Use when you need a classical supervised classification baseline for raw high-dimensional mass spectra (e.g., 85,062 m/z variables from MALDI FT-ICR MSI) with pixel-level normal/tumor labels, to benchmark against a deep learning model.

name: svm-confidence-score-training
description: Use when calibrating in silico structure annotation scores (e.g. CSI:FingerID) from reference-spectra training sets into posterior confidence scores for FDR estimation of novel-molecule annotations.

name: svm-cross-validation-auc-assessment
description: Use when a corrected/processed metabolomics feature table (samples × peaks) and a candidate biomarker list need an unbiased predictive-performance estimate distinguishing phenotypic classes such as CRC vs CE.

name: svm-isotope-pattern-classification
description: Use when LC-MS feature hypotheses (groups of up to six mass traces) must be filtered and validated as plausible metabolite isotope patterns during feature assembly, e.g. when reproducing FeatureFinderMetabo's >95% sensitivity/specificity on human plasma data.

name: svm-metabolite-classifier-training
description: Use when compound databases with pre-calculated fingerprints must be classified as metabolite-like vs non-metabolite-like, or when the FingerScorer SVM for ChemDistiller annotation must be (re)trained or benchmarked.

name: svm-peak-classifier-output-interpretation
description: Decision support for interpreting or post-processing per-peak quality class assignments from WiPP's SVM classifier, e.g. when filtering detected GC-MS peaks by quality class or merging classified peak sets across algorithms.

name: svm-peak-quality-classification
description: Use when preprocessing large-scale GC-MS metabolomics data with unreliable automated peak detection, and you need to classify detected peaks as high/medium/low quality before downstream statistical analysis.

name: svm-random-forest-baseline-classification
description: Use when benchmarking a new SCMS cell-phenotype classifier against conventional ML baselines on the same pretreated single-cell metabolomic feature matrix and identical train/validation/test splits.

name: svm-training-data-generation
description: Use when you need to build or regenerate training data for a classifier that recognizes metabolite isotope patterns from mass-to-charge spacing and abundance ratios, and only theoretical formula simulations are available.

name: svr-based-intensity-normalization
