description: Use when an extracted LC-MS metabolic feature table has already been filtered for noisy features (>20% MVs in QC samples, >50% MVs in study groups) and missing values imputed (KNN), and intensities still need drift correction before statistical analysis.

name: svr-baseline-model-comparison
description: Use when training a new chemical shift prediction model and needing to benchmark it against a legacy SVR predictor per atom type (1H, 13C, 15N) via cross-validated RMSD.

name: svr-drift-correction-modeling
description: Use when detected features from LC-IMS-MS/MS samples must be aligned to a reference sample and coordinates for m/z, drift time, and retention time drift nonlinearly between runs.

name: svr-hyperparameter-grid-search
description: Use when fitting a linear-kernel SVR regression model (e.g., CCS prediction from molecular descriptors) and the regularization parameter C and epsilon must be tuned by k-fold cross-validation to minimize RMSECV.

name: svr-model-training
description: Use when you need to fit a customized CCS prediction model from a curated training set of ion-mobility measurements (e.g. [M−H]−, [M+H]+, [M+Na]+ ions) before predicting or filtering candidate structures by ΔCCS threshold.

name: svr-model-weight-inspection
description: Use when a trained linear SVR CCS-prediction model must be inspected to report how many descriptors RFE retained and which descriptor classes (ATS, Barysz, Kier, TIC, constitutional) dominate its feature weights.

name: svr-rbf-ccs-regression
description: Use when a lipid CCS value must be predicted for a lipid class/adduct covered by the LiPydomics experimental CCS database, or when reproducing/validating the LiPydomics SVR CCS prediction performance against reported MAE/MDAE/RMSE/MDRE metrics.

name: svr-retention-time-regression-baseline
description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking retention-time-based prediction on PredRet chromatographic systems (e.g. baseline_single_perc or all_on_one_perc scenarios), or when quantifying how SVR accuracy scales with the percentage of target-system training data.

name: swath-acquisition-lcms-processing
description: Use when processing multisample DIA-MS/MS data acquired with SWATH acquisition (e.g. SCIEX WIFF lipidomics/metabolomics files) and coeluted fragment spectra must be deconvoluted into compound-specific MS2 spectra without authentic standards.

name: swath-dia-chromatogram-correlation-deconvolution
description: Use when processing SWATH/DIA tandem MS data where MS2 fragments must be reassigned to their precursor ions before compound annotation, e.g. pooled-QC DIA spectra in untargeted metabolomics.

name: swath-dia-ms2-deconvolution
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS files contain DIA/SWATH MS2 scans (typically acquired on pooled-QC samples) and feature-level compound annotation requires associating fragment ions to precursor MS1 features before searching MS2 reference spectra.

name: swath-dia-spectra-deconvolution
description: Use when input is centroid-mode SWATH-DIA mzML data (variable-size windows with m/z neighbor overlap) and pseudo-MS2 spectra must be reconstructed by relinking MS1 features to their true fragment ions.

name: swath-msms-spectrum-quality-evaluation
description: Use when a multisample DIA-MS/SWATH dataset (e.g. SCIEX WIFF negative lipidomics files) has been deconvoluted and per-feature MS/MS spectrum quality must be scored, or when deciding whether correlation-based deconvolution (CorrDec) improves on MS2Dec.

name: swgdrug-seized-drug-spectra-handling
description: Use when EI mass spectra peak lists (m/z, intensity) from the SWGDRUG library or real seized-drug specimens need to be converted into DeepEI-predicted 0/1 structural fingerprints as input to the PS2MS integrated similarity ranking.

name: swisslipids-database-parsing
description: Use when a lipidomics tool's structural similarity or double bond position comparison must be validated against curated reference lipid structure databases rather than against measured data.

name: symbolic-profile-extraction
description: Use when raw ICP-MS ionome measurements (e.g. yeast knockout or HeLa ion concentrations in ppm) must be cleaned and encoded as line-level z-score and symbolic profiles before clustering, network analysis or enrichment steps.

name: symmetric-distance-metric-implementation
description: Use when quantifying the global similarity/distance between two sets of tandem mass spectra (e.g., MGF files from LC-MS/MS runs) with compareMS2 2.0, or when a fully symmetric spectral-distance metric is needed for clustering, phylogenetics, or QC.

name: synonym-duplicate-detection-curation
description: Use when merging metabolite datasets by InChIKey and some entries share the same molecular skeleton but carry conflicting synonyms or duplicate IDs (HMDB, KEGG, ChEBI, CAS, Bin ID, PubChem CID), requiring reconciliation before pathway analysis.

name: synonym-matching-vocabulary-mapping
description: Use when a metabolomics sample-metadata matrix contains freetext field values (inconsistent synonyms, typographical errors) that must be replaced with fixed-vocabulary terms to make datasets interoperable and FAIR.

name: synonym-resolution-against-catalogue-of-life
description: Use when a natural products or metabolomics database stores organism information as heterogeneous free text that must be converted into accepted scientific names with a complete, resolvable lineage for taxonomic scoring.

name: synthetic-benchmark-precision-recall-evaluation
description: Use when validating a peak-list alignment algorithm where the true row-to-feature correspondence across samples can be constructed, and precision/recall of aligned rows must be quantified on synthetic data plus real reference alignments.

name: synthetic-chromatogram-generation
description: Use when validating or benchmarking LC/MS EIC or peak quality metrics (e.g., MCQ index, zigzag index, sharpness, SNR, TPASR) and you need reproducible synthetic chromatograms with known profile types as test fixtures.

name: synthetic-clustered-data-simulation
description: Use when evaluating or validating an integrative clustering method (e.g. KLIC, COCA, kernel k-means) on simulated datasets where the true labels and per-dataset noise levels are known and kernel-weight allocation must be checked.

name: synthetic-complexity-scoring-functional-group-filtering
description: Use when enumerating molecular derivatives from a core scaffold and you must decide which functional groups (from a library, e.g. 204 groups or 30 UNODC groups) are synthetically plausible at each recursion depth.

name: synthetic-data-benchmark-visualization
description: Use when labeled synthetic data with signal/noise peak classes (e.g. createSynthetics output from Zenodo record 5036526) must be compared to a baseline filter such as an intensity (SNR) threshold, and ROC curves are the required evidence per intensity panel.

name: synthetic-drift-simulation-with-known-ground-truth
description: Use when a normalization method (rGAM, tGAM, rLOESS, QC-RLSC) must be benchmarked against a known reference drift, e.g. verifying recovery of simulated drift or testing QCcheck refit behavior on unrepresentative QCs.

name: synthetic-fluorescence-image-simulation
description: Use when validating or stress-testing a colocalization coefficient or thresholding algorithm, and you need simulated red/green images with known colocalized fractions to compare computed coefficients against ground truth.

name: synthetic-gaussian-signal-generation
description: Use when validating mzapy.peaks peak finders against signals of known composition: generate summed-Gaussian 1D signals with recorded ground-truth parameters to quantify detection and parameter-recovery error.

name: synthetic-ground-truth-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when quantifying true-positive peak-detection accuracy of an LC-MS feature-detection tool against a synthetic mzML benchmark with known inserted single and co-eluting (double) peaks, e.g. for benchmarking against MZmine3, xcms, or MS-DIAL.

name: synthetic-lc-ms-data-simulation
description: Use when you need a ground-truth-labeled LC-MS metabolite dataset to quantify precision/recall of a feature-detection algorithm under varied detector noise, mass error (10 or 40 ppm), or distorted elution profiles.

name: synthetic-lethal-interaction-enrichment
description: Use when you have per-metabolite feature-importance rankings from trained random-forest models (e.g. Metab8D top-20 features) and want to test whether top predictors are enriched for curated SynLethDB synthetic-lethal pairs versus a random-feature null.

name: synthetic-lipidomics-dataset-construction
description: Use when a benchmark or test needs lipid identifier pairs at known annotation levels to verify cross-dataset equalization/matching logic, and ground-truth mappings must be constructed rather than harvested from real datasets.

name: synthetic-mass-spectrometry-data-generation
description: Use when you need labeled synthetic mass spectrometry peak data with known signal/noise ground truth (e.g., to compute ROC curves for a classification method) because real peak-level annotations are unavailable.

name: synthetic-metabolomic-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing alignment algorithms on peak lists where no experimental ground truth exists, by creating synthetic replicates with random non-linear RT deviation so true peak correspondences are known a priori.

name: synthetic-metabolomics-data-augmentation
description: Use when labeled pathway data is too sparse to train a pathway-prediction model like NetAurHPD, and a subset of known chemical reactions (e.g., TomatoCyc directional pathways) is available to imitate metabolic activity.

name: synthetic-metabolomics-fixture-generation
description: Use when a downstream analysis module (e.g. OGDA aggregation of Welch t-tests and fold-changes) needs a self-contained, deterministic test input replicating the structure of BinBase GC/MS metabolome data — compound × sample intensity matrices paired with biological metadata triads.

name: synthetic-mzml-ground-truth-scoring
description: Use when comparing peak-detection accuracy of LC-MS data-processing tools on synthetic mzML data where the true feature list is known, e.g. ranking MassCube, MS-DIAL, MZmine3, and xcms by TP/FP/missed-feature counts.

name: synthetic-nmr-spectrum-generation
description: Use when no public annotated NMR spectra database exists and labeled training spectra are needed for deep-learning-based metabolite identification/quantification in 1H plasma NMR.

name: synthetic-nmr-spectrum-simulation
description: Use when you must validate that an NMR fitting implementation reproduces documented lineshape equations — e.g. testing MultiNMRFit's mixed Gaussian-Lorentzian singlet, doublet, triplet, doublet-of-doublets, or quadruplet models against ground truth.

name: synthetic-noise-spike-in-validation
description: Use when benchmarking a spectral denoising or noise-removal method and you need a quantitative recovery metric from spectra with known ground truth (clean reference plus controlled spiked noise).

name: synthetic-omics-count-matrix-generation
description: Use when benchmarking the computational cost of correlation-based network construction across R packages (e.g. MetaNet vs WGCNA or NetCoMi) and reproducible, identical synthetic count-matrix inputs are needed.

name: synthetic-omics-table-generation
description: Use when benchmarking MetaNet (or a comparable correlation-network tool) across a range of feature counts and you need controlled synthetic count tables spanning below and above the 1,000-feature threshold rather than real data.

name: synthetic-pathway-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking pathway-ranking methods (ORA, mPLAGE/PLAGE, GSEA) for robustness to missing or spurious compound annotations, e.g. simulating degraded peak-annotation completeness before trusting method rankings on real metabolomics peak data.

name: synthetic-qc-drift-correction
description: Use when raw LC/MS mzML data lacks standardized experimental QC samples (common for public metabolomics datasets) yet feature intensities must be corrected for batch, run-order, and intensity drift before statistical analysis or pre-training a model like the VAE.

name: synthetic-rank-data-simulation
description: Use when you need to benchmark or validate a MaRR-type reproducibility estimator against a ground-truth simulation, e.g., before applying it to MS-Metabolomics replicate data.

name: synthetic-spatial-omics-data-simulation
description: Use when you need to assess whether an integration model's time and memory consumption scale linearly with spot count, by fitting it to simulated joint ST-SM AnnData inputs of controlled size.

name: synthetic-spectra-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when validating a peak-fitting implementation on spectra where true signal parameters are known, or when deciding whether to fit whole multiplets as single signal models versus independent peaks.

name: synthetic-spectral-parameter-recovery
description: Use when you need to validate a spectral fitting workflow on data with known ground truth — e.g. synthetic 1D 1H NMR spectra with overlapping multiplets at low SNR — to quantify accuracy and precision of recovered parameters.

name: synthetic-spectrum-dataset-partitioning
description: Use when preparing large synthetic EI-MS corpora (multiple spectrum generators over the same compounds) for model pretraining or held-out evaluation and compound-level leakage between generators must be controlled.

name: synthetic-spectrum-pair-generation
description: Use when implementing or verifying a modified-spectrum scoring function (e.g. the ANN-SoLo shifted dot product) and you need ground-truth pairs with known modification-induced peak shifts to test recovery and ranking behavior.

name: synthetic-three-replicate-data-simulation
description: Use when validating a k>2 replicate extension of MaRR: you need controlled synthetic rank lists (pi1, r0 grid, n≈10,000) to check empirical mFDR against nominal alpha and unbiased pi1 estimation.

name: system-suitability-qc-evaluation
description: Use when raw Waters RAW/mzML injections of a system suitability solution (SSS) and pooled QC samples are available before running an untargeted LC–MS metabolomics batch, and you must decide whether the analytical platform is adequately conditioned and stable before acquiring study samples.

name: system-suitability-testing-evaluation
description: Use when a UHPLC-HRMS (or similar) sequence needs pre-acquisition performance checks — e.g. six deuterated acylcarnitine SST standards in mzML format — to verify retention times, EICs, and MS/MS product ions before committing to full data collection.

name: systematic-error-subtraction-normalization
description: Use when large-scale untargeted GC-MS metabolomics batches (thousands of study samples plus pooled QC runs, e.g. an xlsx feature table with batch/sampleType/time metadata) show injection-order drift that neither internal standards nor sum-based normalization can remove.

name: t-sne-node-selection-overlay-rendering
description: Use when exploring LC–MS/MS spectra in a .mgf-based ms2deepscore t-SNE embedding and you need to see the local connectivity (adjacent nodes and edge weights) around one feature of interest before widening the neighborhood.

name: t-test-differential-metabolite-detection
description: Use when two-group metabolomics intensity data (e.g. case vs control, imputed or complete) must be reduced to a significant-metabolite list, and that list's stability across imputation methods must be quantified via MLCI.

name: t-test-multiple-group-comparison
description: Use when comparing metabolite abundance between pre-defined sample groups (e.g. tumor subtypes like MYC-high vs AKT1-high prostate cancer) in a MultiAssayExperiment and you need per-metabolite p-values, adjusted p-values and difference of means.

name: t-test-pvalue-correlation-analysis
description: Use when comparing imputation methods on MNAR-degraded targeted metabolomics data (FFA/BA matrices) where the criterion is preservation of two-group statistical sensitivity, not raw imputation accuracy.

name: tab-delimited-data-import
description: Use when starting a margheRita workflow from MS-Dial-exported feature tables: the inputs are tab-delimited feature data (m/z, retention times, MS/MS spectra, abundances) plus a sample annotation file, and the analysis needs the mRList object.

name: tab-separated-manifest-formatting
description: Use when filtering the ReDU sample-information table (gnps_metadata.tsv schema) by controlled-vocabulary attributes and grouping the selected MassIVE filenames into cohorts for GNPS library search or molecular networking.

name: table-driven-parser-validation
description: Use when a lipidomics dataset built from mass-spectrometric experiments uses vendor shorthand lipid names (headgroup plus acyl/alkyl/alkenyl chain tokens, sphingoid bases, placeholders like 0:0) that must be converted before upload into LipidOne 2.0.

name: table-row-subsetting
description: Use when a table carries per-row categorical annotation terms (e.g. cellular localization, signaling pathway) and the goal is to retain only rows matching a searched category, then attach the annotation label to the subset.

name: tabular-aggregation-and-export
description: Use when reproducing or auditing the chemical composition of a large molecular dataset (e.g. METLIN SMRT) from SDF molfiles plus taxonomy labels, and a per-category percentage table is the required output.

name: tabular-data-format-conversion
description: Use when a calculated MetaMapR network (edge list with source, target, edge-type columns plus a node attribute table) must be handed off to downstream tools like Cytoscape or archived as numerical tables and high-quality graphics.

name: tabular-data-preprocessing-for-classification
description: Use when a labeled tabular table (CSV/Excel/txt) with missing values must be turned into a class-prediction pipeline whose pre-processing, feature selection and estimator parameters are optimized by exhaustive grid search.

name: tabular-data-structuring
description: Use when a C. elegans meiosis paper reports foci-per-nucleus counts for specific genotypes and meiotic zones (e.g. GFP::RMH-1 or GFP::MSH-5 in top-3-ZnF or rmh-2 backgrounds) and these must be tabulated for statistical comparison or reproducibility checks.

name: tabular-data-structuring
description: Use when you need to turn a collection of compound records returned by PeakForest REST endpoints into a structured tabular file, and to verify its completeness against a known collection size (e.g. the 96-compound demonstrator).

name: tabular-data-summarization
description: Use when a spreadsheet or table of entities (e.g. peptide hormone entries with family annotations) must be summarized into a frequency table per category, sorted, validated against reported counts, and plotted.

name: tabular-feature-intensity-export
description: Use when a completed OpenMS feature-linking step (FeatureLinkerUnlabeledQT) has produced aligned feature maps across replicate LC-MS runs and the intensities must be exported to a tabular text file for statistical analysis.

name: tabular-gene-matrix-input-preparation
description: Use when input is a gene-level result table (e.g. differential-expression results with geneID, log2 fold change, and p/padj columns) that must be reshaped to match GraphBio's reference example files before loading into a module.

name: tabular-genomic-output-formatting
description: Use when writing or validating the tab-delimited output of a gene/operon prediction step (e.g. MetaRon's Operon_File.tab) so records conform to the scaftig and gene prediction file format required by the 'op' process.

name: tabular-lipidomics-data-validation
description: Use when a processed lipidomics table carries lipid identifiers such as 'PG 18:1/20:1' or 'FA(18:3)' and you must verify that liputils' Lipid parser extracts the expected fatty acid residues and ambiguity counts before downstream residue analysis.

name: tabular-metabolomics-data-processing
description: Use when a metabolomics or lipidomics feature intensity table (with sample-to-study-group metadata) contains missing values and variables must be separated into truly absent features vs. missing data before imputation and downstream QC.

name: tabular-metadata-standardization
description: Reference for converting a curated software/tool listing (with per-tool name, category, instrument data type, software type, reference) into one consistently-headered CSV governed by a fixed controlled vocabulary.

name: tabular-qc-metric-export
description: Use when Thermo RAW-file acquisition performance must be assessed without database searching — e.g. diagnosing peptide-identification loss in HeLa Pierce digest QC runs by comparing MS1/MS2 TIC medians between underperforming and reference runs.

name: tabular-ranking-and-sorting
description: Use when a feature/compound table with multi-tool annotations (GNPS, Sirius 6, ISDB-LOTUS) must be scored with the decision-theory k function and sorted by increasing k to rank natural products for novelty prioritization.

name: tabular-result-assembly
description: Use when a BinDiscover OGDA query yields a list of significant metabolites (e.g. 15 hits from a human-digestive-tract-vs-bacteria comparison) that must be exported with per-compound annotation columns for downstream enrichment.

name: tabular-result-reproduction
description: Use when a research question asks to reproduce specific reported counts from an article — e.g. how many metabolites from each MS1-only database (KEGG, KNApSAcK, PlantCyc) were retained in the PM database after plant-specific filtering — into a small verified table.

name: tabular-result-table-construction
description: Use when a weighted meta-analysis (e.g. amanida's Fisher-method P-value combination) has produced per-compound statistics held in an S4 result object and they must be exported as a structured table such as sample_combined_pvalues.csv.

name: tabular-result-verification
description: Decision support for validating parameter-tuning tables when a grid search over assignment radii and detection thresholds has produced F1 scores per MCF setup and reported optima must be cross-checked.

name: tabular-results-export
description: Use when an Inventa prioritization run has finished computing the four rank components and the combined score needs to be persisted as a flat TSV in the results folder for downstream review or reporting.

name: tabular-statistical-results-assembly
description: Use when you have a preprocessed metabolomics concentration table (CSV with samples as rows, metabolite concentration columns, a group/factor column) with two or more sample groups and you need per-metabolite ANOVA and pairwise Tukey p-values assembled into one results table.

name: tabular-statistical-results-export
description: Use when a tabular dataset (e.g. Excel/csv with a numerical measurement column and a categorical Condition column) needs two-group or multi-group parametric/non-parametric comparisons, and the named test, statistic and p-value per column must be collected into one machine-readable CSV.

name: tabular-summary-statistics-aggregation
description: Use when a benchmark/runtimes table must be reduced to per-tool summary statistics (means, speedup fold-change) and cross-checked against values reported in a publication's figure or abstract.

name: tabular-time-series-data-manipulation
description: Use when the input is a table with a time axis and per-trace signal columns (e.g. intensities from optical recordings like the bundled Example Data 03), and you need to baseline-correct, transform, smooth or quantify traces before plotting or export.

name: tabular-to-json-record-extraction
description: Use when messy tabular spreadsheet data (Excel or CSV) must be turned into key-based JSON records for a relational database or Metabolomics Workbench deposition, and a tag layer can be inserted into the sheet.

name: tagged-protein-strain-annotation
description: Use when reviewing or reproducing protein–protein interaction evidence from a paper that relies on endogenously tagged worm strains, and you need a structured table linking construct pairs (tag type and fusion position) to the assay outcomes and their figure locations.

name: tailoring-reaction-library-enumeration
description: Use when you must quantify RAIChU's built-in biosynthetic reaction coverage — tailoring reactions, RiPP PTM families, NRPS A-domain substrates/starter units, and PKS KS subtypes/extender units — before relying on it to visualise fully maturated pathways.

name: tampa-contrast-mode-configuration
description: Use when you have a taxonomic profiler output and a ground-truth profile for the same sample (e.g., CAMI2 marine marmgCAMI2_short_read_sample_0) and need to find which specific clades a high-scoring profiler misses.

name: tandem-mass-spectra-annotation
description: Use when you have HCD or CID tandem mass spectra of NRP/PK compounds and need dereplication or de novo annotation against custom building-block sequence databases rather than generic spectral libraries.

name: tandem-mass-spectra-candidate-ranking
description: Use when you have tandem mass spectra and database-retrieved candidate structures and need a fragmentation-only candidate ranking baseline, e.g. to benchmark in silico fragmenters before adding reference, retention-time, or user-defined scores.

name: tandem-mass-spectra-database-search
description: Use when you have experimental high-resolution tandem MS/MS spectra of putative NRP/PK natural products and a curated sequence database (e.g., 146 NRP/siderophore sequences, 85 building blocks) and need ranked compound identifications or dereplication accuracy metrics.

name: tandem-mass-spectra-distortion-simulation
description: Use when evaluating a structure-annotation confidence score (e.g. COSMIC) on reference MS/MS spectra and you need to emulate the lower quality of biological-sample spectra at controlled distortion levels.

name: tandem-mass-spectra-dot-product-computation
description: Use when pairwise distances between proteomics samples must be quantified directly from peak-listed tandem mass spectra (MGF) without peptide identification or spectral libraries, e.g. to build a distance matrix for molecular phylogenetics or data quality control.

name: tandem-mass-spectra-embedding-evaluation
description: Use when you have embedded a set of tandem mass spectra (e.g. NIST20, MoNA) into a vector space and need to quantify whether that space reflects molecular structural similarity or supports analog retrieval.

name: tandem-mass-spectra-library-preparation
description: Use when raw GNPS/MassIVE .mzML experiments must be converted into deduplicated, quality-filtered, paired or unpaired MS/MS spectral libraries (e.g. GeMS, MoNA, NIST20) for self-supervised pre-training or supervised fine-tuning of spectrum annotation models.

name: tandem-mass-spectra-prediction
description: Use when you have a molecular structure dataset (e.g., NIST20 labels.tsv + mgf_files + spec_files.hdf5) and need to predict MS/MS spectra or compare spectrum simulators under matched covariates and hyperparameter sweeps.

name: tandem-mass-spectra-preprocessing
description: Use when raw MS/MS spectra in MGF format must be converted to h5py and normalized/denoised before spectral similarity computation, spectral library search, or training/testing TransExION on GNPS/GNPS_MassBank/mergedGNPS data.

name: tandem-mass-spectra-set-overlap-analysis
description: Use when two or more LC-MS/MS datasets exported as MGF tandem mass spectra need a set-level similarity and distance (not peptide identification) — e.g. species identification, mixture characterization, phylogenetics, or batch-effect QC on spectral content.

name: tandem-mass-spectra-similarity-scoring
description: Use when you have positive and/or negative ionization mode MS/MS peak spectra (mgf, msp, mzML, mzXML, json, usi) and need predicted chemical similarity scores, e.g., to build a unified cross-mode molecular network.

name: tandem-mass-spectral-dereplication
description: Use when experimental tandem mass spectra of natural products (e.g. NRPs/PK siderophores like desferrioxamine B) must be matched against a custom in-silico fragment database to identify the compound producing each spectrum.

name: tandem-mass-spectrometry-data-processing
description: Use when multiple ESI-MS2 records of a single compound exist at different collision-induced dissociation energies and you must merge them into one reference spectrum or score searches with a weighted cosine correlation optimized for ESI-MS2 data.

name: tandem-mass-spectrometry-fragment-matching
description: Use when pairwise alignment of tandem MS/MS fragmentation spectra (m/z arrays with precursor m/z) must be scored with statistical significance (z-test p-values) for structurally related metabolites, e.g. in molecular networking.

name: tandem-mass-spectrometry-spectrum-processing
description: Use when raw tandem MS (MS2/MSn) spectra—especially low-resolution spectra from a miniaturized mass spectrometer—must be converted into candidate molecular structures and scored by fingerprint Tanimoto similarity against known SMILES.

name: tandem-mass-spectrum-clustering
description: Use when raw shotgun proteomics MS/MS data (e.g. PRIDE PXD000561-style datasets with millions of spectra in mzML, mzXML, or MGF files) must be reduced to cluster representatives for more efficient downstream identification.

name: tandem-mass-spectrum-counting
description: Use when you need to describe the size of a set of LC-MS/MS acquisitions, e.g. reporting the default compareMS2 QC metric or validating that downloaded ProteomeXchange files are complete.

name: tandem-mass-spectrum-database-search
description: Use when LC-MS/MS spectra (MGF, mzXML, mzML, or mzData) need to be identified against a database of known natural product structures, especially when exact-formula dereplication by precursor mass alone is ambiguous.

name: tandem-ms-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing MS/MS formula-prediction methods on a labeled test set (e.g. NPLIB1, CASMI2022) and need rigorous metrics such as top-1 accuracy, joint formula+adduct accuracy, and per-spectrum concordance.

name: tandem-ms-annotation-score-extraction
description: Use when a feature-level annotation table contains top candidate structures and scores from multiple MS/MS annotation tools (GNPS FBMN, Sirius 6, ISDB-LOTUS) and per-ion agreement/match indicators are needed for prioritization.

name: tandem-ms-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when a trained formula-identification model must be evaluated on held-out MS/MS spectra to quantify top-5 accuracy, compare against SIRIUS/BUDDY baselines, or reveal performance stratification across molecular properties.

name: tandem-ms-candidate-ranking
description: Use when assigning ranks to candidate structures for an HR-MS/MS peak with no spectral-library match, especially when candidate lists come from PubChem/ChemSpider and reference or retention-time information is available.

name: tandem-ms-confidence-score-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking a tandem-MS structure-annotation confidence score against known ground truth — reference spectra at 10/20/40 eV, merged spectra, and no/medium/high noise — to quantify correct hits versus annotation rate (hop plots) and FDR at a score threshold.

name: tandem-ms-data-preprocessing
description: Use when starting from raw untargeted LC-MS2 .mzML files (e.g. the bryophytes MTBLS709 dataset) that must be preprocessed and dereplicated against spectral databases before SIRIUS/MAW-Py annotation.

name: tandem-ms-database-searching
description: Use when you have centroided tandem MS/MS spectra in an open format (e.g. after OpenMS file conversion and centroiding) and need peptide/protein identifications via database searching before feature detection, retention-time alignment, protein inference, and FDR control.

name: tandem-ms-dataset-acquisition-from-massive
description: Use when a downstream annotation/prioritization task needs the P. mutica MIA alkaloid extract MS/MS data referenced by MassIVE accession MSV95596, or when reproducing the article's 754-feature k-ranking.

name: tandem-ms-dataset-pairwise-comparison
description: Use when you have raw LC-MS/MS dataset files (e.g. MGF with tens of thousands of tandem spectra) and need dataset-level similarity, species-level phylogenetic reconstruction, or QC/batch-effect detection before any database search.

name: tandem-ms-evaluation-set-bookkeeping
description: Use when reproducing or extending benchmark comparisons of tandem MS annotation tools (CycloBranch, NRPro, Dereplicator, Dereplicator+) on matched CID/HCD spectrum sets, where per-condition accuracy deltas and exact recomputation checks are needed.

name: tandem-ms-formula-identification
description: Use when you have unfiltered high-resolution MS/MS spectra (plus MS1 isotope pattern) of a small molecule and need its molecular formula and candidate structure without a reference mass spectral database.

name: tandem-ms-fragment-ion-matching
description: Use when per-sample MGF MS2 spectra have been clustered and cleaned into consensus spectra and structural annotations must be assigned by spectral-library matching, ranked by MQscore and m/z error.

name: tandem-ms-fragment-longitudinal-profiling
description: Use when identifying isomeric metabolites in untargeted LC-MS/MS data acquired at multiple distinct collision energies (NCE 1–100% or stepped 20/40/60%), where single-CE cross-sectional spectral similarity misranks isomers with similar predominant fragments.

name: tandem-ms-metabolite-annotation
description: Use when you have consensus MS/MS spectra (e.g. from MZmine3 feature extraction) with a precursor mass and need to rank molecular candidates retrieved from FoodDB, HMDB, MassSpecGym, NIST23, or GNPS libraries to annotate metabolites.

name: tandem-ms-metadata-feature-engineering
description: Decision support for adding spectral metadata as model input in MS2DeepScore 2.0 training: build CategoricalToBinary/StandardScaler features from precursor m/z, ionmode, adduct, or instrument type and test whether each improves RMSE.

name: tandem-ms-model-inference
description: Use when labeled MS2 spectra (e.g., HDF5 2xN m/z/intensity arrays with lipid_species/adduct/precursor metadata) must be passed through a trained deep learning model to generate lipid species predictions and per-spectrum accuracy metrics.

name: tandem-ms-pairwise-distance-computation
description: Use when you need pairwise distances between multiple LC-MS/MS tandem mass spectra datasets without prior peptide identification, e.g. for phylogenetic trees, batch-effect/outlier QC, or species identification.

name: tandem-ms-pairwise-similarity-computation
description: Use when you hold a cleaned set of annotated tandem MS spectra (e.g. MGF from GNPS) and need an all-pairs spectral similarity or score matrix to retrieve chemically related compound pairs or cluster spectra.

name: tandem-ms-peak-alignment
description: Use when a molecular-networking component (e.g. from a GNPS2 FBMN task) contains multiple related tandem mass spectra and you need to visualize which consensus fragments drive the family's alignment or pinpoint where a modification sits.

name: tandem-ms-peak-filtering-and-intensity-normalization
description: Use when preparing tandem mass spectra (e.g., from a GNPS2 molecular networking task or MGF cluster files) for spectral alignment or consensus peak identification, and noisy or near-precursor peaks would distort alignment.

name: tandem-ms-peak-matching
description: Use when feature-level MS/MS spectra (e.g. an MGF from MZmine FBMN export) fail to yield GNPS library annotations under strict parameters, and you need per-feature GNPS scores (c_g, t_g,i, t_g,s) for downstream aggregation as in MS2DECIDE.

name: tandem-ms-retrieval-metric-computation
description: Reference for evaluating a de novo structure generator on MS2 spectra: you need the retrieval rate and top-1 rate against a holdout set, plus the known ablation numbers (31%/17% naive vs. 45%/25% fingerprint-guided on GNPS) as a baseline to beat.

name: tandem-ms-scan-association
description: Use when you have an xcms-derived feature table (csv with 'mz' and 'rt' columns) plus centroided LC/MS raw data (.mzML) and need to link MS2 spectra to features before MS/MS-based annotation such as Find Patterns or spectral similarity searches.

name: tandem-ms-spectra-clustering
description: Use when a metabolomics or proteomics data-dependent acquisition dataset (vendor raw or mzML/MGF) contains repeated MS/MS spectra of the same molecule and redundancy reduction via clustering into consensus clusters is needed.

name: tandem-ms-spectra-embedding-consumption
description: Use when you have the four input spectra CSV files ([M+H]+ and [M-H]- at 35% and 130% NCE) and need to translate the encoder-generated spectra embeddings into de-novo SMILES structures.

name: tandem-ms-spectral-cosine-similarity-scoring
description: Use when LC–MS/MS untargeted metabolomics features already have isotope-pattern-mapped adducts and fragmentation data (MS2 spectra) are available, so candidate compounds can be scored against their stored reference spectra.

name: tandem-ms-spectral-database-search
description: Use when unannotated tandem MS spectra (e.g. from GNPS datasets) must be assigned to known small molecules in a large structure database, and in silico library coverage is insufficient.

name: tandem-ms-spectral-library-annotation
description: Use when tandem MS spectra must be annotated against a small or tens-of-millions-compound reference database, and candidates must be ranked and scored with fingerprint and fragprint evidence, optionally with isotope/formula filters.

name: tandem-ms-spectral-library-curation
description: Use when building a training or benchmark set for spectral similarity prediction from public MS/MS libraries, especially when spectra from both positive and negative ionization modes must be harmonized for cross-mode model training.

name: tandem-ms-spectral-library-search
description: Use when annotating LC–MS/MS query spectra by direct matching to reference spectra (e.g., MassBank/GNPS/NIST 2017 or CSI:FingerID training structures), or when constructing the spectral library search baseline for benchmarking in silico annotation tools at controlled FDR.

name: tandem-ms-spectral-matching
description: Use when newly acquired tandem MS/MS spectra (e.g. from synthesized compounds) must be searched repository-wide against public metabolomics data to find which public datasets contain the compounds.

name: tandem-ms-spectral-prediction
description: Use when experimental MS/MS spectra of unknown metabolites (e.g., recurrent unidentified spectra like ARUS) need in silico annotation by comparing predicted spectra of candidate SMILES against the experimental spectrum at 2-decimal m/z resolution.

name: tandem-ms-spectral-similarity-scoring
description: Use when you have preprocessed MS/MS peak lists (m/z + intensity) and need a pairwise similarity matrix (e.g. cosine scores for MST edges in MMSA, or GNPS networking edges between spectra in a molecular family).

name: tandem-ms-spectrum-annotation
description: Use when you need to assign metabolite identities to unknown tandem MS spectra by searching a compiled compound database (tens of millions of structures with pre-calculated fingerprints and fragmentation patterns), especially when throughput and scalability matter.

name: tandem-ms-spectrum-formula-scoring
description: Use when you have an MS1 precursor mass and an MS/MS spectrum (MGF) and need a de novo chemical formula assignment without spectrum databases or fragmentation trees.

name: tandem-ms-spectrum-inference
description: Use when you have a molecular structure (e.g., a candidate from NIST20 or PubChem) and need its predicted MS/MS spectrum for C2MS prediction or to augment library-based MS2C retrieval for compounds missing from spectral libraries.

name: tandem-ms-spectrum-prediction
description: Use when reference MS/MS spectra are unavailable for candidate compounds in non-targeted metabolomics, or when validating putative compound annotations by comparing predicted vs. measured spectra for [M+H]+ / [M-H]- precursors.

name: tandem-ms-spectrum-processing
description: Use when starting from raw MS2 spectra (MGF or SIRIUS .ms format) that need molecular formula assignment, fingerprint prediction, and de novo candidate structure generation and ranking before annotation.

name: tandem-ms-spectrum-retrieval
description: Use when you need to pull a specific MS/MS spectrum out of a public resource (GNPS, MassBank, MassIVE, MetaboLights, Metabolomics Workbench, MS2LDA) without downloading the repository itself, and you know its source, accession, or scan number.

name: tandem-ms-spectrum-searching
description: Use when a list of unknown metabolites with MS/MS spectra exists (e.g., KGMN annotations of NIST urine positives) and the goal is to test whether those unknowns recur across public metabolomics repositories.

name: tandem-ms-spectrum-transformer-encoding
description: Use when building contrastive spectrum-to-molecule encoders for MS/MS retrieval: spectra are peak lists with subformula labels (formSpec) or binned spectra (binnedSpec), and candidates must be ranked in a shared embedding space.

name: tandem-ms2-structure-prediction
description: Use when generating or ranking de novo molecular structures from positive-mode, low-resolution MS2/MSn spectra (e.g. from a miniaturized linear ion trap mass spectrometer), especially for unknown compounds not covered by spectral library search.

name: tandem-spectral-similarity-scoring
description: Use when you have MGF peak lists from LC-MS/MS runs and need to compare datasets pairwise by shared/similar tandem mass spectra, estimate mass accuracy, charge states, isotope errors, or set m/z and similarity thresholds before any database search.

name: tanimoto-bin-stratified-sampling
description: Use when preparing training pairs for MS2DeepScore 2.0 — before fitting the Siamese network, to prevent over-sampling of common molecules or easy Tanimoto ranges and enforce equal pair counts per Tanimoto bin.

name: tanimoto-chemical-similarity-scoring
description: Use when re-ranking MS2Query candidate library matches and you need a chemical-structure-based similarity feature alongside spectral scores (Spec2Vec, MS2Deepscore) and precursor m/z features; requires structural annotations (InChIKeys) for query and library candidates.

name: tanimoto-decoy-candidate-selection
description: Use when benchmarking spectrum-prediction models on identification-by-retrieval: you need isomer-decoy candidate sets (true structure + Tanimoto-ranked same-formula decoys) against which to rank candidates by spectral similarity.

name: tanimoto-fingerprint-correlation-analysis
description: Use when comparing spectral similarity measures (e.g., DreaMS embedding cosine, MS2DeepScore, spectral entropy) against molecular structural similarity on tandem MS/MS spectra, or when building a library-retrieval benchmark with precursor m/z constraints.

name: tanimoto-fingerprint-similarity-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating de novo or database-search structure predictions by structural similarity — e.g., computing Tanimoto similarity of top incorrect candidates to the true structure in MS2-based structure elucidation benchmarks.

name: tanimoto-mces-metric-computation
description: Use when you have ranked candidate molecular structures sampled per spectrum (e.g., 100 DiffMS diffusion samples with invalid/disconnected molecules removed) and need to score them against ground-truth molecules for benchmark reproduction.

name: tanimoto-molecular-similarity-computation
description: Use when a task requires quantifying structural relatedness between small molecules (e.g., ECFP fingerprint pairs) to group validation-set molecules by whether they have a training-set counterpart above a Tanimoto threshold such as 90% or 95%.

name: tanimoto-nearest-neighbor-similarity-vs-pubchem-controls
description: Decision support for evaluating whether generated SMILES resemble known metabolites: use when a generative chemical model's samples must be judged for metabolite-likeness against matched PubChem controls.

name: tanimoto-score-prediction-rmse-evaluation
description: Use when a trained MS2DeepScore (or similar Siamese spectral similarity) model must be validated for Tanimoto prediction accuracy on held-out spectra from compounds absent from training, and you need an RMSE plus per-similarity-bin error profile.

name: tanimoto-similarity-bin-comparison
description: Use when comparing prediction accuracy of similarity models across Tanimoto bins — e.g. checking whether a dual-ionization-mode model matches single-mode baselines within each mode, or locating which Tanimoto bin (low vs 0.9–1.0) drives performance differences.

name: tanimoto-similarity-calculation
description: Use when the same MS/MS feature has structural annotations from multiple tools (GNPS, Sirius, ISDB-LOTUS) and you need pairwise chemical-similarity concordance indicators to feed MS2DECIDE aggregation.

name: tanimoto-similarity-candidate-screening
description: Use when evaluating retrieval-based MS2C compound identification: you have a real MS/MS spectrum Y_i for a molecule X_i, C2MS models to score, and need a controlled candidate pool (e.g. 50 compounds including X_i plus PubChem neighbours) to compute Top-1/3/5 accuracy.

name: tanimoto-similarity-computation
description: Use when comparing de novo EI-MS spectral translation outputs against database-search candidates on the same test spectra, using Morgan-fingerprint Tanimoto similarity as the ranking criterion.

name: tanimoto-similarity-computation
description: Decision support for ranking or validating derivative candidates by structural similarity, e.g. testing whether BAM-generated derivatives from anchor-suspect pairs resemble the suspect more than the anchor.

name: tanimoto-similarity-computation
description: Use when you have predicted molecule structures (SMILES) from de novo MS2 spectra interpretation and need to score them against ground-truth structures, rank candidates, or produce statistically tested benchmark metrics.

name: tanimoto-similarity-computation-from-morgan-fingerprints
description: Use when evaluating de novo molecular structure predictions from mass spectra (e.g., SELFIES outputs from MS-Bart) and you need a graded structural-similarity metric alongside exact-match accuracy and MCES distance.

name: tanimoto-similarity-computation-of-incorrect-smiles-predictions
description: Use when evaluating a SMILES-generating model (e.g., substructure-to-structure transformer) on a test set where exact-match accuracy was computed, and you need to characterize near-miss predictions structurally via Tanimoto similarity.

name: tanimoto-similarity-computation-of-molecular-structures
description: Use when comparing a generated or predicted SMILES structure against a reference (or another candidate set) to quantify structural agreement on a 0–1 scale, e.g. evaluating incorrect candidates or dereplication.

name: tanimoto-similarity-deduplication-across-benchmarks
description: Use when assembling a large pretraining corpus of fingerprint–molecule or spectrum–molecule pairs where unlabeled sources (e.g. PubChem) could structurally overlap held-out test molecules of MassSpecGym or NPLIB1, inflating benchmark scores via memorization.

name: tanimoto-similarity-evaluation
description: Use when spectral matches must be judged by molecular structure — e.g. benchmarking Spec2Vec vs cosine scores, or checking whether top-N library hits for unknown queries are true structural analogues (Tanimoto > 0.6).

name: tanimoto-similarity-fingerprint-search
description: Use when MS/MS spectra remain unannotated after library search (e.g. IDSL.CSA against NIST 20/LipidBlast) and you need candidate structures by matching IDSL_MINT-predicted fingerprints against LipidMaps with Tanimoto similarity >= 0.6.

name: tanimoto-similarity-hit-rate-evaluation
description: Use when a ranked-candidate metabolite-identification run (e.g. ChemEmbed or similar embedding-based spectral matching) has produced candidate lists per spectrum and you must quantify ranking performance as top-1 (Tanimoto ≥ 0.95) and top-5 hit rates.

name: tanimoto-similarity-pair-sampling
description: Use when training MS2DeepScore-style Siamese spectral similarity models and you need to reduce training bias by sampling spectrum pairs equally over Tanimoto bins while limiting per-molecule sampling frequency differences.

name: tanimoto-similarity-performance-comparison
description: Use when you have generated/predicted molecule SMILES paired with true SMILES and need a structure-aware metric (Tanimoto via Morgan fingerprints) to quantify performance gaps between conditions, datasets, or retrievers.

name: tanimoto-similarity-prediction-evaluation
description: Use when a mass spectra library with reference structures is available and you must quantify chemical similarity prediction quality, e.g., RMSE between predicted and reference Tanimoto scores on held-out spectrum pairs.

name: tanimoto-similarity-preference-ranking
description: Use when reducing molecular hallucinations in a fingerprint-to-SELFIES generative model: you have a fine-tuned checkpoint, per-input ground-truth structures, and need preference-based ranking of sampled candidates for alignment training.

name: tanimoto-similarity-scoring
description: Use when a Pickaxe network expansion is generating too many compounds to expand further and you have a concrete set of target compounds (e.g. 250 KEGG targets with 4–9 carbons) to bias the network toward.

name: tanimoto-similarity-structure-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating de novo molecular structure elucidation from mass spectra (e.g., MassSpecGym/NPLIB1 predictions) by comparing predicted vs. reference structures via fingerprint overlap, or when supplying similarity-based chemical feedback to guide generation.

name: tanimoto-similarity-thresholding-for-annotation-agreement
description: Use when aggregating multi-annotations of MS/MS spectra and a pairwise structural-agreement term is needed in the knownness score k, including cases where a tool returned no annotation.

name: tanimoto-structural-similarity-calculation
description: Use when building structural similarity networks from a metabolite list (e.g. GC-TOF-MS plasma metabolites) where biochemical pathway knowledge is missing and edges between structurally similar compounds are needed.

name: tanimoto-structural-similarity-candidate-selection
description: Use when prioritizing a single final candidate per feature from MetFrag (e.g. COCONUT-backed) or SIRIUS annotation results for untargeted MS2 .mzML data, by combining cosine-similarity dereplication, MAW-defined metrics, MetFrag scores above 0.75, and RDKit Tanimoto structural matching.

name: tanimoto-structural-similarity-computation
description: Use when MS/MS spectra carry associated chemical structures (e.g. GNPS/MGF entries) and you need pairwise structural similarity scores to evaluate spectral similarity measures or to bin/pair spectra for benchmarking.

name: tanimoto-structural-similarity-computation
description: Use when spectral similarity scores between MS/MS spectrum pairs must be validated against ground-truth structural similarity, e.g. averaging Tanimoto similarity over top-0.1% scoring pairs or over molecular-network clusters.

name: tanimoto-structural-similarity-evaluation
description: Use when comparing MS2 spectral library search or analogue-search methods on spectra whose true structures are known, and you need a chemistry-aware accuracy metric (Tanimoto vs recall) rather than raw spectral scores.

name: tanimoto-structural-similarity-filtering
description: Use when curating a KEGG/BioTransformer-derived metabolic reaction network and you must prune in silico extended reaction pairs whose reactant-product structures are not sufficiently similar (Tanimoto < 0.7).

name: tanimoto-structural-similarity-filtering
description: Use when multiple top-scoring candidate structures per MS2 feature exist from spectral and compound database dereplication and a single prioritized final candidate per feature must be selected.

name: tanimoto-structural-similarity-scoring
description: Use when evaluating entity-level annotation quality of LC-MS feature prioritization results and false positives must be graded by chemical proximity rather than counted as uniform errors.

name: tanimoto-top-hit-search-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking MS/MS-to-fingerprint models on an unannotated study: you need to convert predicted fingerprints into annotation accuracy against a fingerprint reference database, overall and per chemical class.

name: taqman-custom-array-probe-mapping
description: Use when ΔCt qPCR data from TaqMan Custom Arrays (Applied Biosystems) must be mapped to gene symbols and converted into per-gene significance calls against a baseline cell line such as RWPE-EV.

name: target-compound-selection-by-carbon-count
description: Use when a Pickaxe-style network expansion needs an external target-compound set, and targets must be bounded in size (carbon count) and disjoint from the starting metabolome to make similarity-based filtering meaningful.

name: target-decoy-accuracy-estimation
description: Use when designing or validating a targeted lipidomics assay where you must decide how many fragment transitions per lipid (plus which polarity modes) suffice for unambiguous identification against a known background lipidome, and when reproducing a target-decoy accuracy figure from a PRM/MRM.

name: target-decoy-fdr-estimation
description: Use when assigning FDR-controlled confidence values to metabolite ion annotations from METASPACE-ML prediction scores, requiring a single weighted target-decoy ranking and Laplace-smoothed per-ion FDR output.

name: target-decoy-fdr-estimation
description: Use when filtering SSMs from a library search (standard or open/modified) to a confident set at 1% FDR, especially when modified matches must be evaluated separately from unmodified ones via target-decoy decoy-to-target ratios.

name: target-decoy-fdr-estimation
description: Use when you need to quality-control or calibrate the score cutoff of LC-MS retention-time alignment output (e.g., DeepRTAlign information_all.csv/information_target.csv) by measuring how often decoy groups are spuriously aligned.

name: target-decoy-fdr-estimation
description: Use when dereplicating LC-MS/MS spectra with DEREPLICATOR/DEREPLICATOR+ and reported MSM counts must be controlled at a chosen FDR level (0%, 1%, or 3%) rather than by raw score alone.

name: target-decoy-fdr-threshold-sweep
description: Use when you have per-dataset METASPACE/METASPACE-ML target and decoy annotation results and need to decide which of the default FDR thresholds (e.g. 5%, 10%, 20%, 50%) is most reliable for a sample-type group such as animal testing datasets.

name: target-decoy-random-matching-confidence-estimation
description: Use when de novo peptide predictions must be given an FDR-style confidence score for metaproteomics or dark-proteome spectra, especially when comparing de novo peptide detection power against a database search engine at a fixed 1% threshold.

name: target-decoy-separation-analysis
description: Use when a trained GBDT ranking model over target/decoy metabolite annotations needs its per-feature contributions explained, e.g. to check whether rho_spectral dominates separation and rho_chaos is minor.

name: target-metadata-feature-annotation
description: Use when a targeted metabolomics or proteomics dataset needs to be assembled from a metadata (target) CSV and a features CSV into a POMA/MSnbase container so downstream filtering, imputation, normalization, and statistics can reference study groups.

name: target-table-schema-standardization
description: Use when the input is a raw target list spreadsheet for targeted LC-MS integration and rows need identifiers, m/z, expected RT, and positive/negative ion-mode polarity assigned before TARDIS can consume them.

name: targeted-assay-transition-list-generation
description: Use when a targeted PRM/MRM lipidomics assay must be built from a lipid knowledge base and you need precursor m/z, fragment m/z, adduct, and charge-state transitions computed in silico from per-lipid-class rules.

name: targeted-compound-annotation-from-ms1-data
description: Use when you need to reproduce or reproduce-scale compound annotation from MS1-only LC/HRMS datasets (e.g., ST000923's 600 files / 177 annotations) by generating a CSA .msp spectra library in targeted mode and searching it with IDSL.FSA.

name: targeted-feature-extraction-from-standard-library
description: Use when serial-dilution or low-abundance analyte features are missing from a PP (peak-picking-only) feature table but their expected m/z and retention times are known from an in-house standard library CSV, and the goal is to quantify them (e.g., for LOD determination).

name: targeted-feature-extraction-metabolomics
description: Use when an untargeted LC-MS/MS feature table (post feature detection/linking) contains consensus features with missing intensities across samples and quantitative completeness is needed for statistics or downstream analysis.

name: targeted-feature-rescue-from-target-list
description: Use when processing raw LC-MS mzXML data against a known compound list (e.g. a 505-compound drug/pesticide exposome mixture) and conventional peak picking misses expected targets, especially at low concentration levels.

name: targeted-ion-extraction-from-mzml
description: Use when input is raw full-scan MSI-CE-MS data in mzML format plus a targeted mass list (analyte names, m/z values, reference migration times) and ion electropherograms must be extracted for peak annotation.

name: targeted-ion-mz-search
description: Use when you have profile-mode LC-DTIM-MS mzML data and a list of molecular formulae, and need targeted extraction of primary-ion m/z traces with RT-dimension peak picking rather than untargeted feature detection.

name: targeted-lcms-dmrm-data-processing
description: Use when you have peak-integrated targeted LC-MS data (dMRM areas for metabolites and stable isotope labeled IS) in a tab-delimited file with columns aliquot, compound, area, type, injection_time, batch, and you need batch correction, outlier detection, or compound filtering.

name: targeted-lcms-metabolite-targeting
description: Use when LC-MS raw data for targeted metabolites or stable isotope tracers (e.g. 13C6-glucose-labelled cellular metabolites) must be quantified into isotopologue peak-area tables.

name: targeted-lcms-tabular-data-ingestion
description: Use when starting from a vendor peak table exported from tools like SCIEX OS (dMRM polarity-switching MRM runs) and a tab-delimited text file of peak areas must be loaded, checked for missing/incorrect mandatory columns, and turned into a SummarizedExperiment for mzQuality QC workflows.

name: targeted-lipidomics-assay-design
description: Use when building user-defined target lists and fragment libraries for PRM or MRM lipidomics experiments from a set of lipid classes, or when fragment/collision-energy predictions and isotope-labeled transition design are needed before instrument method creation.

name: targeted-lipidomics-transition-list-processing
description: Use when Skyline peak-area exports from PRM/SRM targeted lipidomics runs (e.g. Q-Exactive HF PRM or QTRAP 6500 SRM, 5 µL triplicate injections) must be QC-filtered and quantified for a curated lipid panel.

name: targeted-metabolite-absolute-quantitation
description: Use when untargeted metabolomic profiling has flagged differentially accumulated metabolites and directional group differences must be confirmed with absolute-quantitation assays rather than relative peak intensities.

name: targeted-metabolite-extraction
description: Use when LC-MS/centWave chromatograms of a defined list of target metabolites must be quantified at the isotopologue level, with isotope-pattern similarity scores per adduct (M+H, M+Na, M+K) across samples.

name: targeted-metabolite-feature-matching
description: Use when you have augmented CE-MS/HILIC-MS feature intensity tables (treated vs. control Saccharomyces cerevisiae) and must assign down/stable/up/knock out/induced calls to a known list of target metabolites and count detections per augmentation group.

name: targeted-metabolite-peak-integration
description: Use when performing semi-targeted quantification of metabolites in LC-MS data (e.g. TripleTOF or QE HF .aird files) where EICs must be extracted, peaks selected/integrated, and compounds identified against mz/rt libraries with per-stage method choices.

name: targeted-metabolite-quantification
description: Use when you have vendor LC-MS/MS raw files for a defined panel of small-molecule targets (with or without heavy-labeled internal standards) and need calibrated concentrations rather than a discovery feature table.

name: targeted-metabolite-quantification-with-ms-dial
description: Use when a completed vendor raw file (e.g., Thermo .raw) from an active LC-MS/MS run must be converted to mzML and its user-defined targets quantified/annotated as part of Rapid QC-MS quality control.

name: targeted-metabolomics-benchmarking
description: Use when raw LC/MS mzML files from targeted metabolomics runs must be processed by multiple peak-detection tools and their signal counts and TP/FP rates compared to choose a detector.

name: targeted-metabolomics-data-elaboration
description: Use when you have targeted metabolomics peak-intensity tables with internal-standard and nominal-concentration (calibration curve point) information and need absolute concentrations plus curve/QC accuracy and internal-standard CV metrics.

name: targeted-metabolomics-peak-detection
description: Use when LC-MS data contain compounds with known m/z and RT (e.g., the 12-narcotics demonstration set) and you need targeted peak detection plus S/N quantification rather than untargeted feature finding.

name: targeted-metabolomics-peak-quantitation
description: Use when MRM chromatogram files (mzML or NetCDF from vendor raw data) plus a method file of targeted compounds need automated peak detection, coeluted-peak deconvolution, and absolute quantitation with optional QC-based batch-effect correction.

name: targeted-metabolomics-qc
description: Use when processing targeted or semi-targeted CE-, GC-, LC-MS(/MS) or HPLC metabolomics experiments (mzML acquisitions plus transition/sequence CSVs) where peak picking, calibration, feature QC and quantitation should be automated.

name: targeted-metabolomics-qc-workflow
description: Use when DDA-acquired LC-MS data has been converted to Aird format and quantified in MetaPro, and you need to batch-inspect compound integration QC and/or curate user-approved MS/MS spectra into a homemade spectral library.

name: targeted-metabolomics-quantitation
description: Use when processing targeted or semitargeted metabolomics, lipidomics, or fluxomics injection sequences (.mzML) that require automated peak detection, calibration, and concentration quantitation instead of manual vendor-software processing.

name: targeted-metabolomics-workflow-configuration
description: Use when you need to quantitate targeted LC-MS/MS MRM data (e.g., vendor raw files for bile acids or phospholipids converted to mzML/mzXML) with automatic coelution handling, standard-curve absolute quantitation, and QC-based batch-effect correction.

name: targeted-mrm-data-handling
description: Use when you have peak-integrated targeted MRM/dMRM LC-MS metabolomics data (tab-delimited or SummarizedExperiment) needing QC, batch correction, outlier flagging, compound filtering, or absolute concentration calculation.

name: targeted-ms-matrix-data-processing
description: Use when targeted LC-MS/MS peak areas show injection-order intensity drift and concentrations must be computed via external calibration, comparing correction strategies (IS, QC-based, custom bracketing, weighted bracketing).

name: targeted-ms-quantification-qc-evaluation
description: Use when a targeted LC-MS/MS sequence has been quantified under one or more drift-correction strategies (IS correction, QC-based drift correction, custom bracketing, weighted bracketing) and you must verify whether residual drift remains, per compound, before reporting concentrations.

name: targeted-mz-increment-series-search
description: Use when the goal is to find homologue series at a known m/z increment (e.g. 44.02628) in an LC-MS peak table with mz, rt, and intensity columns, and each detected peak should receive a homologue_id annotation.

name: targeted-proteomics-peak-area-quantification
description: Use when validating a discovery-trained MS feature classifier on an independent targeted (sPRM/Skyline peak-area) cohort, requiring peak-area extraction, feature-group mapping, and AUC reproduction.

name: targeted-quantification-concentration-calculation
description: Use when a MultiQuant-exported peak-area table with injection order, sample-type annotations, and analyte/IS intensities must be back-calculated to concentrations under observed intensity drift and no commercial platform offers bracketing or QC-based correction.

name: targeted-serum-metabolomics-matrix-handling
description: Use when the input is a targeted serum metabolomics intensity matrix (samples x metabolites, e.g. 234 clinical samples, 113 metabolites) plus a sample table with SampleID and group labels, and the goal is automated feature selection such as Boruta before predictive model building.

name: targeted-untargeted-metabolomics-merging
description: Use when you have centroided LC-HRMS mzML files plus a set of molecules with known molecular composition (SumForm_c), adducts, and RT boundaries, and need to benchmark untargeted pre-processing outputs (XCMS, MZmine 2, MS-DIAL) against them.

name: targetedmsqc-metric-adaptation
description: Use when XCMS-pre-processed untargeted LC–MS data needs per-peak quality features from apex-boundary ratio, jaggedness, symmetry, modality, FWHM2base, elution shift, and retention time consistency.

name: tautomer-candidate-ranking
description: Use when a CASMI-style MS/MS challenge has the correct structure present in the PubChem candidate list but several fragment peaks stay unexplained under the 10 ppm/0.002 Da tolerance and tautomers exist in the candidate set.

name: tautomer-canonicalization
description: Use when building standardized SMILES for MS/MS library entries whose source SMILES may depict the same molecule as different tautomers, and a single canonical tautomer is needed before neutralization and downstream matching.

name: taxid-mapping-ncbi-taxdump
description: Use when profiler output profiles carry numeric taxIDs that must be mapped to NCBI taxonomy names/lineages and converted to percentage relative abundances per taxon before ranking profilers or drawing abundance trees.

name: taxon-compound-census-counting
description: Use when a prioritization or novelty score needs the number of compounds already reported for a given species, genus, or family, or when the chemotaxonomic breadth of a family must be quantified from a database like LOTUS.

name: taxon-distribution-summarization
description: Use when a question asks for headline counts of a curated BGC repository (total entries, per-class breakdown such as Polyketide/NRP/RiPP/'Other', or per-taxon counts like Streptomyces/Aspergillus) rather than novel cluster prediction.

name: taxon-level-aggregation-summarization
description: Use when you have a genome-by-module presence/absence matrix (e.g., KEGG modules M00082, M00083, M00086, M00087, M00088, M00157, M00159) and need per-taxon counts or fractions of functional configurations to quantify mutual exclusivity or co-occurrence patterns.

name: taxonomic-abundance-difference-extraction
description: Use when two or more taxonomic profilers receive identical single-value benchmark scores (e.g., UniFrac, F1) on a CAMI sample, and you need to identify the specific clades whose predicted abundances differ.

name: taxonomic-annotation-record-counting
description: Use when you need to quantify what proportion of COCONUT natural products carry organism taxa, geographic origin, or literature-reference annotations, e.g. to reproduce coverage statistics like 31.5% (taxa), 15.4% (continent) and 16.6% (references).

name: taxonomic-distance-reranking-of-candidates
description: Use when annotating LC-MS/MS features of a biological extract against an in silico structure database and you want to reweight spectral matches by how closely the candidate's source organism relates taxonomically to the sample's biosource.

name: taxonomic-distance-scoring
description: Use when you have ranked candidate annotation lists (e.g. from ISDB-DNP, Sirius or MS-Finder) plus resolved taxonomy of the producing organism, and want to re-rank candidates using taxonomic distance to improve precision, recall and F1.

name: taxonomic-hit-aggregation
description: Use when microbeMASST/jobs.py batch search output (_matches.tsv, _datasets.tsv, _count_microbe.tsv) must be parsed and condensed into a per-compound table of taxa and unique sample counts to answer which organisms match a molecule.

name: taxonomic-level-assignment-of-chemical-categories
description: Use when curating or rebuilding a chemical classification ontology from OBO-format term stanzas, and each term must be assigned to a taxonomic level with preferred names and synonyms resolved.

name: taxonomic-lineage-aggregation
description: Use when microbeMASST batch-search outputs (_matches.tsv, _count_microbe.tsv) must be aggregated per NCBI lineage rank and rendered as an interactive D3 taxonomic tree (microbe_tree.html) showing which microbes may produce a queried metabolite.

name: taxonomic-metadata-degradation-simulation
description: Use when you need to validate or re-tune taxonomically informed re-ranking scores (e.g., taxo_scorer weights) under degraded or incomplete taxonomic metadata, testing robustness of the scoring strategy.

name: taxonomic-metadata-resolution
description: Use when processing LC-MS/MS DDA metabolomics samples sample-wise and the input metadata only contains free-text organism binomial names that must be standardized to stable taxonomic identifiers before RDF/SPARQL integration.

name: taxonomic-name-resolution-against-backbone
description: Use when a structural database or annotation output contains free-text organism names and you need each name resolved to a species/genus/family position on a taxonomy backbone (Catalogue of Life) before taxonomically informed re-ranking of candidates.

name: taxonomic-name-resolution-opentree
description: Use when a metadata table's ATTRIBUTE_Species (or genus/family) names may be outdated or synonymized and those names will drive taxon-level database queries such as LOTUS compound counting for the Inventa LC score.

name: taxonomic-phylum-kingdom-counting
description: Use when you have a directory of structured JSON database entries with taxonomy fields and need to compute diversity counts (distinct phyla/kingdoms) to validate reported database statistics.

name: taxonomic-profile-l1-error-computation
description: Use when you need to quantitatively rank taxonomic profilers by L1 norm error against a known ground-truth profile for a specific CAMI sample, at a chosen taxonomic rank.

name: taxonomic-profile-parsing
description: Use when input is a CAMI-format taxonomic profile (taxID, rank, abundance per taxon) that must be mapped onto the NCBI taxdump tree, e.g. for TAMPA-style tree annotation or profiler comparison.

name: taxonomic-rank-constrained-tree-plotting
description: Use when you have one or more taxonomic profiler profiles plus a ground-truth CAMI-style profile and need to visualize which clades at a chosen rank (e.g., class, phylum) drive profiler errors or abundance differences.

name: taxonomic-tree-generation-for-graphlan
description: Use when you have a taxonomy-structured abundance or biomarker table (MetaPhlAn/LEfSe/HUMAnN output, BIOM v1/v2, e.g. 16S vaginal microbiota) and need a GraPhlAn tree + annotation pair for circular rendering.

name: taxonomic-tree-plotting-ete3
description: Use when standardized taxonomic profiles (profiler output plus a gold-standard profile with TaxIDs) need a rank-resolved tree visualization of per-clade relative abundances, e.g., MetaPhlAn vs mOTUs on the CAMI marmgCAMI2 marine sample.

name: taxonomically-informed-annotation-reranking
description: Use when MS/MS annotations from ISDB-DNP, Sirius or MS-Finder exist for spectra of a taxonomically known biological source and correct structures sit at low spectral-matching ranks, so re-ranking with taxonomic distance can boost rank-1 recall.

name: taxonomy-backbone-name-resolution
description: Use when a metabolite or natural-products database stores organism information as free text (e.g., DNP Biological Source field) and you need accepted scientific names with a resolved, species-complete lineage for downstream taxonomic scoring.

name: taxonomy-based-spectrum-filtering
description: Use when a set of consensus MS/MS spectra (e.g., .mgf from MZmine molecular networking) must be labeled as putatively microbial and deconvoluted from host or human-cell-line spectral matches before downstream metabolomics interpretation.

name: taxonomy-hierarchy-modulelist-construction
description: Use when you have a species-level abundance table (e.g. skin microbiome relative abundances) plus sample metadata groups, and want enrichment at a custom taxonomic level (genus) rather than KEGG pathway/module enrichment.

name: taxonomy-name-cleaning-and-filtering
description: Use when building a taxon-restricted census (e.g. reported compounds per family) or a metadata table where species names must be cleaned to up-to-date recognized names before counting distinct genera/species.

name: taxonomy-resolution-open-tree-of-life
description: Use when a NP occurrence pipeline contains raw organism name strings (vernacular, TCM, common names, organ names) that must be mapped to canonical taxa before structure-organism pair harmonization.

name: tcga-gtex-sample-metadata-integration
description: Use when reproducing or extending a pooled TCGA/GTEx RNA-Seq compendium that requires sample-level filtering (organ-size cutoffs, duplicate removal, metadata completeness) and integration into MetaOmGraph's metadata-aware project structure.

name: tcm-deglycosylation-reaction-annotation
description: Use when bridging TCM prototype components to their predictable metabolites in MS data, and a reaction catalog including deglycosylation plus scored m/z and MS2-similarity matching is needed.

name: tcm-extract-compound-identification
description: Use when a low-resolution MS2 spectrum of a marker peak from a TCM/herbal extract was acquired on a miniaturized mass spectrometer and the goal is de novo structural annotation of the contained compound without a library match.

name: tcm-in-vivo-metabolite-annotation
description: Use when you have a mouse/in vivo feature list and an in vitro prototype list (RT + accurate m/z per component) and must annotate prototypes, isomers, and metabolites of TCM components sharing a parent nucleus.

name: tcm-metabolite-bridging
description: Use when you have a PATBS-processed feature table (m/z, MS1, MS2, retention) for prototypes and candidate metabolites and need to score/bridge metabolite–prototype relationships using MS1/MS2 mass-defect windows (±25 mmu) and fragment matching.

name: tcm-metabolite-characterization
description: Use when you have LC-MS feature lists from in vivo TCM dosing (plasma, urine, feces, tissue) plus an in vitro prototype component list and need to characterize metabolites and bridge them to parent prototypes.

name: tcn-model-training-on-tandem-msms
description: Use when training a formula-prediction deep learning model from matched MS/MS spectral libraries (e.g., MoNA Q-TOF, NIST23 Orbitrap) or when reproducing the paper's cross-instrument generalization experiment (Fig. 4j).

name: tdm-data-formatting-nmtran
description: Use when individual concentration records and dosing history (times, amounts, infusion rates, covariates) must be assembled into an NM-TRAN dataset to feed mapbayest() from a mrgsolve-coded population PK model.

name: technical-covariate-regression-analysis
description: Use when you have UK Biobank NMR biomarker data (249 biomarkers plus sample QC fields) and need to quantify, per biomarker, the percentage of concentration variance attributable to each technical covariate to decide which measurements need technical-variation removal.

name: technical-replicate-agreement-analysis
description: Use when per-file human QC annotations from multiple raters must be reduced to consensus labels and quantified for inter-rater agreement, especially on embedded technical replicates.

name: technical-replicate-collapsing
description: Use when an LC-MS/MS feature table contains repeated technical replicate injections (annotated via 'technical_rep' in the sample annotation file) and downstream per-feature tests such as ANOVA must be run over biological replicates only.

name: technical-replicate-metadata-mapping
description: Use when starting an mpactR workflow: you have a Progenesis peak table CSV and a sample metadata CSV with Injection, Sample_Code, and Biological_Group columns, and technical replicates must be linked to biological groups before filtering.

name: technical-replicate-peak-filtering
description: Use when input is centroided, peak-picked replicate MS data (e.g. mzML-derived peak lists, one CSV per replicate injection) and a denoised list of unique MS features is needed before bioactivity scoring in NP Analyst.

name: technical-replicate-peak-filtering
description: Use when processing DIMS SIM-stitched or LC-MS XCMS peak lists where each biological sample has been injected as technical replicates and low-confidence peaks detected inconsistently across injections must be removed prior to alignment.

name: technical-replicate-repeatability-rsd-analysis
description: Use when assessing how repeatable a peak-detection/integration workflow is across technical replicate injections of the same sample, e.g. by computing per-feature RSD of exported peak areas and comparing against reported thresholds.

name: technical-replicate-scheduling-for-lc-ms-batches
description: Use when planning acquisition of a large-scale targeted metabolomics batch series (e.g. >1,000 plasma samples over 44 days) and you need a concrete 96-well plate layout embedding pooled QCs, short replicates, and batch replicates before running samples.

name: technical-replicate-variability-assessment
description: Use when you have ≥2 technical replicates of a pooled QC sample across a targeted compound list (e.g. 8 replicates of a phospholipid QC with 163 retained phospholipids) and need to compare quantitation tools or deconvolution/correction settings by replicate-to-replicate abundance stability.

name: technical-variation-threshold-filtering
