description: Use when QC replicate samples (e.g. pooled QC1 samples) exist in a 1H-NMR metabonomic dataset and you must quantify feature-level technical variation or decide which metabolic features to retain for downstream MWAS analysis.

name: technical-vs-biological-replicate-comparison
description: Use when comparing reproducibility between technical and biological replicate layers of MS-Metabolomics feature matrices (e.g., COPDGene Tech, BioTech PR000438, Bio PR000907) to quantify reproducible metabolites per sample pair and sample pairs per metabolite.

name: teft-structure-prediction-inference
description: Use when low-resolution MS2 spectra from a miniaturized ion trap instrument must be annotated with de novo molecular structures (SMILES) without library matching, especially for unknown natural products or drugs on-site.

name: temporal-gradient-visualization-savitzky-golay-smoothing
description: Use when analyzing a 1,000-step diffusion denoising trajectory to reveal the temporal order in which spectral conditioning resolves atom semantics, simple substructures, and complex functional groups.

name: temporary-file-io-data-exchange-parsing
description: Use when an R process must ingest results produced by an external compiled executable (e.g. a .NET wrapper around the Thermo RawFileReader API) via temporary files, then parse them into typed S3 objects.

name: tenfold-cross-validation-calibration
description: Use when user-supplied reference standard retention times (e.g. from MassBank records) are available and a per-dataset RT–log P model must be calibrated and validated before scoring MetFrag candidates by retention.

name: tensorflow-gpu-checkpoint-management
description: Use when training or reloading a TensorFlow model whose environment is version-pinned (Python 3.8.13, TensorFlow 2.5.0-GPU) and the selected configuration must be saved as an .h5 checkpoint for reuse or prediction.

name: tensorflow-mlp-training
description: Use when small molecules (e.g. SDF/InChIKey inputs) must be converted to spectra predictions via a supervised neural network trained on NIST EI-MS spectra — specifically when a residual MLP regression head over 4096-bit ECFP features is the chosen featurization-and-prediction scheme.

name: tensorflow-model-training-and-evaluation
description: Use when a custom CNN must be trained on LC-HRMS chromatograms to distinguish true chromatographic peaks from background signals (including walls) and evaluated on independent validation chromatograms.

name: tensorflow-model-training-and-serialization
description: Use when building, training, or saving the pSCNN architecture (dual 6-conv subnetworks, 32 kernels of 5x1, ReLU, max pooling, 100-unit dense with dropout 0.2, Sigmoid output) for NMR mixture compound identification.

name: tentative-compound-annotation-curation
description: Use when a GC-MS library-hit table (columns Component.RT, Component.Area, Base.Peak.MZ, File.Name, Compound.Name, Match.Factor) needs per-compound public-database annotation and curation before peak-area extraction.

name: terminology-source-integration-mesh-ncit-cellosaurus
description: Use when user-submitted freetext metadata strings (sample headers in metabolomics submissions) must be mapped onto fixed, curated vocabularies compiled from MeSH, NCBI Taxonomy, Cellosaurus, NCIT and FDA sources.

name: test-set-spectrum-binning
description: Use when raw MS/MS spectra (peak lists of m/z/intensity pairs) must be converted into fixed-length vectors before feeding the MS2DeepScore base network, e.g. to compute 200-dim embeddings for t-SNE clustering or similarity scoring.

name: tfidf-nearest-neighbor-model-retraining
description: Use when a user confirms a new freetext sample metadata term that is absent from an SMetaS header's existing vocabulary and the standardizer's synonym/typo models must be updated to map it.

name: tfidf-nearest-neighbor-term-curation
description: Use when a freetext metabolomics sample-metadata column (csv) must be mapped onto fixed SMetaS vocabularies and many strings are near-matches or synonyms of existing controlled terms.

name: tg-molecular-species-annotation
description: Use when processing DIA-lipidomics MS-DIAL or MZMine feature lists with multiplexed MS2 spectra and confident, FDR-controlled TG molecular-species annotations are needed for downstream differential analysis.

name: theoretical-fragment-ion-cataloging
description: Use when building a searchable 4D sterol lipid database that requires predicted fragment ions for N-Me derivatized (C=C bond-targeted) unsaturated sterols, e.g. to support LC-IM-MS/MS based identification at the isomer level.

name: theoretical-fragment-spectrum-matching
description: Use when you have experimental MS/MS spectra (e.g. CID or HCD, positive mode) of candidate NRP/PK compounds and building-block sequences exported from MassSpecBlocks, and you need to identify the compound whose theoretical b-/a-ion fragment pattern matches the spectrum.

name: theoretical-isotope-distribution-calculation
description: Use when confirming RT-dimension peaks detected for primary ion m/z traces against candidate molecular formulae: a theoretical A/A+1/A+2 intensity pattern is needed to accept or reject detected peaks.

name: theoretical-isotope-distribution-computation
description: Use when high-resolution MS1 isotope peak lists (peak masses and abundances) must be assigned a molecular formula by ranking candidate isotope patterns, or when reimplementing SIRIUS 4's isotope pattern intensity scoring.

name: theoretical-isotope-pattern-simulation
description: Use when reproducing or retraining the metabolite isotope-pattern reference models behind FeatureFinderMetabo's SVM classifier, e.g. to regenerate linear m/z-spacing fits or noise-perturbed training data for metabolite feature validation.

name: theoretical-isotope-pattern-simulation
description: Use when extracting and scoring M+H isotopologues for targeted metabolites in LC-MS data — you need a theoretical isotope pattern per compound, calculated at the MS resolution, to compare against observed EIC peak intensities.

name: theoretical-mass-matching-for-msi-annotation
description: Use when filtered LC-MS/MS peptide identifications and a co-registered imzML/H&E pair are available and per-protein spatial ion images must be annotated with LC-MS/MS-level confidence (e.g., bladder biomarkers smoothelin, Col6a1, fibronectin, myosin-11).

name: theoretical-mz-calculation-for-adduct-ions
description: Use when an established list of identified metabolites (e.g. organ-specific sheets from 'Organ specific metabolite database.xlsx') must be adduct-ion-expanded with theoretical m/z values to build or extend an annotation database for ambient mass spectrometry imaging (AFADESI-MSI) data.

name: theoretical-mz-computation-esi-adduct-lists
description: Use when building or extending a predicted lipid database and monoisotopic m/z values for ESI adducts are needed to match IM-MS features against enumerated lipid species.

name: theoretical-spectrum-fragment-scoring
description: Use when a measured MS2 spectrum must be scored against candidate lipid theoretical fragment spectra (m/z matching within ppm tolerance) to produce Score_matched and Score_ratio pairs for lipid annotation decision trees.

name: therapeutic-class-aggregation-counting
description: Use when you have per-drug LC-HRMS feature counts (e.g., unpredicted BioTransformer features from the ST003991 human liver S9 study) and need per-therapeutic-class totals such as 486,215 features split by anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, cardiovascular, and CNS drugs.

name: thermo-acquisition-sequence-configuration
description: Use when running Rapid QC-MS quality control over a Thermo Orbitrap LC-MS/MS run: you have a Thermo acquisition sequence .csv, Thermo .raw files, and a spectral library .msp and need automated, specimen-level QC assignments minutes after each file is written.

name: thermo-instrument-data-handling
description: Use when a completed Thermo .raw file is written during an active instrument run and must be converted to mzML (MSConvert) then quantified/annotated (MS-DIAL) for automated QC.

name: thermo-raw-to-mzml-conversion
description: Use when the input is a Thermo (or other vendor) proprietary RAW file from a mass spectrometry repository and the goal is an open, Parquet-compatible spectral table matching the arcMS Waters-UNIFI schema (rt, scanid, mslevel, mz, intensity).

name: thermodynamic-gibbs-index-calculation
description: Use when an FT-ICR MS peak table with assigned molecular formulas (e.g., Report.csv) needs per-peak thermodynamic indices such as NOSC/GFE for energetic or chemodiversity analysis.

name: thermodynamically-infeasible-cycle-detection
description: Use when a compartmentalized community metabolic model (SBML, PyCoMo/COBRApy) predicts exchange fluxes or cross-feeding interactions absent from a reference analysis, suggesting a thermodynamically infeasible cycle.

name: thermodynamics-filtering-of-generated-reactions
description: Use when a rule-based network expansion (e.g. Pickaxe over EcoCyc with JN1224min rules) yields more reactions than needed and thermodynamic plausibility should be used to prune physiologically infeasible reactions before metabolomics peak annotation.

name: three-class-diagnostic-metric-evaluation
description: Use when a multi-class LC-MS/metabolomics classifier (e.g., 10-run DenseNet121 ensemble) must be benchmarked on held-out .npy spectra with disease-type labels, and accuracy/precision/recall/F1/AUC plus AUC-curve and confusion-matrix figures are the deliverable.

name: three-level-kmeans-image-segmentation
description: Use when an LA-ICP-MS elemental image (e.g. 56Fe from a MassHunter batch) needs automatic background/ROI separation without hand-set thresholds, as in Pew2's segmentation tool.

name: threshold-based-edge-filtering
description: Use when you have a processed samples-by-metabolites intensity table from Viime and want a network diagram revealing correlated metabolite behavior, including cross-platform (MS/NMR fused) relationships.

name: threshold-based-hit-evaluation
description: Use when query spectra (e.g. ESI-MS2 peak lists from QqQ or QqTOF instruments) are searched against a reference spectral library and you need precision/recall/F-value metrics at a specific similarity-score cutoff.

name: threshold-based-peak-detection
description: Use when a JCAMP-DX or mzML spectrum (NMR, IR, MS) needs its peaks extracted automatically and the user has no better model than an intensity threshold; triggered whenever ChemSpectra's peak-picking dialog is invoked with a default or adjusted threshold.

name: threshold-based-peak-pair-filtering
description: Use when you have a PyINETA peak list from a 13C INADEQUATE spectrum and need to group peaks into same-compound networks before database matching.

name: threshold-calibration-per-fragment-ion
description: Use when per-m/z-bin binary classifiers output probabilities that must be turned into presence/absence peak calls for MS/MS spectra reconstruction, using SingleFrag-style validation-calibrated thresholds.

name: threshold-optimization-weighted-youden-index
description: Use when a binary classifier produces continuous scores (e.g. GNN reaction-pair predictions in MetDNA3) and you need a data-driven decision cutoff rather than the default 0.5, especially when class balance or asymmetric costs make a single operating point critical.

name: threshold-sweep-statistics-analysis
description: Decision support for choosing a ΔCCS threshold when validating a CCS-prediction-based annotation filter over a set of standards with known PubChem candidate lists.

name: tic-aggregation-from-arrow-datasets
description: Use when HRMS data has been converted to Parquet with arcMS and you need a TIC (or similar chromatogram) without loading the full profile-mode file into RAM, e.g. for Waters UNIFI (HD)MSE acquisitions with ion mobility.

name: tic-normalization-benchmarking
description: Use when you have LC/MS MS1 ion-feature matrices (e.g., mzLearn mzML-derived outputs, >150 samples per dataset) and need to quantify whether drift correction is necessary by comparing synthetic QC vs experimental QC vs TIC vs raw normalization via RSD on withheld QC injections.

name: tic-normalization-of-msi-spectra
description: Use when raw imzML MALDI-MSI pixel spectra must be made quantitatively comparable across a tissue section before dimensionality reduction or segmentation, as the first steps of MSIght's MSI pre-processing workflow.

name: tic-normalization-preprocessing
description: Use when raw MS spectra must be intensity-scaled per sample (TIC) before binning into a fixed spectrum_dim (e.g. 9900 for RCC positive mode) and fed to CNN/LSTM classifiers or ML baselines.

name: tic-normalization-single-cell
description: Use when you have raw per-cell peak lists (m/z, retention time, intensity) from single-probe SCMS of single cells and need to remove injection-to-injection intensity variation before peak alignment, feature filtering, or ML classification.

name: tic-normalized-lipid-imaging-data-handling
description: Use when you have a massPix-generated normalised image data matrix (image.norm.csv with lipid annotations, m/z and TIC-normalised intensities per pixel) and need to classify tissue regions by clustering or PCA.

name: tic-normalized-msi-quantification
description: Use when per-pixel MSI intensities must be compared across spatial positions, serial sections, or anatomical regions — e.g. before region-level fold-change testing on registered rat-brain coronal/sagittal volumes.

name: tic-normalized-spectra-reconstruction-evaluation
description: Use when raw high-dimensional MSI spectra (imzML/HDF5, tens of thousands of m/z variables) need TIC-normalized reconstruction error quantification via a VAE, or when validating reported reconstruction MSE targets.

name: tic-signal-smoothing
description: Use when you have a TIC trace extracted from raw AEMS data plus an upstream table of inferred ejection times, and you need to define the time window during which each ejection was detected.

name: tide-percolator-database-search-peptide-identification
description: Use when DDA tandem MS spectra (e.g., from MassIVE MSV000094709) must be searched against a sample-specific metapeptide or environmental protein database with 1% FDR control, to yield confident PSM/peptide counts as a database-search baseline.

name: tidymass-massdataset-object-handling
description: Use when LC-MS untargeted metabolomics results (feature tables, differential-metabolite lists, annotations) must be carried between tidyMass modules or converted to/from external tool formats, e.g. feeding sex-stratified differential metabolites into metpath enrichment.

name: tidymass-package-installation-and-loading
description: Use when beginning an LC-MS untargeted metabolomics analysis in R and the tidyMass packages are not yet available in the environment, or when a reproducible docker-based environment (e.g. the tidymass-case-study image) must be provisioned before data processing.

name: tidymass-package-installation-and-version-checking
description: Use when an R environment must be set up for a tidyMass LC–MS metabolomics pipeline, or when the installed tidyMass package versions must be confirmed to match a published workflow before reprocessing mzML data.

name: tie-aware-rank-computation
description: Use when GNN-SOM assigns identical site-of-metabolism likelihoods to multiple candidate derivatives generated by PROXIMAL2 from an anchor molecule, and a single unambiguous rank must be reported for each suspect.

name: tie-resolution-average-rank-calculation
description: Use when evaluating how accurately a ranked candidate list (e.g. BAM/GNN-SOM derivative rankings for anchor–suspect pairs) places the true suspect, and multiple candidates share the same rank score requiring average-rank tie resolution.

name: time-course-concentration-inference-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating an inference method for absolute metabolite concentrations from relative abundance time-course data where no published comparator exists, so negative controls (random / constant response factors) must be constructed and scored.

name: time-course-metabolomic-peak-table-formatting
description: Use when a raw time-course metabolomic peak table (e.g., LC-MS plasma samples from MetaboLights MTBLS656 or NOREVA_exampledata.zip) must be reformatted, before scanning thousands of NOREVA processing workflows.

name: time-domain-mcmc-spectral-modeling
description: Use when you need to deconvolute high-resolution 1D NMR spectra (e.g., urine metabolomics FIDs/spectra) into peak feature tables and quantify metabolite amplitudes, especially with overlapping peaks.

name: time-domain-spectral-decomposition
description: Use when 1D NMR spectra (simulated, mixture, or biofluid such as urine) contain heavily overlapping peaks that frustrate frequency-domain peak picking, and the goal is automated peak-table extraction and metabolite quantification against ground truth.

name: time-domain-subsampling-of-nmr-fids
description: Use when preparing a binned time-domain FID (e.g., 16,384 complex points) for model-based spectral decomposition where overfitting must be controlled before optimization iterations begin.

name: time-series-baseline-correction
description: Use when the input is a table of signal intensity columns measured along a shared time axis (e.g. intensity traces of neuron activity) and you need to remove each trace's baseline offset before computing or exporting area-under-the-curve or corrected-signal values.

name: time-stamp-based-log-analysis
description: Use when you need to measure how quickly a continuous file-watching pipeline (e.g. QC4Metabolomics with module_File_schedule enabled) detects and schedules newly placed mzML files in near-real-time.

name: time-to-event-survival-data-handling
description: Use when the input is a CSV of survival times, censoring status, and group labels (like GraphBio's surv_example.csv) and the goal is publication-ready per-group Kaplan-Meier survival curves.

name: timeline-diagnostics-visualization
description: Use when instrument QA requires plotting a time-line of QC pool diagnostics (m/z, RT, intensity, peak shape) to detect calibration drift, sensitivity loss or contamination, e.g. MetNexs long-term QC injections on a Waters Synapt.

name: timestamp-delay-calculation
description: Use when a sample cohort has date+time stamps for blood collection, centrifugation, and freezing and you need the pre-/post-centrifugation delays that drive PRIMA Panel performance reports or SPREC assignment.

name: timing-statistics-aggregation
description: Use when you need to quantify and compare the runtime of a software tool across input categories (e.g., cluster types or module counts), requiring replicate timing and statistical aggregation.

name: tims-ccs-linear-calibration-toward-dt-reference
description: Use when TIMS-derived CCS values (e.g., from Vasilopoulou et al. or Tsugawa et al. negative-mode datasets) must be calibrated toward DT reference CCS values and the residual error quantified as MDRE.

name: tims-raw-data-access
description: Use when raw data are Bruker timsTOF .d folders (TDF format) with DDA-PASEF acquisitions and you need frame-, scan-, or spectrum-level access to m/z, intensity, and ion-mobility values in a Python pipeline.

name: timstof-ms1-frame-sampling
description: Use when you need to run the LSH signal-classification algorithm (mzBucket/proteolizard-algorithm) on a subset of a TimsTOF acquisition, or benchmark its runtime as the thread count is swept, without loading the full DDA-PASEF data set into memory.

name: timstof-raw-frame-data-access
description: Use when raw Bruker timsTOF PRO .d/TDF LC-IMS-MS data must be loaded frame-wise in Python (e.g. to select precursor frames by frame id, bin mass axes, or feed hashing algorithms) rather than using vendor software.

name: tissue-biopsy-accessibility-classification
description: Use when intersecting exercise- or condition-responsive DE genes with gene-disease associations and you need to stratify results by whether the underlying tissue is routinely accessible in human biopsies (blood, skeletal muscle, adipose) or not.

name: tissue-distribution-visualization
description: Use when you hold MASST match results for synthesized compounds (e.g., conjugated bile acids) annotated with ReDU biospecimen/tissue and health-phenotype metadata, and you need tissue-distribution or disease-association count tables and ordinations.

name: tissue-enriched-ion-identification-wilcoxon
description: Use when preprocessing a spatial metabolomics peak table matrix (X/Y pixel coordinates plus ion intensity columns) to separate tissue from background pixels, and you have lasso-defined tissue and background region annotations to compare per-ion intensity distributions.

name: tissue-enriched-ion-proportion-analysis
description: Use when you have a peak table matrix of pixels by ion intensities with spatial coordinates and need to quantify the proportion of ions with higher expression in a tissue region versus background, as in SMQVP's QVP3 module.

name: tissue-metadata-annotation
description: Use when building or extending the tissueMASST reference index: public MS/MS files must be tagged with tissue-associated metadata (organism, tissue, disease status) before spectral search queries can be mapped to biological context.

name: tissue-region-annotation-from-lipid-co-localisation
description: Use when a processed MALDI/imzML spatial metabolomics dataset (e.g. murine urinary bladder) must be segmented into anatomical regions and each cluster annotated using known region-defining lipid m/z markers plus differentially expressed m/z peaks.

name: tissue-separation-verification-in-ordination-space
description: Use when a labeled metabolomics feature table (samples x features with tissue/group labels) needs a check that one group forms a distinct cluster in unsupervised PCA space, e.g. buccal gland vs. other tissues.

name: tissue-specific-metabolite-enrichment-filtering
description: Use when a negative-ion-mode LC-MS feature table spans multiple tissue groups and you need features with extreme, statistically controlled enrichment in one tissue versus every other group.

name: tissue-specific-metabolite-filtering
description: Use when a list of statistically significant up/down-regulated ion m/z values from an MSI region comparison needs putative metabolite IDs restricted to those plausible for the imaged tissue.

name: tma-core-background-removal
description: Use when a LA-ICP-MS elemental image (e.g., a 1.5 mm TMA core imaged at 10 µm beam, 40 µm/s) needs automatic tissue-vs-background separation without manual threshold tuning, using multi-level k-means segmentation.

name: tmap-structural-similarity-projection
description: Use when you must quantify how many compounds in a spectral library are new relative to open (GNPS, MassBank EU, MoNA) and commercial (mzCloud, NIST23) libraries, and visualize the overlap pattern as an UpSet plot and TMAP projection.

name: tmap-tree-visualization-of-metabolomics-samples
description: Use when samples have been vectorized into a MEMO MS2-fingerprint matrix and you need an RT-agnostic tree layout to explore clustering, overlay annotations, or cross-check UMAP/PCoA groupings of chemodiverse samples.

name: tmap-umap-embedding-visualization-of-sample-vectors
description: Use when a MEMO sample-by-MS2-fingerprint matrix has been aligned and you must visualize whether samples cluster retention-time-agnostically, including across different LC gradients and MS instruments.

name: tms-derivative-metabolite-accounting
description: Use when recomputing or verifying dysregulated-metabolite statistics from an eRah compound table in which one metabolite occurs in several TMS-derivatized rows (e.g., leucine 1TMS/2TMS) and two-group class comparisons are required.

name: tms-fragment-mz-exclusion
description: Use when preparing GC-EI MS chromatograms (netCDF or mzXML) for eRah deconvolution and column bleed or derivatization-reagent fragments (e.g. m/z 73:75, 147:149, 35:69) would otherwise seed spurious deconvolved compounds.

name: tobit-censored-data-regression
description: Use when metabolomics intensities contain values censored at detection limits (requiring Tobit) or repeated measures requiring mixed effects, and per-metabolite effect estimates with FDR-corrected p-values are needed.

name: tobit-censored-regression-with-detection-limits
description: Use when metabolite intensity values are censored because they fall below/above limits of detection and you need regression associations that correctly handle censoring rather than discarding or imputing those values.

name: tocsy-hsqc-spectral-filtering
description: Use when processing peak-picked TOCSY/HSQC peak tables from complex natural product mixtures prior to spin system construction and filtering out solvent, water, and illegitimate-region artifacts is needed.

name: tocsy-symmetrization
description: Use when processing peak-picked TOCSY/HSQC tables from complex mixture NMR (e.g. MADByTE) and f1/f2 chemical shifts are asymmetric, so TOCSY data must be symmetrized and filtered before spin system construction.

name: token-level-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when scoring lipid species predictions against labels for held-out MS2 spectra and you need both strict whole-sequence accuracy and token/component-level diagnostics rather than a single overall match rate.

name: token-level-lipid-accuracy-scoring
description: Use when evaluating transformer-decoded lipid species predictions on held-out or unseen-species spectra and you need per-spectrum strict-match accuracy plus component-level token accuracy CSVs.

name: tomato-pericarp-metabolomics-data-handling
description: Use when a metabolomics concentration matrix (e.g., introgression-line metabolite profiles) contains missing values and must be completed before computing pairwise correlations such as the |r| >= 0.3, p <= 0.01 Metabolite CN edges.

name: tonsil-b-cell-population-subsetting
description: Use when a scSpaMet single-cell feature table (protein + co-registered SIMS metabolite intensities) from tonsil tissue must be narrowed to germinal-center B cells before pseudotime or metabolite-trajectory analysis.

name: tool-count-cross-validation-across-sources
description: Use when a paper claims a countable quantity (number of tools, modules, datasets) and a companion GitHub repository or README exists that can independently enumerate the same quantity for cross-checking.

name: tool-inventory-comparison-across-frameworks
description: Use when the analysis goal is to determine which analytical tools overlap across two or more Galaxy-based (or standalone) metabolomics toolkits, and which tools are unique to one suite.

name: top-k-accuracy-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking chemical formula identification from tandem MS/MS spectra against published baselines (e.g., reproducing FIDDLE's 88.3% top-1 / 93.6% top-5 accuracy on NIST23 against SIRIUS and BUDDY).

name: top-k-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when spectra have known correct structures (spectral library or labeled benchmark) and you need to compare database-search methods by whether the true structure appears in the top-k ranked candidates.

name: top-k-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when a candidate-generation model outputs ranked SMILES predictions per spectrum and you need Acc_k and Sim_k metrics for k=1,10,50 on held-out EI-MS test splits.

name: top-k-accuracy-evaluation-of-structure-prediction
description: Use when a spectral-to-structure model outputs multiple candidate molecules per compound and you must quantify ranking quality as top-1/top-3 accuracy against known test-set structures.

name: top-k-annotation-accuracy-evaluation

description: Use when you have MS/MS feature spectra (.mgf) and need a 2D overview layout of pairwise spectral similarities (e.g. ms2deepscore scores) to spot locally grouped high-similarity features before detailed network inspection.

name: tsne-embedding-visualization
description: Use when you have a metabolomics feature matrix with sample metadata and need to visually assess sample clustering, batch effects, or confounder-driven structure before classification modeling.

name: tsne-embedding-visualization
description: Use when you must build a structurally informed train/test split — e.g. testing how a spectral-prediction ranker generalizes to molecules dissimilar from its training set — by embedding binary fingerprints and grouping molecules into structural clusters.

name: tsne-local-neighborhood-exploration
description: Use when a precomputed pairwise MS/MS similarity matrix (e.g., ms2deepscore) and a .mgf feature set need interactive local exploration around a densely connected node to support structural hypothesis generation.

name: tsne-projection-of-bgc-embeddings
description: Use when you have pfam2vec (or similar domain) embeddings and need to visually/quantitatively validate that BGCs of the same product subclass cluster together in the learned vector space.

name: tsne-scatter-plot-visualization
description: Use when you need to visually compare chemical-space coverage across multiple mass spectral libraries using normalized chemical identifiers, PubChem fingerprints, and t-SNE dimensionality reduction.

name: tsp-path-optimisation
description: Use when a detected/filtering-surviving list of sample coordinates (e.g. from macroMS sample finding over colonies or droplets) must be ordered into a visit sequence to minimise total stage travel before generating a device geometry file.

name: tsv-csv-metadata-table-export
description: Use when RAW-file acquisition metadata must be extracted from Thermo .RAW mass spectrometry files into structured, analysis-ready TSV/CSV tables for QC, provenance, repository submission, or downstream computational workflows.

name: tsv-feature-table-input-output
description: Use when a metabolomics workflow step (normalization, missing-value imputation, blank masking, batch correction, annotation) must read a feature table from or write one to a TSV file with samples as rows and features as columns.

name: tsv-file-parsing
description: Use when a metadata/sample-information table must be parsed or validated before submitting a GNPS molecular networking job, or when diagnosing why a deposited dataset's metadata fails the GNPS schema.

name: tsv-results-table-generation
description: Use when computing Inventa novelty scores (FC, LC, CC, SC) for an extract set and you need to write the per-sample component scores, newly detected unreported classes, and final priority rank into a consolidated TSV output.

name: ttest-differential-variable-detection
description: Use when evaluating whether a missing value imputation method (e.g., GSimp, QRILC, kNN-TN) preserves the ability to detect differential variables between two groups on MNAR-degraded metabolomics data.

name: tucker-congruence-component-validation
description: Use when performing blind (no prior component knowledge) PARAFAC deconvolution of m/z × RT2 × RT1 sub-tensors from untargeted GC × GC–TOFMS data and you must decide the correct number of components and reject non-chemical (non-Gaussian) loadings.

name: tukey-hsd-significance-letter-annotation
description: Use when comparing distributions of derived molecular descriptors (H/C, O/C, NOSC, GFE, AImod, DBE) across user-defined sample groups and the resulting violin/density plots need statistically justified significance letters on group medians.

name: tukey-posthoc-pairwise-pvalue-computation
description: Use when a metabolomics concentration table (CSV with sample rows, metabolite columns, and a group/factor column) has two or more sample groups and you need, per metabolite, an ANOVA p-value plus pairwise Tukey p-values for every inter-group comparison.

name: tumor-normal-class-separation-visualization
description: Use when a trained probabilistic encoder yields a compact latent representation (e.g., 5-D from a VAE Code layer) of high-dimensional spectra and you need to visually confirm class separation between normal and tumor groups.

name: tumor-region-annotation-overlay
description: Use when raw imzML/HDF5 MSI pixel data (e.g. 100 µm FT-ICR acquisitions with tens of thousands of m/z variables) must be visualized as an ion image and compared against expert-annotated tumor regions from a consecutive H&E-stained section.

name: tumor-subgroup-denominator-reconciliation
description: Use when an analysis needs to test whether genomic alteration calls (e.g. 10q/PTEN loss, 8q/MYC gain) predict or account for protein-level oncoprotein status (phosphoAKT1, MYC) in a cohort of tumors, requiring subgroup denominators to be reconciled before concordance fractions are reported.

name: tumor-subgroup-stratification-table-construction
description: Use when a tumor cohort must be stratified into molecular subgroups (e.g. by biomarker-high/low status such as phosphoAKT1 and MYC) and a table of subgroup counts, percentages, and the marker scoring parameters that produced them is required.

name: tumor-vs-normal-expression-comparison
description: Use when you have an RNA-Seq expression dataset with sample metadata encoding tumor status and organ, and the goal is to identify genes differentially expressed between tumor and matched non-tumor groups within one cancer type.

name: tune-mix-calibrant-feature-matching
description: Use when calibrating collision cross sections on Agilent 6560 ion mobility data: you have tune mix H5 files (e.g. example_tune_pos.h5, example_tune_neg.h5) with known-CCS calibrants and must match detected peaks to reference CCS values per ionization mode.

name: tutorial-dataset-reproduction
description: Use when a task asks to reproduce a bundled tutorial or canonical benchmark dataset (e.g. iris from Fisher 1936) with a published tool's statistical workflow, such as unsupervised PCA on small feature tables.

name: twas-deg-enrichment-intersection-analysis
description: Use when you have TWAS/PrediXcan gene-level association results and a set of condition-responsive DEGs, and need to quantify whether the DEGs are enriched (or depleted) among significant trait-tissue-gene associations with uncertainty quantification.

name: twas-direction-of-effect-analysis
description: Use when you have per-gene direction-of-effect calls (product of DE direction and PrediXcan association direction) aggregated into trait–tissue gene sets and need to test enrichment/depletion of positive effects against a null log-odds of 0 with correlated-trait correction.

name: twim-ccs-calibration-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether a TWIM-MS CCS calibration approach correctly assigns features to biomolecular classes (small molecules, lipids, peptides) and produces accurate calibrated TWCCSN2 values, especially under simulated calibration error.

name: twim-ccs-calibration-parameter-fitting
description: Use when processing traveling-wave ion mobility MS data (e.g. Waters SYNAPT XS) and you need calibrated TWCCSN2 values for features whose biomolecular class is not yet identified.
tools: Waters Major Mix IMS/Tof Calibration Kit

name: twim-ccs-class-assignment
description: Use when processing an experimental TWIM feature spreadsheet (feature IDs, m/z, charge state, retention time, arrival time) from a Waters SYNAPT-class instrument and uncalibrated features must be assigned to a biomolecular class and CCS-calibrated without prior identification.

name: twim-ccs-power-law-calibration
description: Use when processing traveling-wave IM-MS data (e.g. Waters SYNAPT XS) where feature CCS values must be calibrated without prior identification, especially in mixed multiomic samples spanning lipids, small molecules, and peptides.

name: twims-ccs-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when computed CCS values from the snakemake_ccs workflow (ccs.txt Boltzmann averages or HPCCS per-conformer outputs) must be validated against experimental TWIMS CCS values using percent error and the ±3% agreement criterion.

name: twims-ccs-measurement-extraction
description: Use when TWIMS CCS experimental values and instrumental parameters are available in Supporting Information tables and the goal is to compare them against literature CCS values for the same metabolites and adduct states to establish an experimental uncertainty threshold.

name: twims-experimental-ccs-benchmarking
description: Use when predicted CCS values (e.g., from an ML+DFT workflow) must be validated against TWIMS experimental values and literature CCS database values for metabolites in protonated/deprotonated/neutral states.

name: twims-nonlinear-calibration
description: Use when CCS values must be computed from traveling wave-based IMS-MS data (Waters Synapt or SLIM) where arrival times require non-linear (quadratic/cubic polynomial or linearized power) calibration against Agilent tune-mix calibrants.

name: twin-study-variance-component-decomposition
description: Use when SWATH-MS/DIA LC-MS maps from related individuals (e.g. co-twins sampled longitudinally) must be quantified and per-protein variance apportioned into genetic, shared-environment and time effects.

name: two-channel-pixel-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you have background-corrected two-channel (CFP/YFP or red/green) confocal microscopy images from a Zeiss LSM 510 or similar and need to determine whether, and in what proportion of pixels, the two fluorescent signals colocalize beyond random overlap.

name: two-color-histogram-colocalization-pixel-classification
description: Use when you have a background-corrected two-color (e.g., red/green) microscopy image pair and need an automatic, quantitative per-pixel colocalization decision plus M1/M2 coefficients.

name: two-color-image-simulation-generation
description: Use when validating a colocalization algorithm: you need synthetic two-color image pairs with known ground-truth colocalization (100% down to 0%) or a subvisual colocalization case to measure false-positive/false-negative misclassification rates.

name: two-dimensional-cow-peak-alignment
description: Use when multiple NetCDF-derived GCxGC 2D-TIC chromatograms show retention-time shifts that must be aligned to a reference chromatogram before downstream multivariate (MPCA) analysis or sample-group comparison.

name: two-dimensional-histogram-pixel-classification
description: Use when a background-corrected two-channel (e.g., red/green CFP/YFP) confocal image or time series needs automatic, threshold-free classification of which pixels are colocalized, and when subsequent proportion-colocalized coefficients must be computed per region or time point.

name: two-dimensional-signal-preprocessing
description: Use when raw GC×GC-MS data (NetCDF folded into a 2D-TIC) shows noise or baseline drift and must be smoothed, baseline-corrected, or aligned (e.g. wsmooth with penalty=1, lambda=1e1) prior to MPCA.

name: two-group-correlation-comparison
description: Use when an expression matrix is split into two sample groups and the goal is to detect features whose Pearson correlation with a target feature changes significantly between the groups, as in MOG's differential correlation analysis.

name: two-group-parametric-t-testing
description: Use when a numerical measurement column must be compared across exactly two groups defined by a categorical column (e.g. Condition) in Instant Clue, and a parametric t-test is appropriate for the data distribution.

name: two-group-statistical-testing-metabolomics
description: Use when a metabolomics abundance matrix (metabolites x samples) with two group labels must be converted into a significant-metabolite query set for downstream pathway enrichment analysis.

name: two-group-t-statistic-pathway-testing
description: Use when you have PLAGE pathway activity levels per sample and need to identify pathways whose mean activity differs significantly between two pre-defined groups (e.g., smokers vs non-smokers, diabetic vs non-diabetic).

name: two-level-metabolic-network-reconstruction
description: Use when the goal is to reconstruct the metabolisms of one or two KEGG organisms from KGML pathway files and compare them at structural (graph) and functional (reaction-set) levels using MetNet's similarity indexes.

name: two-regime-threshold-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantify whether retention-time drift for monitored compounds in a pooled QC pool is dominated by batch-level offsets rather than by short-term (within-batch) scatter, e.g. to justify batch-wise RT recalibration.

name: two-sample-mr-causal-effect-estimation
description: Use when an agent must test whether altered metabolite levels causally affect a phenotype by combining mGWAS summary statistics for a metabolite with a GWAS dataset (e.g. OpenGWAS ID finn-b-E4_DM2) via two-sample MR.

name: two-sample-t-test-biomarker-testing
description: Use when you have a sample x metabolite relative concentration matrix produced by NMR quantification (NMRQNet csv output) and need to determine which metabolites separate two sample groups, e.g. MDS patients vs. healthy family controls.

name: two-sample-t-test-rank-comparison
description: Use when two reproducibility methods (e.g., MaRR top-k sets vs. copula mixture model sets) yield different top-k transcript sets and you need to judge which method's method-specific genes are more biologically relevant against a quantitative gold-standard rank list.

name: two-sample-tstatistic-testing
description: Use when ranked metabolite sets (e.g. KEGG pathways from PiMP_KEGG) need p-values based on activity-level changes between case and control groups, from a log2-transformed, standardised metabolomics intensity matrix with known experimental groups.

name: two-step-attachment-retrieval-workflow
description: Reference for retrieving PubChem resources that are not directly addressable by CID alone — biologic depiction images (SVG) and annotation attachments (e.g. Mass Spectrometry) — via the two-step PUG-View /data/ → /image/ or /data/key/ pattern.

name: type-i-error-control-assessment
description: Use when evaluating whether a pathway enrichment method (e.g. NetGSA REHE or REML) maintains type-I error control under null conditions while retaining power on dysregulated gene groups in simulated replicate studies.

name: type-i-error-rate-estimation
description: Use when validating that a proposed association test (e.g. PaIRKAT on simulated metabolite pathway graphs) holds its nominal type I error rate before assessing power.

name: typographical-error-fixing-in-metadata
description: Use when a freetext sample metadata table (e.g. csv) contains non-numeric strings like 'allergen exposure' or 'ozone' that must be mapped onto fixed vocabularies such as zeroTimeEvent, drugName, or drugDoseUnit.

name: typographical-error-tolerance-matching
description: Use when sample metadata contains freetext terms (e.g. 'allergen exposure', 'ozone', 'hours/day') that must be resolved to standardized vocabulary entries despite synonyms or typographical errors, or when newly confirmed terms must be added and models retrained.

name: u13c-labeled-internal-standard-ccs-qc
description: Use when LC-IM-MS lipidomics samples are spiked with U13C-labeled standards and you need to monitor or correct CCSN2 bias without additional external calibrant measurements, e.g. TIM-MS data with 0.78%/0.33% mode-dependent bias.

name: ubiquitous-compound-filtering
description: Use when building pathway adjacency from KEGG KGML compound sets: compounds shared by many pathways (water, ATP, phosphate) would otherwise connect nearly every node and must be excluded before edge creation.

name: ukbiobank-field-mapping
description: Use when the input is an exported UK Biobank phenotype field CSV/TSV (Table Exporter or ukbconv format) containing NMR metabolomics fields that must be mapped to short biomarker names, biomarker measurement QC flags, and sample processing flags before analysis.

name: ukbiobank-nmr-data-processing
description: Use when processing raw UK Biobank NMR metabolomics field exports (fields #23651-23948) to remove plate-, spectrometer-, and time-driven technical variation, or to detect non-biological outlier 96-well shipment plates before genetic/epidemiological analyses.

name: ukbiobank-nmr-qc-flag-aggregation
description: Use when post-QC NMR biomarker tables have had the 61 composites and 81 ratios re-derived from the 107 non-derived biomarkers and derived measurements need QC flags propagated from their component biomarkers.

name: ultrahigh-resolution-ms-noise-threshold-application
description: Use when a raw two-column ion mass / intensity peak list from ultrahigh-resolution MS needs a defensible noise cutoff prior to formula assignment, and the analyst must choose and validate an S/N threshold.

name: umap-chemical-space-overlap-visualization
description: Use when you have SMILES sampled from a chemical language model checkpoint and need to verify metabolite-likeness: generated structures should be indistinguishable from withheld test-fold metabolites in fingerprint space.

name: umap-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when you have SMILES structure annotations from two or more MGF-format MS/MS spectral libraries and want to visualize and compare their chemical-space coverage and overlap via dimensionality reduction.

name: umap-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when you have a spatial metabolomics feature matrix (CSV with X/Y pixel coordinates plus m/z intensity columns) and need pixel-level clustering to identify tissue regions, e.g. k=25 clusters over a mouse brain coronal section.

name: umap-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when learned ion-image embeddings (e.g., 512-d vectors from a contrastive encoder) must be compressed to a low-dimensional dense vector before ranking top colocalized ions by distance in an MSI analysis.

name: umap-dimensionality-reduction-of-msi-pixel-spectra
description: Use when raw imzML MALDI MSI pixel spectra need unsupervised grouping by spectral similarity — e.g. for tissue segmentation, matrix/off-tissue pixel detection, or resolving molecular heterogeneity of a cell population — and no cluster number is known a priori.

name: umap-dimensionality-reduction-visualization
description: Use when a trained VAE has produced a low-dimensional latent variable (e.g. 5-dim Code layer output) for tens of thousands of MALDI FT-ICR MSI spectra and you need a 2D embedding to visually assess normal/tumor class separation.

name: umap-embedding-of-metabolic-profiles
description: Use when you have a per-cell normalized metabolic profile matrix (e.g. SpaceM's MORPHnMOL.csv with ~30k cells) and need a 2D visualization of resolved metabolic states after graph-based clustering.

name: umap-embedding-of-ms2-fingerprint-matrices
description: Use when you have an aligned MEMO matrix of MS2 fingerprints (e.g. 1,600 plant extracts) and need a 2D ordination to check whether biologically active samples co-cluster or appear as singletons.

name: umap-embedding-visualization
description: Use when a trained FIORA checkpoint and a test compound set are available and you need to verify that graph embeddings encode chemical class structure (Fig. 4) by UMAP clustering plus per-superclass cosine similarity medians.

name: umap-joint-embedding-of-multi-sample-pixels
description: Use when pre-processing a multi-sample MALDI MSI dataset and you need to identify sample outliers automatically by comparing pixel-level spectral similarity across all samples in one embedding.

name: ump-peak-localization-in-tissue
description: Use when a specific m/z peak identified from MSI analysis (e.g. a tumor-correlated peak from msiPL) must be spatially localized — reconstructing its ion image at 100 µm pixels and checking elevation within a histology-annotated region.

name: unannotated-spectral-dataset-similarity-analysis
description: Use when you have peak-listed tandem mass spectra (e.g. MGF files) from two or more samples and need a quantitative distance matrix of peptide sharing without peptide identifications or a sequence database.

name: unbalanced-group-subsampling-protocol
description: Use when performing stability selection for differential GGM network estimation (DNEA/Filigree-style) on two-condition metabolomics data where group sizes are unbalanced and per-edge selection probabilities must weight the lambda penalty in final network estimation.

name: uncertainty-based-spectrum-filtering
description: Use when MS2DeepScore-predicted Tanimoto similarities contain unreliable spectra (low information content, chimeric spectra, or spectra dissimilar to training data) and you need to filter them using per-spectrum embedding-quality estimates.

name: uncertainty-estimation-of-fitted-spectral-parameters
description: Use when a series of 1D or pseudo-2D NMR spectra (any nucleus, e.g. 1H, 13C, 31P) needs per-signal fitted parameters with reported standard-deviation uncertainties, such as monitoring metabolite signals over a real-time assay.

name: uncovered-peak-missing-fraction-computation
description: Use when computing Spec2Vec similarity scores for spectra against a pretrained Word2Vec model and you must decide whether the score is trustworthy because query peaks/losses fall outside the model vocabulary.

name: undirected-graph-connected-component-decomposition
description: Use when a preprocessed LC-MS peak table contains multiple correlated features per metabolite (e.g. adducts/isotopes) that must be collapsed into one representative per compound before statistics or identification.

name: unidentified-feature-qc-criteria
description: Use when a LipiDex 2 Peak Finder peak table contains unidentified features (possible lipid adducts, isotopes, dimers, or co-eluting spurious peaks) that need to be distinguished from genuine novel lipids sharing a retention time with an identified feature.

name: unifrac-phylogenetic-distance-computation
description: Use when two taxonomic profilers report identical single-value metrics (e.g., UniFrac) against a gold standard and you need to verify the tie and identify which clades actually differ in relative abundance.

name: uniprot-to-gene-symbol-mapping
description: Use when a metabolite-to-protein step yields UniProt IDs (e.g., scraped from HMDB metabolite pages) and downstream over-representation analysis requires current human gene symbols instead.

name: unit-dalton-spectrum-normalization
description: Use when a model produces a probability distribution over molecular fragments with exact atomic-composition masses and you need to convert it into a final mass spectrum at 1 Da (or 0.1 Da) resolution.

name: univariate-differential-feature-testing
description: Use when comparing raw vs. signal-drift-corrected feature matrices from LC-MS metabolomics or proteomics (e.g., XCMS or Skyline outputs) to count significant features via Welch's T-test with BH FDR and assess how correction improves statistical accuracy.

name: univariate-metabolite-threshold-selection
description: Use when a preprocessed metabolomics peak-intensity/concentration matrix with a sample group table (SampleID, group) must be reduced to a subset of significantly changed metabolites via univariate thresholds (P, FDR, log2FC).

name: univariate-statistical-feature-selection
description: Use when you have a QC-passed LC/MS feature table (m/z, retention time, intensities) with infected vs. control/baseline sample groups and need to select significantly altered features before pathway analysis.

name: univariate-ttest-mz-screening
description: Use when you have a normalized m/z peak table from MS metabolomics data with a two-group (or paired) design variable and need to rank m/z values by differential intensity.

name: universal-spectrum-identifier-construction
description: Use when a specific tandem MS spectrum (e.g., a GNPS library entry CCMSLIB accessions, a MassIVE/MetaboLights MSV dataset scan, a MassBank accession, or an MS2LDA motif) must be addressed by URL for retrieval or visualization.

name: universal-spectrum-identifier-spectrum-retrieval
description: Use when a workflow needs to fetch a specific public MS/MS spectrum — e.g. a ProteomeXchange dataset scan like mzspec:PXD004732:...:scan:41840 or a GNPS library entry like mzspec:GNPSLIBRARY:CCMSLIB00000840351 — without downloading the source raw files.

name: unknown-chemical-identification-free-construction
description: Use when you have a real/observed mzML file (e.g. output of a prior Top-N run) and want ViMMS 2.0 chemical input derived from empirically detected peaks rather than synthetically sampled compounds from HMDB.

name: unknown-metabolite-annotation-linking
description: Use when a metabolomics feature table contains unannotated peaks (unknowns) lacking KEGG/PubChem identifiers, and the goal is to connect them to annotated compounds using mass spectral similarity rather than enzymatic or structural relationships.

name: unknown-metabolite-cascade-validation
description: Use when LC-MS/MS peak tables and MS2 spectra from an S9 incubation (or similar in vitro enzymatic reaction) need KGMN unknown-peak annotations reproduced and validated, e.g. expected 39+69/700 pos and 41+106/741 neg peaks.

name: unknown-metabolite-recurrence-analysis
description: Use when a list of putatively annotated unknown metabolites with precursor m/z and MS/MS spectra (e.g., from KGMN on NIST urine data) needs external corroboration via public-data recurrence rather than spectral-library or standard-based validation.

name: unknown-peak-annotation-consolidation
description: Use when a metabolic feature peak (e.g. M153T555, M182T541) is claimed by multiple overlapping KGMN subnetworks with conflicting annotations or base peaks, and annotations must be merged or pruned into one consolidated subnetwork.

name: unlabeled-feature-linking-across-replicates
description: Use when you have feature maps detected separately in multiple LC-MS runs (e.g., technical replicates or a dilution/spike-in series) and need a consensus feature map to extract per-run intensities for label-free quantification and reproducibility analysis.

name: unlabeled-sample-based-correction
description: Use when correcting LC-MS isotope-labeling FAM data from a high-resolution analyzer (e.g., Orbitrap at 140,000/280,000 nominal resolution) and an unlabeled-sample spectrum is available, especially for high-mass metabolites where resolution effects are strong.

name: unlabeled-sample-correction-matrix-estimation
description: Use when correcting LC-MS isotope labeling data on high-resolving-power instruments (e.g. Orbitrap) where an unlabeled sample standard for each compound is available and the correction matrix must reflect the instrument's nominal resolution.

name: unresolved-identifier-flagging
description: Use when a source metabolomics dataset reports metabolite names (e.g. study ST001039 from Metabolomics Workbench) and some PubChem Identifier Exchange lookups return no InChIKey match that must be tracked.

name: unsupervised-cell-population-clustering-visualization
description: Use when you have a metabolite (or other feature) concentration table with biological replicates per population and need to verify, without supervision, that the populations are biochemically distinct before downstream pathway/network analyses.

name: unsupervised-clustering-of-multidimensional-data
description: Use when an unlabeled feature table (rows = samples, columns = numerical measurements) needs pattern discovery, e.g. grouping samples by multiple morphological or omics features without ground-truth labels.

name: unsupervised-conformer-clustering
description: Use when a RDKit conformer ensemble (e.g. ~990-996 conformers per protonation state) has been geometry-relaxed with ASE-ANI and must be condensed to structurally distinct representatives before QM-level optimization and CCS calculation.

name: unsupervised-dimensionality-reduction-of-spectral-images
description: Use when a batch of raw MS runs (LC-MS, LC-IMS-MS, or direct infusion, DDA/DIA) needs rapid, identification-free quality assessment and you want outliers to emerge from an unsupervised projection rather than per-run metrics.

name: unsupervised-metabolome-wide-visualization
description: Use when starting differential metabolomic analysis on a metabolite measurement table and you need an unsupervised check for metabolome-wide group separation before supervised testing.

name: unsupervised-multivariate-exploratory-analysis
description: Use when a metabolomics matrix (.csv, samples in rows, batch levels in column 1) needs an unsupervised PCA/scree check of whether samples cluster by analytical batch before selecting a correction model.

name: unsupervised-multivariate-statistics
description: Use when you have a file-by-chemical annotation matrix built from GNPS MS2 spectral library matches and want an unsupervised, label-free view of how public tandem MS files group by their annotated chemistry.

name: unsupervised-pca-sample-analysis
description: Use when a preprocessed lipidomics data matrix (from LipidSearch or LIQUID output, or Metabolomics Workbench data loaded via do_query()) is available in ADViSELipidomics and the goal is an unsupervised, label-free overview of sample structure and dominant axes of variation.

name: unsupervised-spectral-word2vec-embedding-training
description: Use when building a spectral library search or analogue search pipeline that needs unsupervised spectral embeddings over full library spectra (including unannotated ones), as in MS2Query's Spec2Vec stage on GNPS.

name: untargeted-comparative-metabolomics-preprocessing
description: Use when raw centroided LC-HRMS/MS files (mzML/mzXML) from a comparative metabolomics study (e.g. mutant vs. wildtype) need feature detection, alignment, blank removal, and peak-quality filtering into an analysis-ready feature table.

name: untargeted-lcms-feature-labeling
description: Use when an untargeted LC-MS feature table (XCMS output) contains poorly integrated peaks that manual quality assessment would otherwise need to catch, and you want automated Pass/Fail flagging before downstream statistics.

name: untargeted-lcms-feature-table-processing
description: Use when an untargeted LC–MS dataset has already been peak-picked, retention-time corrected, and grouped in XCMS, and you need chromatographic quality features (sharpness, jaggedness, symmetry, modality, etc.) per EIC as classifier input.

name: untargeted-mass-increment-window-search
description: Use when the input is an LC-MS peak table (feature list with m/z, rt, intensities) and candidate homologue mass increments are unknown, so a bounded scan of mass differences (e.g. mz_min = 10 to mz_max = 20) must reveal series automatically.

name: untargeted-metabolomics-annotation-validation
description: Use when you have IDSL.IPA-generated individual and aligned peak tables (mzXML/mzML/netCDF inputs) and need to validate molecular formula assignments against MS/MS-confirmed identities or report median-rank statistics.

name: untargeted-metabolomics-data-processing
description: Use when raw full-scan LC/HRMS data from population-scale untargeted metabolomics or exposomics studies (e.g. mzXML/mzML files from Orbitrap instruments) must be converted into a peak table without MS2 adduct/fragment handling.

name: untargeted-metabolomics-dataset-processing
description: Use when a batch of untargeted metabolomics datasets (e.g. 20 Orbitrap feature tables + MS2 spectra) must be annotated under competing knowledge-network topologies and compared using decoy-based accuracy, FDR, and same-superclass specificity metrics.

name: untargeted-metabolomics-drug-screening
description: Use when untargeted metabolomics MS/MS runs (mzML or converted vendor files) must be screened for drug exposures, especially when only metabolized versions of a drug may be present rather than the parent compound.
tools: GNPS (Global Natural Product Social Molecular Networking)

name: untargeted-metabolomics-feature-extraction
description: Use when raw LC/MS mzXML files from untargeted metabolomics need peak picking, quantification and alignment into a feature table prior to statistical feature selection and pathway/network analysis.

name: untargeted-metabolomics-feature-scoring
description: Use when a set of untargeted metabolomics extracts (GNPS FBMN job + MZmine 2/3 quant table) must be prioritized for structural novelty, with per-extract FC, FS, LC, CC, and SC scores and a final rank.

name: untargeted-metabolomics-feature-table-processing
description: Use when an untargeted metabolomics MS1 feature table (.csv with name/mz/rt columns) must be linked onto a curated metabolic reaction network before annotation propagation.

name: untargeted-metabolomics-ordination-analysis
description: Use when you have per-tissue untargeted metabolomics peak-area feature tables with sample metadata (study, cohort, genotype) and need to verify whether samples cluster across conditions before running differential or ML analyses.

name: untargeted-metabolomics-parameter-configuration
description: Use when preparing an IDSL.CSA or IDSL.IPA batch run on mzXML/mzML/netCDF LC/HRMS data — a parameter spreadsheet must be filled with workflow selectors (PARAM0001), directory addresses (CSA0005/0008/0009/0011), and thread counts (CSA0004).

name: untargeted-metabolomics-peak-classifier-inference
description: Use when you have an XCMS-processed untargeted LC–MS feature table with peak-quality metrics and want to automatically flag low-quality peak integrations without manual curation.

name: untargeted-metabolomics-peak-table-generation
description: Use when raw LC-MS untargeted metabolomics chromatograms (.CDF files) plus a sample metadata table are available and the goal is to produce a features x samples peak-area/intensity table with retention-time alignment before imputation or correction steps.

name: untargeted-metabolomics-preprocessing
description: Use when starting from centroided (or raw Thermo/Agilent/Bruker) LC-MS/MS mzML files in an untargeted metabolomics study and you need a per-sample feature table with m/z, RT, adduct, and intensities for downstream FBMN/IIMN or statistics.

name: untargeted-metabolomics-processing-parameterization
description: Use when raw CE-MS or LC-MS/HILIC-MS metabolomics acquisitions must be processed non-targetedly with AriumMS and per-method processing parameters (ROI thresholds, m/z error, alignment, occurrence filters) must be selected or DOE-optimized.

name: untargeted-metabolomics-raw-data-processing
description: Use when raw untargeted metabolomics files (mzML, mzXML, or CDF from qTOF, orbitrap, or FT-ICR instruments) must be processed into a feature table and no universal parameter set applies, so centWave peak-picking parameters must be estimated from the data itself.

name: untargeted-mz-window-series-search
description: Use when an LC-MS peak table (mz, rt, intensity columns) must be searched for homologue series with an unknown m/z increment: no candidate step (e.g. 44.02628) is available, so a Da-range sweep (mz_min-mz_max) is required.

name: untargeted-screening-identification-tallying
description: Use when a completed MS-DIAL/MS-FINDER screening yields a list of identified features whose library annotations and unknown IDs must be counted, cross-checked against a reported total (e.g. 83 compounds), and exported as a per-identification-status table.

name: up-down-regulated-ion-counting-across-clusters
description: Use when a k-means (or ROI) segmented MSI peak matrix must be compared one cluster versus the rest to report how many absolutely up- or down-regulated ions each region contains and which m/z values characterize them.

name: up-down-regulated-ion-statistical-testing
description: Use when an MSI peak matrix has been segmented into clusters/ROIs and you need the statistically significant up- or down-regulated ions between two specific regions, with undetected (null) peaks handled explicitly.

name: upgma-hierarchical-clustering
description: Use when you have predicted molecular fingerprints (e.g., CSI:FingerID probability vectors over 2936 molecular properties) for LC-MS/MS chemical features and need a chemical tree for downstream tree-informed metrics like Weighted UniFrac or Faith's PD.

name: upgma-hierarchical-clustering-from-distance-matrix
description: Use when you already have a pairwise distance matrix over datasets/samples and need a rooted tree in Newick format, as compareMS2 2.0 does with its LC-MS/MS dataset distances.

name: upgma-phylogenetic-tree-reconstruction
description: Use when you have pairwise spectral distances between tandem mass spectrometry datasets (e.g. from compareMS2 on MGF files) and need to reconstruct the phylogenetic relatedness of species, proteomes, or samples from those distances.

name: upset-plot-library-coverage-visualization
description: Use when comparing compound/structure coverage across multiple spectral libraries via InChIKeys and you need intersection/union counts plus an UpSet-style visualization of set overlaps.

name: uptake-reaction-perturbation-simulation
description: Use when gap-filled community GEMs exist and you must determine which exchanged metabolites each member depends on, by blocking one uptake reaction at a time and recording biomass-flux reduction.

name: uptake-vs-synthesis-histogram-visualization
description: Use when single-cell isotopologue data (e.g. Scanpy anndata objects from 13C-SpaceM) have been fitted with a binomial uptake model and you need per-cell relative uptake fraction histograms per fatty acid, with modes marked and compared across conditions.

name: urinary-metabolite-consistency-evaluation
description: Use when a urinary (or other) metabolomics dataset compiled from a systematic review contains compounds with more than one report plus statistical significance, and you need to check whether all reports agree on up- vs down-regulation (e.g. the Mallafré et al.

name: urine-cohort-exposome-annotation
description: Use when a curated metabolite database with accurate m/z and retention time must be screened against a large LC-HRMS urine/cohort feature table to quantify which xenobiotic metabolites are present and at what detection frequencies.

name: urine-metabolomics-data-preprocessing
description: Use when you have a standalone (unpaired) urine metabolomics dataset — e.g. a list of 56 named metabolites — that must be normalized and converted to HMDB identifiers before pathway over-representation against GWAS-derived gene sets.

name: urine-metabolomics-qc-sample-exclusion
description: Use when preprocessing urine metabolomics intensity tables (e.g. Mtblmcs values/variables from the ACTION Biomarker Study) and samples must be filtered on collection-protocol, dipstick, and health criteria prior to creatinine normalization.

name: user-confirmed-new-term-annotation
description: Use when after running SMetaS's tf-idf/nearest-neighbors curation pass and the substring-search pass over the fixed vocabularies, non-numeric freetext strings (e.g. 'allergen exposure', 'ozone', 'hours/day') remain unmapped and must be added to specific vocabularies via user confirmation.

name: user-defined-score-integration-metfrag
description: Use when ranking MetFrag candidates for an LC-MS unknown with a measured retention time on a reverse-phase column and a set of reference standards whose RTs and structures (for log P) are available.

name: user-defined-spectrum-filtering
description: Use when converting .MSP/.MGF/.JSON/.CSV spectral libraries (e.g., GNPS, MoNA, MassBank, MS-Dial, or MZmine in-house exports) into a cleaned, standardized FragHub output and you need to drop spectra with too few peaks, excessive entropy-reduction, or peaks above the precursor m/z.

name: user-rating-quality-assessment
description: Use when evaluating spectral-library reliability from user match-rating records, e.g. comparing fraction of rated library spectra below 2.5 average stars across GNPS-Collection, GNPS-Community, NIST, and MassBank.

name: usi-construction-metabolomics
description: Use when a spectrum must be addressed across public repositories (GNPS library/task, MassBank accession, MassIVE/MetaboLights/Workbench MSV identifiers) or compared between resources via a database-independent identifier.

name: usi-endpoint-spectrum-export
description: Use when a spectrum is addressable by a USI (GNPS, MassBank, MassIVE, MetaboLights, Metabolomics Workbench, MS2LDA, ProteomeXchange) and a customized figure or exportable peak list (SVG/PNG/CSV/JSON) is needed for publication.

name: usi-identifier-construction
description: Use when you need a machine-readable, cross-repository identifier for an MS/MS spectrum held in a metabolomics or proteomics repository (e.g. MassIVE MSV accession, MassBank accession) to fetch or render that spectrum.

name: usi-spectra-retrieval-from-public-repositories
description: Use when you have USIs (e.g. `mzspec:GNPS2:TASK-<id>-nf_output/clustering/specs_ms.mgf:scan:<n>`) and need to fetch the corresponding MS/MS spectra to feed a molecular-networking or spectral-alignment pipeline.

name: usi-spectrum-identifier-handling
description: Use when aggregating MASST matches per synthesized compound — e.g., N-acyl amides searched in MSV000089491 or acyl esters in MSV000089493 — where match records must be keyed by USI and MASST job identifier.

name: usi-spectrum-searching
description: Use when you have one or a few MS/MS spectra (a single .mgf from MZmine or a USI list in .csv/.tsv) and want to identify which publicly deposited microbial monoculture datasets or GNPS library entries match those spectra.

name: usi-string-parsing
description: Use when a task requires parsing mzspec:<collection>:<msRun>:<indexType>:<indexNumber> strings from GNPS, MassBank, MS2LDA/MOTIFDB, MassIVE, MetaboLights, Metabolomics Workbench, or ProteomeXchange into fields and mapping each to its backing resource.

name: vae-latent-feature-extraction
description: Use when you have raw, high-dimensional MSI spectra (e.g. 85,062 m/z variables in HDF5) and need a low-dimensional latent embedding (5-D Code layer) for classification, UMAP visualization, or feature extraction.

name: vae-latent-representation-risk-scoring
description: Use when you have an mzLearn-generated MS1 ion-feature matrix for a patient cohort plus survival (OS time/event), IMDC risk class, or treatment-response labels and need VAE-latent-based prognostic/predictive stratification.

name: validated-link-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a microbial genome-metabolome linking score has been computed over candidate BGC/spectrum links and you need to quantify whether the score's upper tail is enriched for literature-validated links, as in Table 1 / Fig 6.

name: validated-link-rank-evaluation
description: Use when a GCF with established homology to a MIBiG BGC (e.g. BGC0001228, BGC0000241) must be scored against all molecular families, and the validated link's rank under each scoring function is needed to judge which score prioritises true links .

name: validated-link-rank-tracking
description: Use when reproducing or auditing NPClassScore-based prioritisation on PoDP paired omics datasets where known validated BGC–metabolite links (e.g. from MIBiG/PoDP records) must be checked for retention and rank improvement after filtering.

name: validated-subcluster-overlap-assessment
description: Use when predicted biosynthetic sub-clusters or sub-cluster motifs must be validated/annotated against experimentally characterised sub-clusters (SubClusterBlast, MIBiG) and quantified genome-wide.

name: validation-accuracy-model-selection
description: Reference for choosing hyperparameters (learning rate, number of convolutional layers, epochs) and the final checkpoint for a CNN trained on augmented NMR mixture spectra, based on validation accuracy.

name: validation-loss-model-selection
description: Use when retraining the GLEAMS Siamese network from gleams/config.py and you must decide whether precursor, fragment, and reference-spectrum feature blocks each contribute — or when comparing trained-model variants by validation loss.

name: validation-set-stratification-by-structural-similarity
description: Use when evaluating a trained RT prediction model on a held-out validation set and you need to determine whether prediction error is smaller for molecules that have a structurally similar molecule (e.g. ≥90% Tanimoto on ECFP fingerprints) in the training set.

name: variable-mode-molecular-variant-search-configuration
description: Use when tandem mass spectra (MGF, mzXML, or mzML) must be searched against a chemical database like COCONUT or NPAtlas in a mode that can explain precursor mass differences via known variant mass shifts, not just exact matches.

name: variance-component-estimation-reml
description: Use when running NetGSA pathway enrichment where exact REML variance component estimation on the entire weighted, directed pathway network is required, or when benchmarking REHE/clustered-REHE runtime and power against the REML gold standard.

name: variance-decomposition-across-omics-views
description: Use when two preprocessed omics matrices from the same samples (e.g. DNA methylation beta values and urine metabolite intensities) need shared latent factors and a per-view variance-explained breakdown.

name: variance-explained-comparison
description: Use when you have a metabolomics matrix (e.g. the 158-lipid, 59-CRC-patient adipose dataset) processed both before and after linear mixed-effects model fitting and need to demonstrate improved group separation via PC1 explained variance.

name: variance-explained-verification
description: Use when you have original (pre-correction) UK Biobank NMR biomarker data plus sample QC fields and need to quantify which technical covariates drive biomarker variance, e.g. to justify or verify QC correction.

name: variance-scaling-parameter-selection
description: Use when a preprocessed metabolomics data table (already normalized and log/sqrt/cube-root transformed) still spans a large dynamic range across metabolites and must be variance-scaled before statistical analysis or PCA-guided data treatment review.

name: variance-stabilization-assessment
description: Use when a metabolite abundance table exhibits high between-sample variance or non-normally distributed metabolite abundances that would distort downstream association or classification statistics.

name: variance-stabilizing-log-transform
description: Use when a metabolite concentration table (post-imputation and post-normalization, from a .csv or .xlsx upload) is right-skewed or spans a wide dynamic range and needs an element-wise log/power transform before scaling and PCA-based treatment selection.

name: variant-coding-impact-annotation
description: Use when you need to annotate coding variants with multiple tools (ANNOVAR, SnpEff, VEP), normalize their impact terms to SO, and quantify agreement against ClinVar-annotated coding impact.

name: variant-left-alignment-normalization
description: Use when building a variant benchmark from a ClinVar VCF for cross-tool (ANNOVAR/SnpEff/VEP) annotation comparison, where caller-dependent left/right shifts of nucleotide-repeat indels would produce inconsistent HGVS notation.

name: variational-autoencoder-fine-tuning-metabolomics
description: Use when a small labeled metabolomics cohort (e.g., binary classification, multi-class, or survival task) must be predicted and a pre-trained metabolomics VAE checkpoint exists to transfer from, outperforming randomly initialized or traditional ML baselines.

name: variational-autoencoder-training
description: Use when you need to learn a compressed latent representation of high-dimensional, TIC-normalized MSI spectra stored in HDF5 (tens of thousands of m/z variables) as the probabilistic feature layer of a pixel-based tissue classification model.

name: variational-autoencoder-training-for-spatial-data
description: Use when paired ST-SM samples (e.g., human ccRCC, GBM, or mouse brain) need cross-modal, cross-sample integration into a joint low-dimensional embedding for downstream clustering, deconvolution-based annotation, or benchmarking against integration tools.

name: variational-autoencoder-training-on-metabolomics-feature-matrix
description: Use when you have a standardized LC/MS1 feature table of blood-sample metabolite intensities (e.g. [n_samples, 2736] floats) and want unsupervised latent embeddings that organize samples by disease or age without supervision.

name: variational-bayes-inference-training
description: Use when you have preprocessed bag-of-fragments MS/MS spectra (e.g. a GNPS MGF set of 5,670 spectra or a ~1,000-peak beer extract) and need unsupervised decomposition into Mass2Motifs rather than supervised spectral matching.

name: variational-lower-bound-optimization
description: Use when high-dimensional, TIC-normalized mass spectrometry imaging spectra (e.g. 85,062 m/z variables from MALDI FT-ICR MSI) must be compressed into a low-dimensional latent space and reconstructed to a target MSE, without prior peak picking or preprocessing.

name: vcf-variant-filtering
description: Use when preparing a ClinVar or other VCF as a benchmark for comparing variant annotation tools and you must define a reproducible, high-review-status variant set with known clinical-significance composition.

name: vcf-variant-type-classification
description: Use when you have per-tool HGVSc/HGVSp/coding-impact annotations for a normalized ClinVar-style VCF and need concordance rates broken down by variant type rather than pooled across all 164,549 two-star variants.

name: vector-raster-figure-rendering
description: Use when a USI-referenced tandem MS spectrum needs to be turned into a publication-ready figure with controlled m/z range, dimensions, peak annotations, or a mirror-plot comparison against a second spectrum.

name: vendor-api-wrapping-in-r

name: vendor-fidelity-visualization-comparison

name: vendor-file-compatibility-handling
