name: vendor-format-chromatogram-extraction
description: Use when raw AEMS data are in a vendor .wiff file and a total ion chromatogram (intensity vs. time) must be extracted from the vendor binary before ejection-time fitting or MRM/full-scan peak processing.

name: vendor-format-raw-data-import-agilent-masshunter-batches
description: Use when the input is a raw LA-ICP-MS vendor export — e.g. an Agilent MassHunter G7200B+ .b batch directory, Perkin Elmer Elan .xl directory, or Thermo Qtegra/iCap CSV/LDR export — and it must be converted into image arrays without manual preprocessing.

name: vendor-format-raw-data-import-perkinelmer-elan-xl
description: Use when incoming LA-ICP-MS acquisition data is a raw vendor export, specifically a Perkin Elmer ELAN '.xl' directory (also Agilent .b batches or Thermo CSV/LDR), and the goal is to load it as an image without manual file conversion.

name: vendor-format-raw-data-import-thermo-qtegra-csv
description: Use when the input is an unconverted vendor acquisition export (Agilent .b batch, Perkin Elmer ELAN .xl directory, Thermo iCap/Qtegra CSV or LDR file, Nu Vitesse image, generic 2D delimited text image, or one-file-per-line CSV set) that must become a LA-ICP-MS image without manual reshaping.

name: vendor-raw-file-conversion
description: Use when starting from vendor-proprietary MS raw files (.raw, .d, or .wiff) that must be converted to mzXML before DIA-NN analysis or QC metric extraction in an iDIA-QC-style pipeline.

name: vendor-raw-file-format-conversion
description: Use when vendor-proprietary LC-MS raw files (e.g., the MTBLS733 raw deposit from Li et al.) must be converted to .mzML or .abf before ingestion into Nextflow4MS-DIAL's data/raw_data/ directory.

name: vendor-raw-file-ingestion-wiff
description: Use when the input data are proprietary vendor raw files (e.g. Sciex .WIFF) that must be processed by MS-DIAL 5 from the command line for headless runs, benchmarking, or cross-platform reproducibility.

name: vendor-software-vs-ccsfind-cross-validation
description: Use when you have drift tube IM-MS DTCCS N2 values from two acquisition/processing routes (targeted CCSfind vs vendor non-targeted software) and need to quantify agreement as percentage bias per compound and per stratum.

name: vendor-to-mzml-format-conversion
description: Use when starting from proprietary vendor raw files of MRM/DDA/DIA datasets that must be converted to an open format (mzML, Aird) before analysis or when benchmarking storage volume across vendor, mzML, and Aird representations.

name: vep-impact-consequence-annotation
description: Use when prioritizing candidate causal genes at molecular QTLs and you need variant-level functional consequence evidence (VEP IMPACT) to mark genes hit by sentinels or LD proxies.

name: vep-transcript-streamlining-parameterization
description: Use when annotating ClinVar or other pathogenic-variant VCFs with VEP and per-transcript HGVS output (HGVSc/HGVSp) diverges from a reference annotation (e.g. ClinVar strings), or when reducing transcript-multiplicity noise before cross-validating VEP output against ANNOVAR/SnpEff.

name: vep-variant-impact-annotation
description: Use when sentinel/proxy variants for molecular QTLs need functional consequence annotation (VEP IMPACT HIGH/MODERATE/LOW/MODIFIER) as input to bottom-up causal gene prioritization.

name: vertical-integration-method-comparison
description: Use when comparing integration methods (e.g., SpatialMETA vs. totalVI, spaMultiVAE, MISO, Seurat v5, Stabmap, SpatialGLUE) on paired ST-SM samples using the four metric families and an overall score.

name: vertical-network-chain-linkage

name: vgg-inspired-multi-branch-network-architecture

name: vimms-framework-configuration

name: vimms-virtual-mass-spectrometer-simulation
description: Use when you need to prototype, optimize, or compare DDA acquisition-controller parameter settings in silico (e.g. SmartROI alpha/beta, WeightedDEW t0/t1) from full-scan mzML files, avoiding costly trial-and-error LC-MS/MS injections on real hardware.

name: vinsmoc-variable-mode-spectral-search
description: Use when query spectra (MGF, mzXML, or mzML) may come from molecule variants — precursor m/z differs from any database molecule by an explainable modification delta — and you need variant identification plus modification-site localization.

name: violin-plot-grouped-attribute-visualization

name: violin-plot-peak-quality-assessment

name: violoin-plot-error-distribution-visualization
description: Use when Retip RT predictions (predicted minus experimental retention time) are available for HILIC or RPLC test/validation compounds and you need to visualize per-model error distributions and quantify true-positive coverage within ±1 min windows, as in Figure 2 of the Retip paper.

name: vip-feature-filtering-for-pls-models
description: Use when a PLS/PLS-DA classifier on metabolomics or integrated gene-expression + metabolomics data is overfit or underperforming, and a compact, statistically filtered feature set is needed to raise cross-validated Q2Y.

name: vip-feature-selection
description: Use when a supervised PLS-DA genotype/colonization classifier (e.g. 3xTg_SPF vs WT_SPF or 5xFAD vs WT per tissue) has been fit on metabolomics feature tables and discriminatory molecular features must be extracted via VIP scores.

name: vip-score-feature-selection
description: Use when a fitted PLS-DA or OPLS-DA model on metabolomics data (e.g. 158 annotated lipids from VAT/SAT of 59 CRC patients) must be reduced to significant/discriminative features for downstream comparison of feature sets.

name: viral-biomass-objective-optimization

name: virtual-mass-spectrometer-integration-testing

name: voigt-fit-integral-normalization-by-nucleus-count

name: voigt-peak-shape-modeling
description: Use when 2D or pseudo-3D NMR cross-peaks overlap and concentrations, or cross-peak specific relaxation parameters (T1/T2, titration, DOSY), must be extracted from deconvoluted components rather than raw peak heights.

name: volcano-plot-data-preparation
description: Use when you have a feature-by-sample intensity matrix (mass_dataset) with a binary group comparison (e.g., tumor vs normal) and need a volcano-plot source table with fold change, p-value, and multiple-testing-adjusted p-value per feature.

name: volcano-plot-generation

name: volcano-plot-interpretation-metabolomics
description: Use when a two-group metabolomics comparison (e.g. tumor vs normal) has been tested per metabolite and you need to display and interpret effect size (dm) versus significance (pval or adj_pval) in a volcano plot.

name: volcano-plot-significant-ion-annotation
description: Use when a trained/adapted MetaPhenotype model classifies SCMS m/z peaks into cell phenotypes and you need to flag which ions are essential discriminators for volcano-plot annotation.

name: volcano-plot-threshold-classification
description: Use when a differential-expression matrix with geneID, log2 fold change, p/padj significance, and optional label columns needs to be visualized as a volcano plot with threshold-based up/down classification for publication.

name: volcano-plot-visualization

name: volcano-plot-visualization
description: Use when a DESeq2/Limma results table (gene, log2FC, p-value, p.adj) is available and a visual summary of magnitude-versus-significance of differential expression is needed.

name: volcano-plot-visualization
description: Use when you have run (or plan to run) run_de() on a metabolites x samples abundance matrix with two group labels and want to visualize which metabolites enter the Fisher's Exact Test enrichment query set.

name: volcano-plot-visualization
description: Use when a peak-aligned, TIC-normalized single-cell (SCMS) metabolomics feature table must be compared between two biological groups (e.g., primary vs metastatic melanoma cells, ± vemurafenib) to flag significantly altered lipid species as biomarker candidates.

name: volcano-plot-visualization
description: Use when a batch-corrected metabolomics feature table (samples in rows, features in columns) needs a differential-abundance visual summary: fit a per-feature linear model, BH-adjust p-values, and render a volcano plot with Log2FC > 1.5 and adj-p < 0.05 cutoffs.

name: volcano-plot-visualization-of-regulated-lipids

name: vote-counting-compound-trend-analysis

name: wall-clock-runtime-profiling

name: wall-clock-timing-comparison-analysis
description: Use when profiling the runtime of an R mass-spectrometry pipeline (e.g. Shinyscreen's mzML extraction and prescreening) to quantify how much parallelisation reduces processing time.

name: warpgroup-style-mean-boundary-peak-reintegration

name: waveform-dc-component-removal

name: wavelet-based-peak-detection

name: wavelet-based-peak-detection-mexican-hat

name: wavelet-based-signal-peak-picking
description: Use when starting from centroid-mode mzML raw LC–MS files (e.g., Waters RAW converted with ProteoWizard msconvert) and you need chromatographic/spectrum peak picking to build an (Rt, m/z) feature table.

name: wavelet-ica-intensity-normalization

name: wavelet-transform-peak-bounds-detection

name: web-api-record-count-aggregation

description: Use when adding or modifying an MSMetaEnhancer WebConverter that queries a throttled public API, and you must verify that asynchronous requests never exceed the service's per-second access limit.

name: web-server-and-cli-prediction-harnessing
description: Use when benchmarking multiple CCS prediction tools (e.g. CCSP 2.0, CCSbase, AllCCS, DeepCCS) on the same molecule set and adduct type to rank them by median MRE/RMSE or to decide which predictor to trust for annotation filtering.

name: web-server-restful-api-workflow-execution
description: Use when a massive untargeted metabolomics table contains multiple putative annotations per feature and needs classification (e.g. origin labels from Tagger) and deduplication via an automatable web workflow.

name: web-service-batch-smiles-submission
description: Use when a filtered set of natural-product SMILES strings (e.g., NP Atlas macrolide entries) must be scored or classified by batch submission to web services such as EMBL-EBI MAIP or the NPClassifier /classify?smiles=<> endpoint.

name: web-service-capability-comparison
description: Use when a task asks which kinds of repository data (e.g., computed properties, annotations, bulk synonyms, tabular data) are served by each of several programmatic interfaces, and which fall outside all of them.

name: web-tool-metabolite-list-submission
description: Use when you have a metabolite name/ID list from a metabolomics study and need group-level pathway enrichment results (top pathways + P values) to compare against published benchmark values.

name: webgl-3d-confidence-region-rendering
description: Use when you have per-replicate QIIME principal coordinates files from jackknifed beta diversity resampling plus a metadata mapping file, and need to render per-sample confidence regions in an interactive 3D PCoA plot.

name: webgl-3d-ordination-plotting
description: Use when you have a QIIME principal coordinates file plus a sample metadata mapping file and need an interactive 3D PCoA plot that scales to thousands of samples (e.g. 5,740 samples, 120 metadata columns) and supports metadata-driven recoloring and visibility toggles.

name: webgl-3d-plot-verification
description: Use when a QIIME principal coordinates file plus metadata mapping file must become an embedded, interactive WebGL 3D PCoA plot whose sample spheres can be verified to render in Chrome.

name: webgl-3d-sphere-rendering
description: Use when you have a QIIME principal coordinates file plus a metadata mapping file and need an interactive, plugin-free 3D browser visualization whose sphere size/transparency can be modified per metadata category.

name: webgl-3d-visualization-deployment
description: Use when a QIIME principal coordinates file (PCoA of beta diversity distances) and a metadata mapping file must become an interactive, plugin-free WebGL 3D scatter for thousands of samples, shareable as a standalone web page or embedded in email.

name: weight-volume-column-normalization
description: Use when a loaded metabolite concentration table (CSV/XLSX) includes a column of sample weights or volumes and per-sample concentration values must be made consistent by dividing through that column, leaving metadata columns untouched.

name: weighted-alignment-score-computation
description: Use when candidate feature pair alignments (FPAs) between two LC-MS feature tables already exist — grouped by m/z with a fitted RT spline — and each alignment must be ranked and validated by a similarity score.

name: weighted-cosine-correlation-search
description: Use when querying tandem mass spectra (e.g., ESI-MS2 from QqQ or QqTOF instruments) against a spectral reference library and you need to quantify identification performance (precision/recall/F) at a fixed similarity-score cutoff.

name: weighted-cosine-similarity-scoring
description: Use when you have paired predicted and experimental EI mass spectra (e.g., NEIMS predictions vs. NIST 2017 measured spectra) and need to quantify prediction quality or benchmark a spectral predictor.

name: weighted-cosine-similarity-scoring
description: Use when matching an observed electron-ionization mass spectrum against a reference/augmented library to identify a molecule and you need ranked candidates with recall@k metrics.

name: weighted-cosine-similarity-scoring
description: Use when scoring ESI-MS2 query spectra against a reference library (e.g. 3045 MassBank ESI-MS2 records of 679 synthetic drugs) to classify compound identifications at a similarity score threshold such as 0.6, or when benchmarking exponent choices.

name: weighted-cosine-similarity-spectrum-comparison
description: Use when a query EI mass spectrum must be identified by ranking it against a spectral reference library, especially when the library has been augmented with predicted spectra (e.g. NEIMS outputs) and recall@k must be measured.

name: weighted-dew-exclusion-window-parameter-tuning
description: Use when tuning dynamic-exclusion behaviour of a DDA method in ViMMS: full-scan mzML files of complex mixtures (e.g. serum/beer extracts) are available and t0/t1 values for WeightedDEW must be chosen by maximizing simulated coverage before instrument validation.

name: weighted-distribution-compound-sampling
description: Use when an unfiltered network expansion would generate too many compounds to expand further, and you want stochastic, similarity-biased pruning toward a set of target compounds rather than a hard cutoff.

name: weighted-dot-product-spectrum-comparison
description: Use when scoring peptide-spectrum matches (PSMs) against simulated theoretical spectra of unlabeled or SIP-labeled peptides — e.g., validating Sipros database-search outputs in stable isotope probing (SIP) proteomics.

name: weighted-dynamic-exclusion-parameterization
description: Use when tuning or benchmarking DDA controller parameters (e.g., WeightedDEW exclusion windows t0/t1) and you need to measure fragmentation coverage of picked peaks in mzML injections of complex mixtures against TopN and optimal upper bounds.

name: weighted-fragment-tree-optimization
description: Use when given a low-resolution MSn peak list from a miniaturized mass spectrometer and a candidate formula constraint set, and you need a maximum weighted fragment tree to annotate top fragmentation peaks.

name: weighted-graph-probability-computation
description: Use when you have a weighted graph combining a spectral network and structural-similarity edges among MetFrag candidate structures, seed nodes from spectral library matches, and need per-node walking probabilities for annotation propagation.

name: weighted-least-squares-calibration
description: Use when converting MRM peak abundances to absolute concentrations for targeted metabolites: calibration standards of known concentration (e.g. 14 standards spanning 0.025–500 mol/mL) are available and regression coefficients per transition are needed.

name: weighted-least-squares-calibration-modeling
description: Use when a targeted metabolomics dataset contains calibration points, QC samples and internal-standard intensities, and absolute concentrations must be back-calculated from signal intensities.

name: weighted-mean-intensity-aggregation
description: Use when a RAMClustR clustering run has assigned features (MS and idMS/MS) to clusters and you need to convert the feature-by-sample abundance matrix into per-cluster spectral intensities and exportable MSP spectra.

name: weighted-mse-loss-implementation
description: Use when training a neural network to regress EI mass spectra as fixed-length (1000-bin) intensity vectors and the loss must weight m/z bins consistently with the downstream cosine-similarity library-matching score.

name: weighted-nearest-neighbor-embedding-multimodal-spatial
description: Use when you have spot-level feature matrices from spatial transcriptomics (e.g. 10X Visium .h5ad), spatial metabolomics (MALDI-MSI peak/intensity matrices), or haCCA-integrated multi-module matrices, and want to compare cluster counts and heterogeneity across modality views.

name: weighted-pathway-similarity-scoring
description: Use when two KEGG organisms' metabolic networks have been reconstructed at the structural and functional levels and you need quantitative global similarity scores (Psim, PsimW, Csim) per organism pair.

name: weighted-penalty-score-match-selection
description: Use when two post-QC LC–MS feature tables (RT, m/z, FI medians) have been candidate-matched but some features remain in clusters with multiple candidate matches and need unique one-to-one correspondence.

name: weighted-regression-model-selection
description: Use when building quantitative calibration curves from a serial concentration standard series (e.g., narcotics standards) and estimating an unknown test sample's concentration by choosing between weighted linear and quadratic fits.

name: weighted-risk-score-construction
description: Use when you have pre-derived hazard-ratio weights and cohort-level metabolite/risk-factor measurements and need to build, apply, and comparatively evaluate weighted risk scores for mortality prediction (C-statistic, IDI) in an independent cohort.

name: weighted-similarity-score-compound-sampling
description: Use when expanding a compound database with Pickaxe rules and unfiltered or similarity-cutoff expansion grows exponentially (e.g. YMDB one-generation expansion gives 575,262 compounds), but you need a fixed-size, target-biased network.

name: weighted-unifrac-computation
description: Use when you have a Qemistree chemical tree plus a feature table of MS1 peak areas and need tree-informed sample comparisons, e.g., to quantify how chemically similar foods or samples are.

name: weighted-unifrac-distance-estimation-on-chemical-tree
description: Use when a metabolomics chemical-feature table (FeatureTable[Frequency]) is paired with a Qemistree hierarchy and you need tree-informed sample distances, PCoA ordination, or PERMANOVA that reduces chromatography-driven batch signal.

name: weisfeiler-lehman-fragment-deduplication
description: Use when enumerating MAGMa substructure-annotation fragments (up to breakage depth 3) from molecule–spectrum pairs and you must collapse isomorphic fragment graphs into canonical nodes before assigning spectral peaks and building the fragmentation DAG.

name: welch-oneway-anova-metabolite-features
description: Use when a preprocessed MetaboSet peak table from MS-DIAL via notame must be tested feature-wise across two or more study groups, and per-feature p-values need multiple-testing correction.

name: welch-t-test-log-transformed-intensities
description: Use when comparing log-transformed GC-TOF MS metabolite intensity distributions between two groups of biological metadata triads (organ/species/disease) and you need per-compound p-values with unequal-variance robustness.

name: welch-test-log-transformed-intensity-comparison
description: Use when comparing metabolite intensities across two broad biological ontology categories (e.g. 'digestive tract' vs 'Bacteria') over many metadata-combination pairs, where unequal variances and log-normal intensity distributions require Welch's t-test on log-transformed values.

name: welch-two-sample-t-test-metabolomics
description: Use when raw per-metabolite p-values are needed from a two-group comparison (e.g., sex) of ungrouped log-transformed metabolite abundances via Welch's unequal-variance t-tests, prior to eigen-analysis-based FWER adjustment.

name: welch-two-sample-ttest-adduct-abundance-comparison
description: Use when validating ion-identity/adduct assignments from an aligned MS1 feature table across experimental conditions where a specific adduct class should change in abundance (e.g. post-column salt infusion of sodium acetate or ammonium acetate vs H2O control).

name: well-predicted-metabolite-identification
description: Use when you have paired microbial feature tables (RA or CLR transformed) and metabolite tables and need to flag which metabolites a MiMeNet model predicts significantly better than chance, rather than reporting only mean SCC.

name: wes-candidate-list-integration
description: Use when a patient has a DeepVariant/Exomiser candidate gene list and per-gene metabolomic enrichment scores, and you need to rank those candidates by network-propagated metabolomic evidence and benchmark against Exomiser's phenotype ranking.

name: wgcna-module-detection
description: Use when you have a metabolite-by-sample quantification matrix (e.g. LC-MS peak areas from a pseudotargeted metabolomics run) and need to group co-accumulating metabolites into modules for biomarker metabolite screening.

name: wgcna-module-detection-metabolomics
description: Use when a normalized metabolite measurement table (e.g. Metabolon®-style data with SUB_PATHWAY annotations) should be partitioned into co-abundance modules and tested against sample traits such as tumor vs normal status or gender, without predefined metabolite sets.

name: wgcna-module-eigenmetabolite-screening
description: Use when analyzing a pseudotargeted metabolomics feature/peak-area table (metabolites × samples) across a mutant or treatment panel to find co-abundance modules and rank samples by module eigenmetabolite for biomarker metabolite screening.

name: wheat-metabolomics-feature-handling
description: Use when a set of MS/MS feature spectra in .mgf format needs a 2D similarity-based overview embedding, or when reproducing the paper's wheat-data t-SNE grouping of features around reference standards like Procyanidin-A2.

name: whittaker-penalized-least-squares-smoothing
description: Use when a group-delay-corrected FID dataframe from 1H-NMR metabolomics data still contains a dominant residual solvent decay that must be separated from the sample signal before apodization and Fourier transform.

name: whittaker-smoother-parameterization
description: Use when a GCxGC-MS chromatogram (e.g., a baseline-corrected 2D-TIC from the MTBLS579 dataset) still contains noise after baseline correction and signal smoothing along the first chromatographic dimension is required before multivariate analysis.

name: whole-cell-cytosol-segmentation-mesmer
description: Use when IMC nuclear channel (DNA-intercalator/Histone 3) segmentation exists but whole-cell boundaries are needed to profile per-cell protein and metabolite signals in spatially crowded tissue.

name: wide-format-data-loading
description: Use when the input is a wide-formatted metabolomics feature table (samples as columns, features as rows) plus a design file, to be fed into any SECIMTools tool or Galaxy-wrapped step.

name: wide-format-feature-table-parsing
description: Use when the input is a SECIMTools wide-format dataset (sample IDs in columns, metabolomics features in rows) plus a design file assigning samples to groups, before running PCA, ANOVA, random forest, or Elastic Net tools.

name: wide-format-feature-table-processing
description: Use when the input is a wide-format feature intensity table (unique feature identifiers as rows, samples as columns) plus a companion design file, and the goal is blank-based quality-control filtering of metabolomic features.

name: wide-format-metabolomics-data-handling
description: Use when a metabolomics feature table (post peak-picking, samples-as-columns/features-as-rows) contains missing values that must be filled before downstream statistical analysis or tool linkage in SECIMTools/Galaxy.

name: wiff-scan-block-binary-parsing
description: Use when raw AEMS data are in Sciex .wiff/.wiff.scan format and you need full-scan (precursor ion or neutral loss) spectra per acoustic ejection rather than vendor MRM output.

name: wikidata-property-mapping
description: Use when a curated, validated TSV of structure-organism-reference pairs (e.g. LOTUS table.tsv.gz from Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.5794106) must be converted into Wikidata-formatted upsert records for batch import.

name: wikidata-structure-organism-triple-retrieval
description: Use when a task requires enumerating or counting LOTUS referenced structure-organism pairs (chemical structure item linked to biological organism item) via the public Wikidata SPARQL endpoint at https://query.wikidata.org.

name: wikipathways-pathway-annotation-mapping
description: Use when a list of differentially expressed genes (e.g. |log2FC| > 1) must be linked to curated pathway annotations by extending a Cytoscape network with a WikiPathways linkset via CyTargetLinker.

name: wilcoxon-mann-whitney-nonparametric-testing
description: Use when comparing GC–MS metabolite relative concentrations between two small, independent sample groups (e.g. 11 disease vs 14 control serum samples) and a nonparametric test is needed to call metabolites significantly dysregulated.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-differential-ion-testing
description: Use when a peak table matrix of spatial metabolomics pixels (X/Y coordinates + m/z intensity columns) needs ion-level tissue-vs-background classification, e.g. to quantify the proportion of tissue-enriched ions.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-differential-testing
description: Use when pixels from an MSI feature matrix (e.g., 14,260 pixels × 3,044 ion peaks) have been assigned to biological regions via UMAP-kmeans clustering and you need a non-parametric per-ion differential test between two region groups (e.g., MB clusters 6/1 vs HIP clusters 23/12).

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-group-comparison
description: Use when comparing a numeric spectral or ranking feature between two independent groups (e.g., correct rank #1 vs lower-ranked FSA formula assignments) where the feature is non-normally distributed, so a rank-based test like Wilcoxon rank-sum with medians/quartiles is required.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-group-comparison
description: Use when comparing relative-abundance metabolomics features (e.g. bile-amidate intensities) across three unordered phenotype groups (non-IBD control, CD, UC) without assuming normality, and per-feature adjusted p-values are needed.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing
description: Use when comparing two unpaired groups on numeric features (metabolomics peak intensities, omics abundances) or when relating a MOFA factor to binary clinical metadata, without assuming normality.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing-with-fdr-correction
description: Use when comparing ion intensities between two spatial metabolomics regions (auto-clustered or manually drawn ROIs) on a feature matrix, and metabolite intensity distributions cannot be assumed normal.

name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-paired-testing
description: Use when two models are evaluated on the SAME set of features (e.g. the 466 annotated metabolites of the IBD PRISM dataset) under paired CV settings, and you need a nonparametric test on paired per-feature SCC differences.

name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-test
description: Use when two structure-prediction methods have been run on the same paired set of MS2 spectra (e.g., 93 CASMI 2017 spectra or a 660-spectrum test set) and you need a significance test on their per-spectrum similarity distributions.

name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-testing
description: Use when two classifiers (e.g., MSMCE-ResNet50 vs. ResNet50 baseline) have been evaluated on the same N = 6 stratified CV folds and you must test whether the paired metric improvement (Accuracy, F1) is statistically significant.

name: win-rate-statistical-comparison
description: Use when ranked candidate structures from a de novo model and one or more database-search methods exist for the same spectra and you must quantify which method is better per spectrum and at k = 1, 10, 50.

name: wine-metabolomics-class-discrimination
description: Use when a peak-based NMR feature/sample/peak-value matrix (e.g. from speaq 2.0 peak picking, grouping and BuildFeatureMatrix) must be tested for features that significantly differ between two or more sample classes.

name: wine-quality-supervised-classification
description: Use when a tabular dataset with a categorical class label (e.g. wine quality rating) must be turned into a class-prediction pipeline whose pre-processing, feature selection and estimator settings are optimised by exhaustive grid search and validated on unseen samples.

name: wine-windows-executable-deployment
description: Use when a vendor-locked Windows executable (Agilent .d, Thermo .raw converter) must run on Ubuntu or another Unix-like OS and no native port exists.

name: within-condition-correlation-threshold-screening
description: Use when quality-controlling an expression dataset where samples should cohere within biological conditions — e.g. before differential-expression analysis, to verify same-organ, same-tumor-status samples show pairwise Pearson correlations >0.70 and to flag low-expression outlier samples.

name: within-pathway-trend-consistency-checking
description: Use when comparing directed vs mixed reporter_score modes on a KO abundance table and you must confirm that directed-mode enriched pathways show consistent within-pathway KO directions while mixed-mode sign cancellation precludes trend interpretation.

name: within-replicate-cv-consistency-evaluation
description: Use when comparing feature-detection/quantification consistency of preprocessing workflows (e.g. two-stage apLCMS vs traditional apLCMS vs XCMS) on replicated multi-batch LC/MS data with known replicate triplets.

name: within-subject-correlation-statistical-testing
description: Use when the same subjects contribute paired/longitudinal metabolomics measurements (e.g., venous and arterial samples at matched time points) and you need to rank metabolites by significance for within-subject differential analysis or feature selection.

name: wmys-regenerated-fingerprint-recall-evaluation
description: Use when you have a lipidomics MS/MS dataset with a reference list of reported lipids and need to measure the recall gain contributed by WMYn-regenerated (5th-level) fingerprints versus a truncated 1st–4th-level library and the MS-DIAL public database.

name: word2vec-embedding-inference
description: Use when you need learnt spectral embeddings from a large MS/MS corpus (e.g. GNPS-derived UniqueInchikey or AllPositive datasets) instead of peak-matching cosine scores, to compare spectra or detect structurally related molecules.

name: word2vec-skipgram-embedding-training
description: Use when you have unlabeled Pfam domain annotations from a large genome corpus and need dense per-domain feature vectors (e.g., pfam2vec.csv) to feed a downstream detector such as the DeepBGC Pfam2VecTransformer.

name: word2vec-spectral-embedding
description: Use when predicted or measured EI mass spectra must be converted into fixed-length dense vectors for approximate nearest-neighbor library matching, e.g. before building or querying an HNSW index over a million-scale in-silico EI-MS library.

name: word2vec-spectrum-embedding-training
description: Use when you need to build a Spec2Vec spectral similarity score and must train (or select a pretrained) Word2Vec embedding from a large processed MS/MS library such as the AllPositive GNPS dataset.

name: workflow-entity-semantic-annotation
description: Use when a Nextflow (or similar) workflow has been packaged as an RO-Crate and its data entities and CreateAction steps need machine-readable semantic metadata to make the crate findable and FAIR-compliant.

name: workflow-good-fair-poor-classification
description: Use when one or more normalized peak tables produced by candidate processing workflows (S1–S4 outputs) must be evaluated for study-specific performance and ranked via the five-criterion Good/Fair/Poor scheme of NOREVA.

name: workflow-handoff-validation
description: Use when running a containerized multi-process workflow (e.g. MS-DIAL → MS-FLO) and you must confirm the automatic transfer of intermediate outputs between processes and validate the downstream result.

name: workflow-process-inventory-extraction
description: Use when you must quantify the structural complexity of a Nextflow workflow — enumerating processes from main.nf and user-facing parameters from conf/*.config and tool parameter files — to compare against another workflow's reported counts.

name: workflow-resource-report-inspection
description: Use when you must audit how a completed Nextflow run recorded runtime, CPU/memory resource usage, container images, parameter settings, and version metadata, or when reproducing provenance outputs claimed in a paper.

name: workflow-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when a ddMS2 centroided mzML sample (~4000 spectra) must be timed through the full PFΔScreen pipeline — 'Run FeatureFinding' followed by 'Run PFASPrioritization' — to verify the sub-1-minute runtime claim.

name: workflow4metabolomics-tabular-export
description: Use when a binned NMR bucket-intensity matrix (rows = buckets over Bin.SpectraPoint spectral points, per sample) from MetaboLights or Metabolomics Workbench must be reshaped into Workflow4Metabolomics .TABULAR or MetaboAnalyst CSV inputs.

name: workflowhub-workflow-registration
description: Use when a computational workflow (e.g. a Nextflow pipeline like action.nf) must be made findable and reusable by packaging it with annotated metadata into an RO-Crate and publishing it on WorkflowHub.

name: worm-metabolomics-sample-grouping
description: Use when an LC/MS metabolomics dataset (e.g. xcms peak table plus raw MS/MS runs from C. elegans WT and hacl-1 mutant or other condition contrasts) must be grouped by sample class before differential filtering in Metaboseek.

name: xcalibur-sequence-table-generation
description: Use when a plate-based (e.g. 384-well) metadata sheet of compounds must be converted into an Xcalibur sequence.csv for Orbitrap ID-X flow injection MSn acquisition.

name: xcms-based-metabolomic-feature-extraction
description: Use when raw LC-MS mzXML files from a hybrid DDA (pooled QC) / DIA (individual samples) metabolomics run need feature extraction before rescue and annotation, or when centWave-based peak-picking is the desired engine.

name: xcms-camera-adduct-cluster-annotation
description: Use when benchmarking an LC-MS feature-detection method against XCMS/CAMERA on the same measurements, and you need XCMS+CAMERA output as a comparable feature map with isotope/adduct annotations resolved.

name: xcms-camera-peak-grouping-configuration
description: Use when raw LC-MS mass-spectrometry files (e.g. the MTBLS146 maternal plasma subset) must be converted into an aligned feature matrix of detected spectral features across biological, blank, and QC samples.

name: xcms-centwave-feature-detection
description: Use when raw LC-MS data in mzXML format (e.g. DDA and DIA-(SWATH) acquisitions from a Bruker Impact II UHR-QqTOF) need peak picking and metabolic feature detection prior to merging features or annotating metabolites via MS2 spectral matching.

name: xcms-centwave-parameter-tuning
description: Use when processing raw untargeted metabolomics mzML/mzXML/CDF data (qTOF, orbitrap, or FT-ICR) into a features table and no dataset-specific centWave parameter set exists, making manual tuning prohibitively time consuming.

name: xcms-eic-extraction-and-evaluation
description: Use when an XCMS-processed untargeted LC–MS dataset (getEIC()/fillPeaks() output) needs per-peak quality features, or when Pass/Fail peak-quality labels must be derived before ML-based peak filtering.

name: xcms-feature-detection-comparison
description: Use when raw LC/MS mzML files are available, an XCMS peak list exists as the baseline, and the goal is to measure which true peaks another detector recovers that XCMS missed after removing blank/degenerate signals.

name: xcms-feature-eic-extraction
description: Use when you have centroid-mode AIF LC-MS chromatograms already processed with xcms and RAMClustR (xcmsSet/RC objects) and need per-feature MS1 and high-collision-energy EIC peak shapes to build pseudo-MS/MS spectra.

name: xcms-feature-grouping
description: Use when starting from raw mzXML/mzML LC/MS runs (untargeted metabolomics) and a grouped peak table is needed as input for isotope-labeling detection or feature-based downstream analysis.

name: xcms-feature-table-generation
description: Use when raw untargeted metabolomics data (.mzML/.mzXML/.CDF) from qTOF, Orbitrap, or FT-ICR instruments must be converted into a features table via XCMS centWave peak detection, grouping, and retention time correction.

name: xcms-feature-table-import
description: Use when you have XCMS run output tables (unaligned and aligned CSVs, e.g. XCMS_unaligned_run1.csv / XCMS_aligned_run1.csv) and a Benchmark.csv that must be loaded into mzRAPP for NPP reliability assessment.

name: xcms-feature-table-processing
description: Use when raw untargeted LC/MS mzXML files (e.g. MetaboLights MTBLS213) must be converted into an XCMS xcmsSet feature table to serve as input for isotopic-label detection downstream.

name: xcms-mzmine-parameter-tuning
description: Use when comparing how consistently XCMS and MZmine detect and correspond LC-MS features on the same centroided mzML dataset, e.g. reproducing the HZV029 discrepancy (10,901 XCMS vs 42,099 MZmine features, ~60% matched).

name: xcms-output-parsing
description: Use when unaligned and aligned XCMS output tables (CSV) from LC-HRMS NPP must be loaded and matched to an mzRAPP benchmark (e.g. MTBLS267-derived Benchmark.csv) to quantify peak picking and alignment reliability.

name: xcms-parameter-tuning-bw-windows
description: Use when XCMS-preprocessed LC-MS peaks need paired grouping results at two RT-window resolutions (large bw = expected maximal RT drift; small bw ≈ inverse of scan frequency) as input to ncGTW misalignDetect.

name: xcms-peak-annotation-integration
description: Use when XCMS-flagged features have been realigned by ncGTW and the realignment output must be converted back into XCMS RT warping functions (xcmsLargeWin@rt$corrected) and relocated apex positions for downstream grouping/peak-filling.

name: xcms-peak-grouping-parameterization
description: Use when preparing XCMS preprocessing outputs for ncGTW misalignment detection: after centWave peak detection (ppm=15, peakwidth=c(2,25)) and retcor, run group() twice (bw=6 and bw=0.3, mzwid=0.05) on the same sample set.

name: xcms-peak-picking-baseline
description: Reference for benchmarking a chromatography–MS marker-identification method against XCMS, or when peak picking on 2D m/z vs retention-time maps is needed and conventional XCMS peak detection is an acceptable baseline.

name: xcms-peak-picking-parameterization
description: Use when raw LC-MS mzXML files must be converted into a per-sample feature table via embedded XCMS peak picking as the PP baseline of a JPA rescue analysis.

name: xcms-peaktable-processing
description: Use when an untargeted LC/MS stable isotope-labeling experiment has already been preprocessed by XCMS (peak picking, alignment, grouping) into an xcmsSet with paired unlabeled/labeled sample tags, and labeled features must be annotated against a metabolite database.

name: xcms-preprocessed-data-handling
description: Use when untargeted LC–MS data has been pre-processed with XCMS (peak-picking, RT correction, grouping) and must be turned into an M11 metric matrix (e.g. 500 peaks x 11 metrics) for Pass/Fail peak-quality classification or evaluation.

name: xcms-preprocessing-output-handling
description: Use when xcms peak picking, grouping, and retention-time correction have been run on raw LC-MS samples (e.g. the faahKO dataset) and the feature matrix must be combined with feature and sample metadata into one coherent R object.

name: xcms-sample-class-annotation
description: Use when an XCMS XCMSnExp/xcmsSet from labeled-vs-unlabeled LC/MS metabolomics experiments must have its samples assigned to condition classes (e.g., CELL_Glc12 unlabeled vs CELL_Glc13 labeled) before geoRge processing.

name: xenobiotic-metabolite-annotation
description: Use when LC-HRMS feature tables (accurate m/z, RT, MS2) from xenobiotic incubation or exposure samples need reaction-guided metabolite annotation without authentic standards or reference spectral libraries.

name: xgboost-gradient-boosted-classifier-training
description: Use when you have expert-labelled DIA-MS files with numeric QC features (precursor metrics like F2/F13/F14 plus DIA raw-file features F1, F3–F12) and need a blinded binary qualified/unqualified LC or MS performance classifier.

name: xgboost-lipid-signature-classification
description: Use when co-registered MALDI MSI and IFM data are available with a marker segmentation mask (e.g. Ly6G-positive/-negative pixels), and the goal is to discover which lipid m/z features distinguish annotated cell populations via supervised ML classification.

name: xgmml-linkset-generation
description: Use when building a custom-made linkset to extend a Cytoscape network with CyTargetLinker, e.g. converting a tab-delimited relationship table (source/target id, type, datasource columns) into a validated XGMML linkset.

name: xgmml-linkset-interaction-mapping
description: Use when a Cytoscape network (gene list, PPI, author-article graph) must be extended with curated external interactions stored as XGMML linksets, and the goal is to attach e.g. pathway, TF-target, or compound-target links to current network nodes.

name: xic-based-feature-assessment
description: Use when you have an MZmine-preprocessed full-scan feature table (.csv with row ID, row m/z, row retention time, peak area) and need to statistically filter which features are real chromatographic signals worth targeting for MS/MS fragmentation.

name: xic-derived-retention-time-annotation
description: Use when you have Thermo .raw files containing spiked-in Biognosys iRT peptides and need observed retention times or an rt-vs-iRT-score calibration line for use-case style targeted analysis in R.

name: xic-instrument-mass-accuracy-filtering
description: Use when you have a repository-scale collection of LC–MS/MS experiments (e.g. mzML files mined from MassIVE GNPS) and need to filter out files/spectra with unreliable precursor m/z before model training, grouping them into quality tiers.

name: xic-intensity-profile-extraction
description: Use when time-resolved, direct-injection MS1 features (e.g. from DBDI-FT-ICR-MS .mgf data) must be converted into per-scan XIC intensity profiles so adduct series such as [M+1-3O+H]+ can be correlated and mass-difference validated.

name: xic-isomer-peak-detection-slope-criteria
description: Decision support for distinguishing co-eluting glycan isomers sharing an identical m/z in LC-MS extracted ion chromatograms, where mass accuracy alone cannot separate them and slope-based edge detection plus a relative intensity threshold is needed.

name: xic-missing-value-imputation
description: Use when an aligned DBDI-MS feature table (one column per scan, one row per feature) contains np.nan fields from scans where a signal was not detected, and downstream identify_adducts() analysis requires uniform-length XICs.

name: xic-pearson-correlation-adduct-detection
description: Use when a direct-injection or plasma-ionization (DBDI) MS dataset has been aligned and imputed into uniform-length XIC feature tables and you need to putatively identify adducts/in-source fragments of the same analyte without chromatographic separation.

name: xic-pointwise-correlation-analysis
description: Use when the input is a time-resolved direct injection MS dataset (DBDI/plasma ionization, .mgf/.mzML/.mzXML) and putative adducts or in-source fragments of the same analyte must be identified without chromatographic separation.

name: xlsx-spreadsheet-field-extraction
description: Use when you have a deposited .xlsx chemical database file and need to pull per-entry name, SMILES, InChI, InChIKey and IUPAC fields for validation, comparison or downstream identifier generation.

name: xlsx-tabular-data-parsing
description: Use when a scientific dataset is distributed as a multi-column .xlsx file and specific rows must be extracted by a metadata criterion (e.g. entries carrying publication references) before further validation or harmonization.

name: xml-source-parsing
description: Use when rebuilding the RaMP database from raw source downloads and each source must be parsed from its native format (HMDB XML, KEGG REST output, Reactome mapping files, GPML XML) into analyte-pathway relations.

name: yaml-configuration-parsing-for-ms-workflows
description: Use when starting a Shinyscreen target/suspect/non-target HRMS prescreening run and a YAML configuration plus a compound-list CSV must be turned into validated inputs with derived precursor ion masses.

name: yaml-driven-deep-learning-model-configuration
description: Use when you need to reproduce or retrain IDSL_MINT transformer models (fingerprint or SMILES translation) from a deposited .yaml configuration plus .msp reference spectra in positive or negative ion mode.

name: yaml-rules-file-authoring
description: Use when suspect screening results (formula and compound annotations with scores and candidate rankings) need automatic, rule-based estimation of Schymanski identification levels and the mapping from scores/labels to levels must be inspectable or customizable.

name: yaml-workflow-reproducibility-archiving
description: Use when running a matchms SpectrumProcessor/Pipeline cleaning job (e.g. on an MS/MS library such as the GNPS public library) and you must guarantee reproducibility and transparency of every filter applied.

name: yeast-lipidome-background-modeling
description: Use when designing or validating a targeted PRM/MRM lipidomics assay and you need to quantify how many precursor-fragment pairs (0, 1, 2, 3 fragments) are required for unambiguous lipid species identification within a defined background lipidome.

name: yeast-metabolic-model-application
description: Use when analyzing yeast LC/MS untargeted metabolomics data with a feature table (e.g. MAVEN-extracted features from mzXML) and you want pathway/network activity prediction without prior metabolite identification.

name: yeast-metabolite-target-counting
description: Use when comparing how many target metabolites each single separation method (HILIC-Orbitrap MS or CE-Orbitrap MS with nanoCEasy interface) detects in yeast extracts versus augmented multi-platform ESI-positive/ESI-negative data evaluations.

name: yeast-mutant-library-ratio-ranking
description: Use when you have MALDI-TOF spectra for many colonies (e.g., 749 colonies at a site-saturation library position) and need per-colony ratios of fatty acyl fragments like C16:1 vs C18:1 to rank and identify mutants.

name: yeast-phenotype-regulation-calling
description: Use when AriumMS-processed augmented feature intensity tables (HILIC [ESI−]/[ESI+], CE alkaline BGE, CE acidic BGE, CE cation) from growth-inhibitor-treated vs. control Saccharomyces cerevisiae extracts must be reduced to per-target regulation calls and per-augmentation detection counts.

name: yeast-two-hybrid-result-interpretation
description: Use when a Results passage describes a yeast two-hybrid assay with a bait/prey protein pair and a positive interaction that must be captured as one row of a physical-interaction evidence table.

name: youden-index-threshold-optimization
description: Use when a binary classifier (e.g., M5 sigmoid outputs on averaged pathway waveform signals) yields probability scores that must be converted into class labels and no operating point is fixed — pick the cutoff maximizing TPR − FPR.

name: z-score-annotation-ranking
description: Use when annotating metabolites in untargeted LCMS studies where fragmentation spectra are unavailable and annotation must rely only on m/z ratios and retention times, i.e., when mass-filtered candidate lists must be ranked by RT agreement.

name: z-score-feature-normalization
description: Use when a multi-sample HRMS feature table (e.g., Agilent .csv export with 136 features from the dienogest/drospirenone time-course at 0, 4, 10, 29 h) is about to be clustered by dm.ms_cluster and per-feature abundance trends must be made comparable before DBSCAN eps/min_samples are set.

name: z-score-normalization-of-rank-metrics
description: Use when aggregating per-model feature-importance ranks across multiple omics feature sets into one global regulator ranking, e.g. combining ranks from 225 metabolite random-forest models over nine feature sets where raw ranks are not directly comparable across classes.

name: z-score-sample-subgroup-stratification
description: Use when a user-defined gene panel (e.g., interferon-stimulated genes) is available and samples in a transcriptomics matrix must be assigned to positive/negative subgroups for downstream per-subgroup DGE and enrichment analysis.

name: z-score-standardization-of-fluxes
description: Use when you have triplicate metabolite intensity measurements at 0 h and 72 h (culture and medium samples) and need to convert raw boundary flux estimates into standardized z-scores for cross-metabolite or cross-species comparison, e.

name: z-score-standardization-with-back-transformation
description: Decision support for imputing missing metabolite values where missingness is due to missing at random combined with a limit of detection (LOD); apply z-score standardization before computing neighbor distances and back-transform imputed values afterwards.

name: zenodo-benchmark-data-retrieval
description: Use when reproducing G-Aligner benchmark evaluations or any task requiring the QE_HF/MTBLS562/TripleTOF_6600 datasets: the deposit DOI 10.5281/zenodo.8313034 supplies mzML raw files, manual annotations and evaluation scripts that must be laid out per the README directory tree.

name: zenodo-benchmark-dataset-download
description: Use when a task requires the raw LC–MS benchmark data (MTBLS562, QE_HF, TripleTOF_6600), manual analyte annotations, or the deposited evaluation scripts needed to reproduce G-Aligner alignment-accuracy comparisons.

name: zenodo-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when a reproduction or audit task requires retrieving the deposited MSnLib spectral files from Zenodo record 11163380 to count MS2 spectra, merge/deduplicate MSn trees, and compute compound coverage against Extended Data Tables 2 and 3.

name: zenodo-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when a workflow needs the NPDB natural products database or seed scaffold files underlying the G.A.M.E. CSCCP solver, and the deposit contents must be enumerated and validated against published counts.

name: zenodo-spectral-archive-retrieval
description: Use when a downstream task needs the curated Spectraverse MS/MS library itself, or must independently verify the reported library statistics (488,630 spectra, 44,237 unique compounds) from the deposited archive.

name: zero-filling-and-line-broadening-parameterization
description: Use when raw time-domain 1H-NMR FIDs (e.g., Daphnia extract spectra) must be converted to frequency-domain spectra with defined apodization (0.3 Hz exponential) and zero-filling (131,072 points) before Fourier transform and automatic phase correction.

name: zero-inflated-gaussian-model-fitting
description: Use when metagenomic/metatranscriptomic gene-cluster abundance or expression tables (e.g. RPKM counts from BiG-MAP mapping) have many zero-inflated values and you need parametric differential testing between grouped samples.

name: zero-intensity-signal-filtering
description: Use when converting mzML or vendor raw files (.d, .raw) to the MZA HDF5 structure and spectra must be stored as jagged 1D arrays with zero-intensity points removed before writing Arrays_intensity/Arrays_mz datasets.

name: zero-order-phase-distortion-application
description: Use when validating that a spectral deconvolution method is robust to phase errors: add a known zero-order phase distortion (e.g., 0.2 rad) to simulated spectra with known ground-truth peak parameters and compare parameter recovery to the phased baseline.

name: zero-variance-feature-filtering
description: Use when preparing CCLE/DepMap-derived omics feature matrices (or any cell-line-by-feature table) as input to Metab8D random forest models and you need to drop features carrying no cross-sample variation before Z-scoring and 5-fold CV training.

name: zero-variance-feature-removal
description: Use when a molecular descriptor or fingerprint matrix (e.g. alvaDesc output for SMRT-like datasets) contains constant features or uninformative fingerprint bits that must be removed prior to regression or model training.

name: zigzag-index-computation-from-derivative-variance
description: Use when LC/MS metabolomics EICs must be filtered before peak detection, especially when the mass chromatographic quality (MCQ) index fails on EICs with high background signals or only a single peak.

name: zinb-gaussian-decoder-modeling
description: Use when integrating matched spot-level ST count matrices and continuous SM metabolite intensity matrices from one or more samples, and you need modality-faithful reconstruction plus batch correction in a shared latent embedding.

name: zinc-smiles-library-filtering
description: Use when preparing a pretraining corpus for a spectra-to-structure model whose synthetic-spectrum generator (e.g. RASSP, limited to 4096 fragment subformulae) imposes hard element-count and formula-complexity constraints on candidate molecules.

name: zodiac-posterior-score-threshold-analysis
description: Use when deposited or locally generated SIRIUS/ZODIAC result files are available and the goal is to pick a ZODIAC posterior-score cutoff for high-confidence molecular formula annotation.

name: zone-of-interest-derivation
description: Use when you need to reproduce Paramounter's automatic parameter-measurement step from raw LC-MS intensity profiles by reconstructing rank-based intensity sorting and the zone-of-interest mechanism in R.

name: zstd-block-compression
description: Use when converting vendor MRM chromatogram data (e.g. Xcalibur/SCIEX OS raw files) into the Aird format and you need compact, fast-decoding RT and intensity arrays for web rendering of hundreds of chromatograms.

name: zwitterion-spectral-library-curation
description: Use when standardizing SMILES annotations in an MS/MS spectral library (MGF/CSV) and rule-based charge neutralization would change the net charge — e.g., zwitterionic metabolites — causing one ionic form to be lost in later filtering.
